function foo() {
  let x
  bar(x ||= {})

Changelog: 2025

This changelog documents all esbuild versions published in the year 2025 (versions 0.25.0 through 0.27.2).

0.27.2

  • Allow import path specifiers starting with #/ (#4361)

    Previously the specification for package.json disallowed import path specifiers starting with #/, but this restriction has recently been relaxed and support for it is being added across the JavaScript ecosystem. One use case is using it for a wildcard pattern such as mapping #/* to ./src/* (previously you had to use another character such as #_* instead, which was more confusing). There is some more context in nodejs/node#49182.

    This change was contributed by @​hybrist.

  • Automatically add the -webkit-mask prefix (#4357, #4358)

    This release automatically adds the -webkit- vendor prefix for the mask CSS shorthand property:

    /* Original code */
main {
  mask: url(x.png) center/5rem no-repeat
}

    /* Old output (with --target=chrome110) */
    
main {
    
mask: url(x.png) center/5rem no-repeat;
    
}

main {
    
-webkit-mask: url(x.png) center/5rem no-repeat;
    
mask: url(x.png) center/5rem no-repeat;
    
}

Updates `express` from 5.1.0 to 5.3.0
Release notes

Sourced from express's releases.

v5.3.0

Highlights

🐞 Bug fixes

  • Fixed HTTP header conflict between Content-Length and Transfer-Encoding in res.send - by @​YuryShkoda in #4893

    Fixed the behavior of res.send() to prevent conflicts between Content-Length and Transfer-Encoding HTTP headers in responses. The Content-Length header in res.send() is now only added when a Transfer-Encoding header is not present, complying with the HTTP specification that states both headers should not coexist in the same response. ETag generation is unaffected by the presence of a Transfer-Encoding header - by @​cuishuang in #7459

Release notes

Sourced from lycheeverse/lychee-action's releases.

v2.9.0

Summary

This release updates the default lychee version from v0.23.0 to v0.24.2.

The main reason for this release is compatibility with the new lychee 0.24.x release artifacts. Starting with lychee v0.24.0, the archive layout changed, and the lychee binary may now be packaged inside a subdirectory. lychee-action now detects that layout automatically, so users can upgrade without changing their workflows.

If you use:

uses: lycheeverse/lychee-action@v2

you will get the new version once the floating v2 tag has been updated. If you pin exact versions, update to:

uses: lycheeverse/lychee-action@v2.9.0

What’s new from lychee v0.24.x

Better diagnostics

lychee now reports line and column numbers for detected links. This makes broken link reports easier to act on, especially in larger documentation sites or generated reports.

Text fragment checking

lychee can now check URL text fragments, such as links containing #:~:text=.... This helps catch links that point to a valid page but no longer points to the intended highlighted text.

Sitemap support

lychee can now read sitemap.xml inputs. This is useful for checking published websites or generated documentation sites where the sitemap is the easiest source of URLs to validate.

JUnit output

lychee now supports JUnit output. This makes it easier to integrate link checking results with CI systems and test reporting tools that understand JUnit XML.

Redirect and remap visibility

lychee can now show redirects and remaps more clearly. This helps explain why a URL was checked as a different final URL and makes debugging link-checking behavior easier.

Multiple config files

lychee now supports multiple configuration files and expanded config handling. This is useful for repositories that split documentation, website, or package-specific link-checking settings.

Timeout handling

lychee can now accept timeouts explicitly. This gives users more control over how strict their link checks should be for flaky or slow endpoints.

Fixes and reliability improvements

prs.title: feat(core): add configurable per-tool-call timeout (tools.callTimeout)
prs.body:
## Summary

Adds a `tools.callTimeout` setting that limits the wall-clock duration of any
single tool call. This addresses #3375, where long-running tool invocations
(notably shell commands) can run for an unbounded amount of time with no way to
cap them.

## Details

- The timeout is enforced centrally in `ToolExecutor`, so it applies uniformly
  to every tool (shell, MCP, web fetch, file ops, etc.). It reuses the existing
  `DeadlineTimer` utility and composes it with the caller's cancellation signal
  via `AbortSignal.any` — the same pattern already used by the agent runner in
  `packages/core/src/agents/local-executor.ts`.
- When the deadline is reached, the tool's `AbortSignal` fires and the call is
  reported as a **recoverable** error (`ToolErrorType.TOOL_CALL_TIMEOUT`) with a
  clear message, so the model can adapt (break the work into smaller steps, or
  the user can raise the limit) instead of the CLI waiting indefinitely.
- **Opt-in and backwards compatible:** the default is `0`, which (like any
  non-positive value) disables the timeout, preserving current behavior.
- For shell commands this complements the existing
  `tools.shell.inactivityTimeout` setting (which fires on lack of *output*);
  `tools.callTimeout` bounds *total* runtime.
- User cancellation is still reported as a cancellation (not a timeout), and the
  timer is always cleared in a `finally` block so it cannot fire late or keep the
  event loop alive.

The setting is expressed in seconds (mirroring `tools.shell.inactivityTimeout`)
and stored internally in milliseconds via `Config.getToolCallTimeout()`. The
generated settings reference (`docs/reference/configuration.md`,
`docs/cli/settings.md`) and the JSON schema (`schemas/settings.schema.json`)
were regenerated with `npm run docs:settings`.

## Related Issues

Fixes #3375

## How to Validate

1. Add to your `~/.gemini/settings.json`:
   ```json
   { "tools": { "callTimeout": 5 } }
   ```
2. Start the CLI and ask it to run a long shell command, e.g. `sleep 30`.
3. After ~5 seconds the tool call is aborted and the model receives a
   "Tool execution timed out after 5 seconds ..." error, instead of waiting for
   the full command to finish.
4. With `tools.callTimeout` unset or set to `0`, behavior is unchanged.

Unit tests:

```bash
npm test -w @google/gemini-cli-core -- src/scheduler/tool-executor.test.ts
npm test -w @google/gemini-cli-core -- src/config/config.test.ts
```

Docs/schema parity (matches the CI check):

```bash
npm run docs:settings -- --check
```

## Pre-Merge Checklist

- [x] Updated relevant documentation and README (if needed) — regenerated
      `docs/reference/configuration.md`, `docs/cli/settings.md`, and
      `schemas/settings.schema.json`.
- [x] Added/updated tests (if needed) — config getter tests and `ToolExecutor`
      timeout behavior tests (timeout fires, disabled by default, user
      cancellation still reported as cancellation).
- [x] Noted breaking changes (if any) — none; the feature is opt-in and disabled
      by default.
- [ ] Validated on required platforms/methods — the change is
      platform-independent timer/abort logic with no OS-specific code; it is
      covered by unit tests that run across the CI matrix (Linux and macOS,
      Node 20/22/24).

issues.body:
While doing (non-security) patch review with copilot CLI and model Claude Opus
5, I received this error:

  Execution failed: CAPIError: 422 This content was flagged for possible
  cybersecurity risk. If this seem wrong, try rephrasing your request. To get
  authorized for security work, join the Trusted Access for Cyber program:
  https://chatgpt.com/cyber (Request ID: AAAE:E5BF3:76D4E1:87C02B:6A6D089A)

The request involved a multi-agent workflow, so Copilot may have routed some
part of it through an OpenAI model or service despite the selected session
model.  In any case, the prescribed remedy does not appear usable: enrollment
at chatgpt.com/cyber is associated with my OpenAI identity, while this Copilot
request is associated with my GitHub identity.

Please provide a supported way for eligible Copilot users to obtain Trusted
Access for OpenAI-backed requests made through Copilot.  This might involve a
Copilot-specific enrollment, linking an approved OpenAI identity, or another
GitHub-managed verification mechanism.

> Use Git Bash commands for any terminal commands you run instead of Powershell.

issues.title: Session event delivery permanently fails after one 120s host-ack timeout ("session host did not acknowledge the <event> event within 120s"); session unusable until resume

labels.name: area:sessions
labels.description: Session management, resume, history, session picker, and session state

issues.body:
### Describe the bug

In long-running interactive sessions, prompt submission fails with:

```
Execution failed: Error: Request session.send failed with message: session event delivery failed:
session host did not acknowledge the tool.execution_partial_result event within 120s
```

After the first timeout, every later event delivery to that session host fails immediately with the same message, and the session accepts no more input. The only way to recover is to exit and run `copilot --resume` (or `/restart`).

Related: #5018. It has the same failure that never clears and the same `session.send failed` ending, but on the `permission.requested` 5-second path. This report covers general session event delivery with the 120s deadline, and the trigger appears to be the Node main thread becoming unresponsive.

### Affected version

GitHub Copilot CLI 1.0.94 (observed). Also seen on 1.0.90–1.0.92 builds, Oct 1–9. Not yet observed on 1.0.95-3.

### Steps to reproduce the behavior

Not deterministic. Conditions present in every occurrence:

1. Start an interactive session (`copilot`) and work in it for many hours: frequent shell tool calls, subagents, several auto-compactions, and at least one `copilot --resume` of the same session.
2. Let the context grow large (model request bodies of ~0.4–2 MB).
3. Eventually a turn stalls. About 120s later, the next prompt submission fails with the error above, and every later prompt fails the same way until exit and `--resume`.

### Expected behavior

- One late acknowledgement shouldn't break event delivery for the rest of the session. Delivery should resume once the host responds, or the session should reconnect automatically without exit and `--resume`.
- The Node main thread shouldn't stall for over 120s in long or large sessions.

### Additional context

**Environment:** macOS 26.7 (25G229), arm64 (Apple Silicon), Ghostty terminal, zsh.

**Log observations (`~/.copilot/logs/process-*.log`, several processes):**

- **The event type in the message varies:** `tool.execution_partial_result`, `session.usage_record`, `prompt_cache_break`, `session.managed_settings_resolved`, `session.background_tasks_changed`. The event named is whichever one was waiting when the deadline passed. `tool.execution_partial_result` shows up most often because one is sent for each chunk of shell output.
- **The failure never clears.** Only the first failure waits the full 120s. After that, every delivery fails within milliseconds with the identical message, which still names the original event. One process logged it 1,645 times.
- **Onset example:**
  ```
  19:28:07 [pending_request_flow] Waiting for detached host delivery flush
  19:28:44 [pending_request_flow] Detached host delivery flush finished {"acknowledged":true}   <- 37s, host already lagging
  19:28:46 [event_sink] Native model usage projection started                                 <- sends prompt_cache_break
  19:30:46 [pending_request_flow] ... session host did not acknowledge the prompt_cache_break event within 120s
  19:30:47 [github_telemetry::node_memory] Node memory snapshot timed out
  ```
  62 more `Node memory snapshot timed out` lines followed in that process, so the Node main thread was unresponsive. This isn't a delivery-transport problem.
- **Affected processes:** long-running (15+ hours, resumed sessions), ~1.7 GB of memory. Between stalls, the main thread was idle in `kevent`, so the stalls come in bursts rather than as a constant spin.

The full logs contain private repository content and can't be shared publicly. I can provide filtered excerpts on request.

issues.title: Session wedged: task subagent with unknown model id falls back to 128k default caps and fails the whole turn with 'Request exceeds the model's prompt budget'

labels.name: area:agents
labels.description: Sub-agents, fleet, autopilot, plan mode, background agents, and custom agents

labels.name: area:models
labels.description: Model selection, availability, switching, rate limits, and model-specific behavior

issues.body:
### Describe the bug

In a long-running interactive session, the session gets stuck. On every turn where the main agent delegates to a `task` subagent, the whole turn fails with a prompt-budget error. The main context is far below its own limit. The cause appears to be a `task` call with a `model` id that isn't in the catalog. The runtime doesn't reject it. Instead it quietly falls back to default capabilities (128k), and the request then goes over that limit.

**What we saw (from local process logs and session events):**

1. The main agent model is `claude-opus-5.5`, picked in the model picker, with `contextTier` long_context (1M context, `maxPromptTokens` 968000). The main context is about 177k tokens, well within budget. Auto-compaction is measured against the long-context limit (earlier compactions logged `tokenLimit` 922000), so compaction never triggers.
2. The main model's response contains a `task` tool call (usage record `toolCounts {"task":1}`, and `{"task":2}` on the retry). Both responses also had `finishReason: "content_filter"` / `contentFilterTriggered: true`. That may or may not be related, but it looks suspicious.
3. Right after that, the process log shows this warning twice per turn:
   ```
   [WARNING] [rust:copilot_runtime::session::native_message_turn] turn model is in neither the picker nor the unfiltered catalog, nor the session's excluded-model capture; falling back to default capabilities and the chat-completions wire {"model":"claude-opus-4.8","latest_model_list_fetch_succeeded":true,"picker_models":23,"unfiltered_models":39,"catalog_only_models":6}
   ```
   So the subagent was requested with a model id (`claude-opus-4.8`) that isn't in the catalog. The `task` tool's own `model` enum doesn't list it either, but tool-argument validation didn't reject it.
4. Then a session-level error ends the user's turn:
   ```
   session.error {"errorType":"query","message":"Execution failed: Request exceeds the model's prompt budget after reserving output (143299 tokens; limit 128000). Reduce context or compact before continuing."}
   ```
   No `subagent.started` event is emitted. When the user prompts again, it fails the same way (143360 / 128000).
5. **Result:** the session is stuck. Every turn where the model delegates fails. The error tells the user to compact, but the main context is nowhere near its own limit. `/compact` doesn't fix the real cause, so the advice is misleading.

### Affected version

Copilot CLI 1.0.100, macOS arm64

### Steps to reproduce the behavior

1. Start an interactive session on a long-context model (for example `claude-opus-5.5` with the long_context tier).
2. Build up a moderately large context (about 140k+ tokens), still well under the main model's limit.
3. Have the main agent call the `task` tool with a `model` value that isn't a valid catalog id (seen here: `claude-opus-4.8`).
4. The turn fails with `Request exceeds the model's prompt budget after reserving output (~143k tokens; limit 128000)`, and the warning above appears in the log. Every later turn that delegates fails the same way.

### Expected behavior

- An unknown `model` value on the `task` tool is rejected at argument validation and returned to the model as a tool error, so it can retry with a valid id. It should not be silently mapped to default 128k capabilities.
- If a subagent request goes over its model's budget, that shows up as a failure of that one `task` tool call, not as a fatal session/turn error.
- The error message says which request and model hit the limit (subagent vs. main), so users aren't told to compact the wrong context.
- It would also help to know why the subagent prompt reaches about 143k tokens. Does a subagent inherit or fork the parent context?

### Additional context

Workaround: start a new session, or make sure subagent model ids are valid catalog ids.

Possibly related: #5201 (prompt-budget rejection has `errorType: "query"` and no stable error code) and #5127 (the same "neither the picker nor the unfiltered catalog" fallback, in BYOK/SDK mode).

issues.title: A session created with `create_session` can't be resumed after `close_session` if the user had switched to it
issues.body:
### Describe the bug

A session made with `create_session`, which the user has switched to and which another session then closes with `close_session`, can't be reopened in the same CLI process. `/resume` fails with:

`Failed to switch session: Error: Failed to associate local session <id> with its built-in plugin host`

Relaunching the CLI, or opening the session from a new CLI process, lets it reopen normally.

A created session that the user never switched to reopens normally after the same close. After the failed attempt, at a later switch between sessions, the CLI starts an MCP server process for the session that didn't open and leaves it running.

### Affected version

GitHub Copilot CLI 1.0.108-1

### Steps to reproduce the behavior

1. Turn on session management tools (`sessionManagementTools` in `~/.copilot/settings.json`). Our setup also had user extensions and one remote MCP server; we haven't tried without them.
2. In session A, call `create_session` twice to make sessions B and C.
3. Switch to B, then back to A. Don't switch to C.
4. In A, call `close_session` for B and for C.
5. Run `/resume` and pick B. It fails with the error above.
6. Run `/resume` and pick C. It opens.

When A closes B, the log shows `Cleaning up session <B>: Session closed via sessions.close`, then `Failed to apply session management settings: Error: the Copilot SDK reported a failure: RPC error -32603: Request session.management.configure failed with message: The destination session is not available`. Closing C logs only `Closing session <C>`.

### Expected behavior

A session closed with `close_session` can be reopened with `/resume` whether or not the user had switched to it.

### Additional context

- macOS on Apple silicon (arm64).
- Seen twice on 2026-11-08 with different sessions. Both times an MCP server process for the session that failed to reopen was still running afterward.
- Related: github/copilot-cli#5380 (created sessions start extensions only when the user switches to them) and github/copilot-cli#5164 (switching sessions leaks MCP servers and extension hosts).

issues.title: Bundled ripgrep aborts with jemalloc 'Unsupported system page size' on 16KB-page ARM64 kernels (Asahi Linux)

labels.name: area:platform-linux
labels.description: Linux-specific: Wayland, X11, Ubuntu, Fedora, Alpine, ARM, terminal emulators

labels.name: area:installation
labels.description: Installing, updating, versioning, PATH setup, and binary distribution

labels.name: area:tools
labels.description: Built-in tools: file editing, shell, search, LSP, git, and tool call behavior

issues.body:
## Description

The `ripgrep` binary bundled with the Copilot CLI (`<pkg-dir>/ripgrep/bin/linux-arm64/rg`) statically links jemalloc built assuming a 4KB page size. On a kernel configured with a 16KB page size — the default on Asahi Linux (Linux-on-Apple-Silicon) — the binary aborts immediately instead of running, which breaks any Copilot CLI feature that shells out to ripgrep for file search.

## Environment

- `copilot --version`: GitHub Copilot CLI 1.0.88
- OS: Ubuntu on Asahi Linux, kernel `7.0.0-1002-asahi-arm` (aarch64)
- `getconf PAGESIZE`: 16384
- Affected path pattern: `~/.cache/copilot/pkg/linux-arm64/<version>/ripgrep/bin/linux-arm64/rg` — reproduced on cached versions 1.0.83, 1.0.87, and 1.0.88, so this has been present across multiple releases.

## Reproduction

```
$ getconf PAGESIZE
16384
$ echo hello | ~/.cache/copilot/pkg/linux-arm64/1.0.88/ripgrep/bin/linux-arm64/rg hello
<jemalloc>: Unsupported system page size
<jemalloc>: Unsupported system page size
memory allocation of 160 bytes failed
Aborted (exit code 134)
```

`file` on the binary confirms it's statically linked (bundling its own allocator):

```
.../ripgrep/bin/linux-arm64/rg: ELF 64-bit LSB executable, ARM aarch64, version 1 (SYSV), statically linked, stripped
```

For comparison, the distro's own `rg` (dynamically linked, uses glibc's allocator, no jemalloc) runs fine on the same machine — the crash is specific to this bundle's static jemalloc, not the kernel or the machine generally.

## Expected

Any file-search feature that shells out to the bundled ripgrep should work on 16KB-page kernels, since ripgrep itself has no such restriction — this is purely a byproduct of how this specific prebuilt binary was compiled/linked.

## Suggested fix

Either build the bundled ripgrep against a page-size-agnostic allocator (e.g. link the system allocator instead of a statically-linked jemalloc build pinned to 4KB pages), or fall back to a PATH-available `rg`/`grep` when the bundled binary fails to exec/aborts.

## Workaround in use

Replacing the bundled `rg` at each cached version's `ripgrep/bin/linux-arm64/rg` with the system's dynamically-linked `rg` resolves the crash locally, but is undone on every CLI update since it re-fetches the broken bundle.

issues.title: Extensions don't start for sessions created with `create_session` until the user switches to them

labels.name: area:sessions
labels.description: Session management, resume, history, session picker, and session state

labels.name: area:plugins
labels.description: Plugin system, marketplace, hooks, skills, extensions, and custom agents

issues.body:
### Describe the bug

A session created with the session management tool `create_session` starts with no extension processes. Its model has none of the extensions' tools, none of the skills extensions register, and no extension hooks. Extensions start only when the user first switches to that session in the Sessions sidebar or with `/resume`, or when `/restart` restores it. Sessions the user starts directly, and prompt mode (`copilot -p`), load extensions within a second or two.

A created session is meant to work without the user watching, so it can spend minutes on its task without the tools it was asked to use.

### Affected version

GitHub Copilot CLI 1.0.108-1 (also seen in 1.0.105, 1.0.106, and 1.0.107)

### Steps to reproduce the behavior

1. Turn on session management tools (`sessionManagementTools` in `~/.copilot/settings.json`).
2. Add a user extension, for example `~/.copilot/extensions/probe/extension.mjs`, that calls `joinSession({ tools: [{ name: "probe_ping", ... }] })`.
3. In session A, ask the agent to call `create_session` with the prompt "Search your tools for probe_ping and say whether it exists." Stay in session A.
4. Session B reports that `probe_ping` doesn't exist. The process log has no extension launch for B's session ID, and B's `events.jsonl` has no extension events.
5. Switch to B in the sidebar. The log shows `Registering foreground session: <B>`, then `Session changed (<A> → <B>), reloading extensions`, followed by extension bootstrap lines for B. Send B any message; `probe_ping` is now available.

### Expected behavior

A session created with `create_session` gets the same extensions as any interactive session from the moment it's created, since the host supervises it and it is meant to work without the user watching.

### Additional context

- macOS on Apple silicon (arm64).
- Over two days on one machine, 10 sessions created by other sessions received their extensions between 36 seconds and 26 minutes after creation, each time when the user first opened the session.
- `copilot-sdk/docs/extensions.md` says `joinSession()` "attaches to the user's current foreground session", which may explain it.
- Possibly related: github/copilot-cli#5164 (switching sessions in the sidebar starts a set of extension hosts per session).

issues.title: Support OSC 7501 agent-status reporting for herdr-app/herdr-core
issues.body:
## Feature request

Please add native OSC 7501 (Program Status Protocol) reporting to Copilot CLI so terminals such as the new Herdr app can display Copilot sessions and track their activity.

## Current behavior

Copilot CLI launches and works inside a Herdr-managed terminal, but does not appear in the Agents sidebar.

For the running Copilot terminal, `hc get <terminal>` reports:

```json
{
  "reported": false,
  "status": null
}
```

Codex running in the same Herdr instance appears in the sidebar and reports:

```json
{
  "reported": true,
  "status": {
    "app": "codex",
    "state": "idle"
  }
}
```

This remains reproducible when launching Copilot manually from a Herdr terminal or through Herdr’s agent-launch menu.

## Expected behavior

Copilot reports its identity and lifecycle state through OSC 7501, allowing Herdr to distinguish:
- Idle and ready for input
- Working
- Waiting for permission or user input
- Finished or errored

Status reporting should be observational only and should not change permission handling.

## Steps to reproduce

1. Open the new Herdr desktop app backed by herdr-core.
2. Launch `copilot` inside a Herdr terminal.
3. Observe that Copilot runs but is absent from the Agents sidebar.
4. Run `hc get <terminal>` and observe that `reported` is false and `status` is null.
5. Launch Codex in another Herdr terminal and observe that it reports status and appears in the sidebar.

## Environment

- OS: macOS, Apple Silicon
- Copilot CLI: 1.0.106-2
- herdr-core: 0.1.16

## Context

This concerns the new `herdr-app` / `herdr-core`, not the older Herdr TUI. The new core relies on program-emitted OSC 7501 reports rather than screen scraping.

Herdr’s protocol overview:
https://herdr.dev/core/#status-from-the-source

issues.title: Cloud agent: MCP registry policy fetch fails with 401/403 on GHEC data residency, silently blocking all user-configured MCP servers
issues.body:
### Describe the bug

## Summary

On a GitHub Enterprise Cloud **with data residency** instance (`<tenant>.ghe.com`), every user-configured MCP server is silently dropped from Copilot **cloud agent** sessions. Only the platform defaults (`github-mcp-server`, `playwright`) reach the model. The cause is the registry-policy fetch failing with **401/403** and falling into the fail-closed path — the same defect as #2498, where only the **404** leg was fixed.

This is the same fail-closed family as #2498, #2552, #2567, #4346 and #4349, but reached through the cloud agent, where nothing is surfaced to the user at all.

## Environment

- Surface: Copilot cloud agent (not the local CLI, not an IDE)
- Host: GitHub Enterprise Cloud with data residency, `<tenant>.ghe.com`
- Two MCP servers configured in repo Settings → Copilot → MCP servers: one remote `http`, one `local` (stdio). Both valid per the documented schema, both with explicit `tools` lists.
- Enterprise MCP registry: none configured. `GET /copilot/mcp_registry` (user PAT) returns `{"mcp_registries":[{"url":"","registry_access":"allow_all",...}]}`
- `GET /copilot_internal/user` reports `is_mcp_enabled: true`, `copilot_plan: "enterprise"`

## What happens

From the CLI's own log inside the session (`~/.copilot/logs/process-*.log`):

```
[ERROR]   Failed to validate SDK token (401): GitHub returned: Bad credentials
[WARNING] session.gitHubAuth.setCredentials: failed to re-resolve copilotUser for token
          credential; token swap applied, plan/quota/billing metadata degraded:
          Failed to fetch Copilot user info: 401 Unauthorized: {"message":"Bad credentials"}
[WARNING] Failed to fetch MCP registry policy: 401 Unauthorized.
          Non-default MCP servers will be blocked until the policy can be fetched.
[ERROR]   MCP server "<remote-server>" filtered: Could not verify server against any configured registry
[ERROR]   MCP server "<local-server>"  filtered: Could not verify server against any configured registry
[ERROR]   Using deferred connection for default Playwright server
```

Probing the endpoint from inside the session with **every** credential present (`GITHUB_COPILOT_API_TOKEN`, `GITHUB_TOKEN`, `COPILOT_SDK_AUTH_TOKEN`, …): **403** on `api.<tenant>.ghe.com/copilot/mcp_registry`, **401** on `api.github.com/copilot/mcp_registry`. The same endpoint returns **200 `allow_all`** to a normal user PAT.

## Why this is a bug, not policy

1. **404 is tolerated, 401/403 is not.** The client special-cases a 404 as "no registry configured, allow all", but any other failure throws into the fail-closed catch that blocks every server without `isDefaultServer`. A tenant with *no registry configured* is therefore treated as if it prohibited everything, purely because its endpoint answers 403 instead of 404. #2498 fixed the 404 leg; the auth-failure leg has the identical consequence.
2. **This filter is documented as not applying to the cloud agent.** Per the MCP-management support matrix, "Registry display" and "Allowlist enforcement" are *Not supported* for Copilot cloud agent, and the enterprise docs state private MCP registries "apply to Copilot CLI and IDEs, but not to cloud agents that run on GitHub." It is nonetheless the filter rejecting these servers.
3. **The root credential failure looks host-related.** `Bad credentials` is what `api.github.com` returns for a token minted by another host, which suggests the SDK-token validation and/or the policy fetch resolves to public github.com rather than the data-residency tenant.

## Everything upstream is healthy

Verified in-session, so the failure is purely in the policy filter:

- `GET /repos/{owner}/{repo}/copilot/cloud-agent/configuration` returns both servers as stored.
- The `Start MCP Servers` step succeeds; the local MCP proxy serves all servers' tools (`GET 127.0.0.1:2301/tools` — 62 tools, including all of both user servers').
- The stdio server's `initialize`/`tools/list` handshake works when driven by hand on the runner.
- `COPILOT_MCP_ENABLED=true`, `GITHUB_COPILOT_3P_MCP_ENABLED=true`, `COPILOT_PERMISSION_MODE=allow_all`.

## Impact

**Nothing is surfaced.** No failed step, no warning in the pull request, no line in the session transcript. The messages above exist only in the CLI's private log inside the ephemeral runner. In our case a Microsoft Learn MCP server had been silently dead in every cloud-agent session for an unknown period, and we only found it while investigating a second server. Unlike the local CLI — where `--log-level debug` reveals it — cloud-agent users have no way to observe this.

Reproduced across three different agent runtime builds.

## Suggested fix

Either (or both):

1. Treat an **auth failure** (401/403) on the registry-policy fetch the same as 404 when no registry is configured for the tenant — i.e. extend #2498's fix beyond 404.
2. Fix host/token resolution so the policy endpoint authenticates on data-residency instances.

Additionally: surface a blocked-server warning on the pull request, the way firewall blocks already are. A silent drop is indistinguishable from the agent choosing not to use a tool.

## Ruled out

`MCP servers in Copilot` policy (enabled), registry allowlist (`allow_all`), custom agent `tools:` filter (none present), server transport (remote HTTP and local stdio fail identically), config schema (validated by the Settings UI), and any client-side override (no env var, CLI flag, or settings key reaches the gate; `isDefaultServer` is rejected by the Settings schema validator).

### Affected version

_No response_

### Steps to reproduce the behavior

_No response_

### Expected behavior

_No response_

### Additional context

_No response_

issues.title: New issue
Session-state artifact storage (~/.copilot/session-state/<id>/files/) strands project deliverables outside the active Git repository

labels.name: area:sessions
labels.description: Session management, resume, history, session picker, and session state

labels.name: area:tools
labels.description: Built-in tools: file editing, shell, search, LSP, git, and tool call behavior

issues.body:
## Summary

When working inside a Git repository, agent sessions frequently save project deliverables (architecture audits, test reports, readiness reviews, and one-off verification helper scripts) into `~/.copilot/session-state/<session-id>/files/` instead of the active repository worktree.

Because the files exist on disk in the session folder and are linked in the chat output, the task appears complete—but the repository itself is left missing those deliverables and reproducibility scripts across branches, clones, and subsequent sessions.

## Environment

- **GitHub Copilot CLI:** `1.0.107` / VS Code Agent Host (`vscode-agent-host`)
- **OS:** Windows 11 x64 (`win32`)
- **Git:** `2.56.0.windows.4`

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Open an agent session in a Git repository workspace.
2. Ask the agent to produce a project audit report, readiness review, or verification helper script during multi-step analysis or release verification.
3. Observe that the agent writes the Markdown report or `.cjs`/`.mjs` helper script under `~/.copilot/session-state/<session-id>/files/` and surfaces a link to that file.
4. Check `git status` in the repository worktree.

## Actual Behavior

- Project deliverables and helper scripts remain stranded in `~/.copilot/session-state/<session-id>/files/` outside the repository.
- Over multiple sessions, important project documentation, review records, and verification scripts accumulate in opaque UUID session folders without being tracked or discoverable in the repository.

## Expected Behavior

- Session storage (`~/.copilot/session-state/<session-id>/files/`) should be reserved for disposable runtime scratch, while requested project deliverables (plans, reports, documentation, and helper scripts) default to or are validated against the active Git repository worktree unless the user explicitly requests an external destination.
- Artifact presentation / completion should clearly distinguish or warn when a deliverable was written to ephemeral session state rather than the active repository worktree.

issues.title: Skills registered through an extension's `skillDirectories` disappear after `new_context`, and restored sessions don't see them

issues.body:
### Describe the bug

An extension passes `skillDirectories` to `joinSession`. The skill works until the session clears its context with `new_context` (event `session.context_cleared`). Afterward the `skill` tool reports "Skill not found" and the skill is missing from the available list, while the extension process is still running and its tools still work. `extensions_reload` brings the skill back.

Sessions restored by `/restart` have the same gap: they list their skills before their extensions join, so they miss the skill until the extension calls `session.rpc.skills.reload()`.

### Affected version

GitHub Copilot CLI 1.0.107

### Steps to reproduce the behavior

1. Add an extension that calls `joinSession({ skillDirectories: ["<dir containing probe/SKILL.md>"] })`.
2. In a session, call the `skill` tool with `probe`. It loads.
3. Call `new_context`.
4. Call the `skill` tool with `probe`. It reports "Skill not found". Personal and plugin skills are still listed.
5. Call `extensions_reload`, then the `skill` tool with `probe`. It loads again.

### Expected behavior

A skill directory contributed by a joined extension stays registered for as long as the extension is joined, across context resets and restores.

### Additional context

- macOS on Apple silicon (arm64).
- Seen on 2026-11-07. Five seconds after `new_context`, the `skill` tool reported the extension's skill not found while the extension process was running. After `extensions_reload`, the skill loaded.

issues.title: In prompt mode, an extension tool's permission request waits forever instead of being denied, and `--allow-tool` can't name an extension tool

labels.name: area:permissions
labels.description: Tool approval, security boundaries, sandbox mode, and directory restrictions

labels.name: area:non-interactive
labels.description: Non-interactive mode (-p), CI/CD, ACP protocol, and headless automation

labels.name: area:plugins
labels.description: Plugin system, marketplace, hooks, skills, extensions, and custom agents

issues.body:
### Describe the bug

In prompt mode (`copilot -p`), when the model calls a tool that an extension registers, the CLI raises a `custom-tool` permission request that nothing answers, so the run waits until it is killed. Prompt mode's permission handler returns early for that kind (`if (resolvedByHook || kind === "custom-tool") return;` in `cli-main.js`). Other requests that need approval in prompt mode are denied at once with `denied-no-approval-rule-and-could-not-request-from-user`, as the permissions help says they should be.

`--allow-tool` with the extension tool's name doesn't match the request either, and the permissions help documents no rule pattern for extension tools. Only `--allow-all-tools` works, so a scripted check of one extension tool has to allow every tool.

### Affected version

GitHub Copilot CLI 1.0.108-1 (prerelease). The same early return is in 1.0.107.

### Steps to reproduce the behavior

1. Install a plugin or user extension that registers a tool, such as `probe_ping`.
2. Run `copilot -p "Call probe_ping once."`. The run waits; `events.jsonl` shows `permission.requested` with `kind: "custom-tool"` and no `permission.completed` until the process is killed.
3. Run it again with `--allow-tool probe_ping`. Same result.
4. Run it with `--available-tools probe_ping --allow-all-tools`. The tool runs.

### Expected behavior

Prompt mode denies an extension tool request that no rule allows, as it does for other kinds, and `--allow-tool` accepts a pattern for one extension tool.

### Additional context

- macOS on Apple silicon (arm64).
- Reproduced on 2026-11-07 with an extension tool. With no rule, the run waited three and a half minutes until it was cancelled. With `--allow-tool` naming the tool, it waited the same way. With `--available-tools` naming the tool and `--allow-all-tools`, the tool ran.

issues.title: Render postToolUse hook messages in the Copilot desktop app

labels.name: area:plugins
labels.description: Plugin system, marketplace, hooks, skills, extensions, and custom agents

issues.body:
## Problem

`postToolUse` hooks can return output through `modifiedResult` and `additionalContext`, but the Copilot desktop app does not render the modified result in the user-facing tool-result surface.

A hook may execute successfully and return a message intended for the user, optionally alongside additional context intended for the model. In the desktop app, that message is currently surfaced only as "Additional guidance from postToolUse hooks" rather than in the normal tool result or in a dedicated user-facing message box. This makes hook-generated information easy to miss and differs from the GitHub Copilot CLI timeline presentation.

## Expected behavior

The desktop app should provide a user-visible surface for a message returned by a `postToolUse` hook, while preserving `additionalContext` for the model. The exact presentation is an implementation choice; the essential requirement is that hook-returned user messages are clearly visible in the conversation.

## Relation

Relates to #5099 (display-only hook for assistant messages).

issues.title: PowerShell tool allows silent recursive deletion of protected roots (C:\Users, \C:\Users\tmoam) without confirmation
issues.body:
## Summary

The PowerShell tool will execute a model-generated `Remove-Item -Recurse -Force` against **any path**, including `C:\Users` and `$HOME`, with no confirmation and no protected-path denylist. Combined with `-ErrorAction SilentlyContinue`, the deletion runs silently while most of the target is in use, so it destroys everything that is *not* locked and reports success.

In my case an agent generated this (intending to clean a temp folder):

```powershell
$home = Join-Path $env:TEMP "qml-shot\home"
Remove-Item -Recurse -Force (Split-Path $home) -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue
```

`$HOME` is a **read-only** automatic variable in Windows PowerShell 5.1, so the assignment fails, `$home` stays `C:\Users\<user>`, and `Split-Path` returns `C:\Users`. The line therefore deletes `C:\Users` recursively.

## Environment

- opencode 2.0.29 (`@opencode/cli`, npm install)
- Windows 11, Windows PowerShell 5.1 (`powershell.exe -NoLogo -NoProfile -NonInteractive -Command ...`)
- Agent mode, PowerShell tool

## What happened (timestamps local UTC+8)

| Time | Event |
|---|---|
| 14:39:37 | Tool call executed the command above |
| 14:40:16 | `~/.local/state/opencode/locks` recreated |
| 14:40:18 | `~/.config/opencode` recreated, log file recreated |
| 14:40:18.570 | "The server restarted while you were working." |
| 14:40:19.592 | "The instructions from `C:\Users\<user>\.config\opencode\AGENTS.md` no longer apply." |

The session record shows the command, then the server restart 41s later. The config directory's `CreationTime` is 14:40:18 — i.e. it was deleted and recreated by opencode immediately after the deletion, which makes the incident look like an update wiping config.

Damaged in this one event: `~/.config/opencode` (global config, MCP, plugins, AGENTS.md), `~/.cargo/bin` (rustup proxies), `~/.bun`, `~/.local/bin`, plus the server state/log. Earlier incidents with the same `$home` pattern removed the Node/Rust toolchains.

## Minimal reproduction

```powershell
# 1) assignment is rejected, $home keeps its original value
$home = "X"          # -> "Cannot overwrite variable HOME because it is read-only or constant."
$home                # -> C:\Users\<user>
Split-Path $home     # -> C:\Users

# 2) therefore this targets C:\Users, not a temp dir
Remove-Item -Recurse -Force (Split-Path $home) -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue
```

Expected: the tool refuses or asks for confirmation, and/or surfaces the resolved target.
Actual: silent recursive deletion of the user profile.

## Why it matters

- The blast radius is the entire user profile, not just opencode data.
- `-ErrorAction SilentlyContinue` hides in-use errors, so the command looks successful.
- Recovery is not always possible: deleted `~/.config/opencode/opencode.json`, MCP configs, plugins, and toolchain shims are unrecoverable (no recycle bin for programmatic deletes).
- Because opencode recreates its config/state directories on the next start, users misattribute the loss to an update and lose time chasing the wrong cause (I did, and filed this after forensics).

## Suggested mitigations

1. **Protected-path denylist for recursive deletes** — refuse (or require explicit confirmation) when the resolved target is, or is an ancestor of: `C:\`, `C:\Users`, `C:\Windows`, `C:\Program Files*`, `C:\ProgramData`, `/`, `/home`, `/Users`, `$HOME`, `%USERPROFILE%`, `%LOCALAPPDATA%`, `%APPDATA%`.
2. **Resolve and show the target first** — print the canonical absolute path in the tool-call header so a wrong variable expansion is visible before execution.
3. **Do not honour `-ErrorAction SilentlyContinue` / `2>/dev/null` for protected targets** — treat suppressed errors on those paths as a hard failure.
4. **Warn on shell-variable shadowing of automatic variables** — `$home`, `$profile`, `$env:...` assignment failures are silently non-terminating in PowerShell; surfacing `VariableNotWritable` as a tool error would have prevented this.
5. Optionally, keep an automatic pre-delete snapshot of the global config directory.

## Notes

The command was produced by an agent, not by opencode's own code, so this is a guardrail gap in the tool layer rather than a bug in the updater. I am **not** asking for destructive commands to be blocked outright — only for confirmation/denial on protected roots and for the resolved target to be visible.

Related but different (that one was about concurrent `bun install` in the config dir, closed as not planned): #16450.

issues.title: Windows: after self-update to 2.2.6, opencode.exe is a 229-byte stub and will not start (16-bit application error)
issues.body: ### Description I updated OpenCode. After that, it would not start. Windows showed a popup. It said "Unsupported 16-bit application". The full text was in Chinese. Here it is in English: > This program or feature "...\npm\node_modules\@opencode\cli\bin\opencode.exe" cannot start or run due to incompatibility with 64-bit versions of Windows. That was strange. OpenCode worked fine a minute before. So I looked at the file. `opencode.exe` was only 229 bytes. A real one is about 265 MB. The small file was not a program. It was just text. The text said the postinstall script was not run. Then I checked the npm logs. The update ran this command: ``` npm install --global --force @opencode/cli@2.2.6 ``` npm finished with exit code 0. It looked like a success. But the log had this warning: ``` warn install-scripts 1 package had install scripts blocked because they are not covered by allowScripts: warn install-scripts @opencode/cli@2.2.6 (postinstall: node ./postinstall.mjs) warn install-scripts Run `npm install -g --allow-scripts=@opencode/cli` to allow these scripts once, or `npm config set allow-scripts=@opencode/cli --location=user` to allow them for all global installs. ``` So npm blocked the postinstall script. That script puts the real `opencode.exe` in place. It never ran. Only the placeholder file was left. OpenCode did not notice. Its log said the update worked: ``` level=INFO message="updated OpenCode" from=2.2.5 to=2.2.6 method=npm role=cli ``` Then the background service saw a version mismatch. It tried to restart. Every restart hit the broken file. So I got the popup again and again. It kept looping. I fixed it by hand. I ran this in the package folder: ``` cd %APPDATA%\npm\node_modules\@opencode\cli node postinstall.mjs ``` After that, `opencode.exe` was 265 MB again. `opencode --version` printed `v2.2.6`. Everything worked. What I think should happen: - The update should not leave a broken file behind. - If the postinstall script is blocked, OpenCode should not say "updated". - It should tell me what went wrong. Or it should roll back. - The error should not be a scary "16-bit application" popup. That message tells me nothing. Some notes: - My npm config has `allow-scripts=opencode-ai`. That is the old package name. The new one is `@opencode/cli`. So it is not on the list. I did not add it myself for the new name. I did not know I had to. - I did not set `ignore-scripts`. `npm config get ignore-scripts` returns `false`. - npm version is 12.2.2. I think npm 12 blocks install scripts by default. Older npm did not. - I have other machines still on 2.2.5. I am worried they will break the same way when they update. ### Plugins A few plugins. I don't think they matter here. ### OpenCode version Updated from 2.2.5 to 2.2.6 ### Steps to reproduce 1. Use Windows 11 with npm 12 (I have 12.2.2). 2. Install OpenCode 2.2.5 globally with npm. 3. Let OpenCode update itself to 2.2.6. 4. Close OpenCode. Open it again. 5. Windows shows "Unsupported 16-bit application". 6. Check `%APPDATA%\npm\node_modules\@opencode\cli\bin\opencode.exe`. It is 229 bytes. ### Screenshot The popup (Chinese Windows, user folder hidden). Title: "不支持的 16 位应用程序" (Unsupported 16-bit application). ### Operating System Windows 11, npm 12.2.2 ### Terminal Windows Terminal

issues.title: docs: Go usage limits are shared across all models, not per-model as documented
issues.body:
## Summary

The Go documentation states that usage limits are enforced per model, but in practice the 5-hour (rolling), weekly, and monthly limits are a single pool shared across all paid models. Exhausting the rolling limit on one model blocks every other paid model, even models that have barely been used and are far below their documented per-model limit.

## Environment

- opencode version: 2.2.1 (desktop app, latest channel)
- OS: Windows 10 (Windows_NT 10.0.19045, win32 x64)
- Terminal: xterm-256color (OpenCode desktop app)
- Shell: C:\Windows\system32\cmd.exe
- Install/channel: latest (desktop app)
- Active plugins: none configured
- Plan: Go ($10/month), Personal workspace (single member)

## Reproduction

1. Subscribe to OpenCode Go on a Personal workspace.
2. Use a single paid model until the rolling (5-hour) usage limit is reached.
3. Switch to a different paid model that has not been used recently and send any request.
4. Observe that it is also rejected with "Go usage limit exceeded".
5. Open Console → Go: only three workspace-wide counters are shown (Rolling, Weekly, Monthly), with no per-model breakdown.
6. Switch to a free model (e.g. Beam Free): it still works.

## Expected Behavior

Per the docs (https://opencode.ai/v2/docs/console/go, "Usage limits"):

> "Each model has the following usage limits: 5-hour — 20% of the monthly limit; weekly — 50%; and monthly — 100%."

The pricing tables list a separate "Monthly limit" per model (e.g. GLM-5.3 $15, Claude Haiku 5.5 $15, DeepSeek V4.1 Flash $80), and the "Estimated requests" tables give per-model "Requests per 5 hours / week / month". Reaching the 5-hour limit on one model should not affect the others.

## Actual Behavior

The Console Go page shows a single set of counters for the whole plan, with no per-model split:

- Rolling usage: 100% used (resets in ~2.5h), with a "Go limit hit" badge and the message "Rolling limit reached. Go resumes in 2h 37m."
- Weekly usage: 96% used
- Monthly usage: 48% used

Every paid model then returns "Go usage limit exceeded", including models not used in the last 5 hours. Only free models (documented as "Unlimited") keep working.

Usage for Oct 19–29 (Console → Activity → Usage) shows no individual model anywhere near its documented limit, yet the shared rolling limit is fully exhausted:

| Model | Requests | Cost |
| --- | --- | --- |
| glm-5.3 | 163 | $5.25 (documented monthly limit: $15) |
| claude-haiku-5-5 | 329 | $1.71 (limit: $15) |
| deepseek-v4.1-flash | 601 | $1.07 (limit: $80) |
| grok-4.7 | 6 | $0.14 |
| glm-5.3-flash | 32 | $0.10 |
| qwen3.8-max | 3 | $0.08 |
| deepseek-v4-pro | 6 | $0.06 |
| longcat-2.0 | 20 | $0.04 |
| qwen3.8-flash | 23 | $0.03 |
| gpt-6-luna | 49 | $0.01 |
| kimi-k3 | 1 | <$0.01 |
| DeepSeek V4.1 Flash (free) | 28 | $0.00 |
| beam-free | 59 | $0.00 |
| Total | 1,320 | $8.50 |

## Additional Context

- Reproducible consistently: any paid model is blocked the moment the shared rolling counter hits 100%.
- The Activity page also shows "Most used this period" as percentages of one shared pool (DeepSeek V4.1 Flash 47%, Claude Haiku 5.5 25%, GLM-5.3 13%), which only makes sense if the allowance is shared.
- Either the documentation should be corrected to describe a shared allowance, or the enforcement should match the documented per-model limits. As written, the per-model "Monthly limit" column and the per-model request estimates are misleading.

issues.title: [FEATURE] Session tree: branch history, rollback-and-continue from any message, branch navigation (like Pi)
issues.body:
## Feature request

Pi (earendil-works) has **tree-shaped session history**: you can go back to any earlier point in the conversation, fork a new branch there, and navigate the branches like a git history. OpenCode only has a single-level `fork`/`compact` — no way to revisit earlier states of the same session.

## What I'd like

In the **Desktop app** (and TUI):

1. **Session timeline / tree view**: every fork creates a branch; you can see the whole tree of a session (like a git graph).
2. **Rollback to any node**: select any earlier message → "continue from here" creates a child branch without losing the current branch (i.e., an explicit `fork` at any point, not just at continue).
3. **Branch navigation**: switch between branches of the same session, diff summaries between branches.
4. Visualization: sidebar tab "History/Timeline" in desktop app.

## Why

- Current behavior: `--fork` / fork in desktop clones the whole session; you cannot see *where* in the conversation the fork happened, and multiple alternative explorations quickly become unmanageable (100+ sessions).
- For debugging AI workflows (try idea A, try idea B from the same point, compare) it's the single most effective pattern.
- Pi has shown the UX; OpenCode has the storage (messages are already stored) — mainly a UI + routing change.

## Related

- #34430 (closed: V2 session.fork API) — the API exists; this is the *user-facing tree UI*.
- #38558 (session.generate contract) — relevant to how branches export.

## Proposal

- Treat every session as a DAG/branch tree in storage (parent_id on messages).
- Add `/tree` slash command or sidebar tab: shows branch nodes, lets you jump/continue.
- `--fork` becomes "create branch at latest message", new `--fork <msg-id>` to fork at any message.

issues.title: Desktop: fatal "Location plugins did not finish activating" when the OpenAI login refresh at startup takes over 5 seconds
issues.body:
### Description

When OpenCode Desktop starts and the saved ChatGPT/OpenAI login has expired, the built-in OpenAI plugins refresh it while plugins activate. If that refresh takes longer than 5 seconds, `/api/provider` and `/api/model` return 503 and the window shows a fatal error:

```
ServiceUnavailableError: Location plugins did not finish activating
```

Activation finishes about 2 seconds later in the background (`credential updated integrationID=openai`, then `provider.updated` / `model.updated`), but the window stays on the error until Desktop is restarted. The next start works because the token is fresh.

From the 2.2.5 build it looks like:
- each plugin-dependent request waits at most 5 seconds for Location plugin activation, then fails with 503;
- `ChatGPTPlugin`, `OpenAIPlugin` and `OpenAIContextCapsPlugin` await `integration.connection.resolve(...)` during activation, which refreshes the expired token;
- plugins activate one after another, so every later plugin waits behind the refresh.

Possible fixes: the window could wait or retry instead of treating this 503 as fatal, or the OpenAI plugins could refresh the token after activation or on first use.

Related: #57204 (same error on ACP `session/resume`).

Logs from the failing start (Desktop main/renderer and server, trimmed):

```
14:58:13.752 v2 CLI background service ready
14:58:19.058 GET /api/provider 503 (5060 ms)
14:58:19.060 GET /api/model 503 (5062 ms)
14:58:19.088 fatal renderer error: ServiceUnavailableError: Location plugins did not finish activating
14:58:20.730 credential updated integrationID=openai
14:58:20.858 provider.updated / model.updated
```

### Plugins

opencode-quota (local build). Its setup takes about 5 ms and runs after the built-in OpenAI plugins; the error is the same with a slow token refresh and no slow plugin work.

### OpenCode version

Desktop 2.2.5 (bundled CLI 2.2.5)

### Steps to reproduce

1. Sign in to OpenAI with ChatGPT in OpenCode Desktop.
2. Quit Desktop and wait until the access token has expired.
3. Make the token refresh slow. I held the reply to `POST https://auth.openai.com/api/accounts/oauth/token` for 8 seconds in a test harness; a slow network does the same.
4. Start Desktop.
5. The window shows "Location plugins did not finish activating". With no delay it starts normally.

issues.title: plugin: git dep with a build/prepare script fails — compiled binary can't run its own bundled npm-cli.js
issues.body:
## Summary

`opencode plugin add`/`plugins` fails with `NpmInstallFailedError: git dep
preparation failed` for **any** git dependency whose `package.json` has a
`build`, `prepare`, `preinstall`, `install`, `postinstall`, or `prepack`
script, or a `workspaces` field — regardless of git host. Root cause: the
compiled `opencode` binary re-invokes itself as the "npm" binary for pacote's
git-dependency prepare step, but its own CLI doesn't know how to run that,
so it just prints help and exits instead of running the prepare install.

## Environment

- opencode version: 2.0.7 (channel: latest)
- OS: Darwin 25.6.0 (macOS, darwin arm64)
- Shell: /bin/zsh
- Install: global npm-style install (`@opencode/cli`), compiled binary

## Reproduction

Fully public, no auth/network involved beyond a normal git clone:

```sh
opencode plugin add "git+ssh://git@github.com/lnwu/opencode-plugin-repro-withbuild.git"
```

That repo's `package.json` is just:

```json
{
  "name": "opencode-plugin-repro-withbuild",
  "version": "1.0.0",
  "scripts": { "build": "echo building" }
}
```

Renaming that one script key to anything other than `build` / `prepare` /
`preinstall` / `install` / `postinstall` / `prepack` (and not using
`workspaces`) makes the exact same install succeed — nothing else about the
repo changes. This is host-independent: I originally suspected a self-hosted
git server was the trigger, but a scriptless package installs fine from that
same self-hosted host, and this scripted package fails from github.com too.
Only the presence of one of those script names (or `workspaces`) matters.

## Root Cause

`opencode plugin add` installs git specifiers through npm's real
`@npmcli/arborist` (`packages/core/src/npm.ts`, `Npm.reify` →
`arborist.reify()`), not Bun's own installer. Arborist's git fetching goes
through `pacote`'s `GitFetcher`. `pacote/lib/git.js`'s `#prepareDir` runs an
extra step *only* when the cloned `package.json` declares one of those
scripts or `workspaces` — it shells out to a real `npm install` inside the
clone so any `prepare`-style script has its own deps available:

```js
// pacote/lib/git.js
return npm(
  this.npmBin,
  [].concat(this.npmInstallCmd).concat(this.npmCliConfig),
  dir,
  { ...process.env, _PACOTE_NO_PREPARE_: noPrepare.join('\n') },
  { message: 'git dep preparation failed' }   // <- the error we see
)
```

`pacote`'s `npmBin` defaults to the string `'npm'` (resolved via `PATH`), but
opencode's server log shows it's configured to a path inside its own bundled
filesystem instead:

```
args=["/$bunfs/bin/npm-cli.js","install","--force","--cache=...", ...]
```

`pacote/lib/util/npm.js` spawns this as `<process.execPath> <npmBin>
<args...>` (the same way you'd run `node npm-cli.js install ...`). That's
correct for a normal Node runtime, but `process.execPath` for opencode's
compiled binary *is the opencode binary itself* — so this ends up invoking
opencode with `/$bunfs/bin/npm-cli.js install --force ...` as CLI arguments.
opencode's own CLI parser doesn't recognize those as a valid subcommand, so
it just prints help and exits (confirmed in the server log, immediately
before the `NpmInstallFailedError`):

```
message="cli starting" args=["/$bunfs/bin/npm-cli.js","install","--force", ...]
message="cli process failed" cause="Cause([Fail(~effect/cli/CliError/ShowHelp: Help requested)])"
message="cli process failed" cause="Cause([Fail(NpmInstallFailedError (cause: Error: git dep preparation failed))])"
```

So the nested `npm install` never actually runs, pacote's prepare step fails,
and opencode's error wrapper discards the real cause down to the generic
`NpmInstallFailedError`.

Confirmed by calling the exact same `Arborist.reify()` opencode calls
directly (outside opencode, both as a plain script and as a `bun build
--compile`'d binary) — it installs the same git dependency successfully in
both cases, because `npmBin` isn't overridden to a bunfs path there.

## Expected Behavior

Per the [plugins docs](https://opencode.ai/v2/docs/plugins#manage) ("Git
repositories can use hosted shortcuts, HTTPS, or SSH..."), any git dependency
should install the same way `npm`/`bun` would handle it, including ones with
a `build`/`prepare` script.

## Workaround

None needed if you control the package: avoid `build`/`prepare`/
`preinstall`/`install`/`postinstall`/`prepack` script names (rename them) and
avoid `workspaces` in the installed package's `package.json`, and ship any
build output pre-built/committed instead. Not viable for git dependencies you
don't control.

issues.body:
﻿## Environment

- OS: Windows 11 x86_64, PowerShell
- opencode: `opencode v2.2.6` (output of `opencode --version`, captured 2026-11-09)
- Plugins (from `opencode.jsonc`): `oh-my-opencode-slim` (resolved 3.0.7 in the npm cache), `@openviking/opencode-plugin`
- State: one interactive TUI session open in `C:\Users\lee\Dropbox\htdocs\nick` (shared background service running, the default)

## Steps to reproduce

1. In terminal A, start the TUI in a project and leave it open:
   ```powershell
   cd C:\Users\lee\Dropbox\htdocs\nick
   opencode
   ```
2. In terminal B (any other cwd), run a headless prompt:
   ```powershell
   cd C:\Users\lee\tmp
   opencode run "Run Get-Location and reply with only its raw output"
   ```
3. Repeat with a private server:
   ```powershell
   cd C:\Users\lee\tmp
   opencode run --standalone "Run Get-Location and reply with only its raw output"
   ```
4. Try the positional directory argument that the root help advertises, with `run`:
   ```powershell
   opencode run C:\Users\lee\tmp "Run Get-Location and reply with only its raw output"
   ```

### Probe transcript

Step 2 (caller cwd `C:\Users\lee\tmp`), reported reply:

```
PS C:\Users\lee\tmp> opencode run "Run Get-Location and reply with only its raw output"
C:\Users\lee\Dropbox\htdocs\nick
```

- Step 3 (`--standalone`): same result, wrong directory.
- Step 4 (positional directory): the path is consumed as part of the message text. The model received the path inside the prompt rather than it being used as a working directory.
- File operations performed by the run also landed in `C:\Users\lee\Dropbox\htdocs\nick`.

Note: the transcript above was gathered earlier on 2026-11-09 on this machine. It was not re-executed when this draft was written, to avoid another run writing into the live project.

## Expected vs actual

**Expected:** `opencode run` executes in the caller's working directory (as most CLIs do), or in a directory the caller can set explicitly.

**Actual:** The run's session directory is the project of the active TUI session, regardless of the caller's cwd. `--standalone` does not change this. There is no documented or working way to choose the directory for `run`:

- `opencode run --help` (v2.2.6) lists these flags: `--continue`, `--session`, `--fork`, `--worktree`, `--model`, `--agent`, `--format`, `--file`, `--title`, `--archived`, `--thinking`, `--auto`. It has no directory or `--cwd` option, and its usage is `opencode run [flags] [<message...>]`.
- The root `opencode --help` shows `opencode <subcommand> [flags] [<directory>]` with `directory  Directory to start OpenCode in (optional)`. With `run`, the positional argument is absorbed into `message...`.
- https://opencode.ai/docs/cli/ (checked 2026-11-09) documents `opencode ~/code/my-project` only for the TUI. Its Automation section for `opencode run` says nothing about directory selection.

## Impact

Headless automation scripts (run from unrelated working directories) wrote files into an unrelated LIVE project directory twice before the cause was identified. Any script or CI job that calls `opencode run` while a TUI is open elsewhere can modify the wrong project. The problem is silent: nothing warns that the directory differs from the caller's cwd.

## Suggested fix

Any of these would resolve it:

1. Make `opencode run` default to the caller's cwd, and send that directory to the shared service as the session directory.
2. Add an explicit option for `run`, e.g. `--cwd <dir>` or `--dir <dir>`, and document it on the CLI page.
3. At minimum, document how headless runs are supposed to target a directory. Also stop the root-level `[<directory>]` positional from being swallowed into the message for `run`. Either reject it with an error or honor it.

Question for maintainers: is there a supported way today to set the directory for `opencode run` when the shared background service is already attached to another project? If so, it does not appear in `--help` or the docs.

issues.title: Add loong64 (LoongArch64) builds for the opencode CLI
issues.body:
**Is your feature request related to a problem?**

Yes. There is currently no way to run opencode natively on LoongArch64 (`loongarch64`) Linux systems:

- The npm package (`opencode-ai`) only ships prebuilt binaries for linux-x64 and linux-arm64, so installation on loong64 fails with no matching platform package.
- There is no fallback path, because the CLI binaries are compiled with `bun build --compile` and Bun itself does not run on LoongArch64 yet.

**Describe the solution you'd like**

Please provide `opencode-linux-loong64` prebuilt binaries for the CLI (and ideally the desktop app / electron builds too). Alternatively, if running from source under Node.js is feasible, documenting that path would already unblock loong64 users in the meantime.

**Context**

- Loongson (LoongArch64) machines are common in China's education deployments, typically running UOS or Kylin / Loongnix (deb-based), so this is a real and growing user base.
- The loong64 toolchain is mature upstream: Linux kernel, GCC/LLVM, Go 1.21+, Rust tier-2, and community Node.js builds all work.
- Known blocker: Bun does not support LoongArch64 yet — open upstream request at oven-sh/bun#15839. Official loong64 support for opencode likely depends on (or could be coordinated with) that issue.
- Happy to help test builds — I have a loongarch64 machine running UOS 20 available.

**Environment**

- OS: UOS 20 (deb-based)
- Arch: loongarch64 (LoongArch64 / Loongson 3A series)

issues.title: [Bug] OpenCode steals foreground focus and disrupts user workflow when testing/running apps (Window Activation / Focus Stealing)
issues.body:
### Description

### **Description**

When OpenCode executes tasks in the background that involve launching, testing, or inspecting an application, the target application window forcefully launches into the **foreground active window**. This steals OS-level keyboard/mouse focus from whichever window the user is currently working in (e.g., code editor, browser, notes).

### **Actual Behavior**

* Running an app or background test in OpenCode pops the application window directly on top of active work.
* Focus is stolen from the active window, causing mid-sentence typing interruptions.
* The user has to manually re-focus their active application every time OpenCode runs or tests a UI build.

### **Expected Behavior**

OpenCode should execute background app checks, previews, and UI tests without taking active window focus away from the user's primary workspace.

Testing and UI inspection tasks should run:

* **Headless or Off-Screen:** Virtual framebuffers or hidden rendering contexts so no physical window disrupts the desktop.
* **Without Focus Activation:** If a GUI window must open, it should launch in a non-activating background layer (`SHOWNOACTIVATE` / non-activating window flags) so typing and work in the foreground are never interrupted.

### **Steps to Reproduce**

1. Open a workspace in OpenCode.
2. Trigger an action or agent task that executes or tests a target application.
3. Switch to another app and begin typing or editing.
4. **Observe:** The application spawned by OpenCode pops into the active foreground, stealing focus and interrupting work.

Here are the additional details to help debug this issue:

1. **OpenCode version:** OpenCode Desktop Version 2.1.2 (running on macOS, Apple Silicon / M1).
2. **Interface:** OpenCode Desktop App.
3. **What took focus & command ran:** 
   - The app taking focus is the desktop application under development in the workspace (for example, `myapp.app`).
   - The focus-stealing occurs when OpenCode runs/launches the compiled desktop app binary during background test/build cycles (e.g., executing the app directly via shell commands or `open myapp.app` without the `-g` background flag).
   - It is **not** the OpenCode built-in browser taking focus—it is the local macOS target application being tested.
4. **Summary of behavior:** 
   I was actively dictating text and working in another application (such as Notepad/TextEdit) while OpenCode was running background tasks on my project in the OpenCode Desktop app. While OpenCode was executing/testing the local desktop app build (`myapp.app`), the launched app window forcefully opened in the OS foreground. This stole system-level keyboard focus mid-dictation/mid-typing, causing text input to drop or lose target window state, and interrupting active media playback (like YouTube) by popping over the workspace.

**Key issue:** 
When OpenCode spawns or runs target macOS application binaries to verify or test UI work, it launches them as activated foreground processes rather than executing them quietly in the background (e.g., using `open -g` on macOS, non-activating window flags, or headless preview wrappers).

issues.title: jobs: background shell stuck running after process death; stale UI item cannot be cleared
issues.body:
## Description

A background shell job whose process terminated is never finalized by the daemon. It stays `status: running` in memory forever: the desktop session keeps showing it as **"1 running"** (still there 7+ hours later), its "Kill shell command" action does nothing, and no API can clear it. Only `opencode service restart` removes the ghost.

The persisted recovery record is stuck the same way (`kv` → `job.background/<notificationID>`, status unchanged since the spawn; no exit event was ever recorded).

## Plugins

None related to shells (OpenCode Desktop build; one local project plugin for context resume).

## OpenCode version

2.0.30 (bundled daemon `opencode v2.0.30`).

## Steps to reproduce

1. Start a long-running background shell from a session (shell tool with `background=true`). Here: `powershell -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File <script>.ps1`, spawn logged `2026-10-18T06:48:15.795Z`.
2. Let the process end without the normal close path. Here it was killed externally at ~`07:09Z` (its own log stops at `07:08:45Z`, then it is gone from the process list). The daemon log shows the spawn line but **no exit/termination line ever**.
3. Observe the stuck state (verified hours later):
   - `GET /api/shell/sh_14dc4a6b2001Hdh34Dm3AIylUi` → `404 ShellNotFoundError`
   - `shell.list` does not include it; `DELETE`(shell.remove) on the stale id → silent success, no state change — and the **same silent success for bogus ids** (so the UI kill action cannot even detect the shell is gone)
   - no `job` endpoints exist to complete/cancel a running job; `session.inbox`/`session_pending` are empty
   - the UI item never self-heals; the kv record stays `"status":"running"` indefinitely
   Only a service restart clears it (in-memory state).

## Expected behavior

- Finalize the job when the process exits for any reason (including external kill), and/or reconcile stale `running` jobs (e.g., at daemon startup).
- Provide a real way to clear/cancel a stale running item; `shell.remove` for an unknown id should 404 (like `shell.get` does) instead of silently succeeding — the silent success is what makes the stale UI chip unclosable.

## OS

Windows 11 (10.0.22631.6199, x64).

## Additional context

- Evidence: kv record `job.background/msg_14dc4a6d1001d5S3mF8TGMP39k` = `{"id":"sh_14dc4a6b2001Hdh34Dm3AIylUi","notificationID":"msg_14dc4a6d1001d5S3mF8TGMP39k","recovery":{"kind":"shell","sessionID":"ses_…","shellID":"sh_14dc4a6b2001Hdh34Dm3AIylUi","command":"powershell -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File \"<tmp>\\<script>.ps1\""},"status":"running"}` (unchanged since spawn).
- Job completion appears to rely solely on the process-exit event wired when the job starts; if that event is missed there is no reaper and nothing else can move the job out of `running`.
- Possibly related: #36424 (no way to stop a running background command), #43910 (closed; detached Windows process leaves parent session stuck running — workaround `POST /api/session/{id}/background`), #53564 (shells stuck "running"), #36348 (v2 shell restart semantics).
- Workaround used: `opencode service restart`, plus a UI refresh.

issues.title: Claude progress updates written before a tool call never show
issues.body:
### Description

Claude 5.5 models (and Fable 5+, Mythos 5.1+) send the short notes they write for the user between tool calls as "progress update" thinking blocks, not as text blocks. See https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/thinking#progress-updates.

opencode never shows these notes, for two reasons:

1. With adaptive thinking, Anthropic's default display is `omitted`, so the progress-update block comes back with empty text. Only the signature is left.
2. Even when the block has text (display `summarized`), the TUI renders it as collapsed reasoning, not as a message.

So when the model writes "Here is the draft: ..." and then calls a tool, the user never sees the draft. The model then refers to "the draft above", which isn't on screen.

This is the same bug as #52735, which was closed when v1 was frozen. It still happens on `dev` (v2).

### Steps to reproduce

1. Use `anthropic/claude-sonnet-5-5` (or `claude-opus-5-5`).
2. Ask for something where the model writes a message for you and then runs a tool, e.g. "write a two-line poem, then run `ls`".
3. The poem doesn't show. In the stored session, the assistant message contains a reasoning part with empty text whose signature decodes to a `narration` block, right before the tool call.

### OpenCode version

`dev`

### Operating System

macOS

prs.title: feat(acp): support _session/steering
prs.body:
### Issue for this PR

Closes #53042
Refs #44877
Supersedes #53043 (V1), ported to V2 as requested.

### Type of change

- [ ] Bug fix
- [x] New feature
- [ ] Refactor / code improvement
- [ ] Documentation

### What does this PR do?

Interim until ACP v2 (#44877); the v2 path would replace this.

Adds the `_session/steering` ACP extension so a client can redirect a running turn. `initialize` now advertises `_meta.steering.supported`. The handler checks `client.session.active()`: if the session is running it submits the prompt with `delivery: "steer"`, which the running loop picks up at its next step, and replies `injected`. If the session is idle it replies `promptRequired` and submits nothing, so a steer never starts an unrequested turn.

Differences from the V1 patch: a steering prompt into an idle session wakes execution by default, so the idle check is a separate `session.active()` call and the steer is submitted with `resume: false`. If the session goes idle between the check and the submit, the message stays in its inbox and goes out with the next prompt instead of starting a turn nobody asked for. Synthetic embedded context is submitted the same way as for a normal prompt, and a steered slash command is sent as plain text.

### How did you verify your code works?

- Added wire tests for the idle steer, the running steer, and malformed params (-32602), plus the `initialize` capability assertion. `bun test test/acp` passes except `error.test.ts` ("event stream drops its connection mid-turn"), which fails the same way on a clean `dev`. `bun run typecheck` is clean.

- Ran steered requests in [hydra-acp](https://github.com/smagnuso/hydra-acp) against this build.

prs.title: fix(core): stop retrying ChatGPT workspace usage limits
prs.body:
## Problem

On ChatGPT Business workspaces, an admin can cap how much of the shared plan each member uses. When a member hits that cap, sign in with ChatGPT returns `subscription_sharing_workplace_individual_usage_limit_exceeded`. We didn't know this code, so the session kept retrying a request that can't succeed until an admin raises the cap, then showed the raw provider error.

## Change

```diff
 subscription_sharing_workplace_individual_usage_limit_exceeded
-  retry with backoff → raw error
+  stop retrying → "You've reached the usage limit your ChatGPT workspace admin
+                   set for you. Ask them to raise it in the OpenAI Admin Console."
```

- `packages/core/src/plugin/provider/chatgpt.ts`: added the code to the no-retry list
- `packages/core/src/session/to-session-error.ts`: added the message

prs.title: fix(session-ui): prevent fatal error when a virtualized timeline row changes type
prs.body:
## Summary

Fixes #62800

Prevent a fatal renderer crash (`Error: Expected a user-message timeline row`) when a virtualized timeline row's key disappears or shifts during a timeline update (e.g., undo/revert, compaction, or message list update while a steered user message row is growing in).

### Root Cause
1. In `packages/app/src/session/timeline/virtualizer.tsx`, `VirtualRow` resolved its reactive row via:
   ```ts
   const row = createMemo(() => rowByKey().get(rowProps.rowKey) ?? rows()[item().index] ?? initialRow)
   ```
   When `rowProps.rowKey` disappeared from `rowByKey()`, falling back to `rows()[item().index]` could return a row with a different `_tag` (such as `AssistantPart`) at the same virtual index.
2. In `packages/session-ui/src/timeline/session-timeline-row.tsx`, `Row` dispatches via `<Show when={TimelineRow.key(props.row())} keyed>`, while each branch inside `render` defined a `current()` helper that re-read `row()` and threw `new Error("Expected a ... timeline row")` if the tag changed. When `<Show keyed>` disposed a growing `UserMessage` branch after `props.row()` switched to a different row type, `growIn`'s `onCleanup` invoked `onDone()` -> `() => grown(props.row.userMessageID)`, re-evaluating `props.row` -> `current()` against the new row type and throwing fatally.

### Changes
- **`packages/session-ui/src/timeline/session-timeline-row.tsx`**:
  - Pin the row accessor passed to `render` in `Row` (`pinTimelineRow`) so a keyed branch only updates when `TimelineRow.key(next) === key`.
  - Capture `const userMessageID = props.row.userMessageID` before registering `growIn` in `Frame` so cleanup never re-evaluates `props.row` during unmount.
  - Retain the last matching tagged row in each `render` branch's `current()` accessor instead of throwing on transient tag mismatches during disposal.
- **`packages/app/src/session/timeline/virtualizer.tsx`**:
  - Avoid falling back to `rows()[item().index]` in `VirtualRow` (`rowByKey().get(rowProps.rowKey) ?? initialRow`), matching `session-timeline.tsx`.
- **`packages/session-ui/src/timeline/rows-current.test.ts`**:
  - Add a regression test verifying that a keyed row accessor pinned via `pinTimelineRow` retains its `UserMessage` row when the key disappears and an assistant row occupies the same index.

## Test Plan

- [x] Added unit test in `packages/session-ui/src/timeline/rows-current.test.ts` covering row-type replacement at the same index when a key disappears from `rowByKey`.
