prs.title: feat(mcp): trust private-network server certificates on first use
prs.body:
### Issue for this PR

Part of #40111. Stacked on #60039 (per-server `tls` config); once that lands, this diff is just the first-use flow.

### Type of change

- [x] New feature

### What does this PR do?

Trusting a private-network MCP server's self-signed certificate becomes a first-use decision instead of up-front TLS config:

1. The first connect to an `https` server at a private IP fails with the presented certificate — fingerprint, subject — and the command to trust it.
2. `opencode mcp trust <url>` shows the certificate's subject, validity, and fingerprint and asks for confirmation. `--yes` skips the confirmation (required without a terminal); `--force` is only needed to re-pin after the certificate rotated.
3. The pin is stored per project in a new `mcp_trusted_host` table (new migration). Later connects are pinned by fingerprint, so a rotated certificate fails the connection instead of being silently accepted, and certificates without IP SANs work because the fingerprint is the identity check.

The trust hint is only added for actual TLS verification failures (self-signed, expired, alt-name, and the Node-style codes); network, protocol, and HTTP failures keep their original message. Hostnames never qualify — the IP literal in the config is the trust boundary, not DNS. An explicit `tls` config takes precedence.

### How did you verify your code works?

- `packages/core/test/mcp-trust.test.ts`: private-host classifier, per-project store, first-use → trust → reconnect, rotation → re-pin with `--force`, and an appliance certificate without IP SANs.
- `packages/server/test/mcp-trust.test.ts` (end-to-end over HTTP), `packages/cli/test/mcp-auth-choices.test.ts`, 56 TLS tests, 92 schema and 10 protocol tests.
- `tsc` clean in schema/core/protocol/client/server/cli; `bun run migration --check` passes.

No UI change (CLI + server).

prs.title: fix(util): hand pacote a real npm so git plugins with a build step install
prs.body:
### Issue for this PR

Closes #49704

### Type of change

- [x] Bug fix

### What does this PR do?

`opencode plugin add github:...` fails with `git dep preparation failed` for any Git dependency that builds itself in `prepare` / `build`.

pacote builds a Git dependency by running `npm install` inside the clone, and takes the binary from `npmBin`. When that name ends in `.js`, `pacote/lib/util/npm.js` spawns `process.execPath` with the script as its first argument. In the compiled binary `npm_execpath` is `/$bunfs/bin/npm-cli.js`, so the child process is opencode itself: it runs its own CLI, never that script, and nothing gets installed.

`strace -f -e trace=execve` over the command shows 23 `git` execs, zero `npm` execs, and one re-exec of the opencode binary with the `npm-cli.js` argument. No npm debug log is written, which fits npm never running.

The change gives pacote a real npm: `resolveNpmBin()` ignores an `npm_execpath` that lives inside the bundle or does not exist, and returns `"npm"`, which pacote resolves through `PATH`. Arborist forwards the option. Machines without npm on `PATH` keep the current behaviour.

I did not build the compiled binary to test this end to end. The failure and the fix were reproduced at the pacote/arborist level, which is where the defect lives.

Related: #60201 skips the preparation instead. That removes the error but leaves packages that build in `prepare` installed without their built entry point — measured here: `dist/` absent with `ignoreScripts: true`, present with a real npm.

### How did you verify your code works?

- `bun test test/npm.test.ts` in `packages/core`: 19 pass, including the new `Npm.resolveNpmBin` case.
- `bun run typecheck` from the repository root: 33 tasks, no type errors.
- Isolated with the pinned `pacote@21.5.1`: `npmBin: "/$bunfs/bin/npm-cli.js"` → `git dep preparation failed`; the same call with `npmBin: "npm"` gets past preparation.
- Same failure from a clean Debian container on 1.19.5 with four public plugins: `numman-ali/opencode-openai-codex-auth`, `griffinmartin/opencode-claude-auth`, `tickernelz/opencode-mem`, `slkiser/opencode-quota`.

### Checklist

- [x] I have tested my changes locally
- [x] I have not included unrelated changes in this PR

prs.title: feat(mcp): support per-server TLS trust for remote MCP servers
prs.body:
### Issue for this PR

Part of #40111

Related: #23506, #14696, #26862, #1694

### Type of change

- [x] New feature

### What does this PR do?

Adds an optional `tls` block to remote MCP server config, so a server with a self-signed or private-CA certificate can be trusted for that one server without changing verification anywhere else (no `NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS`):

- `ca_file` / `ca_pem`: PEM CA bundle, from a file (with `~` or workspace-relative paths) or inline, or both.
- `fingerprint`: pins the exact certificate the server presents, like an SSH host key. OpenCode compares the presented certificate against the fingerprint and then uses the fingerprint as the identity check for the connection. Name matching is deliberately not enforced: LAN appliance certificates often omit the IP SAN a hostname check would require (a self-signed `CN=OPNsense` with no SANs is the common case), and the fingerprint already identifies the certificate.

The TLS options are scoped to the fetch used by that server's transport. A missing CA file or a fingerprint mismatch fails the connect with a specific error instead of the first request. Docs: new "TLS Trust" section on the MCP servers page.

### How did you verify your code works?

- 56 tests in `packages/core/test/mcp-tls.test.ts`: unit coverage for PEM/fingerprint/path validation, plus integration tests that connect a real MCP server over TLS with fixture certificates, including a new appliance-style certificate that has a CN and no SAN (the case a name check rejects).

prs.title: feat(plugin): add experimental model HTTP hooks
prs.body:
### Problem

Plugin HTTP hooks only run for Session requests. `generate` text, image and decision calls send provider requests that no hook can see or change (https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/issues/62096). Anything that has to touch every model request, like the provider client certificates in https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/61832, has no single place to do it.

### Change

Adds `ctx.model.hook("experimental.http.request" | "experimental.http.response", ...)`. It runs for every model HTTP request, whichever Session or API makes it.

```text
who calls             kind                                    hooks that run
Session step       →  primary / compaction / title / generate  model + session
generate.text      →  text                                     model      NEW
generate.image     →  image                                    model      NEW
generate.decision  →  decision                                 model      NEW
```

The event matches the session one, but `sessionID` and `agent` are only set for Session requests:

```ts
{ model, kind, sessionID?, agent?, request }            // experimental.http.request
{ model, kind, sessionID?, agent?, request, response }  // experimental.http.response
```

The session `http.request` / `http.response` hooks are unchanged. Both run in one middleware now, with the model hooks outside:

```text
model request hook → session request hook → send → session response hook → model response hook
```

How it's wired:

- `core/src/model-http.ts` builds the per-call middleware. It's moved out of `session/model-request.ts`, which now calls it.
- `Generate.text` passes it as `http` on `llm.generate`, the same option Sessions use.
- `Generate.image` and `Generate.decisions` build their image/decision client per call on an executor wrapped with `RequestExecutor.middleware`. No changes in `packages/ai`. Downloading URL images afterwards still uses the plain executor, so those downloads aren't hooked.

`generate` calls through the HTTP API run in the global config location, so only globally configured plugins see them. That's noted in the docs.

prs.title: feat(ai): support predicate criteria in decisions
prs.body:
### Problem

A `predicate` decision question only had `instructions`, so there was no way to say what counts as true and what counts as false. System One hosts already accept that as `criteria`, but `ai.decision` had nowhere to put it, so ambiguous yes/no questions (is a preference complaint a defect?) relied on the wording alone.

### Change

`PredicateQuestion` gets an optional `criteria: { true?, false? }`:

```ts
{
  name: "defect",
  type: "predicate",
  instructions: "Is the customer reporting a product defect?",
  criteria: {
    true: "The product itself is broken or faulty.",
    false: "Preference, sizing, shipping, or pricing complaint.",
  },
}
```

Each decision protocol lowers it to what its host reads:

| Protocol | Sent as |
| --- | --- |
| System One (TypeSafe, OpenCode, OpenRouter, Baseten, DigitalOcean, Cloudflare Run) | native `noul` `criteria: { true, false }` |
| OpenAI Decisions (OpenAI, Vercel AI Gateway) | appended to `instructions`, since predicates there have no criteria field |

```diff
 OpenAI Decisions predicate
-  instructions: "Is the customer reporting a product defect?"
+  instructions: "Is the customer reporting a product defect?
+
+  True means: The product itself is broken or faulty.
+  False means: Preference, sizing, shipping, or pricing complaint."
```

Questions without `criteria` are sent exactly as before.

The experimental `/api/experimental/generate/decisions` endpoint accepts the same optional `criteria` on predicate questions (`@opencode/schema` `Generate.PredicateQuestion`), and Core passes it through to `ai.decision`. The generated client types are regenerated.

### Verification

- `bun test test/decision.test.ts test/provider` in `packages/ai`: 1493 pass, 0 fail (new tests cover System One and OpenAI Decisions, including only one side of the criteria set)
- `bun typecheck` and `bun run typecheck:tsc` in `packages/ai`: clean
- `bun run script/test.ts test/generate.test.ts` in `packages/core`: 20 pass (the decision test now sends criteria and checks the System One body)
- `bun typecheck` in `packages/core`, `schema`, `client`, `server`, `protocol`: clean; `bun run generate` in `packages/client`

prs.body:
The Copilot plugin read the account's API endpoint (`copilot_internal/user` → `endpoints.api`) once, at sign-in, and stored it in the credential. The refresh now reads `copilot_internal/user` through the same `SharedCache` (per connection, same interval) and uses its endpoint for `/models` and the model base URLs. The endpoint stored at sign-in is the fallback when the lookup fails.

prs.title: fix(server): stop waiting for plugins in request handlers
prs.body:
### Problem

Plugins are supposed to load in the background, with clients picking up late entries from `*.updated` events. The protocol-level activation wait was removed in `8905af5074` for that reason ("Catalog reads remain non-blocking"). Since then, waits for every plugin crept back into server handlers one PR at a time. Each one blocks for up to 5s and then returns a 503:

| Endpoint | Added in |
| --- | --- |
| `model.list`, `model.default`, `generate.*` | https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/54219 |
| `agent.list`, `provider.list` | https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/57681, https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/59082 |
| `skill.list` | https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/62569 |
| `websearch.query` | https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/55866 (it had already been removed in `5d73a5789f`) |
| `integration.list`, `usage.limits`, `voice.*`, `vcs.init`, `rpc.call`, `artifact.*` | various |

Because every client shares these handlers, one slow plugin install or a slow Console response turned the model list into a 503 for the TUI, desktop and `run`, when it could have returned the built-in models.

### Change

```text
before: request → wait for all plugins (≤5s) → 503 or read
after:  request → read what's loaded now
        client  → refresh on *.updated
```

- Removed every plugin wait from server handlers, and deleted the `awaitPlugins` helper.
- `agent.list` and `skill.list` no longer declare a `ServiceUnavailableError`, since the wait was its only source. I regenerated the OpenAPI spec and the client.
- CLI commands that read once and exit (`opencode models`, `opencode debug agents`, `opencode auth *`) now briefly poll `plugin.list` before reading (`packages/cli/src/services/plugin-startup.ts`), the same way ACP already does. Before this, `auth` called `model.default` only to trigger the server-side wait.
- Server tests that needed plugin-provided entries now wait for the Location's plugins to load before sending requests (`test/fixture/routes.ts`), so they make exact assertions without polling. A test that sets up its own Location may wait; the server may not. The SDK tests poll for the entry they need, because that's what SDK callers have to do now.
- Added a "Plugin Loading" section to `AGENTS.md` so this doesn't come back.

This is intentional for actions too. On a cold Location, `generate.*`, `rpc.call`, `vcs.init`, `websearch.query`, `voice.*` and `artifact.*` fail with not-found until the plugin that provides the model, RPC or provider has loaded. Clients make sure what they need is loaded before they call, the same way they do for lists.

### Out of scope

- The core Session execution paths (`session/prompt.ts`, `session/generate.ts`, the runner) still call `Plugin.awaitActivation`. These waits are in core, not in a request handler, and changing them is a separate decision.
- The app's `syncWhileBooting` retry on 503 (`packages/app/src/providers/catalog/providers.ts`) no longer fires. It's harmless, and I can clean it up in a follow-up.

### Verification

- `bun run check`: 33/33 tasks pass
- `packages/server`: `bun test --rerun-each 3` passes 381/381
- `packages/sdk`: `bun test test/embedded.test.ts --rerun-each 5` passes 70/70
- `packages/cli`: `bun test test/auth.test.ts test/server-connection.test.ts test/acp` passes 118/118


---
<!-- opencode-github-bot:pr-section -->
_Added by the opencode bot (AI-generated)._

Fixes #61443

Related: #57204, #55937

Public API: removes the 503 ServiceUnavailableError from agent.list and skill.list in the OpenAPI spec and client (backwards compatible); on a cold Location, generate.*, rpc.call, vcs.init, websearch.query, voice.*, usage.limits and artifact.* no longer wait for plugins and fail instead
<!-- /opencode-github-bot:pr-section -->

prs.title: fix(core): pin npm cache generations while a plugin instance uses them
prs.body:
### Issue for this PR

Refs #62068

### Type of change

- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] New feature
- [ ] Refactor / code improvement
- [ ] Documentation

### What does this PR do?

`Npm.update` prunes the package cache after each install: `collect()` keeps the two newest generations plus anything younger than 7 days. But a plugin instance keeps importing from the generation it was loaded from for its whole lifetime, so a server that outlives that window loses its generation on a later update — the instance's next lazy import, or the old instance's teardown during a reload, then dies with `ENOENT`, and the location's provider catalog drops the configured providers until a manual `/reload`. This is the cache-cleanup cause flagged on #62068 (the teardown-isolation cause is covered by #57096).

The fix gives cleanup a notion of "in use". When the plugin registry activates an instance loaded from an npm generation, `PluginModule` records a lease marker under `<state>/npm-usage/` (generation path, pid, hostname) and removes it when the instance's activation scope closes. `collect()` consults those markers: a generation held by a live local process is skipped, a dead local process's marker is reclaimed as housekeeping, and a marker from another host — whose process cannot be probed from here — counts as live until it reaches the same 7-day retention the generations themselves get, which bounds a container killed without cleanup.

Why this shape:

- Locally, liveness is the holder process, not a heartbeat: a suspended server keeps its lease, a crashed one stops pinning as soon as its pid is gone, and pid reuse can only delay a prune, never delete a live consumer's generation.
- Foreign hosts have no pid to probe, so their markers expire by `createdAt` instead. A foreign holder that outlives the window stops pinning; that is the price of bounding a container killed without cleanup.
- No refcounting: several locations in one process, and separate processes, can hold the same generation, each with its own marker.
- Markers are written through a unique staging name; the sweep skips `.staging` entries so a concurrent cleanup cannot break the writer's rename, and both sides compare real paths so a symlinked cache (macOS `/var` → `/private/var`, a linked XDG cache) agrees.

### How did you verify your code works?

- New regression test in `packages/core/test/npm.test.ts`: a stale generation pinned through `Npm.pin` survives `Npm.update`'s cleanup while an unpinned stale generation next to it is pruned, and is reclaimed once the pin's scope closes.
- A second regression test: cleanup keeps a marker mid-write (`.staging`), keeps a fresh marker from another host, and reclaims an 8-day-old one.
- `bun test test/npm.test.ts` (19 pass) and `bun test test/plugin/` (537 pass) in `packages/core`, `bun test` in `packages/util` (140 pass), `bun run check` from the root (35/35). The remaining failures in the full `packages/core` run (spawn/process-environment tests) fail identically on a clean `upstream/dev` checkout, so they are pre-existing and unrelated.

### Visual

```svg

    <circle cx="83" cy="36" r="7" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-opacity=".85"/>
    <circle cx="83" cy="36" r="2.5" fill="currentColor" opacity=".9">
      <animate attributeName="opacity" values=".9;.3;.9" dur="1.8s" repeatCount="indefinite"/>
    </circle>
```

prs.title: fix(core): keep another live server's goals running on startup
prs.body:
### Issue for this PR

Closes #62145

### Type of change

- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] New feature
- [ ] Refactor / code improvement
- [ ] Documentation

### What does this PR do?

The goal plugin's startup sweep pauses every active goal whose `boot` doesn't match the current process, because its comment assumes one server process per database. That assumption doesn't hold in normal use: `opencode --standalone`, `opencode acp`, and a service-less `opencode run` all share the database with the managed service, so starting any of them pauses the first server's running goals as "The server restarted while the goal was active" even though that server never restarted.

This gates the sweep on owner liveness, the same way `Schedule` elects a single leader per database:

- Each process refreshes a heartbeat key (`process:<boot>`) in plugin storage every 15 seconds, starting before the sweep runs so a freshly started process never reads as dead.
- The sweep now only pauses a goal whose owner's heartbeat is missing, malformed or older than 45 seconds, and drops stale heartbeats so they don't pile up in storage.

Goals from a crashed or restarted server still come back paused once the heartbeat expires — at most 45 seconds later than before — so the existing recovery semantics are unchanged.

### How did you verify your code works?

- From `packages/core`: `bun test test/plugin/` — 540 pass, and `bun run typecheck` is clean.
- New tests: a live owner's fresh heartbeat keeps its goal running; a goal whose owner stopped heartbeating is paused and its stale heartbeat is dropped; the plugin refreshes its own heartbeat on the interval.
- The existing "pauses a goal an earlier server process left active when the plugin starts" test passes unchanged.

prs.title: fix(core): clean up interrupted shell startup
prs.body:
### Issue for this PR

Fixes #48838.

Revisits the acquisition cleanup in the closed, unmerged #52386 and covers the subsequent ShellTool-to-Job handoff. The regression tests were independently written against current dev.

### Type of change

- [x] Bug fix

### What does this PR do?

Cancelling a shell during startup could leave its process running through either of two ownership gaps: Shell.create could be interrupted before handing the shell ID back, or ShellTool could be interrupted while publishing progress before a Job owned the shell.

Shell.create keeps the manager handle until acquisition finishes. An interrupted wait stops the manager and removes the registered shell after process-scope release. ShellTool then holds an interruptible scoped acquisition through progress, Job registration and foreground waiting; an unsuccessful tool execution cancels its Job if present and removes its shell. Successful background execution transfers ownership to the Job and retains its output and completion notification. Permission preparation and process acquisition remain cancellable.

prs.title: fix(core): cancel a session's background shell jobs on interrupt
prs.body:
### Issue for this PR

#60107 (fixes the interrupt half; see below)

### Type of change

- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] New feature
- [ ] Refactor / code improvement
- [ ] Documentation

### What does this PR do?

Interrupting a session only cancelled the job keyed by the session's own id, which covers a session running as a subagent job. Background shell and image jobs are keyed by their shell/image id and only carry the owning session in `job metadata`, so `jobs.cancel(sessionID)` missed them: the work kept running and its completion notice later woke the interrupted session for a new turn.

This adds `Job.cancelAll({ sessionID, type? })`, which cancels running jobs whose `metadata.sessionID` matches (same shape as `backgroundAll`, but keyed on ownership rather than blocking sessions, which are cleared once work is backgrounded), and calls it next to the existing `jobs.cancel(sessionID)` when the run coordinator settles on a non-shutdown interrupt.

Scope note: this fixes expected behavior 1 from the report in full. For expected behavior 2, jobs cancelled through this path end `cancelled` rather than `error`, so they follow the existing not-admitted notification handling and should not wake the session; the `DELETE /api/shell/:id` → `Shell.NotFoundError` notice path is separate and not changed here.

### How did you verify your code works?

- Two new unit tests in `packages/core/test/job.test.ts`: owned-by-session cancellation leaves foreign and unowned running jobs alone (and lets them complete normally after), and the optional `type` filter. Red before the change, green after.
- `job.test.ts` 17/17; related suites (`session-execution`, `tool-shell`, `subagent-lifetime`, `tool-subagent`, `session-shell`) 127 pass / 0 fail.
- Full `packages/core` suite: 6,993 pass; the only remaining failures are four root-in-container artifacts (two flock "unwritable lock root" tests, global-home isolation, one external-plugin spawn) reproduced identically without this change.
- `bun run typecheck` clean (1,738 files).

### Checklist

- [x] I have tested my changes locally
- [x] I have not included unrelated changes in this PR

prs.title: fix(tui): default animations off inside herdr panes
prs.body:
### Issue for this PR

Related to #57462 (animated tabs cause high CPU/GPU use) and #57676 (lag with the session sidebar visible). Not claiming to close either — this is the multiplexer-specific slice of that work.

### Type of change

- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] New feature
- [ ] Refactor / code improvement
- [ ] Documentation

### What does this PR do?

`tabs.enabled` is already resolved environment-aware: inside herdr panes (`HERDR_ENV=1`) the animated tab rail stays off by default, because a multiplexer re-composites pane output at its own cadence and a continuous animated repaint stream turns into continuous full-region recomposites on the multiplexer's client — felt as flicker/shaking, especially over remote or slow links.

This extends the same policy to `animations`: `resolve()` now fills `animations` (like `mouse`/`tabs`) with `input.animations ?? (HERDR_ENV !== "1")`. An explicit `animations` setting always wins, and the `app.toggle.animations` command keeps working (it writes an explicit value). Outside herdr, behavior is unchanged (default on).

### How did you verify your code works?

- New unit test in `packages/tui/test/config-v2.test.tsx` mirroring the existing tabs-environment test: default on normally, default off under `HERDR_ENV=1`, explicit `true`/`false` override in both directions. Red on the old code, green with the change.
- Full `packages/tui` test suite passes; `bun run typecheck` clean.
- End-to-end capture harness (herdr 0.9.5 client + opencode pane, byte-level VT stream analysis): with animations on, live panes keep the renderer emitting frames continuously; `animations: false` collapses idle repaint output to zero, which removes the repaint pressure that multiplexer clients re-composite.

### Screenshots / recordings

Config-default change only; no visual artifact beyond fewer repaints.

### Checklist

- [x] I have tested my changes locally
- [x] I have not included unrelated changes in this PR

prs.title: fix(core): honor ignoreScripts for git dependency preparation
prs.body:
### Issue for this PR

Closes #49704

### Type of change

- [x] Bug fix

### What does this PR do?

OpenCode installs Git plugins with `ignoreScripts: true`, but pacote 21.5.1 still runs its Git preparation step for packages that declare `build`/`prepare`/`install`/`postinstall` scripts. That step spawns `npm install` inside the clone.

In a compiled OpenCode binary the npm path resolves into Bun's bundled filesystem, so the spawn re-executes `opencode` with `$bunfs/bin/npm-cli.js install ...`. OpenCode prints help and exits, and the install fails with `git dep preparation failed`.

This backports pacote 22's guard into the existing pacote patch: skip Git preparation when `ignoreScripts` is set.

### How did you verify your code works?

Added `skips Git package preparation when scripts are ignored` to `packages/core/test/npm.test.ts`. The test fails before the patch with `git dep preparation failed` and passes after it.

I also ran `bun dev plugin add github:psh4607-works/opencode-agent-sidebar#v0.2.5`; installation succeeds, and the TUI renders the plugin's `Agents` section. Targeted test and `@opencode/core` / `@opencode/util` typecheck pass.

### Checklist

- [x] I have tested my changes locally
- [x] I have not included unrelated changes in this PR

prs.title: fix(util): timed-out shell commands no longer leave child processes running
prs.body:
### Issue for this PR

Related to #59006, which asks for a way to stop an agent's whole process tree. No issue covers this exact case, so this PR fixes one focused part of it: what a shell timeout or abort leaves behind.

### Type of change

- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] New feature
- [ ] Refactor / code improvement
- [ ] Documentation

### What does this PR do?

When a shell command times out or is aborted, `stop` sends SIGTERM to the command's process group. It escalates to SIGKILL only if the leader (`sh`) is still running when `forceKillAfter` ends. The leader usually exits on SIGTERM at once, so the escalation never happens. A child that outlives the SIGTERM (one that handles or ignores it, or one started while the signal went out) keeps running with no parent, and nothing tracks the group any more. A command that keeps starting child processes can then run until the user's process limit is used up.

With `forceKillAfter` set, `stop` now waits for the whole group to empty, not just the leader. If the grace period ends with members left, it sends SIGKILL to the group every 10 ms until `kill` reports ESRCH, for at most one second. A group ID stays reserved while any member is alive, and the loop stops at the first ESRCH, so it only signals the command's own group.

Every `stop` with `forceKillAfter` gets this: the shell tool's timeout and abort, and scope release with `RELEASE_FORCE_KILL_AFTER`, for example a command that exits non-zero or an MCP stdio server. Windows (`taskkill /T`), `detached: false` and stops without `forceKillAfter` are unchanged. A command that exits 0 still leaves its background children running, as before.

This is separate from #61876, which moves shells into the process daemon. It works on the current spawner and doesn't depend on that PR.

### How did you verify your code works?

- New test in `packages/core/test/effect/cross-spawn-spawner.test.ts`. The leader exits on SIGTERM while its child ignores SIGTERM and starts one short `sleep` after another (one at a time, for at most 10 s). It fails on `dev` because the group is still alive after `kill`, and passes with this change. Checked on Linux x86_64 and macOS 27 arm64.
- From `packages/core`, run `bun run script/test.ts test/effect/cross-spawn-spawner.test.ts` (33 pass, 1 skip, 0 fail) and the seven shell/MCP/process files listed in the evidence (206 pass, 24 skip, 0 fail). Run `bun check --no-script` and `tsc --noEmit` in `packages/util`, and `bun check --no-script -b -p tsconfig.tests.json` in `packages/core`; run Prettier and oxlint on the two changed files. The Linux and macOS before/after runs and the timeout transcript also pass.
- Runtime check: a short script runs that command through the spawner, waits 1 s, calls `handle.kill({ forceKillAfter: "3 seconds" })` as the shell tool's timeout does, and lists the group. On `dev`, `kill` returns in 3 ms and two members are still there 4 s later, still starting new `sleep` processes. With this change, `kill` returns after the 3 s grace period and the group is empty. macOS gives the same result.

Not checked: Windows, whose code path is unchanged.

### Screenshots / recordings

No UI change. Below are test and runtime output from Linux, before and after.

The new test on `dev`: it fails because the process group is still alive after `kill`.

![New test failing on dev](https://gist.githubusercontent.com/only21mil/52605abfc780880730e527c7459105fc/raw/dcbc0ed2bdf504637684ef260d6a86c4877c697b/test-before.png)

The new test with this change: it passes.

prs.title: feat(ai): add xAI hosted X search and web search tools
prs.body:
### Issue for this PR

Part of #54168 (this is the `@opencode/ai` library layer; the opencode-side opt-in is a follow-up, see below). Related: #35038.

### Type of change

- [ ] Bug fix
- [x] New feature
- [ ] Refactor / code improvement
- [x] Documentation

### What does this PR do?

`packages/ai` already parses xAI's `x_search_call` / `web_search_call` output items into provider-executed tool events (`protocols/xai-responses.ts`), but there was no way to *request* those tools: the xAI adapter had no `nativeTool`, so any `ToolDefinition.native` failed with "xAI Responses does not support provider-native tool". The Alibaba and Meta Responses adapters already have this seam, so this follows them:

- `protocols/xai-responses.ts`: `nativeTool` on the adapter validates `native.xai` against the two documented hosted search tools, `{ type: "x_search", allowed_x_handles?, excluded_x_handles?, from_date?, to_date?, enable_image_understanding?, enable_video_understanding? }` and `{ type: "web_search", filters?: { allowed_domains?, excluded_domains? }, enable_image_search?, enable_image_understanding? }`. Web search domain lists go under `filters` because that is how the xAI Responses API examples pass them; X search takes its handles at the top level. Anything else, including another provider's native tool, still fails with `InvalidRequest` before any network call. Compaction uses the same `lowerTools`, so it accepts them too.
- `providers/xai.ts`: `XAI.xSearch(options)` and `XAI.webSearch(options)` factories with camelCase options, mirroring `Meta.webSearch()`. The tool names `x_search` / `web_search` match what the stream parser already assigns to the hosted items.
- README: a short xAI section.

Nothing is enabled by default; the tools are only sent when a caller puts them in `tools`. xAI bills them per fetched source, which is why I kept this strictly opt-in and did not add an opencode config switch here. How search gets exposed at the app level is the #35038 discussion, and I'd rather land the library piece first.

One thing worth flagging for whoever has an xAI key: the X search docs say sub-tool calls (`x_keyword_search`, `x_semantic_search`, ...) show up as `custom_tool_call` output items. The Open Responses baseline ignores unknown item types, so if live streams use that shape instead of `x_search_call`, the calls would not surface as tool events. That is pre-existing behaviour on `dev` and out of scope here, but a recorded cassette would settle it.

### How did you verify your code works?

- New tests in `test/provider/xai-responses.test.ts`: lowered `body.tools` with and without options next to a function tool, and rejection of another provider's native tool. They failed first (`XAI.xSearch is not a function`), then passed.

- Request shapes checked against the xAI docs for [X search](https://docs.x.ai/developers/tools/x-search) and [web search](https://docs.x.ai/developers/tools/web-search). I do not have an xAI API key, so there is no new recorded cassette; the response-side parsing of hosted items is unchanged.

prs.title: fix(app): accept a pasted redirect URL for provider sign-in
prs.body:
### Problem

When OpenCode runs on another machine (SSH, exe.dev, a container), a provider's browser sign-in redirects to `127.0.0.1` on the *browser's* machine, so it never completes. https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/61706 added a paste fallback, but only for MCP servers. Provider sign-ins (ChatGPT, Poe, GitLab, Snowflake, plugin providers) still had no way to finish from the desktop/web app, and plugins had no typed way to opt in.

The app also showed any auto sign-in's instructions in the "Confirmation code" box, e.g. `Complete authorization in your browser.`

### Change

```text
browser sign-in starts (attempt.paste = true)
  ├─ browser reaches 127.0.0.1 → completes as before
  └─ it can't → user pastes the URL it landed on
       server checks state → hands code to the same callback
       wrong/foreign URL → error under the field, sign-in keeps waiting
```

```diff
 core
+  oauth/redirect.ts                 # OauthRedirect.pasted: parse URL, check state, return code or provider error
   mcp/oauth.ts                      # uses it (same behavior)
   plugin/provider/chatgpt.ts        + submit
   plugin/provider/openai.ts         + submit (Codex browser)
   plugin/provider/gitlab.ts         + submit
   plugin/provider/poe.ts            + submit
   plugin/provider/snowflake-cortex.ts + submit
 plugin
   effect/integration.ts             + submit? on auto authorizations
   promise/integration.ts            + submit? (Promise form)
   promise/adapter.ts                # passes it through
 app
   providers/connect/machine.ts      # paste: editing | submitting, paste.* events, paste effect
   providers/connect/controller.ts   # paste effect → oauth.complete({ code: url })
   providers/connect/dialog.tsx      # Redirect URL field; instructions no longer shown as a code
```

The paste only hands the URL to the server; polling still decides how the sign-in ends, same as MCP. A paste in flight when the dialog moves on (Back, a failed poll) is ignored, and a resumed sign-in starts editable.

Device-code sign-ins (Copilot, Console, xAI, Codex device) don't need this. DigitalOcean uses an implicit grant (token in the URL fragment) and is left as is.

### Visual

```svg
<svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="240" height="72" viewBox="0 0 240 72" fill="none">
  <style>
    .caret{animation:blink 1s steps(1) infinite}
    .url{animation:type 3s steps(18) infinite}
    .ok{opacity:0;animation:ok 3s infinite}
    @keyframes blink{50%{opacity:0}}
    @keyframes type{0%{width:0}60%,100%{width:132px}}
    @keyframes ok{0%,70%{opacity:0}80%,100%{opacity:1}}
    @media (prefers-reduced-motion:reduce){.caret,.url,.ok{animation:none}.url{width:132px}.ok{opacity:1}}
  </style>
  <rect x="8" y="8" width="224" height="56" rx="8" stroke="currentColor" stroke-opacity=".3"/>
  <text x="20" y="26" font-size="9" fill="currentColor" fill-opacity=".6" font-family="sans-serif">Redirect URL</text>
  <rect x="20" y="33" width="150" height="18" rx="4" stroke="currentColor" stroke-opacity=".4"/>
  <svg x="26" y="37" width="132" height="12" class="url" overflow="hidden"><text y="9" font-size="8" fill="currentColor" font-family="monospace">127.0.0.1/callback?code=</text></svg>
  <rect x="160" y="37" width="1.5" height="10" fill="currentColor" class="caret"/>
  <rect x="178" y="33" width="42" height="18" rx="4" fill="currentColor" fill-opacity=".85"/>
  <path class="ok" d="M192 42l4 4 8-8" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="2"/>
</svg>
```

### Verification

- `bun run check` (root): 33/33 typecheck tasks pass.
- `packages/app`: `bun test src/providers/connect/machine.test.ts`: 24 pass (3 new: paste offered only when `attempt.paste`, rejected paste keeps polling, late paste results after Back/retry ignored).
- `packages/core`: `bun test test/plugin/provider-poe.test.ts test/mcp-oauth.test.ts`: 51 pass. New Poe test fails on `dev` ("OAuth attempt already completing") and passes here.
- Provider suites (chatgpt, gitlab, openai, snowflake, poe, mcp, oauth-page): 120 pass, 1 fail. The failure (`ChatGPTPlugin > rejects a reauthorization callback that returns a different client ID`) also fails on `dev`. `bun test src/providers` in app has 2 failures that also fail on `dev`.

Empty → "Paste the URL from the browser's address bar"; another sign-in's state → "This URL belongs to a different sign-in"; not a URL → "Paste the full URL from the browser's address bar"; right state with a fake code → reached Poe, which rejected the code. No "Confirmation code" box.

prs.body:
Upgrades `effect` and the five `@effect/*` packages from 4.1.0 to 4.1.2, two patch releases.

**Before:** finished fibers kept their last span and its parent chain alive, cancelling an RPC stream could make the client drain the whole server stream, and the OTLP JSON exporter wrote byte values as plain objects.

SQL fragments are now branded, so a plain object shaped like a fragment is bound as a parameter. Nothing in the repo builds fragments by hand.

4.1.2 is six days old, past the three-day `minimumReleaseAge`. The lockfile changes only these packages and their `ws` patch bump.

prs.title: feat(core): tag shell, tool and model-stream spans with session, agent and command
prs.body:
**Traces now say which session ran each shell command, which agent made each step and tool call, and how long the model itself took.**
#60974 already tagged the turn, each step and each tool call with the session. This closes the gaps that remain: shell spans that run outside the turn, the agent name, and a span for the model's own time. Nothing outside tracing changes.

❌ **Before**
1. A shell command typed by the user (`!`) runs outside any turn, so its spans had no session at all.
2. Shell spans never said what command they ran, how it exited, or which tool call started it.
3. The step span covers the model stream and the tools it starts, so "model was slow" and "tool was slow" looked the same.
4. No span named the agent.

✅ **After**
1. Every shell span carries the session from the shell's own record, the command (first 200 characters only, always valid text; never the environment, input or output), whether it runs in the background, and, once it ends, its status and exit code.
2. Shell spans started by the shell tool also carry the tool call id and, when the model asked for it, the background flag. This includes the job that waits on a backgrounded command.
3. A new `LLM.stream` span under each step covers only the provider stream (request sent to stream finished), with provider and model. One span per request, not per event.
4. Steps and tool calls carry `gen_ai.agent.name`.
5. A backgrounded subagent's completion delivery names the parent session, since it runs in the global context.

```diff
  Shell.create / get / wait / result / timeout / remove
-   (session only when called inside a turn)
+   session.id, opencode.shell.{id,command,background,status}, process.exit.code
+   gen_ai.tool.call.id (+ background) when started by the shell tool
  SessionStep.attempt
+   gen_ai.agent.name
+   └ LLM.stream  (provider + model, ends when the stream ends)
  Tool.execute
+   gen_ai.agent.name
```

📊 **Proof**

| Case | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| User `!` shell span has a session | ❌ | ✅ |
| Shell span names the command, truncated | ❌ | ✅ |
| Cutting through an emoji still gives valid OTLP JSON | — | ✅ |
| Tool-started shell span names its tool call | ❌ | ✅ |
| Shell span has exit code | ❌ | ✅ |
| Model time separate from tool time | ❌ | ✅ |
| Step and tool spans name the agent | ❌ | ✅ |

New tests check the exact attribute set on a user shell (session, 200-character command, background, exit 3), that a cut through an emoji still gives valid text, and that a tool-started shell's spans carry the tool call id and the background flag. The recorded runner test now also checks the agent name and that `LLM.stream` sits under the step with provider and model, and still checks every span in the turn has the session.

👀 **Read:** `shell.ts`, the `annotate` helper. It reads the session from the shell's metadata rather than relying on the caller's span annotations, because shells outlive the turn that started them. The shell tool sets the background flag on its spans rather than in the shell's metadata, which clients see. The rest is routine.

<sub>Follows up #60974 · found while reading traces of a stuck session in a local OTLP store · no user reports</sub>

<details><summary>Checks run</summary>

- `bun test test/session-shell.test.ts test/session-runner-recorded.test.ts test/tool-subagent.test.ts`: 24 pass
- `bun test test/tool-shell.test.ts`: 65 pass, 2 fail (the two "conditional substitutions" cases fail the same way on `dev` without this change)

prs.title: fix(core): keep literal backslashes in Unix file names
prs.body:
### Issue for this PR

Closes #60307

### Type of change

- [x] Bug fix

### What does this PR do?

On Unix a backslash is a legal filename character, but `normalizePath` in `packages/core/src/ripgrep.ts` replaced every `\` with `/` on all platforms. `glob` and `grep` therefore reported `actual/name.txt` for a file named `actual\name.txt`, a path that does not exist, so a model reading or editing the reported result targets the wrong file or fails.

That normalization is only needed on Windows, where ripgrep reports separators as backslashes. The function now keeps literal backslashes and only strips a leading `./` or `/` elsewhere.

### How did you verify your code works?

New test in `packages/core/test/ripgrep.test.ts` creates `actual\name.txt` and checks both `glob` and `grep`. Before the change it fails:

prs.title: refactor(core): simplify the Console plugin on ProviderRefresh and a persistent SharedCache
prs.body:
### Issue for this PR

None.

### Type of change

- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] New feature
- [x] Refactor / code improvement
- [ ] Documentation

### What does this PR do?

**Problem**

Most of the Console plugin's load path (`packages/core/src/plugin/provider/opencode.ts`) worked around `SharedCache`. It hid sign-in errors inside a `{ failed }` value, so the cache would share them, and then unwrapped them again. It ran its own semaphore, poll loop and apply step. It also had two fallback paths and kept a `failedSkills` set to force skill retries. That code caused these bugs:

- A project opened while Console wanted SSO again got no organization policies, because the cache shared the SSO error and not the last config.
- After the sign-in moved to another organization whose config failed, the previous organization's policies stayed applied.
- A skill whose download failed was not downloaded again until the Console config changed.
- After a restart with Console down, the plugin started with no policies.

**Change**

```
before                                  after
load ─ semaphore ─ cache.get            ProviderRefresh.start ─ load
       └ {failed} wrap / unwrap                └ cache.lookup → { value, failure }
       └ fallback: this project's copy                  value   → config and policies
       └ fallback: saved copy                           failure → connection status
       └ storage set/remove
skills ─ failedSkills set + force       skills ─ cache.get(failureInterval: 30s)
poll loop + switch handler              (ProviderRefresh handles both)
```

SharedCache gets three new options and one new method. Callers have to opt in, so azure, digitalocean, github-copilot and modal behave as before:

- `persist: codec` writes the last good value to the local KV store, only when it changed. An entry that isn't in memory starts from the saved value and treats it as stale: `interval: infinity` returns it at once, any other interval loads first and falls back to it if the load fails. Values are stored as `{ value }` because KV can't hold a bare `null`.
- `lookup(input)` returns the last good value together with the latest failure. `get` hides one of the two.
- `failureInterval` sets how long a failure with no good value behind it is kept. It defaults to `interval`.
- `forget(prefix)` drops entries from memory and from disk.

The plugin now:
- Uses `ProviderRefresh.start` for startup, polling and account switches.
- Starts with `load(..., { interval: infinity })`. That returns the saved config at once, or waits for Console if nothing is saved.
- Reads SSO and signed-out errors from `lookup().failure`, so every project keeps the last good config while the connection asks the user to sign in.
- Persists the config, instructions and skills lists. Cache keys now start with the connection (`opencode-console:credential:<id>:...`).
- Downloads skills with `interval: infinity, failureInterval: 30s` and runs the skill sync on every check. Cached skills cost no request.
- Listens to `credential.updated` and calls `forget` for a login that was removed.

`opencode.ts` is 26 lines shorter than on `dev` (+162/-188). `shared-cache.ts` is +109/-21.

**Out of scope**

Event watches, the managed `integration.use` deny check, mTLS and the ChatGPT models cache are unchanged.

### How did you verify your code works?

New plugin tests in `packages/core/test/plugin/provider-opencode.test.ts`. The first three fail on `dev`:
- "gives a project opened while Console wants SSO again the workspace's last policies"
- "drops an organization's policies when the sign-in moves to another whose config fails"
- "retries a Console skill whose download failed once per check until it loads"
- "forgets the saved Console config of a removed login" (I checked that it fails when the forget is skipped)

New SharedCache tests in `packages/core/test/shared-cache.test.ts` cover persist and restore, writing only on change (including `null`), `lookup`, `failureInterval` and `forget`. They run on TestClock with no sleeps.

From `packages/core`:
- `bun typecheck` and `bun run typecheck:tsc`
- The Console, watches and SharedCache tests with `--rerun-each 10 --randomize`: 940 pass
- `test/plugin`: 595 pass
- The full core suite. The only failures are 3 shell tests (conditional process substitution x2, compound-parity) that also fail on a clean `dev` locally.

From the repo root, `bun run check` passes.

No feature flag: this is a refactor plus bug fixes.

### Checklist

- [x] I have not included unrelated changes in this PR

`credential.updated` fires when a login is added, renamed or removed, but its payload is empty, so a listener can't tell which login changed. prs.title: fix(core): retry every DNS failure and keep the session's WebSocket through one
prs.body:
**A failed DNS lookup no longer switches a session from WebSocket to HTTP for the rest of its life, and the other DNS errors Bun reports get the same hour of retries as `ENOTFOUND`.**
A 45-minute DNS outage on Nov 4 ended 366 steps across 341 sessions on their first attempt. [#61880](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/61880) already gives `ENOTFOUND` and `EAI_AGAIN` an hour of retries. This PR covers the rest of that path.

❌ **Before**
1. When a session's WebSocket can't connect because DNS is down, the session switches to HTTP and stays there until a restart, even after the network comes back.
2. Bun can also report a failed lookup as `EBADRESP`, `ESERVFAIL` or `ETIMEOUT`. Those spend the general retry allowance (about 10 tries) instead of the hour.

✅ **After**
1. Only that one request uses HTTP. The retry goes back to the WebSocket once DNS resolves again. Other connect failures, such as a refused upgrade, still switch the session to HTTP for good.
2. All five lookup codes get the hour of retries, and requests that never reached the provider are replayed on them too. `ETIMEDOUT` (a socket timeout, not DNS) isn't on the list.

```diff
  websocket connect fails
-   any reason -> httpFallback = true (rest of session)
+   host unreachable -> HTTP for this request only, logged at debug (every retry lands here)
+   anything else    -> httpFallback = true, logged as a warning
- UNREACHABLE = ENOTFOUND, EAI_AGAIN, ENETUNREACH, EHOSTUNREACH, ENETDOWN
+ UNREACHABLE = + EBADRESP, ESERVFAIL, ETIMEOUT (one list, shared with the one-shot retry and aisdk)
```

👀 **Read:** `packages/core/src/session/model-transport.ts`: the connect-failure branch decides between one-request and permanent HTTP. The rest is routine.

<sub>🔍 Found in a week of local session traces (Nov 4 DNS outage) · no user reports</sub>

<details><summary>Checks run</summary>

- `bun test test/session-runner-retry.test.ts test/aisdk.test.ts test/session-runner.test.ts` (packages/core): 302 pass
- `bun test test/session-model-transport.test.ts` (packages/core): 34 pass
- `bun typecheck` in packages/core: clean
- Not measured: every failure in the Nov 4 outage was `ENOTFOUND`, which #61880 already covers, so the new codes are from Bun's resolver, not seen in these traces.

</details>

prs.title: fix(core): stop applying well-known remote config after logout
prs.body:
Closes https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/issues/59320. Replaces https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/59528.

### Problem

`opencode auth logout` on a `.well-known` integration removes the credential, but the remote config (providers, policies) keeps applying, so you still look logged in.

Since https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/53667, config loading falls back to the last saved remote config whenever it can't fetch a fresh one. That was meant for outages, but "no credential" took the same path.

### Change

A source with no credential now supplies nothing, and its saved config is deleted. A failed fetch with a credential still uses the saved config.

```text
                    before      after
fetch fails         saved cfg   saved cfg
no credential       saved cfg   nothing, saved cfg deleted  <- logout
log back in, fetch  saved cfg   nothing until a fetch succeeds
  still failing
```

The check lives in `Config.loadWellknownEntry`, which calls a new `WellKnown.clearCached(origin)` when there's no credential. It doesn't remove the `.well-known` source, so logging back in needs nothing extra. It also fixes people who already logged out, since it checks whether a credential exists rather than reacting to the logout itself.

Thanks to @2SinceJuly for diagnosing this in https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/59528 (credited as co-author) and to @nimrodmoshe05-glitch for the report.

### Out of scope

- Deleting the `.well-known` source when its last credential is removed. Not needed for the fix.
- https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/issues/54645 (stale API key in the shared service after login/logout) is a separate bug.

prs.title: feat(core): experimental sqlite full-text index of session history
prs.body:
Adds an SQLite FTS5 index of session history, built and kept current in the background, behind the new `sqlite_fts` flag. This PR only adds the index; nothing searches it yet. The search tools come in a follow-up.

### Problem

Agents can't search past sessions. Before building search tools we need to know what keeping a full-text index costs on real machines and real databases: how long the one-time backfill of old history takes, and whether users notice it.

### Change

`sqlite_fts` is in the flag registry, so like every other flag it is **on in local and dev builds, off in releases**. Turn it off with `experimental.sqlite_fts: false` or `OPENCODE_FLAGS=-sqlite_fts`. Like `media_blob` and `part_rows`, off only stops new work: an index already built stays, and its triggers keep queueing changed IDs so turning it back on catches up without a rebuild. On a database that never had it on, nothing runs and no triggers exist. The only change for everyone is the migration, which adds two empty tables.

```text
server starts ─► ready right away (never waits on search)
   └─ SessionSearchMaintenance (forked like Schedule.run)
        any loaded location has the flag on?
          ─► ensure: contentless FTS5 table + triggers that only queue IDs
          ─► backfill old history, newest first, only after 5 s with no Session writes
               ≤ 50 messages and ≤ 1 MiB stored bytes per transaction (sizes read before bodies)
               cursor in kv, resumes after a restart
          ─► drain the queue: each message is indexed once, when it finishes
        off?  ─► do nothing (existing index stays; changes keep queueing)
        SQLite < 3.43 (no contentless_delete)? ─► log once, stay off
```

What gets indexed: session titles, user text, finished assistant text parts, and completed compaction summaries, each capped at 64 KiB. Tool calls and output, reasoning, files, and synthetic, system and skill messages are never indexed. Text is tokenized with `porter unicode61 remove_diacritics 2`, and camelCase subwords are appended.

Writes stay cheap: triggers on `session_message`, `session_part` and `session_v2` only insert an ID into `session_search_dirty` (or do nothing if it's already queued), and never touch FTS. So older binaries and SQLite builds without FTS5 keep writing normally. Streaming deltas are ephemeral and never reach the database.

Files:

```text
packages/core/src/session/
├── search-index.ts        # ensure / processBatch / backfillBatch / status / search
├── search-maintenance.ts  # background loop, flag gating, idle-only backfill, logs
└── search-text.ts         # what text is indexed, camelCase expansion, 64 KiB cap
packages/core/src/database/migration/20261105195531_session_search.ts
packages/schema/src/config/flag.ts   # sqlite_fts
packages/server/src/process.ts       # forks the loop next to Schedule.run
```

### Measured on a 37.5 GB real database (online-backup snapshot)

| | |
|---|---|
| Index size | ~114 MB (FTS 98 MB + document map 15.5 MB), 0.3% of the DB |
| Backfill, quiet: Mac / Docker 1 CPU / 0.5 CPU | 4.5 / 5.7 / 5.5 min |
| Backfill with traffic 30 s on / 30 s off, 1 CPU | 13.6 min |
| User p99 ping / read / write **during traffic**, 1 CPU | 10 / 30 / 16 ms (flag off: 8 / 38 / 21 ms) |
| User max during traffic, 1 CPU | 87 / 98 / 36 ms, 0 event-loop stalls > 100 ms |
| Before idle-only + size cap (same test) | p99 118–129 ms, max 408–499 ms, 41 stalls > 100 ms |
| After the backfill | no measurable effect on app reads and writes |

Logs: `session search backfill started`, `session search backfill finished` (ms, batches, slowest batch, documents), and a warning for any batch over 250 ms. These are what we collect from dev-build users.

### Out of scope

- `session_search` / `session_read` tools (follow-up, same flag).
- Durable Objects: two known issues (an async transaction hangs while a timer is pending, and the 100 bound-parameter cap) are not fixed here. Batches are already capped at 50 IDs, which avoids the parameter cap, but the loop is only started by `ServerProcess`, so it never runs in a DO.
- Single stored messages of 8–36 MB still take up to ~0.6 s at 1 CPU when the backfill reaches them. These run only once no Session has written for 5 s, but someone scrolling or typing in that gap can still feel one.
- If Sessions write continuously with no 5 s gap, the backfill waits.

### Verification

- `bun run check`: pass.
- `packages/core`: `bun test test/session-search test/config test/flag*`: 347 pass. Includes tests for flag gating across locations, off keeping the index and catching up when back on, idle-only backfill (fails if the quiet check is removed), the byte cap, the 64 KiB cap, writes from binaries that don't know the index, malformed rows, and concurrent writers.
- CI: all checks pass (unit, typecheck, e2e on Linux and Windows).
- Earlier on this branch: runtime matrix on Bun/Node macOS, Bun/Node Linux and real workerd. SQLite 3.32–3.42 reports unsupported and keeps working; 3.43–3.51 pass.

**A read past the end of a file now returns its last lines, a negative offset reads from the end, and a missing file suggests close names from its own folder.**
In a week of local sessions, 583 reads failed on an offset past the end and 1,526 on a missing file. Each one cost the agent another call or two to find its way.

❌ **Before**
1. `read` with an offset past the end fails: "Offset 900 is out of range for this file (812 lines)". The agent reads again.
2. `read` on a missing file says "File not found", with suggestions only for names in the same folder that contain each other. Typos, a wrong extension, or a path written from the wrong root get no hint.

✅ **After**
1. A read past the end returns the file's last lines (up to 100, or `limit` if smaller, within the 50 KB cap), ending on the last line. The header says `lines 713-812 (offset 900 is past the end; the file has 812 lines)`.
2. "File not found" suggests up to 3 names, all from the one listing of the file's folder that the tool already does, plus at most one extra check. There's no repo-wide search.
   - **Wrong root:** if the path is outside the project but inside its parent folder (`/Users/me/src/a.ts` while the project is `/Users/me/repo`), it checks whether `/Users/me/repo/src/a.ts` exists and is readable. If so, that goes first.
   - **Same folder, ranked:** same name ignoring case (`readme.md` → `README.md`), then same name with another extension (`config.yml` → `config.yaml`), then one name containing the other (only when both are 3+ characters, so `ui.ts` doesn't drag in `db.ts`), then a typo of 1 or 2 letters (`conifg.ts` → `config.ts`). Ties go to the closer full name.
   - **Missing folder:** still names the first missing folder and the nearest one that exists, and ranks that folder's entries against the missing folder name the same way (`libs/` → `lib`).
3. A negative offset starts that many lines from the end, and `limit` counts forward from there like any read. `offset: -50` returns the last 50 lines (`Read file app.log, lines 763-812`), and `offset: -50, limit: 10` returns the first 10 of those (lines 763-772, with the usual "continue reading with offset: 773" note). If the file is shorter, it starts at line 1. The 2000 line and 50 KB caps and the truncation note work the same as a normal read, and a big file only decodes the lines it returns. It isn't mentioned in the tool description; it just works if a model tries it. On a directory it fails with a clear message.

```diff
  read(offset > lines)
-   fail OffsetOutOfRangeError
+   return the tail, ending at the last line
  read(missing file)
-   suggest names in the same folder that contain each other
+   + <project>/<path> when the path was written from the project's parent
+   + same folder, ranked: case → extension → contains → typo, top 3
+ read(offset: -N)
+   start at line (total - N + 1), then read `limit` lines forward as usual
```

📊 **Proof**

| Case | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| Offset past the end, small file | ❌ error | ✅ last lines |
| `limit: 2000` past the end of a 1.8 MB file | ❌ error | ✅ lines 1750–1800 |
| Empty file read with an offset | ❌ error | ✅ 0 lines |
| `conifg.ts` | ❌ no hint | ✅ `config.ts` |
| `config.yml` next to `config.yaml` | ❌ no hint | ✅ `config.yaml` |
| `readme.md` next to `README.md` (case-sensitive disk) | ❌ no hint | ✅ `README.md` |
| `/parent/src/a.ts` with the project at `/parent/repo` | ❌ no hint | ✅ `/parent/repo/src/a.ts` first |
| `ui.ts` near other short names | ✅ no noise | ✅ no noise |
| `libs/x.ts` when only `lib/` exists | ✅ nearest folder | ✅ nearest folder, plus `lib` |
| `offset: -50` on a 3000-line, 300 KB file | ❌ rejected by the schema | ✅ lines 2951–3000 |
| `offset: -50, limit: 10` on the same file | ❌ rejected by the schema | ✅ lines 2951–2960, continue at 2961 |

👀 **Read:** `read.ts` `similar` (the ranking) and `reroot` (the one extra check). `read-filesystem.ts` `textPage`: the tail branch, and in `read` where a negative offset becomes a start line at EOF. `OffsetOutOfRangeError` is deleted; the rest follows from that.

<sub>🔍 Found in a week of local session errors (583 past-end reads, 1,526 missing files) · reviewed before push</sub>

- `bun test test/tool-read.test.ts test/tool-read-filesystem.test.ts test/tool-edit.test.ts test/session-instructions.test.ts` (packages/core): 96 pass
- `bun typecheck` in packages/core: clean
- `bun run check` (repo root): clean

</details>

prs.title: fix(core): terminalize orphaned child sessions suspended by a restart
prs.body:
### Issue for this PR

Closes #62779

### Type of change

- [x] Bug fix

### What does this PR do?

When the server restarts with a subagent mid-turn, the subagent's execution claim survives so the turn can resume. But when no durable background Job can recover it, the restart sweep cleared the orphaned claim with a bare SQL update and published no terminal event. With no terminal, the projector never writes `time_idle`, so the session counts as an active subagent in the sidebar forever (the reporter had phantoms 4-10 days old).

The sweep's own contract says only a terminal event releases a claim, so this makes the sweep terminalize instead of clearing silently:

- `SessionStore.releaseChildClaims` becomes `orphanedChildClaims`, a read that returns the claimed child sessions no recoverable background job owns.
- `resumeSuspendedSessions` publishes `Execution.Failed` (`aborted`: "Execution was orphaned by a server restart and cannot be resumed.") for each, with the claim release as the commit hook, the same pattern the resume-budget exhaustion path already uses.

This works because the projector already maps a `Failed` terminal to `time_idle` + `idle_outcome: "failed"`, and the message updater records why the turn stopped. Recovery stays at-least-once: if the sweep dies mid-loop, the remaining claims are still there for the next boot.

### How did you verify your code works?

New test: the sweep terminalizes an orphaned claimed child (publishes the `Failed` terminal, releases the claim, and does not re-sweep it on the next boot), and `orphanedChildClaims` excludes recoverable children while releasing nothing by itself. Plus a projector test pinning `Failed` -> `time_idle` with outcome `failed`.

The existing "keeps shell owners idle" test caught one interaction: its `seedInbox` helper inserted rows at a hardcoded `enqueued_seq` that the extra aggregate event now occupies. The helper now allocates above what the bus already admitted; the test's exactly-once notice assertions are unchanged.

`bun run test` in `packages/core`: 7023 pass, 12 fail. All 12 are GitLab OAuth and MCP wrapper tests that need outbound network and port binding this sandbox doesn't have; the session suites covering this change (execution, store, projector, run-coordinator, list, view) all pass. `bun run typecheck` is clean (2,014 files).

prs.title: feat(ai): support Venice end-to-end encrypted models
prs.body:
### Issue for this PR

No existing issue.

### Type of change

- [ ] Bug fix
- [x] New feature
- [ ] Refactor / code improvement
- [ ] Documentation

### What does this PR do?

Adds support for Venice's [E2EE models](https://docs.venice.ai/guides/features/tee-e2ee-models). Requests to `e2ee-*` models failed before, because Venice rejects plaintext messages when the E2EE headers are missing. Plain TEE models already worked.

Model ids starting with `e2ee-` now use a new `venice-e2ee-chat` route. It reuses `VeniceChat.protocol` with its own transport. For each request, the transport:

- fetches `/tee/attestation` with a random nonce, and stops unless `verified` is true, the nonce matches, and a model key comes back
- encrypts user and system messages to that key (secp256k1 ECDH, HKDF-SHA256, AES-256-GCM, as the guide specifies) and sends the `X-Venice-TEE-*` headers
- decrypts the streamed `content` and `reasoning_content` deltas with a session key made for that request

Bun's `node:crypto` has no secp256k1 support, so this adds `@noble/curves`. WebCrypto does the HKDF and AES-GCM. The attestation request uses the chat call's header and total timeouts.

Limits, all from Venice's documented format:

- Assistant messages, tool messages and tool definitions are sent in plaintext.
- Attestation relies on Venice's `verified` result. The client does not parse the TDX quote.
- Images and files are rejected for E2EE models.

No feature flag: the new route only applies to model ids that failed before this change.

### How did you verify your code works?

`packages/ai/test/provider/venice-e2ee.test.ts` runs a fake enclave. It decrypts the outgoing messages, encrypts the stream back, and the test checks the plaintext never appears in the request body. Other tests cover failed attestation (not verified, wrong nonce, missing key) and the attestation timeout. The `packages/ai` suite, `bun typecheck`, `typecheck:tsc` and `bun run check` pass. I also ran the crypto helpers under Node 24. I could not test against a live Venice enclave.

prs.title: fix(core): capture snapshots when an embedded repository's status fails
prs.body:
### Issue for this PR

Fixes #61383

### Type of change

- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] New feature
- [ ] Refactor / code improvement
- [ ] Documentation

### What does this PR do?

The snapshot store records an untracked nested repository as a gitlink. On every later capture, `git diff-files` checks that gitlink, and by default Git also runs `git status --porcelain=2` inside the nested repository to see if its work tree is dirty. If that status fails (or hangs, as in the Windows report), the whole capture fails with `'git status --porcelain=2' failed in submodule <dir>`.

A gitlink only stores the nested repository's HEAD, so its dirty state never ends up in the snapshot anyway. This passes `--ignore-submodules=dirty` to that `diff-files` call. HEAD changes are still detected, so a new commit in the nested repository still updates the gitlink (the test checks this too, and it fails with `--ignore-submodules=all`).

### How did you verify your code works?

Added a test to `packages/core/test/git.test.ts` that captures a project with an embedded repository, commits in it, then corrupts its index. On `dev` the last capture fails with `fatal: .git/index: index file smaller than expected` / `fatal: 'git status --porcelain=2' failed in submodule nested`. With the change it returns the same tree. `bun run test` in `packages/core` passes except three shell-scan tests that fail the same way on `dev` with my local bash. `bun run lint`, `bun run typecheck:tsc` and the pre-push `bun run check` pass.

prs.title: fix(core): tolerate missing columns on legacy v1 session table
prs.body:
### Issue for this PR

Closes #54009

### Type of change

- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] New feature
- [ ] Refactor / code improvement
- [ ] Documentation

### What does this PR do?

The V1→V2 data migration fails on every startup with `SQLiteError: no such column: path` when the legacy `session` table predates newer columns. The per-session transaction (including the cursor checkpoint) rolls back, the `migration.v1-v2` marker stays stuck in the `sessions` phase, and the import is retried and fails again on every server start.

Root cause: `v1-migration.bun.ts` copies each legacy row into `session_v2` with a fixed `INSERT ... SELECT` column list that unconditionally references `path`, `metadata`, `cost`, `tokens_*`, `agent`, and `model` on the source table. V1 databases last migrated before those columns were added do not have them, so statement preparation fails. The `opencode-next.db` import already handles this class of problem through `selectNextRows` (pragma-based column projection); the legacy copy had no equivalent.

The fix reads the legacy `session` table's columns with `pragma_table_info` before the copy loop and builds the `INSERT ... SELECT` from only the columns the table actually has. Missing columns are omitted from the insert so `session_v2` defaults fill them (`cost`/`tokens_*` default to `0`, nullable columns to `NULL`). `permission` was previously inserted explicitly as `NULL` and now falls back to its default, preserving the intentional clearing of V1 permission state.

### How did you verify your code works?

- Added a regression test (`imports legacy V1 sessions from tables missing newer columns`) that creates a legacy `session` table without `path`, `metadata`, `cost`, `tokens_*`, `agent`, and `model` — the shape observed in the issue — with one session, message, and part row. It verifies the migration completes, `session_v2` receives defaults for the missing columns with agent/model derived from message data, the projected `session_message` row is written, and the marker reaches `{"phase":"completed"}`.
- Confirmed the new test fails against the unfixed source and passes with the fix.
- Full `packages/core/test/v1-migration.test.ts` run: 27 pass, 0 fail.
- `bun typecheck` in `packages/core` passes.

Note: the local pre-push `bun run check` could not run on Windows because oxlint fails to load its TypeScript plugin via Node ESM (`Unknown file extension ".ts"`); that failure is environmental and unrelated to this change.

### Screenshots / recordings

Not a UI change.

- [x] I have not included unrelated changes in this PR

issues.title: sendUserMessage from an extension command fails in -p mode: 'turn_end could not resolve the persisted assistant entry ID'
issues.body:
### What happened?

An extension command whose handler calls `pi.sendUserMessage(...)` (the documented way for a command to drive a turn) fails in print mode. The turn itself runs, but ends with:

```
Extension error (<boundary>): turn_end could not resolve the persisted assistant entry ID
```

Interactive mode is unaffected. Deferring the call out of the handler (`setTimeout(0)`) trades the error for `Extension runtime is stale`, so a `-p` command can't reliably start a turn either way.

Validated with a minimal two-line extension, nothing else loaded:

```ts
export default function (pi: any) {
  pi.registerCommand("sayhi", {
    handler: async () => { await pi.sendUserMessage("Reply with one word: hi"); },
  });
}
```

### Steps to reproduce

1. Save the extension above as `repro.ts`
2. `pi -e ./repro.ts -p '/sayhi'`

Same result with and without `--no-session`.

### Expected behavior

The turn completes without the boundary error, same as in interactive mode.

### Version

1.3.0

issues.title: kimi-coding rejects tool parameters with root anyOf

labels.name: untriaged
labels.description: This issue has been auto closed and has not been triaged

issues.body:
### What happened?

`kimi-coding` rejects tools whose parameters use a root `anyOf`. Two such tools in the current Pi tool set make every prompt fail with HTTP 400:

```text
tools.function.parameters.type is required and must be "object"
```

Adding a root `type` produces another rejection: Moonshot requires `type` inside the union branches, while also requiring an object root. A root union therefore needs flattening before sending.

### Steps to reproduce

Use Pi 1.5.0 with direct `kimi-coding/k3.1-pro` and the current tool set. Send any prompt. A minimal reproduction is a tool with `parameters: { anyOf: [{ type: "object", properties: { agent: { type: "string" } }, required: ["agent"] }, { type: "object", properties: { all: { type: "boolean" } }, required: ["all"] }] }`.

The same tools work through OpenRouter. Kimi's official client has the matching report and proposed normalization in MoonshotAI/kimi-code#2661 and #2662.

### Expected behavior

Pi should adapt only `kimi-coding` tool schemas: merge object-union properties, intersect required fields, and keep the original schema for local validation. Other providers should receive unchanged schemas.

I can implement this with regression tests.

### Version

1.5.0
