issues.body:
### What do you want to change?

Instructions grow. There might be an AGENTS_JAVA.md (containing java-specific instructions), AGENTS_INFRA.md (containing terraform / pulumi instructions or how to create infra), AGENTS_UI.md (containing instructions on how to setup a vue-vite-tailwind-project) and so on. Currently i use something like this in AGENTS.md:

```
## infrastructure (pulumi, terraform)
Look at the rules in $pblibpath/some/where/AGENTS_INFRA.md
```
Which works somewhat but could be improved.

Suggestion:
1. fully embrace environment-variables in all agents.md files
2. suggest a way to link specific instructions conditionally to not fill up useless context.

IMPORTANT: this is separate from AGENTS.md-files in projects. These instructions are not project-specific but rather domain-specific and global.

### Why?

Improves Quality with more specific Instructions, reduces bloat, saves tokens, improves speed.

### How? (optional)

One way might be to generate a tool get_context_infrastructure_pulumi_terraform() and instruct pi to call it when needed (which then would simply return the file). Or keep a file-tree with the names of the files together with a short comment so pi can get additional context if needed.

Another might be to have a gui where people can select context or put it in dedicated subagents. But subagents to me should be more about orchestration and context management? The current idea would allow for variable levels of nested AGENTS.md e.g.: AGENTS.md -> AGENTS_CODING.md (e.g. Tiering, DDD, general rules and naming..) -> AGENTS_JAVA.md / AGENTS_C#.md etc. which might be hard to implement with a subagent-strategy.

issues.title: Feature: subpath support for `pi install git:`
issues.body:
Re-file of #4529 (auto-closed during refactor).

## Problem

`pi install git:github.com/user/repo` clones the full repository and treats the repo root as the package root. There is no way to target a subdirectory. This makes it impossible to install individual extensions from monorepos like `pi-mono`, where example extensions live at `packages/coding-agent/examples/extensions/subagent/`.

## Proposal

Add `#path/to/subdir` URL fragment syntax to git package sources:

```bash
pi install git:github.com/earendil-works/pi-mono#packages/coding-agent/examples/extensions/subagent
pi install git:github.com/user/mono@v2#packages/my-extension
```

Also via `settings.json` object form:

```json
{
  "packages": [
    { "source": "git:github.com/user/mono@v1", "subpath": "packages/my-extension" }
  ]
}
```

Behaviour:
- Full repo is cloned as now (no sparse checkout)
- Package root resolves to `join(cloneDir, subpath)`
- `npm install` runs in the subpath if it has its own `package.json`
- Multiple subpaths from the same repo share one clone, tracked as separate packages

## Implementation

Working branch rebased onto latest main (`4868222e`), all checks pass (build, typecheck, lint, 119 package manager tests green): [feature/git-install-subpath](https://github.com/Mearman/pi/tree/feature/git-install-subpath)

4 commits:
- `feat: support subpath in git package sources (#subdir syntax)`
- `test: add subpath parsing tests for git URL fragments`
- `docs: document subpath support for git package sources`
- `test: add package manager integration tests for git subpath support`

Supersedes #4529.

issues.title: Extension hook for agent auto-retry: let an extension set the delay or stop the retry
issues.body:
### What do you want to change?

Add an `auto_retry_decision` event, fired in [`_prepareRetry`](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/blob/43472ddb6a6ad9e9bdd74aaa97b22c22cb3e4283/packages/coding-agent/src/core/agent-session.ts#L3924-L3964) after pi computes its backoff and before `auto_retry_start`. It carries `attempt`, `maxAttempts`, pi's `delayMs`, `errorMessage` and the failed `message`. A handler may return `{ delayMs }` (still capped by `retry.maxAgentDelayMs`) or `{ action: "stop" }`. The last handler that returns a value wins, like [`cache_warming_decision`](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/blob/43472ddb6a6ad9e9bdd74aaa97b22c22cb3e4283/packages/coding-agent/src/core/extensions/runner.ts#L1135-L1156).

### Why?

Many providers state the wait only in the error text, e.g. OpenAI's `Please try again in 10.384s` ([openai-node#1477](https://github.com/openai/openai-node/issues/1477)) or Groq's `Please try again in 1.969s` ([continuedev/continue#2343](https://github.com/continuedev/continue/issues/2343)). With the [defaults](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/blob/43472ddb6a6ad9e9bdd74aaa97b22c22cb3e4283/packages/coding-agent/src/core/settings-defaults.ts#L18-L22) (2 s base, 3 retries), pi's backoff ([`retryDelayMs`](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/blob/43472ddb6a6ad9e9bdd74aaa97b22c22cb3e4283/packages/ai/src/utils/retry.ts#L149-L153)) retries after 2 s, 4 s and 8 s, so a server that enforces a 20 s window fails the turn after three retries that all land inside it. When the window is hours long, the three retries are wasted and the turn fails anyway.

#2366 was closed with "we don't interpret rate limits as it's brittle", and a later comment there asked for a way to "intercept the message and do something with the default backoff timer". This is that hook: pi still interprets nothing, and the parsing lives in an extension for the providers its author uses. (#7134 asked for `retry_after` support in core and was auto-closed.)

Today a retry reaches an extension only as the failed [`agent_end`](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/blob/43472ddb6a6ad9e9bdd74aaa97b22c22cb3e4283/packages/coding-agent/src/core/agent-session.ts#L1372-L1373), and the one way to stop it is [`ctx.abort()`](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/blob/43472ddb6a6ad9e9bdd74aaa97b22c22cb3e4283/packages/coding-agent/src/core/extensions/types.ts#L374-L375), which also ends the run. Nothing can change the delay. #9829 (extensions can't see per-attempt retries) was auto-closed.

### How? (optional)

I have a prototype on `6f7f7f2` (the cited files are unchanged on `43472dd`): a new `emitAutoRetryDecision` in `runner.ts` written like `emitCacheWarmingDecision`, about 20 lines in `_prepareRetry` ("stop" undoes the attempt the same way the exhausted-budget branch does), the types and exports, and a short section in `docs/extensions.md`. Six new tests in `agent-session-retry-events.test.ts` cover a delay override, the cap, stop on the first and on a later attempt, no handler, and a throwing handler. `npm run check` is clean.

One open point: the session event `agent_end.willRetry` (what interactive mode reads) is computed synchronously while `agent_end` is emitted ([`_willRetryAfterAgentEnd`](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/blob/43472ddb6a6ad9e9bdd74aaa97b22c22cb3e4283/packages/coding-agent/src/core/agent-session.ts#L1265-L1279)), before `_prepareRetry` runs, so it still says `true` when a handler stops the retry. The prototype documents that rather than moving an async hook into the `agent_end` dispatch; I'd like your preference.

I could implement it myself if this gets an `lgtm`.

tool_search answers "No matching tools found" for a declared direct MCP tool; direct servers are never named in the prompt

labels.name: untriaged
labels.description: This issue has been auto closed and has not been triaged

issues.body:
### What happened?

pi 1.5.0, builtin `mcp` and `tool-search` extensions. One MCP server is configured `"exposure": "direct"` (two tools), two are `"deferred"`.

The direct tools are declared on every request, but the system prompt never names them: `<tools>` lists only tools with a `promptSnippet` (`core/system-prompt.js:84`), and `<mcp_servers>` lists only servers with deferred or codemode tools (`extensions/mcp/index.js:104`). The `tool_search` description says "For MCP tool discovery, always use `tool_search`" (`extensions/tool-search/tool.js:227`), so the model searches for the direct tool. The search only covers deferred/codemode tools that are not yet active (`tool.js:204`), so it answers "No matching tools found." The model reads that as "this tool does not exist" and stops using a tool it already has.

Seen with a Qwen3 27B model: over 16 runs of the same prompt, about half went to `tool_search` first, and every one of those missed a declared tool and fell back to another server.

### Steps to reproduce

1. `mcp.json` with one server `"exposure": "direct"` and one `"deferred"`.
2. `pi -p "use <the direct server> to search for X"` with a model that follows the tool_search hint.
3. The first call is `tool_search("<server>")` → "No matching tools found." → the model gives up on the tool.

### Expected behavior

Either `tool_search` says the tool is already there ("`mcp__x__y` is active; call it directly"), or direct servers get a line in `<mcp_servers>` like deferred ones do. Both are small; I would send a PR for either if that is welcome.

### Version

1.5.0. `pi -ne` does not apply: both extensions involved are builtins.

issues.title: `getContextUsage()` massively overestimates context after retryable network error

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

issues.body:
### What happened?

On Pi 0.99.2, a retryable network error caused `getContextUsage()` to jump from about 42k tokens to 330,081 tokens.

Immediately before the spike:

```text
07:53:53  tokens=42707  hostTokens=42707  inMsgs=583 outMsgs=36
```

After a WebSocket/fetch failure:

```text
07:53:55  tokens=330081 hostTokens=330081 inMsgs=583 outMsgs=36
```

The session history shows:

```text
07:53:52 assistant toolUse  usage=33977
07:53:53 assistant error    usage=0
07:53:53 context_edit       replacement=null
07:53:55 assistant error    usage=0
07:53:55 context_edit       replacement=null
```

Pi's retry path creates these `context_edit` entries via `_omitRecoveryAttempt()`. It appears that the later edit invalidates the previous valid usage anchor, causing `estimateProjectedContextTokens()` to fall back to estimating the whole projection.

This looks like the same underlying issue as #10068, and is still reproducible on 0.99.2, which is the reason why I create a new issue. 

### Steps to reproduce

1. Start a sufficiently long Pi session.
2. Trigger a retryable transport failure, e.g. a WebSocket/fetch failure.
3. Let Pi automatically retry the failed turn.
4. Observe `getContextUsage()` / the context indicator immediately after the retry omission is recorded.
5. The reported context can jump far above the value reported immediately before the failure, without corresponding new conversation content.


### Expected behavior

Omitting a zero-usage failed retry attempt with `context_edit(replacement=null)` should not cause the previous valid context usage to be replaced by a massive full-projection estimate.

### Version

0.99.2

issues.title: MCP tool calls return empty results despite a valid OAuth token — session/auth header not carried after sign-in (Google Workspace MCP)

labels.name: untriaged
labels.description: This issue has been auto closed and has not been triaged

issues.body:
pi 1.5.0, Linux + macOS. Remote OAuth MCP servers over streamable HTTP — Google's official Workspace MCP endpoints (`calendarmcp/drivemcp/gmailmcp.googleapis.com/mcp/v1`).

## Field evidence (three servers, litigation tooling, tokens verified against Google directly)

| Server | Token (`tokeninfo`) | Scopes granted | Direct REST with the SAME token | Via pi MCP |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| gcal | valid | `calendar.readonly` | **2 calendars** (real data) | **0 calendars** |
| gdrive | valid | `drive`, `drive.file`, `drive.readonly`, `drive.appdata` | **5 files** ("PCN spreadsheet", "Letter Of Claim.pdf") | **0 files** |
| gmail-ro | valid | MCP-advertised Gmail scope | 403 (expected — scope is gateway-specific) | 0 threads |

0 calendars is impossible for any Google account (a primary calendar always exists). 0 files refutes the narrow-scope hypothesis (all four drive scopes granted). REST calls with the **identical access token** from `~/.pi/agent/mcp-auth.json` return real data; the MCP layer returns empty. No errors surface anywhere — `/mcp` shows **Connected**.

## Diagnosis

The MCP session is not carrying the token. Google's MCP gateway (serverInfo: `StatelessServer`) answers discovery **unauthenticated** — `initialize` and `tools/list` return 200 with the full tool catalog and no credentials; only `tools/call` returns 401 "missing credential". So a client can fully establish an MCP session with no auth. If pi establishes the session at connect time and does not re-establish it **with the Authorization header** after OAuth completes (or attach the token per-request on streamable HTTP), every tool call rides the unauthenticated session — and Google's gateway returns empty result sets on read paths instead of an error, which is their documented-not-our-favourite behaviour but is indistinguishable from real data to the model.

Possibly related: #10416 (stateless MCP, 2026-07-28 spec) — Google's gateway self-identifies as `StatelessServer`.

## Repro

1. Configure a Google Workspace MCP server (url + `oauth: {clientId, clientSecret, scope}`)
2. `/mcp` → Sign in → shows Connected
3. Call a read tool (`list_calendars`) → 0 results
4. Extract the access token from `~/.pi/agent/mcp-auth.json` and call the REST API directly (`calendar/v3/users/me/calendarList`) → real data

## Asks

1. After OAuth completes, re-establish the MCP session with the Authorization header — or attach the token per-request on streamable HTTP
2. `/mcp` "Connected" should verify an **authenticated** round-trip (a cheap authorized call), not session establishment
3. Surface the authenticated account (email) and granted scopes per server in `/mcp`
4. When the user configures `oauth.scope` and the server advertises different scopes, honour the configured scope or warn that it was overridden

prs.title: feat(ai,coding-agent): send audio and video to Gemini by reference
prs.body:
A user message may carry a `FileContent` block that points at a local path instead of the bytes. Before a Gemini request pi uploads that file to the Files API, waits for Google to finish processing (five-minute bound, since Google sends no notification), and sends `fileData` rather than inline data. The transcript keeps only the path, so a video never lands in the session file. Uploads are cached in ~/.pi/agent/media-cache/google per file version, keyed by path, size and mtime, and re-uploaded when Google is about to expire them.

Media a model cannot take degrades to a placeholder, so a session can move between providers without failing the request. Gemini catalog entries now declare the audio and video modalities models.dev reports. `model.input` accepts both, so a capability the catalog cannot express is not silently dropped.

The TUI attaches files with `/attach` or a clipboard paste, shows them as chips above the input, lists them under the user message, and shows upload and processing progress in the editor status line. A pasted image is now attached as an image instead of being written to a temporary file and pasted as text.

prs.title: feat: prompt cache warming in p2
prs.body:
## Problem

p2 runs Anthropic (and Claude on Radius) with the 5-minute prompt cache and never refreshes it. Every request after a gap of more than 305 s rewrites the whole prompt. In the p2 sessions of Oct 12 - Nov 5 that happened 789 times and cost about $1,430 extra, 26% of p2's spend. Example: a coordinator waits 11 minutes for subagent reports, then its next request writes 579k tokens again ($2.80).

pi-coding-agent avoids this with its cache warmer: over the same period its idle-gap miss cost was 10% of spend, with 3.6% spent on warming. Replaying pi-coding-agent's policy on p2's request log brings p2's cache read+write spend from $4,674 to about $3,618.

## Change

- **pi-ai**: the warming policy moves out of pi-coding-agent into shared helpers (`src/cache-warming.ts`):
  - `getPromptCacheTtlMs`, `getCacheWarmingDelayMs`, `isCacheWarmingReplayable`, `getCacheWarmingRequestOptions`, `evaluateCacheWarming` and the `CACHE_WARMING_*` constants.
  - pi-coding-agent's `CacheWarmer` uses them, with no behaviour change.
- **p2** (pi-durable is unchanged):
  - The Harness's `Models` proxy (`openHarness()`) remembers each `streamSimple` request by the message its `result()` resolved with (a `WeakMap`). `HarnessParts.requestOf(message)` returns it once as a `ModelRequest`: the model, the messages after `beforeRequest`, and the options without the attempt's `signal`, `telemetry` and `onPayload`. Compaction summaries and the refreshes go through `completeSimple` and are not remembered.
  - New plugin `plugins/cache-warming`: a hook-only Durable extension, with one warming run per conversation.
    - `afterResponse` looks up the request with `requestOf` and starts (or replaces) the conversation's run.
    - The refresh resends the request with one output token, no retries and `disableContinuation`.
    - Its usage is added to the conversation's `pi.usage` (`UsageDoc`).
  - Same policy as pi: refresh at 90% of the TTL, up to 60 min while a run streams and 30 min after it settled, and only when the expected savings are at least $0.05.
  - Each refresh asks for the conversation's phase:
    - none while `pi.live.generation` exists (a request in flight, backing off or polled);
    - streaming while `pi.live.run` exists;
    - idle otherwise, but only for top-level conversations (settled subagents and one-shot agents are not warmed);
    - none once the next request would start differently (another model, or a context that no longer starts with the sent messages: reset, compaction), which stops warming.
  - The worker stays alive while a run is armed (new liveness kind `cacheWarming`).
  - New setting `cacheWarming`: `"idle"` (default), `"streaming"`, `"off"`. It switches live through `ExtensionSwitches`.

Radius: the gateway's `/v1/config` already declares `promptCache: { short: 300, long: 3600 }` for Claude 4.8 and 5.x models, so pi-coding-agent and p2 both warm them. Claude 4.5 models on Radius declare none, which is correct: they use budget thinking and cannot be replayed with `maxTokens: 1`.

Not included: a warming status display (pi's `/session` line) and a decision override hook (pi's `cache_warming_decision`).

## Tests

- `npm run check`, `apps/p2` `npm run check`.
- `apps/p2/test/p2/harness-requests.test.ts`: the message `afterResponse` gets is the object `result()` resolved with, so `requestOf` finds it, once.
- pi-coding-agent cache warming tests.
- `apps/p2/test/p2/cache-warming.test.ts`:
  - Warmer tests on mocked timers with fake models: refresh timing and options, the streaming and idle windows, the cost decision, the stop cases, replacement and close.
  - An end-to-end test in a worker, using the fake provider with a short `promptCache`: refreshes repeat the request exactly and add to `pi.usage`.
- Not run: the full `apps/p2` suite.

issues.title: ci: main's Java lane fails to compile — duplicate case labels in SurfaceAdmissionAcceptanceTest (from #16641)
issues.body:
## What happened?

`main` is broken for every PR's Java lane: `SDK Java (fast) / ubuntu-latest / Java 21` fails at **test compilation**, so no Java test runs at all, and the aggregating `Managed Agent fast tier` / `Managed Agent gate` checks fail with it.

```
[ERROR] COMPILATION ERROR :
[ERROR] .../packages/managed-agent-server/verification/src/test/java/com/alibaba/qwen/code/managedagent/SurfaceAdmissionAcceptanceTest.java:[1712,70] duplicate case label
[ERROR] .../SurfaceAdmissionAcceptanceTest.java:[1712,89] duplicate case label
[ERROR] Failed to execute goal maven-compiler-plugin:3.14.1:testCompile (default-testCompile)
        on project qwen-managed-agent-verification: Compilation failure
##[error]Maven suite 'runtime-broker H2 suite' failed with status 1
```

## Root cause

Two `case` labels in the same switch list the same constants. On current `main` (`30e71d37e6`), in `SurfaceAdmissionAcceptanceTest.java`:

```java
// line 1663
case TRANSCRIPT_QUERY, ITEM_LIST, SESSION_RESOURCES, SESSION_AGENT_TRACE -> "{\"sessionId\":\"" + session + "\"}";

// lines 1711-1712
case SESSION_APPROVAL, SESSION_MODELS, SESSION_SKILLS, SESSION_MCP,
        SESSION_CONTEXT_USAGE, SESSION_MODEL_STATISTICS, SESSION_RESOURCES, SESSION_AGENT_TRACE ->
        "{\"sessionId\":\"" + session + "\"}";
```

`SESSION_RESOURCES` and `SESSION_AGENT_TRACE` appear in both, which javac rejects as duplicate case labels — matching the two reported columns on line 1712. Both arms produce the identical `{"sessionId":…}` body, so the fix is to drop the two constants from the later label (or merge the arms); no behaviour change is intended.

## Introduced by

`0e7bf516d1` — `feat(managed-agent): persist Session model statistics and request context (#16641)`. `git log -S` on the multi-label line attributes it to that commit, and it is the most recent commit touching this file.

## Evidence that this is base breakage, not PR-caused

- `main`'s own `Managed Agent gate` run at `0e7bf516d1` is `failure` (2026-11-09 03:32 UTC), and at the current tip `30e71d37e6` is also `failure` (04:02 UTC).
- Reproduced on PR #16711, whose entire diff is one TypeScript test file (`packages/cli/src/serve/managed-workspace-upload.process.test.ts`, +9/−4). It touches no Java source, so the merge commit's Java tree is exactly `main`'s.
- The file is absent from that PR's diff (`git diff --name-only origin/main...HEAD` → one `.test.ts` path).

## Impact

Every open PR inherits a red Java lane it cannot fix from its own diff, and the failure is a compile error rather than a test result, so retries cannot clear it. It also masks real Java regressions: nothing in the verification module executes until this compiles.

## Suggested fix

Remove `SESSION_RESOURCES, SESSION_AGENT_TRACE` from the label at lines 1711-1712 (they are already handled at line 1663 with the same body), then run the module's Java verification per `packages/managed-agent-server/AGENTS.md`.

<details>
<summary>中文说明</summary>

## 发生了什么？

`main` 当前对每个 PR 的 Java 车道都是坏的：`SDK Java (fast) / ubuntu-latest / Java 21` 在**测试编译阶段**就失败，因此一个 Java 测试都没跑，聚合的 `Managed Agent fast tier` / `Managed Agent gate` 随之变红。

错误为 `SurfaceAdmissionAcceptanceTest.java:[1712,70]` 与 `[1712,89]` 的 `duplicate case label`，最终 `maven-compiler-plugin:testCompile` 在 `qwen-managed-agent-verification` 模块上编译失败，`runtime-broker H2 suite` 以状态 1 退出。

## 根因

同一个 switch 里两个 `case` 标签列了相同常量。当前 main（`30e71d37e6`）上：1663 行为 `case TRANSCRIPT_QUERY, ITEM_LIST, SESSION_RESOURCES, SESSION_AGENT_TRACE -> …`；1711-1712 行为 `case SESSION_APPROVAL, SESSION_MODELS, SESSION_SKILLS, SESSION_MCP, SESSION_CONTEXT_USAGE, SESSION_MODEL_STATISTICS, SESSION_RESOURCES, SESSION_AGENT_TRACE -> …`。`SESSION_RESOURCES` 与 `SESSION_AGENT_TRACE` 两处都有，javac 判为重复 case 标签，正好对应 1712 行报告的两个列号。两个分支体都是相同的 `{"sessionId":…}`，因此修法是从后一个标签里去掉这两个常量（或合并分支），不涉及行为变化。

## 引入提交

`0e7bf516d1` —— `feat(managed-agent): persist Session model statistics and request context (#16641)`。对该多标签行做 `git log -S` 归因到此提交，它也是最近一次改动该文件的提交。

## 属 base 自坏而非 PR 引入的证据

- main 自身在 `0e7bf516d1` 上的 `Managed Agent gate` 为 `failure`（2026-11-09 03:32 UTC），在当前 tip `30e71d37e6` 上同样为 `failure`（04:02 UTC）。
- 在 PR #16711 上复现，而该 PR 的全部 diff 只有一个 TypeScript 测试文件（+9/−4），不碰任何 Java 源码，因此其 merge commit 的 Java 树与 main 完全一致。
- 该 Java 文件不在这个 PR 的 diff 内。

## 影响

每个开放 PR 都继承一条无法从自身 diff 修复的红 Java 车道；而且这是编译错误而非测试结果，重跑无法清除。它还会掩盖真实的 Java 回归——在该模块能编译之前，verification 里什么都不会执行。

## 建议修法

从 1711-1712 行的标签中移除 `SESSION_RESOURCES, SESSION_AGENT_TRACE`（1663 行已用相同分支体处理），随后按 `packages/managed-agent-server/AGENTS.md` 跑该模块的 Java 验证。

</details>

issues.title: bug(core): FileChangedWatcher permanently misses a file written into a freshly created subdirectory (chokidar snapshot-then-watch gap)

labels.name: priority/P2
labels.description: Medium - Moderately impactful, noticeable problem

labels.name: type/bug
labels.description: Something isn't working as expected

labels.name: category/core
labels.description: Core engine and logic

labels.name: scope/file-operations
labels.description: File system operations

labels.name: roadmap/hooks-events
labels.description: Roadmap: Hook and event system

labels.name: status/ready-for-human
labels.description: Specified but requires human judgment to implement; not suitable for an autonomous agent

issues.body:
## What happened?

`FileChangedWatcher` can permanently miss a file that is written into a freshly created subdirectory of a watched root. The loss is silent: no `FileChanged` notification is ever delivered for that file, not merely a delayed one.

The mechanism is in chokidar 4.0.3 (the version `packages/core` locks). `NodeFsHandler._handleDir` awaits `_handleRead(dir, …)` — the readdirp snapshot plus child registration — **before** `_watchWithNodeFs(dir, …)` attaches the native watch:

```js
if (!target) {
    await this._handleRead(dir, initialAdd, wh, target, dir, depth, throttler);
    if (this.fsw.closed) return;
}
closer = this._watchWithNodeFs(dir, (dirPath, stats) => { … });
```

A file created after the snapshot completed but before the watch attached is in neither: the snapshot did not see it, and no watch existed yet to report it. Nothing re-reads that directory unless a later event fires on it, so the `add` is lost for the lifetime of the watcher.

## Why it matters

`FileChangedWatcher` backs the `FileChanged` hook for local sessions. A tool or editor that creates a directory and immediately writes into it — a common atomic-write or scaffolding shape — can land in that window, and the hook then never fires for the new file. Under load the window widens because the snapshot and the watch attachment are separated by awaited I/O.

This was found while deflaking `packages/core/src/hooks/file-changed-watcher.test.ts` (PR #16697, issues #16626 / #16668). The test hit the window reliably enough to redden `main` twice in one day, with the signature that only the explicitly registered file was reported and the nested file's event never arrived across all three attempts. The test-side fix creates the directory before the watcher starts so the initial scan attaches the watch deterministically; that removes the test's exposure but does not address the production path.

## What did you expect to happen?

A file written into a newly created subdirectory of a watched root should produce a `FileChanged` notification regardless of how quickly it follows the `mkdir`.

## Anything else we need to know?

Possible directions, not a decision:

- Re-read a directory after attaching its watch, so anything created during the snapshot-to-watch gap is picked up. chokidar's `_handleRead` already has a throttled re-read path (`wasThrottled`) that could be leveraged.
- Attach the watch before taking the snapshot, accepting that the snapshot may then double-report and relying on the existing dedup.
- Track the upstream chokidar issue if one exists, and pin or patch accordingly.

Reproduction shape (this is what the test does): watch a root, `mkdir` a subdirectory, then immediately `writeFile` inside it, and wait for the `add`. On a contended host the notification is sometimes never delivered. A sandboxed round on a faster host lost 0 events in 240 interleaved runs, so reproduction is host- and load-dependent.

<details>
<summary>中文说明</summary>

## 发生了什么？

`FileChangedWatcher` 可能永久漏掉一个写入「被 watch 根目录下新建子目录」的文件。丢失是静默的：该文件的 `FileChanged` 通知永远不会投递，而不只是迟到。

机制在 chokidar 4.0.3（`packages/core` 锁定的版本）。`NodeFsHandler._handleDir` 先 await `_handleRead(dir, …)`（readdirp 快照加子项注册），**之后**才由 `_watchWithNodeFs(dir, …)` 挂上原生 watch。在快照完成之后、watch 挂上之前创建的文件两边都不沾：快照没看到它，当时也还没有 watch 能上报它。除非该目录后续再有事件触发，否则不会重读，于是这个 `add` 在 watcher 的整个生命周期内丢失。

## 为什么重要

`FileChangedWatcher` 支撑本地会话的 `FileChanged` hook。创建目录后立刻往里写文件的工具或编辑器（常见的原子写入 / 脚手架形态）可能落进这个窗口，hook 便永远不为该新文件触发。负载下窗口会变宽，因为快照与挂 watch 之间隔着被 await 的 I/O。

这是在给 `packages/core/src/hooks/file-changed-watcher.test.ts` 去 flake 时发现的（PR #16697，issue #16626 / #16668）。该测试命中窗口的频率足以在同一天两次把 main 打红，签名是只有被显式注册的文件上报、嵌套文件的事件在三次尝试中从未到达。测试侧的修复是在 watcher 启动前创建目录，让初始扫描确定性挂上 watch；这消除了测试的暴露面，但没有解决生产路径。

## 期望的行为？

写入被 watch 根目录下新建子目录的文件，无论它紧随 `mkdir` 多快，都应产生 `FileChanged` 通知。

## 其他需要说明的？

可选方向（未定案）：

- 在挂上目录 watch 之后重读一次该目录，捡回快照到挂 watch 之间创建的文件。chokidar 的 `_handleRead` 已有受节流的重读路径（`wasThrottled`）可利用。
- 先挂 watch 再做快照，接受快照可能重复上报，依赖既有去重。
- 若上游 chokidar 已有对应 issue 则跟踪，并据此 pin 或打补丁。

复现形态（即该测试所做的）：watch 一个根目录，`mkdir` 一个子目录，然后立刻在其中 `writeFile`，等待 `add`。在争用宿主机上该通知有时永不投递。一轮沙箱验证在更快宿主机上 240 次交错运行零丢失，因此复现依赖宿主机与负载。

</details>

prs.title: test(ci): isolate the checkout hook fixture from the release runner git config
prs.body:
## What this PR does

The CI failure-patrol test that plants a global git hook now points git directly at the fixture's own global config file instead of relying on `$HOME` resolution. It also clears the ambient command-line config entries so the fixture's identity and hook are what git actually reads.

## Why it's needed

The nightly release for `v0.27.0-nightly.20261108.6c3d5355de` failed its `quality_scripts` gate solely because this test could not commit in its temporary repository. The release runner exports an empty job-wide `GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL` from its workspace-isolation step, and that variable outranks `$HOME/.gitconfig`, so git found neither the fixture's commit identity nor the planted hook. Pinning the fixture's config explicitly keeps the test's assertion intact — the hook fires under the planted configuration and does not fire after the step's `/dev/null` redirect — while making the test work on every runner.

## Reviewer Test Plan

### How to verify

Run the focused suite with the release runner's git environment simulated: `GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL=/dev/null GIT_CONFIG_COUNT=0 GIT_CONFIG_NOSYSTEM=1 GIT_CONFIG_PARAMETERS= npx vitest run --config ./scripts/tests/vitest.config.ts scripts/tests/ci-flaky-rerun-workflow.test.js`. Expect all 37 active tests to pass.

Then remove the fixture's explicit `GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL` pin and rerun the same command. Expect the test to fail at `git commit -qm seed` with `Author identity unknown`, demonstrating that the pin is load-bearing. Run the suite once more without the release environment variables; expect the same 37 passes.

### Evidence (Before & After)

N/A — the change is test-only; the before/after evidence is the focused test outcome described above.

### Tested on

|     OS     | Status |
| :--------: | :----: |
|  🍏 macOS  |   ⚠️   |
| 🪟 Windows |   ⚠️   |
|  🐧 Linux  |   ✅   |

### Environment (optional)

Local Vitest run on Linux with Node.js 22.

## Risk & Scope

- Main risk or tradeoff: the fixture now pins git config for its own git calls; any future assertion in this block that needs ambient global config must override it explicitly. The negative control already does.
- Not validated / out of scope: a full release-workflow re-run; the focused suite covers the changed test.
- Breaking changes / migration notes: none.

## Linked Issues

Fixes #16680

<summary>中文说明</summary>

## 这个 PR 做了什么

这个 CI 失败巡检测试会预埋一个全局 git hook；现在它让 git 直接读取夹具自己的全局配置文件，而不再依赖 `$HOME` 解析。它同时清空环境中的命令行配置项，确保 git 实际读取的是夹具写入的身份和 hook。

## 为什么需要它

`v0.27.0-nightly.20261108.6c3d5355de` 的夜间发布在 `quality_scripts` 关卡失败，唯一原因是这个测试无法在其临时仓库中提交。release runner 的 workspace 隔离步骤会导出作业级的空 `GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL`，该变量优先级高于 `$HOME/.gitconfig`，因此 git 既找不到夹具的提交身份，也找不到预埋的 hook。显式固定夹具的配置既保留了测试断言——预埋配置下 hook 会触发，而步骤的 `/dev/null` 重定向后不会触发——又让测试在所有 runner 上都能运行。

## 审查者测试计划

### 如何验证

在模拟 release runner 的 git 环境下运行聚焦套件：`GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL=/dev/null GIT_CONFIG_COUNT=0 GIT_CONFIG_NOSYSTEM=1 GIT_CONFIG_PARAMETERS= npx vitest run --config ./scripts/tests/vitest.config.ts scripts/tests/ci-flaky-rerun-workflow.test.js`。预期全部 37 个启用的测试通过。

然后移除夹具中显式的 `GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL` 固定，再次运行同一命令。预期测试会在 `git commit -qm seed` 处失败并报 `Author identity unknown`，从而证明该固定是必要的。最后在不带 release 环境变量的情况下再运行一次；预期同样是 37 个测试通过。

prs.title: fix(ci): only delete label-recovered registrations GitHub reports offline
prs.body:
## What this PR does

Extends the offline-only deletion rule to the label-recovery cleanup path of the ephemeral runner manager. When a slot's identity is recovered from resource labels (no recorded registration name or id), a matching registration is now only deleted when GitHub explicitly reports it offline. An online or status-less match blocks the slot and keeps everything in place for the next cycle, the same way a rejected deletion does. Identities anchored by recorded state keep the exact previous behavior.

## Why it's needed

The identity-less sweep already refuses to delete anything GitHub has not confirmed offline, because an online registration may belong to a live runner outside this host's view and a malformed record with no status must fail closed. The label-recovery path — a single unambiguous identity reconstructed from `qwen.instance` labels — still deleted every name match regardless of status. That is the same destructive operation with a weaker guard. This gap was identified by @doudouOUC during the review of #16648 (closed as superseded by #16628) and is landed here as the agreed follow-up.

The gate deliberately sits at the deletion step, not in the name matcher: the identity-mismatch and ambiguity checks above still see every match, so an online impostor under the slot's name keeps blocking reconciliation instead of being silently ignored.

## Reviewer Test Plan

### How to verify

Run the manager unit suite: `node --test scripts/ci/ephemeral-runner/manager.test.mjs` (no dependencies needed). Confirm the new test: with an orphan container whose label recovers a single identity, a matching registration that is online — or carries no status at all — is never deleted across two cycles, no replacement runner is registered, and the failure keeps reporting. The existing label-recovery tests (offline suffixed registration deleted, legacy bare-name reconciliation with a recorded runner id) are unchanged and green.

### Evidence (Before & After)

N/A — infrastructure manager logic, covered by unit tests (62/62 passing locally, dep-free).

### Tested on

|     OS     | Status |
| :--------: | :----: |
|  🍏 macOS  |   ✅   |
| 🪟 Windows |  N/A   |
|  🐧 Linux  |   ⚠️   |

### Environment (optional)

Node.js `node:test` only; no Docker or GitHub access required by the suite.

## Risk & Scope

- Main risk or tradeoff: a label-recovered slot whose registration GitHub reports online now stays blocked (retrying) instead of deleting it. That is the intended fail-closed behavior, matching the identity-less sweep; the stall alert surfaces a slot stuck this way.
- Not validated / out of scope: live-host rehearsal; the identity-less sweep and state-recorded paths are untouched.
- Breaking changes / migration notes: none.

## Linked Issues

Follow-up from the review of #16648 (superseded by #16628); credited to @doudouOUC's finding.

<details>
<summary>中文说明</summary>

## 这个 PR 做了什么

把「只删 GitHub 明确报告 offline 的注册」这条规则补齐到 label-recovery 清理路径。当槽位身份是从资源标签恢复的（没有记录注册名或注册 id）时，匹配的注册只有 GitHub 明确报告 offline 才会删除；online 或缺 status 的匹配会阻塞槽位、保留现场交由下一周期重试，与被拒删除的处理一致。有记录状态锚定的身份行为完全不变。

## 为什么需要

无身份清扫路径已经拒绝删除任何 GitHub 未确认 offline 的注册——online 注册可能属于本宿主机视野之外的存活 runner，缺 status 的畸形记录必须 fail-closed。而 label-recovery 路径（从 `qwen.instance` 标签恢复出唯一身份）此前对名字匹配一律删除，不看 status：同一个破坏性操作配了更弱的守卫。该缺口由 @doudouOUC 在 #16648 评审中指出（该 PR 已以 superseded 关闭），本 PR 是按约定拆出的 follow-up。

门禁刻意放在删除步骤而不是名字匹配器里：上方的身份不匹配与歧义检查仍能看到所有匹配，冒用槽位名字的 online 注册会继续阻塞对账，而不是被悄悄忽略。

## Reviewer 测试计划

运行 `node --test scripts/ci/ephemeral-runner/manager.test.mjs`（无需依赖）。确认新增用例：孤儿容器标签恢复出唯一身份时，online 或无 status 的匹配注册两个周期内都不被删除、不注册替代 runner、故障持续上报。既有 label-recovery 用例（offline 后缀注册被删、带记录 runner id 的旧式裸名对账）不变且绿。

## 风险与范围

- 主要取舍：label-recovery 槽位的注册若被 GitHub 报告为 online，现在会保持阻塞（重试）而不是删除——这正是与无身份清扫一致的 fail-closed 行为，卡住的槽位由 stall alert 暴露。
- 未验证 / 不在范围：真机演练；无身份清扫与有状态路径未改动。
- 破坏性变更：无。

本地验证：62/62 通过（dep-free），eslint / prettier 干净。

</details>

prs.title: feat(web-shell): add sidebar multi-select with bulk pin and archive
prs.body:
## What this PR does

Adds a persistent multi-select toggle at the right of the sidebar's New session row. Selection shows a count and compact checkboxes, with Pin and Archive in the bottom action bar. Clicking the toggle again, the close control, or Escape clears selection. Rows retain their typography and height, and the header preserves its height when the count appears.

Bulk pin serially reuses existing per-session organization calls, optimistic updates, rollback, and owning-workspace routing. Already-pinned selections are skipped; selecting only pinned sessions disables Pin. Archive executes immediately without confirmation, requires the idle-guard capability, and sends `requireIdle: true`. Current and running sessions remain protected. Both actions retain failed selections for retry while preserving successful work.

## Why it's needed

Managing several sidebar conversations currently requires repeated individual actions or switching to Session Overview. This implements the revised Pin + Archive scope of #16698. Archive is reversible and avoids introducing destructive bulk deletion in the sidebar. The client-side pin approach and partial-success semantics explicitly address the automated triage questions without adding backend routes.

## Reviewer Test Plan

### How to verify

1. Open the sidebar, enter selection from the New session row, select multiple conversations, and exit using the same toggle, close control, and Escape. Check stable typography, row/header height, count, and coexistence with top-row search.
2. Select only pinned conversations: Pin is disabled. Add an unpinned conversation: Pin only pins that conversation. A failed pin remains selected and successful pins persist.
3. Select idle, non-current workspace conversations and click Archive. Expect immediate archive with no confirmation dialog and no deletion. Current/running sessions cannot be archived; daemons without the idle-guard capability disable bulk Archive.
4. Select equal session IDs from different trusted workspaces. Verify independent selection and requests to each owning workspace. Failed archive items remain selected; changing context during a request must not restore old selections.

### Evidence (Before & After)

Before: sidebar conversations expose individual actions. After: persistent selection mode offers Pin and Archive, with no archive confirmation.

![Sidebar multi-select with Pin and Archive](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/codex/sidebar-session-multiselect/docs/design/sidebar-session-multiselect.png)

Validation: full repository build; Web Shell typecheck; 96 focused sidebar tests (including 35 selection/current-session-delete cases); Chromium E2E with mock daemon responses verifies stable toggle geometry, selected count, idle-only archive requests, and absence of confirmation. Changed-file ESLint, formatting, and diff checks pass. Full repository typecheck passes with an 8 GiB heap after the default-heap run exhausted memory. Full preflight/all-repository unit tests were not run. Browser evidence uses synthetic sessions; no real conversations were archived.

### Tested on

| OS | Status |
| :-- | :-- |
| macOS | ✅ |
| Windows | ⚠️ not tested |
| Linux | ⚠️ not tested |

### Environment (optional)

Local Vite Web Shell and Playwright Chromium with the repository mock daemon.

## Risk & Scope

- Actions are serial per-session requests and may partially succeed; completed work is not rolled back as a batch.
- Standalone sessions and archived-session management remain outside this selection mode. No daemon/core API changes or migrations.
- Existing per-row deletion is unchanged. The merged top-row search is preserved; exact bell alignment from the earlier prototype is superseded by that toolbar layout.
- Design: [English](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/blob/codex/sidebar-session-multiselect/docs/design/sidebar-session-multiselect.md), [简体中文](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/blob/codex/sidebar-session-multiselect/docs/design/sidebar-session-multiselect.zh-CN.md).

prs.title: fix(cli): keep one stream-json message id across block-type transitions
prs.body:
## What this PR does

When a single model response streams thinking and then text, the stream-json adapter splits it into two `assistant` snapshots, because one assistant message may carry only one block type. The second snapshot minted a fresh `message.id` and restarted block numbering at 0, so `--include-partial-messages` emitted one `message_start` (id A), a thinking block at index 0, then a text block at index 0 again with a snapshot carrying id B.

This PR keeps the turn's `message.id` across an intra-turn block-type change: the pending snapshot is still closed (the single-type rule is unchanged), but the continuation reuses the id and carries the block counter forward, so the text block streams at index 1.

## Why it's needed

An SDK consumer that pairs streamed blocks with the final `assistant` snapshot by `message.id` — the natural rule, and the one that works for a plain-text response — sees the text as a *second* message. The reporter's integration library rendered a 22-character answer as 44 characters against a real Model Studio endpoint, and the block index reuse makes `(message.id, index)` ambiguous even for consumers that key on both.

The issue asked for a wire-contract decision. This follows option 1 as described there: one `message.id` per model response, one `message_start`/`message_stop` pair, and the text block at index 1 so the two blocks stay distinguishable inside the single message. That is also how Claude Code's stream-json behaves, which this format follows.

## Reviewer Test Plan

### How to verify

Drive one turn that streams thinking and then text, with partial messages on:

```bash
qwen -p "..." --output-format stream-json --include-partial-messages
```

Before: one `message_start` with id A, `content_block_start` at index 0 twice, and two `assistant` snapshots with ids A and B.
After: one `message_start` with id A, block indexes 0 (thinking) and 1 (text), and both `assistant` snapshots carrying id A.

The two added unit tests pin exactly that: one asserts both snapshots share `message.id`, the other asserts the block indexes are `[0, 1]`. Both fail on `main` and pass with the change.

### Evidence (Before & After)

N/A — non-UI wire-format change. Under the unfixed adapter the two new cases fail with `expected 'id-b' to be 'id-a'` and `expected [0, 0] to deeply equal [0, 1]`; with the change the suite is green.

### Tested on

|     OS     | Status |
| :--------: | :----: |
|  🍏 macOS  |   ✅   |
| 🪟 Windows |   ⚠️   |
|  🐧 Linux  |   ⚠️   |

### Environment (optional)

Unit tests only: `npx vitest run` from `packages/cli`.

## Risk & Scope

- Main risk or tradeoff: consumers that relied on the split ids to tell the thinking snapshot from the text snapshot now get one id. They can still distinguish the snapshots by block type and by the block index range, which is what the issue asked for; the alternative (a second `message_start`/`message_stop` pair) would make a consumer counting messages or usage see two.
- Not validated / out of scope: the subagent path keeps its own per-tool-call message ids; this change only affects intra-turn transitions. `content_block_stop` for the final block is still emitted by `finalizeAssistantMessage`, unchanged.
- Breaking changes / migration notes: none in the schema; the `message.id` stability is a behavioral fix.

## Linked Issues

Fixes #15875

<details>
<summary>中文说明</summary>

## 这个 PR 做了什么

当一个模型响应先流式输出 thinking 再输出 text 时，stream-json 适配器会把它拆成两个 `assistant` 快照，因为一条 assistant 消息只能承载一种 block 类型。第二个快照重新生成了 `message.id`，并把 block 序号从 0 重新开始，于是 `--include-partial-messages` 会发出一个 `message_start`（id A）、一个 index 0 的 thinking 块，然后又是 index 0 的 text 块，且快照携带 id B。

本 PR 让同一轮内的 block 类型切换保留 `message.id`：待发送的快照仍然会被关闭（单类型约束不变），但续接部分复用同一个 id 并延续 block 计数，因此 text 块以 index 1 流式发出。

## 为什么需要

按 `message.id` 把流式块和最终 `assistant` 快照配对，是消费者的自然做法，纯文本响应下也一直成立。现在 text 会被当成第二条消息：提报方的集成库在真实 Model Studio 端点上把 22 字符的答案渲染成了 44 字符；而 block 序号复用也让按 `(message.id, index)` 配对的消费者无法区分两个块。

issue 里说明这需要先定线上契约。本 PR 采用其中描述的方案一：一个模型响应对应一个 `message.id`、一对 `message_start`/`message_stop`，text 块用 index 1，使两个块在同一条消息内仍可区分。这也是本格式所对齐的 Claude Code stream-json 的行为。

## 验证

用一个先 thinking 后 text 的回合，开启 partial messages：

```bash
qwen -p "..." --output-format stream-json --include-partial-messages
```

改动前：一个 id 为 A 的 `message_start`，`content_block_start` 的 index 出现两次 0，两个 `assistant` 快照 id 分别为 A、B。
改动后：一个 id 为 A 的 `message_start`，block index 为 0（thinking）与 1（text），两个快照都是 id A。

新增的两条单测分别钉住这两点：一条断言两个快照共享 `message.id`，另一条断言 block index 为 `[0, 1]`。在 `main` 上均失败，应用改动后通过。

## 风险与范围

- 主要风险：原先依赖 id 区分 thinking 快照与 text 快照的消费者，现在拿到同一个 id。它们仍可通过 block 类型与 block index 区间区分，这正是 issue 要求的；另一种做法（再来一对 `message_start`/`message_stop`）会让按 `message_start` 计消息或用量的消费者看到两条。
- 未覆盖：subagent 路径沿用各自的每次工具调用消息 id，本改动只影响轮内切换；最后一个块的 `content_block_stop` 仍由 `finalizeAssistantMessage` 发出，行为不变。
- 破坏性变更：schema 无变化，`message.id` 的稳定性属于行为修复。

## 关联 issue

Fixes #15875

</details>

prs.title: fix(ci): stop staling branches for eslint ignores they never excluded
prs.body:
## What this PR does

Narrows the lint gate freshness verdict so that a base-side addition to the global ESLint ignore list no longer fails every in-flight branch. The check now asks whether the branch's green is still sufficient under the base's gate, rather than only whether the branch contains the base's latest commit touching that config. Everything outside the ignore array is still compared byte for byte, so a change that also tightens a rule keeps failing, and a base-side removal of an ignore keeps failing too.

The narrowing is a post-filter applied only to an already-failing verdict, so a branch that is fresh today pays exactly the API cost it pays today. Any failure while refining — a fetch error, a missing anchor, an entry line the parser does not recognise, or a negated glob on either side — keeps the original verdict rather than weakening the gate.

## Why it's needed

This step is the second largest source of red in the Lint & Static lane. In a sample of the 60 most recent failed CI runs over an eight-hour window, 30 had a red Lint & Static and 9 of those 30 failed here. Reading the trigger out of all nine logs shows every one of them named the same commit, which added a single built-artifact directory to the global ignore list.

Adding an ignore removes files from lint scope. A branch that has not incorporated it therefore lints a superset of what the base gate would lint, so its green is strictly stronger, not weaker. The check failed it anyway, and because the lane validates the branch head alone, the same commit could never turn green on a rerun — the only remedy was merging main and pushing, which restarts the entire matrix. At the current rate of change to the CI workflow and ESLint config, that treadmill is most of what this step produces.

The correctness argument is an exact set condition rather than a heuristic. Lint scope is the tree minus the ignores, so a branch's certification covers the base's scope precisely when the branch's ignores are a subset of the base's. That direction matters: it passes an addition and rejects a removal.

The argument does have a precondition, found during adversarial review rather than assumed. It requires entries to be purely subtractive, and a negated glob re-includes files. Measured through the real lint entry point on the repository's ESLint 9.29.0, a base carrying a negated entry lints a file that a branch without it never checks, while the branch's list is still a subset of the base's. The check now refuses to narrow whenever either side has a negated entry. No such entry exists in the config today, so this costs nothing on current traffic.

## Reviewer Test Plan

### How to verify

Run the collocated helper suite, which is the same battery CI runs in both the dependency-free and full helper steps:

```
node --test .github/scripts/check-lint-gate-freshness.test.mjs
```

Expect 22 passing. The nine pre-existing cases are unchanged and act as the passing control.

To confirm the behaviour change against real data rather than fixtures, call the exported verdict function with `gh api` behind both injected fetchers for a branch that predates the ignore addition. Seven such branches were probed at their real head commits; all seven previously reported this config as stale and all seven now report it fresh. Note what this does and does not prove: the config verdict flips, but several of those branches are still stale on the CI workflow file because main has moved on since, and that file is deliberately out of scope here. This is not a claim that those PRs would be green today.

The load-bearing claims are each pinned by a mutation. Removing the post-filter, inverting the subset direction, dropping either conjunct, consuming the last ignore block instead of the first, letting the refinement's error propagate, failing open on an extraction miss, skipping unparseable lines, matching quoted literals anywhere in a line, applying the narrowing to every gate file, fetching the wrong file, narrowing verdicts that were already fresh, and dropping the negated-glob guard — thirteen mutations, each reddening a named case while leaving 20–21 of 22 passing.

Two reviewer traps worth knowing. First, `isPathIgnored` is not a usable oracle for the negation question: it reports both the re-including and non-re-including shapes as ignored, and only running actual lint over a file with a real violation exposes the difference. Second, a directory-level exclusion short-circuits before negation can apply, so a counterexample needs file-level globs.

### Evidence (Before & After)

N/A — no user-visible or TUI surface. Behavioural evidence is the suite, the mutation table, and the live probe described above, recorded in the verification comment.

### Tested on

|     OS     | Status |
| :--------: | :----: |
|  🍎 macOS  |   ⚠️    |
| 🪟 Windows |   ⚠️    |
|  🐧 Linux  |   ✅    |

### Environment (optional)

Node v24.22.1 on Linux, repository-local ESLint 9.29.0. Unit suite plus live GitHub API probes; no build or sandbox involved.

## Risk & Scope

- Main risk or tradeoff: **this script is itself a gate-defining file, so merging it will redden every in-flight PR once**, exactly as any other gate change does. Those reds are expected and are not regressions; they clear when each branch next incorporates main. The tradeoff is one round of that churn to remove a recurring source of it.
- Not validated / out of scope: the CI workflow file keeps whole-file granularity. A slice-based approach for it was prototyped and rejected on evidence — for the branches measured, the entire base-to-head delta fell inside the lint-relevant slice, so it would have fixed none of the observed reds. The two config-scoped ignore arrays also stay in the byte-compared remainder. No build or typecheck was run: the change touches two helper scripts and two design documents, no TypeScript package, and the suite above is the battery that covers them. macOS and Windows were not exercised.
- Breaking changes / migration notes: none. The gate file list is unchanged, the step's fail-open policy on API errors is unchanged, and the refinement can only remove a failing verdict, never add one.

Design: [English](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/blob/2f620b7348e7389853271ea0cff62c465d683b75/docs/design/2026-11-09-lint-gate-freshness-ignores-subset.md) · [简体中文](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/blob/2f620b7348e7389853271ea0cff62c465d683b75/docs/design/2026-11-09-lint-gate-freshness-ignores-subset.zh-CN.md)

## Linked Issues

None.

<details>
<summary>中文说明</summary>

## 这个 PR 做了什么

收窄 lint 门禁新鲜度判定，使基线侧往全局 ESLint ignore 列表新增条目不再让所有在途分支失败。检查现在问的是「分支的绿在基线门禁下是否仍然充分」，而不只是「分支是否包含基线触碰该配置的最新提交」。ignore 数组之外的一切仍逐字节比对，因此同时收紧规则的改动继续失败，基线侧**移除**一条 ignore 也继续失败。

这道收窄是只作用于已判失败结论的后置过滤，所以今天本就新鲜的分支付出的 API 开销与今天完全相同。细化过程中的任何失败——取文本出错、锚点缺失、解析器不认识的条目行、或任一侧存在负向 glob——都保留原结论，而不是削弱门禁。

## 为什么需要

这一步是 Lint & Static lane 的第二大红灯来源。在一个八小时窗口内最近 60 个失败 CI run 的样本中，30 个 Lint & Static 变红，其中 9 个失败在这里。逐一读出九份日志的触发源后可以看到，每一次都点名了同一个提交——它只往全局 ignore 列表加了一个构建产物目录。

新增 ignore 会把文件移出 lint 范围。尚未纳入它的分支因此 lint 的是基线门禁范围的超集，它的绿只会更强，不会更弱。但检查仍判它失败；又因为该 lane 只验证分支 head，同一个 commit 重跑永远不可能转绿——唯一补救是合入 main 再推送，而这会重启整个矩阵。按当前 CI workflow 与 ESLint 配置的变更频率，这个跑步机就是这一步产出的主要内容。

正确性论证是精确的集合条件，而非启发式。Lint 范围是树减去 ignores，因此分支的认证覆盖基线范围，当且仅当分支的 ignores 是基线的子集。方向很关键：它放行新增、拒绝移除。

这个论证确实有一个前提，是在对抗审计中发现而非假定的。它要求条目是纯排除性的，而负向 glob 会把文件重新纳入。在本仓库的 ESLint 9.29.0 上通过真实 lint 入口实测：带负向条目的基线会 lint 一个不含该条目的分支根本不检查的文件，而分支的列表仍是基线的子集。现在只要任一侧有负向条目，检查就拒绝收窄。今天配置里没有这类条目，因此对当前流量零成本。

## 评审验证计划

### 如何验证

运行同目录 helper 套件，它与 CI 的免依赖和完整两个 helper 步骤跑的是同一份：

```
node --test .github/scripts/check-lint-gate-freshness.test.mjs
```

预期 22 条通过。原有九条未改动，作为成功路径对照。

要用真实数据而非夹具确认行为变化，可在两个注入的 fetcher 后面接上 `gh api`，对早于该 ignore 新增的分支调用导出的判定函数。已对七个这类分支按其真实 head 提交做过探针；七个此前都把该配置报为过期，现在七个全部报为新鲜。请注意这证明什么、不证明什么：该配置的判定翻转了，但其中若干分支仍因 CI workflow 文件而过期（main 此后又前进了），而该文件在本次是刻意排除的范围。这不是「那些 PR 今天会绿」的断言。

每条承重论断都由一个变异钉住：移除后置过滤、反转子集方向、去掉任一合取项、消费最后一个而非第一个 ignore 块、让细化错误上抛、抽取落空时 fail open、跳过无法解析的行、在整行任意位置匹配引号字面量、把收窄应用到每个门禁文件、取错文件、对本已新鲜的结论也做收窄、以及移除负向 glob 守卫——十三个变异，每个都让一条点名用例变红，同时保留 22 条中的 20–21 条通过。

有两个评审陷阱值得知道。其一，`isPathIgnored` 不是负向问题的可用 oracle：它把重新纳入与不重新纳入两种形状都报为 ignored，只有对含真实违规的文件跑实际 lint 才能暴露差异。其二，目录级排除会在负向生效之前短路，因此反例需要文件级 glob。

### 证据（Before & After）

N/A —— 无用户可见或 TUI surface。行为证据是上述套件、变异表与实况探针，记录在验证评论中。

### 测试环境

|     OS     | 状态 |
| :--------: | :--: |
|  🍎 macOS  |  ⚠️   |
| 🪟 Windows |  ⚠️   |
|  🐧 Linux  |  ✅   |

### 环境（可选）

Linux 上的 Node v24.22.1，仓库本地 ESLint 9.29.0。单元套件加真实 GitHub API 探针；不涉及构建或沙箱。

## 风险与范围

- 主要风险或权衡：**这个脚本本身就是门禁定义文件，因此合入它会让所有在途 PR 红一次**，与任何其他门禁改动一样。这些红是预期的，不是回归；各分支下次纳入 main 后即消除。权衡是用一轮这样的 churn 换掉一个反复产生它的源头。
- 未验证 / 范围外：CI workflow 文件保持整文件粒度。针对它的切片方案做过原型并被证据否决——在实测分支上，base 到 head 的全部差值都落在 lint 相关切片内，因此对观测到的红修复率为零。两个 config 作用域的 ignore 数组也留在逐字节比对的 remainder 中。未跑 build 或 typecheck：改动只涉及两个 helper 脚本与两份设计文档，没有 TypeScript 包，覆盖它们的正是上述套件。macOS 与 Windows 未验证。
- 破坏性变更 / 迁移说明：无。门禁文件清单不变，该步骤在 API 错误上的 fail-open 策略不变，且这道细化只可能移除失败结论，绝不会新增。

设计文档：[English](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/blob/2f620b7348e7389853271ea0cff62c465d683b75/docs/design/2026-11-09-lint-gate-freshness-ignores-subset.md) · [简体中文](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/blob/2f620b7348e7389853271ea0cff62c465d683b75/docs/design/2026-11-09-lint-gate-freshness-ignores-subset.zh-CN.md)

## 关联 Issue

无。

</details>

prs.title: test(cli): derive the upload cleanup budget from the lane test timeout
prs.body:
## What this PR does

Derives the managed-workspace upload test's cleanup-marker budget from the lane's own per-test timeout instead of a flat thirty-second constant, so a runner with a fifteen-second ceiling still reports the test's descriptive error rather than being interrupted by a bare vitest timeout.

This implements the non-blocking reuse note left on #16699. That PR merged before the refinement was pushed, so the improvement is carried here rather than amended into a merged diff.

## Why it's needed

#16699 replaced a fixed hundred-iteration poll with a thirty-second wall-clock deadline and disclosed the tradeoff: on a non-ECS lane the per-test ceiling is fifteen seconds, so a genuinely hung child would surface as `Test timed out in 15000ms` instead of `Original upload did not reach cleanup.` The review suggested deriving the deadline from the lane's settle budget so the descriptive error survives on both lane shapes. The helper for exactly this already exists and is already used elsewhere in the package, so this is reuse rather than new machinery.

## Reviewer Test Plan

### How to verify

Run `npx vitest run src/serve/managed-workspace-upload.process.test.ts --coverage.enabled=false --retry=0` from `packages/cli`; expect 5/5. The poll condition, the 25ms interval and the error message are unchanged — only the source of the budget differs.

To confirm the property the note asked for, remove the child's marker write from the generated `paused.mjs` in the live-writer case so the child parks forever at the hooked `unlink` and the marker can never appear. On a fifteen-second lane the case should fail with `Original upload did not reach cleanup.` roughly a second before the runner ceiling, not with `Test timed out in 15000ms`. Observed: failure at **14029ms** with the descriptive error. Restore the line afterwards.

### Evidence (Before & After)

N/A — non-UI, test-only change. Before: a hung child on a fifteen-second lane reports a bare vitest timeout. After: it reports `Original upload did not reach cleanup.` at 14029ms, inside the ceiling.

### Tested on

|     OS     | Status |
| :--------: | :----: |
|  🍏 macOS  |   ⚠️   |
| 🪟 Windows |   ⚠️   |
|  🐧 Linux  |   ✅   |

### Environment (optional)

Local Linux, Node 24, Vitest 3.2.7, retries disabled, on current `main` (`30e71d37e6`). Prettier and ESLint clean; pre-commit passed; suite green 5/5 after the cherry-pick onto this base.

## Risk & Scope

- Main risk or tradeoff: the effective budget becomes lane-dependent — thirty seconds on the sixty-second ECS pool, about fourteen seconds on a fifteen-second lane. That is the intent: the assertion gets to report before the runner interrupts. A healthy-but-slow child still gets far more than the original ~2.5s.
- Not validated / out of scope: the natural CI flake (#16580) was not reproduced locally; the hang witness is a constructed permanent park, not the CI shard's real load. macOS and Windows were not exercised. The sibling `releaseMount` wait in `hosted-user-question.test.ts` is untouched — the verification round on #16699 measured that its fifteen-second budget already surfaces its own assertion on both lane shapes, so no change is warranted there.
- Breaking changes / migration notes: none. Test-only; no production code, public API, or configuration changes.

## Linked Issues

References #16580 (the flake #16699 already fixed; this refines its budget source)
References #16699 (implements its non-blocking review note)

### 测试平台

|     OS     | 状态 |
| :--------: | :--: |
|  🍏 macOS  |  ⚠️  |
| 🪟 Windows |  ⚠️  |

### 环境（可选）

本地 Linux、Node 24、Vitest 3.2.7，关闭重试，基于当前 `main`（`30e71d37e6`）。Prettier 与 ESLint 干净，pre-commit 通过；cherry-pick 到本 base 后套件绿 5/5。

## 风险与范围

- 主要风险或取舍：有效预算变为依赖车道——60 秒的 ECS 池上为 30 秒，15 秒车道上约 14 秒。这正是意图：让断言先于 runner 打断而报告。健康但慢的子进程仍获得远多于原先约 2.5s 的时间。
- 未验证 / 不在范围内：自然 CI flake（#16580）未在本机复现；挂住见证是构造出的永久停住，不是 CI 分片的真实负载。macOS 与 Windows 未验证。`hosted-user-question.test.ts` 中兄弟的 `releaseMount` 等待未改动——#16699 的验证轮已实测其 15 秒预算在两种车道形状下都会抛出自身断言，因此那里不需要改。
- 破坏性变更 / 迁移说明：无。仅测试；没有生产代码、公共 API 或配置改动。

## 关联 Issue

References #16580（#16699 已修复的 flake；本 PR 细化其预算来源）

prs.title: fix(cli): keep the virtualized transcript visible at a zero host height
prs.body:
## What this PR does

The virtualized (VP) transcript now stays visible when the terminal reports a viewport height of zero. A zero height from the host is treated as "not measured yet" and the list falls back to its own measured box height instead of rendering an empty viewport. The host's height only constrains the root box when it is positive, so the existing shrink-to-content behaviour for short transcripts is unchanged.

## Why it's needed

In VP mode the viewport height is derived from the terminal, so it can legitimately be zero for a frame — a small terminal, a resize still settling, or the controls region temporarily taller than the terminal. The list kept that zero and its readiness guard then returned an empty item list, blanking the entire conversation. The reporter of #5142 saw exactly this: history invisible until an unrelated keystroke forced a layout recalculation, after which it appeared again. Treating a non-positive height as unmeasured keeps the transcript on screen while the measurement settles.

## Reviewer Test Plan

### How to verify

Unit-level reproduction: render the list inside a fixed-height box and pass `containerHeight={0}` from the host (the value `MainContent` produces from `Math.max(0, terminalHeight - controlsHeight - tabBarHeight)`). Before this change the frame contains no item text at all; after it, the items render using the measured height.

```console
$ cd packages/cli
$ npx vitest run src/ui/components/shared/VirtualizedList.test.tsx
 ✓ src/ui/components/shared/VirtualizedList.test.tsx (34 tests) 2184ms
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  34 passed (34)
```

The regression test (`falls back to the measured height when the host passes 0`) fails on unmodified `main` and passes with the change; the other 33 tests in the file are unchanged.

Adjacent suites for the same call path:

```console
$ npx vitest run src/ui/components/MainContent.test.tsx src/ui/components/MainContent.show-more-lines.test.tsx
 Test Files  2 passed (2)
      Tests  41 passed (41)
```

### Evidence (Before & After)

Test output before the source change (the added regression test only):

```console
 ❯ src/ui/components/shared/VirtualizedList.test.tsx:1433:31
     expect(lastFrame() ?? '').toMatch(/item-0/);
 Test Files  1 failed (1)
      Tests  1 failed | 33 skipped (34)
```

After the change, the same file is 34/34 green (output in "How to verify" above). No terminal screenshot: the repro is a zero-height frame, which cannot be produced reliably on a normal terminal without shrinking it to a couple of rows, so this is covered by the unit test rather than a tmux recording.

### Tested on

|     OS     | Status |
| :--------: | :----: |
|  🍏 macOS  |   ✅   |
| 🪟 Windows |   ⚠️   |
|  🐧 Linux  |   ⚠️   |

### Environment (optional)

Unit tests only, run from a fresh worktree. `packages/cli` unit tests need the workspace `dist/` outputs, so the run used `npm run generate` plus a temporary vitest config that stubs the repo-wide global setup (not committed).

## Risk & Scope

- Main risk or tradeoff: a host that intentionally passes 0 to collapse the list would no longer be honoured; no caller does that today — the only producer is `MainContent`, where 0 means "no room measured".
- Not validated / out of scope: not verified on a real tiny terminal or a real resize race; the fix is covered by unit tests only, and Windows/Linux were not exercised locally.
- Breaking changes / migration notes: none.

Fixes #5142

prs.title: fix(ci): sweep multi-identity orphan piles instead of stalling the slot
prs.body:
## What this PR does

Lets the disposable runner pool recover from a pile of orphaned containers that carry several different identities, instead of stalling the slot forever, and lands the host-only hotfix that has been running on hz4 with its tests.

Label-based orphan recovery previously required exactly one identity per slot. When the leftovers disagree, the manager now treats the whole pile as orphaned, deletes the resources, and then sweeps the slot's own registrations by name so nothing is left to block the replacement.

The sweep is deliberately narrow. It only runs when every leftover resource carries this slot's identity prefix, and it only deletes registrations GitHub already reports offline — an online registration may belong to a live runner outside this host's view. A foreign or missing label still blocks the slot for manual reconciliation, and a rejected deletion keeps everything in place for the next cycle, preserving the error status for the rate-limit backoff ladder.

## Why it's needed

This is the follow-up to #16597. That change made cleanup recover a lost identity from resource labels, but it refused to act when a slot's leftovers carried more than one identity. Later the same day on hz4, a wedged Docker left several never-started containers with different identities on the same slot after network address-pool exhaustion. The single-identity rule turned that into a new stall: 15 of 30 slots each repeated the same refusal 960 times.

The reasoning that makes the sweep safe is structural: cycles are serial per slot, so when no slot state exists, no cycle of this manager is live for that slot, and every leftover resource in it is an orphan. There is no live runner of this pool for the pile to belong to. The remaining risk — another pool sharing the host, or a runner this host cannot see — is covered by the identity-prefix requirement and the offline-only rule.

The fix has been running as a host-only hotfix on hz4 since 2026-11-08 21:14 and the pool recovered under it. This PR lands that exact logic on top of the current main (keeping the unique-name suffixes, rate-limit backoff, and time-based stall alerts that landed after the hotfix was written), so the repository and the deployed host stop drifting.

## Reviewer Test Plan

### How to verify

Confirm that a slot holding two never-started containers with different identities of the same slot recovers in one cycle: both containers are removed, the slot's offline registration is deleted by name, and a replacement runner is registered.

Then confirm the three guards, which matter more than the happy path: an online registration matching the slot's name is never deleted; a pile containing a foreign or missing identity label deletes no registrations and keeps the slot blocked across retries; and a deletion GitHub rejects leaves the slot unreplenished until a later attempt succeeds.

On a deployed host, the observable outcome is that a multi-container pile no longer produces an endless `manual reconciliation required` loop — the journal shows one `sweeping orphaned resources without a recorded identity` line followed by `cleaned` and a new runner.

### Evidence (Before & After)

Before, from hz4 during the incident — 15 of 30 slots repeating this every retry (960 identical retries per slot):

```
slot 7: Container labels disagree about the runner identity; manual reconciliation required; retrying without replenishing
```

After: the same logic has been running on hz4 as a host hotfix since 21:14 on 2026-11-08; the pool recovered and has been replenishing normally since. This PR's port onto current main is covered by unit tests only and has not been redeployed.

### Tested on

|     OS     | Status |
| :--------: | :----: |
|  🍏 macOS  |   ⚠️   |
| 🪟 Windows |  N/A   |
|  🐧 Linux  |   ⚠️   |

## Risk & Scope

- Main risk or tradeoff: cleanup now deletes resources and registrations in a case where it previously refused. The blast radius is bounded on three axes: only slots with no state file (hence no live cycle), only resources whose labels all carry this slot's identity prefix, and only registrations GitHub reports offline. The existing single-identity recovery path is unchanged, and the ambiguity guards on that path still apply.
- Not validated / out of scope: no local tests, builds or lint were run, at the author's request; correctness rests on the added unit tests running in CI. The port onto current main has not been redeployed to hz4 — the host keeps running the equivalent hotfix until this lands. The underlying Docker wedge that produces the piles is not addressed here.
- Breaking changes / migration notes: none. Deploying this over a host running the hotfix is a no-op behaviorally; the archive of the hotfix binary on the host can be retired after deployment.

Design documentation updated in both languages: [English](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/blob/main/docs/design/2026-11-07-ephemeral-container-runners.md) and [简体中文](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/blob/main/docs/design/2026-11-07-ephemeral-container-runners.zh-CN.md).

## Linked Issues

Follow-up to #16597. References #16514 for the remaining dedicated-host limitations.

<details>
<summary>中文说明</summary>

## 这个 PR 做了什么

让一次性 runner 池能从「同一槽位堆着多个不同身份的孤儿容器」中恢复，而不是永久卡死，并把已在 hz4 上运行的主机侧热修连同测试一起落库。

基于标签的孤儿恢复此前要求每个槽位恰好一个身份。当遗留资源的身份不一致时，管理程序现在把整堆视为孤儿，删除资源，然后按名字清扫本槽位自己的注册，不留任何会阻塞补位的东西。

清扫是刻意收窄的：只有当每个遗留资源都带有本槽位的身份前缀时才执行，且只删除 GitHub 已报告 offline 的注册——online 注册可能属于本主机视野之外的存活 runner。标签属于外部或缺失时仍然阻塞槽位等待人工对账；删除被拒绝时一切保持原样交给下一轮重试，并保留错误状态码供限流退避使用。

## 为什么需要

这是 #16597 的后续。那次改动让 cleanup 能从资源标签恢复丢失的身份，但当槽位遗留资源带多个身份时仍拒绝处理。同一天稍晚，hz4 上 Docker 卡死、网络地址池耗尽后，在同一槽位堆下多个身份不同、从未启动的容器。「单一身份」规则把这变成了新的卡死：30 个槽位中的 15 个各重复同一道拒绝 960 次。

清扫安全性的依据是结构性的：每个槽位的周期是串行的，所以当槽位状态文件不存在时，本管理程序没有该槽位的活跃周期，槽位内所有遗留资源都是孤儿，不可能属于本池的存活 runner。剩余风险——共享主机的其他池、或本主机看不到的 runner——由身份前缀要求和仅 offline 规则覆盖。

该修复自 2026-11-08 21:14 起以主机侧热修形式在 hz4 运行，池子在其下恢复。本 PR 把这段逻辑原样移植到当前 main 之上（保留热修编写之后落库的唯一名后缀、限流退避和时间制滞留告警），让仓库与部署主机不再漂移。

## 评审验证计划

### 如何验证

确认一个堆着两个身份不同、从未启动容器的槽位能在一个周期内恢复：两个容器都被删除、本槽位的 offline 注册被按名删除、并注册了新的 runner。

然后确认三道守护，它们比主路径更重要：匹配本槽位名字的 online 注册永远不删；堆里含外部或缺失身份标签时不删任何注册、且槽位跨重试保持阻塞；GitHub 拒绝删除时槽位不补位，直到后续尝试成功。

在已部署主机上，可观察的结果是多容器堆不再产生无尽的 `manual reconciliation required` 循环——journal 里出现一条 `sweeping orphaned resources without a recorded identity`，随后是 `cleaned` 和新 runner。

### 证据（前后对比）

事故期间 hz4 上，30 个槽位中的 15 个每次重试都在重复这一行（每槽 960 次相同重试）：

```
slot 7: Container labels disagree about the runner identity; manual reconciliation required; retrying without replenishing
```

修复后：同一逻辑自 2026-11-08 21:14 起以主机热修形式在 hz4 运行，池子已恢复并正常补位至今。本 PR 移植到当前 main 的版本仅由单元测试覆盖，尚未重新部署。

### 测试环境

macOS ⚠️ 未测试 · Windows N/A · Linux ⚠️ 未测试

## 风险与范围

- 主要风险与取舍：cleanup 现在会在此前拒绝的场景删除资源和注册。影响范围被三个维度限定：仅限没有状态文件（因而没有活跃周期）的槽位、仅限标签全部带有本槽位身份前缀的资源、仅限 GitHub 报告 offline 的注册。既有单身份恢复路径不变，该路径上的歧义守护依然生效。
- 未验证 / 超出范围：按作者要求未运行任何本地测试、构建或 lint，正确性依赖新增单元测试在 CI 中运行。移植到当前 main 的版本尚未重新部署到 hz4——落库前主机继续运行等价热修。产生孤儿堆的 Docker 卡死本身不在本次范围内。
- 破坏性变更 / 迁移说明：无。在运行热修的主机上部署本版本行为上是无操作；部署后主机上的热修存档即可退役。

设计文档已同步更新中英文版本：[English](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/blob/main/docs/design/2026-11-07-ephemeral-container-runners.md) 与 [简体中文](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/blob/main/docs/design/2026-11-07-ephemeral-container-runners.zh-CN.md)。

## 关联 Issue

#16597 的后续。引用 #16514 跟踪剩余的专用主机限制。

prs.title: fix(cli): never terminally release a config-scoped Hook owner on a detach
prs.body:
## What this PR does

A detach must never terminally release a config-scoped Hook owner. Both held-Runtime drains — the lifecycle-v1 close and the lifecycle-v2 resource settlement — now leave such an owner alone unless the close is terminal, and they decide by which owners the Session actually holds rather than by what the id looks like. A deliberate skip is recorded as an unproven stop, so the observation loops settle on the recovery line instead of certifying a stop that was never issued. One shared builder now produces every owner id, beside the predicate that recognises it.

## Why it's needed

#16116 landed with this defect still in it. The fix was written and verified there, but the PR was squash-merged at an earlier head, so the commit never reached `main` — this PR carries it.

The held-Runtime restore is gated on the resident's lifecycle protocol version, but that field only arrives through the lifecycle-carrying spread. A bare attach carries no lifecycle authority, so the field stays undefined, the gate passes, and the restore runs. The settlement route later writes the field unconditionally, so the same Session closes under v2 and drains whatever the restore seeded — including the deterministic owner an active extension bundle names. That release is terminal and persists a released row under the id the next load recomputes; acquisition refuses any non-acquiring row, so every Hook on that Session is refused after the reload.

Re-pointing the gate would not fix it. A load cannot know which protocol will later close the Session — the same resident can settle through either — so any restore-time gate on the closing protocol is predicting the future. The invariant belongs at the release, where it is decidable. The v1 drain has the same exposure and it predates #16116, so the guard covers both.

Two further defects in the first version of that guard are fixed here as well. The exemption keyed on the id's prefix, but a channel input id is chosen by the caller and constrained only by length, so an ordinary turn could carry that prefix and then never be drained for the rest of its life; the exemption now keys on owners the Harness constructed, which client input cannot reach. And the skip left the drain recorded as proven, so the close certified a confirmed stop for a Runtime it had deliberately left running.

## Reviewer Test Plan

### How to verify

Load an extensions Session that has a durable hold row, without a lifecycle authority, then close it through the lifecycle-v2 path as a close. Before this change the deterministic owner reaches a terminal release; after it, the owner is skipped and the ordinary held id in the same set still drains. A delete on the same Session must still release terminally, and the legacy detach and delete routes must behave the same way as their v2 counterparts.

The coverage is one case run over four arms — v2 close, v2 delete, legacy detach, legacy delete — on a Session whose extension bundle really constructs the owner. Three ids ride the restore: the owner, an ordinary turn, and a caller-chosen id that merely shares the owner's prefix. The ordinary id and the lookalike must drain on every arm; the owner only on the terminal ones. Each arm also asserts the response status and the settle argument handed to the observation loop: the recovery line on the two non-terminal arms, the confirmed-stop line on the two terminal ones. A companion case pins the other direction — a Session with no extension bundle must drain a prefix-shaped id, because it owns nothing to exempt.

Six mutations were run against the committed suite, each restored byte-for-byte afterwards. Removing the unproven-stop marker in the v2 skip fails only the v2 close arm; removing it in the legacy skip fails only the legacy detach arm. Reverting the exemption to the prefix predicate fails the no-owner case and both non-terminal arms. Making the skip unconditional fails both delete arms; making it never fire fails both non-terminal arms. Making the predicate stop recognising builder output fails both non-terminal arms and the builder pin.

Local results on the merged `main` base: full repository build rc 0 with zero type errors, and a package-scoped type build rc 0 after the final edit; the harness suite 723/723 run alone; the Hook and MCP suites 209/209; Prettier clean. The harness suite is the whole file rather than a filter, because both drains changed and every close path is therefore in scope.

### Evidence (Before & After)

N/A

### Tested on

|     OS     | Status |
| :--------: | :----: |
|  🍏 macOS  |   ✅   |
| 🪟 Windows |   ⚠️   |
|  🐧 Linux  |   ⚠️   |

### Environment (optional)

Unit suites only, run from the package directory against the merged `main` base.

## Risk & Scope

- Main risk or tradeoff: a detach now leaves the owner's Runtime running and its obligation owed, so the mount handback still refuses busy and the detach parks on a named recovery-required answer rather than completing. That is the honest outcome — the alternative is the tombstone — and it is the availability half this PR deliberately does not solve. The settlement record now says the stop is unproven, which is a visible change to what a later rebuild is told.
- Not validated / out of scope: stopping the background run without tombstoning the owner needs a keep-READY drain that does not exist on the TypeScript broker today; that is #16579. Windows and Linux were not run locally. The CLI integration suite did not run here. No admission-time restriction was added to the caller-chosen input id space — keying on ownership already makes a prefix collision harmless, and narrowing a client-visible id space is a wider contract change than this fix needs.
- Breaking changes / migration notes: none. The owner id builder is a pure extraction — same prefix, same hashed tuple, same digest — so persisted Broker keys are unchanged.

## Linked Issues

References #16116 — this carries the fix that its squash merge stranded.

References #16579 — this PR does **not** close it. #16579 tracks the availability half (a keep-READY drain so the detach can converge); this PR removes the data-loss half.

<details>
<summary>中文说明</summary>

## 这个 PR 做了什么

detach 绝不能终态释放配置作用域的 Hook owner。两处 held-Runtime 排空——lifecycle-v1 关闭与 lifecycle-v2 资源结算——现在都只在本次关闭为终态时才动这类 owner，且判定依据是「这个 Session 实际持有哪些 owner」，而不是「id 长什么样」。刻意跳过会被记为「stop 未经证明」，于是观察 loop 落在恢复线上，而不是为一次从未发出的 stop 作确认。所有 owner id 现在由同一个构造器产出，与识别它的谓词并列。

## 为什么需要

#16116 合并时这个缺陷仍在里面。修复在那边写好并验证过，但 PR 是在更早的 head 上 squash 合并的，那个提交从未进入 `main`——本 PR 承载它。

held-Runtime 的恢复以 resident 的 lifecycle 协议版本为门，但该字段只通过携带 lifecycle 的展开挂载。裸 attach 不带 lifecycle authority，字段保持 undefined，门成立，恢复照跑。结算路由随后无条件写入该字段，于是同一 Session 以 v2 关闭并排空恢复塞进去的一切——包括 active extension bundle 命名的确定性 owner。该释放是终态的，会在下次加载重算的那个 id 下写入 released 行；而 acquire 拒绝任何非 acquiring 行，于是重载后该 Session 的每个 Hook 都被拒。

把门改指向别处并不能修好它。加载无法预知该 Session 之后按哪个协议关闭——同一个 resident 两条路都可能走——所以任何在恢复时按「关闭协议」设的门都是在预测未来。不变量属于释放点，那里才是可判定的。v1 排空有同样的暴露且早于 #16116，因此守卫覆盖两处。

该守卫第一版另有两处缺陷，本轮一并修掉。豁免原先键于 id 前缀，但频道 input id 由调用方选择、只受长度约束，于是一个普通 turn 可以带上该前缀并从此永不被排空；现在豁免键于 Harness 构造的 owner，客户端输入够不到。另外，跳过原先让排空仍被记为已证明，于是关闭为一个被刻意留活的 Runtime 作了「已确认停止」的确认。

## 评审者测试计划

### 如何验证

不带 lifecycle authority 加载一个有持久 hold 行的 extensions Session，然后经 lifecycle-v2 路径以 close 关闭它。改动前确定性 owner 会走到终态释放；改动后 owner 被跳过，同一集合里的普通 held id 仍被排空。同一 Session 的 delete 必须仍然终态释放，legacy 的 detach 与 delete 路由必须与其 v2 对应臂表现一致。

覆盖是一个用例跑四臂——v2 close、v2 delete、legacy detach、legacy delete——所在 Session 的 extension bundle 会真实构造该 owner。恢复携带三个 id：owner、普通 turn、以及调用方自选的、仅前缀相同的 id。普通 id 与形似 id 在每一臂都必须排空；owner 只在终态臂排空。每臂还断言响应状态与交给观察 loop 的 settle 参数：两条非终态臂为恢复线，两条终态臂为确认停止线。另有一个反向用例：没有 extension bundle 的 Session 必须排空前缀形 id，因为它根本不持有可豁免之物。

对已提交套件跑了六个变异，每次之后逐字节还原。删掉 v2 skip 里的「未证明」标志只让 v2 close 臂红；删掉 legacy skip 里的只让 legacy detach 臂红。把豁免改回前缀谓词会让无主用例与两条非终态臂红。把 skip 改成无条件会让两条 delete 臂红；改成永不触发会让两条非终态臂红。让谓词不再认得构造器产物，会让两条非终态臂与构造器钉子红。

在已合并的 `main` 基线上的本地结果：全仓构建 rc 0、零类型错，最后一次编辑后再跑包级类型构建 rc 0；harness 套件单独全量 723/723；Hook 与 MCP 套件 209/209；Prettier 干净。harness 跑的是整个文件而非过滤子集，因为两处 drain 都改了，每条关闭路径都在范围内。

### 证据（前后对比）

N/A

### 测试平台

macOS 已测；Windows 与 Linux 未在本地跑。

### 环境（可选）

仅单元测试，在包目录内、针对已合并的 `main` 基线运行。

## 风险与范围

- 主要风险或取舍：detach 现在会让 owner 的 Runtime 继续运行、义务继续挂账，因此 mount 交还仍拒 busy，detach 落在具名的 recovery-required 上而非完成。这是诚实的结果——另一条路就是墓碑——也正是本 PR 有意不解决的可用性那一半。结算记录现在声明 stop 未经证明，这改变了后续 rebuild 被告知的内容，是可见的变化。
- 未验证 / 不在范围内：要在不墓碑化 owner 的前提下停掉后台 run，需要 TypeScript broker 上今天尚不存在的 keep-READY drain，即 #16579。Windows 与 Linux 未在本地运行。CLI 集成套件本轮未跑。没有对调用方自选的 input id 空间加准入期限制——按归属判定已让前缀碰撞无害，而收缩客户端可见 id 空间是比本修复所需更大的契约改动。
- 破坏性变更 / 迁移说明：无。owner id 构造器是纯抽取——同前缀、同哈希元组、同摘要——持久化的 Broker key 不变。

## 关联 Issue

引用 #16116——本 PR 承载其 squash 合并所落下的修复。

引用 #16579——本 PR **不**关闭它。#16579 跟踪可用性那一半（keep-READY drain，让 detach 能够收敛）；本 PR 移除的是数据丢失那一半。

</details>
