prs.title: feat(managed-agent): persist Session execution diagnostics
prs.body:
## What this PR does

Persists execution diagnostics for Managed Sessions: per-invocation tool outcomes, explicit file operations from the built-in read, write and edit tools, loaded Skill instructions, and an expandable child-invocation view. Activity statistics and paged activity lists are exposed through a Public GET and a WebShell query each, and WebShell's Session diagnostics dialog gains the Activity tab plus an invocation tree in Child agents.

Each invocation keeps requested, admitted, executed, captured and delivered states separate, so a refused, cancelled or partially delivered call is never shown as a success. Evidence is written alongside the existing message, intent and receipt commits and projected into the existing Session record table atomically with them, raising the stored reader floor to storage 4. Arbitrary Shell or MCP filesystem effects and Skill-to-action causality are not inferred.

This is the third of three stacked PRs split out of #16475 and carries the content previously reviewed as #16499. It also consolidates the hosted tool-turn bookkeeping: policy refusals go through one helper, invocation overrides merge through one method, per-batch diagnostic state resets in one place, and diagnostic file paths use the same rule as the evidence parser.

## Why it's needed

Managed Sessions need durable answers about which calls failed or were refused, which files explicit tools read or changed, and whether a Skill was loaded, all readable after the Runtime stops.

## Reviewer Test Plan

### How to verify

1. Run a Managed Session with an explicit file read and edit, a Skill load and a direct child call. The Activity tab lists each invocation with its own admission, execution and delivery state, and the file and Skill views list only those explicit operations.
2. Trigger a policy refusal, an argument error, a cancellation and a truncated result. Refused and invalid calls are not started, cancelled calls are not counted as executed, and truncated output is shown as partial delivery.
3. Expand child invocations and page them. Restricted children do not leak data, and the tree does not claim whole-subtree totals.
4. Commit a verified external tool outcome above 64 KiB, replay it and rebuild the derived records. The business receipt stays valid and diagnostics report partial coverage without reading object storage under the Session fence.
5. Stop the Runtime and read the activity views. They load without starting a Runtime or Harness.

### Evidence (Before & After)

Fixture-backed renders: [desktop tool activity](docs/assets/managed-execution-diagnostics/activity-tools-desktop.png) and the [390px invocation view](docs/assets/managed-execution-diagnostics/activity-child-mobile.png).

### Tested on

|     OS     | Status |
| :--------: | :----: |
|  🍏 macOS  |   ✅    |
| 🪟 Windows |   ⚠️    |
|  🐧 Linux  |   ⚠️    |

### Environment (optional)

Local focused unit tests only; Java, MySQL, Hosted and browser suites run in CI.

## Risk & Scope

- Main risk or tradeoff: evidence rides on existing journal commits, so its byte budget is bounded and overflow is reported as omitted observations.
- Not validated / out of scope: arbitrary Shell/MCP filesystem auditing, Skill-to-action attribution, multi-level child execution.
- Breaking changes / migration notes: the first execution evidence write raises the Session's reader floor to storage 4.

Design: [English](docs/design/2026-11-07-managed-session-execution-diagnostics.md) | [简体中文](docs/design/2026-11-07-managed-session-execution-diagnostics.zh-CN.md)

## Linked Issues

Split from #16475 (includes #16499). Stacked on #16641.

<details>
<summary>中文说明</summary>

## 这个 PR 做了什么

为 Managed Session 持久化执行诊断：每次调用的工具结果、内置读/写/编辑工具的显式文件操作、已加载的 Skill 指令，以及可展开的子调用视图。活动统计和分页活动列表分别提供 Public GET 和 WebShell 查询接口；WebShell 的 Session 诊断对话框新增“活动”页，并在“子 Agent”页中加入调用树。

每次调用分别记录请求、准入、执行、捕获和交付状态，因此被拒绝、被取消或只交付了一部分的调用不会被显示为成功。证据随现有的消息、意图和回执提交一起写入，并与它们原子地投影到现有的 Session 记录表中，同时把存储的读取方下限提升到 storage 4。不会推断任意 Shell 或 MCP 的文件系统影响，也不会推断 Skill 与后续动作之间的因果关系。

这是从 #16475 拆出的三个叠加 PR 中的第三个，包含此前作为 #16499 评审过的内容。它还收拢了 hosted tool-turn 的诊断记账：策略拒绝统一走一个 helper，调用覆盖信息统一通过一个方法合并，每批次的诊断状态在一个地方重置，诊断文件路径使用与证据解析器相同的规则。

## 为什么需要

Managed Session 需要在 Runtime 停止后，仍能可靠地回答哪些调用失败或被拒绝、显式工具读取或修改了哪些文件、某个 Skill 是否被加载。

## 评审测试计划

### 如何验证

1. 运行一个包含显式文件读取和编辑、一次 Skill 加载和一次直接子调用的 Managed Session。“活动”页列出每次调用及其各自的准入、执行和交付状态；文件和 Skill 视图只列出这些显式操作。
2. 触发一次策略拒绝、一次参数错误、一次取消和一次被截断的结果。被拒绝和参数无效的调用不会启动；被取消的调用不计为已执行；被截断的输出显示为部分交付。
3. 展开子调用并翻页。受限的子 Session 不泄露数据，调用树不声称整棵子树的总量。
4. 提交一个超过 64 KiB 的已验证外部工具结果，回放并重建派生记录。业务回执仍然有效，诊断报告部分覆盖，并且不会在 Session fence 下读取对象存储。
5. 停止 Runtime 后读取活动视图。它们仍能加载，并且不会启动 Runtime 或 Harness。

### 证据（前后对比）

基于 fixture 的渲染结果：[桌面端工具活动](docs/assets/managed-execution-diagnostics/activity-tools-desktop.png) 和 [390px 调用视图](docs/assets/managed-execution-diagnostics/activity-child-mobile.png)。

### 测试平台

|     OS     | 状态 |
| :--------: | :--: |
|  🍏 macOS  |  ✅  |
| 🪟 Windows |  ⚠️  |
|  🐧 Linux  |  ⚠️  |

### 环境（可选）

本地只运行了相关单元测试；Java、MySQL、Hosted 和浏览器测试在 CI 中运行。

## 风险与范围

- 主要风险或取舍：证据附着在现有的 journal 提交上，因此字节预算有上限，超出部分报告为省略的观测。
- 未验证 / 不在范围内：任意 Shell/MCP 文件系统审计、Skill 到动作的归因、多层子 Agent 执行。
- 破坏性变更 / 迁移说明：第一次写入执行证据会把该 Session 的读取方下限提升到 storage 4。

设计文档：[English](docs/design/2026-11-07-managed-session-execution-diagnostics.md) | [简体中文](docs/design/2026-11-07-managed-session-execution-diagnostics.zh-CN.md)

## 关联 Issue

从 #16475 拆分（包含 #16499）。叠加在 #16641 之上。

</details>

prs.title: fix(ci): add bounded, idempotent retry to the SDK release branch push
prs.body:
## What this PR does

When an SDK release reaches the step that publishes the freshly built release branch, the push is now retried up to three times with a short backoff (30s, then 60s) instead of failing the whole release on the first reported error. Before any retry, the step asks the remote for the branch's current commit and compares it with the commit that was just built: if the branch turns out to have landed remotely despite the reported failure, the step logs a notice and moves on; if it landed with different content, the step refuses to force-push and fails closed; only when the branch genuinely never landed does another push happen. The remote lookup matches the branch by its full ref so a similarly named branch (for example a backup branch sharing the same suffix) can never be mistaken for the release branch, and a transient failure of the lookup itself is tolerated and simply leads to another bounded attempt.

## Why it's needed

During the v0.1.29 SDK release (#16490), GitHub rejected the release-branch push with "Unable to determine if workflow can be created or updated due to timeout" — a fail-closed response GitHub can return while deciding whether workflow file changes may be pushed, even when the branch was in fact created remotely. The workflow treated the reported failure as fatal, so a release whose branch had actually been published stopped midway and had to be reconciled and registered by hand. A blind retry would not have helped (the branch already exists on the next attempt), and blindly continuing would risk masking real divergence; the retry therefore reconciles first and only ever continues on an exact match, never force-pushing.

## Reviewer Test Plan

### How to verify

The changed step only runs during SDK releases, so it was verified with an out-of-repo harness that replays the step's shell block verbatim under `bash -e -o pipefail` with a stubbed git, plus one fixture backed by a real git remote. Expected behavior a reviewer can confirm against that harness: a clean first push performs exactly one push with no delay and leaves the step's outputs untouched; a push that keeps failing while the branch never lands gives up after three attempts with 30s/60s backoff and a clear `::error::`; a push that reports failure while the branch actually landed with the same commit succeeds with a `::notice::` and no further push; a branch that landed with different content fails closed with a divergence error and never force-pushes; a reconciliation lookup that itself flakes is treated as "not landed yet" and stays inside the bounded retry instead of being killed by `set -e`; and a colliding branch whose name shares the release branch's suffix is not mistaken for it. Static checks a reviewer can redo in minutes: the workflow still parses as YAML, the edited shell block passes `bash -n`, the push command line is byte-identical to before, no force-push flag appears anywhere, and the diff is a single hunk in one workflow file with everything outside it byte-identical.

### Evidence (Before & After)

N/A — CI-only change with no user-visible surface; behavioral evidence is the scenario list above.

### Tested on

|     OS     | Status |
| :--------: | :----: |
|  🍏 macOS  |   ✅   |
| 🪟 Windows |  N/A   |
|  🐧 Linux  |   ⚠️   |

(CI runs on Linux runners; the local verification harness was exercised on macOS. Windows is not a relevant execution environment for this workflow.)

### Environment (optional)

Out-of-repo shell harness replaying the workflow step under `bash -e -o pipefail` with a stubbed git across eight scenarios (including a real-git fixture with a suffix-colliding branch), plus YAML parse and `bash -n` syntax checks.

## Risk & Scope

- Main risk or tradeoff: a release whose push genuinely keeps failing now takes up to about 90 seconds longer to surface the failure, and reconciliation assumes the remote stays queryable; if it does not, the step still fails, bounded, after three attempts.
- Not validated / out of scope: the change has not been exercised against the real GitHub release path (it only triggers during an SDK release). A pre-existing branch-existence check earlier in the same workflow uses a suffix-matching lookup as well; it was deliberately left untouched (its collision direction fails closed, and changing it would widen this minimal fix) and is proposed as a follow-up issue.
- Breaking changes / migration notes: none.

## Linked Issues

Related: #16490 — the incident that motivated this fix; it was closed after manual reconciliation, so this PR deliberately uses no closing keyword. This PR prevents recurrence.

<details>
<summary>中文说明</summary>

## 本 PR 做了什么

当 SDK 发布流程走到把刚构建好的 release 分支推送到远端这一步时，推送现在最多重试三次、带短暂退避（30 秒，然后 60 秒），而不是第一次报错就让整个发布失败。每次重试之前，该步骤会先向远端查询这个分支当前的提交，并与刚构建出的提交比对：如果分支其实已经成功落到远端（尽管推送返回了失败），该步骤记录一条 notice 后继续；如果远端分支内容与本地不一致，该步骤拒绝 force-push、以失败收敛；只有当分支确实从未落到远端时才真正再次推送。远端查询按完整 ref 匹配分支，名字相近的分支（例如共享相同后缀的备份分支）绝不会被误认为 release 分支；查询本身的瞬时失败也被容忍，只是进入下一次有界重试。

## 为什么需要

v0.1.29 SDK 发布期间（#16490），GitHub 以 "Unable to determine if workflow can be created or updated due to timeout" 拒绝了 release 分支的推送——这是 GitHub 在判断工作流文件改动是否允许推送时可能返回的 fail-closed 响应，即便分支实际上已在远端创建。工作流把这次报错当作致命错误，于是一个分支其实已经发出去的发布中途停摆，只能靠手工对账和补登记收尾。盲目重试于事无补（下一次尝试时分支已存在），盲目继续又有掩盖真实分叉的风险；因此重试前先对账，且只有完全一致才继续，绝不 force-push。

## 评审验证计划

### 如何验证

改动的步骤只在 SDK 发布时触发，因此采用仓库外的验证装置：用打桩的 git 在 `bash -e -o pipefail` 下逐字重放该步骤的 shell 块，另加一个基于真实 git 远端的夹具。评审者可对照该装置确认的预期行为：首次推送即成功时恰好推送一次、无延迟、步骤输出不变；推送持续失败且分支始终未落地时，三次尝试（30s/60s 退避）后放弃并给出清晰的 `::error::`；推送报告失败但分支实际已以相同提交落地时，以 `::notice::` 成功收敛且不再推送；分支以不同内容落地时以分叉错误 fail-closed，绝不 force-push；对账查询本身抖动时按"尚未落地"处理、留在有界重试内而不会被 `set -e` 截杀；与 release 分支共享后缀的碰撞分支不会被误认。评审者几分钟内即可重做的静态检查：工作流仍可作为 YAML 解析，改动的 shell 块通过 `bash -n`，推送命令行与之前逐字节相同，全文无任何 force-push 标志，且 diff 是单文件单 hunk、hunk 之外逐字节不变。

### 证据（前后对比）

N/A——纯 CI 改动，无用户可见界面；行为证据即上述场景列表。

### 测试平台

|     系统     | 状态 |
| :----------: | :--: |
|  🍏 macOS    |  ✅  |
| 🪟 Windows   | N/A  |
|  🐧 Linux    |  ⚠️  |

（CI 在 Linux runner 上运行；本地验证装置在 macOS 上执行。Windows 不是该工作流的相关运行环境。）

### 环境（可选）

仓库外的 shell 验证装置：用打桩 git 在 `bash -e -o pipefail` 下重放工作流步骤，覆盖八个场景（含一个带后缀碰撞分支的真实 git 夹具），另有 YAML 解析与 `bash -n` 语法检查。

## 风险与范围

- 主要风险或权衡：推送确实持续失败的发布现在最晚要多花约 90 秒才暴露失败；对账假设远端可查询，若远端持续不可达，该步骤仍会在三次尝试后有界失败。
- 未验证 / 范围外：本改动未在真实 GitHub 发布路径上演练（只在 SDK 发布时触发）。同一工作流靠前位置有一个既存的分支存在性检查同样使用后缀匹配查询；本次刻意不动它（其碰撞方向是 fail-closed，且改动它会扩大本次最小修复范围），建议作为后续单独 issue 跟进。
- 破坏性变更 / 迁移说明：无。

## 关联 Issue

关联：#16490——促成本次修复的事故；该 issue 在手工对账后已关闭，故本 PR 刻意不使用关闭关键字。本 PR 用于防止复发。

</details>

prs.title: feat(mods): run the prompts a Mod submits in the OpenTUI terminal
prs.body:
## What this PR does

In the OpenTUI terminal, a Mod's `$.prompt.submit({ text, asUser? })` now starts a turn of its own once the session is idle, as it already does in headless runs and in the Ink terminal. Before this, OpenTUI did not take these prompts: `$.session.version()` did not list the method, and a call resolved to `{ drop: 'this host does not run prompts a Mod submits' }`.

- **The terminal opts in.** OpenTUI tells the Mod session at load that it runs these prompts, in the same call that already opts in to `prompt.submit` and the band above the prompt.
- **When it runs.** Once the session is idle, the shell asks the live turn to take the next queued prompt and run it as a turn of its own, sent as Ink sends it: the framed text, the Mod's text as the submitted prompt, the hooks' context, the Mod's name and its recall query. UserPromptSubmit hears it, `turn.start` and `turn.complete` fire, and the transcript records it as the Mod's. It waits for the prompts and commands the person queued, while a dialog is open, while a `!` command runs, and while a submission the person sent is still being routed through the command registry and dispatcher, since that submission may still start a turn. As in Ink, it also waits while a Goal owns the session's turns, so it never runs as the person's Goal turn, and the shell tries again when the Goal lets go of them. OpenTUI runs no background-notification turns, so none holds it.
- **How it shows.** The transcript shows an info line with the same text Ink shows, `Mod <name>: <text>`, with `asUser` too. It is not a user row: it is not logged as the person's input, is not a rewind target and is never handed back to the input box. It does not pass the Mods' `prompt.submit` hooks again, reads no `@` reference and runs no command, even when it is slash-form text. A dual-output sidecar receives the Mod's text and a `mod_prompt` system message, as in Ink.
- **The person stays in control.** Every submission the person sends, prompt or command, resets the Mods' 8-turn count. Esc on a turn, or declining every tool it asks to run, drops the Mods' prompts still queued and refuses new ones until the person sends something; the prompt of a stopped Mod turn is taken out of the conversation so the next prompt does not reach the model behind it. A turn a Mod ends with `$.turn.abort` keeps the queue.
- **Resume.** OpenTUI's resume used to drop `notification` history items. It now draws them as info rows, as Ink does, so a resumed session shows the Mod's line. As a side effect, a resumed session in OpenTUI now also shows the background-agent and cron notification lines that Ink already shows.

The real-terminal integration test `integration-tests/interactive/mods-prompt-submit.test.ts` is no longer Ink-only, so the OpenTUI E2E leg runs it too. Removing the `describe.skipIf` wrapper re-indents the file, which is why its diff is large; the test bodies are unchanged. The user guide and the design document (English and Chinese) describe the OpenTUI behavior.

## Why it's needed

This is step 6, the last step of the `prompt.submit` plan in #13749. After step 5, a Mod that follows up on a turn worked in headless runs and Ink, but in OpenTUI the same Mod's follow-up was dropped. With this change a Mod behaves the same in every host that runs it.

## Reviewer Test Plan

### How to verify

- Install a Mod whose `turn.complete` hook, once, logs whether `(await $.session.version()).qwen.methods` lists `prompt.submit`, then calls `await $.prompt.submit({ text: 'List the TODOs you just mentioned.' })` and logs the result. Start `qwen` with the OpenTUI renderer (`QWEN_TUI_RENDERER=opentui`, under bun) and type `Look at the TODOs`.
  - Expected: after the first answer, the line `Mod followup-mod: List the TODOs you just mentioned.` appears and a second turn runs. The second model request's last user message is the `<qwen:mod-prompt mod="followup-mod">` block with the line naming the Mod.
  - On `main`, the method is not listed, the call resolves to `{"drop":"this host does not run prompts a Mod submits"}` and no second turn runs.
- A Mod that submits at every `turn.complete` stops after 8 Mod turns with `[Mod followup-mod] $.prompt.submit refused: the Mods have started 8 turns since the last prompt from the person`. Pressing Esc during one of those turns stops the chain.
- `/resume` that session in OpenTUI: the Mod's prompt comes back as the same `Mod followup-mod: …` line.
- `npx vitest run src/ui/opentui src/services/mod-session.test.ts src/services/interactive-mod-session.test.ts src/ui/utils/resumeHistoryUtils.test.ts` in `packages/cli`; after `npm run bundle`, `QWEN_E2E_RENDERER=opentui vitest run --root ./integration-tests interactive/mods-prompt-submit.test.ts`, and the same with `QWEN_E2E_RENDERER=ink`.

### Evidence (Before & After)

The built CLI in a real OpenTUI terminal (node-pty, 160×50, bun, `QWEN_TUI_RENDERER_STRICT` so it cannot fall back to Ink) against a loopback OpenAI-compatible fixture, with the Mod above installed through `qwen extensions install`. Before is `main` at `4cea3a792f`, After is this PR; both bundles were built locally from the same tree, Before with the CLI sources of `main`.

Before:

```
  > Look at the TODOs
  ◆︎ Answer 1
  ●︎ [Mod followup-mod] lists prompt.submit: false
  ●︎ [Mod followup-mod] submitted {"drop":"this host does not run prompts a Mod submits"}
```

After:

```
  > Look at the TODOs
  ◆︎ Answer 1
  ●︎ [Mod followup-mod] lists prompt.submit: true
  ●︎ Mod followup-mod: List the TODOs you just mentioned.
  ●︎ [Mod followup-mod] submitted {"text":"List the TODOs you just mentioned.","origin":{"kind":"plugin","name":"followup-mod"}}
  ◆︎ Answer 2
```

| | Before | After |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Model requests | 1 | 2 |
| Second request's last user message | none | `<qwen:mod-prompt mod="followup-mod">\nList the TODOs you just mentioned.\n</qwen:mod-prompt>` and the line saying the Mod sent it and the user did not type it |
| Transcript records | `real_user` | `real_user`; `mod_prompt` with `"mod": "followup-mod"` |

Automated checks:

- `packages/cli`: all of `src/ui/opentui` plus `mod-session`, `interactive-mod-session` and `resumeHistoryUtils` pass, 104 files, 3034 tests. New tests cover the framed turn under the Mod's line with no user row and no input log, an `asUser` slash-form prompt sent bare, one turn at a time, Esc and decline-all stopping the queue (and taking the stopped prompt out of the conversation) while `$.turn.abort` keeps it, the send options and sidecar, the shell's drain (after the turn ends, after held commands, behind a command still being routed or awaiting its defer verdict, and while a Goal owns the turns, running once it lets go), and resume.
- `integration-tests/interactive/mods-prompt-submit.test.ts` passes under both renderers: Ink 2/2 (about 19 s) and OpenTUI 2/2 (about 25 s).
- 14 targeted mutants are caught: the opt-in, the `@` skip, the Mod name, the sidecar message, the Esc stop, the decline-all stop, the orphan strip, the in-flight guard in `runModPrompt`, the `modPrompt` hand-off, the person-submission reset, the prompt subscription, the routing guard, the streaming guard and the resume projection. One guard survives on purpose: the drain also checks that the held-command queue is empty. That queue's own drain marks itself running first, so the check only matters on paths where that drain paused without a turn or a dialog. I kept it as a defensive check.
- `tsc --noEmit` for cli and integration tests, ESLint and Prettier pass on the changed files.

### Tested on

|     OS     | Status |
| :--------: | :----: |
|  🍏 macOS  |   ⚠️   |
| 🪟 Windows |   ⚠️   |
|  🐧 Linux  |   ✅   |

### Environment (optional)

Local bundle (`npm run bundle`); Ink under node 22, OpenTUI under bun 1.4, both through the integration harness's real terminal.

## Risk & Scope

- Main risk or tradeoff: a Mod's prompt now starts turns on its own in OpenTUI too. The same bounds apply as in Ink: the 8-turn limit, the reset on the person's input, and Esc or decline-all stopping the queue. As in Ink, input the person queues during a turn resets the count when it runs, not when it is sent, so a stop the turn before it made still holds until then. Steering text sent into a running turn resets it at once in OpenTUI only; Ink does not count steering.
- Resume side effect: OpenTUI now shows notification lines (background agents, cron, multi-agent replies) on resume, matching Ink; before, it dropped them.
- Not validated / out of scope: macOS and Windows locally.
- Breaking changes / migration notes: none. Sessions whose Mods never call `$.prompt.submit` behave as before.

Design document: [English](docs/design/2026-10-30-mod-prompt-submit.md) · [中文](docs/design/2026-10-30-mod-prompt-submit.zh-CN.md). Both are updated together: §9 (where hosts take the prompts, the new OpenTUI terminal paragraph, the turn limit, what does not run), the decisions (the notification line in both terminals, and why OpenTUI waits for what the person sent) and the acceptance list.

## Linked Issues

Part of #13749.

<details>
<summary>中文说明</summary>

## 这个 PR 做了什么

在 OpenTUI 终端中，Mod 的 `$.prompt.submit({ text, asUser? })` 现在会在会话空闲后启动一个独立的回合，与它在 headless 运行和 Ink 终端中已有的行为一致。此前 OpenTUI 不接手这类提示：`$.session.version()` 不列出该方法，调用返回 `{ drop: 'this host does not run prompts a Mod submits' }`。

- **终端主动声明。** OpenTUI 在加载时告诉 Mod 会话它会运行这类提示，与它声明 `prompt.submit` 和输入框上方区域是同一次调用。
- **何时运行。** 会话空闲后，shell 让实时回合取出队列里的下一条提示，作为独立回合运行，发送方式与 Ink 相同：框文、作为提交提示的 Mod 文本、hook 附加的上下文、Mod 的名字和召回查询。UserPromptSubmit 会听到它，`turn.start` 和 `turn.complete` 都会触发，transcript 把它记为 Mod 的提示。它会等用户排队的提示和命令先运行，并在对话框打开、`!` 命令运行、以及用户发出的提交仍在经过命令注册表和分发器期间等待，因为那条提交还可能开始一个回合。与 Ink 一样，它也会在 Goal 掌管会话回合期间等待，因此不会作为用户的 Goal 回合运行；Goal 放开回合时，shell 会再次尝试。OpenTUI 没有后台通知回合，所以不会有通知拦住它。
- **如何显示。** transcript 显示一条 info 行，文字与 Ink 相同：`Mod <name>: <text>`，`asUser` 时也一样。它不是用户消息行：不作为用户输入写入日志，不是回退目标，也不会被放回输入框。它不会再经过 Mod 的 `prompt.submit` hook，不读取 `@` 引用，也不运行任何命令，即使它是斜杠形式的文本。dual output 旁路与 Ink 一样收到 Mod 的文本和一条 `mod_prompt` 系统消息。
- **用户始终掌控。** 用户发出的每条提交，无论提示还是命令，都会把 Mod 的 8 回合计数清零。在回合中按 Esc，或拒绝回合要运行的全部工具，会丢弃 Mod 仍在排队的提示，并在用户再次发出内容前拒绝新的提示；被停下的 Mod 回合的提示会从对话中移除，这样下一条提示不会排在它后面发给模型。Mod 用 `$.turn.abort` 结束的回合会保留队列。
- **恢复会话。** OpenTUI 的恢复以前会丢掉 `notification` 历史项，现在像 Ink 一样把它们画成 info 行，所以恢复的会话会显示 Mod 的那一行。副作用是 OpenTUI 恢复的会话现在也会显示 Ink 本来就显示的后台 agent 和 cron 通知行。

真实终端集成测试 `integration-tests/interactive/mods-prompt-submit.test.ts` 不再只限 Ink，OpenTUI 的 E2E 一档也会运行它。去掉 `describe.skipIf` 外层后整个文件的缩进被重排，所以 diff 较大；测试内容本身没有变化。用户指南和设计文档（英文和中文）描述了 OpenTUI 的行为。

## 为什么需要

这是 #13749 中 `prompt.submit` 计划的第 6 步，也是最后一步。第 5 步之后，跟进回合的 Mod 在 headless 和 Ink 中可用，但在 OpenTUI 中同一个 Mod 的跟进会被丢弃。这次改动后，Mod 在所有运行它的宿主中行为一致。

## 审阅者测试计划

### 如何验证

- 安装一个 Mod：它的 `turn.complete` hook 只执行一次，先记录 `(await $.session.version()).qwen.methods` 是否列出 `prompt.submit`，再调用 `await $.prompt.submit({ text: 'List the TODOs you just mentioned.' })` 并记录结果。用 OpenTUI 渲染器（`QWEN_TUI_RENDERER=opentui`，在 bun 下）启动 `qwen`，输入 `Look at the TODOs`。
  - 预期：第一个回答之后出现 `Mod followup-mod: List the TODOs you just mentioned.` 这一行，并运行第二个回合。第二个模型请求的最后一条用户消息是 `<qwen:mod-prompt mod="followup-mod">` 块以及注明 Mod 的那一行说明。
  - 在 `main` 上，该方法不被列出，调用返回 `{"drop":"this host does not run prompts a Mod submits"}`，也不会运行第二个回合。
- 每次 `turn.complete` 都提交提示的 Mod 在 8 个 Mod 回合后停止，并显示 `[Mod followup-mod] $.prompt.submit refused: the Mods have started 8 turns since the last prompt from the person`。在这些回合中按 Esc 会终止这条链。
- 在 OpenTUI 中对该会话执行 `/resume`：Mod 的提示以同样的 `Mod followup-mod: …` 行恢复。
- 在 `packages/cli` 中运行 `npx vitest run src/ui/opentui src/services/mod-session.test.ts src/services/interactive-mod-session.test.ts src/ui/utils/resumeHistoryUtils.test.ts`；`npm run bundle` 之后运行 `QWEN_E2E_RENDERER=opentui vitest run --root ./integration-tests interactive/mods-prompt-submit.test.ts`，再用 `QWEN_E2E_RENDERER=ink` 运行一次。

### 证据（前后对比）

构建后的 CLI 在真实 OpenTUI 终端（node-pty，160×50，bun，开启 `QWEN_TUI_RENDERER_STRICT`，不会退回 Ink）中对接本地回环的 OpenAI 兼容 fixture，上面的 Mod 通过 `qwen extensions install` 安装。Before 是 `main` 的 `4cea3a792f`，After 是本 PR；两个包都在本地从同一棵树构建，Before 使用 `main` 的 CLI 源码。

Before：

```
  > Look at the TODOs
  ◆︎ Answer 1
  ●︎ [Mod followup-mod] lists prompt.submit: false
  ●︎ [Mod followup-mod] submitted {"drop":"this host does not run prompts a Mod submits"}
```

After：

```
  > Look at the TODOs
  ◆︎ Answer 1
  ●︎ [Mod followup-mod] lists prompt.submit: true
  ●︎ Mod followup-mod: List the TODOs you just mentioned.
  ●︎ [Mod followup-mod] submitted {"text":"List the TODOs you just mentioned.","origin":{"kind":"plugin","name":"followup-mod"}}
  ◆︎ Answer 2
```

| | Before | After |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 模型请求数 | 1 | 2 |
| 第二个请求的最后一条用户消息 | 无 | `<qwen:mod-prompt mod="followup-mod">\nList the TODOs you just mentioned.\n</qwen:mod-prompt>`，以及说明这条消息由 Mod 发来、用户没有输入它的那一行 |
| transcript 记录 | `real_user` | `real_user`；带 `"mod": "followup-mod"` 的 `mod_prompt` |

自动化检查：

- `packages/cli`：`src/ui/opentui` 全部测试加上 `mod-session`、`interactive-mod-session` 和 `resumeHistoryUtils` 通过，104 个文件、3034 个测试。新增测试覆盖：带框文的回合显示在 Mod 的行下，没有用户行，不写输入日志；斜杠形式的 `asUser` 提示原样发送；一次一个回合；Esc 和拒绝全部工具停下队列（并把被停下的提示移出对话），`$.turn.abort` 保留队列；发送选项和旁路；shell 的排空（回合结束后、暂缓的命令之后、在仍在路由或仍在等待延后判定的命令之后，以及 Goal 掌管回合期间等待、Goal 放开后运行）；恢复会话。
- `integration-tests/interactive/mods-prompt-submit.test.ts` 在两种渲染器下都通过：Ink 2/2（约 19 秒），OpenTUI 2/2（约 25 秒）。
- 14 个针对性变异被测试抓住：声明、跳过 `@`、Mod 名字、旁路消息、Esc 停止、拒绝全部工具停止、移除孤立提示、`runModPrompt` 的进行中检查、`modPrompt` 传递、用户提交清零、提示订阅、路由检查、回合进行中检查、恢复投影。有一项检查是有意保留、没有测试抓住的：排空还会检查"暂缓命令队列是否为空"。那个队列自己的排空会先把自己标记为运行中，所以这项检查只在它暂停、但既没有回合也没有对话框的路径上起作用，作为防御保留。
- cli 和集成测试的 `tsc --noEmit`、改动文件的 ESLint 和 Prettier 通过。

### 测试平台

|     OS     | 状态 |
| :--------: | :----: |
|  🍏 macOS  |   ⚠️   |
| 🪟 Windows |   ⚠️   |
|  🐧 Linux  |   ✅   |

### 环境（可选）

本地打包（`npm run bundle`）；Ink 在 node 22 下、OpenTUI 在 bun 1.4 下，均通过集成测试框架的真实终端运行。

## 风险与范围

- 主要风险或取舍：Mod 的提示现在在 OpenTUI 中也会自己启动回合。约束与 Ink 相同：8 回合上限、用户输入清零计数、Esc 或拒绝全部工具停下队列。与 Ink 一样，用户在回合进行中排队的输入在运行时才清零，而不是发送时，因此前一回合造成的停止会一直保持到那时。发给运行中回合的 steering 文本只在 OpenTUI 中立即清零；Ink 不把 steering 计入。
- 恢复会话的副作用：OpenTUI 恢复时现在会显示通知行（后台 agent、cron、多 agent 回复），与 Ink 一致；此前会丢掉它们。
- 未验证 / 不在范围内：本地未在 macOS 和 Windows 上验证。
- 破坏性变更 / 迁移说明：无。Mod 从不调用 `$.prompt.submit` 的会话行为不变。

设计文档：[English](docs/design/2026-10-30-mod-prompt-submit.md) · [中文](docs/design/2026-10-30-mod-prompt-submit.zh-CN.md)。两者同步更新：§9（宿主从哪里接手提示、新增的 OpenTUI 终端一段、回合上限、不会运行的情况）、设计决策（两种终端都显示通知行，以及 OpenTUI 为什么等用户发出的内容先走）和验收列表。

## 关联 Issue

属于 #13749 的一部分。

</details>

prs.title: feat(web-shell): let managed sessions reuse the host shell
prs.body:
## What this PR does

Managed sessions inside the web shell now reuse the host shell's own chrome instead of maintaining a second managed look:

- **Header:** with `showManagedSessionHeader: false`, the managed page stops rendering its own session title / workspace / phase badge when the host already shows session identity.
- **Copy and hints:** with `alignManagedChatWithHost: true`, the managed composer uses the same placeholder as ordinary sessions and drops the "model is fixed", "approval mode is fixed" and "start a new task" explanations. Capabilities stay enforced exactly as before — nothing is loosened, the hints are just not spelled out.
- **Host slots:** a host-provided `renderWelcomeHeader` / `renderComposerFooter` now renders on the managed page, replacing the built-in welcome block and the fixed-capability hints.
- **Daemon gates:** `WorkspaceSessionProvider` skips the daemon workspace/session gates **only for the managed view** — `managed=1`, or no `managed` param on a page that defaults to the managed home (non-chat page / chat page without a session target). Managed workspaces come from the host HTTP provider, so those gates cannot resolve them. The rule is the same one `App` uses at mount (`managedSelectionFromRoute()`); an explicit local session target in a managed shell keeps every gate, including the `lockWorkspaceCwd` host constraint and the "workspace not found" refusal.

**Scope note:** an earlier revision also projected the managed connection into `ChatPane` through a `connectionOverride` customization field. That path had no consumer — no public entry point injected a connection, and the in-repo managed host mounts the customization provider with an empty value — so it was removed rather than shipped as dead surface. The reachability check and the deleted surface are recorded in the verification comment on this PR.

## Why it's needed

Hosts that already provide navigation and status had to maintain a second shell and a second set of copy next to the normal session UI. The observable problems were two different UIs for the same conversation and a false "workspace not found" for managed sessions whose workspace only exists on the host side.

## Reviewer Test Plan

### How to verify

1. `cd packages/web-shell && npx vitest run --config vitest.config.ts client/components/managed/ManagedSessionsPage.test.tsx`
2. `cd packages/web-shell && npx playwright test --config playwright.config.ts client/e2e/managed-usability.spec.ts --grep @smoke`
3. Related suites for regressions: `client/App.test.tsx`, `client/ManagedAgentWebShell.test.tsx`, `client/ManagedStandaloneApp.test.tsx`, `client/components/ChatPane.test.tsx`, both `WorkspaceSessionProvider*` suites, `ManagedSessionsPage.test.tsx`, `ManagedSessionNavigationRow.test.tsx` → `1865 passed`.

### Evidence (Before & After)

Before (the new host-slot tests against the pre-change production sources): `ManagedSessionsPage.test.tsx` → `3 failed | 168 passed` — the three host-customization assertions fail, the rest pass.

Gate regression, two states this round: with the previous predicate restored, the two new provider tests (`keeps the workspace refusal for a local session without managed=0`, `keeps the lockWorkspaceCwd constraint for a local session without managed=0`) fail; with the scoped predicate they pass. The managed-view tests (`keeps the managed view exempt…`, `keeps the default managed home exempt without a managed param`) pin the other direction so the exemption is not over-narrowed.

After (this head): `WorkspaceSessionProvider.test.tsx` 42/42, `ManagedSessionsPage.test.tsx` 176/176, related nine-file suite `1865 passed`; the real-browser pass mounts the actual `ManagedSessionsPage` with the real Java-managed provider and a stubbed host API, covering five cells (`default`, `header=0`, `align=1`, `welcome=1`, `footer=1`).

### Tested on

|     OS     | Status |
| :--------: | :----: |
|  🍏 macOS  |   ✅   |
| 🪟 Windows |   ⚠️   |
|  🐧 Linux  |   ⚠️   |

### Environment (optional)

macOS arm64, Node v24.19.0, Chromium via the repo's Playwright 1.61.1. Unit/jsdom and real-browser runs both from a dedicated worktree.

## Risk & Scope

- Main risk or tradeoff: the managed behavior activates only when `managedAgentProvider` is injected; hosts that do not inject it keep the existing behavior. The new fields are optional and default to the current UI.
- Reachability: the retained hooks are reachable through the public `WebShell` component (`WebShellProps` carries `managedAgentProvider` plus the two new knobs). The standalone `ManagedAgentWebShell` entry still mounts the customization provider with an empty value, so it does not expose these knobs — unchanged by this PR.
- Not validated / out of scope: a live managed backend (the host HTTP API is stubbed at the wire level), Windows/Linux local runs, and host integrations other than the one used for the manual check. The full-app browser arm for the local-session gate needs a daemon that accepts this origin (remote-access setting); the gate behaviour itself is covered by the provider tests on both arms.
- Deferred: `navigationTarget` `undefined` → `null` (`sidebar:false`) changes the managed page to the `home` layout without page-local navigation. That layout change is intentional and now documented, but its interaction with host-provided sidebars is left for a follow-up rather than widened here.
- Breaking changes / migration notes: none for existing daemon sessions. `managed=0` is the explicit opt-out that keeps the daemon path; no released API is removed (the `connectionOverride` field was introduced and removed within this PR).

## Linked Issues

None.

prs.title: test(cli): give two serve-side CI waits real poll budgets
prs.body:
## What this PR does

Gives two serve-side tests a poll budget that scales with the work they are actually waiting for, instead of a budget that elapses independently of it. Both are test-only changes; no production code, assertion, input, expected value, poll interval, or error message is altered.

The managed-workspace upload suite has a case that launches a real child process, hooks its cleanup path so the process parks itself at a known point, and then waits for a marker file proving the child reached that point. The wait was a fixed count of one hundred iterations of a twenty-five millisecond sleep. The child meanwhile has to boot Node, register a TypeScript loader, import the bootstrap module and run it before it can write the marker, so the fixed count races real I/O. The wait now polls the same condition at the same interval against a thirty-second wall-clock deadline. (Merged state. A post-merge refinement deriving that deadline from the lane’s per-test timeout is described in the comments and carried separately.)

The hosted user-question suite has a parameterized case whose local-process branch waits for a mount release. That wait used the testing library's default one-second budget, while the authorization wait immediately above it in the very same test already uses fifteen seconds for the same asynchronous authority path. The two now share the fifteen-second budget.

## Why it's needed

Both cases reddened `main` on commits whose diff cannot reach them, and each red costs the shard plus its aggregating gate. The upload case failed on a shard whose own load sampling read `load[89.18 93.97 178.24]`: the child had not reached cleanup when the iteration count ran out, and all three attempts threw the identical `Original upload did not reach cleanup.` The question case failed `expected "releaseMount" to be called once, but got 0 times` on all three attempts, at the assertion that sits inside the one-second wait. A budget that is a function of iteration count rather than elapsed time, or that is left at a library default while its sibling in the same test already declares a larger one, is not measuring the thing the test cares about.

## Reviewer Test Plan

### How to verify

Run both suites with retries disabled so a flake cannot hide behind a retry, from `packages/cli`: `npx vitest run src/serve/managed-workspace-upload.process.test.ts --coverage.enabled=false --retry=0` (expect 5/5) and `npx vitest run src/serve/hosted-user-question.test.ts --coverage.enabled=false --retry=0` (expect 37/37). Both were run three consecutive times locally, and once more after rebasing onto the final base.

For the upload case, the load-bearing nature of the budget is directly demonstrable: temporarily shorten the deadline to one millisecond and the case fails with the verbatim CI error `Original upload did not reach cleanup.`; restore it and the case passes. That witness was run and the file restored byte-exactly afterwards. It shows the loop is genuinely waiting on the child rather than passing vacuously, and that the deadline is the binding constraint.

For the question case, confirm the change is an alignment rather than a new policy: the authorization wait immediately above it in the same test already passes `{ timeout: 15000 }`, and the assertion text is byte-identical before and after.

### Evidence (Before & After)

N/A — non-UI, test-only change. Before: the two cases above failed intermittently on unrelated commits with the quoted signatures. After: repeated local runs are green, and the upload deadline mutation still produces the exact CI error.

### Tested on

|     OS     | Status |
| :--------: | :----: |
|  🍏 macOS  |   ⚠️   |
| 🪟 Windows |   ⚠️   |
|  🐧 Linux  |   ✅   |

### Environment (optional)

Local Linux, Node 24, Vitest 3.2.7, retries disabled. Prettier and ESLint clean on both touched files; pre-commit passed on both commits. The upload case was additionally run eight times under 64-way CPU oversubscription (load average up to ~61 on 32 cores), where its duration grew from a 1.9s baseline to 4.7–6.1s.

## Risk & Scope

- Main risk or tradeoff: a genuinely stuck child now takes longer to report than the old two and a half seconds, which is the intended cost of not failing a healthy-but-slow boot. As merged, that deadline exceeds the non-ECS per-test ceiling of fifteen seconds, so on such a runner a pathological hang surfaces as a vitest timeout rather than the descriptive error; the lane where the flake was observed is the self-hosted pool, whose ceiling is sixty seconds. A post-merge refinement derives the budget from the lane timeout with a one-second reserve and was witnessed to report the descriptive error at 14029ms on a fifteen-second lane; it is carried separately, not in this merged diff. The question change raises a ceiling only, so a release that never happens still fails.
- Not validated / out of scope: neither natural failure was reproduced locally. Eight upload runs under load ~61 all passed, and the question case passed even with its budget mutated down to one millisecond under load ~40–60 — on this machine the mount release has already landed by the time the wait starts, so the budget's load-bearing nature could not be demonstrated locally for that case. Its fix rests on the exact CI signature plus the sibling wait in the same test already declaring fifteen seconds, and is ceiling-only. macOS and Windows were not exercised locally. The `rewindFiles` intermittent report and the Java fault-gate lane are out of scope; the former is not a simple validation gap (an unparsed body yields `400 missing_prompt_id`, not the observed `200`), so it needs separate diagnosis rather than a budget change.
- Breaking changes / migration notes: none. No production code, public API, or configuration changes.

## Linked Issues

Fixes #16580
References #16552 (expected to resolve; not locally reproduced, see Risk & Scope)

### 如何验证

N/A —— 非 UI、仅测试改动。改动前：上述两个用例在无关提交上间歇失败，签名如所引。改动后：本机反复运行全绿，且 upload 的截止时间变异仍能产出确切的 CI 错误。

## 风险与范围

- 主要风险或取舍：真正卡住的子进程现在比原先约 2.5 秒更晚报错——这正是「不误杀健康但慢的启动」所要付的代价。按合并时的实现，该截止时间超过非 ECS 的 15 秒单用例上限，因此在这类 runner 上病态挂起会表现为 vitest 超时而非那条描述性错误；观察到 flake 的车道是自建池，其上限为 60 秒。合并后有一项改进把预算改为从车道上限派生并预留一秒，已用「让子进程永久停住」见证在 15 秒车道上于 14029ms 抛出描述性错误；该改进单独承载，不在本次合并的 diff 内。question 改动只抬上限，因此永不发生的释放仍会失败。

prs.title: feat(serve): drain bound-PR watch pending transitions behind an off switch
prs.body:
## What this PR does

Adds the delivery drain for the daemon PR-state watch (the master design's §4 Delivery and §5 Durability). The observation increment already detects head/CI/conflict/state transitions into each PR watch file's `pending`, but nothing delivered them. This drain resolves one recipient per PR across the daemon (one per role group when role-aware actions are configured), admits the transition prompt through the shared prompt admission, and records `delivered`/`served` under the PR's lock with the crash-window semantics: a failed recording write keeps an in-flight mark so a later drain retries only the write, never re-admitting. It restores dormant recipients off the tick with bounded concurrency and the channel's Gone/Unavailable split (Gone recipients are excluded with a rejoin horizon so the drain re-resolves to the next binder), suppresses self-pushed `head_change` per recipient via the autofix-pr pushed-head ledger, and applies the watch-file deletion / `lastBoundAt` rules on scan completeness.

Like the observation, the whole path stays behind the internal off switch and an unpopulated `getPrDrainDeps` seam, so it is production-inert: no admission, restore, or deletion runs until the enablement increment populates the deps. The restore/admission/self-push access are injected dependencies (`wakeSession`, `admitPrompt`, `readPushedHeads`) tested against fakes.

## Why it's needed

The watch store has a writer (observation) but no reader, so a session that follows a PR receives no daemon notification when the PR's head, CI, mergeability or state changes. This is the next increment of the daemon PR-state watch design, completing the delivery/durability layer so the later enablement increment can turn the path on and PR B can migrate the channel watch onto it.

## Reviewer Test Plan

### How to verify

The path is gated off, so there is no user-visible CLI behaviour to drive; verification is the collocated unit tests plus the switch-off parity guard. From `packages/cli`:

```
npx vitest run src/serve/server/pr-watch-drain.test.ts src/serve/server/pr-watch-drain.scenario.test.ts src/serve/server/pr-watch-store.test.ts src/serve/server/pr-watch-observation.test.ts src/serve/server/session-pr-refresh.test.ts --coverage.enabled=false
```

Expected: 205 passed (drain 49 + real scenarios 15 + store 27 + observation 46 + refresh 68). The drain tests cover oldest-first delivery, `delivered`/in-flight dedupe (including the crash window where a key is in `delivered` but its entry is still `pending`), recipient resolution by full identity and recency, partial-scan retention and the caller's coverage signal, self-push suppression judged against the entry's own head with re-resolution and the no-candidate drop, Gone exclusion + rejoin, dormant restore + release (a dormant leader waits instead of falling through to the next binder), role-aware group-suffixed keys and the no-template drop, deletion / `lastBoundAt` / age limits, per-PR failure containment, and non-owner inertness. The refresh suite covers both that the drain seam is never read while the switch is off and that, with the switch on, the drain delivers the tick's transition for the covered workspaces only. The scenario suite (POSIX) drives a real `gh` child through the real observation, bindings scan, watch store and `admitSessionPrompt`, with a real EACCES crash window, a real corrupt sidecar, a real autofix-pr ledger and a restart that clears the admission ring.

Each behavioural guard was mutation-verified on the final head (source restored byte-exact after every row): 20 mutations this round — the coverage signal, the eligible-candidate count, channel-row coverage, the no-template drop, role guidance, the display case, per-PR containment, the `DaemonDrainingError` rethrow, the rejected-admission mark cleanup, the dormant wait, the restore's on-disk `served` merge, the entry-head self-push judgement, `lastBoundAt` refresh, the Gone rejoin prune, the no-binder group skip, the `delivered` cap, the served-group skip, the restore's `recordKey`, the under-lock read-error log, and one-recipient-per-group — each reds its named test (20/20 killed). The macOS path bug was witnessed separately with a symlinked `TMPDIR`: red before the `realpathSync` fix, green after; and passing `live` instead of `ordered` to the drain reds the new caller test.

### Evidence (Before & After)

N/A — non-user-visible (gated-off infrastructure + unit tests). `packages/cli` `tsc --noEmit`: exit 0, zero errors (the 26 pre-existing stale-dist errors cleared after rebuilding `core` then `acp-bridge`). ESLint + Prettier clean on all changed files; both design languages stay in sync (21 headings, 11 table rows each).

### Tested on

|     OS     | Status |
| :--------: | :----: |
|  🍏 macOS  |   ⚠️   |
| 🪟 Windows |   ⚠️   |
|  🐧 Linux  |   ✅   |

### Environment (optional)

Unit tests only (vitest, real temp watch dir + `PathMutexRegistry`, injected fakes for scan/admission/restore/self-push).

## Risk & Scope

- Main risk or tradeoff: the drain's durability semantics (in-flight marks, write-retry, Gone re-resolution) are intricate; they are exercised by targeted unit tests and mutation witnesses, but only run for real once enablement populates the deps.
- Not validated / out of scope: the shared restore extraction from `restoreSessionHandler`, the resume-drain hook, the serve-lifecycle close reorder, and the daemon-level deps provisioning all land with the enablement increment (the drain is inert until then); configuration (§6) and the channel migration (§7) are PR B. No end-to-end delivery through a live daemon was run.
- Breaking changes / migration notes: none — the path is off by default and the refresh is unchanged while off.

Design doc (both versions, complete and synchronized): [English](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/blob/feat/daemon-pr-watch-drain/docs/design/2026-11-08-daemon-pr-watch-drain.md) · [简体中文](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/blob/feat/daemon-pr-watch-drain/docs/design/2026-11-08-daemon-pr-watch-drain.zh-CN.md)

## Linked Issues

Builds on the daemon PR-state watch design (`docs/design/2026-11-04-daemon-pr-state-transitions.md`); follows the observation increment (#16611) and the watch-store foundation (#16590).

<details>
<summary>中文说明</summary>

## 本 PR 做什么

为 daemon PR-state watch 新增投递 drain（主设计 §4 投递与 §5 持久性）。观测增量已把 head/CI/冲突/状态转换检测进每个 PR watch 文件的 `pending`，但没有任何东西投递它们。本 drain 跨 daemon 为每个 PR 解析一个接收者（配置 role-aware 动作时每角色组一个），经共享 prompt 准入投递转换 prompt，并在 PR 锁内按崩溃窗口语义记录 `delivered`/`served`：记录写失败会保留 in-flight 标记，使后续 drain 只重试该写、绝不重新准入。它在 tick 外以有限并发恢复休眠接收者，采用 channel 的 Gone/Unavailable 划分（Gone 接收者被排除并带重新加入时限，使 drain 重新解析到下一个绑定者），经 autofix-pr 自推 head 账本按接收者抑制自推 `head_change`，并依据扫描完整性应用 watch 文件删除 / `lastBoundAt` 规则。

与观测一样，整条路径保持在内部关闭开关与未填充的 `getPrDrainDeps` 接缝之后，因此对生产惰性：在启用增量填充 deps 之前不会有任何准入、restore 或删除。restore/准入/自推访问是注入依赖（`wakeSession`、`admitPrompt`、`readPushedHeads`），用假实现测试。

## 为什么需要

watch 存储有写入者（观测）却没有读取者，因此关注某 PR 的会话在该 PR 的 head、CI、可合并性或状态变化时收不到 daemon 通知。这是 daemon PR-state watch 设计的下一增量，补全投递/持久层，使后续启用增量能打开该路径、PR B 能把 channel watch 迁移过来。

## 评审测试计划

### 如何验证

路径处于关闭状态，没有可驱动的用户可见 CLI 行为；验证为同置单元测试加关闭开关 parity 守卫。在 `packages/cli` 下运行上述 vitest 命令，预期 205 通过（drain 49 + 真实场景 15 + store 27 + 观测 46 + refresh 68）。drain 测试覆盖最旧优先投递、`delivered`/in-flight 去重（含键已在 `delivered` 但条目仍在 `pending` 的崩溃窗口）、按全 identity 与 recency 解析接收者、partial 扫描保留与调用方覆盖信号、按条目自身 head 判自推并重解析与无候选丢弃、Gone 排除+重新加入、休眠 restore+释放（休眠领先者等待而非改投下一个绑定者）、role-aware 组后缀键与无模板丢弃、删除/`lastBoundAt`/年龄上限、单 PR 失败隔离、非 owner 惰性。refresh 套件既覆盖「开关关闭时绝不读 drain 接缝」，也覆盖开关打开时 drain 只为被覆盖的工作区投递本 tick 的转换。场景套件（POSIX）用真实 `gh` 子进程串起真实观测、绑定扫描、watch store 与 `admitSessionPrompt`，含真实 EACCES 崩溃窗口、真实损坏 sidecar、真实 autofix-pr 账本，以及清空准入环的重启。

每个行为守卫都在最终 head 上做了变异验证（每行跑完源码逐字节恢复）：本轮 20 处——覆盖信号、可用候选计数、channel 行覆盖、无模板丢弃、角色指引、展示大小写、单 PR 隔离、`DaemonDrainingError` 上抛、准入被拒的清标记、休眠等待、restore 从磁盘合并 `served`、按条目 head 判自推、`lastBoundAt` 刷新、Gone 重新加入剪枝、无绑定者组跳过、`delivered` 上限、served 组跳过、restore 的 `recordKey`、锁内读错日志、每组单接收者——各自使其点名测试变红（20/20 击杀）。macOS 路径缺陷另用符号链接 `TMPDIR` 见证：`realpathSync` 修复前红、修复后绿；把传给 drain 的 `ordered` 换成 `live` 会让新增调用方用例变红。

### 证据（前后对比）

N/A —— 非用户可见（关闭状态的基础设施 + 单元测试）。`packages/cli` `tsc --noEmit`：exit 0、零错误（依次重建 `core`、`acp-bridge` 后 26 个既有 stale-dist 错清零）。所有改动文件 ESLint + Prettier 干净；双语设计保持同步（各 21 标题、11 表行）。

### 测试平台

Linux ✅（本机）；macOS / Windows ⚠️ 未测。

### 环境

仅单元测试（vitest，真实临时 watch 目录 + `PathMutexRegistry`，scan/准入/restore/自推用注入假实现）。

## 风险与范围

- 主要风险/权衡：drain 的持久语义（in-flight 标记、写重试、Gone 重解析）较复杂，已由定向单元测试与变异见证覆盖，但只有在启用填充 deps 后才真正运行。
- 未验证/超出范围：从 `restoreSessionHandler` 抽取共享 restore、resume-后 drain 钩子、serve lifecycle close 重排、daemon 级 deps 填充均随启用增量落地（此前 drain 惰性）；配置（§6）与 channel 迁移（§7）为 PR B。未跑通过 live daemon 的端到端投递。
- 破坏性变更/迁移说明：无 —— 路径默认关闭，关闭时 refresh 不变。

设计文档（中英两版，完整同步）：见上方英文正文链接。

## 关联

基于 daemon PR-state watch 设计（`docs/design/2026-11-04-daemon-pr-state-transitions.md`）；承接观测增量（#16611）与 watch 存储地基（#16590）。

prs.title: fix(cli): let in-session MCP enable lift glob exclusions
prs.body:
## What this PR does

`qwen serve` now logs a repeated WebSocket upgrade rejection at most once per minute per `reason@client-address`. Every other rejection still gets its 403 and is still counted — only the duplicate journal line is suppressed. An in-session `enable` now also lifts a glob exclusion from `mcp.excluded`, matching how every disable path already applied the pattern.

## Why it's needed

`logReject` in `packages/cli/src/serve/acp-http/index.ts` wrote one stderr line per rejected upgrade with no throttle or dedupe. A client whose upgrade the daemon always refuses — most often the Chrome extension retrying an origin the daemon was never told to allow — reconnects forever, so the journal accumulates thousands of identical lines a day. The issue measured ~4,000–6,000/day for a single extension origin.

Separately, every disable path matched `mcp.excluded` with `matchesAnyServerPattern`, but every enable path removed the entry with an exact `!==` / `includes` comparison. A pattern such as `foo-*` never equals the server name, so it stayed in the list and remained in the runtime union — the dialog then reported `Enabled '<name>'` while the server was still excluded.

This is the server-side third of #13966. The client halves are the extension's reconnect ladder and an autoconnect opt-out; #14022 already covers persisting that ladder across MV3 service-worker restarts.

## Reviewer Test Plan

### How to verify

Log throttle:

- One entry per distinct `reason@address`, holding the last time it was logged. Inside `UPGRADE_REJECT_LOG_INTERVAL_MS` the line is dropped; the socket is still destroyed with the same 403.
- The key includes the reason, not just the address, so a different rejection from the same client (say an expired token after an origin that was previously refused) is still reported immediately.
- The map is re-inserted on each log so it stays in least-recently-logged order, and is capped at `MAX_UPGRADE_REJECT_LOG_KEYS` by evicting the oldest entry. Without the cap, a daemon seeing many distinct rejected clients would grow it without bound.

Enable lifting a glob:

The enable side now filters through the same matcher, in all six places that lift an exclusion:

- `serve/routes/workspace-mcp-config.ts`
- `acp-integration/acpAgent.ts` (settings + live configs)
- `ui/opentui/dialog-data.ts`
- `ui/components/mcp/MCPManagementDialog.tsx`
- `ui/components/extensions/views/McpServerActionsView.tsx`

prs.title: fix(serve): throttle repeated WebSocket upgrade rejection logs
prs.body:
## What this PR does

`qwen serve` now logs a repeated WebSocket upgrade rejection at most once per minute per `reason@client-address`. Every other rejection still gets its 403 and is still counted — only the duplicate journal line is suppressed.

## Why it's needed

`logReject` in `packages/cli/src/serve/acp-http/index.ts` wrote one stderr line per rejected upgrade with no throttle or dedupe. A client whose upgrade the daemon always refuses — most often the Chrome extension retrying an origin the daemon was never told to allow — reconnects forever, so the journal accumulates thousands of identical lines a day. The issue measured ~4,000–6,000/day for a single extension origin.

This is the server-side third of #13966. The client halves are the extension's reconnect ladder and an autoconnect opt-out; #14022 already covers persisting that ladder across MV3 service-worker restarts.

## Reviewer Test Plan

### How to verify

- One entry per distinct `reason@address`, holding the last time it was logged. Inside `UPGRADE_REJECT_LOG_INTERVAL_MS` the line is dropped; the socket is still destroyed with the same 403.
- The key includes the reason, not just the address, so a different rejection from the same client (say an expired token after an origin that was previously refused) is still reported immediately.
- The map is re-inserted on each log so it stays in least-recently-logged order, and is capped at `MAX_UPGRADE_REJECT_LOG_KEYS` by evicting the oldest entry. Without the cap, a daemon seeing many distinct rejected clients would grow it without bound.

```sh
npx vitest run packages/cli/src/serve/acp-http/transport.test.ts
```

### Evidence (Before & After)

Two new cases in `transport.test.ts` cover the change: repeated identical rejections log once while a different reason still logs, and the same rejection is logged again after the window elapses. The file reports 433 passing tests.

prs.title: fix(cli): preserve hosted turn history after interruption
prs.body:
## What this PR does

Preserve the original user instruction together with committed assistant/tool exchanges when a Hosted tool-profile Turn is settled after Harness interruption. Exclude other cancelled or failed Turns as complete groups from fresh and recovered model requests, while retaining completed history and durable audit records. When compression restores raw history, keep unmarked queued guidance within its original Turn's exclusion boundary.

## Why it's needed

As reported in [#14256](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/issues/14256), a Harness crash can leave admitted child or team work running, while later requests lose the user's original prompt and keep its tool exchanges. The lead then receives results or a follow-up without the instruction it was supposed to complete. Removing only the prompt also leaves tool context from user-cancelled Turns in later requests.

## Reviewer Test Plan

### How to verify

1. In a Hosted tool-profile fixture, settle a prior tool Turn as `cancelled` with `stopReason: harness_interruption`, then send a follow-up. Confirm the model receives the original user prompt and its paired assistant/tool records.
2. Repeat with user cancellation, deadline cancellation, and an error. Confirm the later model request excludes the complete prior group, completed Turns remain available, and durable audit records retain the original messages and settlement.
3. Continue a Turn parked in a second tool round. Confirm prior interrupted/completed groups survive, prior user-cancelled groups are absent, and only the parked round's tool results form the resume request.
4. Recover an interrupted channel wake and send a follow-up. Confirm its original channel prompt remains in context and the cancelled wake does not plan a reply.
5. Restore a compression snapshot with a cancelled tool group and marked/unmarked queued guidance. Confirm model and startup Hook history exclude that group while preserving the summary prefix and the next completed group.

The focused suites can be run from `packages/cli`:

```bash
npx vitest run src/serve/hosted-harness-model.test.ts src/serve/hosted-harness-session.test.ts src/serve/hosted-runtime-recovery.test.ts src/serve/hosted-channel-session.test.ts --reporter=dot --coverage.enabled=false
```

### Evidence (Before & After)

The following model-input record types are documented in the local journal/HTTP-route reproduction and verification reports, using a scripted model:

| Prior Turn settlement | Before | After |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `cancelled / harness_interruption` | `['assistant', 'tool_result']` | `['user', 'assistant', 'tool_result']` |
| `cancelled / cancelled` | `['assistant', 'tool_result']` | `[]` |

The final recorded run of the four focused suites on the rebased source, subsequently committed as `7027abc3f62acf8fa43db44ac658d2e24dc86383`, completed successfully:

```text
 Test Files  4 passed (4)
      Tests  905 passed (905)
```

Recorded checks also passed: `npm run build`, `npm run bundle`, `npm run typecheck` across workspaces and integration tests, targeted ESLint/Prettier, and `git diff --check`. These results establish the covered history-selection behavior; physical crash recovery and real-provider request acceptance remain unverified.

### Tested on

| OS | Status |
| :---: | :---: |
| 🍏 macOS | ✅ tested — local journal/HTTP-route fixtures and recorded build/type checks |
| 🪟 Windows | ⚠️ not tested |
| 🐧 Linux | ⚠️ not tested |

### Environment (optional)

Local Node.js/Vitest on macOS, with the real local managed journal, projection, and registered HTTP prompt routes; the model and remote store use mocks. The rebuilt CLI reports `0.26.4`.

## Risk & Scope

- Main risk or tradeoff: History grouping depends on recorded prompt ownership. Already generated compression summaries remain intact; this change does not retroactively erase information incorporated into a summary.
- Not validated / out of scope: No full Spring/MySQL/Broker/Worker SIGKILL rerun or real-provider acceptance test was performed. Broader cancellation-provenance policy and physical child-execution recovery are outside this change.
- Breaking changes / migration notes: No public API or persisted-schema change was identified in the reviewed commit, and it introduces no migration. The change selects model-visible context while preserving durable audit records.

## Linked Issues

Closed: #14256

### Evidence (Before & After)

| Prior Turn settlement | Before | After |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `cancelled / harness_interruption` | `['assistant', 'tool_result']` | `['user', 'assistant', 'tool_result']` |
| `cancelled / cancelled` | `['assistant', 'tool_result']` | `[]` |

四组定向测试在 rebase 后的源码上完成了最终验证，这些源码随后提交为 `7027abc3f62acf8fa43db44ac658d2e24dc86383`，记录结果如下：

```text
 Test Files  4 passed (4)
      Tests  905 passed (905)
```

已有记录还确认以下检查通过：`npm run build`、`npm run bundle`、覆盖 workspace 和 integration tests 的 `npm run typecheck`、定向 ESLint／Prettier，以及 `git diff --check`。这些结果证明了已覆盖的历史选择行为；实机崩溃恢复和真实 provider 请求验收仍未验证。

### Tested on

| :---: | :---: |
| 🍏 macOS | ✅ tested — 本地 journal／HTTP 路由 fixture，以及已有构建／类型检查记录 |

### Environment (optional)

macOS 上的本地 Node.js／Vitest 环境，使用真实本地 managed journal、projection 和已注册的 HTTP prompt 路由；模型及远端 store 使用 mock。重新构建的 CLI 版本为 `0.26.4`。

## Risk & Scope

- 主要风险或取舍：历史分组依赖已记录的 prompt 归属。已生成的压缩摘要保持完整；本次修改不会追溯擦除已纳入摘要的信息。

prs.title: feat(acp): surface retry and model-fallback progress to daemon clients
prs.body:
## What this PR does

The ACP turn loops used to drop provider recovery progress on the floor: a scheduled retry and a fallback-model switch were consumed for bookkeeping but never announced, so VS Code, the daemon HTTP API and Web Shell showed a bare spinner while the core was backing off (up to 60 s before the first rate-limit retry). This PR carries both events across the ACP boundary. The session emits `qwen/notify/session/retry` and `qwen/notify/session/model-fallback` vendor notifications from the shared model-round handler and the four direct response-stream consumers, mirroring the fields the interactive and headless front ends already render (attempt, maxRetries, delayMs, message; fromModel, toModel, statusCode, fallbackIndex). The bridge validates and rebroadcasts them as session-scoped `retry_scheduled` / `model_fallback` SSE frames with the current turn metadata, and the TypeScript SDK learns the two frame types so its event validator keeps them instead of dropping them as unknown.

Two scope notes. The passthrough stream wrapper that re-yields these events emits nothing itself, because the final consumer of the stream announces them; emitting in both places would double-notify. And rendering in Web Shell or the VS Code webview is deliberately left out: both consumers already ignore unknown frame types, so they can adopt the new frames in their own time.

## Why it's needed

From #12020: all front ends share the same retrying core, but only the CLIs tell the user about it. During the first 60 s rate-limit backoff, a daemon or IDE user sees nothing and reasonably concludes the session hung, then cancels and loses the eventual answer entirely.

## Reviewer Test Plan

### How to verify

Unit level: the new tests in the three packages pin each layer. The session test drives a stream yielding a retry event with `retryInfo` through `session/prompt` and asserts the notification payload (including that the `skipDelay` function never reaches the wire); sibling cases cover the bare-retry silence and the fallback payload. The bridge tests cover translation, optional-field omission, malformed-payload drop, and the no-live-session drop. The SDK tests cover narrowing, guard rejection, and the reducer no-op.

Live level: run the daemon, subscribe to a session's SSE stream, and drive a prompt against a model endpoint that fails once mid-stream with a rate-limit-shaped SSE error chunk (e.g. an `error_finish` chunk whose content carries `{"error":{"type":"rate_limit_error",...}}`, the DashScope/gateway shape; a tiny local proxy can inject it). Note that a request-level HTTP 429 status does NOT reach this path: `retryWithBackoff` wraps stream establishment and retries it silently, so the frame only fires for the mid-stream shape (measured on head: HTTP 429 -> turn recovers with zero frames). The stream should show a `retry_scheduled` frame with the attempt, budget and delay before the turn resumes, where before this change nothing appeared between the prompt and the resumed chunks.

### Evidence (Before & After)

N/A (daemon/ACP wire change; covered by unit tests on all platforms in CI).

### Tested on

|     OS     | Status |
| :--------: | :----: |
|  🍏 macOS  |   ✅   |
| 🪟 Windows |  N/A   |
|  🐧 Linux  |  N/A   |

### Environment (optional)

N/A (unit tests only)

### Current merge validation

Validated on the merge with main `7d99e7d26ee493b59293381e96d62e330d5f3773`, now at PR head `fe0b4a6682ca418eaaa75b92b45fe50a8757d9d9`.

- Full workspace build: passed.
- ACP session: **1441 passed**.
- ACP bridge: **1233 passed**.
- TypeScript SDK daemon events and UI normalizer: **556 passed**.
- Scoped typecheck for the ACP bridge, CLI and TypeScript SDK: passed.
- Integration-tests typecheck: passed.
- Prettier and ESLint on all changed files: passed.

The full typecheck was also run and stops in an unchanged mem0 integration test on a pre-existing nullable optional-value error. The same file is unchanged between the merge base and current upstream main, and it is outside this PR. The affected packages were checked separately as listed above; no unrelated product change was made to hide that baseline error.

## Risk & Scope

- Main risk or tradeoff: two new wire literals enter the daemon SSE vocabulary. They are additive; older SDK versions drop unknown frames silently, and Web Shell's mapper already ignores them.
- Not validated / out of scope: Web Shell and VS Code webview rendering; the bridge drops the notifications for sessions with no live entry rather than buffering them, since retry progress is only meaningful mid-turn.
- Breaking changes / migration notes: none.

## Linked Issues

Refs #12020 (first slice; rendering follow-ups stay open).

<details>
<summary>中文说明</summary>

## 这个 PR 做什么

ACP 回合循环此前会把供应商恢复进度直接丢掉：计划中的重试和回退模型切换只被用于内部簿记，从不对外通告，于是核心层在退避等待时（限流首次重试前最长 60 秒），VS Code、daemon HTTP API 和 Web Shell 只能显示一个没有任何文字的转圈。本 PR 把这两类事件带过 ACP 边界：会话层在共享 model-round 处理器和四个直接 response-stream 消费路径中发出 `qwen/notify/session/retry` 与 `qwen/notify/session/model-fallback` 厂商通知，字段与交互式和 headless 前端已展示的一致（attempt、maxRetries、delayMs、message；fromModel、toModel、statusCode、fallbackIndex）；bridge 校验后把它们转播为会话级 `retry_scheduled` / `model_fallback` SSE 帧，并带上当前回合元数据；TypeScript SDK 学会这两个帧类型，事件校验器不再把它们当未知帧丢弃。

两点范围说明：负责透传重抛这些事件的流式包装层自己不发通知，因为事件的最终消费者会发，两边都发会重复；Web Shell 和 VS Code webview 的渲染刻意不在本 PR 内，两个消费方本就会忽略未知帧类型，可以各自择期接入。

## 为什么需要

来自 #12020：所有前端共享同一个会自动重试的核心层，但只有 CLI 会把这件事告诉用户。在首次 60 秒限流退避期间，daemon 或 IDE 用户什么都看不到，合理结论就是"挂了"，于是取消，结果连同最终答案一起丢掉。

## 评审者测试计划

### 如何验证

单元层面：三个包的新测试各自钉住一层。会话测试让携带 `retryInfo` 的重试事件流过 `session/prompt`，断言通知载荷（包括 `skipDelay` 函数不会上线）；同组用例覆盖无 retryInfo 时的静默和回退载荷。bridge 测试覆盖转译、可选字段省略、畸形载荷丢弃和无存活会话丢弃。SDK 测试覆盖类型收窄、guard 拒绝和 reducer 空操作。

实际层面：启动 daemon，订阅某会话的 SSE 流，对一个在流式中途返回限流形态 SSE 错误块的模型端点发起 prompt（如 content 携带 `{"error":{"type":"rate_limit_error",...}}` 的 `error_finish` 块，即 DashScope/网关形态；本地小代理注入即可）。注意请求级 HTTP 429 状态码不走这条路径：`retryWithBackoff` 只包建流阶段并静默重试，实测该形态下回合恢复且 0 帧；只有流内错误形态才会触发该帧。在回合恢复前应能看到带 attempt、预算和延迟的 `retry_scheduled` 帧，而本改动之前 prompt 和后续 chunk 之间什么都没有。

### 证据（前后对比）

N/A（daemon/ACP 线缆协议改动；CI 在各平台跑单元测试）。

| 🪟 Windows |  N/A   |

### 当前合并验证

已在合并 main `7d99e7d26ee493b59293381e96d62e330d5f3773` 后验证，当前 PR head 为 `fe0b4a6682ca418eaaa75b92b45fe50a8757d9d9`。

- 全工作区构建通过。
- ACP session：**1441 passed**。
- ACP bridge：**1233 passed**。
- TypeScript SDK daemon events 与 UI normalizer：**556 passed**。
- ACP bridge、CLI 和 TypeScript SDK 的 scoped typecheck 通过。

## 风险与范围

- 主要风险或权衡：daemon SSE 词汇表新增两个线缆字面量。均为增量；旧版 SDK 会静默丢弃未知帧，Web Shell 的映射器本就会忽略。
- 未验证 / 范围外：Web Shell 与 VS Code webview 渲染；bridge 对无存活条目的会话直接丢弃通知而不缓冲，因为重试进度只在回合进行中才有意义。
- 破坏性变更 / 迁移说明：无。

关联 #12020（首个切片；渲染跟进项保持 open）。

prs.title: feat(web-shell): commit only the selected files from the commit view
prs.body:
## What this PR does

The Web Shell commit view can now commit a subset of the dirty files. It lists every uncommitted file with a checkbox, preselects all of them, and sends the selection with the commit. Unchecked files stay in the working tree, and work the user had already staged outside the selection stays staged instead of being swept in.

Underneath, the shared commit helper and the daemon commit route gained a `paths` option next to the existing `all` flag. The dialog no longer uses `all: true`; it always sends an explicit selection, and refuses to commit when nothing is selected instead of letting git fail on an empty pathspec.

Renames are handled explicitly: either half of a rename selects the pair, because git only records the rename when the deletion and the addition land in the same commit.

## Why it's needed

The commit view always committed everything. A single session that produced two unrelated changes (a bug fix and a refactor, say) could only be split into clean commits from a terminal, which defeats the point of having the dialog. The issue asks for per-file checkboxes so the Web Shell git workflow matches what the CLI already allows.

## Reviewer Test Plan

### How to verify

Unit and route tests cover the new behavior; no manual UI session was run. Reproduce the original gap by opening the commit view with two dirty files and pressing Commit — before this change both files are in the commit, after it only the checked ones are, and unchecking all of them surfaces a "select at least one file" error instead of a daemon call.

### Evidence (Before & After)

N/A — no screenshot or recording was captured for this run.

### Tested on

|     OS     | Status |
| :--------: | :----: |
|  🍏 macOS  |   ⚠️   |
| 🪟 Windows |   ⚠️   |
|  🐧 Linux  |   ⚠️   |

### Environment (optional)

Tests and lint run locally on macOS from a linked worktree; no `npm run dev` session.

## Risk & Scope

- Main risk or tradeoff: the dialog now depends on the diff listing to build a selection. If the list is empty or fails to load, it refuses to commit rather than falling back to committing everything, so a broken diff route blocks committing from the dialog (the CLI is unaffected).
- Not validated / out of scope: no manual UI verification on a running daemon, and no full `npm run build`. `packages/cli` typecheck was not run (fresh worktree reports unrelated TS6305 on unbuilt workspace dependencies); `packages/core` typecheck passes. `packages/web-shell` typecheck reports only the 12 known stale-SDK errors, which are identical on `origin/main`.
- Breaking changes / migration notes: none. `all: true` keeps its previous semantics.

## Linked Issues

Fixes #8446
