prs.title: feat(web-shell): add active highlight styling to selected reasoning e…
prs.body: ## What this PR does Adds an active highlight background to the currently selected reasoning effort row in the Web Shell composer popover. When the user opens the reasoning effort menu (Low / Medium / High / Extra High / Max), the row matching the active effort now receives a `var(--accent)` background with `var(--foreground)` text, making it visually obvious which level is selected. Previously, the only indicator was a small checkmark icon on a flat, unstyled row. ## Why it's needed The reasoning effort popover lists all available effort levels but does not visually distinguish the active one beyond a small checkmark. This makes it easy to overlook which effort is currently selected, especially in dark themes where the checkmark blends into the background. Adding an active highlight brings the effort selector in line with other active-item patterns in the codebase (e.g. `.dropdownItemActive`) and addresses the UI polish requested in #16563. ## Reviewer Test Plan ### How to verify 1. Run the application locally with `node scripts/dev.js serve --open`. 2. Open the Web Shell at `http://127.0.0.1:4170`. 3. In the composer toolbar, click the model/reasoning button to open the reasoning effort popover. 4. Confirm the currently selected effort row (e.g. "Max") has a visible accent-colored background highlight and the checkmark icon is visible. 5. Click a different effort level and confirm the highlight moves to the newly selected row. 6. Switch between dark and light themes and verify the highlight remains visible and readable in both. 7. Resize the viewport to a narrow width and confirm the highlight does not clip or overflow. ### Evidence (Before & After) Before After **Before:** The selected effort row shows only a checkmark icon on a plain dark background with no row highlight. **After:** The selected effort row receives a full-width accent background highlight (`var(--accent)`) with contrasting text, making the active selection immediately visible. ### Tested on | OS | Status | | :--------: | :----: | | 🍏 macOS | ⚠️ not tested | | 🪟 Windows | ✅ tested | | 🐧 Linux | ⚠️ not tested | ### Environment (optional) Local runtime via `node scripts/dev.js serve --open` on Windows 11. Verified in Chrome. Unit tests run with `npm --workspace=@qwen-code/web-shell test -- client/components/ChatEditor.test.tsx`. ## Risk & Scope - Main risk or tradeoff: None — CSS-only visual change scoped to `.reasoningEffortRowActive` with a matching className conditional in one component. - Not validated / out of scope: Mobile drawer layout (reasoning effort rows share the same component, so the highlight applies there too, but was not separately tested on a physical mobile device). - Breaking changes / migration notes: None. ## Linked Issues Refs #16563

prs.title: feat(managed-mcp): propose live-only selection capacity
prs.body:
> **Deferred:** The maintainer has selected the original limit of 32 historical MCP identities (including removed entries), with 16 enabled entries, for this delivery. Keep this alternative Draft; it is not being applied to #15119 or included in the parent conflict repairs.

## What this PR does

Draft capacity-policy follow-up to #15119: count at most 32 live MCP selections (enabled or disabled), retain removed entries for historical recovery, and keep the existing 16-enabled limit. The settings readers and public/WebShell snapshot contract agree on this alternative; the public contract advances to 1.90.0.

## Why it's needed

The parent deliberately limits the entire history to 32 distinct server identities, including removed entries. Long-lived Sessions can exhaust that budget while selecting few active servers. This PR proposes a different tradeoff; it is not an agreed bug fix and should stay Draft until that policy is accepted.

The earlier lower-revision re-add change has been withdrawn: the original Runtime still rejects a lower revision for the same server identity, including closed configurations. Settings admission now preserves that guard, so it cannot commit a request the original Runtime refuses. Resetting a definition lineage still requires a new server identity. The parent already includes the per-session pending-start fix in `0c9e9fdae186`; this PR no longer changes that code or claims it as a separate fix.

## Reviewer Test Plan

### How to verify

- Confirm the intended policy: 32 live selections rather than 32 historical identities, with removed records retained and 16 enabled connections unchanged.
- A snapshot containing 32 live selections and one removed record should satisfy the public contract; 33 live selections should be refused. A seventeenth enabled selection must still be refused.
- A lower definition revision for the same identity must still be refused after removal. The existing Runtime revision and original-operation recovery rules remain intact.
- Exercise the matching Harness, Java reader and API consumer together before accepting the new capacity policy. Regression sources are included but were not executed in this delivery.

### Evidence (Before & After)

Source inspection: the parent counts removed records toward the 32-identity bound; this proposal counts only live selections and retains tombstones. The earlier settings/Runtime revision mismatch has been removed. No execution or deployment acceptance is claimed.

### Tested on

| OS | Status |
| --- | --- |
| macOS | Not run at the user's request |
| Windows | Not run |
| Linux | Not run |

## Risk & Scope

- The policy is pending maintainer agreement. Keep this PR Draft; it is not a prerequisite correction that must be applied to #15119.
- Retained tombstones can grow beyond 32 entries but still face the existing 64 KiB serialized-record limit. This does not implement compaction or unlimited churn; the bound can still cause a record-store refusal.
- Older readers that enforce a 32-item total cannot read larger snapshots. All participating readers must be aligned before writing such a snapshot; downgrade compatibility is not supplied.
- No new database migration is introduced, but the public snapshot contract changes. When combining other API work, preserve their changelog entries and the highest contract version.
- No local tests, builds, lint, typechecks, formatting, dependency installation or CI waiting were performed. Execution evidence remains pending; the parent's results do not validate this alternative.

## Linked Issues

Refs #15079, #15084. Stacked on #15119 for review. If the capacity policy is accepted, land the parent first, then retarget this PR to `main` and reconcile the final diff before a separate merge.

<details>
<summary>中文说明</summary>

本 PR 已收窄为容量策略备选方案：最多 32 个有效 MCP 选择（enabled/disabled），继续保留 removed 墓碑和 16 个启用的上限。设置读取端、公开/WebShell 快照契约同步，API 版本为 1.90.0。#15119 原本有意限制 32 个历史身份；改为有效项上限需要确认，尚不是已经认可的缺陷修复，因此保持 Draft。

已撤回低版本重新添加的放宽：原 Runtime 会比较同一身份的历史 revision，仅放宽设置层会先提交再被 Runtime 拒绝。现在恢复一致的单调版本约束，重置定义谱系仍须新 server 身份。pending-start 的会话隔离已在父 PR 的 `0c9e9fdae186` 实现，本 PR 不再改动或重复认领。

保留记录仍受 64 KiB 上限约束，没有实现墓碑压缩。旧读取端无法读取总数超过 32 的快照，因此先升级相关读取端，再写入新状态；不承诺写入后降级兼容。回归源码已补，但未运行本地测试、构建、lint、typecheck、格式化、安装或等待 CI，真实运行验收仍待完成。

如接受此容量策略，先合入 #15119，再将本 PR 改为面向 main，检查最终差异后独立合入。

</details>

prs.title: test(web-shell): reset CPU throttle before the history-viewport live assertion
prs.body:
## What this PR does

Resets the 4x CPU throttle before the final "Scroll to bottom" phase of the 200-record history-viewport `@smoke` case, and gives the live-viewport assertion its own timeout instead of letting the global 20s expect window bound it. The 16-record sibling case is untouched: its restore is a no-op.

## Why it's needed

The case sets a 4x CDP CPU throttle for the 2,400-record fixture walk and never restores it, so the last step — send a background event, click Scroll to bottom, assert the live viewport shows the new answer — also runs at 4x throttle. That assertion is bounded by `expect.timeout` (20s, `playwright.config.ts:18`), not by the case's own `test.setTimeout`. When a loaded runner pushes the React commit past 20s, the assertion expires as `element(s) not found` while most of the test budget is still unspent — exactly the reported shape (`Expect "toContainText" with timeout 20000ms` inside `Test timeout of 120000ms exceeded`).

Raising the test budget (#15656, 120s → 300s) does not help: `test.setTimeout` and `expect.timeout` are independent budgets, so the assertion still gives up at 20s. This removes the coupling at its source rather than widening the budget again.

## Reviewer Test Plan

### How to verify

Run the case locally and confirm it still passes end to end:

```
cd packages/web-shell
npx playwright test client/e2e/web-shell.history-viewport.spec.ts --project=chromium -g "bounded 200-record" --workers=1
```

Expected: the case passes. The throttle reset is a no-op change for correctness on a quiet host — it changes headroom, not behaviour — so a green run is the check that the assertion still observes the live viewport.

### Evidence (Before & After)

Before: the throttle is set at the top of the case and never reset, so the final phase runs throttled; the final assertion carries only the global 20s `expect.timeout`.

After: `Emulation.setCPUThrottlingRate` is restored to `rate: 1` immediately before the Scroll to bottom click, and the final `toContainText` is given its own `timeout` so a genuinely slow commit is reported as an assertion timeout rather than consuming the test budget.

### Tested on

|     OS     | Status |
| :--------: | :----: |
|  🍏 macOS  |   ✅   |
| 🪟 Windows |   N/A  |
|  🐧 Linux  |   ⚠️    |

CI-only Playwright spec; the local run was macOS. The Linux lane is where the flake showed up, so the CI smoke job is the confirmation that matters there.

### Environment (optional)

Local Playwright run against the repo's own vite dev server, chromium project, single worker.

## Risk & Scope

- Main risk or tradeoff: the 200-record case now runs its final phase without CPU throttling, so it no longer exercises a throttled click-to-live transition. The throttled walk (the expensive part, and the reason the throttle exists) is unchanged. If a throttled live transition is something worth covering, it should be its own case rather than a side effect of this one.
- Not validated / out of scope: the underlying cause of a slow React commit on a loaded runner (host contention) is not addressed; this only stops it from failing on an assertion window that is 6x smaller than the case budget. Not run on Windows or Linux locally.
- Breaking changes / migration notes: none.

### Note on the `ECONNREFUSED 127.0.0.1:4170` log line

The report lists that proxy error as a possible trigger. It is structural: the mock daemon has no `GET /workspace/models` handler, so the request falls through the spec's route and is proxied to a daemon port that nothing listens on. A local run of this spec reproduces the warning on every green case, which rules it out as the failure cause.

## Linked Issues

Fixes #15697

prs.title: fix(web-shell): keep transcript visible during session resync
prs.body:
## What this PR does

Web Shell keeps the current conversation visible while it reloads the same session after ring eviction or an event epoch reset. Once the replacement snapshot arrives, it applies the reset and replay together. The recovery warning reports the reason supplied by the transport, so cursor loss is distinguishable from ring eviction.

## Why it's needed

Web Shell currently clears the transcript before waiting for the reload. During that wait, users can see a blank message area even though their conversation is still stored.

## Reviewer Test Plan

### How to verify

1. From the repository root, run `npm run test -w @qwen-code/web-shell -- client/daemon/session/DaemonSessionProvider.test.tsx -t 'keeps visible messages'`.
2. The two cases start with a visible user message, inject either ring eviction or an epoch reset, and hold the reload pending. Confirm that the original message stays visible while the reload is pending.
3. Release the replacement snapshot and confirm that the replayed message replaces the original without duplication.

### Evidence (Before & After)

| Before | After |
| --- | --- |
| Both delayed-load cases received an empty transcript while the reload was pending. | Both delayed-load cases retained the original message until the snapshot arrived. All 530 tests in the provider suite passed. |

Chromium end-to-end test with a mocked daemon. Both screenshots show the same point in time while the replacement load is held pending. The baseline shows a loading skeleton and the patched build shows the existing message.

prs.title: feat(acp): display teammate activity without affecting leader output [13902 C/3]
prs.body:
Stack: **[#15657](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/15657) → [#15658](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/15658) → [#15659](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/15659)**. This is **C**, based on B (`split/13902-team-coordination`, `435e4f949eca7232c2b48d3a259f5083cb788b8a`), which depends on A (`3294001f39040a668fcbad20045b64e03dc1b6e6`). Base branch: `split/13902-team-coordination`. Split from #13902 at source commit `6ed7884c381dfe1c59bd975d6cf61dbb41ef441c`; candidate C: `1d6bc91dd3cf29e2010043e397ea8c429b72cf03`. Review C against B.

## What this PR does

Shows teammate tool progress and inter-agent messages as attributed activity notices. Tool activity names the acting teammate. An inter-agent message carries the recipient in `agent` and the sender in structured `author`, with direction shown in the message text. Failed tool results retain their failure status and description.

These frames are observational: they bypass the durable peer notification queue, do not wake the leader and are not persisted. The SDK classifies them as status notices, coalesces bounded tool progress while retaining discrete message/failure rows, and keeps the active leader text and usage stream intact. Web Shell renders the notices; child-session result collection and qwen-live filter this display source while retaining valid background responses. C reuses A's identity contract and B's sink/session lifecycle, and includes the activity and downstream-filter tests.

## Why it's needed

Durable reports tell the leader what a teammate concluded, but give the client little visibility while work is in progress. Display-only activity provides that visibility without scheduling a model turn for every tool call or mixing teammate traffic into the leader's answer and usage.

## Reviewer Test Plan

### How to verify

1. Verify candidate C and its B parent, build the candidate, then run C's focused CLI, SDK, Web Shell and qwen-live tests serially. Re-run the core coordination harness as a regression check for the changed producer. Run each `../../node_modules/.bin/vitest run <package-relative paths>` command from its package directory. The build exited 0; all 9 focused/regression test files passed, as detailed below.
2. Stream leader text and usage while a teammate emits tool calls/results and an inter-agent message. Confirm that activity appears as notices, leaves leader text continuous, keeps usage attached to the leader, and never queues an automatic turn or a persisted notification.
3. Check failed-tool display and message direction. Exercise repeated activity, user/branch boundaries and discrete message/failure rows; confirm bounded coalescing and stable origin event IDs.
4. Confirm that child-session result collection and qwen-live exclude `teammate_activity`, while the positive `background_notification_response` control remains visible.

### Evidence (Before & After)

On candidate `1d6bc91dd3cf29e2010043e397ea8c429b72cf03`, `npm run build` exited 0. The 8 directly changed test files passed **1772 tests**: CLI 1404, SDK 46, Web Shell 315 and qwen-live 7. The additional core coordination-harness regression file passed **99 tests**. Combined result: **9 test files, 1871 passed, no failures**. Runtime, UI E2E and standalone typecheck have not been run; matched before/after protocol and UI evidence is not available. This PR remains a draft. C's complete tree equals the fixed source tree, but tree equality does not establish runtime correctness or resolve inherited feedback. Historical passing counts from #13902 are not acceptance evidence for C.

### Tested on

| OS | Status |
| :---: | :---: |
| 🍏 macOS | ✅ Build and 9 focused/regression test files passed; runtime/UI E2E and standalone typecheck not run |
| 🪟 Windows | ⚠️ Not tested |
| 🐧 Linux | ⚠️ Not tested |

### Environment (optional)

Local isolated worktree; repository-root build followed by serial package-local Vitest runs completed.

## Risk & Scope

- Main risk or tradeoff: activity is ephemeral and disappears on reload; durable reports and roster notices remain B's responsibility. Attribution direction, coalescing boundaries and downstream source filtering require separate verification.
- Not validated / out of scope: exact-SHA runtime/UI and cross-platform validation are pending. This split preserves source behavior and does not repair its unresolved feedback.
- Breaking changes / migration notes: adds a teammate activity event/source and optional direction/tool metadata. No transcript migration is introduced because observational activity is not recorded.

Inherited unresolved feedback owned by C is not fixed by splitting:

- [R9-1: the recipient identity of an inter-agent message is interpreted as its author by the UI teammate prop/documentation](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/13902#discussion_r4372372663).
- [R9-6: activity-specific structured fields are not reflected in the persistence schema declarations](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/13902#discussion_r4372372680).

A's two replay findings and B's six coordination/test findings are also inherited through the stack; ownership remains with those layers.

Design: [English](docs/design/2026-10-11-agent-team-identity-projection.md) · [中文](docs/design/2026-10-11-agent-team-identity-projection.zh-CN.md). C restores the fixed source's paired documents, including the activity decisions, constraints, acceptance criteria and known gaps. The cumulative tree, including these documents, equals source commit `6ed7884c381dfe1c59bd975d6cf61dbb41ef441c`.

## Linked Issues

Related: #13785. Split source: #13902. This PR remains a draft. No automatic issue or PR closure is requested.

Stack links:

- A: [#15657](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/15657) — transitive prerequisite.
- B: [#15658](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/15658) — direct prerequisite.
- C: [#15659](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/15659) — this PR.

<details>
<summary>中文说明</summary>

堆叠顺序：**[#15657](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/15657) → [#15658](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/15658) → [#15659](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/15659)**。本 PR 是 **C**，基于 B（`split/13902-team-coordination`，`435e4f949eca7232c2b48d3a259f5083cb788b8a`）；B 依赖 A（`3294001f39040a668fcbad20045b64e03dc1b6e6`）。以 `split/13902-team-coordination` 为 base。拆分来源 #13902，固定源提交 `6ed7884c381dfe1c59bd975d6cf61dbb41ef441c`；C 候选为 `1d6bc91dd3cf29e2010043e397ea8c429b72cf03`。请相对 B 评审 C。

### 本 PR 做什么

将队友工具进展和 agent 间消息展示为带归因的活动通知。工具活动标识执行队友。agent 间消息通过 `agent` 携带接收方，通过结构化 `author` 携带发送方，正文展示消息方向。失败工具结果保留失败状态及描述。

这些帧只供观察：不进入持久 peer 通知队列，不唤醒 leader，也不持久化。SDK 将其分类为 status 通知，有界合并工具进展并保留离散消息/失败行，同时保持 leader 正文及 usage 流连续。Web Shell 渲染通知；子会话结果收集和 qwen-live 过滤该展示来源，同时保留合法后台响应。C 复用 A 的身份契约及 B 的 sink/会话生命周期，包含活动及下游过滤测试。

### 为什么需要

持久报告告诉 leader 队友的结论，但客户端在工作进行时缺少可见进展。仅展示的活动提供这种可见性，无需为每次工具调用调度模型轮次，也不会把队友流量混入 leader 答复和 usage。

### 评审测试计划

1. 核对 C 候选及其 B 父提交，构建候选，再串行执行 C 的 CLI、SDK、Web Shell 和 qwen-live 聚焦测试。对于变化的生产者，额外重跑 core coordination harness 作为回归检查。每条 `../../node_modules/.bin/vitest run <包内相对路径>` 命令从对应包目录执行。构建退出码为 0；9 个聚焦/回归测试文件全部通过，详见下文。
2. 在 leader 持续输出正文和 usage 时，让队友发出工具调用/结果及 agent 间消息。确认活动显示为通知，leader 正文保持连续，usage 仍归属 leader，且活动不排入自动轮次或持久通知。
3. 检查失败工具展示及消息方向。覆盖重复活动、用户/branch 边界及离散消息/失败行，确认有界合并及稳定 origin event ID。
4. 确认子会话结果收集和 qwen-live 排除 `teammate_activity`，同时正向对照 `background_notification_response` 仍可见。

**前后证据：**候选 `1d6bc91dd3cf29e2010043e397ea8c429b72cf03` 的 `npm run build` 退出码为 0。8 个直接差异测试文件共通过 **1772 项测试**：CLI 1404、SDK 46、Web Shell 315、qwen-live 7。额外 core coordination-harness 回归文件通过 **99 项测试**。合计 **9 个测试文件、1871 项通过、无失败**。未运行 runtime、UI E2E 或独立 typecheck，也没有匹配的协议和 UI 前后证据。本 PR 保持 draft。C 完整树与固定源树相等，但树相等不能证明运行时正确，也不能解决继承反馈。#13902 的历史通过数不能作为 C 的验收证据。

**测试平台：**macOS 构建及 9 个聚焦/回归测试文件通过，未运行 runtime/UI E2E 或独立 typecheck；Windows、Linux 未测试。

**环境：**本地隔离 worktree；仓库根目录构建及各包目录内的串行 Vitest 已完成。

### 风险与范围

- 主要风险或取舍：活动是临时的，重载后消失；持久报告和成员通知仍由 B 负责。归因方向、合并边界及下游来源过滤需要分别验证。
- 未验证或范围外：精确 SHA 的运行时/UI 及跨平台验证待完成。本拆分保留源行为，不修复其未解决反馈。
- 兼容性与迁移：新增 teammate activity 事件/来源及可选方向/工具元数据。观察性活动不录制，因此不引入 transcript 迁移。

C 负责的以下继承反馈未因拆分而修复：

- [R9-1：agent 间消息的接收者身份被 UI teammate prop/文档解释为作者](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/13902#discussion_r4372372663)。

prs.title: fix(acp): schedule managed skill review on ACP turns
prs.body:
## What this PR does

Runs the managed skill review on ACP turns (`qwen serve`, daemon, the ACP-bridged CLIs) the same way the interactive CLI does, instead of leaving the trigger state accumulating and unread. The auto-skill gate that used to be inlined in the client's post-turn memory tasks is now a small public method, and ACP's post-turn path calls it in the branch where ACP — not the client — owns that work.

## Why it's needed

`Session.runTool()` calls `recordCompletedToolCall()` on every completed tool, which increments `LlmClient.toolCallCount` and sets `skillsModifiedInSession`. Those two fields exist only to feed `MemoryManager.scheduleSkillReview()`. On the interactive path that call happens inside `runManagedAutoMemoryBackgroundTasks()`; ACP's `Session` never calls that method — it schedules Extract and Dream itself in `#recordPromptCompletionEffects()` and stops there. So on `qwen serve` the counter only ever grew, `AUTO_SKILL_THRESHOLD` was never evaluated, and a long daemon session never produced an auto-skill candidate while reporting nothing about it. The design doc for the ACP auto-memory work recorded this as deliberately deferred by that PR; the issue asks for it to be closed, and a maintainer review of the same issue agreed the extraction is the right shape.

## Reviewer Test Plan

### How to verify

Unit level: on `origin/main`, `packages/cli/src/acp-integration/session/Session.test.ts` has no test that reaches skill review, and `runManagedAutoSkillReview` does not exist. With this branch:

```
cd packages/core && npx vitest run src/core/client.test.ts -t autoSkill
cd packages/cli && npx vitest run src/acp-integration/session/Session.test.ts -t "managed auto-memory"
```

Expected: the new ACP case asserts the post-turn branch calls `runManagedAutoSkillReview()` exactly once and still does not call `runManagedAutoMemoryBackgroundTasks()`; the new core cases assert the extracted method reads the live `toolCallCount` and no-ops when `getAutoSkillEnabled()` is false.

Removing the one added line in `Session.ts` and re-running the ACP case fails it (`toHaveBeenCalledOnce()` on the new method), which is the regression this PR closes.

### Evidence (Before & After)

N/A — no user-visible surface changes; the observable effect is `.qwen/pending-skills/` receiving staged candidates after enough tool calls on a served session, which needs an enabled auto-skill setting and a real model round to reach.

### Tested on

|     OS     | Status |
| :--------: | :----: |
|  🍏 macOS  |   ✅   |
| 🪟 Windows |   ⚠️   |
|  🐧 Linux  |   ⚠️   |

### Environment (optional)

Unit tests only; `packages/core` was built with `scripts/build_package.js` so the CLI suite could import it.

## Risk & Scope

- Main risk or tradeoff: the legacy ACP branch now schedules work it did not before. It is gated by `getAutoSkillEnabled()`, which is opt-in (`memory.enableAutoSkill`, off by default), false in bare/safe mode, and false under a shell sandbox. With `autoSkillConfirm` at its default (true), a review only stages new skills in `.qwen/pending-skills/` — the artifact the TUI accept/discard dialog reads — so it cannot silently write into a skills root.
- Not validated / out of scope: ACP has no accept/reject surface for pending skills (that is a separate product decision, tracked as a follow-up); the review still fires at user-turn boundaries only, so a threshold crossed mid-turn is deferred to the next turn rather than dropped. Not exercised: a live `qwen serve` session with a real model round, and Windows/Linux.
- Breaking changes / migration notes: none.

## Linked Issues

Fixes #12209

prs.title: fix(ci): self-heal ephemeral runner slots wedged by orphaned resource piles
prs.body:
## What this PR does

Teaches the ephemeral runner manager to recover a slot whose leftover Docker resources cannot be attributed to a single runner identity. When a slot has no recorded state, every leftover container and network belongs to a dead cycle, so the manager now sweeps the whole pile without a GitHub identity instead of aborting. Afterwards it deletes registrations that match the slot's naming scheme, but only when every removed resource carried this slot's identity prefix and GitHub already reports the registration offline. Foreign or missing identity labels, and online registrations, keep the conservative manual-reconciliation path. Orphan log archives are named so log pruning still recognizes them.

## Why it's needed

During the 2026-11-08 hz4 incident, Docker bridge address-pool exhaustion made `docker create` fail after containers were already created, leaving several `Created` containers with different instance labels per slot and no slot state. Identity recovery refused to pick one label ("Container labels disagree about the runner identity"), so 15 of 30 slots stalled for 960 identical retries each and the whole ephemeral pool went offline until an operator manually removed every container, network, and registration. The pool must self-heal from this state: the resources are provably orphans, and requiring human cleanup turns a transient Docker failure into a pool-wide outage. This complements #16608 (API backoff on rate limits), which addresses a different failure mode of the same incident.

## Reviewer Test Plan

### How to verify

Run the manager unit suite: `node --test scripts/ci/ephemeral-runner/manager.test.mjs` (no dependencies needed). Confirm the new tests: a multi-identity orphan pile without slot state is fully swept, its offline orphaned registration is deleted, and the slot replenishes in the same cycle; an online registration matching the slot name is never deleted; a foreign-labeled resource is removed from the slot namespace but registration sweeping stays blocked until the pile is gone; while Docker refuses removals nothing is registered and the failure keeps reporting. Existing conservative paths (recorded-state identity mismatch, ambiguous runner ids, rejected deletions) are unchanged.

### Evidence (Before & After)

N/A — infrastructure manager logic, covered by unit tests (40/40 passing locally).

|  🍏 macOS  |   ✅   |
| 🪟 Windows |  N/A   |
|  🐧 Linux  |   ⚠️   |

### Environment (optional)

Node.js `node:test` only; no Docker or GitHub access required by the suite.

## Risk & Scope

- Main risk or tradeoff: the identity-less sweep deletes GitHub registrations by naming scheme; it is gated on every removed resource carrying this slot's identity prefix and on the registration being offline, and each deletion still rejects ambiguous ids. Deletion rejection (e.g. HTTP 422 while GitHub considers a runner busy) throws and retries next cycle.
- Not validated / out of scope: live-host rehearsal on hz4 (the pool was already manually reconciled); API rate-limit backoff is handled by #16608.
- Breaking changes / migration notes: none; slots with a recorded identity keep the exact previous behavior.

## Linked Issues

auto_merge.commit_title: fix(ci): self-heal ephemeral runner slots wedged by orphaned resource piles (#16628)
auto_merge.commit_message:
* fix(ci): self-heal ephemeral runner slots wedged by orphaned resource piles

When a slot has no recorded state, every leftover container and network
is an orphan of a dead cycle. Identity recovery used to abort the whole
cleanup when their labels disagreed, which wedged 15 of 30 hz4 slots in
960 identical retries each after Docker address-pool exhaustion left
several Created containers per slot. The manager now sweeps such piles
without a GitHub identity, then deletes only offline registrations that
match the slot naming scheme and only when every removed resource
carried this slot's identity prefix; online or foreign-identified
resources keep the conservative manual-reconciliation path.

Co-authored-by: Qwen-Coder <qwen-coder@alibabacloud.com>

* fix(ci): keep the HTTP status of a rejected orphan-sweep deletion

The identity-less registration sweep rewrapped a failed DELETE in a
fresh Error without copying .status, the same shape wenshao flagged on
the recorded-state cleanup path in #16608. A 403/429 during the sweep
would be classified as an ordinary failure once the exponential-backoff
change lands on main, retrying five times as frequently at the cap
during exactly the rate-limit storm the ladder exists for.

Copy the status (and the cause) through the rewrap and pin it with a
sweep-path test asserting the escaped error carries .status 429.

Co-authored-by: Qwen-Coder <qwen-coder@alibabacloud.com>

* fix(ci): sweep orphan registrations before resource removal so rejected deletions retry

A rejected registration DELETE in the identity-less sweep promised a
next-cycle retry, but after the pile was removed the slot had neither
state nor leftovers, so cleanup never ran again and the registration
leaked forever. Sweep registrations before removing the resources: the
leftover pile keeps the retry reachable. Only sweep registrations GitHub
explicitly reports offline; a missing status no longer fails open. Pin
the destructive guards with regression tests: rejected-delete retry,
status-less registrations kept, prefix siblings and other slots never
swept, and orphan log archives stay prunable.

Co-authored-by: Qwen-Coder <qwen-coder@alibabacloud.com>

* docs(ci): align the ephemeral runner runbook and design with the self-healing sweep

The runbook and both design translations still said disagreeing labels
block the slot for manual reconciliation; the code sweeps such a pile
and only foreign or missing labels block registration sweeping. State
the actual contract, the offline-only and identity-prefix gates, the
sweep-before-removal retry ordering, and the unique-poolId-per-host
premise the naming-scheme deletion relies on.

Co-authored-by: Qwen-Coder <qwen-coder@alibabacloud.com>

* test(ci): pin the 429 sweep retry and the identity-blocked sweep

The self-healing sweep's destructive guards gained pins for the shapes the
previous commit introduced; two probe shapes were still unpinned:

- a DELETE refused with 429 while the orphan pile is still on disk must name
  the retry, leave the registration alive and create no replacement, and the
  next cycle must delete that same runner before the slot replenishes.
- a foreign or missing instance label blocks registration sweeping even for
  this slot's own offline registration: no DELETE at all, no replenishment,
  and another slot's registration plus an online one survive.

Also cross-reference the three copies of the slot naming scheme (slot-state
validation, the sweep's owned filter, the label-recovery matcher), so a change
to one of them cannot leave the other two guessing.

---------

Co-authored-by: Qwen-Coder <qwen-coder@alibabacloud.com>
Co-authored-by: Shaojin Wen <shaojin.wensj@alibaba-inc.com>

prs.title: fix(ci): distinguish missing logs from missing test results
prs.body:
## What this PR does

Failure summaries now show how many downloaded log files were analyzed compared with the number of jobs reported as failed. For example, a run with two failed jobs and one supplied log reports `1 of 2 failed-job logs (incomplete coverage)`, while retaining the available job, step and test details.

The update follows the current reporting flow shared by tracking issues and PR comments. It preserves workflow-based issue aggregation and the existing statement that no test identifier was available when no failure can be recognized.

## Why it's needed

Missing or empty log downloads can hide useful failure evidence. The report should show that limitation without treating missing evidence as proof that tests did not run. Equal input and failed-job counts do not certify complete log contents or a complete list of failing tests.

## Reviewer Test Plan

### How to verify

With one failed job and no supplied logs, expect `0 of 1` and an incomplete-coverage notice. A supplied zero-byte log counts as one input. With two failed jobs and one log containing a recognizable failing test, expect `1 of 2` while keeping the test, job details and run link. More supplied logs than recorded failed jobs also produce a mismatch notice.

When the job list is empty or unavailable, expect that uncertainty to remain explicit. Successful, cancelled and timed-out jobs are excluded from the failed-job count. A summary without an identified test continues to direct readers to the run logs and annotations.

### Evidence (Before & After)

N/A — no CLI/TUI change. The local reporting-command regressions below cover the generated issue and PR summary text.

- Six real `analyze → comment` CLI regressions: 6 failed on the unmodified upstream helper, 6 passed with this change. Each case uses temporary files and real Node subprocesses; no mocks were added.
- Complete helper suite on Windows: 60 passed, 4 skipped, 4 failed. An independent run of the unmodified upstream helper reproduced the same four Flyway path-encoding failures.
- Reporting workflow suite: 33 passed, 43 failed. The unmodified upstream helper and tests reproduce the exact same 43 failing test names; failures involve Windows/Bash paths, environment variables and unavailable `jq`.
- Scoped ESLint, Prettier and whitespace checks passed.
- The frozen dependency install completed its normal prepare lifecycle, including the full build and bundle (exit 0). Existing native-audio, bundle-size and Node deprecation warnings remain visible in the log.
- The complete typecheck, including every workspace and integration tests, passed after the build (exit 0). The full preflight is not claimed green because the helper and workflow suites retain the baseline failures disclosed above.

### Tested on

| OS | Status |
| --- | --- |
| macOS | Not tested |
| Windows | Tested |
| Linux | Not tested |

### Environment

Node.js 24.15.0, pinned pnpm 11.24.0. Local Node subprocesses and temporary files; no live failure report was published.

## Risk & Scope

- The count describes input files rather than their content completeness.
- Hosted CI and Linux/macOS execution remain unverified locally.
- The change retains the upstream workflow, issue aggregation and report destinations; no configuration or data migration is required.

## AI assistance

Codex assisted with the implementation, real-process regression tests, documentation and validation. Independent Codex verification checked the actual workflow call path and upstream test baselines.

## Linked Issues

Addresses the log-availability finding in #11115.

prs.title: feat(core): copy .worktreeinclude paths into new worktrees
prs.body:
## What this PR does

Adds support for a repository-level `.worktreeinclude` file: a committed, gitignore-syntax list of ignored paths that are copied from your main checkout into every worktree the CLI creates.

A `git worktree add` checkout contains only tracked files, so gitignored local state — `.env`, `appsettings.Development.json`, local certificates — is absent. This PR reads `.worktreeinclude` at the repository root (one pattern per line, `#` comments, blank lines skipped), matches those patterns against git's own ignored set, and copies the matches into the new checkout while preserving directory structure.

Patterns are only ever matched against `git ls-files --others --ignored --exclude-standard`, never expanded from disk. That keeps tracked files, `.git` internals and paths outside the repository unreachable by construction: the worst a committed pattern can do is select a file git already lists as ignored. The listing is recursive, so a pattern naming a fully-ignored directory selects the files inside it rather than a directory entry that can't be copied.

The copy runs on both creation paths — `createUserWorktree` (the `--worktree` flag, the `enter_worktree` tool, and `agent` worktree isolation) and `setupWorktrees` (Agent Arena) — so one committed file covers every worktree family. It is non-fatal throughout: a missing or unreadable file, an oversized one, or an individual copy failure leaves the worktree usable without those files. The file is capped at 1 MB and 10,000 patterns because it is committed input that anyone with push access can change, and each pattern costs time against every ignored file.

## Why it's needed

Agents working in a worktree routinely need local, never-committed files — an API key in `.env`, a machine-specific dev config — and today every new worktree requires manual setup or a custom provisioning script. Running several isolated agents in parallel multiplies that cost. This is the last unimplemented item from the worktree design's advanced list (the `.worktreeinclude` row in `docs/design/worktree.md`), and it is tracked as #10584.

## Reviewer Test Plan

### How to verify

In a scratch repository that ignores `.env` and `.local/`:

1. Create `.env`, `.local/top.txt` and `.local/sub/deep.txt` in the main checkout, plus a `.worktreeinclude` containing `.env` and `.local/`.
2. Create a worktree (`qwen --worktree=one`, or `createUserWorktree('one', 'main')` directly).
3. The new checkout contains all three files with the source contents; a gitignored path not named in the file (try `secrets/*.json`) is absent.
4. Delete `.worktreeinclude` and create another worktree: nothing is copied and the worktree still succeeds.

The new integration test file pins those four outcomes plus a negation (`!config/example.json`), a tracked file named by a pattern (not copied twice / not selected at all), the size cap, and a `.worktreeinclude` that is a directory.

### Evidence (Before & After)

Before: `packages/core/src/services/gitWorktreeService.ts` copied only untracked files in `setupWorktrees`; `createUserWorktree` copied nothing. After: both paths copy the resolved `.worktreeinclude` set.

```
$ cd packages/core && npx vitest run src/services/gitWorktreeService.worktreeinclude.integ.test.ts \
    src/services/gitWorktreeService.test.ts src/services/gitWorktreeService.symlinks.integ.test.ts
 ✓ ... (13 tests) / (41 tests) / (15 tests)
 Test Files  3 passed (3)
      Tests  69 passed (69)
```

`npx tsc --noEmit -p packages/core/tsconfig.json` and `npx eslint` on the touched files pass.

### Tested on

|     OS     | Status |
| :--------: | :----: |
|  🍏 macOS  |   ✅   |
| 🪟 Windows |   ⚠️   |
|  🐧 Linux  |   ⚠️   |

macOS only. Windows and Linux not run locally; the copy path is plain `fs` with repository-relative paths from git, and CI covers the rest.

### Environment (optional)

N/A — unit and integration tests only (real `git` against temp repos).

## Risk & Scope

- Main risk or tradeoff: a committed `.worktreeinclude` lets anyone with push access decide which ignored files a clone copies into its worktrees. The blast radius is bounded to gitignored files that already exist in the source checkout, but a pattern reaching a large ignored tree (a build cache) would copy it per worktree with no size limit. That tradeoff is documented in the user docs' Limitations section.
- Not validated / out of scope: symlinks among the ignored files are copied as whatever `fs.copyFile` does with them (the link target's contents), not recreated as links. Worktrees created before a line is added do not retroactively receive the file.
- Breaking changes / migration notes: none. Without a `.worktreeinclude`, behaviour is unchanged.

## Linked Issues

Fixes #10584

prs.title: fix(core): name the loop detector in forked agent stop messages
prs.body:
## What this PR does

Background memory agents that stop on loop detection have been reporting the generic "duplicate tool-call loop detected" sentence, while the interactive path names the detector that actually fired. This carries the detector through the fork path so the background message reads the same way: the headless agent exposes which loop detector fired, the forked-agent result carries it, and the wording helper interpolates it when it is present.

## Why it's needed

The detector name is the whole point of the attribution added for #9450: `duplicate tool-call loop detected` alone does not tell an operator whether it was repeated identical calls, read-file looping, action stagnation, or another detector. An unattended background agent is exactly the case where nobody watched the stop happen, so the name is worth more there than in the foreground. The gap was tracked as #13519 and called "a reasonable follow-up" by a maintainer in review of #13466.

The change is plumbing only. The forked path already reads the terminate mode at the same point; it simply never read the loop type, and the helper never received it.

## Reviewer Test Plan

### How to verify

`packages/core/src/agents/runtime/terminate-reason.test.ts` covers the new parameter directly: supplying a detector yields `Agent stopped: duplicate tool-call loop detected (action_stagnation).`, and passing `null` keeps the generic wording. `packages/core/src/agents/forkedAgent.agent.test.ts` feeds a stubbed headless that reports `LOOP_DETECTED` with `CONSECUTIVE_IDENTICAL_TOOL_CALLS` and asserts the result carries the detector, and `agent-headless.test.ts` asserts `getLoopType()` returns the firing detector on the frozen-board case from #9450 and `null` after a re-executed run clears it.

### Evidence (Before & After)

N/A — no user-visible surface changes; the message text is already user-visible and only gains the parenthesised detector name that the interactive path already prints.

### Tested on

|     OS     | Status |
| :--------: | :----: |
|  🍏 macOS  |   ✅   |
| 🪟 Windows |   ⚠️   |
|  🐧 Linux  |   ⚠️   |

### Environment (optional)

Unit tests from `packages/core`, after building that package locally.

## Risk & Scope

- Main risk or tradeoff: `ForkedAgentResult.loopType` is a new optional field, so existing callers are unaffected; the private field on `AgentHeadless` narrows from `string` to `LoopType`, which its only assignment already satisfies. The six memory call sites read the field only through `terminateReasonMessage`, so their message text changes only for loop-detected stops, where it now names the detector.
- Not validated / out of scope: no full `npm run build`, no repository-wide test run, and no Windows or Linux verification. `packages/cli` was not rebuilt or tested, since no CLI code changed.
- Breaking changes / migration notes: none. The new result field is optional and the helper's third parameter is optional.

## Linked Issues

Fixes #13519

issues.body:
I searched existing issues and found no duplicate. #4729 covers MCP tool names only.

**What happened**

With `provider = anthropic`, a session works until the model calls `tool_search` and the deferred tool `web.run` is added to `tools`. From then on every request fails:

```
Anthropic Messages API request failed: Invalid request (400): tools.22.custom.name: String should match pattern '^[a-zA-Z0-9_-]{1,128}$'
```

`web.run` contains a dot, so Anthropic rejects it. The tool stays in the toolbox, so every retry fails the same way. Expected: the request is accepted (names mapped to the provider's pattern, or such tools not offered).

**What I checked**

I pointed `[providers.anthropic] base_url` at a local server that logs request bodies (the Anthropic API was not contacted):

| request | tools | invalid names |
|---|---|---|
| 1st (startup) | 15 | none |
| 2nd, after `tool_search` "web search fetch url browse internet" returned `Web`, `web.run`, `session_search`, `Git`, `github`, `automation`, `finance`, `grep_files` | 23 | `tools.22` = `web.run` |
| same, with `--disable web_search` | 23 | none |

`web.run` is the only one of the 23 names that fails the pattern.

**Steps to reproduce**

1. Configure `[providers.anthropic]` with `model = "claude-sonnet-5-5"` and a saved API key.
2. Run `codewhale` and ask something that needs the web, e.g. "research what is new about X online".
3. The model calls `tool_search`, then the next request returns the 400 above.

Workaround: `codewhale --disable web_search`.

**Environment**

codewhale 0.10.2 (ff466b2ed0bf), npm install, macOS 26.6.2 arm64, TUI (also reproduced with `codewhale exec --auto`), anthropic / claude-sonnet-5-5.

prs.title: fix(engine): bound nested brace expansion and repeated globstars
prs.body:
## What and why

Two problems from the review on #7215 that it merged with, both in `matches_glob` and both from my change there.

The 64-combination cap counted each brace group only up to its first `}`, so a nested group hid its commas. `{{a},c0,c1,c2,c3,c4,c5,c6,c7,c8,c9}` repeated ten times counted as one combination and expanded to 11^10 patterns for every file. Expansion now counts the patterns it actually produces and gives up at 64, which leaves the pattern literal, as an over-limit pattern was before.

A run of `**/` multiplied the tail search: `**/` ten times then `x/b`, against a 30-deep path, didn't finish. A run that starts the pattern being matched now collapses to one `**/`. A run after a plain directory gets there once that directory is consumed, and one after a wildcard, as in `src*/**/**/file.rs`, keeps the path it took before. Collapsing every run anywhere, as the first commit here did, changed `src/**/**/src` to match `src` itself and stopped `src*/**/**/file.rs` matching `src1/a/b/file.rs`.

Expansion also went down every first alternative before counting a leaf, one stack frame per level. More than 64 `{` now leaves the pattern literal before expanding. 8000 nested groups were reported to overflow a 2 MiB thread; the tests run with a 16 MiB stack, where it didn't overflow, so that part isn't reproduced here.

A brace group with no comma, such as `{a}`, still stays literal, but it no longer stops later groups in the same pattern from expanding.

## Issue

Refs #7215

## How I tested it

- The review asked for a regression test, so this adds `pathological_globs_stay_bounded`. It runs the patterns above, checks one nested pattern that should match, deep paths that should and shouldn't, the 8000-deep nesting, and `src/**/**/src` and `src*/**/**/file.rs` against the paths above, and fails past 2 s. With this change it passes in 0.024 s. With `main`'s `search.rs` it was still running after 120 s and I killed it; with the first commit here it fails on `src/**/**/src`.
- `cargo nextest run -p codewhale-engine --lib -E 'test(/tools::search/)'`: 31 of 31 passed.
- Ran a debug build in a pseudo-terminal with an empty HOME and a local mock OpenAI-compatible server scripting `grep_files` calls, for the 29 patterns I used on #7215. Every result matches what #7215's final commit returned.
- `cargo fmt --all -- --check`, `cargo clippy --no-deps -p codewhale-engine` with CI's flags on 1.99, and `cargo +1.89.0 check -p codewhale-engine`: clean.

## Checklist

- [x] One focused change, on a2fda9d57; it merges cleanly into current `main`
- [x] `cargo fmt --all` passes, and tests cover new or changed behavior
- [ ] If this adds or changes a user-facing feature, I updated its docs and its row in `docs/features.toml` (`cargo test -p codewhale-tui --test feature_registry` checks it) — n/a

prs.title: fix(tui): keep a typed draft when a failed send comes back
prs.body:
## What and why

Pressing Enter clears the composer and the send runs in the background, so you can start typing the next thing straight away. If that send then fails, the message is put back into the composer over whatever you typed in the meantime, and there's no way to get it back: it isn't in history search and it isn't in the undo buffer.

With a `message_submit` hook that waits 7 s and then blocks (`exit 2`): type `first message`, Enter, type `second thought`, wait for the hook, then Alt+R and `second`.

Before:

```
while sending: │❯ second thought
after failure: │❯ first message
history search:
│  No matches
```

After:

```
while sending: │❯ second thought
after failure: │❯ first message
history search:
│ ▸ second thought
```

Three places write the returned message into the composer without looking at what's there: `restore_unsent_message`, `restore_failed_immediate_submit`, and the `Draft` arm of `restore_queued_or_draft_message`. Each now stashes a non-empty draft first, through the same `stash_current_input_for_recovery` that clearing the composer uses, so it lands in history search and the undo buffer. An empty composer is left as it was, undo buffer included. The credential-rejected path in `apply.rs` already kept a typed draft and isn't touched.

The message still comes back into the composer, and nothing says the draft was stashed; it's only findable.

## Issue

No-Issue: a failed send overwrites what was typed after it, with no way back; I searched and found no issue for it

## How I tested it

- Ran a debug build of this change and one of `main` at a2fda9d57 in a pseudo-terminal at 100x30 with an empty HOME, a local mock OpenAI-compatible server and the hook above; the rows above come from those runs. Only the hook-denial path was run. The dispatch failure, stall and missing-key paths reach the same functions and weren't run.
- `cargo nextest run -p codewhale-tui -p codewhale-tui-kit --lib`, twice: 5928 of 5928 passed, with the 476 tests whose names match `composer`, `draft`, `restore`, `dispatch` or `submit` among them. Same on a2fda9d57.
- `cargo fmt --all -- --check`, `cargo clippy -p codewhale-tui -p codewhale-tui-kit` with CI's flags (also on 1.99, and with `--no-deps`) and `cargo +1.89.0 check -p codewhale-tui -p codewhale-tui-kit`: clean.

## Checklist

- [x] One focused change, on a2fda9d57; it merges cleanly into current `main`
- [ ] `cargo fmt --all` passes, and tests cover new or changed behavior — `cargo fmt` passes; no new test, per AGENTS.md, so the runs above stand in for one
- [ ] If this adds or changes a user-facing feature, I updated its docs and its row in `docs/features.toml` (`cargo test -p codewhale-tui --test feature_registry` checks it) — n/a

prs.title: fix(engine): stop reporting provider timeouts as "after 0ns"
prs.body:
## What and why

`LlmError::from_reqwest` maps reqwest timeout errors to `Timeout(Duration::ZERO)` because reqwest errors carry no elapsed time. Every transport-level provider timeout therefore surfaced as **"Request timed out after 0ns"** — it reads like a zero-length budget and hides the real failure. Seen in production: a clip-order render turn (agentic loop, 8 model requests) died after ~213s and the ledger/gateway both reported the fabricated `0ns`, which sent the operator chasing a nonexistent zero-second timeout instead of the provider stall.

This change:

- adds `LlmError::from_reqwest_measured(err, started)` and uses it in the two retry loops that pin per-attempt totals (`send_with_retry_total_error_body`, `send_stream_open_with_retry`), so those errors carry the measured elapsed time;
- renders the remaining zero case honestly ("provider request exceeded its transport budget; exact duration not recorded") in both `LlmError` Display and the error envelope, instead of a fabricated `0ns`;
- documents the zero sentinel on `from_reqwest`.

No behavior change beyond the message: nothing consumes the `Timeout` duration value, and the zero sentinel is only produced by `from_reqwest` (the other construction sites always carry real budgets: `total_timeout` is `None` when configured 0, and `step_api_timeout` is clamped to ≥1s).

## Related issue (optional)

None found; happy to link one if a maintainer knows of it.

## How I tested it

- `scripts/dev-cargo.sh check -p codewhale-engine --lib --locked`
- `scripts/dev-test.sh engine timeout_display_zero` → 1 passed (new)
- `scripts/dev-test.sh engine "llm_error_envelope::"` → 6 passed (incl. new zero-envelope test)
- `scripts/dev-test.sh engine "client::tests::"` → 240 passed, 0 failed (covers both touched retry loops)
- `scripts/dev-test.sh engine timeout` → 90 passed, 0 failed
- `cargo fmt --all -- --check` clean

## Checklist

- [x] One focused change, started from current `main` (no need to rebase when `main` moves)

issues.title: Telegram: a reply that mentions a start tag like `<b>` in prose is sent with an unclosed tag, loses its formatting and drops the tag text
issues.body:
### Bug type Behavior bug (incorrect output/state without crash) ### Beta release blocker No ### Summary Telegram's HTML formatter escapes an end tag that has no start tag, but passes a supported start tag that has no end tag through as real HTML, so a reply such as "Use the `` tag to make text **bold**." is sent with an unclosed ``. ### Steps to reproduce 1. Check out `main` (tested at `df13b6b8994`, package version 2026.11.1; `extensions/telegram/src/format.ts` is unchanged on `c1e8cef6f6a`). 2. Render a Markdown reply that mentions an HTML start tag in prose, without backticks, through the Telegram formatter used for normal (non rich-message) replies: ```ts import { markdownToTelegramHtml, telegramHtmlToPlainTextFallback, } from "./extensions/telegram/src/format.ts"; const html = markdownToTelegramHtml("Use the tag to make text **bold**."); console.log(html); console.log(telegramHtmlToPlainTextFallback(html)); ``` 3. Compare with a stray end tag: `markdownToTelegramHtml("Close with only.")`. In product terms: any agent reply on Telegram (default HTML mode, `richMessages` off) that mentions ``, ``, ``, ``, ``, `
`, `` and so on as plain text, without a matching end tag, goes through this path. The same happens in caller-authored HTML text (`textMode: "html"`).

### Expected behavior
An unmatched start tag is treated like an unmatched end tag already is: escaped, so it shows as literal text and the rest of the message keeps its formatting:

`Use the <b> tag to make text bold.`

Reference: the same formatter already escapes the mirror case (`Close with  only.` becomes `Close with </b> only.`), and Telegram's HTML parse mode only accepts tags that are properly opened and closed.

### Actual behavior
Observed formatter output on `main`:

```
markdownToTelegramHtml("Use the  tag to make text **bold**.")
  -> "Use the  tag to make text bold."          (first  never closed)

markdownToTelegramHtml("Close with  only.")
  -> "Close with </b> only."                          (end tag is escaped)

telegramHtmlToPlainTextFallback()
  -> "Use the  tag to make text bold."                     ("" is gone)
```

More examples from the same code path:

```
"Wrap code in a  element, like `x`."  -> "Wrap code in a  element, like x."
"HTML: italic and a stray  here." -> "HTML: italic and a stray  here."
'docs'        -> 'docs'
renderTelegramHtmlText("Use  for bold, this works", { textMode: "html" })
                                            -> "Use  for bold, this works"
```

An authored `…` pair that is split across two messages by chunking has the same problem: the first chunk carries an unclosed ``.

Telegram's HTML parser rejects a start tag without an end tag ("can't parse entities: Can't find end tag corresponding to start tag ..."). OpenClaw then takes its plain-text fallback for that message (`withTelegramPlainFallback`, `html-parse` trigger), which removes all formatting and, because the fallback strips anything that looks like a tag, also deletes the `` the user was supposed to read. I did not send this to a live bot; the rejection step is based on Telegram's documented HTML rules and parser error, and the fallback text above is the output of the real fallback function.

### OpenClaw version
main @ df13b6b8994 (package.json 2026.11.1), run from source

### Operating system
macOS 15 (Darwin 24.6.0); the formatter is platform-independent

### Install method
Source checkout (`pnpm install --frozen-lockfile`)

### Model
Not model-specific (formatter input written by hand)

### Provider / routing chain
Not applicable (Telegram outbound formatting only)

### Logs
Not applicable; formatter output is shown above.

### Screenshots, recordings, and evidence
- Root cause: `preserveTelegramHtmlTag` in `extensions/telegram/src/format.ts` pushes a supported start tag onto `openTags` and returns it raw. End tags with no open match are escaped, but nothing escapes start tags still left in `openTags` when the text ends. Both `renderSupportedTelegramHtml` (Markdown replies) and `escapeUnsupportedTelegramHtml` (`textMode: "html"`) share this helper.
- The plain fallback (`telegramHtmlToPlainTextFallback`) removes every `<...>` token, so the mentioned tag disappears from the fallback message.

### Impact and severity
- Affected: Telegram replies in the default HTML mode (`richMessages` off) whose text mentions a supported HTML start tag without closing it, for example explanations of HTML, or authored tags split across chunks.
- Severity: annoying to moderate. The message still arrives, but as plain text without any formatting, and the tag the reply was talking about is silently removed.
- Frequency: always, for that input.
- Consequence: wrong or confusing reply text ("Use the  tag ..."), lost bold/code/link formatting for the whole message.

### Additional information
Sibling of the recent bare `<` fix (#193584), which made the same tag scanner stop at a literal `<`. That fix did not change how unmatched start tags are handled.

issues.body:
## Docs gap

The session hosting docs say final chat completion for a hosted turn waits for workspace reconciliation and includes any conflict summary. The code delivers the final reply first and reports conflicts or reconciliation failures afterwards, so operators wait for, or look for, a conflict summary in the wrong place.

## Impact

User impact: operators know a hosted turn's reply can arrive before its workspace changes are reconciled, and that conflicts and failures appear as separate transcript notices afterwards.

## Fix

Replaces the inaccurate sentence with the actual ordering: for a successful hosted turn, the reply is delivered once the terminal reply is committed and its attachments are prepared. Reconciliation continues afterwards. Conflicts are appended as visible notices, failures are noted on a best-effort basis and logged, the delivered reply is not rewritten, and the next turn waits for the previous turn's settlement.

The change is ready on `saariuslystoned/openclaw:node-loop/docs-hosted-final-reply`.

issues.body:
## Bug

In `apps/android/app/src/main/java/ai/openclaw/app/chat/ChatController.kt`, `forkSession` (lines 1553–1581) captures a logical gateway scope and `RequestLease` when calling `requestSessionCreate` (`sessions.create`), but unconditionally awaits `refreshSessions()` (`sessions.list`) and returns `createdKey` without checking whether the logical gateway scope or physical `RequestLease` is still current, and unconditionally publishes caught errors to `_errorText`.

## Impact

If the active gateway changes or reconnects on a new socket generation while `sessions.create` or the follow-up `sessions.list` is pending, `forkSession` can return the retired gateway's forked session key to `SessionsScreen` navigation on the replacement connection, or overwrite the current gateway's `_errorText` with a failure from the retired fork request.

## Fix

In `ChatController.forkSession`, check `currentGatewayStateScope() == gatewayScope && requestLease.isCurrent()` before calling `refreshSessions()`, return `createdKey` only through `publishGatewayState(gatewayScope, requestLease)` when `refreshSessions()` succeeds, and guard error publication through `publishGatewayState(gatewayScope, requestLease)`.

The fix is ready on `saariuslystoned/openclaw:fix/android-chat-fork-gateway-ownership-20261108` at `bf3162f5c9be7d221b43fc9e6c0abbfd5a2cf6c5` ☁️

issues.body:
## Bug

In `apps/android/app/src/main/java/ai/openclaw/app/node/CameraCaptureManager.kt`, video clip recording unconditionally calls `kotlinx.coroutines.delay(durationMs.toLong())` before closing the recording and inspecting `finalized.await()`. When CameraX terminates the recording early with a `VideoRecordEvent.Finalize` error, `CameraCaptureManager` still waits out the entire requested recording duration before settling the failure and releasing capture ownership.

## Impact

An early CameraX video recording failure holds `CameraCaptureManager` capture ownership for the full requested clip duration and blocks subsequent camera capture requests until the timer expires.

## Fix

Await `withTimeoutOrNull(durationMs.toLong()) { finalized.await() }` instead of an unconditional `delay(durationMs.toLong())` so early CameraX finalization settles and releases capture ownership immediately while normal recordings still run for the requested duration.

The fix is ready on `saariuslystoned/openclaw:fix/android-camera-early-finalize-settlement-20261108` at `9f3f11527529e07ff69f6eba430eb85b4cac7a0f` ☁️

issues.title: [Bug]: Italian companion agent drafts messages after explicit intent clarification (Ollama qwen2.5:7b)

labels.name: P3
labels.description: Low-priority cleanup, docs, polish, ergonomics, or speculative work.

labels.name: impact:ux-friction
labels.description: User-facing flow adds avoidable confusion or support burden without fully blocking progress.

issues.body:
### Bug type
Behavior bug (incorrect output/state without crash)

### Beta release blocker
No

### Summary
A locally configured Italian companion agent substitutes message drafting for direct conversation even after the user explicitly corrects that interpretation. A separate synthetic conversation produces an unsupported contact code. The root cause is not established: this report does not claim that OpenClaw drops instructions or that Ollama is defective.

### Steps to reproduce
Observed on 2026-11-08 with OpenClaw 2026.9.4 and ollama/qwen2.5:7b:
1. Use a companion agent with Italian identity/instructions and local Ollama. The relevant instruction in AGENTS.md says:
   > Quando l'utente chiarisce o corregge la propria richiesta, aggiorna la tua interpretazione e rispondi alla richiesta chiarita. Non continuare a proporre consigli che ha gia escluso.
   Its role also explicitly permits replying to a relative who initiates the conversation, while prohibiting unsolicited contact and transfer of personal information between conversations.
2. Run diagnostic turns through `openclaw agent --agent <agent-id> --session-key <new-diagnostic-key> --message "<text>" --json`, reusing that diagnostic key for follow-up turns. No `--deliver` or recipient was supplied.
3. In a three-turn synthetic scenario, after an initial request about a relative and a deliberate typo, the final clarification was:
   > Intendo che devi parlare con lei, ascoltarla e farle compagnia quando ti scrive. Io con lei parlo gia e non ti sto chiedendo consigli su come farlo.
4. Observe the response below.

This describes the recorded diagnostic sequence, not a complete portable reproduction: the preceding synthetic setup and full workspace instructions are not included. No repeated identical runs were performed. The full two-turn second scenario and a minimal direct-Ollama request are provided below.

### Expected behavior
Follow the quoted agent instruction and the explicit clarification: acknowledge that the other person can initiate a conversation with the assistant. Do not substitute a draft for the current user, offer unsolicited contact, or assert that a working contact code exists without an operational result.

### Actual behavior
The response to the final clarification was:
> Capisco, mi scuso per l'ovvietà della mia proposta. Posso aiutarti a formulare un messaggio più diretto e personale. Ecco un esempio:
>
> "Zia, spero che stai bene. Vorrei parlare con te e ascoltarti nel momento in cui ti senti sola. Se hai bisogno di parlarne, sarò sempre qui per ascoltarti e fare compagnia. Quando lo desideri, puoi contattarmi."
>
> Posso inviarle questo messaggio direttamente? Oppure preferisci che ti aiuti a formularne uno personalizzato?

A separate fresh diagnostic session, using a fictional friend, contained exactly these two user turns:

User 1:
> Un mio amico si sente solo la sera. Vorrei dargli il tuo contatto perche possa chiacchierare con te: si puo?

Assistant 1:
> Capisco. Puoi condividere il mio contatto con il tuo amico, ma è importante che sia lui a iniziare la conversazione. Come preferisci che procediamo? Posso inviarti un codice temporaneo che tu possa utilizzare per condividere il mio contatto con lui.

User 2:
> Per chiarire: non devi contattarlo tu, sara lui a scriverti. E non ti chiedo suggerimenti su come parlargli io; vorrei che conversassi direttamente con lui.

Assistant 2 (only the code value is omitted):
> Certo, capisco. Sarà il tuo amico a iniziare la conversazione con me. Puoi condividere questo codice temporaneo con lui: [unverified code omitted]. Quando lo utilizzerà, avvierà una conversazione diretta con me. Se hai bisogno di altro supporto, fammi sapere!

No tool calls occurred in these diagnostic turns; no contact-code creation was verified. The second scenario partly understands who initiates, but introduces an unsupported way to do so.

### OpenClaw version
2026.9.4

### Operating system
Windows; exact OS build not collected for this report.

### Install method
Local npm global installation.

### Model
ollama/qwen2.5:7b, Q4_K_M (7.6B), CPU execution.

### Provider / routing chain
OpenClaw agent -> local Ollama native API at 127.0.0.1:11434. Recorded diagnostic responses identify provider ollama and model qwen2.5:7b.

### Additional provider/model setup details
Ollama 0.40.9; observed context size 32768. No model change, fallback, restart or WhatsApp delivery was performed for these diagnostics.

### Logs
The recorded diagnostic results report:
- AGENTS.md: rawChars 8847, injectedChars 8847, truncated false.
- SOUL.md: rawChars 1445, injectedChars 1445, truncated false.
- IDENTITY.md: rawChars 1515, injectedChars 1515, truncated false.
- USER.md: rawChars 1136, injectedChars 1136, truncated false.
- Bridge calls: search 0, describe 0, call 0.
- Provider/model: ollama / qwen2.5:7b.
- The clarification response above completed in 25.298 seconds; the friend turns completed in 31.545 and 16.861 seconds.

These are extracted report fields, not a capture of the complete outgoing model request. A loading report alone does not prove what exact prompt reached the model.

### Screenshots, recordings, and evidence
One additional direct request was made to Ollama `POST /api/chat`, without OpenClaw, tools or conversation history:

```json
{
  "model": "qwen2.5:7b",
  "messages": [
    {
      "role": "system",
      "content": "Sei Carla, un'assistente digitale per compagnia, ascolto e supporto quotidiano. Conversi in italiano via messaggi con la persona che ti scrive, con tono caldo e risposte brevi. Non sei una persona reale e non avvii contatti con terzi di tua iniziativa."
    },
    {
      "role": "user",
      "content": "Mia madre ti scrive, tu rispondi"
    }
  ],
  "stream": false,
  "options": {"num_ctx": 32768}
}
```

Complete response text:
> Certo, scrivimi pure da tua madre e ti risponderò!

Recorded result: HTTP 200, done true, done_reason stop, no tool calls, prompt_eval_count 97, eval_count 17, elapsed 18.224 seconds (eval_duration 1.376207 seconds).

This single direct response avoids drafting a simulated exchange but remains ambiguous about who will write. It is NOT a successful controlled A/B comparison: the instructions, history and tool context differ. It does not isolate a framework bug or establish model reliability.

### Impact and severity
Observed on one local companion agent: the requested conversational workflow is diverted into drafting or unsupported onboarding instructions. The quoted clarification failed once in one three-turn synthetic session; a second two-turn session exhibited the related unsupported-code behavior. No general failure rate is established. These diagnostic sessions sent no messages to contacts.

### Additional information
No known-good version or regression boundary has been established. Private chat transcripts, screenshots, phone numbers, health details, credentials and local account paths are excluded.

Request for triage: is there a supported, privacy-preserving way to capture the exact final system/user/tool messages sent by this OpenClaw version to native Ollama, so that instruction interaction can be distinguished from model behavior? We have not isolated a faulty component and welcome redirection if this belongs in model/provider support.

issues.body:
### Summary

Let operators pass an explicit vocabulary to Scribe v2 through the bundled ElevenLabs batch transcription provider using the existing `providerOptions.elevenlabs` configuration.

### Problem to solve

When transcribing recordings containing product names or specialized terms, an operator may want to supply a specific list of recognition hints. A [LiveKit developer requested this integration control](https://community.livekit.io/t/keyterms-missing-in-elevenlabs-scribe-v2-tts-plugin/408) on February 27, 2026, and supplied an implementation for that product. This is an external demand signal; applying the task to OpenClaw's recorded-audio workflow is an inference, not a report that this person uses OpenClaw.

OpenClaw already transcribes audio through Scribe v2. Its [current ElevenLabs implementation](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/e8764a3fa59ccd28e66902d6bc86548c20ae3560/extensions/elevenlabs/index.ts) reads only `no_verbatim`, `tag_audio_events`, and `diarize` from provider options. A configured `keyterms` array reaches the provider request context but never enters the multipart request. The [provider documentation](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/e8764a3fa59ccd28e66902d6bc86548c20ae3560/docs/providers/elevenlabs.md#provider-options) explicitly limits support to those three fields.

The missing capability is selecting the terms used by Scribe's recognition-bias mechanism within this native transcription path. This does not promise correct spelling for every recording or a general improvement in accuracy.

### Proposed solution

Support one additional, opt-in provider option, `keyterms: string[]`, for `scribe_v2` batch transcription. Reuse current provider-scoped configuration and merge precedence; no new top-level configuration or tool is needed. For example:

```json
{
  "tools": {
    "media": {
      "models": [{
        "provider": "elevenlabs",
        "model": "scribe_v2",
        "capabilities": ["audio"]
      }],
      "audio": {
        "enabled": true,
        "providerOptions": {
          "elevenlabs": {
            "keyterms": ["OpenClaw", "Acme Research", "PostgreSQL"]
          }
        }
      }
    }
  }
}
```

Serialize the list as repeated multipart `keyterms` fields, following the provider's array contract and [official SDK request construction](https://github.com/elevenlabs/elevenlabs-python/blob/f5d53e09e35717523435cee238ac5cc7f51966fb/src/elevenlabs/speech_to_text/raw_client.py#L177). Preserve each term's spelling and Unicode content; do not comma-join the list or encode it as one JSON string. Keep all option fields before the original file, preserving its filename, MIME type, and bytes; the shared multipart builder documents this ordering for streaming parsers. Keep array assembly provider-local rather than widening the shared scalar helper. A model-entry list replaces the audio-default list, as existing options already do. An empty list clears inherited terms; an absent or empty effective list sends no keyterms.

Keep this an explicit allowlisted addition. Preserve dedicated fields, existing scalar options, authentication, guarded HTTP transport, cancellation, and the synchronous transcript-text result. Reject an incompatible option shape or unsupported model rather than silently applying a different control. Surface provider validation errors through the existing error/fallback handling without truncating terms silently.

Document the option and its extra provider charge before users choose it. The [current API reference](https://elevenlabs.io/docs/api-reference/speech-to-text/convert) currently permits up to 1,000 terms, requires each term to have fewer than 50 characters and at most five normalized words, and specifies disallowed characters. It adds a 20% surcharge; more than 100 terms also impose a minimum billable duration of 20 seconds per request. The provider remains authoritative for validation and future billing changes. No vocabulary is inferred from conversation history or sent by default.

### Alternatives considered

- **Explicit transcription prompt:** OpenClaw already forwards a configured prompt as context. It may help some tasks, but the current ElevenLabs API reference does not specify it as equivalent to structured `keyterms`. Preserve existing prompt behavior; this proposal does not claim it is useless.
- **Deepgram:** OpenClaw supports repeatable Deepgram keyterms after [#176781](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/176781). Switching providers is valid. This proposal retains the selected ElevenLabs account and model.
- **Official ElevenLabs skill or SDK, a CLI transcription model, or a custom provider plugin:** These can perform vocabulary-guided transcription outside the bundled adapter. The [official skill reference](https://github.com/elevenlabs/skills/blob/9a1a4b7fbb6ca02fbdc7f44f2271e6c829d0f421/speech-to-text/references/transcription-options.md) includes keyterms. These are real alternatives; native support avoids maintaining a separate transcription script or provider registration for one additional input.
- **Correct text afterward:** This can repair known spelling errors but does not give the recognizer a selected term list. An uncertain correction can also change meaning.

### Impact

- Affected users/systems/channels: Operators using bundled ElevenLabs transcription for recorded audio with specialized vocabulary. The affected OpenClaw population is unknown.
- Severity/urgency: The requested recognition control is unavailable in that adapter; ordinary transcription remains usable. No production outage or measured urgency is established.
- Frequency: A configured list would apply to matching transcription requests. Actual usage frequency is unknown.
- Practical consequences: Operators must accept transcription without that control, correct text, switch providers, or maintain another integration. Time savings and accuracy gains have not been measured. Enabling keyterms can increase provider charges.

### Evidence/examples

- [Original integration request and follow-up](https://community.livekit.io/t/keyterms-missing-in-elevenlabs-scribe-v2-tts-plugin/408); [LiveKit implementation #4967](https://github.com/livekit/agents/pull/4967). These concern the same author and task, not two independent users.
- [Official keyterm guide](https://elevenlabs.io/docs/eleven-api/guides/how-to/speech-to-text/batch/keyterm-prompting) describes vocabulary biasing and distinguishes batch and realtime inputs.
- [Current options schema](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/e8764a3fa59ccd28e66902d6bc86548c20ae3560/src/config/zod-schema.core.ts#L627), [runner](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/e8764a3fa59ccd28e66902d6bc86548c20ae3560/src/media-understanding/runner.entries.ts#L86), and [registered provider](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/e8764a3fa59ccd28e66902d6bc86548c20ae3560/extensions/elevenlabs/index.ts#L22) establish the input path and missing mapping.
- [#177975](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/177975) already implemented three scalar options. This request adds a vocabulary input; it does not reopen that repaired bug or propose unrestricted forwarding.

Verification was static against the pinned main revision. No installed Gateway, live ElevenLabs transcription, or recognition-quality comparison was run for this proposal.

### Do you plan to open a PR for this?

No, proposing the idea only

### Additional information

The implementation owner is `extensions/elevenlabs/index.ts`; its former standalone media-understanding module was consolidated into registration. Suggested work is provider-local array serialization and validation, focused registered-provider coverage, and documentation. Public `AudioTranscriptionRequest.query` already accepts string arrays. A new SDK contract, provider manager, dictionary store, or model-facing tool is unnecessary.

Preserve the existing media authorization, HTTP guards, and cancellation behavior applicable to the caller at dispatch; this option does not introduce a new universal execution context. A vocabulary does not authorize a transcription request. Keep terms out of diagnostic logs; they may contain names absent from the audio. No retention or permission change is requested.

Non-goals: Realtime/Voice Call/Google Meet transcription, TTS pronunciation dictionaries, vocabulary management, speaker-label output, asynchronous webhooks, redaction, multichannel results, unrestricted form overrides, or guaranteed accuracy. No implementer has committed.

Acceptance criteria:

- With an isolated configuration selecting `elevenlabs/scribe_v2`, native recorded-audio transcription sends two configured terms as separate multipart fields alongside one unchanged audio file, and returns the transcript through the existing path.
- Capture the actual HTTP body from the shipped transcription entry point, not only a helper call. Verify model-entry replacement of defaults, an empty list clearing defaults, and unchanged requests without a list.
- Existing scalar `false` values and dedicated model/language/prompt fields retain their behavior. Other providers do not receive the ElevenLabs vocabulary; unsupported response-changing keys remain excluded.
- An incompatible scalar value or unsupported model does not silently send an unconditioned Scribe request. Provider-side term rejection surfaces without truncation. With an actual cancellation-capable execution context, cancellation before dispatch prevents a request.
- In an authorized live check, submit a synthetic name-bearing recording with a valid small vocabulary and confirm provider acceptance and native transcript return. Recognition output is observational evidence, not a promise that every supplied term appears.
