issues.body:
### Summary

Add a provider docs page (and, if maintainers want it, a bundled provider like Requesty in #180788) for Standard Compute, an OpenAI-compatible model gateway.

### Problem to solve

Standard Compute is an OpenAI-compatible API (`https://api.stdcmpt.com/v1`, US endpoint `https://us.stdcmpt.com/v1`, Bearer API key). The model id `standardcompute` routes each step to the cheapest capable model across providers vetted for price, uptime and speed, with automatic fallback; catalog model ids from `GET /v1/models` also work. It has opt-in Europe/US compliance rules and does not train on or store prompts.

Today OpenClaw users have to hand-write a custom OpenAI-compatible provider block and guess the model ids. There is no page under `docs/providers/` that gives the base URL, auth variable and model ids, so setup questions end up in support instead of the docs.

Disclosure: I run Standard Compute.

### Proposed solution

A `docs/providers/standardcompute.md` page in the same shape as `docs/providers/requesty.md`:

| Property      | Value                                        |
| ------------- | -------------------------------------------- |
| Provider      | `standardcompute`                            |
| Auth          | `STANDARDCOMPUTE_API_KEY`                    |
| API           | OpenAI-compatible                            |
| Base URL      | `https://api.stdcmpt.com/v1`                 |
| Model catalog | `GET /v1/models` (default model `standardcompute`) |

with Setup steps (create a key, onboard or set the env var, `openclaw models list --provider standardcompute`).

On distribution, I'd follow whichever route you prefer:

1. **Third-party plugin (my default reading of CONTRIBUTING).** A provider plugin already exists at https://github.com/henrikdukefoss/openclaw-standardcompute (Plugin SDK, tests run offline). It is not published on ClawHub yet; I'll publish it there under the ClawHub publishing rules. I understand `docs/plugins/community.md` says the docs don't keep a static third-party catalog, so if a provider page for a community plugin doesn't fit, please say so and close this.
2. **Bundled provider plugin**, following the Requesty conversion in #180788, if you consider a router/gateway provider in scope for core.

### Alternatives considered

- Custom provider config in `openclaw.json` only: works, but users have to know the base URL and model ids, and nothing in the OpenClaw docs tells them.
- ClawHub listing without a docs page: covers install, but provider docs are where people look for base URL and auth details.

### Impact

Affected: OpenClaw users who route through Standard Compute.
Severity: low (setup friction, not a defect).
Frequency: every new setup.
Consequence: hand-written provider blocks and model id guesswork.

### Evidence/examples

- Requesty precedent: #54444 → #180788 (merged 2026-10-23), docs at `docs/providers/requesty.md`.
- Existing plugin: https://github.com/henrikdukefoss/openclaw-standardcompute
- Provider docs: https://docs.standardcompute.com, models: https://docs.standardcompute.com/models

### Do you plan to open a PR for this?

Maybe, with maintainer guidance

### Additional information

I won't open a PR unless a maintainer says one of the routes above is wanted. This request was prepared with AI assistance.

issues.body:
### Bug type

Regression (worked before, now fails)

### Beta release blocker

No

### Summary

`core/doctor/cron-inference-accounts` makes about three whole copies of an agent database for every legacy automation it inspects, so `doctor --lint` on a large state takes minutes and the update rehearsal's lint step times out.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Build main at `7c7a4d5db4a` (`pnpm install && pnpm build`).
2. Use a copy of any SQLite state (APFS clone or plain copy) with at least one `agentTurn` automation whose session target is not `main` and that has no recorded inference account. The check skips jobs that have a binding, and jobs with `sessionTarget: "main"` (`src/commands/doctor/cron/inference-binding-migration.ts:96`). Jobs created before #172792, and plugin-created jobs (#192327), have no binding. To make one, strip the binding from a job in the copy's `state/openclaw.sqlite`:

   ```sql
   UPDATE cron_jobs SET job_json = json_remove(job_json, '$.inferenceBinding') WHERE job_id = '<id>';
   ```

3. Grow the job's agent database with filler, so the copies are easy to see:

   ```sql
   -- in <copy>/agents/<agent>/agent/openclaw-agent.sqlite
   CREATE TABLE repro_filler(id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, b BLOB);
   WITH RECURSIVE n(i) AS (SELECT 1 UNION ALL SELECT i + 1 FROM n WHERE i < 2048)
   INSERT INTO repro_filler(b) SELECT randomblob(1048576) FROM n;
   ```

4. Run only this check against the copy, and watch `<copy>/Library/Caches/openclaw/sqlite-*/` for private snapshot images:

   ```sh
   HOME=$COPY TMPDIR=$COPY OPENCLAW_HOME=$COPY OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR=$COPY \
   OPENCLAW_CONFIG_PATH=$COPY/openclaw.json OPENCLAW_WORKSPACE_DIR=$COPY/workspace \
     node openclaw.mjs doctor --lint --json --only core/doctor/cron-inference-accounts
   ```

   My runs also set the `OPENCLAW_SKIP_*` variables the update rehearsal sets.

My states already had unbound jobs, so I did not run step 2's `UPDATE` myself. The state behind the table below is the SQLite copy that the dev update rehearsal made of a PostgreSQL-backed install. The rehearsal had already run `doctor --fix` on it, and it was left in `~/.openclaw.update-captures/openclaw-update-canary-*` after I stopped the update. It has 39 unbound `agentTurn` jobs, 29 of them on `main`, whose agent database is 3.4 GiB.

### Expected behavior

A read-only check over N automations should read each agent database once per lint pass, or borrow one reusable image the way #194042 and #194267 do for other Doctor reads, so its cost does not grow with N times the database size. The dev update that installed main `87c9eb3fc54f` passed its lint step. That build ran this scan only in interactive `openclaw doctor`. #193570 added it to `doctor --lint`, so the update rehearsal now runs it too.

### Actual behavior

The cost grows with the number of automations times the size of the job's agent database. I ran the check alone (`--only`) on copies of that state:

| Automations kept | Job's agent database | Run time | Snapshot images seen (100 MiB or more) | Bytes in those images |
| --- | --- | ---: | --- | ---: |
| 1 | 7 MiB agent | 2.6 s check (6 s process) | 1 (state DB, 266 MiB) | 0.3 GiB |
| 1 | same agent plus 2 GiB of random filler | 12 s process | 4 (3 of the 2 GiB agent DB, 1 state DB) | 6.1 GiB |
| 1 | `main`, 3.4 GiB | 23.8 s check | 6 (3 of `main`, 3 state DB) | 10.9 GiB |
| 3 | `main`, 3.4 GiB | 60.5 s check | 9 (at least 7 of `main`) | 23.9 GiB |

The watcher sampled every 250 ms, so the image counts are lower bounds. The filler row is the only synthetic data, and it shows that the cost follows the database's size in bytes, not its content.

I also ran a full `doctor --lint --json` on the same copy. The 20 checks before this one each took 1 s or less, except `agent-database-admission` (9.4 s), `database-engine` (14.7 s) and `telegram-general-topic-conversations` (10.1 s). This check was still running when I stopped it after 5.5 minutes. I did not let the full 39-job run finish. At about 20 s and three 3.4 GiB copies per `main` job, it would take about 10 minutes and write about 300 GiB.

On the update path, `openclaw update --yes --channel dev` from `87c9eb3fc54f` failed twice at this step, once with the Gateway running and once with it stopped. The `?` is the updater's own status glyph:

```text
candidate-doctor-lint: doctor --lint --json --severity-min error
  ? candidate-doctor-lint — timed out (303.02s)
    Failing check lint (candidate-checks-timeout): candidate-migration-rehearsal: lint exceeded budget after 303 s (no progress output)
```

With `--timeout 3600`, the candidate's lint ran for more than 15 minutes. Free disk fell from 24 GiB to 16 GiB in about a minute while it made repeated 3.6 GB copies of the main agent database, so I stopped it. Both times the update left the installed build unchanged.

The update runs lint with `--severity-min error`. This check only reports warnings, but the severity filter is applied after the checks run (`src/commands/doctor-lint-runner.ts:558`), so the check still runs in full.

### OpenClaw version

2026.11.1 dev, main `7c7a4d5db4a`. The update attempts targeted `e673256f8a9`; the code cited here is unchanged between the two.

### Operating system

macOS 27.2 (arm64), Node 24.22.2

### Install method

Git checkout on the dev channel. The measurements come from a source build (`pnpm install && pnpm build`).

### Model

N/A (Doctor check, no model involved)

### Provider / routing chain

N/A

### Additional provider/model setup details

The live install uses PostgreSQL stores (13). I did not time this check against the live PostgreSQL state. The numbers above come from SQLite copies, which is what the update rehearsal runs on.

### Logs

Debug log for one `main` automation (`OPENCLAW_LOG_LEVEL=debug`, paths shortened). The same pattern repeats for every job:

```text
+39s SQLite read-only snapshot for <copy>/Library/Caches/openclaw/sqlite-…: 480 B, budget 301 seconds
+39s SQLite read-only snapshot for <copy>/agents/main/agent/openclaw-agent.sqlite: 3.4 GiB, budget 4622 seconds
+52s SQLite read-only snapshot for <copy>/…/openclaw-sqlite-readonly-v2-Gb5SxM: 160 B, budget 301 seconds
+52s SQLite read-only snapshot for <copy>/agents/main/agent/openclaw-agent.sqlite: 3.4 GiB, budget 4622 seconds
+60s SQLite read-only snapshot for <copy>/state/openclaw.sqlite: 265.9 MiB, budget 633 seconds
+60s SQLite plugin catalog read for <copy>/agents/main/agent/openclaw-agent.sqlite: 3.4 GiB, budget 4622 seconds
+60s SQLite read-only snapshot for <copy>/agents/main/agent/openclaw-agent.sqlite: 3.4 GiB, budget 4622 seconds
```

### Screenshots, recordings, and evidence

Where the copies come from, on `7c7a4d5db4a`:

- `src/flows/doctor-cron-checks.ts:19`: the lint check calls `maybeRepairCronInferenceBindings({ shouldRepair: false })`.
- `src/commands/doctor/cron/inference-binding-migration.ts:77`, `:122` and `:137`: for each unbound job, it calls `prepareCronSession` for the job's agent and session, then `resolveCronModelSelection`. The debug log shows a plugin model catalog read of the agent database at that point.
- In a build with logging added to the snapshot producers, only one of the three `main` copies for a job reached a logged producer. That copy was a `prepareSqliteReadOnlyLocationAwaited` call that did not take its reuse-scope branch (`src/infra/sqlite-snapshot-source.ts:348`). Of that function's four callers, only `src/config/sessions/session-entry-read.worker.ts:185` never passes `reuse: true`.
- The reuse scope and its image map are `globalThis` singletons (`src/infra/sqlite-snapshot-reuse.ts`, via `src/shared/global-singleton.ts:43`). A worker thread therefore starts with its own empty map and is outside the CLI's reuse scope. I did not trace which worker or child made the other two copies. The debug log labels them "read-only snapshot" and "plugin catalog read".

### Impact and severity

This affects SQLite installs and update rehearsals where an unbound `agentTurn` automation belongs to an agent with a large database.

- `openclaw doctor --lint` writes about three copies of the agent database per unbound automation. That was 10.9 GiB for one automation on a 3.4 GiB database, and minutes of run time for a few dozen automations.
- `openclaw update` on such an install fails at `candidate-doctor-lint` every time, so the install cannot update. Raising `--timeout` turns the failure into hundreds of GiB of disk writes and quickly falling free space.

### Additional information

Last known good: main `87c9eb3fc54f`, where the scan ran only in interactive `openclaw doctor`. First known bad: the first build with #193570 (merged 2026-11-05), which added the scan to `doctor --lint`.

A second factor makes the update fail at about 300 s. The rehearsal sizes each check's budget from `snapshotCapacity.sqliteBytes + pluginBytes` (`src/infra/update-candidate-canary.ts:217`), at a 300 s floor plus 40 s per 32 MiB. For PostgreSQL state, `sqliteBytes` counts the local `.sqlite` anchor files (`src/infra/update-candidate-state.ts:243`, measured by `measureUpdateStateFiles` in `src/infra/update-candidate-snapshot.ts:131` and `:535`). Here those totalled 168 KiB (plus 3 MiB of plugin files), while the rehearsal copied about 5.4 GB of SQLite, so each check got about 304 s. The failure above reports 303 s. Fixing the check above is enough for this install to pass; the budget sizing is a separate, smaller problem.

Related: #185656 is titled for a transcript-archive bug, but its later comments track whole-database copies during updates. #194042, #194267 and #194325 reduced those copies, but these per-automation reads still copy. #182228 reports a `candidate-doctor-lint` failure on an older build with too little detail to tell whether it is the same cause.

One thing I could not explain: in the real update, the candidate's lint worker sat idle for about 14 minutes (8 s of CPU) before the copying started. I could not reproduce that through the CLI, and nothing above depends on it.

issues.body:
### Bug type

Crash (process/app exits or hangs)

### Beta release blocker

No

### Summary

A managed `/update` run passed candidate admission, then spent **3414.4 s (56.9 min)** inside the `validating` phase — 190% of the default 1800 s step budget — before the updater child was SIGKILLed, leaving the installation on the old version.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Install OpenClaw 2026.10.8 (npm global) on Linux with a systemd user unit `openclaw-gateway.service` and a live gateway serving a non-trivial `~/.openclaw/state/openclaw.sqlite` plus active `~/.openclaw/tmp/plugin-captures`.
2. Trigger `/update` from a chat surface (owner-authorized), or run `openclaw update --yes --json`.
3. Observe `validating` start and then produce no further progress for nearly an hour, while the gateway logs SQLite lock-contention warnings.
4. Observe the updater child exit with `code=null signal=SIGKILL`, and the run fail with `managed-service-handoff-failed` / `gateway-probe-failed`.

### Expected behavior

`validating` should abort at its step deadline (1800 s default) and mark the run failed with a timeout reason, leaving the installation on 2026.10.8 with the gateway healthy and still serving.

### Actual behavior

The `validating` phase ran 3414.4 s without aborting. The updater child was SIGKILLed externally, and the serving gateway spent the same window logging lock-contention warnings and one hard `errcode=5` write failure.

### Evidence

#### 1. The `validating` step ran 3414.4 s against a 1800 s default budget

From `~/.openclaw/state/openclaw.sqlite` → `update_runs` for run `6292d4d0-690b-4e0a-8eb5-9ba6f129cd6f` (trigger `chat`, status `failed`, reason `managed-service-handoff-failed`, created 2026-11-02 09:41:17 local):

```
completed requested
completed installation-inspection
completed notice:ack
completed driver:adopted
completed managed-service update handoff
completed target-resolution
completed snapshot-space-preflight
completed staging
completed candidate-admission     (config/database-schema/node-runtime/plugin-availability all ok)
failed   validating               startedAtMs 1793583822860 -> endedAtMs 1793587237299  = 3414.4 s
failed   managed-service-handoff
failed   gateway recovery verification
```

#### 2. The per-step deadline is computed but does not bound the stuck sub-step

`dist/update-command-Dq3p94lm.mjs:307` (2026.10.9):

```js
const updateStepTimeoutMs = timeoutMs ?? run.defaultStepTimeoutMs ?? 18e5;   // 1800 s
```

1800 s < 3414.4 s, so the deadline should have fired ~16 min into the phase. It did not. The phase that was actually stuck is the candidate state snapshot, and the deadline does not appear to reach that worker.

The SQLite inspection budget is likewise far below the observed duration (`dist/managed-handoff-runtime.mjs`):

```js
SQLITE_INSPECTION_TIMEOUT_MS = 3e5;             // 300 s
SQLITE_INSPECTION_BYTES_PER_SECOND = 33554432;  // 32 MiB/s
// timeout = 300s + ceil(40 * sizeBytes / 32MiB/s) * 1e3
```

#### 3. The managed handoff invokes the updater without `--timeout`

`/tmp/openclaw-update-run-handoff-*/handoff.json`:

```json
"commandArgv": [
  "/home/zhanghao/.local/node-24.22.1/bin/node",
  "/home/zhanghao/.local/lib/node_modules/openclaw/dist/index.js",
  "update",
  "--yes",
  "--json"
],
"commandLabel": "openclaw update --yes"
```

No `--timeout` is passed, so the inner update run inherits only the default step budget, and the handoff itself has no bound for the child.

#### 4. The updater was SIGKILLed, not aborted by a timeout

`handoff.log`:

```
[2026-11-02T01:41:34.623Z] starting managed update command: openclaw update --yes
[2026-11-02T01:41:35.736Z] managed update update command pid=1039566
[2026-11-02T02:40:25.631Z] managed update update command exited code=null signal=SIGKILL
[2026-11-02T02:40:25.634Z] managed update recovery not attempted: no verified recovery result
```

No kernel OOM record appears for the window, and the systemd scope reported 2.0G memory peak / 64.9M swap peak on a host with 7.8 GiB RAM + 3.8 GiB swap. The kill most likely came from the scope teardown (`PartOf=openclaw-gateway.service`, `parentExitTimeoutMs: 330000`) rather than from the OOM killer.

#### 5. The serving gateway was starved for the whole window

Between 10:04 and 10:38 the gateway logged ~40 `audit event persistence delayed by SQLite lock contention` warnings and 6 `slow SQLite transaction step` warnings, plus one hard failure at 10:34:22:

```
[sqlite/transaction] SQLite transaction lock wait failed async=false busyTimeoutMs=0
  database=/home/zhanghao/.openclaw/state/openclaw.sqlite
  operation=state.planner-statistics code=ERR_SQLITE_ERROR
  failureKind=lock-contention sqliteErrcode=5 step=begin
```

`busyTimeoutMs=0` means the gateway's own write got no chance to wait for the lock. A gateway serving real traffic should not see `errcode=5` write failures because an update is running.

#### 6. The snapshot target collides with a file the running gateway already holds open

`lsof` during the run showed the live gateway (pid 514260) holding:

```
/home/zhanghao/.openclaw/tmp/plugin-captures/f73e490e-1ac2-455d-a3fe-206816e9237a/owner.sqlite        FD 32
/home/zhanghao/.openclaw/tmp/plugin-captures/f73e490e-1ac2-455d-a3fe-206816e9237a/owner.sqlite-journal FD 33
```

and the handoff log recorded `Skipped SQLite snapshot reclamation: database is locked (errcode=5)`. The `tmp/plugin-captures` tree is already excluded from ordinary backup volumes (`dist/backup-volatile-filter-D5FSM8Hx.mjs` lists `tmp/plugin-captures` under `VOLATILE_DIRECTORY_RULES`), but the candidate-state-snapshot path still copies that family while the gateway holds a write journal on it.

### Additional provider/model setup details

Not provider-related. Model in use was `minimax/MiniMax-M2.7`.

### OpenClaw version

OpenClaw 2026.10.8 (dc2523e), upgrading to 2026.10.9

### Operating system

Ubuntu 24.04, Linux 6.8.0-142-generic

### Install method

npm global (`/home/zhanghao/.local/lib/node_modules/openclaw`), systemd user unit `openclaw-gateway.service`

### Model

minimax/MiniMax-M2.7

### Provider / routing chain

openclaw -> minimax

### Suggested direction

1. Make the `validating` / candidate-state-snapshot deadline actually reach the worker and terminate it, then fail the run with a timeout reason.
2. Pass an explicit `--timeout` in the managed handoff `commandArgv` so the inner update run is bounded.
3. Exclude `tmp/plugin-captures/**/owner.sqlite` from the candidate snapshot set, or otherwise avoid copying a file the serving gateway holds a write journal on.
4. Configure a non-zero SQLite `busyTimeoutMs` with retry on the gateway write path so transient contention does not become a hard `errcode=5` failure.

### Related

- #186813 — chat-triggered managed update deadlocking against the serving gateway on SQLite
- #166221 — update failing during SQLite preflight / candidate snapshot
- #166526 — idempotent Doctor exceeding its wall-clock budget on large state

issues.body:
## Summary

A compressed transcript archive read can abort the entire gateway process. When the streaming decompressor is torn down before its async init completes, Node raises a native assertion and exits with code 134 (SIGABRT). A per-archive read error should be recoverable; it is currently fatal to the whole Gateway.

## Environment

- OpenClaw 2026.11.1 (4ffdd20)
- Windows, Node 26.12.1, SQLite agent store
- `session.maintenance.coldStorage.enabled = true`; several hundred compressed transcript archives present
- Cold-storage maintenance active (`cold-batch` / `cold-restore` reclamation)

## Observed

The Gateway child process exited with `exitCode: 134`, reported as "Gateway child failed". Captured stderr:

```
Assertion failed: init_done_ && "close before init"
node::(anonymous namespace)::CompressionStream<node::(anonymous namespace)::ZstdDecompressContext>::Close(void)
  at src\node_zlib.cc:519

FATAL ERROR: v8::HandleScope::CreateHandle() Cannot create a handle without a HandleScope
```

Immediately before the abort:

- `cold-batch` reclamation operations completed at T-208s and T-148s.
- A liveness warning recorded `eventLoopUtilization=1`, `eventLoopDelayP99Ms=396.9`, `degradedFor=1807s`, with three concurrent model calls in flight.

The assertion names a **decompress** context, so the failing read is on the archive restore path, not the write path.

## Isolation

`scanArchivedTranscript` streams a compressed archive through a pipeline:

```js
const input = Readable.from(<64 KiB chunks>);
await pipeline([
  input,
  ...(compressed ? [zlib.createZstdDecompress()] : []),
  ...(decodedBudget === undefined ? [] : [bound]),
  scan
]);
```

`pipeline` destroys every stage when any stage errors or the signal aborts. If `scan` rejects early — header/session mismatch, a record exceeding `maxRecordBytes`, or the bounded-read budget going negative — the zstd decompressor is destroyed. When that destroy lands before the decompressor's asynchronous init has completed, Node asserts in `Close()` (`init_done_ && "close before init"`), which is a native abort, not a catchable error.

A single malformed or oversized archive is therefore sufficient to terminate the process rather than fail one read.

## Steps to reproduce (suggested)

1. Enable cold storage and let archives accumulate.
2. Arrange for an early failure inside the streaming scan: an archive whose header session/generation does not match its registry row, or a record larger than `maxRecordBytes`, or a decoded payload that exhausts `decodedBudget`.
3. Read that archive through the archive-read path while the process is busy enough that teardown races stream init (the failure was observed during concurrent model calls with the event loop saturated).
4. The process aborts with exit code 134 instead of returning a read error.

## Expected

A malformed, mismatched, or oversized archive produces an error for that read only. The Gateway continues running and reports the failure.

## Suggested fix

- Do not destroy a decompressor that has not finished initialising. Either await the stream's init/`ready` before allowing teardown, or defer creating the decompressor until the first chunk is written.
- Alternatively, catch and swallow the close-time error during teardown so an early pipeline abort cannot reach the native assert.
- For bounded archives, prefer the synchronous decompress path (`zstdDecompressSync` with `maxOutputLength`), which is already used elsewhere in the cold-storage codec and does not expose this teardown race.

## Related

- #192743 — "read compressed archives as streams instead of refusing expansion": introduced the streaming path above.
- #190690 — the size-ratio refusal that #192743 replaced.

issues.body:
### Bug type
Behaviour bug (incorrect cost/cache behaviour, no crash)

### Environment
- OpenClaw 2026.10.5 (1b58cb9), Linux x64, gateway as a systemd user service
- Provider: direct Anthropic API key, `anthropic/claude-opus-5-5` via `boundary-aware:anthropic-messages`
- `cacheRetention: "long"` (1 h), `agents.defaults.contextPruning.mode: "cache-ttl"` (the value the bundled Anthropic plugin seeds)
- Long-lived, tool-heavy sessions (one human chat session, several worker sessions), 200k-800k prompt tokens
- The relevant code is unchanged on `main`: `packages/ai/src/transports/anthropic-payload-policy.ts` still sends `clear_tool_uses_20250919`, and `docs/concepts/session-pruning.md` still documents the same trigger, keep and clear_at_least values

### Summary
On direct Anthropic API-key routes, `contextPruning.mode: "cache-ttl"` sends `context_management.edits[clear_tool_uses_20250919]` with trigger = max(50k, 0.3 x contextWindow), keep = 3 tool uses, clear_at_least = max(12.5k, 0.05 x contextWindow). Above the trigger, each request clears all but the last 3 tool results server-side. Each time the cleared set grows (one more tool use ages past `keep`), the effective provider prompt changes at the **first** cleared tool result, near the start of the history. The cache read falls back to the tools + system prefix (~20-25k tokens) and the whole history (230k-490k tokens in our sessions) is written again at the 1 h cache-write price, often several times per turn.

`docs/concepts/session-pruning.md` already says "Clearing invalidates the prompt cache from the first cleared result". `clear_at_least` only batches the clearing; it does not stop the rewrite from the top, and none of the three thresholds is configurable. The prompt-cache observer does not see the cause: these busts are logged with `no tracked cache input change` or with unrelated envelope diffs.

### Steps to reproduce
1. Direct Anthropic API key, Opus or Sonnet, `cacheRetention: "long"`, `agents.defaults.contextPruning.mode: "cache-ttl"`.
2. Run one session with many tool calls (file reads, exec) until the prompt exceeds the trigger (for a 1M-token window: 300k tokens).
3. Keep working in the same session with turns a few seconds to a few minutes apart (well inside the 1 h TTL).
4. Watch the gateway log for `[anthropic] server-side context edit: cleared N tool results` followed by `[prompt-cache] cache read dropped`, and `cache_creation_input_tokens` on the same request.

### Expected
Inside the TTL, an append-only turn reads the previous prefix from cache and writes only the new tokens. If clearing must change the prefix, it should happen rarely and only when it pays for itself, and the observer should name it.

### Actual (log excerpts, identifiers removed)
Every bust on one day in a long session is preceded within 200 ms by a clearing event whose count changed:
```
15:53:42.559Z [anthropic] server-side context edit: cleared 244 tool results (~176672 input tokens)
15:53:42.672Z [prompt-cache] cache read dropped 264164 -> 24616 request=2   (29 s after request 1; request 1 message fingerprints are an exact prefix of request 2)
13:52:51.894Z cleared 244 -> cache read dropped 256901 -> 24625   (request 5, gap 4 s)
13:53:18Z     cleared 243 -> cache read dropped 260010 -> 24625   (request 7)
16:08:24.266Z cleared 271 (~314k tokens) -> cache read dropped 271116 -> 24616
```
A request with an unchanged cleared count hits normally (cleared 243: read 264,164, write 1,763).

Over four days (Anthropic only, one gateway): 211 cache busts inside the TTL with no tracked change, 33.9M cache-write tokens, the largest single class of cache writes. In a 30-day attribution over two gateways (102,865 model calls), rewrites of the cached history inside the TTL were 53 % of model spend.

### Mitigation, and what remains
Setting `contextPruning.mode: "off"` stopped the clearing events. Trade-off: no tool-result trimming, so long sessions carry their full tool output and reach compaction earlier.

It did **not** remove warm busts in long sessions; the remaining ones carry causes the observer does report. Gateway log 2026-11-06 to 2026-11-08 on 2026.10.5 with pruning off: 168 `cache read dropped` warnings, 125 of them within the 1 h TTL; 116 of the 125 on request 1 of a run (first call of a turn); median prompt 663k tokens, median read after the drop 22.9k (tools + system only). Tags on the 125 (a line can carry several):
- `imageCleanup(imageCleanup changed provider history)`: 68 (cf. #166272, closed; still seen on 2026.10.5)
- `tools(... description: "exec")`, the exec tool description differs between turns: 60
- `historyRewrite` of an earlier user message, changed fields `envelope.timestamp, envelope.idempotencyKey` or `envelope.__openclaw`: 49 (cf. #182891)
- tool list toggling between turn sources (`removed: "computer", "openclaw"` / `added: ...`): 34
- `no tracked cache input change`: 8

### Asks
1. Make server-side clearing cache-aware: clear only when the rewrite pays for itself (tokens cleared x expected remaining reads > cost of rewriting the history), or clear in large one-shot batches with hysteresis well above `clear_at_least`.
2. Expose `trigger` / `keep` / `clear_at_least` under `agents.defaults.contextPruning`, or add a switch that turns off Anthropic server-side clearing while keeping client-side pruning on other routes.
3. Record server-side clearing in the prompt-cache observer (for example `changes[]: serverToolClearing N -> M`) so these busts are attributed.
4. Keep the per-turn tool surface stable within a session: the exec tool description and the tool list should not change between turns of the same session, or the change should sit after the cached history.

Related: #150060 (same server-side clearing path, content-loss angle), #143017 and #182891 (other prefix rewrites), #166272 (history image prune).

Clear `lastManualMicFlushedTranscript` when a transcription final arrives and when manual-mic capture stops.

issues.body:
# Bug type

Behavior bug (incorrect output/state without crash)

# Beta release blocker

No

# Title

[Bug]: Codex OAuth profile rotation stops tool-using turns instead of continuing safely

# Summary

When a Codex turn reaches an OAuth usage limit after tool actions have completed, OpenClaw marks the attempt as non-replay-safe and stops the turn instead of continuing from the next safe boundary with another eligible OAuth profile.

# Steps to reproduce

1. Configure two eligible OpenAI OAuth profiles for the Codex provider.
2. Start a turn that performs one or more tool actions.
3. During the same turn, exhaust the active profile's Codex usage limit.
4. Observe that OpenClaw surfaces the usage-limit message and stops the turn.
5. Send a new user message and observe that the second OAuth profile is selected successfully.

# Expected behavior

When another eligible OAuth profile exists, OpenClaw should preserve completed tool calls and their results, switch profiles, and continue from the next safe boundary without replaying previously completed tool actions. This should use continuation semantics rather than replaying the whole turn. PR #108966 demonstrates the same safe-continuation principle for Codex tool-terminal turns.

# Actual behavior

The in-progress turn stops after the usage-limit error because the attempt is marked `replaySafe=no`. Auth-profile rotation occurs only on the next separately triggered user turn, so the original workflow does not continue.

# OpenClaw version

2026.10.1 (e178c39)

# Operating system

Ubuntu 24.04

# Install method

npm global

# Model

openai/gpt-5.6-sol

# Provider / routing chain

OpenClaw -> Codex app server -> OpenAI OAuth

# Additional provider/model setup details

Two eligible OAuth profiles were configured. The first profile reached its usage limit during the tool-using turn. A subsequent new turn selected the second profile successfully, confirming that the alternate profile was available. Profile identifiers and account details are intentionally omitted.

# Logs

```text
User-visible error: You've reached your Codex subscription usage limit.
Completed tool actions before the error: 8
Replay classification: replaySafe=no
Observed recovery: the next separately triggered turn selected the other eligible OAuth profile
```

# Screenshots, recordings, and evidence

Related safe-continuation implementation: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/108966

# Impact and severity

- Affected: installations using multiple OAuth profiles with long, tool-using Codex turns.
- Severity: high for state-changing workflows because manual replay can duplicate external actions.
- Frequency: 1/1 observed attempts matching this condition.
- Consequence: the workflow stops and requires a new user turn; blindly retrying risks repeating completed tool actions.

# Additional information

This report does not request replaying the failed turn. It requests a continuation path that carries forward the existing transcript and completed tool results, rotates the OAuth profile, and resumes only unfinished work. For tools with an unknown external outcome, continuation should reconcile or stop at an explicit recovery boundary rather than invoke the tool again automatically.

## Bug

In `apps/android/app/src/main/java/ai/openclaw/app/gateway/GatewaySession.kt`, `downloadScopedMediaTicket` executes `httpClient.newCall(request).execute()` inside a blocking `withContext(ioDispatcher)` block without wiring coroutine cancellation to `call.cancel()`.

## Impact

When the caller coroutine is cancelled or times out while downloading ticketed gateway media, the underlying OkHttp socket read continues blocking the IO thread until the network socket times out or finishes downloading the entire payload.

## Fix

Execute the OkHttp `Call` via a cancellation-aware helper that registers `continuation.invokeOnCancellation { call.cancel() }` before `call.execute()` and rethrows `CancellationException` when the coroutine was cancelled.

The fix is ready on `saariuslystoned/openclaw:fix/android-ticketed-media-download-cancellation-20261108` at `6c09cd9a0f97bc42e743508ac67bc6c3b2a78149` ☁️

2026.9.8 (fc23bc8).

## Bug

In `apps/android/app/src/main/java/ai/openclaw/app/node/LocationHandler.kt`, `handleLocationGet` checks `isForeground() || allowsBackgroundLocation()` only before calling `disclosure.getLocation(...)`. If a `location.get` request is admitted while the app is in the foreground under `LocationMode.WhileUsing`, and the user backgrounds the app while waiting for a fresh GPS fix, `handleLocationGet` still returns the captured coordinates once the fix arrives.

## Impact

A pending `location.get` request in `WhileUsing` mode can disclose coordinates captured after the app has transitioned to the background.

## Fix

Recheck `!isForeground() && !allowsBackgroundLocation()` immediately after `disclosure.getLocation(...)` returns and fail with `LOCATION_BACKGROUND_UNAVAILABLE` before constructing the coordinate payload.

The fix is ready on `saariuslystoned/openclaw:fix/android-location-while-using-background-recheck-20261108` at `ab0091fc9a66825b98fac0fff6cb632b14fe2818` ☁️

## Bug

issues.body:
### Bug type

Behavior bug (incorrect output/state without crash)

### Beta release blocker

No

### Summary

GitHub publication discovery (`src/gateway/github-publication-discovery.ts`) calls `refreshAll` on every config change (an "all" session change with scope `config`, which an agent add or a model switch publishes) and on a GitHub identity or managed profile change. `refreshAll` schedules one refresh per remembered session, up to the LRU's 256, each with `delayMs: 0`. The scheduler starts them together, and each one begins with a session-store target inventory read on the "Session target discovery" worker lane (one worker, 128 pending at most). Past 128 the lane refuses at once instead of queueing (`WorkerTaskPoolCore.enqueue`), so user-turn reads that need the same lane in that window fail with `worker task capacity reached`.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Run a gateway with about 150 agents, each with a few sessions that have read a publication fact.
2. Keep about 40 requests in flight (OpenAI-compatible endpoint or normal turns).
3. Add an agent, or change any config value that publishes a config-scoped session change.

### Expected behavior

The config change refreshes publication facts without refusing user work. Discovery can lag ("Discovery can lag a refresh"), but it should not take the lane's whole capacity at once.

### Actual behavior

On 2026.10.10, local gateway, 150 agents, 40 requests in flight: 130 refusals in the 1.7 s between `config change detected` and `config hot reload applied`. 129 of the reads queued on the lane were these refreshes. The refused reads were user-turn work on the same lane: start-of-run session persistence, the OpenAI-compatible request's session authorization, hook runs and placement evidence.

Production, 2026.10.10, one gateway with about 480 agents (UTC 2026-11-09): 14 refusals in the two seconds before an agent add's reload applied (01:10:25 to :28), and 1 more on the next reload (02:17:57). A restart's startup wave caused 14 more at 01:58, but that came from the startup path that #175030 changes on main.

Upstream main (checked 2026-11-09): #175030 made discovery demand-only, which removes the startup wave over the whole roster. `refreshAll` is unchanged, though: it still schedules every remembered session (up to 256) at delay 0, which is twice the lane's 128-pending limit.

### Suggested fix

Run a wave's refreshes one at a time instead of all at once. The jobs stay the same, with the same ids at the same times. A newer schedule still replaces a pending one, and a superseded or stopped refresh still returns before it reads. The lane has one worker, so the wave already finishes at about that pace. The difference is that it no longer refuses other callers. We run this as a local patch on 2026.10.10: a promise chain owned by the discovery instance, which each scheduled job awaits before it calls `prepareGitHubPublicationFact`. Our test drives the real 2026.10.10 discovery module and the real `GatewayScheduler` with 200 remembered sessions on a 128-pending lane. On a config change, stock refuses 72 refreshes, plus all 10 user reads sent during the wave. With the chain, nothing is refused.

A bounded batch (for example, at most N refreshes pending on the lane) would work too.

### OpenClaw version

2026.10.10 (`refreshAll` is the same on main and in v2026.11.5-beta.1 as of 2026-11-09)

### Operating system

Linux (Amazon Linux 2023), Node 24

### Install method

npm global

### Impact and severity

User turns fail with `worker task capacity reached` for one to two seconds after each agent add or model switch on gateways with more than about 128 remembered sessions. On a multi-tenant gateway, every config change is someone else's change, so the failures look random to the user.

### Additional information

Related: #194873 (the same lane overflowing at startup, from other producers) and #195621 (headroom for Control UI reads during background bursts). Neither changes this producer.

issues.title: Android: ChatController drops gateway ownership when chat.fork completes after a brief disconnect

labels.name: clawsweeper:bulk-filed
labels.description: ClawSweeper detected a high recent issue-filing volume from this author.

issues.body:
## Bug

In `apps/android/app/src/main/java/ai/openclaw/app/chat/ChatController.kt`, `forkMessage` captures `forkGatewayId = activeGatewayId` before launching the `chat.fork` request, but checks `forkGatewayId == activeGatewayId` after `session.request("chat.fork", ...)` completes. Because a brief disconnect clears `activeGatewayId = null` in `onDisconnected()` before `chat.fork` returns, `forkGatewayId == activeGatewayId` evaluates to `false` even when no different gateway has connected.

## Impact

When `chat.fork` succeeds across a brief disconnect/reconnect on the same gateway, `ChatController` drops the forked session switch and leaves `_errorText` unset or stale instead of activating the newly created fork session on that gateway.

## Fix

Retain `lastKnownGatewayId` in `ChatController` across disconnects (updated only when a non-blank gateway connects) and verify `lastKnownGatewayId == forkGatewayId` upon `chat.fork` completion while rejecting completions if a different gateway became active.

The fix is ready on `saariuslystoned/openclaw:fix/android-chat-fork-gateway-ownership-20261108` at `bf3162f5c9be7d221b43fc9e6c0abbfd5a2cf6c5` ☁️

issues.body:
### Summary

Provide a supported way to return a session's auth-profile selection to automatic/configured routing; today a persisted same-provider `@profile` pin can only be replaced by another pin, so it keeps a session off the agent's configured `model.primary` `@profile` indefinitely.

### Problem to solve

A session carrying a persisted auth pin (`authProfileOverride=openai:<profile-B>`, `authProfileOverrideSource="user"`) keeps running on profile B even though the agent's configured primary is `openai/gpt-6.1-sol@openai:<profile-A>`. Observed on 2026.10.10 (549b039), one session over one day (times UTC-4), from the run's `authProfileId`:

```text
14:13–18:58  runs on openai:<profile-B>   (configured primary says @openai:<profile-A>)
19:00:04     profile B hits its Codex 5h usage limit mid-turn (see #169380)
19:00–19:09  runs on openai:<profile-A>   (profile B in cooldown)
20:04–20:41  back on openai:<profile-B>   (cooldown expired; pin still in force)
```

We steer accounts by changing the agent's configured `@profile` from an external quota monitor (it moves agents off accounts that are close to their limits). That works for unpinned sessions, but a pinned session is out of its reach: profile A was at about 20% weekly usage and profile B at about 77%, and the pinned session stayed on B until B's 5h window ran out mid-turn and the raw quota error was sent to the user.

Reading the 2026.10.10 source, the pin can't be dropped back to automatic by any supported route (these are from source and docs, not each run live):

- `resolveSessionAuthSelection` (`src/agents/auth-profiles/session-override.ts`, ~L643) selects `rotatedPinnedProfileId ?? configuredProfileId ?? rotatedProfileId`, so a persisted user pin outranks the configured `@profile`, and user pins "remain strict while their provider is compatible" (~L411).
- `/model default` and `sessions.patch {key, model: null}` keep a compatible pin (`applyModelOverrideWithAuthProfileCompatibility` → `preserveAuthProfileOverride`, `src/sessions/auth-profile-preservation.ts` ~L101; documented in `docs/help/faq-models.md`: "`/model default` keeps a compatible auth pin").
- `/new` and `/reset` preserve user pins (`src/config/sessions/reset-preserved-selection.ts`).
- `sessions.patch` has no auth-profile field (`packages/gateway-protocol/src/schema/sessions-patch.ts`).
- The only documented change is choosing another `model@profile`, which replaces one strict pin with another and adds a session model override.

We could not determine what wrote this pin: there was no `/login` or `/model …@profile` in that chat that we could find. One thing we did see: earlier, our monitor had briefly set the agent's configured primary to `@openai:<profile-B>`. If any path persists the per-turn selection of a configured `@profile` with the default `profileOverrideSource ?? "user"`, that would produce exactly this, which would make it related to #158421 (configured `@profile` resolved as a user pin). That is an inference, not something we reproduced.

### Proposed solution

1. A supported way to clear only the auth selection and return to automatic/configured routing: e.g. `sessions.patch {key, authProfile: null}` and a matching chat command (`/model account default` or similar).
2. Show the pin and its source in `openclaw sessions list/describe` and `/model status`, including a note that it overrides the agent's configured `@profile`.
3. Never persist a selection derived from the agent's configured `@profile` as a `user` pin (related: #158421).

### Alternatives considered

- Re-pinning with `/model <model>@<profile-A>`: moves the session, but leaves it just as stuck the next time the preferred account changes, and adds a model override.
- Editing the session store directly: unsupported and unsafe while the gateway runs.
- Removing profile B from `auth.order`: that only constrains automatic pins; a user pin remains strict.

### Impact

- Affected: operators who steer accounts through the configured `@profile` (multi-account Codex/OpenAI OAuth setups) and any session that has acquired a same-provider user pin.
- Severity: medium-high. Configuration silently stops controlling that session's account, and combined with #169380 it surfaces raw quota errors to end users.
- Frequency: persistent for the affected session, every turn, until manually re-pinned.
- Consequence: uneven account usage, mid-turn usage-limit failures on the long-running main chat, and no supported way to undo it.

### Evidence/examples

Log excerpt and source references above. Related: #169380 (mid-turn continuation after usage limit), #149785 (earlier report, stale-closed 2026-11-02), #158421 (configured `@profile` treated as a user pin), #141795 (`/model … -s` survives `/new`), #87957 (session model/auth state refactor).

### Do you plan to open a PR for this?

No, proposing the idea only

### Additional information

OpenClaw 2026.10.10 (549b039), macOS, Codex app-server harness, provider chain OpenClaw -> Codex app server -> OpenAI OAuth (four profiles in `auth.order.openai`).

issues.body:
## Summary

When two (or more) Telegram bots run in the same Gateway and share a group, a bot's `/reasoning stream` preview ("🧠 …") is stored as an ordinary message in the **other** bot's persistent Telegram message cache (`telegram.message-cache`). The preview is deleted after the final answer, but Telegram never delivers that deletion to the other bot, so the cached copy stays. Every later group turn of the other bot then carries the foreign reasoning text in its `chat_window` history, and Anthropic refuses the whole request:

```
The provider refused this request (category: reasoning_extraction). Revise the request and try again.
```

The trigger is not the preview itself. In our case, a human message started the turn that failed, and the refused request contained the other bot's streamed reasoning only via the chat-window history.

## Environment

- OpenClaw 2026.9.7. The code path is unchanged on `main` (86310c83bf): `src/auto-reply/reply/inbound-meta.ts` → `formatChatWindowMessage`, `extensions/telegram/src/group-history-window.ts` → `selectTelegramGroupPromptContext`.
- Two Telegram bot accounts in one Gateway, both members of the same forum supergroup, privacy mode off.
- Both agents on `anthropic/claude-opus-5-5`, group `reasoningLevel: stream`.

## Steps to reproduce

1. Run bot A and bot B in one Gateway, both in the same Telegram group, with `/reasoning stream` enabled for bot A.
2. Address bot A so it streams a reasoning preview (`🧠 …`) and then answers. The preview is deleted.
3. Address bot B with any ordinary message.

**Expected:** bot B answers.
**Actual:** bot B's request includes lines like `#15820 … Bot A: 🧠 <bot A's reasoning>` in the runtime-context chat window, and the provider refuses it (`reasoning_extraction`). The failure repeats on every group turn of bot B until those cache entries age out.

`sessions.reset` on bot B's group session does not help, because the entries live in the message cache, not in the session. `selectTelegramGroupPromptContext` re-emits everything after bot B's last own message, and bot B cannot produce a new own message while every turn is refused.

## Why it happens

- The streamed preview is a real `sendMessage`/`editMessageText` message, so every other bot in the group receives it as a normal group message and caches it.
- Deletions are not delivered to bots, so the cache keeps the preview indefinitely (up to the 3000-entry cap).
- The chat-window renderer does not know which cached messages were reasoning previews of a sibling account in the same process.

## Possible fixes (any one would do)

1. **Same-process awareness:** when an account deletes its own reasoning preview, drop that message id from the message caches of the other Telegram accounts in the same Gateway, or record preview ids and skip them when rendering chat-window history.
2. **Don't post previews as real messages:** #161528 (live drafts via `sendMessageDraft`) would avoid this entirely, because drafts are not delivered to other bots.
3. **Minimal guard:** skip chat-window lines from bot senders whose body starts with the reasoning-preview prefix when rendering history (`formatChatWindowMessage`).

## Local workaround (for reference)

We patch the built `formatChatWindowMessage` to return `undefined` for a cached message whose body starts with `🧠`, `💭`, `<think>`, `<thinking>`, `reasoning:` or `thinking:` and whose sender is a bot (`sender_username` ends in `bot`) or has no username. Filtering at render time also clears entries that are already cached. In addition, a plugin `before_agent_reply`/`before_dispatch` hook claims turns whose triggering group message is such a preview, so bot B does not start a turn on bot A's reasoning at all.

Related: #161528, #24510, #32911, #129518 (same refusal category, compaction path).

## Bug

In `apps/android/app/src/main/java/ai/openclaw/app/voice/TalkModeManager.kt`, when an active Talk run ends with `state == "aborted"` or `state == "error"` and no streaming assistant text was captured for that run, `finalizeAssistantOnce` still falls back to `fetchLatestAssistantTextFromHistory()` and speaks the previous turn's assistant message aloud.

## Impact

If a Talk mode turn fails or is aborted before producing assistant output, the phone reads the previous assistant response aloud from chat history as if it were the reply to the failed turn.

## Fix

Restrict history fallback recovery in `TalkModeManager` to `"final"` terminal events (`allowHistoryRecovery = state == "final"`) so `"aborted"` and `"error"` runs never recover stale assistant text from history.

The fix is ready on `saariuslystoned/openclaw:fix/android-talk-terminal-failure-no-recovery-20261108` at `664f49c985b5b49ec560ae60469696947462e889` ☁️

### Summary

### Steps to reproduce

Resolve patched versions within the existing major APIs, preserving Zod 3 compatibility consumers and the current parent-package versions.

- RE2JS: [GHSA-gg6h-894w-4m9c](https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-gg6h-894w-4m9c), fixed in 2.8.7. This path is development tooling, not a claim of packaged Gateway exposure.

This is a resolved-dependency finding, not a demonstrated exploit or assessment of deployed reachability. No new vulnerability is disclosed.

### OpenClaw version

2026.10.10, current-main commit above.

Linux ARM64, Node 26.13.0, pnpm 12.15.0.

### Additional information

A narrow same-major override can repair these older transitive pins without that parent upgrade or any release-age exception. issues.body:
### Bug type
Behavior bug (incorrect output/state without crash)

### Beta release blocker
No

### Summary
In a WhatsApp DM session with `verboseLevel: "full"` and message-tool-only visible replies (Codex harness default), ordinary turns deliver only the agent's `message` tool sends. A message that arrives while a run is active is queued as a follow-up (`steering rejected; applying follow-up policy ... disposition=followup-queued`), and the resulting follow-up turn delivers every tool result/output to the chat. One follow-up run with 78 tool calls produced about 215 WhatsApp messages, most of them raw tool output (JSON bodies). An earlier direct turn in the same session, same build and same verbose level, also with 78 tool calls, sent about 2.

So the same session settings produce two very different chat behaviors depending on whether the turn was dispatched directly or drained from the follow-up queue.

### Steps to reproduce
1. WhatsApp DM to an agent on the Codex harness (visible replies resolve to `message_tool`), session `verboseLevel: "full"`.
2. Send a message that starts a long, tool-heavy run (dozens of tool calls).
3. While it runs, send a second message. The gateway logs `steering rejected; applying follow-up policy reason=unknown-source-with-terminal-history disposition=followup-queued channel=whatsapp`.
4. When the follow-up turn runs, watch the chat.

### Expected behavior
A queued follow-up turn applies the same tool-result/tool-output visibility as a directly dispatched turn in the same session and source-delivery mode. If verbose=full is meant to show tool output in message-tool-only mode, direct turns should show it too; if not, follow-ups shouldn't.

### Actual behavior
Direct turn (08:29, 78 tool calls): about 2 outbound WhatsApp messages, outcome `message-tool-only run outcome tool_delivered`.
Queued follow-up turn (15:15, 78 tool calls): about 215 outbound WhatsApp messages over ~30 minutes, mostly tool output, same outcome line `tool_delivered`.

### OpenClaw version
2026.10.10 (549b039)

### Operating system
macOS 27.2

### Install method
Source checkout, gateway under launchd

### Model
gpt-6.1-sol

### Provider / routing chain
openclaw -> codex app-server harness -> OpenAI (ChatGPT subscription)

### Additional provider/model setup details
`agents.defaults.verboseDefault: "off"`; session-level `verboseLevel: "full"`. `toolProgressDetail: "explain"`, `blockStreamingDefault: "on"`.

### Logs
```
15:14:59 [diagnostic] steering rejected; applying follow-up policy reason=unknown-source-with-terminal-history disposition=followup-queued channel=whatsapp sessionId=<session>
15:15:34 [plugins] [reply-guarantee] outbound_recorded {... "correlation":"route","sessionKey":"agent:main:main","runId":"<followup-run>" ...}
... [whatsapp] Sending message -> sha256:<redacted>   (x ~215 between 15:15 and 15:45)
```

### Screenshots, recordings, and evidence
Per-run counts from `trajectory_runtime_events` (tool.call) and gateway `[whatsapp] Sending message` lines. Message bodies are private and not attached.

### Impact and severity
High annoyance for the affected user: a single queued follow-up floods a personal WhatsApp chat with hundreds of internal tool outputs. Workaround: set `/verbose off`.

### Additional information
Code reading (inference, not confirmed at runtime): the follow-up path builds its own gating in `src/auto-reply/reply/followup-turn-execution.ts` (`shouldEmitVerboseToolResult` / `shouldEmitToolOutput` and the `onToolResult` wrapper), and when `verboseToolResult` is true it skips the `message_tool_only` early-return and calls `params.onToolResult` directly. Direct turns go through `dispatch-from-config.execute.ts` `onToolResult`, gated by `shouldSendToolSummariesAsync` / `shouldSuppressProgressDelivery`. This path looks unchanged on current `main`. Related but distinct: #98716 (follow-up honoring `suppressToolErrors`), #194248 and #181592 (follow-up path diverging from direct turns for auto-TTS).

issues.body:
### Bug type

Behavior bug (incorrect output/state without crash)

### Beta release blocker

No

### Summary

On OpenClaw 2026.11.1, **Acknowledge findings and continue** fails on an existing Discord-linked Codex session with `Cannot acknowledge provider review while rotating a native-tool-disabled thread binding`, leaving the conversation paused despite an available continuation and explicit human acknowledgment.

### Steps to reproduce

Observed on a real affected conversation; the initial configuration-drift trigger has not been reduced to a clean-install reproduction.

1. Open the affected Discord-linked session in the native macOS app's Control UI. The session has a saved provider review with `canContinue: true`.
2. Review the findings. In this incident the owner explicitly confirmed the disputed account association and authorized keeping it and continuing.
3. Click **Review findings → Acknowledge findings and continue** in that same conversation.
4. The button enters **Requesting continuation…**, then the request fails. The conversation remains paused and the composer disabled.
5. Incoming Discord messages also fail to start a turn and eventually receive the generic repeated-failures notice.

The acknowledgment in step 3 was directly reproduced once during this investigation. Earlier same-session logs contain a related failure naming `changing the dynamic tool catalog`.

### Expected behavior

The [documented acknowledgment flow](https://docs.openclaw.ai/concepts/model-failover#misalignment-precautions) should continue the exact reviewed conversation when its original runtime, model, policy, and tools remain valid. If compatibility has changed, the UI should identify the conflicting configuration and provide an actionable, supported recovery that preserves the review and history. It should not leave **Try again** as the only practical direction for a persistent compatibility failure.

### Actual behavior

The UI reports that it cannot continue, asks to try again, and truncates the useful part of the reason to `Cannot acknowledge provider review while rotating a ...`. The full gateway error identifies a native-tool-disabled binding. The review remains present with `canContinue: true`; normal input remains disabled.

The Discord account is connected (`running=true`, `connected=true`, `lifecycle=ready`, no channel error). Its sender-to-person association is present and the person retains the admin role. Those observations do not clear the separate provider-review pause.

### OpenClaw version

2026.11.1 (`870926f68774fb720667f5d70b9b3b1c9318ce37`)

### Operating system

macOS 27.2, arm64 (gateway); native macOS OpenClaw app as operator UI.

### Install method

Global npm installation, gateway managed by launchd.

### Model

`openai/gpt-6.1-sol`, Codex harness.

### Provider / routing chain

Discord / native macOS Control UI → OpenClaw Gateway → Codex harness → OpenAI.

### Additional provider/model setup details

The current UI reports Full access and the same model. No model switch, credential replacement, permission expansion, gateway restart, manual state edit, or session reset was performed during this investigation. Exact original tool/runtime configuration drift is not yet established.

### Logs

Identifiers and unrelated log content omitted. Current direct reproduction, 2026-11-08 22:08:27 EST (2026-11-09 03:08:27 UTC):

```text
Codex agent harness failed; not falling back to embedded OpenClaw backend
Cannot acknowledge provider review while rotating a native-tool-disabled thread binding. The reviewed thread is preserved; restore its original tools and runtime configuration, then retry the acknowledgment from the original conversation.
```

Earlier same-session acknowledgment attempt, 2026-11-08 18:51:12 EST:

```text
Cannot acknowledge provider review while changing the dynamic tool catalog. The reviewed thread is preserved; restore its original tools and runtime configuration, then retry the acknowledgment from the original conversation.
```

Incoming Discord messages fail before a new model turn:

```text
SessionWorkStartError: Session "<affected-session>" is paused as a precaution. Review the provider findings in chat before continuing.
discord ingress: spooled update <message> failed after 8 attempts (retry-limit-exceeded); dead-lettered
```

### Screenshots, recordings, and evidence

Captured from the real app; cropped and explicitly redacted. Full account details, private endpoints, session/channel IDs, sidebar, and unrelated conversations are excluded.

**1. Review dialog offers acknowledgment:**

![Provider review dialog with acknowledgment control](https://github.com/saari-co/public-oss-proof-assets/releases/download/openclaw-review-continuation-20261108-v1/01-review-dialog-redacted.png)

**2. Failed continuation leaves the composer disabled:**

![Continuation fails and conversation remains paused](https://github.com/saari-co/public-oss-proof-assets/releases/download/openclaw-review-continuation-20261108-v1/02-continuation-failure-redacted.png)

[Versioned evidence and SHA-256 manifest](https://github.com/saari-co/public-oss-proof-assets/releases/tag/openclaw-review-continuation-20261108-v1).

Source inspection at the installed commit matches the error: [`thread-lifecycle-run.ts:81`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/870926f68774fb720667f5d70b9b3b1c9318ce37/extensions/codex/src/app-server/thread-lifecycle-run.ts#L81) rejects replacement during provider-review acknowledgment; [line 444](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/870926f68774fb720667f5d70b9b3b1c9318ce37/extensions/codex/src/app-server/thread-lifecycle-run.ts#L444) attempts replacement when `restrictedThreadConfigFingerprint` exists and native code mode is now enabled. This explains the observed rejection, not the original cause of the drift.

### Impact and severity

Affected: one confirmed Discord-linked conversation and its Control UI view. Blocks normal conversation use; even short greetings are rejected before inference. The directly observed acknowledgment fails, and multiple earlier incoming messages exhausted retries. A gateway-wide outage is not established.

### Additional information

Related: #190563 (already-mismatched native review/thread recovery). This report has a different immediate error: the lifecycle guard prevents replacement for tool-configuration incompatibility **before** continuation can be accepted. We have not established that the reviewed native ID and stored binding already differ, so this is not presented as proof of the same underlying defect.

Please preserve exact review/thread matching and existing safety checks. The request is for supported compatibility recovery and a useful UI explanation, not clearing the review flag or bypassing acknowledgment. Original history, review state, bindings, and failed inbound messages have been left intact.

First affected and last known-good versions: NOT_ENOUGH_INFO. No fix or workaround is claimed. Report prepared with AI assistance from direct owner-authorized observation and installed-source inspection.


### Follow-up source investigation — 2026-11-09

The saved reviewed native thread and the current persisted binding are now confirmed to differ. The original transcript remains present; its native rollout digest and all 2,854 gateway transcript events were unchanged during investigation. No review flags or bindings were manually edited.

A source-level reproduction identified an additional drift path: cold MCP App preparation can reach native lifecycle setup with an empty dynamic-tool catalog and restricted configuration without consulting the session's pending work-start pause. The source reproduction matches the successor binding's shape; it does **not** establish that this path caused the historical live incident.

A small **prevention-only** patch is available at [commit d3facad989f](https://github.com/saariuslystoned/openclaw/commit/d3facad989f7d6b681f74bb2e21bc642b7e737c3). It reuses the canonical session work-start check throughout cold preparation's existing live effect assertions. Three timing regressions fail on the base and pass with the patch; 230 focused tests and targeted typecheck/lint/docs checks pass, with clean independent source review. The patch is not installed on the affected gateway and does not restore an already-replaced binding.

Safe original-binding recovery remains unresolved: native catalog validation can be reused, but an authentic original native-tool policy attestation is not available through the current owners after replacement. No policy fingerprints were fabricated and acknowledgment guards were preserved.

The owner-authorized operational continuation uses a new conversation with explicit context and links to the preserved original. Its actual Discord inbound/outbound identity check passed. The original review remains pending; this is not an acknowledgment or recovery of the original binding.

No PR was opened: the contributing account is at the repository's 20-open-PR limit. The prepared source branch remains available for maintainer inspection. The issue remains open.

issues.body:
### Bug type

Behavior bug (incorrect authority without a crash).

### Summary

A WhatsApp sender linked to a profile with `operator.admin` is admitted to chat but is not recognized as an owner for the `automations` tool.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Link a WhatsApp sender's canonical E.164 phone to a user profile for the relevant WhatsApp account.
2. Give that profile a Gateway role containing `operator.admin`. Do not add the phone to `commands.ownerAllowFrom`.
3. Admit a message from that sender in an allowed WhatsApp DM or group.
4. Ask the agent to inspect or update a scheduled automation using `automations`.

### Expected behavior

The authenticated sender's current linked administrator role supplies owner authority, as implemented by #153508. A missing link, different account, or revoked administrator role must not grant that authority.

### Actual behavior

The tool rejects the request before looking up an automation:

```text
automations needs the owner's authority, and this turn was not started by the owner. Do not retry automations.
```

The WhatsApp producer in `extensions/whatsapp/src/inbound-policy.ts` declares its primary identity as `kind: "phone"` with no authentication classification, which defaults to `asserted`. The shared ingress runtime only prepares the linked requester/authority from a primary `stable-id` with `authentication: "verified"`. Consequently the profile lookup is skipped even when the link and role are correct. Merely changing authentication to verified still leaves the kind mismatch.

The receive path supplies this identity from the socket session's resolved sender JID, rather than a display name or message body. Unresolved group LIDs do not supply a phone to this helper.

### OpenClaw version

Observed on 2026.11.1 (`1a8b289e7e3d46661127e52aadf955bd8990ea16`); the producer/consumer mismatch is also present on current main `df13b6b8994cefe16f311f29f0301bba511ec617`.

### Operating system

Amazon Linux 2023, Linux ARM64.

### Install method

Node CLI with the WhatsApp plugin; current-main source checkout used for reproduction.

### Model / provider route

Not model-specific: reproduced at the native channel ingress/owner authorization boundary without a model call.

### Evidence and scope

Compared the native ingress descriptors: asserted phone and verified phone both omit linked principal resolution; a verified stable primary reaches it. Existing linked-admin behavior is covered for other channels, but WhatsApp supplies a different descriptor. This report concerns the channel identity handoff, not automation database ownership or a scheduler write failure. No regression introduction date is established.

Searched related open and closed issues/PRs for WhatsApp owner authority, linked administrators, verified phones, and automation ownership. No matching fix found; #153508 is related prior implementation.

issues.body:
## Summary

On an official **2026.10.10-beta.5** Linux x64 Gateway, startup orphan discovery failed with `WorkerTaskError: worker task capacity reached`; cron inventory maintenance hit the same admission error eleven seconds later. The startup warning loses the stack and which capacity limit was exhausted, so the evidence cannot distinguish a task backlog from an oversized inventory payload. This is **overload**, not the original timeout in #181090 (which also has a newer comment reporting this overload signature on Windows 2026.10.10).

## Environment and observed sequence

- OpenClaw 2026.10.10-beta.5, Node 24.22.1, Linux x64, systemd user service.
- Safe restart; old process drained its active work before shutdown. The old process separately encountered the known #144336/#187137 close-failure class; its supervisor started a new process.
- New process startup, UTC 2026-11-07:

```text
22:48:42.504 main-session startup orphan marking failed before channel startup:
             WorkerTaskError: worker task capacity reached
22:48:53.770 Cron maintenance failed
             WorkerTaskError: worker task capacity reached (errorCode=overloaded)
  WorkerTaskPoolCore.enqueue (dist/src-BIG1flG6.mjs:1013)
  WorkerTaskPoolCore.run
  Object.run (dist/worker-task-pool-B7BJD2Oh.mjs:147)
  session-transcript-worker-resources-CcjXBaMn.mjs:300
  runWithSqliteDatabaseAdmissionTurn
  runRead
  Object.readTargetInventory (session-transcript-worker-resources-CcjXBaMn.mjs:354)
  session-store-target-runtime-c7l8yVTE.mjs:76
```

This is one observed boot, **not a deterministic reproducer**. No interrupted work was known to require recovery on this boot; no claim of actual lost user work is made. Provider/model choice is not involved in this local inventory admission failure.

## Matching-tag source trace

- `src/gateway/server-startup-observers.ts:markGatewayStartupMainSessionOrphans()` catches the exception and emits `String(err)`.
- `src/agents/main-session-recovery/main-session-restart-recovery-marking.ts:markStartupOrphanedMainSessionsForRecovery()` awaits `discoverRestartRecoveryStoreTargets()` **before** its per-target try/catch and failed-target recording.
- `main-session-restart-recovery-shared.ts:discoverRestartRecoveryStoreTargets()` calls `prepareSessionStoreTargetInventoryRead(...).withRead(...)`.
- `src/config/sessions/session-transcript-worker-resources.ts:runRead()` sends the inventory to `targetDiscoveryLane.pool.run`.
- That lane uses `createSessionTranscriptHistoryPool()` / `createOwnedWorkerTaskPool()`. `packages/worker-runtime/src/worker-task-pool-core.ts:enqueue()` rejects with the same unstructured message for pending-task and pending-byte exhaustion (defaults 128 tasks / 256 MiB). The generic core also supports shared-compute admission refusal, but this discovery pool does **not** opt into `sharedCompute`.

The cron stack confirms the inventory pool boundary. The startup stack was discarded, so attribution of its precise failing suboperation remains inferred from the exception escaping discovery. Pending count, pending bytes, incoming inventory size, and the responsible callers were not recorded. Increasing a cap or adding blind retries is not justified by this evidence.

## Newer-release status / scope

- **2026.11.1 still has the same pre-channel marking path and catch-and-warn.** A stable upgrade does not establish a repair.
- #181289/#185732 reduced/moved recovery work; #185520 trimmed inventory payloads. They are related improvements, not proof that this admission failure is repaired.
- **2026.11.5-beta.1 includes #185730**, which deletes startup orphan reconstruction entirely and resumes explicit graceful-shutdown markers through `src/gateway/session-restart-resume.ts:resumeMarkedSessions()`. This removes this exact old warning/path, **not** the underlying capacity condition: the replacement still calls `prepareSessionStoreTargetInventoryRead(...).withRead(...)`, and its caller logs `Restart resume discovery failed` on failure. This is source analysis, **not a reproduction on beta.1/current main**.
- #185730 explicitly accepts crash/SIGKILL as lossy (no shutdown marker/no automatic resume). That is a changed contract, not restored crash-orphan coverage.

## Expected / next discriminating evidence

Identify the exhausted limit and inventory operation in the overload diagnostic (counts/byte totals only, no session/config contents), then reproduce the specific boundary on the supported newer path. Establish whether startup can lose an otherwise valid graceful-resume opportunity under that condition before selecting a behavior fix. No request to restore the removed recovery architecture, raise caps, or change accepted crash semantics.

AI-assisted investigation. No local core patches, Gateway restarts for testing, or regression-test claims.
