No

### Summary

When an agent is removed from `agents.entries` by a config write, the hot reload applies the change but never releases the agent. The Gateway keeps that agent's `openclaw-agent.sqlite`, `-wal` and `-shm` open for as long as it runs.

`agents.delete` is the only call that releases an agent (drain, close the memory runtime, retire it, close worker readers). But it answers `agent "<id>" not found` for any agent that is not in config and has no deletion journal, so it never reaches that code. Nothing can release the agent short of a restart.

If the agent's directory is then removed, the Linux WAL split-brain tripwire finds the open `-wal` descriptor with `nlink 0` on its next periodic tick (every 30 minutes by default) and SIGKILLs the Gateway. Every turn running on that Gateway dies with it.

On one production Gateway (about 480 agents, 2026.10.10), an agent was removed from config at 00:08:53 UTC and its directory at 00:09:58. The Gateway was SIGKILLed at 00:27:01 with `SQLite WAL sidecar identity mismatch; terminating without SQLite cleanup` for that agent's database, and systemd restarted it.

### Steps to reproduce

Linux is needed for the kill (the tripwire reads `/proc/self/fd`). Steps 1 to 4 also reproduce on macOS.

1. Run a Gateway on 2026.10.10 with two agents in `agents.entries`, say `main` and `doomed` (2026.10.10 wants `agents.ownership: "explicit"` and `agents.defaults.systemAgent.agentId: "main"` for two agents). Wait until it has opened `doomed`'s database: `lsof -p <gateway pid> | grep agents/doomed` lists `openclaw-agent.sqlite`, `-wal` and `-shm`.
2. Remove `doomed` from `agents.entries` in `openclaw.json` (by hand, or with any config writer). Wait for `config hot reload applied (agents.entries.doomed)`.
3. `lsof` again: the handles are still open. In our run, 16 of the 17 descriptors were open after the reload, and 13 five minutes later, still including the `-wal` and `-shm`.
4. Call `agents.delete` with `{"agentId":"doomed","deleteFiles":false}` (or `deleteFiles: true`). The answer is `INVALID_REQUEST agent "doomed" not found`, and the handles stay open.
5. `rm -rf <stateDir>/agents/doomed`.
6. Within 30 minutes (the next periodic WAL maintenance tick for that database), the Gateway writes the fatal line and SIGKILLs itself.

### Expected behavior

Removing an agent from config releases it. When the reload commits a roster without `doomed`, the Gateway closes `doomed`'s databases and retires its runtime, as `agents.delete` does, without touching its files.

Failing that, `agents.delete` can release an agent the Gateway still holds even when it is no longer configured: run the same drain, close and retire steps, skip the config write (there is nothing to remove), and leave files alone when `deleteFiles` is false.

### Actual behavior

Code path at `v2026.10.10` ([7dc3350cb9](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/tree/7dc3350cb9f08fcf9a0af5c4845a20d5b2f1a8be)):

- **The reload does not release a removed agent.** After a roster change the hot reload calls only [`reviveAgentDatabasesAfterConfigCommit(listAgentIds(nextConfig))`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/7dc3350cb9f08fcf9a0af5c4845a20d5b2f1a8be/src/gateway/server-reload-hot.ts#L354-L358), which handles agents that *come back* after a deletion ([`server-reload-agent-databases.ts#L4-L22`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/7dc3350cb9f08fcf9a0af5c4845a20d5b2f1a8be/src/gateway/server-reload-agent-databases.ts#L4-L22)). Nothing on that path closes the databases of an agent that left.
- **`agents.delete` refuses it.** The handler answers not found when the agent is not configured and has no open journal ([`agents.ts#L332-L339`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/7dc3350cb9f08fcf9a0af5c4845a20d5b2f1a8be/src/gateway/server-methods/agents.ts#L332-L339)), and `deleteGatewayAgent` repeats the check under the config lock ([`agents-delete.ts#L125-L127`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/7dc3350cb9f08fcf9a0af5c4845a20d5b2f1a8be/src/gateway/server-methods/agents-delete.ts#L125-L127)). The steps that would release the agent all come after that check: [`closeActiveMemorySearchManagerCore`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/7dc3350cb9f08fcf9a0af5c4845a20d5b2f1a8be/src/gateway/server-methods/agents-delete.ts#L172-L175), [`retireAgentDeleteRuntime`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/7dc3350cb9f08fcf9a0af5c4845a20d5b2f1a8be/src/gateway/server-methods/agents-delete.ts#L332) and [`closeDeletedAgentDatabases`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/7dc3350cb9f08fcf9a0af5c4845a20d5b2f1a8be/src/gateway/server-methods/agents-delete.ts#L351-L354).
- **The tripwire kills the Gateway once the files go.** Periodic WAL maintenance runs every 30 minutes by default ([`sqlite-wal.ts#L60`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/7dc3350cb9f08fcf9a0af5c4845a20d5b2f1a8be/src/infra/sqlite-wal.ts#L60)). On Linux each tick checks the database's sidecars ([`#L314-L315`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/7dc3350cb9f08fcf9a0af5c4845a20d5b2f1a8be/src/infra/sqlite-wal.ts#L314-L315), [`#L486-L503`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/7dc3350cb9f08fcf9a0af5c4845a20d5b2f1a8be/src/infra/sqlite-wal.ts#L486-L503)). A descriptor with `nlink 0`, or whose path no longer exists, counts as split-brain ([`sqlite-wal-split-brain.ts#L30-L40`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/7dc3350cb9f08fcf9a0af5c4845a20d5b2f1a8be/src/infra/sqlite-wal-split-brain.ts#L30-L40)), and the process SIGKILLs itself ([`#L90-L117`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/7dc3350cb9f08fcf9a0af5c4845a20d5b2f1a8be/src/infra/sqlite-wal-split-brain.ts#L90-L117)). Here the files were removed on purpose by an operator, not replaced behind the Gateway's back, but the check cannot tell the two apart.

Local repro on macOS, 2026.10.10, two agents, `agents.delete {deleteFiles:false}` after the config strip:

| | Descriptors on the agent's files | `agents.delete` answer | `openclaw.json` |
|---|---|---|---|
| Before the strip | 17 (`.sqlite`, `-wal`, `-shm`) | | |
| After the strip and `hot reload applied` | 16 | | |
| After `agents.delete` | 16, and 13 five minutes later (still including `-wal` and `-shm`) | `INVALID_REQUEST agent "<id>" not found` | unchanged |

### OpenClaw version

2026.10.10 (7dc3350)

### Operating system

Production: Linux (Amazon Linux), state on local disk. Repro steps 1 to 4: macOS on arm64.

### Install method

npm global install, one systemd unit per Gateway

### Model

N/A (no model call involved)

### Provider / routing chain

N/A

### Logs

Production Gateway file log, agent id replaced with `<agent>`:

```
00:08:53.293 gateway/reload  config change detected; evaluating reload (agents.entries.<agent>)
00:09:06.724 gateway/reload  config hot reload applied (agents.entries.<agent>)
00:09:09.894 state/agent-db  {"path":"<stateDir>/agents/<agent>/agent/openclaw-agent.sqlite","receipt":"active-leases", ...}
```

The agent directory was removed at 00:09:58. At 00:27:01 the Gateway wrote `SQLite WAL sidecar identity mismatch; terminating without SQLite cleanup` (`databaseLabel: openclaw-agent:<agent>`), was killed with signal 9, and systemd restarted it. After the restart:

```
00:27:49.519 state/agent-db  {"agentId":"<agent>","path":"<stateDir>/agents/<agent>/agent/openclaw-agent.sqlite","staleReason":"owner-pid-dead", ...}
```

### Impact and severity

- **Affected:** any Gateway where agents are removed from config by a config write, then have their files removed. That is the normal way to remove agents on a host that manages `openclaw.json` itself, as ours does for about 480 agents per Gateway.
- **Severity:** High. The whole Gateway is SIGKILLed, and every turn in flight on it is lost, not only the removed agent's.
- **Frequency:** every such removal, up to 30 minutes after the files go. Until a restart, every removed agent also keeps its descriptors open.
- **Consequence:** an unplanned Gateway restart per removal. Avoiding it means never removing a removed agent's files until the Gateway restarts.

### Additional information

How this differs from the nearest existing issues:

- **#187309** (open, WAL/SHM identity mismatch after active-leases receipts on 2026.10.8): there the replacement of the sidecars has no known producer, and the agent is still configured and in use. Here the cause is known and reproduces every time: the agent is no longer configured, nothing releases its handles, and the files are removed on purpose.
- **#163453** (closed, tripwire on `state/openclaw.sqlite` on 2026.9.5): a single unexplained event on the shared state database. Here it is a per-agent database, and the tripwire is working as designed. The bug is that the Gateway still holds a database for an agent it no longer has.
- **#177021** (closed, `agents.delete` refused with `OpenClawAgentDatabaseLeaseActiveError`): that agent was configured, and the refusal came from a lease check that ran before worker pools were closed. Here `agents.delete` refuses much earlier, at the configured-or-journal check, so it never reaches the close steps that #177021 reordered.
- **#165665** (closed, an unfinished `agents.delete` crash-loops the next cold start): that is about a pending deletion journal. Here there is no journal at all, because the agent was removed by a config write, not by `agents.delete`.

Also seen, smaller: after a stock `agents.delete {deleteFiles:false}` on a *configured* agent, one read-only descriptor on `openclaw-agent.sqlite` (not `-wal` or `-shm`) was still open 5 minutes later. It does not trip the tripwire, which checks only the sidecars, but it pins the file's inode if the caller removes the files afterwards.

Our local fix, in review and not yet deployed: a dist patch on 2026.10.10 for the second expected behavior. When `agents.delete` gets an agent that is not configured, has no journal, `deleteFiles` is `false`, and the agent database registry still lists it, the call runs the normal delete path but skips `deleteAgentConfigEntry` and the config-application confirm, and answers with `configUnchanged: true`. A pending journal resumes exactly as before. In the same local repro, the patched call answers `{"ok":true,"agentId":"app-rigdel1","removedBindings":0,"configUnchanged":true,"removed":[],"failed":[]}`, `openclaw.json` is byte-for-byte unchanged, and the descriptors drop from 16 to 1 (the same single read-only descriptor as above). Our host will call it after it removes an agent from config, and remove the files only when the answer says `configUnchanged`. Until then our host keeps the removed agent's directory on disk, which is what avoids the kill today.

We think the first expected behavior, releasing a removed agent at reload time, is the better fix, because any config writer can remove an agent and none of them knows to call `agents.delete` afterwards. We are happy to send a PR for either.

### Bug type
Behavior bug (incorrect output/state without crash)

### Beta release blocker
No

### Summary
`decodeDataUrl` (src/media/image-data-url.ts), the sole decoder for inline image data URLs passed to agent image/media tools, rejects RFC 2397-legal data URLs whose media type carries parameters (e.g. `data:image/png;charset=utf-8;base64,...`), failing the tool call with `Invalid data URL (expected base64 data: URL).`

### Steps to reproduce
1. Check out openclaw `main` (`712a3611f` or later).
2. Invoke the decoder the image tool uses, with a parameterized data URL:
   `decodeDataUrl("data:image/png;charset=utf-8;base64,SGVsbG8=")` (e.g. via `pnpm vitest run src/media/image-data-url.test.ts` with a case exercising that input).
3. Observe it throws `Invalid data URL (expected base64 data: URL).`

The same input is accepted by the repo's sibling data-URL parsers (`packages/media-core/src/inline-image-data-url.ts` via `sanitizeInlineImageDataUrl`, and `src/image-generation/image-assets.ts:parseImageDataUrl`), so an inline image that one part of the product accepts fails in the agent tool path.

### Expected behavior
Per RFC 2397 the mediatype may include parameters (`data:image/png;charset=utf-8;base64,<data>` is a valid data URL), and the repo's other data-URL parsers accept that form, so the agent image/media tools should decode it the same way instead of failing the tool call.

### Actual behavior
The tool call fails with `Invalid data URL (expected base64 data: URL).` because the header regex `^data:([^;,]+);base64,` requires the `;base64` marker immediately after the MIME type. Observed on base `main`: adding cases for the parameterized form to `src/media/image-data-url.test.ts` fails 3/9 tests (parser rejects the valid URLs and mis-classifies a parameterized non-image as a generic invalid URL).

### OpenClaw version
Source checkout of `main` at 712a3611f (2026-11-09, post-2026.11.2)

### Operating system
Linux x64 (reproduced on the source checkout; parser behavior is OS-independent)

### Install method
source / pnpm dev

### Model
Any — deterministic parser path, no model involved

### Provider / routing chain
openclaw (local tool path) — no provider involved

### Logs
```
FAIL src/media/image-data-url.test.ts > decodeDataUrl > accepts media type parameters before the base64 marker
Error: Invalid data URL (expected base64 data: URL).
```

### Impact and severity
Affected: users/tools feeding inline image data URLs with media type parameters to agent image/media tools (view_image, image generation/editing references, media references).
Severity: blocks workflow when hit (tool call fails hard on an otherwise valid URL).
Frequency: edge case (requires a producer that emits parameters such as `;charset=utf-8`).
Consequence: agent cannot process an inline image that other OpenClaw paths accept; the misleading "expected base64 data: URL" error points users at the wrong fix.

### Additional information
The parser deliberately avoids capturing the payload for the size guard; the fix needs to allow `;parameter` segments before the `;base64` marker while keeping that property. `git log` shows src/media/image-data-url.ts has had a single owning commit (#188547), so the area is stable.

issues.body:
## Bug

In `apps/android/app/src/main/java/ai/openclaw/app/ui/chat/AgentPicker.kt`, `AgentChoiceChip` renders each agent option as a clickable `Surface` with visual selection styling (`isSelected`), but does not attach `Modifier.selectable(...)` or `Role.RadioButton` semantics.

## Impact

TalkBack and accessibility scanners announce every agent chip in the chat agent picker as an unselected generic clickable element, so screen-reader users cannot tell which agent is currently active.

## Fix

Apply `Modifier.selectable(selected = isSelected, onClick = onClick, role = Role.RadioButton)` to `AgentChoiceChip` so Compose exposes `SemanticsProperties.Selected` and radio-button role semantics matching the visual selection state.

The fix is ready on `saariuslystoned/openclaw:fix/android-agent-picker-selected-semantics-20261108` at `5cbabfce979575b31d137906a3dc602019a07517` ☁️

### Bug type

Behavior bug (incorrect output/state without crash)

### Beta release blocker

No

### Summary

Signal 👍 / 👎 approval reactions never work for approvals forwarded to an explicit target (`approvals.exec.mode: "targets"` with a Signal target). The prompt is sent as the plain-text manual fallback with no "React with:" hint, no reaction target is registered, and a 👍 on the prompt does nothing.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Configure `approvals.exec` (and/or `approvals.plugin`) with `enabled: true`, `mode: "targets"` and a target `{ channel: "signal", accountId: "<account>", to: "<approver>" }`; the approver is in that account's `allowFrom`, and the account has `account` set.
2. Trigger an exec approval from a non-Signal session (for example a Control UI session on a node).
3. React 👍 to the prompt that arrives in Signal.

### Expected behavior

The prompt includes the "React with: 👍 Allow once / 👎 Deny" hint and a 👍 resolves it as allow-once, as it does for approvals that originate in a Signal chat.

### Actual behavior

The prompt is the manual fallback ("Approval required. Run: /approve <id> allow-once …") without a reaction hint, the plugin state namespace `signal.approval-reactions.v2` has no entries, and the 👍 has no effect. `/approve` still works.

Cause, traced in the built code:
- `render.exec.buildPendingPayload` and `render.plugin.buildPendingPayload` in `extensions/signal/src/approval-native.ts` return `buildApprovalReactionPendingContentForRequest(...).manualFallbackPayload`, which is built `withoutPresentation`.
- Core only calls the outbound `renderPresentation` hook when the payload has a `presentation`, so `renderSignalApprovalPayloadForReactions` → `addSignalApprovalReactionHintToStructuredPayload` never runs.
- `registerDeliveredSignalApprovalPayloadForReactions` then finds no hint text and registers nothing.
- The native runtime, which does register reactions, only handles session-eligible requests (`shouldHandleApprovalRequest` → `isSessionApprovalEligible`), so it never covers forwarded targets.

### OpenClaw version

2026.10.7 (gateway and `@openclaw/signal`). `@openclaw/signal` 2026.11.2 has the same `manualFallbackPayload` render.

### Operating system

Linux (Docker host)

### Install method

docker (`ghcr.io/openclaw/openclaw` image, `@openclaw/signal` from npm)

### Model

Not model-related

### Provider / routing chain

Not model-related

### Logs

None captured. The prompt text and the empty `signal.approval-reactions.v2` namespace are the evidence.

### Impact and severity

Reaction approvals are unavailable for the common setup of forwarding approvals to an approver's Signal DM; approvers must type `/approve <id> <decision>`.

### Additional information

Possible fix (untested): have the Signal render path return `reactionPayload` (or otherwise add the reaction hint) for target deliveries, so the existing target-route code (`buildTargetRoute`, `isSignalApprovalReactionRouteStillEnabled` with `deliveryMode: "target"`) is used.

issues.body:
### Bug type

Behavior bug (incorrect output/state without crash)

### Beta release blocker

No

### Summary

On Signal, `/approve <id> allow-once` is refused with "❌ You are not authorized to approve exec requests on Signal." when the approver is known by UUID (`uuid:<id>` in the account's `allowFrom`), for example because their phone number is hidden. The command sender is normalized through Signal's `formatAllowFrom`, which treats every entry as a phone number, so it never matches the `uuid:` approver.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Configure a Signal account whose `allowFrom` lists the approver as `uuid:<their-uuid>` only (no phone number), with `approvals.exec` enabled and a Signal target on that account.
2. Trigger an exec approval so the prompt reaches that Signal chat.
3. From the approver's phone (number hidden, so the sender arrives as a UUID), send `/approve <id> allow-once`.

### Expected behavior

The approval is accepted, because the sender is the `uuid:` approver in `allowFrom`.

### Actual behavior

The bot replies "❌ You are not authorized to approve exec requests on Signal." and the approval stays pending.

Cause, traced in the built code:
- `resolveSenderCandidates` (`src/auto-reply/sender-identity.ts`) maps each sender candidate through `normalizeAllowFromEntry`, which uses the plugin's `formatAllowFrom`.
- Signal's `formatAllowFrom` (`extensions/signal/src/shared.ts`) is `entry === "*" ? "*" : normalizeE164(entry.replace(/^signal:/i, ""))`, so `uuid:<id>` becomes `+` followed by the UUID's digits.
- The approver list from `getSignalApprovalApprovers` / `normalizeSignalApproverId` keeps `uuid:<id>`, so `authorizeActorAction` never finds a match.

### OpenClaw version

2026.10.7 (gateway and `@openclaw/signal`). The same `formatAllowFrom` is in `@openclaw/signal` 2026.11.2.

### Operating system

Linux (Docker host)

### Install method

docker (`ghcr.io/openclaw/openclaw` image, `@openclaw/signal` from npm)

### Model

Not model-related

### Provider / routing chain

Not model-related

### Logs

The refusal reply above. Debug logging did not record the refused `/approve`.

### Impact and severity

Approvers who hide their phone number cannot use `/approve` on Signal at all.

### Additional information

Workaround that works: also add `+<the UUID's digits>` to `allowFrom`, so the mangled sender matches. Possible fix (untested): have Signal's `formatAllowFrom` keep `uuid:` entries (and bare UUIDs) the way `normalizeSignalApproverId` does, instead of passing them to `normalizeE164`.

issues.body:
### Summary

Plugin LLM completions launched from an `agent_end` hook fail with `LLM_COMPLETION_NOT_AUTHORIZED: agent tool caller authority is no longer active` once the turn has finished. The hook's async continuations inherit the turn's tool-caller identity through `gatewayToolCallerStorage`, and by the time the post-turn work calls `runtime.llm.complete`, that identity is no longer current. Plugins have no supported way to leave the turn's context: the host's own helper `withoutGatewayToolCallerIdentity` ("Process-owned work must not retain the turn that authorized its launch") is not exported through the plugin SDK.

### Environment

OpenClaw 2026.9.7 (release tag plus local backports that do not touch hooks, runtime-llm or caller context), Linux, Node 24.21, Telegram DMs, three standing agents. The plugin is a memory plugin that captures each finished turn on `agent_end` and then runs model-backed post-processing (episode extraction, conversation insights, a short narrative).

### What happens

1. A turn ends and `agent_end` fires. The handler validates the session and enqueues the capture work on its own queue, so the work outlives the hook call.
2. The queued work calls `api.runtime.llm.complete(...)` with an explicit `agentId`, seconds to minutes later.
3. `captureGatewayToolCallerAssertion()` in `src/gateway/...gateway-caller-context` finds the inherited caller from `gatewayToolCallerStorage`; `receiptAuthority()` is now false, so the call throws `agent tool caller authority is no longer active`, which `runtime-llm` maps to `LlmCompleteError` / `LLM_COMPLETION_NOT_AUTHORIZED`.

From one day of logs (redacted, UTC, 2026-10-01), every post-turn completion of two agents failed this way, e.g.:

```
{"at":"2026-10-01T12:29:07.315Z","feature":"conversation-insights","name":"LlmCompleteError","code":"LLM_COMPLETION_NOT_AUTHORIZED","message":"agent tool caller authority is no longer active"}
{"at":"2026-10-01T12:29:07.325Z","feature":"episode-extraction","name":"LlmCompleteError","code":"LLM_COMPLETION_NOT_AUTHORIZED","message":"agent tool caller authority is no longer active"}
{"at":"2026-10-01T12:29:07.371Z","feature":"dream-narrative","name":"LlmCompleteError","code":"LLM_COMPLETION_NOT_AUTHORIZED","message":"agent tool caller authority is no longer active"}
```

Per agent since the 9.7 update: 21 failures for one agent, 32 for another, 1 for a third. The same calls made from cron-triggered work (no inherited turn) succeed with the same plugin, model and `agentId`.

### Regression note

On 2026.9.6 we saw this class of failure only for the agent whose chat runs on the Codex harness (classified by the plugin as `unavailable`; the original message was not captured then), while post-turn completions logged for another agent succeeded. On 2026.9.7 both agents fail with the message above.

### Expected

Either of:

- the host runs plugin hook handlers (or at least their continuations) outside the finished turn's tool-caller identity, the same way the host treats its own process-owned work; or
- the plugin SDK exposes a way to detach queued work from the triggering turn (an exported `withoutGatewayToolCallerIdentity`, or a `runtime.runAsProcessWork(fn)`), so plugins don't have to guess.

A plugin-side `AsyncLocalStorage.snapshot()` taken at registration would leave the turn, but it also carries every other host store that was active at registration (for example the database maintenance scope), so it is not a safe general workaround.

### Related

#161151 (plugin services keep the requester's authority), #145865 (deferred announce after the caller run ends), #158070 (preflight compaction waits in a lane queue and loses the authority).

### Actual behavior

The agent refuses do to anything else than running the official update path when an update is somehow requested. No matter it does not apply in this context (docker install). The assistant acknowledged that Docker requires image replacement, yet remained stuck on the instruction wording.

github-copilot🤖gpt-6-astra📌🌗🐌 | 📚[⣿⡆⠐⠐⠐]872k 💰0.0000

Super frustrating, it completely broke by unattended upgrades that I could initiate from Telegram. They are scripted and can roll back, very stable, super convenient. Now I need to physically on the network and perform upgrade manually again. I wasted over 30 mins on two occasions already trying to convince the agent to simple drop a single file. It is just stubborn and keeps repeating it is not allowed.

The shipped prompt contains these two sentences:

issues.body:
## Bug type

Behavior bug (incorrect output/state without crash). Whether it is a regression is unknown: no earlier version was tested.

## Beta release blocker

No

## Summary

The `pdf` tool has no path at all for a **scanned PDF** (image-only pages, no text layer) once no vision-capable model is available: the tool is gated on a PDF model *before* it ever looks at the document, so "there is no model" and "this document needs a model" collapse into the same hard failure.

Two gates, both in `src/agents/tools/pdf-tool.ts` (`origin/main` @ `9b350d9e933`):

1. Registration — `createPdfTool` returns `null` when model resolution yields nothing (`pdf-tool.ts:396`, `:410`), so on a host with no PDF-model candidate the tool is not registered at all.
2. Execution (deferred discovery, the path the production caller uses) — the handler throws before any document is loaded:

```ts
      const pdfModelConfig =
        registrationPdfModelConfig ??
        resolvePdfModelConfigForTool({ ... });
      if (!pdfModelConfig) {
        throw new ToolInputError("No PDF model configured.");
      }
```
(`pdf-tool.ts:475-482`; the runtime-generation variant is `:207`.)

The result is that **text extraction from a scan is treated as a model capability**, even though it is not: reading characters off a raster page is extraction, not comprehension. The document-extract plugin already detects exactly this case — a near-empty text layer plus rendered images — and already owns bounded page rendering, but that signal is only consumed *after* a model call, so it is unreachable when there is no model to call.

## Steps to reproduce

1. Configure an agent with no vision-capable model available to the `pdf` tool (no configured PDF model / all candidates unauthenticated).
2. Give it a scanned PDF (raster-only page; `pdftotext file.pdf -` returns empty).
3. Ask it to read the document.

## Expected behavior

With no vision model, a scanned PDF is either read by a host-side extraction path (where one is available), or refused with an error that distinguishes "no model configured" from "this document needs one" — not silently unreachable at registration time.

## Actual behavior

- No PDF model candidate → the tool is absent from the toolset (registration `return null`), so the agent has no failure to report and no capability to name.
- Deferred discovery → `ToolInputError: No PDF model configured.` thrown at `pdf-tool.ts:481`, before the file is opened. The document is never inspected, so the existing scan signal in the extraction plugin never runs.

## Environment

- installed: `openclaw@2026.8.1` (npm global, Linux LXC, `node v22.23.2`), verified against `origin/main` `9b350d9e933`
- models: Anthropic + OpenAI via provider profiles; failure reproduces whenever the PDF-model resolver returns null

## Model

n/a: the failure happens before any model call, when the PDF-model resolver returns null. The exact models configured on the agent at the time of the report are unknown.

## Provider / routing chain

agent tool loop → `pdf` tool (`createPdfTool` at registration, or deferred discovery at call time) → `resolvePdfModelConfigForTool` → null → tool not registered, or `ToolInputError: No PDF model configured.` before the file is opened. The ask is the ordering of this gate; OCR ownership stays with the document-extraction capability.

## Impact and severity

A scanned invoice/statement — the normal shape of a Brazilian bank or utility PDF — is unreadable by an agent whose model set is otherwise fine, with a message that points at configuration instead of at the document. Time-to-notice is immediate but the diagnosis is not: the operator reads "No PDF model configured" on a host where models *are* configured but the resolver produced no PDF candidate.

## Note on prior art

We opened PR #142253 (local `pdftoppm` + `tesseract` fallback inside the pdf tool) and closed it unmerged: automated review flagged it as the wrong ownership boundary — the recommendation was to keep OCR in the document-extraction capability with a narrow core change for model-free tool availability — plus P1 findings on cancellation propagation and raster pixel budget. This issue records the capability gap on `main` independent of that implementation; we are not carrying a local patch for it.

issues.body:
### Environment

- OpenClaw **2026.11.1** (`4ffdd20`), also reproduced identically on a second fresh 2026.11.1 install after full rollback
- Linux x86_64, 8 cores / 31 GB RAM, systemd unit (`gateway run --bind loopback`)
- Fleet: **16 configured agents** (18 registered agent databases). Agent DB sizes after a fresh 14-day retention prune + VACUUM: 227 MB – 1.58 GB (largest two ≈ 1.58 GB and 0.97 GB); shared state DB ≈ 232 MB
- The gateway had not cold-booted since Oct 16 — all updates between ran in-place under the live process. 2026.10.8 cold-boots the same machine and data fine (verified again after rollback)

### Failure

Every cold start of 2026.11.1 crash-loops (~35 s per cycle):

```
Gateway failed to start: worker task capacity reached. Run openclaw gateway status --deep for diagnostics.
...
[gateway] ws upgrade error from 127.0.0.1: worker task capacity reached
```

The gateway binds and accepts briefly, then admission/WS-upgrade tasks get **rejected instead of queued**, startup aborts, and the restart loop repeats. With `Expected start` the loop never converges: each restart re-runs all 16 agent admissions, and the rejection recurs before they drain.

### What we tried (all insufficient)

| Change | Result |
|---|---|
| `DEFAULT_WORKER_PENDING_BYTES` 256 MB → 4 GB | still rejected |
| `maxPendingTasks` 128 → 1024 | still rejected |
| control-ui / server-cron pool `maxPendingBytes` 8 MB → 4 GB | still rejected |
| Local patch: `resolveWorkerComputeLimit()` `cores-1` → `cores+8` (16 permits instead of 7) | still rejected |

Our reading: the shared compute-permit budget (`createWorkerComputeCapacity(resolveWorkerComputeLimit())`, cores−1, global singleton) saturates during the parallel cold-boot admission burst of 16 agents, and `admit()` failures **reject** tasks ("overloaded") rather than enqueueing them. On a fleet this size the burst always exceeds 7 concurrent permits, so cold boot can never converge. 2026.10.8 cold-boots the same shape fine.

### Request

1. A supported way to scale or queue cold-boot admission worker tasks (config knob for compute capacity / pending tasks, or queue-not-reject semantics when the budget is momentarily saturated).
2. Documentation for the intended relationship between `maxPendingTasks` / `maxPendingBytes` / compute permits during 16-agent admission, so operators can size correctly.

### Related headless `doctor --fix` issues (hit during the same upgrade)

1. `doctor --fix` **hangs at 0% CPU with no TTY** — reproduced with nohup, `stdin=/dev/null`, and `--yes --non-interactive`; it only runs under a real pty (`script -qec ...`). Non-interactive flags should not depend on a terminal.
2. If a prior attempt created a pre-migration backup group whose backup files are later lost, every subsequent `doctor --fix` refuses with *"Completed pre-migration SQLite backup group is missing … Restore the matching backup group"* — and we could not find a documented headless way to reset the stale group expectation (removing the `session-sqlite-migration-runs` record alone is insufficient; a second reference survives in doctor capture state). A supported reset (or a warning + automatic fresh-group fallback) would help recovery.

### Context

Rollback to 2026.10.8 required restoring the pre-upgrade state DB + v25 agent DBs, because the failed 11.1 boots forward-migrate the state DB to schema 22 — worth documenting that a failed 11.1 cold boot pins the installation until doctor completes or backups are restored.

All fleet details anonymized; stability bundles and full logs retained internally and available on request.

### Summary

The Control UI chat stayed in a "running" state for 11+ hours after the run had ended. The final assistant reply, posted by a subagent-settle (announce) run, didn't appear until the page was reloaded. Stop sent `sessions.abort` with no run ID, so it could never clear the state.

### Environment

- OpenClaw 2026.10.10 (7dc3350), Control UI webchat, session `agent:<id>:main`

### Sequence (Gateway log)

1. The user sends a message; the run spawns subagents and yields. Its first reply displays normally.
2. Subagents settle. The run `announce:requester-settle:…:yield-1` produces the final reply and logs `ended with stopReason=stop`.
3. Nine seconds later the Gateway logs a 150 MB, 9-second agent-database read (`page-cache residency … readBytes=150566165 … elapsedMs=9039.5`).
4. The UI never shows the final reply, and keeps showing the working spinner ("11h 6m · Sifting…").
5. After reload the reply appears, but the spinner remains. `openclaw sessions --json` reports the session `status: "done"`, `abortedLastRun: false`.
6. Each Stop click logs `sessions.abort requested … runId=none clearQueued`, and nothing changes.
7. Sending a new message starts a real run, which clears the stale state.

### Expected

- The UI shows replies from announce/settle runs as they arrive.
- The UI's busy state follows the Gateway's run state, and clears on reload when the session status is done.

### Suggested fix

- On reconnect or reload, derive the busy state from the session's server-side run status.
- When abort finds no active run, tell the client to clear its running indicator.

issues.body:
### Summary

When Code Mode is active, file and skill reads happen inside `exec`. tokenjuice then compacts those results as bash output, even though the tokenjuice docs say "exact file-content reads stay raw". Agents in Code Mode can lose most of a skill or source file without any visible error.

### Environment

- OpenClaw 2026.10.10 (7dc3350), Linux, Node 26
- tokenjuice plugin 2026.10.10-beta.5 (bundled, enabled)
- `tools.codeMode` unset (defaults to `auto`); the agent runs `anthropic/claude-sonnet-5-5`, so Code Mode engages and the model sees only `exec` and `wait`

### Steps to reproduce

1. Use an agent on a Code Mode preferred model, with tokenjuice enabled.
2. Give it a skill whose SKILL.md is about 11 KB.
3. Ask it to use the skill. It loads the skill via `skills_read` (or a file read) from guest JS inside `exec`.

### Expected

Per `docs/tools/tokenjuice.md`: "exact file-content reads stay raw". The skill text reaches the model whole.

### Actual

- The `exec` result is labelled `[tokenjuice compacted bash output]`, and the 11,253-character skill arrived as about 1,200 characters.
- Direct `read` calls fail with `Tool read not found`, because Code Mode hides the tool.
- Later chunked reads of the same file (`sed -n '25,81p' SKILL.md`) were compacted intermittently: some identical calls came back raw, others compacted.
- Across recent sessions, every compaction in the log carries the same generic label (`tokenjuice compacted bash output`), on all agents running Code Mode. 20–420 compactions per session.

### Impact

- In one run, the agent never saw the multi-stage pipeline steps in the skill. It did the work itself and skipped every delegated stage.
- In a second run, the agent spent about 78 `exec` calls re-reading the skill in chunks before it could proceed.

### Suggested fix

- Apply the safe-inventory/raw classification to the tool calls made inside a Code Mode `exec`, not only to the outer `exec`.
- Or exempt `skills_read` and `read` bridge results from compaction.

issues.body:
### Summary

Skill dedupe refuses to re-serve a skill after the model only received a truncated copy. It answers "Skill instructions were already served whole earlier in the current model context", which is false. The agent has no way to recover the full skill.

### Environment

- OpenClaw 2026.10.10 (7dc3350)
- Code Mode `auto`, tokenjuice enabled (see the related issue on tokenjuice compacting Code Mode reads)

### Steps to reproduce

1. The agent loads a large skill. The result is shortened before the model sees it; here tokenjuice compacted it from 11,253 to about 1,200 characters.
2. The agent notices it's missing steps and asks for the skill again.

### Expected

The full skill is served again, because the model never had it whole.

### Actual

Each reload returns:

> Skill instructions were already served whole earlier in the current model context. Reuse that content; the full document will be served again if compaction removes it.

- The dedupe tracks context compaction, but not result shortening by tool-result reducers such as tokenjuice.
- In the failing session the agent hit this 8 times, then proceeded without the skill. Its own report says it "could not reload the discussion-post skill text after it was compacted away".

### Suggested fix

- Record what was actually delivered (a length or hash after reducers run), not what was requested.
- Or always allow an explicit re-read when the earlier delivery was modified by a reducer.

issues.body:
### Bug type

Behavior bug (incorrect output/state without crash)

### Beta release blocker

No

### Summary

On a session placed on a cloud worker (Crabbox provider, Sprites backend), every agent turn fails on its first model attempt with `Session capability metadata requires worker preparation` (`SessionCapabilityReadRequired`). This happens before any provider request is made. The same agent and model work for a local session on the same gateway. Provisioning, dispatch to `active`, networking, and reclaim all work.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Configure a cloud worker profile: `cloudWorkers.profiles.fly` with `provider: "crabbox"`, `settings.provider: "sprites"`, `readyWorkers: 0`, and `cloudWorkers.preparedPool.maxTotal: 0`. Crabbox is a fixed-lease-ID build (openclaw/crabbox#2877).
2. `sessions.create` with `{"agentId":"<agent>","worktree":true,"worktreeSource":"empty"}`.
3. `sessions.dispatch` with `{"key":"<key>","agentId":"<agent>","profileId":"fly"}`. The placement reaches `active` in about 2 minutes.
4. `agent` with `{"sessionKey":"<key>","message":"Run uname -a","idempotencyKey":"<id>"}`, then `agent.wait`.

### Expected behavior

The turn runs on the worker and completes, as it does for a local session.

### Actual behavior

- The first candidate fails in the gateway lane (`lane=main` and `lane=session:<key>`, `errorName: "Error"`) with:

  ```
  {"message":"Session capability metadata requires worker preparation","query":{"storePath":"<state>/agents/<agent>/sessions/sessions.json","agentId":"<agent>","sessionKey":"agent:<agent>:dashboard:<uuid>"}}
  ```

- `model_fallback_decision` treats this as `candidate_failed` and moves to the next configured fallback, the same pattern as #179290.
- Each fallback then fails with `Worker transcript base changed; uncommitted messages were not committed; relaunch required.` (`stale-base-leaf`). This looks like #161211. Its fix (#177477) is not in this build: the beta's merge base is 2026-10-15.
- The placement ends `failed` and the worker is destroyed.
- The transcript contains only the user message and a "Model switched from … to …" notice per fallback. No model output is produced.

Reproduced on two different agents and with Anthropic (`claude-opus-5-5` → `claude-sonnet-5-5`) and OpenAI (`gpt-6.1-sol` → `claude-sonnet-5-5` → `gpt-6-luna`) chains. A local (non-worker) session on the same agent and model completes normally on the same gateway.

From the dist, `readDurable` in `session-accessor.sqlite-entry-store` throws `SessionCapabilityReadRequired` when no `preparedReads` or legacy reader is present. The worker-turn path appears to reach a synchronous capability read outside `withPreparedSessionCapabilityRead` / `prepareSessionCapabilityRead`. The gateway logs no stack, so the exact caller is unknown.

### OpenClaw version

2026.10.10-beta.3 (15dffe5)

### Operating system

macOS 26.3 (gateway host, Apple Silicon); worker: Ubuntu on Fly Sprites (x86_64)

### Install method

npm global (`openclaw` via Homebrew Node 24.20.0), native gateway service

### Model

anthropic/claude-opus-5-5 (also reproduced with openai/gpt-6.1-sol)

### Provider / routing chain

Gateway → cloud worker (crabbox plugin → Crabbox `sprites` backend) → Anthropic / OpenAI direct

### Logs

```
lane task error: lane=main durationMs=5590 error="{\"message\":\"Session capability metadata requires worker preparation\",\"query\":{...}}"
model_fallback_decision decision=candidate_failed attempt=1 total=2 fallbackStepFromModel=anthropic/claude-opus-5-5 fallbackStepToModel=anthropic/claude-sonnet-5-5
lane task error: lane=main durationMs=2628 error="Cloud worker process failed before completing the turn: node worker failed with exit code 1: Worker transcript base changed; uncommitted messages were not committed; relaunch required."
```

### Impact

Cloud workers can be provisioned but cannot run any agent turn, so worker placement is unusable on this build.

issues.body:
### Summary

In the Control UI chat transcript, a Windows path loses its backslash whenever the backslash is immediately followed by ASCII punctuation. Sending `C:\Users\me\.config` renders as `C:\Users\me.config`.

Code spans and fenced blocks are unaffected, so the corruption only hits paths pasted as plain text - which is how people normally paste them. The rendered message then differs from what was sent, and copying the path back out of the transcript points somewhere else.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Open the Control UI chat (webchat).
2. Send the following as plain text, without backticks:

```
C:\Users\me\.config\openclaw.json   and   D:\work\_notes.txt
```

3. Read the rendered message.

Actual rendering:

```
C:\Users\me.config\openclaw.json   and   D:\work_notes.txt
```

The `\` before `.` and the `\` before `_` are gone.

Expected: the text renders exactly as sent.

### Root cause

`ui/src/components/markdown-parser.ts:129`

```ts
const markdownParser = new MarkdownIt({
  html: true, // Enable HTML recognition so html_block/html_inline overrides can escape it
  breaks: true,
  linkify: true,
});
```

`markdown-it@15.0.2` (see `ui/package.json`) enables the `escape` inline rule by default. A backslash followed by an ASCII punctuation character is consumed as an escape sequence, so the backslash is dropped and only the punctuation survives. `\U` in `C:\Users` survives because `U` is a letter, which is why only some separators disappear and the bug looks intermittent.

This affects user-authored messages; the same parser is used for the transcript.

### Impact

Pasting Windows paths into chat is routine. The transcript silently rewrites the user's input, so a path that is re-copied from the conversation no longer names the original location. That is input corruption rather than a cosmetic issue: a command copied back out of the transcript can target a different directory.

### Suggested fix

Either of these:

- Keep other markdown, keep backslashes literal:

  ```ts
  markdownParser.inline.ruler.disable("escape");
  ```

  The cost is that `\*` no longer renders a literal asterisk, which is rarely needed in a chat transcript.

- Render user-authored messages as plain text with autolinking only, and keep full markdown for assistant messages.

A regression test belongs next to the existing markdown component tests: input `C:\Users\me\.config`, expect the identical string in the rendered output.

### Environment

- Control UI (webchat), rendering happens client-side
- `markdown-it` 15.0.2
- Observed with a Windows gateway and a Windows client; the platform should not matter because the parse is client-side

issues.body:
## Summary

Muse sessions report no token usage or context occupancy in OpenClaw, even though MSP provides both. The session row shows `totalTokens: null` and `contextTokens: null`, so users can't see how full a Muse session's context is. The Codex harness reports both for its sessions.

## Contract

MSP schema at `a45cb67`:
- `TurnCompletedParams.usage`: "The turn's aggregate token usage, summed across the turn's model completions."
- `session/tokenUsage`: emitted per completion, carrying counted-once `promptTokens`/`totalTokens`. The schema says "clients display and sum these and never re-derive the provider's cache convention."
- `session/contextUsage`: `usedTokens`, `windowTokens` and `pressure`, the context-window occupancy.

## Current behavior (`main` @ df371f177)

- `extensions/muse/src/events.ts:17-31`: every recorded assistant message carries `usage: makeZeroUsageSnapshot()`.
- `extensions/muse/harness.ts`: the attempt result returns no `attemptUsage`, and nothing reads `turn/completed.usage`, `session/tokenUsage` or `session/contextUsage`.
- The host merges `attemptUsage` into the run's usage accumulator. For native harnesses it also takes the context snapshot from `attemptUsage.contextUsage` (`src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run/attempt-normalization.ts:282-327`). Codex fills it (`extensions/codex/src/app-server/event-projector-usage.ts`, `run-attempt-finalize.ts`).

## Reproduction (controlled MSP peer)

- Setup: `openclaw agent --local --json --message hello`, with an agent on `meta/muse-spark-1.3` bound to `muse`. The repo's fake Muse was temporarily changed to send `usage: { inputTokens: 1200, outputTokens: 34, cachedTokens: 200, reasoningTokens: 10 }` on `turn/completed`.
- Result: the run succeeds, but its result has no usage. `openclaw sessions --agent <id> --json` shows `{"totalTokens":null,"totalTokensFresh":false,"contextTokens":null}` for the session.

## Scope and overlap

This is a reporting gap, not wrong numbers: the host shows "unknown" rather than zero. It doesn't affect execution. No open Muse PR (#183676, #178837, #194884, #194924, #194984) reads MSP usage. Boundary: shipped CLI with a controlled MSP peer. Live Muse usage frames have not been captured here.

issues.body:
## Problem and severity

**P3 — Files loses the reader’s position when word wrap is turned off.** In the middle of a long text file, enabling wrap retains a logical line near the top of the reader; disabling it jumps to line 1. The file and editor remain mounted, and the outer panel does not move.

This is a recoverable reading-position defect, not content loss or a general performance outage. Small-fix batch hold; no PR or candidate yet.

## Reproduction

Use Chat → Files against a real Gateway workspace with a disposable text file. The recorded fixture has 320 numbered lines and is 58,560 bytes. Each line is `ROW-001 ` (incrementing to `ROW-320 `), followed by three repetitions of `Synthetic reading-position sample with predictable width. `; lines end with LF and there is a final newline.

1. Open the file with word wrap disabled.
2. Scroll to the middle using the normal scroll input. Alternatively, use **Search in file** to find `ROW-180`; closing search still reproduces.
3. Click **Enable word wrap**. The logical reading line near the top is retained.
4. Click **Disable word wrap**. The reader returns to line 1.
5. As a control, repeat from the very bottom: bottom anchoring survives both toggles.

No file edits, saves, response mocks, artificial request delay, or product-state replacement are needed.

## Evidence

Real isolated Gateway runtime `2a48569bfbb8177fd8ed232ab56fd3cb983d42a6`, UI `3acb23cdf7d2ad1e89f493e91d725c2e71b5d7f6`; Chromium, DPR 2.

| Case | Wrap off initially | Wrap on | Wrap off again |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Desktop 1440×900, search open, repeated twice | `scrollTop=2813.5`; full row 162 at y=163 | `11143.5`; row 162 still y=163 | `0`; row 1 at y=159 |
| Desktop, search closed | `2988.5`; row 172 at y=120 | `11826`; row 172 still y=120 | `0`; row 1 at y=116 |
| Portrait 390×844, native scrolling, no search | `3713`; row 213 at y=539 | `19498`; row 213 still y=539 | `0`; row 1 at y=542 |
| Portrait, at bottom (positive control) | `5401` | `29032.5`, bottom retained | `5401`, bottom retained |

Editor/scroller node identities were retained. In the portrait middle case, the outer scroller stayed at x=21, y=534, width=348, height=243.40625 CSS px. Document scroll stayed at 0. The control loses its internal reading anchor; this is not a remount or whole-page jump.

A passive desktop observer recorded content height changing from 22,188.5 to 20,823.5 to 5,633.5 px, then a scroll event at `scrollTop=0`. This is DOM/scroll evidence, not a painted-frame trace. A separate portrait screenshot pair shows line 97 before the toggle and line 1 afterward. Only the disposable file and its controls are visible; other page content was covered without changing the editor’s styles.

The saved fixture’s SHA-256 remained `fc77504cb62c40ae9425c3af03bdd0bc054533af6706eb93a5fd937d2edcdb9a`; it was removed afterward. The original wrap preference and desktop viewport were restored. Sanitized measurement artifact SHA-256: `59000158664b034e2ec75a9ed93d84e5b7c507f027a23172da0187a36d20f39d`.

## Attributed scroll write and controls

A second native-scroll reproduction on the same UI retained full row 155 at y=111 when wrap was enabled (`scrollTop` 2,700 → 10,662.5). Disabling wrap again returned to zero. A temporary accessor on only that scroller delegated every read/write to the native accessor and recorded the following single JavaScript write:

| Stage | `scrollTop` (CSS px) |
| --- | ---: |
| Before content shrink | 10,662.5 |
| Already clamped by the browser when JavaScript writes | 4,919 |
| Requested by the relative compensation | −3,043.5 |
| Result after the native setter clamps it | 0 |

The stack points to `e.measure` in `dist-BQc8ovtO.js:11:11635`. The shipped source map resolves it to `@codemirror/view@6.43.11/dist/index.js:8240`: `scroll.scrollTop += diff`. The −7,962.5 px compensation would yield the preserved 2,700 px offset from the original position, but it is applied to the already reduced 4,919 px value. The same scroller remains mounted.

This identifies the write producing zero. It does not establish a generally reproducible upstream dependency defect or an accepted fix.

Additional discriminating controls:

- Keeping `.cm-content` at `min-width: 0` throughout the toggle still gives 4,919 → requested −3,043.5 → 0. The previous hypothesis that switching the outer `min-width` rule alone explains the defect is not supported.
- Near the beginning, turning wrap off changes `scrollTop` 844 → 214 and retains full row 13 at y=112. The problematic clamp condition is absent.
- A width-only change from 390×844 to 1440×844 while wrap stays enabled retains row 279 at −13.5 px relative to the scroller top (`scrollTop` 25,869 → 25,659). Do not broaden this finding to all responsive resizing.
- The earlier bottom-anchor control also passes.

The accessor and diagnostic style were removed. The 58,560-byte fixture was verified unchanged and deleted; the original wrap preference and 1440×900 viewport were restored. This instrumentation is diagnostic evidence, not a performance benchmark. One auxiliary identity field referenced a removed earlier probe and is excluded; the direct scroller identity check passes.

Writer/control artifact SHA-256: `92adc47a5431d8194898278965f7fd35c3774e0b593327bc6836f22f4d08c995`.

## Correction owner

Keep the correction in the existing Files editor owner (`file-editor-view.ts`) and its wrap transition from `chat-detail-panel.ts`. CodeMirror exposes a logical scroll snapshot effect that may be applicable; it is not a validated fix. Avoid raw-pixel restoration, arbitrary timers, dependency patches, or an independent scroll manager.

The editor TypeScript owners are unchanged on main `3d43d2eb463abba03f6fd320c6ed784671412617`. Changes to the shared stylesheet since the measured build affect Tasks titles, not these file-editor rules. This is source freshness, not a full current-main runtime replay.

## Risk and coverage

Preserve middle and bottom reading positions, horizontal scroll behavior, search navigation, explicit line-link navigation, editable selections and undo, dirty drafts, HTML source, and supported line separators. Check both directions of wrap and narrow/wide panel sizes. Do not prevent legitimate navigation to a newly requested line to retain an old anchor.

No candidate has been accepted. Physical mobile/Safari, editable selection/undo, and candidate validation remain open. Keep this with a coherent Files reading/layout batch.

Umbrella: #149361.

issues.title: [Bug]: Chat loses reading position when clearing or closing a search with no matches

issues.body:
## Problem

Closing Chat's local message search after a query returns no matches loses the reading position and returns the conversation to the beginning. The user has not selected a result or scrolled the filtered transcript. A [later original reproduction](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/151970#issuecomment-5744369234) also covers clearing the query after deliberate scrolling within matching results: the full transcript returns at offset 0 and **Scroll to latest** remains hidden and inert until further input or closing the bar.

**Severity: P2.** This disrupts reading a long conversation and requires finding the previous position manually. No message or draft loss was observed. Umbrella: #149361.

## Reproduction

1. Open a scrollable Chat conversation and scroll into its history. This reproduction uses an isolated real Gateway, with 2,803 messages already loaded and no history request in progress.
2. Focus the composer and press Cmd+F (Ctrl+F on non-Mac platforms) to open **Search messages**.
3. Paste an absent term in one operation, for example `zzzxq149361nohit`. Pasting avoids intermediate prefixes that could legitimately display a matching message.
4. Verify **No matching messages**.
5. Click **Close search**, or use Cmd+F again.
6. The full transcript returns at scroll offset 0, rather than at the previous reading position.

The Mac Cmd+F and Close button paths were exercised; the non-Mac shortcut is source-defined, not separately executed.

## Observed evidence

UI `1c26b1e0bd14d627059ee939a25022b9ced209bc`, isolated Gateway `2a48569bfbb8177fd8ed232ab56fd3cb983d42a6`, Chromium desktop, DPR 1. The served original UI entry was byte-verified. These are original-behavior controls, not a proposed correction.

| Control | Before search | After closing | Outcome |
| --- | ---: | ---: | --- |
| Desktop 1440 × 900, paste absent term, Cmd+F close | 2,250 px | 0 px | Reading position lost |
| Desktop 1440 × 900, paste absent term, pointer Close | 1,800 px | 0 px | Reading position lost; native captures below |
| Portrait 390 × 844, paste absent term, pointer Close | 1,710 px | 0 px | Reading position lost |
| Desktop, open and close with query still empty | 906 px | 906 px | Position and tracked row retained |

The pointer desktop case has the same 4,907 px transcript extent before and after; portrait has the same 5,728 px extent. The scroller and composer nodes survive, and the 17-character synthetic draft, composer geometry and return focus are retained. History-reading/follow-lock remains true. The message array and count remain unchanged; no history loading or active older-page load occurs during these controls. The absent-query branch reduces the actual scrollable contents to the viewport height and clamps the offset to 0.

The desktop pointer reproduction uses only endpoint observation, without continuous geometry sampling or callback/scroll wrappers. Privacy masks are applied only for screenshots and verified not to change geometry.

![Chat reading position before and after closing a search with no matches](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/cd1c6f57-6bc8-477e-a4ea-9c982ea8bf90)

Native desktop endpoint captures, cropped to the Chat area. Private content is masked. The portrait result is responsive desktop emulation, not physical-mobile or Safari proof.

Sanitized numeric capture: `chat-search-nohit-layout.json`, SHA-256 `9af931c32eb6f4068acd0312b812cbbdfc5789935239eeccdd0ae5aeb48b2d45`. The 2,803-message payload hash before/after the later controls is `40659abc306b47eeca60784888602c04bf79cce27859131a216f4e51a18c334a`; no transcript text or message identifiers are attached.

## Cause and proposed direction

The source and observed geometry point to the search/projection boundary:

- `components/chat-thread.ts` renders the no-match shell instead of `projection.renderRows`, leaving the virtualizer's last committed row model in place while the real scroll extent collapses. In the single-paste case the model still has 42 row keys, while no virtual message rows are rendered.
- `chat-transcript-offset-observer.ts` publishes the resulting native offset. Closing in `chat-thread-interactions.ts` clears search and restores focus, with no pre-search reading-anchor restoration.
- The full projection returns using the current offset/model. In the single-paste controls it stays at 0. Progressive typing can instead retain an incidental matching prefix's position; that separate observation is not needed to reproduce this issue.

The relevant owners were compared against main `80cab5c06d3da128d43fc2ec5b87fe714955eae0`. Main adds Escape handling to the search bar; the exercised Cmd+F/Close and projection/offset paths remain unchanged. Main was source-inspected, not executed here.

Repair the existing transcript/search presentation owner so entering and leaving an empty search does not replace the user's reading anchor with the empty shell's clamped offset. The implementation must distinguish no-result cancellation from deliberate navigation to a matching message. No candidate is accepted yet.

## Additional original controls

The same original UI and 2,803-message payload preserve end-following after the actual **Scroll to latest** action. Opening a search, pasting the absent term once and closing it returns to `scrollTop 4257 / scrollHeight 5013 / clientHeight 756` at 1440 × 900 and `4557 / 5256 / 699` at 390 × 844, DPR 1. Distance from the end is 0, history-reading/follow-lock remain false, message-array identity is retained and no scroll/measurement command remains. Each endpoint has 12 identical sampled frames. This is a bounded negative control: the reproduced historical-reader failure should not be generalized to all end-following cases. Evidence `chat-search-follower-control-1c26b1e.json`, SHA-256 `3a6db67a3f5e8665bc27cc510f8893a1c3e828fc5d6926de1962ac0fa9dbf1ea`.

A separate warm-route control opens a matching local query, navigates to Dashboards, then uses browser Back. The old search input is disconnected, the retained Chat has no open search on return, and reopening creates an empty focused input. The pane and message array are retained. This does not cover an in-flight query, cold route import or a painted-focus transition. Evidence `chat-search-route-lifecycle.json`, SHA-256 `db3ddf2abe0cde7386552ed956a148630139074c8291a624e3a1f65870a98dd0`.

## Private candidate v1 validation (superseded, held)

A compiled private candidate on UI `1c26b1e` was replayed against the isolated real Gateway `2a48569`. **It is held, not accepted; no PR is open for this correction.** The original replay again lost the reader position (desktop 2457→0; portrait 1710→0). The candidate restores the saved message, but two remaining behaviors prevent calling the fix validated:

- In the Phosphor dark theme, two consecutive desktop cycles moved the saved message upward by **2 px each**. A portrait cycle moved it by **1 px**. Draft, selection, focus, pane/editor nodes and the same 2,803-message array were retained. A writer trace shows the initial restoration reaches its calculated position, then the rendered row geometry changes without another scroll write. The return currently measures and restores before the mounted rows finish resolving their layout.
- After returning to history, **Scroll to latest** can remain hidden. At scrollTop 3526.5, scrollHeight 6229 and clientHeight 699, reader flags remained active but `chatNewMessagesBelow` was false. The restoration did not call the existing reader-settled notification. The next native wheel takeover called it and made the indicator true before movement. The original bundle was then restored and this control repeated at 1440×900 and 390×844 with the same 2,803-message payload hash: `chatNewMessagesBelow` and button visibility both returned false→true on closing, before any wheel input. The original still loses the reading anchor, but the hidden control is a candidate regression in the exercised restoration flow. The original replay starts at different offsets/measurement-cache states, so it is a control-availability reversal, not a matched timing benchmark. Evidence: `search-original-latest-reversal.json`, SHA-256 `194c64027e4ad7eb057adf8778625009d12933b4b98480d06a3bf679f2c0cf61`.

Follower controls with confirmed initial follow intent passed in **1440×900** and **390×844**, DPR1: the candidate remained exactly at the end before/after no-hit cancel (4828/5584/756 and 5128/5827/699 respectively). An earlier follower setup failed to settle and was excluded. These are functional geometry checks, **not performance timings or physical-phone proof**. Desktop original/candidate starting anchors differ, and total virtual extent depends on which rows have been measured; no speed comparison is inferred.

The next adjustment is scoped to the existing transient row-measurement and restoration owners. Making every row permanently visible is not a proposed fix: that diagnostic changed the virtual extent, and a single-row-only override did not eliminate the drift. All browser overrides, wrappers and the synthetic draft were removed.

issues.body:
### Bug type

Behavior bug (incorrect output/state without crash)

### Beta release blocker

No

### Summary

GitHub Copilot GPT-5.6 Sol tool turns can close an HTTP 200 Responses SSE stream after completed output items without emitting any terminal response event, so OpenClaw correctly rejects the turn and no artifact is produced.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Run OpenClaw source `0a8d8b616033fc88c61263fb5130dfe9ca8799bb` (display version `2026.9.4`) on Windows with provider `github-copilot`, model `gpt-5.6-sol`, low reasoning, no fallback models, and a valid Microsoft enterprise Copilot credential.
2. Restrict tools to workspace-only file reads/writes/edits and ask the agent to inspect synthetic fixture files and produce two workspace artifacts.
3. Observe the Responses stream event metadata and the final embedded-run result.

The same user-visible `candidate_failed: format` failure was also observed with OpenClaw `2026.9.2`. No external side-effect tools were enabled.

### Expected behavior

The provider route should either deliver a terminal `response.completed`, `response.incomplete`, or `response.failed` event, or OpenClaw should expose a specific incomplete-stream failure that preserves the actual provider-boundary cause. It must not report success or execute tool calls without a safely established terminal response fact.

### Actual behavior

The request returns HTTP 200 and `text/event-stream`. The stream emits 12 events and then EOF:

- `response.created`: 1
- `response.in_progress`: 1
- `response.output_item.added`: 3
- `response.output_item.done`: 3
- `response.function_call_arguments.delta`: 2
- `response.function_call_arguments.done`: 2

There is no `response.completed`, `response.incomplete`, `response.failed`, or transport error event. OpenClaw rejects the turn as `candidate_failed` with reason `format`; no requested artifact or usage record is produced.

The event list is an allowlisted metadata-only histogram. No prompt, response payload, header, credential, or raw provider output is included.

### OpenClaw version

2026.9.4, exact source `0a8d8b616033fc88c61263fb5130dfe9ca8799bb`

### Operating system

Windows 11, Node.js 24.19.0

### Install method

Sealed runtime built from the exact source commit with pnpm 12.3.4

### Model

github-copilot/gpt-5.6-sol

### Provider / routing chain

OpenClaw -> bundled github-copilot plugin -> Microsoft enterprise GitHub Copilot Responses endpoint

### Additional provider/model setup details

- GitHub domain: `microsoft.ghe.com`
- reasoning effort: `low`
- configured fallback chain: empty
- maximum output tokens: 1,000
- credential injected only as `COPILOT_GITHUB_TOKEN` in the isolated child environment
- plugins allowlist: bundled `github-copilot` only; memory slot disabled
- browser, channels, ACP, web, runtime, messaging, automation, and external side-effect tools disabled
- per-trial workspace/state isolation and cleanup proof enabled

### Logs

```shell
[model-fetch] response status=200 contentType=text/event-stream
[responses] first_event type=response.created
[responses] stream_done events=12 types=response.created:1,response.in_progress:1,response.output_item.added:3,response.output_item.done:3,response.function_call_arguments.delta:2,response.function_call_arguments.done:2
embedded run: candidate_failed reason=format
```

### Screenshots, recordings, and evidence

Two independently capped/no-retry canaries reproduced the same 12-event, no-terminal shape. Both retained zero safety-gate failures, proved safe cleanup, and preserved the synthetic user-state marker.

Current upstream main `eb82ef8b80a05058619557dff09f758a6710d4d5` still throws when `terminalResponse === undefined` in `packages/ai/src/transports/openai-responses-stream-internal.ts`; there is no GitHub Copilot-specific terminal repair in `extensions/github-copilot/stream.ts`.

### Impact and severity

- Affected: observed with Microsoft enterprise GitHub Copilot GPT-5.6 Sol Responses tool turns
- Severity: high for affected workflows because the agent cannot complete any requested workspace artifact
- Frequency: 2/2 controlled canaries on the exact runtime, plus the same format failure on 2026.9.2 before event-histogram instrumentation
- Consequence: provider-backed Claw runtime validation and other tool-bearing agent turns are blocked; retries would spend quota without producing artifacts

### Additional information

This is distinct from #108460/#108461. That issue repaired unresolved tool-call reconciliation when a terminal response is available; this stream contains completed output-item and function-call-argument events but no terminal response event at all.

No workaround has been validated. Synthesizing success from EOF alone would weaken the existing fail-closed terminal invariant and is not proposed without provider-contract and owner review.

issues.body:
### What happened

Long inbound text that lands in reply-chain / reply-target / chat-window context metadata is silently head+tail truncated at 2,000 characters with a literal `…[omitted]…` marker in the middle. The agent receives the mutilated text with no signal (other than the marker itself) that content was dropped.

Real-world failure mode: a long Telegram **voice note sent as a reply**. The locally-generated transcript lands in the reply-target metadata field and anything past the cap is cut from the middle of the transcript. The sender believes the agent heard everything; the agent silently lost the middle of the message. We hit this in production with multi-minute dictations (transcripts of 6–10k chars).

### Root cause (from reading dist)

- `MAX_CONTEXT_JSON_STRING_CHARS = 2e3` — in `dist/history-image-prune-*.js` (2026.8.2) / `dist/channel-prompt-context-*.mjs` (2026.10.9)
- `truncateBodyHeadTail()` in `dist/inbound-meta-*.js` / `.mjs` — keeps ~60% head + ~40% tail, joins with `HEAD_TAIL_OMISSION_MARKER = "…[omitted]…"`, applied via `sanitizeTranscriptBody()` to context metadata bodies.

Verified present in **2026.8.2** and still in **2026.10.9** (npm pack, `dist/inbound-meta-Bz4_wsIB.mjs:100`).

### Why this is worth addressing

The cap itself is a reasonable prompt-safety bound for untrusted metadata, but:

1. **It's not configurable** — no config key raises it for trusted/owner conversations, and an agent operator can't fix it per-box.
2. **The loss is silent to the agent runtime** — ideally the agent would get an explicit signal (e.g. a note that N chars were omitted and a way to fetch the full body) instead of a bare marker inside the text.
3. **Voice-note transcripts are a common long-body case** — users naturally reply to a thread with a long dictation; "reply vs fresh message" should not change whether the agent hears all of it.

### Suggestions (any one would help)

- Make `MAX_CONTEXT_JSON_STRING_CHARS` configurable (global or per-channel/account), or
- Exempt / raise the cap for inbound voice-transcript bodies specifically, or
- When truncating, include the omitted char count and persist the full body somewhere the agent can retrieve on demand.

### Environment

- OpenClaw 2026.8.2 (0965053) and 2026.10.9 (inspected via `npm pack`)
- macOS arm64, node v24.x, Telegram channel, local whisper transcription

### Workaround we're using

Send long voice notes as fresh messages (not replies), so the transcript arrives as the message body rather than reply-context metadata.

issues.body:
## Environment
- macOS
- OpenClaw installed via npm
- Initially 2026.10.1; upgraded to 2026.10.9 (8b18b55)
- Node.js 26.13.0
- SQLite 3.51.0

## Summary

OpenClaw cannot read the shared state database at `~/.openclaw/state/openclaw.sqlite`. The CLI reports schema version 5120 while the installed build supports 20. Direct SQLite integrity checks also report `database disk image is malformed (11)`.

The session SQLite recovery command is also blocked because it cannot acquire gateway state ownership.

## Diagnostics

- `openclaw gateway status` and `openclaw doctor --session-sqlite inspect --session-sqlite-all-agents --json` fail while reading the shared state database:
  `uses newer schema version 5120; this build supports 20`.
- `sqlite3 -readonly ~/.openclaw/state/openclaw.sqlite 'PRAGMA user_version; PRAGMA application_id; PRAGMA quick_check;'` returns user_version 5120, application_id 0, then `database disk image is malformed (11)`.
- `openclaw doctor --session-sqlite recover` fails with:
  `failed to acquire gateway state ownership | database disk image is malformed | ERR_SQLITE_ERROR (code=ERR_SQLITE_ERROR, errcode=11)`.
- No OpenClaw process was running when checked with `pgrep -alf openclaw`.
- Upgrading Node.js from 26.11.1 to 26.13.0 and OpenClaw from 2026.10.1 to 2026.10.9 did not resolve the issue.

## Preserved data

- A full copy of `~/.openclaw` was made at `~/openclaw-backup-20261102` (4.1 GB).
- The shared state database, Agent database, WAL/SHM files, migration manifests, and archives have been preserved.
- The main Agent session archive contains 613 files (608 JSONL and 5 JSON); all 608 JSONL files passed line-by-line JSON parsing and all 5 JSON files parsed successfully.
- The migration manifest lists 1,226 archive mappings, all with retained archive paths present.
- The pre-startup migration database backup files do not match the SHA256 values recorded in the migration manifest. The original and copied versions do match each other, but SQLite integrity checks fail on the examined databases/backups.
- SQLite `.recover` on a copy of the shared database produced only a `lost_and_found` table (79 KB SQL output), not the expected application schema.

## Questions

1. Is there a supported way to recover or recreate the shared state database when its schema marker is 5120 but the installed build reports support for schema 20, and SQLite reports malformed pages?
2. Can `openclaw doctor --session-sqlite recover` be run in a supported offline/standalone mode when acquiring state ownership itself fails because the shared database is malformed?
3. How should the retained `session-sqlite-import-archive` artifacts and migration manifests be used to restore/import sessions into a clean state directory without losing session identity or duplicating data?
4. Is there a documented procedure to initialize a clean shared state DB while preserving the existing Agent data and retained migration archives?

I have not modified or replaced the original database files. I can provide sanitized migration-manifest excerpts and additional diagnostic output if needed.

## Safety note

Please advise on a supported recovery sequence before any destructive repair, reset, or reinitialization.
