issues.body:
### Summary

The `/update` slash-command reference promises a completion or failure notice in the same chat without describing the owner-destination restriction, contradicting the update guide.

### Affected docs path(s) or URL(s)

- `docs/tools/slash-commands.md` ([reference at reviewed commit](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/826999cd5f76f4867a69869489a4fc51cd5e4a35/docs/tools/slash-commands.md#L409))
- `docs/install/updating.md` ([notice restriction at the same commit](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/826999cd5f76f4867a69869489a4fc51cd5e4a35/docs/install/updating.md#L2062-L2070))

### Steps to reproduce / verify

1. Read the `/update` entry in the slash-command reference.
2. Compare its same-chat notice statement with the update guide's explanation of eligible owner destinations and skipped notices.

### Expected docs behavior/content

The slash-command reference should qualify notice delivery and point readers to the update run record or Control UI when the destination is not eligible, consistent with the update guide. Preserve the owner-destination security boundary.

### Actual docs behavior/content

The reference says the command sends a completion or failure notice in the same chat without that qualification. The update guide says group and channel destinations do not inherit an individual's owner authority, and ineligible notices are skipped while the outcome remains in the run record and Control UI.

### Impact

An authorized owner invoking `/update` in a channel can wait for an outcome that will not be delivered there. In one Windows npm installation on 2026.11.1, a Discord channel update was accepted but later failed; the run recorded `noticeDelivered: false` and the log said the lifecycle notice was skipped because the target was not a current command owner. The timeout itself is covered separately by #193962. This is an observation of one run, not a claim that all channel updates omit notices.

### Evidence

The two linked documents describe different delivery expectations. The owner-destination restriction is intentional; see #146079. The incident outcome was retained in the update report. No retry or synthetic update was performed.

### Additional information

This is a documentation report, not a request to loosen notice authorization. Prepared with Codex assistance.

issues.body:
### Observed behavior

On Windows, the exact PowerShell listener query used by `readWindowsListeningPidsResultSync` can exit successfully with empty stdout while a direct IPv4 loopback HTTP request succeeds. In this observation, a separate native netstat query also omitted the listening row, so an empty census is not sufficient evidence that the port is free.

A custom external watchdog was triggering recovery of a healthy Gateway because it treated the missing CIM row as a dead listener. Adding a bounded loopback TCP connection check fixed that local watchdog decision. This is separate from OpenClaw's shipped watchdog/service code.

### Upstream source finding

At main commit `56493a1a999c7f813d13a4431ef8f66fbf22c7c7`, `src/infra/windows-port-pids.ts` returns `{ ok: true, pids: [] }` immediately after a successful empty PowerShell query. It never attempts its existing netstat fallback in that case. Consumers such as `src/infra/restart-stale-pids.ts` can interpret this result as a free port.

A small follow-up can recover the narrower case where PowerShell misses a listener and netstat can see it. It cannot resolve the observed case where both native collectors miss a reachable listener. That broader case needs an authoritative occupancy check or an indeterminate result while preserving process-identity checks before any cleanup.

### Reproduction and boundaries

- Windows, Node 24.22.1; installed OpenClaw 2026.10.9.
- PowerShell command used by the source: `Get-NetTCPConnection -LocalPort <port> -State Listen -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue | Select-Object -ExpandProperty OwningProcess`.
- Observed native subprocess exit code 0, empty stdout; direct HTTP loopback health returned 200.
- Native netstat output contained client-side connection rows but no listener row for the reachable service.
- No PID ownership is inferred from a successful TCP connection; this evidence must not authorize killing an unidentified process.

This report does not establish why Windows omitted the listener, or that the entire Gateway restart path reproduces on current main. The source early-return behavior is covered by an isolated owner-boundary regression test.

issues.body:
## Summary
On macOS (2026.11.1, arm64), `openclaw infer model run` with the default local transport republishes the agent's workspace plugin tree on every invocation. One tiny prompt took 233 s wall (9 s user + 25 s sys CPU, ~450 MB RSS) and then failed with:

The same call with `--gateway` completes in ~4-8 s wall with ~1-2 s CPU and succeeds.

## Steps
1. An agent with workspace plugins installed.
2. `openclaw infer model run --agent <id> --model openai/<model> --prompt "Reply with exactly: pong" --json` (no --gateway), ideally a few in parallel.

## Expected
docs/cli/infer.md describes local `model run` as "a lean one-shot provider completion" that does not start a chat-agent turn or load tools. It should not rebuild/republish the workspace plugin runtime per call (or should reuse a cached publication).

## Actual
Full workspace-plugin publication on every call; times out under moderate load.

## Possibly related
#164854, #152981, #160777 (same publication path, different triggers).

## Workaround
Use `--gateway`.

issues.body:
### Summary

A model can still relay a background command's late failure after the user has told it the task succeeded another way and the command is obsolete. The message reaches the correct conversation, so this is not a routing or privacy problem, but it is a confusing late failure for work the user already considers finished.

Split out of https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/135117 so the fixed routing report can close without losing this. Original reports: [causal-state report](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/135117#issuecomment-5553519044) and [two non-cancelled delayed failures](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/135117#issuecomment-5553565787), thanks @thomasmoenco. @WG-Mojo asked for these to stay distinct from the route-ownership defect.

### Reproduction on current main

Tested on `6d3ff6f8bd62154540fee1ad3a123bdd539d904b` with a real `qwen2.5:7b` agent through an isolated Gateway and the real Discord plugin against a local mock Discord peer:

1. The agent starts a background command in conversation A and ends its owner turn.
2. The user says the task already succeeded another way, the command is obsolete, its eventual failure is already handled, and asks for no later relay, without killing or polling it.
3. The agent acknowledges and says it will take no further action.
4. The command exits with status 7.
5. About four seconds later the agent posts the obsolete command's failure to A.

### What already works

- A qualified `process kill` produces no later failure notification, even when the command already emitted output (https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/153795).
- A terminal poll or terminal `process log` read retires the exact pending completion (https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/183113).
- An unhandled failure is still delivered once, to the originating conversation.

### Why this needs a decision

The completion prompt in `src/auto-reply/reply/agent-runner-run-params.ts` asks models to suppress recovered or superseded results, but a spoken acknowledgement creates no process-owned fact, so the outcome depends on the model. Suppressing all failures, treating parent success as acknowledgement, parsing prose, or discarding on a timer would each hide legitimate failed work, so those are not acceptable fixes.

Options: (1) leave it model-driven and strengthen the completion prompt, which is cheap but not deterministic; (2) add a deterministic way to retire a specific pending completion, which needs a model-facing capability with an ongoing context cost; (3) accept the current behavior and document killing or polling as the supported way to retire a command.

issues.body:
**Version:** OpenClaw 2026.10.10 (d48be80), macOS app host, `memory-core` slot.

## What happens

After a Gateway start, memory files and sessions are not indexed until an
agent calls `memory_search`. In `extensions/memory-core/manager-runtime.js`, only a
`default`-purpose manager calls `ensureWatcher()`, `ensureSessionListener()`
and `ensureSessionStartupCatchup()`. Nothing creates one at boot. Every Gateway
memory RPC (`memory.search`, `memory.search.owner`, used by
`openclaw memory search`) builds a `cli`-purpose manager, which is transient:
it syncs memory files once and never indexes sessions or starts a watcher.

## Reproduction

1. Restart the Gateway (or reinstall the app).
2. Edit a file under `memory/` and add messages to a session. Do not call `memory_search` from an agent.
3. `memory_index_sources` gets no new rows for either source, and no `[memory]` log line appears.
4. `openclaw memory search x`: memory rows update, but sessions do not.
5. `openclaw gateway call tools.invoke --params '{"name":"memory_search","args":{"query":"x"}}'`: sessions catch up and the watcher starts.

Observed on 2026-11-05: indexing stopped at 07:42 when the app relaunched at 07:48, and stayed stopped for about ten hours.

## Expected

The Gateway starts the default memory manager (watcher, session listener,
startup catch-up) at boot, as `resolveSyncConfig()` (`watch: true`,
`onSessionStart: true`) implies. Failing that, a `cli` search should not leave
sessions unindexed.

## Related

openclaw#177685 (CLI search-triggered sync lost on exit), openclaw#177686
(memory watcher ends without logging).

issues.body:
### Bug type
Regression (worked before, now fails)

### Summary
With the state directory (`~/.openclaw`) on an NFS-mounted home directory, 2026.11.2's `openclaw doctor --fix` and Gateway startup both fail while cleaning up SQLite snapshot/publish directories. 2026.10.8 runs from the same NFS state directory (it has warned `SQLite snapshot requires a captured physical file identity` in `openclaw status`, but works). Moving the state directory to a GPFS filesystem makes 2026.11.2's Doctor and Gateway succeed.

### Steps to reproduce
1. State directory on NFS (here: VAST over NFS v3, `df -T` → `nfs`), OpenClaw 2026.10.8 with existing state (agent DB schema v25).
2. Stop the Gateway, `npm install -g openclaw@2026.11.2`, run `openclaw doctor --fix --non-interactive`.
3. Doctor exits 1; `openclaw gateway run` then exits 1 during bootstrap.

### Actual behavior
Doctor:
```
Original state capture was unavailable: … State schema inspection failed (exit): … during pre-migration database backup for <state>/agents/claude/agent/openclaw-agent.sqlite (scope: 12 source paths): SQLite snapshot cleanup failed: <home>/.openclaw.update-captures/doctor-<id>/database.databases/openclaw-sql…
Doctor could not complete maintenance.
SQLite read-only worker snapshot cleanup failed: <home>/.cache/openclaw/openclaw-sqlite-readonly-v2-<rand>
```
Gateway:
```
[gateway] startup phase: cli.main.gateway-run-bootstrap … failed
[openclaw] Reason: Shared-state read scope and cleanup failed
```
With only `~/.cache` and the update-captures directory moved off NFS (state still on NFS), Doctor reports the underlying error:
```
SQLite database cannot be snapshotted safely: <state>/agents/claude/agent/openclaw-agent.sqlite. ENOTEMPTY: directory not empty, rmdir '<state>/agents/claude/agent/.sqlite-publish-<rand>'
```
This looks like NFS "silly rename": a file still open when unlinked is renamed to `.nfsXXXX`, so the directory can't be removed until it's closed. A leftover `openclaw-sqlite-readonly-v2-*` directory contained a 0-byte `owner.sqlite`.

No data was migrated (failure happens before the migration step), so reinstalling 2026.10.8 recovered the install.

### Expected behavior
Either work on NFS (e.g. close handles before removing the staging directory, or retry/tolerate `.nfs*` entries), or have `openclaw update` / `openclaw doctor` detect an unsupported filesystem for the state directory **before** stopping/upgrading, with a clear message.

### What works
- State directory on GPFS plus `XDG_CACHE_HOME` on GPFS: Doctor completes (agent DB v25 → v27) and the Gateway starts.
- A symlinked `~/.cache/openclaw` is rejected (falls back to `~/.cache/openclaw-<uid>` on NFS), so `XDG_CACHE_HOME` is needed.
- With `~/.openclaw` as a symlink to the GPFS location, two skills under the state dir are skipped (`symlink prefix resolves outside the root ancestry`) unless `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR` is also set to the real path.

### OpenClaw version
2026.11.2 (b556fdf); last good 2026.10.8 (dc2523e)

### Operating system
RHEL 8.10, kernel 4.18, glibc 2.28 (HPC cluster; home directory on NFS)

### Install method
npm global, Node 26.12.1

### Additional information
On this host 2026.11.x is additionally blocked by #191841 (`@openclaw/proc-safe` needs glibc 2.34), so the NFS problem was found first and tested separately in an isolated mount namespace on a copy of the state.

issues.title: [Bug] npm update to 2026.11.1 fails in validating: sqlite header probe spawnSync ETIMEDOUT (56k-path batch vs hardcoded 10s timeout)

labels.name: P2
labels.description: Normal backlog priority with limited blast radius.

labels.name: maturity:stable
labels.description: Broken existing behavior primarily owned by an M4/M5 scorecard surface.

labels.name: impact:ux-friction
labels.description: User-facing flow adds avoidable confusion or support burden without fully blocking progress.

issues.body:
## Summary

`openclaw update` from 2026.10.10 to 2026.11.1 (npm mode) fails deterministically in the **validating** phase with:

> global-install-failed: Could not determine whether backup files are SQLite databases. Check that the backup worker can run and the source files are readable, then retry the backup.
> cause: spawnSync /opt/homebrew/Cellar/node/26.12.1/bin/node ETIMEDOUT

The same timeout also kills `openclaw triage`. Rollback is clean every time.

## Root cause

The new-in-2026.11.1 backup verification feeds **all state-owned file paths to the sqlite header probe in a single spawnSync call with a hardcoded 10s timeout** (`probeSqliteDatabaseHeaders` in `dist/backup-sqlite-snapshot-D38jOyo9.mjs`, `timeout: 1e4`). On installations with large state directories the probe child cannot finish within 10s, so every attempt times out; retries accumulate to the observed ~57-61s validating duration before the step gives up.

Measured on the affected machine (macOS 27.0.1 arm64, node 26.12.1, 244k files under `~/.openclaw`):

| probe input size | elapsed |
|---|---|
| 30,000 paths | 7.7s |
| 56,163 paths (real discovery output) | >10s (ETIMEDOUT) |
| 112,638 paths | 20.5s |
| 200,000 paths | 28.4s |

I intercepted the real probe input by staging the npm package and calling `discoverBackupDatabasePaths({ stateDir, config, env: {} })` with a monkey-patched `child_process.spawnSync`. The discovery returned **56,163 paths in one batch**, of which:

- `browser/openclaw` (Chromium profile of the browser tool): **34,082**
- `agents/main`: 6,511
- `wiki/main`: 3,427
- workspaces/skills/memory + agent dirs: remainder

So any long-lived installation with a populated browser profile (or generally >50k state files) cannot update at all.

## Workaround (confirmed)

Temporarily move the largest contributor out of the state dir during the update:

```bash
mkdir -p ~/.openclaw-hold && mv ~/.openclaw/browser ~/.openclaw-hold/browser
openclaw update --yes          # passed: probe input dropped to 22,068 paths, measured 1.16s
mv ~/.openclaw-hold/browser ~/.openclaw/browser
```

The update then completed successfully (2026.10.10 → 2026.11.1).

## Notes

- `openclaw update --timeout 600` does not help — the 10s ceiling is hardcoded in the probe call, not the step deadline.
- `2026.11.5-beta.1` still contains `timeout: 1e4` in `backup-sqlite-snapshot-gLD0JIrr.mjs`.
- Failed-run diagnostics: runIds 85e83ac0-fe3a-4872-b685-d0fd6a01ef37, 772a85f2 (both empty `payload/` in the update capture — the probe runs before anything is written), plus one manual CLI run at ~19:00 CST. Support JSONs are in `~/.openclaw/logs/support/`.

## Suggested fixes

1. Chunk the probe input (e.g. 5k paths per batch) and/or raise/scale the timeout with input size.
2. Exclude high-churn cache-style directories (browser profile caches, plugin-capture leftovers) from the discovery walk — I also found 131k files of stale `tmp/plugin-captures/*/node_modules` trees contributing to the problem; these pile up after plugin builds and are never cleaned.
3. Surface the actual failing input size in the error message (it currently points users toward "backup worker can't run / files unreadable", which sent me down the wrong path initially).

Happy to provide the interception driver script if useful.

issues.body:
### Bug type

Regression (worked before, now fails)

### Beta release blocker

No

### Summary

MCP server runtimes created by heartbeat/follow-up turns can become permanently un-evictable: isRuntimeIdle() in agent-bundle-mcp-manager-lifecycle.ts gates idle eviction on listLiveAgentRunIds()/hasAgentRunContextExecutionOwner() for session-scoped runtimes, and for some run types that live-run marker apparently never clears, so mcp.sessionIdleTtlMs cannot reclaim them no matter how high it's set.

### Steps to reproduce

Configure an agent with one or more stdio MCP servers (e.g. uvx-launched) and an active heartbeat.
Set mcp.sessionIdleTtlMs to a finite value (e.g. 3600000).
Let the Gateway run for several hours under normal heartbeat activity.
Inspect ps aux for service-child-group-anchor.js / the MCP server's process tree repeatedly accumulating in fresh clusters roughly every heartbeat-adjacent interval, each surviving well past the configured TTL.

### Expected behavior

Runtimes idle past mcp.sessionIdleTtlMs are evicted by the scheduled sweep (mcp:idle-runtimes, confirmed running every 60s).

### Actual behavior

Fresh clusters of service-child-group-anchor + MCP server child processes appear repeatedly and are never evicted by the idle sweep; only an external, blunt-force process-age sweep reclaims them.

### OpenClaw version

 2026.11.1 (also reproduced on 2026.10.7)

### Operating system

Ubuntu Linux

### Install method

npm global

### Model

N/A — not model-dependent (process-lifecycle defect in agent-bundle-mcp-manager-lifecycle.ts; reproduces regardless of model)

### Provider / routing chain

openclaw -> anthropic (direct, no proxy/gateway) No Cloudflare AI Gateway or router in the chain for this agent — it's a direct Anthropic API connection via the Claude CLI runtime, so the leak isn't provider-routing related either.

### Additional provider/model setup details

_No response_

### Logs

```shell

```

### Screenshots, recordings, and evidence

Evidence: Confirmed on a live Gateway: with mcp.sessionIdleTtlMs: 3600000 already active, fresh 8-process clusters were created and orphaned at 21:23 and 23:23 (local), both caught only by an external age-based sweep at 5+ hours old — well past the 1-hour configured TTL. isRuntimeIdle's live-run check is the specific mechanism that would explain this: if the run context backing the session is never cleared via clearAgentRunContext/releaseAgentRunContext, or never reached by sweepStaleRunContexts, the MCP runtime reads as permanently busy to the idle sweep regardless of TTL.

### Impact and severity

Medium-high — this is an unbounded resource leak over time (real OS processes), not just a config gap; mcp.sessionIdleTtlMs alone does not fully mitigate it.

### Additional information

This supersedes/replaces #194078 — that issue's terminateOnHostLoss framing was disproven (see comment there). NOT_ENOUGH_INFO on the exact reason the run context isn't cleared for the affected run type — that's the open question for whoever picks this up.

issues.body:
# `skill_workshop` background experience-review retries repeatedly on invalid tool-call arguments, no visible retry/turn cap

## Summary

OpenClaw's automatic post-conversation "experience review" (spawned as `agent:main:internal-session-effects:skill-workshop-review_<uuid>` sessions, using the `skill_workshop` tool) repeatedly produced invalid tool-call arguments for `skill_workshop` and had to retry, burning real paid model calls each time. Observed on `2026.10.5` against a real IONOS AI Model Hub-backed model (`Qwen/Qwen3.5-397B-A17B`) immediately after upgrading from an earlier `2026.10.x` build.

## What we saw

Over one afternoon, 8 separate `skill-workshop-review` sessions ran (one per preceding real conversation turn), together issuing 60 real `skill_workshop` tool calls and consuming ~11.7M real tokens. Of those, at least 4 sessions hit a schema-validation failure:

```
tool_call failed: Invalid arguments for tool "openclaw:core:skill_workshop": <root>: must not have additional properties: "description", "evidence". Expected input: { action: "list" | "view" | "create" | "patch" | "write_file" | "remove_file" | "archive" | "restore"; absorbed_into?: string; content?: string; file_path?: string; name?: string; new_text?: string; old_text?: string; reason?: string; version?: string }.
```

```
tool_call failed: Invalid arguments for tool "openclaw:core:skill_workshop": <root>: must not have additional properties: "evidence", "skill_name"; action: must be equal to one of the allowed values (allowed: "list", "view", "create", "patch", "write_file", "remove_file", "archive", "restore").
```
(raw args used `"action":"update"` — not a member of the allowed enum — together with `evidence`, `skill_name`, `expected_revision`, `proposal_content`, `description` fields that don't exist on the schema at all)

```
tool_call failed: Invalid arguments for tool "openclaw:core:skill_workshop": <root>: must not have additional properties: "expected_revision", "proposal_content", "skill_name"; action: must be equal to one of the allowed values (...).
```

```
tool_call failed: Invalid arguments for tool "openclaw:core:skill_workshop": <root>: must not have additional properties: "proposal_content".
```

Each failure consumed a full real model call before the next retry (confirmed from per-call token telemetry — these aren't free/local validation-only retries). One session needed 11 separate `skill_workshop` tool calls before completing.

We checked the system prompt that drives these review sessions (`experience-review-*.mjs` in the installed package) — it correctly only mentions `action=list`/`view`/`patch` and a `reason` field, and never mentions `update`, `evidence`, `description`, `proposal_content`, `expected_revision`, or `skill_name`. So this doesn't look like a prompt/schema version mismatch on OpenClaw's side — the model itself (in this case `Qwen/Qwen3.5-397B-A17B`, a non-first-party model routed through IONOS AI Model Hub) is repeatedly inventing a richer "proposal/evidence" change-workflow that doesn't exist in the real tool schema, across multiple independent review sessions. In our own experience this particular model is prone to inventing plausible-but-nonexistent parameters/options in general (not specific to this tool), so we don't think this points at a prompt/schema bug — it's raised purely as operational feedback on a fully internal, user-invisible background feature, not a request to change behavior for this model specifically.

## Why we're flagging it anyway

Regardless of whether the root cause is model-side tool-call weakness or something about how the schema/examples are presented, this is a background, automatically-scheduled feature (not something the user directly asked for) that is:
- burning real, billed tokens on invalid retries with no cap we could find in the installed build on these failed arguments, and
- not surfaced anywhere the user would notice (it runs silently as an internal-session-effect; we only found it via telemetry while investigating unrelated metrics accuracy).

Two independent, lower-risk mitigations that seem worth considering regardless of root cause:
1. A max-retry / max-turn budget specifically for `skill_workshop` background review sessions, so a model stuck re-guessing invalid arguments gives up after N attempts instead of continuing to spend real tokens.
2. Including the exact allowed `action` enum and property list directly in the `skill_workshop` tool's description/schema docstring (not just the validator's rejection message), which may reduce how often a model has to discover the real schema via trial-and-error error messages.

## Environment

- OpenClaw `2026.10.5` (`1b58cb9`), upgraded same-day from an earlier `2026.10.x` build
- Model: `Qwen/Qwen3.5-397B-A17B` via IONOS AI Model Hub (OpenAI-compatible endpoint)
- Plugin: `th-m-vogel/openclaw-observability-plugin` (OTel observability plugin, fork) — used only to gather this telemetry, not implicated in the behavior itself

issues.body:
### Bug type

Behavior bug (incorrect output/state without crash)

### Beta release blocker

No

### Summary

Control UI Web Push notifications appear normally on macOS Safari but remain silent even when notification sounds are enabled in macOS, because the service worker does not explicitly request sound with `silent: false`; Apple documents that macOS Web Push defaults to silent.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Run OpenClaw 2026.9.7 and open the Control UI in Safari on macOS.
2. Open **Settings → Notifications** and enable browser notifications.
3. In macOS **System Settings → Notifications**, enable notifications for the Control UI site and enable **Play sound for notification**.
4. Confirm Mac audio is audible with another notification source.
5. In OpenClaw **Settings → Notifications**, click **Send test**.
6. Observe that the OpenClaw Web Push banner appears but no notification sound plays.

Observed on the Control UI origin with Safari Web Push. Telegram notifications on the same Mac produce audible notification sounds under the same system audio state.

### Expected behavior

When notification sound is enabled by the user, OpenClaw Web Push notifications that are intended to get the user's attention should request audible delivery on macOS.

Apple documents that Notifications API sound is **off by default on macOS**, and that an audible notification should explicitly set `silent: false`:

https://developer.apple.com/videos/play/wwdc2023/10120/?time=884

### Actual behavior

The Web Push notification is delivered and displayed, but it is silent.

In both OpenClaw `v2026.9.7` and current `main`, `ui/public/sw.js` constructs the notification options without a `silent` field:

```js
const options = {
  body: data.body || "",
  icon: "./apple-touch-icon.png",
  badge: "./favicon-32.png",
  tag: data.tag || "openclaw-notification",
  renotify: data.renotify === true,
  data: {
    url: data.url || self.registration.scope,
    explicitUrl: Boolean(data.url),
  },
};

event.waitUntil(self.registration.showNotification(title, options));
```

On macOS, omitting `silent` leaves the platform default in effect, which Apple documents as sound off.

### OpenClaw version

2026.9.7

### Operating system

macOS 26.6.2, Safari 26.6.2

### Install method

Self-hosted Gateway / Control UI in Safari

### Model

N/A (the Web Push test path does not depend on model execution)

### Provider / routing chain

N/A (Control UI Web Push test)

### Additional provider/model setup details

The issue is independent of model/provider selection. The failing path is the Control UI service worker notification presentation.

### Logs

```shell
No delivery error observed. "Send test" successfully produces the visible Web Push banner.
```

### Screenshots, recordings, and evidence

Observed evidence:

- OpenClaw **Send test** displays the expected macOS notification banner.
- macOS notification permission for the Control UI site is enabled.
- **Play sound for notification** is enabled for that site.
- System output volume is audible.
- Telegram notifications on the same Mac produce sound.
- OpenClaw's `ui/public/sw.js` omits the Notifications API `silent` option on both `v2026.9.7` and current `main`.
- Apple states that notification sound is off by default on macOS and that sites should set `silent: false` for an audible notification:
  https://developer.apple.com/videos/play/wwdc2023/10120/?time=884

### Impact and severity

Affected: macOS users relying on Control UI Web Push for attention notifications such as approvals, agent questions, or agent completion.

Severity: workflow usability issue. Notifications are delivered visually, but users working in another window can miss them because there is no audible alert.

Frequency: 100% in the observed test setup.

Consequence: the attention-notification feature does not reliably attract attention on macOS unless the user happens to see the banner.

### Additional information

The smallest source-level repair appears to be adding:

```js
silent: false,
```

to the service worker notification options, with regression coverage verifying that Web Push notifications request audible delivery. User notification settings still remain authoritative, as documented by Apple.

No existing OpenClaw issue for this specific macOS Web Push `silent: false` omission was found before filing.

### Bug type

Behavior bug (incorrect output/state without crash)

### Beta release blocker

No

### Summary

One provider catalog discovery attempt reported an SDK module was not fully loaded and skipped discovery on OpenClaw 2026.11.2.

### Steps to reproduce

NOT_ENOUGH_INFO

### Expected behavior

Provider catalog discovery should be able to load its SDK dependencies and return the selected provider's catalog without an `ES Module ... not yet fully loaded` error. The released code already isolates a failed hook from healthy sibling providers; preserving that isolation is part of the expected behavior. See [`runProviderCatalogWithTimeout`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/b556fdf457b026574bf0f1e7b4914b15f3f179ce/src/agents/models-config.providers.implicit.ts#L381-L386) and the [concurrent discovery test](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/b556fdf457b026574bf0f1e7b4914b15f3f179ce/src/agents/models-config.providers.implicit.outcomes.test.ts#L85).

### Actual behavior

A shared OpenClaw log recorded one warning from `agents/model-providers` at 00:05:51 UTC on 9 November 2026. It reported that `provider-auth-runtime.js` was not fully loaded when required, and that provider discovery was being skipped. The affected provider ID is not in the warning. The released source's catch path reports the affected provider IDs unavailable to its callback and returns no catalog for that attempt; the log alone does not identify those IDs or prove the callback was connected. Other providers' behavior is not established by this warning.

The warning occurred during the period following a Gateway startup after upgrade. The daily log is shared by OpenClaw processes and this line has no PID, so the emitting process is unconfirmed. No subsequent successful discovery for that particular provider was established. A loaded/enabled official Codex plugin was separately observed, but the affected provider may or may not have been Codex. No user-visible inference failure was established. No replay or synthetic inference was performed.

### OpenClaw version

Official `2026.11.2`, build `2026.11.2-release-b556fdf457b0-2026-11-07T15-35-25.381Z`, source commit [`b556fdf457b026574bf0f1e7b4914b15f3f179ce`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/b556fdf457b026574bf0f1e7b4914b15f3f179ce). Factory core installed from the official global npm archive. Node.js `v26.12.1`.

### Operating system

Windows 11 x64, build 26200.

### Install method

Global npm install; OpenClaw Gateway uses the Windows scheduled-task owner. Official external `@openclaw/codex` 2026.11.2 was separately inspected as loaded and enabled; the warning does not identify this as the failing provider.

### Model

NOT_ENOUGH_INFO

### Provider / routing chain

NOT_ENOUGH_INFO

### Additional provider/model setup details

The warning does not name the affected provider, model or operation. No inference test or user-facing impact is asserted.

### Logs

Filtered single warning, with only the installation-root path redacted; no stack trace beyond the indicated loader was present in this log entry:

```text
2026-11-09T00:05:51.254Z WARN [agents/model-providers]
Cannot require() ES Module <openclaw>/dist/plugin-sdk/provider-auth-runtime.js because it is not yet fully loaded.
This may be caused by a race condition if the module is simultaneously dynamically import()-ed via Promise.all().
Try await-ing the import() sequentially in a loop instead.
 (From <openclaw>/dist/plugin-module-loader-cache-CJx9mYDU.mjs in non-loader-hook thread); skipping provider discovery
```

### Screenshots, recordings, and evidence

- The error target and loader were verified as paths in the installed `openclaw` package; the text above preserves the package-relative paths and error wording.
- The release [provider-discovery catch](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/b556fdf457b026574bf0f1e7b4914b15f3f179ce/src/agents/models-config.providers.implicit.ts#L361-L386) catches a failing catalog call, optionally reports unavailable for its provider IDs, logs this warning and returns `undefined`. This establishes the source path for the logged consequence, not the identity of the failing provider or a user-facing outage.
- [`#145026`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/145026) addressed an earlier SDK require/import race associated with the Teams scenario in [`#144966`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/144966). Its merge commit is an ancestor of this release; [the target resolver still includes the synchronous evaluation](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/b556fdf457b026574bf0f1e7b4914b15f3f179ce/src/plugins/plugin-sdk-native-resolver.ts#L393-L396). The present warning occurs in provider catalog discovery and names a different SDK entry and a plugin loader; whether it shares the same cause is unproven. It is not evidence that the Teams outage recurred.
- An older [`#112427`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/112427) describes a different Codex startup failure on 2026.7.1. The present warning alone does not establish a Codex failure.

### Impact and severity

NOT_ENOUGH_INFO

### Additional information

One observed warning; frequency, triggering interleaving, regression boundary, affected provider, later retry outcome and practical impact are unknown. No reproduction on current `main` is claimed. A useful next step is to identify the provider and concurrent callers at the catalog/loader boundary and test that provider discovery either completes without a module race or reports a recoverable failure without losing healthy sibling catalogs. No installed code, security setting or timeout was changed to reproduce the event.

Prepared with Codex assistance.

issues.body:
## Summary

A running agent turn pins every plugin in its prepared generation, including plugins the turn never calls. A config write that replaces an unrelated plugin therefore waits on, and then times out behind, turns that don't use that plugin. The write returns `UNAVAILABLE` after the 60 s drain, and the reload applies only after those turns finish. On a gateway with long-running native-harness turns, this blocks config changes to provider plugins for minutes.

## Mechanism (main `62a3f2fc7`)

- **Every plugin is pinned.** The prepared-generation lease [retains runtime plugin work](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/62a3f2fc707069bbf4f47019a4c15617d41ae663/src/agents/prepared-model-runtime.plugin-lifetime.ts#L228) for every invocation instance of the turn's registries ([`runtime-plugin-work.ts:35`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/62a3f2fc707069bbf4f47019a4c15617d41ae663/src/agents/runtime-plugin-work.ts#L35)), not only the plugins the turn actually invokes.
- **Handover needs every replaced plugin to opt in.** A reload can hand a running turn over only if every reserved plugin declares `reload.turnHandover` ([`plugin-turn-handover.ts:38`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/62a3f2fc707069bbf4f47019a4c15617d41ae663/src/agents/plugin-turn-handover.ts#L38), [`manifest-types.ts:440`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/62a3f2fc707069bbf4f47019a4c15617d41ae663/src/plugins/manifest-types.ts#L440)). Otherwise "reload of … keeps running turns on their admitted generations" ([L60](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/62a3f2fc707069bbf4f47019a4c15617d41ae663/src/agents/plugin-turn-handover.ts#L60)).
- **Some harnesses can't opt in.** A native agent harness turn has no model-step boundary to hand over at. Plugins that keep live native sessions, such as `muse` and `acpx`, can't honestly declare `turnHandover`: the manifest contract requires that the plugin keep no in-memory state a later call depends on.
- **The write fails, then the reload retries.** The drain gives up after [`PLUGIN_RELOAD_ADMITTED_WORK_TIMEOUT_MS` = 60 s](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/62a3f2fc707069bbf4f47019a4c15617d41ae663/src/gateway/server-plugin-reload-cleanup.ts#L41) ([L421](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/62a3f2fc707069bbf4f47019a4c15617d41ae663/src/gateway/server-plugin-reload-cleanup.ts#L421)). `config.patch` reports the change as persisted but not applied. The reload is deferred and retried once the holders go idle ([`config-reload.ts:966`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/62a3f2fc707069bbf4f47019a4c15617d41ae663/src/gateway/config-reload.ts#L966)).

## Reproduction (isolated Gateway on main, fictional config)

1. Run one held turn on an agent bound to a native harness. Here that's `muse` with the in-tree fake peer in its `settle` mode, so the turn stays open.
2. Make one `openclaw config patch` that changes two unrelated provider plugins, neither declaring `turnHandover`: `plugins.entries.xai.config.webSearch.inlineCitations` and `plugins.entries.openai.config.personality`.

What happened:

```text
Plugin replacement queued behind 2 retained work item(s) for plugin openai, xai. Running turns keep openai, xai until they finish. New agent runs wait up to the 60s drain budget.
reload of openai, xai keeps running turns on their admitted generations
… 60 s later …
config reload deferred: … plugin openai, xai admitted work did not settle within 60s; the previous plugin generation stays active …
config.patch → UNAVAILABLE "config.patch persisted but was not applied to the active Gateway" (87 s)
… after the held turn ended …
Plugin replacement applied: openai, xai
```

The held turn never called `openai` or `xai`. Turns were not aborted, and new runs on other agents kept working during the drain. The cost is that the config write fails and the reload waits for unrelated work.

## Options

1. **Narrow the lease to plugins the turn has invoked.** Pin a plugin's generation from its first call in the turn, rather than the whole registry at preparation time. A reload of a plugin no running turn has called would then not wait at all.
2. **Allow per-plugin replacement** when no admitted work references that plugin's instance, even while other instances in the same generation stay pinned.
3. **Keep the current design but say so.** Document that a config write to any plugin waits for all running turns, and give native-harness owners a supported way to release unrelated plugins.

Option 1 seems closest to the intent of `turnHandover`, which is about state in the plugin being replaced, not in unrelated ones.

issues.body:
### Summary

An opt-in usage budget contract: per-surface (agent / channel / cron job / subagent) token-cost rollups plus a simple enforceable budget hook that can degrade the model, pause a non-critical schedule, or stop the turn when a configured window is exhausted.

### Problem to solve

Cost attribution and cost *control* are currently two different gaps:

- Attribution is fragmented: #102807 shows usage is provider-keyed rather than credential-keyed so mixed API+subscription installs display the wrong billing mode; #90911 notes per-run token accounting exists on `cron_run_logs` but not on `task_runs`/`subagent_runs`; #156999 shows legacy cron sessions land in an "Unattributed" bucket. Operators cannot answer "which of my automations burned the budget".
- Control is essentially absent: a runaway loop, a session-reset re-seeding storm (see #178953), or a chatty channel can consume a full 5-hour plan window in minutes with nothing in the product to stop or downgrade it. Users discover this only at the provider's rate-limit wall.

With recurring autonomous schedules (cron, heartbeats, subagents) being a core deployment pattern, spend needs to be attributable per surface and bounded per policy, the same way tool execution is gated per turn.

### Proposed solution

1. **Attribution rollup contract**: every model call carries the originating surface (agent, channel, cron job id, subagent run, interactive session) end-to-end, and a single queryable aggregate exposes tokens/cost grouped by surface over a time window. This generalizes the parity ask in #90911 and fixes the bucket problems in #102807/#156999 at the data model layer rather than per-UI-widget.
2. **Opt-in budget hook**: a config-scoped budget (per surface or global, per rolling window). On exhaustion the configured action fires: degrade to a cheaper model, skip/pause a schedule with a recorded reason, or fail the turn with a user-visible error — never a silent continue.
3. **Decision-friendly enforcement point**: the budget check belongs at the owning boundary where the next model call is admitted. The recently introduced provider-neutral `decision_evaluate` capability (#155115) is a natural fit for the "what do I do at the limit" judgment, keeping the mechanism generic and opt-in.

Explicitly **not** proposed: a billing system, per-token pricing tables, or provider-specific quota mirroring beyond what exists today.

### Alternatives considered

- Per-provider usage display fixes alone (e.g. #169428's footer template): treats symptoms; no enforcement.
- External monitoring scripts watching usage files: exactly the out-of-tree watcher pattern the project keeps absorbing back into core (cf. #161049 for cron supervision).

### Impact

- Affected: every operator running unattended schedules or multi-agent setups; mixed API+subscription users.
- Severity: cost surprises at "uninstalled it" magnitude are reported; for subscribed plans, wasted 5h windows block real work.
- Frequency: continuous for automation-heavy installs.
- Consequence: unpredictable spend, rate-limit lockouts, and manual post-hoc forensics across session files.

### Evidence/examples

- #90911 (per-run token persistence parity), #102807 (provider-keyed attribution), #156999 (unattributed cron sessions), #7379 (usage footer ask).
- Session-reset re-seeding as a concrete unbounded amplifier: #178953.

### Do you plan to open a PR for this?

No, proposing the idea only

### Additional information

If the attribution layer lands first (it is independently useful), the budget hook could follow as a small policy gate; happy to split this into two requests if maintainers prefer.

issues.body:
### Bug type

Behavior bug (incorrect output/state without crash)

### Beta release blocker

No

### Summary

With `gateway.tailscale.mode: "serve"` and `gateway.auth.allowTailscale: true`, a Control UI browser that signs in through Tailscale identity skips device pairing (as documented in `docs/gateway/tailscale.md`). That browser can still enable Web Push. `push.web.subscribe` stores its subscription, Settings → Notifications shows **Subscribed**, and **Send test** arrives. Real notifications never arrive, though (agent finished, approvals, questions, failed automations). Event delivery drops every subscription whose device is not paired, and nothing in the UI, the logs, or the docs says so.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Gateway in token mode behind Tailscale Serve: `gateway.bind: "loopback"`, `gateway.tailscale.mode: "serve"`, `gateway.auth.mode: "token"`, `gateway.auth.allowTailscale: true`.
2. On an iPhone, open `https://<host>.ts.net/` in Safari, choose Share → Add to Home Screen, then open the installed app. Tailscale identity signs it in without a token and without a pairing request.
3. Settings → Notifications → **Enable notifications** → allow. Enable the "Agent finished" category.
4. Tap **Send test**. The notification arrives.
5. Send a chat message to an agent and put the app in the background.
6. Wait for the agent to finish.

### Expected behavior

Either the "Agent finished" notification arrives, or the UI or Gateway states that this browser must be paired before it can receive event notifications. Enabling and testing should not report a working setup that cannot deliver anything except tests.

### Actual behavior

- Step 4: the test notification "Web push test notification" arrives (03.10.2026 23:33 CEST).
- Step 6: no notification. The Gateway log shows no Web Push warning for these events.
- The subscribed device (`67c9f219…`) is not in `device_pairing_paired` (`state/openclaw.sqlite`). The subscription row exists, bound to that device ID and to the Tailscale user profile.
- After switching to `allowTailscale: false`, I signed the same installed app in with the Gateway token and approved the resulting pairing request (`openclaw devices approve`). From then on, "OpenClaw agent finished – main: An agent completed its response." arrived (03.10.2026 23:55 CEST). Nothing else changed.

### OpenClaw version

2026.9.8 (`fc23bc8`)

### Operating system

Gateway: Ubuntu 24.04.4 LTS (x64). Client: iOS 26.6.1, Control UI installed as a Home Screen web app from Safari.

### Install method

npm global

### Model

Not model-related.

### Provider / routing chain

Not provider-related. Tailscale Serve → managed loopback listener.

### Additional provider/model setup details

n/a

### Logs

The connection was accepted via Tailscale identity, with no pairing:

```
[ws] authenticated user connected conn=d1ede1a5-… user=<tailscale login>
[ws] ⇄ res ✓ push.web.vapidPublicKey 261ms
[ws] ⇄ res ✓ push.web.subscribe 82ms
[ws] ⇄ res ✓ push.web.test 644ms
```

No `event Web Push delivery failed` line and no other log line appears for the dropped agent-finished events.

### Screenshots, recordings, and evidence

Code on `main` (`5421a780364`):

- `src/gateway/server-methods/push.ts`, `"push.web.subscribe"` (line ~304): it requires only `client.connect.device.id`. The error text says "paired browser device identity required", but pairing is not checked.
- `src/gateway/server-methods/push.ts`, `"push.web.test"` (line ~524): `broadcastWebPush()` sends to every stored subscription with no pairing or scope check. This matches the docs ("Tests intentionally check transport only").
- `src/gateway/web-push-authority.ts`, `resolveCurrentWebPushTarget()` (line ~55): `if (!device || !hasEffectivePairedDeviceRole(device, OPERATOR_ROLE)) return null;`. Event and approval delivery therefore skip subscriptions from unpaired devices.
- `docs/gateway/tailscale.md`: "a verified Tailscale identity skips the bootstrap-token/QR pairing round trip" for Control UI operator sessions.

Combined, a Tailscale-authenticated browser gets a subscription that only test pushes can reach.

### Impact and severity

Affected: anyone using `allowTailscale: true` and Web Push. iOS users are especially likely to hit this, because the documented iOS path (Add to Home Screen) gives the installed app its own storage, so Tailscale sign-in is the convenient way in. Severity: medium. Approval notifications are among the silently dropped events, so approvals can wait unnoticed. Frequency: always, for every unpaired Tailscale-authenticated browser.

### Additional information

Side effect seen in the same setup: the Tailscale sign-in created a second user profile (personal identity, with the Tailscale login as email) next to the shared `gateway-owner` profile. Category preferences set in the installed app were stored on that personal profile. After switching to token plus pairing, the subscriptions moved to `gateway-owner`, which still had default preferences (approvals only), so the categories had to be enabled again. The leftover profile is tracked separately in https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/164580.

Possible directions, not tested:

1. Reject `push.web.subscribe` for unpaired devices, with a message that names pairing.
2. Allow event delivery to subscriptions whose device is currently authenticated through verified Tailscale identity.
3. At minimum, have Settings → Notifications show that this browser is subscribed but not paired, and log a debug line when a subscription is skipped for lack of pairing.

Related: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/142323 (closed). It is about `allowTailscale` forcing the multi-user identity model; different symptom.

issues.body:
## Problem

A saved active Goal is not sufficient to keep pursuit running through child handoffs and Gateway restarts. The UI can retain an unconfirmed Resume receipt while later work executes, and native harness goal state is not integrated with OpenClaw's Goal controls.

## Current source observations

On main at `aff677109f8dae50b4c2dd82a6899ae48982956a`:

- Automatic follow-ups support local and remote-exec Codex, but child-return goal context is consumed only by the built-in harness. The retained return also lacks the Codex placement markers required by its context predicate.
- Goal follow-up and child-return custody are process-local. Restart capture selects live execution owners and accepted inputs, not every active Goal; there is a gap when the previous execution has settled but its successor has not been durably accepted.
- The Codex plugin exposes native goal commands but sets `features.goals: false` for managed threads. Enabling that flag alone is not a fix: native autonomous turns need admitted execution ownership, tool authority, cancellation, transcript/delivery, and accounting.

Related: #177351, #179629. This report does not propose a parallel polling agent or periodically injected prompt.

## Expected behavior and proposed direction

Keep one authoritative continuation owner. Preserve an accepted continuation across normal settlement/restart, give user input and child/tool completions priority, and revalidate the exact session, goal, current principal and execution restrictions at admission. Stop/Pause, blocked/complete/budget-limited goals, replaced sessions, and revoked access must remain terminal for old continuation work. Errors should produce an explicit recoverable outcome, not silently leave a pursuing label with no owner.

Fix the reproducible cross-harness child-return gap first. For native runtime integration, use a narrow capability contract backed by the provider's actual public API, not a second independent goal engine. Codex's autonomous turns require an explicit host admission handoff; Claude Code capability is being checked against its current supported interface rather than assuming it implements Codex's goal protocol.

## Validation plan

Regression coverage for child return to built-in/Codex/CLI execution, exact-identity and stop races, queued user input, lost acknowledgment replay, and restart between predecessor settlement and successor admission. Native autonomous execution must additionally prove that Stop, permissions, accounting and visible replies remain attached to the same admitted owner.

issues.body:
**Version:** first seen on openclaw 2026.10.6, still reproducing on 2026.10.8 (2026-11-04: abort at 03:06:34 with age=379s, `dreaming promotion complete (workspaces=18 ...)` at 03:07:10, run status=ok, 434s). Same code in 2026.10.10 (latest) and 2026.11.5-beta.1: no progress calls in `dist/extensions/memory-core/index.js`, `DEFAULT_STUCK_SESSION_WARN_MS = 12e4` unchanged. Linux arm64, 16-18 dreaming workspaces.

**What happens**

The built-in "Memory Dreaming Promotion" cron runs `runShortTermDreamingPromotion` as an embedded run. It loops over every workspace in a plain `for (const { agentId, agentIds, workspaceDir } of workspaces)` loop (extensions/memory-core/index.js, ~L245-252). Each workspace takes about 15-25s, so with 16-18 workspaces the whole run takes 6-9 minutes.

The loop never calls `markDiagnosticRunProgress` / `markDiagnosticSessionProgress` / `emitCoreSemanticRunProgress`, so `lastProgress` stays at `embedded_run:started`. The stuck-session watchdog then:
- logs `stalled session ... classification=stalled_agent_run reason=active_work_without_progress` every 30s from about 120s on
- fires `action=abort_embedded_run` ("stuck session recovery") at about 360-383s (abort = max(300s, 3 x 120s warn))

The abort doesn't stop the plugin work. The loop keeps going and logs `dreaming promotion complete` 1-3 minutes after the abort, and diary files are written after that. The cron run record ends `status=ok`.

**Evidence (4 nights in a row, same every night, not tied to memory pressure)**
- 10/27: abort 03:06:32, complete 03:09:24
- 10/28: abort 03:06:40, complete 03:08:45
- 10/29: abort 03:06:23, complete 03:07:54
- 10/30: complete 03:06:10, 7ms before the abort would have fired
- Run durations over the last 5 nights: 371-564s, all status=ok. Output checked on disk: every workspace got its REM entry every night (144/144).
- Same pattern right after a fresh gateway restart at low RSS (~6.5 GiB, no heap warnings).

**Why it matters**
- Nightly false "stalled" / "aborted" log noise in any multi-agent install sends operators looking for a hang that isn't there.
- An abort that reports success but doesn't cancel the work is misleading. If the work ever really hung, recovery wouldn't free it.
- There's no workaround: `diagnostics.stuckSessionWarnMs` / `stuckSessionAbortMs` are retired (RETIRED_TUNING_PATHS), and cron `timeoutSeconds` doesn't feed the watchdog.

**Suggested fix**
1. In the dreaming promotion loop, report run progress once per workspace (and per phase), so the stall timer resets while real work is happening. This is the main fix.
2. Make `abort_embedded_run` pass an AbortSignal into plugin-hook embedded runs, and have the dreaming loop check it between workspaces, so an abort actually stops the work. Or, if a run can't be cancelled, don't log it as aborted.
3. Optional: let a cron/embedded-run declare an expected duration or stall budget, as asked for in #140401.

**Repro**
Multi-agent setup with dreaming enabled for 15 or more workspaces, then wait for the nightly promotion run. `journalctl --user -u openclaw-gateway | grep -E "Memory Dreaming Promotion|dreaming promotion complete|abort_embedded_run"`.

**Related (not duplicates):** #140401 (closed: watchdog threshold no longer configurable), #191822 (compaction not counted as progress), #171366 (Code Mode awaitResults aborted), #143396.

issues.body:
## Summary

When a subagent completion event is delivered to the parent session at a moment when the receiving turn is already closing down (the system turn-finalization path where tool calls are no longer permitted), the parent agent **cannot dispatch follow-up work** — even though the completion arrived correctly and the parent has every intention to continue the chain.

In our case a nine-step orchestration chain stalled for **~28 minutes**: the writing subagent finished successfully, its completion event reached the parent, but the parent could only post a text "settled" note (no tool calls allowed in that turn) and the follow-up figure-production step was never dispatched — until an inbound user message woke the session up.

This is distinct from delivery failures (#155019 fixed deliveries not arriving; #186541 covers results lost after plugin reload): here the delivery **succeeds**, but it lands in a turn that is barred from calling tools, so the chain breaks after delivery.

## Timeline (journal, 2026-11-04, CST)

```
13:39:22  Subagent run 1c7c1e83 (status=ok) completion event delivered to parent session.
          The receiving turn was in its finalization phase — tool calls disallowed.
          Parent's only output: a text note: "本回合工具调用已完成，此处收账"
          ("this turn's tool calls are complete; settling the account here")
          → follow-up step (figure production) never dispatched. Chain stalled.
13:39–14:07  No further dispatch activity (~28 minutes stall).
14:07:16  Inbound user message wakes the session; the follow-up run (69a07cb8)
          is finally dispatched by the parent.
```

Retrospective confirmed: the subagent itself was healthy and its acceptance records were intact — this was neither a subagent failure nor a parent logic omission. The single failure point was the receiving turn's tool constraint.

## Reproduction characteristics

- **Probabilistic**: earlier completion events in the same orchestration chain were delivered into turns that could still call tools, and follow-ups were dispatched normally. The failure requires the completion to land inside the finalization window — a race between "subagent finishes" and "receiving turn closing".
- Observable on any chained orchestration where step N+1 is dispatched from step N's completion event (multi-step pipelines driven by subagent completion rather than by user turns).

## Environment

- OpenClaw 2026.10.8 (Linux x64, systemd --user gateway)
- Parent session: Feishu DM direct conversation; nine-step writing pipeline (write subagent → figure-production follow-up)

## Suggested direction

A delivered subagent completion that requests continuation should be able to **start a fresh turn in which tools are callable**, instead of being folded into an already-closing turn where the only remaining capability is text output. Concretely, one of:

1. If the receiving turn is finalizing, queue the completion as a **new turn trigger** (same as any other wake event) rather than delivering it into the closing turn;
2. Or allow the finalization path to grant a minimal "dispatch follow-up" capability for settled child completions;
3. At minimum, log and surface "completion arrived but tools disallowed — chain may stall" so operators can detect the stall without waiting for a user to notice.

## Related

- #155019 — delivery of subagent results (fixed not-arriving); our case is the step *after* delivery.
- #186541 — subagent results not reaching the parent after plugin reload; same event domain, different failure point.

issues.body:
## Summary
`message` tool inline buttons built with `action.type: "callback"` produce a `callback_data` prefixed with `tgcb1:<checksum>:<value>` (opaque plugin-only format). When tapped, the Telegram ingress handler drops the callback with `if (opaqueCallbackData) return;` because no plugin has registered the namespace. There is no fall-through path that delivers the callback back to the model as synthetic text, so button taps do nothing.

## Repro
1. Send a Telegram inline button via the `message` tool:
   ```json
   {"presentation": {"blocks": [{"type": "buttons", "buttons": [{"label": "X", "action": {"type": "callback", "value": "x"}}]}]}}
   ```
2. Tap the button. Nothing happens. Raw-update log shows the callback arrived; `answerCallbackQuery` fires; then silence.

## Root cause (v-current dist paths)
- Builder: `dist/button-types-B2h0t2EL.js:37` — `action.type: "callback"` → `buildTelegramOpaqueCallbackData(value)` → `tgcb1:<checksum>:<value>`
- Dispatcher: `dist/plugin-runtime-DAKxyCb0.js:59` — no plugin match returns `{handled: false}`
- Drop site: `dist/telegram-ingress-spool-Dd3cDhXe.js:3781` — `if (opaqueCallbackData) return;`

Compare `dist/button-types-B2h0t2EL.js:38` (raw `value` field) which uses `callback_data` unwrapped and falls through to synthetic-text delivery via ``genericCallbackText = `callback_data: ${data}` `` at ingress line 3540. That path works.

## Workaround
Use flat `{label, value}` shape instead of `{label, action: {type: "callback", value}}`. Callback arrives to the model as inbound text `callback_data: <value>`.

## Suggested fix
At `telegram-ingress-spool-…js:3781`, if `opaqueCallbackData` is present but no plugin handled it, fall through to the same synthetic-text delivery used by the raw-`value` path (`callback_data: <opaqueCallbackData>` inbound), instead of returning. Alternatively, only wrap in `tgcb1:` when the caller is a plugin with a registered namespace.

## Environment
- OpenClaw (npm global) — Pi5, Linux 6.18.39
- Node v22.23.2
- Telegram DM, `capabilities.inlineButtons: "dm"`
- Confirmed via raw-update log at 21:48:01 EDT on 2026-08-19

prs.title: fix(ai): truncate retained Responses V2 user text without splitting surrogate pairs
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

A ChatGPT Responses V2 session at the 64,000-token retention cap can retain half an emoji. `retainV2Users` binary-searches a UTF-16 code-unit limit and emitted `part.text.slice(0, low)`; an odd boundary leaves a lone high surrogate in the window that `finish()` returns and `captureOpenAIResponsesCompaction` stores as `JSON.stringify(output)` for the next request. JSON escapes that surrogate as `\ud83d`, so parsing it back yields the same ill-formed string; any bare-text UTF-8 encoding renders it as U+FFFD.

- Problem: the retention cut is made in UTF-16 code units, not code points.
- Solution: `truncateUtf16Safe(part.text, low)`, already used at six other truncation sites in `packages/ai`.
- What changed: one import and one call site; the existing retention case is now an `it.each` (BMP + astral).
- What did NOT change: the estimation predicate, no egress sanitizer, and the window is only ever one code unit shorter.

## Why This Change Was Made

`packages/ai` already treats unpaired surrogates as rejected (`utils/sanitize-unicode.ts`) and every other bounded-text emitter uses `truncateUtf16Safe`; reusing the canonical owner fixes the producer without a second truncation policy. Rejected: sanitizing the whole Responses payload at egress (a broader root-owner change), and switching the estimate to code points (changes every input's token estimate). Risk: astral text at the exact boundary retains one code unit less; all other shapes are byte-identical.

## User Impact

Long ChatGPT Responses sessions with emoji near the retention cap keep a well-formed, byte-faithful replay window instead of a dangling surrogate persisted into replay state and rendered as U+FFFD next turn.

## Evidence

### Shipped CLI session (`9b8aea400ac`)

Two real `openclaw agent --local` turns from `src/entry.ts` per arm, `OpenClaw 2026.11.1 (9b8aea4)`. Turn 1 sends the astral-boundary message (255,968 ASCII `a` + 200,000 `😀`); turn 2 sends `continue`. The native-backend gate requires a `chatgpt.com` URL, so a process-local socket redirect reaches a loopback scripted Responses endpoint (no hosts file, no fetch stub, no production logic change); it returns one compaction item for `compaction_trigger`, otherwise a normal reply. Both arms share config, session-id scheme and endpoint. The candidate mirrors the current head's one-line fix into the shipped dist chunk for the run, then restores it.

```console
$ node --import tsx/esm src/entry.ts --version
OpenClaw 2026.11.1 (9b8aea4)
embedded run auto-compaction complete: reason=threshold compactionCount=1 willRetry=false
TURN1_EXIT=0 TURN2_EXIT=0

ARM=base       turn1 compaction_trigger=true  replay=false
ARM=base       turn1 replay=true retained={"units":256000,"wellFormed":false,"tailCodeUnit":55357,"utf8RoundTripEqual":false}
ARM=base       turn2 replay=true retained={"units":256000,"wellFormed":false,"tailCodeUnit":55357,"utf8RoundTripEqual":false}
ARM=candidate  turn1 compaction_trigger=true  replay=false
ARM=candidate  turn1 replay=true retained={"units":255999,"wellFormed":true,"tailCodeUnit":56832,"utf8RoundTripEqual":true}
ARM=candidate  turn2 replay=true retained={"units":255999,"wellFormed":true,"tailCodeUnit":56832,"utf8RoundTripEqual":true}
```

`replay=true` means the request's `input` carries the `compaction` checkpoint plus the retained user text; turn 2 is a later CLI turn replaying the persisted window. Frozen main ends that window in `U+D83D` (lone high surrogate) and loses a bare-text UTF-8 round trip; the candidate ends in `U+DE00` (one complete emoji) and round-trips byte-faithfully.

### Boundary traces and regression

A `node --import tsx` script drives the real collector `observe()` → `finish()`, serializes as `captureOpenAIResponsesCompaction` does and parses back. Frozen main vs candidate on the astral boundary, with a BMP control:

```console
$ node --import tsx tmp-probe-333-shipped.mts   # frozen main
astral {"emittedUnits":256000,"wellFormed":false,"tailCodeUnit":55357,"jsonHasLoneEscape":true,"jsonUtf8RoundTripEqual":true,"parsedWellFormed":false,"textUtf8RoundTripEqual":false}
$ node --import tsx tmp-probe-333-shipped.mts   # candidate
astral {"emittedUnits":255999,"wellFormed":true,"tailCodeUnit":56832,"jsonHasLoneEscape":false,"jsonUtf8RoundTripEqual":true,"parsedWellFormed":true,"textUtf8RoundTripEqual":true}
```

The escaped JSON text is UTF-8 safe; the damage is the ill-formed string surviving parsing and bare-text UTF-8 encoding.

The committed regression runs `requestPreparedOpenAIResponsesCompaction` through the real transport and asserts on `finish()` output (only `fetch` is stubbed). RED restores the production file from `origin/main` and keeps the new `it.each`; GREEN is the current head, run twice:

```console
$ CI=1 ./node_modules/.bin/vitest run --config test/vitest/vitest.proof-bug333.config.ts
RED   FAIL  ... > bounds retained astral input without reviving older users
      AssertionError: expected { type: 'message', role: 'user', …(1) } to match object { content: [ { …(2) } ] }
      Tests  1 failed | 13 passed (14); EXIT=1
GREEN Tests  14 passed (14); EXIT=0
GREEN Tests  14 passed (14); EXIT=0
```

Test-line budget: the regression folds into the existing case with zero net test-line growth (`203 → 203` lines), verified `Test lines OK: 6589535; ceiling: 6589535; slack: 0.` The shared scalar is untouched; no allocation record is needed. Frozen main and candidate each ran in separate processes; proof scripts and the scoped vitest config are local-only, not committed.

What was not tested: no live OpenAI/ChatGPT endpoint (no credentials); the scripted endpoint is loopback-local. We claim neither an HTTP 400 nor damaged JSON bytes — only ill-formed UTF-16 that survives the JSON round trip.

Open PR collision check: same-day changed-file lists for the latest 300 open PRs, a GraphQL sweep of the 100 most recently updated ones, and searches for `surrogate`/`utf16`/`compaction`/`truncation` found no open PR touching either changed file; the surrogate-family PRs (#195282, #194954, #194591, #175649, #1935xx) change other files.

prs.title: fix(android): recheck foreground state before returning pending WhileUsing location fix
prs.body:
## Summary

Recheck `!isForeground() && !allowsBackgroundLocation()` immediately after `disclosure.getLocation(...)` completes in `LocationHandler.handleLocationGet` (`apps/android/app/src/main/java/ai/openclaw/app/node/LocationHandler.kt`) and return `LOCATION_BACKGROUND_UNAVAILABLE` instead of disclosing coordinates if the app moved to the background while waiting for a fresh fix under `LocationMode.WhileUsing`.

Fixes #195648

## What Problem This Solves

In `LocationHandler.handleLocationGet`, foreground/background location eligibility (`!isForeground() && !allowsBackgroundLocation()`) was only checked before invoking `disclosure.getLocation(maxAgeMs, timeoutMs, ...)`. When a `location.get` request is admitted while the app is in the foreground under `LocationMode.WhileUsing` and waits for a fresh GPS fix, the user can background the app before the platform fix arrives. Once `disclosure.getLocation(...)` resolves, `handleLocationGet` previously constructed and returned the coordinate payload even though the app was now in the background without background location authorization.

Rechecking `!isForeground() && !allowsBackgroundLocation()` after `disclosure.getLocation(...)` ensures that coordinates resolved after the app leaves the foreground are rejected with `LOCATION_BACKGROUND_UNAVAILABLE` unless background location access (`LocationMode.Always` with background location enabled and granted) is active.

## Evidence

- Added Robolectric unit test suite `LocationForegroundTransitionTest` (`apps/android/app/src/test/java/ai/openclaw/app/node/LocationForegroundTransitionTest.kt`) verifying:
  - `whileUsingDoesNotDisclosePendingFixAfterAppBackgrounds`: starts `handleLocationGet` in the foreground under `LocationMode.WhileUsing` while waiting for a fresh GPS fix, transitions `isForeground` to `false` before the simulated GPS fix arrives, and asserts `result.ok == false`, `result.error?.code == "LOCATION_BACKGROUND_UNAVAILABLE"`, and `result.payloadJson == null`.
  - `pendingFixStillSucceedsWhenForegroundOrBackgroundAccessRemainsAllowed`: verifies that pending fixes still succeed when the app stays in the foreground under `WhileUsing` or backgrounds under `LocationMode.Always` with background location enabled.

prs.title: fix(android): retain gateway ownership across chat fork completion
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves
When a chat fork (`forkSession` or `forkSessionAtEntry`) is in flight across a Gateway switch, reconnect, or socket retirement:
1. `forkSession` previously checked the connection lease only when dispatching `sessions.create`, then unconditionally ran `fetchSessionsForCurrentWindow(archived = false)`, returned `createdKey` to callers that navigate the active chat view, and published errors via `updateErrorText(err.message)` without verifying that the originating connection lease and `requestCacheScope` were still current.
2. `forkSessionAtEntry` triggered `fetchSessionsForCurrentWindow()` when `!isCurrentSessionAction(snapshot)` even if `snapshot.gatewayScope != currentCacheScope()`, and `runOutboxSessionMutation` published `updateErrorText(err.message)` when `switchGeneration == null` even after `snapshot.gatewayScope` had been replaced.

This change binds `forkSession` and `forkSessionAtEntry` post-RPC roster refreshes, returned session navigation keys, and error banner updates to the originating Gateway lease and cache scope (`publishGatewayState` / `snapshot.gatewayScope == currentCacheScope()`).

## Evidence
- Added `ChatControllerForkGatewayTest` covering:
  - `forkResultRetainsGatewayOwnershipAcrossCreateAndRosterRefresh`: verifies `forkSession` across `sessions.create` and `sessions.list` suspend points under `None`, `Gateway`, `Reconnect`, and `Socket` retirements.
  - `forkFailureCannotReplaceAnErrorOwnedByTheReplacementGateway`: verifies failed `forkSession` calls cannot overwrite `_errorText` owned by a replacement Gateway or reconnected scope.
  - `forkAtEntryRetainsGatewayOwnershipForRosterRefreshAndErrors`: verifies `forkSessionAtEntry` does not trigger a roster refresh or overwrite `_errorText` after the Gateway scope changes.

Fixes #195646

## What Problem This Solves

Stopping gateway discovery on macOS or iOS can be followed by a late browser callback that changes “Stopped” back to “Searching…” or repopulates the cleared gateway list.

## User Impact

Stopped discovery stays stopped: callbacks from retired browsers no longer change the current discovery status or results. No configuration, connection-authority, or protocol changes.

This restores stricter callback handling deliberately removed in #170823 as a best-effort tradeoff. Native impact assessment and the discovery owner's decision on reversing that tradeoff remain necessary before landing; this PR does not claim that approval.

The existing shared browser-session owner invalidates its generation before cancelling browsers and drops state and result callbacks from earlier starts. The supplied branch is transplanted unchanged onto main at `8012956a65c37fc4cda5f56d73017a32bb105ef7`.

prs.title: improve(gateway): reduce shared-session Git authorization allocations
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Shared-session Git operations repeatedly allocate equivalent sharing targets and caller-policy projections during their live authority checks.

## User Impact

Lower main-thread allocation during repeated shared-session Git operations. Authorization behavior, runtime configuration, and database schemas are unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

Reuse unchanged published entry/member facts and their prepared mutation wrapper after validating the retained owner. Extend the existing audience snapshot to retain the caller projection under its consumption owner; compare live config/access/profile/policy/scope facts before reuse, and evaluate membership from the current consumption frame.

The final Git guard and generic source assertion composition remain intact. Nested assertion names represent distinct responsibilities, and synchronous callbacks can revoke authority between checks. This change reuses calculated facts, never a cached allow decision. Production delta is +41 lines: retaining prepared wrappers/projections and preserving nested membership restoration requires that growth. No additional global cache or scan is introduced.

## Evidence

Baseline: `df13b6b8994cefe16f311f29f0301bba511ec617`. Node 24.22.1; 1,000 synthetic profiles, 5,000 sessions, 32 retained member-authorized sessions interleaved serially. Five serial A/AA/B triplets per operation and mode. Authority samples measure 20,000 warmed checks; real-Git samples measure 320 commands in a 62,033-file / 1.116 GB workspace. Allocation and timing use separate processes; allocation sampling includes collected objects. Both checkouts use identical fixture-parent paths.

Cells contain medians and min–max ranges across five run means. The nearest-rank p95 across five means is the displayed maximum, **not per-command tail latency**. Paired changes include their full spread. Parent/main-thread CPU excludes native Git child CPU.

Another test covers interleaved consumers, nested membership restoration, mutable scopes, config publication, and profile revocation. - Focused test command completed in 136.78 s, including compilation. The new prepared-policy case took 439 ms; new Git cases took 147–798 ms. [Exact-head CI is green](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/42563947024) on `de1c52531ea677ac61285da43a91c0e0ec8d930e` after the connectionless-client correction (565 s). The +79-line test allocation is for those distinct security contracts.
- `pnpm check:changed` completed. Three introduced issues were fixed and their assertion-safety, database-worker, and scripts typecheck gates reran green. Core/test typechecks, lint, formatting, dead-export checks, and remaining gates passed. The sole unresolved gate is the inherited changelog attribution failure below.
- Codex autoreview, P0–P2, runtime candidate against the pinned base: scoped-clean, no findings. Supplied unchanged authority owners were included as review context. No directly importing Control UI module was found for the changed Gateway modules.

CI found and this PR fixed an introduced regression: eager scope snapshot access crashed for supported internal/plugin callers without a connect handshake. The existing Talk test reproduced the failure locally; the owner now uses the same connectionless/non-admin contract as `isGatewayAdmin`. All 71 tests in the three affected Talk files pass (285.13 s including compilation), and a fresh Codex P0–P2 review of the correction is scoped-clean. No fixtures or permission defaults were changed.

Exact warmed work counts per command: `prepareSessionSharing` 1 -> 0; `prepareProjectedSessionSharing` 1 -> 1; database path identity inspection 1 -> 1; profile-authority closure reads 4 -> 4. These counts use the corrected candidate.

Introducing commit `266a7aa0fe69e2b5fe6445c4ceb1e15b5360c957` ([#194364](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/194364)) expanded forbidden handles without updating archived entries, all present at its parent. The synthetic database contains metadata (4.8 MB plus 5.3 MB WAL), not a multi-gigabyte transcript corpus; local measurements use APFS, not btrfs. Parent/main-thread CPU excludes Git child CPU. prs.title: fix(android): scope automations selectedJobId state to activeGatewayStableId
prs.body:
## Summary

Key `selectedJobId`'s `rememberSaveable` state by `activeGatewayStableId` in `CronJobsSettingsScreen` (`apps/android/app/src/main/java/ai/openclaw/app/ui/SettingsScreens.kt`) so switching the active gateway while the Automations settings route remains mounted retires the previous gateway's open job detail and unsent draft, while preserving them across same-gateway transport reconnects.

Fixes #195647

## What Problem This Solves

In `CronJobsSettingsScreen`, `selectedJobId` was stored in `rememberSaveable { mutableStateOf<String?>(null) }` without keying on `activeGatewayStableId`. When a user opened or edited an automation job on Gateway A and switched the active gateway to Gateway B while `CronJobsSettingsScreen` stayed mounted, Gateway A's `selectedJobId` remained non-null (`selectedJobId != null`), keeping `CronJobDetailSettingsScreen` mounted and causing its `LaunchedEffect(jobId, isConnected, operatorAdminScopeAvailable)` to automatically request Gateway A's job ID from Gateway B and retain Gateway A's unsent draft.

Scoping `selectedJobId` with `key(activeGatewayStableId)` ties the open automation selection to the active gateway identity: a transport reconnect on the same gateway preserves the open job detail and unsent draft, whereas switching to a different gateway resets `selectedJobId` to `null` and unmounts `CronJobDetailSettingsScreen` (which disposes the previous gateway's draft via `DisposableEffect(jobId)`).

## Evidence

- Added Compose/Robolectric test `CronJobsGatewayOwnerTest` (`apps/android/app/src/test/java/ai/openclaw/app/ui/CronJobsGatewayOwnerTest.kt`) verifying:
  - Reconnecting to the same gateway preserves the open automation detail view and unsent editor draft (`"Unsent original edit"`).
  - Switching `activeGatewayStableId` from the original gateway to a replacement gateway while `SettingsDetailScreen(..., SettingsRoute.CronJobs)` stays mounted returns to the automations list (`"Search automations"`), clears `cronEditorDraftMemory` for the job ID, and makes no automatic `cron.get` detail request against the replacement gateway until the user explicitly selects a job on the replacement gateway.
