## What Problem This Solves

Fixes the SQLite source-revision worker pulling config and plugin code into its standalone build after snapshot cleanup gained logging.

## User Impact

Restores the small worker’s existing dependency boundary. Snapshot cleanup and NFS deferral behavior remain unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

Move publication-directory cleanup out of the file hashing module and import it only from the snapshot publication owner. The moved function is byte-for-byte identical; the old export is removed and every caller uses the new module. The native PR wrapper inventory includes the module so extracted wrappers retain the same runtime imports.

## Evidence

- Baseline failure: [scheduled main CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/42562039354/job/128980612485).
- Reproduced the existing esbuild graph assertion on the base: 128 inputs, including eight forbidden config/plugin modules. On this commit: 10 inputs and none forbidden. All 31 standalone worker graph assertions pass using the pinned esbuild 0.28.2.
- Formatting, commit-hook checks, and whitespace checks passed. Existing graph assertions and snapshot transfer tests are preserved.
- [Exact-source CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/42563654540) targets the source extraction at `8b31bef956596331932fedf1a0fd2735263270ef`. The final head adds only the missing wrapper inventory entry; its closure checks remain pending.
- [CI runtime build-graph tests passed](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/42563654540/job/128985719565): 33 tests in 6.633 seconds, including the SQLite source-worker assertion in 13 milliseconds. The job has separate failures.
- Full workspace dependencies are unqualified locally. Typechecking, full build, and the snapshot transfer tests remain pending CI. Final committed-range review found no actionable defects, including in the inventory correction.

The initial CI run exposed the omitted inventory entry in [wrapper closure tests](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/42563654540/job/128985719491); it also reproduces the separate [Discord declaration failure](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/195694).

prs.title: fix(knowledge): distinguish same-name transcript authors
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes readable chat transcripts assigning the same author label to different people who share a display name and the final four digits of their IDs. Their messages, reply targets and mentions all become indistinguishable, such as two different authors both rendered as `Sam#1234`.

## User Impact

Same-name authors use their complete IDs for disambiguation throughout the transcript and chunk metadata. Unique display names retain their existing output. Labels for same-name authors become longer; the existing byte-budget packer accounts for them.

## Why This Change Was Made

Stop truncating the ID in the existing author-label owner. Every renderer already consumes that map, so this one-line change covers messages, headers, replies, mentions and metadata together.

Related: #194640, a transcript output-boundary fix from an external contributor merged by obviyus on November 7. Bounded searches found no matching open fix for this author-ID suffix collision.

## Evidence

### Conflict resolution against current main

Rebased onto `1bf2a85e6ab5918472f7df1b8cf2cb0c9f056a2e`; candidate `b7bdc9e974c39da602af9a5b1e08df613736797f`. The overlapping transcript fixture now preserves both this full-author-ID regression and #195126’s deleted-reply behavior. Both normal and deleted cases assert distinct message/reply/mention/thread author labels; the deleted reply preview remains `[deleted]`.

- Current-candidate validation passed in an offline, secretless container capped at 512 MiB / 0.5 CPU: actual regression file **2 tests passed**, focused strict TypeScript, real CLI collision/control **2/2**, multipart replay, Node parse, Oxfmt, 72-rule Oxlint and diff check. The focused Vitest harness retains the unchanged temporary-directory lifecycle and real temp helper while omitting unrelated vault infrastructure; hosted CI remains the broader integration check. No full local suite was run.
- Native staged test-line ratchet passed against the full candidate tree: **6,578,744 / 6,578,744** lines. The existing 4-line regression allocation remains unchanged; no shared ceiling increase.
- Fresh independent read-only agent review of the complete current base/head diff: no actionable findings. This is an independent agent review, not an autoreview or ClawSweeper run.
- Current-head [hosted CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/42486648609) **passed**, including baseline ratchets, production/test types and lint. The [actual owner-test job](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/42486648609/job/128750193841) passed both `exports chat chunks (deleted=false)` (**59 ms**) and `exports chat chunks (deleted=true)` (**17 ms**), **46.17 s** including setup/transform. Earlier CI below applies only to its explicitly stated historical head.

The original before/after evidence below is historical; the new replay checks the rebased candidate.


- **Real CLI before/after:** Node 24.22.2 in non-root, offline, secretless Docker, limited to 256 MiB and 0.5 CPU. The actual `chat-transcript.mjs` command reads synthetic normalized chat JSONL and writes transcript, raw rows and chunk metadata; no mocked renderer or helper substitutes for the CLI.
- **Before:** IDs `111111111111111234` and `222222222222221234`, both named Sam, become `Sam#1234`. The generated transcript makes a reply look like the same author talking to themselves and both mentions resolve to the same text. CLI exits successfully, but the independent output assertions fail.
- **After:** distinct full-ID labels appear in all these output positions. The unique-name control has a byte-identical transcript hash before/after. Raw rows and input bytes are preserved in both cases.
- **Longer-label budget check:** also replayed the updated committed multi-day/thread fixture through the real CLI. Its six messages still produce three chunks (179, 830 and 463 bytes), all within the 1,000-byte budget, with the expected cross-day reply, mention and thread labels. This standalone fixture replay is separate from Vitest.
- Node syntax, Oxfmt, focused native Oxlint (72 rules, zero findings) and `git diff --check` pass. Combined exact-head primary CLI/format/lint wall time: **3.980 seconds**. Prior-head (`d0c697c0c71354a7753a2f8435c50138822bf26d`) hosted CI passed the actual `chat-transcript.test.ts` regression (**1 test, 58 ms**; **45.65 s** including transform/setup), full lint and type checks. See the [owner test job](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/42453070079/job/128646562974).
- Simplification: **production +1/-1**. The existing end-to-end regression now gives the two authors the same name and colliding ID suffixes and asserts their correct labels; no new test setup. Formatting expands the test by **4 net lines**, covered by a separate 4-line allocation; the shared scalar is unchanged.
- Independent read-only agent review of base `04d0d241c166e706664123f28104d3e43cce2fd3` through head `d0c697c0c71354a7753a2f8435c50138822bf26d`, complete diff, label consumers, regression fixture and actual receipts: no actionable P0–P2 findings. This was a separate agent review, not an autoreview or ClawSweeper run; the corresponding hosted test/lint/type checks have since passed.

The proof covers standalone transcript generation on synthetic exports, not live Discord acquisition or a Gateway/model session. This targets suffix collisions among authors sharing a display name; it does not introduce a global escaping scheme for arbitrary display-name text.

### Recorded direct-CLI receipts

These machine-produced records were checked against the source bytes at the stated commits. They contain only synthetic names/IDs/content and no credentials or private paths.

Fixes #195539

## What Problem This Solves

<!--
Describe the concrete user, product, or operational problem.
Use one short, plain-language sentence. For fixes, prefer:
"Fixes: <what goes wrong> when <trigger or condition>."
For other changes, describe the need without inventing a bug.
Name the affected workflow, not the code-level cause.
-->

Fixes: node binary checks return an unusable path when an earlier PATH entry contains a directory or non-executable file, and miss Windows names that already include an executable extension.

## User Impact

<!--
"User impact: <what users, operators, or developers can now do or expect>."
Lead with the concrete outcome in plain language, usually one sentence.
For internal-only changes, say there is no user-visible change; do not invent a benefit.
Keep important risks, breaking changes, migrations, and required user actions visible here.
-->

User impact: `system.which` skips unusable PATH shadows and finds explicit Windows executable names while retaining fresh node-local results and the existing response format. No configuration changes or migrations are required.

This is a draft: runtime and native Windows verification are still pending.

## Why This Change Was Made

<!--
Briefly explain how the change addresses the problem without repeating the impact.
Keep the body short. Leave file lists, internal acronyms, and root-cause walkthroughs
in the diff or optional <details>; include technical detail only when it explains
behavior or a material tradeoff. Do not hide risks or required actions in <details>.
-->

Reuse `isExecutableFile` from the shared executable-path owner for regular-file and POSIX execute-permission checks. Try an explicit PATHEXT suffix as written before suffix expansion.

The node-specific probing loop remains deliberately: the full shared PATH resolver treats dotted basenames and empty PATHEXT entries differently. This preserves node input filtering, PATH fallback, suffix probing, and uncached results without redesigning lookup semantics. The source patch’s duplicate executable validator was removed; the final production delta is +24/-16 lines and the regression-test delta is +65/-0 lines.

## Evidence

Summarize what was checked and the result; note meaningful gaps. Link long output
or put it in optional <details>, keeping the useful evidence summary visible.

- Added two `handleInvoke` regressions covering directory/non-executable shadows, symlinks, filtered input, fresh installs/removals, explicit Windows suffixes, dotted basenames, and the existing bare-file policy. These tests have not been executed.
- **Passed:** focused oxfmt check; supported syntax-only boundary lint on both changed TypeScript files; `git diff --check`; test-line ratchet against the exact prepared base (`--no-merge-base`): 6,592,088 lines, equal to the ceiling. The separate 65-line allocation covers exactly these regressions; the shared scalar is unchanged.

prs.title: fix(plugins): keep repeat updates with current artifacts a no-op
prs.body:
Related: #195653

## What Problem This Solves

A repeat `openclaw update` unnecessarily reinstalls current ClawHub artifacts and reports “plugins updated.” Skipping that installation must still preserve manifest repair and capability-consent review.

## User Impact

Healthy, accepted artifacts produce a clean no-op. Missing/invalid required manifests and stale/missing acceptance follow the ordinary reinstall/review path. Actual installs, host repairs, and record rewrites continue counting as changes.

## Why This Change Was Made

ClawHub retention requires matching source/artifact identity, present runnable entrypoints, healthy host links, and the consent owner's fresh inspection of valid package manifests and current capability coverage. The consent owner preserves its existing official and disabled-update exemptions. Failed retention checks fall through to the existing staged installer and consent handler; acceptance is persisted after review, and refusal is reported normally.

Artifact identity contracts now live with their owner, removing the helper-to-installer import cycle. The added assertions were removed using the real record/union contracts. No config/schema/dependency/release changes.

## Evidence

- `update-noop.test.ts` now exercises the real updater, ClawHub installer, archive installation, and consent owner using synthetic registry/archive I/O. Cases cover healthy no-op, one npm record rewrite, stale/missing acceptance, declined consent, missing/invalid plugin manifests, changed digest, and missing entrypoint. Successful repairs assert usable manifests and persisted current acceptance. The old contract-incomplete installer stub and duplicate ClawHub table are removed.
- Serial named local test attempts (`update-noop.test.ts`, `clawhub.test.ts`) were stopped at cold worker compilation as required on the production host. No local runtime pass or baseline red/green result is claimed; PR CI owns that proof and test timing.
- Touched-file tsgo, oxlint, oxfmt, whitespace checks, and commit-hook ratchets passed. Exactly 51 net repair test lines are allocated separately; PV's 127 + PV2's 51 = 178 final net test lines. Shared scalar unchanged.
- Fresh final local Codex autoreview, P0–P2, base `e08aa74ea39e35d01ba8e8f84e317747aba1bf3f` through the staged snapshot committed as `2edfa6636fd02434644dcbd07827ff0860bd909f`: `scoped-clean`, no actionable findings. Static scoped assessment; runtime/complete graph proof remains CI-owned.

### Prior-head CI attribution

All four failed jobs and the separate failed commit status were inspected through the API. These are the five failing entries, rather than five distinct failed jobs:

| Entry | Cause and action |
| --- | --- |
| [check-guards-architecture](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/42563087163/job/128984097873) | PR-caused helper/installer all-import cycle. Removed the back-reference and placed shared contracts with the artifact owner. |
| [checks-fast-baseline-ratchets](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/42563087163/job/128984097877) | PR-caused two uncommented assertions. Removed both; no baseline exception. |
| [checks-node-changed-compact-large-4-3](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/42563087163/job/128984098173) | Main-owned source-capture import/GC caller-retention failure on Node 24.22.1. Its test is unchanged; a static traversal of 183 value-import/reexport modules rooted at capture-directory and scheduler reaches no changed PR file. Bare/dynamic imports were not expanded. No matching scheduled-main job exists, so identical baseline runtime failure is unproven. No unrelated source/test change or retry masks it. |
| [openclaw/ci-gate check](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/42563087163/job/128986448232) | Rollup of those three failed jobs. |
| [openclaw/ci-gate commit status](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/42564026955) | Security-review policy correctly propagates failed CI; its review job itself succeeded. |

The new head requires fresh CI; prior-head results are attribution evidence only. No merge.

prs.title: improve(workers): reuse verified prepared snapshots and worker code
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fresh cloud sessions repeat completed snapshot setup and worker-code extraction instead of reusing verified prepared content.

## User Impact

Fresh, unpinned default-branch sessions can reuse a compatible completed snapshot only when its revision belongs to the admitted default-branch history. Explicit refs and existing pinned sessions retain exact-source preparation. Seed-only requests still prepare the requested revision without running an unauthorized setup recipe. The actual completed base reaches preparation, inspection and binding; current repository access remains required.

Verified worker packages are reused through exact aliases; damaged or missing code falls back to verified archive installation. Legacy peers retain registration-time verification. Only negotiated peers defer content verification to first binding, with the full verification timeout; exact binding replay preserves private edits.

**Status:** signed corrections are now published for **proof**, not landing. AUTH-2, UPGRADE-3 and dependency #193873 remain open. GitHub currently reports merge conflicts; the new head has not completed broad CI qualification. No server deployment, ready transition or merge was performed.

**Landing dependency:** older-snapshot behavior requires [managed publication recovery #193873](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/193873). Publication is not dependency acceptance. Capture normalization and diagnostics are separately covered by #193776.

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing admission, prepared-workspace and installer owners serve the flow. The correction preserves actual-base propagation, main's preparation callback, hash memoization, capture verification, diagnostics and timing coverage. Strict requests exclude receipt-only fields. A negotiated capability preserves old/new verification-stage compatibility without a protocol-version bump.

The admitted repository/account owner checks snapshot ancestry. Missing or oversized comparison responses decline optional reuse only after repository/account revalidation; authentication, revocation, cancellation and transport failures still fail closed. The metadata size limit is unchanged.

Original PR and contribution: @galiniliev. Automated actual-base repair and qualification: @roboclaw-bot.

## Work sessions

- [Original discussion with @galiniliev](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/dashboard/1f24e3f3-e7d6-4966-b666-e5868987619d)
- [Implementation and verification](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/subagent/70153122-6ab4-4eea-96e9-a8b689da6467)
- [Implementation and verification — first-bind and seed-only regressions](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/subagent/649d3ef7-7e03-41fc-b728-f1e3cc134da1)
- [Implementation and verification — mixed peers and snapshot lineage](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/subagent/acd66058-9c68-4d20-bd3e-3bb4b94b466b)
- [Implementation and verification — comparison fallback boundaries](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/subagent/b0bc6b4e-8b23-422c-85ab-e11a9c70d9f7)

## Evidence

### Published identity and scope

- **Head:** `60f2916cfa679b55b25313d55f0fc5b8e676496d`; **tree:** `413b4fa30707ba457f030cf94c0c32cff765c9f6`.
- Native `prepare-publish-for-proof` fast-forwarded `e45cfac4d439cec7ef2e75542fa5967fa9643849` to this exact candidate. Receipt: `PUSH_PURPOSE=proof`, `PUSH_REPLACED_HOSTED_ANCESTRY=false`, pending findings `AUTH-2,UPGRADE-3`.
- Remote readback matched the full tree and all **33 changed blobs**. All four new commit signatures, parent links and Galin co-author trailers were verified. Prior hosted ancestry and both earlier signed main merges remain intact.
- This publication contains the strict registration fix, unique receipt-helper export, measured per-PR test allowances, first-bind/memo/replay regressions, mixed-peer negotiation, seed-only handling and admitted snapshot-lineage checks. Global test baselines were not raised.

### Source-pinned local proof

These results belong to their stated executing sources; they are not summed into a fictitious final-head suite.

| Source | Completed proof |
| --- | --- |
| `32b13317…` | Original **93-test** correction proof retained with its immutable source bundle. |
| `adbf95d3…` | **175** owner/direct-consumer tests, including the original 93 and three new cases; **321** test-routing checks. Types, lint, formatting and safety/growth guards passed. |
| `50ae028d…` | **238** owner/direct-consumer cases plus **17** native transport/startup cases on supported Node 26: **255 distinct passes**. Legacy cross-process proof measured five cold registration reads, zero first-bind reads and zero private-edit replay reads. Types, native lint, formatting and ratchets passed. |
| **`60f2916c…`** | **119** owner/read-consumer cases plus **4** exact-revision fallback caller cases: **123 distinct passes**. Final **82-case** owner replay passed and is not double-counted. Core/scoped test types, six-file lint/formatting, max-lines, test-lines and diff checks passed. No new allowance was added for this final correction. |

Pre-fix runs reproduced the first-bind timeout and seed-only rejection, legacy verification-stage incompatibility, topic-only snapshot retention, and unavailable/oversized comparison failures. The fixes preserve fail-closed identity/repository changes and strict wire rejection of unknown fields.

**Recorded runtime limitation:** the `50ae028d…` pinned-Bun startup replay had one fixture `spawnSync sh ETIMEDOUT` before the fence assertion. That case and the complete 17-case suite passed on Node; this does **not** establish a Bun timeout repair.

### Independent source review

The whole incoming branch from `abe11702825e31e250244fd2ea1f0abd22dc0c24` through `50ae028d…` completed **27/27** canonical P0–P3 review passes with **206 complete owner bodies in every pass** and six preserved composition datasets. Its complete **FINDINGS** report identified the two comparison fallback defects.

The exact final `60f2916c…` correction then received a focused independent canonical P0–P3 review: **scoped-clean, zero findings**. This is composite source-pinned review evidence, not a relabeling of the earlier whole-source report or a claim of installed production acceptance. Historical composition views are not combined execution proof. The reviewer model remained `openai/gpt-6.1-sol`, high thinking, tools off.

### Hosted CI

The earlier [CI run 42233989169](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/42233989169) failed for `e45cfac…` while executing merge `8ec803862669addf1279d0b98dda2d7a2c011b1c`: **103 pass, 43 skipped and 6 failed contexts**. Its owned export, allocation, memo/startup and strict-registration defects are addressed by this correction; that old run is not relabeled green.

Initial checks on `60f2916c…` showed **7 success and 4 skipped**, with no failing or pending checks in that observation. Only automation/context/security workflows were attached; **no broad CI workflow run was present for this head**, and GitHub reported a merge-conflicting state. These checks are not full qualification.

### Important proof gaps

prs.title: fix(discord): preserve literal mentions inside code #195585
prs.body:
Closes #195585

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: Discord rewrites native mention tokens (`<@id>` / `<@!id>`) inside inline and fenced code when the same user is also mentioned in prose, so the agent receives code that differs from what the sender typed.

## User Impact

User impact: people can paste code samples containing mention-shaped literals and the agent now receives the original bytes, while ordinary prose mentions still render as `@name`. There is no configuration change and no behavior change outside Markdown code ranges.

## Why This Change Was Made

`resolveDiscordMessageText` owns the model-facing text projection, but its mention rewrite scanned the whole message as flat text. Discord ingress already has a Markdown code-range owner (`findCodeRegions` via `openclaw/plugin-sdk/text-chunking`) used by mention activation. This change partitions the original text once, rewrites mentions only in prose ranges, and copies code ranges verbatim. It preserves the earlier literal-label fix (#130778, callback replacement and id fallback) and adds no parser, configuration, or SDK surface.

Scope note: escaped prose mentions (`\<@id>`) and forwarded-snapshot text are outside this issue and are unchanged.

## Evidence

**Validation status:** the production fix and both regression cases pass locally. Extension tests, the Discord extension lane, formatting, targeted lint, and the test-line ratchet pass. Type checking and Discord E2E were not run on this host and are deferred to PR CI; no typecheck or E2E pass is claimed.

### Red (base, before the fix)

- Restored only `message-text.ts` to the base blob `2b91cc660932459853a4ee3d62aa64a0db34408f`, keeping the new tests.
- Command: `pnpm test extensions/discord/src/monitor/message-text.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`
- Result: `Tests 2 failed | 10 passed (12)`. Both new cases fail because code tokens are rewritten, for example `const user = '@a$...';` instead of `const user = '<@!1>';`.
- Duration: 166.67s (transform-dominated cold run); shard 174.05s.

### Green (with the fix)

- Same command: `Tests 12 passed (12)`.
- New cases pass: `resolves mentions with literal inline code`, `resolves mentions with literal fenced code`.
- Duration: 32.51s; shard 39.49s.

### Consumer suites

- Command: `pnpm test extensions/discord/src/monitor/message-text.test.ts extensions/discord/src/monitor/message-handler.preflight.test.ts extensions/discord/src/monitor/message-handler.process.ack.test.ts extensions/discord/src/monitor/message-handler.context.test.ts extensions/discord/src/monitor/message-handler.context-history.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`
- Result: 5 files passed; `97 passed` in the extension shard and `13 passed` in `extension-database-workers`; exit 0.
- Duration: 81.36s and 76.77s; shard total 167.56s.

## What Problem This Solves

`openclaw templates add @openclaw/api-integration-engineer` currently treats the package name as a local path and fails instead of acquiring the published Template.

## User Impact

Users with Templates Labs enabled can Add an ordinary agent directly from a ClawHub package name, or preview it with `--dry-run`. Local directories and `CLAW.md` sources still work. Existing agent IDs and workspaces are not overwritten. Trust acknowledgments, plugin capabilities, and dependency installation consent remain separate requirements. No managed-Template update/remove lifecycle or retained source cache is introduced.

## Why This Change Was Made

Reuse the existing ClawHub resolver to select an exact published version, verify package identity and SHA-256, and safely extract it for the existing stateless Add operation. Preview uses the existing artifact-preserving inspection scope so stored plugin metadata remains readable without changing operator state; actual Add retains mutation ownership. Temporary-source cleanup does not replace an already-reported Add outcome.

## Evidence

- Public CLI reproduction failed on the base with `read_failed`; registry acquisition regressions pass with this change. Identity, family, digest, exact-version, trust, partial-outcome, and cleanup boundaries are covered.
- Live isolated command: `pnpm openclaw --profile template-cli-proof-20261108 templates add @openclaw/api-integration-engineer --dry-run --json`. Verified published `0.1.2`, SHA-256 `2ca03dddf4729c808acbabe22d2dff5a1f43b2489fa5787abd4bf502630520a7`, 154855 bytes; exit 0, no blockers, no product config/state changes. Repeated after the preview repair.
- Live Add using the same package with explicit `--agent-id registry-cli-proof --workspace <isolated-workspace> --json` completed with nine workspace files. Repeating it rejected the collision; workspace and config bytes remained unchanged, with no retained Template source cache.
- Populated-state/custom-provider real-CLI preview regression: red on `8e3d69239419`, green after the inspection-scope repair; full isolated tree bytes unchanged.
- Final affected suites: 53 tests passed (CLI, process-state, MCP config, command-path policy), 57 seconds overall. Changed CLI tests took under 0.5 seconds of test time; process-state suite took about 5 seconds and exercises ownership/SQLite artifacts through subprocesses rather than mocked admission. Earlier startup, resolver, Gateway Add, and state-owner suites also passed.
- Running-owner ownership regression: reproduced the stale refusal expectation on `f28f546ff584`; updated it to prove successful state-preserving preview and continued refusal of actual Add. The focused test passed in 0.12 seconds (15 seconds wrapper wall time).
- Canonical `pnpm tsgo:core`, config/CLI test typecheck, focused type-aware lint, formatting, docs links, whitespace, and test-line ratchet passed. The initial broad TypeScript invocation selected unrelated UI/declaration diagnostics; canonical targeted checks are green. Source CLI runtime build completed during the live proof; full declaration/package build and broad/platform CI remain for PR CI.
- Independent read-only review: initial observation-forwarding finding fixed; repair follow-up found no actionable issues. Local ClawSweeper reviewed base `594190c75e5d` to `8e3d69239419`, identified the now-fixed preview-admission issue; repair review covered `8e3d69239419..f28f546ff584` and confirmed the inspection owner but caught the stale ownership-test expectation. That finding is resolved in `64f30dc6a1c3` with the focused red/green proof above; no new production changes followed the review. Both local reviews completed at high confidence; no hosted review or GitHub mutation was performed by the reviewer.

Simplification: shared acquisition and stateless Add remain the sole owners; no additional downloader, cache, schema, or lifecycle was added. Most runtime diff churn is extraction/reindentation around the existing Add flow. Growth is needed for registry acquisition and nonmutating preview. Production TypeScript grows by 100 net lines, while tests grow by 229 net lines against the merge base. Exactly 229 net regression-test lines are allocated for acquisition/trust failures and real-CLI state preservation; the shared baseline is unchanged. CI seconds are not yet available.

prs.title: feat: let sandboxed plugin tabs invoke declared session actions
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Plugin tabs need narrowly authorized session actions without receiving Gateway credentials or a general-purpose parent HTTP proxy. This replaces #80388 and builds on #107323.

## User Impact

Plugins can expose declared actions for the parent-selected session. Revoking device authority or session access while an action waits now prevents the action from running. Failed action-enabled pages show a sanitized explanation and Retry, which obtains a fresh grant before reloading.

Existing canonical session navigation and the direct iframe flow for tabs without actions are preserved. The unused `allowChatNavigation` schema field is removed; no second public navigation API is introduced.

## Why This Change Was Made

The bridge keeps authorization in the existing Gateway dispatcher, registered action scopes, trusted session context, persisted access checks, and payload/result schemas. Sandboxed pages receive neither bearer tokens nor mutation cookies.

This refresh addresses the [latest review](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/110102#issuecomment-5005741905): recheck both authorities synchronously immediately before invoking the plugin handler, provide recoverable page errors, remove the obsolete schema field, and repair the reported lint errors. Earlier navigation and causal MessagePort test fixes are retained; branch history is preserved.

## Evidence

Validated source: [`edbac97f93bc`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/110102/commits/edbac97f93bc6fc633779cdee607b081abc0063c).

- **Gateway: 6 tests pass.** The real dispatcher, persisted session authority, and row-preparation boundary are exercised. Current authority permits one action effect; revoking the device or removing session membership while preparation is held returns `UNAVAILABLE` with **zero effects**.
- **Plugin UI: 51 tests pass** across document, page, and bridge suites. New cases cover an HTTP failure followed by Retry with a fresh grant, policy-error reporting, and redaction of a redirect error's private URL/token.
- **Regression sensitivity demonstrated:** keeping the new tests but restoring affected production files from `82f71f3` makes both authorization-revocation cases and all three new error/retry cases fail. The current-authority control still passes. Restoring the repaired files produces the passing results above.
- **Independent review:** no actionable high/medium-priority findings in the 11-file refresh.
- **Static checks pass:** changed-file formatting, type-aware oxlint, UI stylelint, UI i18n catalog validation, and `git diff --check`. The PR context/evidence policy also accepts this description locally.

**Remaining verification gaps (not waived):**

- **Browser/screenshots/end-to-end evidence is blocked.** Chromium crashes with `SIGTRAP` before loading the isolated fixture; a minimal launch without PR code reproduces the crash, including with `--no-sandbox`. The installed stock Firefox ESR also exits before Playwright can connect; no Playwright-patched Firefox is installed. No current-head browser assertions, network captures, or before/after screenshots were produced. Historical captures are not presented as current proof. Full Gateway startup, authenticated WebSocket flow, production cookies, plugin discovery, and deployment remain unverified. The retained navigation tests pass in the focused UI suite, but their separate base-fail replay has not been recorded.
- The broader changed-file check stops at the line-cap ratchet because this host's Git 2.34.1 does not support `git cat-file --batch -z`. Its preceding conflict-marker check passes; later gates and broader type checks are not claimed as passing.
- Replaying the two previously failing chat-test files yields 8 passing assertions but an unhandled Lit `ChildPart has no parentNode` exception in `chat-message.mcp-app.test.ts`. The run therefore fails. Those files are unchanged, but that alone does **not** establish that the failure is unrelated to this PR; causality remains unresolved.
- New-head hosted CI has not yet been validated. Maintainer review and the screenshot requirement remain outstanding.

<details>
<summary>Reproduction commands and local test cost</summary>

```sh
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/gateway/server-methods/plugin-host-hooks.registry.test.ts --maxWorkers=1
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs ui/src/pages/plugin/plugin-ui-document.test.ts ui/src/pages/plugin/plugin-page.test.tsx ui/src/pages/plugin/plugin-ui-bridge.test.ts --maxWorkers=1
```

On an isolated service capped at 50% CPU and 6 GiB RAM, final command wall times were 558.46 s and 64.49 s respectively (Vitest-reported durations: 492.82s and 45.86s). The persisted-authority scenarios exercise the real persistence/projection/dispatcher boundary with a causal preparation barrier, not sleeps or a mocked authority decision. CI seconds are not yet measured; these resource-capped local times are not CI estimates.

The old-source regression runs failed as expected in 866.35 s (authorization) and 51.30 s (page errors/retry). Production files were restored and their checksums verified afterward.

All verification used a separate checkout and private test state/config under resource limits. The live Gateway was not restarted, reconfigured, deployed to, or used as a test target.

</details>

## Remaining Maintainer Decision

The public `sessionActions` bridge still needs maintainer sponsorship and a long-term owner. This is an updated review candidate, not a merge request or a waiver of exact-head CI, screenshots, or owner review.

prs.title: fix(sandbox): preserve prepared templates across Gateway shutdown
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Graceful Gateway shutdown during idle sandbox-template validation marks an otherwise usable template unfinished. Restarted turns then reinstall dependencies for the same source commit. An interrupted incremental refresh also changes the previously published generation before replacement preparation succeeds.

## User Impact

Matching resumed sessions keep using the last-good prepared template after interruption. Source changes still require their own dependency installation, shared by callers requesting those inputs. No configuration or database schema change is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

Idle validation now leaves publication intact. Replacement builds and incremental refreshes use a separate generation; the existing database worker publishes it and retires the previous selection in one transaction. Incremental refresh still applies the source delta and reinstalls into cloned dependencies. Source and destination readers retain custody through uncertain native outcomes.

Source-worktree refresh gives the staged clone independent Git registration and index state. Collection removes its private directory before retiring that path's Git registration, including when an interrupted clone still contains the old generation's Git link. Unknown validation outcomes retain the existing quarantine contract.

Production growth is **101 lines**: independent staged Git metadata and atomic publication replace in-place mutation. No additional cache, admission setting, or scan is introduced. The real lifecycle workload is committed and documented. Measurement tooling from #195655 is included; this PR includes that measurement-only proposal. Related: #195443.

## Evidence

**Ready for code review. Production-shaped performance qualification is running; the acceptance results and exact-head CI outcome will be added before closeout.**

- Regression tests fail before the fix: settled validation/replacement abort loses the ready generation; source refresh mutates the old HEAD/index/files; an interrupted copied Git backlink prevents subsequent collection. The fix passes 64 owner/source tests, including native APFS, plus 14 sandbox-template tests.
- Real Gateway CLI, native Git, real dependency installation, WebSocket-accepted turns, supported restart intent and SIGTERM: both baseline and candidate exit with code 0 and no terminating signal. Accepted turns resume automatically without resending. In the two-session same-input reproduction, baseline changes ready to preparing and performs one additional install; candidate preserves the same ready generation and performs zero.
- The separate mid-install reproduction preserves the old generation's source hashes on the candidate. Its new pinned source legitimately needs one install after restart. The baseline performs two: startup prewarming requests the old remote default, then resumed turns request the new pinned commit. Those are different input identities, not duplicate same-input waiter work.
- Fresh independent Codex autoreview is scoped-clean through P2. Runtime builds, types, lint, formatting, import boundaries, database-worker and schema guards pass. `pnpm check:changed --base df13b6b8994cefe16f311f29f0301bba511ec617` fails only on the 20 historical changelog-credit entries reproduced on that exact main base. This is the unresolved main regression introduced by commit `266a7aa0fe69` / #194364, not a passing check or ignored noise.

Acceptance declared before the scale series: use a synthetic 62,000-file / 1.1 GB workspace, approximately 35 GiB agent database and 5,000 sessions; two A/A controls followed by five interleaved baseline/candidate drain pairs, with 20 accepted resumed turns. Candidate must keep the last-good generation, perform zero same-input reinstalls, and reach p50/max first-provider readiness below 60 seconds. Report total recovery including successor startup separately from preparation after Gateway readiness, process CPU, cumulative main-thread allocation, sample spread and actual fixture sizes. The full-size fixture uses APFS; a separate real btrfs/Podman qualification is being prepared, with its database-size limitation kept explicit.

No deployment, production access, or merge is performed by this PR.

prs.title: fix(cron): a job targeting another agent's session never runs
prs.body:
> **AI-assisted: yes**

Closes #190123

## What Problem This Solves

- Fixes an issue where a user on a multi-agent gateway who scheduled work into another agent's
  conversation with `openclaw cron add --session session:agent:<other>:…` and no `--agent` got a job
  that could never run. The create was admitted for one agent while the job's own session belonged
  to another, so the due run failed in milliseconds (`cron job agent is unavailable: worker`, or on
  the reporter's install `SQLite session store path belongs to agent main; requested agent worker.`)
  and the one-shot (`at`) job was then auto-disabled as a permanent error: the payload never ran and
  nothing told the creator why. On today's `main` the same command in a two-agent roster does not
  even reach that point — it is refused with `invalid cron.add params: Multiple agents are
  configured, but this operation has no explicit owner.` Either way the scheduled work is silently
  lost.
- The CLI made this worse by naming the wrong owner: it printed `No --agent specified; the job will
  run with the configured default agent.` for a job whose session already named one.
- **Related:** #190123 (reporter's source trace names the create default and the owner resolver);
  #190156 (earlier attempt at this report, withdrawn by its author before merge — it changed the
  global owner-resolution precedence and left the due-run leg on `job.agentId` untouched). This PR
  takes the narrower route: name the execution agent once at `cron.add` admission, and leave global
  attribution precedence alone. Fix signal labels: `clawsweeper:queueable-fix`,
  `clawsweeper:fix-shape-clear`, `clawsweeper:source-repro`.

## Why This Change Was Made

- **Intended outcome:** one execution agent is named before any `cron.add` admission step reads it,
  so caller-scope matching, creator-session and inference capture, declaration matching, and the
  persisted row all agree on the same owner. `bindCronCreateExecutionAgent`
  (`src/gateway/server-methods/cron-caller-scope.ts`) resolves it — an explicit `agentId` wins,
  otherwise the job's own session reference decides (`sessionTarget` `session:<key>` first, the same
  precedence the run uses through `resolveCronSessionTargetSessionKey`, then the legacy scoped
  `sessionKey`) — and `cronAddHandler` applies it to the request *before* it builds anything else.
  That one resolved `jobCreate` then flows unchanged into `cronCreateMatchesCallerScope`,
  `captureCronCreatorSession`, the `matchesExisting` declaration matcher, and `context.cron.add`.
- This re-points the earlier revision of this PR, which bound the agent inside `CronService.add`.
  That happened *after* two gateway consumers had already read the unresolved input, leaving two
  real inconsistencies (both raised in review):
  - `cronAddHandler` handed `matchesExisting` the unresolved `jobCreate`, so
    `cronJobMatchesDeclarationScope` compared the configured default (`main`) against the stored
    owner (`worker`) and excluded the row it should have converged onto — repeating a declaration
    would have created a second job instead of preserving the first one's id and history;
  - `captureCronCreatorSession` ran before that binding, so it loaded the execution session and
    captured inference for the configured default agent while the job was stored for another.
  `src/cron/service/ops-mutations.ts` is therefore back to `main`: the service no longer re-resolves
  ownership, and there is exactly one binding point.
- Also removed: the previous revision's `manageAll` exception in `cronCreateMatchesCallerScope`. It
  was unreachable — `CRON_MANAGEMENT_METHODS` (`src/gateway/cron-creator-authority-grant.ts`) lists
  `cron.list/get/update/run/remove/bind` and excludes `cron.add`, `mintCronCreatorAuthorityGrant`
  throws for a management method outside that list, `getCronManagementAuthority` only returns inside
  a redeemed method-bound management context, and the one other caller (`cron.update`) passes a
  `creatorScope` built with `manageAll: undefined`. Its test fabricated the capability with
  `vi.fn()` instead of reaching it through admission. Creation authority is unchanged from `main`:
  an agent turn still cannot create a job that another agent would execute, and a scoped caller
  targeting a foreign session is refused exactly as before (`cronPatchSessionRefsMatchCaller` already
  refused it on `main`).
- Deliberately **not** changed: `tryResolveCronJobEffectiveAgentId`'s precedence (explicit id →
  scoped `sessionKey` → configured default), so visibility, scheduling, run receipts, and the Doctor
  heartbeat cutover keep their existing attribution semantics; already-stored jobs are never
  reinterpreted or migrated. Detached targets (`isolated` / `current` / `main`) name no agent and
  still fall back to the caller scope or configured default, and a malformed `session:` target names
  no owner instead of throwing out of a pure resolver.
- **Out of scope:** no change to run-time session resolution, delivery, the one-shot disable policy,
  the SQLite scope check, or existing stored jobs; no config surface added; no other create path
  (plugin `service-cron`, `templates-add`) is re-pointed; no refactor of the caller-scope module.
- **Highest-risk area:** `cron.add` admission — a job that used to be stored without an `agentId` now
  stores the session's agent, which is visible to declaration convergence, agent-filtered listings,
  and inference capture.
- **How is that risk mitigated?** The value is written only when the input carries no `agentId` and
  its own session reference names one, and every consumer downstream reads that same value.
  Regression tests run through the real admission boundary (`handleGatewayRequest` +
  `cronHandlers["cron.add"]` + a real `CronService` on an on-disk store) and cover the persisted
  owner, repeated-declaration convergence, agent-filtered listing, both caller-scope outcomes, an
  ownerless row stored by an older build, the declaration matcher's input contract, and the CLI
  warning.

## User Impact

- **Success criteria:** on a gateway with per-agent session stores, `openclaw cron add --name probe
  --at <t> --session session:agent:worker:dashboard:<uuid> --message ping` (no `--agent`) warns
  `No --agent specified; the job will run with agent worker, named by its session.`, stores the job
  with `agentId: "worker"`, reports `worker` in `cron list`, and the due run really executes a turn
  in `agent:worker:dashboard:<uuid>` under `agentId=worker` instead of dying against `main`. An
  identical repeated `--declaration-key` converges onto the same job id. An agent turn still cannot
  create a job for another agent, and a job stored by an older build still loads and lists unchanged.
- **What should reviewers focus on?** `src/gateway/server-methods/cron-caller-scope.ts`
  (`bindCronCreateExecutionAgent`, plus the reverted `cronCreateMatchesCallerScope` /
  `applyCronCreateCallerScopeDefault`), `src/gateway/server-methods/cron-add.ts` (the single binding
  point), `src/cron/agent-id.ts` (`resolveCronJobSessionRefAgentId`),
  `src/cli/cron-cli/register.cron-add.ts` (warning text), and the regressions in
  `src/gateway/server-methods/cron.gateway-policy.integration.test.ts` (`Gateway automation
  execution agent`), `src/gateway/server-cron.session-target.test.ts`,
  `src/gateway/server-methods/cron-caller-scope.test.ts` (`create-time execution agent`), and
  `src/cli/cron-cli.test.ts`. Also `docs/cli/cron.md`: the create-time precedence this introduces
  (explicit `--agent` → the job's own agent-qualified session reference → configured default) is now
  documented separately from stored-job ownership, which is unchanged.

## Evidence

- **Real environment tested:** yes — a real `openclaw gateway` process and the real `openclaw` CLI,
  both run from this branch's source (`node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs src/entry.ts …`, self-reported
  `OpenClaw 2026.10.9`), against an isolated state dir with per-agent SQLite session stores
  (`session.store: "<state>/sessions/{agentId}.sqlite"`), token auth, and a local
  OpenAI-compatible endpoint on `127.0.0.1` standing in for the model provider so a due turn can
  complete offline. Worktree `aispace/worktrees/issue-190123`, head `c9b5ca8e25d`, base
  `origin/main` `36ddf502c84`, Node v26.12.1. The before legs restore `origin/main` copies of the
  four touched source files and re-run the identical commands against an identically configured
  gateway.
- **Distinct accounts, final effect (added in this revision):** the run above was repeated against a
  second isolated state dir whose two agents own **separate provider credentials** — `main` resolves
  `localmain/proof-model-main` (key tail `1111`), `worker` resolves `localworker/proof-model-worker`
  (key tail `2222`), both served by one local endpoint that logs the `Authorization` header it
  receives. This is the leg that shows target-derived agent selection picking the *account*, at the
  last observable effect (the provider HTTP call), rather than only in the stored row.
- **Agent-turn authority chain, allowed and nearest-forbidden, at the provider HTTP boundary
  (head `acd435275ff`):** the same two-account gateway was reconfigured with

prs.title: fix: updates survive interrupted heartbeat runs
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes updates failing in post-install Doctor when Gateway shutdown leaves a legacy heartbeat run marker.

## User Impact

Interrupted heartbeat runs can migrate during updates. Live or unproved work remains pending with a warning. Notification-producing recovery now converges through the next Gateway cron startup instead of repeatedly deferring or quarantining the legacy job. No schema, protocol, or config option changes.

## Why This Change Was Made

Doctor revalidates its held offline maintenance owner and uses cron's existing recovery kernel. Ordinary interrupted runs settle before conversion. When recovery needs live notification dispatch, only that recovery attempt rolls back to its savepoint; Doctor still commits the ordinary payload conversion with the original run marker, history, and receipt intact. Gateway startup can then decode the row and use its normal recovery and notification path. Both fresh conversion and resumed config retirement retain the pending execution facts when they disable the monitor, so startup restores its recorded result without re-enabling it.

The live/unproved refusal remains update-advisory because its conversion transaction and config writer do not commit. Lost maintenance authority and integrity failures retain their existing failure behavior. The candidate contains the repair; published updater parents need no new marker.

## Evidence

- Deep10 Windows cell: **2026.9.3 → candidate, installed-schtasks, FAIL**, activating / post-install Doctor, natural updater exit 1 after 301,480 ms. Original production source: `a35b92ce`. [Windows run 42555488755](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/42555488755). Receipt names: `deep10/windows/2026.9.3/verified.json`, `deep10/windows/2026.9.3/doctor.stderr-tail.txt`, `deep10/windows/2026.9.3/exception.json`, `deep10/windows/source-owner-audit.md`; report: `deep10.md`, Windows section. The retained evidence does not establish whether the run was live or abandoned.
- The update-Doctor table covers stopped, live, unproved, notification-producing, disable-during-conversion, and disable-during-resumed-cutover cases. The last two preserve the pending marker through disablement, then check the restored last-run timestamp/status/error/duration, a ten-failure counter, one unchanged history entry, disabled state, and no quarantine after startup. General config preflight and native service transport remain fixtures; a full native Windows upgrade is unverified.
- [CI run 42560047339, job 128974686985](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/42560047339/job/128974686985) failed in the PR's live-owner fixture: runtime-pin migration was seeded after acquiring live Gateway custody. The seed now runs before acquisition; the live lock and refusal/warning assertions are retained.

prs.title: fix(acp): tolerate owner-repair verdicts on discarding close with clearMeta (#151859)
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Partially addresses openclaw/openclaw#151859 (task-maintenance discard teardown), resolving the P1 review blocker identified on openclaw/openclaw#152131 while complementing the task-maintenance cleanup deduplication in openclaw/openclaw#152613.

When an ACP session record has an unmigrated or unverifiable backend locator (raising `isAcpOwnerRepairRequired` with `SESSION_OWNER_MIGRATION_REQUIRED`), automated task maintenance cleanup (`loadTaskAcpSessionCloser` in `src/tasks/task-registry-acp-cleanup.ts`) fails closed every minute even though it explicitly requests to destroy both persistent state and stored metadata (`discardPersistentState: true`, `clearMeta: true`, and `allowBackendUnavailable: true`). Because teardown was blocked by the record's own provenance verdict, residue records survived and triggered repeated maintenance failures indefinitely.

*(Note: Gateway CLI deletion in `src/gateway/session-reset-acp.ts` returns earlier from cancellation and omits `clearMeta`; this PR focuses strictly on the maintenance closer path where `clearMeta: true` and `discardPersistentState: true` are supplied together).*

In #152131, an attempt was made to permit discard-close past owner-repair verdicts, but it inadvertently suppressed owner-repair errors even when `clearMeta` was false or omitted. That introduced a P1 state lifecycle violation (`[P1] Preserve ownership failures when the session metadata is retained`), because an unmigrated session metadata entry would be retained on disk after a reset without notifying the operator or prompting for offline migration.

## Why This Change Was Made

To satisfy the product owner's state lifecycle decisions (*Preventative Preservation & Action Observability*):
1. **Strictly gate owner-repair bypass on `clearMeta: true`**:
   - In `src/acp/control-plane/manager.close-session.ts`:
     - Recovery branch allows `ACP_SESSION_INIT_FAILED` with `isAcpOwnerRepairRequired(acpError)` **only** when `Boolean(input.discardPersistentState) && Boolean(input.clearMeta)` and `input.allowBackendUnavailable`.
     - In both the fast-reset branch and recovery branch, fresh-session preparation catches `isAcpOwnerRepairRequired(freshError)` **only** when `input.clearMeta` is `true`.
2. **Preserve fail-closed semantics for retained resets**:
   - When `clearMeta` is `false` or omitted (undefined), owner-repair errors are **always preserved and rethrown**, whether `discardPersistentState` is `false` or `true`. Stored metadata in the session store and SQLite database remains byte-for-byte intact.
3. **Comprehensive Regression Coverage**:
   - In `src/acp/control-plane/manager.owner.test.ts`:
     - Fast-reset path (`identityHasStableSessionId` false): verifies retained resets (`clearMeta: false` and `undefined`) across both `discardPersistentState` variants reject with `SESSION_OWNER_MIGRATION_REQUIRED` and leave metadata intact; verifies discarding reset with `clearMeta: true` deletes metadata and bypasses runtime close.
     - Recovery path (`identityHasStableSessionId` true): verifies retained resets reject and leave metadata intact; verifies non-discarding close rejects; verifies discarding close with `clearMeta: true` succeeds, records `runtimeNotice`, and deletes metadata without invoking `runtime.close`.

## User Impact

- Task registry maintenance cleanly purges residue ACP sessions whose backend locators are unverifiable or unmigrated, stopping perpetual maintenance log spam without manual intervention.
- Sessions undergoing non-destructive resets or retaining metadata are strictly protected from silent provenance mutation and continue to fail closed with directions to run Doctor repair.

## Evidence

### Real Runtime Verification: ACPX Backend Wiring & Production Task Closer

Executed against real SQLite session storage (`openclaw.sqlite`) wired to the actual ACPX locator check (`assertAcpxSessionOwnerLocator`) and production maintenance closer (`loadTaskAcpSessionCloser`):

```text
=== ACPX & TASK REGISTRY MAINTENANCE CLEANUP VERIFICATION ===
[Setup] Unmigrated ACPX session initialized in SQLite:
  • sessionKey: legacy-session-1
  • backend: acpx | mode: persistent
  • state database: openclaw.sqlite

[Backend] Verified authentic ACPX locator check:
  • Exception: AcpRuntimeError [ACP_SESSION_INIT_FAILED]
  • Detail code: SESSION_OWNER_MIGRATION_REQUIRED
  • Message excerpt: ACP session "legacy-session-1" has an unqualified or unverifiable backend locator. Stop the Gat...

[Test 1] Retained reset attempt (clearMeta: false)...
  -> Rejected as expected: fail-closed against unmigrated state
  -> Error detail: ACP_SESSION_INIT_FAILED [SESSION_OWNER_MIGRATION_REQUIRED]
  -> Stored metadata in SQLite preserved byte-for-byte: true

[Test 2] Invoking actual loadTaskAcpSessionCloser() from src/tasks/task-registry-acp-cleanup.ts...
  • Task closer loaded successfully from production task registry
  -> Production maintenance cleanup completed successfully!
  -> Metadata purged from openclaw.sqlite (readAcpSessionEntry?.acp): undefined (deleted)

=== ALL PRODUCTION & BACKEND VERIFICATION CHECKS PASSED ===
```

### Data-Model & Migration Compatibility Proof

- **SQLite Schema Version**: Unchanged (native state schema remains `v17`, verified by `pnpm check:native-state-schema-version`).
- **Data Migration / Backfill**: None required. No table schema, column, or type definitions are modified.
- **Backward & Forward Compatibility**:
  - Pre-existing session entries in `openclaw.sqlite` remain byte-for-byte intact and fully backward-compatible across upgrades.
  - Normal operations and retained resets (`clearMeta: false` or omitted) continue to fail closed and preserve stored metadata byte-for-byte in SQLite without modification.
  - Only explicit destructive cleanup (`clearMeta: true` and `discardPersistentState: true` with `allowBackendUnavailable: true`) removes the session record from SQLite.

### Automated Suites & Ratchets

- **Unit & Control-Plane Test Suites**:
  - `src/acp/control-plane/manager.owner.test.ts`: 10/10 tests pass across unit and acp projects.
  - Full `src/acp/control-plane/`: 42 files, 329/329 tests pass.
- **Ratchet & Quality Audits**:
  - `pnpm oxlint`: 0 warnings, 0 errors.
  - `pnpm check:line-cap-ratchet`: 2 changed files; no growth/violations.
  - `pnpm check:assertion-safety`: OK, 0 new unannotated assertions.
  - `pnpm check:changed`: All 21 checks passed (typecheck core, typecheck core tests, format, ratchets, Knip deadcode, import cycles).

prs.title: feat(ui): add saved gateway account switching
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

This repair closes the remaining Gateway-profile correctness and proof gaps:

- Active profile removal uses the returned survivor projection directly, so the deleted URL cannot be reintroduced by fallback loading.
- Query-aware migrated credentials are sent only to their owning exact endpoint at the outgoing WebSocket client boundary.
- Successful token-mode migration retires the old origin-scoped token; clearing an owned migrated profile retires both exact and legacy slots.
- Query-distinct profiles cannot recover a neighboring profile's credential.

Profiles remain local browser metadata. Credentials remain session-scoped; no server-side account or shared credential store was added.

## Evidence

- Pushed head: `9b7ed952e4a4d0fd5367c96074b62b93496f38cb`.
- `npx --yes pnpm@12.3.4 exec vitest run ui/src/app/settings.node.test.ts ui/src/app/gateway-store.auth.test.ts ui/src/app/gateway-registry.test.ts ui/src/app/gateway-store.test.ts --reporter=dot` — **117/117 passed** across 4 suites.
- `npx --yes pnpm@12.3.4 exec oxfmt --check ui/src/app/settings.ts ui/src/app/settings.node.test.ts ui/src/app/gateway-store.auth.test.ts ui/src/pages/connection/connection-page.ts` — passed.
- `npx --yes pnpm@12.3.4 tsgo:ui` — passed from an independently owned checkout install.
- `npx --yes pnpm@12.3.4 ui:build` — passed: **3,401 modules**, **840 finalized sidecars**, startup JS gzip **345,895 B** under the **352,235 B** limit; startup CSS **44,978 B** under the **51,200 B** ceiling.

## Fresh headed-browser proof

Run on 2026-09-11 against exact-head build `8023b23`/the pushed repair checkout, using disposable token Gateways and temporary state:

- `ws://127.0.0.1:19889` with a synthetic redacted token label `personal`.
- `ws://127.0.0.1:19890?account=team` with a synthetic redacted token label `team`.
- Real headed Chromium opened `http://127.0.0.1:19889/settings/connection`; the UI reached the actual WebSocket Gateway handshake and displayed token-authenticated connected state for both endpoints.
- Browser flow added and switched to the query-bearing Team profile, then confirmed removal of the active Team profile. The page reconnected to the surviving `19889` profile and the removed row stayed absent.
- The outgoing-boundary regression captured the actual client constructor options: migrated exact URL plus its owned token; after token-mode hello, the exact token key existed and the legacy origin key was gone.
- The clear regression seeded an owned origin-migrated token, cleared it, and verified both that profile and a query-distinct neighbor loaded with an empty token; the legacy key was absent.
- Browser storage and console diagnostics were redacted: no token values were retained. Browser console reported 2 development/runtime errors from the session; no zero-console-error claim is made.

## Limitation

After the browser's first successful token handshake, the Gateway issued a device grant. Clearing the visible Gateway secret and clicking Connect therefore remained connected through device authentication; this does not claim that clearing revokes an existing device grant. The no-token-reuse claim is proven at the outgoing client boundary and by the storage regression, while the live browser proof confirms the real handshake, profile switching, survivor removal, and endpoint identity.

The final post-push exact-head startup check launched runtime `9b7ed95` but detected that the runtime build stamp was still from `8023b23` while the rebuilt UI was `9b7ed952`, and correctly returned HTTP 503 rather than serving a mixed build. The interactive headed-browser receipt therefore comes from the immediately preceding compatible runtime; the final-head changes are covered by the 117-test suite, exact-head UI build, and the outgoing-boundary regression.

No new ClawSweeper review was requested.

prs.body:
Related: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/143752

## What Problem This Solves

The installed-update lane must reject changed helper code, metadata and runtime dependencies before using them as evidence. This slice adds standalone application/dependency admission through the canonical package scanner and npm owners. Import-occurrence reporting composes with upstream Control UI import-map resolution, preserving raw specifiers, mapped targets, existing callbacks, missing-file checks and silence on parse failure.

## User Impact

No product runtime or public API change. This is part 2 of 5; it does not enable the final installed lane. The observer parent, https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/192937, is merged. Native integration is frozen at baseline `43dae0b46f1eb1dcfed7434196ff3bf1aa8a9b2a`; landed observer behavior, declarations, Node/Bun fixes and allocation remain intact. Descendant restacking and qualification are separate work.

## Why This Change Was Made

Application admission binds selected executable closures, finite initialization metadata, schema assets and reviewed dependency records. Native npm cache/SRI checks and complete portable dependency-tree comparisons retain the canonical ownership boundaries. Current reference dependencies remain `@openclaw/fs-safe@0.27.1` and `@openclaw/proxyline@0.4.1`.

The native one-file/two-hunk parser integration retains both `onImportOccurrence` and `controlUiImports` with consistent parameter/call order. It preserves upstream mapped-target/CSS/preload validation and publishes occurrence callbacks only after a successful parse. The expanded existing import-map regression checks mapped edges, raw specifiers and UTF-16 provenance, alongside unmapped require/URL/outside-UI and parse-failure behavior.

Fresh emitted bytes from `7ef902d3b4126b2f1f5d58aaad3d1340b1e0315d` support the current-only contracts. Independent selected-mode review classified all 17 unresolved dynamic occurrences and all eleven import tuples through consequential callers, guards, failures and retirement paths. The reviewed closures contain **73 SQLite-session files, 1,517 finalizer-check files and eleven SQLite-heartbeat files**. The graph's zero pending imports and collector roles were not substituted for selected-mode reachability. Six SQLite database families, all 19 finite metadata guards and five schema assets remain enforced. The closures retain consequential static initialization and footer retirement; asynchronous staging and nested GC execution remain excluded by their selected-mode caller guards. Current agent schema 41 was inherited from upstream; this PR does not advance a schema version. Historical reference/SRIs and historical schema 25 are unchanged.

The dependency-gate correction models `@npmcli/arborist`, `@npmcli/config`, `cacache` and `pacote` in the existing exact-name tooling allowance because their actual owner is `createRequire(npmCli)`. This allowance is package/workspace scoped, including descendant fallback; it is not file scoped. No root dependency, wildcard exclusion or artificial consumer was added. Three unused internal exports became private with matching declaration removals, retaining the real extraction/inspection APIs. The final driver slice, https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/192954, must restore the `installedTerminalNpmOwner` export and declaration together with its existing real consumer. That child is unchanged here.

Product runtime +0/-0. Production tooling/configuration/declarations +969/-11 (net +958); test code +470/-5 (net +465); historical fixture +806; allocation metadata +2. Total: 13 paths, 2,263 gross lines. Positive tooling growth provides independent package/dependency admission and canonical import-occurrence provenance with matching declarations, retaining existing resolver and npm ownership. The separate **465-line allocation** exactly matches this slice's own test LF growth: 350 contract-test lines plus 115 parser-test lines. prs.title: fix(ui): keep native plugin footer proof compatible with transcript overlap
prs.body:
Related: #195508

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes the native plugin UI footer test failing at 1280px after the transcript was intentionally extended behind the composer’s rounded corners. This is a maintainer-requested repair of [scheduled main run 42562039354, job 128980605704](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/42562039354/job/128980605704).

## User Impact

Test-only change; product rendering remains unchanged. Built-in, delegated, and failing-plugin fallback composers retain footer containment and transcript content clearance checks at 1280px and 640px.

## Why This Change Was Made

[12eaf8ac11b5](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/12eaf8ac11b523e767c66a3ccef40b16341644bb) added intentional viewport overlap and matching bottom padding in #195508. The native plugin helper still required the viewport itself to end above the footer. It now checks the usable content edge, subtracting the scrollport’s actual bottom padding, including ResizeObserver adjustments. Insufficient clearance still fails. The same footer owns transcript lookup and composer containment.

Simplification: one helper changed, +6/−6 lines; no production changes, new tests, allocation records, baseline changes, retries, timeout increases, or skips.

## Evidence

- Original failure: only `separated` differs (`true` expected, `false` received). `committed`, `contained`, and `inputOutsideContext` are `true`; `content` and `background` are `"none"`, as expected.
- Direct oxlint 1.89.0 on the touched file passed; touched-file oxfmt passed; `git diff --check` passed.
- Independent local autoreview (Codex, GPT-6.1 Sol), P0–P2, completed with no actionable findings. Reviewed the final local diff against `e08aa74ea39e35d01ba8e8f84e317747aba1bf3f`, with the footer E2E, overlap CSS, and transcript layout owner as evidence. No source changes followed review.
- Browser E2E was deliberately not run on the production Team Gateway host. Existing scheduled CI supplies the failing reproduction; this PR’s CI must supply post-fix browser proof. Local test wall time / CI seconds: not available yet.
- The named-file TypeScript check did not provide valid proof: import resolution expanded into unprepared workspace packages and failed on missing declarations (for example `@openclaw/normalization-core/record-coerce`) and missing JSX context. No broader local check or dependency preparation was attempted; types remain pending CI.

Original PR author and this commit’s author are both @roboclaw-bot. Preserved verified human credit for @vyctorbrzezowski and the requested @steipete coauthor credit in the commit.

prs.title: fix(sessions): replay a queued follow-up across an interposed command exchange
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

A follow-up message queued while a run is active is dropped when `/stop` is used. The dispatcher mirrors the stop's
command exchange into the transcript, and the queued follow-up's replay admission then resolves the **command row** as
the current turn, refuses with `Persisted user turn changed before replay admission`, and the message is never answered.

Reproduced with the reporter's fixture (`extensions`-free, real session manager + real transcript): on `main` the queued
follow-up ends with `0` model calls and that error; with this change it is answered.

## Why This Change Was Made

`src/agents/sessions/session-manager-current-turn.ts` decides which transcript entries the current-turn walk may step
over. It already treats context metadata, compaction markers and runtime/system custom messages as traversable because
they are not model-facing turns. A delivered command exchange is the same kind of row — a transcript mirror of the
dispatcher's reply — but it was not listed, so the walk stopped on it.

The fix marks rows whose `idempotencyKey` is `command-input:*` or `command-reply:*` as traversable. Nothing else changes:
real user turns still stop the walk, and the admission still requires the prepared user message to match exactly.

## User Impact

A queued follow-up survives `/stop`: it is persisted once and gets answered instead of silently disappearing behind a
generic "couldn't finish this reply". Commands that are not mirrored (`/new` etc. still write their exchange the same
way) behave the same, and no transcript bytes change.

## Evidence

Reporter's fixture, run with `node scripts/test-projects.mts <file>`:

| case | base | this branch |
|---|---|---|
| no interposed write (control) | answered | answered |
| Workshop notice interposed (control, #181473) | answered | answered |
| **`/stop` exchange interposed** | `Persisted user turn changed before replay admission`, 0 model calls | 1 model call, `FOLLOWUP_ANSWERED` |

- Base: `2 failed | 4 passed` (both reader modes fail on the interposed case). Fixed: `6 passed`.
- Neighbours: `attempt-session-replay.test.ts` 61 passed; `session-manager-bounded.test.ts` 28 passed;
  `session-manager-async-entries.test.ts` 9 passed.
- `oxlint`: 0 warnings, 0 errors. The new test file carries an allocation in
  `config/test-lines-allocations/stop-exchange-replay-admission.txt`.

### Why there is no gateway-level trace here

Two environment limits, each verified rather than assumed, so a reviewer knows exactly what is missing and how to close
it:

1. **Gateway e2e cannot run in this container.** The built vitest runtime is available (`node
   scripts/prepare-vitest-runtime.mjs --with-ai-package` succeeds), but e2e tests fail in the process supervisor with
   `service child cleanup identity lost: native owner closed without kernel descendant extinction` — reproduced by
   running the smallest existing e2e file, `test/gateway-restart-lane.e2e.test.ts` (`1 failed`), which never reaches this
   PR's code.
2. **Gateway RPC auth does not resolve.** With an isolated `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR`/`OPENCLAW_CONFIG_PATH`, `gateway.auth.mode:
   "none"` still answers RPC with `token_missing`, and a token accepted by the gateway answers `token_mismatch`, so a
   scripted `chat.send`/`sessions.create` trace cannot be produced. `src/gateway/auth.ts:526-542` returns `{ ok: true }`
   for `mode: "none"`, so the configuration is not taking effect on the isolated run — unresolved here.

What a reviewer can run instead, in an environment where either limit is lifted: start the gateway with the mock provider
(`scripts/e2e/mock-openai-server.mjs`, config shape in `scripts/e2e/lib/fixtures/mock-openai-config.mjs`), queue a
follow-up during a turn, send `/stop`, and confirm the queued message still gets a model call instead of failing with
`Persisted user turn changed before replay admission`.

## Scope

One production file (the traversal predicate), the reporter's regression test registered next to
`attempt-session-replay.test.ts` in `test/vitest/vitest.database-worker-core-paths.mjs`, and the allocation file.

## AI Assistance

This PR was prepared with AI assistance from the issue report and its attached fixture; the author reviewed the change
and its evidence.

### Gateway-level proof: what a CI-shaped test would need

I could not produce this here (no provider endpoint on this machine), but the pieces are in the repo:

- `test/helpers/openclaw-test-instance.ts` starts a real Gateway with isolated state without Playwright
  (`startGateway` / `port` / `url` / `cli`), so the queue/stop sequence can be driven over the Gateway API.
- `scripts/e2e/mock-openai-server.mjs` is an OpenAI-compatible mock with `MOCK_RESPONSE_CHUNK_DELAY_MS`, which keeps a turn
  running long enough to queue a follow-up and send `/stop` — that is the whole sequence this PR changes.
- With those two, a `*.real-gateway.e2e.test.ts` can assert: first turn streaming -> second `chat.send` queues ->
  `/stop` -> the queued message receives an assistant reply (base: user row only, no reply).

The existing `ui/src/e2e/*.real-gateway.e2e.test.ts` suites do not run a model (they append to the transcript directly), so
there is no fixture to copy for this yet.
