prs.title: feat: let the memory slot owner report its own dreaming status
prs.body: Related: #138366 ## What Problem This Solves A memory plugin that owns the memory slot and does its own consolidation has no way to describe its dreaming on the Memory page. The page reports dreaming as disabled or unscheduled while it in fact runs every night. Two host assumptions cause this: - `resolveMemoryDreamingConfig` gives all three phases the same expression, so a plugin whose REM and deep passes run on separate schedules, or whose light pass is event-driven, cannot say so. - The promotion counters come from memory-core's own store, which stops advancing once another plugin takes over consolidation. The workaround is worse than the symptom. Setting `dreaming.enabled: true` on the slot owner makes memory-core create its managed promotion cron at the same frequency, so the same workspace gets two consolidation passes in the same minute. ## Why This Change Was Made `MemoryPluginCapability` already has this shape once. `publicArtifacts` lets a non-`memory-core` slot owner contribute data through an optional provider, while the host keeps ownership of semantics. This PR applies the same pattern to dreaming: ```ts export type MemoryPluginCapability = { publicArtifacts?: MemoryPluginPublicArtifactsProvider; dreaming?: MemoryPluginDreamingProvider; // added // … }; ``` The contract is reporting-only. Lifecycle, memory-core's managed sweep cron and the dream actions stay with memory-core. The full rules are in `docs/plugins/sdk-overview/memory-and-context.md`: - **Overlay.** `doctor.memory.status` overlays the report field by field on the host resolution. Without a provider the response is unchanged. - **Every status path.** The provider is consulted with a search runtime, without one, and when the plugin answers through its own `providerRuntime` (new in this revision, see below). - **Owner lock.** Any report arrives as `reportedByProvider: true`. That locks the page's switch against turning the host sweep on, since both would dream at once. A running host sweep can still be turned off. The Off confirmation then says that the orphan-cron cleanup from #156667 (now on main, at plugin reload and at startup) removes the promotion job memory-core already scheduled. - **Switch and scene.** Reported `enabled` arrives as `reportedEnabled`. The switch keeps showing the memory-core configuration it writes. The Dreams scene lights while the owner reports running, or while a phase is enabled and scheduled. - **Counters.** Reported counters arrive as `reportedStats` next to memory-core's figures, not in their place. The Dreaming status line and Settings > Memory › Activity show the owner's counters, with n/a for any it omits. The Review lists keep memory-core's figures, entries and actions, together with a note that says so. - **Schedule rows.** Settings > Memory › Sleep schedule takes each phase's state from its own `enabled` and `scheduled` flags while an owner reports. ## Revision on current `main` This revision merges current main and resolves the two P2 findings of the last review: - **Provider-runtime slot owners.** A plugin that registers both `providerRuntime` and `dreaming.getStatus` took the provider-runtime branch, which returned before the dreaming lookup. That reply now carries the same composed dreaming section. `respondProviderMemoryStatus` keeps its authority checks, health and close. Test: `doctor.dreaming-provider.test.ts` › "composes the slot owner's report into a provider-runtime health reply". - **Admitted-plugin value contract (#163818).** The report now crosses by reference. The validator and copier helpers, their tests and the matching docs are gone. A throw or a `null` report still keeps memory-core's resolution. - **Ported onto main's new owners.** The payload fields now live on the `gateway-protocol` `DoctorMemoryDreamingPayload` type. The Dreams controls, review and confirmation dialog are now Solid. Settings > Memory › Overview is memory-core's packaged browser view (`extensions/memory-core/browser/overview.tsx`). Main's phase chips no longer show times, so the earlier "last run" chip helper was dropped. `lastRunAtMs` still appears in the Overview schedule rows. ## Evidence **Before / after on current main** (`pnpm dev:ui:mock`). Both runs use the same `doctor.memory.status` fixture: slot owner `acme-memory` reports REM/deep schedules, an event-driven light phase and `promotedToday: 4`, while memory-core's own count is 2 and the host switch is off. | | Before (main) | After (this PR) | |---|---|---| | Overview: phases and counters | | | | Dreams: scene and switch | | | **Live.** The previous revision of this change, on a 2026.10.10 build, has been running in a production installation since 2026-11-05 with a third-party memory slot owner that dreams on its own schedule. The Memory page shows the owner's schedule and counters, and memory-core's sweep stays off. **Tests** (`pnpm test --maxWorkers=1`, wall time on a shared host): - `src/gateway/server-methods/doctor.dreaming-provider.test.ts`: 9 passed (59 s) - `src/gateway/server-methods/doctor.test.ts`: 33 passed (63 s); `doctor.memory-provider.test.ts`: 1 passed (62 s) - `src/plugins/memory-state.test.ts`: 28 passed (10 s); `registry.dual-kind-memory-gate.test.ts`: 6 passed - `ui/src/pages/agents/memory/memory-panel.test.ts`: 43 passed, 1 skipped (pre-existing) (22 s); `toggle-confirmation.test.ts`: 5 passed; `view.test.ts`: 20 passed; `dreaming.test.ts`: 26 passed - `extensions/memory-core/browser/overview.test.tsx`: 28 passed (12 s) - `tsgo:core`, `tsgo:ui`, `tsgo:extensions` and the gateway-methods / ui-pages / plugins-platform / extensions test projects: clean. `oxlint` and `oxfmt` on all changed files: clean. No real timers, sleeps or Gateway boots in the new tests. **Plugin SDK surface.** The budget comment adds +3 type-only exports (`MemoryPluginDreaming{Provider,Status,PhaseStatus}`). `plugin-sdk:surface:check` already fails on `main` itself (3862 > 3859 exports, 2233 > 2232 callable). This PR adds exactly its +3 type exports on top of that and no callable.

prs.title: feat(telegram): offer each configured model runtime as its own /model picker button
prs.body: Supersedes #163908, which the inactivity bot closed. Same change, now merged with current `main`. The review history on #163908 still applies, and the points it left open are covered below. Related: `pickerRuntimes` (2026.9.5 release notes, `docs/concepts/models.md` › "Choose the same model with different runtimes") ## What Problem This Solves In the Telegram `/model` picker, a model with several configured runtimes (`agents.defaults.models["/"].pickerRuntimes`, for example API and Claude CLI) appears as a single button, and that button carries only the default route label. The Control UI and the Discord picker already offer each runtime as its own choice. On Telegram, the other runtime is only reachable by typing `/model --runtime `. ## User Impact Telegram shows one button per offered runtime, labelled with the existing route prefix (`API · Claude Opus 5.5`, `Claude CLI · Claude Opus 5.5`). Tapping one selects the model and pins that runtime for the session, and ✓ marks the active model/runtime pair. Models with a single runtime look exactly as before. Picking the configured runtime of the agent's default model still resets the session to its default. ## Why This Change Was Made The picker data already carries `runtimeChoicesByModel`; the Telegram list did not use it. - `model-buttons.ts` expands a model into one entry per runtime variant. The new callback is `mdl_rt_{runtime}_{provider/model}`. When that does not fit Telegram's 64 bytes, an opaque `mdl1~r:{sha256}` is used instead. Runtime selections resolve only against the variants the picker offered. - `model-runtime-variants.ts` (new) builds the variants per model, with the configured runtime first. - `bot-handlers.callback-router.ts`: pagination counts entries, and a runtime button applies `applySessionModelSelection` with `runtime: { kind: "set" }`. - `commands-models-catalog.ts` exposes `modelRuntimeIds`. This is the runtime each multi-runtime model uses with no session pin, resolved from config and auth for any provider. It is optional and absent for single-runtime models. - `commands-models.ts` / `command-ui.ts`: the direct `/models ` reply pages over the same runtime rows as the callbacks. - `ChannelCommandAdapter.buildModelsListChannelData` gains five optional inputs. Adapters that ignore them keep one row per model. No config, storage or protocol changes, and existing `mdl_sel_*` / `mdl1~m:` callbacks keep working. ## Revision on current `main` This revision merges current main. The one real conflict is main's role-policy filter for CLI alias twins in `loadModelsProviderData`. It now runs after `modelRuntimeIds` is filled and also drops the runtime id of a model it filters out. Behaviour and callbacks are otherwise unchanged from the last reviewed head `abb6c39d7bb`. ## Evidence **Before / after (live Telegram, `pickerRuntimes` set on the Anthropic models):** | Before | After | |---|---| | | | **Real behavior proof.** ClawSweeper asked for this as "Add real behavior proof". Since 2026-10-18 the change has been running in a production installation: first on a 2026.10.4 build, and since 2026-11-05 on a 2026.10.10 build with this exact port. It serves three daily-use Telegram bots, and selecting a runtime from the picker moves subsequent turns to that runtime. A logged CLI↔API switch is shown below. ``` cli exec: provider=claude-cli model=claude-opus-5-5 trigger=user useResume=false cli turn: provider=claude-cli model=claude-opus-5-5 durationMs=17379 cli exec: provider=claude-cli model=claude-opus-5-5 trigger=user useResume=true session=present [model-fetch] response provider=anthropic api=anthropic-messages model=claude-opus-5-5 status=200 ``` Session entry afterwards: `modelOverride: "claude-opus-5-5"`, `agentRuntimeOverride: "openclaw"`. Still open from the review: Telegram **Test Server userbot** evidence via the repository `telegram-e2e-userbot` skill, covering revised selection, the configured-default reset, and direct-reply/callback pagination. It needs Convex-leased team credentials that I do not have. If a maintainer can run that lane, or lease me the credentials, I'll add the recording. **Owner decision.** The five optional `ChannelCommandAdapter` inputs are additive, and adapters that ignore them are unaffected. They still need a maintainer's yes or no. **Tests** (`pnpm test --maxWorkers=1`, merged base `d189a554154`, wall time on a shared host): - `extensions/telegram/src/model-buttons.test.ts`: 13 passed (11 s); `model-runtime-variants.test.ts`: 5 passed (9 s); `command-ui.test.ts`: 5 passed (64 s) - `src/auto-reply/reply/commands-models.test.ts`: 19 passed (70 s, includes "reports each model's configured runtime regardless of the session runtime pin"); `commands-models-order.test.ts`: 1 passed; `commands-models.catalog-recovery.test.ts`: 6 passed - `extensions/telegram/src/bot.test.ts -t model`: 5 passed - `tsgo:core`, `tsgo:extensions`: clean. `oxlint` (core + extensions tsconfig) and `oxfmt --check` on the changed files: clean. No real timers, sleeps, or Gateway boots in the new tests.

prs.title: fix: enable browser OAuth behind trusted reverse proxies
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes disabled MCP sign-in when an authenticated reverse proxy preserves the browser's public Origin but rewrites Host to the internal Gateway address.

## User Impact

Operators can use browser OAuth at the configured HTTPS `gateway.publicOrigin` behind a trusted proxy. Existing origin admission and administrator requirements remain enforced. An extra allowlisted origin alone does not become a callback address.

## Why This Change Was Made

The sign-in capability and callback resolver now consume the connection's existing authenticated policy. MCP, model-provider and channel-account sign-in share that decision. Pending callbacks recheck the configured origin and proxy authority before accepting a response.

## Evidence

- Before: a real Gateway accepted the trusted-proxy connection but omitted `mcp.authLogin`; the regression failed. Matching Host to Origin made the original code pass, isolating the cause.
- After: the same public/internal address mismatch advertises `mcp.authLogin` for a paired Control UI administrator. Wrong-origin admission remains rejected.
- Callback tests cover success, a changed public origin, revoked proxy policy, missing proxy authentication and a merely allowlisted origin.
- Focused Gateway hardening, MCP login/tool invocation, model login and channel-account login suites pass. Production and test typechecks, focused lint, formatting and assertion-safety checks pass.
- Separately, the official 2026.10.10 terminal OAuth flow completed discovery, browser approval, PKCE exchange and credential persistence against a disposable OAuth/MCP provider; its authenticated probe listed `proof__echo`. A disposable Luma attempt using the shared public client metadata reached Luma's login screen. No Luma account was signed in and no customer Gateway was accessed or changed.

A real Control UI browser also completed sign-in through an HTTPS proxy with public Origin `https://localhost:19842` and rewritten Host `127.0.0.1:19841`: the button was enabled, the provider registered `https://localhost:19842/oauth/provider/callback`, PKCE exchange completed, and the UI showed **Signed in**. The Gateway then invoked `proof__echo` through its authenticated `/tools/invoke` route and returned **Authenticated connector reply**. The fixture recorded two successful exchanges (terminal and browser) and one tool call.

Actual Luma consent and customer deployment remain unverified. No live customer state or credentials were used.

<details>
<summary>Test cost and scope</summary>

The changed hardening file retains its existing 11 Gateway cases (62.4s wall time, including cold worker setup); no extra Gateway boot was added. The callback file passes all 27 cases in 14.94s wall time including worker setup; its new cases use the existing lightweight session fixture. Hosted CI timing is pending. The separate allocation covers exactly 87 net regression-test lines for ingress and callback-revocation boundaries; the shared test-line scalar is unchanged.

The production change reuses the existing authentication/configuration owners and callback lifetime. It adds no proxy-header trust, new configuration option, provider-specific code, or credential storage mechanism.
</details>

prs.title: fix(apple): encode fixed-width numeric gateway parameters
prs.body:
Fixes #195543

## What Problem This Solves

Apple gateway requests fail to encode when their parameters contain native Swift fixed-width numbers such as `UInt`, `Int32`, `UInt8`, or `Float`.

## User Impact

These numeric parameters encode as JSON numbers instead of failing the whole request with “Unsupported type.” No configuration, protocol, or migration changes are required.

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing AnyCodable normalization owner widens unsupported native integers using exact conversions and binary floats to Double, leaving the previously supported native types and Foundation normalization path intact.

Applied the supplied [fix branch commit](https://github.com/saariuslystoned/openclaw/commit/e560fdf66f6410c286e5035aa9bd0b6368d08e24) unchanged onto fresh main `3855c896edd83827405dfe21df89f85b1130246d`. Simplification retained the single normalization owner, with no new helpers or state: +9 production lines and +11 test lines for the encoding regression.

## Evidence

- **Contributor’s macOS/Xcode runner:** @saariuslystoned reports that the Swift tests ran red before the fix and green afterward. These results were supplied by the contributor, not independently rerun here; runner logs and test duration were not supplied.
- **Linux sandbox:** clean patch application, `git diff --check`, staged whitespace check, full diff/caller inspection, identical patch IDs, and exact blob comparison of both changed files against the donor branch passed. `pnpm docs:list` completed and relevant protocol guidance was reviewed.
- **Independent Auto Review:** reviewed the complete local candidate against `3855c896edd83827405dfe21df89f85b1130246d` at its default P0 coverage; scoped-clean, no P0 findings. This is not broader-priority review or native runtime proof.
- **Not run here:** Swift tests/builds, SwiftLint, and SwiftFormat; those tools are unavailable in this sandbox. The added test checks JSONEncoder output for UInt, Int32, UInt8, and Float, plus equivalent integer equality. Generated RequestFrame/native gateway execution was not independently exercised here. Local Swift wall time and CI seconds are not yet available.

Contributed by @saariuslystoned (Bobby Bones). ☁️

## Work sessions

Linked for team reference; these sessions aren’t public.

- [Original discussion](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/dashboard/512344a4-21ba-477e-819a-276de6add6a9)

prs.body:
Closes #182409 ## What Problem This Solves Staged chat images offer preview and removal, but no way to cover selected regions before sending them. ## User Impact Users can apply opaque rectangles to a flattened PNG copy while preserving the original file and sibling attachments; sending stays explicit. ## Why This Change Was Made Uses the current image editor, modal and attachment-admission owners, retaining editing work until a replacement is accepted. ## Evidence ### Technical CI follow-up (2026-11-07) Current head `7146ffe98e8ab3195028fe651c10ba53d0a0f1eb`, tree `2276ef492dac95c93ac150dd45b21d642e84e3ba`; previous maintainer head `81a20f5dfafe084974f0ba1c3c8ea2d9fa308baa` is preserved. The wrapped full-width **Redact image** label intercepted the existing native preview click. It is now an existing-token 24 px corner icon button with the same accessible name, tooltip, disabled state and handler. Async edit lifetime, rejected Apply, PNG admission and payload custody logic are unchanged. This follow-up does not resolve the built-in placement/product decision: **the PR stays Draft**. The same native Chromium owner regression fails on unchanged `81a20` (ordinary preview pointer click intercepted, both LTR/RTL) and passes on this head; no forced click, click offset or longer timeout. It runs the actual `AttachmentPreview` with shipped styles. The original failing hosted Side chat preview/send/retry E2E lane is left to fresh PR CI; it was not rerun locally or claimed green. Current built acceptance: `node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs PROOF_ROOT/redaction-built-proof.mjs CHECKOUT NEW_OUTPUT`. The normal UI build has clean commit7146 identity; browser-served entry bytes match the recorded build hash. In real Chromium152, **Main and Side chat** each pass ordinary default-center image preview/Escape, keyboard Redact, native pointer cover → Undo → cover again → Apply, and preview of the replacement. Independent decoded PNG readback sees opaque-black center `[0,0,0,255]`, original-orange corner `[255,165,0,255]`, dimensions32×32 and a byte-identical sibling. Recorder readback contains exactly one replacement PNG and one unchanged sibling per send, zero original images. Main uses `chat.send`; Side chat uses `sessions.companion.ask`. prs.title: fix(ui): prevent premature cron transcript E2E faults
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The Cron transcript E2E loading and recovery cases can time out because their history fault is injected during the initial Cron visit.

## User Impact

Scheduled Control UI checks exercise the intended transcript-loading and recovery behavior reliably. Production behavior is unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

Intercept Cron's own lazy `run-transcript.runtime.ts` implementation instead of the shared `message-visibility.ts` dependency. The shared dependency is emitted in a Chat boot chunk and can be requested before a transcript opens. Both existing scenarios and all their assertions remain intact; no retries, timeout changes, skips, or baseline changes.

Related: #194165, which introduced these interception targets.

## Evidence

- [Failed scheduled job](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/42562039354/job/128980605611), head `1bc50e0517ad`: the loading case timed out with its roster already ready and Cron routing still pending. Retained browser diagnostics show the recovery case aborting `control-ui-boot-chat-HoVKL6We.js`, then completing its guarded reload during `installCron`, before the later navigation waiter was registered. These are two effects of the same premature interception.
- The prior scheduled run `42551085643` at `43dae0b46f1e` passed. The compare range contains no direct changes to the Cron transcript modules, interception helpers, or chunk-group configuration. Current main and open PR ownership checks found no matching repair.
- Focused formatting and `git diff --check` passed. Direct repository-config oxlint could not start because this worktree lacks `eslint-plugin-solid`; full configured lint and typechecking remain CI proof gaps.
- Browser E2E was deliberately not run on the production Team Gateway host. Exact-head PR CI must validate all seven existing Cron transcript cases; no local pass is claimed. The original failing file took 73.523 seconds, including the two 30-second timeouts; fixed-head duration is pending CI.
- Independent Codex autoreview, P0–P2, reviewed the complete local change against `e08aa74ea39e35d01ba8e8f84e317747aba1bf3f` plus the lazy owner and bundle-resolution/chunking context: scoped-clean, no actionable findings. This was static review, not browser proof.
- Simplification pass: two module-path substitutions; production LOC delta 0 and test LOC delta 0. No added machinery or allocation growth.

## What Problem This Solves

macOS packaging always consumes the available CPU-wide Swift job budget, leaving no supported way to reduce build pressure on a busy machine.

## User Impact

Developers can set `OPENCLAW_MAC_SWIFT_JOBS=3` to cap total Swift jobs across architectures. The existing CPU-count default remains; this limits jobs, not memory.

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing architecture controller validates the requested budget before creating work, caps it to available CPUs, and divides it among active architectures. A budget of one serializes architectures. No additional scheduler or state owner is introduced.

## Evidence

The local evidence below was collected on the affected beta before porting this narrow fix to current main. Fresh current-main checks are pending.

- Existing packager/controller suite: 103 tests pass, including bounded and serial builds, invalid input before writes, cancellation, and cleanup.
- Affected tooling TypeScript, lint, formatting, shell syntax, and diff checks pass.
- Canonical arm64 app, CLI, and MLX compilation and signed runtime validation completed with a three-job budget in the composed candidate.
- SwiftBuild's worker/scheduler contract was traced to verify that its jobs argument is consumed.

prs.title: fix(feishu): let isolated topics process messages concurrently
prs.body:
Related: #72972, #89687, #96315

## What Problem This Solves

Configured Feishu topic sessions currently share a group-wide ordinary-message execution queue. A long run in topic A therefore delays unrelated topic B, even when their conversation contexts are isolated.

This change uses the existing canonical session identity for execution scheduling. Different topics can run concurrently within the configured agent concurrency limit. Messages within one topic remain FIFO. `group_topic_sender` additionally separates senders. Default group/direct-message scheduling and out-of-band control commands retain their existing behavior.

## Design

Durable receipt identity remains the shipped `chat:<chatId>` format. The durable-ingress production module is unchanged against the original PR base. No topic-scoped durable format, new schema, migration, dependency, or configuration option is introduced.

Before debounce buffering, the receiver registers an ordering reservation. It then releases durable intake while retaining the message claim until adoption or abandonment. Execution awaits the existing keyed sequential queue and the complete message handler. Receiving later messages therefore does not start a second ordinary run in the same execution queue.

A message without reliable native `thread_id` creates a group barrier: it waits for earlier reservations and blocks later topic work. Registering every reservation before intake handoff includes the complete durable backlog. Such fallback messages bypass batching. Same-topic debounce batches preserve sender identity.

The existing five-minute execution-queue timeout remains unchanged: a timed-out handler can continue running while later same-key work proceeds. This PR does not promise unlimited-duration mutual exclusion.

## Maintainer decision requested

Please confirm that existing `group_topic` and `group_topic_sender` settings should enable topic-scoped inbound execution scheduling. Prior merged work intentionally retained group-wide ordinary-message FIFO. This proposal changes that boundary only for configured topic isolation, while preserving per-queue FIFO and unidentified-topic barriers. No extra opt-in setting is proposed. Maintainer acceptance remains pending.

## Evidence

### Built-Gateway runtime proof (scheduling repair)

Tested/build-info commit: `0dd05196b1022bd8dcc3c46a91d226514cf3ad50`.

An isolated built Gateway received eight authenticated, encrypted, locally signed Feishu webhook event replays. The run used real Feishu message/thread references, real message metadata lookup, real model calls, and actual Feishu replies. Exact output message IDs from this Gateway's streaming logs were independently fetched; all eight expected reply markers were present.

This is a signed-envelope replay, not naturally delivered WebSocket traffic. The replay uses native `topic_group` envelopes referring to existing ordinary-group threads. It does not claim a newly provisioned native topic group was tested. The model was `magpie/group/gpt-6.1-sol`; `maxConcurrent: 4`; debounce disabled for the distinct backlog messages. Nonzero debounce is covered by integration tests.

The first phase admitted A1, waited for its model start, then admitted same-topic A2 followed by different-topic B. A1 requested a bounded 35-second command. B completed before A1, while A2 started only after A1 completed.

The second phase admitted A1, waited for its model start, then admitted A2, A3, F, B in that order. F's signed envelope omitted native `thread_id`; the real Feishu API hydrated its native session. The observed execution order was A1,A2,A3,F,B.

Sanitized runtime observations, November 8, 2026, America/Los_Angeles:

| Phase / message | Model start | Dispatch complete |
|---|---|---|
| Concurrency / A1 | 19:14:24.218 | 19:15:07.719 |
| Concurrency / B | 19:14:24.499 | 19:14:29.237 |
| Concurrency / A2 | 19:15:07.910 | 19:15:11.291 |
| Barrier / A1 | 19:15:11.463 | 19:15:55.783 |
| Barrier / A2 | 19:15:55.938 | 19:16:00.358 |
| Barrier / A3 | 19:16:00.504 | 19:16:04.678 |
| Barrier / F | 19:16:05.373 | 19:16:09.411 |
| Barrier / B | 19:16:09.579 | 19:16:14.559 |

All eight Gateway-created replies matched `PR194688_V6_<phase>_<message>_DONE` on independent readback. The isolated Gateway was stopped and temporary bot/provider credentials were removed afterward. Production receiver configuration and service were not changed for this run.

## Latest-stable retained-data upgrade

Official npm `openclaw@2026.11.2` was installed as an isolated consumer with its own dependencies. Repository metadata points to the canonical OpenClaw repository. Package integrity:

`sha512-SgBml4WLp8V1DdAYkrTPLzVdA/iYo3iuHCtm4788GjaG83QZdd1VeOTlue0HBJGdn3SbFE06b6uPs+AM5ShMgg==`

The published stable queue owner acknowledged three Feishu writes before stopping with pending rows and retained WAL. The complete stopped state was copied before migration; no raw SQL seeded the queue.

Commit `0dd05196b`'s built `doctor --fix --non-interactive` performed backed-up schema migration from 22 to 39 using isolated state and home paths. The candidate queue and Feishu ingress then recovered IDs `stable-one, stable-two, stable-three` and bodies `one, two, three`, once each in order. Pending: 0; failed: 0.

Every original configuration field retained its value, including global and per-group topic isolation. Doctor added normal `agents/meta/wizard/skills` metadata; configuration byte identity is not claimed. This upgrade check ran on `0dd05196b`; the subsequent heartbeat repair does not change the durable-ingress module or migration code. It exercises durable delivery, not a model turn.

## Deferred-custody repair

Current head: `426e9db4ead55b4f53653c83173e4c72fabadf13`.

The latest review found that early-deferred backlog messages could expire the five-minute adoption watchdog while waiting behind healthy runs. The receiver now sends the existing lifecycle heartbeat at the interval supplied by durable ingress while it owns debounce/barrier/queue waiting.

At the actual sequential execution start, the receiver stops heartbeats for every constituent in a batch. Abort, abandonment, and queue rejection also stop them. The normal execution/adoption watchdog therefore remains effective once the execution slot starts.

A regression uses the actual durable queue with a 300ms adoption watchdog and holds the active run for 900ms. Both topic-only and fallback-barrier cases lost queued claims before this repair. Both now retain the claims and execute the backlog in order. The affected two suites pass 32 tests. The heartbeat repair also passes its full build, source/test typechecks, targeted lint, formatting, and diff checks. Build-info records the current head. The real Gateway observations above are explicitly from scheduling commit 0dd05196b; they are not relabeled as a runtime run of this subsequent heartbeat repair.

## Validation and review repairs

Coverage includes topic concurrency, same-topic FIFO, missing-thread/root fallback, nonzero debounce, different senders, defaults/overrides, controls, abandonment, rejection, and timeout behavior.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes images being sent through the wrong provider when a separately registered provider uses a historical media alias, and retained image tools continuing with a removed credential after logout. The follow-up repair preserves valid provider-scoped migration and inherited shared-credential recovery.

## User Impact

Declared providers keep their own routing and credentials. Retained tools refuse removed or replaced stored credentials without cancelling unrelated valid work. Unclaimed legacy aliases, explicit standalone model choices and intentional local no-auth behavior remain unchanged. No configuration migration is introduced.

## Why This Change Was Made

Reuse the existing provider-identity, captured-generation and physical credential-authority owners. Selected-provider/config context now reaches credential preparation and migration checks, preserving [PR #143310](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/143310)'s scoped migration contract. Valid producer-owned inheritance can recover a derived store without overriding a readable local credential or using retained credential bytes as authority.

The credential-read operation keeps its existing reader and authority owners. The readiness repair integrates main `ac14d103530304ed29cda071b1a44131ac9b76e0` without rewriting PR history and preserves both live database-admission checks and retained credential checks. Existing authored image-model configuration now lives in a coherent runner sibling with the same function body, removing the runner’s introduced line-cap growth without changing state, policy, or model routing.

prs.title: fix(deep-research): keep surrogate pairs whole in bounded research text
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

A `deep-research` report rendered from text containing an astral character — emoji, CJK Ext-B — was cut in half when the label hit its UTF-16 budget. `researchPlainText` bounded with a raw `.slice(0, maxLength)`, so a surrogate pair straddling the boundary produced a lone surrogate. That lone surrogate travelled into the rendered report and into the portable export's source titles, where JSON serializes it verbatim and every UTF-8 client renders `U+FFFD`.

The budget is reachable through validated input, not only through hostile model output. TypeBox `maxLength` counts code points while `slice` counts UTF-16 units, so the largest schema-valid value can still overflow the unit budget by one:

| request field | schema | stored as | passes | raw `slice` result |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `sources.documents[].title`, 255 `a` + `😀` | `text(256)` | 256 code points / 257 units | yes | 256 units ending `d83d` |
| same plus one more `a` | `text(256)` | 257 code points | no | rejected |
| `question`, 7,999 `a` + `😀` | `text(8_000)` | 8,000 code points / 8,001 units | yes | 8,000 units ending `d83d` |
| model `statement`, 999 `a` + `😀` | `maxLength: 1_000` | 1,000 code points / 1,001 units | yes | 1,000 units ending `d83d` |

Measured against this branch's `parseValue` + `researchRequestSchema`.

## Why This Change Was Made

`extensions/deep-research/src/evidence.ts:66` `researchPlainText` is the extension's only text-budget owner: it backs `markdownText` (`:71`), and therefore every visible string in `renderResearchDocument` (question 8,000; finding statement 1,000; unresolved gap 1,000; source title 256; source url 2,048) plus the portable-export title (`portable.ts:288`). Its comment already records the invariant — "source passages remain byte-for-byte evidence" — so the budget was simply measuring the wrong unit: UTF-16 code units instead of whole characters.

The surrogate-safe primitive already exists here and is already the plugin convention: `truncateUtf16Safe` (`packages/normalization-core/src/utf16-slice.ts:58`), re-exported from `openclaw/plugin-sdk/text-utility-runtime` and consumed by `extensions/a2a/src/task-store.ts`, `extensions/acpx/src/pi-session-catalog.ts` and others. It keeps the identical UTF-16 budget and only steps back one unit when the boundary falls inside a pair, so no caller's cap grows and no new helper is added.

Deliberately unchanged: source `text` pass-through (still byte-for-byte), citation markers and their offsets, the 60,000-byte corpus bound, `evidenceProblem`, and the `.replace().trim()` normalization order.

## User Impact

- Rendered reports and portable exports keep emoji and CJK Ext-B characters whole instead of ending in `U+FFFD`.
- No behavior change for ASCII text or for text that does not straddle the budget; only a pair at the boundary steps back one unit.
- Finding dedup keys in `portable.ts` keep the same budget, so finding identity is unchanged.

## Evidence

**Envelope boundary is reachable** — table above, printed by `parseValue(researchRequestSchema, …)` and `parseValue(extractionSchema, …)`.

**Real engine, before and after.** `runPortableResearch` (`extensions/deep-research/src/portable.ts:158`) is the production engine whose `report` and `sources` are retained verbatim as the job result; only the external `ResearchIO` model/search/fetch boundary is stubbed. Input: a supplied document titled `"a".repeat(255) + "😀"` and a schema-valid 1,000-code-point statement `"a".repeat(999) + "😀"`.

Shipped `main` (`a1b45a46555`, only `evidence.ts` reverted):

```
status: completed
source title: length 256 lastUnit d83d loneAt 255
report finding line: length 1007 tail "\ud83d [S1]" loneAt 1039
report loneSurrogate: true
exported title JSON tail: "aaa\ud83d"
```

This branch:

```
status: completed
source title: length 255 lastUnit 61 loneAt -1
report finding line: length 1006 tail "a [S1]" loneAt -1
report loneSurrogate: false
exported title JSON tail: "aaaa"
```

`loneAt` is a code-unit scan that reports the offset of an unpaired surrogate; `-1` means none. Nothing downstream rewrites these bytes: `jobs.ts` retains `result.report` as the job result and the `deep_research` tool returns that saved report for `{ "action": "result" }`.

**Regression test (folded into the existing `evidence.test.ts`, no new file).** With only `evidence.ts` reverted to `origin/main`:

```
× keeps an astral character whole when it straddles the budget
  AssertionError: expected 'aaaa…' to be 'aaaa…' // Object.is equality
Tests  1 failed | 4 passed (5)
```

With the fix:

```
✓ keeps an astral character whole when it straddles the budget
✓ keeps an astral character whole when it ends exactly at the budget
Tests  5 passed (5)
```

The second case is the control: text whose boundary lands exactly after a complete pair must not be shortened further.

**Full extension suite** — `npx vitest run extensions/deep-research`: `Test Files 10 passed (10)`, `Tests 106 passed (106)`.

**Checks** — `oxlint` (0 warnings, 0 errors), `oxfmt --check` (clean), `check-test-lines-ratchet` against the rebased base (`Test lines OK: 6590241; ceiling: 6590241; slack: 0`). The added regression is covered by a 17-line grant in `config/test-lines-allocations/deep-research-evidence-plaintext-surrogate.txt`, equal to the regression's net growth.

Typecheck was not runnable on this host: the pinned `tsrs` binary needs glibc ≥ 2.34 and the host has 2.28, so `tsgo` exits before reading any project (the shared checkout fails the same way). The production diff is a one-line swap to an already-exported, already-consumed plugin-SDK function with the same `(value: string, maxLength: number) => string` contract.

prs.title: fix(github): recover saved repository publications
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Repository-backed sessions can publish against their selected source branch instead of the current default branch, and saved publication requests cannot recover from pre-effect outages or retained-worker reconnects.

## User Impact

Publication integrates the accepted checkpoint with one observed target tip in private worker Git state while preserving later edits, the editing index, the original request and existing PR metadata. Explicit retries revalidate the original requester and publisher; they never force-push or adopt an unmatched external head.

New capture still requires the authoritative disk. Existing App-publication restrictions are unchanged. Live Gateway-to-GitHub publication and cloud acceptance are not yet verified.

## Why This Change Was Made

Use existing checkpoint, receipt, placement/runtime recovery and transfer owners. Retained Git ancestry is usable only when its tree matches the saved input. Hold the editing reservation during input capture, admit retained compute before reconnect, and keep later merge work private. Background ref fetching does not delay activation; failure receipts retain bounded safe transport facts, not command output.

No database schema or existing protocol-version change. The node feature uses the existing workspace-result capability, absent from stable v2026.11.1. Restored-transfer custody and intentional App-publication prohibition remain.

Review repairs give the native merge test one canonical Vitest owner, sort registrations, update RPC requester assertions, extract unchanged native transfer types to remove an import cycle, and register reopening writes under their existing publication authority owner. No transfer algorithm change was added by these review repairs.

## Evidence

**Fresh restored-checkout qualification:** 212 tests across six files pass: writer guard 104, canonical project configuration 33, CLI ownership 11, and requester/native merge/sessions.github suites 64. Runtime prerequisite build, zero-cycle Madge/import checks and database-worker ratchet pass. Inspected dependency/executable targets remain task-local; no shared dependency installation was repaired or adopted.

**Authority qualification:** fresh real core-owner cases cover allowed publication, revoked original requester and reassigned placement. Allowed execution reaches a loopback sink; denied cases stop before credential/network effects. The credential/provider callbacks are synthetic. This is production core-owner qualification, not live private-provider acceptance or one fused production worker/provider execution.

**Earlier source-equivalent evidence, with custody limits:**

- Original source-ref destination and same-key retry regressions were reported red on the pinned base. Real Git plus Gateway HTTP transfer exercised retained-history reconstruction, nonmatching-history refusal, unchanged HEAD/index/later edits and transfer custody. The managed-merge regression covered upstream changes, original retry identity, lost-push-response reconciliation and unchanged checkpoint/PR body.
- Stable `v2026.11.1` production-store replay was reported: a fixture-seeded row written through the stable owner was moved into isolated current state and read/retried with original IDs, digest and checkpoint retained. This qualifies a stored-row path, not a deployed Gateway upgrade; GitHub transport remained fixture-owned.
- Reported 50 native/recovery/workflow and 42 publication tests, targeted lint/format/typechecks, plus a conflict-free current-base test-line composition with 21 lines of slack. The repair adds exactly 156 allocated regression lines; shared scalar unchanged. Historical 80-line debt was observed against an older pinned composition, not asserted as current CI attribution. Earlier publication-suite timeouts remain unresolved; passing replay is not a root-cause fix.
- Independent P0–P3 reviews were reported clean within their selected scope but disclosed omitted security-sensitive material and no reviewer execution. They are not represented as complete proof of omitted authority context. Fresh coverage reconciliation remains separate from current exact-head CI and hosted review.

**Verified native publication:** reviewed checkout loss occurred before remote dispatch. Its four signed repair commits survived and were restored unchanged. The documented scoped full-checkout workflow published exact head `7a4185da18076093594a8122005d1bc8bc483aa0`, preserving the original four-commit parent chain with `PUSH_REPLACED_HOSTED_ANCESTRY=false`. Complete GitHub readback verifies tree `e94af85375308b589cd8f14dd2629047c2a3db18` (66,732 entries), all 11 changed blobs, all four valid signatures, human coauthor credit and unchanged original PR metadata. Native review/correction preparation, prepare-push and post-push review refresh completed; no merge was attempted.

**Remaining limits:** old raw logs, stable fixture and independent-review artifacts were not recovered. Earlier results above are source-equivalent reports, not fresh execution. Full declaration build, typecheck/lint/format and stable replay were not repeated in the restored checkout; fresh exact-head CI supplies only what its actual completed jobs establish. Earlier full build preceded a final validation correction and emitted an unchanged advisory chat-boot budget warning. No real model turn, cloud provisioning/reconnect or product-owned live GitHub publication was run. Maintainer-tool branch publication is not proof of runtime recovery acceptance.

prs.title: fix(android): stop media downloads when their caller is canceled
prs.body:
Fixes #195635

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: canceled Android attachment loads keep their HTTP request running until the network timeout instead of stopping with the caller.

## User Impact

User impact: leaving or canceling an attachment load promptly releases its active download, without waiting for the existing timeout. No configuration or migration is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

Keep HTTP-call cancellation attached throughout the ticketed download, including response-body reads, while preserving response closure, playback retries, and existing authentication, redirect, MIME, and size limits.

This applies the exact patch from [the corrected contributor commit](https://github.com/saariuslystoned/openclaw/commit/6c09cd9a0f97bc42e743508ac67bc6c3b2a78149), not a later branch head.

## Evidence

- The regression uses a real stalled-header HTTP request, checks immediate call cancellation and bounded coroutine completion, then verifies a subsequent download succeeds.
- @saariuslystoned reports passing `:app:testPlayDebugUnitTest`, `:app:ktlintCheck`, and `:app:assemblePlayDebug`, plus verification on a Pixel 10 Pro XL. These checks were not independently rerun here; this environment has neither Java nor adb.
- The applied patch matches the corrected commit’s stable patch ID, and the complete resulting Android tree matches that commit. Android sources and relevant build/code-generation inputs are equivalent on the refreshed base; shared localization changes affect Apple entries only, and the package-script change affects a Windows test command only.
- Fresh source/simplification review and independent review found no actionable correctness defects; `git diff --check` passes.
- Coverage limits: the new cancellation regression stalls response headers, not a response-body read. No separate stalled-body caller-cancellation test, thirdParty validation result, or red-on-base execution was supplied. There are no layout changes.

Contributed by @saariuslystoned. ☁️

## Work sessions

Linked for team reference; these sessions aren’t public.

prs.title: fix(muse): allow slow starts without missing-install errors
prs.body:
Fixes #195521

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: Muse startup on a busy host or a large local store could fail after 30 seconds with misleading install/sign-in guidance. Startup cancellation also failed to reach chat acquisition, could interrupt another caller sharing the starting host, and lost non-Error cancellation reasons.

## User Impact

Muse has up to 120 seconds to initialize, and catalog reads allow that window plus 30 seconds. Startup deadlines report a timeout rather than suggesting a reinstall. Canceling a chat or catalog wait preserves that caller's reason without aborting another live waiter. The starting host is stopped when its last waiter cancels. A genuinely stalled startup takes longer to fail. No configuration change or migration is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

Keep host startup ownership in the existing Muse pool: forward the turn signal, race each caller's wait independently, and track live waiters before aborting shared startup. Reuse the existing SDK abort helper. The catalog owner exports its deadline derived from the startup limit. Test gates stay under the suite cleanup owner, with named pipes on Windows.

The supplied timeout fix and prior test-directory cleanup are retained. Main was integrated only to resolve an actual import conflict, preserving upstream Muse usage reporting; the reviewed base is `e08aa74ea39e35d01ba8e8f84e317747aba1bf3f`.

## Evidence

- [Contributor-reported live proof by @saariuslystoned](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/195548#issuecomment-6731114716) exercises the earlier timeout fix with delayed Muse startup: main +40s failed after 33s with misleading guidance; the fix's no-delay control succeeded in 18s; +40s succeeded in 48s; +130s failed after 124s with the correct 120-second timeout. These are the contributor's runs, not RoboClaw's, and do not validate this cancellation follow-up.
- Added production-boundary regressions for canceling chat during host startup and retrying, one canceled waiter alongside a surviving shared-startup waiter (one host spawn), and exact Error/string/object cancellation reasons. Tests drive the existing fake MSP process and actual harness/pool rather than mocking acquisition.
- The Muse production leaf typecheck (`node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p extensions/muse/tsconfig.json`) passed after correcting a possibly-undefined mutable entry capture in the startup callback. Targeted formatting, extension lint (0 warnings/errors), and staged whitespace checks passed. The staged test-line ratchet passed with the original 50-line allocation plus an explicit 83-line allocation for the cancellation regressions and portable startup gate.
- Independent source-only Auto Review (OpenClaw engine, `openai/gpt-6.1-sol`, P0–P2) reviewed the eight-file diff and full affected sources. Its actionable Windows socket finding was fixed with a named-pipe gate and statically rechecked; it reported no other actionable P0–P2 findings. This is not runtime proof.
- **Remaining coverage gaps:** focused automated tests, red/green execution, and Windows execution have not run here because no approved secretless fork runner is available; contributor code was not executed locally. The static production leaf excludes test files, so test-file typechecking remains a coverage gap. Delayed catalog discovery and the new cancellation scenarios still need executable proof. Prior-head CI does not validate these changes; updated-head CI is required.

Contributed by @saariuslystoned (Bobby Bones). ☁️

Co-Authored-By: Bobby Bones <159389674+saariuslystoned@users.noreply.github.com>

## Summary
- Adds `tools.toolSearch.maxResultChars` (`number | "auto"`) to configure the pre-wrapper character budget for network-sourced Tool Search control results (`renderToolSearchControlText` in `src/agents/tool-search-control-result.ts`).
- Preserves the existing `20,000`-character default (`19,988` characters + `\n[truncated]`) when `tools.toolSearch.maxResultChars` is unset.
- Supports `"auto"` to scale with the active model's live tool-result cap (`resolveLiveToolResultMaxChars`) minus the external-content wrapper overhead, and clamps explicit numeric limits at or under the active model's live tool-result budget so wrapped results are never cut mid-marker by the outer tool-result guard.
- Consciously raises the `core` config baseline count budget in `docs/.generated/config-baseline.counts.json` by +1 (`2638` -> `2639`) and updates `docs/.generated/config-baseline.sha256` for the new `tools.toolSearch.maxResultChars` setting requested in #194857.

## What Problem This Solves
Network-sourced Tool Search (`dispatch_action` / `call_tool` and Code Mode) control results were hardcoded to truncate at `20,000` characters (`19,988` characters + `\n[truncated]`) in `renderToolSearchControlText` (`src/agents/tool-search-control-result.ts`) before `wrapExternalContent`, even when the active model's context window and live tool-result budget (`resolveLiveToolResultMaxChars`) could safely accommodate larger structured responses (#194857). Operators and high-context agents had no configuration knob to raise or auto-scale that pre-wrapper character limit while preserving the `<<<END_EXTERNAL_UNTRUSTED_CONTENT ...>>>` boundary against outer truncation.

## Evidence
- Verified schema, config resolution, and runtime truncation behavior with Vitest unit tests in:
  - `packages/gateway-protocol/src/schema/worker-gateway-tool.test.ts` (validates `maxResultChars: "auto"` and positive integers in `AgentToolSurfacePresentationSchema.properties.toolSearch`, rejecting `0`, negative, non-integer, and unknown string values).
  - `src/agents/tool-search-config.test.ts` (verifies `resolveToolSearchConfig` omits `maxResultChars` when unset and retains `"auto"` or positive integer values).
  - `src/agents/tool-search-runtime.test.ts` (`scales network control output with maxResultChars='auto' or clamps a fixed limit to the live budget`: verifies a `30,000`-char network payload is preserved un-truncated under `maxResultChars: "auto"` with a `200,000`-token context window, and that `maxResultChars: 50_000` on a `32,000`-token context window is clamped prior to wrapping so `<<<END_EXTERNAL_UNTRUSTED_CONTENT id="...">>>` remains intact).
- Verified `pnpm config:docs:gen` baseline artifacts (`docs/.generated/config-baseline.sha256` and `docs/.generated/config-baseline.counts.json`).

Fixes #194857

prs.title: fix(ui): restore saved theme after an initial preference read fails
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: the Control UI can stay on its browser-mirrored theme after the first profile-preference read fails, even after the server recovers, until the connection is restarted.

## User Impact

Saved appearance preferences recover automatically without restarting the gateway. Three automatic retries are paced at 1, 2, and 4 seconds; after exhaustion, a later normal synchronization can retry. Successful reads remain cached. No persistence, configuration, stylesheet-timeout, or permission changes are included.

## Why This Change Was Made

The shell retained both initialization readiness and the unsuccessful appearance-read promise as completed work. Keep failure/backoff state with that existing read owner instead: redundant reconciliation shares pending backoff, replacement reads retire its timer, and disconnect/reset cancel it. Existing connection/profile/context guards still reject obsolete results.

The production defect and matching recovery are reproduced independently. Attribution to the original reported native-app incident remains provisional: its original WebView read error was not captured.

## Evidence

### Real persisted-Gateway recovery

The production Control UI was served by an isolated **real built Gateway**. Synthetic Knot/Dark, **JetBrains Mono** interface font, and **Lora** chat font were saved through actual `users.prefs.set`, read back, and retained across a Gateway process restart. No profile database/storage shortcut or mocked successful preferences reply was used.

A transparent Playwright WebSocket bridge forwarded traffic to that Gateway. It replaced only the **first actual successful** `users.prefs.get` response with a synthetic `UNAVAILABLE` error. The retry's actual server response was forwarded unchanged (held briefly only to capture the pre-recovery screen). In the fresh recovery browser context:

- Exactly **1 connect**, **2 preference requests**, and **2 actual server replies**.
- Appearance changed from **Claw/System/theme-default fonts** to **Knot/Dark/JetBrains Mono/Lora**, without reconnecting.
- Both preference values were asserted in application state. Computed body and chat-preview fonts were asserted independently; both webfaces loaded successfully.
- Gateway-served production entry bytes matched the local built asset (SHA-256 `725308ab29aa3142165aa7947265a0e98cebe1035f1a51f403f64b69b8a5b039`).
- Real-Gateway scenario: **13.05 s**. Combined real-Gateway + committed bundled-browser recovery proof: **2 passed**, 65.75 s Vitest / 67.97 s wrapper wall time, including setup/build work. These are focused scenarios, not a full-suite pass.

**Before recovery** — the first read failed; the real retry reply is held for this capture.

![Before recovery: Claw and System with theme-default interface and chat fonts](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/1a259c14-989d-4f79-beda-dc450a8f6c7f)

**After recovery** — the unchanged real server reply restores all four saved preferences on the same connection.

![After recovery: Knot and Dark with JetBrains Mono interface and Lora chat fonts](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/4f127fcf-3a21-4036-8159-93f0637b5315)

### Regression, checks, and review

- **Original red → green, bundled UI:** one synthetic initial read failure leaves the unmodified base on Claw/System with no second read; the fixed production UI retries without reconnecting. The existing primary regression now also asserts both saved font preferences and actual computed typography instead of adding a duplicate recovery scenario.
- **Owner/consumer coverage:** original six-file run: 85 tests passed. Current changed owner suite: **48 passed**, 0.98 s Vitest / 3.01 s wrapper wall time, including rejected/protocol-valid `no_durable_identity` recovery, paced exhaustion, later synchronization, deduplication, and retirement.
- **Test contract repair:** the initial CI test-type failure was PR-caused: an accent-shaped inferred mock reply rejected valid replies. The fixture now uses the real `UsersPrefsGetResult` union; no cast or fabricated entries were added. Both `test/tsconfig/tsconfig.core.test.ui-app.json` and `test/tsconfig/tsconfig.core.test.ui-e2e.json` pass.
- **Other checks:** targeted lint/format, `git diff --check`, and staged test-line ratchet passed. Original UI production typecheck/controller-guard proof remains valid: production code is unchanged by this evidence follow-up. Runtime and production UI builds completed; the UI size report emitted small gzip-budget warnings, not a claimed clean size-budget result.
- **Fresh independent review:** Auto Review, OpenClaw engine / GPT-6.1 Sol, complete updated local candidate against `f0493786e0284f3231ff34358a69d96729ee0f97`, P0–P2: **scoped-clean, no findings**. This is scoped code review, not a whole-repository review or independent replay of test execution.
- **Limits:** Chromium/real-Gateway recovery is proven; native macOS/WebKit and original-incident attribution are still not claimed. The initial failing external read is deliberately injected, not a captured original incident.

<details>
<summary>CI attribution, earlier browser-suite investigation, and change cost</summary>

Initial-head CI at `239fa7d5119c0ad911ee95db80ecbb165c8403be` was not green. The [PR-caused test-type error](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/42560085114/job/128975582165) is repaired and both affected test-type leaves pass locally. No claim is made that CI on the updated head is green.

Other initial-head browser failures were investigated separately rather than relabeled by job name:

- Cron's initial-roster failure matches the same test/signature in [scheduled main](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/42556669675/job/128964187118); [PR job](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/42560085114/job/128974787649).
- Native-plugin Built-in 1280 composer-footer `separated=false` matches [scheduled main](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/42556669675/job/128964187055); [PR job](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/42560085114/job/128974787572).
- Three omitted-image variants and the compact subagent-waiting summary failure reproduced in a bounded unchanged-production-base comparison (45.92 s): matching visible-image timeout and summary `getAttribute` timeout signatures.
- **Still unconfirmed:** cron history-processing's duplicate-history-request failure. The bounded base replay passed; main's same test had a different navigation-wait timeout. This individual failure is not conclusively attributed to baseline.

The earlier full theme-boot run also had four intermittent hidden-transcript startup timeouts (1440 px light/dark saved, 1440 px dark/system saved, 390 px light/dark saved, and 390 px light/system unsaved). An unchanged-base run reproduced the same timeout in two cases (1440 px dark/light saved and dark/system saved), not conclusive attribution for every variant. Full patched run: 70.40 s; baseline comparison: 46.88 s. The recovery scenario uses Appearance independently of transcript positioning.

Simplification: no additional read owner or global polling loop; production +32 net lines. The exact **174-line test allocation** covers distinct recovery/lifecycle, protocol typing, font restoration, and browser-transport regressions. The standalone real-Gateway capture script and generated media remain proof artifacts, not additional committed duplicate test scaffolding.

</details>

Contributor credit: Jacqueline Henriksen — original RCA and reproduction.

prs.title: fix(gateway): avoid unnecessary cold-start initialization
prs.body:
Related: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/192547

## What Problem This Solves

Constrained ARM64 Gateways can pass health checks and still run out of memory before completing a model turn. This change removes optional runtime initialization from startup and request preparation, and reduces the source text retained by runtime module loaders.

## User Impact

Headless Gateways with `gateway.controlUi.enabled: false` defer browser-oriented prewarming and initial full provider discovery until needed. Default Control UI startup stays eager. Provider scope, authentication, tool authority and public SDK contracts are preserved. Remote catalog updates retain deferred discovery until demanded; repeated scoped model-picker reads reuse captured discovery.

Workspace templates load only for eligible sandboxes. Optional session-display warming is skipped headless while materialization, readiness and real reads remain intact. Pure lease-error and computer-frame bookkeeping stay separate from heavy schema and tool loading. Sandbox/media context, broker Execa and compaction load through existing demand owners.

Session-patch publication is separated from maintenance, archive and transcript imports. Gateway turns avoid loading the local CLI owner and broad session barrel; local/system command admission, transactions and cleanup remain with their existing owners.

The build change shortens local identifiers in unified Node output while preserving module-origin labels and top-level names. Standalone runtime process bundles are minified with function and class names preserved. Declaration-only output is unchanged. No new configuration option is added.

When automatic cron is disabled, startup and explicit refresh now borrow the database worker only for finite reconciliation. The host keeps its subscriptions, startup recovery and manual runs. Enabled schedulers retain their timer lease, and shutdown joins an accepted disabled borrow before releasing it. This removes permanent idle retention; it is not a measured RAM or runtime acceptance claim.

**Strict ARM64 acceptance remains unresolved. Source-size reductions are not measured RAM savings.**

## Evidence

Candidate: `82429b60c4c9216da2d9fab56dbe29b5472bb2a3`, tree `6c7dff3a688574dd17c693a377e22f3c98ea6b56`. This signed incremental fix follows `15e32b03`, which integrated frozen main `dec19a6a` for the reported PR conflict.

- The real disabled-cron regression fails on `15e32b03`: its native worker remains alive under repeated critical-memory notifications before service stop. With the fix, the worker exits and a subsequent public manual run succeeds (2.11 seconds). A second regression holds an actual native command, stops the service, proves drainage waits, forwards the request and verifies joined cleanup with no subsequent scheduler dispatch.
- All four lifecycle cases passed, including the existing enabled-scheduler cases. Selected startup-recovery, manual due/force/timeout, row/config refresh, worker enablement and Gateway lazy-stop siblings passed across six files. Final targeted lint, cron typecheck, formatting and diff checks passed. The native test-line ratchet passed with five lines spare; the two native lifecycle regressions have an exact 162-line allocation, with the shared scalar unchanged. Source checks used host Node 26.13.0 and the native wrapper's configured Bun runner.
- Fresh independent source review found no blocker. Required local ClawSweeper reviewed exact range `15e32b03..82429b60` and all three changed files, finding no actionable source issue. Its result was **inconclusive / medium / neutral** because its read-only sandbox could not execute tests or lint. The writable focused checks above passed separately; the local report is not represented as a clean runtime validation.
- Prior `15e32b03` evidence remains labeled to that head: 422 local tests across 21 files, one skipped test; qualified ARM64 build and all static artifact gates passed. Its normal constrained primary still failed service OOM after health, with 6 hierarchical OOM events and 1 kill. No real reply or soak passed; conditional 512 MiB was skipped and owned resources closed. Those artifacts do not qualify this new head.
- The minification regression and its original scoped review remain valid for unchanged build code: B7's 751-byte output exceeded the 600-byte bound after behavior checks passed; the changed build meets the bound and preserves names, origin bindings, relocated execution and the lazy edge. The 15e integration separately received review of its 11 overlapping paths.
- Hosted CI for `15e32b03` finished with two source-attributed inherited failures (caller-retention and a two-line baseline ratchet debt), plus their aggregate failure. Other required checks and security passed; fresh native attribution is retained. This is not a green CI result or a current-head exception. `82429b60` still needs current CI, a fresh exact ARM package and normal constrained runtime qualification.

R1 stays open until the final package produces the real `CARDPUTER_GATEWAY_OK` response, completes a 60-second soak, stays at or below 928 MiB peak and records zero OOM under unchanged 1 GiB outer / 768 MiB service limits. Conditional 512 MiB remains gated on primary PASS.

prs.title: fix(talk): pick a working transport when switching voice providers
prs.body:
Related: #195149

AI-assisted: Yes. [OpenClaw session log](https://gist.github.com/Marvinthebored/9c586bbec4eaf7eb2f14a270dc39ffd9).

## What Problem This Solves
Talk settings can retain Gateway relay after switching to a provider that is not configured for that surface, even when the provider supports a browser session. Talk startup then fails instead of using the available WebRTC route.

## Why This Change Was Made
The provider picker considers both the catalog's transport capabilities and readiness for the currently selected Gateway-relay surface and the target provider’s effective model. Inactive provider entries resolve their own model or default, not the previous provider’s top-level model override. If relay is unavailable for the target provider and it advertises browser sessions with WebRTC, the picker selects WebRTC. Other incompatible transports use the first compatible client-owned route, then the provider's first supported route.

## User Impact
Changing providers selects a transport available to the target provider, removing the need to repair the transport manually before starting Talk.

## Evidence
- Cross-provider regression: with xAI, `grok-voice-latest`, and `gateway-relay` saved, inactive OpenAI readiness now uses its own model after the top-level override is cleared. The two new catalog cases fail on the previous PR head (2 failed, 17 passed) and pass after the repair (19 passed). They cover the subscription-ready default and an unready provider-specific model override.
- `node node_modules/vitest/vitest.mjs run --config test/vitest/vitest.gateway.config.ts src/gateway/talk/handlers/catalog.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`: 19 passed.
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run ui/src/pages/config/talk.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`: 38 passed, including keeping a ready relay and explicitly writing `webrtc` when relay is unavailable.
- Stored-data compatibility: no persisted fields, schema, defaults, or migration change. The existing active-provider catalog test still verifies that saved top-level model overrides provider-local configuration; the new cases use the existing saved configuration shape.
- Live patched Settings/save/Talk-start evidence is pending. Unit tests do not establish successful real provider startup. The isolated test Gateway does not copy production subscription OAuth credentials; startup proof awaits authentication in that test instance.

A pending chat metadata catch-up refresh could overwrite a newer publication failure by incorrectly marking the prepared runtime as available.

## What Problem This Solves

A stuck or cancelled Muse turn can close the shared host and fail sibling OpenClaw sessions on the same agent.

## User Impact

Cancelling one session no longer interrupts another session’s Muse host. This uses one host per active OpenClaw session rather than one per agent; idle hosts still close after five minutes.

## Why This Change Was Made

Include the OpenClaw session ID in the existing pool key and retain it during reacquisition. Turns in the same session keep reusing their host, while unscoped catalog reads keep their separate shared host. Update the session documentation to match.

## Evidence

The base-relative candidate contains only six Muse fix, test, fixture, allocation, and documentation files.
- Replaced the pool-only direct-close test with a regression through the production harness, SDK, and real stdio fixture. Two different OpenClaw sessions have active turns on the same workspace/credentials. One waits at a real MSP approval; the other acknowledges `turn/interrupt` but never settles. Neither finishes at 4,999 ms. At 5,000 ms the harness force-closes the stuck host; the sibling stays active and successfully completes after its approval is released. The test never calls `runtime.close()` itself.
- Red/green proof: with both production owners restored to the exact base above, the new test fails because the sibling returns `failed` instead of `ok`. Restoring the session-scoped fix makes it pass. The separate same-session host-reuse regression remains.

- Targeted test TypeScript, three-file type-aware lint, formatting, whitespace, and test-line ratchet pass. The task-specific allocation is exactly 91 net test lines; the shared baseline is unchanged.
- Fresh independent Auto Review (OpenClaw engine, P0–P2, complete local candidate against the base above with full harness/pool/fixture/event-consumer context): **scoped-clean, no findings**. The reviewer confirmed that the regression reaches the real interrupt and force-close path; tests were executed separately, not by the reviewer.
- Simplification removes the weaker direct-close test rather than duplicating it. No additional production behavior changed in this review correction.
- Limits: deterministic Unix-socket/stdio fixture proof, not an authenticated Meta or full Gateway run. The new gated regression is not run on Windows.

prs.title: fix(auth): recover in-flight runs after shared OAuth token rotation
prs.body:
Fixes #195517

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an in-flight run failing with HTTP 401 after another run rotates their shared OAuth account token, including providers that exchange the OAuth source for a runtime token.

## User Impact

A replay-safe run can recover once using the same account’s canonical credential instead of ending with a sign-in error. Direct OAuth retries require a changed token; runtime-exchange providers can re-exchange an unchanged source when only the runtime token expired. Explicit reconnects and account-identity changes cannot revive the old run. No configuration change or migration is required. Existing outer replay-safety restrictions remain unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

Canonical OAuth resolution now has one shared owner for request auth, direct 401 recovery, and runtime exchanges. It omits the captured store, keeps the selected profile locked, settles sibling publication, and retains the run’s captured authorization around lookup and refresh admission. Runtime exchange validates that same authorization before provider egress and again before installing its result. The canonical source and exchanged runtime token remain separate; scheduled refreshes use the same path as auth-error refreshes.

The original fork diff at `462ef9d8d2cff63335a4b4267c45b8a62cc98a96` was applied to main `2995860edbf34e5a4d18793a118a13c273a2bd98`. The exact follow-up commit `a7c0dae964146323bb6eda2b5a1e31aab6b23af8` addressed direct retry authorization. The runtime-exchange correction in `aef09e9b865a3466641dd9ba27d4dcab66439f60` follows PR head `3cfa6cb3fcf5153c690411a3a574b984b3304656` without replacing branch history.

## What Problem This Solves

Cold declaration preparation scans and fingerprints the checkout before compiling, then discards that fingerprint.

## User Impact

No user-visible change. This removes an unnecessary preparation pass from extension lint and package-boundary jobs while retaining cache validation and complete declaration emission.

## Why This Change Was Made

The pre-compilation snapshot used to participate in the post-compilation comparison. That contract has been replaced by native compiler input receipts; the discarded signature remains. Cache hits still validate through `matchesReceipt`, and cold or stale inputs still compile and validate through `after.record`.

## Evidence

Not accepted for landing: the measured cold and warm medians did not improve. Closing this experiment without merging; the removed call is redundant, but these results do not establish a meaningful preparation-time benefit.

Focused native preparation and cache tests passed (15 passed; 2 platform-specific checkout alias cases skipped). Full SDK declaration preparation, targeted lint, and formatting passed. Independent local review found no actionable correctness issues.

Acceptance rule, fixed before measurement: compare the existing `node scripts/prepare-extension-package-boundary-artifacts.mts --mode=package-boundary` command on one isolated macOS checkout, five alternating baseline/candidate pairs, removing the SDK receipt before each cold run and retaining output trees. Record cold and warm wall, CPU, and peak RSS; accept only if cold preparation improves without a material regression and emitted declarations remain identical.

Five interleaved pairs, after one excluded cold/warm warm-up:

| Phase / metric | Baseline median | Candidate median | Baseline p95* | Candidate p95* |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| cold wall | 69.43 s | 79.13 s | 108.85 s | 216.65 s |
| cold CPU | 112.26 s | 128.43 s | 153.01 s | 235.70 s |
| cold peak RSS | 5204.77 MiB | 5185.70 MiB | 5218.89 MiB | 5224.53 MiB |
| warm wall | 6.77 s | 7.09 s | 24.16 s | 33.49 s |
| warm CPU | 7.43 s | 7.59 s | 18.19 s | 24.16 s |
| warm peak RSS | 716.52 MiB | 698.42 MiB | 726.77 MiB | 724.92 MiB |

*Nearest-rank p95 with five samples is the maximum. All 22 runs succeeded and produced identical 14,224-file declaration inventories. Initial host load was [6.83837890625, 5.81201171875, 4.87255859375]. Timing varied substantially, especially in the final pair; these data do not establish that the deletion caused a regression, but they fail the required improvement criterion. No whole-job or dollar savings are claimed.

The single changed call is not retained on main. Further experiments should target a larger share of declaration compilation or repeated CI work.

prs.title: fix(gateway): serialize GitHub publication refresh waves across remembered sessions
prs.body:
## Summary

Serialize background GitHub publication fact refreshes per discovery instance (`refreshTail` queue in `startGitHubPublicationDiscovery`) so that `refreshAll` invalidations on config, GitHub identity, or managed profile changes process remembered sessions one at a time instead of starting up to 256 concurrent preparations at `delayMs: 0`.

Fixes #195649

## What Problem This Solves

`startGitHubPublicationDiscovery` caches up to 256 recently read sessions and subscribes to config-scoped `sessionChanges`, `githubIdentityChanges`, and `onManagedGitHubProfileChanged`. When any of those fires `refreshAll(true)`, `refresh(key, true)` schedules every remembered session at `delayMs: 0`. On the next scheduler wake, all queued callbacks start concurrently and call `prepareGitHubPublicationFact`, which immediately enqueues work onto the `"Session target discovery"` worker lane (`maxConcurrent: 1`, `maxPending: 128`). Once more than 129 remembered sessions refresh at once, the discovery lane overflows its 128-pending queue and live user turns that need session target discovery fail with `worker task capacity reached`.

By chaining background preparations sequentially per discovery instance (`refreshTail`), at most one background publication refresh runs `prepareGitHubPublicationFact` at a time, leaving the `"Session target discovery"` lane available for live turns. If an in-flight refresh is superseded by a workspace rebind, removal, explicit re-refresh, or owner shutdown, its slot is released immediately so replacement work is not blocked; queued entries that are superseded while waiting exit before calling `prepareGitHubPublicationFact`.

## Evidence

- Added unit test `serializes config-triggered refresh waves and skips superseded entries` in `src/gateway/github-publication-discovery.test.ts` warming 200 remembered sessions, triggering `sessionChanges.emit({ all: true, scope: "config" })`, and verifying:
  - `maxInFlight === 1` across the entire 200-session refresh wave.
  - A session (`wave-1`) superseded by `wave-1-next` while waiting in the serialized queue is skipped without invoking `prepareGitHubPublicationFact` for the stale `wave-1` entry.
- Verified all existing tests in `src/gateway/github-publication-discovery.test.ts` continue to pass (including synchronous single-session wake behavior, removed-binding revocation, and workspace rebind replacement).
