prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes Control UI theme, preference, and agent-list requests failing with `worker task capacity reached` when background reads fill the shared-state reader queue.

## User Impact

Authenticated Control UI reads retain queue headroom during background bursts. The existing worker count, 128-task ceiling, byte limit, and database authority checks remain unchanged. Ordinary Gateway reads can now receive an explicit overload four entries earlier; CLI capacity is unchanged. This does not preempt running reads or fix a main-thread freeze.

## Why This Change Was Made

The Gateway already attests Control UI connections. Its request envelope now lends the three read methods a classification that expires when the handler settles, excluding agent and synthetic callers. The shared-state read owner reserves two entries per existing worker inside the current limit. No configuration, pool, cache, queue, or schema is added.

The production change is +35 lines because the existing pool had no interactive admission class. The base execution frame exposes the classification without importing Gateway types into the database reader. The 183-line regression allocation covers real worker/RPC saturation, caller isolation, and expiration in two tests.

## Evidence

- Exact-parent regression fails at the first `themes.list` success assertion; the fix passes all three real handlers under a 128-read SQL burst.
- Six focused files / 80 tests passed. New regression test time: 4.357 seconds; its cold compilation-inclusive invocation took 61.79 seconds.
- Matched Linux real-Gateway probes with a signed Control UI WebSocket: baseline failed all 15 UI reads across five saturated bursts; candidate passed all 15 (106–221 ms). Ordinary reads admitted per 128-read burst were 127/128/128/128/128 before and 123/124/124/124/124 after. The lower ordinary allowance is intentional.
- Affected Chromium `question-guest.e2e.test.ts` passed after the import repair: one test, 3.756 seconds; invocation 57.20 seconds.
- `pnpm check:changed --staged` completed. One test-only brace formatting error was corrected and targeted lint passed. All remaining stages passed except the inherited changelog gate described below.
- CI exposed a type-inclusive Madge cycle. Fixed by projecting the live classification through the existing base execution frame; the exact Madge check now reports zero cycles. Nineteen affected tests, targeted core typecheck, and lint passed.
- CI also exposed a stale source-lifetime pool fixture that deliberately threw for its unconfigured snapshot method. The failure reproduced locally; an explicit idle snapshot fixes it, with all 33 tests across the three fixture consumers passing. Production behavior is unchanged.
- Codex autoreview through P2 is scoped-clean for the complete policy/import repair and the subsequent test-only fixture repair; no actionable findings.

Three clean adjacent real-Gateway pairs used a synthetic 35.196 GiB agent database with 5,000 sessions and a btrfs workspace containing 62,000 files / 1.14 GB. A local deterministic model fixture drives the real Gateway/session/tool paths, with 20-second child responses, child concurrency eight, and interactive concurrency four. Each run spawned 15 native children with managed worktrees, sent 40 interactive messages, and issued 123 signed Control UI read requests. All children, expected visible replies, UI reads, worktree deletions, and Gateway exits passed. Production hashes match final head `7f1df6a424730d2ca1170dbc573c12617ccd90b0`.

| Metric | Baseline | Fix |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Batch time, sum of three runs | 279.431 s | 285.344 s |
| Interactive admission p99, 120 samples | 0.170 ms | 0.148 ms |
| Interactive reply p99 | 969.9 ms | 972.3 ms |
| Mean Gateway process CPU | 51.804 s | 53.676 s |
| Mean main-thread CPU | 20.315 s | 21.255 s |

Observed batch throughput is 97.93% of baseline, within the 10% regression limit. Clean baseline durations were 88.946/97.623/92.862 seconds; individual pair throughput changes were −2.20%/+3.61%/−7.30%, so small timing differences should not be treated as causal speedups. Percentiles use nearest rank; these finite samples do not establish a production tail guarantee. CPU includes Gateway worker threads and the profiler capture envelope; allocation sampling covers the main isolate. The reused fixture retained two parent/foreground sessions per trial, growing from 5,004 to 5,016 across the clean sequence; per-run counts and database sizes are recorded.

The large fixture did not reproduce the separately reported minutes-long dispatch wait, so this PR makes no dispatch-starvation fix claim. prs.title: fix: avoid repeated database copies during cron lint
prs.body:
Fixes #195502

## What Problem This Solves

Doctor cron inference-account lint repeatedly copies large agent databases for unbound jobs, making lint take minutes and causing update rehearsals to time out.

## User Impact

Doctor reuses each agent database’s read-only inspection image across jobs, including configured agent directories and symlinked state/store paths, while preserving account warnings and per-job model/account selection. Distinct session and auth/catalog databases each retain their own image. Update rehearsals reuse their already-private database images. The candidate Doctor must contain this fix; no schema or configuration migration is needed.

## Why This Change Was Made

The inspection scope prepares and owns the image, and session, credential, and catalog workers borrow its captured physical identity. Preparation resolves the configured auth/catalog path through the same owner as those readers. Images are indexed by canonical source path and matched against retained file identity and birthtime, so filesystem aliases share bytes while replaced sources are refused. Source checks, read-only opens, schema ownership, and cleanup remain checked at their existing boundaries.

Snapshot selection and borrowed-image identity validation live in a small sibling module. The session reader remains unchanged at 709 counted lines, below the original base’s 710. Normal cron execution and repair authorization retain their existing paths.

Thanks to @etzelm for the measurements and isolated reproduction: one automation on a 3.4 GiB agent database produced about three agent copies and took 23.8 seconds. Those are the reporter’s measurements, not new benchmark results.

Reviewed both related diffs: #193643 changes readiness warnings and #192376 captures accounts for plugin-created jobs. This change does not alter those policies or touch their files.

## Evidence

- Corrected the production-detector regression to use the same artifact-preserving agent scope as `doctor --lint`. Its table covers default and configured agent directories, four unbound jobs, an existing session model override, unchanged source families, and exactly one preparation per physical database.

This covers scoped lint copy counts, configured directories, aliases, source identity, and cleanup. The shared scalar is unchanged; current CI ratchet validation is pending.

- Read the failed [prior-head test job](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/42556893791/job/128964967925): the missing agent inspection scope caused new WAL/SHM files before the copy-count assertion; that setup defect is repaired here. [PR CI run 42559831564](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/42559831564) is in progress for head `7b54023f5132a4d916a5644af64788a547dbbcda`. prs.title: fix: bound reloadable chat history
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Long chat sessions retain more transcript bodies as readers page. This change bounds reloadable resident history, releases evicted bodies from presentation caches, and keeps older/newer navigation reversible.

## User Impact

Ordinary residency targets **400 entries / 3,145,728 serialized JSON code units / eight source segments**. Source atomicity, the current reader packet and live/pending/error custody have explicit exceptions; one bounded staged packet is separately charged. These are retained-body targets, not a whole-pane RAM ceiling.

Readers can move older/newer, return to Latest and restore semantic bookmarks. Search states its loaded-window scope; export loads complete history separately. Capacity/unavailable outcomes are visible. A local command after an authoritative empty-history read stays before the first later turn, including after resident-prefix retirement and older-page admission. Unloaded or unknown history never implies the beginning. Command replies retain transient custody and retire rather than entering persistent raw history.

**Tradeoff: bounded residency makes a full 900→1→900 traversal perform more pagination and rendering work. Historical matched comparisons remain rejected, with substantial wall-time and renderer-CPU regressions disclosed below. The owner accepts that product tradeoff after investigation; this is no numerical benchmark pass or speedup claim.**

## Why This Change Was Made

Canonical source/packet/cursor ownership controls trimming, reopening, continuity and retirement. SQLite and actor-memory reads certify same-snapshot Stop continuation; UI admission revalidates a fresh selected packet. Numeric adaptive budgets cross awaits, prepared bodies do not. One synchronous owner performs final prefix fit and accepted-prefix receipt adoption. Visible fitting reads commit without an unnecessary fallback/staged read, while sparse/raw progress, smaller-envelope retries and cancellation retain their existing contracts.

Accepted raw source facts and one canonical publication owner govern local-output placement; empty views, stale reads, pending inputs and unavailable outbox storage do not confer authority. Local occurrence placement preserves consecutive command order without inventing durable sequence zero. Edge-only history traversal advances navigation while preserving the original held packet bodies, certificate and opaque endpoints; actual cuts or body changes still revoke that custody.

One native offset producer supplies paging/follow facts before callback-induced rendering, preserving input/link ownership and anchor ordering. Its accepted reader-policy baseline is independent of geometric synchronization: measuring the current position before scroll capture cannot consume upward paging intent. Presentation-owned partial retirement releases dormant bodies while preserving safe survivor seeds. One shared weak derivation owner preserves exact digest bytes for fresh immutable stream/snapshot envelopes and per-source reactions. Reply-preview revisions follow final lookup facts; releasing nonempty quote bodies still invalidates their previews.

Integration uses fixed **99f4ff69c621e6cb67b10514502fb1922deee547**, through signed native successors of earlier 650/21cd/ed40 integrations. Seventeen historical overlap contracts preserve incoming readiness, prefix/anchor cancellation, mount/queue and input recall alongside M3 residency/source retirement. Navigation-only admission now lives in the existing lazy packet runtime; ordinary hydration preparation remains eager, and successful navigation commits synchronously through the already-resolved module. Incoming asset policy plus only the previously accepted 9,306 B M3 Chat allowance remains unchanged. prs.title: fix(android): preserve repeated dictation after an earlier idle flush
prs.body:
Fixes #195638

## What Problem This Solves

Later manual-mic utterances can be silently discarded when their text matches an earlier idle-flushed partial whose final transcript was revised or empty, or whose capture session stopped.

## User Impact

Repeated dictated input can reach the chat again after those transitions, while the final transcript corresponding to an already-sent partial remains deduplicated. No settings, migrations, or user action are required.

## Why This Change Was Made

Retire the existing `flushedPartialTranscript` marker on every final transcription event and centrally in `stopTranscription`, rather than retaining it until a matching final happens to arrive. The patch is the unchanged parent-to-commit diff from [`952ebb42f2b43709533a4b7bb089b5cd60eb94ce`](https://github.com/saariuslystoned/openclaw/commit/952ebb42f2b43709533a4b7bb089b5cd60eb94ce).

## Evidence

- Applied cleanly to `df13b6b8994cefe16f311f29f0301bba511ec617`; the prepared two-file diff is byte-identical to the pinned source diff. `git diff --check` passed.
- The added regressions exercise matching/revised/empty transcription finals, a later identical utterance, and reconnect with ignored events from the retired session. They use the production transcript/queue owner with synthetic provider sessions, not real audio capture.
- Contributor-reported on the frozen commit: `:app:testPlayDebugUnitTest`, `:app:ktlintCheck`, and `:app:assemblePlayDebug` passed; Pixel 10 Pro XL verification passed. These were not rerun here. The entire Android tree and relevant external protocol/i18n/asset/build inputs are unchanged between the source commit's parent and the target base, allowing reuse of that reported evidence.
- Fresh source and review-only simplification passes found no actionable defects. Auto Review reviewed the complete local candidate against the exact base above at its default P0 coverage: `scoped-clean`, no findings. This is not a P1–P3 certification.
- Remaining limits: no independent JVM/device run, no executed red-on-base regression proof, and no independently observed live-Gateway replay of the precise repeated-utterance scenario. Exact-head PR CI has not been evaluated as part of this preparation.

Contributed by @saariuslystoned ☁️

Co-Authored-By: Bobby Bones <159389674+saariuslystoned@users.noreply.github.com>

Linked for team reference; these sessions aren’t public.

- [Implementation and verification](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/subagent/4841f008-5fd1-45a5-8ded-095abd442a53)

prs.title: feat(signal): surface read receipts as next-turn context
prs.body:
Fixes #195552

## What Problem This Solves

An agent sending results over Signal cannot tell that an admitted direct recipient has opened a message because inbound read receipts are discarded.

## User Impact

Signal read receipts now become context for the agent’s next turn without triggering an unsolicited reply. Delivery receipts and group read state are not included. Signal’s existing reader-side privacy setting still controls whether receipts are sent; no new configuration is required.

Signal may delay receipts for edited messages and report the revision timestamp rather than the original message timestamp. This change passes through those upstream semantics.

## Why This Change Was Made

Admit read receipts through Signal’s durable ingress and reuse the established system-event path used for reactions, with the normal direct-sender access checks and suppression of the account’s own receipts. Other incoming events retain the existing message path; no core contract or new state store is introduced.

Applied [the supplied read-receipts commit](https://github.com/saariuslystoned/openclaw/commit/b89298b9295a6c562959f2dd93b2b317d9258ad7) to fresh main, then repaired the stale startup-configuration routing found during review. Receipt dispatch now uses the same current-runtime configuration owner as ordinary inbound messages, so live DM-scope and binding changes do not leave receipts routed to an old session. A monitor-level regression protects this repair.

## Evidence

- Refreshed base: `594190c75e5d8e8bc0471f2d7a77792f3417a005`.
- Red/green ingress proof: the new receipt test fails with no receipt dispatched against the original ingress implementation, then passes with the supplied change.

prs.title: fix(gateway): bind QR/device-key browser pairings to the shared-auth generation
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Browser device tokens are verified against the live shared-auth generation on every reconnect, and a token without an `issuer` is refused as `legacy-browser-token`. The connect path only stamped the issuer when the session itself carried the shared credential, so a Control UI paired through a **QR/setup-code bootstrap** (`PAIRING_SETUP_BOOTSTRAP_PROFILE`, i.e. `openclaw qr` — not the `control-ui`/`control-ui-owner` profiles that #118231 covers) or through a **bare device-key pairing approved on the Gateway** received a bare token. It worked until the first Gateway restart; then every reconnect failed with `unauthorized` and the UI discarded its credential.

## User Impact

Anyone who pairs the Control UI with the QR/setup code (or approves a device-key pairing from the Gateway) on a token/password-protected Gateway has to re-pair after every Gateway restart. After this change that pairing survives restarts like a token-login pairing does. Sessions that authenticated with shared auth keep their session-bound generation; node tokens and Gateways without shared auth are unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

Reproduced on OpenClaw 2026.9.6 and 2026.11.2 (Android/AOHP Gateways, two phones): `device_pairing_paired.tokens_json` for the browser had no `issuer`; after `SIGTERM` → listening, the reconnect logged `unauthorized … auth=device-token` and the UI dropped its token. The gateway was refusing a token it had itself issued moments earlier, on the documented pairing path. Passing the live generation into `issueGatewayConnectDeviceTokens` and binding browser-related tokens to it when the session has no generation of its own is the smallest change that makes the issued token pass the verifier's own rule.

Changes:
- `src/gateway/server/ws-connection/connect-device-tokens.ts`: new `requiredSharedGatewaySessionGeneration` param; bind browser-related tokens to it when the session is not shared-auth bound.
- `src/gateway/server/ws-connection/connect-device-pairing.ts`: pass `context.handler.getRequiredSharedGatewaySessionGeneration?.()` at the call site.
- `src/gateway/server/ws-connection/connect-device-tokens.test.ts`: QR/bare-pairing browser gets the live generation; shared-auth session keeps its own; node token untouched; no shared auth → no issuer.
- `CHANGELOG/Unreleased.md`: Fixes entry.

## Evidence

- `pnpm vitest run src/gateway/server/ws-connection/connect-device-tokens.test.ts` — 4 passed
- `pnpm tsgo:core`, `oxfmt`, `oxlint` — clean
- On-device: patched the same change into a 2026.11.2 dist on a Pixel 6 Gateway; unpaired/re-paired the Control UI via QR. The stored token now carries `issuer: {kind: "shared-gateway-auth", generation: <live>}` matching the Gateway's live generation. Restarted the Gateway from its supervisor: `SIGTERM 04:08:31 → http server listening 04:08:45 → webchat connected 04:08:46`, no `unauthorized` line, no re-pair prompt.

prs.title: fix(discord): acknowledge interactions during global rate-limit pauses
prs.body:
Fixes #195529

## What Problem This Solves

Discord slash commands, components, and modals can miss their initial acknowledgment deadline when an unrelated bot-global pause holds interaction callbacks. A callback receiving its own global 429 can also retry immediately instead of honoring Retry-After.

## User Impact

Initial interaction callbacks can proceed during an unrelated global pause, while each rate-limited request still waits for its own Retry-After and route limits. Ordinary REST requests remain paused. Follow-up webhook requests are unchanged; no configuration or migration is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

Applies @saariuslystoned’s contributor fix, with review-driven corrections for short route resets and a callback’s own global 429. The existing scheduler selects the next eligible request using its request-specific retry deadline, route bucket, and applicable global pause. Other eligible callbacks remain free to proceed; no second dispatch path or timer owner is introduced.

## Evidence

- Original regression: the callback was held by a global pause on main at `521bfc46880bdecbd39ffa2f67904f768ea03fe9`. The short per-route reset regression also remains covered.
- New regression against prior PR head `83bfd48acc110345682d417f2ccc12be4d0c7653`: a callback with a 100 ms global Retry-After dispatched twice at 0 ms. With the repair it retries at 100 ms, a different callback dispatches at 0 ms, and an ordinary request waits until 100 ms.
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/discord/src/internal/rest.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`: **22 passed**; 7.62 seconds command wall time, 5.03 seconds Vitest duration. The new case took 3 ms. CI for the pushed head is pending.
- Discord production and extension-test TypeScript checks, scoped Oxlint, formatting, whitespace checks, and the exact-base test-line ratchet passed.
- Fresh native Auto Review, P0–P2, reviewed the complete candidate against the exact main base above, tree `2d05174aa091e21d4fcc0e54a142082179936135`, with full scheduler, transport, errors, routes, authority, and test context: **scoped-clean, no findings**. The reviewer did not rerun tests.
- Simplification: one scheduling owner; the repair adds a single per-request deadline using the existing parsed retry duration. Whole-PR delta: production +31/−11, tests +79. The exact 79-line allocation covers the three distinct timing scenarios without changing the shared test budget.
- Proof uses real RequestClient and scheduler with synthetic HTTP responses and a controlled clock. No live Discord rate-limit test or full build was performed; no package/build boundary changed.

prs.title: feat(agents): keep absolute workspace paths out of cached system-prompt prefix (#191485)
prs.body:
Closes #191485

## What Problem This Solves

When multiple agents configured with identical instructions (AGENTS.md, SOUL.md, IDENTITY.md) run in separate isolated workspaces, their system prompts diverge before character 2,200 due to absolute workspace paths in injected file headings and the `## Workspace` section, preventing prefix prompt cache sharing at the provider.

## User Impact

User impact: Multi-agent setups using shared template instructions across separate workspaces can now benefit from prompt-prefix cache reuse at providers supporting prompt caching (e.g. Anthropic prompt caching, OpenAI prefix caching), reducing input token latency and inference overhead for templated multi-agent deployments.

## Why This Change Was Made

1. **Workspace-relative headings**: Files located inside the agent workspace now render their prompt headings as workspace-relative paths (`## AGENTS.md` instead of `## /abs/path/AGENTS.md`), while files outside the workspace retain their original paths.
2. **Symlink and canonical alias support**: Recognizes canonical workspace identity when workspaceDir is supplied as a symlink or alias (e.g. `/tmp/alias` -> `/tmp/real`), ensuring context files reporting resolved paths render relative headings while genuinely external files stay absolute.
3. **Loader-generated missing-file marker normalization**: Generated `[MISSING] Expected at: <path>` bootstrap markers inside the workspace are normalized to workspace-relative paths (`[MISSING] Expected at: BOOTSTRAP.md`), preserving the configured bootstrap budget cap and preserving genuine loaded file content that begins with missing-file text.
4. **Directory section placement**: The `## Workspace` and `## Directory Roles` sections containing absolute workspace paths were moved below `SYSTEM_PROMPT_CACHE_BOUNDARY` adjacent to `## Runtime`.
5. **Cache key identity**: The stable prefix cache key now tracks `headingPath` and file `contentHash` via `projectStableContextFiles` rather than raw file objects with absolute paths, enabling cross-workspace cache hit evaluation while preserving invalidation upon content changes and keeping `system-prompt.ts` within its line cap.

## Evidence

### 1. Shipped Workspace Loader & Native Runtime Provider Request Trace

Executed end-to-end through OpenClaw's shipped workspace loader (`resolveBootstrapContextForRun`) reading real files from isolated temporary directories on disk, followed by the native runtime turn executor (`createNativeRuntime` + `rt.withTurn`) capturing actual serialized HTTP request payloads sent to the provider model endpoint:

```
================================================================================
  OPENCLAW SHIPPED WORKSPACE LOADING & PROVIDER REQUEST PROOF TRACE
================================================================================

Step 1: Isolated Disk Workspaces Created
  - Agent A: /tmp/ws-a-9F2kL1/
      * AGENTS.md: "# Agent Instructions\nBe helpful."
      * SOUL.md:   "[MISSING] Expected at: /old/TOOLS.md\n# Soul\nConcise."
      * IDENTITY.md: "# Identity\nv1.0"
      * Absent BOOTSTRAP.md: left unwritten on disk
  - Agent B: /tmp/ws-b-4mN8vX/
      * AGENTS.md: "# Agent Instructions\nBe helpful."
      * SOUL.md:   "[MISSING] Expected at: /old/TOOLS.md\n# Soul\nConcise."
      * IDENTITY.md: "# Identity\nv1.0"
      * Absent BOOTSTRAP.md: left unwritten on disk

Step 2: Shipped Workspace Loading (resolveBootstrapContextForRun)
  - Loader A reads files from /tmp/ws-a-9F2kL1 on disk
      * Preserves genuine SOUL.md content starting with missing-file text
      * Detects absent BOOTSTRAP.md -> generates missing marker
  - Loader B reads files from /tmp/ws-b-4mN8vX on disk
      * Preserves genuine SOUL.md content starting with missing-file text
      * Detects absent BOOTSTRAP.md -> generates missing marker

Step 3: Native Runtime Turn Execution (createNativeRuntime -> rt.withTurn)
  - Runtime A bound to workspace /tmp/ws-a-9F2kL1
  - Runtime B bound to workspace /tmp/ws-b-4mN8vX
  - Model requests captured at mock provider endpoint (POST /v1/chat/completions)

================================================================================
  SERIALIZED PROVIDER REQUEST PARITY (Before Directory Section)
================================================================================
Request A System Prompt Length:    1,918 chars
Request B System Prompt Length:    1,918 chars
Working Directory Marker Offset:   Index 1,700 in both requests
Shared Prefix A (0..1700):        1,700 chars
Shared Prefix B (0..1700):        1,700 chars
Prefix SHA-256 A:                 b2e8a1f7d493...
Prefix SHA-256 B:                 b2e8a1f7d493...
Exact Byte Parity (A === B):      TRUE (100% BYTE-IDENTICAL MATCH)

================================================================================
  INJECTED HEADINGS, MARKERS & PRESERVED INSTRUCTIONS (Outgoing Provider Payload)
================================================================================
Heading AGENTS.md:                "## AGENTS.md" (clean workspace-relative)
Heading SOUL.md:                  "## SOUL.md" (clean workspace-relative)
Heading IDENTITY.md:              "## IDENTITY.md" (clean workspace-relative)
Heading BOOTSTRAP.md:             "## BOOTSTRAP.md" (clean workspace-relative)
Preserved User File Content:      "[MISSING] Expected at: /old/TOOLS.md\n# Soul\nConcise." (retained)
Generated Missing Marker:         "[MISSING] Expected at: BOOTSTRAP.md" (normalized)
Absolute paths in Headings:       NONE (0 occurrences of /tmp/ws-*)

================================================================================
  DYNAMIC SUFFIX & DIRECTORY FACTS (Preserved after cache boundary)
================================================================================
Directory Section Offset:         Appears after prompt cache boundary
Request A Directory Content:      "Working directory: /tmp/ws-a-9F2kL1"
Request B Directory Content:      "Working directory: /tmp/ws-b-4mN8vX"
Cross-contamination:              None (A contains only wsA; B contains only wsB)
================================================================================
```

### 2. Base vs. Head Comparison

| Metric | Before Fix (Base) | After Fix (Head) |
|---|---|---|
| **Early Prefix Divergence** | Diverges at character 2,081 (`Working directory:`) | **100% byte-identical** before directory section |
| **Injected Headings** | `## /abs/path/to/ws-a/AGENTS.md` (absolute) | `## AGENTS.md` (workspace-relative) |
| **Missing File Marker** | `[MISSING] Expected at: /abs/path/BOOTSTRAP.md` | `[MISSING] Expected at: BOOTSTRAP.md` (budget-capped) |
| **Directory Roles** | In stable prefix (prevents cache reuse) | In dynamic suffix (below cache boundary) |
| **Symlink Aliases** | Aliased workspace paths diverge | **Canonical roots unified into relative headings** |
| **Provider Request Cache** | Distinct prefixes across separate workspaces | **Potential prompt-prefix cache reuse across isolated workspaces sharing template instructions** |

### 3. Automated Verification
- **Provider request test**: `src/agents/cross-workspace-provider-cache.test.ts` writes real files to isolated temporary workspaces on disk, invokes the shipped `resolveBootstrapContextForRun` loader, exercises real file preservation and absent bootstrap marker normalization, executes the native runtime turn, and asserts byte-for-byte prefix parity in outgoing provider requests.
- **Unit tests**: `src/agents/system-prompt.test.ts` and `src/agents/system-prompt.blind.test.ts` verify relative heading rendering, placement of directory facts below `SYSTEM_PROMPT_CACHE_BOUNDARY`, and symlinked workspace alias resolution.
- **Quality Ratchets**:
  - `checks-fast-baseline-ratchets`: **PASS** (108 test lines allocated matching net delta; 0 slack).
  - `check-line-cap-ratchet`: **PASS** (0 violations or over-cap growth).

prs.title: fix(deep-research): truncate retained-job title without splitting surrogate pairs
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`projectResearchJob` (`extensions/deep-research/src/view-projection.ts`) derives the title shown in the retained-research jobs list with `job.request.question.slice(0, 160)`. `String.prototype.slice` counts UTF-16 code units, so when a question reaches the 160-unit boundary with an astral character (emoji, CJK Extension-B, etc. — two UTF-16 units) straddling it, the slice lands mid-pair and emits a lone high surrogate (U+D83D). That lone surrogate is serialized verbatim by the `deep-research.view.v1.list` / `read` gateway methods (`JSON.stringify` keeps it as `\ud83d`) and rendered as U+FFFD by clients, so the jobs list shows a corrupted title.

## Why This Change Was Made

The repo already has a canonical surrogate-pair-safe owner, `truncateUtf16Safe` (`packages/normalization-core/src/utf16-slice.ts`), re-exported from `openclaw/plugin-sdk/text-utility-runtime`. Replacing the raw `slice` with `truncateUtf16Safe(question, 160)` keeps the same 160-unit budget but steps back one unit when the boundary sits inside a surrogate pair, so the title is always a complete code point.

## User Impact

Research jobs whose question contains emoji / rare CJK characters and reaches the 160-UTF-16-unit limit now show a clean, complete title in the retained-research jobs list instead of one ending in a replacement character.

## Evidence

### Live response from a running patched Gateway (not a unit test)

A local proof harness boots a **real Gateway** (`startGatewayServer`), loads the **real patched `deep-research` extension** from `<repo>/extensions/deep-research` via `plugins.load.paths`, connects an operator client, creates a session, starts a retained research job whose question is exactly `"x".repeat(159) + "🙂"` (161 UTF-16 units) through `deep-research.view.v1.start`, then reads the jobs back through `deep-research.view.v1.list`. Both responses below are verbatim terminal output from that running Gateway (local paths, temp dirs, and the node executable are redacted).

The Gateway confirms the extension really loaded and is active before the request:

```text
health -> ... "plugins":{"loaded":["deep-research"],"errors":[],"unavailable":[]} ... "coreReady":true ...
PROOF plugins.list deep-research entry -> {"id":"deep-research","installed":true,"enabled":true,"state":"enabled","origin":"config","runtime":{"state":"active"}}
sessions.create -> {"ok":true,"key":"agent:main:dashboard:surrogate-proof","sessionId":"eb3fb07d-b164-4776-b050-95f491065e05","entry":{"sessionId":"eb ...
list(before) -> {"version":1,"sessionId":"eb3fb07d-b164-4776-b050-95f491065e05","incarnation":"b567689fc9af9425b65bce6db3e8fc985a819eed5a3d54af7811d10cdab942ab","jobs":[]}
```

**GREEN — patched code (`truncateUtf16Safe`).** `start` accepts the boundary question and the returned job title is 159 `x` characters (the astral character is dropped whole):

```text
start -> {"version":1,"sessionId":"eb3fb07d-b164-4776-b050-95f491065e05","incarnation":"b567689fc9af9425b65bce6db3e8fc985a819eed5a3d54af7811d10cdab942ab","job":{"version":1,"jobId":"477fa7fe7e27d1f8c69a507fc4647636658db8d6c13e210dd6ca53a5ea212869","question":"xxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxx🙂","title":"xxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxx","state":"queued","phase":"queued","summary":"Accepted","createdAt":1794195534360,"updatedAt":1794195534360,"cancelRequested":false,"actions":["cancel"],"sources":[],"findings":[],"gaps":[],"limitations":[],"citations":[],"revision":"10d9ac3d52a805a7bb488d06697ad060c31bbb1654d5415f7ca62eff1fa721c7"}}
```

The subsequent `deep-research.view.v1.list` response from the same running Gateway, with the retained job's `title`:

```json
{
  "version": 1,
  "sessionId": "eb3fb07d-b164-4776-b050-95f491065e05",
  "incarnation": "b567689fc9af9425b65bce6db3e8fc985a819eed5a3d54af7811d10cdab942ab",
  "jobs": [
    {
      "jobId": "477fa7fe7e27d1f8c69a507fc4647636658db8d6c13e210dd6ca53a5ea212869",
      "title": "xxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxx",
      "state": "queued",
      "phase": "queued",
      "summary": "Accepted",
      "createdAt": 1794195534360
    }
  ]
}
```

```text
TITLE_LENGTH=159 UTF16_UNITS=159
TITLE_RENDERED="xxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxx"
PROOF OK: running Gateway returns a surrogate-safe retained title.
Test Files  1 passed (1)
```

### Pre-fix behaviour on the same running Gateway (RED control)

With the single production line temporarily reverted to `job.request.question.slice(0, 160)` and the exact same harness/Gateway flow, the `start` response now contains the lone high surrogate `\ud83d` serialized into the title:

```text
start -> {"version":1,"sessionId":"eccd8f3a-e5b9-43f5-b70e-bad134cce2b3","incarnation":"6ec3806b51782d642d9d1cfaf138fa66e214d23a623a6357cb34ec22d6fd4997","job":{"version":1,"jobId":"eeebd90ba5f71c1ea307daf901d40039ffaa6aedff5510fa4f21e3ff414b7b61","question":"xxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxx🙂","title":"xxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxx\ud83d","state":"queued","phase":"queued","summary":"Accepted","createdAt":1794195726375,"updatedAt":1794195726375,"cancelRequested":false,"actions":["cancel"],"sources":[],"findings":[],"gaps":[],"limitations":[],"citations":[],"revision":"ed75a65ae1a8c83cf57e502c7b62abe91746fe780be8fb345c6c18fa3097b142"}}
```

And `deep-research.view.v1.list` returns the same corrupted title:

```json
{
  "version": 1,
  "sessionId": "eccd8f3a-e5b9-43f5-b70e-bad134cce2b3",
  "incarnation": "6ec3806b51782d642d9d1cfaf138fa66e214d23a623a6357cb34ec22d6fd4997",
  "jobs": [
    {
      "jobId": "eeebd90ba5f71c1ea307daf901d40039ffaa6aedff5510fa4f21e3ff414b7b61",
      "title": "xxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxx\ud83d",
      "state": "queued",
      "phase": "queued",
      "summary": "Accepted",
      "createdAt": 1794195726375
    }
  ]
}
```

```text
TITLE_LENGTH=160 UTF16_UNITS=160
TITLE_RENDERED="xxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxx\ud83d"
AssertionError: title is not surrogate-safe: length=160 rendered="...\ud83d"
Test Files  1 failed (1)
```

The RED title is 160 UTF-16 units: 159 ASCII `x` plus the lone high surrogate `\ud83d` left behind when `slice(0, 160)` cut `🙂` in half — exactly the value the Gateway serializes to clients, which render it as U+FFFD. The GREEN title is 159 units and contains no unpaired surrogate. The production file was restored to the patched version after the control run (`git diff HEAD` is empty).

### Regression test

`extensions/deep-research/src/view-projection.test.ts` keeps the focused regression ("truncates the title without splitting a surrogate pair at the 160-unit boundary"), asserting the projected title for the same `"x".repeat(159) + "🙂"` question is exactly 159 `x` characters. RED (`slice`) fails this assertion; GREEN (`truncateUtf16Safe`) passes.

### What was not tested

The proof uses `start` with `acceptOnly`, so the job is retained as `queued` and no real model/provider research run was performed. The title projection under test is produced before any provider work and is identical on the `list` / `read` paths.

prs.title: fix(linux): show why discovered gateway connections fail
prs.body:
Fixes #195554

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: the Linux desktop app shows only “CONNECT FAILED” when opening a discovered Gateway is rejected, hiding the reason the user needs to recover.

## User Impact

User impact: the native connection error appears beneath the discovered Gateway list and clears on a new attempt, a changed discovery list, or a handoff to remote connection setup. Existing connection checks and status labels are unchanged.

prs.title: fix(infra): accept Linux kernels without PID namespaces for Gateway state ownership
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Since the Gateway state-ownership lease records a PID-namespace identity, `readGatewayLockProcessNamespace` reads `/proc/self/ns/pid`. Linux kernels built without `CONFIG_PID_NS` — Android GKI (Pixel 6 6.1, OnePlus 13 6.6), some embedded configs — have no such link: `ls /proc/self/ns/` shows `cgroup mnt net time time_for_children uts` and nothing else. The read throws, the process identity becomes `null`, and `classifyGatewayOwnerProcessNamespace` answers `unknown` for every previous owner, so the Gateway and `doctor --fix` refuse state ownership ("cannot verify Gateway ownership from this process (different PID namespace); the owner heartbeat is fresh") until the heartbeat is >90 s stale.

## User Impact

Under a supervisor with `RestartSec=5` the heartbeat never goes stale, so on these kernels the Gateway crash-loops (`status=78`, start-limit-hit) after any non-clean exit, and `doctor --fix` cannot run either. With this change the Gateway starts normally; EACCES or a missing `/proc` keep today's cautious `unknown` behaviour, and a different boot id still classifies the old owner as `dead`.

## Why This Change Was Made

On a kernel without PID namespaces every process shares the one initial namespace, so a same-host, same-boot owner *is* this namespace and PID liveness is the right rule. Recording a sentinel (`LINUX_PID_NAMESPACE_UNSUPPORTED`) when `/proc/self/ns/pid` is `ENOENT` but `/proc/self/ns` exists lets the existing comparison yield `same` without touching the classifier.

Changes:
- `src/infra/gateway-lock-payload.ts`: `readLinuxPidNamespaceInode()` with the `ENOENT` + `/proc/self/ns`-present fallback; exported `LINUX_PID_NAMESPACE_UNSUPPORTED`.
- `src/infra/gateway-lock-payload.test.ts`: EACCES → unreadable; missing `/proc` → unreadable; kernel without PID namespaces → sentinel, `same` for a prior owner on this boot, `dead` across a reboot.
- `CHANGELOG/Unreleased.md`: Fixes entry.

## Evidence

- Reproduced on OpenClaw 2026.11.2 on a Pixel 6 (LineageOS 23.2, kernel 6.1 GKI, `# CONFIG_PID_NS is not set` in `/proc/config.gz`): `Gateway failed to start: failed to acquire gateway state ownership | cannot verify Gateway ownership from this process (different PID namespace); the owner heartbeat is fresh` on every start, 43 restarts; `doctor --fix` refused the same way, also from inside the container's own PID namespace and after 100 s stopped.
- With the equivalent patch applied to the installed dist: `http server listening` 8 s after a single start, stable since.
- `pnpm vitest run src/infra/gateway-lock-payload.test.ts src/infra/gateway-lock.namespace.test.ts` — all passed; `oxfmt`/`oxlint`/`pnpm tsgo:core` — clean.

prs.title: fix(teams-meetings): accept newer Microsoft work meeting links
prs.body:
Closes #146824

## What Problem This Solves

The Teams meetings plugin rejects Microsoft's short work invitations and fails to recognize a work meeting after Teams redirects a classic invitation to teams.microsoft.com/light-meetings/launch?coords=.... The latter was reproduced with a private, zero-invitee synthetic meeting: the AI guest was admitted normally, but native status remained inCall=false and speechReady=false, and speak returned spoken=false because neither parser recognized the admitted page. No private invitation or participant data is included here.

## User Impact

Users can supply short work invitations to the existing workflow. Classic work invitations and their observed light-meeting redirect resolve to the same work-thread identity, allowing existing status, recovery, transcript, leave and audio guards to recognize the page without granting authority from a Leave button alone. Different short-link passcodes, work conversations and session owners remain separate.

**This is source/build proof, not a deployed voice fix.** Actual guest admission was observed on unmodified official 2026.10.9; native two-way audio on this candidate remains unqualified. Tenant admission, isolated participant routing, media readiness and trusted-official plugin provenance still apply.

## Why This Change Was Made

Microsoft documents the short work format [here](https://techcommunity.microsoft.com/blog/publicsectorblog/march-2025---microsoft-365-us-public-sector-roadmap-newsletter/4394967). A real admitted-page observation additionally exposed the work-host light-meeting route, which previously existed only for consumer coordinates.

Sanitized observed work coordinate shape:

    {"conversationId":"19:meeting_SYNTHETIC@thread.v2","tenantId":"synthetic","organizerId":"synthetic","messageId":"0"}

One self-contained decoder is called by the Node parser and serialized into the browser parser. It accepts a single bounded Base64 coordinate value containing a flat string-valued JSON object and a valid conversation thread. Duplicate query fields and JSON keys (including escaped key spellings), malformed coordinates and unsafe origins are rejected. Its thread must equal the session's expected classic work thread; it does not derive a work thread from a numeric short meeting ID. Existing consumer coordinates are unchanged. Session ownership and request-owned cleanup are not relaxed.

No dependency, permission, trust-policy, workflow, configuration, or production-installation change is included.

## Review Follow-up

Earlier actionable ClawSweeper findings remain addressed: login guidance follows ownership denial without granting login pages meeting controls; the caption-rerender fixture proves its observer was installed before detaching the old control. The restored short-link audio-capture ownership regression remains intact and is not removed by this follow-up.

## Evidence

- Candidate: 28d1c0659d6b6ec1ddaeb6946441694093c807c4. Follow-up base: f7b2da91097e6e575401cc9b5faef8ee63ea260d. That prior head's CI was green; it is not candidate CI.
- 57 focused tests pass (33 work-light regressions plus 24 URL tests), using the repository's Vitest runner with a local configuration projecting the SDK's pure page-script factory to its **actual source owner**. Generated status/leave/audio scripts and ownership logic are real, not stubbed. This bounded local run does not replace the normal extension CI suite.
- The restored short-link audio ownership test file is unchanged. Broader sibling suites could not collect locally under this bounded projection (they also require the wider SDK adapter factory); the normal CI harness has now run them successfully, as recorded below. Normal local extension config and guarded lint cannot load against the pre-existing dependency tree (missing proc-safe/Solid tooling and the required TypeScript fork). No dependencies were installed or altered to conceal that mismatch. These local environment gaps are now covered by the passing current-head CI jobs below; they are not relabeled as local passes.
- The new decoder passes strict TypeScript compilation with unchecked-index checking. Complete plugin source bundles successfully in ordinary and minified ESM builds with host SDK imports external. Formatting and diff whitespace checks pass. These are not release packaging or installation qualification.
- Tests exercise both parsers, actual status/leave/audio scripts, cross-host and malformed/duplicate fields, mismatched conversation/meeting identities, consumer controls, stale session owners and leave-pending rejection. The regression fails on the base.
- Independent review found a nested-shadow duplicate-key bypass in the initial local decoder. Raw flat-object grammar is now validated before token deduplication, with three real Node/browser regressions for shadowed object/array values. Independent read-only subagent review of the complete five-file change against f7b2da91097e6e575401cc9b5faef8ee63ea260d, followed by a focused security correction review, found no remaining blocking findings on this candidate. This is independent source review, not ClawSweeper or autoreview. The reviewer identified a pre-existing consumer-coordinate base64 Node/browser parity gap; consumer semantics are intentionally unchanged here and that hardening is follow-up scope. Exact-head CI has completed successfully; the separately requested hosted ClawSweeper review completed and requests real candidate authority-chain proof, not another source change.

## CI on the Current Head

[CI run 41193134299](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41193134299) completed **successfully** for `28d1c0659d6b6ec1ddaeb6946441694093c807c4`. The [normal changed-extension harness](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41193134299/job/124514087634) passed **186 tests across 7 Teams files** (178/6 plus 8/1): work-light, URL, short-link, platform-adapter, caption capture, caption ownership and runtime. This includes the restored short-link audio ownership regression and does not use the local SDK projection. Production types, test types and guarded lint all pass; `openclaw/ci-gate` is success. No workflow rerun was requested. This is selected repository CI, not every repository test or live deployment proof.

[Hosted ClawSweeper review](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/146828#issuecomment-5651874677) completed for this exact head via [run 41193411634](https://github.com/openclaw/clawsweeper/actions/runs/41193411634). It found no definite introduced defect, but **remains blocked for real candidate behavior/authority proof**: successful owned status/captions/capture/leave, and production-owner rejection of another passcode/conversation and reassigned session before effects or continued capture. Passing CI and synthetic fixtures do not clear that request. The exact upstream dependency is the supported candidate installation or maintainer-run validation requested below; no new review is requested until such evidence exists.

## Release and Live-Proof Request

Please provide a **trusted official release or supported preview containing this candidate**, with immutable source head, package version, host/API compatibility and provenance, or run native validation as a maintainer and return sanitized evidence. The local build cannot satisfy trusted-official provenance and will not be installed to bypass it.

Inspected official npm latest 2026.10.9 and beta 2026.10.10-beta.5 runtime bytes still lack work-host conversationId recognition; the official ClawHub catalog reports latest 2026.10.9. A newer host release alone is not a compatible plugin artifact.

After owner-managed installation of an actually compatible official artifact, native live qualification still needs sustained speech readiness after control returns, receiving-side nonce and benign web consultation, denial of private/shell/agent-switch requests, clean leave/rejoin, reconnect and the requested long-duration boundary. No live test was repeated against the known-unfixed installed parser. Existing isolated-agent setup and working fallback are untouched.

prs.title: fix(gateway): paired-node Claude continuations retain Gateway context
prs.body:
Closes #145636

## What Problem This Solves

A Claude CLI continuation on a healthy paired node can fail with a Gateway-runtime or capability error after its originating request ends. Detached work retains a live Gateway resolver but deliberately does not retain the direct request context.

## Why This Change Was Made

The two paired-node readers now use the existing resolver-first `getInProcessGatewayRequestContext` in the current request-scope owner. This integrates with main's `PluginRuntimeExecutionFrame` storage instead of reintroducing the former AsyncLocalStorage owner or a second accessor. A resolver returning `undefined` remains authoritative: stale direct context cannot revive a retired owner.

The command policy, expected connection and pairing generation, dispatch-time authority, and skill/run/placement lifecycle checks remain intact. There are no configuration, protocol, database-schema, or public SDK changes.

## User Impact

A detached Claude continuation can use its still-live Gateway and connected paired node. A retired owner fails before any node lookup, policy check, or dispatch.

## Evidence

- Conflict refresh onto main `f76e79be6a8fc934afd0faf1315f0261cfc4bafe`; current head `eb7a861ea7c06c277806dd2c6d0dba6b0f9c0443` also checks the captured Gateway remains current at dispatch and skill authority use. [Remote focused tests](https://github.com/ZengWen-DT/openclaw/actions/runs/40626335729) passed 18 tests across both affected Gateway suites on a temporary child of this head. Full CI and refreshed real-node proof remain pending; earlier evidence below refers to the revisions identified there.

Reconciled against main `cdfe6cf00705aa2f59dbbe8040d333cd7d597984`; candidate `2220ac4be308a06c58c1c1fc774bf8a83115414d`. The production diff is two reader substitutions, plus focused regression coverage.

### Actual Gateway and signed-node boundary

The same temporary source-runtime fixture starts the actual Gateway with an isolated home, config and state, loads a startup plugin through the normal loader, and captures its real context in an authenticated RPC. A separately signed WebSocket node completes normal local device pairing and command approval, verified in the persisted pairing records. After the capture RPC finishes, the fixture invokes the production `invokeNodeClaudeCliRun` in a resolver-only scope and repeats with a retired resolver plus deliberately stale direct context.

Main before the fix, observed with clean shutdown:

```json
{"resolverOnly":{"directContext":false,"dispatched":0,"ok":false,"error":"Gateway node runtime unavailable"},"retiredOwner":{"staleDirectContextPresent":true,"additionalDispatches":1,"ok":true}}
```

Exact candidate after the fix:

```json
{"head":"2220ac4be308a06c58c1c1fc774bf8a83115414d","expectedFixed":true,"actualGateway":true,"signedNode":true,"devicePaired":true,"commandApproved":true,"resolverOnly":{"directContext":false,"dispatched":1,"result":{"ok":true,"payload":{"exitCode":0,"stderrTail":"","truncated":false},"payloadJSON":null,"error":null}},"retiredOwner":{"staleDirectContextPresent":true,"additionalDispatches":0,"result":{"ok":false,"error":{"code":"UNAVAILABLE","message":"Gateway node runtime unavailable"}}}}
```

The fixture exited 0, and the Gateway reported a clean shutdown.

This exercises real Gateway startup, plugin loading, authenticated RPC, signed WebSocket transport, persisted device/command pairing, NodeRegistry and the changed production invocation owner. The node returns a synthetic successful Claude-command payload. It does not establish live Claude model inference or a full terminal-close/Web-composer UI walkthrough.

The fixture uses synthetic data only. Update checks, telemetry and hosted catalog refresh are disabled with the documented config/environment opt-outs. Proof code and generated logs are temporary and are not committed.

### Regression coverage and checks

- Before the two reader substitutions: 13 failures / 3 passes across the invocation and paired-node skill suites. Detached dispatch failed unavailable; stale-context retirement incorrectly dispatched; skill preparation failed its Gateway/capability boundary.
- After, on the identical candidate tree: 27/27 tests across node invocation (5), paired-node skills (11), request-scope owner (7), and native Bash execution policy (4). Existing coverage for command denial, pairing-await authority retirement, capability requirements, skill delivery/authoring and publication retirement remains active under the resolver-only scope.
- Combined focused command: `pnpm test src/gateway/node-agent-cli-runtime.test.ts src/gateway/node-claude-skill-runtime.test.ts src/plugins/runtime/gateway-request-scope.test.ts src/agents/cli-runner/execute-plugin-native-bash.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`, 85.02s wall time including the first compiled-subprocess generation.
- Per-file exact-head cost using `pnpm test <file> --maxWorkers=1`: `node-agent-cli-runtime.test.ts` 5/5, 34.08s wall (21ms test bodies); `node-claude-skill-runtime.test.ts` 11/11, 65.68s wall (23901ms test bodies). The existing skill suite exercises real node-command subprocess/SQLite lifecycle boundaries; no new per-test Gateway boots, timers, or serial configuration were added. Hosted [changed-node CI job](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/37098465276/job/111133298553) passed both files separately: invocation 5/5 in 22.88s (15ms test bodies), skills 11/11 in 19.83s (9.768s test bodies).
- Independent `autoreview --engine codex --mode local --base cdfe6cf00705aa2f59dbbe8040d333cd7d597984 --max-priority P2`: scoped-clean, no accepted/actionable findings.
- Four-file type-aware lint (`node scripts/run-oxlint.mjs --tsconfig config/tsconfig/oxlint.core.json <changed files>`) passed in 22.70s. Formatting and `git diff --check` passed. The aggregate check passed conflict, line-cap, max-lines, assertion-safety, database-worker, timeout-race, dependency, config, plugin-boundary and other prerequisite guards, plus the core graph boundary and full production-core typecheck.
- Hosted [CI run 37098465276](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/37098465276) passed on this exact head, including `openclaw/ci-gate`, production types, all selected test-type stripes, lint, selected tests and guards. The [fresh review](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/145741#issuecomment-5644398815) resolves the previous integration concern and finds no actionable introduced issues: overall Platinum, proof Diamond.
- Full repository build/check/test is not claimed as locally passed. The bounded `check:changed --base cdfe6cf00705aa2f59dbbe8040d333cd7d597984 --head HEAD` attempt ran 605.19s and stopped at its 600s budget during the broad 27-graph test-typecheck lane: `agents-root` passed, `agents-other` was interrupted (143). Remaining test graphs and later aggregate checks were not completed locally. The separate changed-file type-aware lint passed; the subsequent hosted CI run completed successfully and covers the selected global verification gates.

### Historical CI failure

[The old head's native-Bash policy job](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/34680714684/job/103518938237) reported `allowlist/on-miss`: expected `allow`, received `deny`, after 7.764s with a 5s fixture run budget. That is consistent with timeout-sensitive authority rejection, but the historical assertion omitted the denial message and run outcome, so the exact denial reason cannot be established from that log.

The integrated main already contains [the Date-based watchdog change](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/62a8182e40d955ddcd509ba977badb37ea691d2a) and the independent [native-Bash fixture stabilization in #115184](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/ce11e2e25c3b0ad6360b8c4e5bd7f17357f81c42), which freezes the policy matrix's Date clock and asserts a non-timeout exit. The local native-Bash matrix passes 4/4 on this candidate. No native-Bash production policy, test fixture, or CI configuration is changed by this PR; a passing replay is not being presented as proof of the old run's exact cause.

## What Problem This Solves

- The unscheduled-policy regression fails on base `53f72c781296a2d757e6dd1057342f1b2d30f45a` and passes with this fix; its own-agent restriction control remains rejected.

## What Problem This Solves

Signal messages lose native text styles before reaching the agent, so a correction such as “Book ~~Friday~~ Monday” arrives without its strikethrough.

## User Impact

The agent and pending group history retain bold, italic, strikethrough, monospace, and spoiler formatting. Command matching, raw/command bodies, and native quotes continue to use plain text. No configuration changes or migration are required.

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing Signal mention renderer now carries native style ranges through UTF-16 mention expansion using the shared Markdown range-editing and marker-rendering helpers.

The supplied branch also needed repairs: emphasis now surrounds code instead of becoming literal code content; crossing ranges and paragraphs split into valid emphasis spans; touching ranges merge; code retains line breaks and literal backticks; italics work without word separators. These stay within the Signal renderer rather than introducing a second formatter or changing the shared Markdown API.

Source: the one-commit diff from `saariuslystoned/openclaw:fix/signal-inbound-text-styles` (`ff2943eb9c4c3fd73523ca8b50299129099bb382`), applied onto upstream main `594190c75e5d8e8bc0471f2d7a77792f3417a005`, with the repairs above.

prs.title: fix(media): accept parameterized image data URLs
prs.body:
Closes #195618

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes image tools rejecting valid inline images when the data URL includes a media-type parameter such as `charset=utf-8`.

## User Impact

The same inline image now loads through `view_image` and image references for generation tools, including URLs such as `data:image/png;charset=utf-8;base64,...`.

## Why This Change Was Made

Allow media-type parameters before the base64 marker in the shared decoder's header match. The decoder still checks image MIME types, payload characters and decoded-size limits before allocating the image buffer, and keeps the payload outside the regular expression.

## Evidence

On Linux with Node v24.22.1, generated a real 8×8 PNG and called the production native `view_image` tool plus image/video generation reference loaders using isolated state. Ordinary data URLs loaded successfully on the base; adding `charset=utf-8` produced the reported error in all three paths. With the fix, both forms return the same decodable 8×8 PNG, and generation reference bytes match the input.

The regression failed on the base in the decoder and both consumer suites. Existing native-image and staged-reference cases now cover parameterized PNG inputs, including all three generation-tool names. Decoder cases also cover multiple parameters, MIME casing, wrapped base64, non-image rejection, missing base64 markers and size checks before decoding.

All 180 tests in the decoder and five consumer suites passed. Core and affected test typechecks, targeted typed lint, formatting and `git diff --check` passed. The test command took 282.29 seconds including initial worker compilation; changed-file test execution was 0.302 seconds for the decoder, 16.078 seconds for the image tool and 1.645 seconds for shared references. [PR CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/42559662370) passed on `54bc2fb6bead`: 552 seconds elapsed, with 4,050 aggregate job seconds across 34 executed jobs.

Fixes #195628

## What Problem This Solves

The Android agent picker visually marks the current agent but does not expose that selection on its dropdown rows to screen readers.

## User Impact

Screen-reader users can distinguish the active agent before and after switching agents. The existing appearance and click behavior are unchanged; no migration or user action is required.

prs.title: fix(github): avoid full-store scans during publication hydration
prs.body:
Related: #195488, #195505

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes slow GitHub publication content hydration when a partial clone already has the target commit but has not registered the publication URL's filter. Also fixes incomplete hydration when that URL has a tree filter.

## User Impact

Publication can read the complete target tree offline without scanning the entire promisor store for content connectivity. No migration or configuration change is needed.

**Performance tradeoff requiring owner acceptance before landing:** the already-registered control has a 12.3% higher median wall time and a 40.6% higher observed p95 in this five-sample comparison. Temporary metadata adds three local Git commands, about 13–15 ms median JS process CPU and 1.1 MiB sampled V8 allocation. This PR is ready for review, not a claim that every publication path is faster.

## Why This Change Was Made

Reuse the existing isolated object-store transport for content hydration and explicitly request the complete missing-object closure with `--no-filter`. The inventory is limited to the current tree: missing blobs have no descendants; missing trees need their file contents. Keep `--refetch` so an existing partial-clone commit cannot cause Git to exclude promised-but-missing descendants.

The isolated helper does not move packs: native Git writes directly through `GIT_OBJECT_DIRECTORY`. Filtered metadata packs retain their `.promisor` markers. Complete unfiltered content packs can legitimately be ordinary packs; adding a marker is unnecessary. Both classes enter the existing bounded consolidation owner. No additional compactor, cache, dependency, or configuration. Production delta is +4/−4 lines (net zero).

## Evidence

Two native regressions fail on parent `df13b6b8994cefe16f311f29f0301bba511ec617`: blob:none performs whole-store connectivity; registered tree:0 leaves contents missing. Both pass with this change, including offline content reads and unchanged original markers, refs, and shallow boundaries.

- Publication suites: 28 files, 525 passed, 23 skipped. Focused index suite: 26 passed.
- Maintenance suites: 19 passed, one Linux-only skip; native 19→3 pack consolidation preserves ordinary/promisor partitions, local objects, and offline contents.
- Filtered publication/project/base-refresh native probes preserve `.promisor`; removing a required marker makes fsck report 128 missing blobs, restoring it passes. Complete ordinary content passes fsck. Git 2.54/2.56 follow-on fetch probes find no extra blob-copy pack.
- Exact test-line ratchet: 6,591,995 / 6,591,995, zero slack; scoped allocation of 48 for 51 new test lines with 3 lines of parent headroom.
- Fresh full-context Codex autoreview: no actionable findings. No changed module is imported by Control UI.
- `pnpm check:changed`: all code checks pass; sole failure is 20 changelog-attribution violations, reproduced identically against exact-parent checker and changelog inputs. Introducer: #194364 / `266a7aa0fe69`. This remains an unresolved main regression, not a green check.

### Synthetic timing evidence

Actual publication owner, 13,536 refs / 1,610 packs, two shallow roots, three stale commit-graph layers, no MIDX, blob:none, 128 missing 64 KiB blobs. Local file transport on APFS / Apple Silicon / Apple Git 2.54 / Node 26.12.1. No production data. Five counterbalanced baseline/candidate pairs per registration state plus five A/A pairs; warm spawn worker; restore fixture after each sample. One-minute host load 14.65–17.84. At n=5, observed p95 is the maximum; all samples retained.

Acceptance recorded before measurement: eliminate whole-store content connectivity, preserve one fetch / 128 objects / 8,392,352 bytes and complete offline contents; report every regression. Existing committed workload:

```sh
node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs scripts/perf/publication-fetch-measure.ts \
  --fixture <synthetic-fixture> --output <new-output-directory> --contents --allocation
# Baseline adds --base-file <transport.ts saved from the exact parent>.
```

| Metric, median / observed p95 | Unregistered before | Unregistered after | Registered before | Registered after |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Owner wall (ms) | 2,007.45 / 5,146.82 | 1,271.78 / 1,456.78 | 1,168.36 / 1,248.46 | 1,311.56 / 1,755.58 |
| Native CPU (ms) | 2,260.00 / 2,820.00 | 1,490.00 / 1,650.00 | 1,440.00 / 1,480.00 | 1,500.00 / 1,780.00 |
| JS process CPU (ms) | 21.99 / 22.31 | 35.07 / 35.24 | 21.60 / 22.20 | 36.82 / 82.61 |
| Peak native RSS (MiB) | 98.94 / 99.69 | 32.70 / 32.75 | 32.73 / 32.81 | 32.72 / 32.81 |
| Sampled V8 allocation (MiB) | 1.92 / 1.99 | 3.04 / 3.09 | 1.94 / 1.96 | 3.05 / 3.24 |

All 30 samples fetched one pack with 128 objects / 8,392,352 bytes. Median Trace2 `consume_refs` drops 915.576→34.569 ms for an unregistered URL; registered control 3.601→35.778 ms. A/A wall medians 2,025.42/2,067.14 ms (+2.06%); observed maxima 2,107.11/3,500.50 ms. This is a native content-connectivity proof, not a GitHub/network benchmark or evidence of stable production tail latency. The fixture has no linked worktrees and is smaller in total objects/data than a large deployed clone.

Pack eligibility is established; sustained consolidation throughput is not. Finalized ordinary/promisor packs are considered separately each hourly pass under existing count/data/index budgets. A large or dense index backlog can outpace that bounded drain. No maintenance-policy change is included.

prs.title: fix(sessions): preserve yielded roots across Gateway restarts
prs.body:
Related: #195387, #195420

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: a dashboard or operator session waiting in `sessions_yield` can be killed as an orphan after a Gateway restart, and a failed child-completion handoff can leave its requester active indefinitely.

## User Impact

Recorded yield waits survive restart without a startup model turn when their dependency can still complete. When the wake source is gone, the original parked run ends with a visible recorded failure. Stop, reset, and newer turns keep their ownership. Executing children retain the existing shutdown policy; this change does not replay them.

## Why This Change Was Made

Shutdown discovers yielded requesters through the existing registry index. Startup follows their exact dependency chain, including current completed-child handoffs, and retains the parked lifecycle. Retired receipts cannot establish liveness. Failed handoff settlement retains the original requester run identity and closes that lifecycle at the durable completion owner. Restored child waits reach the existing unreachable-wait settlement owner.

No configuration, cache, schema, or migration is added. The existing receipt map moved into its mutation owner; duplicate checks during synchronous shutdown enumeration were removed. Production growth is **205 lines**, needed for source reachability and exact recorded terminal settlement. The **284 added test lines** have a separate allocation. The truly interrupted mid-turn orphan branch remains.

Integration note: #195420 independently fixes premature abandonment after requester notices. It overlaps `subagent-registry-sweep-settle.ts` and the yielded-settlement test table; preserve its committed-requester check/live-notice case when combining. This PR does not duplicate its listener change. #192845 separately owns delivery-only fallback after an admitted parent stalls.

## Evidence

The baseline actual Gateway restart loses the dashboard root's marker and kills it. On the final runtime, a fully drained dashboard root receives a visible, run-correlated failure when shutdown stops its child, with zero additional root model calls. Existing actual restart scenarios also prove retained-child continuation/result delivery and requester-finish settlement. Surviving parked root chains are covered at the restart owner; they are not claimed as an end-to-end live-root success test.

**395 targeted tests/scenarios pass:** 24 restart-owner tests, 368 registry/lifecycle tests, and three actual restart scenarios. Local command wall: restart owner 45.17 s; seven owner suites 245.82 s; dashboard restart 31.73 s (20.751 s test). Existing continuation/finish cases took 24.939/28.366 s. Process restart and real SQLite lifecycle/notice ownership justify the longer cases. CI seconds are pending.

Runtime build passed (1m 41.4s). Codex autoreview is clean at P0–P2; its completed-child receipt finding was fixed and covered. All task-related `pnpm check:changed` gates pass after the test-only corrections. Its sole remaining red is the unchanged changelog attribution guard: 20 historical entries, byte-identical to the exact main parent `712a3611f957`. Commit `266a7aa0fe69` / #194364 added the rejected handles without reconciling existing records. This is an unresolved main regression, not noise; no guard was disabled or unrelated release history edited.

A synthetic **35.129 GiB / 10,000-session / one-million-event** SQLite fixture used five counterbalanced pairs, separate allocation samples, and A/A controls:

| Owner | Wall ms | Process CPU ms | Sampled host allocation |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Shutdown | 12.504 → 21.148 | 38.925 → 49.648 | 848 kB → 1,182 kB |
| Startup | 122.925 → 107.078 | 168.386 → 152.445 | 8.431 MB → 8.346 MB |

Shutdown adds four required root markers: +8.64 ms, +10.72 ms CPU, +333 kB host allocation. Worker tasks remain 1/shutdown and 10/startup. Baseline kills four roots; candidate keeps all four parked, with zero model admissions. Timing A/A drift was +0.74%/−1.48% wall/CPU for shutdown and +1.56%/+2.79% for startup. Host load varied substantially; no startup speedup claim. Allocation excludes worker isolates, and these owner timings exclude full process startup, registry hydration, and workspace traversal. No production data or access was used.

prs.title: fix(memory): redact credentials before session ingestion
prs.body:
## Problem

The memory-core session-ingestion path can turn transcript lines into candidate snippets and persisted session-corpus entries. If a transcript line contains a credential, storing the unredacted snippet at this intermediate stage can leave the secret in memory-ingestion artifacts even if a later display or promotion path sanitizes it.

This protection must not depend on the logging preference `logging.redactSensitive`: disabling log redaction must not disable credential redaction before data is persisted into memory-ingestion storage.

## Change

- Add `redactMemoryIngestionText` as a dedicated security-runtime helper backed by the mandatory default credential redaction policy (`redactToolPayloadText`).
- Export the helper through `openclaw/plugin-sdk/security-runtime`.
- Apply redaction immediately after snippet normalization and before candidate content/hash creation and session-corpus persistence.
- Keep operator-configured redaction patterns in scope while ensuring the default credential policy remains enforced when logging redaction is set to `off`.

## Regression coverage

- Verify a synthetic credential is removed before candidate and corpus persistence, and is absent from rendered candidates and recall snippets while safe surrounding text remains.
- Verify default credential patterns and an operator-configured pattern are still redacted when `logging.redactSensitive: "off"`.
- Update the product-boundary test to assert that the intermediate session corpus does not retain the raw synthetic secret.

## Validation

- `src/logging/redact.test.ts`: 51 tests passed.
- `extensions/memory-core/src/session-ingestion.test.ts`: 10 tests passed.
- Oxfmt check passed for all six changed files.
- `git diff --check` passed.
- The full dreaming-pipeline test in `redaction-product-boundaries.test.ts` timed out at 120 seconds and remains unverified; the narrower promotion-boundary test passed.

The change is limited to the six files in this PR and does not modify the active OpenClaw installation or user workspace.
