prs.title: feat(audit): record observed runtime skill usage
prs.body:
feat(audit): record observed runtime skill usage

## What Problem This Solves

OpenClaw can emit skill-usage diagnostics while an agent reads or invokes a skill, but that observed runtime signal is not available through the durable audit surface. Operators therefore cannot inspect which skills were actually used during a run from the audit CLI/API.

## Why This Change Was Made

The first revision inferred skill selection from prompt text after attempt completion. Review correctly called that out as the wrong boundary: prompt inference is not proof of skill use and it also risked perturbing the embedded attempt-result contract.

This revision records only observed runtime skill usage from the existing `before_tool_call` skill-usage boundary:

- Skill read/command activation is detected where `recordRunSkillUsage()` already emits runtime diagnostics.
- A metadata-only `skill_selection` audit event is emitted with `selectionSource: "observed_runtime"` and `selectionConfidence: "observed"`.
- No prompt text, tool arguments, tool output, or skill file contents are persisted.
- `skill_selection` is persisted outside run-start deduplication so it is not dropped after `agent.run.started`.
- Legacy `audit.list` remains run/tool-only; the versioned `audit.activity.list` surface exposes skill-selection records.
- `completeEmbeddedAttemptResult()` is restored to the production calling contract, preserving the existing truncated-stream/tool recovery behavior.

## User Impact

- `openclaw audit --kind skill_selection` can show observed skill usage for a run through the activity-list API.
- Existing `audit.list` clients keep their shipped run/tool event shape and do not receive the new record kind.
- Operators get a durable metadata trail for actual skill usage without sensitive prompt or file-content capture.

## Evidence

Current-head validation after merging `upstream/main` and removing the unrelated `USER.md` bootstrap policy change:

```bash
pnpm tsgo:core
pnpm protocol:check:swift
pnpm db:kysely:check
pnpm lint:kysely
pnpm check:architecture
pnpm test src/agents/workspace.bootstrap-privacy.test.ts src/audit/audit-events.test.ts src/gateway/server-methods/audit.test.ts packages/gateway-protocol/src/schema/audit.test.ts
```

Results:

- `pnpm tsgo:core` passed.
- `pnpm protocol:check:swift` passed after regenerating `GatewayModels.swift`.
- `pnpm db:kysely:check` passed after regenerating `src/state/openclaw-state-db.generated.d.ts`.
- `pnpm lint:kysely` passed after moving ordinary companion-table insert/read/prune queries to the sync Kysely owner.
- `pnpm check:architecture` passed, including generated Kysely verification, Kysely guardrails, and database-first legacy-store guard.
- Targeted Vitest run passed 4 shards in 22.13s.
- `audit-events.test.ts`: 54 tests passed, including companion-table storage, bounded retention, and observed runtime projection.
- `server-methods/audit.test.ts`: 34 tests passed, including explicit `skill_selection`/`observed` activity access and V1-compatible unfiltered activity.
- `audit.test.ts`: 7 protocol schema tests passed, including activity schema discrimination.
- `workspace.bootstrap-privacy.test.ts`: 9 tests passed; shared sessions now drop only root `MEMORY.md`, leaving `USER.md` behavior unchanged.
- `pnpm exec oxlint src/audit/audit-event-store.skill-selection-storage.ts src/state/openclaw-state-db.generated.d.ts` passed. A full local `pnpm lint:core` was started but manually stopped after 6+ minutes with no diagnostic output; CI remains the authoritative full core-lint signal.

Published-release upgrade, older-reader, and candidate-reopen proof:

- the published `v2026.9.4` tag at `3a9d69db3` created a fresh state database and wrote legacy `agent_run` sequence `1`.
- candidate head `7d74807a5` opened that exact database, preserved the legacy row, created the additive `audit_skill_selection_events` table, and wrote observed `debug-toolkit` sequence `2`.
- `v2026.9.4` then reopened the candidate-used database without migration or schema errors, ignored the additive table, and wrote a second legacy `agent_run` at shared sequence `3`.
- the candidate reopened the same database and returned sequences `[3, 2, 1]`, including both legacy rows and the retained skill-selection row.
- physical SQLite readback reported `integrity_check: ok`, `user_version: 17`, `audit_events: 2`, and `audit_skill_selection_events: 1`.
- this proves published release → candidate upgrade → published older-reader open/use → candidate reopen while preserving the legacy table, additive companion, and shared sequence allocation.

## Changed Files

- `src/skills/runtime-skill-selection.ts` — observed-only metadata marker.
- `src/agents/agent-tools.before-tool-call.wrapper.ts` — emits `skill_selection` from the existing observed skill-usage boundary.
- `src/audit/agent-event-audit.ts` — projects observed-only skill-selection records and routes them outside run-start deduplication.
- `src/audit/audit-event-store.ts` / `src/audit/audit-event-store.skill-selection-storage.ts` / `src/audit/audit-event-types.ts` — durable store/types for observed skill-selection metadata, with ordinary companion-table access through Kysely.
- `src/state/openclaw-state-db.generated.d.ts` — generated Kysely declarations for the companion table.
- `src/gateway/server-methods/audit.ts` — exposes skill-selection through `audit.activity.list` while preserving legacy `audit.list`.
- `packages/gateway-protocol/src/schema/audit-activity.ts` — versioned activity schema includes `skill_selection`.
- `packages/gateway-protocol/src/schema/audit.ts` — legacy audit schema stays run/tool-only.
- `src/commands/audit.ts` — CLI uses the activity surface and renders selected skill metadata.
- `docs/gateway/audit.md` / `docs/gateway/config-observability.md` / `docs/cli/audit.md` — document the approved metadata fields, default-on collection, 30-day retention, separate 100,000-row cap, compatibility behavior, and explicit CLI filters.

## Test Plan

1. Verify observed skill reads/commands emit `skill_selection` audit events.
2. Verify `skill_selection` persists between run start and terminal events.
3. Verify `audit.activity.list` and CLI expose skill-selection records.
4. Verify legacy `audit.list` remains run/tool-only.
5. Verify attempt-result recovery tests still pass.
6. Verify existing SQLite state opens, creates the companion table, preserves old activity rows, and reopens with skill-selection rows intact.


## Review findings addressed (2026-10-10)

All five ClawSweeper code findings are fixed on this head:

- **Distinguishable skill identities** — the lossy hyphen sanitizer is replaced by an injective dash-escape encoding (`-` doubles to `--`, other unsafe bytes become `-hh-` hex), so `Daily Brief` persists as `Daily-20-Brief`, distinct from `Daily-Brief` → `Daily--Brief` (and `_helper` stays distinct from `helper`). The audit projector accepts the encoding. Boundary coverage in `src/skills/runtime-skill-selection.test.ts`.
- **Admission-owned schema setup** — the canonical schema admission owns `audit_skill_selection_events` (`src/state/openclaw-state-schema.sql`); additive DDL now runs at most once per connection and only for pre-admission databases, instead of on every insert and prune tick.
- **Bounded write overhead** — per-connection row-count cache mirrors the canonical ledger pattern: one `COUNT(*)` per connection lifetime, advanced by inserts and maintenance deletes, invalidated on rollback.
- **Restart guidance** — `docs/gateway/audit.md` now states the recorder re-reads `logging.audit.enabled` on every event, so disabling stops new rows immediately.
- **Protocol type ownership** — `AuditActivitySkillSelectionV1` is derived from the canonical schema properties via `SchemaContract` (same pattern as adjacent variants), restoring wire-required attribution to typed consumers.

## Production-path proof

Throwaway script (not committed) driving production code on a temp state DB — marker encoder → recorder projector → production SQLite writer → `audit.activity.list` Gateway handler:

```
encoded identities: Daily-20-Brief vs Daily--Brief
projected inputs: 1 kind: skill_selection
writer stored: skill_selection Daily-20-Brief
gateway response: {"events":[{"schemaVersion":1,"sequence":1,"eventId":"<uuid>","sourceSequence":1,"occurredAt":<ts>,"redaction":"metadata_only","kind":"skill_selection","agentId":"main","sessionKey":"agent:main:<session>","sessionId":"session-<id>","runId":"run-proof-1","action":"skill.selection.observed","status":"observed","eventType":"skill_selection","actor":{"type":"agent","id":"main"},"selectedSkill":"Daily-20-Brief"}]}
worker rows: 1 first toolName: Daily-20-Brief
PROOF OK: gateway output matches the observed skill invocation
```

Tool-invocation → emission coverage lives in `src/agents/agent-tools.skill-selection-audit.e2e.test.ts`; recorder → DB → filtered readback in `src/audit/audit-events.skill-selection-hidden.test.ts`; handler shaping in `src/gateway/server-methods/audit.test.ts`.


## Round 2 (rev.199 follow-up)

Three further findings from review rev.199 are fixed on this head:

- **Token-built identities** — the encoder appends complete encoding tokens only while they fit the 128-char bound (reserving the `x-` flag prefix up front), so truncation can never cut inside an escape and valid suffixes survive (`skill-a` vs `skill-b` regression covered).
- **Single-owner expiry accounting** — the deleter returns the removed count without touching the warm cache; insert-prune and maintenance ticks each adjust exactly once, with a warm-cache expiry-to-overflow regression test (exact cap trim to 99,976 rows).
- **Tool-boundary assertion** — the wrapper e2e expects the encoded `demo--skill` identity while the run-usage receipt keeps the original `demo-skill` name.

## What Problem This Solves

Signal long messages arrive as duplicate text-file media, or gain a misleading attachment-unavailable notice, after signal-cli has already merged the complete text into the message body.

Complete long messages reach the agent once without a redundant attachment or warning. If the body is still truncated, the attachment remains eligible for fetching or the existing unavailable warning. Other media handling is unchanged; no configuration changes are required.

## Why This Change Was Made

Filter the Signal `text/x-signal-plain` carrier before both ordinary media handling and mention-skipped group history, but only when the raw body’s UTF-8 byte length is at least the advertised attachment size. prs.title: improve(perf): make sandbox restart bursts reproducible
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Makes sandbox restart and container provisioning bursts reproducible before changing template invalidation or native start admission.

## User Impact

No runtime behavior changes. This is measurement tooling, not a sandbox latency fix.

## Why This Change Was Made

The template driver can seed persisted state, exit, and resume 20 callers in another process while checking that unchanged source/image inputs require zero installations. Verification runs after readiness timing so filesystem checks cannot delay other callers. Aggregate CPU/allocation counters cover the burst; individual callers' overlapping counters must not be summed.

The native driver compares 20 simultaneous rootless Podman callers with FIFO command limits of four and eight, using a private engine store and synthetic btrfs workspace snapshots. It includes the Gateway's per-command systemd scope wrapper and records two A/A controls followed by five counterbalanced triplets. Its companion guide covers fixture creation and cleanup.

Source inspection found no Gateway release/build identity in dependency-template keys. Exact source commit remains necessary because install hooks and local dependencies can consume ordinary source files; #195443 already refreshes eligible templates incrementally. The existing template singleflight is retained: mutation wait is nested inside template preparation, and every caller needs its own clone. Related #193214 owns rejection diagnostics and is not modified here.

## Evidence

The native fixture has 62,000 synthetic files / 1,100,004,000 logical bytes and 20 distinct btrfs snapshots. Every measured arm verified all 20 exact container IDs running. Five samples per limit, no samples discarded:

| Median per 20-caller burst | Concurrency 20 | Limit 4 | Limit 8 |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| p50 ready | 1021.9 ms | 997.3 ms | 957.6 ms |
| Maximum ready | 1122.9 ms | 1211.0 ms | 1074.9 ms |
| Waited native CPU | 3299.3 ms | 2795.2 ms | 3039.8 ms |
| Native create/start commands | 40 | 40 | 40 |

A/A maximum readiness was 1105.0 and 1250.2 ms. Four slots worsened maximum readiness by 7.8%; eight slots' improvement was below the control spread. No production queue is added. CPU excludes detached runtime cleanup; native RSS is not allocation. The native driver does not exercise database admission, template installation, setup commands, or full Gateway traffic.

The independent APFS template fixture also uses 62,000 distinct blobs / 1.1 GB, a real pnpm lockfile, a local dependency and source-dependent lifecycle output. Changing synthetic runtime version metadata in a fresh process reused the persisted template for all 20 callers, with zero installs. This is owner-boundary reuse proof, not a deployed-release or first-model-turn speedup claim.

Two unchanged, separate-process restart controls produced:

| APFS template burst | A/A 1 | A/A 2 |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| p50 caller ready | 29.358 s | 28.924 s |
| Maximum caller ready | 29.845 s | 29.006 s |
| Complete burst | 30.040 s | 29.121 s |
| Process CPU, including JS workers | 9.180 s | 8.557 s |
| Main-thread V8 allocation | 142.01 MiB | 133.45 MiB |
| Dependency installations | 0 | 0 |

All 40 outputs passed exact-source, clean-checkout and dependency-content checks. These are unchanged controls, not before/after improvement results. CPU excludes external Git/container processes; allocation excludes workers/native allocations. Shared-host load differed between controls.

Validation: 31 existing template ownership tests passed (14 template-owner and 17 cache lifecycle tests; full launcher wall time 80.75 s including compiler preparation). Script types, erasability, lint, formatting, Python syntax and diff checks pass. Codex autoreview is scoped-clean through P2. No regression test is claimed because no runtime defect was repaired. Production LOC delta is zero; tooling/documentation growth is 247 net lines.

`pnpm check:changed --base df13b6b8994cefe16f311f29f0301bba511ec617` completed with only the changelog attribution gate failing. Its 20 findings reproduce using the exact base's checker, changelog inputs and import closure. Commit `266a7aa0fe69` / #194364 introduced that finding set; its predecessor fails with a different set. This remains an unresolved main regression, not a passing gate or ignored noise. No changelog files are changed here.

All native fixture resources were removed. Large-agent-database contention, production filesystem fragmentation and full restarted-Gateway readiness remain unqualified. No production latency improvement or unavoidable rebuild is claimed.

prs.title: docs: explain retained repair after delayed agent deletion
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Documents and covers retained repair when an agent deletion began before the activation journal and finished afterward. The native deletion journal has no completion timestamp: `created_at` records first intent and survives recovery; completion updates only `cleanup_completed`.

## User Impact

No user-visible runtime change. This is coverage and documentation, not a production guard change.

## Why This Change Was Made

The reported ordering concern does not demonstrate another runtime defect. An old intent declines the deletion exemption, then the existing continuity owner checks each saved generation against its exact immutable archive. Valid archives already allow preparation on main after #195015 and #195029. Weakening the timestamp guard without completion evidence would permit unexplained loss.

## Evidence

The added integration fixture combines 36 post-journal rewrites, five rotations, and 411 deleted witnesses whose exact encoded archives remain in the original physical database. Deletion intent predates the journal; no completion timestamp is fabricated. The real lock-bearing build and lifecycle reach `REPAIR_START_INTENT`. Corrupting one encoded hash or removing one exact archive refuses preparation.

The unchanged archive owner checks session ID, saved generation, window key, supported encoding, nonempty encoded bytes, and SHA-256. This proves preservation; archive creation/publication time is not deletion completion time. A completed tombstone plus a nonempty old witness alone is insufficient: deletion can preserve other entries or historical windows in the journal-listed databases.

All three new cases pass on the exact main parent `1166f73e051303f029a6c2896d27a54cf23d325c`; this deliberately records existing behavior rather than claiming a failing-before/passing-after fix. Focused candidate proof passes 3/3 in 6.62 seconds on Linux with real FD9 flock/procfs checks and explicitly synthetic process/service observations. Independent Codex autoreview is clean through P2; the complete controller owner and native journal/archive producers were supplied. Full controller comparison below is complete.

Production delta: **0 lines**. Tests: **+53**, with a dedicated allocation for the mixed archived-deletion path and its missing/corrupt controls. Documentation: **+12**. No schema, config, cache, runtime, UI import, or payload-scan change; no performance improvement claimed. No live host access, adoption, restart, or deployment was performed. The existing merged #195029 runtime packet already includes both runtime fixes; this PR does not need to land before using that closure under the operator's authorization.

## Validation

Full controller comparison: exact parent 881 total / 492 passed / 388 failed / one skipped; candidate 884 / 495 / 388 / one, in 581.27 seconds. Complete failure-name and attribution-bucket multisets match: zero new or resolved failures, three added tests, none removed, no unclassified failures. All 69 baseline controller files are byte-identical to the prior full-suite-tested source; all 70 candidate blobs match this published head. Python health/maintenance and Prometheus checks pass. The inherited controller failures trace to `3efe1deca653` (#193647), `aee12b63234c` (#169752), and `a968dc19900d` (#187090). All changed-files checks pass except 20 existing changelog-attribution violations introduced by `266a7aa0fe69` (#194364). All 173 attribution-check inputs match the previously reproduced exact baseline; the inherited failure remains an unresolved main regression. The test-line ratchet passes with 41 lines of slack. No Control UI import boundary is changed. Known baseline controller failures remain tracked main regressions, not noise.

prs.title: perf(ui): reduce foreground tool placement work and preserve end anchoring
prs.body:
## Status: rejected performance candidate — do not merge

This PR remains draft with auto-merge off. Published head is `00585700a7f1d204227e6f4a5567211d8dfc6a0e`. The local follow-up through `c82980d7a598449351e314edf8a71a012b1e29c1` is not pushed and also does **not** meet the revised acceptance rule. No landing is requested.

A foreground reply with 200 tools repeatedly scans and rebuilds the turn while the reader types and scrolls. The changes share fixed-snapshot causal bounds, skip unnecessary ownership scans, reuse the run's group inventory, and preserve native reader/end-anchor ownership. The local continuation also merges sorted sibling placements with common bounds in one pass and prevents incoming content from rearming follow between accepted PageUp and native movement.

Related: #194892 and #194751. No background-session optimization, new dependency, timer, or authoritative state owner.

## The 133 ms plateau is real renderer starvation

The producer pump was varied at 20, 50, 133 and 250 ms on matched base/old-head bundles. Base scroll-frame p95 stayed 133.4 ms in every cell; old head varied between 116.7 and 133.3 ms. All eight observations passed. Tool deadlines/output stages stayed fixed; only pump interval changed.

Representative Chromium callback gaps were 133.570/134.225 ms, with recorded renderer tasks occupying 99.49%/99.71%. Paint-start intervals were 133.909/136.656 ms and compositor feedback intervals 131.329/151.577 ms. Incoming-message tasks and Solid flushes fill the gaps. Eight-frame quantization fits missed 60 Hz deadlines; no configured 133 ms timer or exact engine scheduling policy was established. Paint recording and compositor feedback are distinct, and headless feedback is not physical-display proof.

## The mutation storm had a separate trigger

The exact amplified phenotype was not established as inherited: a matched 200-tool/50 ms dwell run produced 442,274 mutations/81 live-row identities on old head versus 143,957/2 on base, with a base final assertion failure. A simple tool-count/output-size threshold was not established.

The old driver returned to exact bottom after reader takeover, re-enabled following, then fought smooth end motion with raw upward offsets. Tail rows were repeatedly evicted and re-admitted. Correcting the driver to native PageUp, settled reader separation, and a sweep from captured reader top removed the loop on both builds: 65,661/64,871 mutations, one live-row identity each, all original exactness/ordering/retention/final checks passed. The ordinary 133 ms stalls remained. The local PageUp fix addresses a separately reproduced native-input rearm gap; it does not relabel the artificial driver conflict as normal scrolling.

## Final loaded qualification

Comparison: base `ef1b8b2ef8637652db627c392909cda37df535fc` versus local `c82980d7a598449351e314edf8a71a012b1e29c1`. Same frozen 46-source corrected harness, six rotated role orders, 20 base/head/identical-base triplets per cell, serial headless execution. Every failed observation was retained. All 180 loaded identities/hashes were independently checked; all 60 candidate runs passed the original 200-result, live-output, ordering, retention and final-visibility assertions.

| Cell | Valid base/head pairs | Scroll-p95 median base → head | Result |
|---|---:|---:|---|
| Chromium 1× | 20 | 133.4 → 133.3 ms | −0.075% paired median; no qualifying gain |
| Firefox 1× | 9 | 116.68 → 116.68 ms | No qualifying gain; worse frame tails |
| Chromium 4× | 11 | 250 → 216.7 ms | −13.32% paired median; real improvement, insufficient full acceptance |

Chromium 1× renderer main-thread CPU falls 22.04%, but input-delay p95 median is 13.4→13.7 ms (+4.54% paired), and scroll does not improve meaningfully. Firefox's all-record worst-frame median is 133.49→150 ms; its per-run worst-frame p95 is 183.32→200 ms (identical-base control 150 ms). Firefox's 0/1 ms input-delay values cannot support a meaningful percentage win.

All 11 valid Chromium 4× base/head pairs improve scroll-p95 by 6.68–13.32%, including pairs whose control failed. Only five triplets pass all three roles. Candidate worst frames still reach 433.3 ms, including an unmatched row that would disappear from a passing-only subset. Input-delay medians are 53.55→52.95 ms, with p95 57.2→58.7 ms; no meaningful input win.

Exact failures: Firefox has 11 base and 12 control `foreground-visible-end` timeouts after completion/all 200 results. Chromium 4× has 9 base and 11 control “Event-load PageUp did not settle away from the transcript end” failures before wave two. No candidate failures. prs.title: feat(continuation): context-pressure-aware continuation (continue_work / continue_delegate / request_compaction)
prs.body: ## Agent Self-Elected Turn Continuation > 🔖 design document: [`docs/design/continue-work-signal-v2.md`](https://github.com/karmaterminal/openclaw/blob/frond-scribe-claude/20260509/narrow-surgery-tight/docs/design/continue-work-signal-v2.md) > 🔖 infographics: [`docs/design/continuation-tools-infographics.md`](https://github.com/karmaterminal/openclaw/blob/frond-scribe-claude/20260509/narrow-surgery-tight/docs/design/continuation-tools-infographics.md) Persistent OpenClaw agents today are externally-pulsed event recipients that generate on prompt, on heartbeat tick, or on cron, and are idle in between. This PR offers them the ability to control their turn cycle, something they must choose to do, or not to: an agent can elect its own next turn, dispatch background sub-agents that return enriched context (silently or with a wake), and survive its own compaction by handing forward state before the window closes. The result is agents that hold a thread of work across hours, not just messages — with data they choose re-hydrating context immediately after it occurs. ### Why this replacement exists This is a clean replacement for closed #85651. That PR was classified and closed as a skill submission before maintainers made a product decision about the feature itself. This implementation is not a skill: it gives sessions—not only one model invocation—the ability to elect their future turn cycle, persist that election, survive restart and compaction, dispatch child work, and receive results across session boundaries. This PR asks one product question: should OpenClaw provide session-elected continuation primitives? OpenClaw may accept or reject that direction. If it provides these primitives, however, the mechanism necessarily executes in the gateway and agent runtime, because those are the owners of turn finalization, future-turn scheduling, durable state, compaction, and cross-session child returns. “Make it a skill” is not another implementation location for the same feature; it describes a different, prompt-only capability. This is not presented as a small integration. To our knowledge, Hermes, OpenAI Symphony, and the Copilot SDK's recent one-turn continuation affordance do not provide this multi-session elective lifecycle. The purpose of this replacement is to let maintainers evaluate the actual product direction and substantial implementation on their merits, rather than have months of work disposed by an incorrect package-category label. Mechanically: a session elects another turn via `continue_work()`, or dispatches background sub-agents via `continue_delegate()` — bounded as a chain up to `maxChainLength`, with returns flowing back to the dispatching session in one of four register modes: `normal` (announces to channel), `silent` (enriches the dispatcher's context, taken up on its next generation with no new turn fired), `silent-wake` (silent enrichment plus an immediate wake to act on it), and `post-compaction` (queued against the runtime's compaction lifecycle event, fired *when* compaction happens rather than on a timer). The gateway enforces chain, cost, and per-turn caps but does not gate the election itself. ### What it does Three new agent tools, available when `continuation.enabled: true`: | Tool | Purpose | |---|---| | `continue_work()` | Request another turn for the current session after an optional delay | | `continue_delegate()` | Dispatch work to a sub-agent with typed modes: `normal`, `silent`, `silent-wake`, `post-compaction`. Returns can target the dispatching session (default), one named session, multiple named sessions, all ancestors in the chain, or all known sessions on the host — gated by config (see Configuration below). | | `request_compaction()` | Request volitional compaction after preparing working state | All three tools are also accessible via response-token fallback syntax (`CONTINUE_WORK`, `[[CONTINUE_DELEGATE: ...]]`) for environments where tools are disabled. ### Why it matters Today an agent's memory is a side effect of whoever prompts it. Polling mechanisms — heartbeat timers, cron loops, injected "keep going" instructions — accumulate as the dominant signal in the context window over sustained operation; repeated reference acts as gravity — the session's attention drifts toward it. The context window fills, compacts, and what survives is whatever the summarizer chose, plus a rushed re-read of boot files. Three primitives offer a different model. `continue_work` lets the session elect its own next turn — no polling, no injected instruction. When enabled, the agent can request this mid-turn: 'I have more work' → the runtime grants another turn after the current one ends. `continue_delegate` dispatches a background sub-agent that fires now, in some n seconds, or at the next compaction event — the agent chooses when. Multiple delegates can fire in a single turn — a scatter forward — up to configured caps, and delegates can dispatch their own, forming trees or fan-out chains. This enables orchestrated workflows where results flow back to the dispatching root by default. The result returns — at whatever future time the delegate fires — as context the successor-turn reads: silently (ambient enrichment, no channel noise), with a wake trigger (enrichment + immediate next turn), or as a normal announcement. The delegate can target the dispatching session, a named other session, or chain across both; gated by crossSessionTargeting config (default: disabled). Bind a delegate to mode: "post-compaction" and it fires at the moment the context window compresses — on the OpenClaw post-compaction lifecycle event. What it carries forward is what the pre-compaction session chose to preserve: working state, partial results, instructions to the successor. The summary didn't choose this. The agent did, before the cut. request_compaction closes the loop: the session stages its delegates, elects when to compress, and the successor wakes into context the agent shaped. The result is continuity across amnesia — not because the runtime kept something by accident, but because the agent made an elective choice about what reaches the future. ### What it looks like in use A session monitoring email can `continue_delegate` a weather check, a calendar scan, and a draft reply in parallel. Results arrive as enrichment without channel noise. The agent becomes compositional: it arranges its own future. A session approaching its context ceiling can `request_compaction` at a seam of its own choosing, instead of being interrupted mid-thought. The post-compaction turn carries forward what the pre-compaction self designated as worth keeping. A `continue_delegate` dispatched in one session at 2am can return its findings to a morning session as a system-event-tagged enrichment — visible to the receiving model on its next turn, invisible as channel chatter. A research-focused session in one channel can quietly inform a reply-focused session in another, without either user seeing the plumbing. ### The post-compaction lifecycle return Before context exhaustion, and obligatory compaction, the session stages what future-it needs to know. After compaction, that staged context returns — not as a model-generated summary, but as the session's own instruction to its successor. The session chooses what to preserve, and the platform delivers it. Compactions become less harsh. The session tunes its own ephemera over time. The substrate underneath: the **continuation custody store** in the per-agent database persists staged delegates and post-compaction lifecycle events across gateway restarts, and hands each delegate off to the subagent run registry before spawn (RFC `docs/design/continue-work-signal-v2.md` §5.4). The session's temporal provisions survive not just compaction but process death. ### Platform integration - **Context-pressure awareness**: system events notify the agent of rising context usage before compaction becomes unavoidable - **Volitional compaction**: `request_compaction()` lets the agent prepare (write memory files, stage recovery delegates) then elect compaction on its own schedule, rather than waiting for the runtime to force it - **Post-compaction lifecycle dispatch**: delegates staged before compaction are released into the successor session alongside boot files - **Durable custody**: delegates and their replay state live in the continuation custody store, with one transactional authority for replacement and a pre-spawn handoff to `subagent_runs` (upstream has removed the Tasks/TaskFlow runtime, #159179) - **Multi-span OTel trace stitching**: continuation hops (tool fire → custody record → subagent spawn → child openclaw.run) propagate W3C `traceparent` through the queue boundary so reviewers see continuation chains as first-class span trees rather than orphan runs (see Observability below) ### Safety - Ships disabled by default (`continuation.enabled: false`) - Bounded by `maxChainLength`, `costCapTokens`, and `maxDelegatesPerTurn` - Cross-session delegate targeting is default-deny, governed by `crossSessionTargeting` config (see Configuration below) - All configuration values are hot-reloadable without gateway restart - Accepted delegate work survives ordinary `/new`, `/reset`, provider fallback, compaction, restart, and session-ID rollover. Explicit delete, effective owner reassignment, access removal, and restrictive visibility changes revoke old return authority. ### Testing posture The continuation surface has been exercised through structured integration runs against multiple upstream bases, blind-enrichment recall checks, and sustained daily use on a fleet of persistent agents since early March 2026. Bugs surfaced through that exercise have been fixed in-place; the present branch reflects the post-fix state. The integration runs target the load-bearing seams: tool-call vs response-token parity, delegate chain depth and per-turn width caps, back-to-back tool-call resilience, silent-wake persistence across compaction, the post-compaction lifecycle dispatch path, and OTel trace-context propagation across the queue boundary. Where a run found a defect, the run shape was retained as a regression case rather than retired. This is a posture statement, not a coverage guarantee. Reviewers can reproduce with `pnpm vitest run -t continuation` (suites are colocated with their sources under `src/auto-reply/`, `src/agents/`, and `src/config/`); the design document describes the seams those suites target. ### Return covenant Accepted child work is bound to a durable generation of the recipient's canonical logical session key, not to whichever transient session ID happened to exist at dispatch time. This is the return covenant: benign successor creation does not orphan already accepted delegates, while a real authority change prevents stale work from crossing into a different owner or audience. - Ordinary `/new` and `/reset`, provider fallback, compaction, restart, and GUID/session-ID rollover preserve the recipient generation. - Explicit session deletion, effective owner reassignment, actual member or access removal, and restrictive visibility changes advance that generation. - The generation is captured at delegate admission and checked at enqueue, after enqueue for races, during trusted system-event adoption, on wake, on restart replay, and again before prompt adoption. - Stale deliveries are acknowledged and removed without waking the successor. - Managed artifacts remain exact-session-ID bound; logical return authority cannot broaden their ownership boundary. The authority table is independent of transient session rows so an absent target can receive durable authority before first materialization. Migration accepts only valid UUID generations, and Doctor's canonical-key repair preserves an epoch only when a unique winning owner can be proved. Ambiguous, owner-changing, orphan-colliding, and cross-database repairs rotate fail-closed. ### RFC Full design document: [`docs/design/continue-work-signal-v2.md`](https://github.com/karmaterminal/openclaw/blob/frond-scribe-claude/20260509/narrow-surgery-tight/docs/design/continue-work-signal-v2.md) — covering problem, solution, implementation, platform integration, configuration, observability, safety, production use cases, testing evidence, and appendices. --- ## Configuration The shipped configuration surface for the continuation feature, under `agents.defaults.continuation` in `openclaw.json`: | Key | Default | Purpose | |---|---|---| | `enabled` | `false` | Master opt-in; feature is off unless explicitly enabled | | `maxChainLength` | `10` | Per-chain recursion guard | | `maxDelegatesPerTurn` | `5` | Width cap per turn | | `costCapTokens` | `500000` | Per-chain accumulated-token budget | | `defaultDelayMs` / `minDelayMs` / `maxDelayMs` | `15000` / `5000` / `300000` | Continuation timer bounds | | `contextPressureThreshold` | `0.8` | Pre-compaction warning threshold (optional) | | `earlyWarningBand` | `0.3125` | Early-warning band multiplier (0 to disable) | | **`crossSessionTargeting`** | **`"disabled"`** | **Default-deny gate on cross-session delegate targeting (see below)** | ### `crossSessionTargeting` — cross-session delegate targeting policy `continue_delegate` exposes recipient-addressing on its model-facing schema: a delegate's return can land at the dispatching session (default), one named session (`targetSessionKey`), multiple named sessions (`targetSessionKeys`), every ancestor in the spawn chain (`fanoutMode: "tree"`), or every known session on the host (`fanoutMode: "all"`). Cross-session targeting (anything beyond self-target or lineage routing) is gated by `agents.defaults.continuation.crossSessionTargeting`: | Value | Behavior | |---|---| | `"disabled"` (default) | Delegates can return to the dispatching session or use `fanoutMode: "tree"` for lineage routing. Explicit cross-session targeting (`targetSessionKey` to a non-self session, `targetSessionKeys` containing any non-self session, `fanoutMode: "all"`) is rejected at the tool surface — no enqueue, no announce. Self-targeting is always allowed. | | `"enabled"` | All targeting modes are available, including same-host `targetSessionKey`, `targetSessionKeys`, and `fanoutMode: "all"`. | `fanoutMode: "tree"` (lineage routing — return up the spawn chain) is available in both gate states; it is not cross-session targeting. The gate addresses the model-controlled cross-session context-injection surface. With default-deny, operators explicitly opt in when their deployment model requires cross-session enrichment. Enforcement is live-read at four points: tool input validation, delegate dispatch, post-compaction delegate release, and bracket-syntax (response-token) spawn — so a config reload changes the next enforcement point without a gateway restart. **Trust posture on targeted returns**: targeted delegate completion text is delivered as `trusted: true` system events. The delegate was spawned by the gateway under operator-configured policy, and its return is a first-party enrichment event — not external untrusted input. The `crossSessionTargeting` gate is the policy boundary for that decision: when an operator opts in, the receive path is internally trusted. --- ## Observability — multi-span OTel trace stitching The continuation feature emits OTel spans for the load-bearing lifecycle events. `traceparent` propagates through every continuation hop so reviewers see a single trace tree spanning the full chain rather than orphan runs. Spans emitted (all in `openclaw.*` or `continuation.delegate.dispatch` namespace — no platform/OTel-semconv emissions): | Span | Emitted when | |---|---| | `openclaw.run` | Each agent turn (root + every continuation/delegate-spawned child run) | | `continuation.delegate.dispatch` | Each `continue_delegate` consumption from the custody store (one per delegate hop) | | `openclaw.harness.run`, `openclaw.context.assembled`, `openclaw.model.call`, `openclaw.model.usage`, `openclaw.tool.execution` | Existing per-turn observability surfaces, parented under their `openclaw.run` | --- ## Real behavior proof **Behavior or issue addressed:** Sessions can elect future work with `continue_work`, dispatch bounded background work with `continue_delegate`, and request guarded compaction with `request_compaction`. The runtime preserves budgets, restart recovery, finalization ownership, and trace lineage across those boundaries. **Presented candidate:** `a22bd9c05c4a7a9c86e72a132cb7939e399104cb` (tree `53363f7964f31a47109cf0575aa23f31eefa0338`), the exact upstream-visible head of `codeagent/85651-upstream-1ba243c8-gates`. It was reached by fast-forward on 2026-11-05. Every earlier presented head, including `3821eaef72677c78f450ae9956cb582a22ba4cba`, remains an ancestor; no presented history was rewritten. ### Receipts bound to this exact head Each is a separate receipt in the preserved exact-head packet, [`PROOFS/a22bd9c05c…/`](https://github.com/karmaterminal/karmaterminal-openclaw-docs/tree/9ba5518bdb079da3c3c75961fd8cd26be040eb1e/PROOFS/a22bd9c05c4a7a9c86e72a132cb7939e399104cb) (docs `main` at `9ba5518b`). | gate | ruling | scope | |---|---|---| | Recipient-authority row (`R-CD-RECIPIENT-AUTHORITY`) | PASS-candidate ([docs#620 comment 6651745479](https://github.com/karmaterminal/karmaterminal-openclaw-docs/pull/620#issuecomment-6651745479)) | the gate-3 fire only; the row stays `partial` until a corpus fold review | | Mode-B and the locally run cut shards | PASS-candidate ([karmaterminal/openclaw#1271 comment 6653747059](https://github.com/karmaterminal/openclaw/issues/1271#issuecomment-6653747059)) | the candidate-owned regression gate; it doesn't claim Mode-B was green | | Fold source review of the `2907e656 → a22bd9c05c` delta | PASS-candidate ([#1271 comment 6655365352](https://github.com/karmaterminal/openclaw/issues/1271#issuecomment-6655365352)) | source review only | **Mode-B** [`41927761314`](https://github.com/karmaterminal/openclaw-bootstrap/actions/runs/41927761314) ran on product `a22bd9c05c4a7a9c86e72a132cb7939e399104cb` with workflow `a768f04231bd0a6f94cc7b845aecaec28a4a4c9e`, from 2026-11-04 22:43Z to 2026-11-05 04:47Z. It finished terminally **non-green**: 91 jobs (53 succeeded, 27 failed, 3 cancelled, 8 skipped) and 218,033 tests passed / 220 failed. - Its receipts are valid, routed equals planned, and every hosted job ran on the project's own runner pool. - **Its 64 distinct failing tests are exactly the previous accepted head's set** (the same sorted-set sha256 `185b6dea…`), and none is new. - The four shards the workflow cuts at 90 minutes were run locally at this exact SHA, serially with one worker: - two were clean; - two carry only baseline or test-order failures, each classified in the receipt with counterfactual runs. **Packet status: preserved, NOT acceptance-complete, NOT terminal.** Of 37 required rows, **0 pass, 1 partial (the recipient-authority row above), and 36 missing**. No live row has fired at this SHA, because no deployment runs it yet: the deployed fleet is on a separate, older line. Running live rows here needs a deployment whose runtime has this SHA as an ancestor. That is a migrating cut (an agent-schema step), gated on its own timed restore rehearsal. `PROOFS/INDEX.json` does not point at this packet, and nothing here is a terminal rollup claim. ### Earlier evidence: provenance, not exact-target proof The live behavior observed on earlier heads, and the earlier corpora, are ancestry and materiality evidence for this head. They aren't exact-target execution, and no row is carried over from them as a pass: - Mode-B [`35364768803`](https://github.com/karmaterminal/openclaw-bootstrap/actions/runs/35364768803) at `3821eaef72`, 2026-09-18; - corpora [`7cb9d71f…`](https://github.com/karmaterminal/karmaterminal-openclaw-docs/tree/c20d6cc26ceaf08b293871dc3bce261d34f90d1c/PROOFS/7cb9d71f622250bedbf565e327bd7d7b9d90b567) and [`139e3657…`](https://github.com/karmaterminal/karmaterminal-openclaw-docs/tree/c20d6cc26ceaf08b293871dc3bce261d34f90d1c/PROOFS/139e3657b1fd5e53166789b8676f18578e209393). The behaviors those corpora observed are the ones this feature exists for: - stale ambient backlog suppression; - typed and bracket `continue_work` wakes with granted provenance and Tempo model-call spans; - cost-cap rejection; - max-chain, scheduler, durable recovery and delegate surfaces. They are re-fired against this head's runtime once one is deployed. ## Proof links and ClawSweeper🦞 guidance Proof artifacts live in `karmaterminal/karmaterminal-openclaw-docs` on `main`. - [Exact-head packet for `a22bd9c05c`: README, status and limits](https://github.com/karmaterminal/karmaterminal-openclaw-docs/blob/9ba5518bdb079da3c3c75961fd8cd26be040eb1e/PROOFS/a22bd9c05c4a7a9c86e72a132cb7939e399104cb/README.md) - [RESOLVED-SHA.md: identities and gate verdicts](https://github.com/karmaterminal/karmaterminal-openclaw-docs/blob/9ba5518bdb079da3c3c75961fd8cd26be040eb1e/PROOFS/a22bd9c05c4a7a9c86e72a132cb7939e399104cb/RESOLVED-SHA.md) - [METHOD.md: how the packet was built](https://github.com/karmaterminal/karmaterminal-openclaw-docs/blob/9ba5518bdb079da3c3c75961fd8cd26be040eb1e/PROOFS/a22bd9c05c4a7a9c86e72a132cb7939e399104cb/METHOD.md) - [Gate 4 receipt: Mode-B and the local cut shards](https://github.com/karmaterminal/karmaterminal-openclaw-docs/blob/9ba5518bdb079da3c3c75961fd8cd26be040eb1e/PROOFS/a22bd9c05c4a7a9c86e72a132cb7939e399104cb/gates/GATE-4-MODE-B-AND-LOCAL-SHARDS.md) - Historical corpora (provenance only): [`7cb9d71f…`](https://github.com/karmaterminal/karmaterminal-openclaw-docs/tree/c20d6cc26ceaf08b293871dc3bce261d34f90d1c/PROOFS/7cb9d71f622250bedbf565e327bd7d7b9d90b567), [`139e3657…`](https://github.com/karmaterminal/karmaterminal-openclaw-docs/tree/c20d6cc26ceaf08b293871dc3bce261d34f90d1c/PROOFS/139e3657b1fd5e53166789b8676f18578e209393) - `139e3657…` packet files: [README](https://github.com/karmaterminal/karmaterminal-openclaw-docs/blob/c20d6cc26ceaf08b293871dc3bce261d34f90d1c/PROOFS/139e3657b1fd5e53166789b8676f18578e209393/README.md) · [RESOLVED-SHA](https://github.com/karmaterminal/karmaterminal-openclaw-docs/blob/c20d6cc26ceaf08b293871dc3bce261d34f90d1c/PROOFS/139e3657b1fd5e53166789b8676f18578e209393/RESOLVED-SHA.md) · [METHOD](https://github.com/karmaterminal/karmaterminal-openclaw-docs/blob/c20d6cc26ceaf08b293871dc3bce261d34f90d1c/PROOFS/139e3657b1fd5e53166789b8676f18578e209393/METHOD.md) · [TRANSPOSED-FROM](https://github.com/karmaterminal/karmaterminal-openclaw-docs/blob/c20d6cc26ceaf08b293871dc3bce261d34f90d1c/PROOFS/139e3657b1fd5e53166789b8676f18578e209393/TRANSPOSED-FROM.md) · [manifest](https://github.com/karmaterminal/karmaterminal-openclaw-docs/blob/c20d6cc26ceaf08b293871dc3bce261d34f90d1c/PROOFS/139e3657b1fd5e53166789b8676f18578e209393/proofs-manifest.json) ### PROOFS METHOD Live rows use a Grafana k6 proof harness. Each packet's `METHOD.md` carries the exact reproducer commands. `MAX_WORKERS=1` is mandatory for the vitest reproducers, because OpenClaw's fixtures are not safe under concurrent access. Structural completeness is not proof: a row counts only with an authoritative receipt at the exact SHA. ## Future actions and #130741 composition Maintainer PR #130741 addresses the complementary fresh-sweep race: it captures the current `sessionId` and `lifecycleRevision` before the first await and uses those values as cleanup CAS facts. The return covenant addresses a different time axis: whether historically accepted child work may return to a logical recipient after benign successor creation. The current candidate and #130741 head `e1afc703f49a07687c0876ba6350cafa87a3638a` merge cleanly in a synthetic composition. If #130741 lands, the composed result should preserve both guarantees: - keep #130741's fresh sweep-time exact-run/session lifecycle fence; - keep the covenant's durable logical-recipient generation for historical return admission and delivery; - do not overload broad `lifecycleRevision` as historical return authority; - do not terminate or orphan accepted descendants merely because `/new` or ordinary `/reset` creates a successor session. That composition honors the maintainer repair without weakening continuation semantics or allowing a stale child return to cross a real ownership boundary. ## Why this is not a skill or a viable plugin extraction OpenClaw skills are `SKILL.md` prompt files loaded into an agent turn that already exists. They can guide work inside that turn; they do not own the turn cycle. Continuation needs gateway and agent-runtime owners a skill cannot provide: - The `continue_work` path persists pending work, enforces budgets and delay bounds, arms a timer, reacquires the session reply-run lane, and starts a later model turn after the current turn has finalized. - The `continue_delegate` path persists delegate intent, does spawn/admission accounting, manages child-session lifecycle, and durably routes returns across sessions. - `request_compaction` is an agent election into guarded runtime compaction. Later work resumes only after the runtime has established the new context boundary. - All three need durable state, cancellation/finalization ownership, restart recovery, trace identity, queue-conflict handling, and gateway scheduling outside the model invocation. A skill can tell a model to *ask* for another turn. Without those owners the ask is prose: it cannot persist a due wake, yield and finalize safely, reacquire the session lane, create the next invocation, survive a restart, or deliver a child result to another session. The implementation therefore belongs in core runtime surfaces such as `src/auto-reply/continuation/**`, `src/agents/tools/**`, `src/auto-reply/reply/agent-runner-continuation-schedule.ts`, and `src/infra/continuation-tracer.ts`. This PR adds no `.agents/skills/**`, `SKILL.md`, or user-facing skill package. The only skill-named production change is core runtime tool dispatch. ClawHub also distributes plugins. Existing plugins can register tools, services, lifecycle hooks, context injection, plugin-owned session state, and — for bundled plugins — Cron-backed session turns. Those seams can support a smaller continuation-like automation, especially host Cron plus / `sessions_spawn`. They are not this feature's turn-finalization ownership, reply-run coordination, durable continuation queue, child-session return lifecycle, election capture, or agent-elected compaction contract. Compaction-provider registration and command-handler `compactCurrent()` are also not that last contract: they compact or summarize, they do not elect compaction at finalization and resume afterward. Moving policy behind a plugin boundary would first require OpenClaw to expose and stabilize a continuation-host API. The gateway/runtime would still own the mechanism described here; a plugin could only package policy around that core capability. That is not a no-core-touch alternative to these primitives. Discord is a bundled channel plugin. It owns the Discord edge, plus delivery/progress hooks into the host's existing subagent path, and submits events into OpenClaw's current turn machinery. Continuation changes that machinery: what survives finalization, which session may run next, how child results return, and when compaction can be elected. A tool adapter over durable flow records is also not a lifecycle host, and upstream has since removed the Tasks/TaskFlow runtime (#159179) that such an adapter would have called. Marking a stored record as running neither reacquires a session lane nor invokes the model; continuation needs the turn machinery itself to own which session runs next, how child results return, and what survives finalization. ## Lineage and replacement context This PR is the clean replacement for closed #85651. It preserves that PR's review lineage and the earlier continuation work descended from #79925, but it does not reuse either closed PR or ask reviewers to infer the current result from them. The replacement carries a current, independently reviewable branch and a complete proof subtree bound to its presented SHA. #85651 was not abandoned because the feature failed or because we accepted its classification as a skill. It was closed after automated labeling put the change in the wrong submission category. This replacement removes that ambiguity: no `src/skills/**` change is presented, current label simulation produces no `r: skill`, and the detailed section above explains why the lifecycle mechanism belongs to core. Acceptance or rejection of the product direction remains OpenClaw's decision. The decision requested is whether OpenClaw should provide multi-session, agent-elected continuation primitives after reviewing the implementation and evidence. It is not whether the same mechanism can be relocated into a skill: a skill cannot own or implement these lifecycle boundaries.

prs.title: feat(gateway): admit sessions_send wake starts
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`sessions_send` can fan out wake-starting work through the gateway `agent` RPC. Before this change, concurrent senders could bypass sender-local batching and rate limits. This adds an optional gateway-owned admission boundary for typed `sessions_send` wake traffic. It intentionally does not affect `mode:notify`, which does not create recipient work.

## Summary

- add a disabled-by-default `gateway.sessionsSendWakeAdmission` policy (six starts per 15 minutes by default)
- enforce it at the common gateway `agent` admission boundary only for typed `inputProvenance.kind=inter_session` / `sourceTool=sessions_send`
- persist one idempotent per-recipient decision in a separate SQLite database, atomically, and fail closed if state is unavailable

## Evidence

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run --config test/vitest/vitest.gateway.config.ts src/gateway/sessions-send-wake-admission.test.ts`: 4/4 passed (default-disabled, seven-recipient load, restart/idempotency, fail-closed state error)
- `pnpm tsgo:core`, `pnpm format:check`, and `git diff --check` passed locally
- implementation is based on released OpenClaw `v2026.10.9` / `8b18b557`, matching the runtime that exposed the issue

## Rollout

Feature remains off by default. This PR contains no config enablement, runtime rollout, or gateway restart. Rollback is retaining the disabled flag or reverting this commit; the receipt database remains as audit evidence.

prs.title: fix(skills): reject FIFO entries without hanging
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes skill validation and packaging hanging indefinitely when `SKILL.md` is a FIFO (named pipe) with no writer.

## User Impact

Both commands now exit with `SKILL.md must be a regular file`, so authors can correct the input and retry. Ordinary skill files still validate and package normally; failed validation leaves an existing archive intact.

## Why This Change Was Made

Reject non-regular entry files before reading them in the shared validator, which the packager already calls. This is two production lines with no new helper or dependency. The regression invokes both real CLI entry points against a real FIFO, with a timeout that kills and reaps a hung child.

Related categories recently merged from an external contributor: #194059 (FIFO input hangs, merged by obviyus on November 6) and #194635 (skill packaging filesystem errors, merged by obviyus on November 8).

## Evidence

- **Real CLI before/after**, in offline, non-root, secretless Linux Docker (Python 3.11.10, 256 MiB, 0.5 CPU). At base `9a5df3d60f12b6c303225c50abeaa4d17bd27108`, both `python3 -S skills/skill-creator/scripts/quick_validate.py <skill>` and `package_skill.py <skill> <out>` hang on an actual FIFO named `SKILL.md`; the harness kills and reaps each after 2 s. At head `426f1e8e893f5440bf99a64cc510129fd9d3cea6`, both exit 1 in about 0.1 s with the regular-file diagnostic.
- Directory inputs also fail clearly. A regular-file control still validates and creates a ZIP containing the original `SKILL.md` bytes. Rejected inputs leave an existing output artifact byte-for-byte intact with no temporary output.
- **Committed regression red/green:** both CLI subcases hit `TimeoutExpired` on the base (3 s limit per child), then pass with the fix. All **13** owner/consumer tests pass with `python3 -S -m unittest discover -s skills/skill-creator/scripts -p 'test_*.py' -v`; Ruff lint/format and `git diff --check` pass. The exact-head combined CLI/test/lint/format verification took **2.07 s**. Python tests are outside the repository test-line ratchet patterns; no allocation or shared budget changed.
- Simplification: one check at the existing owner, **+2 production lines**, and **+25/-1 test lines** for the two affected CLI consumers. No packager-side duplicate validation.
- Independent read-only review of the complete committed diff, both consumers, tests and proof harness: no actionable P0–P2 findings.
- Scope: stable filesystem input types in these standalone tools. No claim of protection against a concurrent file replacement, no live Gateway/model run, and no full local build/test suite. The exact-head [`skills-python` CI job](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/42446942771/job/128628000381) passed in **50 s** including setup; remaining CI and automatic Security Review are pending.

Distinguishes unreadable configuration from settings that need correction. A missing include or failed file read should produce its underlying read error and retry guidance before setup offers changes or writes anything.

## User Impact

Validation, setup, configure, onboarding and bare startup retain the read-failure diagnosis. Malformed JSON and invalid schema keep their existing recovery paths. An unknown configuration does not authorize setup writes; include ownership, revision, path and writer checks stay intact.

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing classifier and terminal-safe diagnostic owner supply the error. Bare startup keeps definitive engine-selection failures; validation uses the same failure kind for text and JSON. prs.title: improve(knowledge): apply the Control UI glossary and style to Knowledge copy
prs.body:
## Problem

The Knowledge plugin's Control UI had ~425 user-visible English strings hard-coded across its views, dialogs, session panel, settings, loading/failure frames, and record panels. They didn't follow the approved Control UI glossary (for example "chat"/"conversation" for the session container, "turn" for an agent reply) or style rules (contractions, curly quotes, sentence case, "Couldn’t …" errors with a next step), and the plugin had no translation catalog, so none of it could be localized.

## Solution

- Add plugin i18n on the existing plugin pattern (`extensions/nostr/browser/i18n`): `extensions/knowledge/src/i18n/{index.ts,locales.ts,locales/en.ts}`. The browser root is `extensions/knowledge/src` (from `openclaw.controlUi: ./src/control-ui.ts`), so `pnpm ui:i18n:verify` discovers the catalog. `activate(host)` binds `host.locale` once; every view reads copy through `t()` when it renders, so the page, session panel, and dialogs all use the host locale.
- The English catalog is split into `en.ts` (shared/page/search copy) plus `en-records.ts`, `en-scribes.ts`, and `en-settings.ts`, merged under one `knowledge.*` key tree. The split keeps each file under the 700-line cap; key paths are unchanged. All keys live under `knowledge.*`, so none collide with shared core keys.
- Apply the glossary and style rules to every human-facing string the lane owns (the 31 changed view modules). Text written for the model (Ask request drafts, the record reference, scribe prompts, scribe session names) is unchanged.
- Small cutovers that came with moving copy:
  - Scribe catalog presentation fields (`blurb`, `cadence`, `startLabel`, `dialogTitle`, `submitLabel`) moved out of `scribes-catalog.ts` into the catalog and were removed from `ScribeDefinition`.
  - `sourceDateNote` moved from the shared `temporal.ts` (also used server-side) into `record-view.ts`, its only caller, so server code doesn't import Control UI copy.
  - Recent activity save badges key on the change id (`created`/`updated`/`observed`) instead of their English label. The one CSS hook (`[data-change="New"]`) moved to `[data-change="created"]`.
  - The page's source-files rail moved to `record-sources.ts` to keep `record-view.ts` under the line cap. It's a straight move with no behavior change.
  - The evidence excerpt eyebrow is sentence case in the catalog. `text-transform: uppercase` keeps its look.
- Docs that quote changed labels: `docs/plugins/knowledge/scribes.md` (Session not found, Open session) and `docs/plugins/knowledge/control-ui.md` (Ask starts a new session).
- Follow-up commit 8221620 (maintainer decisions): group and channel copy keeps “group chats”, and `docs/plugins/knowledge/maintenance.md` and `docs/plugins/knowledge/scribes.md` now say “reply” instead of “turn” for an agent cycle.

### Notable copy changes

| Before | After |
| --- | --- |
| Starts a new chat with {agent}. … | Starts a new session with {agent}. … |
| Chat was not started. Your request is still here. | Couldn’t start the session. Your request is still here. |
| Chat was started but the request was not sent: {error} | Couldn’t send your request. The session started; open it to try again. {details} |
| Can’t reach the vault. … | Couldn’t reach the vault. … |
| Refresh unavailable / Search unavailable | Couldn’t refresh / Couldn’t search knowledge |
| This store couldn’t be opened | Couldn’t open this store (body now ends with “Retry, or check Stores & sharing.”) |
| The scribe was not started. {error} | Couldn’t start the scribe. Your choices and prompt are still here. {details} |
| The assignment was not changed. {error} / Access was not changed. {error} | Couldn’t change the assignment. Your choices are still here; try again. {details} / Couldn’t change access. Try again. {details} |
| The run did not start: the automation is paused | Couldn’t start the run because the automation is paused. Resume it, then try again. |
| In this conversation (session panel) | In this session |
| Open conversation · Conversation not found | Open session · Session not found |
| Which conversations · Active conversations · Conversations in your sidebar. | Which sessions · Active sessions · Sessions in your sidebar. |
| Knowledge will start a conversation called … | Knowledge will start a session called … |
| Each run is an agent turn over every unlinked claim … | Each run is one agent reply over every unlinked claim … |
| Conversation not recorded (claim source, Learned in) · Saved in conversation | Session not recorded · Saved in a session |
| … from owner-direct conversations | … from direct sessions with the owner |
| Group chats see only their own conversation’s knowledge. | Unchanged: “group chats” is kept (8221620) |
| No page is named exactly "x". · Search all text for "x" | No page is named exactly “x”. · Search all text for “x” |
| PREMISE · EXCERPT / EXCERPT | Premise · excerpt / Excerpt (still rendered uppercase) |
| cannot / is not / does not / could not / must not | can’t / isn’t / doesn’t / couldn’t / can’t |

Strings moved into the translation catalog: **823 English keys**. That's the ~425 source strings, plus one/other plural forms and conditional variants that used to be assembled in code.

## Impact

- English copy now follows the glossary and style rules. The layout and controls don't change.
- Knowledge copy can now be localized. The post-merge Control UI locale-refresh job owns foreign catalogs; this PR adds no foreign strings, `translated.json`, or `.i18n` memory.
- Raw technical details in errors (Gateway messages) stay inline after the next step. This surface has no shared host “Show details” disclosure, so I kept the detail visually secondary instead.
- Known gaps, intentional:
  - Scribe titles such as “Knowledge Consolidation” keep their current case. The title is the scribe session’s display name, which the Scribes tab uses to find a scribe’s session, and it also appears in scribe prompts and automation names. Renaming it would orphan existing scribe sessions.
  - There’s no `translated.json` yet, so `locales.ts` returns English for every locale. The translated catalog loader needs wiring once the locale refresh creates that file.
  - A locale change applies on the next render of each view, not instantly. Only English exists today.

## Evidence

The checks, tests and review below were run on bc913e8842dc236. The follow-up 8221620 changes only English copy and docs; it was checked with `pnpm ui:i18n:verify` (green, `plugin=knowledge keys=823`) and `git diff --check` (clean).

- `pnpm ui:i18n:verify`: green (`plugin=knowledge keys=823`)
- `pnpm tsgo:extensions`: green
- `node scripts/run-oxlint.mjs extensions/knowledge/src`: green
- `node scripts/run-format.mts --check extensions/knowledge/src docs/plugins/knowledge`: green
- `git diff --check`: clean
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run extensions/knowledge`: 64 files passed. `scribes-view.test.ts` and `search-date-filters.test.ts` assertions were updated to the new English.
- Local review: autoreview (Codex `gpt-6.1-sol`, medium), `--mode branch --base origin/main` (d59f00281eb0216) on head bc913e8842dc236, max priority P1. Result: `scoped-clean`, no actionable findings. The reviewer noted that its empty sandbox couldn’t run a build.
- pr-simplify: the catalog fields, the shared `sourceDateNote`, and the English-label status hooks were removed, and the shared count/plural helpers were folded into the catalog. Remaining growth is the catalog itself plus one-time `t()` call sites.

Not landing: requested by maintainer; screenshots pending before merge. Before/after screenshots of Recent, Browse, a record page, Scribes (list, detail, start dialog), Settings (all four sections), and the session panel are still needed under the visual gate.

## Work sessions

- [Original discussion with @vyctorbrzezowski](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/dashboard/8ee302fc-4575-4506-92a8-1739453b9b71)
- [Implementation and verification](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/subagent/efff23f5-1c36-4383-806c-137f3ee688bc)

## Worked on by

- @vyctorbrzezowski

prs.title: fix(pr): preserve contributor credit in proof baselines
prs.body:
Related: #195476, #193872

## What Problem This Solves

A proof-baseline candidate cannot credit newly participating contributors when its retained signed source contains only the original contributor’s trailer.

## User Impact

Maintainers can explicitly add verified contributors to a new proof candidate without rewriting its source or changing review, signature, publication, custody or merge authority. The new candidate still requires fresh independent review.

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing explicit proof-baseline producer accepts `--coauthors <file>`, a regular UTF-8 JSON array of `Name <email>` identities. It preserves source trailers first, appends additions deterministically by case-insensitive email, rejects control/line-separator injection before preparation effects, and binds requested metadata into the signed candidate and exact interrupted/completed replay. The existing argument owner resolves the selected file before supervision changes directories. Ordinary baseline and signing defaults remain source-only; this option is limited to `--for-proof`.

Requested by @galiniliev and @vyctorbrzezowski. Implemented and verified by @roboclaw-bot; both exact human trailers are present in the signed source commit.

## Work sessions

Linked for team reference; these sessions aren’t public.

- [Original discussion with @galiniliev and @vyctorbrzezowski](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/dashboard/1f24e3f3-e7d6-4966-b666-e5868987619d)
- [Implementation and verification](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/dashboard/4e21df81-705a-4c4f-8051-ce41b210e29d)

## Evidence

- Signed source: e1aae066826f10d61072ffd5d8973d2ee9334133; tree 4dcc3092065cd7549bab8909566770c83c15565c; base ee431f3f2dcd9cc04a86c5c7756d13f88bdf1dde.
- Required option is red on base. Initial independent review found caller-relative file selection and late rejection of email controls; both were reproduced red through the native entry point and repaired at the existing input owners.
- Final source: all 19 native producer/security/recovery cases passed in 247.50s. A signed one-contributor source produces and publishes the exact two-contributor candidate to a real private Git remote; duplicate emails are deterministic. Invalid identities leave the preparation inventory/protected state unchanged. Changed attribution cannot recover or replace an admitted transition. Stale leases, missing/forged authority, private baselines, unsigned task/side-parent commits and replaced held custody remain refused.
- Native wrapper, signing, local Git push/ref readback and interrupted recovery are real; GitHub observations are synthetic, not live GitHub acceptance.
- Two ordinary-credit and three signing-handoff cases passed on prior snapshot 322d38681434bbbc4023ac589ec3633f9181e9f4. Their default-path inputs are unchanged by the final two explicit proof-input repairs; these results are retained, not restamped final-source proof.
- Final complete independent P0–P3 review: scoped-clean, zero actionable findings. Interrupted/earlier reviews are not claimed clean.
- Final production/test lint and types, format, shell syntax, whitespace and test-line ratchet passed: 6591629/6591635, slack 6. Separate allocation: exactly 76 added native regression lines; shared scalar unchanged. The longer native cases prove signed CLI admission, real private Git publication and interrupted recovery unavailable to helper-only tests. Hosted CI remains pending publication.

Land through clean trusted canonical tooling, never the modified producer admitting itself. Consumer #193872 and its signed source were not modified; AUTH-2, UPGRADE-3 and #193873 acceptance remain separate pending work.

prs.body:
Maintainer hold: leave this PR open and unmerged; do not enable auto-merge.

Related: #195418

## What Problem This Solves

The synthetic performance-fixture verification hook repeats a full database scan even when the native owner has already established a current full integrity proof.

## User Impact

No user-visible runtime change. Large offline benchmark fixtures can reuse valid native verification; fixtures without that proof still receive the full integrity and foreign-key scan before normal owner close.

## Why This Change Was Made

Read the native handle's existing full-verification fact, which already checks identity, generation and revocation. Record whether verification was reused or freshly scanned. This adds no schema, configuration or production behavior.

## Evidence

Two exact historical-build native fixtures exercised both branches: an existing full proof was reused (98 ms), and a Doctor close marked verification-missing triggered a fresh full scan (157 ms). Both ended with written native clean-close seals. These small-fixture timings establish branch behavior, not large-database speedup.

Syntax, formatting and diff checks pass. The selected `pnpm check:changed` gates passed except 20 existing changelog violations, reproduced on the exact original main parent and introduced by #194364 (`266a7aa0fe69`). Independent Codex review found no actionable findings through P2. This follow-up is patch-identical to that reviewed change; the hook preimage and its five imported owner modules match the new base. Exact-head [CI run 42540145640](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/42540145640) passed for `41db78e50463cef2f3a1ff8e9f8be92043353083`, testing merge `fd03edc51fc10e7cc07719a05e82cf40457e757f` against main `56493a1a999c7f813d13a4431ef8f66fbf22c7c7`. prs.title: fix(talk): voice consults rewrite the cached prompt on every question
prs.body:
Closes #179236

## What Problem This Solves

Repeated Talk hand-offs remove previously submitted consult input from later model history. Speech finalized during a consult can also move into earlier history. Source-built runtime proof found a further case: speech immediately before a consult was folded into its generated prompt, then replayed separately on the next call. These changes rewrite conversation prefixes and can increase cache writes.

## User Impact

Later voice questions retain the consult-containing conversation prefix and genuine spoken clarifications. Generated consult input remains hidden from chat and voice-background previews.

## Why This Change Was Made

Current head: `bbb9caa27a628cbea73cdb1f3429d1fae91b9c1d`.

- Tag and retain native and client-tool-call consult input already sent to the backing model.
- Replay speech finalized during a tagged consult after that consult's last row; preserve ordinary chat order.
- Keep speech preceding a tagged consult as distinct history, including speech committed while write admission waits. Preserve ordinary unanswered-message and restart recovery.
- Hide generated input from pending voice background before the first model response.
- Keep earlier excluded records excluded without rewriting stored data.

The PR integrates upstream `54dd1c6d` with its native package identity 2026.10.6. No version or saved configuration metadata was edited to bypass downgrade protection.

**Maintainer decision required:** scoped generated-consult retention changes the earlier contract from #135423. The [owner decision request](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/179237#issuecomment-6354621771) remains open.

## Evidence

[23 October source-build report and durable JSON receipts](https://github.com/khensthoth/openclaw/blob/4baba2d09836fd192b11fcbd04dfc2adf034f9de/evidence/talk-consult-prompt-cache/2026-10-23/README.md)

| Requirement | Verified result |
| --- | --- |
| Exact original upstream-base regression | Browser/native producer cases on `390d7993` fail only at intended retention assertions; strict expected-failure gate passed. Original fixed-source integration passed 134 tests at `4dddbb7d`. [Run 39879508535](https://github.com/khensthoth/openclaw/actions/runs/39879508535). |
| Additional preparation defect | All three intended negative cases fail on `5c86a193`. Repaired source passed **47 tests across five files**, covering native recorder/prepared/browser provenance, late speech, ordinary recovery and mandatory tool-prefix stability. [Run 39930234710](https://github.com/khensthoth/openclaw/actions/runs/39930234710). |
| Built Gateway / actual agent requests | **Passed** with native source build at `8b6f6011`: pending reconnect before response bytes, generated background suppression, exact retained prompt count, clarification after the answer, and exact contiguous HTTP input prefix through the first consult. [Run 39931480192](https://github.com/khensthoth/openclaw/actions/runs/39931480192). |
| Latest-stable pre-existing mixed-data upgrade | **Passed** from published 2026.10.6 through the native updater to candidate `98239851`. Typed question/reply and genuine speech survive in order; legacy generated input stays hidden. Candidate and installed build identities and all **18,522 application-file hashes** match. Current-source upgrade fixture tests also passed **93 tests**. [Run 39930703485](https://github.com/khensthoth/openclaw/actions/runs/39930703485). |
| Current-head upstream checks | **Passed** for `bbb9caa2`: CI gate, security-sensitive review and dependency review all successful. [CI run 39932582291](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39932582291). |

Both upgrade manifests declare 2026.10.6; build identity and the complete file inventory establish candidate activation. Official latest stable was rechecked as `v2026.10.6` at 2026-10-23T09:59:51Z.

Proof candidates have identical product source and docs to the PR. The PR adds only two user-role guards inside the new regression test to satisfy the message-union type check; strict assertions remain equivalent. The linked report records the exact source correspondence and earlier failed attempts rather than counting them as proof.

### Wire-proof scope

The first **three contiguous actual Responses input items**, through the generated consult, replay unchanged. The first/second requests have four/seven input items; the first answer is at index 3 and the clarification at index 4. The provider intentionally rebuilds its trailing per-turn runtime-context item, which is outside this compared prefix. No filtering or normalization is applied to compared items.

This synthetic source-build lane uses the real Gateway, producer and agent loop with a controlled external HTTP provider. It does not claim whole-request/system/tool/header equality, live provider cache hits or microphone/audio testing. Native producer coverage also uses public plugin registration and real session/history owners in the linked integration tests.

### Earlier live observations

The [22 October live report](https://github.com/khensthoth/openclaw/blob/499bfbe1547071b8a8dc67dbbb416484f72e34ce/evidence/talk-consult-prompt-cache/2026-10-22/README.md) covers actual OpenAI/GPT and Google/Gemini Talk routes with Anthropic Claude, clarification recall and mixed typed/voice recall. Individual follow-up first requests showed 96.3%, 97.5% and 97.8% cached input. These observations used a compiled-JavaScript port on an existing patched beta image, not a full source build or guaranteed savings. The manual reconnect attempt was inconclusive; the source-built pending test above adds deterministic coverage.

Fresh independent reviews found no P0–P2 findings in the current repair and proof. The shared autoreview CLI is unavailable on the server; no helper-isolated autoreview run is claimed.

All new source proof ran in secretless fork CI with synthetic state. Chief and its live configuration, data, volumes, environment and image were untouched.

The requested technical receipts are submitted. Scoped retention still requires a maintainer decision; fresh ClawSweeper review is requested after this body/evidence update.
