prs.title: fix(macos): window titles stay English with another app language
prs.body:
Fixes #195560

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: four macOS window titles remain English when the app uses another language, including their system-visible names in window navigation and accessibility surfaces.

## User Impact

User impact: Connection, Agent Events, Add Gateway, and Welcome to OpenClaw resolve their titles through the existing app-language catalog. No configuration changes or migration are needed. Native rendering and VoiceOver validation remain pending; this PR is intentionally a draft.

## Why This Change Was Made

AppKit window titles take plain strings, so these four literals bypassed localization. Resolve each title with `String(localized:)`, matching existing window-title code, without changing window lifecycle, activation, sizing, or other strings. Regenerate only the source-owned native inventory using the unchanged canonical generator.

## Evidence

- Applied the exact four Swift substitutions from `saariuslystoned/openclaw:fix/macos-window-titles-localization` at `a692af6083e81bde98f1e7b43745caa1ab11a884` onto fresh upstream main `df13b6b8994cefe16f311f29f0301bba511ec617`. No other issue's unmerged changes are included.
- `node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs scripts/native-app-i18n.ts baseline --write` and `node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs scripts/native-app-i18n.ts verify` passed. Verification reports 4,679 unique entries, no inventory drift, and 1,662 macOS source keys.
- Exact source/scope assertions and `git diff --check` passed: five files, four one-line Swift replacements, and four generated inventory sites (5,912 → 5,916). Removing those four sites restores the fresh-main inventory byte-for-byte. The generator, locale catalogs, and translation memory are unchanged.
- All four catalog keys have 22 locale entries, including English. This verifies entry presence, not translation quality or runtime behavior.
- Reused the completed independent source review of the identical two-commit source delta: no actionable findings. prs.title: fix(agents): avoid redundant catalog copies during model listing
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Model catalog requests construct mutable session registries and deep-copy full catalog baselines even though they only need to publish inventory. Catalog overlays also repeatedly parse identical transport URLs.

## User Impact

Background and scoped catalog publication use a narrow lookup over the canonical parser, avoiding session baseline copies. Route comparisons skip redundant URL parsing and reuse existing comparison results. Session refresh, registration, fork isolation, source precedence, request authentication, OAuth modification, serving limits and route-bound capabilities remain covered. No configuration or migration is required.

**HOLD: performance acceptance failed. Do not merge.** The current candidate improves median worker heap and warm latency, but cold latency and several tail/GC observations worsen. These results are not a packaged Gateway RSS claim.

## Why This Change Was Made

The publication owner needs catalog rows and availability, not a mutable session lifecycle. Both owners share source composition; the session registry retains its existing refresh/fork responsibilities. The route comparator now avoids work when raw endpoints match after API identity is established. No cache or public API is added.

Production delta: **+202 net lines**. The growth establishes the publication boundary over one parser; the route correction adds eight net lines. Tests: **+156 net lines**, with an exact allocation. The extracted registry no longer needs its large-file exception. Related: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/194683

## Evidence

Exact head: `577255fde2e3e4413867df842186cafb499f30fb`; tree: `bb57b2dbd2461ce0cd99d2ac71784ebe9f1bce64`.

- **98 tests in eight files passed on Node 24.22.1 and the repository-pinned Bun**, covering route identity, metadata/inference overlays, config merges, registry siblings, static/full publication and real-worker ownership. Publication observes zero mutable registry constructions with a positive control.
- Targeted type-aware lint, max-lines guard, pinned formatting, diff checks and commit hooks passed. A fresh full candidate build passed; its build identity matched the native source carrier.
- Independent source review and canonical autoreview of the correction found no actionable P0–P2 defects. Review does not establish performance acceptance.
- Proof used [Blacksmith Testbox](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/42553411317), lease `tbx_01m6z3m0k5w67hyvr3vzc4hdyv`. Native completion settled with exit 0 on the exact source/tree. Archive SHA256: `0581892642dd0197c1ad6443d8180e349d811af44b33cefc44c5f5513261fbde`.
- [Current-head PR CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/42557980618) is in progress. The previous head's two failures are repaired: the static fixture now mocks the publication entry point, and the obsolete large-file baseline entry is removed. Both formerly failing jobs now pass on this exact head (`checks-fast-baseline-ratchets` and `checks-node-changed-compact-small-7`). The latest CI snapshot has 66 successful jobs, one active and 25 skipped; full CI completion is not claimed.

### Performance rule declared before measurement

Compare complete baseline `7c0d3ab5a28774d2efefee24d535970539b27a1d` and candidate builds on the same host, using the unchanged committed controller. Run five serial alternating baseline/candidate pairs with a fresh fixture per launch:

```sh
node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs scripts/perf/catalog-worker-retention-measure.ts \
  --built-worker <baseline-or-candidate-build> --output <fresh-fixture> \
  --workspaces 1 --models 1000 --configured-models 1000 \
  --providers 2 --discovery-models 100 --runtime-plugin \
  --task-rounds 20 --measure-tasks
```

Require identical ordered catalog/runtime hashes and no mutable registry construction for publication. A measurable allocation/retention reduction must not worsen other measured metrics; a 20% adverse cell stops acceptance, and smaller adverse movement needs investigation or explicit owner acceptance. This rule was preserved for the route correction; earlier failures are not waived.

### Current measurement: HOLD

Ten serial launches and 200 identical ordered outputs; every request returns 1,200 entries, 1,000 configured entries and 1,200 runtime models. Source/dependency-input/build digests stay fixed before and after; dependency-input digests match between arms. This does not independently hash every installed dependency file. Four available CPUs, approximately 14 GiB available RAM; observed cgroup limits are unlimited and no memory-pressure events were observed.

Values are **cohort median [minimum–maximum]**. With five runs, cohort nearest-rank p95 is the maximum. Each warm-request p95 is the maximum of 19 requests.

| Metric | Baseline | Candidate | Median change |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Cold post-GC worker heap, MiB | 88.096 [88.090–88.142] | 87.577 [87.575–87.599] | -0.589% |
| Warm sampled peak worker heap, MiB | 166.712 [145.995–198.135] | 143.726 [142.722–174.855] | -13.788% |
| Final ordinary worker heap, MiB | 111.042 [105.798–142.495] | 100.399 [90.516–126.880] | -9.585% |
| Whole-launch peak process RSS, MiB | 957.500 [943.855–1035.020] | 926.090 [887.961–975.070] | -3.280% |
| Final process RSS, MiB | 944.270 [925.977–1015.207] | 919.266 [869.727–967.285] | -2.648% |
| Cold request, ms | 1040.668 [925.458–1222.893] | 1098.880 [996.600–1167.906] | **+5.594%** |
| Warm request median, ms | 96.173 [89.974–137.271] | 87.353 [79.986–99.794] | -9.171% |
| Warm request p95, ms | 141.115 [115.417–195.522] | 129.926 [117.210–170.889] | -7.929% |
| Worker total CPU, ms | 1788.869 [1629.451–2400.187] | 1697.888 [1460.208–1763.941] | -5.086% |
| Total GC, ms | 100.244 [73.726–127.520] | 96.936 [91.518–100.884] | -3.301% |
| All-GC p99, ms | 4.180 [3.558–7.048] | 5.017 [4.235–6.248] | **+20.049%** |
| Scavenge p99, ms | 1.711 [1.394–2.123] | 2.063 [1.645–2.951] | **+20.530%** |
| Scavenge maximum, ms | 1.902 [1.550–2.135] | 3.116 [1.731–6.546] | **+63.803%** |

Adverse paired cells above the threshold:

- P1: all-GC p95 +37.652%, max +35.031%; Scavenge p99 +26.996%, max +68.662%; incremental total +368.739%, p95/p99/max +1003.001% each; major p95/p99/max +35.031% each; loop p95 +27.984%.
- P2: Scavenge max +206.558%; incremental total +99.695%, p95/p99/max +233.426% each.
- P3: warm request p95 **128.622→170.889 ms (+32.861%)**; all-GC p95 +58.777%; Scavenge total +29.332%, p95 +49.249%, p99 +45.632%, max +52.834%.
- P4: all-GC total +24.132%, p95 +38.706%, p99 +41.020%; Scavenge total +25.919%, p95 +38.792%.
- P5: worker system CPU 20.030→28.119 ms (+40.384%); all-GC p99 +27.872%, max +61.719%; Scavenge p99 +72.459%, max +55.153%; major total +36.769%, p95/p99/max +61.719% each.

These are 37 numeric cells, including overlapping GC statistics, not 37 independent regressions. Smaller adverse cells also remain unresolved: cold latency, P5 peak/final heap (+17.801/+19.926%), P2 RSS, P3 CPU and loop tails. No owner acceptance or causal explanation has cleared them.

Worker heap is isolate-local; process RSS includes the controller and all isolates. Final ordinary heap is not post-GC, and sampled peaks are not continuous maxima. Fewer scavenges do not establish allocation savings or explain longer tails. No full-Gateway under-load result is claimed.

### Earlier failed candidate and diagnosis

The previous `cbf9ce7` five-pair matrix also failed: peak worker heap median 145.979→175.473 MiB (+20.20%) and maximum-GC-pause median +41.62%. Archive SHA256: `dc449aea6d9e9c92eb3c8b7b3d6db6243b0445a05368918bec18bd9361fda1c7`. That failure remains evidence.

Separate allocation/CPU and isolate-matched GC diagnostics preserved all 80 outputs and found repeated normalization/route-selection work. Allocation sampled approximately 1.62 GiB over 19 warm refreshes; inclusive stack attribution overlaps. The trace did not reproduce the prior peak regression, but altered GC timing and controller collections prevent treating it as a replacement acceptance run. Archive SHA256: `10edf9517677d37c5b267dc5eee58cfbf28092fc70d0762060052f433b0ac29f`.

Follow-ups: remove duplicate provider-owner selection without breaking in-place model-ID mutation or config/generation ownership; measure compiled discovery/auth imports before proposing an import-boundary change. Do not cache handles across rows or attach them to published rows.

## Retention diagnostic (declared before measurement)

On the same frozen baseline/candidate builds, run five alternating pairs of the existing catalog-worker workload with `--task-rounds 101` and without `--measure-tasks`. This collects worker heap after GC at each revision. Require all 1,010 ordered outputs and counts to match and source/dependency/build hashes to remain fixed. Compare the post-GC trajectory, final heap and last-20-revision spread; report any continuing growth. Forced collections make this a retention diagnostic, not normal latency or RSS acceptance proof, and a finite trajectory cannot prove absence of every leak. The previous load-matrix acceptance rule remains unchanged. Run only if at least ten minutes remain on the owned lease; otherwise record the gap.

### Retention diagnostic result

All ten launches completed 101 requests each (initial revision 0 plus 100 catalog replacements), with **1,010 identical ordered outputs**, 102 collected-heap samples per launch, and unchanged source/dependency-input/build digests. Final archive SHA256: `4db24bf1b95c7ad254def9d04cb6827f0ac47cf2b5f78fd54180f4900c9d3b95`.

The initial command stopped after nine successful launches at its conservative five-minute headroom check (native exit 1). The longest completed launch took 41.84 seconds. With nearly four minutes remaining, only the missing P5 candidate launch was completed under a two-minute admission margin; the same lease, original deadline, source and compiled builds were retained. That completion settled with native exit 0. No measured launch was rerun, and the initial failure is not relabeled successful. The Testbox is now stopped.

| Post-GC worker heap | Baseline | Candidate |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Median final heap at revision 100 | 88.503 MiB | 87.939 MiB |
| Median of each run's last 20 samples | 88.484 MiB | 87.908 MiB |
| Observed last-20 range across all runs | 88.305–88.672 MiB | 87.753–88.105 MiB |

Every run gains retained heap between revisions 20 and 100: the median per-run increase is **575,664 bytes baseline / 558,424 bytes candidate**. Cohort medians move 87.953→88.503 MiB and 87.405→87.939 MiB respectively. The fitted last-20 slopes are slightly negative, but that final window does not establish a stable plateau or a no-leak verdict. This finite synthetic fixture uses forced collections. The candidate's final retained footprint improves by only **0.564 MiB**, leaving the roughly 88 MiB baseline unresolved.

V8 `code_and_metadata_size` grows over revisions 20–100 by median 567,532 bytes baseline / 559,556 bytes candidate. Code lifecycle is an observed contributor, but these counters overlap heap: their similar sizes do not prove all heap growth is JIT, and subtracting them would not establish a leak remainder.

Process RSS at the final checkpoint has cohort median **787.4→866.0 MiB (+9.98%)**, moving the wrong way; pair 3 rises **21.89%**. It includes the controller and other isolates and cannot be assigned solely to catalog heap. This diagnostic neither establishes an RSS win nor clears the failed uninstrumented load-matrix gate.

prs.title: fix(matrix): message bursts become separate turns despite messages.inbound debounce
prs.body:
Closes #165823 Related: #161505 ## What Problem This Solves Fixes: Matrix turns every line of a quick text burst into separate agent turns, even when `messages.inbound.debounceMs` or `byChannel.matrix` is configured. ## User Impact With `messages.inbound.byChannel.matrix` (or the global `debounceMs`) set, a burst of Matrix messages from one sender gets one reply. The Matrix default stays 0, so nothing is delayed unless the operator opts in. ## Why This Change Was Made Rebuilt on the durable Matrix ingress (the earlier head targeted the replay-claim API that main has since removed). It follows the Mattermost fan-in debouncer from #166499: - Ingress `dispatch` hands each event and its claim lifecycle to a room-keyed `createChannelInboundDebouncer` and returns `{ kind: "deferred" }`. `canAppend` only merges contiguous text from the same sender and thread root, and `serializeImmediate` keeps everything in room order, so a burst never jumps ahead of another sender's message. - A flush fans the batched claims into one lifecycle (`fanInChannelIngressLifecycles`). Adopting the merged turn completes every claim; a gated turn settles them; a handler failure fails each claim so the drain's retry policy applies; shutdown or an aborted claim cancels them back to the queue. - The merged event keeps the latest event id (reply threading), joins bodies with newlines, keeps each event's HTML in `formatted_body` (escaped plain text otherwise, joined with `
`) so the handler's matrix.to pill check still validates mentions, and merges `m.mentions`. - Media, voice notes, edits, real replies (not thread fallbacks), the bot's own events, and control commands dispatch alone. Command bypass strips the mention prefix the way the handler does (bot MXID, room display name, every agent's mention patterns), so `@Bot: /stop` is never delayed. Prefix lookup is async, so it is chained per room. - Pre-startup history and E2EE decryption are now handled by ingress before delivery, so the old pre-startup predicate and repeat-emit filter are gone. - Monitor shutdown closes the debouncer with task admission: pending batches and late deliveries return to the durable queue instead of being dropped. - The delay is read from live config.
Test-only changes - `index.test-helpers.ts`: the fake ingress passes a full claim lifecycle and records it; the fake runtime gains a `messagesConfig` knob and a `mock-isolation` note (`config/test-mock-exports-baseline.txt` drops that entry). - `index.test.ts`: handler failures and late post-shutdown events are now asserted on the claim lifecycle (`onFailed` / `onCancelled`) rather than as a rejected delivery; the shutdown-order test waits for the handler to start before aborting.
## Evidence - Original defect: the new `index.test.ts` case "merges a Matrix text burst when messages.inbound.byChannel.matrix is set" fails with `index.ts` reverted to main (handler called 2 times, no batching) and passes with the fix. - `inbound-debounce.test.ts` (16 tests): merge on latest event, single adoption per claim, gated-turn settle, failure fans out `onFailed`, immediate dispatch for edits/replies/commands (MXID, display-name pill, mention pattern)/images, arrival order under async prefix lookup, room order across senders and threads, HTML and mention merge, own messages, shutdown cancellation. - `index.test.ts`: burst merge through the monitor wiring and a debounce delay committed after startup. - Local gates on this head: `pnpm test:extension matrix` pass; `pnpm check:changed --base upstream/main` typecheck-all, format, mock-export ratchet, dead-export scan, plugin boundaries pass; oxlint on `extensions/matrix` clean; `pnpm format:docs:check` clean. - Earlier live run (2026.9.8 Gateway, previous implementation, `byChannel.matrix: 3000`): a five-line Element burst produced one user-triggered agent turn. Not re-run on this head.

prs.title: feat(control-ui): show worker lifecycle and telemetry
prs.body:
Closes #163982

## What Problem This Solves

The Systems page hides worker lifecycle history, can leave a reclaimed worker shown as `Attached` until reload, and does not connect live dedicated workers to the CPU, memory, and disk telemetry their enrolled nodes already report.

## User Impact

Operators can distinguish active workers from recent destroyed or failed workers, inspect lifecycle/provider/profile/lease/error details, see terminal state changes without reloading, and troubleshoot or right-size live dedicated workers from the same resource graphs used for base systems.

Workers without dedicated node telemetry show an explicit not-reported state. Shared-host workers do not expose whole-host statistics as if those measurements belonged to one worker.

## Why This Change Was Made

The Systems inventory now retains terminal worker records, groups active and historical workers separately, and refreshes canonical `environments.list` data when durable `sessions.changed` events or worker placement changes arrive.

For dedicated workers, the Gateway additionally projects the enrolled node identity. The Systems inventory joins that exact identity to `node.list`, reuses the existing host-stat history and graphs, and continues polling while the worker is selected. No provider shell probe, SSH command, or second telemetry poller is introduced.

## Evidence

### October27 identification repair

Short worker IDs now remain visible beside lifecycle status. [Exact-head regression results and before/after screenshots](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/163995#issuecomment-6456168501). This fixes the same-profile identification finding; history-policy acceptance and main integration remain pending.

### Earlier lifecycle and telemetry evidence

The following results document earlier tested revisions; they are not a new full-suite or live-runtime qualification of the October27 head.

Live Apple Container lifecycle, captured from the same Systems page without a reload:

**Before reclaim — worker is Attached**

![Systems sidebar showing an attached worker](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/ff22cbbe-35d0-4d25-a08c-6799626eb040)

**After reclaim — worker moved to Recent worker history as Destroyed**

![Systems sidebar showing the reclaimed worker as destroyed](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/ee681765-dd7b-4cad-adf6-0708837275eb)

- Live transition observed in about one second and repeated twice without reloading.
- Disposable live telemetry proof: an Apple Container worker reached `ready`, published a dedicated node identity, and reported Linux host stats with 5 CPUs, load averages, 4.26 GB memory capacity, and 541.13 GB disk capacity through `node.list`. The worker was reclaimed; provider and Apple Container inventories were empty afterward.
- Focused validation:
  - Gateway environment projection: 20/20 pass.
  - Gateway protocol schema: 22/22 pass.
  - Systems telemetry/UI: 36/36 pass, including distinct session and telemetry-node names.
  - Changed-file formatting and lint: pass.
  - Core and UI typechecks: pass.
  - Production Control UI build: pass.
- Earlier branch-wide validation:
  - `node scripts/check-changed.mjs --base origin/main`: pass (335.15 s).
  - `pnpm test:changed`: 20,926 pass / 3 skip; one unrelated `shell-viewport.test.ts` RAF-coalescing assertion failed under the full parallel lane, then passed 3/3 isolated reruns (11/11 each).
  - Upstream `control-ui-performance`: pass. The local check showed a nondeterministic gzip edge 24–30 B over the 373,454 B startup limit while raw startup JS stayed exactly 1,208,683 B with and without the Systems reconciliation helper, confirming this patch does not change the startup asset set.
  - Repo autoreview helper was attempted but unavailable because its local Codex credential returned HTTP 401; no review verdict was produced.

The two older `Destroying` rows visible in the screenshots predate this worker and are a separate provider-history cleanup issue.

prs.title: fix(telegram): route bound conversations when agent selection is ambiguous
prs.body:
Closes #159334

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: a Telegram conversation with an active session binding fails with `AgentSelectionRequiredError` on a multi-agent install that has no channel-wide Telegram route, so its messages are never processed.

## User Impact

User impact: runtime-bound Telegram conversations reach their bound agent regardless of how many agents are configured. Conversations without a binding, or whose binding names no agent, keep today's behavior — including still requiring an explicit channel owner. A binding revoked or replaced while a message is being routed no longer leaves the former owner selected.

## Why This Change Was Made

`prepareTelegramConversationRoute` asked ordinary agent selection for a route before looking at the binding, and ordinary selection refuses an ambiguous roster. It now selects the base route inside the SDK's `resolveRuntimeConversationBindingRouteAsync({ resolveRoute })` (and `inspectRuntimeConversationBindingRoute({ inspection, resolveRoute })` for route-owner inspection): the binding owner's canonically classified `boundAgentId` arrives before ordinary selection, and when it is set the base route is derived from session-only config with that agent as the default. This is the shared binding-owner selection Slack, Discord and iMessage use, so Telegram no longer re-implements the session-key/metadata classification. Topic overrides, configured bindings, and the runtime-binding step that follows are unchanged.

### Binding changes during resolution (review follow-up)

An earlier revision chose the agent from a synchronous binding read and then let `resolveRuntimeConversationBindingRouteAsync` read the binding again after an `await`, so a binding revoked in between could leave the former owner selected; that revision guarded it with a re-prepare/retry loop.

Since merging current `main` (`4ee4606`), agent selection runs inside the `resolveRoute` callback of the single awaited inspection, so the agent and the binding facts come from the same read. There is no second read to diverge from, and the retry loop is gone. The same applies to `prepareTelegramConversationRouteInspection` (new on `main`), whose `resolve(inspection)` now selects the agent from the inspection it is handed. `inspectTelegramConversationRouteAsync` shares the inbound path with `touchBinding: false`.

## Evidence

New cases in `conversation-route-owner.test.ts`, all on a two-agent config with no route bindings:

- inbound `resolveTelegramConversationRoute` selects the bound agent and session, reports `runtime-bound`, and touches the binding once;
- `inspectTelegramConversationRouteAsync` selects the bound agent without touching liveness;
- a sentinel `global` session with `metadata.agentId` selects that agent;
- a binding that names no agent still rejects with `AGENT_SELECTION_REQUIRED`;
- a binding revoked just before the awaited inspection rejects with `AGENT_SELECTION_REQUIRED` instead of routing to the former owner;
- a binding replaced just before the awaited inspection routes to the new owner and its new binding.

Negative controls: with `main`'s `conversation-route.ts` (`4ee4606`), 4 of these 6 fail with `AGENT_SELECTION_REQUIRED` (the bound-agent, inspection, sentinel-metadata and replacement cases); the no-agent and revocation cases pass there, as intended, since both assert that rejection.

```text
$ pnpm test extensions/telegram/src/conversation-route-owner.test.ts
19 passed (19)
$ pnpm test extensions/telegram
passed 63 Vitest shards
$ pnpm tsgo:extensions && pnpm tsgo:extensions:test
0 errors
```

Focused regression cost: `pnpm test extensions/telegram/src/conversation-route-owner.test.ts` — 19 tests, 16.4 s Vitest duration / 20.8 s wall time locally. `oxlint`, `oxfmt --check` and the assertion SAFETY ratchet are clean on the changed files. The test fixture uses `agents.entries` (the authored shape since `agents.list` was retired on `main`).

**Live Telegram proof:** not included. The `telegram-e2e-userbot` harness needs Convex-leased team credentials, which I don't have as an outside contributor. The evidence above is unit-level through the real binding-routing SDK with a test adapter.

AI-assisted. I reviewed the change and ran the tests and negative controls above locally.

prs.title: fix(backup): preserve literal repository and restore paths
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Backup commands silently trim quoted filesystem paths. `backup git init --repository '/private/backup '` initializes `/private/backup` instead of the requested directory; `backup sqlite list` similarly reports the wrong repository. A neighboring directory can therefore be adopted even though the operator supplied a different name.

## Why This Change Was Made

Preserve the original nonblank path through the whole existing owner chain:

- The shared Git/SQLite/schedule argument resolver expands a leading home prefix and resolves the original text, retaining the existing all-whitespace rejection.
- The snapshot directory owner uses fs-safe's absolute-path creation contract rather than the root-relative adapter that trims requested paths. Canonical existing ancestors retain the existing alias behavior; directory pins, ownership/mode/ACL checks, and durable publication remain in place.
- The Git repository check removes the command's final line terminator instead of applying the general text-output helper's `.trim()` to a filesystem path.

The archive command already preserves literal arguments. Existing home expansion and fs-safe APIs solve the remaining gap; no new path library, global normalizer change, config surface, storage format, or fallback is introduced. These layers belong in one repair: fixing only the CLI resolver still leaves real repository creation failing.

## User Impact

Quoted repository, snapshot, restore-target, and scratch paths keep their leading/trailing spaces. The native acceptance proof below specifically exercises Git initialization and SQLite listing; the command suites cover the shared resolver's other callers. Blank required values still fail with the same error. [Backup CLI reference](https://docs.openclaw.ai/cli/backup) now states the literal-path contract.

## Evidence

Base native build: `b6d8eb287e0898d2c50d89abaef749e4c25ca66a`. Tested source and native build: `038885153418fff113651caa105b6933a44eba38`, OpenClaw `2026.11.1`, Linux / Node 24.22.1, November 9, 2026. The inspected main `5f84a8166dc524a4eab375b16030239acbefc92b` leaves all three changed production owners unchanged from base.

### Real CLI RED → GREEN and filesystem readback

The same frozen external driver runs the actual built CLI with a private configuration, state directory, and repositories. Before each Git case it creates the distinct trimmed-name neighbor with a sentinel file. No path resolver, Git process, filesystem operation, or CLI result is mocked.

| Supplied argument | Base result | Tested head result |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Absolute `<fixture>/git absolute ` | Returns trimmed path; `.git` appears in the neighbor; requested `.git` absent | Returns exact trailing-space path; requested `.git` exists; neighbor `.git` absent |
| Relative ` relative git ` | Returns `<fixture>/relative git`; initializes that neighbor | Returns `<fixture>/ relative git `; initializes the exact requested directory |
| SQLite `<fixture>/sqlite repository ` | Reports the trimmed repository | Reports the exact existing trailing-space repository; snapshots remain empty |

Both neighbors' sentinel contents remain unchanged. After each head initialization an independent native `git -C <exact-path> rev-parse --absolute-git-dir` resolves to the exact requested `.git` directory. An ordinary repository succeeds on both revisions. Passing three spaces as the required repository still returns structured `Missing required --repository value.` with exit 1 on both revisions.

Actual head readback excerpt (`<fixture>` replaces only the temporary prefix):

```text
backup git init --repository "<fixture>/git absolute " --json
  -> {"repositoryPath":"<fixture>/git absolute "}, exit 0
stat("<fixture>/git absolute /.git") -> directory
stat("<fixture>/git absolute/.git") -> ENOENT
git -C "<fixture>/git absolute " rev-parse --absolute-git-dir
  -> "<fixture>/git absolute /.git\n", exit 0
backup sqlite list --repository "<fixture>/sqlite repository " --json
  -> {"ok":true,"repositoryPath":"<fixture>/sqlite repository ","snapshots":[]}
```

To repeat, choose a private parent directory, create `backup` as a neighbor, then run `openclaw backup git init --repository '<parent>/backup ' --json`. Inspect `.git` under each distinct spelling with `stat` and Git itself. Repeat with a relative name containing spaces at both ends. No remote push is needed.

<details>
<summary>Focused validation, cost, and limitations</summary>

```sh
node ../replace-four-backup-path-proof-20261109.mjs "$PWD" green ../backup-path-green.json
```

The base run changes only `green` to `red` to assert the observed wrong-directory behavior. Driver SHA-256: `ef3f6d8eb8c31f5fe3066e9624d0f6fc4ca5033d43f7afc1e3c6696e01b6a898`. The recorded source head and native build commit both equal the tested head above.

- Acceptance RED: two real Git initializations target the trimmed neighbor; SQLite listing reports the trimmed name. Three shared-resolver regression assertions also fail on base.
- `OPENCLAW_VITEST_RUNTIME=node node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/commands/backup-shared.test.ts src/commands/backup-git.test.ts src/commands/backup-sqlite.test.ts src/commands/backup-schedule.test.ts --maxWorkers=1 --reporter=dot`: 65 passed, 189.77s wrapper including 108.866s cold worker compilation.
- `OPENCLAW_VITEST_RUNTIME=node node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/snapshot/git-backup.test.ts src/snapshot/local-repository.test.ts --maxWorkers=1 --reporter=dot`: 71 passed, 3 platform/fixture skips; final 418.26s wrapper including 131.970s cold worker compilation. Real-Git cases cover new literal directories, a spaced intermediate component, mode 0700, and adoption of an existing literal repository through its parent alias. Existing unsafe-permission and snapshot/restore regressions pass.
- Scoped source-backed `tsgo`, typed `oxlint` over all changed production/test files, `oxfmt`, `git diff --check`, and one-page MDX check: passed.
- Staged test-line ratchet passed: 6,589,106 / 6,589,138 ceiling. A 30-line allocation covers 32 added backend-test lines minus 2 removed shared-test lines; no shared scalar baseline change.
- Native `sourcePerformance` build of the committed head passed in 4m30.6s; exact-built-head CLI GREEN followed that build.
- Author simplification and test-value audit completed; no independent model review is claimed. Seven files form one complete path repair: production +27/−31, tests +37/−7, docs +4/−3, allocation metadata +2. The backend consolidation removes more production code than it adds; separate partial PRs would leave the native path broken.

Compatibility/security: no config/default, Git remote, database/schema, backup format, dependency, or permission-policy change. Original directory trust and durability checks remain. Home expansion and blank-value behavior retain their existing contracts. No new alias-creation guarantee is introduced.

Not tested: real remote repositories/push, live production backup data, native end-to-end restore/schedule execution, Windows/macOS, the full repository suite, or upstream PR CI before opening. Other command callers and existing backend restore behavior have focused suite coverage; the real process proof is the Git-init/SQLite-list boundary shown above.

</details>

prs.title: fix(ui): session New window/New tab always fails with "Allow pop-ups" in the macOS app
prs.body:
> **AI-assisted: yes**

Closes #144582

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users of the native macOS app choosing "New window" or "New tab" from the Control UI session tab menu would always see the toast "Allow pop-ups for this site, then try again." There is no way to allow pop-ups for the embedded WKWebView, so both actions were dead ends (the same actions work in a regular browser).

- **Related:** #144582 (labels: clawsweeper:queueable-fix, clawsweeper:fix-shape-clear, clawsweeper:source-repro).

## Why This Change Was Made

The web side reserves an inert `about:blank` popup via `window.open` and later redirects it to the session route. The macOS shell's `createWebViewWith` delegate classifies the `about:blank` request as ignorable and returns nil, so `window.open` returns null and the UI reports a blocked popup. The fix hands the final session URL to the existing native `openclawLink` bridge (already used by the Browser panel's external open) whenever that bridge is present, and keeps the previous `window.open` reservation as the browser fallback.

- **Intended outcome:** inside the macOS app, New window / New tab from the session menu hand the final session URL to the native link bridge instead of failing; no popup-blocked toast. The receiving default browser opens the Control UI session route; it needs its own gateway sign-in, so a previously paired browser renders the session directly while a never-paired browser lands on the Control UI login gate (an explicit sign-in surface) rather than the session.
- **Out of scope:** creating a native dashboard window/tab for the session (the shell has no such API today; whether to add one is flagged as a maintainer decision below); browser popup semantics are unchanged.
- **Highest-risk area:** routing the action through the native bridge hands a credential-free URL to the default browser, which does not inherit the app's WebKit credentials — a browser that never signed in to this gateway will not see the session.
- **How is that risk mitigated?** The native receiver already validates main-frame + trusted same-origin source before opening; the posted URL intentionally carries no credentials (Gateway credentials must not be exposed in URLs), and an unauthenticated receiving browser is stopped at the login gate, which the E2E now asserts explicitly. Without the bridge (regular browsers), or if the post throws, the previous flow including the blocked-popup toast is preserved and covered by tests.

## User Impact

macOS app users can open a session from the session menu's New window / New tab items again: the session route now opens through the native link handoff in the default browser instead of failing with an impossible "Allow pop-ups" instruction. The receiving browser must be signed in to the gateway itself: an unpaired browser reaches the Control UI login gate (explicit sign-in) rather than the session; a browser that has already paired renders the session directly. Regular browser behavior is unchanged.

- **Success criteria:** with the native link bridge present, both menu actions post the final same-origin session URL and never call `window.open`; without the bridge, the previous reservation + toast flow is kept. The posted URL grants nothing on its own: a never-paired receiving browser stops at the login gate without rendering the session.
- **What should reviewers focus on?** `ui/src/lib/sessions/session-menu-navigation.ts` (bridge handoff placed before the popup reservation); regression fixtures in `session-menu-navigation.test.ts` ("hands … to the native shell link bridge instead of a blocked popup", "falls back to the browser popup when the native link bridge rejects the post"); the real-Gateway E2E in `ui/src/e2e/session-menu-native-bridge.real-gateway.e2e.test.ts` (real Gateway + served Control UI + a page-level `openclawLink` bridge stand-in, covering both actions, the posted destination loaded verbatim in a paired isolated browser context, and the never-paired context stopping at the login gate).

## Evidence

- **Real environment tested:** Linux, Node 26, Playwright Chromium, a real Gateway child process built from this branch (`createOpenClawTestInstance`), and the Control UI served from this branch's source. The page-level `window.webkit.messageHandlers.openclawLink` bridge is installed through a browser init script before any page script runs — the same surface the macOS dashboard shell installs — and, like the native receiver, it does not open anything inside the source browser. The handoff destination is verified in isolated browser contexts that share no cookies, storage, or page state with the source page, modeling how an external default browser receives the `NSWorkspace.open` handoff: one context signs in to the gateway once through the Control UI's gateway confirmation surface (the analog of a previously paired default browser) and then navigates to the posted URL verbatim with no credential parameters appended; a second, never-paired context loads the same posted URL and must stop at the Control UI login gate. The macOS app itself is not runnable in this environment.
- **Exact steps or commands run after this patch:**
  ```bash
  node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run --config test/vitest/vitest.ui-e2e.config.ts --configLoader runner ui/src/e2e/session-menu-native-bridge.real-gateway.e2e.test.ts
  node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run ui/src/lib/sessions/session-menu-navigation.test.ts ui/src/app/native-link-routing.test.ts
  node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run test/vitest-ui-e2e-config.test.ts
  pnpm exec oxfmt --check ui/src/e2e/session-menu-native-bridge.real-gateway.e2e.test.ts
  pnpm exec oxlint ui/src/e2e/session-menu-native-bridge.real-gateway.e2e.test.ts
  node scripts/run-tsgo.mts -b test/tsconfig/tsconfig.core.test.ui-e2e.json --builders 1
  ```
- **Evidence after fix:** real-Gateway E2E (`session-menu-native-bridge.real-gateway.e2e.test.ts`, head `d626215`) output:
  ```text
  ✓ hands session New window and New tab to the native link bridge instead of a popup 28328ms
   Test Files  1 passed (1)
        Tests  1 passed (1)
  ```
  Both "New window" and "New tab" from the session menu post to the bridge:
  ```json
  [
    { "type": "open-link", "url": "http://127.0.0.1:<port>/chat/main/native-bridge-proof", "target": "external" },
    { "type": "open-link", "url": "http://127.0.0.1:<port>/chat/main/native-bridge-proof", "target": "external" }
  ]
  ```
  with zero `window.open` reservations from the menu code and no "Allow pop-ups" toast. The destination is then verified the way an external default browser receives it, in isolated contexts that share no state with the source page: the paired context first signs in once through the Control UI's gateway confirmation surface, then navigates to the exact posted URL verbatim — no `gatewayUrl` or token parameters appended — and renders the session's transcript, so the loaded session comes from the handed-off URL plus the receiving browser's own independent sign-in state. The never-paired context loads the same posted URL and stops at the `openclaw-login-gate` sign-in surface without ever rendering the session: the handoff grants nothing by itself, and an unauthenticated browser reaches an explicit sign-in flow instead of the session.
- **Observed result after fix:** with the `openclawLink` bridge present, `open-new-window`/`open-new-tab` hand the final same-origin session URL to the bridge and never touch `window.open`; the blocked-popup toast no longer fires. A receiving browser already signed in to the gateway renders the intended session from the posted URL; a never-paired receiving browser is stopped at the login gate. Without the bridge (regular browser), the previous reservation + fallback flow is preserved (covered by unit tests).
- **Before evidence:** with `session-menu-navigation.ts` restored to its pre-patch state (same worktree, patched E2E), the E2E fails — `AssertionError: expected undefined to deeply equal { type: 'open-link', …(2) }`, `Test Files 1 failed (1)` — the bridge never receives anything because every attempt goes through the `about:blank` popup reservation, matching the report (so the destination steps are never reached on unpatched code). At unit level the regression tests fail on main with `AssertionError: expected "vi.fn()" to be called … Number of calls: 0`.
- **What was not tested:** live macOS app / WKWebView runtime and the native Swift receiver (no macOS hardware in this environment); the native receiver path is unchanged and covered by existing native tests.
- **Proof tier:** L2 (real Gateway, real served Control UI, real browser; the WKWebView host bridge surface is installed at page level as the shell does, not mocked at module level; the handoff destination is verified in isolated browser contexts — one paired through the real sign-in surface, one never-paired — rather than a state-sharing same-browser tab).
- **Proof limitations:** no macOS environment available; the WKWebView message-handler transport and the Swift-side `NSWorkspace.open` handoff would need a reporter/maintainer repro on macOS. The bridge contract asserted in the E2E matches the existing native `DashboardWindowController.receiveLinkMessage` validation (main frame, trusted same-origin source, http(s) URL). The posted URL is credential-free by design: it grants session access only in a browser that already signed in to the gateway, and an unpaired browser lands on the login gate (now asserted explicitly). Whether the macOS session actions should instead open an app-owned authenticated destination (a new app window/tab that retains the app's WebKit credentials, as the ClawSweeper review recommends considering) is an open maintainer decision — this PR keeps the external-browser handoff and makes its sign-in requirement explicit and tested rather than building new native windowing unilaterally.
- **Review state:** Follow-up on the ClawSweeper review of `8d40173`: reworked the E2E destination step that previously appended `gatewayUrl` and token parameters before loading the posted URL (which overstated what an unpaired default browser receives) — the destination now signs in explicitly first and loads the posted URL verbatim, and a never-paired negative case asserts the login gate; the destination-access claim in this body is corrected accordingly. Rebased onto latest main (`d626215`). CI lanes pending on the updated head. Note: `checks-ui-e2e-real-gateway` previously failed on `quota-reset-status.real-gateway.e2e.test.ts` ("expected 'Signed in' to be 'Ready'") — a main-level failure unrelated to this PR's files (the same test fails identically on other current PRs, e.g. #146400) and not chased here.

prs.title: fix(agents): ask_user ignores the question number in replies like "1. Deny"
prs.body:
Closes #190485
Related: #173760, #173845, #146646

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: a multi-question `ask_user` answer is saved as `1. Deny`, lands on the wrong question, or is rejected when the user numbers each reply line the way the prompt numbers the questions.

## User Impact

User impact: replying `1. Deny` and `2. Approved` on separate lines answers question 1 with `Deny` and question 2 with `Approved`, in any line order. A reply that answers only some questions is still rejected and the question stays open. Multi-question prompts now label questions `Question 1: Deploy` and number each question's options from 1. On Telegram and Signal, the old `1. Deploy` header ran together with the option lines into one list (`4. Checks`), so answering by the displayed number picked the wrong question. Single-question cards rendered as Telegram messages or Teams cards now number their options to match "Reply with the number".

Compatibility: in a multi-question reply, a line starting with digits, a dot and whitespace (`2. Approved`) is read as an answer to that question number. `1.5`, `Node.js: 22` and `U.S. region: East` parse as before. A line matched to a question by number or id no longer also fills another question by position. On main, `2: Approved` alone completed question 1 with the text `2: Approved`; it is now rejected as incomplete.

## Why This Change Was Made

The reply parser only treated `:`, `=` and `-` as key separators. `1. Deny` stayed positional, so the agent received `1. Deny` as the answer, reordered lines landed on the wrong question, and questions with fixed options rejected the reply. Numbered lines are now a separate rule that requires whitespace after the dot, checked before the unchanged keyed syntax. The single-question card text now uses the same `1. Label - description` lines as the text prompt.

Multi-question prompts numbered each question (`1. Deploy`) directly above options that also start at `1.`. Telegram and Signal render markdown lists with their own numbering, so the header and the options became one list: `1. Deploy`, `2. Staging`, `3. Production`, `4. Checks`. Questions are now labelled `Question 1: Deploy`. That is not a list marker, so each question's options render from 1, and the question number is the one the `1. answer` rule binds.

The first revision of this PR also copied a single-line reply into every question. That was wrong: it invented answers the user never gave and broke the incomplete-answer contract from #146646. It is removed. The multi-question guidance wording is left to #173845, so this PR no longer touches that string.

The live replies in #190485 were each a single line for a two-question card, so they were incomplete and their rejection was correct. That issue is corrected.

## Evidence

- Regression table in `src/agents/harness/user-input-bridge.test.ts` (5 rows): 5/5 pass. With `user-input-bridge.ts` from main (`1b15b48e2f3`), 2 rows fail: `1. Deny\n2. Approved` is saved as `"1. Deny"`, and a lone `2. Approved` fills question 1 with `"2. Approved"`. With the previous head (`303c244630d`), 4 rows fail: lone `2` answers both questions, `1.5\n2.5` becomes `5`/`5`, and `Node.js: 22` / `U.S. region: East` split at the dot.
- Consumers: 18 test files, 354 tests pass locally, including the 3 suites that failed in [run 41326074085](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41326074085): `dispatch-from-config.question-custody` 17/17, `session-accessor.question-answer-transcript` 8/8, and `test/contracts/ask-user-msteams-presentation` 2/2 (updated to the numbered lines).
- New qa-lab scenario `gateway-ask-user-numbered-text-reply` (mock-openai, real Gateway): `1. Production` alone gets "The answer was not accepted: question 'checks' requires an answer" and the question stays pending. Then `1. Production\n2. E2E\n3. Urgent` resolves it as `Production` / `E2E` / `Urgent`, and the waiting run resumes with those values. With main's parser, the same reply is stored as `1. Production` / `2. E2E` / `3. Urgent` and the scenario fails.
- Multi-question prompt through Telegram's markdown renderer: on `b2b86091a7f` the numbered lines are `1. Deploy`, `2. Staging`, `3. Production`, `4. Checks`, `5. Unit`, `6. E2E`, `7. Lint`. On this head they are `1. Staging`, `2. Production`, then `1. Unit`, `2. E2E`, `3. Lint`, under `Question 1: Deploy` and `Question 2: Checks`. The new test in `test/telegram-question-gateway.test.ts` fails on `b2b86091a7f` and passes here. Signal's renderer showed the same merged list before and per-question lists after.
- Telegram plugin against a local Bot API stub (scripted model, not live): after an incomplete `1. Production` was rejected, the reply `3. Urgent` / `2. E2E` / `1. Production` reached the agent with the rejected line replayed in front of it (#193159), as `1. Production` / `3. Urgent` / `2. E2E` / `1. Production`. On `b2b86091a7f` those four lines resumed the agent with Production / E2E / Urgent. On main `f5f27c3ef6e` the same four lines resumed it with `1. Production` / `3. Urgent` / `2. E2E`. A three-line reply without the replay was not run on main.
- Card text from the real Telegram and Teams renderers for a single question with options: main shows `- Staging (Recommended): Safer default`; this branch shows `1. Staging (Recommended) - Safer default`. Channels without a presentation renderer already received the numbered prompt text.
- `pnpm run tsgo:all`, oxlint, oxfmt and `git diff --check` are clean. 22 test files (474 tests) pass locally. Test-line growth is 94 lines, recorded in `config/test-lines-allocations/ask-user-numbered-reply-lines.txt`. `checks-fast-baseline-ratchets` fails because main is over its test-line ceiling before this PR's lines count: the 11-03 run reported `over by: 834; net delta: +59`. Replaying it on this head merged with `982f3b1ee2b` gives `over by: 49; net delta: +94`, and `982f3b1ee2b` alone is `over by: 49; net delta: 0`. An allocation cannot exceed the PR's own growth, so this clears once main is back under its ceiling.
- Not covered: no live Telegram run yet. The qa-lab scenario answers through `chat.send`, which reaches the same parser and `question.resolve` call as a Telegram reply but delivers the rejection notice another way. In the Telegram stub run the rejection notice did not arrive, on main as well: #193159, which this PR does not change.

prs.title: fix(heartbeat): classify prepared-model-runtime generation supersession as preemption, not agent-runner-failure
prs.body:
## Summary

Fixes the recurring `heartbeat-main` false **`agent-runner-failure`** (job `7bf06607`), observed live on 2026-09-09 (e.g. run `18:17:12` → failed `18:23:44`, and repeated hourly).

**Root cause — a TOCTOU race in the runtime, not config or network.** The heartbeat run passes its point-in-time idle guards (`resolveHeartbeatWakeStage`), then `main` re-prepares its runtime and bumps the *published owner generation*. When the heartbeat's model turn goes to acquire that owner, `prepared-model-runtime` throws `PreparedModelRuntimeOwnerNotPublishedError` ("prepared model runtime plugin generation was superseded"), which fast-fails **every** model-fallback candidate in a few ms and surfaces as `Embedded agent failed before reply`.

Because this arrives as a **thrown** error (carried on the model-fallback summary's `cause`), not an abort-signal supersession, `resolveReplyOperationAbortReason` did not recognise it, so the run was classified `failed` → a false `agent-runner-failure` alert. The **non-throwing** supersession path already maps to a benign `preempted` skip; this makes the thrown path consistent.

Live evidence (sanitized), run history, and the full write-up are attached to the ops report.

## Fix

Teach `resolveReplyOperationAbortReason(replyOperation, error)` to detect a prepared-model-runtime generation supersession carried by the **terminal error** — direct, `cause`-chained, or inside a model-fallback summary — via a new `isPreparedModelRuntimeSupersessionError` chain-walk (mirroring the existing `resolveRestartLifecycleError` walk). It then returns `"superseded"`, and the existing plumbing (`handleAgentExecutionError` → `resolveReplyOperationAbortReason(op, err)` → `{kind:"aborted", reason}` → heartbeat dispatch) maps it to a `preempted` skip.

Any other thrown error stays a real, visible failure — this **preserves error visibility** and only reclassifies the genuine race. A lower turn timeout or more retries would *not* fix this (verified in the prior diagnosis); the failure interleaves with healthy 260 ms `no-route` skips.

## Not a duplicate-delivery bug

The "duplicate log entries" are duplicate `applyJobResult` WARN emissions, not duplicate sends: the authoritative `cron runs` history has **one** finished run per failure while the raw log has two WARN lines, and all 50 runs report `deliveryStatus: not-requested`. Heartbeat sends nothing here, so there were zero duplicate chat messages.

## Tests

New `src/auto-reply/reply/reply-operation-abort.superseded-classification.test.ts` (8 cases): the classifier (direct / fallback-summary-cause / cause-chained / genuine-negative) and the abort-reason resolution. The two integration cases go **RED** when the one wiring line is reverted, and the genuine-failure case stays classified as a real failure. `tsgo -p tsconfig.core.json` and `-p tsconfig.extensions.json` both exit 0; touched existing suites (`heartbeat-wake.preemption`, `heartbeat-runner.failure-delivery`, `heartbeat-runner.tool-response`) stay green (52 + 8 = 60 passed).

## DEPLOY
- target: none (merge only)
- service: agent-runtime
- depends-on: none
- supersedes: none
- frontend-touched: no
- migrations: no
- env-vars: none
- feature-flag: none

prs.title: feat: add native Celeris, Fastino, Nace and Perplexity decisions
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Several native APIs evaluated in Artificial Analysis Decision Index v2 cannot be selected as OpenClaw Decision models.

## User Impact

Adds opt-in text/JSON Boolean, Choice, and Score support for:

- Celeris-1.1 Decision: `celeris/celeris-1.1-decision`.
- Perplexity Decider v1.2: `perplexity-decisions/pplx-decider-v1.2`. Native auth is separate from existing Perplexity/OpenRouter search.
- Nace Drex Max v1.1: `nace/drex-max-v1.1`.
- Hosted Fastino GLiDE: `fastino/fastino/GLiDE`.

These are Decision-only entries. Connecting credentials does not select models or change chat defaults. Image inputs and vendor extensions are not exposed in this first stage. New plugin packages are development-checkout candidates, not claimed npm releases.

**Draft / remaining proof:** no credential-authorized live inference was performed. Fixtures do not establish account access or production reliability. API smoke proof remains required.

**Exclusions:** Clef is not registered: its official API silently truncates long state, without a verified reject/no-truncation mode. Fastino's current hosted ID is unversioned, so this is not a verified pin to benchmark v1.2. Baseten Elephant/Mammoth, OpenRouter Jev 1.14, OpenAI Luna Decision support, and Anthropic Haiku 5.5 chat support already exist. Benchmark inclusion does not establish a native typed Decision endpoint for Haiku.

## Why This Change Was Made

Official API contracts, not social labels, determine support. Celeris/Nace reuse the OpenAI Decisions codec. Perplexity uses its distinct named-question format. Fastino maps fractional `expected_level`, not integer argmax `score`, and always sends `store: false`.

The existing prepared HTTP executor is shared instead of duplicating auth, live admission, proxy/TLS, deadlines, cancellation, credential-reflection rejection, and release. No chat fallback, automatic retry, provider-specific config leaves, or benchmark-derived token prices are added.

## Evidence

- `pnpm build` passed in 212.5s. The UI report emitted non-fatal gzip warnings: chat boot 1266.7 KiB / 1266.4 KiB cap; new boot 784.5 KiB / 784.4 KiB cap. These warnings are not attributed to this change or baseline.
- **88 focused tests passed:** 10 new native integration cases; 64 existing OpenAI/ClawRouter/SDK cases; 14 prompt-prefix stability cases. New suite: 258ms test time, 47.78s wrapper wall including cold compilation. CI seconds are not available.
- Native proof covers real manifest-to-Decision-picker projection, host env-key isolation, registered provider-to-guarded-HTTP assembly, native bounds, distributions/usage, retention, and GLiDE score semantics. Only external DNS/fetch are fixtures.
- Core, all four package boundaries, and focused test typechecks passed. Targeted type-aware lint, format, export synchronization, and diff checks passed.
- Docs: 16,533 internal links, zero broken; config examples passed; MDX passed for 1,439 files. Follow-up install guidance matches automatic plugin application; its two-file MDX check passed.
- Config baseline was generated: plugin paths **5018 → 5081** are exactly 21 existing generic management paths per new plugin. Core/channel counts and hashes are unchanged. All three new plugin config schemas are empty; no spare budget was added.
- Simplification consolidated four duplicated test files into one integration owner. Production TypeScript +550/−156 (net +394), tests +329. The test allocation protects four wire routes, picker discovery, and credential isolation; shared lifecycle tests remain at their existing owner.
- Local autoreview (Codex, configured GPT-6.1 Sol), P0–P2, implementation candidate against `0e13ef0ab3f8f093a3daba4b53fcd07d5485837d`: no actionable findings. An optional unchanged auth implementation was excluded by the helper's sensitive-filename guard, not renamed/copied; the reviewer retained that context limitation and did not replay tests/live inference. Generated config artifacts were separately checked; runtime source is unchanged since review.
- SDK API comparison timed out during declaration rendering after 420s; no compatibility verdict was produced. Runtime comparison pins `0e13ef0ab3f8f093a3daba4b53fcd07d5485837d` → `42efe8d442637fbd09c732d5bc9752f2dd599adc`; later commit is docs-only. Not ready for landing.

Thanks @vincentkoc for the request and evaluation context.

- Celeris: [models](https://docs.celeris.ai/models.md), [Decisions](https://docs.celeris.ai/decisions.md). Official endpoint: `https://inference.celeris.ai/celeris-1-decision/v1/decisions`.

</details>

prs.title: fix(proxy): escape terminal diagnostic values
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`openclaw proxy start` and human-readable `proxy validate` output print filesystem paths and diagnostic strings directly. A path or destination containing terminal escapes, line breaks, tabs, or carriage returns can clear or rewrite the displayed diagnostic and add apparent output lines. Ordinary Unicode text is valid data and should remain readable without controlling the terminal.

## Why This Change Was Made

Use the existing `terminalText` formatter at the proxy CLI's human presentation boundary: startup URL/CA/database fields, configuration problems, destination URLs, and both successful/failed check details. Escape values before applying the existing styles. Do not modify the validation owner or its inputs, persistence, JSON diagnostics, raw blobs, or inherited child-process I/O. No custom sanitizer, dependency, configuration, or second output mode is added.

## User Impact

Proxy startup and validation diagnostics retain their own line layout even when a configured path or supplied URL contains controls. Operators can still read ordinary Unicode names and see escaped `\n`, `\t`, and `\r`. Exit codes, recovery guidance, JSON data, and existing proxy-credential redaction remain unchanged. [CLI reference](https://docs.openclaw.ai/cli/proxy) documents the human/JSON distinction.

## Evidence

Base native build: `b6d8eb287e0898d2c50d89abaef749e4c25ca66a`. Tested source and native build: `5398b23970eb5e239518f00c6f1da314366d42f4`, OpenClaw `2026.11.1`, Linux / Node 24.22.1, November 9, 2026. The subsequently inspected main `5f84a8166dc524a4eab375b16030239acbefc92b` has the same unfixed proxy CLI owner.

### Real CLI RED → GREEN

The same frozen external driver ran the actual built CLI with a private configuration and state directory. Its payload contained `café`, U+001B followed by `[2J`, LF, TAB, and CR. Nothing in the CLI, validation, capture store, or returned output was mocked.

| Actual CLI scenario | Base | Tested head | Independent control/readback |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `proxy start --port 0`, controls inside the real state-directory name | CA/DB paths emit raw controls | Paths display `café\nforged\tvalue\rend` without raw controls | Original-path CA file exists; session read back through `proxy sessions --json` |
| `proxy validate`, invalid destination containing the payload | Raw controls in check line | One escaped check line; exit 1 | `--json` retains the original destination and `Invalid allowed destination URL` |
| `proxy validate`, missing CA filename containing the payload | Raw controls in Problems | Escaped error and existing CA recovery guidance; exit 1 | `--json` retains the original error string |

Across all three scenarios, raw-payload observations change from 3/3 on base to 0/3 on head, and escaped-payload observations change from 0/3 to 3/3. An ordinary invalid-destination control still reports the same validation error and exit 1. JSON retains the original diagnostic strings on both revisions.

Actual head output excerpts (`<fixture>` replaces only the temporary directory prefix):

```text
Debug proxy: http://127.0.0.1:43049
CA cert: <fixture>/state café\nforged\tvalue\rend/debug-proxy/certs/root-ca.pem
Capture DB: <fixture>/state café\nforged\tvalue\rend/state/openclaw.sqlite
Press Ctrl+C to stop.

  ✗ allowed invalid:café\nforged\tvalue\rend — Invalid allowed destination URL

proxy sessions --json:
{"sessions":[{"id":"5864d1d9-e33e-4b02-9f1f-79b9b08beaa6",
"mode":"proxy-start","endedAt":1794195993353,...}]}
```

The shown backslash sequences are printable characters in head's human output. The CA file was checked at the original filesystem path containing the actual controls. The native proxy exited cleanly on SIGTERM and its persisted session has a numeric `endedAt`. No private-key bytes were read or printed.

To repeat the validation case from Bash:

```bash
openclaw proxy validate --proxy-url http://127.0.0.1:9 \
  --allowed-url $'invalid:café\e[2J\nforged\tvalue\rend' \
  --denied-url invalid:ordinary
```

Repeat with `--json`: the original destination remains in `checks[0].url`.

prs.body:
Fixes #195547

## What Problem This Solves

Signal status updates currently require new messages instead of updating an earlier message in place.

## User Impact

Users can edit the account's earlier Signal messages through the existing message edit action, using native or container transports. Signal's own edit eligibility rules still apply.

Revision tracking is bounded and process-local. After a restart or eviction, an edit targets the supplied message ID; callers should retain the latest returned ID. Live client behavior and reaction/pin preservation have not been verified.

## Why This Change Was Made

Expose Signal editing through the existing action and send owners, and track the latest known revision for subsequent edits. No new configuration option or persistent store is introduced.

**Repair to the supplied branch:** the container adapter previously dropped the edit timestamp and would send an ordinary new message. Translate it to the REST API’s `edit_timestamp` field, which is supported by the [upstream request contract](https://github.com/bbernhard/signal-cli-rest-api/blob/787d204e155d0c73840a615a5e90c697bacaa6f1/src/api/api.go#L128-L145) and [send handler](https://github.com/bbernhard/signal-cli-rest-api/blob/787d204e155d0c73840a615a5e90c697bacaa6f1/src/api/api.go#L564-L567).

The repair adds three production lines in the existing transport adapter. Simplification replaced the mock-only send test with real loopback transport coverage and removed incomplete receipt casts. Overall: +64 net production lines and +77 net regression-test lines; the allocation covers action discovery, revision chaining, and native/container success and rejection without an ordinary-send fallback.

## Evidence

- Applied fork commits `784ac03d68349723b79bddf734e9a286ad46f71f` and `e93a88182b12aede727f82124f74af5cb6e6f7c2` onto refreshed main `ee431f3f2dcd9cc04a86c5c7756d13f88bdf1dde`, then repaired the container translation.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes garbled gateway names in Apple clients when Bonjour service names contain escaped non-ASCII characters, such as the curly apostrophe in “Bobby’s Mac”.

## User Impact

## Summary

- add a bounded scheduled/manual matrix for the npm `latest` and `extended-stable` release lines
- run current `main` tooling against each shipped line's source and bytes through the postpublish verifier, Plugin SDK renderer, and ClawHub dry-run packer
- let the existing plugin pretag checker separate the shipped source root from the trusted tooling root while preserving existing callers
- materialize shipped source as archive data only after trusted restore-only setup, without a dynamic checkout or shipped dependency install
- add workflow and packer contract coverage, including guards for the cache/execution boundary and SDK rendering of identical `main`/tag commits

## Why

RRI-587 identified three regressions that reached shipped releases because current publication tooling was never exercised against the last-shipped stable and extended-stable inputs. This lane keeps that compatibility proof on protected `main`, resolves immutable npm tags, uses read-only permissions, bounds each matrix job to six hours, and retains SDK evidence for 30 days.

## Scope decision

Moving the operator invocation of `release:candidate --skip-dispatch` is intentionally left as a release-controller follow-up. The current checklist already performs its early Plugin SDK review before waiting for Full Release Validation; changing when the controller invokes that checklist is separate orchestration policy and is not needed for this causal compatibility lane.

## Validation

prs.title: improve(mcp-relay): apply the Control UI glossary and style to Connected apps copy
prs.body:
## Problem

The MCP relay **Connected apps** page (`extensions/mcp-relay/src/control-ui.ts`) hard-coded all of its English in the view. The plugin had no translation catalog, so the post-merge locale refresh couldn't translate it. Some of the copy also broke the approved Control UI glossary and style rules: an all-caps eyebrow label, a passive "is required" sentence, "do not" instead of a contraction, and "embedded browser sessions" (which reuses the product noun *session* for a different concept). Errors showed the raw request message as the whole alert, with nothing saying what failed or what to do next.

## Solution

- Added the plugin's English source catalog at `src/i18n/locales/en.ts`, at the path `control-ui-plugin-i18n-catalog.ts` derives from `openclaw.controlUi`. The view now reads every string through `translateControlUiMessage`.
- Added `src/i18n/{index.ts,locales.ts}` on the nostr/whatsapp pattern. This page is plain DOM, not Solid, so `locales.ts` keeps the translated catalog in module state and the page re-renders when it loads. The page also re-renders on host locale changes; date formatting follows the locale too.
- `src/i18n/locales/translated.json` is committed as `{}`. The brief said to leave it absent, but without the file the plugin's Control UI build fails: the unresolved dynamic import trips "Control UI builds must bundle their browser dependencies". The empty file holds no translation values; the locale refresh bot fills it after merge.
- Errors now follow "Couldn’t {verb} {thing}. {Next step}." The redacted raw message moves under a collapsed **Show details**. The Control UI SDK has no shared disclosure component for plugin pages, so this uses a native `<details>`.
- Static `innerHTML` templates are now `element()` builders, so translated text is only ever set as text content.
- Manifest config hints: `Default Agent` → `Default agent`, and the help text says "new sessions" instead of "new conversations". I regenerated `docs/.generated/config-baseline.sha256` to match (only the plugin baseline hash changed).

### Notable copy changes (old → new)

| Where | Old | New |
| --- | --- | --- |
| No read access | Read access is required to view connected apps. | You need read access to view connected apps. |
| Consent eyebrow | CONNECTION REQUEST / CONNECT ANOTHER GATEWAY | Connection request / Connect another Gateway (CSS `text-transform: uppercase` keeps the look) |
| Consent, no permission | …permissions do not allow connecting an app. | …permissions don’t allow connecting an app. |
| Revoke hint | Revoking an app ends its MCP access and embedded browser sessions. … | Revoking an app ends its MCP and embedded UI access. … (matches the existing revoke notice) |
| Load failure | *(raw message)* / The request failed. Try again. | Couldn’t load connected apps. Try again. + Show details |
| Approve / deny failure | *(raw message)* | Couldn’t connect {app}. Reopen the app’s connection page. / Couldn’t deny {app}. Try again. + Show details |
| Revoke failure | *(raw message)* | Couldn’t revoke {app}. Try again. + Show details |
| Pairing failure | *(raw message)* / Pairing failed. Try again. | Couldn’t create a pairing code. Try again. + Show details |
| Invalid relay return | The relay returned an invalid return address. Reopen the app’s connection page. | The relay returned an invalid return address. (now the detail; the next step is in the summary) |
| Config hint label | Default Agent | Default agent |
| Config hint help | Optional agent for new conversations; … | Optional agent for new sessions; … |

Moved into the translation file: **53 keys** (`ui:i18n:verify`: `plugin=mcp-relay keys=53`). About 9 existing strings changed, 6 are new (5 error summaries and "Show details"), and 2 manifest hints changed. The rest moved unchanged.

Left as is on purpose:
- "Gateway owner": an owner principal, not a role name. See the open question below.
- "Full access, including administration": names an activity, not the role.
- `ui-tunnel*` transport errors.
- The model-facing `recommendedPrompts`.

## Impact

- The Connected apps page becomes translatable through the existing locale refresh. English rendering is unchanged except for the copy above.
- The error alert is now a `div` with the summary and a collapsed details element. It got small margin and details styles, so expect a slight visual change in error states.
- Known limit: the page label in the navigation is resolved once at activation (`registerPage` takes a static string), so it stays English until the next activation.

## Evidence

- `extensions/mcp-relay/src/control-ui.test.ts`: 7/7 pass. Assertions follow the changed English. The refresh-failure case now checks the summary and that the collapsed (closed) details hold the raw message.
- `pnpm ui:i18n:verify`: green (`plugin=mcp-relay keys=53 locales=0 unused_translations=0`).
- `pnpm check:changed` on the committed head: all lanes ok, including typecheck extensions and extension tests, lint extensions, format, the dead-export scan, the Control UI i18n catalog, the bundled channel config metadata and the config docs baseline. One check failed, `changelog attributions`, and it fails the same way on `origin/main` (existing `Thanks @steipete-oai` entries in `CHANGELOG/2026.6.8.md` and `2026.7.1.md`). This PR doesn't touch those files.
- Plugin Control UI build (`scripts/build-plugin-control-ui.mts extensions/mcp-relay`): succeeds.
- `git diff --check`: clean.
- pr-simplify pass: I removed an unused `Translator` type export that the dead-export scan flagged. There's no new state beyond the error-detail fields and the locale tracking the re-render needs.
- Local review: local ClawSweeper isn't installed on this host, so I used autoreview, the documented fallback (Codex, `gpt-6.1-sol`, branch mode, merge base `d59f00281eb0216` → head `2cd7495c4c6`, max priority P2). Result: `scoped-clean`, no actionable findings. The reviewer noted that unchanged SDK and build contracts weren't in its context; the build and verify runs above cover them.

Before/after screenshots are pending and will be added before landing (visual gate).

Not landing: requested by maintainer; screenshots pending before merge.

prs.title: fix(discord): avoid reconnects after server-requested heartbeats
prs.body:
Fixes #195530

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: a healthy Discord connection is unnecessarily reconnected when Discord requests a heartbeat shortly before the client's next scheduled heartbeat.

## User Impact

User impact: Discord stays connected while the requested heartbeat is awaiting its acknowledgment, avoiding needless reconnects and their risk of missed events or extra IDENTIFY calls. No configuration changes or migrations are required.

## Why This Change Was Made

Answering a server-requested heartbeat now restarts the heartbeat interval, giving that heartbeat a full interval to receive its ACK. The existing gateway remains the sole owner of the timer; genuinely missing ACKs still trigger the resumable zombie-recovery path.

The contributor's two-file patch is unchanged. Simplification review retained the shared timer helper and the three distinct regression/control cases: requested-beat timing, acknowledged cadence, and missed-ACK resume behavior. Production delta: +25/-14 lines; test delta: +55 lines.

prs.title: fix(qa-channel): match canonically equivalent message searches
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

QA Channel message searches miss visually identical text when the message or attachment uses a different canonical Unicode form. For example, searching `CAFE\u0301` does not find a message containing `Café`, despite the existing case-insensitive search.

## User Impact

QA message search finds canonically equivalent message text, attachment filenames, alternative text, and transcripts. Message IDs, original text, attachment contents, account/conversation selectors, deletion filtering, and result limits retain their existing contracts. Accents remain significant: this does not introduce accent-insensitive or fuzzy matching.

## Why This Change Was Made

`searchQaBusMessages` is the single search owner behind QA Channel's HTTP search action and the channel client. Normalize the query and its complete lowercase search projection to NFC at that owner; keep storage and returned message objects verbatim. JavaScript's built-in normalization is sufficient. No dependency, option, schema, state migration, or second search implementation is added.

## Evidence

Base: `b6d8eb287e0898d2c50d89abaef749e4c25ca66a`. Tested head: `da23982e40c2c30868d214e405d420535890df78`.

Real path: the production QA bus server, started through its public `bus-api.ts`, received actual loopback HTTP requests to `/v1/inbound/message`, `/v1/actions/search`, `/v1/actions/read`, and `/v1/actions/delete`. No bus methods, normalizers, responses, or network calls were mocked. The same external driver and request bodies ran on base and head; only its expected RED/GREEN outcome differed.

| Searchable field | Stored value / query | Base matches | Head matches |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Message text | `Café` / ` CAFE\u0301 ` | 0 | 1 original ID |
| Attachment filename | `Café` / ` CAFE\u0301 ` | 0 | 1 original ID |
| Attachment alternative text | `Café` / ` CAFE\u0301 ` | 0 | 1 original ID |
| Attachment transcript | `Café` / ` CAFE\u0301 ` | 0 | 1 original ID |
| All four fields, opposite direction | `Cafe\u0301` / ` CAFÉ ` | 0/4 | 4/4 original IDs |

The `\u0301` notation identifies the actual combining character sent in the JSON request, rather than a literal backslash sequence. Each literal-search control returned the same original ID on both revisions. Every other-account, other-conversation, different-word, and deleted-message control returned zero matches on both revisions. Independent HTTP reads retained the original text and attachment strings, including decomposed Unicode.

Actual head readback excerpt, Linux / Node 24.22.1 / November 9, 2026:

```text
POST inbound/message text="Café" -> message.id=<created-id>
POST actions/search query=" CAFE\u0301 " -> messages=[{id:<created-id>,text:"Café",...}]
POST actions/read messageId=<created-id> -> text="Café", attachments=[]
POST actions/search query="CAFE\u0301", accountId="other" -> messages=[]
POST actions/search query="CAFE\u0301", conversationId="other" -> messages=[]
POST actions/delete messageId=<created-id>; literal search -> messages=[]
all 8 canonical-direction/field combinations: 8 matched, 0 failed
```

<details>
<summary>Reproduction, focused checks, cost, and limitations</summary>

Proof command, run with the same frozen driver on each checkout:

```sh
node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs ../replace-four-qa-search-proof-20261109.mjs "$PWD" green ../qa-search-green.json
```

The base run uses `red` instead of `green` only to assert the expected eight misses. Driver SHA-256: `4965161d6d7efd6854bc73bff4b8fe9542bbb4b2a27149f810dbb1822911b2d5`.

To repeat an individual case against a local QA bus, post a synthetic inbound message with `conversation:{id:"search-proof",kind:"direct"}`, `senderId:"synthetic-proof"`, and `text:"Café"`; then post `{query:"CAFE\u0301"}` to `/v1/actions/search`. Compare the result with the actual created ID and read the message through `/v1/actions/read`. For attachment cases put the stored text only in `fileName`, `altText`, or `transcript` of an attachment with `kind:"file"` and `mimeType:"text/plain"`.

Validation:

- Regression RED: four parameterized cases fail on the base with an empty result instead of the created ID.
