- In each run, four actual menu selections were independently read back from the Gateway: `(off, null) → (off, off) → (high, off) → (high, on)`. Supported RPCs then cleared the overrides, and reopening the menus verified inheritance again. A separate explicit-Off session remained unchanged. The same app process served all openings.
- Source/binary hashes, authenticated app status, action/AX records, RPC receipts, screenshots, and cleanup receipts are retained in each run's `real-app-menu-proof` artifact. Codex executed and reviewed this current-head proof; it does not replace Eisenh0rn40's original contribution below.

**Baseline run status:** its functional observations completed, but the workflow failed cleanup verification because the Gateway child had not exited when its wrapper returned. That run is not reported as green. The candidate run added a bounded process-group drain wait and verified both groups retired and the test Keychain was deleted.

**Proof limits:** this is an unbundled development application with generated OS input, not signed-release packaging, physical human clicks, model inference, restart durability, or direct measurement of private submenu object identity. Default loopback policy automatically paired operator/node clients. Both runs show the separate Mac-node warning “Development worker source runner is missing”; the primary operator connection and tested menu RPCs succeeded. prs.title: fix(ui): keep IME composition Enter from connecting from the login form
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Enter that confirms an IME candidate on the login form's Gateway URL or
secret field called `connect()` before the user finished composing, starting
a connection with a partially-typed value. CJK/IME users entering the
Gateway URL or secret (for example while an input method stays active) could
trigger a premature connect.

The login form is the last Enter-submitting text field in the Control UI
without the shared input-local IME guard: the chat composer, browser address,
skill editor, and plugin credentials already reuse `isComposingKeyboardEvent`.

## Why This Change Was Made

Reuse the existing input-local IME owner from #177545 (`ui/src/lib/ime.ts`):
`isComposingKeyboardEvent` recognizes active composition (`isComposing` or
`keyCode 229`) and the bounded WebKit commit-Enter grace after
`compositionend`; `recordCompositionEnd` / `clearCompositionEnd` retire the
marker on keyup and blur. This is the same pattern as the browser address
input (#194136) and the skill editor (#195356). No new timer, global state,
or controller API; URL normalization and connect behavior are unchanged.

Precedent: #194136, #195356 (same IME guard on other Enter-submitting fields).

## User Impact

IME users connecting to a Gateway no longer have a candidate-confirmation
Enter start a connection with an unfinished URL or secret. An intentional
Enter (after composition commits) still connects exactly as before; blur and
the Connect button are unchanged.

## Evidence

**Red on base, green with fix.**

Base: `826999cd5f76f4867a69869489a4fc51cd5e4a35` (upstream main CI ratchet base)
Head: `ea3b4ab8fb9ae7a6d533271f2ef76189d9c22686`

### Discriminative regression tests

- `ui/src/components/login-gate.test.ts` (jsdom): composing Enter
  (`isComposing: true`, `keyCode: 229`, and WebKit grace) on the URL and
  secret fields does not call `onConnect`; a later ordinary Enter does.
  - Base: `expected "vi.fn()" to not be called at all, but actually been called 1 times` (red)
  - Head: 21 passed (the single remaining failure, `explains setup codes`,
    is a local Node 24.13.1 `Uint8Array.fromBase64` limitation — CI runs
    Node 24.22.1 where the API exists; it fails identically on base).

### Native IME drive (real Chromium, CDP)

`startControlUiE2eServer` (source) + mock Gateway that rejects a stale token
→ the login gate shows its URL/secret fields. CDP `Input.imeSetComposition`
starts a native composition on the URL field:

- Composing Enter (`Input.dispatchKeyEvent`, keyCode 229):
  - Head: connect request count **unchanged** (delta 0).
- Commit composition (`Input.imeSetComposition` empty), then ordinary Enter:
  - Head: connect request count **+1** (normal connect still works).

The collector ran against the **built production Control UI** (`dist/control-ui`,
commit `97eba82c9321`, `dirty: false`) in native Chromium (`/usr/bin/google-chrome`,
headless). The synthetic Gateway recorded every `connect` request and rejected
the stale token with `AUTH_TOKEN_MISSING`. No live Gateway, session, credential,
or config was touched.

Receipt (`login-gate-ime-receipt.json`):

```json
{
  "status": "PASS",
  "positiveControl": { "delta": 1, "connectCount": 2 },
  "composingEnter":    { "delta": 0, "connectCount": 1 },
  "committedEnter":    { "delta": 1, "connectCount": 2 }
}
```

Screenshots of the login gate during the CDP probe (composing draft retained,
no navigation; error banner visible):

![Composing Enter retained draft](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/wangmiao0668000666/openclaw/ea3b4ab8fb9ae7a6d533271f2ef76189d9c22686/login-gate-ime-composing-closeup.png)

![Composing Enter after keyCode 229](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/wangmiao0668000666/openclaw/ea3b4ab8fb9ae7a6d533271f2ef76189d9c22686/login-gate-ime-after-closeup.png)

### Test-line budget

`config/test-lines-allocations/login-gate-ime-composition.txt` allocates the
39 added regression lines; `scripts/check-test-lines-ratchet.mts --base
826999cd5f76f4867a69869489a4fc51cd5e4a35 --no-merge-base` reports
`Test lines OK: 6586781; ceiling: 6586781; slack: 0` (the branch was
integrated with the CI ratchet base so the allocation exactly matches the
added lines; CI `checks-fast-baseline-ratchets` passes).

### Impact surface

| File | Change |
| --- | --- |
| `ui/src/components/login-gate-solid.tsx` | `submitOnEnter` guards with `isComposingKeyboardEvent`; both inputs add `onCompositionEnd`/`onKeyUp`/`onBlur` retirement (+10) |
| `ui/src/components/login-gate.test.ts` | two IME discriminative tests (+39) |

Two-way door: a revert fully restores prior Enter behavior. No migration, no
new persisted contract, no config change.

### Not tested

- Physical Japanese/Chinese IME hardware and WebKit/Safari (the shared IME
  owner's WebKit grace is covered by its existing consumers' tests; the
  CDP probe dispatches composing Enter on Chromium).

## Cleanup

All proof runs used the built Control UI with a mock Gateway (synthetic
stale token); no real Gateway, session, credential, or config was touched.
The CDP probe scripts were removed after capture.

prs.title: fix(ui): avoid duplicate images after tool inspection
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

When an assistant inspects images that it also delivers in its reply, the Control UI can render inspected previews outside their tool disclosure. This also affects a single assistant message that batches a text-only call before an image-inspection call.

## User Impact

Delivered images remain in the assistant reply. Inspected images stay inside expandable tool details, with tool names and file paths preserved. No configuration changes or migrations are needed.

## Why This Change Was Made

Keep image-bearing results tool-owned when combining calls and results, including when media is appended to an existing text-only bundle. Preserve the tool name and file detail on the disclosure. The change reuses the existing transcript projection and renderer.

## Evidence

- Extended the existing renderer regression for an isolated image call and both batched call orders. Text then image fails before the repair because expanded tool details contain zero images; afterward all three inspected images remain under the tool disclosure while the three delivered images remain in the assistant gallery.
- 14 message-rendering tests and 8 activity-coalescing tests pass. The renderer file took 1.76 seconds overall, including 443 ms of test execution; the coalescer file took 2.07 seconds.
- Targeted UI typecheck, lint, formatting and `git diff --check` pass.
- The renderer regression adds exactly 43 test lines. A separate 43-line allocation under the normal test-cost policy preserves this behavioral coverage without raising the shared scalar or adding spare budget. The focused test-line ratchet passes against the retained PR base. This allocation-only follow-up leaves product and test source unchanged, so the existing behavioral, visual and independent-review proof is reused.
- The screenshots below exercise the real Control UI with the shared mock Gateway and labeled synthetic PNGs. Both use the same batched read_file → view_image transcript and an identical crop above the composer. They are browser UI proof, not a live-model run.
- Independent review of the complete candidate identified only the known defect in the old staged snapshot and explicitly confirmed the working-tree repair fixes it. The reviewed repair was staged and committed unchanged; no additional P0–P2 findings remained.

- Current-head CI [run 42552500508, attempt 1](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/42552500508) completed with one root failure: 59 lines of inherited test-budget debt. Its tested baseline has 6,590,133 lines against a 6,590,074 ceiling; this PR adds exactly 43 lines and 43 allocation, preserving the same debt. The unchanged ratchet permits existing debt with zero or negative growth, so main passing does not establish absence of debt. All other selected jobs passed, including security checks. CI remains failed; this is scoped inherited-debt attribution.

### Before

Inspected previews render outside the tool-output container; the delivered gallery remains below.

![Before: batched inspection previews outside tool details](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/20714d22-ac3e-40a6-a76a-1feeced1b38e)

### After

The inspected previews belong to the expandable Tool output container. The delivered gallery remains below, and both tool names and paths are preserved.

![After: inspected previews inside tool details and delivered gallery preserved](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/73364df4-a214-40c7-a524-324aa857df5a)

<details>
<summary>Scope</summary>

No new state or renderer. The complete change adds nine net production lines and 43 regression-test lines. The follow-up repair adds three production lines and extends the existing regression rather than adding a second test fixture.

</details>

## Worked on by

- @vyctorbrzezowski

## Work sessions

Linked for team reference; these sessions aren’t public.

- [Discussion, implementation and verification](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/dashboard/b024f90c-d5d5-491b-8e2d-5fe0dc75e939)

prs.title: fix(github): expire cached detail reads on elapsed time
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The GitHub detail reader (`controlUi.githubDetail`, `tools.github read`) caches issue/PR/commit documents in a process-local map keyed on the host wall clock. A `+5 min` correction expires every cached detail at once and re-issues the repository and item reads; a `−5 min` correction serves PR heads and check state well past their 30-second window.

## User Impact

After a laptop resume, NTP step or VM restore, a long-lived Gateway keeps serving cached details until their real 5 minutes / 30 seconds pass, instead of bursting fresh GitHub reads — and never serves an entry past its real window. Windows, LRU pruning and the GitHub-driven 429 cooldown are unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

`detailCache` is module-private: all three expiry writes and both freshness reads sit in one closure in `extensions/github/src/detail.ts`, and no entry leaves the module, so the five sites move to `performance.now()` together. This completes the elapsed-time cutover #190894 already made in the sibling `extensions/github/src/preview.ts`, and matches the elapsed-cache sweep #193147 for Mantle discovery and Nextcloud Talk room kinds.

The existing checks-expiry case drove the window with a `Date.now` spy only; it now advances both clocks so its ordering assertions hold either way. The checks-recovery regression in `detail-checks.test.ts` likewise advances the elapsed clock alongside its wall-clock spy.

Classification: `behavior-completing`. Production delta `+5/−5`; test delta `+24` with a scoped `github-detail-clock-elapsed` allocation.

## Evidence

- **Base** `54b059c478f` (current `main`) → **candidate** `db24c6c4669`.
- **RED on base** (current `main`, new tests applied): the elapsed-time discriminant fails because a backward wall-clock step keeps the `Date.now`-keyed cache alive past its real window:
  ```text
  × GitHub detail public read boundary > expires cached reads on elapsed time even when the wall clock steps back
  × GitHub detail public read boundary > expires cached visibility failures   (clock spy now drives performance.now)
  ```
- **GREEN on candidate**: `detail.test.ts` + `detail-checks.test.ts`, `62 passed (62)`. The discriminant pairs an independent `performance.now` spy (advanced 6 minutes) with a `Date.now` spy stepped backward 1 hour, so a `Date.now`-based cache would never lapse while the real elapsed window has already passed.
- **Real-entry matrix**: same shape proven in #192583 on identical bytes — a real exported read against a loopback HTTPS GitHub stub: `+600 s` step → base re-reads, candidate holds; `−600 s` step plus real elapsed seconds → base serves stale, candidate refreshes; control runs match request-for-request.
- **Shipped Gateway trace**: the same matrix through `src/index.ts gateway run` and the real `controlUi.githubDetail` WebSocket handler reproduced it identically (recorded on #192583).
- **Checks**: `git diff --check` clean; oxlint clean; `check:test-lines-ratchet` covered by the scoped `github-detail-clock-elapsed` allocation.

## Relation to #191210 / #192583

This branch carries the same fix as my earlier #191210 / #192583, which were closed because the automated review was held by its input scanner (a pre-existing URL fixture in `detail-checks.test.ts`, `role: base`), not by any finding in this change. The discriminant test here is rewritten with the paired wall/elapsed clock spies proven in #193147's Nextcloud Talk cases. Current `main` still has all five `Date.now` sites.

## Merge Danger

Two-way door: reverting restores the wall-clock windows with no state migration or published-contract change. Blast radius is the process-local GitHub detail cache only; the 429 cooldown that must follow GitHub's own epoch stays on wall clock by design.

prs.title: fix(gateway): Control UI rejects /workspace file links written by sandboxed agents
prs.body:
Fixes #169491

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: clicking a `/workspace/...` file link written by a sandboxed agent in the Control UI fails with "outside the workspace", and saving through that link fails too.

## User Impact

For `workspaceAccess: "rw"` sandboxes, `/workspace/...` links open and save in the Control UI. For `ro` sandboxes, `/agent/...` links (the agent workspace mount) do the same. The read boundary is unchanged: the translated host path must still be inside the session workspace root.

## Why This Change Was Made

Sandboxed agents name files by their container path. `sessions.files.get` and `sessions.files.set` resolved that path against the host session root, so `/workspace/report.md` landed outside the root and was rejected.

- The derivation of a session's sandbox layout and local container mounts moves out of `openclaw sandbox explain` into `resolveSandboxSessionWorkspace` (`src/agents/sandbox/session-workspace.ts`). Explain and the Gateway now share it, and explain's behavior is unchanged.
- When a requested absolute path falls outside the session root, `sessions.files.get` and `sessions.files.set` translate it through those mounts with the existing `resolveSandboxFsPathWithMounts`. The normal containment check then decides access. Paths already inside the root are not touched.
- Container-only backing stays authoritative, in line with #148893 ("file tools must follow realized visible container backing"). Before translating, the Gateway asks the live container through the existing mount owner. The new `sandboxContainerShowsPlannedBind` in `mount-plan.ts` reuses `inspectSandboxMounts` and `resolveSandboxContainerOnlyMounts`, the same realized checks the file bridge uses. The deepest realized mount over the link must be the bind that the current plan places there, from the same source, with nothing container-only (volume, tmpfs, covered mount) over it. Otherwise the link is not translated and stays `outside_session_boundary` for `get` and `set`. This also covers an image tag rebuilt after the container was created. If the container is not running, or the backend is not Docker (Podman can target a remote machine), the backing cannot be established and the link is not translated. The check runs only for a container path outside the session root, so ordinary previews do not pay for it.

Not in scope, named on purpose:
- Under `ro`/`none`, `/workspace` is a separate sandbox copy outside the session workspace. Opening it would widen the read boundary, so it remains `outside_session_boundary`. That needs a separate security/product decision.
- Touched-file entries recorded under container paths still don't map to workspace files, so a linked file opens as `kind: "read"` rather than `"modified"`. The touched-file list for sandboxed sessions deserves its own fix.
- The `set` response's `file.path` echoes the request path. For a translated link that is the host path. `root` already exposes the host workspace to the same client.

## Evidence

**Real Gateway + Docker sandbox** (Windows 11, Docker 29.7.2, `openclaw-sandbox:bookworm-slim` built with `scripts/sandbox-setup.sh`, `sandbox: { mode: "all", scope: "session", workspaceAccess: "rw" }`, scripted local mock model through `scripts/e2e/mock-openai-server.mjs`):
1. `chat.send` makes the model call `exec`. It runs inside `openclaw-sbx-workspace-…` and writes `/workspace/report.md`, which appears in the host workspace. The assistant replies `Done. Open [report.md](/workspace/report.md).`
2. `sessions.files.get {path: "/workspace/report.md"}` (what the Control UI sends for that link):
   - `main` (`c832c45a`): `INVALID_REQUEST session file not found`, `details.reason: "outside_session_boundary"`.
   - This PR: `file.path: "report.md"`, `workspacePath: "report.md"`, content `written inside the sandbox`.
3. `sessions.files.set` on the same link with the returned hash: the host file now reads `edited from the Control UI`. The same result holds on the final head `7286807c`.

**Real Docker, hidden backing, image rebuilt after the container was created** (the reviewer's scenario): the image `openclaw-sandbox-proof:volume` declared `VOLUME /workspace/hidden` when the sandbox was created, then the tag was rebuilt without it (`docker image inspect` → `null`). The host workspace holds a different `hidden/report.md`.
- Live container mounts: `bind:/workspace bind:/workspace/.openclaw/sandbox-skills/skills volume:/workspace/hidden`.
- The agent's `exec` writes into the volume: `docker exec … cat /workspace/hidden/report.md` → `written inside the sandbox`. The host file still reads `HOST FILE hidden under the image volume`.
- An earlier head of this PR (`22f384a4`, configured tmpfs mask only) returned the **host** file `HOST FILE hidden under the image volume` and its hash for that link, which is the wrong file.
- Final head: `get` → `outside_session_boundary`. The host file is unchanged.

The normal `rw` link proof above was re-run on the final code: `get` returns `written inside the sandbox`, and `set` writes `edited from the Control UI`.

**Tests:**
- New `sessions-files.sandbox.test.ts`:
  - `rw /workspace/…` and `ro /agent/…` fail on `main` and pass here.
  - `none /workspace/…` stays `outside_session_boundary` both before and after.
  - Saving through `/workspace/…` fails without the `set` translation, and an in-root absolute host path is not remapped.
  - Links whose live backing is container-only, or that cannot be verified (no running container), are refused for `get` and `set`, and the hidden host file stays unchanged.
- `mount-plan.test.ts` "planned bind visibility": a path shown through the planned bind is accepted. A path under a volume the image declared, or whose live bind source differs from the plan, is refused. These are platform-independent with a local source namespace.
- `sandbox-explain.test.ts`: 11/11 pass after the extraction.
- `mount-plan.test.ts`: on this Windows host, 16 existing namespace-translation cases fail identically on unmodified `main`. The 3 new cases pass.
- `tsgo:core` and oxlint on the changed files pass.

**CI notes (heads `22f384a4` and `9c79be80`):** these failing checks are outside this diff:
- `server-methods.session-scoped-reads.test.ts` "… retains shared VIEW and hides foreign drafts before I/O" (`sessions.files.list`, `sessions.files.get`, and `sessions.branches.list`, which this PR does not touch): `User profile catalog is not ready`.
- `agents-mutate.test.ts` "protects every journaled path claimed as a surviving agent workspace" and "settles recovery without touching a journaled directory claimed by another agent".
- `check-lint-core-1` (full `src/gateway` lint stripe): `src/gateway/server-methods/users-github.test.ts:679` `no-unnecessary-type-arguments`. That is an upstream file this PR does not touch. The changed files pass oxlint and format locally.
- `test/scripts/eager-import-closure.test.ts` "resolves wrapper package exports…" failed in CI but passes locally on both `main` and this branch. I have not explained that one yet.

**Not verified locally (Windows host):** three existing `sessions-files.test.ts` cases fail identically on unmodified `main` here: two `EPERM` symlink creations, and "omits transcript paths outside the workspace". I did not run the full `check:changed` lane set or `tsgo:core:test` for this branch. Tests ran on base `c832c45a` before rebasing onto `aee12b63`; upstream changes between the two touch `src/agents/sandbox/context.ts` but none of the files changed here. Please rely on CI for the rest.

prs.title: fix(ui): keep plugin credential drafts out of IME commits
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Pressing Enter to confirm an IME candidate (Chinese, Japanese, Korean input) in the
plugin credential secret input could save the literal draft before the user actually
submitted it. Two paths are affected:

1. A keydown with `isComposing: true` (or `keyCode 229`) reached the `onKeyDown`
   handler and committed the draft.
2. WebKit can deliver the committing Enter after `compositionend` with both composition
   flags cleared; that Enter also committed the draft.

## User Impact

Users entering credential literals in the Plugins page with an IME (most CJK users)
could have their partially-typed secret committed and sent to the Gateway
mid-composition, before they pressed Enter to actually submit. The draft is stored as
a literal credential value, so this both surprises the user and can persist an
unintended value.

## Why This Change Was Made

The shared input-local IME guard (`ui/src/lib/ime.ts`, introduced in #177545) already
covers the browser toolbar (#194136), the skill library editor (#195356), the login
form, the command palette and the chat composer. The plugin credential editor was the
remaining secret input handling Enter without that protection. This applies the same
contract so a composing Enter is ignored and only a genuine submit (non-composing
Enter, blur, or Save) commits the draft.

Precedent: #194136, #195356 (same IME guard on other Enter-submitting fields);
#194436 (independently validated this exact credential-editor repair; closed without
merging after a proof request — this PR supplies the shipped proof and resolves the
conflict against current main).

Fix classification: `behavior-completing` (extends the established IME guard to the
last Enter-submitting credential input).

## Evidence

**Product head:** `8222f7b4217` (single clean fix commit, no proof files in the PR branch).
**Proof branch:** `proof/cred-editor-ime` @ `ee298d9eb72` (frozen collector + receipts + screenshots, outside the PR branch so the duplicate-scan stays clean).
**Base (current main):** `e673256f8a9351607912329020857906643a1c1c` — the credential
editor on main has no IME guard (confirmed: `ui/src/pages/plugins/credential-editor.tsx`
imports nothing from `lib/ime.ts`).

### Discriminative browser regression tests

`ui/src/pages/plugins/credential-editor.browser.test.tsx` (real Chromium) — three new
cases:

| Case | Base | Head |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Composing Enter (`isComposing: true`) does not commit | **RED**: `expected "vi.fn()" to not be called at all, but actually been called 1 times` | GREEN |
| WebKit post-compositionend Enter (grace window) does not commit | **RED**: same assertion | GREEN |
| Ordinary Enter after composition commits exactly once | — | GREEN |

Head: `27 passed (27)`.
Base: `2 failed | 25 skipped (27)`.

### Shipped proof — built Control UI + native Chromium CDP composition

Frozen collector `collector-cred-ime.mjs` (SHA256 pinned in `head-receipt.json`, both on the `proof/cred-editor-ime` branch: https://github.com/wangmiao0668000666/openclaw/blob/proof/cred-editor-ime/proof-cred-editor-ime/collector-cred-ime.mjs) drives the **built** production Control UI
(`vite build` → `dist/control-ui`, commit pinned, `dirty: false`) in **native Chromium**
via the official synthetic Gateway, opening the real Plugins → Workboard → Settings →
"Search API key" credential editor (`plugins.credentials.inspect` reports `missing`).

Native CDP `Input.imeSetComposition` starts a real browser composition; composing Enter
uses `Input.dispatchKeyEvent` (keyCode 229); the ordinary Enter is a genuine keyboard
press. `config.set` request count is the observable side effect.

| Scenario | config.set delta (Head) |
| --- | --- |
| Ordinary Enter (positive control) | **+1** |
| Composing Enter during native composition | **0** (draft retained) |
| Commit composition, then ordinary Enter | **+1** |

Base run (same frozen collector, same built base UI): aborts at
`AssertionError: composing Enter must not commit — 1 !== 0` — a composing Enter commits
on main. [`base-receipt.md`](https://github.com/wangmiao0668000666/openclaw/blob/proof/cred-editor-ime/proof-cred-editor-ime/base-receipt.md),
[`head-receipt.json`](https://github.com/wangmiao0668000666/openclaw/blob/proof/cred-editor-ime/proof-cred-editor-ime/head-receipt.json),
[screenshots](https://github.com/wangmiao0668000666/openclaw/tree/proof/cred-editor-ime/proof-cred-editor-ime).

### Checks

- `oxlint` on both changed files: 0 errors / 0 warnings.
- `oxfmt --check`: clean.
- Test-line allocation: `config/test-lines-allocations/credential-editor-ime-composition.txt`
  (33 added lines, matching the +33 test diff).

## Merge Danger

Two-way door: a revert fully restores prior Enter behavior. No migration, no new
persisted contract, no config change. The shared IME helper and the credential commit
path remain their existing owners; this only suppresses the composing-Enter commit.

## Impact surface

| File | Change |

prs.title: fix: preserve shared worktree history during agent fetches
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes agent fetch/pull commands changing the history boundary shared by other linked worktree sessions. Extends #195498 and preserves #195516's filtered fork-fetch behavior.

## User Impact

Shallow-changing fetch/pull commands in a repository with registered linked worktrees fail before transport with an actionable hint. Standalone repositories, including sandbox projections, retain normal semantics. Normal fetch obtains new tips. For older history, agents can use GitHub's commit/compare API; operators can repair managed local history with `openclaw doctor --fix` during maintenance, then agents can retry `git log`.

This is the existing PATH performance guard, not a security boundary. Absolute Git paths, aliases/functions, native harness shells, remote node exec, and SSH/Crabbox sandboxes remain outside its scope. Existing shallow bases still require owner-controlled repair. Timing is not uniformly better: the final five-sample run showed +1.27 ms for normal-fetch median and a slower refused-deepen p95; retain these tradeoffs before landing.

## Why This Change Was Made

Linked worktrees share `.git/shallow`, including with the primary checkout. The shim resolves the common directory only for fetch/pull commands with shallow options, preserving Git's global repository selectors such as repeated `-C`. It refuses depth, deepen, shallow-since, shallow-exclude, unshallow, and update-shallow options when linked worktrees are registered. Ordinary commands gain no repository lookup. The check precedes the fork-fetch filter exemptions and argument rewrite; both repository queries reuse one global-option handler.

A real partial-clone experiment showed why silently stripping options is wrong: a depth-less fetch preserved the shallow file and fetched new tips, but did not acquire older history. Refusal preserves shared state and an honest command result. No global host config, new runtime configuration, cache, or schema change.

## Evidence

The real agent-exec regression failed on original main parent `ea50f6e38218` because `--depth` changed the shared shallow file. During preparation, #195516 landed in the same owner, producing a real conflict; this head integrates it against main `43dae0b46f1eb1dcfed7434196ff3bf1aa8a9b2a` and adds explicit-filter/depth-limited fork interaction coverage. The final benchmark also proves that exact new parent's shim still mutates the shared boundary.

**Nine focused owner/shim tests pass on the integrated candidate.** They cover all six option families with fetch/pull, primary checkout and repeated `-C` routing, no transport, identical shallow bytes, standalone semantics, new tips, and old history after owner-controlled unshallow. Main's fork filtering/hydration and existing offline-probe/blob-hydration/negotiated-fetch cases pass too. Expanded real-Git case: 6.763 s; whole command: 47.98 s including compilation. CI seconds pending. No changed runtime module is imported by `ui/src`.

The committed workload uses 62,001 files / 1.116 GB logical materialized content, 20,001 existing commits, initial depth10 then deepen4000, fresh private linked metadata, warm filesystem, and five interleaved samples per lane. Rule recorded before execution: shallow changes and transports one→zero; ordinary fetch retains its Git process count; report timing regressions and A/A controls. Git 2.54.0 (Apple Git), macOS; not Linux/btrfs or production timing.

| Operation | Median / p95 wall ms | Median CPU ms | Median peak RSS MB | Objects / received bytes | Shallow changes |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Baseline deepen 4000 | 178.21 / 209.46 | 440 | 15.79 | 8,002 / 750,910 | 1 |
| Guarded refusal | 26.23 / 228.74 | 10 | 5.24 | 0 / 0 | 0 |
| Normal fetch A1 | 56.88 / 58.70 | 40 | 6.68 | 2 / 259 | 0 |
| Normal fetch A2 | 56.61 / 59.47 | 40 | 6.67 | 2 / 259 | 0 |
| Normal fetch guarded | 58.15 / 61.16 | 40 | 6.65 | 2 / 259 | 0 |

Counts meet the rule; normal fetch remains four Git process starts. Candidate normal-fetch median +2.2% versus A1, refused-deepen p95 +9.2%; no claim that every timing improved. p95=max of five samples; CPU precision10ms; host load13.89. A superseded pre-integration baseline under load54–56 showed +20.3% normal-fetch median and a large tail; it was not labeled neutral. This rerun followed changed baseline/candidate code, not a retry for green. RSS is not cumulative allocation, which remains unmeasured. No database fixture: this Git boundary performs no session/database access. No production/deployment access.

Reproduce with `node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs scripts/perf/agent-git-probes.mts --scratch-parent <scratch-dir> --shared-shallow --baseline-shim <base-shell-script>`, exporting `AGENT_GIT_SHIM` from pinned main `43dae0b46f1e` to the baseline shell file first.

Production delta **+30 lines**, regression allocation **+86 lines**, benchmark extension **+91 lines**. Growth adds the missing policy at the existing owner and reuses its real fixture/framework; duplicate repository argument handling was eliminated during integration.

`pnpm check:changed --base 43dae0b46f1eb1dcfed7434196ff3bf1aa8a9b2a --timed` completed on integrated head `a88c45fba0f5`: all checks passed except 20 archived changelog-attribution violations. Formatting, production/test/script typechecks, all three dead-export scans, core/scripts lint, and the runtime guards passed. The same20 errors reproduce using the exact rebased main parent's archived checker/import closure/changelogs. Introducing policy change: `266a7aa0fe69` / #194364; retained prior-lane proof also reproduced them there. This is an unresolved main regression, not noise. No release-owned changelog edits are included. Exact +86-line test allocation passes.

Fresh integrated **Codex autoreview is scoped-clean at P0–P2**, final source verification complete. No source changed afterward. No full package build, live model/Gateway deployment, Docker daemon, or native-allocation profile was run for this follow-up; actual exec/shim owners and real partial-clone transport are covered locally. Exact-head CI follows publication. **Ready PR requested; do not merge.**

prs.title: feat(ios): open matching chats from push notifications
prs.body:
Related: #193113

## What Problem This Solves

An ordinary iOS push notification opens the app but does not take someone to the chat the notification is about.

## User Impact

A push with an optional session destination can open that existing chat on the currently connected Gateway, after checking the current profile's access, without sending a message. Notifications without a destination keep their existing behavior. Missing, inaccessible, or wrong-Gateway destinations leave the current screen unchanged; taps do not automatically switch Gateways.

## Why This Change Was Made

This extends the existing `push.test` path and `openclaw nodes push --session <key>` rather than adding a general notification operation or arbitrary deep links. The Gateway resolves the destination and supplies its own identity. APNs sends revalidate through the existing session-read owner, and iOS resolves the destination on its current authenticated route before calling the existing `openChat` owner. Cold-launch handoff and reconnect use existing lifecycle owners, with duplicate-tap suppression and Watch/approval precedence preserved.

This does not add counters, registrations, or background wakes. The public changes in #193491 (unread badges) and #193033 (main-chat discovery) were inspected; this change preserves those owners. The API direction is presented for maintainer review, not as an already accepted product decision.

## Evidence

- Red/green regression: the new optional destination was rejected by the original closed request schema; it passes with the schema and generated runtime validators updated.
- **100 focused tests passed across five files:** protocol schema, APNs payload/refusal behavior, Gateway push handling, existing session visibility, and CLI option forwarding. The CLI test wrapper also completed its runtime build. These are synthetic/mocked boundary tests, not real APNs or iPhone acceptance.
- `pnpm tsgo:core` passed using workspace-local Node 26.12.1.

Real APNs/iPhone foreground/background/cold-launch tap flows and revoked-pairing behavior remain unverified for this PR, and there are no device before/after captures. Exact published-head CI and owning acceptance remain outstanding. This PR is ready for review; auto-merge remains off.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: mobile Web UI toasts cannot be dismissed with an upward swipe, and their close button is hidden until interaction.

## User Impact

Users can swipe a toast upward to dismiss it or use the always-visible X button on mobile. Buttons, links, and scrolling through long error details retain their existing behavior. No configuration or migration is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

Recognize deliberate, single-touch upward gestures in the shared toast presentation and use its existing dismissal callback. Preserve native scrolling in overflowing content, including persistent chat diagnostics. Keep mobile close-button visibility in the base stylesheet so the renderer fallback also retains it.

## Evidence

- The new browser regression fails on the original implementation for both missing swipe dismissal and hidden mobile X, then passes with the fix.
- Focused browser regressions: 33 tests pass in 30.75 seconds, covering transient toasts and persistent chat notices in Chromium (18 tests), plus the complete shared-toast suite in WebKit (15 tests). The swipe and oversized-error scrolling assertions now run successfully in WebKit.
- Full Control UI flow: copy a session ID through the real menu, resize to 390 × 844, and dismiss the resulting toast with native Chromium touch input. Before: toast remains. After: toast dismisses. The screenshot uses synthetic data.
- UI typecheck, focused lint/stylelint, controller guard, and diff checks pass.

- Chromium and WebKit browser regressions pass. Physical devices and native WebKit touch input were not tested.
- Current-head CI [run 42551611580, attempt 1](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/42551611580) completed with one root failure: the test-line ratchet. Its tested baseline has 6,589,626 test lines against a 6,589,567 ceiling (59 over). This PR adds 63 lines and a matching 63-line allocation, leaving the same 59-line debt. The unchanged policy permits existing debt when growth is zero or negative, so a passing main job does not mean the debt is absent. All other selected jobs, including security checks, passed. This is inherited-budget attribution, not passing CI.

| Before | After |

prs.title: fix(voice-call): long replies never play and the caller hears silence
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

A caller hears **complete silence** instead of a long reply.

`playTtsViaStream` hands the whole reply to `synthesizeForTelephony(text)` as a single request and
races it against a fixed `synthesisTimeoutMs` (default 8000ms) that does not scale with text
length. When the reply is long enough that one request loses the race, the turn fails before a
single speech frame is sent, so nothing at all is played.

## Why This Change Was Made

Speech directives are resolved **once** over the complete reply, then the resolved spoken text is
split into segments of at most 320 characters and played back-to-back inside the same serialized
`queueTts` slot. Each segment synthesizes under its own deadline, so no single request has to
cover an unbounded amount of text.

Resolving before splitting is what keeps the directive contract intact: a split can never divide a
directive block, and one resolved override set applies to every segment. Because the whole reply
stays inside one queue slot, ordered playback, barge-in cancellation and a single completion mark
per turn all continue to hold.

The playback body moves to `providers/twilio/stream-tts-playback.ts`, leaving `providers/twilio.ts`
smaller than before.

### Second defect, found by this change

Segmented playback makes long replies actually play, which exposed a latent duplicate-delivery bug.
Early delivery awaits the transport, and that await lasts as long as the reply takes to speak. A
reply long enough to outlive the runner's block-reply flush join leaves the await abandoned while
audio is still playing - and `deliveredEarly` was only assigned once `onEarlyText` resolved. During
playback the flag stayed `false`, `resolveReplyDelivery` reported `"missing"`, and the runner
delivered the same reply a second time. Delivery is now claimed at handoff and reverted only on a
real failure.

This is only reachable with segmented playback: on current `main` a long reply never plays at all,
so playback never lasts long enough to outrun the join.

## User Impact

- Long replies are spoken instead of dropped. No configuration change; no new public API.
- Long replies are spoken **once**, not twice.
- Short replies take the same path as before.
- Cost: segmented playback adds about 2.6 s of keep-alive silence at each segment boundary. See
  the limitation note under Evidence.

## Evidence

A redacted exact-head capture from live Twilio calls is posted as a follow-up comment on this PR.
Headline results, from a build pinned to this head:

```
split into 16 segments [273,301,270,315,187,315,294,297,243,305,312,261,200,261,255,91]
frames seg=1/16  frames_sent=815 frames_expected=815
   ... every segment 1..16, frames_sent == frames_expected ...
frames seg=16/16 frames_sent=276 frames_expected=276
mark_sent  name=tts-<ts>-6 total_bytes=2055273 est_ms=256909
mark_acked name=tts-<ts>-6
```

- 4,180 characters across 16 segments played to completion, in order. Longest segment 315, inside the 320 cap.
- Exactly one completion mark per reply, acknowledged by the carrier.
- Barge-in on the same binary produced `abort_during seg=1/12`, `seg=1/2`, `seg=1/5`, each cancelling the remainder.
- Pacing holds to the millisecond: segment 1 is 815 frames x 20 ms = 16.30 s expected, 16.305 s measured.

**Limitation this capture also shows.** Wall-clock was 295.8 s against 256.9 s of audio: about 39 s
of keep-alive silence across the 15 segment boundaries while the next segment synthesizes. This PR
deliberately does not pipeline synthesis ahead of playback, which is what keeps ordering, barge-in
and the single mark simple. Pre-synthesizing the next segment during playback is a reasonable
follow-up.

**Why this fails on current `main`.** The slowest segment synthesized 312 characters in 3,676 ms
(~11.8 ms/char), so one whole-reply request for 4,180 characters projects to roughly 49 s against
the 8,000 ms deadline. That is an extrapolation from measured per-segment rates on this head, not
an observed failure of `main`.

**Provenance.** Temporary `[voice-call][diag]` counters produced the capture and are **not part of
this PR**; they emit counts and timings only and cannot change which branch runs. Earlier traces in
this PR's history came from different revisions and are not exact-head proof - disregard them.

### Rebuilt against current main

The previous head was ~24,300 commits behind `main` and conflicted. Per the repo's guidance for
drift at that scale this was not rebased: the branch was rebuilt fresh off `main` and the intent
re-expressed against upstream's current shape.

Upstream had deleted two helpers the earlier revision depended on, so a textual merge would not
have compiled:

| Deleted upstream | Previously used for | Now |
|---|---|---|
| `telephony-audio.ts` (`chunkAudio`) | slicing audio into 160-byte frames | `muLawAudio.subarray(offset, offset + CHUNK_SIZE)`, matching main |
| `convertTelephonyTtsOutput` | mulaw/PCM output conversion | main's current inline format detection |

Also realigned: `twilioApiRequest` -> `createTwilioApi` (renamed upstream), and the now-orphaned
`raceWithTimeout` import removed.

### The duplicate-delivery fix is proved by a failing test

```
AssertionError: expected 'missing' to be 'pending' // Object.is equality

Expected: "pending"
Received: "missing"

 > extensions/voice-call/src/response-generator.test.ts:362

 Test Files  1 failed (1)
      Tests  1 failed | 35 skipped (36)
```

The pre-existing `"awaits in-flight early delivery"` test cannot catch this: it always resolves the
delivery inside the generator's lifetime, so it never models an abandoned flush join.

### Local gates on this head

```
oxfmt --check             exit 0
oxlint                    0 warnings, 0 errors (149 files)
vitest                    9 files, 135 tests passed
tsgo:extensions:test      exit 0 (clean)
max-lines ratchet         OK, 396 grandfathered suppressions
assertion-safety ratchet  OK, 2381 files, 5408 grandfathered assertions
```

## Review response

| Review item | Status |
|---|---|
| Resolve the GitHub-reported merge conflict while retaining current main's playback behavior and the bounded-synthesis change | **Done.** Rebuilt on current `main`; `sendMarkAndWait`, drift-corrected pacing, per-synthesis abort handling and `clearAudio`-on-failure all preserved in the extracted module. GitHub now reports `MERGEABLE`. |
| Add real behavior proof | **Done.** Redacted exact-head capture posted as a follow-up comment: segmented completion, ordered frame delivery, one acknowledged mark per turn, and barge-in cancelling the remainder. |

---

## Closed without merging

Closing in favor of a one-line configuration change. Recording the measurements here so the reasoning is not lost.

### Why

The root cause this PR identified is correct: `synthesisTimeoutMs` is a fixed deadline that does not
scale with text length. But segmentation is an expensive way around it, and the failure it prevents
turned out to be effectively unreachable in the deployment that motivated the PR.

Measured against the local Kokoro TTS server backing these calls:

| Reply text | Synthesis | Audio produced |
|---|---|---|
| 320 chars | 3.2 s | ~19 s |
| 700 chars | 6.1 s | ~42 s |
| 1400 chars | 12.6 s | ~84 s |
| 2200 chars | 18.8 s | ~131 s |

That is ~8.5 ms/char, so whole-reply synthesis crosses the 8000 ms default at roughly **900 characters**.

Two findings made segmentation the wrong trade:

1. **The failure is rarely reached.** `response-generator.ts` already delivers per block,
   accumulating `blockReplyPayloads` and flushing each through `onEarlyText` at `text_end`
   boundaries. Each `playTts` call receives one block, which in practice sits well below the ~900
   character cliff. The whole-reply path only applies when block boundaries are unreliable.

2. **Synthesis outruns playback ~6:1.** 320 characters costs 3.2 s to synthesize but yields ~19 s of
   speech. Because this PR deliberately does not pipeline, every boundary inserts a real synthesis
   gap mid-reply - the ~39 s of keep-alive silence across 15 boundaries already visible in the
   capture above. Total dead air is comparable to waiting once up front, but redistributed into
   pauses that sound like a dropped call.

### What was done instead

A voice-call-scoped `tts.timeoutMs` of 30000, moving the cliff from ~900 to ~3500 characters with no
code change. Scoped to the plugin so other TTS surfaces keep the 8 s ceiling. A timeout is a ceiling
rather than a delay, so the happy path is unaffected.

### If this is revisited

Scale the deadline instead of chopping the audio - essentially what this PR's own problem statement
describes:

```ts
const synthesisTimeoutMs = Math.max(configured, chars * msPerChar);
```

That addresses "a fixed deadline that does not scale with text length" directly, without per-segment
prosody resets, inter-segment gaps, or the duplicate-delivery and unbounded directive-resolution
bugs that segmentation introduced and then had to fix.

The branch is retained; nothing here is lost.

prs.title: fix(voice-call): long replies never play and the caller hears silence
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

A caller hears **complete silence** instead of a long reply.

`playTtsViaStream` hands the whole reply to `synthesizeForTelephony(text)` as a single request and
races it against a fixed `synthesisTimeoutMs` (default 8000ms) that does not scale with text
length. When the reply is long enough that one request loses the race, the turn fails before a
single speech frame is sent, so nothing at all is played.

## Why This Change Was Made

Speech directives are resolved **once** over the complete reply, then the resolved spoken text is
split into segments of at most 320 characters and played back-to-back inside the same serialized
`queueTts` slot. Each segment synthesizes under its own deadline, so no single request has to
cover an unbounded amount of text.

Resolving before splitting is what keeps the directive contract intact: a split can never divide a
directive block, and one resolved override set applies to every segment. Because the whole reply
stays inside one queue slot, ordered playback, barge-in cancellation and a single completion mark
per turn all continue to hold.

The playback body moves to `providers/twilio/stream-tts-playback.ts`, leaving `providers/twilio.ts`
smaller than before.

### Second defect, found by this change

Segmented playback makes long replies actually play, which exposed a latent duplicate-delivery bug.
Early delivery awaits the transport, and that await lasts as long as the reply takes to speak. A
reply long enough to outlive the runner's block-reply flush join leaves the await abandoned while
audio is still playing - and `deliveredEarly` was only assigned once `onEarlyText` resolved. During
playback the flag stayed `false`, `resolveReplyDelivery` reported `"missing"`, and the runner
delivered the same reply a second time. Delivery is now claimed at handoff and reverted only on a
real failure.

This is only reachable with segmented playback: on current `main` a long reply never plays at all,
so playback never lasts long enough to outrun the join.

## User Impact

- Long replies are spoken instead of dropped. No configuration change; no new public API.
- Long replies are spoken **once**, not twice.
- Short replies take the same path as before.
- Cost: segmented playback adds about 2.6 s of keep-alive silence at each segment boundary. See
  the limitation note under Evidence.

## Evidence

A redacted exact-head capture from live Twilio calls is posted as a follow-up comment on this PR.
Headline results, from a build pinned to this head:

```
split into 16 segments [273,301,270,315,187,315,294,297,243,305,312,261,200,261,255,91]
frames seg=1/16  frames_sent=815 frames_expected=815
   ... every segment 1..16, frames_sent == frames_expected ...
frames seg=16/16 frames_sent=276 frames_expected=276
mark_sent  name=tts-<ts>-6 total_bytes=2055273 est_ms=256909
mark_acked name=tts-<ts>-6
```

- 4,180 characters across 16 segments played to completion, in order. Longest segment 315, inside the 320 cap.
- Exactly one completion mark per reply, acknowledged by the carrier.
- Barge-in on the same binary produced `abort_during seg=1/12`, `seg=1/2`, `seg=1/5`, each cancelling the remainder.
- Pacing holds to the millisecond: segment 1 is 815 frames x 20 ms = 16.30 s expected, 16.305 s measured.

**Limitation this capture also shows.** Wall-clock was 295.8 s against 256.9 s of audio: about 39 s
of keep-alive silence across the 15 segment boundaries while the next segment synthesizes. This PR
deliberately does not pipeline synthesis ahead of playback, which is what keeps ordering, barge-in
and the single mark simple. Pre-synthesizing the next segment during playback is a reasonable
follow-up.

**Why this fails on current `main`.** The slowest segment synthesized 312 characters in 3,676 ms
(~11.8 ms/char), so one whole-reply request for 4,180 characters projects to roughly 49 s against
the 8,000 ms deadline. That is an extrapolation from measured per-segment rates on this head, not
an observed failure of `main`.

**Provenance.** Temporary `[voice-call][diag]` counters produced the capture and are **not part of
this PR**; they emit counts and timings only and cannot change which branch runs. Earlier traces in
this PR's history came from different revisions and are not exact-head proof - disregard them.

### Rebuilt against current main

The previous head was ~24,300 commits behind `main` and conflicted. Per the repo's guidance for
drift at that scale this was not rebased: the branch was rebuilt fresh off `main` and the intent
re-expressed against upstream's current shape.

Upstream had deleted two helpers the earlier revision depended on, so a textual merge would not
have compiled:

| Deleted upstream | Previously used for | Now |
|---|---|---|
| `telephony-audio.ts` (`chunkAudio`) | slicing audio into 160-byte frames | `muLawAudio.subarray(offset, offset + CHUNK_SIZE)`, matching main |
| `convertTelephonyTtsOutput` | mulaw/PCM output conversion | main's current inline format detection |

Also realigned: `twilioApiRequest` -> `createTwilioApi` (renamed upstream), and the now-orphaned
`raceWithTimeout` import removed.

### The duplicate-delivery fix is proved by a failing test

```
AssertionError: expected 'missing' to be 'pending' // Object.is equality

Expected: "pending"
Received: "missing"

 > extensions/voice-call/src/response-generator.test.ts:362

 Test Files  1 failed (1)
      Tests  1 failed | 35 skipped (36)
```

The pre-existing `"awaits in-flight early delivery"` test cannot catch this: it always resolves the
delivery inside the generator's lifetime, so it never models an abandoned flush join.

### Local gates on this head

```
oxfmt --check             exit 0
oxlint                    0 warnings, 0 errors (149 files)
vitest                    9 files, 135 tests passed
tsgo:extensions:test      exit 0 (clean)
max-lines ratchet         OK, 396 grandfathered suppressions
assertion-safety ratchet  OK, 2381 files, 5408 grandfathered assertions
```

## Review response

| Review item | Status |

| Resolve the GitHub-reported merge conflict while retaining current main's playback behavior and the bounded-synthesis change | **Done.** Rebuilt on current `main`; `sendMarkAndWait`, drift-corrected pacing, per-synthesis abort handling and `clearAudio`-on-failure all preserved in the extracted module. GitHub now reports `MERGEABLE`. |
| Add real behavior proof | **Done.** Redacted exact-head capture posted as a follow-up comment: segmented completion, ordered frame delivery, one acknowledged mark per turn, and barge-in cancelling the remainder. |

---

## Closed without merging

Closing in favor of a one-line configuration change. Recording the measurements here so the reasoning is not lost.

### Why

The root cause this PR identified is correct: `synthesisTimeoutMs` is a fixed deadline that does not

prs.title: fix(android): show Gateway-owned pending inputs and recover sends by receipt

Closes #191605 ## What Problem This Solves Fixes: Android hides inputs queued on the Gateway while a response is running and lacks original-ID receipt reconciliation in its local outbox after an acknowledgment interruption. ## User Impact User impact: Android displays recent Gateway-owned pending inputs beside the composer (`Gateway inputs` / `Queued on Gateway: `) and reconciles local sends using their original submission identity without automatically replaying uncertain input. The read-only view shows the latest retained page rather than the entire queue; the Gateway count and `Showing recent inputs only.` disclose older inputs. Existing 48h local retention, Room SQLite outbox schema, and older-Gateway recovery remain unchanged. ## Why This Change Was Made Reuse the existing Room outbox (`ChatCommandOutbox`, untouched at the schema/entity/DAO layer), `ChatController` history owner, and advertised `chat-input-custody-v1` contract. Exact `consumed` and `cancelled` receipts retire local copies; `started`/pending and missing receipts after bounded retention do not mean consumption or replay permission. Queue display stays out of canonical transcript history and suppresses duplicate local optimistic rows by submission identity. prs.title: fix(config): accept model refs listed by the selected native harness
prs.body:
Resubmission of #195063, closed by the active-PR limit.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: `openclaw config set agents.entries.<id>.model.primary meta/muse-wonder-full-1.0` fails with `Unknown model` even when that model is bound to the `muse` runtime and `openclaw models list --refresh --provider meta` lists it.

## User Impact

User impact: you can select a model that only an agent harness offers, such as Muse Wonder Full, as an agent's model when the ref is bound to that harness's runtime. Unknown IDs, models the harness does not list, and refs on other runtimes are still rejected as before.

## Why This Change Was Made

Config validation acquires a prepared runtime that does load the harness catalog (Muse answers `model/list`). Validation then checks the ref only through host API resolution, and that cannot build a harness-listed row because the row has no host transport. Spark passes only because `extensions/meta` also lists it statically; Wonder Full is native-only (docs/providers/meta.md).

The turn path (`embedded-agent-runner/run/model-setup.ts`) and the spawn path (`model-runtime-choice.ts`) already accept such a row through `resolveNativeOwnedRuntimeModel`. Validation now resolves the ref's runtime the same way (`resolveAgentHarnessPolicy`, then `resolveAutoAgentHarnessId` for `auto`) and applies that helper before host resolution.

Accepted gap: a ref with no explicit runtime that only one native runtime discovers is still rejected, as on `main`. Binding it with `agentRuntime.id` makes it pass.

## Evidence

- **Real behavior proof** ([comment](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/195073#issuecomment-6721994048)): shipped `openclaw config set` against real Muse Code 1.4.14's account catalog, with isolated state. On main, all three cases are rejected. On this PR, the Muse-listed model is saved, and the unlisted and `openclaw`-bound controls are rejected with config unchanged. No model turn runs.
- **Regression test** in `src/cli/config-model-validation.runtime.test.ts`: a fixture harness lists `pin-alpha/native-only`.

  | Case | `main` | first lenient draft (any native row) | this PR |
  |---|---|---|---|
  | `native-only` on `pin-native` | ✗ rejected | ✓ | ✓ |
  | `native-unlisted` on `pin-native` (control) | ✓ rejected | ✓ rejected | ✓ rejected |
  | `native-only` on `openclaw`, harness still loaded (control) | ✓ rejected | ✗ accepted | ✓ rejected |

  `config-model-validation.runtime.test.ts` + `config-model-validation.test.ts`: 32/32 pass.
- **CLI entry with a controlled MSP peer.** Setup: isolated state dir, the repo's `extensions/muse/src/test-support/fake-muse.mjs` as `muse`, and `test/fixtures/model-catalog/muse-meta-account.json` as its `model/list` response.
  - `main`: `config set ... meta/muse-wonder-full-1.0`, with the ref bound to `muse`, exits 1 with `Unknown model`. The request log shows `model/list` served, and `models list --refresh` lists the model.
  - This PR: the same command succeeds.
  - Controls on this PR, all rejected:
    - `meta/muse-imaginary-9`.
    - `meta/muse-wonder-full-1.0-contributor` when the fake catalog doesn't list it.

prs.title: fix(signal): compute command authorization for registered plugin commands
prs.body:
Fixes the Signal part of #135502.

## What problem this solves

Signal asks for a command-authorization decision only when the inbound text is a built-in control command (`isControlCommandMessage`). A command registered by a plugin through `api.registerCommand(...)` never gets that decision. So an allowlisted, paired sender who is also the configured command owner can send `/voice` (talk-voice, which uses the default `requireAuth`), and core rejects it with "⚠️ This command requires authorization." A plugin that sets `requireAuth: false` and checks `isAuthorizedSender` itself sees `false`.

## What changed

- `resolveSignalAccessState` now receives the inbound text (`commandText`) and requests command access whenever the shared `shouldComputeCommandAuthorized` probe matches. That probe covers built-in controls, registered plugin commands and bang commands, and other channels (Buzz, ClickClack, Feishu) already use it.
- `event-handler.ts` passes `messageText` instead of the narrow boolean, so that file does not grow. The group mention bypass still uses the narrow control-command detector, so plugin commands do not gain a new way past `requireMention`.
- Microsoft Teams is out of scope here. ClawSweeper's Oct 7 review on #135502 found Teams already requests authorization at admission and dispatch.

## Evidence

**Unit:** a new `access-policy.test.ts` case registers a plugin command and expects `commandAccess.authorized === true` for an allowlisted direct sender. It fails on `main`'s access policy and passes with this change. The three existing command cases now pass `commandText: "/status"` instead of `hasControlCommand: true`. The full Signal extension suite passes: 38 files / 488 tests and 6 files / 46 tests.

**Physical device, real Signal:** two test accounts on Android 17 phones. A Pixel 10 Pro Fold sends; a Pixel 10 Pro XL's account has `signal-cli` 0.14.7 as a linked device, feeding an isolated Gateway's Signal channel (DM pairing approved; that sender is also `commands.ownerAllowFrom`). The model is a local synthetic stub, and none of these commands reached it.

| Gateway | `/status` (built-in) | `/voice` (plugin command, default `requireAuth`) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `main` `90dfe90f3` | status card | **"⚠️ This command requires authorization."** |
| this branch `09c7112e8` (`/status` reports `09c7112`) | status card | **"Talk voice status: provider: system …"** |

**Denied senders, same setup on head `421fdf8e4`:**

| Sender state | `/voice` result | Model requests |
| --- | --- | --- |
| DM-admitted by pairing, but `commands.allowFrom.signal` lists only another ID | **"⚠️ This command requires authorization."**; no handler output | 0 |
| Same sender after restoring config (no `commands.allowFrom`) | "Talk voice status: …" | 0 |
| DM admission removed (allowlist without the sender, `ownerAllowFrom: []`) | no reply | 0 |

The first row is the admitted but command-denied case: the sender was authorized a minute earlier, the Gateway hot-reloaded the denying policy, and the next `/voice` was refused before reaching the handler.

**Revocation while dispatch is waiting, same setup on head `421fdf8e4`:** the Signal inbound debounce was set to 10 s (`messages.inbound.byChannel.signal: 10000`). That holds a plugin command before dispatch; built-in control commands skip the debounce.

| Step | Time | Result |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Control: sender authorized, sends `/voice` | 09:35:03 | No reply during the 10 s hold, then "Talk voice status: …" |
| Sender authorized, sends `/voice` | 09:35:57.5 | Held by the debounce |
| `commands.allowFrom.signal` set to an unrelated ID while it is held | 09:36:00.6 | `config hot reload applied (commands.allowFrom)` at 09:36:04 |
| The held `/voice` is dispatched | after the hold | **"⚠️ This command requires authorization."**, no handler output, 0 model requests |

The authorization decision is made when the held message is dispatched, not when it arrives, so rights revoked while it waits are honored.

**Ordinary group text that mentions a plugin command** is covered by the unit test "does not block ordinary open-group text that mentions a plugin command". These test phones have no Signal group.

Five earlier PRs for this issue (#135549, #135555, #137326, #137970, #139637) closed without merging, citing capacity, inactivity or the lack of real Signal handler proof. This PR includes that proof.

## Checks

- `pnpm test extensions/signal`: pass.
- `pnpm check:line-cap-ratchet`: OK, with no growth in the over-cap `event-handler.ts`.
- Formatting: clean.
- Test lines: a 16-line allocation in `config/test-lines-allocations/signal-plugin-command-auth-135502.txt`.
- Known base condition: `main` (`e32051ef9` through `b595ee78e`) is already 12 lines over the test-line ceiling before this change (`net delta: 0` on unchanged main). The ratchet may therefore flag this PR for the pre-existing debt, not for its own 16 allocated lines.
- Not run locally: `oxlint` (the gateway-only workspace lacks `eslint-plugin-solid`) and the full extension typecheck (the only errors are an unrelated missing `@openclaw/crabbox-provider` module; there are no Signal errors).

prs.title: fix(voice-call): interrupting a reply leaves the agent working on the abandoned question
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

A caller interrupts a reply, and the agent keeps working on the question they just abandoned.

Barge-in today is audio-side only: queued telephony audio is cleared and the active reply is
cancelled, so the caller is no longer talked over. But the agent run behind that turn continues.
The caller waits out work they already interrupted, and the reply that eventually arrives answers
a stale question.

## Why This Change Was Made

Adds an opt-in `bargeIn.abortAgentRun` that also aborts the in-flight run for the call. The abort
is immediate: it signals the run's abort signal, which the exec tool observes to kill its child
process right away rather than waiting for a tool-call boundary.

History handling is delegated, not reimplemented. Tool calls that already completed stay persisted
by the embedded runner, so the next run resumes with that work intact. Tool calls killed mid-flight
are left without results, and the existing transcript repair layer synthesizes the placeholders on
the next run. The interrupted question is deliberately not carried forward: it is already in session
history, and the barged-in utterance becomes the next turn on its own.

Two supporting changes, both needed for the abort to behave:

- **`command-queue`**: an `AbortError` is a deliberate cancellation, not a lane task failure.
  Without this, every interruption wrote two error lines for work that was cancelled on purpose.
  Added alongside the existing classifications rather than replacing them -
  `isExpectedRunCancellation` does not cover a bare `AbortError`.
- **`exec`**: log the killed child on abort, so an operator can see which process died with the
  run. Logs the derived verb+target label, never the raw command, since command arguments can
  carry tokens.

## User Impact

- Opt-in and off by default: `bargeIn.abortAgentRun` defaults to `false`, so existing installs
  keep today's audio-only behaviour on upgrade.
- With it enabled, interrupting stops both the speech and the work behind it.

**Scope: the streaming path only.** The flag is read where the streaming trigger lives; the realtime
bridge is unchanged. This is a deliberate, disclosed asymmetry rather than an oversight - realtime
and streaming are mutually exclusive (`config.ts` rejects both being enabled), so the realtime half
could not be exercised on the hardware available to verify this, and I would rather ship the half
that is demonstrable than the half that is not. Realtime is a straightforward follow-up.

## Evidence

Captured on a live outbound Twilio Programmable Voice + Media Streams call, on a build pinned to
**this PR head (`eab0c21bf13`)** - `openclaw --version` reported `2026.11.1 (eab0c21)`. Call,
session and run identifiers are redacted; only structure and timings remain.

```
21:25:50 Outbound call initiated: callId=<redacted> providerCallId=<redacted> mode=conversation
21:26:37 barge-in aborted agent run callId=<redacted> source=streaming runId=voice:<redacted>:1794191181510
21:26:37 Response generation aborted by barge-in <redacted>
21:27:28 barge-in aborted agent run callId=<redacted> source=streaming runId=voice:<redacted>:1794191234177
21:27:28 Response generation aborted by barge-in <redacted>
21:27:44 barge-in aborted agent run callId=<redacted> source=streaming runId=voice:<redacted>:1794191254652
21:27:44 Response generation aborted by barge-in <redacted>
21:28:07 Call finalized callId=<redacted> endReason=completed
```

Three interruptions, three **distinct** `runId` values, each followed within ~60-80 ms by
`Response generation aborted by barge-in`. The distinct run ids are the point: turns overlap
because the inbound response handler is void-called, so an abort must target the run belonging to
the interrupted turn and never a stale or replacement run. No `barge-in agent run abort failed`
line appeared, so the guard never had to swallow a throw.

An earlier call on the parent commit (`cc6d7c42e10`) produced seven aborts with seven distinct run
ids plus one `found no tracked agent run` - the negative control, where interrupting with no run
in flight is a silent no-op. That commit differs from this head only in a type annotation, a test,
and gate metadata, but I am citing it as supporting rather than exact-head evidence.

### What this capture does not show

**The immediate child-process kill is unproven.** `exec: abort killed child` only fires when the
interrupted turn was running a shell command, and neither capture happened to interrupt one -
there was no `exec` activity in either window. The unit test
`bash-tools.exec.abort-kill-log.test.ts` covers the line in both the foreground (killed) and
backgrounded (survives) cases, but I have not demonstrated it on a live call. Happy to capture it
on request.

Requirement "completed tool results survive the kill" likewise rests on the delegation argument
above and on the existing transcript-repair layer, not on a dedicated test.

## Local gates

```
oxlint                    0 warnings, 0 errors
tsgo:extensions:test      clean
tsgo:core:test            agents-root, agents-other passed
vitest                    8 files passed
baseline ratchets         9 of 10 OK (max-lines, assertion-safety, database-dialect,
                          timeout-race, mock-exports, test-lines, config-docs,
                          plugin-inventory, database-worker)
line-cap ratchet          FAILS by one counted line - see below
```

### The line-cap failure is known and I could not clear it honestly

```
extensions/voice-call/src/webhook.ts: 829 -> 830 counted lines (cap 700)
```

`webhook.ts` is 946 raw lines against a 700 cap, grandfathered, and the growth ratchet rejects any
increase. The feature's footprint there is already down to seven lines - two imports, one field, a
constructor assignment and three call sites - after extracting two sibling modules
(`webhook/barge-in-abort-trigger.ts` for the whole abort concern, and `webhook/webhook-logger.ts`
for the `[voice-call]` prefix wrapper the abort guard consumes).

That leaves it **one counted line** over baseline. Closing the gap would mean carving further
unrelated code out of `webhook.ts`, which widens this PR into refactoring you did not ask for. I
would rather surface it: if you want a specific decomposition of that file, say which and I will
follow it. The config-doc budget also moved 5018 -> 5020 for the one new key, with the baseline
regenerated in this PR.

## Provenance notes

This branch was ported fresh onto current `main`, not rebased: the source branch sat on a base
24,034 commits behind, on top of a local integration branch carrying unrelated work. Only the
barge-in scope is here. Deliberately excluded: the chunking work (#118727), deepgram changes from
closed PRs, a queued-message-marker removal that upstream has since extended rather than dropped,
and an `isOpenAIResponsesApi` parameter removal that fights the documented Codex-normalization
design.
