prs.title: refactor(github): migrate repository integration to a plugin
prs.body:
## Summary

Depends on #192349. Review and merge the SDK foundation first.

GitHub repository integration spans account connections, repository discovery, execution identity, publication, and browser presentation. This PR moves the vendor implementation into the bundled `github-repositories` plugin using [the Plugin SDK foundation](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/192349).

The plugin supplies the existing GitHub workflows. OpenClaw retains sessions, approvals, local Git custody, durable account/publication records, and recovery. Generic SDK additions belong to the foundation; this consumer supplies GitHub registration, lifecycle, configuration migration, and presentation.

**Upgrade:** run `openclaw doctor --fix` to move legacy native GitHub settings into `plugins.entries.github-repositories.config`. Explicit plugin allowlists and deny rules remain authoritative; include `github-repositories` to use this integration.

The independent `github` plugin continues to own `github_read`, `github_search`, public link previews, and reader views. GitHub Copilot, Gateway sign-in, and verified profile identity remain separate owners.

## Ownership

| Capability | `github-repositories` supplies | OpenClaw retains |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Accounts and OAuth | Credential selection, GitHub transport, refresh policy, and connection presentation. | Canonical managed/personal account records, profile authority, config writing, and refresh settlement. |
| Repository sources | Discovery, URL admission, authenticated clone/fetch, repository/object identity, and worker adapters. | Picker/session admission, checkout storage and leases, worktree placement, accepted checkpoints, and recovery. |
| Execution identity | Identity facts, credential scrubbing, private child-launch adapters, and supported sandbox preparation. | Command policy, approvals, final launch, and sandbox provisioning/permission. |
| Publication | GitHub targets/content, remote operations, and author/coauthor policy. | Local Git/index custody, verified participant/consent facts, exact receipts, accepted-operation settlement, and live effect authority. |
| Agent tools | `github_identity_status`, `github_publish`, and their policy descriptions. | Caller-bound dispatch, workspace access, tool/child-policy ceilings, handoff, and cleanup. |
| PR/check presentation | Reads, subscriptions, plugin read store, badges, actions, Settings, and session accessories. | Session/audience admission, layout, navigation, captured requests, and retained operations. |
| Board and Doctor | GitHub Actions binding, secret/config metadata, migration, and health checks. | Grant preparation, config persistence/migration orchestration, managed service scheduling, and cleanup. |

The plugin entry registers repository and execution contributions, tools, Board data, Gateway methods, and a V2 managed account service. The manifest declares startup activation, Settings views, secret exclusions, and Doctor participation. Heavy handlers load when invoked. The host keeps its existing stores and lifecycle owners. The released `GatewayRequestContext.githubOAuthService` lookup remains a guarded projection of the canonical plugin-owned service through the documented December 31, 2026 compatibility window; it does not create a second account service.

### Repository and execution

The qualified source `github-repositories/repositories` feeds the repository picker and follows `sessions.create` into session, checkout, and worker preparation. Default worktree preparation uses source-owned `resolveBase()` to observe authenticated remote HEAD, hydrate the selected commit, and follow a renamed default branch. Explicit selectors preserve their Git namespace and literal branch names; missing refs remain actionable. The host verifies the commit locally without ambient-origin fetches, retains safe local branch updates under checkout custody, and pins ref/commit before setup. Retries retain that accepted pin. The isolated Fake Forge plugin uses the same contract with a local transport and an HTTPS canonical origin. GitHub callbacks perform authenticated transport; the host retains destinations, cancellation, pinned commits, and recovery.

Worker preparation returns immutable repository/object identities and a nonsecret cache partition. The host revalidates the lease around Git-pack preparation; the plugin asserts caller and credential authority at effects. Cache identity is not access authority. Admitted credential readers retain the original dispatch actor and request; issued credentials register cleanup with the host.

Execution uses the SDK environment provider. Local wrappers enclose the reviewed command after policy/approval. Sandbox preparation explicitly selects backend and scope rather than copying local identity. Declared exclusions keep bearer credentials out of nonsecret environment facts and prepared repository snapshots.

### Publication and lifecycle

The plugin consumes `native-github-account-host`, `native-github-publication-host`, and `native-github-session-read` to work with the existing native records and receipts.

- `github_publish` uses caller-bound Gateway operations and the existing publication/handoff owner. Session and approval checks remain in force. PR preparation retains the selected requester through the existing host continuation; publication keeps its existing accepted-operation settlement.
- The plugin supplies typed provenance and Git author facts. Core records and compares existing receipt fields for replay and uses the author for source-integration commits. Live request/account assertions authorize effects; verified participant/consent facts stay host-owned.
- PR automation reads the session’s own publication without an import-authorship preflight. A different captured target retains its existing authenticated read workflow. The recipe retains jobs after authentication, inspection, network, and checkout blockers and after successful remediation; cleanup is reserved for a verified merged/closed result.
- Plugin-owned `session-pr:v1` declarations retain their SHA256 identity bytes. Wire/storage DTOs and accepted publication records retain their contracts.
- Refresh, publication-provider installation, and session presentation use managed scheduler, Gateway, and plugin-instance lifetimes. The legacy service projection shares its existing exact-Gateway lookup across native and compiled module graphs. Native source loading and compiled SDK consumers use the same canonical owner and installed publication-host lookup. Accepted publication and checkout transfers remain one-use operations under that owner; cleanup, replacement, and revocation end stale capabilities.

### Browser presentation and reader independence

Control UI V2 contributions provide Profile connections, Agent tools Settings, session PR/check accessories, actions, and retained publication operations. They reuse host controls, responsive layout, serialized config mutations, and captured requests. Plain host-owner subscriptions feed plugin-local reactive state across the separately bundled Solid runtimes. The plugin read store owns PR presentation. Hovercards preserve the compact ten-PR limit and remaining count; branch/diff metadata occupies an adjacent row in the existing accessory layout. Branch and publication controls stay in the native Environment section through the generic `session-environment` slot; published PRs use the separate context section.

Explicit shorthand such as `owner/repo#123` names `reader: { pluginId: "github", id: "github" }`. Both contributions must be admitted and active; the reader owns URL filtering and remote reads. Checkout names, project aliases, and adjacent links never infer a destination, so formatting needs no background project-catalog read.

Public `github.preview` and `github.detail` use the reader's data path directly, so disabling `github-repositories` leaves public reading operational. Enabled managed identity retains its current-selection checks; disabled integration skips that managed selection and uses the existing service/environment/anonymous public path. GitHub App installations verify identity with a temporary installation token and support public reads/search scoped to the requested repository. Temporary tokens are revoked before delivery; App access does not broaden the public-only reader or enable shell execution/publication. Request authority is checked during reads and before delivery. Session/Enterprise readers retain their admitted session-specific path.

Disabling repository integration removes its operations, managed service, tools, and browser contributions. Disabling `github` removes public reading without changing repository ownership. Neither operation broadens allow/deny policy.

Session rows render passive plugin badge facts through the native row renderer. The same bounded, data-only facts join the existing scoped sidebar snapshot, so PR indicators survive a reload before plugin reconnect. Pending results retain facts only for the same complete session target and current registration; ready-empty results and retirement clear them. No plugin code, catalog, new storage manager, or capture timer is persisted.

## Configuration and upgrade

Canonical settings live under `plugins.entries.github-repositories.config`:

| Setting | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `system` | Shared managed GitHub execution identity. |
| `agents.<id>` | Complete per-agent identity override and optional sandbox permission. |
| `host`, `apiBaseUrl` | Matching GitHub or Enterprise endpoint pair. |
| `service.host`, `service.token` | Gateway-side discovery and reader service credential. |
| `repositorySearch.useNativeCredentials` | Explicit opt-in for native-credential repository search. |

`openclaw doctor --fix` invokes the plugin-owned transform for `tools.github`, per-agent `tools.github`, `gateway.github`, `gateway.controlUi.github`, and `gateway.projects.nativeGitHubSearch`. Explicit canonical values win, identities remain atomic, and unknown legacy fields remain available for explicit repair. Normalization is idempotent; conflict warnings omit credential values.

Managed OAuth records, personal connections, and accepted publication state retain their existing storage owners. Runtime reads canonical configuration; migration does not add a legacy runtime reader or rewrite receipts. Explicit allowlists, deny rules, disabled entries, and independent-reader policy are preserved.

See `docs/plugins/github.md` and `extensions/github-repositories/config-migration.test.ts` for configuration and migration details.

## Test scope

Native contracts remain with their host owners. GitHub unit and integration suites live with the plugin; native UI fixtures activate its declared public browser entry and consume protocol events. Coverage includes canonical configuration migration, serialized writes, account selection and retirement, publication handoff, worker credentials, execution approvals, browser freshness and independent reader admission. A standalone fixture allocation covers real provider setup, typed public adapters, lifecycle cleanup and passive-badge reload proof; the shared scalar is unchanged. A separate exact allocation covers App status/read lifetime, automation target/blocker guidance, and App capability presentation regressions.

## Validation

- Full local `pnpm build` passes, including SDK declarations, all 102 bundled plugins, all 167 public SDK subpaths and Control UI. Core, Gateway, agent-execution, extension and UI typechecks pass for the affected scopes. The supported local package passes tarball inventory and import-graph integrity checks.
- The intervening handoff and worker-recovery owners pass 98 targeted cases. Publisher installation rollback passes eight host/loader cases; native-menu error isolation and plugin-owned live/persisted badge parity pass 31 UI cases, with affected production/test typechecks and scoped lint.
- A supported local CLI turn with both GitHub plugins disabled executes successfully with the independent Fake Forge identity and no GitHub token in its child environment.
- Published 2026.10.9 state survives Doctor migration, a second idempotent Doctor run and restart, preserving its project, managed worktree, session and published request. Explicit deny remains authoritative when both GitHub plugins are also allowlisted: two Doctor runs and a restart leave both plugins unloaded and absent from UI/repository catalogs while OpenAI remains active. A separate real Gateway interruption during an accepted publication resumes the same request/account/destination through idempotent replay and produces exactly one PR with the expected commit. A crash after a remote effect with its response lost remains synthetic-fault coverage.
- Focused native checkout/publication, RPC, execution identity/approval, sandbox, App/OAuth/Git transport and browser suites pass. Cached badge reload and cross-tab deletion proof includes actual persisted badge facts; capture cadence is unchanged.
- Real isolated Gateway checks verify App identity, public PR reading/search, and refusal to disclose a private PR despite installation access. Native identity also publishes to disposable public/private repositories, resumes an advanced private head, refreshes the base, and uploads/associates sandbox evidence.
- A real scheduled auto-fix occurrence reads the selected PR's feedback, verifies the requested edit, and publishes to the same PR while retaining its job. The 14 recipe contract cases pass; repeated fresh-observation behavior remains unqualified as described below.
- Focused repair suites pass: 63 App/reader/RPC cases, 15 connections cases, 14 automation cases, and the SDK readiness regression.
- Targeted account lifecycle proof verifies unavailable selection and exact-config recovery with real reads; seven credential/profile retirement and cleanup cases pass. Nineteen publication response-loss, duplicate replay, authority, and restart-recovery cases pass through the real host/plugin adapter with synthetic GitHub faults.
- Fresh isolated Fake Forge proof passes: plugin transport supplies the advanced remote commit, the host owns the managed worktree, and one real successful agent `exec` receives `FAKE_FORGE_IDENTITY=sdk-trial`. The Gateway remains available locally; the model is a synthetic loopback fixture.
- Production and test compiler-boundary guards pass without exemptions. English catalogs load through the declared public artifact and retain Vite dependency watching and fresh reloads; source localization verification passes.
- Startup JavaScript gzip passes its unchanged cap: 90,661 bytes against 90,687 bytes. Startup/auth behavior, native Agents settings, browser subscription cleanup and reconnect have focused passing proof.

Interactive OAuth issuance, distinct-account isolation, native Codex-harness execution, Enterprise endpoints, real cloud provisioning, factory-native proof issuance/redemption, and migration from the newer 2026.11.1 release remain unqualified. Reliable full recurring auto-fix monitoring also remains unqualified: the complete recipe can return quietly without reading fresh feedback, and that failure mode is reproduced on untouched upstream as well. Live feedback-to-publication execution is verified separately.

## Browser evidence

Existing sanitized synthetic captures illustrate shorthand and desktop/mobile Settings presentation; they are not live OAuth or current-head runtime qualification.

| Shorthand before | Shorthand after |
| --- | --- |
| ![Shorthand before the reader-owner fix](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/9596a8ed-17fd-4809-9c45-f0bc359d40af) | ![Shorthand after the reader-owner fix](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/dd794946-ed7c-4567-a1bf-4862d23afb6d) |

| Native desktop | Plugin desktop |
| --- | --- |
| ![Native GitHub connections](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/333e056f-5322-429d-a30e-f3d785d89120) | ![Plugin GitHub connections](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/ef691381-28d5-4da0-9261-6b99f58de6b5) |

| Native mobile | Plugin mobile |
| --- | --- |
| ![Native mobile GitHub connections](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/6434b428-a4cb-459b-a1ba-fae5794d1c02) | ![Plugin mobile GitHub connections](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/0d36dcdc-6584-48e5-9ba9-4258b70a85c3) |

The Environment row uses the host control wrappers and explicit plugin icon/diff styling. The following synthetic browser captures show the repaired layout.

| Before | After |

prs.title: feat(ai): record bounded prompt presence checks for frozen injection expectations
prs.body:
# Prompt presence checks for frozen injection expectations

Implements the approved PRI-1119 minimal design v1.2 (Tier B): bounded, fact-only presence checks that verify whether a frozen injection expectation's full body text appears inside the **pre-submission request object**, on both the `openai-responses` and `openai-completions` paths.

## What this does

- **Pure bounded checker** (`packages/ai/src/transports/prompt-presence-check.ts`): three mutually exclusive outcomes — `full_hit` / `checked_missing` / `unknown` with explicit reasons (`assembly_truncated`, `body_over_limit`, `expectations_over_limit`, `scan_region_over_limit`, `cumulative_scan_over_limit`, `unparseable_content`, `check_failed`). Caps: per-body 64 KiB, per-message region 8 MiB, expectation count 64, message count 512, and a **cumulative UTF-8 scan cap (32 MiB) covering legal AND wrong-role regions — exceeding it never outputs `checked_missing`** (owner condition 1).
- **responses path**: the existing egress observer frame computes `presenceCheck` (with per-attempt index) when the request carries a frozen expectation set (options-keyed carrier). The `provider.prompt.observed` event gains `presenceCheck` (+ `requestIndex` stamped by the runner wrapper).
- **completions path** (previously zero observation): a checkpoint after `onPayload` replacement and before `encodeBody` emits the same event channel with `egress: "completions"`, `attemptIndex: 0`.
- **runner**: per-run `requestCount` on the run-scoped prompt state (incremented once per attempt assembly), expectation set frozen by the prompt-build phase **after the size guard**, carrier bound per request, `requestIndex` stamped on emitted events.
- **plugins**: optional structured `injectedExpectations` field on the before_prompt_build result (validated passthrough; merged by concatenation across plugins).

No request mutation. No body persistence. Requests without frozen expectations are unaffected: no carrier → no `presenceCheck` field → no measurable added cost.

## Owner acceptance conditions — where implemented

1. Cumulative scan cap (32 MiB default) over legal AND wrong-role regions; exceeding yields `unknown:cumulative_scan_over_limit`, never `checked_missing`.
2. Expectations carry `bodyComplete`; truncated-assembly fragments force `unknown:assembly_truncated` and can never yield `full_hit`. The injecting plugin freezes expectations after its size guard and marks completeness by containment.
3. Event identity reuses existing fields: envelope `runId`, wrapper-stamped `requestIndex` (run-scoped ordinal, incremented per attempt assembly), egress-closure `attemptIndex` + `payloadVariant`. Tests cover same-run multi-request, concurrency isolation, and retry attempt indexing.
4. Event size measured in UTF-8 bytes (table below).

## Measured on the implementing machine (script: `packages/ai/src/transports/prompt-presence-measure.mts`)

| fixture | runs | median | p95 | event bytes (UTF-8) |
|---|---|---:|---:|---:|
| representative: 18 expectations × ~2.2 KiB bodies, 58k-char system region | 30 | 0.111 ms | 0.192 ms | 2,994 |
| representative: 1 expectation, same region | 30 | 0.008 ms | 0.010 ms | 249 |
| boundary: 64 expectations × 64 KiB bodies (under limits) | 10 | 128.620 ms | 129.286 ms | 10,702 |

## Tests

- `packages/ai/src/transports/prompt-presence-check.test.ts` — 20 fixtures (containment, roles, parts, no-concatenation, prefix-not-hit, limits, cumulative cap, truncated-assembly rule, exception fail-open, completions roles).
- `src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/provider-prompt-state.presence.test.ts` — 6 tests (carrier binding + event stamping, same-run multi-request ordinals, concurrency isolation, absent-expectation untouched events, truncated-assembly rule through the real transport chain, retry attempt indexing).
- Regressions green: existing observer/transport suites 36/36; runner-side scoped tsc clean for touched files.

## Trust boundary

The check runs inside the host process (host-recorded, not third-party). It observes the pre-submission request object — the exact object `encodeBody` serializes into the wire body via body-override. It does not prove network-peer bytes or model-context inclusion.

prs.title: fix(macos): preserve MLX model config cache reuse
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

MLX model-type detection can perform a network lookup during helper startup even when model configuration is cached locally.

## User Impact

Reuse cached model configuration and retain MLX settings. Preserve Control UI transcript ownership, composer scroll state, reactive menus and shadow-parent loading styles.

## Why This Change Was Made

Pin the [official config-only detection repair](https://github.com/Blaizzy/mlx-audio-swift/commit/d60236dee82de1173fc20757dad82a5116db1ddf) and its qualified SwiftPM dependency graph.

Supporting regression fixes preserve reactive menu presentation and retry only explicitly rejected, retryable busy responses in the plugin test. The upstream combined gateway scenario, lifecycle guards, layout assertions, compression policy and performance limits remain intact.

The branch incorporates upstream retention-helper export repairs [34d5b3f](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/34d5b3fd2911a25dbb97f791e3161a999b0fa130) and [72110f3](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/72110f30e8dd47bdabf35190f7f3cebb16c23ccc). Earlier hosted attempts used a merge revision without those repairs; their failures remain recorded.

Replaces https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/187506, with credit to @dependabot. Keep the original open until this replacement merges and its latest scope is confirmed covered.

## Evidence

The [latest correction](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/3d4cefc419735d1cecb69b6ca32dfb575a1fd5ed) lets terminal MLX source audits use the remaining original cleanup time after the child succeeds and retires its resources. Earlier checks still use the work deadline. Integrity checks and the 27/30-minute deadlines remain unchanged.

The regression reproduces the old failure. Both affected suites passed on the byte-identical precommit draft under Node and Bun: **54 tests each, zero skips**. Script/test types, scoped lint, formatting and normal commit hooks passed. These are local tooling tests; fresh hosted macOS qualification is still required. The test allocation is exactly **3,199 lines**. The local ratchet against the frozen preparation base still fails by **16 inherited lines**, without added allowance for that deficit.

Ordinary [CI at the preceding head](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/42508047924) completed successfully, with its effective Security run also successful. This does not provide hosted pass credit for the latest correction.

The preceding head's [Full validation](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/42525816231) failed: 96 jobs succeeded, five failed and 11 were skipped. Its five failures are accounted for:

- Docker seed rejected source candidate `2026.11.1` below the selected Codex minimum `2026.11.5-beta.1`; no Docker lane ran. A coherent source release cohort is required.
- The central-lint fixture repair landed upstream in https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/195197.
- The Logs E2E deferral repair landed upstream in https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/195434.
- The real-Gateway rejection response took **2,207 ms** against its unchanged **2,000 ms** limit. One focused local diagnostic passed, but the hosted cause remains unknown.
- The terminal MLX audit exhausted work time after the child succeeded; the latest correction addresses this defect and still needs hosted qualification.

The two separately landed upstream repairs are not incorporated into this branch yet. They do not supply this head with runtime credit.

Local checks at `699a1968ba042c8e59e2d2ae1b098c5e2093ec6c`:

- **237 passes across 14 phases**: 236 named identities and one gallery identity inferred from pinned source. The run recorded 1,283 selector exclusions and eight Linux-only skips; no mandatory case was skipped. One completed 24-case wrapper phase is included once.
- **92 configuration/plugin/memory fixture passes**: 86 named identities and six authorization cases inferred at group level.
- **50 performance-checker cases**, **17 cleanup guards**, **one combined real-gateway scenario** and **two lifecycle-contention cases** passed.
- Production type checking passed. Two retention suites passed **11 cases**: ten fully named and one with a partially redacted parameter.
- Menu contracts passed **33 Chromium and 33 WebKit cases** on this commit.
- The paired production build passed against `234007727335d626bea45f1c660e50f1efb16dab`. Normalized JavaScript gzip totals changed by **+495 bytes for Chat** and **+625 bytes for New Session**; CSS gzip totals decreased by **14 bytes** for each route. Startup totals, request counts and the baseline's performance limits remained unchanged.


Fresh exact-head hosted qualification remains required before merge, including macOS MLX, SDK, Android, WebKit and retention/lifecycle contracts. Deferred GitHub gates, skipped jobs and historical results do not supply pass credit.

prs.title: fix(logging): capture bounded Node 24 stall stacks
prs.body:
Related: #195424

## What Problem This Solves

Node 24's native CPU profiler ignores the interval and buffer-limit options used by the bounded stall recorder, so the existing runtime gate reports long Gateway stalls without JavaScript frames. Removing that gate would enable an uncapped profiler.

## User Impact

Long Node 24 stalls can include bounded JavaScript self/inclusive frames without a configuration change. The implementation is ready for review and remains unmerged. **The lead-requested steady-state heap/latency acceptance is met**, with the CPU context and individual outliers reported below. Opaque native calls can still produce kernel-only evidence.

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing observer worker obtains up to three interrupted stacks, at most 16 frames each, once heartbeat age reaches 500 ms. It does not start a profiler or open a debugger listener. Three shared credits cap queued stack payloads; source maps/custom stack hooks are disabled, late dispatch is discarded, and existing redaction and the 2 KiB report cap apply. `sampleMode=interrupt` and null self CPU durations identify point observations rather than measured CPU durations. Node 26 keeps its bounded native recorder.

The native gate originated in #169535: Node 24's `v8.startCpuProfile()` accepts no options and uses `kNoSampleLimit`. The separate cold-profiler code-map startup cost is already mitigated for repeated bounded Node 26 captures by #170932. Keeping only an inspector session connected does not retain an active profiler's code map.

A continuous 10 ms inspector profiler was measured and rejected: median paired main/process CPU +11.51%/+16.29%, stop/extraction 73.51–98.73 ms (median 84.19), serialization 6.49–11.36 ms (median 7.14), and 4.20–4.95 MB of uncapped profile JSON after about a minute. Starting before boot took 11.09–11.54 ms; this does not contradict the previously observed much larger late-start cost. `--cpu-prof` uses the same uncapped machinery and exit-file lifecycle. Linux perf/JIT maps require suitable launch-time symbols and perf-event permissions, so they remain an explicit diagnostic alternative.

## Evidence

### Idle path

There is no new production timer or worker. The existing main heartbeat and observer poll run every 250 ms. The added idle work is a counter/conditional, eight shared bytes, a registered capture closure and small empty containers per health sample (1 s active / 10 s idle). Node 24's ordinary health sampling neither calls `getCallSites` nor creates an inspector session. The threshold test verifies healthy heartbeats cause no connection/evaluation and the first connection occurs only once heartbeat age reaches 500 ms.

All five candidate steady-state measurement windows recorded **zero inspector attempts**. Two/one startup attempts occurred in candidates 1/2; all are retained, not excluded or retrospectively exonerated. Observer CPU median was **0.02501% of one core [0.02297–0.03532%]**, versus baseline **0.02467% [0.02411–0.02882%]**, including identical benchmark telemetry. The median paired absolute increase was **0.000895 percentage points**, about **0.54 ms normalized to a minute**. Sampled observer heap stayed below 9 MB in these runs.

An already requested interrupt can remain pending while native execution is uninterruptible; the short path allows only one pending request. The session disconnects on completion, and dispatch over 100 ms late is discarded. This is a bounded diagnostic path, not hard real-time interrupt cancellation. Heartbeat age is sampled every 250 ms; it is not an exact callback-duration threshold.

### Fixed-work steady-state acceptance

Node 24.22.1, real built Gateways and WebSockets, synthetic fixture: 10,800 sessions, 4,300 settled runs, four agents, 36 projects, 40 plugins, 64 clients/four exact subscriptions, eight concurrent turns. Three warmup cohorts/30 s, then six measured cohorts/48 turns over at least 60 s. Each arm completed exactly **96 calls per core polling method (384 total), 20 patches, 48 agent calls and 48 waits**. Same pristine fixture and absolute state path each time. This models cardinality, not a full 35 GiB database or btrfs workspace.

Opening A/A, five interleaved pairs in AB/BA/AB/BA/AB order, closing A/A: **14 steady-state runs**, no injected stalls. Both exact source heads, complete built file trees, preload/runtime/fixture hashes, host load, commands and raw results were pinned. No run was omitted or repeated.

The lead-authorized rule was recorded before the first run: for each heap end/observed peak and RPC p95 metric, the positive median of all five signed paired B/A percentage deltas must fit within the larger absolute change of the two A/A controls. **All nine metrics pass.** The original stricter experiment remains historical evidence; its flags were not relabeled or erased.

| Metric | Median paired B/A | Paired range | A/A envelope |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Live heap end | +12.71% | -24.08% to +44.35% | ±14.75% |
| Observed peak heap | +2.08% | -2.38% to +37.92% | ±14.88% |
| agent p95 | +0.17% | -3.84% to +97.26% | ±10.93% |
| agent.wait p95 | -0.41% | -4.95% to +129.47% | ±42.37% |
| chat.history p95 | -2.55% | -4.87% to +17.59% | ±7.52% |
| connect p95 | -0.82% | -15.78% to +7.78% | ±9.01% |
| sessions.diff p95 | +0.60% | -2.56% to +87.51% | ±13.32% |
| sessions.list p95 | -0.85% | -29.31% to +50.32% | ±8.95% |
| sessions.patch p95 | -1.14% | -4.21% to +101.60% | ±10.53% |

| Metric | Baseline median [range] | Candidate median [range] |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Heap end (MB) | 550.61 [522.20–638.74] | 612.60 [484.93–769.21] |
| Observed peak heap (MB) | 648.99 [630.19–667.36] | 669.11 [649.46–869.14] |
| Main CPU (% one core) | 24.45 [23.32–26.83] | 24.38 [23.42–29.11] |
| Process CPU (% one core) | 53.53 [50.65–57.56] | 52.43 [50.94–63.49] |
| Observer CPU (% one core) | 0.02467 [0.02411–0.02882] | 0.02501 [0.02297–0.03532] |

MB is decimal. Latency is each run's nearest-rank p95; percentages summarize paired deltas, not pooled request percentiles. Ratios of the arm medians differ from medians of paired ratios. Heap values are live samples, not allocated-byte volume or continuously observed maxima. This Node 24 runtime does not expose the total allocated-byte counter.

CPU remains explicit context: paired main CPU **+0.044% [−4.966%, +8.497%]** is within its 2.587% A/A envelope. Whole-process CPU **+3.531% [−7.415%, +10.292%]** exceeds its tighter 0.939% envelope (paired absolute median +1.788 percentage points of one core). That is not erased or described as a proven zero-overhead result; causal attribution to the recorder is not established. Observer cost is measured separately above. RSS end paired median −1.314%; post-GC retained heap +0.048% [−0.234%, +1.493%], which does not replace the raw heap gate.

The first candidate remains an outlier: heap end +44.35%, agent.wait p95 +129.47%, actual measured duration 77.011 s versus 60.003 s. Every other acceptance arm is approximately 60 s. The heap-end median clears the 14.75% A/A envelope by only 2.05 percentage points; this is acceptance under the stated noise criterion, not a universal performance bound.

The prior feedback-sensitive workload generated more polling during slow runs (one pair: 3,378 versus 1,733 core RPCs), confounding work and memory/latency. This follow-up keeps the same fixture/transport/turn shape but bounds polls with `--list-interval-ms 600000`, omitting `--poll-seed` and `--poll-between-rounds`.

### Separate periodic-stall proof

A separate candidate run injected six 1.2 s CPU spins at +5/15/25/35/45/55 s. It reported six **unattributed** stalls of 1200, 1241, 1219, 1202, 1221 and 1202 ms. Each had three interrupted samples, `stallCpuLeaf` in self frames and `stallCpuOwner` in inclusive frames; all six reports were **680 bytes**, without report truncation.

The 18 injected captures totaled **1.888 ms**, median **0.104 ms**, maximum **0.128 ms**. Maximum worker-observed round trip was **4.265 ms**; maximum connect call **0.017 ms**. Capture time alone is not total inspector overhead. The entire observer used **29.224 ms CPU over 70.008 s (0.04174% of one core)**, including polling/telemetry, with sampled observer heap at most **9.019 MB**.

One additional natural capture occurred early in the measured window (0.584 ms); one post-window capture was 111.688 ms late and rejected. All attempts are retained. The 76.735 s periodic run is excluded from steady-state acceptance.

Earlier Linux Node 24.22.1 proof identified the owner/leaf in 5/5 trials with simultaneous R/running kernel evidence; report extraction median 0.277 ms, max 1.263 ms, largest report 886 bytes. The new real 1.2 s regression fails on exact parent `e673256f8a9351607912329020857906643a1c1c` and passes with the fix, including queued-microtask ordering. A natural 1,366 ms synthetic-workload stall also identified the synchronous plugin-generation `requestSync` wait; that does not identify a production stall's source.

### Reproduction and validation

CI repair at `17e6e4f1e84cf0193cd967e3e7df4efe29a50a7f`: fetched the failed `check-lint-core-1` job log once. The full scripts lane caught unbound methods that the prior single-file check missed. Rebased onto current `origin/main` (`43dae0b46f1e`), removed two duplicate label-presence assertions while retaining real owner/microtask/report-cap proof, and allocated exactly **91** net new test lines. The requested no-merge-base ratchet passes with **6,589,626 lines / 6,589,626 ceiling, zero slack**. The complete failed job scope passes locally: core stripes 1/5 and 2/5 plus full scripts/resource-safety lint. Stripe 2 uses the CI `GITHUB_ACTIONS=true` policy, which reports the same five unchanged size-limit warnings seen in the fetched CI log; the stricter non-CI local variant reports these as errors, so that variant is not claimed green. No rule or suppression was changed. Node 24 tests: **25 passed, two skips**; real observer preload smoke, formatter parity, and scoped P0–P2 Codex review also pass. Pushed with an exact old-head lease; CI on the new head is pending, and this PR remains unmerged.


Use the committed fixture/transport harness and `stall-recorder-cost-preload.mjs?interrupts=measure` on both builds. Restore fresh state between arms. Core measurement invocation:

```sh
node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs scripts/perf/transcript-broadcast-measure.ts \
  --entry "$ENTRY" --gateway-preload "$PRELOAD" --state-dir "$STATE" \
  --scenario memory-soak --clients 64 --exact-clients 4 --runs 8 --plugins 40 \
  --duration-ms 60000 --warmup-ms 30000 --soak-rounds 6 --round-interval-ms 10000 \
  --memory-interval-ms 5000 --chunks 200 --chunk-interval-ms 10 --prompt-kib 16 \
  --retained-profile-ms 0 --reset-every-rounds 0 --row-mode sidebar --limit 200 \
  --list-interval-ms 600000 --mixed-rpc --list-filter-churn --diagnostics
```

Only the separate proof appends `&proof=interrupt-periodic` to the preload import. Measurement head was `9d043d400ac9`. The CI follow-up rebases onto `43dae0b46f1e` and replaces the benchmark prototype patch with a `Session` subclass using `super` (no unbound methods or lint suppression). The production recorder files remain byte-identical to the measured implementation; performance measurements were not rerun for this benchmark/test-only repair.

Node 24 focused tests: 25 passed, two existing platform/runtime skips; Bun: 22 passed, five skips. The extended threshold suite passed all four tests. Both production builds passed. Isolated Codex autoreview found no actionable P0–P2 findings. The benchmark CI lint failure was corrected; CI-equivalent local oxlint, formatting and the real observer smoke check pass. Final-head CI status is reported separately.

`pnpm check:changed` completed; its formatting failure was corrected and rechecked. The remaining changelog-attribution failure is a confirmed main regression: #194364 (`266a7aa0fe69`) introduced 20 forbidden historical attributions, reproduced on the exact parent (0 → 20 on the same release files). It is not noise; release archives are unchanged here.

No configuration, schema, cache or UI import changes. Production growth **+131 lines** implements bounded capture/queue ownership and shares the frame formatter. No production access or live changes. This enables evidence collection; it does not claim the recurring production blocking owner is identified or removed, or guarantee opaque native-frame coverage.

Release-note context: long CPU-bound Node 24 Gateway stalls can now include bounded JavaScript stack evidence.

prs.title: docs: containerized gateway networking, host model servers, and rootless Podman troubleshooting
prs.body:
Related: #194988

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: a containerized gateway cannot reach model servers running on the host, and nothing in the docs explains why published ports go unreachable, config edits get rejected, or container starts fail on SELinux hosts — operators reverse-engineer error strings like `Blocked: resolves to private/internal/special-use IP address` and `cannot verify Gateway ownership from this process`.

Affects anyone running the gateway in rootless Podman or Docker with local models (llama.cpp, LM Studio, Ollama, vLLM) or scripting a hosted-primary + local-fallback setup.

## User Impact

Users can now: point a local provider at a host model server from inside a container (with the SSRF-guard caveat and both fixes explained), understand why `loopback`/`tailnet` binds strand published ports and what to use instead, script the non-interactive hybrid setup (hosted primary, local fallback), and self-recover from three rootless-Podman failure modes (config ownership lock, keep-id mismatch on one-off commands, SELinux relabel denial).

## Why This Change Was Made

The documented behavior is incomplete, not the code: bind modes, the config ownership lock, exact-origin SSRF trust, and onboarding flag handling all behave as designed, but the containerized-gateway docs describe host-centric semantics only. Each section documents observed behavior — verified against source and reproduced on a real rootless Quadlet deployment — rather than proposing changes.

## Evidence

- Source verification: bind fallback semantics in `src/gateway/net.ts`; ownership-lock error text and the 90-second heartbeat in `src/infra/gateway-lock-payload.ts`; link-local exclusion from exact-origin trust in `src/agents/provider-network-policy.ts` and `src/infra/net/ssrf.ts`; `--custom-*` flags ignored beside a hosted `--auth-choice` in `src/commands/onboard-non-interactive/local/`.
- Real deployment: all three troubleshooting failure modes reproduced on Fedora rootless Podman with the Quadlet; the alias `baseUrl` is rejected while a LAN-IP `baseUrl` works.
- Docs checks: `pnpm docs:check-links` passes (16,476 links, 0 broken); `docs:check-links:anchors` shows only two pre-existing failures that reproduce unchanged on the unmodified upstream tip; `pnpm docs:check-config-examples` passes (the json5 patch fence validates); `oxfmt` clean on touched files.
- Issue: #194988 (with closed predecessors #68684, #79850, #163315 — code paths fixed, docs gap remained).

<details>
<summary>Commits in this PR</summary>

- `docs(podman): reach host model servers from a containerized gateway` — alias setup, link-local SSRF caveat, both fixes, cross-link from local-models
- `docs(local-models): add non-interactive hybrid setup recipe` — hosted-primary + local-fallback scripting sequence
- `docs: warn that container bind modes strand published ports` — Quadlet note, Docker networking note, troubleshooting entry
- `docs(podman): add rootless container troubleshooting` — ownership lock, SELinux relabel, keep-id entries

</details>

Two leftovers from the Control UI copy sweep remained in core copy:

- In Settings › Appearance › Tab icon, the notice for a locked lobster read “This lobster is not unlocked in this browser.” The Control UI style rules call for contractions.

prs.title: improve(clawrouter): apply the Control UI glossary and style to ClawRouter copy
prs.body:
## Problem

The ClawRouter pool page (`extensions/clawrouter/src/control-ui.tsx`) hard-coded every English string inline. That made the copy untranslatable, and some of it didn't follow the approved Control UI style: no contractions, sentences ending fragments with periods, passive "is required" phrasing, a raw error message shown as the alert headline, two different names for the same "enabled state unknown" concept, and Gateway status messages pointing at a "Model Providers" page whose actual label is **Models**.

## Solution

- Add a plugin-owned English catalog on the Nostr/Workboard pattern: `src/i18n/locales/en.ts`, `src/i18n/locales.ts`, and `src/i18n/index.ts`, using `translateControlUiMessage`. `browserRoot` is `src/` (the dirname of `openclaw.controlUi`), so `pnpm ui:i18n:verify` picks the catalog up automatically.
- Move **70 strings** into `en.ts` (68 under `clawrouter.*`, plus the shared `common.refresh` and `common.refreshing`, which match core English exactly). Composed strings such as "Observed {date} · Policy {policy}", "{used} used / {limit} monthly limit", and "{count} subscriptions with headroom · {unknown} unknown" are now single templates instead of JSX fragments.
- Apply the glossary and style rules to every human-visible string the lane owns, including the four Gateway pool status messages in `index.ts` that this page renders.
- Errors: the alert now reads "Couldn’t load the ClawRouter pool. Try Refresh." The redacted technical detail is still shown, but as a secondary hint line under the alert. Plugin views have no shared "Show details" disclosure on `main` (`ControlUiComponents` has none), so per the sweep brief the raw detail stays visually secondary and inline.
- `locales.ts` serves English only. This plugin has no `translated.json` yet, and the sweep brief says to leave it absent. A static import of a missing JSON file would break the esbuild bundle, so the lazy loader isn't added yet (see the open question below).

The `ClawRouter` page title and nav label stay as literal product names.

### Notable copy changes

| Before | After |
| --- | --- |
| Could not load the pool. Try refreshing. *(only for non-Error failures; otherwise the raw message was the alert)* | Couldn’t load the ClawRouter pool. Try Refresh. *(raw detail shown below as a hint)* |
| Read access is required to view the ClawRouter pool. | You need read access to view the ClawRouter pool. |
| Selections: {n}. API-equivalent value is not a subscription charge. | Selections: {n}. API-equivalent value isn’t a subscription charge. |
| Enabled state unknown *(grant badge)* | Enabled state not reported *(same as the extra-usage wording; one name per concept)* |
| Not reported. *(extra-usage fragment)* | Not reported |
| ClawRouter pool status is unavailable. Check the ClawRouter connection and try Refresh. | Couldn’t load ClawRouter pool status. Check the ClawRouter connection and try Refresh. |
| Configure a ClawRouter key in Model Providers, then try Refresh. | Configure a ClawRouter key in Models, then try Refresh. |
| The ClawRouter key was rejected. Check or replace it in Model Providers. | The ClawRouter key was rejected. Check or replace it in Models. |
| This ClawRouter deployment does not expose pool status. … | This ClawRouter deployment doesn’t expose pool status. … |

All other strings moved into the catalog with their English unchanged.

## Impact

- The English copy is the same apart from the rows above. Layout and markup are unchanged, except that a failed refresh now shows a fixed alert plus a secondary detail line.
- No docs quote the changed labels. `docs/providers/clawrouter.md` and the README reference **Refresh**, **Not reported**, and **ClawRouter**, which are unchanged.
- Foreign locales: none yet. The post-merge locale refresh owns parity. `ui:i18n:check` parity is non-strict on PRs.

## Evidence

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run extensions/clawrouter/browser/pool.test.ts extensions/clawrouter/pool-gateway.test.ts`: 3 + 12 passed. The browser test assertions are updated for the new alert headline, the detail line still being redacted, and the "You need read access" copy.
- `pnpm ui:i18n:verify`: green, `plugin=clawrouter keys=70 locales=0`.
- `pnpm tsgo:extensions`: green.
- `node scripts/run-oxlint.mjs <touched files>`: no problems.
- `node scripts/run-format.mts --check <touched files>`: clean.
- `pnpm check:control-ui-controllers`: OK.
- `git diff --check`: clean.
- `scripts/build-plugin-control-ui.mts extensions/clawrouter`: bundle builds.
- pr-simplify pass: removed duplicate keys (one "Observed {date}", one "Subscription") and collapsed repeated enabled/disabled ternaries into one helper. Production delta: +260/−126 across 6 files. Most of it is the new 90-line `en.ts` plus the line-wrapping of `t(...)` calls.
- Local review: autoreview (Codex engine, gpt-6.1-sol), branch mode, base `d59f00281eb0216` → head `14ab4736fa24`, max priority P2. Result: scoped-clean, "patch is correct (0.9)", no findings. Local ClawSweeper wasn't set up on this host.

**Not landing: requested by maintainer; screenshots pending before merge** (the visual gate needs before/after screenshots of the pool page, including the refresh-failure state).

## Open question

Leaving `translated.json` absent means that after the locale refresh writes it, nothing loads it until a follow-up adds the Nostr-style `loadMessages` loader. The alternatives are to commit an empty `{}` `translated.json` with the loader now, or to add both in the first locale refresh.

## Work sessions

- [Original discussion with @vyctorbrzezowski](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/dashboard/8ee302fc-4575-4506-92a8-1739453b9b71)
- [Implementation and verification](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/subagent/a37a5704-38f5-40e9-87b9-fbcec400e40e)

## Worked on by

- @vyctorbrzezowski

prs.title: improve(x): apply the Control UI glossary and style to X replies copy
prs.body:
## Problem

The **X replies** Control UI page hard-codes its English copy in `extensions/x/src/control-ui.tsx`. Several strings also break the approved Control UI glossary and style rules:

- "bot" where the copy means the agent
- "Administrator" as the role name
- "hidden helpers" for subagents
- fragment sentences that end in periods
- raw server error text shown as the only error message

The empty-state hint also put the internal config key `allowFrom` in normal copy.

## Solution

- Add a plugin-owned English catalog on the Nostr pattern: `extensions/x/src/i18n/{index.ts,locales.ts,locales/en.ts}`. The browser root is `src` because `openclaw.controlUi` points at `./src/control-ui.tsx`. **63 strings** moved into the catalog under the plugin-specific `xReplies.*` namespace, so no key collides with the shared core catalog.
- Translate the page, navigation label, and page label through `translateControlUiMessage`. The view tracks `host.locale` in its existing presentation store.
- Notices are now typed keys (`added`, `removed`, `guestsOn`, …) translated at render time instead of English strings held in state.
- Request failures are wrapped in a small `RequestFailure` that records which action failed. The alert now reads "Couldn’t {verb} {thing}. {Next step}." and the redacted server message follows inline as secondary text (`<small>`, muted). The plugin SDK host components (`ControlUiComponents`) on main have no shared "Show details" disclosure, so as the sweep brief directs, the raw detail stays visually secondary and inline.
- Copy that wraps inline elements (`<time>`, the repository link) uses a small `withSlots` helper. It splits the translated string at `{name}` placeholders, so translators control word order.
- `locales.ts` is English-only for now, and other locales fall back to English, which is today's behavior. `translated.json` isn't added, per the sweep brief. The Nostr-style lazy `translated.json` loader can't be wired until that file exists, because the bundler can't resolve a missing import.

### Notable copy changes

| Old | New |
| --- | --- |
| Choose whose mentions the bot can answer publicly. | Choose whose mentions the agent can answer publicly. |
| Administrator access is required to manage X replies. | You need admin access to manage X replies. |
| Bot account | Agent account |
| Applies to the selected bot account. Guests get repository answers with hidden helpers of the same agent. No writes, commands, visible work sessions, or other agents. Maintainers keep their normal access. | Applies to the selected agent account. Guests get repository answers from this agent and its hidden subagents. They can’t write, run commands, open visible sessions, or use other agents. Maintainers keep their normal access. |
| Per guest, per UTC day / `3 mentions` | Mentions per guest, per UTC day / `3` (no more "1 mentions") |
| Could not resolve on X: @a, @b. Check the declared profiles. | Couldn’t find @a, @b on X. Check the declared GitHub profiles. |
| No manual entries yet. Add a maintainer above or set `allowFrom` in config. | No manual entries yet. Add a maintainer above or in config. |
| *(raw server error)* / The request failed. Try again. | Couldn’t load X replies. Try again. · Couldn’t add this account. Check the handle and try again. · Couldn’t remove this entry. Try again. · Couldn’t change guest mode. Try again. *(the redacted server detail follows as secondary text)* |
| No successful sync yet.Entries update… *(missing space)* | No successful sync yet. Entries update… |

All other strings moved into the catalog with unchanged English. They were already in sentence case, used the single ellipsis character, and had no straight quotes.

### Out of scope / unchanged

- Server-generated text the page displays verbatim: the guest readiness `blockedReason` from `guests.ts`/`monitor.ts` and the GitHub sync `message` from `verified-github.ts`. That text also feeds channel status and the agent path, so it stays with its backend owners.
- Agent-facing and X-posted text (the guest policy prompt, tool text).
- Docs: `docs/channels/x.md` quotes **X replies**, **From GitHub**, **Guest mode**, and **Refresh**, and none of those labels changed.

## Impact

UI copy only. The plugin's operator RPCs (`x.allowlist.*`, `x.guests.set`), state, and authorization are unchanged. Foreign locales keep showing English until the post-merge locale refresh adds `translated.json` and the lazy loader is wired.

## Evidence

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/x/browser/control-ui.browser.test.tsx`: 4/4 passed. Assertions were updated for the new admin-required copy and for the error alert (`Couldn’t add this account. Check the handle and try again. Rejected [REDACTED]`), which still proves redaction.
- `pnpm ui:i18n:verify`: green (`plugin=x keys=63 locales=0`).
- `pnpm ui:i18n:check`: fails as expected with "missing verified translations" for all 22 locales of the new `x` catalog. That CI step is `continue-on-error`, and foreign parity is the post-merge `control-ui-locale-refresh` bot's job. No foreign files were hand-edited.
- `pnpm tsgo:extensions`, `pnpm tsgo:extensions:test`: pass.
- `node scripts/run-oxlint.mjs --tsconfig extensions/tsconfig.json extensions/x`: pass. The one warning is pre-existing, on an unchanged line.
- `pnpm check:control-ui-controllers`: pass, no ratchet changes.
- `scripts/build-plugin-control-ui.mts extensions/x`: bundle builds.
- `oxfmt`, `git diff --check`: clean.
- pr-simplify: the remaining machinery is the catalog and translator, one `RequestFailure` class (it carries which action failed to the error summary), and `withSlots` (it keeps inline elements inside translatable sentences). A planned slot was dropped once `allowFrom` left the copy.
- Local review: autoreview (Codex `gpt-6.1-sol`, medium), `--mode branch --base origin/main --max-priority P2`, on candidate `e48ff37`. Result: scoped-clean, no actionable P0–P2 findings. The final head differs only by removing the `allowFrom` slot from the empty-state string. Verify, test, lint, and typecheck were re-run on it.

**Not landing: requested by maintainer; screenshots pending before merge.** The visual gate requires before/after screenshots of the X replies page before this lands.

## Work sessions

- [Original discussion with @vyctorbrzezowski](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/dashboard/8ee302fc-4575-4506-92a8-1739453b9b71)
- [Implementation and verification](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/subagent/0bf8c201-1ee4-45d1-87f1-4556319f55ac)

prs.title: improve(workboard): apply the Control UI glossary and style to Workboard copy
prs.body:
## Problem

Workboard's Control UI copy didn't follow the approved Control UI glossary and style rules. It had straight apostrophes, a `...` placeholder, "could not" / "cannot" errors with no consistent form, "Board agent" capitalized mid-sentence, the British "Cancelled", and "board conversation" used for what is a session. Its errors also showed internal RPC text: `sessions.create returned no key` and `workboard response did not include a card`. About 19 user-visible English strings were still hard-coded in `extensions/workboard/browser/` instead of living in the plugin's translation source, so they could never be translated.

## Solution

- Rewrote the existing English in `browser/i18n/locales/en.ts` to follow the rules. Errors now read "Couldn’t {verb} {thing}. {Next step}." The copy uses contractions, curly apostrophes and the `…` character, sentence case, and **session** as the container noun.
- Moved the remaining hard-coded English in `browser/` (execution, loading, mutation and normalization errors; the stale-session fallback; the "Workboard is no longer active" message; widget registration labels; the board-kind suffix on duplicate sidebar names) into `en.ts` and called it through `t()`.
- `host.ts` calls `translateControlUiMessage` directly instead of `t()`, because `i18n/index.ts` imports `host.ts` and using `t()` there would create an import cycle.
- Two places that had the same stale-session fallback in different words (normalization and card alerts) now use one key.
- Updated `docs/plugins/workboard.md`, which quotes the sidebar suffix: **Planning (Cards)** / **Planning (Sessions)**.

Notable copy changes (old → new):

| Where | Old | New |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Page load failure | Workboard could not load. Check your connection and reload this page. | Couldn’t load Workboard. Check your connection and reload this page. |
| Delete without write access | Connect with write access to delete this board. | Couldn’t delete this board. Connect with write access and try again. |
| Bulk edit stopped | The operation stopped. Remaining cards are still selected; refresh and try again. | Couldn’t apply changes to every card. Remaining cards are still selected; refresh and try again. |
| Sessions board agent missing | The board conversation's agent is unavailable. Choose a configured agent or update the board's conversation. | Couldn’t open the board session. Its agent is unavailable; choose a configured agent or update the board’s session. |
| Sessions board create failed | The board conversation could not be created. Try again. | Couldn’t create the board session. Try again. |
| Rules help | The Board agent can edit column rules and session scope. | The board agent can edit column rules and session scope. |
| Note placeholder | Add a decision, blocker, or proof note... | Add a decision, blocker, or proof note… |
| Dispatch help | …this board's Ready cards… | …this board’s Ready cards… |
| Refresh status | Refresh failed | Couldn’t refresh |
| Session status | Cancelled | Canceled (American English, same as core approvals copy) |
| Widget card not loaded | This card is not loaded yet. | This card isn’t loaded yet. |
| Start, hard-coded | sessions.create returned no key | Couldn’t start a session for this card. Try again. |
| Card payload, hard-coded | workboard response did not include a card | Couldn’t read the updated card. Refresh the board and try again. |
| Gateway missing, hard-coded | Gateway client unavailable | Couldn’t refresh Workboard. Connect to the Gateway and try again. |
| Scheduled start, hard-coded | Scheduled cards cannot start before their scheduled time. | Couldn’t start this card. Scheduled cards can’t start before their scheduled time. |
| Already started, hard-coded | This card already has an execution. Refresh its details or use Edit to clear its session link before starting another. | Couldn’t start this card. It already has a linked session; refresh its details or use Edit to clear its session link. |
| Stop, hard-coded | Refresh this card's session details before stopping it, or use Edit to choose its session. | Couldn’t stop this card’s session. Refresh its session details, or use Edit to choose its session. |
| Changed card, hard-coded | This card changed. Refresh its details before starting or stopping it. | Couldn’t start or stop this card because it changed. Refresh its details and try again. |
| Stale fallback, hard-coded (×2) | Session has not reported… / Linked session has not reported recent activity. | Linked session hasn’t reported recent activity. |
| Inactive plugin, hard-coded | Workboard is no longer active. Reload the plugin to continue. | Workboard is no longer active. Reload this page to continue. |
| Unknown error, hard-coded | Unknown workboard error. | Unknown Workboard error. Refresh and try again. |
| Sidebar duplicate name | Planning (cards) | Planning (Cards) |

String count: 12 existing English values rewritten. 19 hard-coded literals moved into translation calls: 14 go to new `en.ts` keys and the rest reuse 3 existing keys (`widget.boardLabel`, `cardsBoard`, `sessionsBoard.kind`). No foreign locale, `translated.json`, `.i18n/*.tm.jsonl` or `*.meta.json` file was edited. The post-merge locale-refresh bot owns parity.

Raw Gateway error text still shows inline in the existing Workboard error toast. Workboard has no shared "Show details" disclosure on `main`, and the copy written here no longer includes internal names.

## Impact

Only copy and translation sources change; behavior doesn't. Two edge cases are accepted:
- Widget registration labels and the stale-reason fallback are resolved when they're created. A locale switch picks them up after the next refresh or reload; before this change they were always English.
- The session label `buildCardSessionLabel` writes for new card sessions, and agent-facing template drafts, stay as they are. They're stored data or model-facing text, not Control UI copy.

prs.title: fix(proxy): reject FIFO and oversized CA bundles without hanging
prs.body:
> **AI-assisted: yes**

Related: #110032

## What Problem This Solves

- Fixes a problem where `openclaw proxy validate --proxy-ca-file <path>` (and the matching `tools.proxy.tls.caFile` config / `OPENCLAW_PROXY_CA_FILE` override) hangs forever when the configured CA bundle path points to a FIFO or another special file: the loader opened the path with a plain `readFile`, which waits for a writer that never comes, so proxy startup and validation stall without any message.
- Also fixes the unbounded side of the same read: an oversized (or garbage) bundle file was read fully into memory with no ceiling, and its content was then used as TLS trust material, surfacing later as an unrelated "fetch failed" in proxy checks instead of a clear configuration error.

**Related:** None (no issue; this revives the stalled hardening direction from #110032 with the requested real-behavior proof, the async reader for the async loader, and an explicitly justified bundle ceiling).

## Why This Change Was Made

- **Intended outcome:** CA bundle loading goes through the shared bounded secret-file readers, imported directly from `@openclaw/fs-safe/secret` (which owns both implementations), so the module keeps a dependency-package import closure and refuses non-regular files with the reader's existing message while bounding the read at an explicit ceiling. The async startup loader uses the reader's async form; the inherited child-process routing loader keeps its synchronous form. No new helper, no global behavior change.
- **Out of scope:** No proxy URL handling, TLS agent, or validation-logic changes. No schema, defaults, dependencies, or migration changes.
- **Bundle ceiling rationale:** 4 MiB covers every realistic trust bundle with wide headroom — a single root CA PEM is ~2 KiB and this machine's full system trust bundle (~130 certificates) measures 210,565 bytes (~206 KiB), so 4 MiB admits well over 2000 root certificates, more than any known OS or enterprise trust store, while still rejecting pathological inputs. An earlier 256 KiB revision of this PR could have rejected previously working large enterprise bundles; 4 MiB removes that compatibility risk (verified below with a 421 KB bundle built from a real system trust store).
- **Highest-risk area / mitigation:** a caller that depended on a trailing newline in the bundle content — TLS consumers trim/normalize PEM themselves, and the reader trims content, so trust material is unchanged.

## User Impact

- **Success criteria:** pointing `--proxy-ca-file` (or `tools.proxy.tls.caFile` / `OPENCLAW_PROXY_CA_FILE`) at a FIFO, a symlinked FIFO, a device file, or a bundle over 4 MiB now fails within seconds with "proxy CA file could not be read (...): Managed proxy CA file at ... must be a regular file." / "... exceeds 4194304 bytes."; a normal bundle (including a symlinked one, and enterprise-scale multi-root bundles far above a single system store) still validates exactly as before.
- **What should reviewers focus on:** `src/infra/net/proxy/proxy-tls.ts` (two loader functions routed to the `@openclaw/fs-safe/secret` readers) and `src/infra/net/proxy/proxy-tls.test.ts` (regular/symlink/FIFO/oversized/empty/system-trust-scale coverage for both loaders).

## Evidence

- **Real environment tested:** built Linux CLI from both refs (shipped entry point `node openclaw.mjs`), each running `openclaw proxy validate` against a real local HTTPS forward proxy (TLS listener, CONNECT) whose endpoint certificate is signed by the evidence CA — trust for the proxy endpoint is only possible through `--proxy-ca-file`. Head build provenance: the head dist was built at `572f9d4b` (same runtime `proxy-tls.ts` as pushed head `4aac95613a5`; the only later change is inside the test file) on 2026-11-07; base build is main @ `a6ee6a18a5d`.
- **Exact steps or commands run after this patch:**
  ```bash
  # fixtures: evidence CA + 127.0.0.1 server cert (openssl), mkfifo ca.pipe,
  # 4194305-byte (4 MiB + 1) bundle, and a 421 KB enterprise-scale bundle
  # (2x this machine's real 210 KB system trust bundle + the evidence CA)
  node https-connect-proxy.mjs server.pem server-key.pem 18443   # real HTTPS CONNECT proxy
  HOME=<isolated> timeout 15 node openclaw.mjs proxy validate \
    --proxy-url https://127.0.0.1:18443 \
    --proxy-ca-file <ca.pem|ca.pipe|oversized.pem|enterprise-scale.pem> \
    --allowed-url https://<internal-registry-reachable-from-this-network>/
  ```
- **Evidence after fix:** same four commands, base vs head (full logs: base run and head run captured 2026-11-07, exit codes and timings as printed by the CLI wrapper):
  ```text
  | Case                          | main @ a6ee6a18a5d                    | head @ 4aac95613a5                         |
  |-------------------------------|---------------------------------------|--------------------------------------------|
  | normal CA bundle              | exit 0 in 5.2s, "Proxy validation passed" | exit 0 in 5.6s, "Proxy validation passed" |
  | FIFO                          | exit 124: hung 17s, killed by timeout | exit 1 in 2.7s: "Managed proxy CA file at ... must be a regular file." |
  | oversized 4 MiB + 1           | exit 1: bundle accepted unbounded, then "✗ allowed ... — fetch failed" | exit 1 in 2.9s: "Managed proxy CA file at ... exceeds 4194304 bytes." |
  | enterprise-scale 421 KB bundle| exit 0 in 3.3s, "Proxy validation passed" | exit 0 in 3.5s, "Proxy validation passed" |
  ```
- **Observed result after fix:** normal trust and the proxy deny canary behave identically on both refs (allowed destination HTTP 200 through the proxy, loopback canary blocked at the connection level); the FIFO and oversized cases go from a hang / silent trust failure to a sub-3-second exit 1 with an actionable message; a real-system-trust-scale bundle (421 KB, above the previous 256 KiB revision's ceiling) validates identically on base and head, so existing large deployments keep working.
- **Upgrade run with an existing configured bundle (data-model compatibility):** an existing deployment was simulated end-to-end through the config path (no CLI flags): an isolated `HOME/.openclaw/openclaw.json` stores `proxy.enabled: true`, `proxy.proxyUrl: https://127.0.0.1:18446`, and `proxy.tls.caFile` pointing at the 421 KB enterprise-scale bundle. Pre-upgrade, the base build (main @ `a6ee6a18a5d`) validates that stored config: exit 0 in 8.1s, "Proxy validation passed", `Source: config`, allowed destination HTTP 200 through the real HTTPS CONNECT proxy, loopback deny canary blocked. Post-upgrade, the head build runs against the **same untouched HOME/config/bundle** (sha256 of both `openclaw.json` and `configured-bundle.pem` verified identical before and after: `e4a32fb9…` / `388752b9…`): exit 0 in 4.8s, "Proxy validation passed", `Source: config`, same allow/deny results. The stored-config upgrade path therefore preserves an existing configured CA bundle — the same validation the CLI-flag runs show, exercised through the persisted config a real user would have.
- **Stable-release upgrade run (v2026.11.2 → head, the requested latest-stable-to-head gate):** the same existing-deployment simulation repeated with the pre-upgrade side running the published latest stable release `openclaw@2026.11.2` (npm-installed package, shipped entry point `node openclaw.mjs`, package lifecycle scripts enabled) instead of main. An isolated `HOME/.openclaw/openclaw.json` stores `proxy.enabled: true`, `proxy.proxyUrl: https://127.0.0.1:18447`, and `proxy.tls.caFile` pointing at the same 421 KB enterprise-scale bundle. Pre-upgrade, v2026.11.2 validates that stored config: exit 0 in 4.0s, "Proxy validation passed", `Source: config`, allowed destination HTTP 200 through the real HTTPS CONNECT proxy, loopback deny canary blocked. Post-upgrade, the head build (`4aac95613a5` runtime) runs against the **same untouched HOME/config/bundle** (sha256 of both `openclaw.json` and `configured-bundle.pem` verified identical before and after: `82151603…` / `388752b9…`): exit 0 in 3.7s, "Proxy validation passed", `Source: config`, same allow/deny results. A user upgrading from the latest stable release therefore keeps a working configured CA bundle.
- **Before evidence:** on main @ `a6ee6a18a5d` the FIFO run produced no output for 17 seconds and was killed by `timeout` (exit 124, "Command interrupted by SIGTERM"); the oversized run loaded the whole 4 MiB+1 bundle and only failed later as "✗ allowed ... — fetch failed" in the allowed-destination check.
- **Chain:** `openclaw proxy validate` → `runProxyValidation` → `loadManagedProxyTlsOptions`/`loadManagedProxyTlsOptionsSync` → `readSecretFile`/`readSecretFileSync` from `@openclaw/fs-safe/secret` (regular-file admission + 4 MiB bound).
- **Readback:** the CLI's own validation output above (exit codes, stdout/stderr messages, per-check results) — no mock or in-process harness.
- **Control:** allowed destination returns HTTP 200 only when the proxy endpoint certificate verifies against the provided CA bundle; the loopback deny canary is verified blocked (connection-level destroy) — a wrong or garbage bundle cannot pass these checks (base's oversized run shows exactly that).
- **Other callers checked:** both loaders (`loadManagedProxyTlsOptions`, `loadManagedProxyTlsOptionsSync`) are the single choke point for `--proxy-ca-file`, `tools.proxy.tls.caFile`, and `OPENCLAW_PROXY_CA_FILE`; all three inputs resolve through `resolveManagedProxyCaFileForUrl` into these two functions, and their callers (`proxy-validation.ts`, `proxy-lifecycle.ts`, `active-managed-proxy-tls.ts`) already wrap loader failures into their existing error paths.
- **Tests:** `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run src/infra/net/proxy/proxy-tls.test.ts` — 12 passed (exit 0), including a system-trust-scale multi-root bundle (~130 roots, >200 KB) that must keep loading. RED on main for the defect assertions (empty bundle resolves, oversized async/sync resolve, FIFO async times out, FIFO sync child killed by its hard timeout), GREEN on head for all 12. No test retry settings, timeouts, assertion coverage or baselines were relaxed.
- **What was not tested:** Windows/macOS (the FIFO cases are Linux `mkfifo`; regular/symlink/oversized coverage is platform-independent and the CI matrix covers the rest). No schema, defaults, dependencies, or migration changes.
- **Proof tier:** L2+
- **Proof limitations:** none
- **Review state:** addresses the ClawSweeper P2 finding (readers now imported directly from `@openclaw/fs-safe/secret`, keeping the extracted wrapper's import closure — the wrapper-closure check `checks-node-compact-small-2` passed on the previous push of this import fix), the bundle-ceiling compatibility concern (ceiling raised 256 KiB → 4 MiB with the enterprise-scale real-behavior run above), and the requested data-model compatibility proofs (upgrade runs with an existing stored config from both main @ `a6ee6a18a5d` and the latest stable release v2026.11.2, above). All CI checks are green on head `4aac95613a5` — including `check-lint-core-3` (the earlier failure was fixed in the test file) and the `checks-node-compact-small` wrapper lane with the direct `@openclaw/fs-safe/secret` import. Awaiting re-review of the v2026.11.2 stable-release upgrade run.

prs.title: feat: let clients load agent rosters without portraits
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Large inline portraits can dominate `agents.list` responses and delay mobile clients that need the agent roster before opening a conversation.

## User Impact

Clients can request a fresh authorized roster without downloading portraits by sending `includeAvatars: false`. Existing clients keep the same response when they omit the option or pass `true`.

This is opt-in: clients must request the lightweight roster. It does not change portrait caching policy, authorization, or the default avatar representation, and it has not been deployed.

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing roster projection now skips avatar resolution and omits `identity.avatar` and `identity.avatarUrl` on explicit opt-out. Names, emoji, theme, routing and model metadata remain intact. This removes image work from roster bootstrap without introducing a server cache or a second roster endpoint.

The schema, generated validator, and protocol documentation are updated. Older gateways can reject the new parameter; clients may retry the legacy request only for that parameter-validation error.

## Evidence

- Five new regression cases exercise the real RPC handler, validator, authorization, and roster projection for local, inline-data and remote portraits, plus Control UI HTTP avatar representations. They fail against the base with `INVALID_REQUEST` and pass with this change.
- Lightweight requests make zero avatar-resolver calls, omit both image fields, and preserve the rest of the authorized roster. Legacy and explicit-true responses match. A synthetic 32 KiB local image loses its image payload from the serialized response.
- 14 focused tests pass: five new roster cases, five existing roster authorization cases, and four existing avatar cases.
- Targeted TypeScript checking, lint, formatting, and `git diff --check` pass.
- Protocol schema generation, Swift/Kotlin native protocol generation, and generated validator freshness checks pass.
- Local canonical autoreview (Codex, P0–P2) completed on the full working-tree change against `6bd45e1ba9820b30300db404037bc5aa76648c02`, with the affected production owners supplied as source context: scoped-clean, no actionable findings. Review was static; it did not execute project code.

Not verified: end-to-end mobile latency or live gateway deployment. The tests establish work and payload removal, not a measured network speedup.

### Running-Gateway transport and latest-stable compatibility proof

Verified on reviewed head `0329434db09ac58286eca3ddf400f39addcf563e` using isolated synthetic state and real authenticated loopback WebSocket connections. Started the official latest-stable `openclaw@2026.10.8` package (`dc2523e5a5c7a309517fd7fa834add938231d526`), captured legacy requests, stopped it, ran the reviewed runtime's ordinary backed-up `doctor --fix --yes --non-interactive` migration, and started the reviewed Gateway against the same state.

- Configured valid local PNG, inline data-URI, and public-placeholder remote portraits.
- Stable `{}` response: 200,220-byte payload. Stable rejects the new option with `INVALID_REQUEST: unexpected property 'includeAvatars'`.
- After upgrade, `{}` is deep-equal to the entire stable legacy payload. `{includeAvatars:true}` is also deep-equal to `{}`.
- `{includeAvatars:false}` returns 2,517 bytes, deep-equal to the legacy payload with only `identity.avatar` and `identity.avatarUrl` removed from each agent. All non-portrait fields are preserved.
- Both fixture Gateways shut down cleanly. No production service/configuration was changed. This proves payload/transport behavior, not mobile/Tailscale latency or the package-updater installer. No model credentials/calls were needed; unrelated plugin/browser/model Doctor health gaps in the disabled-integration fixture are not claimed as passing.

[Full redacted request/response excerpts and commands](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/186812#issuecomment-6474332805). No code change was needed for this feedback. Upstream maintainer acceptance of the optional public RPC projection remains outstanding; this evidence is not owner approval.
