prs.title: feat(node): enroll with owner-approved OpenClaw ID invitations
prs.body:
Related: #193982 (node transport, merged), #194001 (Gateway node admission, merged), #194007 (Access node invites, merged), #195507 (one automatic node pairing per approved listing, merged; found by this PR's live proof)

## What Problem This Solves

Headless nodes need an owner-approved way to join an OpenClaw ID claw without a user account or a Gateway token.

## User Impact

Adds `openclaw node join <openclaw-node-link>` and sends the same link through `openclaw connect`. The node shows a six-digit code and its signed command list. The owner compares the code and approves on the Access page. After approval, the node checks that it was admitted, then connects in the foreground, or installs a user service with `--service`.

- **Discovery origin.** Set it with `--discovery-url` or reuse the one saved with the node's target; there is no production default. The origin is never derived from the claw hostname or relay URL.
- **Re-joining.** `node join` now refuses a node that is still admitted, and leaves the new invitation unused. To change a node's commands, the owner removes it on the Access page and sends a new link. Plain reconnects use `openclaw node run` or the installed service.
- **Supervision.** A foreground `node join` now runs under the packaged node supervisor, the same as `connect`. Supervisor restarts use `node run`, never the one-time link.
- **Labs preview limits.** Unix hosts and native-process workers only. Node is the qualified runtime; Bun streaming qualification is still pending.

## Why This Change Was Made

The node signs the command manifest it actually prepared, with its own local key, and Discovery only ever sees the redemption proof. Before the runner saves the target, the node checks the root, claw and hostname pins, the highest same-claw binding sequence it has seen, signed snapshot freshness, and its own listing. The first connection reuses that prepared runtime. The service is installed only after a successful first hello and a clean shutdown.

**ClawSweeper's re-enrollment finding (P2).** A membership snapshot lists node keys only; it says nothing about which invitation or description the owner approved. A node that is already admitted would therefore look approved before the owner had decided on the new invitation. The node now checks Discovery before mailing the redemption, and refuses if it is already listed. It doesn't wait on the new invitation, and it doesn't spend it.

**Accepted edge (named in code).** Suppose an earlier invitation for the same node key is still pending and the owner approves it later. That approval can also complete a newer join that is waiting. Binding completion to one specific invitation needs a signed per-invitation outcome, which doesn't exist yet and is tracked as openclaw-607; this PR adds no protocol statement. The Gateway pairs only the commands from the description the owner approved (`approveOpenClawIdNodePairing`), so this edge can't widen what the node may run. A Discovery that lies about pending state can, at most, cause the same mismatch; it can't grant access.

**Authority at admission and execution.** Gateway #194001 owns this. Admission resolves the tunnel peer against the Gateway's current authority, not Discovery's snapshot. `resolveGatewayConnectPolicyFailure` and request dispatch then re-check `isOpenClawIdTunnelPrincipalCurrent` before any work runs. A new real-Gateway test covers both cases. A node key the Gateway doesn't list (pending, or removed after the node fetched its descriptor) is refused before pairing. A live node session is closed with code 4001 on its next request once its listing is removed. Existing coverage includes `authority.nodes.test.ts`, where pending nodes don't resolve and removal closes connections, and the pairing suite's stale-principal case.

**Stored data.** This PR adds no new store, field or migration. Node config stays in SQLite `nodeHost.config` v1, as in 2026.11.2. The `openclaw-id` target shape already shipped in #193982. Existing Gateway-mode targets keep loading unchanged; only an explicit `node join` replaces the saved target. See Evidence for the upgrade check.

**Test lines.** The allocation is 542, exactly this PR's net test-line delta. Against current main the ratchet reports 32 lines of slack; that headroom was already on main and isn't allocated by this PR.

## Evidence

- **Re-enrollment regression.** `refuses re-enrollment while old membership still lists W, before spending the invite` is red against the previous enrollment source and green with the fix.
- **Focused suites.** 172 passed, 7 native-binding tests skipped, across enrollment, join, runner, connect/register CLI, node daemon, the Gateway node-pairing suite and the native node-host suite. The node launcher suite passed 15/15, including the new `["node","join"]` supervised-restart case.
- **Static checks.** `pnpm tsgo:core`, scoped oxlint and oxfmt, and `pnpm deadcode:exports` all passed with 0 entries. `loadNodeTunnelKey` is exported again because `openclaw-id-join.ts` uses it; #195338 had made it private. The mock-isolation ratchet passes; each orchestration mock in the join suite states why it is isolated.
- **Independent Astra review.** It found two P2s. The supervisor bypass is fixed. The pending-earlier-invitation edge is accepted as described above, pending openclaw-607. Neither finding bypasses Gateway enforcement.
- **Stored-data upgrade (isolated profiles, env cleared of live-Gateway variables).** 2026.10.10 configured a node host in plain Gateway mode against an isolated 2026.11.2 Gateway: it saved SQLite `nodeHost.config` v1 and paired. The PR head's `node run` with no flags then loaded that config and connected with the existing pairing (0 pending requests). The config bytes were unchanged (same hash). A failed `node join` (Discovery unreachable) left the config unchanged apart from creating the node's 0600 endpoint key, and `node run` connected again afterwards. Note: main is versioned 2026.11.1, so a 2026.11.2 → PR head run is a version downgrade and stops at the newer-config check; that is why the upgrade was seeded from 2026.10.10.
- **Exact-head CI on `7cf477a8e9e5`:** 73 passed, 52 skipped, 0 failed. Current head `eac8b7f06c2f`: CI is running.
- **Follow-up `eac8b7f` (ClawSweeper P3, after the live run):** failed descriptor or membership verification now names a recovery step. A stale membership snapshot asks the operator to have the claw owner check that the Gateway is online and connected to OpenClaw ID, then join with a new link; an invalid descriptor asks them to check `--discovery-url` with the owner. Only error strings and the stale-snapshot test assertion changed; enrollment logic didn't. The live proof below ran on `7cf477a`, and the enrollment, join and connect suites pass 46/46 at `eac8b7f`.
- **Rebase onto main (with #195507):** `git range-diff ac26a0d7f1f8..70d8109b8a56 origin/main..7cf477a8e9e5` shows all 4 commits unchanged (`=`).

### Live proof on the staging testnet (build `7cf477a`, this PR's head)

**Setup:**
- **Gateway:** an isolated Gateway on a Mac Studio, built from `7cf477a8e9e5` with its own profile, port and state, and linked as the throwaway staging claw `ocid517proof2-e61zr.crabd.xyz`. The Studio's own Gateway wasn't touched.
- **Owner:** used real Chromium against the real staging OpenClaw ID, Discovery, loader and relay. They signed in, enrolled with the recovery kit, and opened **Access** over the tunnel. This Gateway has no model configured, so the default landing goes to model setup; the harness opens the app with `?session=main`. Node admission doesn't depend on this.
- **Nodes:** ran this PR's shipped CLI on a Linux host, each in an isolated profile, with environment variables from the host's own Gateway cleared.

All 9 checks passed in one run:

| # | Check | Result |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Owner signs in and opens **Access**, then **Nodes**, over the tunnel | pass |
| 2 | Denied invite | Codes matched (`794-600`) and the owner selected **Deny node**. The invite reads `denied` and no node is listed. The waiting node never connected and, when cancelled, reported "no target was saved". |
| 3 | Approved invite | Codes matched (`865-003`) and the owner approved. The Gateway logged `admission allowed … path=relay` and then repeated admissions with `path=direct`. The node reported `connected … via OpenClaw ID (direct)`, and its device was auto-paired as `openclaw-id-node`. |
| 4 | A node command runs | `node.invoke system.which` over the tunnel returned `{"bins":{"sh":"/usr/bin/sh"}}` |
| 5 | Re-enrolling the admitted node with a fresh invite and more commands | Refused (exit 1) with "This node is already admitted … ask the owner to remove it on the Access page, then join with a new link". The fresh invite stays `open`, unused. |
| 6 | A pending node (code shown, not approved), given the admitted node's saved target | Never connected. For 90 seconds it got only `socket hang up` / 1006. The Gateway logged no admission for its key: it was refused at relay/tunnel admission, before any Gateway stream. |
| 7 | Owner removes a live node after it has retrieved its descriptor | The live session ended: the node exited 1 with "OpenClaw ID node access was removed or is not admitted; re-join this node". Restarting `node run` from the saved target never connected (`socket hang up`), and the Gateway logged no admission for that key between removal and the new approval. |
| 8 | Re-joining after removal with a new invite and more commands (`system.which,system.run`) | The node waited and connected only after the owner compared the code (`061-592`) and approved. The Gateway then auto-paired the same device (`approvedVia: openclaw-id-node`, 0 pending Devices approvals). `node.list` shows `system.run` and `system.which`. `system.which` worked, and `system.run echo` returned exit 0 with `stdout: "ocid517-ok"`. |
| 9 | `--service` | Approved (code `379-356`). The join installed the isolated user unit `openclaw-node-ocid517svc.service`, which became `active`. After `systemctl --user restart`, the journal shows a new `node host gateway connected … (direct)` and `node.list` shows the node connected again. |

**Path:** every node was admitted over the relay first and then moved to a direct path, according to both the node diagnostics and the Gateway's tunnel log.

**Before #195507:** an earlier run on build `70d8109`, against a claw since retired, passed steps 1–7. Step 8 then failed: after removal and a new approval, the Gateway answered `device pairing required` and left a non-repair pending node request. #195507 fixed that in the Gateway; step 8 above is the after.

**Cleanup:**
- The service unit is uninstalled, and the user unit list matches the list recorded before the run.
- The local node profiles and secrets are removed.
- The claw is retired in Discovery staging; queries show 0 claw, member and relay-key rows.
- The isolated Gateway is stopped. Its profile was backed up, then removed.
- The staging lock was taken for the run and released afterwards.

**Remaining limits:**
- The proof used Linux nodes with Node as the runtime. macOS, Windows and Bun weren't exercised (see the Labs preview limits above).
- Steps 6 and 7 show refusal at relay/tunnel admission. The Gateway's own refusal of unlisted and removed keys is covered by the real-Gateway test in this PR.

prs.title: fix(gateway): scope image capability discovery
prs.body:
## Summary

- scope attachment image-capability fallback to the selected provider instead of rebuilding every provider catalog
- keep runtime-only models by using the existing request-scoped live catalog path
- retry the complete Gateway projection when its published runtime owner is replaced during scoped discovery

## Root cause and owner

Attachment admission first reads the lifecycle-published catalog. When a selected runtime-only model is absent or has provisional text-only metadata, current main falls back to `readOnly: false`, which rebuilds the full cross-provider catalog inside the request. The provider-scoped catalog machinery exists, but this Gateway caller did not use it.

The canonical owner is the Gateway catalog projection. The second read now carries the selected provider into the existing prepared request-scoped live catalog. The projection checks the published owner before and after the asynchronous scoped read and reacquires the full owner on replacement, so catalog, config, agent identity, and auth projection never mix generations.

## ClawSweeper findings

- Early owner replacement: fixed by retrying at the Gateway projection boundary; the regression replaces the owner during scoped discovery and proves only the replacement catalog returns.
- Final provider I/O fence: the old branch tried to turn generation liveness into a public provider-auth revocation contract, but that was incomplete and added a large cross-plugin surface. This port removes that contract. Published-generation liveness governs whether results may publish; it does not retroactively revoke already-started provider requests. Results from a retired generation are discarded and the owner is reacquired.
- Runtime-only models: retained. An independent P1 review caught and rejected an intermediate static-only rewrite; the final branch uses the existing scoped live mode.
- Test-cost evidence: recorded below for the new image-capability file and the combined focused Gateway set.

## Scope

Seven Gateway files changed against integrated main: 222 insertions and 60 deletions. Reuses the existing scoped catalog owner; no provider/plugin implementation changes, new configuration, or cache.

## Validation

- Integrated main: `1f01f4944d45eb265081f8bfbf8d3e8e54ff4266`; resolved conflicts while retaining current static-capability and projection owners.
- Three focused Gateway suites: 86 tests passed (image capability, catalog projection, session utilities).
- Core production typecheck and targeted lint passed; `git diff --check` clean.
- Fresh autoreview against integrated main, P0–P2: no actionable findings in the seven-file candidate diff. Surrounding loader implementations were not included in the isolated reviewer bundle; integration assurance also relies on focused tests and source inspection.
- Previous validation counts and hosted evidence were for the old head and are not current-head proof.
- No new real-channel/live-provider proof was run.
- CI follow-up: the new catalog mock now accepts the loader's optional argument. The affected Gateway-server test-type leaf passed; 16 catalog tests passed. Current head: `8a7567d2df5d`. Replacement exact-head CI is pending, not claimed green.

prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Resolves a problem where maintainers cannot refresh secret-backed native translations for review without also creating and arming an auto-merge generated PR.

## Why This Change Was Made

Adds an explicit non-publishing dispatch mode that runs the existing bounded locale matrix and validation, then uploads an allowlisted binary patch artifact. The default publishing path remains unchanged.

Secret-backed non-publishing runs execute only from the trusted `main` workflow. The operator supplies an exact source SHA; that SHA must be the current head of one open, non-draft PR targeting `main` with GitHub's current review decision `APPROVED`. Each locale worker revalidates the exact PR head and current approval immediately before the translation-secret step. Branch-selected preflight support was removed: guards inside branch-controlled YAML cannot independently guarantee secret isolation. Manual runs use the trusted main workflow definition.

## User Impact

No direct user-facing change. Maintainers gain a review-only native translation refresh path that cannot push, open a PR, or enable auto-merge, while non-publishing source selection requires current exact-head review approval.

## Evidence

### November 2 review-readiness repair

- Removed the branch-selected preflight mode and restored the main-only dispatch contract, addressing the P1 workflow-boundary finding without adding another execution path.
- Focused workflow contract regression: fails on the previous head at the branch-admission condition; passes after the repair (1 test, 4.97s runner wall).
- Workflow validation passed, including pinned tooling fallback and zizmor.
- Changed-surface checks passed: formatting, root-test typechecks, dependency/coercion/dead-export guards, and script/test lint. `git diff --check` passed.
- Repair delta: 12 insertions / 37 deletions across workflow and guard test; removed the separate preflight input, scheduling branch, and branch-dispatch route.
- Local autoreview of this repair against `7bf16b8fd47f07612777b4957b1a14bbc66eba42`: scoped-clean at P0–P2; no actionable findings.
- Remaining integration proof: no new credentialed translation run was dispatched. The earlier hosted translation/artifact run predates the current approval checks, so it does not prove approved and revoked-source behavior for this head. That remains an explicit pre-merge validation gap.

### CI integration repair

- Integrated main `1f01f4944d45` to resolve a concrete CI failure: the new non-publishing upload step retained an old action pin while main's canonical workflow helper required the updated pin.
- Both upload steps now use main's existing upload-artifact v7.0.2 pin; the dispatch/security repair is unchanged.
- Focused workflow regression: 1 passed on the integrated candidate. Full workflow validation, including zizmor, passed. `git diff --check` passed.
- Current head: `ae494551c445`; replacement exact-head CI is pending. Prior failed run is not claimed passing.

### Earlier branch evidence (not current-head proof)

prs.body:
Related: #142663

## What Problem This Solves

`/tools verbose` advertises automation creation during management-only turns, even though execution rejects `add`. Inventory construction has no run ID, so deriving its description and schema from an exact-run execution grant incorrectly falls back to the unrestricted surface.

## User Impact

Discovery inside an admitted management-only turn no longer advertises creation. Fresh remote administrator turns retain creation through the existing `callerScopedCreation` distinction. Execution authorization is unchanged.

This fixes the discovery mismatch only; the reported Telegram creation rejection is not claimed fixed.

## Why This Change Was Made

- `resolveCronToolManagementMode` reads admitted scope, deployment policy, liveness, and any supplied run ID without requiring an execution grant.
- `bindCronManagementGrant` reuses that classification while retaining its exact-run, live caller authority and operational-instance checks.
- Automation descriptions, schemas, and compact summaries use the admitted mode. Summary wording stays in the existing description-presets owner, keeping `cron-tool.ts` within its line limit.
- Discovery outside an admitted turn still describes the configuration surface, not per-turn execution authority.

## CI Repair

Rebased onto upstream `24e758688a6db34e1f9079f65faff3269bf15978`, which contains [#181647](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/181647), `05d779c0c931c8c0bbccf9cce93a47fbb54e6ef9`. That upstream repair distinguishes the admitted restart source ID from the interrupted execution run ID, addressing the three failures previously reproduced on CI's upstream base without this PR.

Removed this PR's duplicate exact action-enum assertion, which had become stale when upstream added `bind`. The real command-handler regression remains; existing schema and authority tests protect permitted actions and the creation boundary. No upstream assertions, skips, retries, or approval gates were changed by this PR.

## Evidence

- Real command-handler regression covers `/tools verbose` in an admitted management-only scope. Authority coverage distinguishes discovery from execution grants and preserves fresh remote creation.
- 128 focused tests passed using repository-pinned Bun `1.4.4-canary.1+807211511`: 20 restart-continuation cases plus 108 authority, tool, inventory, and prefix-stability cases across the six affected suites.
- [New-head native CI passed](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40344290316), including `checks-node-changed-5` and the native `openclaw/ci-gate`. The final rollup had 66 passing checks and none pending; only the maintainer-approval commit statuses remain red.
- Standalone command smoke outside Vitest, with isolated state and synthetic admitted scopes: management-only output omits `add job`; fresh remote creation output includes it. This is command-boundary proof, not a live Gateway/model session.
- Targeted production and touched-test typechecks, lint, formatting, and whitespace checks.
- Fresh independent review was attempted, but both reviewer processes failed at service capacity; no fresh review verdict is claimed. The authority implementation is unchanged from the previously reviewed patch. This update rebases that patch, removes the duplicate enum assertion, and relocates the unchanged summary expression.

The security-sensitive guard still requires current-head approval from a maintainer with `maintain` or `admin` access. A previous-head approval would not carry over after this rebase.

prs.title: fix(browser): omit unparsable gateway hint from extension pairing
prs.body:
Closes #186454

## What Problem This Solves

A browser node whose relay is local but whose Gateway is remote receives a pairing string the shipped Chrome extension always rejects, so setup ends at "Manual setup required (malformed_response)".
- Problem: for `gateway.mode: "remote"` over plaintext `ws://`, the pairing builder copied the remote Gateway URL into the optional `gateway` hint even though the extension accepts only `wss://` or loopback `ws://` hints. `parseGatewayHint` returned null, so `validatePairingFields` rejected a pairing whose relay URL and token were valid.
- Solution: publish the optional hint only when the extension can parse it. The relay URL, token, and relay validation are unchanged.
- What changed: one shared URL predicate in `extensions/browser/src/browser/extension-pairing.ts` now drives both relay-URL validation and hint emission; a regression test covers the plaintext remote case in `extension-pairing.test.ts`.
- What did NOT change: the extension's URL policy, relay transport validation, `wss://` hint behavior, and `--gateway-url` validation errors.

## Why This Change Was Made

The producer emitted optional metadata its only consumer is guaranteed to reject; fixing the producer keeps the plaintext-connection restriction intact.
- Best fix: omit unusable optional hints at the producer instead of relaxing the extension's URL policy (a plaintext non-loopback Gateway is still refused).
- Alternative: make the extension tolerate the hint — rejected because the hint carries no authority and widening that check increases risk for every pairing.
- Risk / non-goals: only the unusable-hint case changes; local loopback hints and `wss://` remote hints keep their current bytes.

## User Impact

`openclaw browser extension pair` and the native macOS bootstrap now hand the installed extension a pairing it accepts when the browser node uses a local relay in front of a plaintext remote Gateway, instead of requiring manual setup.

## Evidence

End-to-end on this branch: the shipped CLI produced the pairing string, the installed unpacked extension (Google Chrome 138, MV3 service worker) accepted it, and the extension authenticated to the real loopback relay daemon.

```text
$ openclaw browser extension pair --json          # this branch
{"pairingString":"ws://127.0.0.1:19199/extension#<token>","relayPort":19199,"remote":false}

Chrome 138 + unpacked extension, relay daemon on 127.0.0.1:19199:
[1] pre-fix CLI pairing (…?gateway=ws%3A%2F%2F192.168.1.20%3A8080…)
    extension parse : null
    pair message    : {"ok":false,"error":"Invalid pairing string."}
[2] fixed CLI pairing (…/extension#<token>)
    extension parse : {"relayUrl":"ws://127.0.0.1:19199/extension","token":"<token>"}
    pair message    : {"ok":true}
    relay daemon    : [browser/extension-relay] extension authenticated and connected to relay
    status          : {"paired":true,"state":"on","relayUrl":"ws://127.0.0.1:19199/extension"}
```

| Case | Before | After |
| --- | --- | --- |
| browser-node + plaintext `ws://192.168.1.20:8080` | hint emitted, parser returns null, extension rejects | hint omitted, extension pairs and connects |
| browser-node + `wss://gateway.example.com:9444` | parser accepts | parser accepts (unchanged) |
| direct-remote `wss://…:9443` | parser accepts | parser accepts (unchanged) |

The new regression test is red on `origin/main` and green with the fix; the relay integration test still passes:

```text
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/browser/src/browser/extension-pairing.test.ts --run
 ✓ omits a plaintext non-loopback gateway hint that the extension cannot parse
 Test Files  1 passed (1) · Tests  5 passed (5)

$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/browser/src/browser/extension-relay/gateway-relay-route.integration.test.ts --run
 Test Files  1 passed (1) · Tests  9 passed (9)
```

What was not tested: native-host registration and the macOS app bootstrap were not exercised (no macOS host); the CLI entry point, the installed extension, and the standalone relay daemon covered that path instead.

## AI Assistance

This PR is AI-assisted. Used source reading plus `node --import tsx` and a headless Google Chrome run to trace the pairing builder into the shipped extension and the live relay. The implementer understands the code: the extension rejects any pairing whose `gateway` hint fails its own `isAllowedWebSocketUrl` check, so the producer must not emit a hint that check rejects. All evidence above is from real local runtime execution.

prs.title: fix(codex): retain native thread reasoning effort
prs.body:
## Summary

- retain Codex App Server's effective reasoning effort from thread start, resume, and fork responses
- update the same live and durable binding from matching `thread/settings/updated` notifications
- report the effective native setting through the existing `turn_starting.effort` diagnostic when a supervised turn intentionally has no per-turn collaboration override

## Root cause and canonical fix

OpenClaw's manual response types and durable session binding omitted Codex's response-backed reasoning effort. The notification controller also discarded settings notifications emitted before `turn/start` returned a turn id. Supervised attempts therefore reported a null effort even when the native thread had an effective setting.

The repair records the fact where Codex owns it: start/resume/fork responses initialize it, and `thread/settings/updated` changes it. All binding writers carry the same nullable field. Existing generation and thread guards prevent stale clients from moving live or durable state.

This current-main rewrite does not add `thread_ready.reasoningEffort` or another event field. It fills the long-standing `turn_starting.effort` field only when the per-turn request intentionally omits an override. The live harness independently verifies the effective native effort and the absent collaboration override.

## Dependency contract

The integrated plugin pins `@openai/codex` 0.164.0. The sibling Codex source was inspected directly at commit `fdf23b4097bf19adf2286c64316da2d2a9fedae6`: `codex-rs/app-server-protocol/src/protocol/v2/thread.rs` defines response-backed nullable `reasoning_effort` for thread start/resume and `ThreadSettings.effort` for settings updates. Native thread facts remain separate from per-turn overrides.

## Coverage and change shape

Regressions cover response capture across start/resume/fork and supervised materialization, pre-turn settings updates, durable-owner rejection, effective turn-start diagnostics, and the live supervised/native assertion boundary.

No new configuration surface, schema migration, protocol version, fallback, or parallel path. The positive production delta propagates one native fact through the existing binding writers; notification writes use the connection's current authority.

## Validation

- Current head: `ae1b83e6b0bd`; integrated main: `1f01f4944d45`.
- 89 tests passed across three affected files during conflict repair.
- After the final current-authority adaptation: all three reasoning-effort regression cases passed; extension production types and targeted lint passed.
- Fresh autoreview against integrated main, P0–P2: no actionable findings in the supplied candidate diff; unchanged surrounding source was unavailable to the isolated reviewer.
- `git diff --check`: clean.
- No fresh credentialed live Codex run. Historical CI and hosted review are not current-head evidence.

prs.title: fix(memory): expire embedding probe cache on elapsed time
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The memory plugin's embedding-availability probe cache is keyed on the wall clock. A backward wall-clock step (e.g. an NTP correction, laptop resume, or VM restore) makes `Date.now()` read *smaller* than the recorded `expireAtMs`, so the 30-second probe cache never lapses. The Gateway keeps serving the stale embedding-availability result until real wall time catches back up — long after its real window.

The sibling recall cache in `active-memory` moved from `Date.now()` to `performance.now()` in #193358, and the same cutover landed for the GitHub detail cache (#195450), Mantle discovery, and Nextcloud Talk room kinds (#193147). This embedding probe cache was left on the wall clock.

## Why This Change Was Made

`manager-provider-lifecycle.ts` writes `expireAtMs: checkedAtMs + EMBEDDING_PROBE_CACHE_TTL_MS` and reads `Date.now() >= cached.expireAtMs` with the same wall clock; `manager.ts` reads the inherited probe's `expireAtMs` the same way. All five sites move to `performance.now()` so the window measures elapsed time, not wall position. TTLs, probe policy, eviction and result data are unchanged.

The `primaryRecoveryRetryAt` window (same 30s budget) is the sibling wall-clock site in this file and moves together.

## User Impact

After a wall-clock rollback, a long-lived Gateway no longer keeps serving a stale embedding-availability probe (provider up/down, error reason) past its real 30-second window — the probe re-runs when its elapsed window actually elapses. Normal-clock behavior is unchanged. No new setting, error text, public SDK export, stored format, or migration.

## Evidence

**Red on base, green with the fix** (real `extension-database-workers` vitest shard, Node 24.22.1):

- **Base** (`7c7a4d5db4adf174b324cfe47c17123808a7de61`): new discriminant test fails — after the probe is cached, an elapsed `performance.now` step past the TTL with a backward wall-clock step still returns the cached result:
  ```text
  × memory index > expires cached embedding probe readiness on elapsed time even when the wall clock steps back
  ```
- **Candidate**: same file, 12 passed (12), including the discriminant test.

The discriminant test writes a probe, then pairs an elapsed `performance.now` (advanced past the 30s TTL) with a backward `Date.now` (an hour back) — a `Date.now`-keyed cache could never lapse under those reads, while the real elapsed window has already passed.

### Pre-existing assertion adapted

The existing "caches embedding probe readiness across transient status managers" case asserted `cacheExpiresAtMs - checkedAtMs === 30_000` with exact equality. `performance.now()` returns a high-resolution float, so the same TTL arithmetic now yields `30000.000000000007`; the assertion moves to `toBeCloseTo(30_000)` with the behavior unchanged. All other existing cases pass unmodified (`manager-provider-lifecycle.test.ts` 12/12; `manager.borrowed-connection.test.ts` 22/22 covering the `manager.ts` inheritance read).

### Impact surface

| File | Change |
| --- | --- |
| `extensions/memory-core/src/memory/manager-provider-lifecycle.ts` | `checkedAtMs`/`nowMs` and `primaryRecoveryRetryAt` write+read move to `performance.now()` (−4/+4) |
| `extensions/memory-core/src/memory/manager.ts` | inherited-probe read moves to `performance.now()` (−1/+1) |
| `extensions/memory-core/src/memory/manager-provider-lifecycle.test.ts` | discriminant test (+19) + existing equality → `toBeCloseTo` (−2/+2) |

Two-way door: a revert restores the wall-clock windows with no state migration or published-contract change. Blast radius is the process-local embedding probe cache only.

## Precedent

Same cutover, already merged: #193358 (active-memory recall cache), #190894/#195450 (GitHub detail + preview), #193147 (Mantle / Nextcloud Talk). This completes the same elapsed-time sweep for the memory plugin's probe cache.

prs.title: fix: Pull requests shows an old task's PR when a worktree name is reused
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: a session's **Pull requests** block shows an unrelated, older pull request when its managed worktree reuses the name of a retired one.

Reported by @vyctorbrzezowski: a new session on worktree `openclaw/cool-crab-2` (branch created 2026-11-08) listed #154218, which another session opened from an earlier `openclaw/cool-crab-2` branch on 2026-09-21. The new session never read or mentioned that PR.

## User Impact

User impact: the Pull requests block no longer shows another task's PR just because a recycled worktree name produced the same branch name. Pull requests opened from the current branch, and branches checked out from an existing PR, still appear as before.

## Why This Change Was Made

Branch discovery asks GitHub for PRs by `owner:branch` name only. Managed worktree names become available again after a retired worktree's registry record expires (30 days), and the older PR on GitHub keeps that head branch name indefinitely.

The checkout context now reads the branch's Git creation entry. When Git created the branch from the default branch, as managed worktrees do, PRs opened before that moment are skipped. Other start points (`HEAD`, `FETCH_HEAD`, a remote branch) may be adopting an existing PR, so they stay unfiltered, as do missing or expired reflogs.

Accepted edge case: a branch created from the default branch and then reset onto an older PR's commits will hide that older PR. Discovery through publication receipts and bound PRs is unchanged.

## Evidence

- New regression test in `src/gateway/control-ui-session-prs-branch.test.ts` uses a real Git checkout created from `origin/main`. It runs the real `checkout.context` read and the session PR loader against a stubbed GitHub list containing an older same-name PR and a current PR. It fails on `main` (`[154218, 103469]`) and passes with this change (`[103469]`). It also checks that a branch created from its remote counterpart is not dated.

prs.title: fix(worktrees): stop leaving branches after recovery expires
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Managed branches retained for snapshot-loss or detached-worktree recovery survived after expiry removed their recovery refs and registry rows. Repeated retirement accumulated orphaned local branches.

## User Impact

Recovery expiry now deletes eligible managed branches and retains retryable ownership when deletion fails. Ordinary `openclaw worktrees gc` also cleans existing orphaned `openclaw/*` branches in repositories recorded by the registry or pending allocations. It reports failures through the existing GC receipt and logs successful deletion counts.

The extra orphan-cleanup RPC request and CLI mode from the first revision have been removed. There are no protocol, generated-validator, UI, config, schema, or retention-period changes. GC selects repositories from its existing owner inventory; callers cannot supply arbitrary cleanup targets. Repositories with no remaining registry or pending records are not discovered by this sweep.

## Safety and Recovery

Only direct managed heads without an attached Git worktree, live/retained registry reference, or pending allocation are eligible. Unknown recovery refs preserve every candidate in the repository. Native Git retains its checked-out-branch protection. Existing leases and the clean Git environment own deletion; the same closure-bound guard is revalidated synchronously after ref-queue admission and immediately before each native deletion command.

Normal removal keeps its ancestry-safe branch deletion (#148765). Missing Git metadata with surviving checkout files preserves recovery ownership. Explicit snapshot retirement requires an independent ordinary branch or remote-tracking source; a managed branch cannot provide durable custody after its row is forgotten.

## Evidence

Exact head `69823b6f1ec8f2db21d71c25843e327674064dba` passed [CI run 42550750226](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/42550750226), including the original failing `checks-node-changed-compact-small-2` shard.

CI run 42540143974 failed two interrupted-expiry cases because their last assertions still required orphan branches after complete retirement. The repaired tests keep every interruption/custody assertion, additionally prove the branch survives the interrupted pass, and require it to disappear after settlement. The new authority test uses real GC, state-owner capture, and guards; it covers write-only, revoked, replaced-owner, and authorized requests. A delayed native-effect test checks actual allocation-lease expiry, and a persisted v2026.11.2-shaped row verifies restore and expiry without any new cleanup field.

Focused proof: 43 exact-state race cases, 25 GC cases, 21 removal-safety cases, 20 snapshot-retirement cases, five orphan/upgrade/churn cases, and four real GC authority cases. The existing zero-allocation and single-linked-worktree-inventory no-op guarantees remain asserted; GC inventory performance cases are separated into their own file to preserve the line cap, and assert the exact new repository metadata work; the GC test also discovers a branch added between passes. The two updated branch-deletion assertions fail against the pinned pre-fix lifecycle owners because the branch survives settlement; all 43 cases pass on the final fixed sources (185.94 s).

`pnpm check:changed` completed. Three unnecessary default type arguments in the new tests were corrected and focused core lint passed. Every other code/type/format/schema/export gate passed. The remaining failure is the same 20 changelog-attribution violations reproduced by the actual guard on exact main parent `61db4b336f89957d7916580871b288d0d8c9ba82`. #194364 / `266a7aa0fe69e2b5fe6445c4ceb1e15b5360c957` introduced that signature without correcting historical release artifacts; its parent already had a different failing signature. This is an unresolved main regression for follow-up, not a passing check.

Codex P0–P2 autoreview is scoped-clean. The exact test-line allocation is +479 lines (6,589,675 total / 6,589,707 ceiling; 32 slack). Handwritten production growth is +237 lines, with zero generated changes, reduced from +295 handwritten / +14 generated. The remaining growth implements safe ownership classification, native batch deletion/reconciliation, and existing GC/retirement integration. No production system was accessed or modified.

Follow-up CI exposed two stale GC inventory expectations, now reproduced and corrected with exact metadata-command assertions and the existing checkout/lease constraints intact. The extracted inventory and maintenance files pass together (20 passed, one platform-specific skip). CI also merged in newer main containing #195488 (`3908a3e4619905ab8589d220147292779f1df2f1`): its shared transport renamed the temporary directory, leaving the existing clone-identity test watching a removed prefix. The test now invokes the real shared transport helper and revokes identity at its handoff after awaited staging setup, preserving every revocation and authorized-effect assertion. It no longer depends on the temporary-directory name, so it also remains compatible with peer #195505. The three refresh cases fail with the same boundary assertion on an unmodified checkout of exact main parent `61db4b336f89957d7916580871b288d0d8c9ba82`; all six clone/refresh cases pass after repairing the boundary hook. This is a proven main test regression with a named introducer, fixed here. The final rebase preserves all reviewed worktree owner changes byte-for-byte.

Synthetic scale proof uses 13,531 refs, 3,145 local heads, 1,843 managed heads, 1,598 real linked worktrees and 1,228 registry records. Every one of five cleanup samples removes exactly 615 orphan heads, preserves the entire remaining ref set, and finds zero candidates on the next pass: 12,916 total refs / 1,228 managed heads. On macOS/APFS with Node 26.12.1, collector median wall time is 812 ms populated preview, 2,757 ms cleanup, 992 ms clean next pass. Median Node CPU is 652/674/646 ms; native Git CPU 330/2,170/500 ms; main V8 allocation 5.681/8.405/6.819 MiB. Five A/A previews have 814 ms median and 1,037 ms p95 (31.67% range/median); shared-host variance prevents a speedup claim. This measures the collector under real custody, excluding fixture setup, GC preflight and other GC stages. It does not measure publication fetch latency or unrelated agent databases/workspace files.

This PR remains open and must not be merged automatically.

prs.title: fix(agents): avoid catalog rebuilds for unknown credential providers
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Model-catalog reads rebuild static provider catalogs when credentials for unrelated, uninstalled providers change. Those provider IDs also accumulate in the worker generation's retained scope.

## User Impact

Catalog workers reuse static provider results across unknown credential-provider changes while continuing to refresh credentials and account-specific models. No configuration, migration, or operator action is required. RSS savings have not been measured.

## Why This Change Was Made

Reuse the worker's existing provider-ownership discovery to admit only normalized references with a known plugin owner into static scope. Preserve aliases, different plugin/provider IDs, sibling scope growth, and generation invalidation. No new retained cache.

## Evidence

- Exact head: `8a27e0f0fe7127d583cb7aae0ea9b24f1cdd1b91`; source base: `aa9531e37637d977792513c3082d575916bd4325`.
- [Production build and artifact/CLI checks passed](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/42391469757/job/128460298010).
- [Real-worker regression and sibling shard passed](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/42391469757/job/128460321656): Node 64 files/665 tests; Bun 64 files/664 tests plus one unrelated skip. Both Gateway and standalone cases passed in both runtimes. Unknown credential provider A → B → removal keeps one static build, current credentials, expected model rows, directory rejection and drained tasks.
- Formatting, diff checks, native pre-commit checks, production/core test type checks, guards and security-fast passed. Independent source review and local autoreview found no actionable P0–P2 findings. Hosted ClawSweeper review is active for the unchanged head.
- Production +6 net lines; tests +36 net lines extend the existing fixture without extra cases or worker calls. The exact test allocation leaves the shared scalar unchanged.

The broader manual run is not a green full-suite result: other shards failed in package-lifecycle admission, Doctor/config convergence, exec completion timing and decision deadlines; their inspected owners are unchanged by this PR. Other broad-run results remain under investigation. Required ready-PR CI still applies. The earlier invalid dispatch and stopped Testbox allocation produced no runtime proof. Baseline-red execution and paired RSS/timing measurements remain unavailable.

Follow-up diagnosis: measure the catalog worker's compiled import graph and mutable model-registry copies before changing their ownership or mutation isolation.

Release note: avoid rebuilding static model catalogs for credential providers without an installed plugin owner.

prs.title: fix(muse): label partial replies when the provider stream fails
prs.body:
Closes #195100

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes partial Muse answers appearing complete when the provider stream ends unexpectedly and the native turn fails.

## User Impact

Users keep the available text and see an explicit incomplete-response notice, including when the text already streamed. The attempt still fails; ordinary completed replies retain their existing text. The notice is also retained in the transcript.

## Why This Change Was Made

Qualify the authoritative settled `agentMessage` once in the existing Muse projector, then use that text for live updates, final replies and retained history. The correction stays within the plugin and preserves the existing core APIs, permissions, retries and replay policy.

Related work: #195271 addresses the same issue by mapping `cutOff` to `stopReason: "length"`. I independently tested its exact head `22d99f7db4ea6b6afca642d004c5c2baec417964` with the same controlled failed-terminal CLI cases. Its native transcript did contain `length`, but both returned payloads still contained only the unqualified partial text. This PR addresses that remaining visible-reply path with a separate projection change. The comparison covers each approach individually; validation of the two approaches together remains outstanding.

## Evidence

The results below come from independently executed local checks. The tested base is `0566b7771956f0f5dcb1a1ce32a729e7c5f5d9e7`. Before publication, main `141890196ac07d6c7d86d77fbf998ea2b04875b3` was checked: Muse, Meta, the adjacent core run code, dependency files and applicable contribution rules were unchanged, and the reviewed patch applied cleanly. The tested source is unchanged by publication.

Hosted PR validation: [CI run 42495876461](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/42495876461) completed successfully on exact head `54108325147978e53a7097136dec05e81af65eca`: **28 successful jobs, 30 skipped jobs**, with a **7 min 2 s** workflow window. These totals distinguish successful jobs from skipped jobs and describe the repository's scoped PR CI.

### Real CLI before and after

Ran the supported entry point with isolated configuration, state, ports and fictional credentials:

```sh
pnpm openclaw agent --local --json --agent main --message fixture:cutoff
pnpm openclaw agent --local --json --agent main --message fixture:cutoffsettled
```

The real Muse SDK starts the reviewed local MSP subprocess. It emits a committed partial `agentMessage` with `cutOff: true`, followed by a failed native terminal. The first case streams before completion; the second delivers only the settled item.

| Observation | Base | This change | #195271 at the head above |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Streamed and settled-only payload | Partial text only | Partial text plus notice | Partial text only |
| Native transcript text | Partial text only | Partial text plus notice | Partial text only |
| Native assistant message stop reason | `stop` | `stop` | `length` |
| CLI exit / final stop reason | `1` / `error` | `1` / `error` | `1` / `error` |

The complete returned text after this change is:

```text
Partial answer: the first two steps are

[Response incomplete: the provider stream ended unexpectedly.]
```

Read-only SQLite inspection confirms exactly one matching assistant record for each cutoff run. All retain `incomplete_turn`, `fallbackSafe: false` and `replayInvalid: true`. Normal-success and failed-without-partial CLI controls preserve their existing behavior. The normal CLI runtime build and its bootstrap/control-plane checks completed successfully.

The competing mapping retains the failed attempt's final `error` stop reason: the core error branch precedes the ordinary length-notice path. The real CLI results above confirm this behavior.

### Regression and static checks

- Red on unchanged production code: all **3 new harness regressions fail at the missing notice**; 55 unrelated cases were excluded from that red selection.
- Full non-live Muse suite: **65/65**; full non-live Meta suite: **16/16**; four adjacent payload/terminal files: **142/142**. Total: **223 distinct passing tests**.
- The changed harness file was separately rerun: **58/58**, command wall time **24.779 s**, Vitest duration **21.14 s**. The 223 count covers distinct tests; this rerun provides additional timing evidence. Scoped hosted CI timing is recorded above.
- Extension production/test types, Muse package typecheck, scoped type-aware lint, changed-file formatting, whitespace and the test-line ratchet pass on the reviewed source.
- Duplicate completed tool/message delivery yields one tool-result observation, one synthetic file append and no repeated effect after an explicit fresh continuation. The failed attempt remains replay-unsafe, including when prior potential side effects exist.
- The exact **82-line** test allocation covers the owning harness cases and the existing subprocess peer's cutoff/duplicate scenarios, including its SDK-shaped SourceRange correction. The shared scalar is unchanged. Production growth is two net lines.
- Independent AI-assisted source review of the complete four-file patch completed with zero actionable code findings. A second independent AI-assisted evidence review verified the CLI/raw-output/native-database comparison. Author simplification and test-audit passes were completed. Optional local autoreview was unavailable, and local ClawSweeper remains unrun.

<details>
<summary>Commands, runtime and resolved local environment issues</summary>

Node 24.22.1, pnpm 12.15.0, the repository-pinned Bun `1.4.4-canary.1+191755ec1`, Muse SDK 1.4.14, macOS arm64. Each checkout has its own physical dependency installation. Tests use a supported local SQLite library and `TMPDIR=/tmp`.

```sh
pnpm test:extension muse --maxWorkers=1
pnpm test:extension meta --maxWorkers=1
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run/payloads.test.ts src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run/payloads.errors.test.ts src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run/terminal-resolution.test.ts src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run/terminal-resolution.settled-request.test.ts --maxWorkers=1
pnpm test extensions/muse/harness.test.ts --maxWorkers=1
pnpm tsgo:extensions
pnpm tsgo:extensions:test
node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p extensions/muse/tsconfig.json --noEmit
node scripts/run-oxlint.mjs --tsconfig extensions/muse/tsconfig.json extensions/muse/src/events.ts extensions/muse/harness.test.ts extensions/muse/src/test-support/fake-muse.mjs
node scripts/run-format.mts --check extensions/muse/src/events.ts extensions/muse/harness.test.ts extensions/muse/src/test-support/fake-muse.mjs
```

Initial environment failures are retained in local evidence: absent SQLite configuration, sandboxed build-lock process inspection, missing generated SDK declarations before normal wrapper preparation, and overlong macOS Unix-socket paths in existing catalog cancellation cases. The unchanged full Muse suite passes with a short `TMPDIR`, preserving the existing timeouts, assertions, safety checks and shared budget. The passing totals cover completed successful runs; earlier setup failures and the interrupted initial suite are retained separately.

</details>

**Validation scope:** the evidence exercises the real OpenClaw CLI, SDK and native storage with a controlled MSP peer. The file-effect case covers duplicate delivery and explicit fresh continuation. Live Muse network interruption, provider recovery and automatic core replay remain unverified. Peer logs capture requests and terminal summaries; a complete bidirectional trace remains unavailable. The existing peer emits a cancellation notification on cleanup after failure, while both compared CLI results retain failure. Full MSP conformance, browser/channel UI, live provider behavior, cross-platform release behavior and the full-repository CI suite remain outside this validation scope.

## AI Assistance

Prepared with AI assistance. The complete patch and CLI/native-storage evidence received independent AI-assisted reviews.

prs.title: fix(memory-wiki): honor system agent for CLI defaults
prs.body:
Fixes #188953

## What Problem This Solves

On an explicit-ownership multi-agent install with `agents.defaults.systemAgent.agentId` set, `openclaw wiki` without `--agent` asks for an agent that is already configured. The CLI still resolves its default through the deprecated `resolveDefaultAgentId`, which only accepts legacy raw markers or a sole agent; the configured system agent is ignored.

In plain terms: the user already told OpenClaw which agent is the default work owner, but the wiki command does not read that setting. This change uses the same owner-aware resolver as other CLI operations.

## Why This Change Was Made

`resolveAgentOperationAgentId` is the existing core resolver for CLI operation owners: it consults the explicit ownership system agent before falling back. It was not reachable from the memory plugin, so this adds it through the existing private-local-only `memory-core-host-runtime-core` facade instead of expanding the public plugin SDK surface.

The CLI preAction, gateway request context, and active-memory query fallback now use the same owner-aware helper. `config.ts` keeps its lightweight legacy fallback because Doctor imports it and must not cold-load the memory runtime/Kysely graph; the CLI resolves the system agent first and passes the explicit agent ID into config resolution.

## User Impact

`openclaw wiki search`, `get`, `status`, and `doctor` work without `--agent` when `agents.defaults.systemAgent.agentId` is configured, matching other CLI operation surfaces. The misleading "add an agent" hint is no longer shown when an owner is already configured. `--agent` remains authoritative.

## Evidence

Focused memory-wiki CLI/config/gateway/query suite:

```text
$ node_modules/.bin/vitest run --config test/vitest/vitest.extension-memory.config.ts \
    extensions/memory-wiki/src/cli.test.ts extensions/memory-wiki/src/config.test.ts \
    extensions/memory-wiki/src/gateway.test.ts extensions/memory-wiki/src/query.test.ts --maxWorkers=1
Test Files  4 passed (4)
Tests       99 passed (99)
```

The new regression uses `agents.ownership: "explicit"`, two entries, and `agents.defaults.systemAgent.agentId: "main"`, then runs the real `registerWikiCli` preAction without `--agent` and asserts the doctor resolves the `main` agent-scoped vault.

Base red check (production changes reverted, regression kept):

```text
FAIL  ... > resolves agents.defaults.systemAgent for the default CLI agent
Error: No default memory-wiki agent is configured. Pass --agent <id>, or add an agent with `openclaw agents add`.
```

Shipped CLI, built from commit `22ecfe63017` (code-identical to the current head; the only later commit is an empty review-refresh commit) in a clean checkout and run against an isolated Gateway with fresh state:

```console
$ node dist/index.js wiki status
Wiki vault mode: isolated
Vault scope: agent (main)
Vault: ready (.../state/wiki/main)
...
EXIT 0

$ node dist/index.js wiki status --agent ops
Wiki vault mode: isolated
Vault scope: agent (ops)
Vault: ready (.../state/wiki/ops)
...
EXIT 0
```

The config has `agents.ownership: "explicit"`, `main` + `ops`, `agents.defaults.systemAgent.agentId: "main"`, and `plugins.entries.memory-wiki.config.vault.scope: "agent"`.

Latest-stable upgrade on the same state (v2026.10.9 release `8b18b55`):

```console
# release build 2026.10.9 (8b18b55): create the main vault and one source page
$ node dist/index.js wiki init --agent main
Initialized wiki vault at .../upgrade-state/wiki/main (9 dirs, 5 files).
$ node dist/index.js wiki ingest upgrade-source.md --agent main
Ingested upgrade-source.md into sources/upgrade-source.md. Refreshed 16 index files.

# this build 2026.10.9 (22ecfe6): migrate the release state, then read with no --agent
$ node dist/index.js doctor --fix
Doctor complete.
$ node dist/index.js wiki status
Vault scope: agent (main)
Vault: ready (.../upgrade-state/wiki/main)
Pages: 1 sources, 0 entities, 0 concepts, 0 syntheses, 9 reports
EXIT 0

$ node dist/index.js wiki status --agent ops
Vault scope: agent (ops)
Vault: ready (.../upgrade-state/wiki/ops)
EXIT 0
```

The source page created by the release build is still present and counted after the upgrade; the configured vault path and settings are unchanged. This is also the data-model compatibility check for the stored vault.

The config module intentionally keeps the lightweight legacy resolver so Doctor enumeration does not cold-load the memory/Kysely graph.

## AI Assistance

This PR is AI-assisted. Used source inspection and the existing memory-wiki CLI test harness to trace the owner-resolution gap through the four call sites and add the explicit-ownership regression. The implementer understands the code: the private facade exposes the core operation-owner resolver, and memory-wiki now consumes it instead of the deprecated legacy-only default.

prs.title: fix(agents): stop exec-completion wakes from rewriting the prompt cache
prs.body:
> **AI-assisted: yes**

<details>
<summary>Additional instructions</summary>

**MUST:** Keep **Allow edits from maintainers** enabled for this PR so maintainers
can help update the branch when needed.

</details>

Closes #191128

## What Problem This Solves

- Fixes an issue where users whose agent runs background commands (`tools.exec.notifyOnExit`, default `true`) would pay a full prompt-cache write on **every** exec-completion wake: the woken turn's system prompt is built in `minimal` mode, so it drops Execution Bias, the skills catalog, Memory Recall, Docs and Delegation and renders "Subagent Context" instead of "Conversation Context" — a different prefix from the conversation's normal turn (39,754 → 32,290 chars, diverging at ~char 90 in the reporter's capture).
- The wake's tool access is unchanged by this PR: the finite producer ceiling introduced for #183589 stays exactly as it is.
- **Related:** #183589 / #183594 / #190410 keep the finite ceiling for tool access (untouched here); #186285 / #186306 (fc46600a98) stopped a finite ceiling from dropping the skills catalog, but minimal mode itself still applied. Fix-signal labels on the issue: `clawsweeper:queueable-fix`, `clawsweeper:fix-shape-clear`, `clawsweeper:source-repro`.

## Why This Change Was Made

- **Intended outcome:** a turn woken by a background exec completion keeps the prompt mode of the run that started the exec, so the system prompt prefix is byte-identical and the provider prompt cache is read instead of rewritten.
- The default session-event policy in `createOpenClawCodingTools` records the producing run's own authorized surface as the wake's ceiling. That list is a *provenance* fact, not a policy narrowing, but `toolPolicyRestrictsTools()` treats any non-empty allowlist without `*` as restrictive — which is what forced `minimal`. This PR separates the two questions: the ceiling still bounds tool access, and a new non-enumerable provenance fact on the allowlist (same mechanism as the existing `TOOL_ALLOWLIST_INTERSECTION` metadata) tells the two prompt-mode gates that nothing was removed.
- The fact is recorded only when the producing turn held its session's normal surface: no runtime allowlist, no turn-scoped plugin grant, no collector contract, no delegated authority, no sender/group/sandbox/subagent/inherited restriction, no tool withheld from the turn, non-empty surface. Configured `tools.allow`/`tools.deny` are deliberately not treated as narrowing — the woken turn re-resolves them from the same config, so its prompt matches the conversation's normal prompt in that case too.
- **Out of scope:** no change to tool access, to the ceiling's contents, to session-event admission, or to any wire/schema/config surface (the fact is a non-enumerable symbol property, so it never reaches JSON, the gateway protocol, or persisted state).
- **Highest-risk area:** a wake that *should* stay minimal getting the full prompt.
- **How is that risk mitigated?** Every turn-scoped narrowing source listed above keeps the prompt minimal (asserted case-by-case in `src/agents/session-event-producer-surface.test.ts`), the fact is dropped by any plain copy of the list — so an unmodelled path degrades to today's behaviour, never to wider access — and the prompt gates are the only consumers; `applyEmbeddedAttemptToolsAllow`, construction planning and native deny policy still read the list itself.

## User Impact

prs.title: fix: Latest stops short of the final chat reply
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: after returning to a tool-heavy chat and choosing **Latest**, scrolling can stop above the final reply even though all tools have finished. The final reply stays below view and the Latest button can disappear.

## User Impact

Latest now continues to the completed answer while row heights settle. Upward reader intent, ordinary scrolling, tool order and final content retain their existing behavior. This is a focused correctness follow-up to #195441; the saturation experiments remain separate and unqualified.

## Why This Change Was Made

A shrinking estimated transcript can temporarily clamp the native viewport to its current bottom before it reaches the destination of an in-flight scroll. Both completion sites now require the issued destination and the native bottom to agree with the current position before retiring the command. This uses the existing scroll owner and preserves its moving/idle pixel tolerances; there is no new timer or state owner.

prs.title: fix(media): carry provider status and code into failure markers
prs.body:
Fixes #188043

## What Problem This Solves

When a media provider call fails, the agent marker was the fixed string `[Audio attachment could not be analyzed]` and the operator log kept only `reason=ProviderHttpError`, so a rejected credential, an exhausted account, a rate limit, and a timeout were indistinguishable. The agent now sees a bounded structured summary, and the operator warning keeps the provider code.

- Problem: status and code were dropped; the previous revision of this branch fixed that by forwarding the provider's whole error message into agent context, which also forwarded response-body detail and request ids.
- Solution: the marker renders only `provider request failed (HTTP <status> code=<code>)`; the full message stays on the diagnostic attempt reason and verbose log; the compact operator summary carries the code because it is annotated into the message head before the response detail.
- What changed: `src/media-understanding/media-failure-reason.ts` (owner of the two representations), `runner.ts` / `apply.ts` (which representation each audience receives), and `runner.entries.ts` (helpers moved out to stay within the lint budget).
- What did NOT change: provider transport and request payloads, marker text for non-provider failures (still the plain marker, as on `main`), and the bounded-marker/overflow budget.

## Why This Change Was Made

An agent marker and an operator log are different audiences: the marker crosses a disclosure boundary into the conversation model, while the log stays local. Keeping one string for both is what produced the leak and the truncation. The split reuses the shape `ProviderHttpError` already carries (`status`, `code`/`errorType`, `requestId`) instead of new plumbing, and accepts only a bounded taxonomy-shaped code (`^[A-Za-z0-9_.-]{1,64}$`) so arbitrary text can never reach the marker.

- Best fix: yes — one owner decides the two representations; callers do not re-derive them.
- Alternative: sanitizing the message (whitespace, redaction, length caps) — rejected; it does not establish a disclosure boundary for arbitrary response detail.
- Risk / non-goals: an existing provider error without `code` renders status only; a CLI-backend failure keeps the plain marker because its message is arbitrary output, not a taxonomy.

## User Impact

The agent can now say whether a failure was authentication (`HTTP 401`), quota (`HTTP 429 code=insufficient_quota`), rate limiting, or a provider outage, without the conversation model receiving provider response bodies, request ids, or account detail. Operators see the code in the Gateway warning instead of a bare status.

## Evidence

Shipped Gateway flow (real `openclaw gateway --port 18999`, real `gateway call chat.send` with an audio attachment, media provider pointed at `api.deepseek.com` with an invalid key). Gateway log — the operator warning keeps the code:

```console
[media-understanding] audio: failed (0/1) reason=Audio transcription failed (HTTP 401 code=invalid_request_error)
```

The marker the agent actually receives, read from the shipped session transcript (`agents/main/agent/openclaw-agent.sqlite`):

```console
Transcribe this voice note.
[media attached: media://inbound/note---793f0547-….ogg]

[Audio attachment could not be analyzed: provider request failed (HTTP 401 code=invalid_request_error)]
```

Reviewed head vs new head, same in-process script, real provider through the compatible audio adapter:

```console
# reviewed head 153b421b1e6
agent marker: [Audio attachment could not be analyzed: Audio transcription failed (HTTP 401): Authentication Fails, Your api key: ****8078 is invalid (request_id: 72ddece0-…) [type=authent…]
operator compact summary: Audio transcription failed (HTTP 401)
marker leaks provider body: true

# new head 69203e57e1a
agent marker: [Audio attachment could not be analyzed: provider request failed (HTTP 401 code=invalid_request_error)]
diagnostic attempt reason: ProviderHttpError: Audio transcription failed (HTTP 401 code=invalid_request_error): Authentication Fails, … [type=authentication_error, code=invalid_request_error]
operator compact summary: Audio transcription failed (HTTP 401 code=invalid_request_error)
marker leaks provider body: false
```

Tests (`546 passed`, media-understanding + status) and gates:

```console
$ node node_modules/vitest/vitest.mjs run src/media-understanding src/status
 Test Files  52 passed | 1 skipped (53)
      Tests  546 passed | 5 skipped (551)
```

`media-failure-reason.test.ts` covers: provider summary carries status+code only; arbitrary runtime errors produce no summary; unsafe codes are dropped; the adapter-shaped message keeps `code=` through `summarizeDecisionReason`; a 180-character detail does not push the code out. `oxlint`, `run-format`, and the changed-file `tsc` pass; CI is 56/56.

What was not tested: Windows runtime, and providers that report the code only in the response body without a `code`/`errorType` field (they render status only).

## AI Assistance

This PR is AI-assisted. Used `git log -S`, source tracing across the media runner/disposition/renderer owners, and a real-provider `node --import tsx` script for before/after evidence. The implementer understands the code: the provider error's structured fields feed a bounded label for the model while the full message stays on the diagnostic attempt reason. All evidence above is from real local runtime execution.

prs.title: fix(ui): restore compact cards for long pasted text
prs.body:
Related: #165763; restores the compact paste interaction removed by #191699.

Thanks @vyctorbrzezowski for the report and product direction, and @Oldrich333 for the original paste-provenance report and work in #165776.

## Work sessions

Linked for team reference; these sessions aren’t public.

- [Discussion, implementation and verification](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/dashboard/98bfa432-6d67-4e9f-85a1-ef6a534d41cf)

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: pasting a long excerpt beside an existing Control UI draft fills the message input instead of producing a compact, inspectable card.

## User Impact

Long pastes become previewable, removable cards again in Chat and New Session. Their contents reach the model as the sender’s own text, while uploaded files and PDFs retain external-content isolation. Pastes into an empty input stay inline. No configuration or migration is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

Preserve the existing clipboard-origin field through attachment preparation and the shared live/history prompt renderer instead of discarding the compact presentation. Only extracted paste-origin text loses the document wrapper; filenames never decide its treatment. Existing sanitization, upload admission, image-paste precedence, and saved-card controls remain in place.

## Evidence

- Native Chromium clipboard flows pass in both Chat and New Session, checking the compact card, full preview, unchanged paste bytes, and explicit origin in the submitted request. The production Control UI build used by these scenarios succeeds. Existing retained-card preview, copy, restore, and history cases passed as well.
- 67 focused attachment/composer recovery tests and 44 focused Gateway/media tests pass. The final Gateway staging and document-context files were rerun successfully (27 tests).
- The source-origin regression fails on base `7c7a4d5db4adf174b324cfe47c17123808a7de61`: paste text has a file/external-content wrapper and loses surrounding whitespace. With this change it preserves the text without that wrapper; upload-origin and unspecified-origin controls remain wrapped.
- Chat-test typecheck, scoped type-aware lint, formatting, and `git diff --check` pass. No live-model response or full package build is claimed; broad PR CI is pending.
- Fresh independent Codex autoreview, P0–P2, covered the complete local candidate against that base and found no actionable findings. The reviewed snapshot is committed as `88a526deaabf8edd7eb045a5a62869973dc0b6c0`.

The 40-line regression allocation covers distinct clipboard intake, sandbox staging, prompt treatment, and native browser assertions. Existing owners and persistence formats are reused; no new state store or protocol field is introduced.

### Before and after

Actual Control UI components, using the same synthetic clipboard text at 1280 × 900.

| Before | After |
| --- | --- |
| ![Before: long paste expands the composer](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/401f270c-881b-4f42-ba1f-81ff66e66a18) | ![After: compact paste card preserves the existing draft](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/82e35e73-6381-4a4d-ad86-663b86b3cac0) |


## Worked on by

- @vyctorbrzezowski

prs.title: fix(ui): avoid extra reply blocks after steering
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: steering an active reply can separate its tools, working indicator, and continuing text into extra response blocks.

## User Impact

The earlier response stays above the steering message, and the continuation shares one response block for its text and tools. No configuration changes or migrations.

## Why This Change Was Made

Use the confirmed target execution consistently when choosing reply boundaries, while the steering message supplies the continuation's stable identity. This keeps the split at the human input without hiding work or redesigning the transcript.

Related: #164982, a broader unmerged reply-ownership change. This patch is limited to the confirmed-steer boundary mismatch.

## Evidence

[Controlled same-conversation before/after screenshots and complete browser recordings](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/195264#issuecomment-6723000085)

- 240 tests passed across 13 relevant grouping, streaming, steering, and retained-presentation suites.
- Ten focused steering regressions passed after final test cleanup (1.07 s invocation; 14 ms maximum individual case). The original reproduction failed on the baseline in the new-tool and persisted-text/working-indicator cases. CI seconds are not available yet.
- UI production types, the UI-chat test graph, focused lint, and formatting passed.
- The baseline and patched UI concurrently observed one conversation from one isolated Gateway. A third browser used normal composer/Steer controls; the model performed real file reads. No fabricated or replayed socket events or scripted model responses. Both views use a 1280×900 light-theme viewport.
- Corrected visual evidence: the original 41-event stills caught a detached status indicator and did not clearly demonstrate the reported split. Their internal block count was insufficient visual proof. The replacement pair comes from the existing simultaneous recordings at a 13.5-second seek in each. Both show the same text and steering messages. Before, “Here's what I found regarding the failure of npm start” starts a second assistant block with another avatar below the file-read row. After, the same text continues inside the existing reply without another avatar; the next steering message remains below it.
- Paired controls cover the second steer, completion, reload of that same saved conversation, and an ordinary follow-up. Settled controls show the same content on both sides; they are not presented as additional differences. The evidence comment retains both complete simultaneous recordings.
- The baseline grouping owner matches inspected main at `61093f1d32cb0042c858796f87f86920f910bd6d`; bundle source maps distinguish baseline and patch. This is not a blanket claim of zero scrolling movement or flicker.
- Production UI build passed. Its advisory bundle report measured chat boot JS at 1266.6 KiB against a 1266.4 KiB threshold; the threshold was not changed.
- Fresh independent code review of the complete uncommitted snapshot at base `035349bce1ae603d10c2d99fef629ac0254cc140`: no actionable findings. The reviewer independently traced input identity, live tools/streams, persisted grouping, and transcript projection, and verified the diff. Coverage limits: no direct optimistic-to-durable input replacement test, no history page missing the steering boundary, and no blanket mounted-DOM retention claim.

The production change adds 10 lines and removes 2. The 226 new regression-test lines cover distinct live/persisted, delayed-result, repeated-steer, and history-prepend transitions; the separate allocation records exactly that growth. The live proof harness is retained locally rather than added to routine CI.

Requested by and co-authored with @vyctorbrzezowski.

## Work sessions

Linked for team reference; these sessions aren’t public.

- [Original discussion with @vyctorbrzezowski](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/improve-perceived-responsiveness-during-session-a3d1f812261a4da5b505dc55806024cb)
- [Implementation and verification](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/dashboard/5b5f4f5f-9fbc-4a2a-bec1-afbf3f7709db)

## Worked on by

- @vyctorbrzezowski

prs.title: improve(codex): explain local model ownership denials in diagnostics
prs.body:
Related: #165739, #178731
Related discussions: https://community.openclaw.ai/t/394 and https://community.openclaw.ai/t/406

## What Problem This Solves

Local Codex owner-verification refusals and inactive harness-host errors currently hide which guard rejected the work, making distinct incidents difficult to investigate.

## User Impact

Operators get bounded denial reasons in the existing `agent/embedded` logs. Execution behavior, the owner/model 403 response, permissions, cancellation, cooldown policy, audit collection, and retention are unchanged. This is diagnostics only, not a claimed fix or shared root cause for the linked reports.

## Why This Change Was Made

Carry closed reasons from the existing metadata parser and native source owner to the HTTP/WebSocket relay logger. Record the core host's first failing branch once, using only its existing run correlation. Unknown underlying exceptions remain unknown; no error text, stack, request payload, metadata values, headers, credentials, or private URLs are added to these records.

Retained native sources still outlive legitimate foreground completion, pending owners still wait for their real turn, and all existing final-effect checks remain in place. There is no new public API, tool, configuration, authority registry, event store, or delivery behavior.

## Evidence

- **Regression:** nine initial HTTP cases failed on admitted base `3001551e277ce47a34033f0a298f5c9a26983df3` because the diagnostic record was absent while 403/zero-upstream-effect assertions passed. All six core branch/dedup regressions also failed on that base for missing records, then passed with the change.
- **Focused proof:** 143 passing tests across HTTP, WebSocket model policy, inference routing, native hook relay, direct child authority, and retained host-source lifetime. Synthetic secret-bearing metadata/errors remain absent from diagnostics and responses. Revocation during token resolution still prevents upstream I/O; independently retained valid work still succeeds.
- **Checks:** core production types; narrowly selected canonical Codex source-production and core/Codex test types; typed lint; formatting; docs MDX; diff checks; test-line, maximum-line, line-cap, assertion-safety, timeout-race, and mock-export ratchets.
- **Independent review:** bound Auto Review, local mode against the exact base above, P0–P2: `scoped-clean` with no findings.
- **Limits:** no live Windows/native-service reproduction or historical causal attribution. Standalone `extensions/codex/tsconfig.json` package-boundary typechecking remained red on missing packaged declarations and out-of-root source imports, including after maintained SDK declaration preparation; the canonical source graph and changed test graph pass. Broad PR CI is pending, not claimed green.

<details>
<summary>Scope and proof cost</summary>

The simplify pass retained the existing decision owners and logger rather than adding a diagnostic manager or durable state: net +138 production lines, +261 test lines, +21 documentation lines. The separate 261-line test allocation covers exactly this change's real-boundary denial, privacy, and revocation regressions; the shared baseline scalar is unchanged.

Changed-file test bodies total 0.656 s (HTTP), 0.176 s (WebSocket policy), and 0.075 s (host-source lifetime). Observed cold/configured shard wall times included 45.99 s for the final HTTP shard and 41.80 s for the host shard; compilation dominates those totals. The sibling direct-authority shard took 23.53 s. CI seconds are not yet available.

Native metadata contracts were personally inspected in the pinned Codex `rust-v0.164.0` source (`codex-rs/core/src/responses_metadata.rs` and `client.rs`); no dependency or protocol changes are included.

</details>

## Worked on by

- @jjjhenriksen
