prs.title: fix: reduce managed worktree base refresh delays
prs.body:
Related: #195488

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes slow managed-worktree creation when refreshing an advanced default branch in a shared clone with many refs and fragmented packs.

## User Impact

Default-base refresh avoids reading unrelated session histories before Git negotiation. Existing base selection, ancestry, shallow boundaries, partial-clone transport settings and source-ref authority are preserved.

The change adds six short local Git commands for isolated metadata/configuration: median JS thread CPU rises by 13.4 ms (+59%) and exact V8 allocation by 5.54 MiB (+25%). Median baseRefresh wall time falls 49%, native CPU 70% and native peak RSS 48%; this tradeoff needs maintainer acceptance before landing. This PR is for review, with no merge requested.

## Why This Change Was Made

A negotiation tip does not constrain Git's preceding `mark_complete_local_refs` walk. Base refresh now reuses the shared object-store transport introduced by #195488. The remote-fetch portion lives in `base-fetch.ts`; the preparation/cohort owner remains in `base-ref.ts`.

The transport resolves conditional Git configuration in the original worktree, then uses temporary refs with the existing object directory. It promotes the actual fetched default tip through the existing source-ref queue with compare-and-swap. A missing physical cached commit keeps source-side repair; custom ref mappings keep ordinary Git fetching so their extra destinations retain Git's semantics. Origin's standard mapping is unchanged. The Git environment helper now appends its maintenance/hook policy without discarding caller-owned configuration entries.

Narrowing the refspec alone is not a permanent fix: real Git left all 5,259 synthetic origin refs after narrowing plus `fetch --prune`, and full project refresh explicitly fetches every upstream head. Removing nondefault refs also changes the cached branch picker, explicit-base resolution and tracking-ref absence semantics. No ref-retention policy or local orphan cleanup is changed here.

## Evidence

Acceptance: the advancing default still resolves to the fetched commit with usable ancestry, one fetch and the same transferred objects; unrelated-ref completeness work disappears and baseRefresh wall/native CPU improve. Report all setup-cost regressions.

| baseRefresh metric | Parent median / p95 | Candidate median / p95 |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Wall, ms | 1174.545 / 1188.630 | 604.117 / 686.689 |
| Native CPU, ms | 980.000 / 980.000 | 290.000 / 310.000 |
| JS thread CPU, ms | 22.679 / 23.921 | 36.094 / 40.086 |
| Native peak RSS, MiB | 63.000 / 63.609 | 32.516 / 32.578 |
| Exact V8 allocation, MiB | 22.264 / 24.812 | 27.802 / 29.007 |
| Ref completeness, ms | 739.474 / 744.185 | 0.026 / 0.035 |

Both arms: one fetch, two received objects, one have. Commands: 8 → 14. A/A wall medians: 1172.91 / 1173.96 ms (0.09% drift). Five samples per arm; p95 is the maximum. The earlier exploratory run had noisy A/A controls and is not used for the final timing claim. Final repeat ran after local validation completed, on frozen head `dfd9322c83f7ea7a75b5c7f377f36d2a8c85a9ab`.

Workload: the committed `scripts/perf/worktree-base-refresh-measure.ts --advancing`, with the fixture generated by `scripts/perf/publication-ref-completeness-fixture.py`. It invokes the production default-base owner and records only the `baseRefresh` phase. The synthetic repository has 13,536 refs, 1,609 packs, 263,693 packed objects, blob:none, two shallow roots, three stale graph layers and no MIDX. Five counterbalanced A/B pairs and five A/A pairs; fresh disposable copies, native Git, Trace2, exact Node 26 V8 allocation counters and native CPU/RSS. Example:

```sh
node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs scripts/perf/worktree-base-refresh-measure.ts \
  --seed <fixture>/base --base-file <saved-parent-base-ref.ts> \
  --output <fresh-output> --advancing
```

APFS/Apple Silicon, Apple Git 2.54.0 and Node 26.12.1; local file transport. This measures base refresh, not a complete Gateway send, production network latency, an 800M-object repository or a large agent database. Linked worktrees and non-shallow behavior are also exercised by native regression tests.

Focused proof: 124 tests passed with one existing skip across base refresh, Git execution/repair/maintenance and project-clone runtime; the final extracted owner passed its 72 focused tests. The packed-unrelated-ref regression fails on the parent and passes with this change. Native SHA-1/SHA-256 shallow partial linked-worktree, conditional URL rewrite, custom mapping, missing physical cached tip and existing cancellation/authority cases pass. Codex review is clean after fixing Git's Windows null-config filename.

Before this CI repair, `pnpm check:changed` passed all code checks (types, lint, format, Knip, import cycles and ownership guards). Its only failure is the existing changelog-attribution regression, reproduced on exported exact-parent inputs at e530455b80498c0fa927bed2e2168ea7f5475786 and introduced by #194364 / 266a7aa0fe69. This is a main regression, not an ignored failure. The reviewed files are byte-identical across the rebase; the final test-only adjustment removes one duplicate assertion.

After rebasing onto `61db4b336f89957d7916580871b288d0d8c9ba82`, the test-line ratchet passes exactly: 6,589,280 / 6,589,280. The scoped 52-line allocation funds the remaining excess after trimming and using the latest parent's headroom; shared scalar unchanged. Net regression-test growth is 84 lines. Production growth is 69 lines, paying for preserved effective configuration, physical-tip/custom-mapping fallback, and source ref publication; existing remote-fetch logic was moved, not duplicated. No new runtime configuration, cache, schema or UI-imported module.

### CI repair after dfd9322c

Candidate head: `3a30674087d8374d9262ad8d15ac006a5c94763b`; rebased parent: `61db4b336f89957d7916580871b288d0d8c9ba82`.

Reproduced both reported failures locally after rebasing. Madge found the type-only `base-fetch.ts` → `base-ref.ts` backedge; `ResolvedWorktreeBase` now lives in dependency-free `base-ref.types.ts`, with no barrel re-export. Both `pnpm check:import-cycles` and `pnpm check:madge-import-cycles` report zero cycles.

All three refresh identity cases reproduced at `reachedBoundary`: the shared transport had renamed the temporary-directory prefix, so the unchanged Gateway test never invoked its identity-revocation hook. Restoring `openclaw-project-fetch-` preserves that boundary. The source-effect guard remains in `runProjectCheckoutGit` (`beforeRun: assertCurrent`, `startRun`, and the original signal), including fetch attempts/retries that write into the shared object directory and source ref updates. The unchanged Gateway clone-identity suite now passes all six real-Git cases (allowed, retired and rotated identities for clone and refresh), after reproducing three refresh failures before the fix. No test or identity/lease assertion was weakened. Fresh Codex autoreview reports no actionable P0–P2 findings; core TypeScript and scoped lint checks pass.

This repair is 12 production lines added and 12 removed, with zero new test lines; the existing scoped allocation stays at 52. The performance table above remains the measurement from pinned head `dfd9322c`, not a new post-rebase measurement: this repair changes type placement and a temporary-directory prefix, without changing fetch argv or fetch count.

<details>
<summary>Ref-policy and maintenance comparison</summary>

Git 2.56.0, five native samples per arm, same two-object/one-have update. Under shared-host load, baseline/A/A wall drift was 10.2%; narrowing's apparent wall change is noise because its census is unchanged.

| Native fetch arm | Median wall | Median completeness |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Existing refs | 1,089 ms | 718 ms |
| Narrow refspec only | 943 ms | 722 ms |
| Explicitly remove 5,257 origin refs | 710 ms | 474 ms |
| MIDX plus graph attempt | 262 ms | 170 ms |
| Removal plus MIDX | 211 ms | 132 ms |

MIDX write: 183 ms, 160 ms CPU, 55 MB peak RSS at this fixture scale. The shallow graph write changed no bytes. Whole-store MIDX rebuilding was deliberately removed by #182204; these small-fixture numbers do not establish its cost at hundreds of millions of entries. Staging removes this request's ref census without making that repository-wide maintenance mandatory.

</details>

prs.title: improve(nostr,memory-core): apply the Control UI glossary and style to plugin copy
prs.body:
## Problem

The Nostr profile panel and the Memory overview/search views had copy that didn't follow the approved Control UI glossary and style rules: Title Case buttons and labels (`Hide Advanced`, `Import from Relays`, `Save & Publish`, `Public Key`, `Edit Profile`), straight quotes and `...`, "Could not" / "does not" with no contractions, lowercase "gateway", internal jargon ("host memory search runtime"), and error messages that didn't use the "Couldn’t {verb} {thing}. {Next step}." pattern. Nostr also had one hard-coded English label (`NIP-05`) outside its catalog.

## Solution

- Rewrote the English source catalogs in `extensions/nostr/browser/i18n/locales/en.ts` and `extensions/memory-core/browser/i18n/locales/en.ts` to follow the glossary and style rules.
- **Shared-key collision:** Nostr's `common.hideAdvanced`, `common.showAdvanced`, `common.importFromRelays`, `common.saveAndPublish` and `common.publicKey` share keys with the core catalog (`ui/src/i18n/locales/en.ts`), and `ui:i18n:verify` requires a plugin's English to match the core text for any shared key. These five now live under plugin-owned `channels.nostr.*` keys.
- Removed those five core `common.*` keys from `ui/src/i18n/locales/en.ts`; nothing reads them any more (approved by Vyctor; `ui:i18n:baseline`, `ui:i18n:verify` and `tsgo:ui` pass).
- Moved the hard-coded `NIP-05` profile-fact label into the Nostr catalog (`channels.nostr.nip05`). The truncated public key now uses `…`.
- Nostr save/import failures now show `Couldn’t update/import the profile. Try again.` with the raw detail after it. Before, a failed request showed only the raw server message (e.g. `Invalid profile`). Both paths share one `failure()` helper in `controller.ts`, which also removed the duplicated prefix logic.
- Placeholders are unchanged on every key that keeps its name (`{prefix}`, `{error}`, `{message}`, `{engine}`), so existing translations still pass verification.
- **Raw error detail:** the Plugin SDK has no shared "Show details" disclosure for plugin settings views, so the raw detail stays inline after the sentence. This matches the existing core pattern (`Couldn’t load cloud device profiles. Try again. {error}`).

### Notable copy changes (old → new)

| Surface | Old | New |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Nostr button | Edit Profile | Edit profile |
| Nostr button | Save & Publish | Save & publish |
| Nostr button | Import from Relays | Import from relays |
| Nostr button | Show Advanced / Hide Advanced | Show advanced / Hide advanced |
| Nostr label | Public Key | Public key |
| Nostr label | Display Name | Display name |
| Nostr label | NIP-05 Identifier | NIP-05 identifier |
| Nostr label | Lightning Address | Lightning address |
| Nostr hint | Click "Edit Profile" to add your name, bio, and avatar. | Click “Edit profile” to add your name, bio, and avatar. |
| Nostr placeholder | Tell people about yourself... | Tell people about yourself… |
| Nostr error | Request timed out after 30 seconds; the server may still have applied the change — check the profile before retrying. | Couldn’t confirm the profile change within 30 seconds. It may still have applied, so check the profile before you try again. |
| Nostr error | Profile update failed: {error} | Couldn’t update the profile. Try again. {error} |
| Nostr error | Profile import failed: {error} | Couldn’t import the profile. Try again. {error} |
| Nostr error | Profile publish failed on all relays. | Couldn’t publish the profile to any relay. Try again. |
| Nostr public key | `abcd1234...wxyz5678` | `abcd1234…wxyz5678` |
| Memory search placeholder | Search this agent's memories | Search this agent’s memories |
| Memory search error | Memory search failed: {message} | Couldn’t search memories. Try again. {message} |
| Memory file error | Could not load this memory file: {message} | Couldn’t load this memory file. Close and reopen it to try again. {message} |
| Memory file | This memory file cannot be shown as text. | This memory file can’t be shown as text. |
| Memory notice | Update the gateway to search memories from the Control UI. | Update the Gateway to search memories from the Control UI. |
| Memory hero | Host memory search is unavailable | Memory search is unavailable |
| Memory hero | {engine} does not provide a host memory search runtime. … | {engine} doesn’t provide Gateway memory search. … |
| Memory hero | Checking this agent's memory engine and dream cycle. | Checking this agent’s memory engine and dream cycle. |
| Memory hero | The gateway is offline, so memory status is unavailable. | The Gateway is offline, so memory status is unavailable. |
| Memory button | Open Settings | Open settings |

**Counts:** 28 user-visible strings changed (16 Nostr catalog strings, 10 Memory catalog strings, 1 hard-coded Nostr label moved into the catalog, 1 ellipsis in the formatted public key). 1 string moved into a translation file (`NIP-05`). 5 Nostr keys moved from `common.*` to `channels.nostr.*`.

## Impact

- English-locale users see consistent sentence case, contractions and typography, and errors that say what failed and what to do next.
- Foreign locales: translated.json, `.i18n/*.tm.jsonl` and `*.meta.json` weren't hand-edited. Keys that kept their names still show their existing (now stale) translations. The five moved Nostr keys show English until the post-merge control-ui-locale-refresh bot runs. Their old translations stay as unused entries (`unused_translations=110`, which verify allows).
- No docs quote the changed labels.

## Evidence

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run extensions/nostr/browser/profile.test.tsx extensions/memory-core/browser/memories.test.tsx extensions/memory-core/browser/overview.test.tsx`: 3 files, 51 tests passed. The assertions on changed English are updated. The Swedish locale-switch test now waits for an unchanged translated label (`Användarnamn`), because `saveAndPublish` moved to a new key.
- `pnpm ui:i18n:verify`: green (memory-core keys=67, nostr keys=62, 22 locales each; no shared-key disagreement; referenced keys resolve).
- `pnpm tsgo:extensions` and `pnpm tsgo:extensions:test`: pass.
- `oxlint` on both browser dirs: 0 errors. The 2 warnings are pre-existing, in the untouched `memory-core/browser/components.tsx`.
- `pnpm check:control-ui-controllers`: OK. `oxfmt` applied. `git diff --check`: clean.
- pr-simplify: every hunk is copy, a key reference, or the shared `failure()` helper, which replaced duplicated prefix logic. No new state or modules.
- Local review: autoreview (Codex `gpt-6.1-sol`, medium), `--mode branch`, base `d59f00281eb0216`, head `0e93cfcfc4e6`, max priority P2. Result: `scoped-clean`, no findings. Local ClawSweeper wasn't set up in this checkout.

Before/after screenshots are pending before landing (visual gate).

Not landing: requested by maintainer; screenshots pending before merge.

## Work sessions

- [Original discussion with @vyctorbrzezowski](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/dashboard/8ee302fc-4575-4506-92a8-1739453b9b71)
- [Implementation and verification](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/subagent/768dfbde-95a0-4e7a-94fc-906d3a5c6c7f)

## Worked on by

- @vyctorbrzezowski

prs.title: fix(gateway): native apps fail to connect after fractional idle-time beacons
prs.body:
Fixes #195501 ☁️

## What Problem This Solves

macOS and iOS operator clients can fail to connect after another client reports fractional idle seconds, because the hello presence snapshot promises an integer.

## User Impact

Native clients can continue connecting after fractional idle-time beacons. No configuration changes or migrations are required.

## Why This Change Was Made

Apply the three-file diff from `saariuslystoned/openclaw:fix/gateway-presence-integer-last-input` at `0cb8fe70ecd5f9f3fe0453a0d6afad2f558395c0` onto refreshed main (`61db4b336f89957d7916580871b288d0d8c9ba82`). Both existing presence writers floor finite non-negative idle seconds and clear invalid numeric values, keeping normalization at the presence owner rather than adding client-side workarounds.

The focused regression adds 23 test lines; its separate allocation protects fractional input, invalid-value clearing, and the upsert/heartbeat path without changing the shared test budget. Simplification review retained the existing owner and one shared normalizer: production +16/-1, tests +23/-0.

## Evidence

- Regression fails on refreshed main with `expected 4.5 to be 4`; with the fix, `src/infra/system-presence.test.ts` passes 9/9 (1.52 seconds runner wall time; 526 ms Vitest duration).
- Existing consumer suites pass: `src/gateway/server.health.test.ts` 2/2 and `packages/gateway-protocol/src/schema/system-event.test.ts` 2/2.
- Core production and infra-test typechecks, targeted lint, formatting, and `git diff --check` pass.
- Auto Review, local snapshot against `61db4b336f89957d7916580871b288d0d8c9ba82`: scoped-clean at the default P0 priority, no findings. Review covers the supplied diff, not unchanged context.
- The applied files match the fork commit exactly. Native macOS/iOS reconnects were not exercised; CI timing and broad CI results are pending.

Contributed by @saariuslystoned.

## Work sessions

Linked for team reference; these sessions aren’t public.

- [Discussion, implementation and verification](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/dashboard/b43f2919-3714-40e4-a1d5-fb7a3ba35f1d)

Co-Authored-By: Bobby Bones <159389674+saariuslystoned@users.noreply.github.com>

prs.title: fix(openclaw-id): allow one automatic node pairing per approved listing
prs.body:
Related: #193993 (`openclaw node join`), #194001 (Gateway node admission and pairing)

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: an OpenClaw ID node that the owner removed on the Access page and then approved again with a new invitation still needs a second manual approval under **Devices** before it can connect.

## User Impact

When an owner approves a node again with a new invitation after removing it, the node pairs automatically on its next connection, the same as on its first approval. The behavior everywhere else stays the same:

| Case | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| First owner approval, first connection | pairs automatically | pairs automatically |
| A second device using the same node key and approval | manual | manual |
| Pairing removed only under **Devices** while the node is still approved | manual | manual |
| Node removed on **Access**, then approved again with a new invitation | **manual (bug)** | pairs automatically, once |
| First connection paired manually, then that pairing removed | manual | manual |

## Why This Change Was Made

The Gateway records that a node key has used its one automatic pairing. That record was keyed by the node key alone and deliberately survives removal, so a second owner approval of the same key could never pair automatically. The record is now keyed by the listing the owner signed: the claw, its root key, and the sequence number the node was listed at. These are the same provenance fields already stored on the node token and used to remove its pairings.

The protocol gives a node a fresh listing sequence only when the owner approves it again after it was removed. Approving a node that is still listed keeps its sequence. So a new automatic pairing always needs a new owner approval on Access.

**Security:**
- A new automatic pairing needs a new owner approval: the owner compares the six-digit code and explicitly approves.
- The commands and capabilities granted are unchanged. Only the subset the owner reviewed in that approval qualifies.
- A pairing removed under **Devices** never returns on the same listing.
- A manual approval over the tunnel still uses up that listing's automatic pairing, in the same transaction that issues its token.

**Upgrade:** there is no migration. Old records keyed by the node key alone are simply not read. They exist only on main and development builds: #194001 merged at 09:17 PST on 2026-11-08, after 2026.11.2 was published at 01:48 PST, and 2026.11.2's `dist` does not contain `devicePairing.openclawIdNode`. Accepted edge case for development builds only: after upgrading, a still-approved node listing can pair automatically once more without a new owner approval. That includes a device whose **Devices** pairing was removed by hand, or a second device on that listing if it connects before the existing device's next token issuance.

## Evidence

- **Red on main, green with the fix**, in the real-Gateway node-pairing suite (`server.auth.openclaw-id-node-pairing.test.ts`, real SQLite pairing broker):
  - New test: after removal and a new approval, the node pairs automatically once. Under that listing, a second device and a **Devices**-only removal both stay manual. On main it fails with `expected false to be true` at the re-pair.
  - Extended test: a manual pairing uses up its listing's automatic pairing, and a newly approved listing then pairs automatically. On main it fails at the re-pair.
- **Focused suites:** 17/17 passed across `authority.nodes`, the node-pairing suite, `node-principal` and the node pairing lifecycle tests.
- **Independent Astra review:** no P0–P2 findings. One P3 docs wording finding (re-approving a still-listed key keeps its listing) is fixed. It also confirmed the development-build upgrade consequence named above.
- **Static checks:** `pnpm tsgo:core`, scoped oxlint and oxfmt, `git diff --check`, the mock-exports ratchet and `pnpm deadcode:exports` (0 entries) all pass. The test-line ratchet passes against `origin/main` with an allocation of exactly 34, this PR's net test lines. The 32 lines of reported slack were already free on main.
- **Before, live staging (2026-11-08):** in #193993's live run on the staging testnet, a node was removed on Access, approved again with a new invitation and admitted over the tunnel. The Gateway then answered `device pairing required` and left a non-repair pending node request. The after evidence comes from the same live flow on a build that includes this fix and will be added here.

prs.title: fix: native Codex oauth/token without a host profile should still forward unlisted models
prs.body:
Fixes #194980

### What Problem This Solves

A native Codex login that has not selected a host auth profile is an `oauth` or `token` account. `resolveCodexForwardCompatModel` forwarded a model missing from the static patch table only when `authProfileMode` was absent. Models already in the static table are unchanged.

### Why This Change Was Made

The unlisted branch now accepts `authProfileMode === undefined || authProfileMode === "oauth" || authProfileMode === "token"`. It still requires `authProfileId === undefined` and `providerConfig?.auth === undefined`. `api_key`, and `oauth` that already has an `authProfileId`, still return `undefined`.

An earlier head also passed that account mode in from agent execution and off-catalog runtime choice. That expansion did not finish runtime selection: the later membership check still reads model scope, and the Codex auth policy does not belong in core. Those callers and the account-scope readiness API are removed. The repair stays on the provider resolver.

The existing spark-routing test moved to `extensions/openai/openai-codex-spark-routing.test.ts` so the provider test file could take the new cases without growing past its line cap. That test's assertions are unchanged.

### User Impact

A profile-free native Codex `oauth` or `token` context can resolve a model id that is not yet in the static patch table when that context reaches the provider resolver. A selected host profile and API-key auth still do not receive that forward path.

### Evidence

Resolver contract, exact command `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/openai/openai-provider.test.ts -t "delegates an unlisted first-party model|does not extend native model forwarding" --maxWorkers=1` on `bd5140669e8`: parent exit 1 for `oauth` and `token`; head exit 0. `api_key` with no profile, and `oauth` with `authProfileId` `openai:selected`, stay `undefined`.

## What Problem This Solves

OpenClaw rejects `medium` for Gemini 3.1 Pro Preview, or sends `HIGH` when the setting reaches the Google request builder directly.

## User Impact

`/think medium` and `--thinking medium` now select Gemini 3.1 Pro Preview's native `MEDIUM` effort. The default for this reasoning model stays adaptive.

## Why This Change Was Made

The model policy, payload sanitizer, and shared Google request builder applied the original Gemini 3 Pro level rules to 3.1 Pro Preview. The policy excluded `medium`, and the payload layers independently mapped it to `HIGH`. Use a shared model check to recognize the documented 3.1 Pro Preview IDs at all three boundaries. Original Pro mappings, fixed-tier routes, and legacy numeric budgets keep their previous behavior. [Google's thinking-level documentation](https://ai.google.dev/gemini-api/docs/thinking)

## Evidence

- 362 focused tests passed across 10 files on the implementation commit, including GenerateContent, Interactions, provider policy, and prompt-prefix stability. Core and extension type checks, lint, and formatting passed.

prs.title: fix: avoid full-history downloads when agents fetch fork PRs
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes multi-gigabyte history downloads when an agent reviews a contributor PR by fetching its GitHub fork URL from a shallow workspace projection. Related: #195433, #195498.

## User Impact

Normal agent GitHub fork fetches in blobless repositories transfer commits and trees; checkout and diff fetch needed file contents later. HTTPS and both standard GitHub SSH URL forms work. Explicit filters and `--no-filter` remain authoritative; full repositories and non-GitHub URLs retain native defaults. This uses the existing POSIX agent Git wrapper, including its Docker/Podman mount; invoking a Git binary directly bypasses it.

## Why This Change Was Made

Git's default partial filter belongs to an exact remote name, so configuring `origin` and the origin URL does not cover a contributor URL. The existing wrapper now supplies `--filter=blob:none` for GitHub URL fetches in repositories already configured for blobless fetching. Native Git persists the fork promisor and handles later hydration. Global Git options, including repository selection, are preserved. No fork list, separate remote registry, host object-store mount, application configuration, database change, or model-facing text is added.

Git v2.53 source explicitly [registers filtered fetch remotes](https://github.com/git/git/blob/v2.53.0/builtin/fetch.c#L2064-L2095) and [stores their promisor/filter keys](https://github.com/git/git/blob/v2.53.0/list-objects-filter-options.c#L310-L365). URL rewriting changes the transport address, not the remote's filter identity; wildcard/default filter experiments also fetched blobs. Native multi-promisor fallback may print an origin rejection before the fork successfully supplies its unique blob.

## Evidence

A synthetic 2,037,976-object repository with 62,000 files / 1.18 GB current content was projected by the real checkout owner. The incident-shaped fork branch fetch ran through the exported agent shim, with local transport mapped from a synthetic GitHub URL. Two fresh baseline projections and two candidate projections produced:

| Metric | Before | After |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Objects added per fetch | 1,974,966 | 988,964 |
| Blobs added per fetch | 986,002 | 0 |
| Pack bytes added | 975,382,614 | 96,430,042–96,430,075 |
| Median fetch wall time | 56.907 s | 23.804 s |
| Median process-tree CPU | 166.43 s | 117.68 s |
| Median peak RSS | 1.642 GB | 640 MB |

In both candidate samples, diff hydrated exactly one fork-only blob absent from origin, then checkout hydrated 1,000 additional current blobs. Source config stayed byte-identical; projections used no alternates. This is macOS/APFS, Apple Git 2.54, warm filesystem, local transport proof, not live production or Linux-container timing. A separate native semantics probe passed on Git 2.56. Cumulative native allocation was not measured.

The committed regression runs the real projection builder and agent exec tool. It fails on the base because the fetch imports both fork blobs; it passes with the fix. It also covers HTTPS/SSH URLs, `git -C`, `--`, lazy hydration, explicit opt-out, and full repositories. The focused shim/launcher/sandbox suites passed 44 tests (the expanded real-Git test took 4.67 seconds; hosted CI timing is pending). Targeted production/test typechecks, lint/format, the exact 71-line allocation ratchet, and independent Codex P0–P2 autoreview pass. `pnpm check:changed` completed with one inherited failure: 20 forbidden changelog thanks entries. Every other selected check passed, including all core/test type graphs, full core/tooling lint, dead exports, and runtime guards. The same 20 violations reproduce using the exact main parent `08f98e29e816fb199b51e3c5c16e643f33fc55a5` checker and inputs; they were introduced by `266a7aa0fe69` / #194364 and are absent from that commit's parent failure set. This is an unresolved main regression, not a green aggregate check.

Production growth is 41 lines in the existing shim, required to preserve Git's global options and insert the filter before fetch arguments. The 71-line test allocation extends the existing integration fixture instead of adding another harness. The simplification pass leaves native Git owning promisor registration and hydration.

prs.title: fix(gateway): avoid slow group changes with unrelated stores
prs.body:
Closes #167716
Replaces #167717, closed by its author while this adoption was in progress.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: renaming or deleting a small session group performs unnecessary category-write sweeps of unrelated agent stores, including stores left by retired agents.

## User Impact

User impact: group rename and delete skip stores with no members to move; empty groups require no category-write sweep. No client, configuration, schema, or migration changes are required. A concurrent assignment in a skipped store retains the source group and returns a retryable partial-change error rather than losing membership.

## Why This Change Was Made

Reuse the membership snapshot already produced by the existing owner to select the stores to update. Keep category-write authorization, session recency, and the independent all-store membership check before retirement unchanged. The original production change is preserved; its two regressions are adapted to the current shared fixtures.

Original fix and regression design by @Marvinthebored in #167717, adopted at the author's request. The local implementation commit retains Marvinthebored as author and includes the verified co-author trailer.

## Work sessions

- [Discussion, implementation and verification](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/dashboard/dc37b418-938e-4ae6-a533-f3b93a91cde4)

## Evidence

### Tempbook qualification status — 2026-11-08

**Not ready for publication or landing.** Current main still does the unnecessary category-worker sweeps, and the candidate removes them without a correctness failure. Current latency gains remain **unproven**: the required quiet-host ABAB campaign was not run. During this work the 16-core macOS host had unrelated native builds/tests and simulator activity, with observed 1-minute load above 110 and about 18–20% CPU idle at the busiest sampled point; after our checks finished, load remained above 50 with about 49–55% idle. No unrelated process was stopped. There are **zero qualifying cold or warm latency samples**, so there is no present-day median/p95/range comparison or acceptance claim. The historical October results below are context only.

**Pinned comparison:** current-main baseline `61db4b336f89957d7916580871b288d0d8c9ba82`, tree `a6fffd842d497bdbd78b3f8ebe4a4f5102a0522e`; corrected prospective merge `ffa2066bd16e51081ea0dda3ad16493d9017334c`, tree `f7b1e6dfcee69941668c4d152d8ce0a8300f6908`. The local native prepared head is `9ffe67d4c44958ecdd7a7d113eb1fa8c381ecf47`; it has not been pushed. Published head remains `c9a370084a10b150cdf607df2616457d32a4538e`. The comparison contains current main plus the PR and a test-only consolidation, rather than comparing the old PR runtime against main. Production and benchmark code were not changed during this qualification.

During preparation, main advanced four commits to `2995860edbf34e5a4d18793a118a13c273a2bd98`. No session-group or category-write files changed in that delta; it does include SQLite header/read-only-location changes. The tests and diagnostic above are bound to the captured `61db4b3` baseline, not that newer runtime. Refresh both comparison trees before the still-pending timing campaign.

Both arms use Node **24.22.1**, separate frozen pnpm **12.15.0** installs with identical lockfile bytes, and fresh `sourcePerformance` builds. Full source, build-info, entry hashes and build-file manifests are retained with the local proof. The same committed `scripts/perf/session-group-registration-measure.ts` drives both arms (SHA-256 `11c6d03bf5602874a99ca9391bb8e911e537115909d37f1c26df80fb7c32399f`).

| --- | ---: | ---: |
| One-member rename: category-worker calls across two stores | 2 | 1 |
| Empty-group deletion: category-worker calls across two stores | 2 | 0 |

These count calls to the existing category-write worker owner, **not instrumented physical writes or worker-process spawns**. Current workers are persistent. The independent retirement check still scans all stores. Shared physical stores, discovered retired owners, archived membership, unchanged session recency, affected counts, unrelated categories, authorization changes, interrupted mutations and retry remain covered by source review and focused tests. A concurrent assignment into a skipped store retains the source group and returns the retryable partial-change error; retry completes.

**Validation:** 49 focused Gateway/RPC/sharing tests passed (148.48 s wall). The original candidate exceeded the current test-line budget by 16 lines. Core types, focused test/benchmark types, lint, formatting, line caps, script erasability and diff checks pass. The first benchmark typecheck failed because the temporary external config inferred the wrong root directory; correcting that config resolved TS6059 without changing product code or compiler checks. Fresh full-context P0–P2 autoreview found no actionable findings after the final test repair.

**Separate CPU diagnostic, excluded from latency qualification:** both real built Gateway CLIs completed 63 authenticated loopback mutation requests each, including first-use plus 20 warm rename/populated-delete/empty-delete cycles and all membership/catalog/recency/bystander readbacks. Each emitted 25 valid CPU profiles, including session-group/SQLite owner paths, and shut down with exit 0. No model call, provider credential or real user state was used.

prs.title: fix(codex): redact credentials in dynamic tool error content
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Thrown and failed Codex dynamic-tool paths were putting raw `errorMessage` / failure `message` text into `contentItems` without running it through `sanitizeToolResult`. Successful and middleware-adjusted result paths already redacted credentials, so a thrown tool error that embedded a bearer token (or similar secret) could still surface the credential in the app-server tool-result content.

**Configuration-dependent gap:** `formatToolExecutionErrorMessage` → `redactSensitiveText` uses configured `logging.redactPatterns` **in place of** defaults. Model-visible `sanitizeToolResult` / `redactModelVisibleToolPayloadText` **combines** custom patterns with built-in tool payload patterns. So under a nonmatching custom `redactPatterns` config, diagnostic/error formatting alone still leaks an unregistered synthetic bearer, while catch-path `sanitizeToolResult` keeps built-in bearer protection.

## Why This Change Was Made

Reuse the shared `sanitizeToolResult` helper from `openclaw/plugin-sdk/agent-harness-runtime` on the two remaining failure content builders:

- `createCodexDynamicToolBridge` catch path in `dynamic-tools.ts` (thrown execution errors)
- `createFailedDynamicToolResponse` in `dynamic-tool-response-state.ts` (failed response factory)

Non-goals: no change to success-path redaction, budget truncation, or middleware ordering.

## User Impact

**Before:** A dynamic tool that threw (or failed via the shared failed-response helper) could return `contentItems` containing unsanitized credentials from the error text — especially when `logging.redactPatterns` replaced diagnostic defaults with patterns that do not cover bearer tokens.

**After:** Thrown/failed dynamic-tool error content is redacted with the same `sanitizeToolResult` used on successful result content (built-ins always apply for model-visible output).

## Evidence

- Production catch path: `extensions/codex/src/app-server/dynamic-tools.ts` now sets `text: sanitizeToolResult(errorMessage)`.
- Shared failed factory: `extensions/codex/src/app-server/dynamic-tool-response-state.ts` sanitizes the failure `message` before building `contentItems`.
- Regression: `extensions/codex/src/app-server/dynamic-tools.test.ts` spies `readLoggingConfig` with nonmatching `redactPatterns` `[String.raw`\bunrelated-only-[A-Za-z0-9]+\b`]`, asserts `formatToolExecutionErrorMessage` still contains the synthetic bearer (before), and asserts model-visible `contentItems` do not (after `sanitizeToolResult`). Mock restored in `finally`.
- Diagnostic harness: `scripts/codex-dynamic-tool-error-redact-proof.mts` prints the actual protocol response JSON.





### Custom-pattern regression (exact head `67505f4ca5c4`)

```text
Product head: 67505f4ca5c482f9eac9474cd0a6f25bf4afc2bd
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/codex/src/app-server/dynamic-tools.thrown-error-redaction.test.ts --reporter=verbose
PASS redacts credentials from thrown dynamic tool error content items under custom logging patterns
```

Configures logging.redactPatterns=["never-match-custom-redact-pattern-141271"] via isolated OPENCLAW_CONFIG_PATH so formatToolExecutionErrorMessage still contains the synthetic bearer (defaults bypassed), then asserts the bridge response does not.

## Real behavior proof

- **Behavior or issue addressed:** Thrown dynamic-tool error content could include unsanitized credentials when diagnostic redact patterns replace defaults.
- **Canonical reachability path:** `createCodexDynamicToolBridge` → tool `execute` throws → `formatToolExecutionErrorMessage` → catch builds `contentItems` with `sanitizeToolResult(errorMessage)` → `toCodexDynamicToolProtocolResponse`.
- **Boundary crossed:** Extension dynamic-tool error content → shared `sanitizeToolResult` from plugin-sdk agent-harness-runtime (model-visible policy merges built-ins).
- **Shared helper / provider constraint check:** Reused existing `sanitizeToolResult`; no new helper.
- **Real environment tested:** Local diagnostic harness against production `createCodexDynamicToolBridge` + `toCodexDynamicToolProtocolResponse` under custom `logging.redactPatterns`. **Live Codex binary was NOT used** — this records the actual protocol response object returned toward Codex, not a full app-server binary round-trip.
- **Exact steps or command run after this patch:**

```text
$ node --import tsx scripts/codex-dynamic-tool-error-redact-proof.mts
# writes /workspace/codex-runtime-proof.txt
```

- **Evidence after fix (diagnostic transcript):**

```text
# Codex dynamic-tool thrown-error redaction diagnostic
# Generated: 2026-09-07T14:53:48.289Z (UTC)
# Proof surface: createCodexDynamicToolBridge → handleToolCall catch path
#               → toCodexDynamicToolProtocolResponse (JSON contentItems)
# Live Codex binary: NOT used (unavailable / not required for this harness)
# Synthetic credential only — non-usable fixture.

logging.redactPatterns = ["\\bunrelated-only-[A-Za-z0-9]+\\b"]
(nonmatching custom patterns replace diagnostic defaults;
 model-visible sanitizeToolResult merges built-ins.)

## Before catch-path sanitizeToolResult
formatToolExecutionErrorMessage(...) under custom redactPatterns:
{
  "formatted": "Upstream failed: Authorization: Bearer bearer-model-visible-credential-1234567890"
}
contains synthetic credential: true

sanitizeToolResult(formatted) alone (model-visible built-ins):
{
  "sanitizedAlone": "Upstream failed: Authorization: Bearer bearer…7890"
}
contains synthetic credential: false

## After fix: protocol response returned toward Codex app-server
toCodexDynamicToolProtocolResponse(createCodexDynamicToolBridge.handleToolCall(...)):
{
  "contentItems": [
    {
      "type": "inputText",
      "text": "Upstream failed: Authorization: Bearer bearer…7890"
    }
  ],
  "success": false
}

success: false
contentItems text contains synthetic credential: false
contentItems text contains "Authorization: Bearer": true

## Summary
- Under custom nonmatching redactPatterns, diagnostic formatting LEAKS the synthetic bearer.
- After sanitizeToolResult on the catch path, protocol contentItems do NOT contain it.
- This records the actual protocol response object, not Vitest expect() output.
```

- **Vitest (distinguishing regression):**

```text
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/codex/src/app-server/dynamic-tools.test.ts -t 'redacts credentials from thrown' --reporter=verbose
 ✓ |extension-codex| extensions/codex/src/app-server/dynamic-tools.test.ts > createCodexDynamicToolBridge > redacts credentials from thrown dynamic tool error content items 38ms
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  1 passed | 172 skipped (173)
[test] passed 1 Vitest shard in 25.56s
```

- **Observed result after fix:** Under custom nonmatching `redactPatterns`, diagnostic formatting still contains the synthetic bearer; protocol `contentItems` after the catch-path sanitizer do not (`Authorization: Bearer bearer…7890`).
- **What was not tested:** Live Codex app-server / `@openai/codex` binary round-trip. Proof surface is the real bridge + protocol response object.
- **Fix classification:** Root cause fix

- [x] AI-assisted (Cursor)
- [x] I understand what the code does
- [x] Change is focused and does not mix unrelated concerns

prs.title: fix(agents): retract running deferred dispatcher when nested target starts
prs.body:
Fixes #194168

## What Problem This Solves

Discord progress mode with `toolProgress: true` renders **two identical rows** for each deferred tool call while it runs: one for the `dispatch_action` dispatcher and one for its nested target. Both rows share the same label and `running` status at the same time, even though the transcript records a single execution. This fix retracts the dispatcher row as soon as its nested target starts, so the live draft shows exactly one row per tool call. Independent tool calls with identical labels remain separate.

## Problem

With Discord progress mode and `toolProgress: true`, a deferred tool call dispatched through `dispatch_action` renders as **two identical rows** in the live draft while it runs: one for the dispatcher and one for its nested target. Both rows show the same label and the same `running` status at the same time.

The transcript shows each tool call executed exactly once.

## Root cause

`dispatch_action` is a pure forwarding wrapper. It publishes its own visible prepared item (`tool:<dispatcher-call-id>`) when it starts, and its nested target (`tool_call:<parent>:<name>:<seq>`, `parentToolCallId` = dispatcher id) publishes a second visible item with an identical label. The existing wrapper suppression (`resolveCompletedActivityWrappers` / `finalizeToolActivity`) only collapses a completed wrapper **at run termination**, so while the target is still running both rows stay on the draft.

## Fix

Represent a deferred dispatcher and its nested target as one live operation at the producer (`src/agents/embedded-agent-subscribe.handlers.tools.start.ts`):

- When a nested target starts (`lifecycleProvenance: "nested"`) **with a visible activity**, look up its parent dispatcher from the tracked tool starts.
- If the parent is a `dispatch_action` wrapper that is still visible, retract its row by emitting an `update` item event with `hideFromChannelProgress: true` (the channel progress compositor clears the row by item id).
- Persist `hideFromChannelProgress` on the parent's start record so the dispatcher's terminal event stays hidden too — the run-termination collapse in `finalizeToolActivity` is unchanged.

A nested target whose activity is hidden (for example a routine `progress_card`, or a `wait`/`process.poll` child) does **not** replace the dispatcher: the shared activity owner (`resolveCompletedActivityWrappers`) keeps a wrapper visible when none of its children contributes a visible row, so the dispatcher stays visible until terminal collapse. This matches the routine-wrapper preservation policy established in #165358 and avoids leaving neither the dispatcher nor a hidden routine target countable.

A `dispatch_action` that fails to dispatch (no nested target) keeps its own visible row with the error, so no information is lost. Independent tool calls with identical labels stay separate because they have no parent/child relationship.

## Evidence

### Regressions (each fails on the prior head, passes with the fix)

1. `retracts a running deferred dispatcher once its nested target starts` — a visible `web_search` target replaces the running dispatcher row.
   - Before: the dispatcher receives no retraction update → assertion `expected [] to have a length of 1` fails.
   - After: exactly one `phase: "update"` item event with `hideFromChannelProgress: true`, and the target row stays visible.

2. `keeps a running deferred dispatcher when its nested target is routine` — a `progress_card` target (hidden activity) does not replace the dispatcher.
   - Before: the dispatcher is retracted anyway → assertion `expected [ { itemId: 'tool:dispatcher', ... } ] to have a length of +0 but got 1` fails.
   - After: no retraction update is emitted and the dispatcher stays visible.

```
Test Files  1 passed (1)
     Tests  15 passed (15)
```

### Related suites (all pass)

- `src/infra/agent-activity-events.test.ts` — 25 passed
- `src/channels/progress-draft-compositor.test.ts` — 59 passed
- `extensions/discord/src/monitor/message-handler.draft-preview.rest.test.ts` — 16 passed

### CI-equivalent checks

- `oxlint --type-aware --deny=warn` — clean
- `node scripts/run-format.mts --check` — clean
- `check-test-lines-ratchet` — pass (new test lines covered by `config/test-lines-allocations/issue-194168-deferred-dispatcher.txt`, 87)
- `check-test-mock-exports --prune` — 6387 → 6387, no new violations
- typecheck on changed files — 0 errors

## What was not tested

No live Discord round trip was run in this environment. The regression exercises the producer event stream (`handleToolExecutionStart`), which is the source both channels and the Control UI consume; the Discord draft-preview test suite confirms the retraction path (`hideFromChannelProgress` + item id) is honored by the compositor.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes candidate update checks and rehearsals failing when a nested SQLite header probe reads successfully but cannot remove its private snapshot.

## User Impact

Candidate updates continue with a warning for disposable header-snapshot cleanup failures. Read, acquisition, validation, identity, and native read-close errors still fail; Doctor and other default callers retain strict cleanup. Persistent cleanup failures can leave temporary directories for later cleanup.

## Why This Change Was Made

Pass the existing candidate-only `cleanupFailure: "warn"` policy through both nested header probes. Reuse the existing warning logger and directory owner, retaining bounded removal retries and later cleanup custody. Cleanup warnings preserve the successful result or original read error.

Header inspection now lives in a small sibling module, with all callers and mocks migrated. Snapshot preparation stays within its local size budget: 660 counted lines against a 700-line limit. The shared source-read timeout remains 30 seconds. Both candidate operations load this inspector lazily at their execution boundary, avoiding mixed static/dynamic imports in production bundles.

prs.title: fix(node): reconnect after OpenClaw ID server rotation
prs.body:
Related: #193993, #193982

## What Problem This Solves

Saved OpenClaw ID nodes keep dialing the server key from enrollment, so an honest Gateway key rotation cannot be discovered on reconnect.

## User Impact

Nodes refresh and verify current signed server authority and membership before connecting, retire an active connection when its server key changes, and preserve learned trust across restart and refused re-enrollment. Verified node removal stops the host with a rejoin instruction.

Preview targets without an explicit Discovery origin must rejoin. Pairing assumes the invitation remains secret; the six-digit comparison does not protect against a stolen invitation combined with control of pairing delivery. Existing freshness/v1 bounded-replay limits remain.

## Why This Change Was Made

Enrollment and reconnect share one bounded, node-signed Discovery client and descriptor verifier. The canonical SQLite writer retains the strongest binding pin, membership order, and binding-retirement facts without overwriting unrelated node settings. Persistence completes before dialing; failed persistence stops further attempts. Periodic authority refresh continues during active traffic.

This is one repair commit on top of `openclaw-517/node-join`, not a replacement for the draft feature stack.

## Evidence

- Original source failed the real Unix bridge regressions (8 failed, 4 passed), the protocol retirement regression (1 failed, 8 passed), and the SQLite stale-startup regression. The repair passed all 106 focused tests, including 21 SQLite config tests and four native Gateway integration tests. prs.title: feat(iroh-ffi): add uniffi bindings for the OpenClaw ID tunnel
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The native OpenClaw ID node apps (macOS, iOS, Android) need an iroh transport that meets `openclaw/tunnel/1`. The official `iroh-ffi` bindings (v1.0–v1.2) can't: they report a closed connection only as reason text, with no numeric application close code, and they offer no QUIC keep-alive setting. Their macOS package is also Apple-silicon only.

## User Impact

None yet. This adds a standalone crate that generates Swift and Kotlin bindings. No app uses it until the macOS/iOS and Android node PRs stacked on this one.

## Why This Change Was Made

Josh chose an OpenClaw-owned UniFFI crate over waiting for an upstream patch or deferring native nodes. The crate pins the same iroh version as the Node addon (1.4.1) and adds UniFFI 0.31.2. It exposes only what the tunnel needs:
- bind with iroh's Minimal preset, only the selected relay and a required keep-alive;
- connect to an already-verified endpoint key;
- bidirectional streams;
- **full-range numeric close codes** (`i64`, so every legal QUIC code 0…2^62−1 round-trips);
- a home-relay watcher that ends on shutdown;
- a shutdown that interrupts pending reads, accepts and connects;
- an optional `CancelToken` on `connect`, `openBi` and `acceptBi`, so a caller can abandon one dial or one stream wait without shutting down the endpoint or closing the connection.

The native seed copy is zeroized on every bind path. There is no key getter, default relay, discovery service, pkarr, or TCP proxy. The existing Node/N-API crate is unchanged.

Two things apps must handle:
- **Swift `Task.cancel()` does not reach Rust** (UniFFI 0.31.2's generated Swift has no cancellation hook). Pass a `CancelToken` to `connect` and cancel it from the task's cancellation handler; use `stop`/`reset` for streams and `endpoint.shutdown()` for a whole route. **Kotlin must not cancel a coroutine around a native call either:** UniFFI 0.31.2 lowers the result when the Rust future becomes ready, so freeing a ready future before it's lifted leaks the handle (an open `Connection`, or an `Endpoint` still holding its key). Kotlin runs native calls under `NonCancellable` and uses the same explicit signals.
- **Android** must call `OpenClawIrohAndroid.install(applicationContext)` before `bind`. Without it, `bind` fails closed.

## Evidence

Run locally (Linux, Rust 1.99):
- `cargo test --locked`: 6 tests, all passing. Five are real loopback integration tests covering streams, the exact 2^62−1 close code, rejection of -1 and 2^62, keep-alive validation, the relay watcher ending, shutdown interrupting a blocked read, accept and connect, a `CancelToken` aborting one hanging dial while the endpoint stays usable, and a `CancelToken` abandoning a blocked `acceptBi` and a credit-starved `openBi` while the connection keeps working in both directions. The sixth is a unit test for seed erasure.
- `cargo clippy --locked --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings`, fmt, actionlint and shellcheck all clean.
- Bindings regenerate deterministically. A temporary Python UniFFI smoke test ran the async transport.
- The release host library was 13,180,024 bytes before the `CancelToken` change.
- An independent read-only review of the first commit found no verified P0–P2 issues. A second review of the follow-ups through `3113717` (CI NDK setup, `CancelToken` on `connect`, the jni fix) checked the cancel race, handshake cleanup on drop, FFI `Send`/`Sync` and binding checksums, and found one P2. Its finding: calls typed as the generated `EndpointProtocol` must pass `cancel:` explicitly, because Swift protocol requirements carry no default arguments. That's left as is: this API is new, nothing outside this stack calls it, and callers are expected to pass a token for each dial. The later stream-wait tokens (`2dd6b82`) follow the same reviewed pattern and are covered by their own test.

Left to this PR's CI (the `iroh native binding` workflow, which runs on drafts). At `92c2506`, **Linux and Android pass**: all four Android ABIs (arm64-v8a, armeabi-v7a, x86_64, x86) with 16 KiB alignment. Both macOS slices build. The iOS slices failed there: `netdev` 0.46.x (pulled in by iroh's `netwatch` 0.19.3) uses `libc::in6_ifreq` on every Apple target, and `libc` 0.2.190 limited that type to macOS.

`Cargo.lock` now pins `libc` at 0.2.189, the version n0's official iroh-ffi v1.2.0 ships its iOS builds with; nothing else in the lockfile moves. `libc` has no RustSec or OSV advisories, and the one memory-safety fix in 0.2.190–0.2.191 (`af_alg_iv` trait impls) isn't used by any locked crate. `scripts/check-pins.sh` fails if the pin drifts while `netdev` 0.46.0–0.46.3 is locked, and a new `iroh native binding audit` workflow runs it plus `cargo audit` (0.22.2) on lockfile changes and weekly. The pin comes off once a `netdev` that skips that code on iOS reaches the lockfile (0.47 already does; `netwatch` 0.20 still needs 0.46). Locally, all six Rust tests pass with the pin. **CI at `031aad5` passes:** [`iroh native binding`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/42314731390): linux, android and **apple**. The apple job built all five Rust targets (macOS arm64 + x86_64, iOS device, iOS simulator arm64 + x86_64), wrote the three-slice XCFramework (`macos-arm64_x86_64`, `ios-arm64`, `ios-arm64_x86_64-simulator`) and typechecked the generated Swift. [`iroh native binding audit`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/42314731430) passed: the pin check, and `cargo audit` over 412 locked crates found no vulnerabilities, only two unmaintained-crate warnings (`basic-toml` RUSTSEC-2026-0374, `paste` RUSTSEC-2024-0436). `OPENCLAW_IROH_APPLE_PLATFORMS=macos scripts/build-apple.sh` still builds a macOS-only XCFramework, and `PACKAGING.md` documents the pin and the opt-in contract for Swift consumers.

Consumer-lane evidence (not this PR's CI): the Android lane built a host `.so` from `92c2506` with locked, offline Rust 1.99 (13,185,944 bytes, sha256 `5075327bfbed3e3cf89ab261b24648917d2781c03b37cc09b28bdb7bb1d66a0b`; the ABI is unchanged at the current head). It loaded the library on the JVM through the matching generated Kotlin/JNA binding. A loopback smoke passed HEAD framing, FIN, the 62-bit close code, a `CancelToken` dial and a pre-cancelled dial. The generated Kotlin emits seven `UNUSED_EXPRESSION` warnings under Kotlin 2.4.21. The Android app compiles the binding in its own `:openclaw-iroh` module so the app's warnings-as-errors stays on. On the Studio (Apple silicon), the macOS lane built the arm64 macOS library from source, linked it through SwiftPM, and passed a Swift → Rust loopback (streams, FIN, 62-bit close, `CancelToken` with endpoint reuse). The Swift run used `2dd6b82`, which has the same ABI as the current head.

Not yet proved: on-device runs, iOS device and simulator runtime, and the apps actually using the bindings in shipped builds.

Related: stacked on #193993.

prs.title: fix(markdown-core): stop shattering text for an unusable IR chunk limit
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`renderMarkdownIRChunksWithinLimit` — exported from the public `openclaw/plugin-sdk/text-chunking` surface — ran every non-`Infinity` limit through `resolveIntegerOption(limit, 1, { min: 1 })`. That fallback is `1`, so a `NaN`, zero or negative limit became a one-character step and the chunker emitted one chunk per character. A 95-character reply reached the transport as **80 separate messages**.

`chunkText` in the same package already returns the whole text for the same input: `normalizeChunkLimit` maps `NaN` to `0`, leaves zero and negative alone, and `chunkText` treats a non-positive limit as "no cap". Two chunkers in one package disagreed about what an unusable limit means, and each side's tests pinned its own answer — `render-aware-chunking.test.ts` asserted `[markdownToIR("abc"), Number.NaN, ["a", "b", "c"]]` while `chunk-text.test.ts` asserted `NaN -> ["abc"]`.

The existing comment already described the right contract and implemented half of it:

```
// Callers pass Infinity to mean "no size cap" ... resolveIntegerOption rejects non-finite values
// and would fall back to 1, shattering the text into one chunk per character; emit the whole IR as one chunk.
if (options.limit === Number.POSITIVE_INFINITY) {
```

It says **non-finite**, but only `Infinity` was special-cased.

## Is this replacing a deliberately retained fallback?

The one open review question. Checked the basis before answering it:

- `#193956` has **`reviews: 0`**, and its `mergedBy` is a merge click — no maintainer statement on that PR describes invalid-limit semantics as a retained contract.
- Its own body calls the behavior a defect and names the goal as removing it:

  > The deliberately **loud** per-character `NaN` behavior of `renderMarkdownIRChunksWithinLimit` (pinned by `render-aware-chunking.test.ts`) is intentionally left untouched.

  > The sibling helpers in `src/shared/text-chunking.ts` already return whole text for `NaN`, so this also **removes a divergence between the two chunking implementations**.

- "Intentionally left untouched" is scope discipline from a PR that touched two other files, not a ruling that one-character splitting is correct.
- Its stated premise was **incomplete**: *"This is the single owner of the broken normalization."* `chunkText` reaches `normalizeChunkLimit`; `renderMarkdownIRChunksWithinLimit` never did — it ran its own `resolveIntegerOption`. That is why `render-aware-chunking.ts` still carried the defect after `#193956` merged.

**This PR deletes that second normalization and routes both chunkers through the owner `#193956` introduced. It completes the claimed single owner rather than adding a contract.** Production code shrinks by six lines.

Why the two paths cannot both stand: `src/plugin-sdk/text-chunking.ts:54-58` exports `renderMarkdownIRChunksWithinLimit` from the **same file** as `chunkText` and `chunkTextRanges` — one public SDK surface, two answers for one input. A plugin passing the same `NaN` gets whole text from `chunkText` and one chunk per character from `renderMarkdownIRChunksWithinLimit`.

`#195329` (`src/shared/text-chunking.ts`) and `#193956` (`chunk-text.ts`) already moved two of the three paths to "unbounded"; this is the third. Two independent contributors proposed the same direction (`#193973`, `#194020`); `#194020` was closed for scope bloat — reminder accounting and Windows executable selection — not because the direction was rejected.

If a maintainer does want the one-character fallback kept as a public contract, that is a separate discussion, but it would leave two exports of the same module contradicting each other, with the falling-split side pinned only by a test inside the package.

## User Impact

Plugin and channel-adapter authors calling the exported `renderMarkdownIRChunksWithinLimit` with a bad computed limit — `Number(envValue)` on an unset variable, arithmetic over an optional setting — got an outbound message shattered across dozens of channel messages instead of delivered once.

`Infinity` already meant "no cap" and keeps working exactly as before; nothing changes for a usable finite limit.

## Why This Change Was Made

Both chunkers now read limits through one owner, `packages/markdown-core/src/chunk-limit.ts`, which keeps the non-positive path `chunkText` already relied on. `chunk-text.ts` loses its private copy of the function and `render-aware-chunking.ts` drops its `Infinity`-only special case.

The module is deliberately **not** exported from the package barrel, so `normalizeChunkLimit` does not become new public API — `packages/markdown-core` has a root `.` export and `export * from "./chunk-text.js"` would have leaked it.

## Evidence

Real guarded HTTP transport, not a stub client: a `node:http` loopback server receives the actual POST bodies, while `ssrf-runtime` rewrites only the `chat.googleapis.com` hostname and `getGoogleChatAccessToken` returns a synthetic token. Everything from `formatGoogleChatTextChunks` inward is shipped code — `sendGoogleChatMessage` -> `fetchJson` -> `withGoogleChatResponse` -> `fetchWithSsrFGuard` -> real socket.

Same proof file, same transport, only the library files switched:

Before (`origin/main`):

```
BUG378 {"len":95,"nan":80,"zero":80,"negative":80,"infinite":1,"finite":5}
```

After (this branch):

```
BUG378 {"len":95,"nan":1,"zero":1,"negative":1,"infinite":1,"finite":5}
```

`Infinity` and the finite `20` control are unchanged; only the unusable limits move.

Tests:

- The `NaN` row in `render-aware-chunking.test.ts` fails on `origin/main` with `expected [ 'a', 'b', 'c' ] to deeply equal [ 'abc' ]` and passes with the fix; `0` and `-1` rows added alongside it.
- Full `packages/markdown-core` suite: 11 files / 195 tests pass.
- `src/plugin-sdk/text-chunking.test.ts` (4), `extensions/telegram/src/format.test.ts` (80, including its `rejects NaN instead of repeatedly emitting chunks` contract) and `extensions/slack/src/format.test.ts` (45) pass.
- `oxfmt --check` clean over 57728 files, `git diff --check` clean.

One note for reviewers: `extensions/slack/src/format.ts:513` carries the same `resolveIntegerOption(limit, 1, { min: 1 })` pattern and normalizes *before* calling the library, so it needs its own change and is intentionally not part of this PR.

prs.body:
## Summary

Adds an optional `telnyx.noiseSuppression` setting to Voice Call. When it is set, inbound realtime calls run Telnyx per-call noise suppression (`Denoiser`, `DeepFilterNet`, `Krisp`, or `AiCoustics`) on the caller's audio before it reaches the realtime model.

It is off by default. With the setting unset, calls without media streaming and outbound dials send exactly the same Telnyx requests as before.

## What Problem This Solves

Background speech from a TV or another person in the room reaches the realtime model as if the caller had said it. Telnyx can isolate the caller's voice per call, for example with Krisp's telephony voice isolation model.

Voice Call couldn't use that, because it starts streaming inside the `answer` command and Telnyx rejects `suppression_start` while streaming is active (422, code 90045).

## Change

When `telnyx.noiseSuppression` is set and the call streams media, `TelnyxProvider.answerCall` runs these steps in order:

1. `answer` without the stream fields.
2. `suppression_start` with the configured direction, engine and engine config. This step is capped at 5 seconds so the stream token stays valid. If it fails or times out, Voice Call logs a warning and streams without suppression.
3. `streaming_start` with the same stream settings the answer would have carried.

When the setting is unset, the single `answer` still carries the stream fields inline, unchanged from today.

The config is validated in both the manifest schema and `normalizeVoiceCallConfig`; `engineConfig` requires `engine`. The docs in `docs/plugins/voice-call/realtime-and-streaming.md` cover the direction semantics, the engine fields, and the Telnyx number setting below.

**Prerequisite:** set the number's own noise suppression to `disabled` in Telnyx. A number-level setting engages the default engine at answer, and a later `suppression_start` collides with it; Telnyx returns a 500 for that collision.

## Failure handling

| Step that fails | Result |
| --- | --- |
| `answer` (setting on) | Voice Call sends a best-effort hangup, then reports the answer failure. Telnyx may have answered before its HTTP response was lost; that answer carries no stream, so without the hangup the caller would sit on silence until duration cleanup. |
| `answer` (setting unset) | Unchanged. The answer carries the stream inline, so a lost response still connects media, and no hangup is sent. |
| `suppression_start` | Logs a warning and streams without suppression. The call continues. |
| `streaming_start` | Voice Call hangs up the answered call and reports the failure. |

Both hangups share one helper, and a failed hangup is only logged. This resolves the earlier silent-call window when the answer response is lost: the contributor-side cleanup option from the review is implemented in `2df6212`.

## Evidence

The live runs below are real inbound calls to a Telnyx local number through a source build of this branch, loaded as a bundled plugin. The setup used a Call Control app with number-level suppression `disabled`, a Tailscale funnel, OpenAI realtime, and `inboundPolicy: allowlist`.

Hostnames, call control IDs and the caller are redacted. Timestamps are local (UTC-5).

The current head, `4e0e93d73af`, is `2df6212` rebased onto main `24015bf60cb`, plus test-only commits for the review's P3 findings; the two generated config baseline files were regenerated, and `docs/plugins/voice-call/configuration.md` was merged with main's new Twilio call recording section. Since `2df6212`'s base, the only main change to the Telnyx provider, the runtime, the webhook or the media stream is one line in `runtime.ts` from #189687 that passes Twilio's `record` setting to the Twilio provider, so the runs below on `2df6212` exercise the same Telnyx answer path as the current head.

### Upgrade from current stable v2026.10.8, on head `2df6212`

All runs used one profile, one state directory and one config file.

**A. Stock `v2026.10.8` (`dc2523e`), config without `noiseSuppression`.** Four inbound calls were answered and streamed. The first three ended with the model calling `openclaw_end_call` (`endReason=hangup-bot`). The gateway was stopped during the fourth call's setup; v2026.10.8 closed that record as `completed` on shutdown.

**B. Checkout of this branch (`2df6212`), same profile, config untouched.** `openclaw doctor --fix` ran the core state migration for the newer build. That migration belongs to v2026.10.8 to main, not to this plugin. After it, the gateway started and three inbound calls behaved exactly as before:

```
22:12:37.815 [voice-call/events] Inbound call accepted: caller=sha256:<redacted> allowlisted=true
22:13:28.983 [voice-call/lifecycle] Call finalized callId=8fea48a4-... endReason=hangup-bot
22:13:34.990 [voice-call/events] Inbound call accepted: caller=sha256:<redacted> allowlisted=true
22:13:55.616 [voice-call/lifecycle] Call finalized callId=05f267e5-... endReason=hangup-bot
22:14:01.298 [voice-call/events] Inbound call accepted: caller=sha256:<redacted> allowlisted=true
22:14:37.845 [voice-call/lifecycle] Call finalized callId=0a54b7ad-... endReason=hangup-bot
```

**C. `noiseSuppression` added with `config set ... --strict-json`, no other change.** The config was Krisp with `krisp-viva-tel-lite-v1.kef`. The call was a normal conversation with no suppression warning and no answer failure:

```
22:15:40.991 [voice-call/events] Inbound call accepted: caller=sha256:<redacted> allowlisted=true
22:15:42.112 [voice-call] Realtime bridge starting for call 28ab70e0-... (providerCallId=v3:<redacted>, initialGreeting=queued)
22:16:14.703 [voice-call/lifecycle] Call finalized callId=28ab70e0-... endReason=hangup-bot
```

**D. Rejected `suppression_start` on the same head.** The model was set to a name Telnyx does not accept, and two calls were placed.

Both calls had `suppression_start` rejected. On the first, Telnyx's own `streaming_start` then failed to reach the media destination, and Voice Call hung the answered call up through the shared helper. The second call streamed without suppression and finished normally.

```
22:24:50.955 [voice-call/events] Inbound call accepted: caller=sha256:<redacted> allowlisted=true
22:24:51.486 [telnyx] Noise suppression failed to start for call 70f2a343-... (providerCallId=v3:<redacted>); streaming without it: Telnyx API error: 422 {
  "errors": [ { "code": "10000", "title": "Invalid request",
    "source": { "pointer": "/noise_suppression_engine_config" },
    "detail": "The 'noise_suppression_engine_config' parameter model must be one of: krisp-viva-tel-v2.kef, krisp-viva-tel-lite-v1.kef, krisp-viva-pro-v1.kef, krisp-viva-ss-v1.kef." } ]
}
22:24:52.886 [voice-call/events] Failed to answer inbound call v3:<redacted>: call answered but Telnyx streaming_start failed; hanging up: Telnyx API error: 422 {
  "errors": [ { "code": "90046", "title": "Media Streaming failed", "detail": "Failed to connect to destination" } ]
}
22:24:53.750 [voice-call/lifecycle] Call finalized callId=70f2a343-... endReason=completed

22:24:57.684 [voice-call/events] Inbound call accepted: caller=sha256:<redacted> allowlisted=true
22:24:58.077 [telnyx] Noise suppression failed to start for call 3e06844d-... (providerCallId=v3:<redacted>); streaming without it: Telnyx API error: 422 { ...same 10000 error... }
22:24:58.939 [voice-call] Realtime bridge starting for call 3e06844d-... (providerCallId=v3:<redacted>, initialGreeting=queued)
22:25:17.777 [voice-call/lifecycle] Call finalized callId=3e06844d-... endReason=hangup-bot
```

Thirty seconds after the hung-up call, the existing realtime stream watchdog logged `Realtime stream WebSocket never connected within 30s` for `70f2a343`. That call was already finalized, and the warning had no effect on it or on the next call. The watchdog belongs to the stream token issued before the answer; this PR does not change it.

### Stored call history after the upgrade

These records were read back with `openclaw voicecall tail` on `2df6212` after legs B through D. They include the four calls that v2026.10.8 wrote before the upgrade:

| Call | Written by | Started | Answered | Ended | State | End reason |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 61706121 | v2026.10.8 | 17:46:45 | 17:46:46 | 17:47:32 | hangup-bot | hangup-bot |
| 368ae1dc | v2026.10.8 | 17:47:36 | 17:47:37 | 17:48:06 | hangup-bot | hangup-bot |
| a7d22a6f | v2026.10.8 | 17:48:15 | 17:48:16 | 17:48:49 | hangup-bot | hangup-bot |
| 49b062ca | v2026.10.8 | 17:49:07 | 17:49:08 | 17:49:09 | completed | completed |
| 8fea48a4 | 2df6212 | 22:12:37 | 22:12:38 | 22:13:28 | hangup-bot | hangup-bot |
| 05f267e5 | 2df6212 | 22:13:34 | 22:13:35 | 22:13:55 | hangup-bot | hangup-bot |
| 0a54b7ad | 2df6212 | 22:14:01 | 22:14:02 | 22:14:37 | hangup-bot | hangup-bot |
| c96579c8 | 2df6212 | 22:14:51 | 22:14:52 | 22:14:53 | completed | completed |
| 28ab70e0 | 2df6212 | 22:15:40 | 22:15:42 | 22:16:14 | hangup-bot | hangup-bot |
| 70f2a343 | 2df6212 | 22:24:50 | - | 22:24:53 | completed | completed |
| 3e06844d | 2df6212 | 22:24:57 | 22:24:58 | 22:25:17 | hangup-bot | hangup-bot |

All 11 records in the store load on the new build with their original timestamps and end reasons, including the four written by v2026.10.8.

`49b062ca` and `c96579c8` are calls that were in setup when the gateway was stopped. Each build closed its record as `completed` on shutdown.

`70f2a343` is the streaming-failure call from leg D. It has no `answeredAt` because the hangup came before Telnyx's `call.answered` webhook was processed.

So on `2df6212`, all three live paths ran against real Telnyx: Krisp on, a rejected `suppression_start`, and a `streaming_start` failure cleaned up with a hangup.

The one path not exercised live is a lost `answer` response, which can't be arranged against Telnyx on demand. The unit tests cover it.

### Earlier runs (head `c1a26c2`, [comment](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/183266#issuecomment-6458928065))

- Krisp in a room with a multi-voice video playing: the model stayed on the caller through English and Korean speech.
- The same rejected-suppression and streaming-failure paths as above.
- An upgrade from v2026.10.7.

### Tests

- `runtime.telnyx-answer.test.ts` starts the real runtime with Telnyx and realtime enabled and POSTs a `call.initiated` webhook to its listener. It mocks only the outbound HTTP edge and asserts the Telnyx commands for three paths: unset, Krisp, and rejected `suppression_start`. It replaces the constructor-forwarding test the review flagged.
- `providers/telnyx.test.ts` covers:
  - the request order and payloads,
  - engine field mapping,
  - the 5 second suppression bound,
  - fail-open on network errors,
  - hangup on a failed stream-less answer (and none on a failed inline-stream answer),
  - hangup on a failed `streaming_start`, even when that hangup fails,
  - unchanged outbound dials.

  The unset-answer case is folded into the existing streaming-answer test.
- `config.test.ts` covers the rejection cases.

## For the voice-call owner

This adds one optional block, with 10 config paths, under `telnyx`. It stays inside the existing Telnyx provider, and the defaults are unchanged. ClawSweeper recommends approving the optional capability. A maintainer decision on exposing it is the remaining item I can't close from the contributor side.
