prs.title: fix(gateway): reject FIFO TLS material without blocking validation
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

A configured Gateway TLS certificate, private key or CA path that is a FIFO without a writer blocks startup before TLS validation can report the invalid input. Public certificate inspection has the same admission gap. The existing byte-limited cert/key reader cannot help while `open()` is waiting for a writer.

This is a malformed local material path, not a claim that OpenClaw normally creates FIFO certificates or that an untrusted remote user can configure these paths.

## Why This Change Was Made

Admit configured material nonblockingly on POSIX, check the opened descriptor is a regular file, then use the existing read policy. Both server startup and read-only public certificate inspection use this owner. Keep configured symlinks, current 64 KiB cert/key limits and the existing uncapped CA-bundle contract. Windows retains its current open mode.

Read the full TLS owner, startup preparation/kernel caller, local HTTPS probe, certificate inspection, renewal consumer and adjacent tests. Renewal retains previously accepted material on reload failure. The installed fs-safe bounded descriptor implementation was inspected: its limit applies after opening; the generic regular-file API rejects symlinks, so substituting it would change supported configured paths. No new package, timer, fallback or config option is needed.

All-state semantic/symbol searches and open TLS PR changed-file checks found no active implementation of this fix. Historical #110046 proposed new fixed input caps and was closed for inactivity with unresolved compatibility concerns. This patch does not adopt that policy or replace certificate-generation code: it preserves today's cert/key bounds, uncapped CA reads and staged generation/publication safeguards. #171105 fixes SSH probe endpoint selection in a different owner.

## User Impact

Invalid nonregular material now reaches the normal required-TLS startup failure path and produces an actionable diagnostic instead of blocking inside the reader. Regular material and symlinks still start an actual HTTPS listener with the configured certificate. Invalid TLS never falls back to an unencrypted listener.

Three existing path inputs now explicitly reject nonregular descriptors; this validation change matters for compatibility. The reproduced no-writer FIFOs block unattended startup. A finite writer can make some FIFO PEM inputs work today: rejecting that use is a compatibility choice requiring owner acceptance, not established by the no-writer reproduction. This refresh does not claim that acceptance. No config/default addition, protocol/schema, dependency, trust policy, certificate generation or migration change. CA bundles gain no size cap; ordinary files and their configured symlinks retain the observed behavior.

## Evidence

**Current-head refresh, 2026-10-23:** `6d7d81bb96031b2f70d365399b89f2699e30cb59`, after a normal merge of main `7559fb21a57059bd7483fb8c0a7117aff9794f92`. Linux, Node 24.22.1, source OpenClaw 2026.10.6. Main's flattened TLS tests and newer coverage were retained; only the FIFO regression was carried into that structure. Production remains +19/-8 and tests +48/-0 against this main; two files.

Current source-runtime command:

```sh
node ../gateway-tls-fifo-live-proof-20261023.mjs "$PWD" ../maintenance-172741-proof-v2-20261023-run green
```

At `2026-10-23T01:07:04.063Z`, all six real Gateway startup scenarios passed on the exact rebuilt head:

| Scenario | Current result | Observation time |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Regular cert/key/CA | actual HTTPS readiness and matching peer fingerprint | 23.156s |
| Symlinked cert/key/CA | same HTTPS identity; links retained | 20.086s |
| Ordinary invalid PEM | real startup-failure artifact, no TCP listener | 15.028s |
| Writerless certificate FIFO | regular-file failure artifact, no TCP listener | 14.488s |
| Writerless private-key FIFO | same rejection | 13.981s |
| Writerless CA FIFO | same rejection | 14.070s |

Waiting FIFO reads 3/3 on the historical base become 0/3 on the current head. Configuration/material preservation 6/6; no FIFO writers or watchdog timeouts. Invalid runs still needed explicit cleanup of the harness-owned process groups: no natural CLI exit guarantee is claimed. The current driver only removes a retired heartbeat field from its synthetic configuration; the original driver and historical RED remain unchanged. One failed obsolete-config attempt is retained as a fixture failure. Current driver SHA-256 `dacd6ec63a1a3cdff9151aa95cbd48d916357da1a61894bbd2e9efdd0e603693`; receipt SHA-256 `fb5ed121e5098c03385b180a3853005a3abfc8a2e7549ad68c062969aaa074fd`.

**Installed stable → exact-head upgrade proof:** PASS in isolated local Linux container `leon-tls-installed-upgrade-20261023`, Node 24.22.1 / glibc 2.35, starting `2026-10-23T01:17:19.716Z`.

- Start from a fresh copy of the official OpenClaw 2026.10.6 installation, shipped build `fe06181dc5ecc01cf8904abbfc26925925efefbc`. Read installed TLS settings and establish actual CA-verified HTTPS through configured certificate/key/CA symlinks; fingerprint matches.
- Back up the isolated config, state and workspace. Perform a normal npm 11.19.0 install of the private exact-head runtime package over the same prefix (exit 0, 46.309s). Installed build-info now identifies `6d7d81bb96031b2f70d365399b89f2699e30cb59`, package version 2026.10.6. This is not a published release or SDK certification.
- Read back the same TLS settings and actual HTTPS certificate identity. Stable HTTPS readiness 16.063s, candidate 24.391s; these include startup and are not performance claims.
- Replace only the isolated certificate link with a writerless FIFO. The installed candidate reports the existing regular-file startup error in 13.572s, creates no TCP listener, and retains the FIFO. Restore the original link.
- Original config, certificate, private key, CA and workspace artifact are byte-identical after the upgrade and controls; all three symlinks remain symlinks. Config SHA-256 `daa2106d727620d8f970614b950495aaccf9d9eb1b8d7b4b70b9f148418e6600`; workspace artifact SHA-256 `3452af9dd340934ffae02a6d2a4a67adf45a13067211dd37dbe84c7eb98ce4f8`; zero FIFO writers. No production configuration, channels, credentials or recipients were used.

Installed-proof invocation inside that container:

```sh
node /harness/probe.mjs /candidate/openclaw.tgz 6d7d81bb96031b2f70d365399b89f2699e30cb59
```

Harness SHA-256 `5991d8b7246755d6b669038daa0ade06b8d714b748bc7c92f3e1925010a17a75`; package SHA-256 `38c61dc095c2d7e646d7b73f8aa125028c521464db6834f994d8a0fa54c866c1`; receipt SHA-256 `f5087287fdee9b2a148eba87480ff20338fe17384c8b810052922fde9004cfbb`. Raw receipts/logs/backups are outside the product branch; the redacted readbacks above are the published evidence. This is a local container, not remote Crabbox/Testbox.

Current checks: `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/infra/tls/gateway.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` — 17/17 PASS, 119.06s Vitest / 129.13s wrapper including cold compilation, local container `leon-tls-merge-tests-20261023`. `OPENCLAW_VITEST_RUNTIME=node node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/gateway/server-tls-renewal.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` — 4/4 PASS on this head. Focused supported Go types, type-aware lint, formatting and diff checks passed. Exact committed `pnpm build sourcePerformance` passed in 289.0s; UI build and canonical runtime tarball integrity/import-graph validation passed for the installed proof. No hosted-CI success or human approval is claimed.

Not tested at this head: external PKI/client authentication, actual automatic certificate rotation, native Windows/macOS, broad release gates or natural failure-process exit. Finite-writer FIFO compatibility remains a maintainer decision even though the installed ordinary-file upgrade and no-writer controls passed.

**Historical acceptance RED/GREEN and prior-head validation (not current-head execution):**

Linux, Node 24.16.0, built OpenClaw 2026.10.3. Identical native Gateway CLI harness on unmodified main base and the prior clean committed head. Each case uses its own home/config/state/workspace, loopback port, synthetic local auth token and one-day locally generated certificate. No channel, remote provider or model turn is exercised.

```sh
node openclaw.mjs gateway run --port <isolated-port> --bind loopback
```

Proof command: `node gateway-tls-fifo-live-proof.mjs checkout new-output-directory green` (`red` on the base).

The harness reads HTTPS `/readyz` through the generated CA and compares the peer certificate fingerprint. Invalid cases check that no TCP listener remains, read the real `gateway.startup_failed` stability JSON and verify source material/config bytes or FIFO/symlink type.

| Scenario | Unmodified main base | Committed head |
|---|---|---|
| Regular cert/key/CA | HTTPS 200, matching peer fingerprint; 25.42 s | Same verified HTTPS; 20.23 s |
| Symlinked cert/key/CA | HTTPS 200, matching fingerprint; links retained; 20.80 s | Same, links retained; 22.07 s |
| Ordinary invalid PEM | Startup failure artifact; no listener; 14.21 s | Same existing failure path; 14.68 s |
| Writerless certificate FIFO | Still waiting at 30.02 s; no failure artifact | Regular-file error in failure JSON; no listener; 14.84 s |
| Writerless private-key FIFO | Still waiting at 30.07 s; no failure artifact | Same explicit rejection; 13.39 s |
| Writerless CA FIFO | Still waiting at 30.00 s; no failure artifact | Same explicit rejection; 13.29 s |

Unresolved TLS input reads: **3/3 → 0/3**. Input/config preservation: **6/6** on each version. These are end-to-end observation times including Gateway bootstrap, not reader performance guarantees. The 30 s watchdog diagnoses the original block; it is not a new production timeout.

The claim is that TLS input validation returns and publishes startup failure, not that the entire Gateway CLI naturally exits within a deadline. Both an ordinary invalid PEM control and rejected FIFO runs remained alive at the observation point; the harness explicitly terminates its owned process groups afterward. An earlier check requiring immediate process exit failed and is not counted as successful proof. A separate command-lifecycle repair is outside this reader change.

```text
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/infra/tls/gateway.test.ts src/gateway/server-tls-renewal.test.ts --maxWorkers=1
  GREEN: 21 passed across two files; 113.83 s wrapper
  TLS file: 17 passed, 91.21 s dominated by transform; renewal: 4 passed

node scripts/run-oxlint.mjs --type-aware --tsconfig config/tsconfig/oxlint.core.json src/infra/tls/gateway.ts src/infra/tls/gateway.test.ts
  exit 0
oxfmt --check src/infra/tls/gateway.ts src/infra/tls/gateway.test.ts
git diff --check
  clean
node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs scripts/build-all.mts runtime
  exact committed-head build passed, 3m 41.6s
```

The regression checks server cert/key/CA admission and public inspection in a killable child, so a blocking-open regression cannot strand the test worker. Existing coverage retains symlink chains, exact leaf byte limits, large CA bundles, safe certificate generation and renewal behavior. CI seconds are unavailable.

Two files: production **+19/-8 (net +11)**, tests **+48/-0**; no generated/lock files. The added owner logic shares descriptor admission across both existing entries and the CA read without growing another reader path.

Both runs use harness SHA-256 `61a6994c0c35d2c1872680b52c38d359cfc396798a312d760dca19b544ed3a56`. Receipts and logs are retained locally; the observations above are the published evidence, not a claim of hosted artifacts.

prs.title: feat(cron): read retained run transcripts from the CLI
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Closes #167242.

Operators inspecting a completed automation can list its run summary, but the native cron CLI cannot read the retained transcript for a selected job/run. Today they must manually construct `gateway call cron.history` JSON. A truncated summary can be mistaken for truncated output and lead to unnecessary reruns; [#69678](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/69678) describes duplicated digest delivery during that diagnosis.

Add `openclaw cron history <id> --run-id <runId> [--cursor <opaque>] [--limit <n>]`, with JSON output and the existing `automations` alias. This reads whatever the existing transcript owner retains. It does not recover absent output or change summary limits, retention, delivery, UI navigation, or conversation continuation. The broader #69678 and #155588 requests are not claimed fixed.

## Why This Change Was Made

The CLI is the missing owner surface. The Gateway already implements `cron.history`, and the Control UI already uses recorded job/run identity and opaque pagination. The implementation reuses existing cron registration, option inheritance, integer/string validation, error handling, and JSON output. Limits, authorization, run binding, visibility, pagination and storage remain owned by the existing Gateway method.

Existing-solutions preflight: the generic public RPC is a functional alternative, but it requires hand-authored parameters rather than a discoverable native command. No plugin, dependency or new integration is necessary. The retained owner work merged in [#158776](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/158776) establishes the existing owner contract; that merge is not endorsement of this new CLI proposal. This is an I1 Feature issue created by this contributor, not a claim of prior human approval.

## User Impact

Operators can select and page a retained transcript without rerunning the automation or manually assembling RPC JSON. Missing/blank selectors, blank cursors and invalid integer limits fail before a request; opaque cursor bytes pass through unchanged. The server retains its default/max limit decisions.

Four files against the refreshed main: production +30/-0, tests +112/-0, documentation +27/-1; no generated or lock files. The production additions register one command and include it in existing JSON output routing. No config/default, protocol/schema, permission, dependency, migration, scheduling or storage changes. For custom/shared-session jobs, the existing owner can return shared conversation messages, including later messages; this command does not promise run-exclusive content.

## Evidence

**Current-head refresh, 2026-10-23:** `51062ae517f180c63ec3384ff6651d47081d855b`, tree `7ef1e5d99c2f15a424bac12e4ee41482aa856349`, after a normal merge of main `7559fb21a57059bd7483fb8c0a7117aff9794f92`. Linux, Node 24.22.1; source build version 2026.10.6. The upstream-deleted broad test file remains deleted. The eleven retained-history command cases now live in the focused `register.cron-history.test.ts`; a redundant oversized-output mock assertion was removed. The production command contract is unchanged. This supplies updated code/proof, not human acceptance of the proposed CLI surface.

The exact committed runtime was rebuilt with `pnpm build sourcePerformance` (PASS, 279.7s); `dist/build-info.json` matches the current head. Both public-entry scenarios were rerun:

```sh
node ../cron-history-cli-proof-20261008.mjs --root "$PWD" --phase green --expected-head 51062ae517f180c63ec3384ff6651d47081d855b
node ../cron-history-gateway-proof-20261023.mjs --root "$PWD" --phase green --expected-head 51062ae517f180c63ec3384ff6651d47081d855b
```

- Public CLI/WebSocket transport: **11/11 PASS**, 40.485s, `2026-10-23T00:58:40.471Z` to `00:59:20.956Z`. The unchanged driver verifies native/alias requests, inherited connection options, exact cursor/limit transport, and invalid-input zero-request controls. Receipt SHA-256 `b5a7faa57827692bf4140ce5296fb2c264112bf6179018e4beecd49730c4b96d`.
- Actual compiled Gateway/SQLite: **7/7 PASS**, 55.524s, `2026-10-23T01:07:29.037Z` to `01:08:24.561Z`. Public CLI reads the recorded older generation after its alias is gone, both actual owner-issued pages and content beyond 2000 characters; output matches the generic RPC, and missing-run/cross-run cursor errors remain structured. Canonical record/transcript digest before=after `7185a19864fe43cd58492511ff4649e33a8b7cff3bce242557a6076d7965e1d0`; runtime digest before=after `f23eb9689af59b51e8ed393ca692ebf2683904353cbf432d3ade15900987dd5a`; Gateway exits 0. Receipt SHA-256 `ab77508f7c26f4fe7ac5d6a1bf23e798cd42ee38707b9e0dcd528e77ae4170e9`.

It updates only the fixture for current job preflight and the moved compiled codec chunk; no raw SQL, production handler replacement, provider call or channel send. Driver SHA-256 `f8685ac4aa0e081a3795c5df9a5c1b8dacc38efafb65b29462af302d7c0b05a9`. The original driver and historical RED remain unchanged. Two failed fixture attempts (new agent-auth preflight; obsolete compiled chunk prefix) are retained as failures, not counted as passing runs.

Raw receipts and logs remain outside the product branch. The redacted exact-head readbacks above are the published evidence. Owner acceptance of a new public CLI command remains a separate decision.

**Historical acceptance RED/GREEN and prior-head validation (not current-head test results):**

Prior candidate `b1a933e4b1da9b9a8d261ec5b88b7f23bf84b855`, tree `ffe589a447911d6159f57921a14ad4c563a80025`; baseline `8bacf4fe0cb70318567bb7d8bb3a44325af71205`. That follow-up fixed two CI-reported shadowed test variables (+4/-4); production and assertions were unchanged. Both original harnesses were rerun on that prior commit.

`node cron-history-cli-proof-20261008.mjs --root <built-owner-root> --phase red|green --expected-head <exact-head>`

Transport GREEN: **11/11 PASS**, 23.53s. Actual Gateway/SQLite GREEN: **7/7 PASS**, 47.62s, Gateway shutdown exit 0. A disabled job is created through the public API; existing compiled storage-owner helpers seed terminal records and two retained generations. There is no raw SQL, handler substitution, provider call or channel send.

Receipt SHA-256:

Actual Gateway candidate canonical record/transcript digest before=after: `6d894c3e22710356adfb14d93905e879a6c8cf8019e49cbcfc9b5e7b1093a446`.

Validation:

Measured two-file wrapper duration 141.89s, including 117.772s first-checkout compiled-worker preparation.

prs.title: fix(cli): agents list no longer blames the Matrix plugin for core deprecation warnings
prs.body:
Related: #190243

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: `openclaw agents list` prints two `[DEP_PLUGIN_SDK]` warnings that blame the bundled Matrix plugin, although the caller is core.

```
(node:…) [DEP_PLUGIN_SDK] DeprecationWarning: Plugin matrix: createPluginStateSyncKeyedStore is deprecated; use createPluginStateKeyedStoreV2 and await its operations instead.
(node:…) [DEP_PLUGIN_SDK] DeprecationWarning: Plugin SDK: PluginStateSyncKeyedStore.entries is deprecated; use await openKeyedStoreV2().entries() instead.
```

## User Impact

User impact: the agents inventory no longer suggests that a plugin needs updating when no plugin action can clear the warning. The agent list, routing rules, and provider/account status are unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

`agents list` built its provider inventory through the synchronous `listReadOnlyChannelPluginsForConfig` resolver. That resolver probes bundled channel plugins' persisted auth state; the bundled Matrix probe (`hasAnyMatrixAuth`) uses the deprecated sync keyed-store API, so the warning is attributed to "Plugin matrix" even though core chose the sync path.

#190243 fixed the same root cause in `status`, `channels list`, and `doctor` by using the existing async resolvers. `agents list` was missed: it already runs in an async command, and the async resolver is used by the neighbouring `channels list` path. This change switches that one call site; the public plugin SDK is untouched.

## Evidence

Real CLI, same isolated state and two-agent config with one Telegram binding, before and after this change. The fixture keeps its existing state database (`state/openclaw.sqlite`) between runs:

Before (`main` at e673256f8a9):
```
$ openclaw agents list --bindings
Agents:
- main
  Workspace: /tmp/oc-proof/ws/main
  Agent dir: $OPENCLAW_HOME/.openclaw/agents/main/agent
  Routing rules: 0
- ops
  Workspace: /tmp/oc-proof/ws/ops
  Agent dir: $OPENCLAW_HOME/.openclaw/agents/ops/agent
  Routing rules: 1
  Routing rules:
    - telegram accountId=work peer=group:-100123
Routing rules map channel/account/peer to an agent. Use --bindings for full rules.
Channel status reflects local config/creds. For live health: openclaw channels status --probe.
# stderr:
(node:…) [DEP_PLUGIN_SDK] DeprecationWarning: Plugin matrix: createPluginStateSyncKeyedStore is deprecated; ...
(node:…) [DEP_PLUGIN_SDK] DeprecationWarning: Plugin SDK: PluginStateSyncKeyedStore.entries is deprecated; ...
```

After (this branch, same `OPENCLAW_HOME` and state database):
```
$ openclaw agents list --bindings
# same stdout, byte-for-byte: diff before.out after.out -> no output
# stderr: 0 bytes; DEP_PLUGIN_SDK lines: 0
$ echo $?
0
```

Regression test: the new command-boundary test `src/commands/agents.list.dep-warning.test.ts` loads a synthetic bundled setup channel whose sync persisted-auth export emits `DEP_PLUGIN_SDK`, then runs `agentsListCommand` and asserts no such warning is emitted. On the base commit it fails on that assertion because the command used the sync resolver; with this change it passes. The fixture exercises the real plugin loader and saved-auth probe rather than asserting which mock was called.

Checks:

prs.title: fix: avoid history downloads during agent Git probes
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes multi-minute history downloads when an agent checks an absent commit in a partial clone with `git cat-file -e/-t`, `rev-parse --verify`, or `merge-base --is-ancestor`.

## User Impact

These probes now stay offline in POSIX Gateway exec and its Docker/Podman sandboxes, preserve Git's exit status, and explain how to fetch explicitly using an available common tip or query GitHub. Ordinary `show`, `log -p`, `blame`, and `diff` still hydrate missing blobs. No configuration change is needed.

The PATH wrapper is a performance default, not a security boundary. Absolute Git paths, aliases/functions, native harness shells, remote nodes, SSH/Crabbox sandboxes, and standalone embedded contexts without Gateway startup are outside coverage. Content reads naming an absent commit can still trigger Git's lazy history fetch. This PR is intentionally unmerged: the measured fixed launch overhead is a tradeoff for maintainer acceptance.

## Why This Change Was Made

Git's [lazy-fetch owner](https://github.com/git/git/blob/v2.53.0/promisor-remote.c#L22-L65) hardcodes `noop` negotiation and `blob:none`. A missing commit therefore fetches its reachable commit/tree closure without offering common-history tips. Disabling lazy fetch globally also breaks historical blob reads. Newer Git's negotiationInclude option can bound some transfers but does not keep probes local.

The existing managed CLI/PATH owner installs one portable probe shim; sandbox resource mounts expose only that credential-free directory read-only. The shim performs no preflight Git call, workspace scan, cache, or configuration write. The native Git child receives PATH without the shim to avoid recursion. Explicit `git fetch origin <sha> --negotiation-tip=origin/main` retains ordinary negotiation; substitute a locally available common tip as needed.

## Evidence

A real exec-tool regression fails on base `7c7a4d5db4adf174b324cfe47c17123808a7de61`: the missing-commit probe unexpectedly succeeds after fetching. The candidate fails locally with recovery guidance and zero fetch children/packs. Tests cover local hits, valid negative ancestry, cold historical reads, explicit fetch recovery, unchanged repo config, and sandbox mount/PATH isolation. All 52 focused tests passed; the final strengthened owner suites also passed (17 tests). The regression itself takes approximately 3 seconds; suite wall time includes repository compilation.

Committed workload: `node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs scripts/perf/agent-git-probes.mts --scratch-parent <directory>`. Acceptance was recorded before running: zero implicit fetches/objects/bytes for absent-object probes, working explicit fetch and blob hydration, five interleaved samples plus A/A controls. Synthetic fixture: 62,001 files, 1.116 GB materialized content, 20,001 existing commits; macOS/APFS, Git 2.56.0, warm filesystem cache with fresh Git metadata per sample. This reproduces the mechanism with ~40k offered objects, not a million-object transfer. No production data or production-host access.

| Flow | Before median / p95 | After median / p95 | Objects / received pack bytes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Missing-commit probe | 402.06 / 435.52 ms | 21.05 / 45.54 ms | 40,067 / 3,912,552 → 0 / 0 |
| Present-commit probe | 11.51 / 12.41 ms | 20.44 / 21.46 ms | 0 / 0 both |
| Missing-blob read | 53.78 / 57.05 ms | 62.70 / 68.94 ms | 1 / 104 both |
| Explicit negotiated fetch | — | 52.99 / 54.60 ms | 2 / 259 |

Missing-probe aggregate native CPU: 2,710 ms → below the timer's displayed precision; peak RSS: 31.13 → 8.77 MB. A/A present-probe medians were 11.51 and 11.28 ms. **Fixed overhead is real:** present probes cost +8.93 ms (+77.6%); blob median is +16.6%, p95 +20.8%. Five-sample p95 is only the observed maximum. No Linux/btrfs timing or cumulative native-allocation measurement is claimed; RSS measures footprint, not allocation volume. A no-prompt native Allocations profiler feasibility probe could not produce a capture; no permission changes were made. The rejected global-no-lazy variant failed all four historical-read controls; the shim passed them.

Production source delta: **+89 lines**, necessary for selective command behavior and existing-owner host/sandbox delivery; no obsolete competing path existed to delete. Test delta: +190 lines with an exact independent allocation, covering one behavioral owner and distinct sandbox transport/isolation contracts. The reproducible benchmark adds 269 tooling lines. The previous type assertion is removed and its baseline shrunk.

`pnpm build:ci-artifacts` passed (5m 6.8s). Codex autoreview of the full staged snapshot against the pinned base, P0–P2 coverage, is scoped-clean with no actionable findings. The exact 190-line test allocation and assertion ratchet pass. UI browser tests were not selected: no changed runtime module is imported under `ui/src`. The sandbox checks exercise real shell PATH delivery and the production mount owner, not a live container deployment.

`pnpm check:changed` completed. Core/test/script typechecks, format, all three dead-export scans, core lint, and the remaining guards passed. The initial new assertion-ratchet failure was repaired by removing the casts and shrinking the baseline; its targeted rerun passes. Six benchmark-only brace lint findings were corrected; the narrow lint rerun and independent review both pass. The changelog-attribution check remains a verified **main regression**: all 20 failures reproduce on exact base `7c7a4d5db4adf174b324cfe47c17123808a7de61` and first appear in `266a7aa0fe69e2b5fe6445c4ceb1e15b5360c957` / #194364. The introducing commit's parent fails with a different, now-resolved 26-entry signature. This PR does not edit release-owned changelogs.

prs.title: fix(browser): release console and predicate wait handles
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes Gateway memory growth when a long-lived managed browser tab logs values or repeatedly runs predicate waits.

## User Impact

Repeated browsing releases unused JavaScript handles after each observation or wait. Console text, bounded network diagnostics, navigation guards, and cancellation behavior are preserved. No configuration or migration is needed. Explicit disposal has CPU and allocation costs, quantified below; no merge is requested.

## Why This Change Was Made

The console observer copies text but never uses the argument handles Playwright creates for the event. Predicate waits dispose the document handle but previously discarded a second handle returned by `waitForFunction`. Dispose both at their existing owners, including a predicate that finishes after its caller is interrupted.

## Evidence

Current head: **`f29d8d00a2f3e90ee9de4dbbcdb04aed591e9302`**, rebased onto `7c7a4d5db4adf174b324cfe47c17123808a7de61`. The declared CPU/timing/allocation comparison is complete. This PR is ready for review and remains unmerged.

### Real Gateway A/B with A/A controls

Three isolated Gateways: A1 and A2 use the exact rebased parent; B uses the fix. Each starts its own managed Chromium, warms 20 mixed browsing steps, then completes the same 200 measured steps. Five interleaved **A1/B/A2 triples in each of two separate modes** produce 30 samples: untraced timing and sampled allocation. All samples are retained.

Each 20-step batch logs 400 console objects, performs 400 fetches and 20 predicate waits, and includes one navigation and one browser snapshot. Calls use real `browser.request` WebSocket RPCs. CPU/allocation come from the Gateway main isolate through the measurement preload, not the driver. Process CPU also includes threads in that Gateway process; it excludes Chromium and separate worker processes. GC and full heap capture run outside timing. Loaded browser-owner source hashes were verified against all three checkouts.

Per browsing step, baseline pools five A1 and five A2 samples; B has five samples. Values are **median / p95**; MB means 1,000,000 bytes.

| Metric | Parent A1/A2 | Fixed B | Median change |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Wall time, ms/step | 582.18 / 964.62 | 595.80 / 979.32 | +2.34% |
| Gateway main-thread CPU, ms/step | 67.09 / 98.80 | 74.57 / 106.12 | +11.15% |
| Gateway process CPU, ms/step | 110.11 / 152.95 | 122.21 / 160.09 | +11.00% |
| Sampled allocation, MB/step | 15.584 / 15.828 | 17.962 / 18.104 | +15.26% |

Paired median changes against each triple's mean control are wall +1.80%, main CPU +7.68%, process CPU +5.82%, allocation +15.19%. Unchanged A/A ranges are wall −22.64%..+3.75%, main CPU −27.96%..+2.48%, process CPU −22.25%..+4.25%, allocation −0.38%..+1.99%. Host load1 ranged 17.69–43.09.

**Cost requiring owner review before merge:** CPU triple 3 is 63.38 ms/step (A1), 80.59 (B), 64.95 (A2): **+25.59% paired CPU**, above the declared 20% guard. It is retained, not dismissed as noise. The median CPU and allocation increases are also explicit costs; this is not an all-metrics performance-pass claim. The fix adds 420 disposal calls per 20-step batch; no dependency cap or runtime setting was changed to hide retention.

**Allocation and GC:** the earlier +13.03% number measured the browser owner directly: 271.957 → 307.386 MB per 20-step batch, equivalent to **+1.771 MB/step**. The completed real-Gateway comparison measures **+2.378 MB/step (+15.26%)**, or +47.55 MB per batch. These are cumulative sampled allocations, including objects collected during the batch, not live-heap increases. In separate quiescent main-heap captures after GC, warm-to-200-step heap growth is **92.535 MB (A1), 77.902 MB (B), 91.008 MB (A2)**. After closing the page and collecting again, residual growth above warm is **4.799 / 4.308 / 3.452 MB** respectively: B is inside the A/A range. The extra allocation does not accumulate as additional retained heap in this workload; legitimate bounded request history remains while the page is open.

| Main-heap client `_JSHandle` count | A1 | Fixed B | A2 |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| After 20 warmup steps | 421 | 1 | 421 |
| After 200 additional steps | 4,621 | 1 | 4,621 |
| Page closed | 1 | 1 | 1 |

Each instance served 4,400 fetches including warmup. At the measured checkpoint all three have identical request/response/ManualPromise counts: **8,826 / 4,413 / 48,559**; after close, **2 / 1 / 23**. Console and network assertions pass. The earlier longer 16,020-fetch soak established Playwright's existing protocol-history plateau; no independent abandoned-waiter leak was reproduced. OpenClaw's network log already stores bounded metadata with weak Request keys.

Rerun the committed real-Gateway comparison with prepared dependencies and a baseline checkout:

```sh
node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs scripts/perf/browser-protocol-comparison.ts \
  --baseline-entry /path/to/baseline/src/entry.ts \
  --candidate-entry src/entry.ts \
  --executable /path/to/chromium \
  --output /path/to/new-output-directory
```

The preliminary port-overlap attempt produced no measured samples. A short two-instance diagnostic was excluded because reusing A for both controls doubled its browsing history relative to B. The final three-instance run corrects both issues and retains every completed sample.

### Watcher investigation

No watcher lifecycle patch is justified by the measured path. A real Linux Gateway ran six worktree/model-turn/retirement cycles plus 1,200 extra session create/delete cycles over 63,001 synthetic files / 1.24 GB. Every retirement returned to **1,095 FSWatcher objects**, with no duplicate native path/mode registration. This does not establish the production retaining paths or coverage of larger databases/other filesystems. No private data was used.

### Validation and review

- **CI failure fixed:** Node IPC messages are validated as unknown at the preload boundary, fixing the original `TS2345` error. `pnpm tsgo:scripts`, targeted script lint, formatting, and diff checks pass. [Exact-head CI run 42544933921](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/42544933921) succeeded, including `check-test-types`; the PR rollup had 57 passing and 55 skipped checks, with no failed or pending checks at verification.
- The two disposal regressions fail on unchanged runtime. All 76 affected browser tests passed; both runtime owners are byte-identical to that previously tested fix after rebase. New real-Gateway behavior assertions also pass.
- Exact test allocation remains **9 lines**, matching the net test delta. Ratchet: **6,588,840 / 6,588,910**, slack 70. Runtime production delta remains **+6 LOC**, necessary owner cleanup; no new runtime cache/config/schema/dependency/export.
- Fresh Codex autoreview of the complete candidate against `7c7a4d5d`: **scoped-clean at P0–P2**, no actionable findings. Committed bytes match the reviewed candidate.
- Historical watcher coverage: 29 tests pass under Bun, plus Node parent-death cleanup. One macOS/Node event-forwarding test timed out on the earlier candidate and parent `c1dbd2b6`, at different event-delivery phases. No first-bad commit was established; it remains an unresolved platform-test gap, not a proven inherited-failure exception. It was not rerun in this script-types repair.
- The earlier `check:changed` run on `c1dbd2b6` had 20 changelog-attribution violations traced to #194364; that historical red is recorded separately from the now-green exact-head CI.

prs.title: fix(agents): keep exec approval followup observation deadline on the monotonic clock
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

When an async `exec_approval_followup` run completes on the gateway, OpenClaw keeps observing it for a bounded 6-minute window before deciding whether to resume the originating session. That observation window is budgeted on the wall clock (`Date.now()`) but consumed by the monotonic timer that backs the gateway `agent.wait` RPC. When the system wall clock is adjusted (NTP step, VM clock sync, or a laptop waking from hibernation), the two clocks diverge and the observation window is distorted.

- **Problem**: `waitForAgentFollowupRun` seeds `observationDeadline = Date.now() + timeout` and reads `remainingMs = deadline - Date.now()`, passing that budget into a gateway wait consumed on the monotonic clock (`performance.now()` / `setTimeout`). Budget computed in one clock domain, spent in another.
- **Solution**: align the whole observation budget to the monotonic clock — seed `observationDeadline` and read `remainingMs` / `retryDelayMs` with `performance.now()`, matching the monotonic consumer.
- **What changed**: `src/agents/bash-tools.exec-approval-followup.ts` (3 deadline reads `Date.now()`→`performance.now()`; per-wait budget rounded up with `Math.ceil` for the gateway `agent.wait` integer `timeoutMs` schema); the deadline regression test now controls the monotonic clock.
- **What did NOT change**: the transport retry/backoff policy and the observation lifecycle (reason `"deadline"`, `transportErrors` accounting) are untouched.

## Why This Change Was Made

The observation deadline is a pure process-local closure (never serialized/persisted/cross-process), so a monotonic clock is the only correct source. The gateway consumer already computes its own monotonic `DispatchDeadline`; passing it a wall-clock-derived remaining budget is a cross-clock-domain mismatch. Switching the three reads keeps the seed and every remaining-budget read on the same (monotonic) domain, zero external contract change.

- **Best fix**: yes — one canonical owner, no new parser/policy branch.
- **Alternative**: keep `Date.now()` and rely on the per-wait `Math.min` cap; rejected because the cap only bounds a single wait, not the total observation window, nor the `retryDelayMs <= 0` exit from a forward wall jump.
- **Risk**: low — `Math.ceil` on the remaining budget never shrinks the observation window and always yields an integer accepted by the gateway validator.

## User Impact

Exec approval follow-ups for async commands now complete on a stable, clock-skew-proof observation window. Under NTP/hibernation clock steps, a healthy agent run is no longer prematurely declared complete (dropping slow terminal output), and a finished run is no longer observed far beyond its deadline.

## Evidence

**1. Shipped exec-host public-entry clock-skew proof, both directions.** Driven through the exec-host **public shipped entry** `sendExecApprovalFollowupResult` (`bash-tools.exec-host-shared.ts`) — the exact function `exec-host-node.ts` / `exec-host-gateway.ts` call after an approved async exec. It registers the handoff, then `sendExecApprovalFollowup` runs through the **production** `GatewayRecoveryRuntime` the Gateway registers at startup — **no** `registerGatewayRecoveryRuntime` override, **no** internal-function call. Both the `agent` dispatch (production `recovery.dispatchAgent` → real in-process `agent.run`, accepted against a synthetic-provider run that stays pending) and the wait (production `recovery.waitForAgent` → shipped wait transport) are unmodified shipped code. A 30 s wall step (−30 s / +30 s) is injected inside `waitForAgentFollowupRun` via a `Date.now` proxy; a pass-through probe on `recovery.waitForAgent` records the round-1 budget handed to the wait transport. (Observation budget shortened 6 m→20 s as a disclosed control; the per-wait cap cannot mask it.)

```console
# BACKWARD (−30s rewind)
[proof] production recovery runtime present = true (Gateway auto-registered)
[proof] recovery.waitForAgent budget timeoutMs=20000 -> shipped wait transport   # post-fix: BOUNDED
[proof] recovery.waitForAgent budget timeoutMs=49999 -> shipped wait transport   # pre-fix: INFLATED +30s
# FORWARD (+30s jump)
[proof] recovery.waitForAgent budget timeoutMs=20000 -> shipped wait transport   # post-fix: BOUNDED, observation proceeds
[proof] outcome=undefined elapsed=2652ms / NO agent.wait dispatched             # pre-fix: observation ENDED IMMEDIATELY (drops slow output)
```

| leg | skew | production-recovery budget (round 1) | window |
|---|---|---|---|
| post-fix | −30 s | 20000 | bounded |
| pre-fix | −30 s | 49999 | inflated +30 s |
| post-fix | +30 s | 20000 (proceeds) | bounded |
| pre-fix | +30 s | none (ends immediately) | drops slow output |

Keeping the budget on the monotonic clock makes the shipped wait budget immune to wall-clock steps in both directions. The accepted run stays the sole delivery owner (`direct_deliveries=0`; no competing direct delivery), and the integer `timeoutMs` passes the shipped `validateAgentWaitParams`.

**2. Integer-boundary proof (P2).** `performance.now()` is fractional; the `agent.wait` schema requires an integer `timeoutMs`. `sendExecApprovalFollowup` was driven through a recovery runtime whose `waitForAgent` re-runs the shipped validator on the exact params. Same fractional remaining budget (59999.75 ms), before vs after the one-line `Math.ceil`:

```console
before: [waitForAgent] timeoutMs=59999.75 -> shipped validator: REJECT
after : [waitForAgent] timeoutMs=60000   -> shipped validator: ACCEPT
```

`Math.ceil(59999.75) === 60000` never shrinks the budget; `Math.max(1, ...)` keeps the positive minimum.

**3. Regression.** Pre-fix the new test fails (`Number.isInteger(59999.75)` false); post-fix it passes, full suite green (18/18).

**What was not tested**: the divergence itself (NTP/hibernation) is injected by the proof; direct-delivery and session-resume paths are unchanged and covered by existing suites.

**Collision check**: `origin/main` still has the wall-clock reads (bug live); sibling PR #181942 touches the same three reads for the same defect; #181942 open.

prs.title: fix: show multi-question reply format
prs.body:
Closes #173760

AI-assisted. Substantially follows the shared-guidance and regression shape from #173845 by @D41910; the commit credits Winoren as co-author.

## Summary

- Show one bounded, copyable multiline example in the initial multi-question prompt and invalid-answer recovery notice.
- Document the same accepted reply format.
- Derive the regression's successful reply from the displayed example so guidance and parser behavior cannot drift.

## Issue

Closes #173760.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: messaging-channel users can be told to answer every `ask_user` question by number or id without being shown that each answer needs its own keyed line.

## User Impact

User impact: after an incomplete grouped answer is rejected, the user sees a concrete two-line reply template and can fill it in while the same question remains open.

## Root cause

The multi-question parser already accepts one keyed answer per line, but the shared prompt owner and rejection notice exposed only abstract wording. A normal one-line prose reply fills question 1 and leaves later required questions empty, so the recovery path repeated guidance that did not demonstrate the required shape.

## Why This Change Was Made

The shared prompt guidance is the canonical owner for this format. Reusing one bounded constant in the initial prompt and rejection notice fixes both user-visible paths without changing parsing, validation, authorization, custody, or question lifecycle. #190513 remains complementary parser/numbering work; #193400 remains complementary correction-delivery work.

## Verification

- Exact upstream base: `c61a7c0cf6b72f9c35ad8acdc432e132f4d86a50`; the five touched files were unchanged from the reproduced `95363ce54afd893d89cc6bd6645578dba52888d0` snapshot.
- Before source oracle: exit 1. A one-line two-question answer populated `where`, left `game` empty, and found no copyable example in prompt, rejection, or docs.
- After the same oracle: exit 0. It extracted `1: <answer for question 1>\n2: <answer for question 2>`, filled it as `1: Lisbon\n2: 2000`, and mapped both keyed answers while confirming the rejection notice and docs use the same format.
- `node --experimental-strip-types --check` passed for all four touched TypeScript files.
- `node scripts/docs-list.js` passed.
- `git diff --check` passed.
- Production delta: `+6/-2` (net +4); tests `+13/-6`; docs `+10/-3`.

## Before/after

Before:

```json
{"answers":{"where":"either is fine, and lets do X","game":""},"hasExample":false,"docsExplain":false,"reproduced":true}
```

After:

```json
{"example":"1: <answer for question 1>\n2: <answer for question 2>","completeAnswer":"1: Lisbon\n2: 2000","answers":{"destination":"Lisbon","budget":"2000"},"correctionUsesShared":true,"docsExplain":true,"fixed":true}
```

## Real behavior proof

- **Behavior addressed:** Multi-question text prompts and invalid-answer recovery now show the keyed multiline reply shape the existing parser accepts.
- **Real environment tested:** Exact current OpenClaw source snapshot on macOS with Node 22.22.3; source-level behavior oracle plus syntax/docs/diff checks.
- **Exact steps or command run after this patch:** Node source oracle reading the production prompt, rejection, parser contract, and docs; `node --experimental-strip-types --check` on the four TypeScript files; `node scripts/docs-list.js`; `git diff --check`.
- **Evidence after fix:** The oracle derived `1: Lisbon\n2: 2000` from the displayed example, resolved both keyed answers, confirmed both runtime messages share the guidance, and exited 0.
- **Observed result after fix:** The user-visible recovery text now contains a copyable answer that satisfies both questions without changing parser or lifecycle semantics.
- **What was not tested:** No live Telegram account, deployed Gateway, external model/API, or focused Vitest run.

## Risk and scope

Low. This changes shared bounded guidance, one recovery string, one documentation paragraph, and assertions around the existing custody flow. No config, schema, protocol, persistence, parser, validation, authorization, or delivery lifecycle changes.

## Not tested

Focused Vitest did not start. Blacksmith Testbox failed before allocation because the local `blacksmith` executable is unavailable. Local dependency installation failed first because the configured npm mirror lacks `@pnpm/macos-arm64@12.15.0`, then because Corepack's pnpm 12.15.0 cache was incomplete. The repository formatter and autoreview also could not bootstrap through the same blocked network path; no passing claim is made for them.

prs.title: docs(gateway): correct Gateway port precedence for named profiles
prs.body:
Related: #191428

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: the documented Gateway port precedence points to `18789` when a named profile is selected and no port is set.

## User Impact

Operators who select a named profile with `--profile <name>` or `OPENCLAW_PROFILE` and set no port can find the port the Gateway actually uses: `19001` for `dev`, otherwise a port derived from the profile name. They can also see that `--profile dev` puts `19001` ahead of `gateway.port`.

## Why This Change Was Made

Port resolution checks the named-profile default after `gateway.port` and before `18789`. When `--profile dev` selects the profile and `OPENCLAW_GATEWAY_PORT` is unset, the CLI sets that variable to `19001`, so `19001` takes precedence over `gateway.port`. #191428 corrected the `dev` case of the named-profile default, but the precedence statements in the Gateway runbook, the Gateway configuration reference, and the ports FAQ still end at `gateway.port` → `18789`. This change adds the missing step and the `--profile dev` exception to all three, and states the default without documenting how the derived port is computed. Documentation only; runtime behavior is unchanged.

## Evidence

- Source at `90d24e96bea190397435b7126ebbc824e35d315a`: [`resolveGatewayPort`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/90d24e96bea190397435b7126ebbc824e35d315a/src/config/paths.ts#L358-L372) returns `OPENCLAW_GATEWAY_PORT`, then `gateway.port`, then the named-profile default for `OPENCLAW_PROFILE`, then `18789`. [`resolveProfileGatewayPort`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/90d24e96bea190397435b7126ebbc824e35d315a/src/cli/profile-utils.ts#L25-L36) returns `19001` for `dev` and otherwise derives a port from the name. [`--profile` sets `OPENCLAW_PROFILE`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/90d24e96bea190397435b7126ebbc824e35d315a/src/cli/profile.ts#L126), and [for `dev` with no `OPENCLAW_GATEWAY_PORT` it also sets that variable to `19001`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/90d24e96bea190397435b7126ebbc824e35d315a/src/cli/profile.ts#L150-L152), which the resolver reads before `gateway.port`. [`openclaw gateway` applies `--port` before the resolver](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/90d24e96bea190397435b7126ebbc824e35d315a/src/cli/gateway-cli/run.ts#L490-L496).
- [Existing resolver cases in `src/config/paths.test.ts`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/90d24e96bea190397435b7126ebbc824e35d315a/src/config/paths.test.ts#L151-L158) cover `OPENCLAW_PROFILE=dev` resolving to `19001`, `gateway.port` taking precedence over the profile default, and a non-`dev` profile resolving to a derived port. They call the resolver directly and do not exercise the `--profile dev` CLI step.
- On a Linux development host with this change applied to `90d24e9`, `pnpm format:check` (oxfmt), `node scripts/check-docs-mdx.mjs`, and `pnpm lint:docs --no-globs` passed on the three changed files; markdownlint linted 3 files and reported 0 issues. In a review checkout of the same commit, `git diff --check` on the same patch exited 0 with no output.
- Local ClawSweeper review (`--local-range` from base `90d24e9`, covering this diff and description) ran three times and reported no findings, risks, or security concerns.
- Documentation only; runtime tests were not run.

prs.title: fix(cli): models status no longer prints a core SDK deprecation warning
prs.body:
Related: #190243

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: `openclaw models status` prints a core-internal `[DEP_PLUGIN_SDK]` warning that blames the plugin SDK, and `openclaw doctor` prints the same warning when auth profiles exist:

```
(node:…) [DEP_PLUGIN_SDK] DeprecationWarning: Plugin SDK: resolveAuthStorePathForDisplay is deprecated; use provider/profile identifiers for displays (there is no public async database-path replacement) instead.
```

No installed plugin can clear it: the callers are core's own model-status and doctor display paths.

## User Impact

User impact: `models status` (human and `--json`) and `doctor` no longer show a plugin-SDK deprecation that points operators at plugin maintenance. The displayed auth-store path and every other field are unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

Three core display callers resolved the auth-store path through the deprecated synchronous `resolveAuthStorePathForDisplay`:

- `src/commands/models/list.status-command.ts` for the human "Auth store" row and `auth.storePath` in `--json`;
- `src/commands/models/list.auth-overview.ts` for the per-provider profile detail;
- `src/commands/doctor-auth.ts` for auth-profile findings.

The async twin already exists and is already used by the model directive reply path (`directive-handling.model.ts`). The command and doctor call sites are async, so they can await the same owner. `resolveProviderAuthOverview` becomes async to await it. The public SDK compatibility exports are untouched.

## Evidence

Real CLI on Linux with fresh isolated state, before and after this change:

Before (`main` at e673256f8a9):
```
$ openclaw models status
...
Auth store    : $OPENCLAW_HOME/.openclaw/agents/main/agent/openclaw-agent.sqlite
...
(node:…) [DEP_PLUGIN_SDK] DeprecationWarning: Plugin SDK: resolveAuthStorePathForDisplay is deprecated; ...

$ openclaw models status --json   # valid JSON; same warning on stderr
"storePath": "/tmp/oc-proof/state-models/.openclaw/agents/main/agent/openclaw-agent.sqlite"
```

After (this branch): identical human output and `storePath`, with zero `DEP_PLUGIN_SDK` lines. With a configured `auth.profiles` entry, `openclaw doctor` likewise no longer emits the `resolveAuthStorePathForDisplay` warning (the unrelated #195109 coding-tools warnings are left to that PR).

Regression tests:
- `src/commands/models/list.auth-overview.test.ts` fails on the base commit when the sync resolver is used and passes with the async owner.
- `src/commands/models/list.status.test.ts` covers the command's human and JSON paths with the same sync-resolver guard.
- `src/commands/models/list.auth-overview.secret-ref.test.ts` keeps the resolved-credential coverage on the async result.

Checks:
```
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run src/commands/models/list.status.test.ts \
    src/commands/models/list.auth-overview.test.ts \
    src/commands/models/list.auth-overview.secret-ref.test.ts
[test] passed 3 Vitest shards

$ node scripts/run-format.mts --check <6 files>
All matched files use the correct format.
$ ./node_modules/.bin/oxlint <6 files>
Found 0 warnings and 0 errors.
$ node scripts/check-test-lines-ratchet.mts
Test lines OK: 6588309; ceiling: 6588350; slack: 41.
$ node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs scripts/check-test-mock-exports.mts
Mock factory ratchet OK: 6357 grandfathered factories.
```

CI follow-up: the status test's throwing sync mock now carries an explicit return type, and its mock factory has an isolation annotation, so the obsolete mock-exports baseline entry was pruned.

Review: local `autoreview` (claude engine, claude-fable-5) on the full committed range raised one P0 claiming `resolveAuthStorePathForDisplayAsync` does not exist. Verified rejection: `src/agents/auth-profiles/paths.ts:62` exports it at the reviewed head, the branch build emitted it, and the built CLI ran the changed path with exit 0 and zero deprecation lines; the commands test typecheck reports no error in the changed files. No other findings. The Codex engine could not reach its service from this environment, so the alternate engine was used.

prs.title: docs(gateway): add 120-port spacing to multi-gateway FAQ and config docs
prs.body:
Related: #184694

## What Problem This Solves

The Gateway FAQ and the Gateway configuration reference tell operators who run several Gateways on one host to use unique ports, but omit the 120-port spacing between base ports that the multiple-gateways guide and the Gateway runbook require.

## User Impact

Operators reading either page now see that base ports must be at least 120 apart, so they do not pick nearby base ports whose derived sandbox, browser control, and CDP ports overlap.

## Why This Change Was Made

Each Gateway derives additional ports from its base port: the sandbox host, when active, uses base + 1, browser control uses base + 2, and browser profile CDP ports by default run from base + 11 through base + 110. The multiple-gateways guide states the 120-port rule, and #184694 added the same wording to the Gateway runbook checklist. This change adds that wording to the multi-gateway answer in the FAQ and to the multi-instance isolation section of the configuration reference. Runtime behavior is unchanged.

## Evidence

- Port derivation at `90d24e9`: the sandbox host port is the Gateway port + 1 unless configured (`src/agents/sandbox-host.ts` L21, L253-267). Browser control is base + 2, and the default CDP range starts at control + 9 and spans 100 ports, through base + 110 (`extensions/browser/src/config/port-defaults.ts` L15-29); browser config applies these helpers to the resolved Gateway port (`extensions/browser/src/browser/config.ts` L260-263).
- `docs/gateway/multiple-gateways.md` L20 and `docs/gateway/index.md` L194 at the same commit already state the 120-port rule; this PR does not change them.
- On a Linux development host at `90d24e9` with this change, these checks passed: `pnpm format:check` (oxfmt) on the two changed files reported "All matched files use the correct format."; `node scripts/check-docs-mdx.mjs` reported "Docs MDX check passed (2 files)"; `pnpm lint:docs --no-globs` linted the 2 changed files and found 0 issues; and `git diff --check` on the same patch in a review checkout exited 0 with no output.
- Local ClawSweeper review (`--local-range`, base `90d24e9`, this diff and description) ran three times with no findings, risks, or security concerns.
- Not changed here: above base port 65425 the default CDP range falls back to `18800`-`18899`, and above 65533 browser control falls back to `18791` (`extensions/browser/src/config/port-defaults.ts` L3-8, L10-29), so 120-port spacing alone does not separate such a Gateway from one on the default port, `18789`.
- Documentation only (+2/-2); runtime tests were not run, and Gateways were not started side by side. The overlap is derived from the source, not observed.

prs.title: fix: keep filesystem fixtures valid across fs-safe upgrades
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The fs-safe upgrade exposed filesystem fixtures that assumed synchronous reads and direct exclusive creation at the final lock name. These fixtures missed their intended fault or contention boundary after asynchronous admission and crash-safe staged publication, contributing to the full scheduled CI failure behind #194589.

Related: #194560, #194589.

## User Impact

Prepares the regression suite for the coordinator's fs-safe patch upgrade. This draft contains fixture changes only; dependency pins, lockfile, and runtime behavior are unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

Keep fault injection attached to the actual operation: recognize exclusive sibling stages, observe an existing lock for contention, model both metadata paths consistently, and inject read/cache conditions at the owning boundary. Synthetic volume statistics now preserve real bigint identities. Existing confinement, ownership, cleanup, FIFO, and error assertions remain intact.

The investigation also found two upstream regressions, fixed in openclaw/fs-safe#1079 and openclaw/fs-safe#1081. The non-9p preparation optimization is openclaw/fs-safe#1080. Those corrections are tested together here without landing the dependency bump.

## Evidence

- Reproduced the relevant failures with published fs-safe 0.27.1, 0.27.2, and 0.28.0. Async-read fixture differences begin at 0.27.2; staged-publication differences begin at 0.28.0. Adapted read cases also pass on 0.27.1.
- A local packed library containing all three upstream fixes, plus its matching native addon, passes all 16 originally failing test files: 280 tests passed, one Windows-only test skipped. This includes full lifecycle, migration, state-owner, build-ownership, capacity, workspace, sandbox, memory-read, prewarm, and affected tooling files.
- The real async FIFO swap still rejects. The explicit nonblocking flag contract is additionally covered upstream by `test/path-stress-regression.test.ts` and `test/pinned-open.test.ts`; both async and sync opens consume the shared flags in `src/pinned-open.ts`.
- Formatting, targeted typechecks/lint, test-line budget, and `git diff --check` pass. Net test growth is 40 lines, with an exact allocation; no new test cases were added.
- Independent isolated Codex P0–P2 review of the complete candidate against `f6a8ce9a6f2207121b7ffd5c6d65365fe1875d84` is clean. Review covers the supplied diff; runtime proof is the separate test execution above.
- Exact Windows execution remains a gap: the available remote provider rejected that target before provisioning. The Windows-only contender case must be covered by the full matrix before the actual re-bump lands.

Release-note context: test-only upgrade compatibility preparation; user-facing fs-safe fixes belong to the linked upstream changes.

### Full matrix required for the actual re-bump

Changed-scope PR CI is insufficient. The real manifest generator produces the same main matrices for a same-revision manual main-tier run and the schedule: 75 Node jobs, five Windows jobs, two macOS Node jobs, four Android jobs, plus the same UI/contracts/QA matrices, using the repository's configured hybrid backend.

On the canonical re-bump branch, after verifying its head:

```sh
branch='<canonical-rebump-branch>'
head=$(gh pr view <rebump-pr> -R openclaw/openclaw --json headRefOid --jq .headRefOid)
actual=$(gh api "repos/openclaw/openclaw/git/ref/heads/$branch" --jq .object.sha)
test "$actual" = "$head"
gh workflow run ci.yml -R openclaw/openclaw --ref "$branch" \
  -f target_ref="$head" -f validation_tier=main \
  -f test_runtime_policy=bun-all -f include_android=true
```

Use that branch as `--ref`; dispatching from `main` with a different target fails the same-revision guard. Bind results to the selected checkout SHA. No full-matrix workflow was dispatched as part of this fixture-only draft.

prs.title: fix: progress-card updates discard unrelated session caches
prs.body:
Related: #178731

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: updating or clearing a progress card invalidates cached session facts even when no session entry or transcript changes.

## User Impact

Progress-card updates and dismissals retain valid session-scoped cache receipts. Schema changes and real session mutations still invalidate them; authorization, commit admission, rollback, and dismissal revision checks are unchanged. No configuration or migration is required.

This is a narrow write-classification repair, not a demonstrated fix for the Codex child-completion authority failure discussed in #178731.

## Why This Change Was Made

The card writer leaves its affected session scopes unspecified, so card-only writes conservatively invalidate every tracked session scope. Certify an empty session-impact set only around the two card-row mutation sites. Keep lazy schema creation and the enclosing transaction outside those scopes, and restore any caller's enclosing session-write scope afterward.

The incognito memory actor is unchanged. No new cache, authority owner, retry, or guard exception is introduced. The production change is seven net lines; the existing worker regression is extended rather than adding another Gateway fixture.

## Evidence

- Before the repair, the public progress-card tool/RPC-handler path through the actual durable worker fails token preservation for both default and custom stores. The memory-kernel regression independently fails on the warm card update.
- After the repair, all 34 focused tests pass across the card kernel (11), real durable worker (7), incognito actor adapter (3), and SQLite scope owner (13). The final worker fixture also passes all seven cases after removing an unnecessary SQLite-only schema-admission call.
- Coverage preserves cold-schema invalidation, warm updates and clears, stale dismissal CAS, reset clearing, global write-revision advancement, enclosing session mutation invalidation, commit-denial rollback, FIFO behavior, and non-replay after a lost committed reply.
- Core production typecheck and the canonical other and gateway-root test typecheck scopes pass. Changed-file typed lint, formatting, whitespace, line-cap and test-line checks pass. The dedicated 64-line allocation covers the new receipt/scope-restoration regression and extensions to the existing real-worker test; the shared baseline is unchanged.
- Independent Auto Review through the OpenClaw engine reviewed the complete local candidate against 7c7a4d5db4adf174b324cfe47c17123808a7de61 at P0–P2 and returned scoped-clean with no findings. The reviewer did not execute tests.
- Proof uses real SQLite on Node 24.20.0 with synthetic content. Full suite/CI and live native Codex child-to-parent or Telegram delivery are not claimed. There is no visual UI change.

Investigation and PR requested by @jjjhenriksen (Jacqueline Henriksen).

prs.title: docs(slash-commands): qualify /update notices to owner destinations
prs.body:
Fixes #195449

## What Problem This Solves

The `/update` row in `docs/tools/slash-commands.md` promised a completion or failure notice "in the same chat". The update guide (`docs/install/updating.md#from-chat`) and the code both limit those notices to owner destinations. `src/gateway/update-run-notice-target.ts` skips any target that is not a current command owner, and any account whose `actions.sendMessage` policy disables sends. The run records the skipped notice either way.

## User Impact

An owner who runs `/update` from a group or channel no longer waits for a notice that will never arrive in that chat. The reference now says the outcome stays in the update run record and in Control UI.

## Why This Change Was Made

This is a docs-only change. The `/update` row and the paragraph under the table now match the update guide and the notice-target code:

- Notices go to the same chat only when that chat is an owner destination and its account allows sends.
- Otherwise the notice is skipped, and the outcome stays in the run record and Control UI.
- Owner destinations are `commands.ownerAllowFrom` entries or a linked administrator's direct conversation. Group and channel chats do not inherit a person's owner authority.

The owner-destination boundary from #146079 is unchanged.

| | main | this branch |
|---|---|---|
| `/update` row | "sends a completion or failure notice in the same chat" | same chat only for an owner destination whose account allows sends; otherwise skipped, outcome in run record and Control UI |
| matches `docs/install/updating.md#from-chat` | no | yes |

prs.title: fix(ci): leave PostgreSQL shard 1 headroom for PG16 smoke
prs.body:
Related: #195409

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes PostgreSQL conformance shard 1/3 timing out on pull requests when its PG17 tests leave too little time for the separate PG16 Gateway cron smoke.

## User Impact

No user-visible runtime change. Storage and updater PRs retain every conformance test and the PG16 smoke within the existing three-job layout and 30-minute job budgets.

## Why This Change Was Made

Reserve 150 seconds on shard 1 when comparing candidate assignments. The PG16 command took 139.37–141.43 seconds in successful baselines, including a second worker preparation of about 72 seconds; the reservation also leaves a small allowance for its service lifecycle. The planner previously balanced only PG17 work.

All callers retain one deterministic assignment, including scheduled runs without the additional smoke. With the committed timing model and current inventory, PG17 estimates change from 1,582.964 / 1,583.292 / 1,583.315 seconds to 1,500.094 / 1,649.072 / 1,649.034 seconds. Including the reservation, the estimated tail drops from 1,732.964 to 1,650.094 seconds. This redistributes work instead of raising the timeout. These are planning estimates; actual runner timing remains variable.

## Evidence

Successful unrelated PR baselines already consumed nearly the whole 1,800-second cap:

| Baseline job | Entire job | Separate PG16 command |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| [128851427694](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/42519965910/job/128851427694) | 1,769 s | 139.37 s |
| [128862969996](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/42523720314/job/128862969996) | 1,768 s | 141.43 s |

Related #195409 completed PG17 successfully but was cancelled during PG16 twice: jobs [128886667725](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/42531384512/job/128886667725) and [128897625637](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/42531384512/job/128897625637), each 1,815 seconds including termination/cleanup.

- Existing planner test file: 5/5 pass via `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs test/scripts/postgres-conformance-shards.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` (1.18 s wrapper wall time; 144 ms Vitest duration). The new regression fails on the original planner: equal PG17 costs of 200/200/200 instead of the smoke-aware 100/250/250. Eight new test lines have a scoped budget record because existing tests did not protect this reservation.
- Real runner `--list` selection: all 179 targets retained exactly once across the three shards; reversed-input planning remains deterministic.
- Typecheck restricted to the two touched TypeScript files and their imports using the tooling-test compiler options; touched-file type-aware lint, formatting, and `git diff --check` pass.
- Simplification pass retained one allocator change (+8 net production lines), one regression (+8 test lines), three documentation lines, and the required numeric allocation record.
- Independent local autoreview: P0–P2, scoped-clean for the candidate against `a272894e35656b6aa92d9d5dbea2f18a99459726`; only a test-local variable rename followed to satisfy lint. Local ClawSweeper was unavailable (checkout had unrelated changes and no built runner).

Broad validation and actual PostgreSQL timing are deferred to this PR's CI. No local PostgreSQL/container run was performed on the production host.

prs.title: fix(android): notify when an automation result is delivered
prs.body:
Closes #144395 ## What Problem This Solves Fixes: a backgrounded Android app shows no notification when an automation delivers its result into a conversation. ## User Impact Automation results announced to a conversation now post the same conversation notification as a normal assistant reply while the app is in the background, targeting the conversation that holds the result. Tapping it opens that conversation with the result visible, instead of the empty run conversation the issue reports. Foreground behavior is unchanged. ## Why This Change Was Made Reply notifications only came from `chat` final events. An announced automation result is written directly to the destination conversation's transcript and reaches clients as `session.message`, whose `message.openclawAutomation.kind` is `"cron"`. The run's own session keeps its messages hidden, so notifying for that session showed an empty chat; current main sends no message on that final event, so no notification is posted at all. The `session.message` handler now passes tagged cron results to the existing `onAssistantReplyFinalized` notifier, owned by the destination conversation. This reuses the marker Control UI already reads in `assistantMessageIsAutomationResult`. Untagged transcript messages, including mirrored sends, do not notify.
Root cause - `ChatController` handled `session.message` only through `applySessionEvent`, which refreshes history and session metadata. - `publishAssistantReplyFinalized` runs only for `chat` events with `state: "final"` and assistant text. - The Gateway writes `openclawAutomation: { kind: "cron", jobId, runId }` on announced results (`src/sessions/background-session-result.ts`), and `src/gateway/session-message-cron.test-support.ts` asserts it on the live `session.message` payload.
## Evidence Built the Play debug APK twice from clean `git archive` exports: `f4976c96853` (the `upstream/main` base) and `eac55fbf4f0` (this PR's commit). The two trees differ only in this PR's files, and only the fix APK's dex contains `openclawAutomation`. Each APK was installed on an API 36 emulator paired to an isolated Gateway (temp state, loopback port, mock model) with an isolated automation that announces to the phone's conversation. With the app backgrounded and connected (operator and node sessions in the Gateway log), the job ran via `openclaw automations run `. - Main: run `ok`, `deliveryStatus: delivered`, 0 chat notifications (`dumpsys notification`). - Fix: run `ok`, `delivered`, one `openclaw.chat.` notification with text "Security report: 0 upgradable, 0 security updates", using the same conversation tag as an ordinary reply in that chat. - Control: an ordinary backgrounded reply (`openclaw agent --session-key `) posts a notification on both builds. - Edge cases (fix): a second background run re-posts the same notification (count stays 1, new `when`); a run while the app is in the foreground posts nothing (`when` unchanged). - Tap (fix): tapping the notification body launches `ConversationNotificationLaunchActivity`, then `MainActivity` with `CONSUME_CONVERSATION_NOTIFICATION`, and lands on Chat in the destination conversation with the latest result visible. - Tap with a different, empty conversation selected: the tap switches to the destination conversation, the app requests `chat.history` (Gateway `--verbose --ws-log compact` log), and Chat shows the result. With the destination already selected, history is refreshed when the result arrives, so the tap needs no new request. - `ChatControllerTerminalAckTest.automationResultMessagePublishesItsDestinationConversation` fails with only the new call removed and passes with it. `./gradlew :app:testPlayDebugUnitTest --tests 'ai.openclaw.app.chat.*' --tests 'ai.openclaw.app.ConversationNotification*' :app:ktlintCheck`: 825 tests, 0 failures. `git diff --check` clean. | main: no notification | fix: automation notification | |---|---| | | | | fix: notification in shade | fix: after tap | |---|---| | | | | fix: other conversation selected | fix: after tap | |---|---| | | |
Emulator run output ```text main (f4976c96853, apk sha1 26a07bcc71ae) chat notifications before: 0 "ok": true, "status": "ok", "summary": "Security report: 0 upgradable, 0 security updates", "deliveryStatus": "delivered", chat notifications after: fix (eac55fbf4f0, apk sha1 967066be1715) chat notifications before: 0 "ok": true, "status": "ok", "summary": "Security report: 0 upgradable, 0 security updates", "deliveryStatus": "delivered", chat notifications after: tag=openclaw.chat.3bf83c613cab4a4029a19010 importance=4 android.text=String (Security report: 0 upgradable, 0 security updates) edge (fix): second background run while one notification shows before: count=1 when=1794143202128 after: count=1 when=1794143321512 edge (fix): run while MainActivity is resumed before: count=1 when=1794143321512 after: count=1 when=1794143321512 control (fix): ordinary backgrounded reply before: count=1 when=1794143321512 after: count=1 when=1794143380121 control (main): ordinary backgrounded reply before: count=0 after: count=1 when=1794143415428 tap (fix): notification body notification_clicked [0|ai.openclaw.app.debug|1|openclaw.chat.3bf83c613cab4a4029a19010|...] START u0 {act=ai.openclaw.app.action.OPEN_CONVERSATION_NOTIFICATION ... cmp=./ConversationNotificationLaunchActivity} START u0 {act=ai.openclaw.app.action.CONSUME_CONVERSATION_NOTIFICATION flg=0x24000000 ... cmp=./MainActivity} tap (fix): different, empty conversation selected 03:01:10 notification_clicked openclaw.chat.3bf83c613cab4a4029a19010 03:01:10.535 res sessions.patch 03:01:10.551 res chat.history tap (fix): destination already selected 02:57:50 event session.message (result delivered, app backgrounded) 02:57:51 res chat.history 02:58:13 tap, no new chat.history needed
