prs.title: fix(subagents): stops a finished sub-agent's chat being deleted before its parent reads the result
prs.body:
Related: none. I found no existing issue or PR for this symptom (searched open and closed PRs and issues for `shouldPreserveSubagentForMaintenance`, `requesterSettleWake`, `capEntryCount`, and the touched file paths).

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: a `cleanup: "keep"` sub-agent session is deleted by session maintenance (the `session.maintenance.maxEntries` cap) after the child finishes but before the parent has consumed its completion, so the parent's continuation can no longer read the child it was told to keep.

## User Impact

User impact: when a parent is still busy (or yielded) at the moment its child finishes, a new session that triggers a cap pass no longer removes the kept child. The parent's resumed turn can read the child with `sessions_history`, and the child's lineage/tool-policy snapshot stays valid until the completion settles. Once the requester settles, the child becomes ordinary cap-eligible again on the next maintenance pass. No config, schema, or migration change.

## Why This Change Was Made

`completeCleanupBookkeeping` stamps `cleanupCompletedAt` in the same step that arms `requesterSettleWake`. `shouldPreserveSubagentForMaintenance` returned `false` as soon as `cleanupCompletedAt` was set, so the child dropped out of maintenance protection while the requester still owed the completion. Sub-agent keys are disposable for the cap, so `capEntryCount` could delete the row inside that window.

The fix preserves the child while `requesterSettleWake` exists, and carries only the wake's `status` in the compact maintenance projection (`projectSubagentRunForMaintenance` / `SubagentRunMaintenanceRecord`) so persisted-only and live reads agree. This matches what the registry sweeper already does: it does not archive a run while its wake is outstanding (`subagent-registry-sweeper.ts`, the `entry.requesterSettleWake && !isCompletionAuthorityRetired` skip) and it resumes the wake every pass. Existing settlement paths clear the wake, which releases protection with no new timer, flag, or retry.

A one-line doc qualification in `docs/reference/session-management-compaction/maintenance.md` states the exception, since that page described sub-agent sessions as unconditionally disposable.

**Known boundary (not changed here):** if a requester session row disappears out-of-band (not through `sessions.delete`/reset, which drain and retire the obligation), the resume path keeps the wake owed by design ("the durable wake stays owed"), so it never clears. Before this PR that state already pinned the registry run; with this PR it also pins that one child row. Giving the wake owner a terminal outcome for a permanently missing requester is a separate change to deliberate temporary-unavailability behavior, so I left it out of this fix.

AI-assisted: written and verified with Claude Code; reviewed by a separate Codex pass and a separate Claude pass before filing (findings below).

## Evidence

**Regression tests fail on stock source and pass with the fix.** Stock = `git checkout origin/main -- src/agents/subagents/registry/subagent-delivery-state.ts src/agents/subagents/registry/subagent-registry.types.ts` with the new tests kept; base `85c39026a90`.

```
node node_modules/vitest/vitest.mjs run \
  src/agents/subagents/registry/subagent-registry-maintenance.completion.test.ts \
  src/agents/subagents/registry/subagent-registry-maintenance.test.ts --maxWorkers=1
```

Stock (red):

```
 × ...maintenance.test.ts > protects a pending requester wake after child cleanup, including restored rows
 × ...maintenance.test.ts > protects a dispatching requester wake after child cleanup, including restored rows
 × ...maintenance.completion.test.ts > retains completion policy through maintenance until requester settlement
   → promise rejected "Error: completion requester policy changed" instead of resolving
AssertionError: expected [] to deeply equal [ 'agent:main:subagent:child' ]
 Test Files  2 failed (2)
      Tests  3 failed | 5 passed (8)
```

Fixed (green):

```
 ✓ ...maintenance.test.ts > protects a pending requester wake after child cleanup, including restored rows
 ✓ ...maintenance.test.ts > protects a dispatching requester wake after child cleanup, including restored rows
 ✓ ...maintenance.completion.test.ts > retains completion policy through maintenance until requester settlement
 Test Files  2 passed (2)
      Tests  8 passed (8)
```

The tests assert both sides: the child is protected (and its captured policy stays current) while the wake is `pending` or `dispatching`, across persisted-only and live reads; after the wake clears, protection is released, the next cap pass deletes the row, and the captured policy check rejects. The completion test runs real maintenance (`applySessionEntryLifecycleMutation` with `maxEntries: 1`) through the host SQLite broker, so it is registered in the existing forked lane `test/vitest/vitest.database-worker-core-paths.mjs`.

**Checks on the changed files:** `check-test-lines-ratchet` OK (124 added test lines allocated in `config/test-lines-allocations/subagent-maintenance-settle-wake.txt`), `oxfmt --check` clean, `scripts/run-oxlint.mjs --tsconfig config/tsconfig/oxlint.core.json` clean, `scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p tsconfig.core.json` exit 0, `git diff --check` clean.

**Live runtime proof on two isolated gateways (red vs. green).** Bundle: https://github.com/Marvinthebored/openclaw/blob/proof/pr-193869/README.md

Same config overlay `session.maintenance = { mode: "enforce", maxEntries: 2 }` on both. Red = upstream main `95a3ccde141` plus other pending patches that do not touch the subagent registry or session maintenance; green = red plus this PR's source change, nothing else. Parent on the Claude CLI, children `cleanup: "keep"`. The cap pass runs on session creation, so each scenario opened a side session while the parent was still busy or yielded (wake owed).

| Scenario | Red | Green |
|---|---|---|
| Parent busy (spawn, then long tool calls); side session created while wake pending | kept child row deleted with wake `pending` | row survived; released by the first cap pass after the wake cleared (~2 s later) |
| `sessions_yield` with fast + slow child | both kept rows deleted before settlement (wake `pending`, then `dispatching`) | both kept; released ~2 s after delivery settled |
| Same yield flow; resumed turn calls `sessions_history` on the fast child | `No session found: agent:main:subagent:<id>` despite `cleanup: "keep"` | `sessions_history` succeeded; rows released after settlement |

Red lost the kept row in 3/3 runs that hit the window; green kept it in 3/3 and released it after settlement (deletion timestamps: `deleted-archives-red.txt` / `deleted-archives-green.txt`; per-run wake state: `runtime-proof.json`). Two earlier runs per build did not hit the window and behaved the same on both.

Red, resumed parent reads its kept child:

![red: No session found](https://github.com/Marvinthebored/openclaw/blob/proof/pr-193869/R5-red-no-session-found.png?raw=true)

Green, same step:

![green: sessions_history ok](https://github.com/Marvinthebored/openclaw/blob/proof/pr-193869/G5-green-history-ok.png?raw=true)

Gap: these runs reproduced the missing kept session, not a fail-closed policy-rejection log line; the policy-snapshot consequence is covered by the completion test above.


<details>
<summary>Pre-filing review findings and what I did</summary>

- Both reviewers: an out-of-band removed requester leaves the wake owed forever, which now also pins its child row. Not changed; disclosed above as a known boundary (the registry run was already pinned in that state).
- Codex: the maintenance doc described sub-agent sessions as always disposable. Fixed with a one-sentence qualification.
- Claude: a run whose completion authority is retired in memory keeps protection until restart. Same as existing kill-tombstone protection in this function; not changed.
- Checked and not real: retry cap exhaustion and terminal dispatch failure both clear the wake; `cleanup: "delete"` deletes the child before the wake is armed, so this does not block deletion; protected rows above `maxEntries` are already handled (the cap picks only unprotected victims); the SQLite maintenance projection does not strip `requesterSettleWake`.

</details>

Related: #190403

## What Problem This Solves

The iOS drawer does not let users manage session groups from their headers. The drawer and Sessions tab also need consistent group ordering and new-session defaults.

## User Impact

Long-press a custom group header to create a session in that group, edit its folder and working-copy defaults, rename or create a group, reorder it, or delete it. Empty groups stay available. Tap a header to fold or unfold its sessions. Sessions whose category has no saved defaults can still create another session in that group.

- [Before and after group controls](https://github.com/Marvinthebored/openclaw/tree/f3e52d0d24c2c50b8e158d56f6a2fc77ef258ee9/ios-drawer-groups).

Drawer search now hides group headers with no matching sessions, while empty groups still show outside search; covered by `drawer search hides group headers without matches`. iOS simulator (Xcode 27.2): OpenClawKit tests 60/60 passed; app tests `CommandSessionGroupingTests`, `SessionGroupStoreTests`, `SessionGroupMigrationTests`, `OpenClawTypographyTests`, `SwiftUIRenderSmokeTests`, `RootTabsPresentationTests`: 108 swift-testing cases passed, exit 0. prs.title: fix: retain native child results after interrupted admission on 2026.11.1
prs.body:
Related: #166022, #166023.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: a completed native Codex child's result is permanently dropped on 2026.11.1 when its first parent admission is interrupted after accepting the hidden input, for example with `SESSION_WORK_START_CHANGED`.

## User Impact

The parent can receive the result on a bounded later attempt without executing it twice. Cancelled or committed inputs, replaced sessions and revoked custody still prevent admission. No configuration or schema migration is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing reconciler treats every previously accepted input as blocked. This repair permits at most three deterministic successor identities only when the old input is interrupted, unconsumed, unowned and has authoritative evidence of no transcript commit. The old input remains inert. Unavailable evidence uses the monitor's existing bounded retries; claim-owned recovery is unchanged. The extra transcript read is opt-in and confined to this blocked-input recovery path.

This backport targets `release/2026.11.1`. `main` removed this recovery implementation in #185730; this PR does not restore that obsolete path there.

## Evidence

- [Exact-head native behavior and retained-principal proof](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/195376#issuecomment-6727360042): real profiled TUI/device-token execution recovers an interrupted hidden input through `:readmit:1` exactly once. Revoking that same captured operator source after interrupted acceptance prevents every successor model turn and transcript commit; requester replacement also prevents delivery. A separate trace correlates the same source from admission through retained custody to its actual revocation signal. Fresh canonical `pnpm build:runtime` passes, including all 14 runtime postbuild checks.
- The earlier device-token observation is fully attributed: ephemeral CLI clients deliberately remain unprofiled and did not capture operator custody. Their existing Gateway/system continuation is a different authority path. Both CLI and profiled TUI controls were compared with the unchanged release base: CLI accepted work can continue, whereas profiled-source revocation blocks delivery. The PR head additionally proves rejection between interrupted acceptance and successor model I/O. No further production change was needed; see the corrected proof for source links, redacted traces and offline SQLite receipts.
- The real isolated Gateway regression fails without the repair: after accepting and interrupting the hidden input before model/transcript execution, the next completion stays undelivered. With the repair, a successor commits the result once; repeated delivery does not execute it again. The exhaustion control accepts no more than the original identity plus three successors.
- All 93 tests pass freshly on `release/2026.11.1` plus this patch: Gateway 9, recovery 55, pending-input storage/memory 14, and SDK 15 (five files, four canonical shards). The wrapper took 463.42 seconds including cold worker preparation and imports. Coverage includes cancellation, committed inputs, live ownership, settlement during a read, failed reads, dirty transcript projection, requester replacement and revoked custody.
- The release-target core typecheck, touched-file typed lint, formatting, whitespace and canonical line-cap ratchet pass with no new violations. The focused test typecheck also passed on the previously tested installed baseline.
- Independent Codex source review of the unchanged patch found no actionable P0-P2 defect. Unrelated append-only native-handoff helpers from the installed baseline are excluded from this backport.
- Local deployment on the existing patched 2026.11.1 baseline passes the documented npm/Doctor procedure and authenticated Gateway health/RPC checks on the expected new build. The loaded Codex plugin comes from the local bundle. All 15,436 runtime files match the validated archive, with the previous 167 bundled plugins retained. This is operational proof for the local backport, not a live model reproduction or a full release-target package-build claim.

The automated regressions use real Gateway input staging, SQLite persistence, deduplication and SDK dispatch with a fixed agent-command boundary. The linked runtime proof separately exercises the real native app-server/model, Gateway and completion monitor without that mock. Neither claims universal recovery after every abort.

prs.title: fix(gateway): cancel steer document rendering on active run abort
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Steer document rendering (`renderInboundDocumentContext` at `chat-send-input-dispatch.ts:522`) does not forward the active run's cancellation signal. When a user interrupts a turn whose inbound attachment is still being extracted, the in-flight extraction keeps running until it naturally finishes or the process is forced to exit.

Related interrupt-forwarding repairs: #194391 (image descriptions), #194399 (attachment downloads), #194262 (marketplace list), #194076 (plugins search).

## User Impact

Interrupted steers cancel their in-flight document extraction promptly instead of leaving extraction running to completion. The repair forwards the same already-owned `activeRunAbort.controller.signal` that the surrounding admission path already uses for the run's abort signal.

## Why This Change Was Made

`renderInboundDocumentContext` already accepts an optional `signal` ("Cancels in-flight extraction") and threads it through `extractFileContext` into the attachment `getBuffer`/download cancellation path added by #194399. The call site was the only non-test caller that did not pass it. Forwarding the existing signal requires no new machinery — the abort controller is already in scope and already used for the late-reply abort signal at the same call site.

## Evidence

- Discriminating regression (remote, real test entry): the steer-document suite asserts the render mock receives an `AbortSignal` (mirroring #194399/#187438). On the unpatched production the steer-document case fails (133/134); with the one-line fix the suite passes 134/134. A control run with the assertion removed and unpatched production passes 134/134, confirming the failure is caused by the missing signal, not by the render-content assertions.
- Regression check: the adjacent `chat-send-message-injection` and `chat-send-steering-custody` suites pass (51 tests).
- Formatting, whitespace and staged line-cap checks pass. The test file is a grandfathered oversized file; the change nets zero counted lines (adds the mock assertion, removes a redundant `toBeDefined`).

prs.title: fix(telegram): honor group mention activation for commands
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Telegram currently treats an authorized bare slash command as an effective mention in groups. That lets `/steer` start an agent turn, or `/stop` / `/new` affect a session, even when the group's effective activation is `mention`.

This patch makes Telegram group and forum-topic commands follow the effective mention policy before native dispatch, text-command admission, media download, pending-text cancellation, or ingress supersede. It uses the existing `requireMention` / `/activation` contract; there is no new config surface.

| Context | Bare command | Command addressed to this bot |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Group/topic with effective `mention` activation | Ignored | Admitted if sender is authorized |
| Group/topic with effective `always` activation | Admitted if sender is authorized | Admitted if sender is authorized |
| DM, including direct-message topics | Admitted if sender is authorized | Admitted if sender is authorized |

Existing mention patterns and reply-to-bot implicit mentions remain recognized. A command addressed to another bot is not treated as addressed to this one. This intentionally changes the documented Telegram group command exception; the issue discusses the compatibility choice.

Fixes #164065.

## Evidence

- Frozen-base maintenance exact head `ca11b494906febdb43343c0cf356636530624027` is signed over immutable base `432ade6f500de6cdb0bcd4b0948a07bf466672f1`; clean merge tree `5be45911627da8853f95316bb4805a346e309b1a`. The deterministic preflight passes every selected lane, including full core/extension/test/script type graphs, Plugin SDK surface budgets, dead exports, touched lint/format, architecture/ratchet guards, import cycles, and `git diff --check`. A lockfile-frozen dependency refresh changed no tracked source or lockfile bytes.
- The latest exact-head review found media pre-download omitted configured participant mentions. This head now reuses the canonical group-thread mention facts there, preserves exclusive ACP binding behavior, and passes a registered-handler photo-caption regression addressed to a configured participant.
- Telegram command-gate and ingress-supersede tests: **26/26 passed**, including bare `/steer`, `/steer@bot`, other-bot addressing, DM, always-active group, and pre-adoption cancellation cases.
- The targeted native `/login` group test passed after updating its input to `/login@BotUsername`; it still proves that device codes are not sent publicly. The preceding hosted run had one failure because the old fixture expected a response to a bare command in a mention-gated group.
- Worker-backed Plugin SDK session read: the focused `session-store-runtime` read test passed. This replaces the new synchronous SQLite lookup flagged in the first PR review.
- Previous-head CI on `0afec71` found two branch-owned omissions: the new public async read exceeded the Plugin SDK export/callable budgets by one, and a bot-topic fixture still expected bare group `/status` to dispatch. Head `307710f` records that one-export expansion and tests both ignored bare `/status` and addressed `/status@openclaw_bot`. [Exact-head CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/37555349607) passed, including the SDK surface test and the Telegram extension shards; the aggregate `openclaw/ci-gate` also passed.
- The branch was rebased once onto upstream `b0c330d27df4` and force-pushed as signed head `0a0c63af2c3e`. A merge-tree check against current upstream `ae64a98a4eb1` is clean.
- The prior run also hit SQLite worker admission refusal in an ordinary channel-DM test, followed by a dependent zero-reply assertion. The command gate does not run for that non-command DM input. It did not recur in the exact-head full shard, but its root cause was not established; no code change is claimed as its fix.
- `oxfmt` on the two latest changed files through the repository's qualified tooling-owner pre-commit hook and `git diff --check`: passed. Earlier touched-code `oxlint` and assertion-safety checks passed on preceding heads; the latest changes add no assertions or casts.
- An isolated exact-head `check:changed` run passed the branch-owned gates, including formatting, policy ratchets, Plugin SDK exports/surface budget, plugin boundaries, core typecheck, all 27 core-test typecheck graphs, extension and extension-test typechecks, and script typecheck. The only nonzero gate was the full-tree Knip scan reporting two unused exports already present with identical references in the immutable base (`readSessionEntryCreationTransition` and `RESTART_CONTINUATION_CONTEXT_PREFIX`); neither file nor any reference to either symbol is changed by this PR.
- [Fresh hosted CI on `0a0c63a`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/37877199608) completed with 65 successful, 23 skipped, and 3 failed jobs. The two root failures are outside this PR's diff and byte-identical from the rebase base/current `main`: an existing two-file Madge cycle in `prepared-model-catalog-{fingerprints,worker}.ts`, and two `unbound-method` lint findings in `scripts/e2e/lib/upgrade-survivor/package-activation-fault.mjs`. - Repository-supported Crabline Telegram integration proof passed on the exact PR tree: the real Telegram plugin and an ephemeral Gateway ran against a local Bot API transport with a mock provider. In a mention-gated group, bare `/status` and `/steer` produced no outbound reply, zero provider requests, and no session mutation; `/status@crabline_bot` was admitted; another-bot addressing stayed quiet. Bare DM `/status` and bare `/status` in an always-active group remained admitted. This is transport-emulated integration evidence, not Telegram Test Server/TDLib proof.
- Real Telegram Test Server behavior proof is still pending. The exact-head repository doctor was attempted, but no existing Convex launcher could authenticate and no QA broker environment pair was available, so it stopped before acquiring a credential or starting a Gateway. A maintainer/credential-owner run of the group-capable `telegram-e2e-userbot` route is required; the automatic DM-only Mantis plan cannot prove this group-policy change. No live Gateway, Telegram account, or production configuration was changed.

## Review focus

Please confirm that making effective group/topic `mention` activation authoritative for commands is the desired compatibility contract, and review the one-function public Plugin SDK expansion required for the nonblocking session read. The patch keeps bare commands in DMs and `always` groups, and gates the early cancellation paths so an ignored command cannot still interrupt pending work.

Related: #50490

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: iMessage groups keep replying to unmentioned messages after an owner runs `/activation mention`.

## User Impact

User impact: iMessage group owners can use `/activation mention` and `/activation always` to change reply behavior without editing channel config.

## Why This Change Was Made

The iMessage ingress gate only resolved `requireMention` from channel config and never consulted the routed session's persisted `groupActivation`. This change reads the activation mode from that exact session and gives it the same precedence over group config used by Telegram and WhatsApp. Authorized control commands still bypass mention gating so owners can switch modes.

## Evidence (exact head)

- Exact candidate head: `f1c66eb055618f0aa79505abd7bfacb1498445c8`; frozen base: `432ade6f500de6cdb0bcd4b0948a07bf466672f1`; clean merge tree: `de8299f6f3c4776fce1a0e00db9843f8289c8f7a`.

Core and extension TypeScript gates and touched-file formatting pass under Node 26.7.0.
- Production path exercised by the mock-Gateway proof: `resolveIMessageInboundDecision` in `extensions/imessage/src/monitor/inbound-processing.ts` → `createIMessageGroupActivationResolver` in `group-activation.ts` → runtime `getSessionEntryInWorker` → SQLite worker-backed read; admission uses `createHostChannelIngressRuntime`. The test calls the production decision function with a routed group and real isolated SQLite store, not Apple's Messages transport.

Command owner-gating/persistence is separately covered by `commands-session.activation.test.ts`. This distinction matters: it is not a single end-to-end live Apple/command receipt.

prs.title: feat(apple): add opt-in OpenClaw ID node foundation
prs.body:
## Approved decisions / draft boundaries

**Draft only — do not mark ready or merge.** Stacked on `openclaw-517/node-ffi`.

1. **Durable node enrollment approved:** the app-private native node-target table and migration are implemented behind `OpenClawIDNodeTrustStore`; schema and file ownership are shown below. The in-memory store remains for pure protocol tests. App/controller integration is still incomplete.
2. **Separate iOS node key approved:** W is generated per enrollment identity in the dedicated `ai.openclaw.node-enrollment` Keychain service, never reused from the phone's operator/client-pairing identity. It is non-synced and `AfterFirstUnlockThisDeviceOnly`, not in SQLite or config.
3. **iOS build status corrected:** #194174 pins libc 0.2.189; [CI at `031aad5`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/42314731390) built all five Apple Rust targets and the three-slice XCFramework. iOS builds now; iOS runtime and app integration remain unproven. This PR's Swift adapter/runtime lane stays macOS-only.

## What Problem This Solves

Apple nodes need a node-role-only enrollment and tunnel foundation, plus a private macOS worker bridge, before they can connect through OpenClaw ID.

## User Impact

This is an incomplete, opt-in foundation, not a usable end-to-end enrollment feature. Native transport requires `OPENCLAW_IROH_NATIVE=1` and a source-built XCFramework; default builds remain artifact-free and unchanged. Without native packaging, binding fails closed with a readable error. The approved app-private schema/migration below is added; Gateway/shared and client-credential database formats are unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

Shared Swift code owns local node identity, pinned/fresh trust validation, signed enrollment, tunnel framing and node-role WebSocket transport. Uncertain enrollment delivery retries the exact signed redemption bytes, preserving Discovery deduplication. The native adapter uses per-operation cancellation and one connection-lifetime close observer. The macOS bridge uses an owner-only Unix socket and restricts access to worker routes.

A separate path-filtered workflow checks the default build, builds a same-revision universal macOS XCFramework, and exercises native Swift and opted-in shared tests. The FFI workflow now builds iOS slices; this lane remains scoped to macOS adapter/runtime proof.

Refs: openclaw-517.7, openclaw-517.8. Depends on the node-FFI branch; complements Android #194194.

## Approved native schema and restart behavior

**Owner/path:** the shared Apple native node adapter owns `URL.applicationSupportDirectory/OpenClaw/node-enrollment.sqlite`: normally `~/Library/Application Support/OpenClaw/node-enrollment.sqlite` on macOS, and the iOS app's sandboxed Application Support directory on iOS. The library accepts an explicit URL for isolated tests; controller selection/wiring is not implemented. This uses the existing `OpenClawNativeStateSQLite` primitive but a separate app-private file, because the TypeScript Gateway owns shared state and client/operator credentials have a different schema and lifecycle.

**Migration:** `apple-node-targets-v1`, empty version 0 → `PRAGMA user_version = 1` in one immediate transaction. Nonempty unrecognized v0 files, unsupported versions and incompatible v1 schemas are refused. SQLite uses `synchronous = FULL`; there is no timed pin/high-water pruning. Exact schema:

```sql
CREATE TABLE openclaw_id_node_targets (
  hostname TEXT NOT NULL PRIMARY KEY,
  claw_id TEXT NOT NULL,
  root_fingerprint TEXT NOT NULL,
  binding_sequence INTEGER NOT NULL,
  snapshot_sequence INTEGER NOT NULL,
  snapshot_issued_at INTEGER NOT NULL,
  snapshot_binding_sequence INTEGER NOT NULL,
  enrollment_id TEXT,
  discovery_origin TEXT,
  relay_url TEXT,
  server_key TEXT,
  peer_key TEXT,
  evidence_json TEXT,
  CHECK (binding_sequence >= 1 AND snapshot_sequence >= 0 AND snapshot_issued_at >= 0
    AND snapshot_binding_sequence >= 1),
  CHECK ((enrollment_id IS NULL AND discovery_origin IS NULL AND relay_url IS NULL
    AND server_key IS NULL AND peer_key IS NULL AND evidence_json IS NULL)
    OR (enrollment_id IS NOT NULL AND discovery_origin IS NOT NULL AND relay_url IS NOT NULL
    AND server_key IS NOT NULL AND peer_key IS NOT NULL AND evidence_json IS NOT NULL))
) STRICT;
PRAGMA user_version = 1;
```

The nullable target fields are all absent for an observation-only row or all present for a previously accepted enrollment. W and join secrets never enter this table. Binding pin, snapshot binding retirement, and membership `(seq, issued_at)` stay separate. The adapter rereads and merges/checks the current row inside the transaction, checks cancellation/current-attempt authority at effects, and acknowledges only durable commits.

**Restart does not require a new invite.** Reopen returns refresh metadata, not a dialable target. With the retained W, the existing client sends a signed descriptor GET (no redemption POST), re-verifies fresh signed evidence against durable pins/high-water marks, persists observations, and only then yields a verified target. Stored evidence cannot substitute for the fresh response. App/controller wiring, UI, device runtime and distribution notices remain open.

## Evidence

- **Durable trust / restart refresh (`c62fe1fd2500fce9ca9f74bae8bddb64d47e9803`):** exact-source isolated macOS compilation passed; **13 focused enrollment tests passed in 0.028s**, including actual SQLite empty-v0 migration, persisted independent high-water after reopen, two-owner merge/stale-commit refusal, signed GET-only reconnect without a new invite, rollback refusal after reopen, SQLite ABORT at both observation and target commit, canceled/revoked attempts, and foreign-schema refusal. The migration/store are new capabilities, not a claimed base-reproduced existing persistence bug. An independent read-only OpenClaw subagent reviewed the eight-file delta against `502b7ec259b5` for P0–P2 and found one P2: SQL LIKE treated the reserved-prefix underscore as a wildcard. The real native SQLite regression was **red** on that implementation (four failed assertions), then **green** after the two queries used literal-prefix GLOB; the coordinator confirmed this scoped correction, and no other verified P0–P2 findings remain. This was the coordinator-authorized subagent route, not helper-isolated/validated autoreview. Normal commit hooks, whitespace, scoped repository formatting and docs MDX passed. Local SwiftFormat/SwiftLint are unavailable; local workflow lint is blocked by missing Python venv/ensurepip. **Exact-head [Apple CI passed](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/42541187810):** artifact-free shared tests **25/25**, same-revision bindings and macOS XCFramework built, native loopback **1/1**, opted-in shared tests **25/25**. Terminal logs confirm durable migration/reopen, foreign-schema/revoked-attempt refusal and both storage-failure cases passed in both shared configurations. [Workflow Sanity](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/42541187629) also passed on this exact head; local tool limitations above remain local only.
- **Simplification:** enrollment and restart refresh share one verifier and one persistence/publication path. Necessary new state is one app-private table/schema owner plus its actor adapter; no duplicated signature/rollback policy or Keychain bytes in SQL. This slice adds 268 production Swift lines and removes 19, plus 145 Swift test lines (outside the JS/TS test-line ratchet), 47 documentation lines and one comment-only workflow correction. The first two persistence attempts were harness permission failures before exercising storage; the final sandbox grants only task-owned state and required ancestor metadata, while denying network/operator data/Keychain/preferences. No app/controller or device-runtime proof is implied.

- **Trust retirement correction (`ae4fc193d83e09f49bb74975f71394c88283b751`, protocol #194459):** signed four-attempt enrollment regression failed before the fix (binding retirement dropped 5 → 4 and replay returned a target), then all 10 enrollment tests passed in the same sandboxed exact-source macOS harness (0.023s); newest membership and maximum snapshot binding sequence now remain independent, with future-snapshot exclusion unchanged. The coordinator independently reviewed the staged delta and red/green logs with no verified P0–P2 findings; normal commit hooks passed. [Exact-head `swift` CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/42387168644) **passed** (2026-11-07 16:02:21 UTC): artifact-free shared tests **22/22**, same-revision bindings and universal macOS XCFramework build, native loopback **1/1**, and opted-in shared tests **22/22**; the new trust-retirement regression passed in both shared configurations.

- **Foundation:** 36 focused tests passed: 19 shared enrollment/tunnel tests plus 17 macOS bridge tests. Bridge proof includes upload and response larger than 2 MiB each way under a sandbox denying operator state and non-loopback outbound networking. The proof caught and repaired CRLF header truncation; the golden signature test now verifies cryptographically rather than requiring byte-identical signatures.
- **Default/native opt-in:** default build passed with the XCFramework physically absent; native build passed with it restored. After adding immutable redemption retries, 21 focused shared tests passed. The retry regression failed on the original owner with a lost response and passed with identical POST bodies through lost-response/429/503/acceptance; cancellation stops retries.
- **Native linking:** source-locked Rust build, SwiftPM compile/link and macOS app product link passed on Studio. The app was not launched. Real Swift → Rust loopback proved stream bytes/FIN, typed close codes, cancellation preserving other streams, and endpoint reuse.
- **Current macOS-only follow-up:** fresh arm64 framework rebuild and Swift compile/link passed; sandboxed loopback passed again. Generated binding hashes match the source. Earlier Apple commits are patch-identical after rebase onto `fad580f3ef88`; only the CI platform-selection delta changed.
- Independent source reviews found no verified P0–P2 issues in the reviewed integration and follow-up deltas. Normal commit hooks and whitespace checks passed. These are scoped reviews, not proof of the unfinished app flow.
- **CI at `d95076cbaad161af54891a4882bae71a23486213`:** [Workflow Sanity](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/42247081573) passed, including actionlint and zizmor. [Apple node native transport — swift](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/42247081566) **passed**: default artifact-free build, same-revision bindings and universal macOS XCFramework build, native Swift package tests, and opted-in shared adapter tests. Completed 2026-11-06 at 16:13:27 UTC. This establishes the scoped macOS CI gate, not Intel runtime, iOS, or end-to-end app enrollment. That historical iOS build failure has since been resolved by #194174; this result remains macOS-only evidence on its recorded head.

<details>
<summary>Retained local evidence paths (not public artifact links)</summary>

Under `/home/josh/.openclaw/workspace/reports/`:

- `ocid-node-apple-studio-20261106/shared-after.log`, `bridge-after.log`, `bridge.sb`, `validated-foundation.patch`
- `ocid-node-apple-native-20261106/PROOF.md`, `native-retry-red-tests.log`, `native-retry-green-tests.log`, `native-default-tests.log`, `native-optin-tests.log`, `native-token-macos-link.log`, `final-studio-logs.tar.gz`
- `ocid-node-apple-macos-20261106/PROOF.md`, `native-host-build.log`, `native-framework.log`, `native-package-build.log`, `native-loopback-current.log`, `native.sb`, `source-artifact-sha256.txt`

The fresh harness initially referenced an obsolete build layout and failed before test execution. Only the bundle path was corrected; isolation was unchanged, and the actual loopback test then passed.

</details>

### Unverified / before distribution

- iOS adapter/app integration and device/simulator runtime remain unproven. Multi-platform FFI compilation and XCFramework assembly passed in #194174; they do not prove this app flow.
- Intel runtime; CI will cross-build Intel but executes tests only on its runner architecture.
- Full unfiltered suites, including Keychain/preferences tests; deliberately not run against the operator's desktop state.
- End-to-end app enrollment, controller/lifecycle wiring, background/network-change behavior, and screenshots. Durable library storage and invite-free refresh are now covered by focused SQLite-backed proof, not a completed app flow.
- Pinned SwiftFormat 0.63.1 / Swift lint: unavailable, not installed. Local workflow lint tooling remains unavailable, but the hosted Workflow Sanity actionlint/zizmor checks passed (linked above).
- **Third-party license notices:** separate shared P2 before-distribution release gate across both native crates. The partial `generate-apple-notices.py` and `apps/ios/Resources/Licenses/iroh.txt` remain untracked and are not in this PR; inventory/source-obligation completeness is not claimed.

prs.title: fix(browser): report crashed tabs as tab-scoped failures
prs.body:
Closes #194667

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: the browser tool reports a crashed tab as a generic 20 s timeout and tells the agent the whole browser is unavailable, even though the browser and its other tabs keep working. `navigate` on a crashed target waits the full request budget, and the tab list gives no hint that the target is dead.

## User Impact

User impact: a crashed tab now fails fast with tab-scoped guidance to open the page in a new tab (or retry once a busy page settles), instead of steering the agent into browser-wide troubleshooting. `snapshot`, `screenshot`, and `navigate` all take that path; `tabs` marks targets observed as crashed in both the JSON payload and the CLI text output, and implicit tab selection prefers a healthy tab. Existing-session and extension-relay drivers keep their current behavior.

## Why This Change Was Made

A crashed renderer leaves its Chrome target listed while every page-level CDP command stalls. Snapshots waited out the full action budget and then attached the browser-wide unavailability hint, and `navigate` timed out the same way. The fix adds one bounded `Page.getFrameTree` liveness probe before snapshot and navigate work, maps Playwright `Target crashed` errors to a 409 with tab-scoped recovery text, and keeps the observed crash on the tab record for listing, the CLI handle list, and implicit selection. A dead renderer and a long-blocked main thread look the same to that probe, so the wording names both and suggests a retry once the page settles. Snapshot media helpers moved to a sibling module to stay under the file line cap.

## Evidence

- `pnpm test extensions/browser/src/browser/cdp-liveness.test.ts extensions/browser/src/browser/target-crash.test.ts extensions/browser/src/browser/routes/tabs.test.ts extensions/browser/src/browser/routes/agent.snapshot.local-managed.test.ts extensions/browser/src/browser/client-fetch.loopback-auth.test.ts extensions/browser/src/browser/server-context.selection.crash.test.ts` — 6 files, 93 tests passed.
- Real renderer crash (gated Chromium test, system Chrome): `OPENCLAW_BROWSER_CRASH_E2E=1 PLAYWRIGHT_CHROMIUM_EXECUTABLE_PATH=... pnpm test extensions/browser/src/browser/cdp-liveness.chromium.test.ts` — `Page.crash` then probe rejects with `BrowserTargetCrashedError` inside the bounded probe window.
- Independent live check by @wr-web (`Page.crash` + CLI on Windows) confirmed snapshot/screenshot on `906d205`; their navigate and tab-list findings are wired in `76b7e18520f` and `905b07cae7b`.
- Base behavior reproduced locally: after `Page.crash`, the listed page's WebSocket accepts connections but `Page.getFrameTree`, `Runtime.evaluate`, and `Accessibility.getFullAXTree` never answer; a healthy page answers in milliseconds.
- `pnpm check:changed` — all checks pass except the repo-wide `changelog attributions` check, which already fails on `origin/main` from untouched `CHANGELOG/` files (no changelog changes in this PR). The test-line allocation is sized to the final diff so the baseline ratchet stays at its existing slack.
- Gap: no full Gateway + agent turn was run; request-boundary behavior is covered by the route tests and the real Chromium probe test.

prs.title: fix(cli): message read loads every plugin when the channel plugin is external
prs.body:
Closes #185280

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: `openclaw message read --channel discord` loads the full plugin registry locally (about 0.5 GB and 20+ s of CPU per call) when Discord is installed as an external npm plugin. The Gateway already owns the action.

## User Impact

User impact: Gateway-owned `message` actions on external channel plugins now go straight to the Gateway without loading the plugin locally. A `message read` against npm-installed Discord drops from about 27 s wall / 31 s CPU / 526 MB to about 11 s wall / 12 s CPU / 430 MB on our host. The remaining time is CLI startup; plugin loading is gone (see Evidence).

**Risk: this adds a public manifest field**, `channelConfigs.<id>.gatewayMessageActions` (documented in `docs/plugins/manifest/surfaces.md`).
- It is optional. It is used only when the channel plugin is neither bundled nor loaded in the CLI process. A bundled or loaded plugin's `actions.resolveExecutionMode` still decides.
- An external plugin's manifest is untrusted data. Here it only chooses the Gateway route. The Gateway still runs its own account, target, and read-authority checks with its loaded plugin.
- Existing external Discord installs benefit after the next `@openclaw/discord` release that ships this manifest. Older plugin packages keep today's behavior.
- An undeclared action to an external channel now runs one extra validate-only config pass and one metadata snapshot read (~0.2 s) before the existing local preload.

## Why This Change Was Made

Fixing `isGatewayOwnedMessageAction` alone does not help. With the predicate forced to `true` on `main`, `runMessageAction` → `resolveOutboundChannelPlugin({ allowBootstrap: true })` still bootstraps the plugin, measured at 14.4 s / 596 MB. The message route needs a channel plugin object, even for actions it only forwards to `message.action`.

So the decision moves into manifest metadata, and the route gets a plugin object that needs no runtime:

- The manifest mirrors the actions the runtime adapter sends to the Gateway. A Discord test keeps the list equal to the discovered actions whose `resolveExecutionMode` is `"gateway"`, so the runtime adapter stays the single owner.
- When the scoped channel plugin is not available locally, the message CLI asks the existing runtime-free manifest channel adapter (`src/channels/plugins/read-only.ts`). For a declared action, it returns that adapter with Gateway-only `actions` and `outbound.deliveryMode: "gateway"`. The CLI passes it to the normal `runMessageAction` through the scoped plugin registry, so routing, target, account, and policy code is shared, not duplicated.
- Dry-runs, broadcasts, and undeclared actions keep the current local preparation path.

Production +190/−21 (including the 38-line Discord manifest entry and one line in `scripts/pr-lib/wrapper-components.txt`, because the manifest normalizer now imports `src/channels/plugins/message-action-names.ts`), tests +100, docs +15/−9.

The delegated adapter reads the normalized, typed `record.channelConfigs` with an own-property check, so it adds no type assertions.

## Evidence

**Before/after measurement** (taken on the first revision; the review repairs do not touch the runtime path). Release-shaped packages built with `scripts/package-openclaw-for-docker.mjs` from `main` (`ed141d0198`) and from this branch, so Discord is not bundled. Both runs use:
- the same `@openclaw/discord` package, built from this branch with `scripts/plugin-npm-publish.sh --pack` (the old core ignores the new field)
- a separate isolated `OPENCLAW_HOME` per variant
- a loopback test Gateway on port 28789

Command: `openclaw message read --channel discord --target channel:123456789012345678 --limit 1 --json`, 3 runs each, measured with `/usr/bin/time`.

Every run reaches the test Gateway's `message.action`, which the Discord plugin rejects with "read target channel is not allowed" (dummy token, allowlist policy). So all six runs exercise the same CLI → Gateway path. The host was busy (load average ~8), so absolute times are inflated for both variants.

| Run | Before wall | Before CPU (user+sys) | Before max RSS | After wall | After CPU (user+sys) | After max RSS |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | 31.0 s | 35.0 s | 525 MB | 13.4 s | 10.3 s | 431 MB |
| 2 | 25.5 s | 29.7 s | 524 MB | 10.5 s | 13.4 s | 429 MB |
| 3 | 24.3 s | 29.0 s | 528 MB | 9.0 s | 10.8 s | 429 MB |
| **Mean** | **27.0 s** | **31.2 s** | **526 MB** | **11.0 s** | **11.5 s** | **430 MB** |

CPU profiles of one run each:
- Before: `loadPluginRegistryHandle` 24.6 s inclusive, of which `createPluginGenerationArtifact` is 17.4 s.
- After: `loadPluginRegistryHandle` and `bootstrapOutboundChannelPlugin` 0 ms, `resolveGatewayDelegatedChannelPlugin` 0.2 s, `resolvePluginMetadataSnapshot` 1.2 s. The rest is CLI module loading.

**Tests.** Each of these was red before the fix.
- `src/cli/program/message/helpers.test.ts`: a read on an external channel whose manifest delegates it skips `loadPluginRegistryHandle`, runs config-ready in validate-only mode, and runs `messageCommand` against the delegated adapter. Undeclared actions still finish full config-ready and preload. 53 passed.
- `src/channels/plugins/read-only.test.ts`: a delegated read through the real `runMessageAction` reaches `message.action` with no runtime or setup load (fixture markers). This caught the outbound bootstrap during development. The same test checks that undeclared actions and disabled plugins are not delegated. 30 passed (the three delegation cases are folded into one regression; it goes red when `outbound.deliveryMode: "gateway"` is removed).
- `extensions/discord/src/channel-actions.test.ts`: the manifest list equals Discord's discovered Gateway-mode actions. 12 passed.

prs.title: fix(crabbox): recognize Boat in cloud worker OS discovery
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Boat cloud-worker profiles show no operating-system choices because Crabbox advertises `boat` as an alias of its canonical `ascii-box` provider. OpenClaw also lacked a Boat-specific setup guide.

Requested in https://x.com/heyneighbor/status/2119233044204929269.

## User Impact

Operators can discover Boat's advertised Linux target and follow documented setup paths for either hosting a Gateway on Boat or using a cold Crabbox cloud-worker profile. The hosting guide uses private port forwarding rather than public Gateway exposure.

**Draft / qualification gap:** live Boat allocation, node enrollment, an agent turn, workspace reconciliation, and teardown have not been tested. That requires Boat account credentials and authorization for a short-lived billed VM. No Boat resource was created. Full build and PR CI remain pending.

Boat's SSH/fixed-lease support is not proof of support for the Crabbox tool-sandbox backend, OpenClaw desktop, or warm images; the guide distinguishes these capabilities and keeps snapshots/reserves disabled in the example.

## Why This Change Was Made

Consume canonical IDs and aliases from the existing Crabbox catalog, pointing them at the same cached metadata. Crabbox remains the owner of native Boat API access, authentication, VM lifecycle, and durable lease identity. There is no new vendor plugin, SDK surface, credential store, configuration option, or lifecycle manager.

The guide was checked against Boat's official documentation at https://docs.boat.dev/ and the upstream Crabbox Boat provider guide. It documents the adapter's legacy authentication/configuration names rather than assuming `boat login` configures Crabbox.

Simplification pass: reuse the existing catalog owner and cache; no parallel provider implementation. Net production growth is 6 lines. Net test growth is 28 lines, covered by the exact, separate test-line allocation for alias discovery and mapped-catalog coverage; the shared baseline is unchanged.

## Evidence

- Reproduced with the real installed Crabbox catalog: before the fix `boat` returned no operating systems while `ascii-box` returned Linux; after the fix both return Linux. This is an offline catalog check, not a live VM test.
- New Boat regression failed on the original production code and passed with the fix. It covers aliases/canonical IDs sharing one catalog request, unmapped sizes remaining absent, and unknown providers remaining absent. Existing mapped-catalog coverage now exercises an advertised alias too.
- 95 focused tests passed across the worker provider, platform filtering, binary discovery, and profile suggestion suites (172.37 seconds wall time, including 125.39 seconds of worker compilation). After reducing the regression fixture for lint, the touched provider suite passed again: 67 tests, 60.89 seconds wall time. The final subsequent edit only renamed a shadowing fixture parameter.
- Targeted `tsgo` for the changed production module and repository ambient declarations: passed. Scoped repository lint: no problems in both changed TypeScript files.
- Docs MDX, config examples, and internal-link checks passed; 16,485 internal links checked, zero broken. Docs formatting clean across 1,421 files. Staged `git diff --check` passed.
- Local autoreview (Codex), P0–P2, complete staged change against base `a606a90b4bf57c143ad51677dd56a4c2426304e2`: scoped-clean, no actionable findings. Production and documentation are unchanged since that review; subsequent changes only made the test fixture minimal/lint-clean and adjusted its exact line allocation.
- CI seconds are not yet available; this PR remains a draft pending qualification.

prs.title: fix(ui): local performance base comparison reports false plugin UI growth after a full build
prs.body:
Related: #194544

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: `pnpm ui:check-performance:base <sha>` reports false Control UI growth on a no-op or dependency-only diff when the local checkout has a full `pnpm build`, which blocks local proof for every PR that runs it while main is already over its absolute caps.

## User Impact

Developers and agents get a trustworthy local performance comparison: a change that does not touch the Control UI now measures +0 B, and the report lists both sides' plugin UI inventories so any remaining difference is attributable. CI is unchanged (a fresh checkout packages only Settings presenters on both sides). Budgets, thresholds and the growth policy are untouched.

## Why This Change Was Made

Two causes stacked up, both only on the local path:

1. **Different plugin inventories.** The candidate's Control UI build consumes every plugin UI its checkout has packaged: all of them after a full build, Settings presenters only in a fresh checkout. The archived base only ever packaged Settings presenters, so the six extra plugin entries in the candidate's distribution inventory read as growth. The wrapper now reads the candidate's packaged inventory and asks the base's own builder (the existing `--prepare-settings` owner, which already runs the canonical build, asset-copy and metadata-copy steps) to package those plugins too. No new build list or step sequence lives in the wrapper.
2. **Silent no-op on macOS.** `os.tmpdir()` is a symlink (`/var` → `/private/var`). Node resolves the archived builder's `import.meta.url` to the realpath, so its direct-run guard never matched `argv` and base preparation silently did nothing; the base only got Settings presenters because its own Vite plugin re-prepared them. The wrapper now realpaths its temporary root. Linux CI's `/tmp` is not a symlink, which is why CI never saw this.

The base packages plugins with its archived builder on purpose, so builder changes stay visible in the comparison. Consequently bases that predate this change still package Settings presenters only; the new inventory line makes that visible. Once this lands, comparisons against current `main` pick it up.

Behavior change worth noting for CI: if a PR adds Settings views to an existing plugin UI, the base now packages that plugin too, so the comparison counts the added Settings entry rather than the whole plugin entry. That matches what full release builds ship.

## Evidence

Local, on a loaded shared Mac Studio (`nice`d), candidate checkout packaged with the canonical plugin asset build, asset copy and metadata copy for all ten plugin UIs (what a full build produces).

**Before** (current wrapper vs `origin/main` f6a8ce9a, no-op diff): FAILED

```
startup JS gzip vs base: 90782 B -> 90782 B (+0 B)
chat boot JS gzip vs base: 1295227 B -> 1295856 B (+629 B)   raw 4175975 -> 4178705 (+2730 B)
new boot JS gzip vs base:   802650 B ->  803279 B (+629 B)   raw 2614086 -> 2616816 (+2730 B)
violations: largest JS gzip 551.0 -> 551.7 KiB (cap 551.3), new boot JS gzip 783.8 -> 784.5 KiB (cap 784.4)
```

The +2,730 B raw delta matches the attribution from #194544 exactly.

**After** (this wrapper vs a base commit containing this change, candidate = that commit plus a comment-only UI edit to force a real base rebuild instead of input reuse): passed

```
Control UI plugin distributions: candidate clawrouter, deep-research, knowledge, mcp-relay, memory-core, nostr, openclaw-id-access, whatsapp, workboard, x; base <same ten>.
startup JS gzip vs base:   90782 B ->   90782 B (+0 B)
chat boot JS gzip vs base: 1295856 B -> 1295856 B (+0 B)
new boot JS gzip vs base:   803279 B ->  803279 B (+0 B)
```

An intermediate run with only the inventory fix still showed `base memory-core, nostr, whatsapp` and +629 B, which is how the macOS temp-root no-op surfaced.

**Regression tests** (red on the base, green with the fix):

- `test/scripts/control-ui-performance.test.ts` › "packages the candidate's plugin UI inventory into the base": candidate holds an extra packaged plugin UI; asserts both inventories match and identical inputs are reused at +0 B. The archived-comparison fixture now runs under a symlinked `TMPDIR` and its fake builder keeps the real direct-run guard; reverting the realpath fix fails with `base none`, reverting the request fails on mismatched inputs.
- `test/scripts/build-plugin-control-ui.test.ts`: the Settings builder packages a requested non-Settings plugin UI and leaves an unrequested one alone.

Also ran: both test files in full (54 passed), `run-oxlint` on changed files, tooling `tsgo` leaf, `check:script-erasability`, `oxfmt --check`.

prs.title: fix(automations): updating an automation's owner fails with an unreadable schema error
prs.body:
Closes #187329

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: when an agent tries to change an automation's `owner` (or `declarationKey`) through the automations tool's `update` action, it gets an unreadable Gateway validation dump (`invalid cron.update params: at /patch: unexpected property 'owner'; … must match a schema in anyOf`). This happens because the tool schema advertised `owner` as a field for both add and update.

## User Impact

User impact: agents now get a plain error that names the field and says what to do: `owner can only be set by action="add"; remove it from the update patch`. The tool schema also marks `owner` as add-only, as it already does for `declarationKey`, so models stop offering it as a patch field. Creating automations with an owner is unchanged. Ownership stays create-only, because transferring ownership would widen the authorization boundary, and that request is tracked separately in #171451.

## Why This Change Was Made

`cron.update`'s closed patch schema deliberately leaves out `owner` and `declarationKey`, but the automations tool shared one job schema across add and update and let both fields through to the Gateway. The update path now rejects these two create-only fields before any Gateway call. The schema description for `owner` now says "(add only)", matching the existing `declarationKey` wording. The ClawSweeper review chose this direction (clarify create-only, do not admit ownership patches).

## Evidence

- **Merged current `main` (2026-11-03, `7f9c37d`).** Only the regenerated prompt snapshots conflicted; they were taken from `main` and regenerated (`pnpm prompt:snapshots:gen`, `prompt:snapshots:check` current). `main` brought `cron-tool.ts` to its 700-line lint cap, so `0bedba0` moves the `owner`/`declarationKey` check from the tool's `update` case into `updateCronJobFromAgentTool` (`cron-tool-write.ts`), before `cron.update`. The error text is unchanged. One ordering difference: an admin update that also patches `payload.toolsAllow` reads the job (`cron.get`) before the check runs; `cron.update` is still never sent.
- After the merge: `cron-tool.input.test.ts` › "rejects create-only owner / declarationKey in an update before any Gateway call" still fails with the check removed (`promise resolved … instead of rejecting`) and passes with it; `cron-tool.test.ts` (58), `cron-tool.schema.test.ts` and `agent-tools.prefix-stability.test.ts` pass; `pnpm tsgo:core`, `pnpm tsgo:core:test`, oxlint and oxfmt are clean. The live proof below was taken on `8bd133c`, before the merge.

- Regression test: `src/agents/tools/cron-tool.input.test.ts` › "rejects create-only owner/declarationKey in an update before any Gateway call".
  - On `main`: `AssertionError: promise resolved "{ content: [ { …(2) } ], …(1) }" instead of rejecting`. The patch went to the Gateway, which rejects it.
  - With the fix: both cases throw the actionable error, and the Gateway is never called.
- Cron tool suites pass: input, schema, tool, management, output-contract, automation, creator-cap and stream-exec-policy (8 files, 163 tests). `agent-tools.prefix-stability.test.ts` also passes.
- The prompt snapshots are regenerated with `pnpm prompt:snapshots:gen`, and `pnpm prompt:snapshots:check` is current. The only drift is the new 29-character `owner` description in the serialized cron tool schema.
- **Live proof (2026-10-30, isolated Gateway, this PR's head `8bd133c` vs. its base `e07baef`):**
  - Setup: an isolated Gateway built from this checkout (separate state dir, loopback port). Each turn is a real agent turn through the Gateway's OpenAI-compatible endpoint (`POST /v1/chat/completions`, `model: "openclaw/main"`, a fixed `user` so the turns share one session). With shared-secret auth that endpoint runs owner-sender turns. The model is a local stub that answers each user turn with one tool call, `dispatch_action { id: "automations", args }`, and the tool result the model receives back is recorded. The job under test is created by the agent in the same session (`action: "add"`), so it is the agent's own automation.
  - Why the earlier attempt was blocked: `openclaw agent` and `chat.send` from the CLI are not owner-sender turns here, so `automations` answered `automations needs the owner's authority, and this turn was not started by the owner` before the update was tried. `/tools/invoke` does run as owner (with `gateway.tools.allow: ["automations"]`), but it returns the generic `tool execution failed` to the HTTP caller; the Gateway log shows the PR's message there (`[tools-invoke] tool execution failed: Error: owner can only be set by action="add"; …`).
  - Model-visible results, base build:
    ```
    update { owner: { sessionKey: "agent:main:main" } }
      error: invalid cron.update params: at /patch: unexpected property 'owner'; must have required property 'jobId'; at root: unexpected property 'id'; must match a schema in anyOf
    update { declarationKey: "daily-hello" }
      error: invalid cron.update params: at /patch: unexpected property 'declarationKey'; must have required property 'jobId'; at root: unexpected property 'id'; must match a schema in anyOf
    update { name: "agent-job-renamed" }
      ok, stored name is agent-job-renamed
    ```
  - Model-visible results, PR head (fresh state dir, same steps):
    ```
    update { owner: { sessionKey: "agent:main:main" } }
      error: owner can only be set by action="add"; remove it from the update patch
    update { declarationKey: "daily-hello" }
      error: declarationKey can only be set by action="add"; remove it from the update patch
    update { name: "agent-job-renamed" }
      ok, stored name is agent-job-renamed; owner unchanged (agent:main:openai-user:<session>)
    ```
- Local checks: `pnpm tsgo:core`, the core test typecheck shards for these paths, and oxlint on the changed files are clean. The line-cap and test-lines ratchets pass.

## What Problem This Solves

## User Impact

Explicit Gemini CLI selections reject unusable accounts before a turn starts. Valid API keys and Gemini-owned OAuth remain supported, and unspecified-runtime selections retain the documented OpenClaw API fallback.

Execution and readiness now share credential admission. Catalog projection preserves that decision, and default-model selections retain their resolved provider scope even when stored override fields are cleared. Static key references still require materialization; OAuth refresh remains owned by Gemini CLI.

Inspectable sanitized Gateway evidence: [retained baseline and candidate observations](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/195241#issuecomment-6729543254). - The same 57 focused cases changed from 12 failures / 45 passes to 57 passes. Another 43 existing regression cases passed, for 100 total; the combined local run took 144.66 seconds.

prs.title: fix(muse): correct README claim that auto never picks Muse
prs.body:
> **AI-assisted: yes**

Closes #194886

## What Problem This Solves

- The Muse plugin README (`extensions/muse/README.md`) told users the harness is "opt-in only" and that `auto` never picks it. That contradicts the canonical Muse guide and current native-catalog routing, so users reading the package README could wrongly conclude that explicit runtime configuration is always required, or misunderstand why a discovered native Muse model is selected.
- **Related:** #194886 (reporter prepared a README-only correction); separate from startup-cancellation PR #194884, which does not touch the README. Labels on the issue: `clawsweeper:queueable-fix`, `clawsweeper:fix-shape-clear`, `clawsweeper:source-repro`.

## Why This Change Was Made

- **Intended outcome:** The README selection paragraph now matches the documented and implemented behavior: explicit selection via `agentRuntime.id: "muse"` on a `meta/*` model or the `meta` provider, plus the existing implicit route where a model discovered by exactly one native runtime can use that runtime when no authored API binding or host credential takes precedence (an API catalog row alone is not an API credential). Explicit runtime choices and required cloud workers keep their existing runtime policy.
- **Out of scope:** No runtime policy or code change is requested or made; no changed links. The `extensions/copilot/README.md` wording is a different plugin and left untouched.
- **Highest-risk area:** None — docs-only, +6/−2 lines in one README.

prs.title: fix: identify exhausted budgets in worker capacity warnings
prs.body:
Fixes #194873

## What Problem This Solves

Worker capacity warnings hide which task or byte budget was exhausted and which discovery operation was refused.

## User Impact

Operators can distinguish pool and shared-compute budget exhaustion with bounded operation labels and numerical context. Limits, rejection codes, release signaling, and recovery behavior remain unchanged; no migration or configuration change is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

The admission owner now describes its refusal, and the existing startup warning preserves that message. Discovery producers supply their known operation kinds before lazy input preparation; the host restricts labels to its finite vocabulary and classifier. The real-worker fallback consumer asserts the enriched message while retaining error identity, no provider rotation, and stable user-facing failure guidance.

## Evidence

- Original focused proof: 224 tests across nine suites passed, covering actual discovery producers and startup warnings, all four budgets, privacy, release signaling, custody, cleanup, and discovery consumers.
- First CI check failed `checks-node-changed-compact-large-33` because an existing real-worker fallback test expected the old exact message. Reproduced locally (1 failed/2 passed), then repaired the exact enriched expectation. The same Node/real-worker file passes 3 tests; four related fallback/classifier/reply suites pass 146 tests. These are separate follow-up runs, not a fresh combined run of all prior tests. Hosted CI results on the follow-up head are not yet established.
- Original package build and focused static proof remain valid. Follow-up agent-test typecheck, touched-file lint/format, test-line ratchet, and diff checks pass.
- Follow-up real-worker file: 7.18s command wall/5.57s Vitest duration with one worker. Prior preparation 5.34s/3.67s; Gateway startup 5.84s/3.38s. CI seconds unavailable. Allocation 137 exactly covers original 133 regression lines plus 4 lines for the complete fallback diagnostic assertion.
- Author simplification passes and fresh independent parent source/evidence reviews completed for the original range `3651abf03ad..c9658b29374` and test-only follow-up `c9658b29374..b96d9c171e0`. Local autoreview and ClawSweeper were not run by the author.

The synthetic startup proof uses real pool admission and startup observers with discovery I/O replaced and a test-owned pool; it is not a full live Gateway boot or a reproduction/fix of the original overload recovery incident. Broad remote CI remains outstanding.


### Additional instrumented Gateway runtime evidence

The preceding startup-test limitation describes the original in-process harness. A separate disposable runtime experiment now executes the official CLI and built production Gateway startup from `b96d9c171e0f194a817e4fe10268f0f481be09af` and base `3651abf03ad802976e1a9a6fd46967ef96ef2e38`, with explicitly documented pressure instrumentation. No discovery, admission or warning function is substituted; the actual discovery pool is filled with128 synthetic unresolved lazy tasks at its unchanged default limit.

The candidate's native warning reports `task=sessionTranscript.session-target-inventory`, `pendingTasks=128 maxPendingTasks=128` and `inputBytes=2212`. The base's native warning remains generic. Both reach real HTTP readiness200 (`ready:true`, `coreReady:true`), release the synthetic pool to0, and exit0 cleanly. The qualified diagnostic oracle is red1 on base and green0 on candidate; setup failures are separately excluded.

This is instrumented full-startup proof with synthetic state, loopback binding and providers/channels disabled, not unmodified published execution or a live-user Gateway. Node safety guards deny real-home/network/service access; three synthetic supervisor queries are blocked before execution. Initial readiness snapshots include cold-start CPU degradation, so no steady-state performance claim. No original saturation cause or overload recovery fix is claimed. Runtime task-count budget is exercised; other budget reasons retain earlier focused coverage. Reproducible sanitized fixture, machine results and exact terminal excerpt are ready for publication-owner review. No new source changes or commit were made for this evidence; remote CI/review status was not queried by the worker.

prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes Doctor and Gateway startup failures when NFS leaves busy SQLite snapshot cleanup directories behind, while preserving best-effort candidate update checks.

Fixes #195396.

## User Impact

Verified snapshots can finish with a cleanup warning when NFS retains a busy directory. Doctor/Gateway preflight and strict snapshot callers still surface genuine cleanup failures. Candidate checks log cleanup hiccups separately, preserving their successful result or original read error.

## Why This Change Was Made

Close the published target before removing staging. Recognize regular `.nfs*` aliases and defer only classified final-removal `EBUSY`/`ENOTEMPTY` after private snapshot retirement. Keep identity, content, integrity, publication, and backup validation intact.

Candidate shared-state reads, isolated rehearsal source cleanup, and their parent schema inspection staging explicitly select warning-only cleanup. The shared parent helper remains strict for Doctor callers; unconfirmed worker termination still fails and retains staging. A warning never claims that cleanup or retirement succeeded.

## Evidence

- Mechanical refresh onto fetched main `ac26a0d7f1f8`. GitHub's compare API confirms it contains `3fa60aed3456`, the fix for the inherited legacy refusal-notice TS2345. All four existing code/test patches are identical through rebase; the refresh commit adds only an inherited-debt allocation record.
- Re-ran exactly two focused files, separately: candidate cleanup **20 pass** (49.91 seconds including cold worker preparation), snapshot transfer **23 pass** (7.87 seconds). These cover warning-only candidate cleanup and strict snapshot errors with NFS filesystem faults. Before this mechanical refresh, all 88 focused tests and touched-file lint/typecheck/format checks passed. Existing tests and assertions are unchanged by the refresh.
- The PR's own allocation remains exactly **215** test LF lines. Current main alone is **19 over** its ceiling (6,586,741 / 6,586,722); the unadjusted PR carries the same 19-line debt with its own growth fully funded. A separate `pe4-195409-base-debt.txt`, labeled as inherited main debt, funds exactly 19. Final CI-equivalent merge-index ratchet passes: **6,586,956 / 6,586,956; zero slack**. Whitespace checks pass.
- Prior independent local autoreview, P0–P2, found no actionable findings in the code candidate. Range-diff preserves that patch through the mechanical rebase. The review included unchanged Doctor callers; it was static, and omitted unchanged staging-token source following the prior helper filename refusal. The implementation author inspected that source directly.
- Native NFS live proof remains **MISSING**: the earlier Linux Testbox request exceeded ten minutes in queue and was stopped, with cancellation verified. Filesystem fault injection does not establish native NFS behavior.

prs.title: fix(cron): agent-less automations cannot be added or edited on multi-agent gateways
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: on a Gateway with several agents and `agents.defaults.systemAgent.agentId` set, `openclaw automations add` without `--agent` and `openclaw automations edit <job-id> --model ...` on an agent-less job fail with `invalid cron.update params: Multiple agents are configured, but this operation has no explicit owner. Select an agent explicitly; CLI callers can pass --agent <id>, ...` (`cron.add` likewise). The scheduler itself runs that same job on the configured system agent, so the job works but cannot be created or have its model changed without repeating `--agent` on every call.

## User Impact

User impact: agent-less automations now add and edit on the agent the scheduler runs them on. The inference-account capture for `cron.add` and `cron.update` resolves the owner the documented way (`docs/cli/cron.md`: explicit `--agent`, then an agent-qualified session key, then `agents.defaults.systemAgent.agentId` or the legacy/sole-agent fallback). When no owner is resolvable at all, the request now fails with the cron-specific hint (`Agent-less cron job has no resolvable owner. Pass --agent <id> when creating or editing the job, or set agents.defaults.systemAgent.agentId.`) instead of the generic selection error. Jobs with an explicit `agentId` are unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

`src/gateway/server-methods/cron-input-validation.ts` resolved the account owner with `resolveDefaultAgentId(cfg)` in three places (create capture, scheduled operator source, update capture). That helper is marked `@deprecated` in `src/agents/agent-scope-config.ts` because it only honors a raw legacy default marker or a sole agent and throws `AgentSelectionRequiredError` otherwise; it ignores `agents.defaults.systemAgent.agentId`. The run path (`src/gateway/server-cron-targets.ts`, `src/cron/local-service.ts`) uses `resolveCronJobEffectiveAgentId(job, tryResolveAmbientOwnerAgentId(cfg))`. The three sites now share one small helper that applies that same resolution, so validation and execution agree on the owner.

## Evidence

- New `src/gateway/server-methods/cron-input-validation.owner.test.ts` (two cases: an agent-less edit on an explicit two-agent fleet with `systemAgent.agentId: "main"` resolves; the same fleet without a system agent rejects with the cron ownership hint): without the change `2 failed (2)` (both reject with `AgentSelectionRequiredError: Multiple agents are configured, but this operation has no explicit owner`, `agentIds: ['main', 'worker']`), with it `2 passed (2)`.
- Consumers unchanged: `cron.validation.test.ts`, `server-cron.test.ts`, `server-cron.session-target.test.ts`, `cron.list-scoped.test.ts`, `server-cron-completion.test.ts` and `src/cron/isolated-agent.auth-profile-propagation.test.ts` (the existing test of the update capture): 160 + 120 + 40 = 320 passed across their three shards, 0 failed.
- `oxlint --type-aware` on the two TypeScript files: 0 warnings, 0 errors. `oxfmt` clean, `tsgo -p tsconfig.core.json` clean (exit 0), line-cap ratchet OK (2 changed source files, no over-cap growth) and max-lines ratchet OK.
- Field data from one Gateway on 2026.11.1 (`agents.ownership: "explicit"`, two agents, `agents.defaults.systemAgent.agentId: "main"`): `2026-11-07T16:15:08 [ws] res ✗ cron.update 1ms errorCode=INVALID_REQUEST errorMessage=invalid cron.update params: Multiple agents are configured, but this operation has no explicit owner. ...` for `automations edit <id> --model ...` on an agent-less job, and `2026-11-07T18:52:36 [ws] res ✗ cron.add 2ms errorCode=INVALID_REQUEST errorMessage=invalid cron.add params: Multiple agents are configured, ...` for `automations add` without `--agent`; the same job runs on `main` from the scheduler, and the same edit succeeds with `--agent main`.


### Runtime proof (isolated Gateway)

Full trace in the proof comment: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/194890#issuecomment-6717691469. Summary: an isolated Gateway (own state directory, loopback port, loopback OpenAI-compatible stub provider that logs the model and the sha256 prefix of the bearer key per request, synthetic keys) ran from the released `openclaw@2026.11.1` package and then from the same package with this PR's change transplanted into its `dist` cron chunk, on the same state directory.

- 2026.11.1, single agent: agent-less job j1 created and run (`succeeded`, request with main's key).
- 2026.11.1, agents `main` + `worker`, `agents.ownership: "explicit"`, `systemAgent.agentId: "main"`: `cron add` without `--agent` and `cron edit <j1> --model ...` fail with `Multiple agents are configured, but this operation has no explicit owner`.
- 2026.11.1 + this change, same state: j1 loads with its stored binding unchanged; `cron edit <j1> --model stub/stub-b` and `cron add` without `--agent` succeed; j1 and j2 run `succeeded`, both requests carry main's key, never worker's.
- Replaced key (same profile id) → later run `failed` with `Automation inference account was replaced ...`, 0 provider requests. Profile removed with `models auth logout` and Gateway restarted → later run `failed` with `MCP_AUTHORIZATION_RETIRED` (rendered as `... was removed or signed out ...` on current main), 0 provider requests.
- Another principal's personal account: not reproducible in a CLI-only isolated setup (needs the live human authority of `preparePersonalModelAccountSelection`, a path this PR does not touch); stated as a limit in the proof comment.
