prs.title: fix: Gateway retains completed reply runtimes after catalog reloads
prs.body:
Related: #150955, #159373.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: completed replies keep unnecessary model runtime objects alive when native async resources retain their context across catalog reloads.

## User Impact

User impact: ended turns release these closed runtime objects without configuration, permission, or restart-behavior changes. This does not establish that the original multi-minute outage is fixed.

## Why This Change Was Made

Keep borrowed snapshots, target data, and acquisition references with their existing owners. Separate persistent catalog status/live-generation readers from acquisition and publication-result scopes. Preserve the complete native source-authority metadata, live registration checks, and accepted-write settlement order.

## Evidence

Same maintained, loopback-only real Gateway flow: four sessions, 36 verified native tool captures, eight hot catalog reloads confirmed by `models.list`, then 65 seconds quiet plus GC. Native callbacks remain cached through the census.

| Post-GC ModelRegistry objects | Warm baseline | After eight reloads |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Base | 6 | 46 |
| Fixed candidate | 2 | 2 |

Acceptance was written before replay: final survivors ≤ warm baseline + one live successor. All 69 completed health RPCs succeeded; maximum outside intentional heap-snapshot windows was 8.9 ms. Gateway shutdown was clean.

Rerun: `node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs scripts/perf/gateway-catalog-context-retention.mjs NEW_SYNTHETIC_ROOT`. This measures constructor survivors, not throughput.

- Original-owner red/green GC regressions plus native Node target-data disposal/refusal proof. Focused catalog/generation checks (63) and target/authority/accepted-write checks (111) passed; dispatch and finalizer/custody siblings also passed. Reentrant revocation, replacement, abort, FIFO/custody and native-source metadata remain covered.
- Core/affected-test types, targeted lint/format, sourcePerformance build, both unused-file scans and exact 165-line regression allocation passed. No shared test ceiling change. New catalog-auth GC case: 83 ms; native target case: 681 ms. Native attempt-lane case takes ~12 s to load the real controller under Node/V8. CI seconds pending.
- Native AutoReview, P0/P1 scoped-clean: base `a5888561dd11438c28591ac57e5951ae1c8e13ce` → local tree `c6ff6b167bb9decd8d35dfda89e8018f0c652c6e`. Static review; runtime acceptance above is separate.

**Remaining gap:** overall post-GC heap still grows from 517 MB to 620 MB in this fixture (base: 517 MB to 623 MB). Neither that remaining heap growth, the multi-minute freeze, nor the restart-interlock concern is claimed resolved. Raw heap/CPU profiles remain private.

## Contributor credit

Requested by Jason O’Neal. Original report by @meircohen; retaining-path evidence by @shadow-enthusiast in https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/159373#issuecomment-6279805344.

prs.title: fix(cli): a claude-cli retry after a first-turn output refusal starts a new Claude session
prs.body:
Closes #192735

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: when a `claude-cli` turn's output is refused as unparseable in the session's **first** turn (for example `CLI JSONL output exceeded 8388608 characters`), the same-model fallback retry starts a new Claude session and re-sends the brief, so the work and context from the failed first turn are lost. The same failure in a later turn already resumes the existing session.

## User Impact

User impact: a spawned subagent (or any chat) whose first `claude-cli` turn overflows the stream limit is resumed by the retry in the same native Claude session, the way later-turn failures already are. Later turns, resumed or forked sessions, non-Claude CLI backends, sessions whose native transcript was never flushed, and runs whose settlement authority has ended keep their current behavior, because the existing first-session owner and its guards decide the write.

## Why This Change Was Made

The stream parser already knows the native session id when it refuses the output, but the executor threw a plain format `FailoverError`. Nothing had been bound before the first turn, so the retry ran with `useResume=false`. The executor now raises that refusal with the parser's partial output attached (`createCliStreamRefusalError`, kept in a `WeakMap` so the shared `FailoverError` shape does not change). The refused output also carries the executed prompt (`finalPromptText`), the same way a returned turn does, so a kept session still gets its reseed receipt. The CLI runner hands it to the existing `persistStoppedFirstCliSession` owner before rethrowing. The command attempt path, which spawned subagents use, now wires that owner the same way the reply-candidate path does, unless the run preserves its binding. That owner was added for directly stopped first turns, and it keeps all of its guards: no existing or reused binding, Claude CLI only, binding not disabled, native transcript flushed, and the session owner's settlement check. Callers that do not wire the owner (room events, preserved provenance) still bind nothing.

## Evidence

- Regression test: `src/agents/cli-runner/execute.output-limit.test.ts` › "keeps a refused first turn's native session for the retry to resume". It runs the real executor and CLI runner with a plugin-owned stream that emits `system/init` with a native `session_id` and then exceeds the turn output budget.
  - On `main`:
    ```text
    × keeps a refused first turn's native session for the retry to resume
    AssertionError: expected "vi.fn()" to be called once, but got 0 times
     ❯ src/agents/cli-runner/execute.output-limit.test.ts:134:21
        134|     expect(persist).toHaveBeenCalledOnce();
    ```
  - With the fix: the refusal is still thrown as the same `FailoverError` (`reason: "format"`), and the first-session owner receives `{ sessionId: "native-first-turn" }`.
- Command-path regression: `attempt-execution.cli.test-support.ts` › "resumes a first-turn session that the CLI runner kept after a format refusal". The first attempt keeps its session through the runner callback and throws a format `FailoverError`; the next attempt must resume that session.
  - Without the command-path wiring:
    ```text
    × resumes a first-turn session that the CLI runner kept after a format refusal
      → expected [ undefined, undefined ] to deeply equal [ undefined, 'refused-first-turn' ]
    ```
  - With it: the retry runs with `cliSessionId: "refused-first-turn"`.
- The existing guard cases in `cli-runner.interrupted-partial-output.test.ts` (resumed turn, unflushed transcript, superseded run, refused write) still pass.
- `pnpm test` on `execute.output-limit` (4), `cli-runner.interrupted-partial-output` (8), `cli-runner.reliability` (63) and `command/attempt-execution.cli` (88): all pass.
- Local checks: oxlint and oxfmt on the changed files are clean, `pnpm tsgo:core` passes, and the line-cap and import-cycle checks pass. The mock-factory check reports only `ui/src/pages/model-providers/profiles-view.test.tsx` and `ui/src/pages/sessions/sessions-page-cloud-stop.test.ts`, which are on `main` and untouched here. The core test typecheck shards that include this code pass. The `gateway-root`/`gateway-server` shards fail only on `ui/src/i18n/locales/en-terminal.ts(30,5): TS1117` (a duplicate `closeSessionTitle` key on current `main`).
- Test lines: `main` is currently over the test-line ceiling. This PR adds 58 test lines and allocates them in `config/test-lines-allocations/cli-first-turn-refusal-resume.txt`.
- Not separately tested: the reseed receipt itself also needs a history-prompt fixture. The change passes the same `params.prompt` the normal return path uses.
- **Live run with the real Claude CLI (2026-11-06, `claude --version` 2.1.318 with a subscription login, `claude-haiku-5-5`).** This head `ae4f621` against its `main` base `1db1416`, same steps, fresh state for each.
  - Setup: an isolated Gateway built from this checkout (separate state dir, loopback port). The model is `anthropic/claude-haiku-5-5` on the `claude-cli` runtime, with a same-model fallback `claude-cli/claude-haiku-5-5`, as in the issue's steps (the two refs count as separate candidates). Turns are sent with `openclaw agent --session-key agent:main:proof838 --json`.
  - How the first turn overflows: the turn limits are process constants (`cli-output-stream-limits.ts`), so the Gateway's `PATH` starts with a small `claude` wrapper. It runs the real Claude Code binary with the same argv and stdin. For the first agent-turn spawn only (argv has `--session-id` and no `--resume`, once per run), it holds Claude's `result` record and first writes 20,050 padding lines (`{"type":"system","subtype":"proof_padding"}`), then the result. So the Claude session is real, and Claude has finished and recorded the turn by the time OpenClaw refuses its output. All other spawns pass through unchanged. The padding is the only synthetic part.
  - Turn 1 prompt: "Memory check, step 1. Pick one random 6-digit number that does not appear anywhere in this conversation. Reply with exactly: picked <number>".
  - Turn 2 prompt: "Memory check, step 2. List every number you have picked in this conversation, oldest first, including any reply that may not have been delivered. Reply with exactly: picks <n1>, <n2>, ...".
  - The picked value exists only in Claude's own reply. Neither turn's `finalPromptText` contains it (231 and 216 characters, the same in both runs), so OpenClaw's prompt does not give turn 2 the first value.
  - Base `1db1416`:
    ```text
    11:35:08.565 spawn --session-id=30c9524e-688d-442b-9b93-8b5ad7fcbe21 --resume=-   (padded)
    11:35:11 Claude record system/init session_id=30c9524e-688d-442b-9b93-8b5ad7fcbe21
    11:35:13 Claude first-turn result text='picked 482917'   (then 20,050 padding lines)
    [agent/cli-backend] cli terminal failure: provider=claude-cli model=claude-haiku-5-5 ... error=CLI JSONL output exceeded 20000 lines; refusing to parse output.
    [model-fallback/decision] decision=candidate_failed requested=anthropic/claude-haiku-5-5 candidate=anthropic/claude-haiku-5-5 reason=format next=claude-cli/claude-haiku-5-5
    11:35:20.894 spawn --session-id=28996a5c-685d-4d0c-9b53-b25ceff91ef1 --resume=-   <- retry starts a new Claude session
    turn 1 reply: picked 684209      binding sessionId=28996a5c-…
    turn 2 reply: picks 684209       <- the first attempt's 482917 is unknown
    ```
  - This head `ae4f621`:
    ```text
    11:46:24.946 spawn --session-id=5124d4d8-1a9d-4832-bcb4-af37c83062b7 --resume=-   (padded)
    11:46:26 Claude record system/init session_id=5124d4d8-1a9d-4832-bcb4-af37c83062b7
    11:46:28 Claude first-turn result text='picked 482915'   (then 20,050 padding lines)
    [agent/cli-backend] cli terminal failure: provider=claude-cli model=claude-haiku-5-5 ... error=CLI JSONL output exceeded 20000 lines; refusing to parse output.
    [model-fallback/decision] decision=candidate_failed requested=anthropic/claude-haiku-5-5 candidate=anthropic/claude-haiku-5-5 reason=format next=claude-cli/claude-haiku-5-5
    11:46:32.783 spawn --session-id=- --resume=5124d4d8-1a9d-4832-bcb4-af37c83062b7   <- retry resumes the same Claude session
    turn 1 reply: picked 739046      binding sessionId=5124d4d8-…
    turn 2 reply: picks 482915, 739046   <- includes the refused first attempt's value
    ```
  - Claude Code's own transcripts (`~/.claude/projects/<workspace>/<session id>.jsonl`, user and assistant text only):
    ```text
    base  30c9524e…  user "Memory check, step 1."                      assistant "picked 482917"
    base  28996a5c…  user "Memory check, step 1." (with the retry prefix) assistant "picked 684209"
                     user "Memory check, step 2."                      assistant "picks 684209"
    head  5124d4d8…  user "Memory check, step 1."                      assistant "picked 482915"
                     user "Memory check, step 1." (with the retry prefix) assistant "picked 739046"
                     user "Memory check, step 2."                      assistant "picks 482915, 739046"
    ```
  - In both runs the refusal is the same `format` failover, and the fallback chain moves to `claude-cli/claude-haiku-5-5` the same way. Only the retry's session differs. Turn 2 reuses the warm Claude process in both runs.
  - The head run also has two spawns with neither `--session-id` nor `--resume` (11:46:36 and 11:46:48). They take no session arguments, so they cannot resume or write either Claude session. They are probably the Gateway's activity recap, an isolated utility completion: the base run logged `[activity-summary] Activity recap deferred` at that point instead. I did not confirm this from a head log line.
  - Haiku's "random" picks are close to deterministic (482917 and 482915 as first picks). The proof rests on the first attempt's exact value reappearing only in the resumed session, not on how random the value is.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

prs.title: fix(discord): preserve fenced code after marker lines with trailing text
prs.body:
Closes #127656

<details>
<summary>Additional instructions</summary>

Allow edits from maintainers is enabled.

</details>

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users receiving long Discord code blocks would see later code rendered as prose when the block contained a fence-like line with trailing text, such as ` ```not-a-close`. The same defect affects ordinary channel messages and webhook replies.

## Why This Change Was Made

Discord's chunker closed a block after checking only the fence marker and its length. Its closing rule now matches the existing shared Markdown contract: the marker must match, be at least as long as the opener, and have only spaces or tabs after it. CRLF fence lines are recognized, while backtick-containing info strings are not misclassified as block openers. The outer reasoning italic marker is separated before scanning, and generated closing italics are placed on a separate line after code fences with space reserved in the transport budget.

The repair stays in the Discord chunk owner; no SDK, dependency, or configuration changes. Separating the existing reasoning wrapper preserves its formatting contract while enforcing actual fence endings. Wrapper restoration also runs when only one nonempty message survives, placing the closing delimiter before trailing whitespace.

## User Impact

Code remains fenced across Discord message boundaries, including code that looks like a Markdown heading. Actual closing fences still return following text to prose, and outgoing messages remain within the transport limit.

## Evidence

- September 12 integration: rebased onto main `366335ad9cd6`, preserving the allocation improvements from #142447 and all upstream webhook tests. The only manual conflict joined independent test additions; `git range-diff` confirms unchanged repair logic. **237 tests passed across four suites**, covering chunking, ordinary sends, webhooks, and native-command replies. Targeted formatting, typed lint, `git diff --check`, and a fresh independent branch review passed for the rebased candidate `e211bb56f01b`. [GitHub CI passed on this head](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/34673184167).

- Before the repair: the three affected suites reported **9 failed, 193 passed**. The new failures cover false closers, CRLF, channel HTTP payloads, and webhook HTTP payloads.
- At the previously reviewed head `8a07c53835eb`: three suites reported **207 passed** under Vitest 5.0.0, including an additional regression for reasoning markers after synthetic closing fences. The tests use `mdast-util-from-markdown` as an independent semantic oracle and capture requests through local HTTP servers using the real Discord send paths.
- Review follow-up: the single-surviving-chunk regression failed for both `Reasoning:` and `Thinking...` before correction (**2 failed, 103 passed** in the chunk suite). Both now parse as actual emphasis, including when trailing blank lines are discarded. A further pair of cases for `__hello__` also failed before correction (**2 failed, 105 passed**) and now preserve strong emphasis rather than losing a content-adjacent underscore. The final 207-test run covers this correction.
- The initial repair passed full Discord plugin validation with isolated fork workers: **246 files, 3,343 tests passed**. A subsequent review found the synthetic-fence reasoning edge case; its new test failed before correction, and the final focused run above includes the correction. The default worker run previously exited unexpectedly after 2,812 passing tests; the isolated rerun completed without failures.
- Before the September 12 rebase, changed-scope formatting, lint, production/test typechecks, plugin boundaries, dead-export checks, and runtime import-cycle checks passed; that head also passed [GitHub CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/34071825635).
- Independent `autoreview --mode branch --base origin/main --max-priority P2`: **scoped-clean**, with no actionable findings.

```sh
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/discord/src/chunk.test.ts extensions/discord/src/send.sends-basic-channel-messages.test.ts extensions/discord/src/send.webhook.chunk-limit.test.ts extensions/discord/src/monitor/native-command-reply.test.ts
pnpm test:extension discord --pool=forks --isolate --maxWorkers=1
node scripts/check-changed.mjs -- extensions/discord/src/chunk.ts extensions/discord/src/chunk.test.ts extensions/discord/src/send.sends-basic-channel-messages.test.ts extensions/discord/src/send.webhook.chunk-limit.test.ts
git diff --check
```

Validation used Node 24.19.0 on macOS arm64. Live Discord client screenshots were not captured: this environment has no dedicated test bot/channel credentials. Local HTTP payload evidence does not claim a live Discord round trip.

Related follow-up: the shared `hasBalancedFences` test helper still uses the old marker-only closing rule. These regressions deliberately use the independent Markdown parser instead of that helper.

prs.title: fix(android): keep model names during temporary catalog gaps
prs.body:
Closes #195456

Related: #192252 (delayed-picker behavior is not addressed).

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: Android's composer replaces a known model name such as `Beta` with the raw ID `beta` when the catalog temporarily clears, even though the selected model has not changed.

## User Impact

The unchanged selection keeps its familiar name during disconnects and catalog gaps. Fresh catalog metadata replaces that name; changing Gateway, agent, session, or model clears it. Model selection, availability, eligibility, and request ordering remain unchanged.

**Draft — validation is incomplete.** Android compilation, executable red/green regression proof, lint, and real Android/Gateway before-and-after evidence are still required before this is ready for review.

## Why This Change Was Made

Keep a display-only name in the existing composer, keyed by its existing Gateway/agent/session owner and the selected model reference. The current catalog still owns model choices and capabilities. An authoritative blank name clears the remembered name rather than reviving an old alias.

## Evidence

- `git diff --check` passed.
- Independent Auto Review of the complete local candidate against `621ea221a4b074868c0d8c1191db783729068bd9`, covering P0–P2: **scoped-clean**, no findings. This is source review, not execution proof.
- [ClawSweeper's review of this head](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/195473#issuecomment-6729070920) found no actionable code defects; its remaining before-merge item is Android compilation and lint. Native/regression execution evidence is still pending.
- Completed the requested `pr-simplify` pass over the full candidate: retained one display-only state value under the existing composer owner and the two distinct regression groups. No extra source changes or test-only production seams were warranted.
- Added two real `ChatScreen` Compose-fixture regressions for unchanged `lab/beta` through disconnect/empty catalogs, fresh and blank names, cleared eligibility, and Gateway/agent/session/model invalidation. These use synthetic fixture data and have **not been executed**.
- Rechecked the repository's strict Android proof entry on 2026-11-09: it stopped before Gradle because Java and the Android SDK are absent. The supported focused Android Testbox attempt also stopped before source upload: this workspace lacks the source-capsule base ref (`origin/main`), and the provider diagnostic separately reports the Blacksmith CLI missing. **No compilation, lint, or tests executed.** No native screenshots or real Gateway proof are claimed.

<details>
<summary>Required follow-up verification</summary>

An Actions-authorized maintainer can dispatch the existing [CI workflow](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/workflows/ci.yml) from `main` with `target_ref=6d958f56ff856723a9ce19549de62aa1a4aeb57a`, `include_android=true`, and `validation_tier=main` to run the normal Android lanes without marking this draft ready. Confirm the checked-out SHA and actual Android job results; skipped jobs are not proof. Native before/after acceptance remains separate.

Run the unchanged new regression against the base to establish the intended `Beta` → `beta` failure, then run the candidate for green. Test wall time and CI time remain unmeasured.

```sh
cd apps/android
./gradlew :app:testPlayDebugUnitTest \
  --tests 'ai.openclaw.app.chat.ChatControllerCatalogTest' \

Inspect and deliver sanitized before/after screenshots in chat and embed them here. The Compose fixture capture hook is not a substitute for this native proof.

The simplified change adds 7 net production lines, 87 regression-test lines in the existing fixture, and a short Android README note. No controller, catalog, request, or selection-policy implementation changes.

prs.title: feat(android): enroll OpenClaw ID nodes with opt-in native transport
prs.body:
## Storage contract approved (Josh)

Josh approved the proposed Android durable storage contract on **November 8, 2026, at 16:28 PST** ("Approve: 1", relayed by the coordinator): one encrypted `SecurePrefs` record keyed `node.openclaw-id.$stableId`, where `stableId` is `openclaw-id|${clawId}|${rootFingerprint.substringAfter(':')}`. Approved fields are `claw`, `root`, `host`, `discovery`, `relay`, `admitted`, `seed` (W), and `trust` containing `binding`, `seq`, `issued`, and `snapshotBinding`.

The approved behavior advances durable high-water state for a newer signed removal snapshot and never exposes a dial target after storage failure. Node keys are separate from device-auth keys across platforms. The existing `OpenClawIdNodeStore.kt` / `NodeRuntime.kt` implementation matches this storage shape; no source change is needed.

**Keep this PR draft:** storage approval does not waive device/emulator proof, a real enrollment-to-Gateway connection, UI screenshots, or the license-notice distribution gate; these remain open.

Related: #194174 (native crate base). Coordinated work: `openclaw-517`; Android lane `openclaw-517.9`.

## What Problem This Solves

Android needs an explicit, owner-approved way to enroll as an OpenClaw ID node and reach its Gateway through the native tunnel without acquiring operator or chat credentials.

## User Impact

Opt-in builds provide an experimental paste-or-scan node invitation flow with a separate Discovery HTTPS origin, a six-digit verification code, and owner approval of the declared capabilities. This is node-only access, not an operator/chat login.

Native packaging is **opt-in with `-PopenclawIrohNative=true`**. Existing default build lanes remain unchanged: they do not require Rust/NDK or package this native transport. Generated Kotlin still compiles unconditionally; attempting an OpenClaw ID node connection without native packaging fails closed with a clear “native transport not packaged” error. Ordinary Gateway connections retain their existing path.

## Why This Change Was Made

The Android adapter uses the OpenClaw-owned UniFFI crate from native commit `92c25067451b1a105b1e83615da641e352c51e7c`, with matching checked-in Kotlin bindings. Enrollment verifies pinned signed trust evidence before dialing the verified server key over `openclaw/tunnel/1`; no TCP proxy, default relay, hostname dial, or direct WebSocket fallback is added.

Native suspend calls drain under `NonCancellable`, explicit cancellation signals terminate the underlying work, and returned resources are disposed if cancellation wins the handoff. Cancelling admission may retire this node's single connection; reconnect recreates it. Endpoint initialization is lazy and seed buffers are erased.

The dedicated path-filtered `android-iroh-native.yml` owns its NDK/Rust provisioning and verifies a pinned rustup-init checksum before execution. Shared Android actions, CodeQL, and the native owner's `iroh-ffi.yml` are unchanged relative to the base.

Scope/simplification: this is the Android consumer stage stacked on the separately owned native crate, not a second transport owner. The earlier shared CI provisioning and obsolete guard allocation were removed in favor of one opt-in packaging lane. Necessary growth is enrollment/trust verification, framing, the transport adapter, explicit UI intent, and distinct replay/cancellation/EOF regressions; the checked-in protocol fixture accounts for 1,127 lines. Against the native base: 39 files, 4,737 insertions and 19 deletions. No native crate changes are included in this consumer diff.

## Evidence

Passed:

- **24 focused JVM tests**, compiling the production OpenClaw ID sources with the generated Kotlin bindings, covering enrollment, tunnel framing, WebSocket behavior, durable replay protection after refusal, and native cancellation/cleanup.
- **Real host JVM → generated Kotlin/JNA → Rust loopback at native commit `92c25067451b1a105b1e83615da641e352c51e7c`**: framed HEAD status 101, FIN, maximum 62-bit numeric application-close code, explicit connect cancellation token, and a typed pre-cancelled dial. Built from the exact archived source with locked Rust 1.99.0 inputs; Linux x86_64 only, not Android JNI proof. Native library SHA-256: `5075327bfbed3e3cf89ab261b24648917d2781c03b37cc09b28bdb7bb1d66a0b` (13,185,944 bytes).
- Kotlin formatting, native i18n inventory checks/regeneration, actionlint 1.7.12, and `git diff --check`.
- Default protocol checks, without a protocol-base override.
- Independent cancellation follow-up resolved both prior P1 findings; the opt-in correction review found no new verified P0–P2 issues. Coordinator also inspected the opt-in rework.

**Packaging passed** at head `b3959bc24da3d965326483351b68cdae9ba213b3`: [PR run](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/42246599743) and [push run](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/42246594975), verifying the default APK excludes iroh and the opt-in Android variants build and pass their tests; this is build/packaging evidence, not device-runtime proof.

The unmodified generated binding builds in `:openclaw-iroh` with compiler warnings allowed, while the app retains its unchanged `allWarningsAsErrors(true)` gate; no native-generator-owner action is required.

**Unverified / required before completion:**

- Full Gradle build and task graph; opt-in native APK packaging/loading for all four ABIs; release shrinking/R8, APK size and ZIP alignment.
- Device/emulator execution, including a 16 KiB-page device; real enrollment-to-Gateway connection.
- Before/after screenshots of the new UI (not yet captured).
- Android Keystore behavior and foreground-service/lifecycle behavior.
- **Distribution license-notice gate:** the `openclaw-517` P2 task remains open. The inventory covers 285 crates; 20 archives lack notices. Complete transitive notices and MPL source-availability obligations for **UniFFI and `attohttpc`** are not complete. The current iroh/Tailscale notice is partial, not clearance to distribute.

No host SDK/NDK installation or app distribution was performed. Storage approval is recorded above; this draft does not waive remaining device/runtime proof, screenshots, or the distribution gate.

prs.title: feat(control-ui): inspect people and role permission limits
prs.body:
Related: #162980
Related: #162979

## What Problem This Solves

People cannot inspect saved roles and configured permission ceilings from the current Control UI.

## User Impact

Adds read-only **People** and **Roles** views under **Settings → People & permissions**, plus **View permissions** in person activity cards. Guests remain self-scoped. These views do not assign roles, grant access, or claim that a configured ceiling is someone’s live permission set. No migration or operator action is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

Reuses the canonical profile directory, applied configuration reader, and Gateway-provided effective roles and assignment sources. Profile changes retire obsolete reads, and open views load policy when read access becomes available. Query decoding stays behind the page’s lazy boundary; shared settings components own selection styling.

This current-base Solid implementation is scoped to permission inspection. It does not add the older proposal’s saved-role badge inside activity cards, modify that draft, or introduce a second authorization owner.

## Evidence

- **Refreshed against c1dbd2b6eebc59ed6db9d9756df1d0555d5407f9 through the supported same-workspace owner**, without conflicts, specifically to integrate the upstream repair for the failing legacy-notice core typecheck. Current published head is 8bf24d2fde8e5c9fd52c0094a071639103e2922b. The feature remains the same 23-file delta; no permission behavior or grants were added during integration.
- **Focused proof on the refreshed candidate:** 64 unit cases pass (7.07 seconds wall); all seven affected browser cases pass (69.66 seconds including build/worker preparation). These cover guest denial/self-scope, access loss/gain, resolved roles, invalidation/stale replies, person-card navigation, both views, local filtering, phone overflow, no role writes, and the shared census. This is production-UI/mock-Gateway boundary proof, not live server authorization proof.
- Production UI types and the formerly failing root-other test type graph pass. The test-line ratchet passes at 6,588,645 / 6,588,693 (**48 lines slack**), with only the existing scoped **+418 LF** allocation and no scalar increase. Scoped lint/stylelint, English, controller, format, and whitespace proof remains valid for the unchanged feature delta.
- Fresh independent Gateway-native Auto Review against the refreshed base reports **scoped-clean, no actionable P0–P2 findings**. [Completed hosted review](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/195408#issuecomment-6727288167) explicitly names current head **8bf24d2fde8e5c9fd52c0094a071639103e2922b** and rates **readiness 3/6, proof 5/6, quality 4/6**, with **no actionable findings**. Partial coverage of the broader linked request limits readiness; the omitted activity-card role badge remains out of this scoped patch. The review’s only before-merge item is maintainer use of the inherited-failure admission path for the unrelated Compact Details failure, or waiting for its upstream repair. The [request acknowledgement](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/195408#issuecomment-6729261474) confirms completion; [workflow run](https://github.com/openclaw/clawsweeper/actions/runs/42540401313). No merge or exception admission is performed here.
- Current production UI build completes. An initial local build could not create Rolldown’s thread pool; a serial build with task-scoped RAYON_NUM_THREADS=2 succeeds without changing source or budgets. It still reports a Chat-boot gzip advisory overage. Historical measurements against implementation base 44662c4c196431fdabf9ae3b1ddae62368f6857d were CSS +47 B and New/Chat boot −16 B; these are not asserted as fresh c1db-relative measurements.
- **Current-head CI has finished with a baseline-attributed failure, not green:** [run 42536774287](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/42536774287) passes all five core test-type shards, production/test types, ratchets, UI unit shards, performance, and i18n. Its only failed test job is [browser shard 5/7](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/42536774287/job/128903116865), at the same Compact Details line 94/missing summary reproduced on the clean admitted base and candidate. Two aggregate/status failures accompany that one job. No assertion, timeout, retry, permission, or budget was weakened. The bounded public readback reports 3 failed instances, 51 passed, and 49 skipped/neutral, but exposes only 100 of 126 total instances; it is not a complete job inventory.

<details>
<summary>CI attribution and exact refreshed-base proof</summary>

### Compact Details: reproduced on the current clean base and candidate

The [current-head CI failure](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/42536774287/job/128903116865) waits for a Subagents summary in chat-subagent-waiting.e2e.test.ts:94. After the supported base refresh admitted c1dbd2b6eebc59ed6db9d9756df1d0555d5407f9 in this existing worktree, the exact case was run once on that clean source tree, then once with the feature restored. **Both fail at the same line and missing summary** (25.08 and 28.22 seconds wall, respectively; both use the current local harness’s unchanged 10-second action wait). The index and all 23 candidate files were verified restored byte-for-byte. Each invocation owns a fresh bundled-UI build; no prior candidate artifact was used for the base run.

A reversible native-host diagnostic on the earlier candidate showed the correct parent, all four child rows, and desktop presentation. The [fixture’s children](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/c1dbd2b6eebc59ed6db9d9756df1d0555d5407f9/ui/src/e2e/chat-subagent-waiting.e2e.test.ts#L57-L72) have ordinary agent:main:dependency-N keys with no subagent classification. [The Details owner filters to native subagents](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/c1dbd2b6eebc59ed6db9d9756df1d0555d5407f9/ui/src/pages/chat/components/chat-details-background.tsx#L213), whose [classifier requires a native key or explicit classification](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/c1dbd2b6eebc59ed6db9d9756df1d0555d5407f9/ui/src/pages/chat/chat-spawned-subagent.ts#L88-L90). [Merged #195354](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/195354) intentionally removed ordinary-child Details rendering and retained the native collection. The stale scenario also expects that removed ordinary-child observer renderer.

The failure is therefore **baseline-attributed, not fixed here**. Its test and determining owner modules are outside this PR’s delta. Existing desktop/mobile exclusion tests and the independent live-observer run/incarnation/connection test also pass (three selected cases, 6.42 seconds wall). Rewriting the obsolete scenario or restoring intentionally removed product behavior is not part of this permission-view patch.

The current hosted shard reports 145 files / 567 tests passed and one failed file/case (425.25 seconds), timing out at line 94 while reading aria-expanded from the missing summary. The [terminal aggregate gate](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/42536774287/job/128905502305) fails for that selected browser job. Its informational comparison labels the signature new but explicitly says selected scope was not compared; this does not replace the exact clean-base reproduction above. No additional substantive failure appeared in the bounded watch.

### Former core-type failure: upstream repair now integrated and checked

[Prior core-type job](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/42526340082/job/128871444270) reported TS2345 in test/chat-history-legacy-refusal-notice.e2e.test.ts:46: .map(readRunFailureNotice) supplied an array index to the callback’s options parameter. [#188553](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/188553) introduced that call in the old merged base. The refreshed canonical source now uses an explicit one-argument callback, and the actual root-other type graph passes locally with the new test present. All five current-head hosted core test-type shards also pass. Neither the upstream test nor helper becomes part of this PR’s feature delta.

### Earlier investigated failures

The original census P2 is repaired and re-proven: its existing nine-case unit suite was red before the repair and green afterward; all five census/route-asset browser cases pass on the refreshed candidate.

Original-head run 42523270185 used base 465c110e4975690406b48709d58a581756c85b82, whose immutable-source test-line count was already 92 over its ceiling. The original PR’s matching 406 LF/allocation preserved that debt. The current refreshed-base ratchet passes with 48 lines slack; no scalar or unrelated allocation was raised by this patch.

The former short-tail warm-reload timeout did not reproduce in the exact local case or ten-case original file order, and passed the subsequent old-head CI run. Those passing replays were never claimed as a local fix or as current-head CI.

</details>

All captures use fictional identities and the production UI with mocked Gateway fixtures. The before comparison uses the exact base card implementation on the same current shell and fixture, not a complete base-app screenshot.

prs.title: feat: let agents manage personal session groups
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Guests cannot ask their agent to organize the personal collections they already use in the sidebar.

## User Impact

Agents can read, create, rename, reorder, and remove the current person's collections. Signed-in guests with session-write access now synchronize **only personal collections** through their own profile; their other preferences remain browser-local. Existing profile-scoped browser layouts are adopted before remote collections are applied. Independent changes merge; conflicting edits to the same collection retain the local layout with an error instead of overwriting either copy. Read-only and profileless connections keep browser-local behavior.

Shared groups, session metadata, project defaults, and access grants are unchanged. Agent operations still require the current person's own single-participant Control UI turn.

## Why This Change Was Made

Reuses the existing preference and compare-and-swap owners for both the sidebar and agent. The old guest browser-local policy made an agent's server-only snapshot incomplete; this revision explicitly cuts over personal collections without importing unrelated preferences. One shared normalizer serves every caller. Existing queue composition and saved confirmation handle overlapping edits and older queued layouts. Write-only profile operations stay with the existing write owner rather than loading with profile reads. There is no new database schema, permission store, configuration option, or broader role grant.

## Evidence

- **Hosted P1 repaired:** an existing local Focus collection was absent from the agent snapshot and disappeared after the agent added Later. The composed preference/tool regression reproduced both failures before the repair and now passes through agent editing, preference refresh, and reload.
- **Compatibility and concurrency:** 9 focused group cases cover prior browser-local layouts, independent remote groups, same-group conflicts, authority revocation, overlapping remove/rename operations, foreign pending edits, and queued layouts from before the merge-base metadata. Missing historical confirmation remains a retained conflict rather than an invented edit base. Two additional defects found by independent review were reproduced red and repaired before publication.
- **Real browser + real isolated Gateway:** the final production-UI flow passes with only session read/write scopes: visible create/order/rename/remove, the actual production personal-group tool adapter over authenticated Gateway RPC, reload, a fresh browser using the same profile, and another profile's isolation. Only the personal-group preference is written; no shared mutations occur. Scenario 12.436 s; complete command 72.376 s including build/setup. This does not claim a model turn, a latest-stable app upgrade, or deployed Team acceptance.
- **Focused checks:** 196 preference/lifecycle cases pass. Another 50 current-base dispatcher, self-archive, and prompt-prefix cases pass. The 16-case preference-handler suite includes the real agent-to-Gateway dispatcher and SQLite owner under session-only scopes. Affected production/test types, scoped lint, formatting, localization verification, and whitespace checks pass.
- **Fresh native Auto Review, P0–P3:** no actionable findings on the complete candidate against prepared base c74999244a71333ad02074c307c5b1bed69579aa; reviewed local tree ab5e23df85351b3bdf175a4202c7e5cea0553594. The reviewer inspected supplied source and evidence, not independently rerun tests, and explicitly retained the warm-reload gap below.
- **Release performance:** using the canonical comparison build settings, the strict absolute budget checker passes: startup JS 90,829 B; Chat boot 1,296,492 B; New boot 802,758 B gzip. CSS remains 325,050 B gzip. No budget or baseline was raised. The earlier boot-size crossings were repaired by removing write machinery from profile reads and consolidating navigation composition bookkeeping.
- **Test cost:** the allocation is exactly 336 net test LF; the real ratchet passes at 6,587,639 LF with a matching ceiling. The shared scalar is unchanged. The required growth protects dispatch authority, migration, concurrency, and the browser/Gateway boundary; nearby helper moves add no second persistence implementation.
- **Remaining validation gap:** boot-manifest regeneration reaches New Session and initial Chat readiness but times out on Chat's warm reload at the existing 60-second composer assertion. Bounded attempts are retained; the original generator and manifest are unchanged. Its cause and baseline runtime attribution are unproven. The successful real-Gateway reload flow and strict budget check do not turn this failed capture into a pass.
- **CI:** this cleanup integrates the prepared target base to remove the previously attributed 92-line inherited debt. Earlier failed CI is historical evidence; the new pushed head needs its own results. No tests, timeouts, or permission guards were weakened.

- Jason O'Neal

prs.title: fix(channels): channels remove asks to disable an unknown channel before reporting it does not exist
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: `openclaw channels remove --channel <id>` with an id that is not a channel asks `Disable nope account "default"? (keeps config)` first, and only after the operator answers does it report `Unknown channel "nope"`. In a non-interactive shell the prompt cannot be answered, so the command ends with `wizard cancelled` and the real reason is never shown.

## User Impact

User impact: an unknown channel id now fails immediately with the existing `Unknown channel "<id>". Run openclaw channels list --all to see configured and installable channels.` message, in interactive and non-interactive shells alike. Known channels are unchanged except that the confirmation names the channel by its label (`Disable Telegram account "default"?`), which the wizard path already did. `--delete` already skipped the prompt and is unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

The command asked for confirmation before resolving the channel plugin; the unknown-channel and plugin-not-installed checks ran afterwards. The resolution block now runs first and the confirmation uses the resolved channel, so the same checks happen in the same order as the rest of the command, just before any prompt.

## Evidence

From source on `main` at 826999cd5f, macOS, Node 26.7.0, fresh state directory, no TTY.

Before:
```
$ openclaw channels remove --channel nope
◆  Disable nope account "default"? (keeps config)
│  ● Yes / ○ No
└  Setup cancelled.
wizard cancelled
```

After (same build plus this change):
```
$ openclaw channels remove --channel nope
Unknown channel "nope". Run `openclaw channels list --all` to see configured and installable channels.
$ openclaw channels remove --channel nope --delete      # unchanged
Unknown channel "nope". Run `openclaw channels list --all` to see configured and installable channels.
$ openclaw channels remove --channel telegram           # known channel still confirms
◆  Disable Telegram account "default"? (keeps config)
```
Exit 1 in all three cases, as before.

Tests:
- `pnpm test src/commands/channels.remove.test.ts src/cli/channels-cli.test.ts`: 35 passed.
- New case "rejects an unknown channel before asking for confirmation" runs the command with `--channel nope` and asserts the confirm prompt is never called, the unknown-channel message is printed, exit 1, and no config write. It fails on `main` (`expected "vi.fn()" to not be called at all, but actually been called 1 times`) and passes with the change.
- Test-line budget: 9 added lines, allocated in `config/test-lines-allocations/channels-remove-unknown-channel.txt`.
- `pnpm tsgo:core`, `oxfmt --check` and `oxlint --type-aware` on both files: clean.

Local autoreview / local ClawSweeper were not run.

prs.title: fix(gateway): page-cache warming fails every 15 min on kernels without /proc/self/io
prs.body:
Fixes #177056

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: the scheduled database page-cache warm fails on every 15-minute cycle and never warms anything on Linux hosts whose kernel has no procfs IO accounting (stock Microsoft WSL kernels, `# CONFIG_TASKSTATS is not set`), because `readIo()` throws `ENOENT` for `/proc/self/io` before warming begins.

## User Impact

User impact: on affected hosts, recent chat history is warmed again after startup memory pressure instead of silently skipping the optimization, and the gateway no longer emits a recurring `database page-cache warm failed (state)` WARN every 15 minutes that masks real warnings. There is no configuration change and no behavior change on hosts where `/proc/self/io` exists.

## Why This Change Was Made

The warmer treats IO counters as an environment capability instead of a hard requirement:

- **Probe once per pass.** `readIo()` returns `null` on `ENOENT`; other errors still propagate. A pass without counters keeps running instead of aborting in `warm()`.
- **Keep the safeguards.** Byte budget, pacing, cancellation and reader cleanup must not be bypassed when counters are missing. The worker now reports conservative per-step byte estimates (`estimatedReadBytes` + `ioCountersUnavailable`), and the scheduler uses those estimates for both pacing and the pass budget via one `accountedBytes()` helper. State warming charges the exact bytes read per chunk; agent warming charges bounded per-query estimates that deliberately over-estimate the work (metadata step ~512 KiB, payload batch = max(payload bytes, 8 x 64 KiB), projection query ~2 MiB).
- **Real counters unchanged.** When `/proc/self/io` is readable, `readBytes`/`diskBytes` and the pacing math are byte-for-byte the previous behavior; the estimate is only consulted when `ioCountersUnavailable` is true.
- **Observability.** Startup trace and the completion log now include `estimatedReadBytes` and `ioCountersUnavailable`, so operators can tell which accounting mode a pass used.

Tradeoff: on counter-less kernels, warming stops earlier than it would with exact byte accounting because estimates intentionally over-estimate. That direction is the safe one for pacing, and the structural caps (4096 sessions, 32 messages/session, 64 KiB/message) still bound the work.

## Evidence

Environment used (real host, not simulated): Ubuntu 26.04.1 on WSL 3.0.3.0, kernel `6.18.54.1-microsoft-standard-WSL2`:

```
$ zcat /proc/config.gz | grep TASKSTATS
# CONFIG_TASKSTATS is not set
$ cat /proc/self/io
cat: /proc/self/io: No such file or directory
```

Before this change the same gateway emitted 17 x `database page-cache warm failed (state): Error: SQLite read-only worker ENOENT: ... open '/proc/self/io'` in the first ~3.7 h after a 2026.10.4 -> 2026.10.5 upgrade; the previous day on 2026.10.4 had 0.

Tests from the review checklist (3 files, run on the host above, so the unmocked cases exercise the real missing `/proc/self/io`):

```
$ node_modules/.bin/vitest run src/infra/sqlite-page-cache.worker.test.ts \
    src/infra/sqlite-page-cache-residency.test.ts \
    src/gateway/server-runtime-services.maintenance.test.ts --maxWorkers=1
Test Files  3 passed (3)
     Tests  10 passed | 1 skipped (11)
```

Added regressions (fail before the fix, pass after):

- `completes an agent warm when /proc/self/io is unavailable, using bounded estimates` - forces `ENOENT` for `/proc/self/io`, asserts the pass completes, reports `ioCountersUnavailable`, and closes every reader.
- `enforces the state byte budget via estimates when /proc/self/io is unavailable` - asserts the byte budget is still enforced and the pass stops `limited` with bounded estimates instead of throwing.

Existing tests keep their counter-path assertions and branch only when the host genuinely lacks counters, so CI continues to verify the real-counter behavior unchanged.

Gate checks:

```
$ node_modules/.bin/oxfmt --check <3 changed files>
All matched files use the correct format.
$ node_modules/.bin/oxlint <3 changed files>
Found 0 warnings and 0 errors.
$ git diff --check
(clean)
```

`pnpm build` is running locally; CI will also exercise the full build and type gate.

Compatibility: no config, schema, or persisted-state changes. The only payload additions are two fields on the internal `PageCacheProgress` worker result.

prs.title: feat(research): show a quiet research card in the chat
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

#194780 removed the Deep research chat card so the side panel was the only entry point, with a redesigned card to follow. Without it, a `deep_research` call in the chat shows only a text summary, which never updates as the research progresses.

This brings the card back as one quiet row that matches the other cards in the chat. It builds on Josh Lehman's (@jalehman) original card from #194780 and credits him as co-author. The design was picked by Vyctor from three prototypes rendered in the real chat.

## User Impact

When the agent starts or resumes research, a card appears in the conversation at that tool call:

- **Title:** the research question, two lines at most.
- **Detail line:** the current step while running ("Gathering evidence (round 1)"); otherwise the outcome ("Report ready", "Partial report", "Paused", "Cancelling", "Failed"…). After that come the counts: sources, findings and open gaps.
- **Actions:** **Read report** (or **View progress** before a report exists), plus a quiet Cancel or Resume when allowed.

Only failures add color. The search icon pulses gently while research runs, but not when the user has reduced motion turned on. The line above the card now says "Started deep research" (or "Resumed…"). Before, it repeated the state at call time, so it could say "running" next to a finished card. On narrow screens the actions and counts wrap whole; no count is ever split. The side panel still works on its own, from Explore panels.

## Changes

- Restore the `research-job` inline view, version 1: the backend descriptor, the `api.inlineView` result on start/resume, and the browser registration. The whole result stays under the existing 24 KB limit.
- Fixes for the three findings ClawSweeper raised on Josh's original card:
  - **Errors show on the card.** A rejected Cancel/Resume, or a failed first read, appears as a line on the card instead of failing silently.
  - **Import through the API barrel.** The view contract now comes from the plugin's `api.ts`, not `src/`, which fixes the boundary check.
  - **Read report opens the report.** It opens the panel on the **Report** tab, and View progress opens **Progress**. A one-time tab request is handed from the card to the panel.
- Card views use the research client in a mode that never touches the panel's saved pending-start state, so a card can't clear a start the panel is recovering.
- Header controls and the session-menu action stay removed.

## Evidence

**Before:** Josh's original card from #194780, which was removed before landing.

![Before: original card](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/9d7382b5-ecb4-470b-8a94-d4ccb6c93316)

**After** (real native plugin bundle in the Control UI chat, mock Gateway):

Running:
![Running, dark](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/35b66a3a-e241-468f-bbe7-9ed8796bb887)

Report ready:
![Report ready, dark](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/05ba8022-a42d-4f96-afbf-12e5ce162d8f)

Cancelling:
![Cancelling, dark](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/a823460d-2452-4bfb-a3b3-fa4cfde4f2fd)

Failed:
![Failed, dark](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/f14c0863-d4dc-4f21-83c4-0491464d29a0)

Paused (light):
![Paused, light](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/6f8d65c5-518b-456c-8986-d72bf3acda50)

Partial report (light):
![Partial, light](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/b545088f-1499-455a-9a56-a5860f83ea3e)

Mobile, 390 px (running, ready):
![Mobile running](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/2e481286-abd3-4f1e-be6e-c199bee2a4d4)
![Mobile ready](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/5eb14dd0-d443-4f5e-8801-7ebbd2823817)

I captured running, cancelling, paused, partial, ready and failed in dark and light at desktop width and in dark at 390 px, and inspected every capture.

Tests and review:
- `ui/src/e2e/deep-research-plugin.e2e.test.ts`: 3/3 pass. The card scenario checks:
  - a failed first read shows an alert;
  - the running step appears in the status;
  - a rejected Cancel shows its error and stays retryable;
  - counts update to the partial state;
  - **Read report** opens the panel with the Report tab selected.
- `pnpm test extensions/deep-research` passes (104 tests), including the large-result check, which now also requires the inline view in the result.
- `pnpm tsgo:extensions`, `pnpm tsgo:test:ui`, oxlint, oxfmt, `pnpm lint:plugins:no-extension-src-imports` and `git diff --check` pass.
- Local autoreview (Codex, P0–P2) against `origin/main`, final head: scoped-clean. Earlier passes found two things, both fixed: read errors hidden before a job loads, and long status text that couldn't wrap on narrow cards.

Not tested: a live Gateway run. All UI proof uses the mock Gateway.

Please don't enable auto-merge on this PR; it's here for review.

prs.title: fix(muse): settle canceled startup without stopping other callers
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes cancellation waiting for Muse initialization, and prevents one canceled startup caller from stopping another caller sharing the same host.

## User Impact

Canceling a Muse attempt during startup settles without requiring a successful initialization. Other callers sharing the startup remain usable, and the last canceled waiter waits for host teardown. Already-leased warm hosts remain protected. No configuration or migration is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

Forward the attempt’s existing abort signal into the existing Muse pool. Keep cancellation ownership per waiting caller while retaining the SDK’s subprocess teardown owner. This does not change accepted-turn, busy-resume, permission, or reset policy and does not add an adapter.

Related work: #183676 covers busy-resume/approval observation/retention; this change avoids those implementation hunks. The README automatic-selection contradiction is a separate follow-up, not part of this PR.

## Evidence

- Public base: `ade7c07d4c70a08ea0b294de27ddc519120e817e`.
- Base: deliberately withheld initialization makes the harness cancellation test time out; canceling one of two startup callers kills the surviving caller’s peer. The existing verification cancellation control passes.
- Candidate: **59/59 tests passed** across Muse harness, runtime, and verification suites. Includes stopped-peer/no-dispatch/no-binding checks, a surviving startup caller completing a real model-list request, and the existing warm-host control.
- These are **synthetic owning-path tests** using production Muse code, the pinned SDK, and a disposable MSP subprocess, not live Muse or whole-Gateway proof. No credentials or provider calls used.
- Targeted source and package-boundary typechecks, focused lint/format, whitespace, and test-line ratchet passed. The +116 test-line allocation is exactly the two distinct boundary regressions; existing fixture/control coverage is reused.
- Historical initial native Auto Review on the complete local candidate against that base: **P0/P1 scoped-clean**, no findings. It did not independently execute tests or validate live behavior. The published head `eeb8a98ece6dd5cf55a32a9ecc2901c654ff44f1` was fetched from the public PR and its Muse tree matches the reviewed/tested candidate exactly. The range from the stated base contains only the six intended files.

- Historical exact-head supplemental Auto Review: **P0–P2 scoped-clean**, no findings, commit `eeb8a98ece6dd5cf55a32a9ecc2901c654ff44f1`. Static only; the initial preparation rejected symlinked SDK evidence. A tracked-evidence run completed without that SDK input and explicitly did not independently verify SDK teardown semantics or execute tests.
- The coordinator reports an independent read-only Codex review, `muse_exact_head_review`, **P0–P3 substantive coverage, no actionable findings**, on all six changed files and their pool/harness lifecycle, catalog caller, abort helper, fixture, and boundary contracts. Reviewed tree: `e783c1657b96233c41b8341b81f07592e2876009`, matched to the published head by full-tree and six-blob comparisons. This reviewer executed no code; this is not live Muse, whole-Gateway, Windows, CI, or hosted ClawSweeper proof.
- Publication parent `3c2fd048d9917e7d41dcd6aa4eba12cfcb9f7afc` has the same tree as reviewed base `ade7c07d4c70a08ea0b294de27ddc519120e817e`; it introduces no source drift.
- Additional finite-sweep coverage on the unchanged candidate: **29/29** existing tests passed (native-catalog precedence, Muse event finalization, registration cleanup), 62.23s wrapper. These supplement, rather than replace, the 59 startup/consumer tests.
- PR is non-draft at this head. Successful automation/security-gate jobs are not presented as a substantive code review.
- [Published ClawSweeper review](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/194884#issuecomment-6716788694) from [successful review run 42442999394](https://github.com/openclaw/clawsweeper/actions/runs/42442999394), for exact head `eeb8a98ece6dd5cf55a32a9ecc2901c654ff44f1` against captured base `d32a595ba9663735f0bd9585511158b656420cf1`: **no actionable findings**, **Before merge: None**, and **Ready for maintainer review**. prs.title: fix: plugin tools disappear for agents with separate workspaces
prs.body:
Related: #194674 (merged; this is a separate workspace-recovery fix).

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes enabled plugin tools, including `x_search`, disappearing from effective tool inventory when an agent uses a workspace different from the Gateway's discovery workspace.

## User Impact

Agents with separate workspaces recover the Gateway's available plugin tools while retaining their existing tool and authentication policy. No configuration migration is needed. This PR covers inventory recovery; actual X invocation and citations remain pending on a separate Research execution failure.

## Why This Change Was Made

The recovery guard compared a fingerprint captured for Gateway plugin discovery with one computed using the agent's execution workspace. It now compares the Gateway's discovery workspace while continuing to use the caller's config; tool creation still receives the agent's actual workspace.

Current-owner, manifest-identity, discovery-fingerprint, plugin-policy, narrow selected-model scope and retain/release guards remain intact. No new credential source or global fallback is introduced. Temporary Research timeout diagnostics are excluded.

The integration tests use real selected-model acquisition, the admitting Gateway registry and bundled XAI tool construction. A schema-only mock would not cross the discovery-workspace fingerprint guard that caused the empty inventory. Shared provider/owner setup and a three-row XAI table remove 96 lines from the initial tests while preserving all four cases. The remaining net growth is 177 regression-test lines. The separate allocation record grants exactly those 177 lines under the documented test-line policy; the shared scalar and all other allocations remain unchanged. This preserves existing base slack rather than consuming a moving shared allowance.

## Evidence

- **Red:** on `60521f723188be7c91b768d424cafa1ef1e49453`, real selected-model acquisition passes with equal workspaces and fails with distinct workspaces: expected `['x_search']`, actual `[]`. Both affected baseline files match source base `963de16b208f24f398172db276fba482af98277c`.
- **Green code/test source:** all four cases pass at `5efaa44c7e70e9f1a5220a2c48b4a2735bc0b18b`: direct OpenAI/Codex preview metadata, real selected-model acquisition with equal and distinct workspaces, and full Gateway recovery without widening the selected-model generation. Synthetic inherited XAI OAuth is present; no provider inference or X fetch occurs.
- Negative and lifecycle coverage retains changed discovery precedence, mismatched manifest identity, disabled plugins, unavailable current owner, no cold plugin reload, execution-workspace delivery, and retained work during owner closure.
- **Measured cost:** the focused file passes 4/4 in 70.02 seconds of wall time including compilation/import; reported case times total 3.874 seconds. File-specific CI seconds are not separately available. The cold wall time is why this uses the real composition only at its owning boundary rather than duplicating it across layers.
- Core types, affected test types, type-aware lint, formatting and whitespace checks pass for the unchanged code/test bytes. The allocation-only follow-up reuses that runtime proof and validates the native ratchet against both source base `963de16` and CI's exact merge `a921c919268147d320de3976c6fa03840c6290ff` over base `4f84bfd25e78aa35f6eb5fb17c5332d271fdfb29`. The old CI failed by 51 lines because newer main reduced shared slack from 177 to 126; the allocation preserves both bases' existing slack.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: Control UI chat links return 404 when an outside source adds an unknown query parameter, such as `homescreen=1` on a Home Screen shortcut.

## User Impact

User impact: Chat links with extra query parameters redirect to the same chat path with only recognized parameters kept. Recognized parameters still undergo validation, and session authorization remains unchanged.

A 302 redirect removes unknown parameters before the return path or app receives them, including `token` and `gatewayUrl`. This lets otherwise valid chat links open without passing unintended settings to the app.

Checked at `ea459ad` before pushing:

prs.title: fix(agents): Claude Code session limit notice skips rate-limit fallback
prs.body:
Related: #118793

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: when a Claude Code (`claude-cli`) turn fails with the subscription-window notice as its error text, for example `You've hit your session limit · resets 2:50pm (America/New_York)` (also `You've hit your limit · resets 5pm` and `You've hit your 5-hour limit · resets 3pm`), the failover classifier returns `unknown` instead of `rate_limit`, so an exhausted subscription window is handled like an unexplained failure. Where only the error text is classified, as described in #118793, the classifier returns `null`, the run decision becomes `surface_error`, and the configured fallback chain is never consulted.

## User Impact

User impact: when the notice is the error text, it now counts as a rate limit. The failover decision records `rate_limit` with status 429 instead of no reason, so everything that keys on the reason (the fallback step, auth-profile cooldown where an OpenClaw auth profile exists, reply copy) sees a known, retryable reason. Only the `hit your ... limit ... resets` forms change: `weekly limit` and `monthly limit` were already `rate_limit`, and `You've hit your monthly spend limit` stays `billing` because the billing check still runs first.

What this does not fix:

- Claude Code can also exit with code 1 and print the notice only on stderr. That run error stays `Claude Code process exited with code 1` with no reason, because OpenClaw attaches stderr to the error for display only and deliberately never classifies it (`src/infra/error-diagnostics.ts`). The runtime proof below shows that shape unchanged. Classifying stderr would change that design, so it is not part of this PR.
- The user-facing copy. No copy text changes here; which copy the user sees depends on the path. The known-failure reply (`buildKnownAgentRunFailureReplyPayload`) forwards the notice with its reset time, for example `⚠️ You've hit your session limit · resets 6:10am (UTC)`. It forwards the whole CLI error text through the user-facing sanitizer, as it already does for `weekly limit` notices, so other lines that share stderr with the notice are forwarded too (token-like query values are masked). The external-run failure reply (`buildExternalRunFailureReply`) and the saved-history copy (`renderRecordedAssistantFailureCopy`) use the generic rate-limit template, `⚠️ The AI service needs a short break. Please try again in a few minutes.`, which drops the reset time and understates the wait for a multi-hour subscription window. A bounded, reset-aware formatter for these boundaries was suggested in review as a separate follow-up and is not part of this PR.

## Why This Change Was Made

`PERIODIC_USAGE_LIMIT_RE` in `src/agents/failover/message-patterns.ts` only knew `daily|weekly|monthly ... limit`, and `ERROR_PATTERNS.rateLimit` knows `usage limit` but neither `session limit` nor the bare `hit your limit · resets` form. Claude Code names the window by its reset time, so the periodic pattern now also accepts `hit your <up to two words> limit ... reset(s)`. The new rows are tagged with provider `claude-cli` in the classification corpus, and the CLI exit-error tests cover both the plain text and the structured `result` record.

## Evidence

Runtime proof on the released CLI (isolated, local, redacted):

- Setup: the published `openclaw@2026.11.1` npm package, run as `openclaw agent --local` with a minimal environment and a fresh state and config directory (`OPENCLAW_PATH_BOOTSTRAPPED=1` keeps the CLI from moving `/usr/bin` ahead of the stand-in on `PATH`). Primary `anthropic/claude-opus-5-5` on the `claude-cli` runtime, configured fallback a loopback OpenAI-compatible stub model (`synthetic/fallback-model`). A stand-in `claude` executable answers `--version`, `auth status --json` and the stream-json `initialize` handshake, then fails the user turn with `You've hit your session limit · resets 6:10am (UTC)`. No network beyond 127.0.0.1, no real credentials. `before` is the unmodified package; `after` is the same package with only this PR's matcher change applied to its bundled `message-patterns` chunk (diff below), because this host cannot run the full source build. Two turns per run, same results in both turns.
- Notice as the failed `result` record (the shape this PR fixes):
  - before: `model fallback decision: decision=candidate_failed requested=anthropic/claude-opus-5-5 candidate=anthropic/claude-opus-5-5 reason=unknown next=synthetic/fallback-model detail=You've hit your session limit · resets 6:10am (UTC)`; structured fields `reason: "unknown"`, no `status`, `fallbackStepFromFailureReason: "unknown"`.
  - after: `model fallback decision: decision=candidate_failed requested=anthropic/claude-opus-5-5 candidate=anthropic/claude-opus-5-5 reason=rate_limit next=synthetic/fallback-model detail=You've hit your session limit · resets 6:10am (UTC)`; structured fields `reason: "rate_limit"`, `status: 429`, `fallbackStepFromFailureReason: "rate_limit"`, then `decision=candidate_succeeded ... candidate=synthetic/fallback-model`, and the reply came from the fallback model.
- Notice on stderr with exit code 1 (not changed by this PR): before and after both log `cli terminal failure: provider=claude-cli ... error=Claude Code process exited with code 1` followed by `stderr (process-wide; may include earlier turns): You've hit your session limit · resets 6:10am (UTC)`, and `decision=candidate_failed ... detail=Claude Code process exited with code 1` with no reason, then the same fallback.
- Limits of this setup: on 2026.11.1 the configured fallback runs even for `unknown`, so what changes here is the recorded reason and status. The native Claude login has no OpenClaw auth profile in this setup, so turn 2 tried Claude Code again in both variants and a profile cooldown is not observable here.
- Bundle change used for `after` (2026.11.1 predates the Chinese quota alternatives on main; the added alternative is identical):

  ```diff
  -const PERIODIC_USAGE_LIMIT_RE = /\b(?:daily|weekly|monthly)(?:\/(?:daily|weekly|monthly))* (?:usage )?limit(?:s)?(?: (?:exhausted|reached|exceeded))?\b/i;
  +const PERIODIC_USAGE_LIMIT_RE = /\bhit your (?:[\w-]+ ){0,2}limit\b[^\n]{0,40}\bresets?\b|\b(?:daily|weekly|monthly)(?:\/(?:daily|weekly|monthly))* (?:usage )?limit(?:s)?(?: (?:exhausted|reached|exceeded))?\b/i;
  ```

Field data from 2026.11.1 on one host (claude-cli runtime, real Claude Code at its session limit): `model_fallback_decision` events with `decision: "candidate_failed"`, `reason: "unknown"` and `errorPreview: "You've hit your session limit · resets 10:20pm (Europe/Berlin)"` (the result shape this PR fixes), next to `cli terminal failure ... error=Claude Code process exited with code 1` lines whose stderr carries the same notice (the stderr shape this PR does not change). An earlier version of this description presented those stderr lines as fixed by this change; the runtime proof shows they are not.

Tests and checks:

- Classification corpus (`src/agents/failover/failover-classification.corpus.test.ts`), three new rows: without the pattern change `3 failed | 61 passed (64)`, with it `64 passed`.
- `src/agents/cli-runner/exit-error.test.ts`, two new tests through `createCliExitFailoverError`: without the change `2 failed | 5 passed (7)`, with it `7 passed`.
- Consumers unchanged: `user-copy.test.ts` + `classify.test.ts` 65 passed, `src/llm/utils/retry.test.ts` 40 passed, `provider-429-precedence.test.ts` 6 passed.
- `oxlint --type-aware` on the four TypeScript files: 0 warnings, 0 errors. `oxfmt --check` clean, docs formatting clean, `tsgo -p tsconfig.core.json` clean, line-cap and max-lines ratchets OK.
- User-facing copy on this branch (temporary local vitest probe, not committed; the plain text and the structured `result` record give the same results): `buildKnownAgentRunFailureReplyPayload` returns `⚠️ You've hit your session limit · resets 6:10am (UTC)`; `buildExternalRunFailureReply` and `renderRecordedAssistantFailureCopy` return `⚠️ The AI service needs a short break. Please try again in a few minutes.` With an extra stderr line before or after the notice, the known-failure reply forwards that line as well (token value masked); a `weekly limit` notice on the same path behaves the same way.

prs.title: fix(skill-workshop): show what whole-file SKILL.md writes and drafts drop
prs.body:
Closes #194826

_Prepared for Cosmin Toma (RUF agentic team)._

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: an agent silently wipes most of a live skill when it sends a short change note as the content of a whole-file `SKILL.md` write or draft.

## User Impact

User impact: when a `SKILL.md` rewrite or draft would drop most of a live skill, the agent (and the user reviewing drafts) now sees how much is removed and which sections disappear, before anyone relies on it. Nothing is blocked; writes still land and can be undone with `restore`.

## Why This Change Was Made

In #194826 (on 2026.7.1-2) an 87-line change note replaced a 387-line skill through the old proposal flow, and nothing showed the loss. On `main` that flow is gone, but `write_file` of `SKILL.md` and `draft` still replace the file whole, and the tool contract never says so.

This PR:

- adds `skillReplacementReport(before, after)` in `skill-lint.ts`: body line count before/after (`SKILL.md body: 387 → 87 lines (-78%).`), up to 8 removed `##` sections (code blocks ignored), and a non-blocking advisory when the new body is under 60% of the old one;
- shows that report on `patch`/`write_file` of an existing `SKILL.md`, on `draft` for a live skill, and on `view draft`;
- adds a `change-note` lint advisory when the title starts with Fix / Proposal / Change(s) / Changelog (only when the write introduces it, like the other rules);
- states in the tool description, the `/learn drafts` prompt and `docs/tools/skill-workshop.md` that `write_file`/`draft` content is the complete file and replaces it whole.

Advisory rather than blocking: writes are versioned with `restore`, and the codebase has no override-flag pattern for this. The Control UI already shows a diff before applying a draft.

Known nits: a legitimate title such as `# Change management` gets the change-note advisory; every `SKILL.md` patch now carries a one-line size summary; with the shrink advisory a write can end with four advisory lines instead of the documented three.

Possible follow-up, not in this PR: `skill_library` `update` with `proposal_content` also replaces `SKILL.md` whole.

## Evidence

On `main` at d44c9ad92 with this commit applied:

- `pnpm test extensions/skill-workshop`: 16 files, 140 tests passed.
- New tests: `skill-lint.test.ts` (report and `change-note` rule) and `tool.test.ts` ("shows what a whole-file SKILL.md rewrite or draft drops from the live skill"), which reproduces the incident: a 65-line skill rewritten with a `# Fix: …` note via `draft`, `view draft`, and `write_file`.
- `pnpm tsgo:extensions`, `oxlint extensions/skill-workshop`, and `git diff --check` pass. (On the original base 1ad3ec3d2 also oxfmt, `lint:docs` and the pre-commit hooks.)
- Gap: no end-to-end run against a live Gateway with a real agent; the change only adds text to tool results.
