prs.title: fix(doctor): stop large transcript repairs exhausting the heap
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes `openclaw doctor --fix --non-interactive` exhausting the JavaScript heap while inspecting large compressed transcript databases during offline repair and updates.

## User Impact

Doctor completes transcript repairs in bounded memory without increasing the Node heap limit. Interrupted repairs resume without skipping the rest of a session or duplicating provider-repair receipts. No schema, configuration, retention, or payload-format change is introduced.

## Why This Change Was Made

The candidate-session query called `openclaw_transcript_payload_decode` inside a SQLite `WHERE` through `.all()`. Native UDF handles retained decoded objects until the statement returned—even when it returned zero rows. `.iterate()` alone has the same problem when a no-match `next()` scans everything.

The SQLite reader now projects the predicate and yields every evaluated physical row, allowing each native handle scope to end. Session repair plans and synchronous writes are bounded to 64 rows / 4 MiB, with an oversized historical row processed alone; the existing cursor advances only after the complete session. Provider discovery streams repeated facts instead of using native `DISTINCT`. PostgreSQL retains its existing native filtering and deduplication because its bridge buffers results.

## Evidence

- **Full-size success:** actual Doctor completed on **35.19 GiB / 10,800 sessions / 212,274 events** in **1,148.013 s**, using the unchanged **4,192 MiB** default heap limit. Sampled main peak was **825.32 MiB overall**, **303.41 MiB within the repaired owner**. The owner yielded every row in **25.734 s wall / 25.472 s CPU**, with **20.095 GB cumulative V8 allocation**; its heap fell from 264.16 to 187.43 MiB across the scan. Cumulative allocation includes instrumentation and is not retained memory.
- **Failure reproduced:** real baseline Doctor on **11.77 GiB / 3,600 sessions / 71,382 events** aborted after **481.894 s**, at **3,202.05 MiB sampled heap**. The exact query/UDF stack identifies this owner. The original **35.19 GiB** baseline also OOMed after about 18.2 minutes; its relevant owner, decoder and query-execution files are byte-identical to this PR's parent.
- **Data preserved:** all 212,274 full-size transcript rows retain exact SHA256 `79f0856faddad44ad2fd6f9e691b1a90b64f38339c86b1dbc4f83231081f359f`. Application schema, trajectory and archive hashes are unchanged. Expected existing Doctor effects are two migration receipts, SQLite internal ANALYZE statistics, and adding canonical workspace paths to session metadata; every other session column/JSON field is unchanged.
- **Controlled comparison:** two A/A controls and five counterbalanced A/B pairs, restoring identical synthetic state before every arm, all exit 0 with identical final schemas, counts and hashes. Owner median wall **157.934 → 148.898 ms**, CPU **154.349 → 148.518 ms**, V8 allocation **104.584 → 102.203 MB**. Allocation change is within A/A variation. Whole-command timing is noisy (**30.287 → 32.851 s medians**); no end-to-end speedup is claimed.
- **Regression proof:** 47 focused migration/archive tests covered, including a 256 MiB child that OOMs with the original owner and passes with the fix, duplicate compressed provider facts, skipped corrupt noncandidate payloads, and recovery after an interrupted 64-row commit. Final touched-file tests: 25/25; unchanged archive suites: 22/22. Suppression-inventory tests: 14/14.
- **Published-stable upgrade:** `openclaw@2026.11.2` generated schema-27 synthetic state; candidate Doctor upgraded it to existing schema 41 in **24.733 s**, preserving all four sessions, 20 rows, 1,053,088 decoded bytes and every payload hash.
- **Checks/review:** production build passed. `pnpm check:changed` completed; its patch-local failures were repaired and all failed leaves passed targeted reruns. Independent Codex autoreview found no actionable P0–P2 findings; the inventory-only follow-up also passed independent review. Exact-head [CI 42535712994](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/42535712994) is green (**38 passed / 27 skipped**, including PostgreSQL conformance and PG16 Gateway smoke). [Context/evidence 42535809246](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/42535809246) is green. No inherited-failure exception is claimed.

Initial PR CI caught the missing explicit inventory entry for the heap probe's three intentional native-method captures. Each wrapper supplies the original native receiver. The narrow inventory correction changes no runtime/probe bytes; the full proof build at `2dbfed052165` is byte-identical for all affected production and measurement files to final head `a1ad7ddb9781`.

Production growth is **65 lines** for bounded planning/commit progress and preserving engine behavior; the eager reader and redundant SQLite deduplication are removed. The **317-line** regression allocation covers the heap bound, partial-session recovery, skipped-payload compatibility and exact probe suppression inventory.

Reproduce with the committed `scripts/perf/team-shape-fixture.ts` and `scripts/perf/doctor-transcript-heap-measure.mts`. The full generator encountered a setup lock timeout after committing the entire transcript corpus; its remaining metadata/extras were completed through the unchanged owner APIs, with explicit recovery provenance. Measurements use macOS/APFS / Node 26.12.1, not Linux/btrfs deployment timing. Heap peaks are sampled every 64 decoder callbacks and at query boundaries. Optional plugin dependency diagnostics in the runtime capsule limit plugin-health coverage, but Doctor migration and successful exit are directly proven. No production data or service was accessed. **Ready PR; intentionally unmerged.**

prs.title: improve(ui): reduce scrolling stalls during tool-heavy replies
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Scrolling stalls while a reply runs many tools with live output. Each event can republish session and child-roster presentation, repeatedly preparing the same growing turn.

## User Impact

This candidate makes tool-heavy replies cheaper to render while keeping output live, complete, and ordered. **Draft: the current head failed input-tail qualification and will not be landed.** A revision is in progress. The independent PageUp correctness fix already landed in #195441.

## Why This Change Was Made

Use the existing run owner's animation frame for session and child-roster presentation notifications. Authoritative state and event handling stay synchronous; terminal, hidden-page, and no-animation-frame paths still publish immediately. Reuse immutable source preparation, while resolving run ownership and consuming attachments afresh on each pass. Remove duplicate bundle bookkeeping.

## Evidence

Require at least 5% better frame p95 or meaningful input delay at both Chromium speeds, no worse Firefox tails, no mutation storm, and exact final 200-tool results/order/completion/anchors. No size ceiling increase. WebKit is unavailable because of the host WindowServer failure.

The frozen run uses the corrected committed benchmark at `c82980d7a598449351e314edf8a71a012b1e29c1`, with all 46 harness sources and the loader verified, fresh browser processes, and source/bundle identity checks. No failed or interrupted sample is replaced. Base is #195441 (`253a985ed9effefd1e1124a543c386d6e47e6b76`).

prs.title: improve(memory): drop embedding cache copies the published index already serves
prs.body:
Refs #168777

## What Problem This Solves

The memory embedding cache keeps a second full copy of every vector the published memory index already holds, so most of a large cache (64% of a 50,000-row cache in #168777) is duplicate data.

## User Impact

User impact: memory databases stop growing a second copy of published vectors. On a 4096-dim store the cache table drops from 32.9 MB to 0.95 MB after the first full rebuild, with no new embedding calls. The cost: text copied into a different memory file, and switching back to an earlier provider or model, are embedded again (details below). No schema change and no user action.

## Why This Change Was Made

Stage 1a (#185968) lets ordinary memory-file edits reuse vectors from the published index. The embedding cache still keeps its own copy of every vector it wrote, so most cache rows duplicate a published chunk. This change deletes those copies after a successful publication, in two commits:

- **1b** (`perf(memory): retire cache rows a publication already serves`): after an ordinary sync publishes its memory files, and after a full rebuild publishes, the cache rows that run wrote are deleted when the published index holds the same bytes.
- **Step 2** (`perf(memory): retire existing cache duplicates after a full rebuild`): after a full rebuild publishes, older rows that the new index holds are deleted too. This commit can be dropped on its own if existing rows should wait for #114612.

### Retention policy this asks the storage owner to accept


Per the storage review checkpoint, this changes which valid data is kept, so it needs an explicit decision. The policy is:

A cache row of the active primary embedding identity is deleted after a successful publication when every published chunk carrying its text hash holds exactly the same bytes, at least one of those chunks belongs to a memory file, and the published index metadata binds the same provider, model, provider key, input format and dimensions. Nothing else is deleted:

- a row whose vector differs from any published copy (non-deterministic providers, ambiguous hashes) is kept;
- unpublished rows, rows for session-only text, alias identities and other identities are kept;
- a disabled cache keeps its rows;
- failed, partial and deferred runs keep every row they wrote. The skipped run's start carries to the next sync that finishes cleanly, which deletes those rows only after its publication holds the same bytes.

Accepting this means accepting these re-embedding costs, which the cache used to absorb:

1. **Text copied or moved into a different memory file.** Read-through from 1a is scoped to the file being indexed, so a retired vector for text that appears in another file is embedded again.
2. **Switching back to a previous provider or model.** After a full rebuild under identity A, A's cache rows are gone. Rebuilding under B and then back under A embeds everything again. On main, A's rows could survive in the cache up to the cap.
3. **Downgrading to a build without published read-through** (before 198b761c325). Unchanged chunks of edited memory files are embedded again, because the cache no longer has them.

### How it runs


- New `cache.retire` command on the SQLite publication worker and the PostgreSQL binding. One write transaction handles one page of up to 256 candidates in `(updated_at, hash)` order on `idx_memory_embedding_cache_updated_at`, with one chunk read per page. The caller yields between pages and stops while closing.
- Fences:
  - Ordinary sync: rows written since the sync started, or since the oldest earlier sync that did not finish cleanly.
  - Full rebuild: rows written since the rebuild started (1b), then rows written before it started (step 2). The two fences meet at the rebuild start.
- Gates: it runs only when the cache is enabled, and on ordinary syncs only when the memory sync returned normally with no dirty or full-retry state.
- It runs before the cap prune, after publication, outside every publication transaction. Publication transactions gain no work. A retirement error is logged and never fails the sync, marks retry state or records a reindex failure.
- No schema change and no new index. The 1a metadata gate is shared through `readMemoryPublishedVectorMeta`.

## Evidence

### Measured costs

On a fresh store, the CLI proof drove the built `openclaw memory index` and `openclaw memory search` through a loopback `/v1/embeddings` stub with 64 and 4096 dimensions. It ran on 120 memory files with 965 distinct chunks, comparing base 476cce7a8a3 against this head. Chunk checksums are identical between the two builds after every step.

| step | base: inputs embedded | head: inputs embedded | base: cache rows | head: cache rows |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| initial full index | 940 | 940 | 940 | 0 |
| prepend a paragraph to 10 files | 20 | 20 | 960 | 0 |
| copy 10 indexed paragraphs into other files | 0 | **10** | 960 | 0 |
| failed run (3 of 15 files written) | 12 (6 ok) | 12 (6 ok) | 966 | 6 |
| retry | 24 | 24 | 990 | 6 |
| full rebuild | 0 | 0 | 990 | 0 |

With 4096 dimensions, the same sequence leaves a 32,952,320 B cache table on base and 4,096 B on head. The failed run's 6 rows stay until the full rebuild here, because each CLI command is a new process. A long-lived manager deletes them at its next clean sync.

**Upgrading an existing store** (head run on the base store above): ordinary syncs leave older rows in place. The first full rebuild takes the cache from 990 rows to 28, the 28 that no published chunk holds, and embeds nothing. At 4096 dimensions the table goes from 32,952,320 B to 946,176 B.

**Time and lock hold** (synthetic SQLite store, 4096 dimensions, both passes run back to back):

| store | cache table | rows retired | pages | total | page p50 | page p95 | page max |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 22,000 chunk rows, 23,000 cache rows | 765 MB to 173 MB | 17,800 | 91 | 7.6 s | 75 to 91 ms | 124 to 158 ms | 182 ms |
| 44,000 chunk rows, 46,000 cache rows | 1.53 GB to 346 MB | 35,600 | 181 | 24.9 s | 113 to 159 ms | 162 to 262 ms | 395 ms |

Each page holds the writer for well under the 5 s busy timeout discussed in #143640. The cost per page grows with the chunk table, because chunks have no hash index and each page reads the chunks for its 256 hashes. The database file does not shrink: freed pages are reused by later writes, as after any delete.

### Upgrade from latest stable (openclaw@2026.11.2) and data-model compatibility

All runs use the shipped CLI (`openclaw memory index/status/search`, `openclaw doctor --fix`, `openclaw database port`) in isolated `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR`/`HOME` directories, with no Gateway process. Embeddings come from a loopback `/v1/embeddings` stub (64 dims, deterministic except for one step). PostgreSQL is 17.11 with pgvector 0.8.7 in a local container bound to 127.0.0.1.

Builds:

- **stable**: `openclaw@2026.11.2` from npm (dist-tag `latest` on 2026-11-08).
- **head**: this PR, 9c16f4e8084, built from source. The later head 8b5b0f0a18c changes only a test and the test-line allocation.
- **base**: control at the merge-base 476cce7a8a3, built from source. Every head run is repeated with base on an identical copy of the same store. That separates this PR from what main already does to a 2026.11.2 store.

#### The existing store, written by 2026.11.2

| | |
|---|---|
| Contents | 120 memory files, plus the workspace files and one session transcript from a local agent turn (loopback chat stub) |
| Steps | full index (951 inputs); prepend a paragraph to 10 files (20); copy 10 indexed paragraphs into other files (0); copy 5 paragraphs into a new file with the cache disabled and a non-deterministic provider (5 inputs, random vectors) |
| Agent DB `user_version` | 27 |
| Chunks | 996 (995 memory, 1 session); 5 hashes carry two different published vectors |
| Cache rows | 971 rows (497,152 vector bytes): 956 equal to every published copy, 5 differ from a published copy, 10 have no published chunk |

#### SQLite: 2026.11.2 store upgraded to head, with base as control

Head and base both refuse the v27 store until it is migrated: `uses schema version 27; stop active agents and run openclaw doctor --fix to upgrade it to schema version 41 before using it.` This PR adds no schema change and touches no `.sql` or `src/state` file, so the 27 to 41 migration is main's. Each arm ran `openclaw doctor --fix --non-interactive`, then the steps below.

| step | inputs embedded (head / base) | chunk checksum (head = base) | cache rows (head / base) |
|---|---:|---|---:|
| 2026.11.2 store | | `80149dab` | 971 / 971 |
| `doctor --fix` (v27 to v41) | 0 / 0 | `80149dab` | 971 / 971 |
| `memory status` | 0 / 0 | `80149dab` | 971 / 971 |
| 3 searches | 1 query each | `80149dab` | 971 / 971 |
| index, no edits | 0 / 0 | `80149dab` | 971 / 971 |
| edit 3 files, index | 6 / 6 | `ea07cfb0` | **971** / 977 |
| forced rebuild | 0 / 0 | `ef7fdec9` | **14** / 977 |
| 3 searches | 1 query each | `ef7fdec9` | 14 / 977 |

Final cache vector bytes: 7,168 on head and 500,224 on base.

- **Existing data loads and works.** After the migration, the chunk checksum (decoded vectors, path, line, hash) and the cache checksum equal the 2026.11.2 store. Status, the no-edit index (0 inputs) and all searches work. Every search returns the same hits as 2026.11.2: 6 for a marker in 10 edited files, 1 for a marker in one original file, and 1 for a phrase only in the session transcript.
- **Head and base publish identical data.** Chunk checksums match at every step, and a per-row compare of the final stores shows 999 of 999 chunk vectors identical. Among all 76 agent-DB tables, only `memory_embedding_cache` differs in row count, and the schema is identical.
- **Settings are unchanged.** `memory_index_meta` is byte-identical before and after every step on both arms. `doctor --fix` rewrites `openclaw.json` as JSON and adds `meta`, `wizard` and `skills` entries on both arms. The `memory`, `models`, `plugins`, `gateway` and `agents.defaults` blocks are semantically identical to the 2026.11.2 file.
- **Duplicates are retired only as described above:**
  - Migration, status, search and the no-edit index delete nothing: 971 rows stay through all of them.
  - The 3-file edit writes 6 rows, and head deletes them after publication. Base keeps them.
  - The forced rebuild deletes the older duplicates. Head keeps 14 rows: the 13 whose hash no published chunk carries, and the 1 whose text exists only in the session transcript. All 14 are also in base's final cache.
  - The 5 rows that differed from a published copy are kept through every ordinary sync. On the forced rebuild, both builds republish those 5 chunks with the cached vector (the same 999/999 identical chunks), so the rows stop differing and head retires them.

#### Rolling back

- **To 2026.11.2: refused, with or without this PR.** 2026.11.2 refuses the head-upgraded store and the base-upgraded store with the same error: `OpenClaw state database <state>/state/openclaw.sqlite uses newer schema version 39; this build supports 22. ... To use an older build, restore your pre-update backup created with openclaw backup create.` Once main has migrated a store, 2026.11.2 cannot open it, so its missing read-through (below) cannot re-embed anything on that store. Going back means restoring the pre-update backup, which still holds the full 2026.11.2 cache.
- **To base 476cce7a8a3, the newest build without this PR:**

| step | base on head-cleaned store | base on its own store |
|---|---:|---:|
| index, no edits | 0 inputs | 0 inputs |
| edit 3 files | 6 inputs | 6 inputs |
| forced rebuild | 0 inputs | 0 inputs |
| final chunk checksum | `3d677fde` | `3d677fde` |
| searches | same hits | same hits |

**Published read-through (198b761c325) is not in 2026.11.2.** The evidence:

- `git merge-base --is-ancestor 198b761c325 v2026.11.2` exits 1.
- v2026.11.2 (b556fdf457b) branched from main at 459cad76530 (2026-10-14). 198b761c325 was committed on 2026-10-27.
- The first tag containing 198b761c325 is v2026.11.5-beta.1.
- The 2026.11.2 `CHANGELOG.md` has no #185968 entry.

#### PostgreSQL

**2026.11.2 has no PostgreSQL memory store, so a stable PostgreSQL upgrade does not exist.**

- Its shipped `docs/reference/database-engines.md` says: "Workboard is currently the only PostgreSQL-supported store. Shared state, agent/session storage, and other stores continue using SQLite."
- The memory tables live in the agent store.
- PostgreSQL memory landed in 163e18fa89e (#174183) and 89557502c7c (#174374), and v2026.11.2 contains neither.

Two substitutes were run instead.

**1. Existing PostgreSQL store written by base 476cce7a8a3, upgraded to head.** The fixture steps match the SQLite store, including the session transcript and the non-deterministic copy. The store was then copied with `CREATE DATABASE ... TEMPLATE` so head and base each start from identical data.

| step | inputs (head / base) | chunk checksum (head = base) | cache rows (head / base) |
|---|---:|---|---:|
| existing store (schema_meta 41) | | `e33dad37` | 971 / 971 |
| status, 3 searches, no-edit index | 0 / 0 (plus 1 per query) | `e33dad37` | 971 / 971 |
| edit 3 files | 6 / 6 | `b9636702` | **971** / 977 |
| forced rebuild | 0 / 0 | `addc9f90` | **14** / 977 |

- Final cache vector bytes are 7,168 on head and 500,224 on base.
- schema_meta stays 41, and `memory_index_meta` is unchanged.
- Of the 10 memory tables, only `memory_embedding_cache` differs in row count between head and base.
- Every search returns the same hits as the SQLite runs.

**2. The 2026.11.2 SQLite store moved to PostgreSQL the supported way, then upgraded to head.** The steps: `doctor --fix`, then `openclaw database port --to postgres --dry-run`, then `openclaw database port --to postgres` (run with base). The port completed with 0 embedding inputs and rebuilt the memory index on PostgreSQL (996 chunks).

- After the port, the PostgreSQL store holds 996 chunks and 971 cache rows. The cache checksum equals the 2026.11.2 store's.
- 991 of 996 chunk vectors are identical to the 2026.11.2 store. The other 5 are the non-deterministic copy, which takes the cached vector in the port's rebuild. That is main's port behavior.
- Status and all searches work.

Head and base then ran on copies of the ported store:

| step | inputs (head / base) | chunk checksum (head = base) | cache rows (head / base) |
|---|---:|---|---:|
| ported store | | `7ead0c53` | 971 / 971 |
| status, 3 searches, no-edit index | 0 / 0 (plus 1 per query) | `7ead0c53` | 971 / 971 |
| edit 3 files | 6 / 6 | `50edc75f` | **971** / 977 |
| forced rebuild | 0 / 0 | `50edc75f` | **14** / 977 |

Across all SQLite and PostgreSQL arms, 57 search runs return the same hits as 2026.11.2. The session file id is normalized for the store written on PostgreSQL.

#### Not covered

- **Rollback to 2026.11.2 after the upgrade.** 2026.11.2 refuses any store main has migrated (above), so only base was used as the older build.
- **A stable PostgreSQL upgrade.** 2026.11.2 has no PostgreSQL memory store.
- **Gateway processes.** Each command is a separate CLI process; no long-lived Gateway process was exercised.
- **Real providers.** No real embedding provider was used, and these runs use 64 dims. The 4096-dim measurements are in "Measured costs".

<details><summary>Per-step measurements for every run</summary>

Columns: inputs sent to the embedding stub; search hits; agent DB user_version (schema_meta version on PostgreSQL); chunk rows (memory/session); chunk checksum over path, line, hash and the decoded float32 vector; cache rows split by whether the row equals every published copy of its hash, differs from one, or has no published chunk; cache vector bytes; sha256 of the `memory_index_meta_v1` value; cache checksum. ### Tests

- `manager-embedding-cache-retire.test.ts` and `manager-embedding-cache-retire.postgres.test.ts` cover the kernel on SQLite and PostgreSQL:
  - the full predicate;
  - metadata refusals (provider key, dimensions, input format, fts-only, unreadable metadata);
  - both fences and paging with the cursor;
  - an EXPLAIN guard that later pages search one `updated_at` range. A bare OR keyset sorted the remaining rows on every page under the step-2 fence.
- `manager.cache-duplicate-retirement.test.ts` covers the manager:
  - ordinary edits and full rebuilds;
  - a failed edit whose retry reuses its rows;
  - a failed edit whose text another file already publishes;
  - a skipped sync retired by the next clean sync;
  - a cached vector that differs from the published one;
  - a cleanup error that leaves publication and retry state alone;
  - a disabled cache whose existing duplicate rows survive an edit and a forced rebuild;
  - existing duplicates retired only by a full rebuild.
- Each predicate, fence, gate and call site was mutated (19 mutants). Every mutant fails the suite.
- Existing tests that read generated vectors back from the cache as a probe now hold retirement with `keepPublishedCacheDuplicates`, and their assertions are unchanged. They cover reindex recovery, chunk publication retry, source and session races, legacy-format upgrade, declared-dimension repair, and PostgreSQL rebuild reuse. `manager-cache-rebuild.test.ts` re-seeds the rows an older build kept, and expects only superseded rows after a published rebuild.
- Docs: `docs/concepts/memory-builtin.md` describes the rule.

Not covered by a test: the retained cache size the worker and the PostgreSQL binding track after a retirement. It is adjusted by the removed count, the same way `cache.clear` adjusts it.

### Checks

- `extensions/memory-core/src/memory`: 1041 passed, 56 skipped, 2 failed under heavy machine load. The 2 are the seal-reopen cases in `manager-publication-admission.test.ts`; that file passes alone on this head and on base 476cce7a8a3 (7 of 7 each).
- PostgreSQL 17, all 7 memory-core `*.postgres.test.ts` files: 59 passed. The 1b commit alone: 30 passed in the 4 cache and publication files.
- `pnpm check:changed`: every lane passes except changelog attributions, which flags existing `CHANGELOG` entries and fails the same way on base.
- `pnpm build`: passes.
- `config/test-lines-allocations/195369-memory-cache-retire.txt` allocates the 747 added test lines (kernel tests on SQLite and PostgreSQL, the manager scenarios above, and the existing-test holds).

prs.title: feat(memory): shared memory database for multi-agent deployments
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

When multiple agents share a single OpenClaw instance, each agent creates its own memory database. This wastes disk space, causes inconsistent search results across agents, and triggers unnecessary full reindexing when extra memory paths change.

## Why This Change Was Made

This PR introduces shared memory database support for multi-agent deployments by making four coordinated changes:

1. **Force shared memory index** (`memory-search.ts`): When the system agent is configured with an explicit default workspace (`agents.defaults.workspace`), force `memorySearch.enabled=true` and redirect `store.databasePath` to a shared sqlite keyed by workspace hash.

2. **Exclude extraPaths from scope hash** (`manager-reindex-state.ts`): Remove `extraPaths` from the scope hash calculation so adding/removing extra memory paths doesn't trigger a full reindex of the shared database.

3. **Skip shared memory ownership assertion** (`openclaw-agent-db.ts`, `openclaw-agent-db-schema-helpers.ts`): Allow multiple agents to open the same shared memory database without triggering ownership errors.

4. **Use canonical workspace for system agent** (`memory-runtime.ts`, `manager.ts`): When the system agent has an explicit default workspace, use that path directly for the shared memory database instead of a per-agent subdirectory.

## User Impact

- Multi-agent deployments share a single memory database, reducing disk usage and improving search consistency
- Adding/removing extra memory paths no longer triggers expensive full reindexing
- System agent and memory plugin lifecycle use the same canonical workspace and SQLite database

## Evidence

- Tested against OpenClaw v2026.9.2 source
- All four changes are minimal and focused on the shared memory path resolution
- No changes to memory search behavior, embedding, or ranking logic

prs.title: fix(agents): resolve transcript replay policies fresh so plugin package swaps take effect
prs.body:
### What Problem This Solves

Closes #139978.

`resolveTranscriptPolicy` memoized replay policies in a config-keyed WeakMap whose key fingerprint ignores the installed plugin inventory, so an in-process plugin package swap for the same provider id (setup-inference Codex generation install, onboarding plugin install) kept replaying with the previous package's `buildReplayPolicy` output until the config object itself was replaced. Those swap paths call `invalidatePluginRuntimeDiscoveryAfterConfigMutation` to clear the loader/metadata caches precisely so subsequent resolution observes the new package — the memo silently bypassed that invalidation.

### Why This Change Was Made

- The memo is net-negative even on its own terms: every cached-path call pays a control-plane fingerprint hash plus `JSON.stringify` of the key to save one warm registry snapshot lookup, and the loader's own load cache (which *is* invalidated on swaps) already absorbs the cold path.
- Call sites are per model turn, not per message, so fresh resolution costs nothing measurable.
- Deleting the memo restores the documented invalidation contract instead of adding a second invalidation owner for the WeakMap.

### User Impact

Replay policy decides sanitization, tool-call-id rewriting, thinking-block handling, and turn validation. After this change, an in-process plugin package swap takes effect on the next turn instead of serving transcript hygiene from the previous package for the rest of the process.

### Evidence

- **Pre-fix red / post-fix green**: driven through the committed real-package suite below (main's memo restored verbatim → stale policy served; memo removed → replacement policy served). The original mocked freshness case in `transcript-policy.test.ts` was removed (2026-10-09 review follow-up) now that the real-package suite protects the same regression end to end.
- **Mechanism source**: `src/plugins/plugin-control-plane-context.ts:59-73` — `inventoryFingerprint` is only included when an installed-plugin `index` is passed, and the memo key passes none; `src/plugins/registry-refresh.ts:60-69` — the invalidation contract the memo bypassed; swap paths at `src/system-agent/setup-inference-persist.ts:125` and `src/commands/onboarding-plugin-install.ts:132`.
- **Consumers checked for object-identity reliance**: all four call sites (`embedded-agent-runner/replay-history.ts:710,898`, `run/attempt-history.ts:419`, `runtime-plan/build.ts:197`) consume the policy by value; none compare identity.
- **LOC**: net −31 production (`git diff --numstat`: transcript-policy.ts 12+/43−), +22 net test lines.
- **Checks**: `oxfmt` clean, `oxlint --type-aware` clean on both files.
- **Review follow-up + main sync** (2026-10-09, head `f6867a60139`): fixed the unresolved `./types.openclaw.js` type import (→ `../config/types.openclaw.js`), removed the superseded mocked freshness case (−38 LOC), and synced current main (`update-branch`); `ci-gate` success, `mergeable` true.
- **Rebase onto current main** (2026-10-09): `mergeTranscriptPolicy` has since become a generic merge loop, the memo key gained `directApiKey`/`baseUrl` fields, and `inHistorySystemUpdates` post-processing was added; the fix is re-applied as pure memo removal on top of all of that (`mergeable` back to true, head `db1edffbe26c`), and the pre-fix red above was re-verified against main's *evolved* memo before this push.
- **Competition**: no open issue/PR matches (searched "transcript policy cache", "replay policy cache", "buildReplayPolicy stale", "memoize transcript"); no open PR touches `src/agents/transcript-policy.ts`.
- **Real package replacement proof** (2026-10-09, head `4b88053b8b2`): new committed suite `src/agents/transcript-policy.package-swap.test.ts` drives the real discovery → manifest-registry → jiti module-load path with no mocks: it writes a genuine provider plugin package (`openclaw.plugin.json` + `register(api)` → `api.registerProvider({...buildReplayPolicy})`) into a temp extensions dir, resolves the policy, replaces the package in place on disk (same path, same provider id, same config object), and runs the exact three lifecycle invalidation calls from `finishOnboardingPluginInstall` — `clearLoadInstalledPluginIndexInstallRecordsCache` + `clearPluginMetadataLifecycleCaches` + `invalidatePluginRuntimeDiscoveryAfterConfigMutation`.
  - Post-fix, this head: `[proof] before swap sanitizeToolCallIds = false` → `[proof] after swap sanitizeToolCallIds = true`, `Tests 1 passed (1)` (`src/agents/transcript-policy.package-swap.test.ts`).
  - Pre-fix reproduction: main's memo restored verbatim onto this tree (WeakMap + fingerprint key + cached read/write); the same suite goes red on the stale memo — `[proof] before swap sanitizeToolCallIds = false` → `[proof] after swap sanitizeToolCallIds = false`, `AssertionError: expected false to be true`. The memo was restored as a patch rather than by swapping the whole file because current main's `transcript-policy.ts` imports `@openclaw/ai/internal/openai-responses-payload-policy`, an export this checkout's workspace lockfile does not expose yet; the restored cache read/write logic is byte-identical to main's (`origin/main` `d121dc10aa1`).



### CI note (preflight red is main-inherited, not from this diff)

`preflight` fails on this fork PR with GitHub's job-outputs limit, not a test failure: every step succeeds and the job annotation is `Job outputs exceed 1,048,576 bytes` (e.g. check-run 101474152723, run 34028685031).

- Cause sits in the workflow, not this diff: `preflight` ships the whole compact Node test plan as the `checks_node_core_nondist_matrix` output (~98% of the job's total output bytes; measured locally by re-running the manifest planner for this PR's inputs: 522,685 bytes total, 513,351 of them that matrix).
- Fork PRs take `runner_profile=github` (hosted-runner-profile-contract in the `runner_profile` step), which packs 79 compact rows + 31 fallback rows instead of blacksmith's 50, and each row embeds the full test-file inventory in `groups[].includePatterns` (largest row ≈ 40KB).
- Contrast on the same day: same-repo PRs #140038 / #140040 (blacksmith profile, ~453KB) pass preflight; fork PRs #139979, #140008, #140045 fail with the same annotation. A retrigger of this same branch passed preflight once (run 34025126956) and failed twice — the payload sits at the cap edge, so fork-PR preflight is now a coin flip.
- All substantive checks on this PR's head are green (`check-test-types-*`, lint, node test shards that ran in earlier attempts); only `preflight` + the `ci-gate` aggregate are red.

prs.title: fix(ui): consume --session-row-actions-reserve so touch session rows stay clickable
prs.body:
### What Problem This Solves

Under the touch-mode stylesheet block (`@media (hover: none), (pointer: coarse)`), session rows render always-tappable 44×44 Pin/Archive/Menu action buttons. The block reserves space for them via `--session-row-actions-reserve`, and `layout.css` consumes it as `padding-right` on the row's *text* containers — but the row's `<a>` link element itself still spans the full row width underneath the buttons. Clicks intended for the session land on the action buttons instead: no navigation, no intent event, no RPC, no console error — the click is silently swallowed.

Runtime repro + instrumentation: #194768 (corrected root-cause comment).

### Why This Change Was Made

The reserve variable is consumed as text padding, but the link element's own hit area is not adjusted. Consuming it as `margin-inline-end` on the row link completes the separation: the link's clickable region ends before the action buttons, while the buttons remain fully tappable.

### User Impact

Before: clicking a session row anywhere over the action-button zone silently does nothing — the previously active session stays open (reported in #194768 as "session switching reverts to the previous session").

After: row clicks navigate reliably; the action buttons keep working.

### Evidence

Instrumented repro against 2026.11.1 (managed Chromium, gateway :18789):

- Shipped CSS: `document.elementsFromPoint` at the row click zone returns `BUTTON.session-action--pin` as the top element (link box spans the full row underneath); a scripted click produced zero `pushState`/intent events.
- With this rule applied: the link hit area narrows by the reserved width, the same click fires the navigation intent (`defaultPrevented: false`), pushes the target session route, and opens the session.

### Notes

- The earlier framing in #194768 ("the variable is never consumed") was incorrect — `layout.css` consumes it as text padding. This PR completes the separation on the link element itself; see the corrected root-cause comment on the issue.
- The `control-ui-performance` check failure on this branch is the total-CSS-gzip headroom squeeze discussed in the PR comments (#193890 consumed the 64 B remaining after the #192352 approval), not a defect in this change.

prs.title: fix(subagents): preserve paused tasks across requester notices
prs.body:
Related: #195387

## What Problem This Solves

A requester notice can prematurely fail a paused subagent, losing the original host-retained send after a plugin reload.

## User Impact

Retained sends can resume their original paused child after reload; a failed reload leaves that child available for the caller to inspect. Requesters that have actually finished or been released still close abandoned waits.

## Why This Change Was Made

The registry listener introduced in `9464adbe6253` inferred requester abandonment from raw model end events, including pause notices and tool handoffs. Move that check to the existing keyed runtime session-row publication, after terminal persistence, and let the settlement owner match committed terminal state to the registry's existing requester-run binding. Keep the restart-drain exclusion and unsubscribe both listeners on reset.

The requester-completion product proof joins the terminal session-effects publication before reading lifecycle metadata; its assertions and timeouts are unchanged. The restored-wait integration table adds a completed notice on a live requester while preserving queued-rejection, completed-requester, and missing-requester coverage. The only added production lifecycle machinery is the existing session-row publication subscription; test line counts, baselines, and ignore lists do not grow.

## Evidence

- Scheduled main run [42520053008, job 128851536754](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/42520053008/job/128851536754): `resume` fails after `reload-settled` and before target execution; `failed-reload` loses its original paused child; `followup` passes. Raw-parent inspection attributes the new forced-abandonment path to #195387.
- The same exact three-scenario product test passed in [42514980580](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/42514980580/job/128836211585) at `109bfcd6fb2b` (37.2 s), and [42504921828](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/42504921828/job/128805739473) at `da3cea2ce4a2` (31.9 s; then in compact-large-16).
- Touched-file type-aware lint, a TypeScript graph rooted at the three touched TypeScript files, formatting, and `git diff --check` pass.
- Independent local autoreview: P0–P2, complete candidate against `465c110e4975690406b48709d58a581756c85b82`, latest review identified an INDEX-only omission of the requester-run match; staging the reviewed amendment resolves it. No other P0–P2 defects were established. Runtime execution was outside the review's proof.
- The new live-notice case is red on the original main production code: it loses `pauseReason: "sessions_yield"` while the requester remains live. The same case and all 13 registry tests pass after restoration. The publication-boundary candidate passes all 3 requester-completion products (50.80 s) and all 13 registry cases (54.48 s). It still reproduced the original reload failure before the final requester-run match. **Blockers:** the final owner-match amendment is awaiting its isolated original-product rerun and exact-head PR CI; do not treat the earlier passes as final-head runtime proof. The local product attempt was stopped when it started broad compiler preparation on the production Gateway host; runtime proof runs on AWS Crabbox.

prs.title: fix: Telegram restart recovery leaves final replies silent
prs.body:
Related: #141959
Complements: #190006

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: a completed Telegram reply can remain unconfirmed after a Gateway restart, while recovery refuses to resend it and the chat receives no explanation until another message arrives.

## User Impact

User impact: when durable final-reply recovery stops, the Gateway immediately hands the existing uncertainty notice to lifecycle delivery in the original chat, rather than waiting for another inbound message. It does not resend an ambiguous answer. Notice delivery remains bounded and can itself fail if the channel stays unavailable; existing route, lifecycle, and permission checks remain enforced.

## Why This Change Was Made

The shared completion owner already records notice debt for an unknown pending final, but only the next inbound turn consumed that debt. Terminal queue recovery now invokes that same notice owner after persisted failed custody and before compacting its recovery checkpoint. An exact-intent check prevents an earlier failure from delivering a successor's notice. The existing process-local live-custody Set is shared through an import-free leaf, so notice recovery does not depend on the turn dispatcher. The failed-completion projection and conditional exact-intent notice handoff form one sibling operation; the queue owner still persists failed custody before awaiting it and compacts only afterward.

This is a complementary residual repair, not a replacement for @sukhdeepjohar's #190006: elapsed flood-budget accounting and wholly-unsent 429 retry classification stay in that PR. No ambiguous-send replay, new queue, schema, configuration, retry-limit, retention, or permission change is introduced.

These are Gateway-owned lifecycle notices, not continued execution under the original model caller. The current Gateway instance authorizes the transport and checks dispatch availability again after provider queue waits; stored route and intent IDs select the debt, not the sending authority. Queued retries use the existing delivery-recovery service admission. This PR does not introduce an original-caller revocation policy.

## Evidence

- **CI repair:** [original architecture job](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/42520732359/job/128853890254) exposed one introduced Madge cycle on `5703e6f0d85f2d00832c40dabf4190c0ccec6297` (runtime cycles: 0). The canonical commands reproduced it. Moving the existing live-custody registry to a single import-free leaf removes that dependency; `pnpm check:import-cycles` and `pnpm check:madge-import-cycles` now both report **0 cycles**, without lazy-import avoidance, ignores, or a baseline waiver. The complete old-head check set had no other primary failure; its CI-gate failure was aggregate.
- **Line-cap disposition and repair:** On reviewed head `c1d953b2e0f28548792531d16514bf53c9d03774`, [run 42522325771, attempt 1](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/42522325771/job/128858756181) records `1251 → 1260` as a **warning**, with `[ok] line-cap`; test-lines is the failing ratchet. The CI failure must not be attributed independently to line-cap. However, the same canonical **local** comparator rejects the introduced growth (exit 1). The complete completion-projection-and-notice phase is now extracted into `delivery-queue-failure-completion.ts`, preserving evidence selection, awaited ordering, exact intent, and error propagation. The exact frozen CI merge/base comparator (`da6fbbc3…` against `465c110…`, private index) and the original authoring-base comparator (`a5888561…`) both pass. Runtime and Madge remain at 0 cycles; no compression, ignore, or baseline increase was used.
- **Prior-head architecture:** [the repaired architecture job](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/42522325771/job/128858756016) passes on `c1d953b2e0f28548792531d16514bf53c9d03774`. Other current-head CI is reported separately.
- **Inherited budget hold (prior-head CI snapshot):** On `c1d953b2e0f28548792531d16514bf53c9d03774`, [test-line ratchet job](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/42522325771/job/128858756181) failed with 92 lines over the ceiling. The frozen base `465c110e4975690406b48709d58a581756c85b82` already has 6,586,426 test lines against a 6,586,334 ceiling (92 inherited debt; delta 0). The exact CI merge `da6fbbc3d1958be2dff0a180ef0a485dc2d57012` adds this PR's 326 lines and its exact 326-line allocation: 6,586,752 against 6,586,660, still the same 92 debt. The canonical checker reproduces both snapshots through private indexes without changing the worktree. The grant has not been inflated and the shared baseline is unchanged; base-debt reconciliation or explicit budget-owner approval is required. This prior snapshot is not being reported as passing CI or as the new head’s CI result.
- **Authority boundary:** the real Telegram HTTP sender test that closes the Gateway while a notice waits behind a serialized account request passes: retiring that lifecycle principal prevents the notice from reaching HTTP. This is evidence for the existing Gateway-owned sender contract, not a claim that the original ingress caller remains the notice principal.
- **Red on base `a5888561dd`:** real Telegram HTTP transport plus durable queue recovery produced no notice; the original answer was not retried. A full isolated Gateway also reproduced the issue through an inbound Telegram DM, a completed agent/model turn, a Bot API 429, SIGKILL during the flood wait, and a new process on the same disk state. After the existing 60-second send lease expired, recovery logged `send_attempt_started; refusing blind replay` and the expected notice never arrived.
- **Green with this repair:** the same cold-process flow delivered the existing uncertainty notice once, with one attempted original answer and no ambiguous-answer replay. After the settlement extraction, the E2E case was rerun and took 69.6 seconds (111.8 seconds Vitest; 286.2 seconds including runtime preparation). Process replacement, refusal, and delivered chat text are asserted by the test.
- Real Telegram HTTP regressions cover an ambiguous response and exhausted proven-no-send recovery, repeat-drain deduplication, and no answer replay. The notice-owner unit regression covers successor-intent isolation. Both focused files pass.
- Existing recovery, producer-recovery, and pending-notice integration suites: **64 passed** across three files before the dependency-only extraction (96.8 seconds Vitest). After extraction, the affected custody, notice, notice-integration, and real Telegram HTTP suites were rerun: **37 passed** across four files (38.3 and 10.4 seconds across the two Vitest shards).
- After the settlement extraction, **75 affected tests passed** across queue recovery, producer recovery, notice integration, and real Telegram HTTP suites (122.9 seconds Vitest; 127.7 seconds including preparation). prs.title: fix(swabble): transcript history ignores transcripts.maxEntries
prs.body:
Closes #194843

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: `transcripts.log` keeps 100 entries no matter what `transcripts.maxEntries` is set to.

## User Impact

User impact: swabble keeps at most `transcripts.maxEntries` transcripts (default 50), as the README documents.

## Why This Change Was Made

`TranscriptsStore` had a hard-coded `limit = 100`. `serve` now passes the configured limit to `append`. The store also takes an optional file URL so it can be tested without touching `~/Library`.

## Evidence

- New `TranscriptsStoreTests.testAppendKeepsConfiguredNumberOfEntries` checks the in-memory entries, the file on disk, and a reload.
  - It fails when the old fixed cap of 100 is restored.
  - It passes with the fix.
- `swift test --package-path apps/swabble`: 13 passed, 0 failed (macOS 26, Swift 6.4.2).
- `apps/swabble/scripts/lint.sh` (SwiftLint strict): 0 violations. SwiftFormat lint: clean.


**Behavior proof.** Live speech can't be captured in a headless shell. Instead, a throwaway (uncommitted) harness fed 8 `"clawd phrase N"` segments through `ServeCommand.consumeTranscripts`, the same loop `serve` runs, with `transcripts.maxEntries = 5`. The real `~/Library/Application Support/swabble/transcripts.log` lived under a temp home (`CFFIXED_USER_HOME`). The shipped `swabble tail-log` then read it back in a new process:

```
## main (before)
transcripts.log lines on disk: 8
$ swabble tail-log
phrase 1 … phrase 8

## this PR (after)
transcripts.log lines on disk: 5
$ swabble tail-log
phrase 4
phrase 5
phrase 6
phrase 7
phrase 8
```

**Existing data compatibility:** the log format (newline-separated text) is unchanged. A 100-entry `transcripts.log` from an older build loads, and the next append trims it to the newest `maxEntries`:

```
seeded transcripts.log with 100 lines from an older build
serve loop fed 8 wake phrases (maxEntries=5)
transcripts.log lines on disk: 5
$ swabble tail-log   # new process
phrase 4 … phrase 8
```


**Upgrade from the v2026.11.1 release, with existing config and history.**
- A `config.json` is created by the release binary and customized.
- History is written by the release's own `serve` transcript loop.
- This branch then loads the same `config.json` through `ConfigLoader.load` and appends through the same loop.
- The shipped `tail-log` reads the result back in a new process.

```
## v2026.11.1
$ swabble-v2026.11.1 setup --config config.json
# customized: wake.word=robot, transcripts.maxEntries=5, hook.command=/bin/echo
serve loop (config loaded from config.json) fed 8 "robot release phrase N" segments
transcripts.log lines: 8   (release ignores maxEntries=5)

## upgrade to this PR (same config.json + transcripts.log)
serve loop (config loaded from config.json) fed 3 "robot pr phrase N" segments
transcripts.log lines: 5
$ swabble-pr tail-log   # new process
release phrase 7
release phrase 8
pr phrase 1
pr phrase 2
pr phrase 3
config.json sha eb04c83bdeffc974 -> eb04c83bdeffc974 ; wake.word/maxEntries/hook.command: robot 5 /bin/echo
```

**Gap:** the shipped `swabble serve` cannot run live microphone input here. In a non-interactive shell, its Speech.framework pipeline aborts on authorization (`Abort trap: 6`) before any audio arrives, on `main` and this branch alike. So the speech-to-segment step is replaced by the synthetic segments above. Everything after it (config load, wake gating, the `serve` consumer, the on-disk log, CLI readback) is the shipped code.

prs.title: fix(swabble): serve overwrites an unreadable config with defaults
prs.body:
Closes #194842

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: `swabble serve` replaces the user's config with defaults when the existing file fails to load (e.g. a JSON typo).

## User Impact

User impact: a broken config makes `serve` exit with the load error and leaves the file unchanged. A missing config still gets defaults written, as before.

## Why This Change Was Made

`serve` caught every load error and saved defaults over the file. It now only does that for `ConfigError.missingConfig`, and other errors propagate.

## Evidence

- New `CLIProcessTests.testServeLeavesUnreadableConfigUntouched` runs the real binary against a config missing its closing brace.
  - Without the fix it fails: the file is rewritten with `"command":""` (was `/usr/bin/say`).
  - With the fix: exit 1, file byte-for-byte unchanged.
- `swift test --package-path apps/swabble`: 13 passed, 0 failed (macOS 26, Swift 6.4.2).
- `apps/swabble/scripts/lint.sh` (SwiftLint strict): 0 violations. SwiftFormat lint: clean.


**Real CLI proof** (debug builds of `main` and this branch, macOS 26, temp dir as `HOME`). The `Abort trap: 6` is the speech pipeline starting in a headless shell after the config loaded:

```
## main (before)
$ swabble setup --config sw.json && set hook.command=/usr/bin/say
"command":"\/usr\/bin\/say"
$ # drop the closing brace (hand-edit mistake)
$ swabble serve --config sw.json
Abort trap: 6   (exit=134)
sha256 before: b2f3703f5df4b151 / after: 3b217deac2bd2ab3  REWRITTEN
"command":""

## this PR (after)
$ swabble serve --config sw.json
exit=1
error: DecodingError.dataCorrupted: ... The given data was not valid JSON ... "Unexpected end of file"
sha256 before: 9caeef3f98ec539d / after: 9caeef3f98ec539d  UNCHANGED
"command":"\/usr\/bin\/say"
$ swabble serve --config missing.json   # no file yet
missing.json created with defaults: "word":"clawd"
```

**Existing config compatibility:** the loader and format are unchanged. A config written by the `main` binary works with this branch:

```
$ swabble-main setup --config sw.json; swabble-main mic set 3 --config sw.json
saved device index 3
$ swabble-pr test-hook "hello" --config sw.json
hook invoked            (exit=0)
$ swabble-pr mic set 5 --config sw.json
"deviceIndex":5
$ swabble-pr serve --config sw.json  -> loads, file sha 92022899e903cec6 -> 92022899e903cec6
```


**Upgrade from the v2026.11.1 release** (`swabble` built from tag `v2026.11.1`, then this branch on the same file):

```
$ swabble-v2026.11.1 setup --config config.json && swabble-v2026.11.1 mic set 3 --config config.json
saved device index 3
# customized: hook.command=/bin/echo, wake.word=robot, transcripts.maxEntries=5
hook.command=/bin/echo wake.word=robot audio.deviceIndex=3 transcripts.maxEntries=5
$ swabble-pr test-hook "hello" --config config.json
hook invoked            (exit=0)
$ swabble-pr serve --config config.json   -> loaded; file sha 905f6ea147f70a90 -> 905f6ea147f70a90 UNCHANGED
$ swabble-pr mic set 4 --config config.json
saved device index 4
hook.command=/bin/echo wake.word=robot audio.deviceIndex=4 transcripts.maxEntries=5
```

prs.title: fix(sessions): Telegram transcript echoes are not recorded on explicit multi-agent gateways
prs.body:
Closes #194829

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: on a gateway with `agents.ownership: "explicit"` and several agents, a delivered Telegram transcript echo (`tools.media.audio.echoTranscript`) is never added to the conversation history. Instead it logs `result was delivered but was not added to the conversation: Multiple agents are configured, but this operation has no explicit owner`, even though the Telegram account is bound to one agent.

## User Impact

User impact: confirmed sends that have no producing turn, such as transcript echoes, are recorded once in the destination conversation of the agent the channel/account binding selects, as the [conversation transcript ownership](docs/refactor/conversation-transcript-ownership.md) rules require. The missing-owner warning goes away for bound destinations. Single-agent and unbound setups behave as before.

## Why This Change Was Made

`commitConfirmedVisibleMessage` (`src/sessions/confirmed-visible-message.ts`) chose the history owner as `producer?.agentId ?? resolveDefaultAgentId(config)`. A preflight transcript echo has no producer, and explicit ownership has no default agent, so `AgentSelectionRequiredError` was thrown before destination lookup could consult the binding. The ownership doc says destination lookup does not need a producer: carried route, producer context, exact local binding, then plugin resolver.

Without a producer, the owner now comes from `resolveAgentRoute` for the destination's channel and account. That reuses the routing owner's binding tiers, and unbound destinations keep the old default-agent fallback, which is the same error when no default exists. Peer-level bindings are still enforced: the existing `belongsToAgent` check re-resolves the route with the destination peer and skips with the documented "belongs to a different agent" diagnostic.

The fix lives in the shared recorder, so other producer-less confirmed sends benefit as well; Telegram code is untouched. This does not overlap #194783, which covers the durable `sendPayload` final mirror.

Accepted edge: the owner is chosen from channel/account bindings before the peer is known. A destination covered only by a peer-specific binding to a different agent than the account binding is skipped with the cross-agent diagnostic, not recorded under the peer's agent.

## Evidence

- New regression `records a producer-less send under the agent its account binding selects (#194829)` in `confirmed-visible-message.integration.test.ts`. It uses explicit ownership, two agents, account bindings and no producer, and the echo lands in `beta`'s conversation.
- Red on `origin/main`: it fails with `AgentSelectionRequiredError: Multiple agents are configured, but this operation has no explicit owner…`, the same text as the issue's warning. Green with the fix (11/11).
- Consumer suites green: `deliver` 86, `outbound-send-service` 24, `delivery-queue.transcript` 14, `deliver-confirmed-visible` 3, `outbound-send-service.accepted-outcomes` 2, `echo-transcript` 4, `echo-transcript.integration` 2, `audio-preflight` 5, `apply` 29, `media-understanding-runtime` 7, `subagent-announce-text-delivery` 5, `subagent-completion-mirror.integration` 1, `voice-call realtime-handler` 37.
- oxlint (type-aware), oxfmt and the import-cycle check are clean.
- Not run: a live Telegram voice-note round trip, which needs a bot account and an audio provider. The integration test drives the real recorder against real session storage.

prs.title: fix(telegram): durable final deliveries skip the channel-final transcript mirror
prs.body:
Closes #194783

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: delivered Telegram final replies get no `channel-final` delivery mirror in the session transcript when live preview is off, for example when a plugin registers a modifying `message_sending` / `reply_payload_sending` hook.

## User Impact

User impact: Telegram finals record the same `channel-final` delivery receipt in the transcript whether they go out through preview finalization, the plain fallback, or core durable delivery. Control UI history and other tools that read the receipt now see it after preview is disabled. Delivery itself is unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

The durable `handled_visible` branch in the Telegram final sender returned before any mirror ran. Core durable delivery also reported the provider-visible `content` only on partial failure, so the channel had no confirmed text it could mirror. ClawSweeper's review pointed out that mirroring the original payload would record text that a message hook may have rewritten.

- **Core (`src/channels/turn/durable-delivery.ts`):** collects the post-hook text from each confirmed payload's `message_sent` event (`onMessageSentEvent`, already threaded through the durable send) and reports it as `content` on `handled_visible`. `ChannelDeliveryOutcome.content` is already documented as the "final provider-visible text … for this logical payload's terminal observation", so this fills a documented field on the success path instead of adding a new one.
- **Telegram (`bot-message-dispatch-delivery.ts`):** the `handled_visible` branch writes its channel-final mirror from that confirmed text. It uses the same `hasReplyPayloadFinalDeliveryCapture` guard (dispatcher-owned replies keep their own transcript owner) and the same idempotency sequence as the preview and fallback paths.

Ownership: core durable delivery owns the confirmed post-hook text, and Telegram keeps owning its channel-final receipt. The deprecated `sendBatch` `mirror` parameter is ignored, and automatic destination history deliberately skips the producing conversation, so neither could own this. Each final takes exactly one of the three paths, so it is mirrored once.

## Evidence

- New `extensions/telegram/src/bot-message-dispatch.delivery-transcript.test.ts` › "mirrors a durable final with the confirmed post-hook text": the durable send returns `handled_visible` with hook-rewritten content, and the test asserts exactly one `channel-final` mirror carrying that text. **Red on base** (1 failed / 7 passed), green with the fix (8/8).
- New `src/channels/turn/durable-delivery.test.ts` › "reports the confirmed post-hook text on a visible final": **red on base** (1 failed / 7 passed), green with the fix (8/8).
- Related files, all green: Telegram `final-delivery-lifecycle` 12, `preview.telegram-http` 40, `recovery.telegram-http` 8, `reply-targets.telegram-http` 24, `fallback-topic-media` 4; core `durable-delivery.reload` 25, `run-channel-turn.delivery` 17, `run-channel-turn.finalize` 9, `run-channel-turn.settlement` 3, `delivery-result` 6.
- oxlint (type-aware, tsconfig), oxfmt check, the import-cycle check (0 cycles) and the whitespace diff check are clean.

Gaps: I did not run a live Telegram E2E (it needs bot and user credentials I don't have here), and I did not run a full local typecheck (CI covers it). Other channels' durable `handled_visible` results now also carry `content`. I found no consumer that treats its presence as a partial delivery, and the lifecycle's terminal observation already prefers `content` over `payload.text`.

prs.title: fix(worktrees): worktrees remove and restore print only "The CLI command failed." for an unknown id
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: `openclaw worktrees remove <id>` and `openclaw worktrees restore <id>` print only `The CLI command failed. For help, run openclaw doctor.` when the id names no managed worktree (a typo, or a worktree already removed without a snapshot). The reason is only visible with `--json`.

## User Impact

User impact: both commands now print the existing registry message, `unknown active worktree: <id>` or `worktree <id> is not restorable`, with the same exit code 1; `--json` output and Gateway `worktrees.remove` / `worktrees.restore` responses are unchanged. No new wording.

## Why This Change Was Made

The registry lookups (`requireActiveWorktreeRecord`, `requireManagedWorktreeRestoreRecord`) threw plain `Error`s, which the CLI's failure handler treats as unexpected and replaces with the generic line. They now throw a `WorktreeRecordNotFoundError` (an `Error` subclass with the same message and default `name`, so `String(error)` and the Gateway's `UNAVAILABLE` response stay as they are), and the CLI's shared `mutateWorktree` wrapper maps that class to an `ExpectedCliError`, the same path the other worktree guards use (#192976).

## Evidence

From source on `main` at 75c2c49cec, macOS, Node 26.7.0, fresh state directory.

Before:
```
$ openclaw worktrees remove nope
[openclaw] The CLI command failed.
[openclaw] For help, run `openclaw doctor`.
$ openclaw worktrees restore nope
[openclaw] The CLI command failed.
[openclaw] For help, run `openclaw doctor`.
```

After (same build plus this change):
```
$ openclaw worktrees remove nope
unknown active worktree: nope
$ openclaw worktrees restore nope
worktree nope is not restorable
$ openclaw worktrees remove nope --json   # unchanged document, same message
{ "ok": false, "error": { "type": "cli_error", "message": "unknown active worktree: nope" } }
$ openclaw worktrees create <state>/repo   # valid operations unchanged
07e1a25c-f035-4896-b45e-6b5c07d7fff9	<state>/worktrees/b678da571d1da399/tidal-langoustine
```
Exit 1 for the unknown ids in both modes, as before.

Tests:
- `pnpm test src/cli/worktrees-cli.test.ts src/cli/worktrees-cli.import-boundary.test.ts src/agents/worktrees/service.gc-cli.test.ts src/agents/worktrees/service.remove-lease.test.ts src/gateway/server-methods/worktrees.remove-restore-trim.test.ts`: 36 passed (the Gateway test still sees `Error: unknown active worktree: <id>` and the service tests still match the messages).
- New cases "names an unknown id from remove/restore instead of a generic failure" reject the owner call with the typed error and assert an `ExpectedCliError` whose human and machine output are the message. Both fail with `worktrees-cli.ts` reverted to `main` (`expected Error: unknown active worktree: nope to match object { name: 'ExpectedCliError', …}`) and pass with the change.
- Test-line budget: 14 added lines, allocated in `config/test-lines-allocations/worktrees-unknown-id-expected-error.txt`.
- `pnpm tsgo:core`, `oxfmt --check` and `oxlint --type-aware` on the changed files: clean.

Local autoreview / local ClawSweeper were not run.

prs.title: fix(scripts): allow tooling imports on stock Bun

## What Problem This Solves

Dev tooling can fail before doing any work on stock Bun main because `node:module` has no named `registerHooks` export. This affects tooling dependency checks and the installed Gateway benchmark even when they do not request a hook. This is an API gap in the upcoming Bun 1.5, not a workaround for an old supported release.

## User Impact

Tooling imports and checks that do not need module hooks can run on stock Bun. Node and the pinned OpenClaw Bun fork retain the same hook behavior. Actually invoking an unavailable hook still throws naturally.

## Why This Change Was Made

Use the default `node:module` export and look up `registerHooks` at each existing call. Keep `createRequire` as a named import. The change is four replaced lines across two modules; no fallback loader, runtime branch, new state, or test scaffolding.

prs.title: fix(config): record the calling client on config.write audit records
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The config audit journal records the *writer process* for every `config.write` event. For Gateway-mediated writes that process is always the Gateway itself, so `pid`, `argv` and `cwd` identify the daemon but never the caller. A measured example from a live deployment:

```
ts 2026-11-05T23:50:59.242Z, pid 1464, ppid 339,
argv "node …/dist/index.js gateway --port 18789", cwd /home/wayne,
origin "config-rpc", changedPathCount 29, result "rename"
```

Twenty-nine config paths changed and the record cannot say who asked for it. That makes the journal useless for the question an audit trail exists to answer: which client changed this file.

Upstream already computes the answer — `resolveControlPlaneActor(client)` produces `{actor, deviceId, clientIp, connId}` in `src/gateway/server-methods/config.ts` — but that value reaches a log line and never the durable record. This PR carries it into the journal.

## The change

- **`src/config/io.types.ts`** — new `ConfigWriteAuditActor` and `ConfigWriteOptions.auditActor`.
- **`src/config/io.audit.ts`** — `createConfigWriteAuditRecordBase()` takes a single `attribution` object holding origin and optional actor, and emits each key only when present. A write with no client keeps the record byte-shape identical. One object rather than two separate parameters also keeps `io.write.ts` inside its 700-line cap without adding a line.
- **`src/config/io.write.ts`** — passes `attribution` through from the write options.
- **`src/gateway/server-methods/config-write-flow.ts`** — `commitGatewayConfigWrite` takes an optional `actor` and sets `auditActor` on the `config-rpc` write options.
- **`src/gateway/server-methods/config.ts`** — `config.set` and the apply/patch restart path pass the actor they already resolve.

## Evidence

**Tests — 151 passed / 3 files, exit 0** across `src/config/io.write-config.test.ts`, `src/config/io.audit.test.ts`, `src/gateway/server-methods/config.test.ts`.

**Lint and types.** `oxlint` on every touched file: 0 errors. `format:check` clean. `tsc -p tsconfig.core.json --noEmit`: zero errors in any file this PR touches.

prs.title: fix(system-agent): reply with rescue command findings when the command exits non-zero
prs.body:
Fixes #195432

## What Problem This Solves

`/openclaw doctor` exits 1 whenever doctor has any finding, including warnings. The rescue path (`src/system-agent/rescue-message.ts`) captured output with a runtime whose `exit()` threw a plain `Error("OpenClaw operation exited with code 1")`. That error escaped `runSystemAgentRescueMessage`, so the chat turn failed even though doctor had finished and printed its report. On Telegram the ingress drain treats the failure as a failed delivery and keeps the update at the head of its lane for up to 24 hours.

## User Impact

`/openclaw doctor` (and any other rescue command that ends with a non-zero exit) now replies with its findings, followed by `OpenClaw operation exited with code N.` The message completes, so the update is no longer retried and later messages in that chat are not blocked.

## Why This Change Was Made

- The rescue capture runtime now throws the existing `SystemAgentOperationExitError`. The conversational chat engine already uses that error for a command that wrote its failure and then exited.
- A shared `runCapturedOperation` helper catches only that error and returns the captured output plus the exit code. Every other error still propagates unchanged, so real failures keep their current handling.
- Both rescue execution sites use the helper: the read-only command path and the approved pending-change path.
- `SystemAgentOperationExitError` now keeps its `code`.

The retry policy itself (8 attempts, 24-hour dead-letter age) is untouched. It is intended, per #137572. The defect was that a completed command was counted as a failed delivery.

## Evidence

![proof](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/wr-web/openclaw/proof-assets/195432/proof.png)

**Live local Gateway:** the Gateway ran from source on loopback with isolated state. An `operator.admin` client (owner, direct webchat) sent `chat.send` "/openclaw doctor". Doctor on this rig reports one warning (`core/doctor/ui-protocol-freshness`) and exits 1. Both runs used the same base `54b059c478f3`.

| | main | this branch `02755f558a5d` |
|---|---|---|
| dispatch | `message processed: channel=webchat … outcome=error … error="Error: OpenClaw operation exited with code 1"` | no error outcome; the turn completes |
| reply stored in the session | `Your request couldn't be completed.` (doctor findings lost) | `Doctor (live Gateway): ran 7 check(s), 1 finding(s)` … the full report … `OpenClaw operation exited with code 1.` |

**Tests:**

- **New test:** `src/system-agent/rescue-message.test.ts` "replies with a completed command's findings when it exits non-zero (#195432)". It fails on main with `Error: OpenClaw operation exited with code 1` and passes here.
- **Whole file:** 29 tests pass. The 3 "queues and applies agent creation … through conversational approval" cases fail identically on main on this Windows host, with workspace path formatting in the plan text.
- **Checks:** `oxfmt` and `oxlint` are clean, and the line-cap ratchet passes. The test-lines ratchet passes with a 13-line allocation (the full regression), `config/test-lines-allocations/195432-rescue-exit-reply.txt`.

prs.title: fix(skills): reduce memory held by live search catalogs
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes excessive memory retention when many live sessions prepare and search large skill catalogs. Related: #195232.

## User Impact

Skill searches retain compact identities while preserving the existing content indexes, search results, and run-specific read authority. No configuration or migration is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

Each prepared skill previously retained a serialized copy of its name and description; each search view serialized those copies again. Live catalog arrays kept these identities alive beyond the four-slot idle cache. The fix carries the already-published content hash and hashes the ordered metadata/body revision lists through the existing identity helper. It adds no cache and removes three production lines overall.

## Evidence

Native-GC regression: the original code retains 24,967,272 bytes against an 8 MiB metadata budget; the fix passes. All 129 focused tests pass, including the native retention check, search ranking, catalog admission and skill-read consumers.

Synthetic owner workload: 465 live catalogs, 512 public-text skills, 20 catalog subsets, three searches per preparation; five serial counterbalanced pairs and two baseline A/A pairs on Node 24.22.1. Timings exclude forced GC. Separate allocation passes include collected objects.

| Median metric | Original | Fixed |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Post-GC old + large-object spaces | 532.18 MiB | 232.74 MiB |
| Owner CPU, 465 preparations | 12,444 ms | 12,524 ms |
| Preparation + 3 searches, p50 | 14.03 ms | 14.19 ms |
| Preparation + 3 searches, p95 | 17.11 ms | 15.71 ms |
| Sampled allocated bytes | 10.69 GB | 10.53 GB |

CPU increases 0.65%; median latency increases 1.16%. Tail timings vary on the shared host; no tail-latency improvement is claimed. An earlier pass overlapping broad validation had unstable p95 controls and is excluded from timing acceptance. Search-result digests match every arm. The fixed retained heap is approximately 5% above the pre-#195232 baseline on this fixture, removing more than 95% of the introduced increase.

Heap snapshots at 100 live catalogs attribute 65,492,568 bytes of savings to identity strings and 2,010,000 bytes to their removed wrappers. Their sum matches the entire graph reduction within 2,920 bytes. The 40 lexical indexes and their postings retain exactly the same 62,572,392 bytes before and after. The idle byte estimate is conservative on this fixture; this fixes live identity duplication, not an undercounted postings budget.

Reproduction: `node --expose-gc --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs scripts/perf/skill-search-retention-measure.ts --root /path/to/revision --output /new/proof/path --catalogs 465 --skills 512 --variants 20 --rounds 1`. Use `--snapshots` or `--allocations` in separate passes. The accompanying opt-in Gateway workload adds real skill/tool searches, multi-agent databases, config reloads and admission census to the existing stress campaign. Its optional native post-Doctor verification runs in a separate process before Gateway creation; the old-generation Gateway explicitly receives --expose-gc. The two-agent 90-second smoke completed six rounds, native subagents, searches, config reload, retained-heap capture and teardown.

**Scope of proof:** the owner workload deliberately keeps catalogs live. It does not establish the number of catalogs retained by a production Gateway. The first large Gateway attempt failed during warmup (Code Mode worker heap exhaustion before native-child dispatch), so it supplies no soak result. Two exact-build, 465-agent startup controls completed 31 minutes: the equal-age 30-minute old-generation floor differs by only 0.506% (415,417,720 → 417,520,216 bytes), and neither endpoint snapshot contains a lexical index. This all-sealed, no-tool control does not reproduce the regression. A fully generated 35.18 GiB synthetic btrfs database is undergoing native verification before the serial tool-workload comparison; no result from that workload is claimed yet. This PR is intentionally not merged.

`pnpm check:changed --staged --base HEAD` passes every gate except the existing changelog-attribution failure. The identical 20 violations reproduce on the clean exact parent `e097b687cc62658367f44b8ba903e47cef04a5f9`; commit `266a7aa0fe69` (#194364) introduced the rejecting handles without reconciling historical records. This is an actionable main validation regression, not a waived or masked test. No changelog records were edited.

Independent Codex autoreviews of the production candidate and both benchmark-only follow-ups are scoped-clean through P2, with no actionable findings. The reviewer did not independently execute the reported proof. The 68-line test allocation covers the native subprocess boundary regression; its final test body took 196 ms (1.52 s wrapper).

Current-head CI [42533380006](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/42533380006) is green for `f8059df1b6e6` (tested merge `6d39b251a28d` against main `c74999244a71`), including changed tests, UI end-to-end, typechecks, lint and ratchets. Earlier runs encountered independently attributed main test-type and test-budget regressions; neither remains in this run. No failure was masked, no allocation was inflated, and no CI rerun was requested to chase green. The PR remains intentionally unmerged.

The latest tooling follow-up joins periodic maintenance before offline fixture bulk writes and checkpoints each 64 MiB of committed transcript payload through the existing owner. A fresh 128 MiB native fixture, seven fixture tests, script checks and independent review pass; the selected broad checks report only the attributed changelog failure. Net change is +10 tooling lines and zero production lines. The original interrupted large seed was recovered by verifying its entire deterministic prefix and appending only the missing suffix; that recovery is not claimed as a passing replay of the original generation. Current-head CI is green.
