prs.title: fix(codex): Codex turns fail when a plugin MCP server shares a configured server's name
prs.body:
Closes #194825

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: every Codex-harness turn fails with `url is not supported for stdio in mcp_servers.<name>` when a plugin bundles an MCP server with the same name as a server in `mcp.servers`.

## User Impact

User impact: a configured MCP server now wins a name collision with a plugin's bundled server for Codex turns, as it already does for the merged static surface. Codex turns start, and fallback chains ending in a Codex model work again.

## Why This Change Was Made

Codex receives MCP servers from two projections: the bundle thread patch and the user-server (configured) projection. The bundle patch kept bundled names that an enabled configured server already owns, so Codex merged both into one `mcp_servers.<name>` table carrying the plugin's `command` and the configured `url`. That combination is rejected at `codex-rs/config/src/mcp_types.rs:321` (`throw_if_set("stdio", "url", …)`) in the sibling `../codex` checkout.

The bundle patch now drops entries shadowed by an enabled configured server, using the same enabled/session-override rule as the user-server projection. This happens before plugin data dirs are prepared, so a shadowed plugin server no longer gets a data dir either.

Cutover: the bundle path projected durable "Allow Always" grants only for configured names (#136019). Those names can no longer appear in the bundle patch, and the user-server projection already projects their grants (`bundle-mcp-codex.user-config.test.ts`), so that dead filter and its test are removed. The optional `agentId` field stays on the exported `LoadCodexBundleMcpThreadConfigParams` SDK type, because removing it would change a public contract.

Accepted edge: when a configured server is enabled but excluded for the agent by `isCodexMcpServerAllowedForAgent`, the bundled copy is still dropped. The operator configured that name, so it is not silently replaced by the plugin's server.

## Evidence

- New regression `leaves a same-named bundled server to the enabled configured server (#194825)` reproduces the issue's shape (bundled stdio `gbrain` plus configured HTTP `gbrain`). The patch now holds only `notes`, and `gbrain` is in `userStaticServerNames`.
- Updated `lets user config disable a same-named bundled server unless the session enables it`: a session override enables the configured server, which now owns the name rather than shipping the bundled copy alongside it.
- Red/green: both cases fail against `origin/main`'s `codex-mcp-config.ts` (2 failed / 5 passed) and pass with the fix (7/7).
- Sibling suites green: `bundle-mcp-codex.user-config` 12/12, `run-attempt.configured-mcp` 23/23, `thread-lifecycle.configured-mcp-ownership` 5/5, `attempt-startup*` (20, 9, 4, 3), `mcp-app-session-preparation` 4/4, `run-attempt-client-prewarm` 5/5.
- oxlint (type-aware), oxfmt and the import-cycle check are clean.
- Not run: a live Codex app-server turn. It needs a ChatGPT-authenticated codex-cli plus a plugin bundling a same-named stdio server. The reporter verified the equivalent local patch on 2026.11.1 with codex-cli 0.167.0.

prs.title: fix(templates): templates add and dev put a new agent's workspace under ~/.openclaw even with --profile or OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: `openclaw templates add` and `openclaw templates dev` place a new agent's workspace under `~/.openclaw/workspace-<id>` when no `--workspace` is given, even when the CLI runs with `--profile <name>` or `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR`. Every other agent-creation path (`agents add`, the Gateway's `templates.add` plan) puts that default beside the other agents' workspaces in the active state directory, so a profile install ends up writing into the real home directory's `.openclaw`.

## User Impact

User impact: with a profile or a custom state directory, a template agent's default workspace now lands in that state directory (`<state>/workspace-<id>`), the same place `agents add` and the Gateway use, and `templates dev` previews that path. Runs without a profile or `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR` resolve to the same `~/.openclaw/workspace-<id>` as before, and an explicit `--workspace` is unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

`buildTemplateAddPlan` computed its fallback from the home directory, while `buildGatewayTemplateAddPlan` and `agents add` compute theirs from `resolveStateDir()`. The CLI `templates add` and `templates dev` paths call `buildTemplateAddPlan` directly and pass `workspace` only when the operator gives `--workspace`, so they hit the home-based fallback. The fallback now uses `resolveStateDir()`, which already honors `--profile` and `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR` and still resolves to `~/.openclaw` otherwise.

## Evidence

From source on `main` at 75c2c49cec, macOS, Node 26.7.0, `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR=/private/tmp/ocp2-IY33`, template project created with `openclaw templates create`.

Before:
```
$ openclaw templates dev /private/tmp/ocp2-IY33/tpl1
Template dev preview: tpl1@0.1.0
Agent: tpl1
Workspace: /Users/<user>/.openclaw/workspace-tpl1
```

After (same build plus this change):
```
$ openclaw templates dev /private/tmp/ocp2-IY33/tpl1      # OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR=/private/tmp/ocp2-IY33
Template dev preview: tpl1@0.1.0
Agent: tpl1
Workspace: /private/tmp/ocp2-IY33/workspace-tpl1
$ OPENCLAW_PROFILE=demo openclaw templates dev <project>/tpl1   # no OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR
Workspace: ~/.openclaw-demo/workspace-tpl1
```
Without a profile or state-dir override the default stays `~/.openclaw/workspace-tpl1`.

Upgrade scenario (existing install, same build plus this change): an agent that an earlier release created with the old default, recorded in config as `agents.entries.tpl1.workspace = <home>/.openclaw/workspace-tpl1`, with `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR` now set.
```
$ openclaw agents list
- main      Workspace: <state>/workspace/main
- tpl1 (Tpl1)  Workspace: <home>/.openclaw/workspace-tpl1
$ openclaw templates dev <state>/tpl1                  # same template again
Agent: tpl1-2
Workspace: <state>/workspace-tpl1-2
$ openclaw templates dev <state>/tpl1 --agent-id tpl1  # explicit existing id
Agent: tpl1
Workspace: <state>/workspace-tpl1
Blocked actions: 1
ERROR agent_id_collision $.agent.id: Agent id "tpl1" already exists; Templates never merge into existing agents.
$ openclaw agents list                                   # unchanged
- tpl1 (Tpl1)  Workspace: <home>/.openclaw/workspace-tpl1
```
The existing agent keeps its configured workspace and files (`<home>/.openclaw/workspace-tpl1/AGENTS.md` still present); this change only decides where a *new* agent's workspace goes when no `--workspace` is given, and Templates never merge into an existing agent, so nothing already recorded in `agents.entries` moves.

Tests:
- `pnpm test src/templates/application-schema.test.ts src/templates/add-stateless.test.ts`: 36 passed.
- New case "defaults a new agent's workspace to the state directory" plans a template without `context.workspace` under a stubbed `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR` and expects `<state>/workspace-analyst`; it fails on `main` (the plan resolves to `~/.openclaw/workspace-analyst`) and passes with the change.
- Test-line budget: 15 added lines, allocated in `config/test-lines-allocations/template-default-workspace-state-dir.txt`.
- `pnpm tsgo:core`, `oxfmt --check` and `oxlint --type-aware` on both files: clean.

Local autoreview / local ClawSweeper were not run.

prs.title: feat(backup): omit Doctor migration originals from archives on request
prs.body:
Closes #183277

**Decision needed:** should `openclaw backup create` keep Doctor's retained pre-migration originals
(`<database>.pre-startup-migration-<id>.bak` and `.scoped.bak`) in archives?

- **A. Keep them by default and add an opt-out flag (this PR, recommended).** Default archives do not change.
  Operators who already keep a separate pre-upgrade backup can pass `--exclude-migration-backups`.
- B. Omit them by default and add a flag to keep them. This gives smaller archives with no action, but a restored
  archive silently loses the rollback path that `repair-and-recovery.md` tells users to keep with their
  pre-upgrade backups.
- C. No code change, only a docs note on archive size.

I recommend A. It keeps today's recovery coverage, matches the ClawSweeper recommendation on the issue, and
follows the existing opt-in `--exclude-worktree-templates` flag (#190822). If you prefer B, the same matcher and
reporting work with the default flipped.

## What Problem This Solves

Full backup archives carry every retained Doctor original as raw bytes next to the live database snapshot.
That makes archives much larger and slower after each update, with no way to leave the originals out.

## User Impact

User impact: operators can run `openclaw backup create --exclude-migration-backups` to leave Doctor's retained
pre-migration originals out of an archive. Each omitted file is listed as `excluded`. Archives made without the
flag are unchanged.

A restored archive made with the flag cannot roll back the last migration with those originals. The docs say
so. The flag never deletes or changes the originals on disk; `openclaw update cleanup` still owns their
retention.

## Why This Change Was Made

- The flag matches only Doctor's exact producer names, `<database>.pre-startup-migration-<uuid>.bak` and
  `<database>.pre-startup-migration-<uuid>.scoped.bak`, beside the shared state database and each registered
  agent database. Look-alike names, other `.bak` files, `.postgres.bak` export directories and session-store
  recovery copies stay included.
- The exclusion goes through the backup resource plan, like `--exclude-worktree-templates`. Each omitted file
  appears in `skipped` (kind `migration backup`, reason `excluded`) in the dry-run plan, the text and JSON
  output, and the archive manifest. The reason is not `regenerable`, because these files are recovery
  artifacts.
- The name rule was inline in the migration manifest's restore check. It is now one exported predicate that
  the manifest and backup planning share, so backup cannot drift from what Doctor and update cleanup
  recognize.
- `docs/cli/backup.md` documents the flag and its rollback tradeoff. `repair-and-recovery.md` points to it.

## Evidence

**Shipped CLI, real Doctor originals.** On an isolated state directory, OpenClaw 2026.11.1 (latest stable)
created two agents. Current main's `openclaw doctor --fix` then migrated the databases (agent schema 27 to 41,
state 22 to 39), which left three real originals: one agent `.bak`, one state `.bak` and one state `.scoped.bak`.
Each run below is `node openclaw.mjs backup create` from a `pnpm build` of that commit.

| Run | Members | Uncompressed bytes | Originals in archive | Compressed bytes |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| main, default `--verify` | 58 | 4,692,781 | 3 (2,158,592 bytes) | 159,413 |
| this PR, default `--verify` | 59 | 4,805,384 | 3 (2,158,592 bytes) | 176,928 |
| this PR, `--exclude-migration-backups --verify` | 56 | 2,647,516 | 0 | 134,042 |

- Main rejects the flag: `OpenClaw does not recognize option "--exclude-migration-backups"`.
- Default archives keep the same member names and sizes on main and on this PR. The one extra member on this PR,
  `state/openclaw.sqlite.seal`, is the state database's clean-close seal. It appeared on disk between the two
  runs and is unrelated to this change.
- On this PR, the default and flagged archives differ only by the three originals. The manifest grows by 724
  bytes for the three new `skipped` entries.
- Main and the default run each warn four times about SQLite files archived as opaque bytes, three of them for
  the originals. The flagged run keeps only the unrelated warning.
- `backup restore` of the flagged archive into a fresh target returns `ok: true` and
  `sqliteInventoryVerified: true`, and restores 56 entries with no `.pre-startup-migration` files. The restored
  agent and state databases pass `PRAGMA integrity_check` at `user_version` 41 and 39, the same as live.
- The three originals on disk have identical SHA-256 before and after all runs.

<details>
<summary>Text output with the flag</summary>

```
Skipped 7 paths:
- workspace: ~/.openclaw/workspace (missing)
- agent: ~/.openclaw/agents/work/agent (covered by ~/.openclaw)
- plugin skills: ~/.openclaw/plugin-skills (regenerable)
- managed state: ~/.openclaw/tmp (regenerable)
- migration backup: ~/.openclaw/agents/work/agent/openclaw-agent.sqlite.pre-startup-migration-575fa006-78d6-861b-8b22-2d62c7a52f3c.bak (excluded)
- migration backup: ~/.openclaw/state/openclaw.sqlite.pre-startup-migration-575fa006-78d6-861b-8b22-2d62c7a52f3c.bak (excluded)
- migration backup: ~/.openclaw/state/openclaw.sqlite.pre-startup-migration-aa5e7499-c95e-4e0f-a82c-379b91b423d6.scoped.bak (excluded)
```

</details>

**Regression test** (`src/infra/backup-create.ownership.test.ts`, "backup Doctor migration originals"): a
default archive contains full and scoped agent originals and a full state original. A flagged archive omits
exactly those, keeps look-alike names, lists each as `excluded` in the result and manifest, restores, and leaves
the originals on disk. It fails on main (`expected true to be false` on the first flagged archive member check)
and passes with this change. It builds two real archives with `--verify` and restores one: 7.5 s on a
quiet machine, 14.3 s under heavy load (`pnpm test src/infra/backup-create.ownership.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`:
15 passed).

**Checks run**

- `pnpm test src/infra/backup-create.ownership.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`: 15 passed.
- Consumers of the changed plan, manifest predicate and CLI: `backup-resource-inventory`, `backup-shared`,
  `register.backup.product-path`, `register.backup.offsite`, `backup.create-verify`,
  `backup-verify-completeness`, `backup-create.worktrees`, `doctor-migration-backup`,
  `update-command-missing-originals`, `doctor-session-sqlite-recovery-inventory`, `doctor-session-entry-state`:
  all passed.
- `pnpm check:test-lines-ratchet`: OK. This PR adds an 83-line allocation for the regression, like the record
  for `--exclude-worktree-templates`.
- `pnpm check:changed`: formatting, core and test typechecks, lint, line caps, import cycles and the other guards
  pass. Two checks fail identically on main without this change: `changelog attributions`
  (`CHANGELOG/records/2026.6.8.md`) and the dead export scan (`parseDarwinProcessBirths` in
  `src/process/command-reservation-census.ts`, plus `scripts/lib/control-ui-gesture-probe.ts`). Neither file is
  touched by this PR.

Not covered: PostgreSQL-backed stores (Doctor writes `.postgres.bak` directories there, which this flag does
not touch) and Windows.

prs.title: fix: avoid slow follow-ups from native rollout size rotation
prs.body:
Related: #175256

## Summary

Avoid needless history rebuilding on ordinary Codex follow-ups when the saved native rollout is large but its active context is safe.

## What Problem This Solves

A long-running conversation waited about 91 seconds before accepting a follow-up. OpenClaw rotated the existing native thread because its append-only rollout exceeded `maxActiveTranscriptBytes`, then rebuilt history and synchronously compacted the host mirror. Saved rollout size includes old and compacted records; it is not the current model input size.

## User Impact

Ordinary follow-ups retain the reusable native thread when saved-log bytes are the only pressure. This avoids that replacement's history import and seed preparation. Native token-pressure recovery and legitimate fresh-thread bounded seeding remain in place.

No new setting, schema, retention policy, deletion, or deployment. No measured latency, cache-hit, or cost improvement is claimed.

## Why This Change Was Made

Remove the competing saved-byte rotation decision rather than add another threshold or cache. Preserve safe-path/file-descriptor checks, the token snapshot reader, projected-turn and reserve calculations, authority checks, and the supervised-thread exception.

The regression coverage exercises a native-compacted rollout above 2 MB through the production startup caller, both with and without a context engine. Connection-policy and abort-listener tests now trigger real token pressure rather than the removed saved-byte trigger. The 98-line test allocation is the exact net regression growth; the shared baseline is unchanged.

A separate, explicitly approved 43-line allocation reconciles inherited test-budget debt. Upstream `dd2e7c34b037e052ae181634a7fb19c67e46f9be` already contained 6,571,220 test lines against a 6,571,177 ceiling. This is not additional test growth, a disabled check, or a production change.

Original implementation: @VACInc. Follow-up review and regression coverage: @roboclaw-bot, with @VACInc credited on the commits.

## Evidence

Final head: `e887efe6262fbc204e965f4b9ae7d63828ff6e51`.

- **Exact-head applicable CI is green:** [run 42438851049](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/42438851049), including the test-line ratchet, bundled-extension tests, production/test types, lint, security-fast, and `openclaw/ci-gate`. Unselected/skipped platform lanes are not claimed as executed.
- **102 focused tests passed:** startup 18, history lifecycle 19, overflow recovery 7, bounded host seed 18, and connection 40. Covers token/projected-input pressure, authority, supervised threads, custom home, safe-path discovery, bounded reads, genuine overflow recovery, and connection-policy/abort-listener cleanup.
- The saved-rollout regression fails against the parent implementation. The image-heavy lifecycle regression fails in both engine modes on the parent by creating `thread-selected-2` instead of retaining `thread-selected-1`; all 19 lifecycle cases pass with the candidate.
- Obsolete startup and connection expectations were reproduced before repair. Assertions were retained and moved to real token-pressure fixtures, not deleted to make CI pass.
- Focused type-aware lint, formatting, and `git diff --check` passed.
- `pnpm build:ci-artifacts` passed in **4m 37.3s** on unchanged production code. Advisory UI bundle-size warnings were not build failures. Final reconciliation changes allocation metadata only; it does not invalidate the build or runtime proof.
- Independent Codex review of the complete candidate, followed by fresh reviews of the image-regression and connection-repair deltas, found **no actionable P0–P3 concerns**. The final metadata-only reconciliation was checked against upstream counts and passed CI. Reviewers did not independently execute tests.
- Hosted ClawSweeper is **not claimed as approved**: its [exact-head generation run 42439032304](https://github.com/openclaw/clawsweeper/actions/runs/42439032304) failed with `codex_or_content_failure` and produced no published review artifact. The independent reviews above provide substitute review.

Tests ran in non-hydrated AWS leases with no instance-role credentials and temporary HOME directories. Initial runtime/test bytes were the original draft plus the reviewed test patch (SHA-256 `cf645f75fd37660ce0db9ba29e5e04dfbb06b4439f1ae463758e12e0dea4bdfe`). The final lifecycle file was separately hash-verified (`e600f9ba60fecf8dad1b08930634fe47b4b6f086c6d5f4fe14375624a57f724c`) and revalidated. The final connection patch was applied to exact head `ba3ca53`, tested in run `run_6d1762382e12756fbbd24cc586841f8e`, then committed as `88a166b7`; subsequent changes are allocation metadata only. No operator Gateway or private conversation was used as a fixture.

Measured file wall times including compilation/setup: startup 65.80 s, final history lifecycle 28.44 s, overflow 14.25 s, host seed 52.04 s, connection 81.49 s. In the preceding hosted run, the bundled-extension job took 173 s, production types 32 s, test types 100 s, and lint 203 s. Hosted values are whole-job elapsed time, not per-file runtime or billed compute. The lifecycle and connection suites exercise the production ownership boundary; compilation/setup dominates the connection wall time (individual cases complete in milliseconds to 3.4 s), so helper-only tests would miss the caller regressions.

### Image-heavy repeated compaction regression (#175256)

The earlier fix moved host byte-bound compaction to genuine fresh-thread seed consumption. This change preserves that owner and removes another route that unnecessarily forced the same seed work. With a compacted native rollout and host history containing over 2 MB of opaque image bytes, two ordinary follow-ups and a cold client resume keep the same native thread in both engine modes. They cause **zero additional bounded-seed preparations, zero selected-history injections, zero native compaction requests, and zero historical-media preparation calls**. The original fresh start still prepares one seed.

Existing bounded-seed media accounting and token-overflow tests remain passing; large *active* token pressure is not ignored. This is production-caller boundary proof with synthetic protocol I/O and opaque image data, not live decoder/provider or full Gateway restart proof. It cannot guarantee arbitrary image request sizes or eliminate legitimate native compaction.

### Remaining limitations

No live-provider/channel end-to-end run, full Gateway restart/plugin-refresh experiment, or interleaved before/after latency and token/cache benchmark was performed. The passing lifecycle tests are deterministic boundary proof, not those live experiments.

Native token pressure can still pause a turn. Large saved files still consume disk; this change does not reclaim logs. Missing or malformed token snapshots can require scanning older data; no new scan-time bound is introduced. Request-size protection is separate from active context: existing WebSocket/node transport bounds remain unchanged, and no new guarantee for arbitrary image-heavy requests is claimed. Retaining useful history may retain more active input tokens than a smaller replacement summary.

**No merge is authorized by this review task.**

<details>
<summary>Original incident and source investigation</summary>

Sanitized measurements from one real Codex app-server conversation:

| Event or measurement | Observed baseline |
| --- | --- |
| Message received | t=0 |
| Existing native rollout | 7,169,386 bytes (6.84 MiB) |
| Configured `maxActiveTranscriptBytes` | `2mb` (2,097,152 bytes) |
| Rotation diagnostic | `codex app-server native transcript exceeded active byte limit; starting a fresh thread` |
| Context-engine input | 559 messages |
| Native thread creation RPC | 29 ms |
| Total thread lifecycle preparation | 88,204 ms |
| History injection RPC within that lifecycle | 272 ms |
| Host compaction completed during preparation | 107,775 tokens before compaction |
| Turn accepted | approximately t=91 s |
| First assistant output | approximately t=94 s |
| Final answer / full dispatch completion | approximately t=110 s |

The 272 ms history injection must not be mistaken for the entire history-preparation cost: the asynchronous bootstrap callback runs before that measured RPC. Most of the approximately 88-second lifecycle gap surrounds bounded-seed preparation and host compaction. There is no finer profile proving how every millisecond inside that interval was spent.

The source chain is:

1. `extensions/codex/src/app-server/startup-binding.ts`: `rotateOversizedCodexAppServerStartupBinding` compares the full native rollout's filesystem size with `maxActiveTranscriptBytes` and clears the binding when it crosses the threshold. It runs before normal turn execution. The observed route did not meet the context-engine thread-bootstrap exemption.
2. `extensions/codex/src/app-server/context-engine-history.ts`: a replacement invokes the asynchronous `historyBootstrapItems` callback; only the subsequent `thread/inject_items` RPC has the `thread-start-seed-history` duration span.
3. `src/agents/harness/host-seed.ts`: `bindBoundedSeed` bounds imported history and attempts host compaction before omitting unsummarized history that does not fit. This path awaits `compactEmbeddedAgentSessionDirect` before handing the prepared history to Codex.
4. Codex owns the existing native thread's working history and native compaction. Its persisted rollout also contains older records and compaction records; total saved-file bytes are not the active model input. The inspected Codex dependency routes `thread/inject_items` through `request_processors/turn_processor.rs` to `inject_response_items`; rollout records are maintained by `codex-rs/rollout`. Recheck the actual installed Codex revision during live validation.

The incident runtime was OpenClaw 2026.11.1 at base `27ea834825c92c2f4a1de833bceb1a3b21a8de23`, with overlays #193550, #193775, and #193899. The byte-trigger owner and fresh-seed owner were unmodified by those overlays, and the same byte trigger was present on current upstream when this draft was prepared. #193550 also gates host compaction model requests, so its contribution to time *inside* the compaction interval is not independently isolated. #193775 changes access-program selection; #193899 changes model output-budget defaults. The proposal targets the evidenced unnecessary rotation, not every possible contributor to summarization latency. Private transcript identifiers, paths, message content, and screenshots are deliberately excluded.

</details>

prs.title: fix(agents): prefer the provider's explicit credential-recovery instruction
prs.body:
Closes #194809

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: a provider 401 that states its own credential recovery (OpenCode `api_key_expired`: "Create a new API key in OpenCode Console. Signing in will not renew it.") was answered with the generic `Re-authenticate with: openclaw models auth login --provider … --force` hint — an action the upstream error explicitly rules out, and one that cannot renew a stored API key at all.

## User Impact

User impact: when the classified failure carries an explicit credential-replacement instruction from the provider, the remediation hint surfaces that sentence instead of the re-auth command. Providers without such an instruction keep the existing re-auth hint unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

`buildFailoverRemediationHint` maps `reason: "auth"` to the provider's re-auth command unconditionally. Some credentials are stored API keys, not OAuth logins — for those, the provider's own error text is the actionable recovery. The hint now checks the classified error's raw provider message for an explicit key-replacement instruction and, when present, surfaces that sentence (extracted, length-capped) before falling back to the command.

## Evidence

- Two regressions in `failover-error.test.ts`: an OpenCode-shaped `api_key_expired` failure yields a hint containing the provider's "Create a new API key" sentence and NOT the re-auth command; a control without the instruction keeps the exact existing re-auth hint. `node scripts/test-projects.mts src/agents/failover-error.test.ts` — 57/57 passing.
- `pnpm check:changed`: all lanes pass except the pre-existing red lanes on current `main` untouched by this diff (`changelog attributions`, and the `dead export scan` flagging `extensions/google/provider-policy.ts`). The 22 added test lines have a matching `config/test-lines-allocations/auth-remediation-provider-instruction.txt` record.
- Not exercised: a live OpenCode provider with an expired key; the classified-failure unit tests stand in.

prs.title: fix(ui): scope agent session management and preserve owner filters
prs.body:
Depends on [#194755](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/194755); this branch is stacked on its `5adf1572` head. Scope changes are `4ab20e2e` and `56aed841`; current head `c82b75dc` integrates the exact upstream context used for validation.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes agent session management mixing chats from different agents and hiding the selected agent’s own conversations behind an implicit personal-owner filter.

## User Impact

Authenticated agent management starts at **All owners**, showing the selected agent’s authorized conversations. Saved owner filters remain active and intersect with that agent, including when the result is empty. Restricted guests keep the **Involving me** default.

## Why This Change Was Made

Retain the selected agent in every session-list query, including reads with an explicit owner. Preserve a saved owner choice when the current or bounded owner facet omits it, rather than silently replacing that choice. Agent switching, empty results, background refreshes, and reloads therefore retain the same intended query scope. The visible agent picker subscribes to the existing authorized roster inventory for unread badges and the latest conversation, then projects it through the selected agent and owner. This avoids depending on the sidebar cache that owner changes correctly retire; no cross-agent rows enter the sidebar.

This changes the initial presentation default, not the Gateway’s authorization: session membership still comes from the Gateway, and explicit owner selections remain supported.

## Evidence

- Synthetic baseline captures reproduce the problem: selecting Mentor A can show a Main conversation while omitting Mentor A’s student discussions.
- Final browser proof passed 5/5 (18.72 s wall): three selected-agent scenarios cover the default, an explicit human owner, and an explicit agent owner; two existing page-scope regressions also pass. Assertions cover query agent/owner intersection, switching to existing and empty agents, saved-owner retention, and reload without cross-agent rows.
- Owner/query/preference unit contracts passed 68/68 (1.12 s wall), including the guest-specific default. Scoped UI, E2E and component type checks, lint, formatting, and the test-line allocation check passed.
- Fresh independent review found no actionable P0–P2 defects. These are source-branch tests with a mocked Gateway and synthetic data.

- Broader CI exposed eight expectations for the old cross-agent/default-self behavior. Owner-specific tests now explicitly select that owner. The retained resume/unread assertions also found and verify the independent picker inventory fix. The seven affected/sibling test files pass 150/150 on the exact merged head; the five browser cases and strict types also pass.
- Canonical performance against upstream `4cedec0f`: Chat boot 1,295,020 B (base 1,295,231 B; cap 1,295,248 B), New 802,413 B (base 802,603 B). Request counts remain 20/15; no budgets changed. Exact-head CI passed for `c82b75dc` (45 successful checks; 39 intentionally skipped checks).

**Mentor A selected in both captures**

| Before | After |
| --- | --- |
| ![Mentor view mixes Main chat and hides student conversations](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/c65f93dc-4e9f-43a6-948a-e0caf0b8fdcb) | ![Mentor view shows only its authorized owner and student conversations](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/4005d5a8-f2fe-4167-b13b-ea1140fe1fe6) |


### Follow-up: bounded agent inventory

At `bc2ffd8a2`, selecting an agent fetches an authorized, current agent-scoped session list with the selected owner filters rather than treating a bounded all-agent roster as complete. The result is discarded if connection, route, filter, selected agent, or latest click changes while the request is in flight. Request failure leaves the current selection in place and shows an error. Regression cases cover a truncated roster, inaccessible or deleted rows, request failure and a changed filter; 52 focused UI tests, `pnpm tsgo:ui`, targeted lint and the normal commit hook passed. Unread badges remain limited to the roster. The independent full pre-commit lint reported unrelated existing src/test errors; these tests use synthetic Gateway responses, not an installed live Gateway.


### CI follow-up

At `9b64b0d65`, picker code is lazy-loaded with intent and connection checks before and after loading. Madge reports no import cycles; seven bundled-browser cases, including the four previously failing scope/pagination scenarios, and 53 unit cases pass. `tsgo:ui`, targeted lint and line-cap checks pass. Against upstream `13ab261c`, the independently checked test-line ratchet passed without a new allocation. The integrated branch measured chat boot -212 B and New Session +3 B gzip, below their existing budgets; this is not a substitute for exact-head CI or performance-owner review.


### Final CI repair

At `9b69e34af`, the lazy loader uses Solid `lazyModule` and passes the Control UI controller guard without exceptions. Tests now await the actual agent selection and rendered state: 172 focused unit cases, three browser cases and seven E2E cases passed; typecheck, targeted lint, import-cycle and line-cap checks passed. A 239-line allocation matches the added behavioral tests on exact CI merge `9a82300` and base `74e1ecf`; the ratchet passes with no spare lines. The integrated deterministic build against `13ab261c` measured chat +128 B gzip (8 B under cap) and New Session +214 B; performance-owner evaluation is still required. Exact-head CI is pending.

prs.title: fix: recover releases from authenticated original receipts
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes release publication recovery when the original qualification parent failed to retain its final plan but its original admission, successful child receipts, and exact publication artifacts remain available.

## User Impact

Release operators can recover an already-qualified beta without rebuilding its artifacts or rerunning its successful qualification. This does not change the candidate or relax historical-plan verification.

## Why This Change Was Made

A separate read-authorized recovery workflow authenticates the original admission, required jobs and dispatches, child attempts, producer identities, and complete artifact digests, then records a new publication admission under trusted main tooling. Existing publisher consumers retain the original candidate and producer identities. Large binary archives are hashed as bounded streams; buffered ZIP limits remain unchanged.

The original failed parent is not relabeled successful, and its unavailable plan is not reconstructed. Original producer success and current operator authority remain required.

## Evidence

Open for review with remote-only validation underway. Local tests, builds, installs and preflight are prohibited for this release task and were not run.

- Original beta.2 five-child dispatch bindings and green child evidence authenticated separately; normal CI includes 12 attempts and 246 composite workload jobs.
- Original tested core tarball and qualified npm package match SHA-256 `f91397ac62deabc724bcc2a368e17a78b0680b236401d67258af3736c068dae2`.
- Static diff inspection caught the initial 256 MiB binary-buffer limit; streaming repair authored for the 402,006,833-byte shared image and retained approximately 1.8 GB Docker archives. Actual retained-payload streaming and successful aggregate/consumer authentication remain pending; rejection tests do not establish those success paths.
- Independent source review covered the full change and subsequent repair deltas. The prior approval of dispatch ordering was withdrawn after remote CI exposed a real regression; the corrected one-file delta received fresh independent review with no actionable findings. The earlier escape concern was a nested-output display error; direct source-byte inspection confirmed the literals are correct. Author simplification removed the unused download injection.
- Reviewed base `465c110e4975690406b48709d58a581756c85b82`; original committed head `92f7e230a303d0a59ce44579210d1f2ee2d38b73`. Local review-helper execution was unavailable; this narrative independent review is not a helper machine verdict.
- Initial CI exposed unpinned workflow actions and omitted explicit cache policy. Repair `933ac94c974b0b9528bb626fc45aaaea2b476df5` reused canonical sibling pins and retained `cache-mode: off`. Its formerly failing compact-small check passed on prior head `17ddd0d1d1fd8702ce415700122c2ffa433ff8aa`; that is prior-head evidence only.
- Further CI exposed formatting/lint, recovery return-type inference, declaration/fixture contracts, and mock-export completeness failures. Reviewed repair `d36a827691a1ffe5a6caba61d14fb692d10da1d5` addressed them; published head `a4fb9dcfdf7f1970a43c7b56a770b34e4c4f1315` had its identical tree `2c4329a121660c93e06af0da95a1514f6fbabc71`.
- On that prior head, run `42527106336` passed baseline-ratchets (job `128873506739`), guards (`128873506965`), and production types (`128873789049`). The earlier 177-line budget debt is historical; no exception or grant was needed in this observed run. The allocation remains exactly 572 own net regression-test lines, with shared scalar and guards unchanged.
- Repair `9d8464b542224a75c85cb701d8d13026f97ca414` awaited readiness checks and both dispatch callers and supplied the missing `expectDefined` context. The type diagnostic was at `expectDefined`, not `validateFullReleaseNpmPreflight`. No dedicated deferred/rejected async regression was added; this remains a proof gap.
- Its published head `bcb87d193902936864982fb91e551f53c91389b6` failed the existing real candidate CLI authority-revocation regression in run `42527858862`, compact-small-5 job `128875897615`: a tooling lookup after the authority check revoked permission, but POST still occurred (exit 0 instead of 1). This was a patch-introduced ordering defect, not a flaky test. The test remains unchanged.
- Corrective commit `7bd3cf74cd32d6cabc9f55871d57000d0e13d8a7` restores tooling/source reads -> await final live operator authority -> POST, preserving async propagation and persisted no-retry intent. Published head `4d0693b5f14dee80d5d62b14b067bf5a284529a3` has its reviewed tree `b3609d308cc498483495d4848b2c4c7d8358c2b9`. Current-head CI is pending; the prior failure is not yet proven repaired by execution.
- The parent reports lint, core3 types, production types, and baseline gates passing at prior head `bcb87d193902936864982fb91e551f53c91389b6`; those are prior-head evidence only. The unchanged core5 `chat-history-legacy-refusal-notice` test failure at line 46 was attributed to `map(readRunFailureNotice)` on main `0d4c07fb`, introduced by `86cb0bde` (#188553): its optional second options argument receives the map index. This PR changes neither that test nor its owner; it is inherited and not repaired here.
- `git diff --check` passed on the inspected snapshots. Static review is not runtime proof or successful real aggregate authentication.

Remaining tooling CI and successful owner-boundary execution will be recorded before release publication. Landing retains the applicable CI/review gates. No recovery dispatch or release publication has occurred.

After release consumers and closeout finish, review removal of the one-off recovery producer/workflow and simplify retained support. Preserve verifiability of issued receipts rather than blindly reverting their reader.

prs.title: fix(plugins): plugins init prints "Created ../../.." for a project directory outside the launch directory
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: `openclaw plugins init <id> --directory <path>` reports the new project as a chain of parent references when the directory is outside the launch directory, for example `Created ../../../../../private/tmp/demo/demo-plugin` when run from a repository checkout. `plugins build` prints its `Wrote` / `Updated` lines the same way.

## User Impact

User impact: paths outside the launch directory are printed as given (absolute), paths inside it stay relative (`Created plugins-scratch/inside-plugin`), and the launch-directory-removed case still prints the absolute path. No other output changes.

## Why This Change Was Made

`formatCwdRelativePathOrAbsolute` always returned `path.relative(cwd, target)`, which for a target outside the launch directory is `..`-prefixed and harder to read or paste than the path the operator typed. It now keeps the relative form only when the target is inside the launch directory, otherwise the absolute target, and keeps the existing fallback when `process.cwd()` is unavailable.

## Evidence

From source on `main` at 826999cd5f, macOS, Node 26.7.0, run from the repository checkout.

Before:
```
$ openclaw plugins init demo-plugin --directory /private/tmp/ocp3-j3l6/demo-plugin
Created ../../../../../private/tmp/ocp3-j3l6/demo-plugin
```

After (same build plus this change):
```
$ openclaw plugins init demo-plugin --directory /private/tmp/ocpi-XXXX/demo-plugin
Created /private/tmp/ocpi-XXXX/demo-plugin
$ openclaw plugins init inside-plugin --directory ./plugins-scratch/inside-plugin
Created plugins-scratch/inside-plugin
```

Tests:
- `pnpm test src/infra/safe-cwd.test.ts src/cli/plugins-authoring-command.test.ts`: 36 passed (the existing "finishes init with an absolute directory after the launch directory is removed" case is unchanged).
- New `src/infra/safe-cwd.test.ts`: inside-cwd paths stay relative, the cwd itself uses the fallback, outside paths (a sibling directory and the parent) come back absolute, and a missing launch directory keeps the absolute path. The two outside-path cases fail on `main` (`expected '../elsewhere/demo' to be '/work/elsewhere/demo'`) and pass with the change.
- Test-line budget: 23 added lines, allocated in `config/test-lines-allocations/plugins-init-created-path.txt`.
- `pnpm tsgo:core`, `oxfmt --check` and `oxlint --type-aware` on both files: clean.

Local autoreview / local ClawSweeper were not run.

prs.title: fix(sandbox): prevent full-blob history downloads during commit fetches
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes multi-gigabyte history downloads when an agent fetches commits from the selected GitHub repository inside a fresh shallow sandbox checkout.

## User Impact

New projections fetch commit/tree history without historical blobs, retrieving file contents when checkout or diff needs them. Sandbox object-store and credential isolation are preserved. Existing projections, other hosts/forks, and other URL spellings still need explicit `--depth` or `--filter=blob:none`; the sandbox workspace documentation explains this.

## Why This Change Was Made

Git applies partial-clone defaults by the supplied remote **name**: configuring `origin` alone does not affect `git fetch https://…`. The checkout owner now reconstructs a credential-free GitHub HTTPS address and configures `origin` plus its URL spellings with/without `.git`. Projections cloned from older dependency templates acquire the defaults before admission. Native Git replaces the selected origin URL and all six filter keys idempotently; URL-named defaults use Git’s native no-URL configuration shape. Template creation followed by projection initialization leaves exactly one section and one value per key for each selected remote name. Git-fetch advice stays in workspace documentation; the publication tool description is unchanged from main. Template keys, source packing, and the existing managed PR preparation/publication path are unchanged. No new cache, database schema, or user configuration option.

Read-only host alternates would still reveal private host objects and are deliberately not used. Managed `prepare_pr` remains the existing route for eligible PR continuation; it is not replaced by an arbitrary-ref broker.

## Evidence

The real checkout owner seeded a projection at `465c110e4975690406b48709d58a581756c85b82`. Fetching the three full commit IDs beginning `c074824a27c9`, `eb377ac59e6c`, and `465c110e4975` from public GitHub produced:

| Metric | Before | After |
|---|---:|---:|
| Added unique objects | 1,510,437 | 761,253 |
| Added unique blobs | 749,184 | 0 |
| Added pack bytes | 6,053,612,130 | 269,611,497 |
| Fetch wall | 274.66 s | 33.34 s |
| Client CPU | 278.38 s | 53.70 s |
| Peak RSS | 1,126 MB | 252 MB |

One network sample per arm; no p95 claim. Subsequent status/diff/log/checkout/edit/commit passed. On-demand hydration increased that inspection from 45.58 to 81.35 seconds, while combined fetch+inspection fell from 320.24 to 114.69 seconds. Final pack storage after inspection was 6.26 GB versus 620 MB.

A committed synthetic generator reproduces 62,000 files / 1.181 GB current source and 1,567,271 Git objects. Acceptance: zero added historical blobs, lower pack bytes, working status/diff/log/checkout/commit. A/A controls returned identical counts and 36.70/37.73-second fetches. Five fresh, interleaved A/B pairs returned identical counts per arm:

| Synthetic metric | Before | After |
|---|---:|---:|
| Added objects / blobs | 1,504,268 / 751,003 | 753,265 / 0 |
| Added pack bytes | 742,587,253 | 73,104,100 |
| Fetch wall median / p95 | 39.46 / 45.91 s | 15.90 / 22.63 s |
| Total local Git CPU median | 60.78 s | 57.76 s |
| Peak RSS median | 1,301 MB | 530 MB |

Local transport includes both upload-pack and fetch CPU. Fresh checkouts, warm filesystem cache, macOS/APFS; btrfs/Podman and agent-database scale are not qualified. The measured owner/fetch flow does not open agent/session databases. No production data was used.

Reproduce with `python3 scripts/perf/sandbox-projection-fetch-fixture.py --output <new-directory>`, then use its `fixture.json` values with `node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs scripts/perf/sandbox-projection-fetch-measure.ts`; the header documents baseline, interleaving, frozen-owner and allocation options.

Five instrumented old/new owner pairs at the initial PR head `fc469967` used the frozen original owner with unchanged dependencies. Owner wall median/p95 was 23.78/37.29 → 25.27/57.97 s; main-isolate CPU median 671.7 → 685.0 ms; sampled allocation median 38.98 → 38.75 MB. No checkout-preparation speedup claimed; these preparation-cost samples predate the idempotency revision, which replaces all seven keys through native Git. They are retained as prior-head evidence, not new-head preparation timings. There is no per-turn work. Shared-host load and separate allocation instrumentation limit timing precision.

The regression fails on the original owner because an obsolete blob is downloaded. Current focused checkout/template proof: 18 tests pass; the unchanged GitHub tool and prefix-stability suites previously passed 28 and 14 tests respectively. Existing workspace/PR-preparation cases: 128 passed, 2 existing skips. Existing original-PR publication tests: 20 passed, using synthetic transport with real Git/custody/receipts; no live GitHub publish is claimed. The initial old-template test was moved to the existing database-worker suite after its core-only fixture correctly refused broker admission. A prior combined runner was stopped by source-stability verification after an in-flight prompt edit; the affected final suites passed on stable source. The revised checkout/template run passes 17 tests, including unconfigured, same-origin and previous-origin templates. The same-origin regression applies configuration during template creation and again during projection initialization; it fails on `fc469967` with three origin sections and passes with exactly one section and one value per key for each selected remote. An incomplete mocked Git result caught by typechecking was corrected.

Fresh Codex autoreview against `3b7e9c2ad537beda9d6974cadefac962b7d01cf4`: complete local change, P0–P2, no actionable findings. Production delta **+50 lines**, needed for safe URL-derived native Git defaults. Regression delta **+167 lines**, with a scoped allocation for real Git and older-template behavior. Most remaining additions are the requested reproducible fixture and measurement tooling.

`pnpm check:changed --base 465c110e4975690406b48709d58a581756c85b82 --timed` completed: all lanes passed except the corrected test-fixture type error and an inherited changelog-attribution failure. The complete core-test typecheck, final production typecheck and final format check pass after correction. The remaining 20 changelog-credit violations reproduce identically from an immutable source snapshot of the exact base. [#194364](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/194364), commit `266a7aa0fe69e2b5fe6445c4ceb1e15b5360c957`, introduced this specific failure set by expanding forbidden handles without updating the archived entries; its parent has none of these 20 violations (it fails on a different human-credit set addressed by that PR). This is a main-branch regression requiring separate repair, not ignored noise.

Lead-review revision: removed fetch advice from the publication tool description, made every Git-config write idempotent, and clarified retained-template behavior in workspace docs. Focused 59-test rerun and targeted lint/format pass. The test-line allocation covers exactly 167 net test lines added by this PR. Duplicate fetch verification was removed from the template tests; actual URL/origin fetch coverage remains in the checkout tests. No inherited debt is allocated. Current revision production and changed-test typechecks pass; fresh Codex P0–P2 autoreview is scoped-clean with no actionable findings.

CI follow-up: rebased onto `3b7e9c2ad537beda9d6974cadefac962b7d01cf4`, including the earlier core-test type fix and `826999cd` test-budget repair. The overlap with #195443 was resolved by preserving its retained-template checkout/reflog/repack sequence and applying fetch configuration afterward. Its refresh regression is included in the 18 passing focused tests. The allocation is exactly 167, matching the PR’s net test-line growth without inherited debt. `node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs scripts/check-test-lines-ratchet.mts --base origin/main --no-merge-base` passes with zero slack.

Environment-isolation follow-up: the source origin read and every destination config write now receive the checkout allowlist as both `baseEnv` and `env`, including fresh and retained-template paths. A real Git regression poisons ambient `GIT_DIR`, `GIT_WORK_TREE`, and `GIT_CONFIG_PARAMETERS`; it fails before this fix because the source config changes, and passes with the source config byte-identical and the intended destination origin configured. Windows/POSIX boundary tests now check the new config calls as well as init/checkout. Retained-template tests reject a forged ambient origin. The 18 focused tests, targeted lint/format, and exact-growth ratchet pass; production/changed-test typechecks and fresh full-PR Codex P0–P2 autoreview also pass.

prs.title: fix(config): stop auto-restoring hand-authored configs missing meta (#126806)
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Closes #126806.

A valid, schema-passing `openclaw.json` that an operator wrote by hand (or deployed via dotfiles/Ansible/Nix) — one without a `meta` block — was silently replaced by the previous `openclaw.json.bak` generation the next time any command loaded config, including read-only ones like `openclaw models list`. The operator's `update.channel` value and agent roster were dropped into a `openclaw.json.clobbered.<ts>` sidecar behind a single log line: recoverable, but not obvious.

## Why This Change Was Made

`loadConfig` runs suspicious-read recovery *after* validation succeeds, so the restore only ever applies to configs that validate cleanly. `missing-meta-vs-last-good` was on the recoverable-reason list, and OpenClaw's own writer always stamps `meta.lastTouchedVersion` — so a valid config lacking `meta` was, by construction, hand-authored, the exact file a silent revert hurts most. The write path already treats the identical signal as benign (`missing-meta-before-write` is only logged; `resolveConfigWriteBlockingReasons` does not block), so the read path was stricter than the write path and reverted on it.

The fix removes `missing-meta-vs-last-good` from `isRecoverableConfigReadSuspiciousReason` (`src/config/io.observe-recovery.ts`). A valid config is now left untouched on read; the independent observe path (`observeConfigSnapshot`) still records the anomaly as a warning (`Config observe anomaly: … (missing-meta-vs-last-good)`) — the "at most, a warning" the issue asks for. `gateway-mode-missing-vs-last-good` and `update-channel-only-root` stay recoverable because they describe genuinely clobbered shapes.

Two follow-up commits close the residual windows that first fix left open:

- `9637d635e2b` — once a metadata-free config has been *accepted* and recorded as the last-known-good baseline, a later suspicious read could still auto-restore an older `.bak` generation over the operator's accepted file. The recovery source-eligibility check refuses a `.bak` whose bytes differ from a hand-authored accepted baseline, so a revert to *older* bytes is blocked while a `.bak` holding the accepted bytes itself still restores.
- `40bf9d02050` — that skip still left a *recognized valid clobber* active when Gateway had promoted the accepted bytes to `${configPath}.last-good`. The read recovery path now prefers that retained payload, accepting it only when its bytes hash to the recorded accepted-baseline hash (`prepareLastGoodRecoverySource`); a recognized clobber is then repaired from the operator's own accepted config instead of staying active. When no hash-verified copy exists (no `.last-good`, or its bytes diverged), the skip remains fail-closed with an explicit unavailable-baseline warning (`Config auto-restore from backup skipped: … accepted baseline is hand-authored and no verified last-good copy exists`) — divergent bytes are never restored. The last-known-good promote/recover owner moves to its own module (`src/config/io.last-known-good.ts`) so the read path stays under the file-size budget.
- `634bab43c8e` (`40fac9dcfc3` adds docs only) — closes the two findings from that review. **Acceptance bookkeeping (P1):** both observers (`observeConfigSnapshot`/`observeConfigSnapshotSync`) advanced `lastKnownGood` only on completely clean reads, so the *accepted* warning-only read itself — the hand-authored edit — left the stale product-written fingerprint in place; a later recognized clobber then compared against that stale baseline, bypassed the hand-authored guard, and restored the pre-edit `.bak` over the live settings. A valid read whose anomalies are not recoverable now advances the baseline while the warning stays, with the recoverable/acceptance predicates owned in one place (`isAcceptedConfigRead` in `src/config/io.observe-suspicious.ts`). **Source selection before backup preparation (P2):** the `.last-good` branch sat behind `.bak` read/parse/prepare/`gateway.mode` checks, so a missing, unparsable, rejected, or gateway-mode-less `.bak` short-circuited recovery before the verified promoted payload was ever consulted. Selection now needs only the retained baseline's hash and runs before any source-specific preparation; `.bak` preparation runs only when `.bak` is the selected source.

## User Impact

Operators who hand-author or config-manage a valid `openclaw.json` without a `meta` block no longer have it silently reverted to an older `.bak` generation by a read-only command — neither on the metadata-only read itself, nor later when a clobbered shape arrives (Scenario F). The accepted read itself becomes the recorded baseline, so later recovery compares against the operator's bytes rather than the pre-edit generation. When Gateway has promoted their accepted config, a later recognized clobber is repaired from that exact accepted payload even when the `.bak` is missing, unreadable, or rejected (Scenario D); otherwise the clobber is left in place with an explicit warning instead of being silently reverted or silently ignored (Scenarios C/E). Configs that genuinely lost their `gateway.mode` or collapsed to an `update.channel`-only root are still auto-restored as before whenever the accepted baseline is a product-written config (Scenario B).

## Evidence

## risks
- **Removed recovery fallback for `missing-meta-vs-last-good`**: configs that previously auto-restored on missing-meta alone no longer do. This is the intended fix — those were almost exclusively hand-authored valid files; a genuine clobber that lost *only* `meta` while keeping every other field valid is near-impossible (corruption truncates/damages, it does not surgically strip `meta`), and even then the file still validates and is left flagged. The observe path still records the anomaly; `.bak`/`.clobbered` backups remain for manual restore.
- **Skip is fail-closed only when no verified copy exists**: with a recognized clobber and a metadata-free accepted baseline whose `.bak` differs, recovery now repairs from the hash-verified `.last-good` payload (Scenario D). Only when that payload is missing or diverged does the read leave the recognized clobber active with the explicit unavailable-baseline warning — the operator compares against the retained `.bak`/`.last-good`/`.clobbered` artifacts and restores manually, or rewrites the file. This trades one automatic repair for never restoring unverified bytes; the skip warns with the exact reason and the observe anomaly is still audited.
- **`.last-good` payload trust is hash-scoped**: the promoted payload is accepted only when its bytes hash to the recorded accepted-baseline fingerprint hash; a diverged `.last-good` (partial write, operator edit, tampering) is never restored (Scenario E). The fingerprint itself is Gateway-promoted state in the shared SQLite health store, so the trust boundary matches the existing last-known-good promotion contract rather than widening it.
- **`size-drop-vs-last-good` sibling**: the issue traces the same read-stricter-than-write asymmetry for size drops but did not reproduce it; the write side blocks `size-drop:` unless `allowConfigSizeDrop` is set, so it is a weaker case. Intentionally out of scope here — flagged for a separate change with its own reproduction.

## bestSolution
Removing `missing-meta-vs-last-good` from the recoverable-reason list at its owner (`isRecoverableConfigReadSuspiciousReason`), plus source eligibility that prefers the hash-verified promoted `.last-good` payload and otherwise fails closed with an explicit warning, is the canonical fix set: the observe path provides the warning, recognized clobbers are repaired from the operator's own accepted bytes whenever a verified copy exists, and recovery for the unverifiable state stays explicit instead of silently reverting or silently ignoring.






## Main rebase (head 718ae1765c4)

Resolved the merge conflicts flagged in the review against current main (which now includes the config deslop in #157146):

- `src/config/io.observe-suspicious.ts`: main's deslop removed `isRecoverableConfigReadSuspiciousReason` and made any suspicious reason trigger recovery (`suspicious.length === 0`). The merge restores this branch's policy — `missing-meta-vs-last-good` is excluded from auto-restore and drives the accepted-baseline advance instead — because reverting a valid hand-authored config is exactly the bug this PR fixes.
- `src/config/io.observe.ts`: kept the `isAcceptedConfigRead` import alongside main's move of `NormalizedConfigIoDeps` to `io.read.types.js`.
- `src/config/io.observe-recovery-effects.ts` / `io.last-good-recovery-source.ts`: follow main's `@openclaw/fs-safe/atomic` and `io.read.types.js` import locations.

Verified on the merged head: `tsgo` clean; the recovery suites (`io.observe-recovery.test.ts`, `io.observe-recovery.accepted-baseline.test.ts`, `io.health-state.test.ts`, `io.load-env-restore.test.ts`, `io.observe-freshness.test.ts`) — 109/109 pass. The remaining before-merge items are the maintainer decisions on the accepted-baseline fallback behavior, which the Scenario G / real-CLI evidence above documents.

prs.title: fix: crashed SQLite store worker leaves no reason in logs or metrics
prs.body:
<!--
Optional linked context:
Add a visible `Closes #<issue-number>` or `Related: #<issue-number>` line
below this comment.

Required PR title:
type: user-facing description
Use a parenthesized scope only when it adds clarity:

Types: feat, fix, improve, refactor, docs, chore.

fix: task list fails to load when user has no environments
Avoid implementation details such as:
fix: add null check to task query

**MUST:** Keep **Allow edits from maintainers** enabled for this PR so maintainers
can help update the branch when needed.
-->

Closes #163150

## What Problem This Solves

<!--
Describe the concrete user, product, or operational problem.
Use one short, plain-language sentence. For fixes, prefer:
"Fixes: <what goes wrong> when <trigger or condition>."
For other changes, describe the need without inventing a bug.
Name the affected workflow, not the code-level cause.
-->

Fixes: when a SQLite store worker thread disappears, the worker lifecycle counters call it an
unattributed `exit` and the Gateway log says nothing, so an operator cannot tell a crash from a
retirement the broker asked for.

## User Impact

<!--
"User impact: <what users, operators, or developers can now do or expect>."
Lead with the concrete outcome in plain language, usually one sentence.
For internal-only changes, say there is no user-visible change; do not invent a benefit.
Keep important risks, breaking changes, migrations, and required user actions visible here.
-->

User impact: a retirement the broker requested now shows its own reason (`closed`, or `failure`
when the slot had already failed) in the stability bundle's `workerLifecycle`, and a worker that
leaves without any request writes exactly one warning line naming its cause to the log file, so a
lost storage worker is diagnosable from the bundle and the log instead of only from a repro.

## Why This Change Was Made

<!--
Briefly explain how the change addresses the problem without repeating the impact.
Keep the body short. Leave file lists, internal acronyms, and root-cause walkthroughs
in the diff or optional <details>; include technical detail only when it explains
behavior or a material tradeoff. Do not hide risks or required actions in <details>.
-->

The lifecycle registry takes the retirement reason from whatever the worker's owner recorded
before native exit; without that record it falls back to `exit`, which
`docs/gateway/prometheus.md` already defines as "an owner did not specify a reason". The task-pool
owners do record it, the SQLite store worker owner never did, so every one of its retirements
landed in the fallback. Reasons are now recorded where this owner asks the worker to leave, and on
the `error`/`messageerror` events that precede native exit. A departure that no one requested has
no other witness, so it is logged once at warn; requested retirements stay silent because their
caller already reports the outcome. Nothing in the broker's failure path changed, and the log line
carries only the redacted error text.

## Evidence

<!--
Show the most useful proof that this change works. Screenshots, screencasts,
terminal output, focused tests, CI results, live observations, redacted logs,
and artifact links are all useful. For user-visible UI changes, follow the root
AGENTS.md "Product and validation" screenshot completion/landing gate; these other
forms of evidence do not replace the required screenshots in chat AND the PR.

Reviewers will inspect the code, tests, and CI. Use this section to make the
validation easy to understand, not to restate the diff.
Summarize what was checked and the result; note meaningful gaps. Link long output
or put it in optional <details>, keeping the useful evidence summary visible.
-->

Failing test first, then the fix, on `src/infra/sqlite-worker-broker-lifecycle.test.ts`:

```
 FAIL  src/infra/sqlite-worker-broker-lifecycle.test.ts > SQLite worker slots > attributes a broker-requested retirement instead of an unattributed exit
AssertionError: expected +0 to be 1
    207|       await lifecycle.retire(slot);
  >  209|       expect(retirementCount("closed")).toBe(closedBefore + 1);

 FAIL  src/infra/sqlite-worker-broker-lifecycle.test.ts > SQLite worker slots > reports a worker that leaves on its own once, naming its cause
AssertionError: expected +0 to be 1
  >  253|     expect(retirementCount("failure")).toBe(failureBefore + 1);
```

After the change the same two tests pass, and they check both halves of the symptom against the
real registry and the real log-file transport: a retirement the owner asked for adds a `closed`
count and leaves `exit` unchanged, and a worker that throws on its own adds a `failure` count while
the log file holds one `left without a retirement request` line containing the cause text.

```
 TEST  src/infra/sqlite-worker-broker-lifecycle.test.ts
 ... > attributes a broker-requested retirement instead of an unattributed exit 87ms
 ... > reports a worker that leaves on its own once, naming its cause 178ms
```

Adjacent lanes, run locally with the same config:

```
 src/infra/sqlite-worker-broker.test.ts   Tests 10 passed, Duration 42.94s
 src/infra/worker-cpu.test.ts             Tests 7 passed with sqlite-worker-logging.test.ts,
                                          Duration 20.95s
```

Local gates: `oxfmt --check` clean on both files (28ms), `run-oxlint.mjs` on the core tsconfig
reported "Found 0 warnings and 0 errors" (68.1s), `git diff --check` clean, and
`check-line-cap-ratchet.mts` reported "Line-cap ratchet OK: 2 changed source files; no new
violations or over-cap growth". `check-changed.mjs --dry-run` listed the CI gates this diff
selects. Pre-commit hooks ran normally; no hook was skipped.

Cost of the new tests, per the repo validation rules: they add 87ms and 178ms inside a file whose
targeted run takes 26s with a warm transform cache and 212s cold on this machine. Neither test
sleeps, polls, or uses a wall-clock timer; they await the worker `online` event, the slot's own
exit promise, and `flushLogger()`.

Gaps worth naming: the run was Windows, where the six pre-existing cases in this test file already
fail at `fileURLToPath("file:///openclaw/...")` with `ERR_INVALID_FILE_URL_PATH` before this
change and in code this diff does not touch, so those cases are covered here by CI's Linux infra
lane; the two new tests derive their carrier URL from `import.meta.url` so they run on both
platforms. `pnpm tsgo:core` refuses a worktree that shares its install with the main checkout
("Declaration input escapes checkout"), so the typecheck gate was not run locally and is left to
CI. No live Gateway was started on this machine; the log-line half is proven by reading the file
the file transport actually wrote.

CI on head `e129273e8` (server-recorded base `dbb580aed`, which is 171 commits behind current `main`): 129 check runs = 67 success / 59 skipped / 1 neutral (CodeQL) / 2 failure. The two failures are `checks-windows-node-test-5` (completed 2026-10-02T08:19:37Z) and the 2 s aggregate `openclaw/ci-gate` that follows it in the same run. The failing case is `test/scripts/write-unified-entry-dts.test.ts > write-unified-entry-dts > reuses unaffected canonical groups while rebuilding runtime after input edits`, and it throws `ERR_PACKAGE_PATH_NOT_EXPORTED: Package subpath './record-coerce' is not defined by "exports"` from a `package.json` inside that test's own temporary fixture project (`%TEMP%\oc-vt-8AAiWh\openclaw-sdk-declarations-5DFbNf\Project\node_modules\@openclaw\normalization-core`), imported from `src/process/exec-result.ts` in the same temp tree. This diff is two files, both `src/infra/sqlite-worker-broker-lifecycle.*`: it touches none of `test/scripts/`, `packages/normalization-core/`, or `src/process/`, and `packages/normalization-core/package.json` on this head does export `./record-coerce`.

What is deliberately not claimed here: inheritance is not proven. That node-id was re-run in a clean detached worktree checked out at this PR's base commit `dbb580aed`, and it fails there too - but with a different, Windows-only error while the fixture links its compiler (`EPERM: operation not permitted, symlink '..\typescript\bin\tsc' -> '...\Project\node_modules\.bin\tsgo'`), so this machine's harness cannot exercise that fixture path and no local verdict about the CI error is available. For reference, the same `checks-windows-node-test-5` check completed with `success` at 2026-10-02T15:23:03Z on unrelated head `5ce2d2d6` (#163594). No rerun, re-push, or rebase was dispatched to chase a green signal, per the repository's validation rules; naming this failure is offered so a maintainer can weigh it against the two lanes this change actually touches.

prs.title: fix(skills): skills commands refuse the configured system agent in a multi-agent fleet
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: in an explicit multi-agent roster with `agents.defaults.systemAgent.agentId` set, every workspace-backed `openclaw skills` command run without `--agent` (`skills`, `list`, `info`, `check`, `install`, `update`) fails with `Multiple agents are configured, but the skills command has no explicit owner. Pass --agent <id>.` The docs say these commands fall back to "the default agent", and `agents list` reports the system agent as that default (`isDefault: true`). `hooks list`, `sessions` and `models status` already use it on the same config.

## User Impact

User impact: `openclaw skills ...` without `--agent` now targets the configured system agent's workspace, like `hooks`. `--agent`, current-directory inference, and the failure for a fleet with no configured owner are unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

`resolveSkillsWorkspace` went straight from cwd inference to `resolveDefaultAgentId`, which only accepts raw legacy markers and otherwise requires a sole agent. It now checks `tryResolveLegacyCompatibilityAgentId` first, the same order `hooks-cli` uses for its report target (#123868). The two existing skills tests with closed `agent-scope` mocks get the new export: one gains an entry, the verify test now spreads the real module (its mock-exports baseline entry is pruned).

## Evidence

Built CLI from source, macOS, Node 26.7, offline, fresh state directory. Before: `main` at 465c110e49 (`skills-cli-gateway.ts` is unchanged since). After: this branch on 98fad049dc. Config:

```json
{"agents":{"ownership":"explicit","defaults":{"systemAgent":{"agentId":"ops"}},
  "entries":{"alpha":{"workspace":".../ws/alpha"},"ops":{"workspace":".../ws/ops"}}}}
```

Before:
```
$ openclaw skills check
Multiple agents are configured, but the skills command has no explicit owner. Pass --agent <id>.
$ echo $?
1
$ openclaw hooks list --json | jq -r .workspaceDir
.../ws/ops
```

After:
```
$ openclaw skills check
Skills Status Check
Agent: ops

Total: 56
✓ Eligible: 23
$ openclaw skills list --json | jq -r .workspaceDir
.../ws/ops
```
Without `systemAgent` the same two-agent roster still exits 1 with the existing `Pass --agent <id>.` message, before and after. `skills check --agent ops` is identical before and after.

Upgrade from latest stable, same state directory (macOS, Node 26.7, offline). The fleet above plus a workspace skill `ws/ops/skills/deploy-notes/SKILL.md`, first used with `openclaw@2026.11.2` from npm:

```
$ openclaw --version
OpenClaw 2026.11.2 (b556fdf)
$ openclaw skills check
Multiple agents are configured, but the skills command has no explicit owner. Pass --agent <id>.
$ echo $?
1
$ openclaw skills list --agent ops --json | jq -r .workspaceDir
.../ws/ops        # deploy-notes listed as openclaw-workspace
```

Then this branch (27b58cffb, merged with current main) on that state. Current main asks for `openclaw doctor --fix` first ("Client credential migration is incomplete or stale"), which is unrelated to this PR, so the run includes it:

```
$ openclaw doctor --fix --non-interactive
Doctor: database migrations
Doctor: legacy config migration
...
Doctor complete.
$ openclaw skills check
Skills Status Check
Agent: ops

Total: 57
✓ Eligible: 24
$ echo $?
0
$ openclaw skills info deploy-notes
deploy-notes ✓ Ready
$ openclaw skills list --json | jq -r .workspaceDir
.../ws/ops        # deploy-notes still listed
$ openclaw agents list --json | jq -c "[.[] | {id, isDefault}]"
[{"id":"alpha","isDefault":false},{"id":"ops","isDefault":true}]
```

The `agents` block of the config is unchanged after the upgrade (doctor only adds `meta`, `wizard` and `skills`), and the SKILL.md hash is unchanged (`31086cb0...`). The same upgraded state with `agents.defaults` removed still exits 1 with `Pass --agent <id>.`

Tests:
- New `src/cli/skills-cli-gateway.test.ts` runs the real resolver against the config above (only the config reader is mocked): it expects `ops` and its workspace, then expects the ownerless fleet to keep throwing. On `main` it fails with `AgentSelectionRequiredError: Multiple agents are configured, but the skills command has no explicit owner. Pass --agent <id>.`; it passes with the fix (2 ms test time).
- `pnpm test src/cli/skills-cli*.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` (8 files, 68 tests) and `pnpm test:extension skill-workshop` (135 tests, it reuses this resolver): pass.
- `pnpm tsgo:core`, `pnpm tsgo:core:test`, `oxfmt --check` and `oxlint --type-aware` on the touched files: clean. `pnpm check:test-mock-exports`: OK.
- Test-line budget: 31 added lines, allocated in `config/test-lines-allocations/skills-system-agent-owner.txt`. After merging current main (826999cd5 granted the inherited overage), `pnpm check:test-lines-ratchet --base origin/main` reports OK with 0 slack.

prs.title: fix: avatars and backgrounds fail on Tailscale-authenticated connections
prs.body:
Related: #182689, #188268, #162252

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: agent/user avatars and saved backgrounds fail to load when a same-origin Control UI connection authenticates through Tailscale but receives a device token rejected by the HTTP image route.

## User Impact

These images use the confirmed Tailscale identity without first presenting an incompatible Bearer credential. Other authentication methods and cross-origin connections retain their existing credential selection. Geolocation retains its ordinary Bearer credentials.

This is a bounded client image-read repair. It does not change server token issuance, revocation, pairing, scopes, rate limits, writes or explicit file-access approvals. Wider media/icon loaders remain in the separate #182689 discussion.

## Why This Change Was Made

Select image identity before sending the request, never by retrying an HTTP denial under a different identity. Reuse the Gateway owner's current-client/current-hello check and retire pending reads on disconnect/stop. Keep the background loader's profile, revision, cancellation, size and MIME checks.

### Review follow-up

- **Geolocation regression fixed:** the shared connection context now retains separate ordinary and image credential lists. Only image callers select image credentials. The new real geolocation-consumer test fails on the first revision and passes with this split. Its transport fixture calls the production HTTP authentication function, which requires a token for this non-image route.
- **Real image HTTP boundary evidence:** a managed-Tailscale Gateway server fixture serves agent avatars, user avatars and the current person's private background without Bearer. The same routes reject the invalid Bearer, and another profile's private background is denied. Only the external Tailscale whois response and image normalization are fixture-controlled, not the authorization decision.
- **Retirement evidence:** the actual registered background route withholds private bytes after role reduction or profile reassignment, for both managed Tailscale and trusted proxy. Existing actual avatar authority tests also cover role/alias changes before bytes are returned. No server permission broadening was added.
- **Owner decision still open:** this evidence supports the bounded selection, but does not grant the requested human authentication-owner approval or establish that a changed HTTP principal is the same identity as an earlier WebSocket hello. Review of the intended preselection/reassignment contract remains required.

## Evidence

Current repair head: `fc379be4db71ef198474964d63e0e8571530941e`.

- Refreshed onto upstream `826999cd5`. It includes the core test-type fix and missing upstream test allocation. The former was classified as pre-existing by the failed-check tool. This branch's allocation covers only its own 358 net TypeScript test lines.
- Original real-loader and production-bundled Chromium red/green evidence remains valid for the original failure. The first-revision geolocation regression independently reproduces (1 failed / 5 passed), then passes after the credential split.
- **254 focused tests passed across 11 files:** the final changed/affected UI and registered-background selection is 154/154, plus 100/100 in the actual avatar, agent-response and HTTP authentication suites. No full-repository test run is claimed.
- Targeted type-aware lint, UI production types, UI app/component and gateway-root test types, formatting, whitespace, the exact-base test-line ratchet and UI production build passed. Tested and publishing diffs match (`18b90d09596fc74a5bf913dd9bf788a8dcde036abbda86abff9449f2a2009c85`).
- The final production-bundled Chromium regression passed: one image request without Authorization and a decoded rendered image. This intercepts the network response, so it complements rather than replaces the separate actual HTTP authorization tests.
- Source tests ran on macOS / Node 24.22.1 with isolated synthetic state. The HTTP tests use the production registered routes, profile store and authorization code with a controlled external identity lookup. This is not a live Tailscale daemon/proxy test or native companion acceptance test.
- Direct author review and `pr-simplify` completed. Narrowed the helper name to image authentication and retained the existing connection/cache owners. Whole diff versus refreshed base: production +63/-23, tests +375/-17. No generic post-denial identity fallback or new credential persistence was added. No independent local reviewer is claimed. Current-head CI and human security review remain required.

### Before

The synthetic agent image is rejected and the existing mascot fallback renders.

![Before: mascot fallback instead of the configured synthetic avatar](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/e4d79444-98e9-475a-b2fb-05b040e3fa36)

### After

The same synthetic image renders as a teal avatar. No user photos, real credentials, or production data are present in either capture.

![After: the synthetic teal avatar renders through the confirmed identity](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/b6ff49bf-314b-44db-aeed-518252a6c77c)
