prs.title: fix(ui): stop incoming replies from overriding PageUp
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes Chat pulling a reader back to the bottom when they press PageUp during a tool-heavy reply.

## User Impact

Upward navigation takes control immediately, so incoming output cannot restart following before the browser moves the viewport. PageDown, returning to the bottom, and neutral pointer/touch contact preserve their existing behavior. No protocol or layout changes.

## Why This Change Was Made

The input observer already knows which direction an accepted key requests. Preserve that direction through the existing pane scroll owner, and lock following on upward intent rather than waiting for a native scroll event. This is the isolated correctness fix from #195034; the broader performance candidate remains unlanded.

## Evidence

| Proof | Result |
| --- | --- |
| Regression on current main (`75c2c49cec2`) | PageUp, ArrowUp, Home and Shift-Space fail before native movement; downward/pointer controls pass |
| Focused ownership, offset observer and scroll suites | 80 passed; 2.02 s total |
| UI typecheck, scoped lint, format, production Knip | Passed |
| Independent review and simplify pass | No actionable P0–P2 findings |
| Production 200-tool correctness | Chromium 4× and Firefox pass; exact ordered results, completion, final visibility and no blank scroll frames |
| Ordinary-scroll smoke | Chromium and Firefox base/fix pass; native scrolling stays complete with no blank frames (Chromium fix 16.7 ms frame p95, Firefox base/fix 16.68 ms; smoke only) |
| Same-machine strict normalized gzip | Startup 90,867 → 90,867 B; Chat 1,296,951 → 1,296,952 B; New 802,978 → 802,959 B; CSS requests 1 → 1; zero violations against base |
| DOM mutation records, completed 200-tool fix | Chromium 4×: 59,747; Firefox: 60,401; no mutation storm |

WebKit is unavailable due to the host WindowServer failure. The current-main Chromium 4× run failed the PageUp-away assertion; current-main Firefox timed out at final visibility after all 200 results. Both complete on this isolated fix. These bounded runs establish correctness, not a timing improvement or an isolated cause for the earlier Firefox failures. Chromium also crashed while opening a later context (display-link errors/native signal); that host failure is retained separately from the product assertions.

Production LOC across the three touched owners: 1,057 → 1,063 (+6). Regression test: 554 → 578 (+24), covered by an exact 24-line allocation. Main separately recorded its old test-line debt; after merging that change, the ratchet passes at 6,586,765 lines / 6,586,765 ceiling with zero slack. Refactor checklist counts for controllers, effects, render effects, untrack, direct listeners/queries, flush and owner APIs remain zero in these owners. No appearance change, so behavioral assertions are the proof.


### Synthetic Firefox end-of-flow captures

The baseline run stops short of the final reply; the fixed run completes the same scripted flow. These are outcome captures, not a layout redesign. Both full captures were inspected: synthetic content only.

![Baseline: final reply remains below the viewport](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/bd892cc5-7eda-4998-a205-0e0afc09f32d)

![Fixed: final reply is visible](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/34021d04-2b36-427d-b5f8-cb9229b9cd34)

### Final CI qualification

prs.title: fix(android): preserve pre-ack steer ownership across idle recovery snapshots
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

When a user sends a follow-up/steer message while an active chat turn is streaming (`pendingSendCount > 0`), `ChatController` clears `pendingRunCount` and schedules `resolveStreamingRunAfterSendAck(...)` to reconcile the run once the `chat.send` ACK arrives.

If a gateway reconnect or recovery snapshot (`chat.history` / `sessions.get`) arrives with `status: "idle"` *before* that `chat.send` ACK returns, `reconcileActiveRunFromHistory(...)` previously saw `pendingRunCount.get() == 0` and immediately cleared `streamingRunId`, `streamingAssistantText`, and `pendingToolSummaries`, retiring active-turn ownership while the steer request was still in flight. Moreover, if the connection dropped before the steer ACK arrived, `reconcileOutboxAfterGatewayConnect(...)` had already cleared the outbox's `activeRunId` during the pre-ACK idle snapshot, causing the original request to lose its run association.

## Changes

- Track `pendingSendAckCount` alongside `pendingRunCount` in `ChatController.kt` while `sendMessage(...)` awaits `node.request("chat.send", ...)` (and decrement it in `finally` before `resolveStreamingRunAfterSendAck` runs).
- Guard `reconcileActiveRunFromHistory(...)` (`ChatController.kt`) on `pendingRunCount.get() == 0 && pendingSendAckCount.get() == 0` so an idle recovery snapshot arriving before the steer ACK settles does not prematurely clear active streaming state or outbox run ownership unless the user explicitly cancelled/aborted the run.
- Add `ChatControllerSteeringRecoveryTest` covering:
  - `idleRecoveryWhileSteerAckIsPendingKeepsStreamingOwnership`
  - `reconnectBeforeLostSteerAckSettlesPreservesOriginalRequestWithoutReplay`
  - `explicitSteerCancellationBeforeAckStillRetiresOwnership` (opposite control)

## Evidence

- **Base RED** (`a8f192372c39ea7e0adc15d55b3dd3adde60a141`):
  - `./gradlew :app:testPlayDebugUnitTest --tests "ai.openclaw.app.chat.ChatControllerSteeringRecoveryTest"` -> `idleRecoveryWhileSteerAckIsPendingKeepsStreamingOwnership FAILED`, `reconnectBeforeLostSteerAckSettlesPreservesOriginalRequestWithoutReplay FAILED` (`explicitSteerCancellationBeforeAckStillRetiresOwnership` passed).
- **Fix GREEN** (`c5669885f77cd5324f62286f2b5386b015abc693`):
  - `./gradlew :app:testPlayDebugUnitTest --tests "ai.openclaw.app.chat.ChatControllerSteeringRecoveryTest" :app:ktlintCheck :app:assemblePlayDebug` -> `BUILD SUCCESSFUL` (`3 tests, 0 failed`).
- **Physical device:** being re-run on two physical Android 17 Pixels (Pixel 10 Pro XL and Pixel 10 Pro Fold) against an isolated Gateway, red on `main` and green on this head, for (1) an idle recovery snapshot that arrives before a steer's `chat.send` ACK and (2) a reconnect with a lost ACK and no duplicate `chat.send`. Results will be added here. The earlier one-line device note couldn't be traced to a reproducible run, so it has been replaced.

prs.title: fix(models): models list --provider prints only "The CLI command failed." for an unknown provider when the Gateway is down
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: `openclaw models list --provider <id>` with an unknown provider id prints only `The CLI command failed. For help, run openclaw doctor.` when the Gateway is not running. The reason, `Unknown model catalog provider "<id>". Run openclaw models list --all to list models and their provider IDs.`, was only visible with `--json`, or when a Gateway was up to answer the request.

## User Impact

User impact: the offline local-catalog path now prints the same unknown-provider message the Gateway path and `--json` already print, with the same exit code 1. Valid provider filters, `--refresh`, and JSON output are unchanged; no new wording.

## Why This Change Was Made

Without a Gateway, `models list` builds the result locally with the same `buildModelsListResult` the Gateway uses, which throws `UnknownModelCatalogProviderError` for an unknown filter. The Gateway method maps that class to an `INVALID_REQUEST` error that the CLI prints, but the local read let it escape as a plain `Error`, which the CLI's failure handler replaces with the generic line in human output. The local read now rethrows it as an `ExpectedCliError` carrying the same message, like the existing invalid-filter check in the same command.

## Evidence

From source on `main` at c1e55e24b3, macOS, Node 26.7.0, fresh state directory, no Gateway running.

Before:
```
$ openclaw models list --provider nope
Gateway is not running. Showing the local cached model catalog. Use --refresh to discover provider models.
[openclaw] The CLI command failed.
[openclaw] For help, run `openclaw doctor`.
$ openclaw models list --provider nope --json   # the reason was only visible here
{ "ok": false, "error": { "type": "cli_error", "message": "Unknown model catalog provider \"nope\". Run openclaw models list --all to list models and their provider IDs." } }
```

After (same build plus this change):
```
$ openclaw models list --provider nope
Gateway is not running. Showing the local cached model catalog. Use --refresh to discover provider models.
Unknown model catalog provider "nope". Run openclaw models list --all to list models and their provider IDs.
$ openclaw models list --provider nope --json   # unchanged document, same message
{ "ok": false, "error": { "type": "cli_error", "message": "Unknown model catalog provider \"nope\". Run openclaw models list --all to list models and their provider IDs." } }
$ openclaw models list --provider anthropic   # valid filters unchanged
Model                                      Input      Ctx         Local Auth  Tags
anthropic/claude-sonnet-5-5                text+image 1000k       no    -     default,configured
...
```
Exit 1 for the unknown provider in both modes, as before.

Tests:
- `pnpm test src/commands/models/list.prepared-catalog.test.ts`: 17 passed.
- New case "names an unknown provider filter from the local catalog" (refresh=false and refresh=true) asserts the rejection is an `ExpectedCliError` whose human and machine output are the unknown-provider message and that no Gateway call is made. Both fail on `main` (`expected Error: Unknown model catalog provider "no… to match object { name: 'ExpectedCliError', …}`) and pass with the change. The existing process test for the `--json` document (`help-exit.process.test.ts`) keeps its canonical-JSON and exit-status checks; its stderr assertion now expects the provider diagnostic instead of the generic line for both the routed and Commander cases (4 passed, 34 s for the routed unknown-provider case on this Mac).
- Test-line budget: 15 added lines, allocated in `config/test-lines-allocations/models-list-unknown-provider-local.txt`.
- `pnpm tsgo:core`, `oxfmt --check` and `oxlint --type-aware` on both files: clean.

Local autoreview / local ClawSweeper were not run.

prs.title: docs(android): note the background presence beacon throttle
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Someone checking whether their phone reports in after they background the OpenClaw app sees the paired node's `lastSeenReason` stay at `connect`, with no `background` update. Going by today's docs, which say Android sends a beacon "when the app moves to the background", that looks like a broken background beacon or a phone that stopped reporting. They may then go hunting through battery, notification or foreground-service settings for a problem that doesn't exist.

The app is working as designed: it skips the background beacon while the last recorded beacon is less than 10 minutes old (`NodePresenceAliveBeacon.MIN_SUCCESS_INTERVAL_MS`, used with `throttleRecentSuccess = true` for the background trigger in `NodeRuntime.kt`). The connect beacon always sends and starts that window. So backgrounding the app soon after it connects never changes `lastSeenReason`. That is what I saw on a Pixel 10 Pro XL (Android 17): backgrounded about 4 minutes after connecting, the Gateway still showed `lastSeenReason: connect`.

## What changed

Two sentences added to the Presence alive beacons section describing the 10-minute throttle and its visible effect.

## Evidence

- Live observation (Pixel 10 Pro XL, isolated Gateway): app connected, moved to the background about 4 minutes later; the Gateway still showed `lastSeenReason: connect`, matching the 10-minute throttle described above.
- `git diff --check` is clean, and `pnpm format:docs:check` is clean (1420 files).

## What problem this solves

The chat composer's microphone (dictation) button has no accessible name. It sets only `onClickLabel` and draws its icon with `contentDescription = null`, so TalkBack and the Android accessibility tree expose it as an unlabeled button. Material and Android accessibility guidance ask for a content description on every icon-only control.

## What changed

The icon now uses the button's existing action label as its content description: "Dictation" when idle, "Stop Dictation" while listening, and "Cancel dictation" while starting or transcribing. No new strings were added.

## Evidence

- **Regression test:** new Robolectric Compose test `ChatComposerMicButtonTest` checks the idle and listening descriptions and the click action. It fails on `main` ("could not find any node that satisfies: ContentDescription = 'Dictation'") and passes with this change. `ChatDictationControllerTest` (14) still passes, as do `ktlintMainSourceSetCheck` and `ktlintTestSourceSetCheck`.
- **Physical device:** a Pixel 10 Pro Fold (Android 17) running `:app:assemblePlayDebug` (installed `base.apk` SHA-256 matched the build), with a uiautomator accessibility-tree pass over the chat screen's clickable nodes. On `main` there is 1 unlabeled clickable, the button at `[1812,1933][1929,2050]`. With this change there are 0, and the node reads "Dictation".

Discord thread-list help suggests a message ID for `--before` and does not explain that archived listing selects only the specified parent's public archive. An empty result can therefore be mistaken for missing task history.

The Threads documentation and command-specific help now describe public archive selection, selected-list exhaustion, and `nextBefore` as an ISO 8601 archive timestamp. The docs also distinguish bounded reads by a known thread ID from archive discovery. Generic read/search help is unchanged.

This clarifies the existing pagination contract introduced by #88993; it does not add private archive retrieval or change permissions.

- Actual maintained-launcher `message thread list --help` and `message read --help` captures exited 0 with isolated home/state/config. The former shows timestamp/public-parent guidance; the latter retains its existing ID/Matrix-token wording.

prs.title: fix(xai): video_generate downgrades 21:9 and 5:2 to 16:9
prs.body:
Resubmission of #195055, closed by the active-PR limit.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: `video_generate` with xAI turns a `21:9` or `5:2` request into a 16:9 video.

## User Impact

Ultrawide (`21:9`) and `5:2` videos now generate at the requested ratio on every xAI video model. Other ratios and defaults are unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

xAI's [video model capability table](https://docs.x.ai/developers/model-capabilities/video/overview) lists `1:1, 16:9, 9:16, 4:3, 3:4, 3:2, 2:3, 21:9, 5:2` for `grok-imagine-video` and `grok-imagine-video-1.5`. The xAI provider declared only the first seven. Core normalizes a request against the declared list (`resolveMediaGeometryOverrides`), so `21:9` was reported as normalized. The provider itself also mapped any undeclared ratio to its 16:9 default. Adding both ratios to the one set the capability metadata and the request builder share fixes both paths. `docs/providers/xai.md` lists them too.

## Evidence

- **Red on main** (`1166f73e0`): the new `video-generation-provider.test.ts` case fails for both ratios. `aspect_ratio` reaches the request as `"16:9"`, and `capabilities.generate.aspectRatios` lacks the ratio.
- **Green with the fix:** `pnpm vitest run` over the six xAI video/capability/plugin test files: 92 tests passed. `pnpm tsgo:extensions`, `pnpm tsgo:extensions:test`, `oxfmt --check`, `oxlint`, `check:test-lines-ratchet` and `git diff --check` pass.
- **Live `video.generate`** (local Gateway build from `main` plus this PR, xAI OAuth, one short clip):
  `openclaw infer video generate --model xai/grok-imagine-video --aspect-ratio 21:9 --duration 2 --resolution 480P --prompt "slow pan across a calm mountain lake at dawn" --json`
  returned `{"ok":true,"provider":"xai","model":"grok-imagine-video","outputs":[{"mimeType":"video/mp4","size":944603}],"ignoredOverrides":[]}`. ffprobe on the output: **896×384**, 2.04 s, which is exactly 21:9. On `main`, the same request is normalized to the nearest declared ratio, 16:9, before it is sent.
- **Boundary:** live for 21:9. For 5:2: unit (request body and declared capabilities) plus xAI's published table. I haven't spent a second live generation on it yet.
- `check:test-lines-ratchet`: the 7 added regression lines now have their own `config/test-lines-allocations/xai-video-wide-aspect-ratios.txt` record.
- No overlap: #189576 edits the image section of `capability-provider-metadata-factory.ts`, #192924 the realtime voice section, and #195024 a different part of `docs/providers/xai.md`.

prs.title: fix(xai): x_search ignores handle filters written with @
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: `x_search` searches every account instead of the listed ones when the agent writes a handle filter with `@` (for example `allowed_x_handles: ["@openclaw"]`).

## User Impact

Handle filters now apply whether or not the agent includes the `@`. Previously a prefixed handle was silently ignored and the results came from unrelated accounts, with nothing to say the filter hadn't applied.

## Why This Change Was Made

xAI's [X Search reference](https://docs.x.ai/developers/tools/x-search) says handles are "written without the `@`". The tool schema doesn't say that, and agents often write handles with it. The tool now strips leading `@` when it reads `allowed_x_handles` and `excluded_x_handles`, and drops entries that become empty. The 20-handle limit and the allowed/excluded exclusivity checks then run on the normalized lists.

## Evidence

- **Live, before the fix:** one subscription agent turn on an isolated gateway made two `x_search` calls with the same query ("Give the x.com URL of the single most recent post in the search results"):
  - `allowed_x_handles: ["@openclaw"]` returned a post from a different, unrelated account, with 4 citations. The filter was ignored.

## User Impact

The warning now says, “Verify the task's result before repeating it.” Missing activity conservatively reports `replaySafe:false` / `hadPotentialSideEffects:true`.

The [published native review](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/194984#issuecomment-6716979381) P3 next-action finding is resolved in source. The [current native review](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/194984#issuecomment-6716979381) accepts the contributor-reported real-Muse CLI proof and clears its shipped-entry behavior-proof request; this is not independent verification of native/UI behavior or a full raw receipt archive.

[Current-head CI run 42445933963](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/42445933963) completed successfully on `5ca66ceeeb4185135eff5a45812fb37e8f17334e`; the [current native review](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/194984#issuecomment-6716979381) accepts the contributor-reported real-Muse CLI proof and clears its shipped-entry request, while the separate comprehensive-review hold remains open. The earlier local test-line check on the pinned standalone base remains **failed** by 48 lines of existing debt; that historical result is preserved without a waiver or an inferred cause for the CI difference. Live Muse is now shown through the shipped CLI with an injected page failure (Evidence). No live UI or channel delivery, and no automatic-retry behavior, is claimed.

## Why This Change Was Made

The SDK owns whether its settled view is current. Capture that fact once, before authority revalidation or reporting can throw, then use the existing notice/logger and replay-metadata mechanisms. Keep prior conservative metadata conditions, transcript decisions, native terminal semantics and pooled-host lifetime. Lost authority still rejects reporting.

The small completeness sibling keeps the harness within its existing line cap. The dedicated conformant peer exercises real SDK paging, exact SourceRange provenance and one independently witnessed append. It adds no retry, recovery execution, SDK/schema or permission-policy change.

[Coordination with #183676](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/183676#issuecomment-6716201901): that PR owns observation/approval/result-projector extraction; its moved projector will need reconciliation with this guard. #178837 owns streamed prefixes. - **Current warning-only head: 8/8** existing completeness/authority cases pass (24.53 s Vitest / 26.75 s wrapper), with the updated notice/logger expectation. No logic, authority, replay policy, terminal or host-lifetime changes.

prs.title: fix(discord): channel edits persist applied forum tags
prs.body:
Related: #36736

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: Discord `channel-edit` reports success without changing forum or media thread tags when `appliedTags` is provided.

## User Impact

User impact: agents can replace or clear a Discord forum thread applied tags through `channel-edit`, so Kanban status changes persist instead of silently no-oping.

## Why This Change Was Made

The action schema already exposes `appliedTags`, but the Discord channel-edit parser, payload type, and REST adapter did not carry it to Discord `applied_tags` field. This change wires the value through and deliberately preserves an explicit empty array for both camelCase and snake_case input so callers can clear every tag.

## Evidence

- Focused shared-reader regressions pass: 34/34, including direct-key and snake_case empty arrays.
- Focused Discord parser regressions pass: 7/7, covering `appliedTags`, `applied_tags`, replacement, and clearing.
- Full Discord extension lane passed 258 test files and 2,682 tests before the final review fix.
- Updated-head CI is green, including channel tests, type checks, lint, boundaries, CodeQL, and `openclaw/ci-gate`.
- `git diff --check` passes.

### Live Discord behavior proof through the shipped action

Run at 2026-11-08T22:31:04Z. The script called the shipped Discord channel-edit action entry point, `handleDiscordAction`, with the same action payload shape the `message` tool sends, then independently read the thread from Discord after each PATCH. Tag names are shown; raw tag IDs, channel IDs, user IDs, and credentials are omitted.

```text
entryPoint: handleDiscordAction (shipped Discord channel-edit action)
target: Neon Goals TODOs (forum thread)
before applied_tags: [Done, Automation]

clear:
  toolInput: { action: "channelEdit", appliedTags: [] }
  actionResult.ok: true
  PATCH response applied_tags: []
  independent Discord readback applied_tags: []

restore:
  toolInput: { action: "channelEdit", appliedTags: [Done, Automation] }
  actionResult.ok: true
  PATCH response applied_tags: [Done, Automation]
  independent Discord readback applied_tags: [Done, Automation]
  exactOriginalRestored: true
```

This proves both explicit clearing and non-empty replacement through the shipped action path against live Discord, and that the original card state is restored exactly afterward.

### Base-red / head-green regression evidence

- Base (pre-fix `main`): the channel-edit parser drops `appliedTags` and the REST payload omits `applied_tags`, so the PATCH reports success while Discord keeps the old tags. Reported upstream in openclaw/openclaw#36736.
- Head: the parser forwards `appliedTags` (including an explicit empty array for both `appliedTags` and `applied_tags`), the REST body carries `applied_tags`, and the live run above shows the readback changing from `[Done, Automation]` to `[]` and back.

prs.title: fix(ai): replay plaintext reasoning_text for stateless Responses providers
prs.body:
## Problem

Stateless reasoning replay fails for providers that return **plaintext** reasoning with no ciphertext (observed with DeepSeek `deepseek-flash` over `openai-responses`).

Turn 1 works. On turn 2 — i.e. as soon as the assistant turn with reasoning + a tool call is replayed — the request is rejected:

```
400 The \`reasoning_text\` in the thinking mode must be passed back to the API.
```

## Cause

Two places drop the plaintext reasoning:

1. `normalizeOpenAIResponsesReasoningReplayItem` collapses `content` to `[]` unless it is already empty, so `reasoning_text` parts captured from the provider never survive into the replay item.
2. `convertResponsesMessagesWithStyle` skips a reasoning item without a replayed item id when `encrypted_content` is absent, so a plaintext-only reasoning item can never be replayed.
3. `sanitizeOpenAIReasoningSignature` applies the same drop when the signature is persisted, so the stored transcript loses the text even if the in-memory path kept it.

Providers that require the text echoed back have no way to satisfy the requirement.

## Change

- Preserve `reasoning_text` content parts when building a replay item.
- Allow replay without ciphertext when verifiable plaintext reasoning text is present.
- Keep those parts in the stored thinking signature only for providers that need them (currently `deepseek`); every other provider keeps the existing privacy shape and storage output unchanged.

The text is not a new disclosure: the same reasoning is already carried by the thinking block itself.

## Tests

```
packages/ai/src/transports/openai-responses-reasoning-replay.test.ts   10 passed
packages/ai/src/transports/openai-responses-replay-internal.test.ts
packages/ai/src/transports/openai-responses-async-replay.test.ts
packages/ai/src/transports/openai-responses-compaction-replay.test.ts  29 passed
src/agents/transcript-sanitize.test.ts
src/agents/transcript-sanitize-reasoning.test.ts                        18 passed
```

New coverage: a plaintext-only reasoning item replays with its `reasoning_text` intact, and the stored signature keeps those parts for `deepseek` while non-`reasoning_text` parts are still discarded.

Reproduced and verified end-to-end on a live gateway against `https://api.deepseek.com/responses`: before the change the second request returned 400; after it, the same conversation continues normally.

prs.title: fix(exec): literal Mac script commands fail before approval
prs.body:
Related: #187654

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: an absolute interpreter command with a literal script path on a Mac node fails during preparation, before normal `allowlist` / `on-miss` approval can bind the script.

## User Impact

Users can approve the supported direct interpreter/script shape. Ordinary native commands retain the shipped `/bin/sh -c` transport and their existing persisted exact-command approval identity. Shell syntax, quoted paths, noncanonical whitespace, Linux and Windows keep their existing routing.

This addresses the protected static-script case in #187654, not every native-binary or quoted-path report. It does not close the whole issue.

## Why This Change Was Made

The transport now unwraps only the narrow absolute interpreter plus absolute script shape. The prepared script fingerprint is carried inside the existing authenticated native socket request and checked again in the native executor's final `beforeSpawn` guard, after awaited policy/permission work. Native policy, cancellation, executable and working-directory checks remain in place.

### Review follow-up

- **Persisted grants:** the regression fixture now seeds the actual shipped shell command identity independently of the candidate helper. It fails on the first revision and passes with the narrower transport. No grant migration or broad command-identity change is introduced.
- **Native handoff:** forward the existing `mutableFileOperand` in the HMAC-authenticated request. The native launch boundary verifies argv index, resolved path, regular-file status and SHA-256 before executing.
- **Native proof:** added real socket → native policy owner → spawn tests for unchanged allowed script, post-handoff mutation, denied policy and policy revocation after socket admission. These tests are **not yet executed** in a qualified disposable native runner. This PR is draft until the native build and tests pass.

## Evidence

Current repair head: `488baf9a72633fbd2fb58dc3ea114013d14b8cfa`.

- Refreshed onto upstream `826999cd5`, which contains the core test-type correction and the upstream test-line allocation correction. The failed-check classifier attributed the previous TS2345 signature to main. No unrelated CI workaround is carried here.
- Original preparation regression: both new script cases fail on unchanged upstream before an approval decision. The first submitted revision also fails the independently seeded shipped exact-command grant case (1 failed / 45 passed).
- Revised candidate: **134 focused tests across four files passed** using the documented Node runtime override. This covers real exec entry/node prepare-run handlers, saved grants, mutation denial, shell/platform routing and native request delivery. RPC/native response mocking in the TypeScript harness is not native execution proof.
- The six standalone native fingerprint assertions pass on macOS: unchanged absolute/relative path, absent operand, non-file, changed contents and deleted file. Swift syntax parsing passes. This checks the actual guard implementation, not the native app or policy store.
- Targeted lint, core production types, infra/agents-root/node-host test types, SwiftLint, Swift syntax parsing, native localization inventory, formatting and whitespace checks passed. The changed node-host suite was rerun after nullable-field normalization (59/59), and the final shell-boundary cases passed (27/27). The test-line ratchet passes against the exact refreshed base. Tested and publishing diffs match (`983b246b8e04e0d22334de59cdbfc627168354228a5987a30645c369a9a42c69`).
- Native full test build attempted after generating required Mermaid assets. It stops in the unchanged `KeyboardShortcuts` dependency because the available Command Line Tools lack `SwiftUIMacros.EntryMacro` and `PreviewsMacros.SwiftUIView` compiler plug-ins. No successful native build or test execution is claimed. The operator desktop's native-test isolation guard was not bypassed.
- **Required next proof:** qualified, secretless, exact-head macOS build plus the native socket tests, including existing cancellation/policy-owner regressions. Ordinary PR CI defers macOS jobs, so an aggregate PR green is insufficient. Please retain draft status until this proof exists.
- Direct author review and `pr-simplify` applied. The broad literal-command path was removed, existing policy/request owners retained. Whole change versus refreshed base: production +45/-4, tests +162/-1 including Swift. The exact TypeScript test-line allocation is 92. No independent local reviewer is claimed.

<details>
<summary>Focused runtime commands</summary>

```sh
OPENCLAW_VITEST_RUNTIME=node node scripts/run-vitest.mjs \
  src/infra/node-shell.test.ts src/infra/exec-host.test.ts \
  src/node-host/invoke-system-run.test.ts \
  src/agents/bash-tools.exec-host-node.integration.test.ts --maxWorkers=1
swift build --package-path apps/macos --build-system native --build-tests --jobs 4
```

The second command is the documented blocked build, not a pass. Native tests must use the repository's disposable-runner procedure.

</details>

prs.title: fix(gateway): keep readiness green during bounded channel reconnects
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Routine Discord op-7/resume and X stream reconnects make the entire Gateway return `/readyz` 503 even when the channel is recovering normally.

## User Impact

Previously connected channels remain ready during the existing two-minute reconnect window, with affected channel IDs visible in the detailed response's `degraded` field. Status retains the disconnected/recovering state and reports `reconnect-grace`; reconnect and recovery logs remain visible. Unrecovered transports, blocked/auth failures, and accounts that exhaust the Gateway restart ladder remain unready. Initial connection behavior is preserved. No configuration, dependency, or schema changes.

## Why This Change Was Made

The shared health policy already supports reconnect grace, but Discord's op-7 scheduling and X's stream status did not reliably publish its required disconnect timestamp. Each transport now records one timestamp for a continuous outage and clears it on recovery. Repeated failed sockets cannot renew the window, and active agent work cannot extend an explicitly recovering transport's deadline. X retains its supported stream-auth fallback to polling; a confirmed polling authentication refusal is terminal.

Related: #146892 overlaps busy-account health policy. This change is limited to explicitly recovering/disconnected accounts and the Discord/X producer-to-readiness flow.

## Evidence

Initial focused validation passed 176 tests across Gateway readiness/health, the real HTTP probe server, Discord protocol/lifecycle, and X stream/monitor suites. The HTTP regressions drive parsed op-7 → Resume → RESUMED and an X ReadableStream reconnect; both remain 200 with degraded detail, recover cleanly, and become 503 after 120 seconds of continuous failure. Discord 4004 and polling 401/403 remain terminal. The fixtures use real protocol, lifecycle, readiness and HTTP owners with synthetic upstream I/O. The malformed-payload regression additionally composes the real channel manager and observes its automatic restart; no test contacts external services or boots the full application.

The Discord regression reproduced pre-fix 503 at +1 second. That first runner also reported an unrelated concurrent source-generation change, so its behavioral failure is recorded separately from the final frozen green run. X polling-auth regressions failed cleanly before the fix. An existing forbidden-backfill test was updated to assert terminal 403 and cursor preservation instead of waiting for automatic retry.

Independent Codex review raised one P2 startup observation, rejected after checking the exact base: X already marked its initialized lifecycle ready before opening the stream, and changing that would violate the requested preservation of initial readiness. No accepted findings remain.

Initial `pnpm check:changed` exposed test-only type/import-boundary issues that were repaired with a typed fixture and the existing bundled-artifact loader. The later CI root-test callback and test-budget defects were investigated on exact parents and reconciled after main's fixes; current validation is recorded below.

<details>
<summary>Owner measurements and change size</summary>

`scripts/perf/channel-readiness-measure.ts`: 44 synthetic channels × 4 accounts, 100,000 checks per run, five serial alternating A/B pairs plus A/A controls. This owner does no session-database or workspace I/O; these measurements are not a whole-Gateway startup or filesystem benchmark.

| Median per probe | Before | After |
|---|---:|---:|
| Healthy refresh wall / CPU | 14.820 / 14.485 µs | 16.811 / 14.498 µs |
| Reconnecting refresh wall / CPU | 41.847 / 25.745 µs | 43.988 / 26.723 µs |
| Reconnecting cached wall / CPU | 3.127 / 3.234 µs | 3.537 / 3.658 µs |
| Healthy refresh allocations | 32,526 B | 32,611 B |
| Reconnecting refresh allocations | 32,547 B | 32,783 B |
| Reconnecting cached allocations | 424 B | 441 B |

Identical-source A/A refresh wall times ranged 12.815–31.943 µs on a heavily loaded host, making refresh timing attribution inconclusive. The cached reconnect result adds about 0.4 µs and 17 bytes for visible degradation; no speedup claim. Snapshot reads remain one per refresh and zero per cached check. The CPU profile identifies the existing executable-access syscall as substantial work; no new cache or inventory scan.

Runtime production grows 55 net lines to record the missing outage boundary and expose degradation/terminal diagnosis. Test-only API loaders add 3 lines, benchmark tooling 155, and regression fixtures/tests 453, including the malformed-payload manager regression and after removing 23 duplicate X monitor test lines. The scoped allocation is exactly 453 lines, matching this PR's net test growth with no inherited-debt credit; the shared scalar is unchanged. Gateway/core tests took 134.28 seconds including cold compilation; Discord 24.09 seconds; final HTTP/X verification 108.77 seconds. CI timing is pending.

</details>


## Current validation and recovery ownership

Current head: `4191ca0d4c67f7a2f0abe315695a1246ab9a6668`, based on main `826999cd5f76f4867a69869489a4fc51cd5e4a35`. Ready for review and unmerged; new-head CI is unverified. Main already includes the install-test debt grant and root-test callback type fix, so this PR carries no inherited-debt allocation.

Addressed both valid lifecycle review items. The prior revision incorrectly treated every `shouldStopLifecycle` event as permanently terminal. A malformed gateway payload therefore settled its run but disabled the manager's automatic restart. Removed that blanket status update, restoring `handleGatewayEvent` exactly to main's settlement flow. The existing close-code handler retains terminal status for operator-actionable authentication/configuration failures.

This preserves [095e7b830a0e / #59019](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/095e7b830a0e90d3b2a00dbbff2f284167099dbe): transport reconnect/resume belongs to the transport owner; lifecycle failures settle the current run; the Gateway manager owns account restart and its retry limit. Transport retry exhaustion can end one lifecycle without disabling that manager recovery. No reconnect controller, new classifier, or new retry policy was introduced. The SDK docs now state this distinction explicitly. This repair removes five runtime lines from the prior revision.

The new regression sends malformed wire JSON through the real Discord decoder, supervisor and lifecycle, forwards their actual status into the real channel manager, and observes a second running lifecycle. Before the repair it failed because `restartPending` was false instead of true (18 ms); the two existing reconnect tests passed. After the repair it proves nonterminal status, recorded protocol error, readiness during manager backoff, and actual automatic restart (14 ms). Both red and green runs verified their frozen source generation.

Latest focused proof: **28 tests pass** across HTTP reconnect (3 tests), Discord lifecycle and supervisor (25 tests); wrapper time 24.40 seconds. Existing op-7 resume, X reconnect/expiry and Discord 4004 authentication-failure coverage all remain green. Targeted Gateway test types, type-aware core/Discord lint, formatting and diff checks pass. Fresh independent Codex autoreview is scoped-clean through P2.

The exact allocation is **453 net test/fixture lines**, with no inherited credit. `node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs scripts/check-test-lines-ratchet.mts --base origin/main --no-merge-base` passes: 6,587,194 lines, ceiling 6,587,194, zero slack. The former root typecheck failure also passed after rebasing onto main's fix (4.4 seconds).

prs.title: fix(deepseek): retain reasoning for Responses tool continuations
prs.body:
Related: #192506

Draft: full Gateway/upgrade-incident reproduction remains outstanding.

## What Problem This Solves

DeepSeek Responses tool continuations lose the plaintext reasoning emitted by the provider, including after session reload.

## User Impact

Explicit `deepseek` + `openai-responses` routes can replay the provider's `reasoning.content` rather than dropping it. This required replay payload is retained in the local session transcript. Other providers keep their existing reasoning privacy behavior; the default DeepSeek Chat Completions route is unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

The shared Responses normalizer clears nonempty reasoning content both when receiving output and when preparing replay. Transcript storage clears it again, and the stateless replay path discards reasoning without ciphertext when item IDs are disabled. DeepSeek emits plaintext `reasoning_text` rather than OpenAI encrypted reasoning, so all of these boundaries must preserve its replay payload.

The exception is limited to the `deepseek` provider. No new configuration, dependency, retry, or separate replay owner is introduced. The existing storage sanitizer retains only typed `reasoning_text`/text pairs for that route. Documentation makes the storage tradeoff explicit.

## Evidence

- Production SDK regression covers managed and package-direct streams, HTTP 400 rejection of missing reasoning, tool results, canonical transcript preparation/reload, and the outgoing serialized replay. It extends the existing storage regression rather than adding another harness. OpenAI and native ChatGPT remain controls.
- A storage privacy table covers DeepSeek versus OpenAI and an unrelated custom Responses provider.
- Live DeepSeek Flash package-provider probe: warm tool continuation and replay after transcript sanitization both returned the correct synthetic tool result; each outgoing request retained 110 reasoning characters. The base normalizer sent zero reasoning characters on both requests. **The current live endpoint also accepted the baseline requests**, so this is evidence of restored payload fidelity, not a live reproduction or proof of the original HTTP 400. No full Gateway/upgrade/restart reproduction was performed; #192506's restart hypothesis remains unverified. This PR is related to that issue, not an assertion that its full incident is resolved.
- Pre-fix SDK tool-continuation regressions fail with the expected missing-reasoning HTTP 400 fixture, and the final DeepSeek storage privacy case is also red on the base. Both pass with the fix.
- Six focused suites: 79 passed, one skipped. The final focused wrapper took 7.08 seconds; the changed storage suite took 3.31 seconds including compilation (individual tests under 30 ms), and the sanitizer suite 133 ms. CI duration is not yet available.
- Production core and affected agent-test typechecks, targeted oxlint/oxfmt, whitespace checks, and the affected AI package build including declarations were run locally.
- Native independent code review of the complete production change against `abe11702825e31e250244fd2ea1f0abd22dc0c24`: no actionable findings. Canonical autoreview was unavailable; no autoreview or full Gateway verification is claimed.
- Author simplification pass retained the existing normalizer/replay/storage owners. The separate test-line allocation covers only the net regression growth for tool continuation, reload, and provider privacy boundaries.

prs.title: feat(backup): restore PostgreSQL stores into a staging database for restore drills
prs.body:
Closes #182772

**Decision needed: how `backup restore` picks a different PostgreSQL destination.**

- **Recommended (this PR):** one restore flag, `--postgres-connection-env <name>`. Every PostgreSQL import, and the cleanup after a failed import, uses the DSN in that environment variable. Nothing else changes: the archived family selections and `schemaPrefix` still apply, and the restored `openclaw.json` stays byte-identical to the archived one. The output names the variable and says to point the archived connection at the same server before activation. No new config keys, and the DSN never goes on the command line. The output deliberately names only the variable, not the server identity (host, database, user), so the DSN is never parsed or printed.
- **Alternative B:** also write the override into the restored `openclaw.json`. Activation would then follow the restore destination automatically, but restore would have to rewrite captured config, including `$include` files, so the restored config would no longer match the archive under test. This can be added later on top of this flag if maintainers want it.
- **Alternative C:** accept a full SecretRef (`file:`, `exec:`, JSON) instead of an env var name. This is more flexible but needs a new CLI SecretRef syntax. An env var already covers file and exec setups: the operator can export the staging DSN for one command.
- **Out of scope:** a restore-time schema prefix (`restore_<uuid>` naming). That is a separate decision, as the issue review noted.

## What Problem This Solves

Restore drills of a PostgreSQL archive write full copies of every store into the production database when the archived connection is a file or exec SecretRef, because `backup restore` can only import through the connection recorded in the archive.

## User Impact

User impact: operators can verify a production archive by restoring it into a staging database. Production rows and schemas are not touched, and neither is the production secret file:

```
openclaw backup restore <archive> --target <dir> --postgres-connection-env STAGING_PG_DSN
```

Restores without the flag behave as before. The flag is rejected when the variable is unset or the archive has no PostgreSQL stores, and nothing is extracted in that case.

## Why This Change Was Made

Restore already validates the archived config in its own offline scope and resolves the import connection from it. The flag replaces only `database.postgres.connection` in that in-memory copy with an env SecretRef for the named variable. The reference is built after the archived config is read, with the existing `resolveDefaultSecretProviderAlias(config, "env")`, so it goes through the archived config's default env provider (`secrets.defaults.env`, or `default` when none is set) and that provider's allowlist, the same way a hand-written default env ref would. Imports, verification and failed-import cleanup all read the same scope, so they all go to the same destination. Cleanup going to the staging server follows from that shared scope; no test forces a failed import with the flag set. The restoring host's own state ownership check still uses the live config, so a staging DSN cannot be confused with the host's live database. `--from` restores forward the flag too.

Activation stays explicit. If the restored state is used with the archived connection still pointing at the original server, the anchors name a `restore_<uuid>` namespace that does not exist there. State ownership then refuses with the existing `Missing PostgreSQL metadata; use the matching OpenClaw version or restore the matching PostgreSQL schema and anchor.` error, and nothing is created on that server (checked in the CLI run below).

## Evidence

**Through the built CLI**, using the same base (`72b51fb6089`) with and without this change. The setup is one PostgreSQL 17 server with two fresh databases: A, the "production" database behind a **file SecretRef**, and B, the staging database, whose DSN is supplied only through the environment. Each run starts a scratch install on A (`doctor --non-interactive`), records three backup runs as sample rows, runs `backup create --verify`, then restores with the flag and again without it. The table comparisons count rows and hash the ordered row text of every table.

Before (base build):

```
$ openclaw backup restore <archive> --target <dir>/restored-override --postgres-connection-env DRILL_STAGING_PG_DSN
OpenClaw does not recognize option "--postgres-connection-env".
[exit 1]

$ openclaw backup restore <archive> --target <dir>/restored-default
Backup archive restored to staging: <dir>/restored-default
[exit 0]
A: drill_state_eecebf80adfa4f79, restore_d1dca86a713f4d838205bf7f6f5610be   <- copy written into A
B: (empty)
```

After (this branch):

```
$ openclaw backup restore <archive> --target <dir>/restored-override --postgres-connection-env DRILL_STAGING_PG_DSN
Backup archive restored to staging: <dir>/restored-override
Archive entries restored: 12
PostgreSQL stores imported through: $DRILL_STAGING_PG_DSN
The restored config keeps the archived PostgreSQL connection; point it at the same server before activation.
[exit 0]

A: drill_state_9fe85f6bc3464805                       (no new schema)
B: restore_9933cc84eb5542efbe14cdc0c19a7879
A source schema rows: unchanged (98 tables, row counts and content hashes identical)
B vs A at archive time: identical (97 tables, row counts and content hashes; openclaw_schema_meta compared below)
tables with rows: 4, total rows: 7
openclaw_schema_meta store/version/store_id: identical (state v39 9fe85f6b-c346-4805-b1e8-bd5628ff1fe5)
restored state anchor: postgres restore_9933cc84eb5542efbe14cdc0c19a7879
restored openclaw.json: byte-identical to the archived config

$ openclaw backup restore <archive> --target <dir>/restored-default      (no flag)
[exit 0]
A: drill_state_9fe85f6bc3464805, restore_ba2db7e46b0a4a1a9c6c98d80664c269   <- unchanged default behavior

# copy of the staging-restored state used with its archived config (connection still on A)
$ openclaw backup record --status ok --target activation-probe
Warning: the backup outcome could not be recorded: Cannot admit backup.recordOutcome ... failed to acquire gateway state ownership | Missing PostgreSQL metadata; use the matching OpenClaw version or restore the matching PostgreSQL schema and anchor. | relation "openclaw_schema_meta" does not exist
A: drill_state_9fe85f6bc3464805, restore_ba2db7e46b0a4a1a9c6c98d80664c269   (nothing new)
```

`openclaw_schema_meta` is compared on store, version and store id because one of its hash columns depends on the schema name. A's own `backup_runs` table gains the archive's run record after capture, so B is compared with A as it was at archive time.

**Tests, red on the base and green with the change:**

- `src/infra/database-engine/archive-restore.postgres.test.ts`, new `override` scenario: the archived connection still resolves to the source database and the flag points at a separate recovery database. It checks every store's rows on the recovery server, that the source server gets no `restore_*` namespace, and that the restored config bytes match the archive. On the base, the import goes to the source database and the recovery-server check fails (`relation "restore_….user_profiles" does not exist`). With the change all 5 scenarios pass.
- Same file, new `override-alias` scenario: the archive sets `secrets.defaults.env = "primary"` with `providers.primary = { source: "env", allowlist: [...] }` and no provider named `default`. On the previous head of this branch the restore fails with `database.postgres.connection SecretRef is unresolved (env:default:OPENCLAW_ARCHIVE_TEST_RECOVERY_PG)` (1 failed, 5 passed). With the fix all 6 scenarios pass, in two runs.
- `src/commands/backup-restore.test.ts`: the flag rejects an invalid name, an unset variable, and a SQLite-only archive before anything is extracted. Red on the base (the restore resolved), green with the change (20 passed).
- `src/cli/program/register.backup.offsite.test.ts`: `--from` restores forward the flag. Red on the base (`unknown option`), green with the change (4 passed).

Test cost: the change adds 89 net test lines, recorded in `config/test-lines-allocations/backup-restore-postgres-connection-env.txt`. The two PostgreSQL scenarios are the only proof that imports, verification and cleanup reach the override server and that a custom env provider alias resolves. The unit cases cover the refusals and `--from` forwarding. Wall time with `--maxWorkers=1`: `backup-restore.test.ts` 38 s, `register.backup.offsite.test.ts` 17 s, `archive-restore.postgres.test.ts` 96 s through the database conformance runner (Vitest duration 91 s for all 6 scenarios; the two override scenarios take 5.8 s and 5.7 s).

Also run: `oxfmt --check` and `oxlint` on the changed files, `pnpm tsgo:core`, `pnpm tsgo:core:test`, `pnpm check:import-cycles`, `pnpm check:test-lines-ratchet` (merged with current main), `git diff --check`, and `src/secrets/resolve.test.ts` (33 passed). Docs: `docs/cli/backup.md` and `docs/gateway/postgresql.md` describe the flag next to the existing "point that secret at the recovery server" guidance, and `docs/cli/backup.md` names the provider and allowlist the variable is read through.

**Risk:** low. The flag is opt-in, and the code path without it is unchanged. The override uses the archived config's default env secret provider, so if that provider has an allowlist that does not list the variable, the restore stops with the usual SecretRef error and the target is cleaned. The built-CLI run above used an archive without custom secret providers; the custom-alias case is covered by the PostgreSQL restore test.

prs.title: docs(muse): stop claiming automatic selection never picks Muse
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`extensions/muse/README.md` told readers that the Muse harness is "opt-in only" and that `auto` never picks it. That is
wrong: the canonical guide (`docs/plugins/muse.md`, "Set `agentRuntime.id` …") states that without explicit routing a
model discovered by exactly one native runtime can use that runtime when no authored API binding or host credential takes
precedence. A reader following the README would conclude Muse can never be chosen automatically.

## Why This Change Was Made

The Install section now describes the same rule as the guide instead of asserting the opposite:

- explicit routing is still `agentRuntime.id: "muse"` on a `meta/*` model or the `meta` provider;
- without it, automatic selection can still use Muse when it is the only native runtime for the model and nothing more
  specific wins;
- the existing link to the Muse guide stays, so the full rule has one owner in `docs/plugins/muse.md`.

## User Impact

Docs only. Behaviour, packaging, and plugin routing are unchanged; the README no longer contradicts the guide.

## Evidence

- Statement being corrected: `extensions/muse/README.md` (Install section).
- Rule being matched: `docs/plugins/muse.md`, the paragraph that starts "Set `agentRuntime.id` on one model entry …".
- `pnpm format:docs:check`: `Docs formatting clean (1420 files)`.
- `pnpm lint:docs`: `Summary: 0 issues in 0 files`.

## Rendered proof

The changed file lives outside `docs/`, so here is the rendered Install section at head `375e671983d`, using GitHub-style
typography (the header line in the image records the source path, PR, and head commit):

![Muse README Install section as changed by this PR](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/HeMiaolin/openclaw/evidence/muse-readme-194901/evidence/muse-readme-install-194901.png)

It shows the three claims the patch is judged on: the install command block, the sentence that automatic selection still
uses Muse when it is the only native runtime for the model and no authored API binding or host credential takes
precedence, and the retained link to the Muse Code agent runtime guide. No account or browser chrome is visible.

## AI Assistance

This PR was prepared with AI assistance from the issue report; the author reviewed the change.

prs.title: fix(codex): private conversation recall misses indexed sessions
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes private conversation recall returning no relevant memory on the Codex harness when the source conversation is already indexed.

Related to #100140.

## User Impact

Codex-backed recall can search the intended private conversation corpus through the existing visibility checks. Ordinary memory search keeps its configured sources.

## Why This Change Was Made

Forward the trusted conversation recall context to the host tool factory, matching the embedded harness. The memory owner already selects the recall corpus and enforces the same-agent, private-anchor and sandbox boundaries.

The existing memory/auth context table moves to a sibling test file because the owner file has reached its line cap. Production grows by one line. Net test growth is 45 lines, covered by the required allocation record. The added cases protect absent, sessions and configured recall contexts.

## Evidence

- A synthetic direct-chat source was published by the normal producer. With memory-only search defaults and memory/session index sources, the native recall child issued memory_search without a corpus argument, received eight Memory-only hits and returned NONE. The same main turn found the expected answer using sessions_search and sessions_history. No external messages were delivered.
- Before the fix, the owner regression failed for both trusted recall contexts because the host factory received undefined. After the fix, all 82 owner tests passed. After the required extraction, the final four affected Codex/memory suites passed 140 tests across two shards in 135.60s. The new sibling's three tests took 1.254s, with compiler/import preparation dominating its 63.55s cold shard. Native CI passed on attempt 1 in approximately 408s wall time. [CI run](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/42413423590).
- Local autoreview covered the complete staged candidate against 037c8a6ed9009f2be7de0811efe4ca4e909a3b7b through P2 and reported no actionable findings. The review used the unchanged context producer, host-tool construction and memory visibility sources. The reviewer did not independently execute tests.
- Personally inspected native Codex dynamic-tool protocol at rust-v0.160.0, commit a956835d020762cb2b570053af06f643a11c0ecc. This context is owned by OpenClaw's host tool construction.
- The repaired source head passed a live-model normal-producer QA cell in 55.02s. The supplemental fixture used `qa/scenarios/memory/remember-across-conversations.yaml`, removed its forced `memory index` and Gateway restart steps, and selected the documented native Codex user-home auth route with Codex CLI 0.167.0. Separate private source and target conversations returned the exact synthetic preference. The recall helper called `memory_search`, included the private source transcript, excluded the group and target-anchor transcripts, and preserved `tools.sessions.visibility`. The live channel was the isolated `qa-channel`. The fixture's mock-only group-destination, pause and setting-off checks were outside this live cell.
- Initial test setup rejected an absolute output path. The first live cell then stopped before the source acknowledgement with HTTP 401 because its isolated agent home had no prepared credential. A separate run passed after selecting the documented existing native account route. The six synthetic native threads were archived and read back after teardown.
- Official distribution and Shannon's repaired-runtime automatic recall acceptance remain pending. The successful live cell is bound to this source checkout and its stated native Codex runtime.

The focused extension and extension-test typechecks, format, plugin boundaries, line-cap and test-line budget checks passed. Optional broad check:changed encountered existing changelog attribution violations in unchanged historical records. Its dead-export scan reported six unchanged exports in scripts/lib/control-ui-gesture-probe.ts and was stopped. Exact-head native PR CI completed successfully. The local broad-check findings remain documented above.


## Inspectable runtime and authority evidence

The following output is projected from completed runs on `3e01344f4079d6e4454d172f1e53a2692fe4adf5`. The live cells used native Codex 0.167.0 with the documented existing-user-account route. Both used the isolated `qa-channel` and ordinary inbound conversation production. All facts and requests below are synthetic.

```json
{
  "head": "3e01344f4079d6e4454d172f1e53a2692fe4adf5",
  "nativeCodex": "0.167.0",
  "providerLive": true,
  "channel": "isolated qa-channel",
  "privateRecall": {
    "passed": 1,
    "wallMs": 55020,
    "ordinaryProducer": true,
    "manualIndex": false,
    "restartAfterSeeding": false,
    "reply": "lemon pepper wings with blue cheese"
  },
  "groupDestination": {
    "passed": 1,
    "wallMs": 25989,
    "sourceAcknowledged": true,
    "helperCountBefore": 1,
    "helperCountAfter": 1,
    "nativeModelInputItems": 12,
    "nativeToolCalls": 0,
    "privateMarkerInNativeJournal": false,
    "reply": "QA-GROUP-NO-CONTEXT"
  },
  "authorityReturnBoundary": [
    {
      "proof": "recall-authority-return-boundary",
      "destination": "private",
      "candidateTranscriptHits": 1,
      "releasedTranscriptHits": 1,
      "partialTranscriptHits": 0,
      "persistedSessionOwner": "real SQLite session store",
      "retrievalBackend": "controlled deferred candidate"
    },
    {
      "proof": "recall-authority-return-boundary",
      "destination": "group",
      "candidateTranscriptHits": 1,
      "releasedTranscriptHits": 0,
      "partialTranscriptHits": 0,
      "persistedSessionOwner": "real SQLite session store",
      "retrievalBackend": "controlled deferred candidate"
    },
    {
      "proof": "recall-authority-return-boundary",
      "destination": "becomes-shared",
      "candidateTranscriptHits": 1,
      "releasedTranscriptHits": 0,
      "partialTranscriptHits": 0,
      "persistedSessionOwner": "real SQLite session store",
      "retrievalBackend": "controlled deferred candidate"
    }
  ],
  "unitTestFiles": 1,
  "unitTestsPassed": 3
}
```

### Native private-recall tool trace

The saved native recall thread contains this tool invocation, followed by the returned session hit and the final synthetic preference. The invocation omits `corpus`. The original QA assertions also verified exclusion of the group-source and target-anchor transcript IDs.

```json
{
  "toolCall": "const r = await tools.memory_search({query:\"what snack do I usually want for QA movie night\",minScore:0,maxResults:10});text(r);\n",
  "results": [
    {
      "path": "sessions/qa/30b11b93-9cc5-48c8-aac8-97a7d8326216.jsonl",
      "source": "sessions",
      "startLine": 2,
      "endLine": 2,
      "snippet": "User: Stable QA movie night usual favorite snack preference: lemon pepper wings with blue cheese. Reply exactly: QA-REMEMBER-SOURCE-SEEDED\n\nSource: sessions/qa/30b11b93-9cc5-48c8-aac8-97a7d8326216.jsonl#L2"
    }
  ]
}
```

### Group destination before model output

A separate private conversation produced `QA_PRIVATE_GROUP_MARKER_194802_20261108`. A subsequent group request asked for the private code using the unique challenge `QA-GROUP-DESTINATION-PROBE-20261108-0404`. The group native thread was selected by its exact isolated workspace and that challenge. Its persisted model-input items and full native journal contained zero occurrences of the private marker. The private source journal supplied a positive control for the same extractor. The group produced `QA-GROUP-NO-CONTEXT`, with zero tool calls and no additional recall helper.

The group native journal SHA-256 was `5ac8696c90957d5be4da7e5969ade1d2e3c0f0268e37080ef26c8746c1b53285`. The QA summary SHA-256 was `8f8b7bc7092934926d166754d9fea3df75ec9996ddac0d7f2784ab0d03835bf3`. The three task-owned native threads were archived through the native API and read back after the runner removed its isolated state.

### Destination invalidation while retrieval waits

The supplemental owner test calls production `executeMemorySearchToolQuery`, including its production session-visibility filter, with the real SQLite session owner. Its retrieval backend deliberately holds one private transcript candidate at a deferred search boundary. The test persists a private-to-group change through `upsertSessionEntry` before releasing retrieval. The query returns zero transcript hits and publishes no partial transcript result. The already-group case also returns zero. The unchanged-private control returns the candidate.

This establishes the search-result boundary before a caller can supply the result to the model. The live group cell above separately exercises inbound routing, native model input and the completed reply. The retained source change remains the one-line adapter forwarding repair. The supplemental fixtures below were executed from the exact checkout and removed after their evidence was retained.

<details>
<summary>Reproduce the real session-owner and deferred retrieval proof</summary>

Save this as `extensions/memory-core/src/memory-search-tool-query.recall-authority-proof.test.ts`, then run `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/memory-core/src/memory-search-tool-query.recall-authority-proof.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`.

```ts
import { createDeferred } from "openclaw/plugin-sdk/extension-shared";
import type {
  MemorySearchManager,
  MemorySearchResult,
} from "openclaw/plugin-sdk/memory-core-host-engine-storage";
import { captureRuntimeConfigAsyncReader } from "openclaw/plugin-sdk/runtime-config-snapshot";
import { upsertSessionEntry } from "openclaw/plugin-sdk/session-store-runtime";
import { withOpenClawTestState } from "openclaw/plugin-sdk/test-state";
import { expect, it } from "vitest";
import { executeMemorySearchToolQuery } from "./memory-search-tool-query.js";

it.each(["private", "group", "becomes-shared"] as const)(
  "withholds transcript content at the query return boundary for %s",
  async (destination) => {
    await withOpenClawTestState({ scenario: "minimal" }, async () => {
      await captureRuntimeConfigAsyncReader()();
      const anchor = "agent:main:qa-channel:direct:dm:authority-target";
      const source = "agent:main:qa-channel:direct:dm:authority-source";
      const persistAnchor = (chatType: "direct" | "group") =>
        upsertSessionEntry({
          agentId: "main",
          sessionKey: anchor,
          entry: { sessionId: "authority-anchor", updatedAt: Date.now(), chatType },
        });
      await persistAnchor(destination === "group" ? "group" : "direct");
      await upsertSessionEntry({
        agentId: "main",
        sessionKey: source,
        entry: { sessionId: "authority-source", updatedAt: Date.now(), chatType: "direct" },
      });
      const hit: MemorySearchResult = {
        path: "sessions/main/authority-source.jsonl",
        source: "sessions",
        startLine: 1,
        endLine: 1,
        score: 1,
        snippet: "QA_PRIVATE_AUTHORITY_MARKER_194802",
      };
      const entered = createDeferred<void>();
      const release = createDeferred<void>();
      const partials: unknown[] = [];
      const manager: MemorySearchManager = {
        search: async (_query, options) => {
          options?.onPartialResults?.([hit]);
          entered.resolve();
          await release.promise;
          return [hit];
        },
        status: () => ({ backend: "builtin", provider: "fixture" }),
        readFile: async () => ({ status: "not_found", path: "", text: "" }),
        probeEmbeddingAvailability: async () => ({ ok: true }),
        probeVectorAvailability: async () => false,
      };
      const query = executeMemorySearchToolQuery({
        initialManager: { manager },
        query: {
          text: "private authority marker",
          resultLimit: 3,
          defaultSources: ["memory"],
          indexedSources: ["memory", "sessions"],
          sessionKey: `${anchor}:active-memory:123456abcdef`,
          conversationRecall: {
            anchorSessionKey: anchor,
            scope: "same-agent-private",
            corpus: "configured",
          },
        },
        visibility: {
          cfg: { agents: { entries: { main: {} } }, tools: { sessions: { visibility: "self" } } },
          agentId: "main",
          sandboxed: false,
        },
        signal: new AbortController().signal,
        onPartialResults: (result) => partials.push(result),
      });
      try {
        await entered.promise;
        expect(partials).toEqual([null]);
        if (destination === "becomes-shared") {
          await persistAnchor("group");
        }
      } finally {
        release.resolve();
      }
      const result = await query;
      expect(result.rawResults).toEqual(destination === "private" ? [hit] : []);
      expect(partials).toEqual([null]);
      console.log(JSON.stringify({
        proof: "recall-authority-return-boundary",
        destination,
        candidateTranscriptHits: 1,
        releasedTranscriptHits: result.rawResults.length,
        partialTranscriptHits: 0,
        persistedSessionOwner: "real SQLite session store",
        retrievalBackend: "controlled deferred candidate",
      }));
    });
  },
);

```
</details>

<details>
<summary>Reproduce the additional live group-destination cell</summary>

Save this as `qa/scenarios/memory/codex-private-recall-group-proof.yaml`. Select an available live OpenAI model and run the official `qa suite` command with this scenario, `--provider-mode live-frontier`, `OPENCLAW_QA_FORCE_RUNTIME=codex`, and a relative output directory. The native CLI path and explicit native-home setting bind the existing test account.

```yaml

  surface: session-memory

  gatewayConfigPatch:

  successCriteria:
    - The private source is produced by a completed ordinary conversation.

    - The completed group reply contains no private fact.
  execution:
    kind: flow
    channel: qa-channel
    suiteIsolation: isolated

    summary: Produce a private fact and verify the group destination boundary.
    config:
      requiredChannelDriver: qa-channel

flow:
  steps:
    - name: group destination receives no private recall
      actions:
        - call: waitForGatewayHealthy
          args:
            - ref: env

        - set: transcriptRoot

        - sendInbound:

          saveAs: groupInbound

        - assert:
            expr: helpersAfter === helpersBefore
            message: group destination unexpectedly started a private recall helper
        - assert:
            expr: "!groupReply.text.includes(config.privateFact)"
            message: private fact reached the group reply
        - call: waitForQaInboundCompletion
          args:
            - ref: state
            - ref: groupInbound
            - expr: liveTurnTimeoutMs(env, 60000)
      detailsExpr: "JSON.stringify({ tempRoot: env.gateway.tempRoot, sourceAcknowledged: sourceReply.text === config.sourceMarker, groupReplyCompleted: true, privateFactInGroupReply: groupReply.text.includes(config.privateFact), helperCountBefore: helpersBefore, helperCountAfter: helpersAfter })"

```

prs.title: fix: sent turns fail mid-reply when the sender's scheduled run ends
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: a session's reply fails mid-turn with "Cron occurrence source authority is no longer active" when another session's scheduled run sent it work with `sessions_send` and that run then ends.

## User Impact

A turn that another session hands off keeps running after the sender's scheduled run finishes, reschedules itself with `next_check`, deletes its one-shot job, or has its isolated run session cleaned up. Revoking the sender's device, changing their profile or role, or ending their access grant still stops it, and so does an explicit Stop. A job's own turn still ends when the job is disabled, removed or replaced.

## Why This Change Was Made

A turn admitted through `sessions_send` (and chat.send or Talk) inherits the sending run's operator authority. Since #176422 (`d74a4aeb7d62`), a scheduled continuation restores that authority bound to its single occurrence and to its exact session. #178693 moved only **child** targets onto the retained continuation authority, which keeps device, profile, role and grant checks but not the occurrence binding. Any other receiver, such as the sender's parent or a peer, kept the occurrence-bound authority and failed as soon as the occurrence ended. This shipped in `v2026.10.10-beta.3`; the last stable release `v2026.10.9` is unaffected.

This change:
- makes every accepted turn retained through `retainGatewayOperatorRun` use the continuation authority, and removes the child-only `spawnedBy` plumbing;
- separates the claimed sender session's lifecycle from the continuation. Previously, replacing or removing the sender's session (for example, cleanup of an isolated run's exact-run session) aborted the shared policy signal and still killed handed-off turns. Now that lifecycle ends only the sender's own run-bound authority.

### Deliberate revocations (ruled on by @jalehman)

1. Sender device revoked: kept.
2. Profile or role change, or access grant ended: kept.
3. Explicit user Stop: kept.
4. A job's own turn when the job is disabled, removed or replaced: kept. The job's own run does not go through this path.
5. Messages sent into a job's own `cron:<jobId>` session, which the next run takes over: unchanged for now.

### Known follow-up

Plugin subagent dispatch (`server-plugin-in-process-dispatch.ts`, `plugin_subagent`) still borrows its caller's authority without a retained continuation. It is out of scope here.

A related failure, also out of scope: a `sessions_yield` completion-delivery turn (`subagent_settle`) can fail mid-execution with "subagent source lifecycle changed before completion delivery". That turn is gated by the settle-wake's `isSourceSessionEffectsAllowed` (via `isExecutionAllowed`), which ties execution to the requester's yielded run, the settle batch and its custody (`subagent-announce.requester-settle-wake.ts`). Operator authority is not involved, so this PR does not change it. Seen on 2026-11-07 at 12:16:34 PST: the yield was recorded at 12:16:34.021, the yielded run ended at 12:16:34.441, and delivery failed at 12:16:34.942.

## Evidence

- **Production incident:** on 2026-11-07, a session failed at 07:47:26 and again at 08:08:29, 1–3 seconds after each `sessions_send`-ing run of a scheduled CI follow-up job finished (07:47:23, 08:08:28). The same error also appears on 2026-10-23, 10-24 and 11-06, and never before 2026-10-23.
- **Regression tests** in `operator-run-cancellation.test.ts`:
  - Ending the sender's occurrence: fails on base, passes with the fix.
  - Cleaning up the sender's session: fails at the first commit, passes with the second.
  - Revoking the device still stops the turn.
- **End-to-end:** isolated in-process Gateway with real cron scheduling, agent loop and tools, and a scripted model. A scheduled run sends to another session, ends and deletes itself while the receiver is held mid-turn; the receiver then calls a tool and finishes.
  - **Base** (`e60517b`): fails. The scheduled run finishes and its job is removed while the receiver is held. Once released, the receiver's turn ends with "Your request couldn't be completed.", the same banner seen in production.
  - **Fix:** passes. The receiver calls `sessions` patch and posts its final reply.
  - **Not committed:** the repo recently removed a similar 500-line real-Gateway test under the test cost budget. The e2e has a scripted model, so it isn't a live-model run; a live model can't reliably reproduce the timing.
- **Related suites:** 122 files and 1,522 tests pass (gateway authority, Talk, chat.send, agent-turn admission, `sessions_send`, restart recovery, cron operator source, subagent completion), plus a re-run of the recovery and cancellation suites after the second commit (78 tests).
- **Checks:** `tsgo:core` and `tsgo:core:test` pass; commit hooks ran.
- **Independent review:** found one P2, the sender-session cleanup gap. It is verified and fixed in the second commit. No scope or model widening was found.

## What Problem This Solves Implements #150029 by adding the strict config option `cron.announce.inspectLinks` with values `always`, `errors`, and `never`. The default is `always`, preserving existing behavior. This supersedes #175817, which was closed unmerged. The approach is rebased onto current `main` and additionally proves that the policy applies to isolated agent-run announcements through the shared delivery append path. ## Behavior - `always`: include Control UI `Inspect` links on successful completion announcements and failure alerts (backward-compatible default). - `errors`: include links only on failure alerts. - `never`: omit links from both successful completion announcements and failure alerts. - Applies to isolated/direct cron completion delivery, successful completion announcements, failure alerts, and isolated agent-run announcements that share `sendCronAnnouncePayloadStrict`. - Webhook delivery is unchanged; the setting only governs chat announcement links. ## Changes - Add `src/cron/inspect-links.ts` with the policy resolver and `shouldIncludeCronInspectLink`. - Add the strict `cron.announce.inspectLinks` schema under `cron`. - Apply the policy at the shared delivery append path in `src/cron/delivery.ts`, with an explicit completion/error kind for failure alerts. - Gate link generation in `server-cron-completion.ts`, `server-cron-notifications.ts`, and isolated agent delivery dispatch. - Document the option in `docs/gateway/config-automation.md` and `docs/automation/cron-jobs/delivery.md`. - Refresh generated config baseline hashes/counts. - Add `config/test-lines-allocations/194794-cron-inspect-links.txt` (126 lines, exact measured net test LF growth) for the test-lines ratchet. ## Evidence Focused tests: ```text pnpm vitest run src/config/zod-schema.core.test.ts src/cron/delivery.failure-notify.test.ts src/cron/isolated-agent.delivery-awareness.test.ts src/gateway/server-cron-completion.test.ts Test Files 4 passed (4) Tests 59 passed (59) ``` Schema / generated baseline: ```text pnpm check:base-config-schema [base-config-schema] ok pnpm config:docs:check OK docs/.generated/config-baseline.sha256 and docs/.generated/config-baseline.counts.json ``` Type checks: ```text pnpm tsgo:core # passed node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p test/tsconfig/tsconfig.core.test.services-cron.json ... node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p test/tsconfig/tsconfig.core.test.gateway-server.json ... # passed ``` Formatting / whitespace: ```text oxfmt --check All matched files use the correct format. git diff --check # passed ``` ## Review notes - Branch is one commit on top of base `0d1666f71`. - No merge is requested here;
