prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`docs/channels/whatsapp.md` describes markdown conversion before chunking but never documents `channels.whatsapp.markdown.tables`, even though the shared channel account shape accepts it and every WhatsApp send resolves the mode at runtime. Users have no documented way to change table rendering for WhatsApp, while Signal, Telegram, Twitch and Nextcloud Talk all document the same key.

- Problem: `channels.whatsapp.markdown.tables` is missing from the WhatsApp docs.
- Solution: document the accepted values, the runtime default, the `block` fallback and the per-account override in the text chunking accordion, and list the key in the configuration pointer table.
- What changed: `docs/channels/whatsapp.md` (2 lines).
- What did NOT change: no code or behavior changes; documentation only.

## Why This Change Was Made

The key is live configuration, not a schema leftover: `buildChannelAccountSchemaParts` injects `markdown` into the shape WhatsApp spreads into both the root section and each named account, and `resolveMarkdownTableMode` reads it on the outbound and monitor paths. The wording mirrors `docs/channels/signal.md` ("`off | bullets | code` (default `bullets`); `block` falls back to `code`") because WhatsApp applies the identical fallback in `markdownToWhatsAppChunks`, so the two channel pages now agree on the same shared key.

## User Impact

Users can discover the table mode for WhatsApp, its `bullets` default, that `block` is accepted but renders like `code`, and the `channels.whatsapp.accounts.<id>.markdown.tables` override without reading source. No behavior changes.

## Evidence

**Schema** — `src/config/zod-schema.channel-messaging-common.ts:78` declares `markdown: MarkdownConfigSchema` inside the shared account shape; `src/config/zod-schema.providers-whatsapp.ts:29` spreads `accountShape` into `WhatsAppCommonShape`, which `WhatsAppAccountSchema` (line 45) and `WhatsAppConfigSchema` (line 52) both use.

**Runtime type** — the enum leaf is `src/config/zod-schema.core.ts:491`:

**Default** — `extensions/whatsapp/src/shared.ts:212` sets the channel plugin default that the resolver falls back to:


`src/config/markdown-tables.ts:47` reads that plugin default, so an omitted key renders `bullets`, not the generic `code` fallback.

**Consumer** — `extensions/whatsapp/src/send.ts:134` and `extensions/whatsapp/src/auto-reply/monitor/inbound-dispatch.ts:399` both call `resolveMarkdownTableMode({ cfg, channel: "whatsapp", accountId })`, and `src/config/markdown-tables.ts:26-37` prefers `accounts.<id>.markdown.tables` before the channel root. prs.title: docs(discord): document the auto-thread per-channel keys
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`extensions/discord/src/config-schema.ts` defines four auto-thread keys on each guild channel entry, and the Discord monitor reads all four on every guild turn, but `docs/channels/discord/threads-and-sessions.md` documents none of them. The page already refers to "auto-threads" when explaining `thread.inheritParent`, so readers meet a feature name with no way to turn it on or tune it.

- Problem: `autoThread`, `autoThreadName`, `autoArchiveDuration` and `includeThreadStarter` are missing from the Discord docs (a grep for `autoThread` across the Discord doc tree only reaches an unrelated mention in `access-control.md`).
- Solution: document each key with its accepted values, runtime default, applicable scope, and per-account override in the existing "Thread behavior" list.
- What changed: `docs/channels/discord/threads-and-sessions.md` (4 lines).
- What did NOT change: no code or behavior changes; documentation only.

## Why This Change Was Made

Each key is live configuration with regression coverage, so the "History, context, and thread behavior" accordion is the place readers already look for thread keys, next to `thread.inheritParent` which is documented there. The wording follows the `channels.discord.guilds.<guild>.channels.<channel>.<key>` pattern already used by the `requireMention` bullet two lines below, and the `generated` naming note restates the JSDoc shipped with `autoThreadName`.

## User Impact

Users can now enable auto-threads per guild channel, choose between message-derived and model-generated thread names, pick one of the four archive windows, and drop the thread starter from follow-up context, without reading `threading.auto-thread.ts`. No behavior changes.

## Evidence

**Schema** — `extensions/discord/src/config-schema.ts:67-88` declares all four keys on `DiscordGuildChannelSchema` through `buildGroupEntrySchema`:

```typescript
includeThreadStarter: z.boolean().optional(),
autoThread: z.boolean().optional(),
autoThreadName: z.enum(["message", "generated"]).optional(),
autoArchiveDuration: z.union([z.enum(["60", "1440", "4320", "10080"]), z.literal(60), ...]).optional(),
```

**Runtime type** — the enum leaves are inline at line 76 (`["message", "generated"]`) and line 80 (`["60", "1440", "4320", "10080"]`, also accepted as numbers), so no value outside those sets is documented.

**Default** — `autoThread` is off unless set, since `extensions/discord/src/monitor/threading.auto-thread.ts:158` returns early without a truthy `channelConfig.autoThread`. The archive window falls back to `60` at `threading.auto-thread.ts:204-206`. `includeThreadStarter` defaults to true at `extensions/discord/src/monitor/message-handler.context.ts:295`:

```typescript
const includeThreadStarter = channelConfig?.includeThreadStarter !== false;
```

**Consumer** — `threading.auto-thread.ts:158` gates creation, `:161-169` skips forum, media, voice and stage channels, `:195-199` skips bot-authored messages, `:204` passes `autoArchiveDuration`, and `:220` renames the new thread only when `autoThreadName === "generated"`. `message-handler.context.ts:190` and `:295` consume `autoThread` and `includeThreadStarter` for context assembly. Scope is confirmed by `extensions/discord/src/config-schema.ts:198` and `:245`, where `guilds` sits on the account base inherited by both `channels.discord` and `channels.discord.accounts.<id>`.

prs.title: docs(signal): document the group ingest option
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`docs/channels/signal.md` enumerates the supported fields of `channels.signal.groups` twice — once in the Groups section and once in the Provider options list — and both enumerations stop at `requireMention`, `tools` and `toolsBySender`. `ingest` is a live field of the same group entry: it is what makes mention-skipped group messages reach the internal `message:received` hook, and nothing in the Signal docs points at it.

- Problem: `channels.signal.groups.*.ingest` is undocumented while the pages that claim to list the group-entry fields omit it.
- Solution: add `ingest` to both enumerations and state what it does, what it does not do, and how the `"*"` entry and the default behave.
- What changed: `docs/channels/signal.md` (3 lines).
- What did NOT change: no code or behavior changes; documentation only.

## Why This Change Was Made

The two enumerations are the places readers already go to for per-group overrides, and each is written as an exhaustive list, so the missing field reads as "not supported" rather than "not mentioned". Telegram documents the identical group `ingest` option on its own access-control page, so leaving it out of Signal breaks the cross-channel symmetry users rely on. The wording follows the runtime contract verified below: mention-gated messages stay in the group history window, `ingest` only adds hook delivery, and the check is strictly `=== true`.

## User Impact

Users can discover and set `ingest: true` to observe mention-skipped group messages through `message:received` hooks — for example to log or route group chatter without waking the agent — and can tell that it never starts a turn, that `"*"` supplies the value for entries that leave it unset, and that omitting it keeps the hook silent. No behavior changes.

## Evidence

**Schema** — `extensions/signal/src/config-schema.ts:155-160` declares the field on the group entry:

```typescript
const SignalGroupEntrySchema = buildGroupEntrySchema(
  { ingest: z.boolean().optional() },
  { omit: ["skills", "enabled", "allowFrom", "systemPrompt"] },
);
```

**Runtime type** — plain `z.boolean().optional()`, no enum leaf to track. `buildGroupEntrySchema` (`src/channels/plugins/config-schema.ts:75-89`) starts from `ChannelGroupEntrySchema` (`:60-69`: `requireMention`, `tools`, `toolsBySender`, `skills`, `enabled`, `allowFrom`, `systemPrompt`) and drops the four omitted keys, so the documented set `requireMention`, `tools`, `toolsBySender`, `ingest` is exactly the accepted set for a Signal group entry.

**Default** — off. `extensions/signal/src/monitor/event-handler.ts:1060` requires a strict `true`:

```typescript
(signalGroupPolicy.groupConfig?.ingest ?? signalGroupPolicy.defaultConfig?.ingest) === true
```

The fallback chain is per-group entry, then the `"*"` entry (`src/config/group-policy.ts:128`: `const defaultConfig = groups?.["*"]`), then unset — so an omitted `ingest` never fires the hook.

**Consumer** — `extensions/signal/src/monitor/event-handler.ts:1020-1092`, inside the `isGroup && requireMention && canDetectMention && mentionDecision.shouldSkip` branch. The skipped message is logged, recorded into the group history window, and then — only under the condition above — handed to `fireAndForgetHook(triggerInternalHook(createInternalHookEvent("message", "received", …)))` before the branch `return`s without dispatching a turn. The event name matches the canonical hook documented in `docs/automation/hooks/event-types.md:33` (`message:received`). Scope comes from `extensions/signal/src/config-schema.ts:162` and the account base, so it applies to `channels.signal.groups` and `channels.signal.accounts.<id>.groups` alike.

**Test** — `extensions/signal/src/monitor/event-handler.mention-gating.test.ts:243` exercises the inherited form with `"*": { requireMention: true, ingest: true }`.

- `node scripts/check-docs-config-examples.mjs` (`pnpm docs:check-config-examples`) — pass, 1,421 files, 1,381 fences validated

prs.title: docs(line): document the thread binding policy keys
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`extensions/line/src/config-schema.ts` attaches the shared thread-binding object to the LINE config, and LINE is one of the channels whose ACP bindings that policy governs — `docs/channels/line.md` even documents `/acp spawn <agent> --bind here`. But a grep for `threadBindings` in that page returns nothing, so LINE readers cannot discover the per-channel or per-account override, while Discord, Matrix, and Telegram each document the same keys on their own pages.

- Problem: `channels.line.threadBindings` and `channels.line.accounts.<id>.threadBindings` are undocumented, including the accepted keys and their defaults.
- Solution: list the accepted keys with the defaults the resolver applies, name both scopes, link the shared thread-bound-sessions page, and state what `enabled: false` does on LINE.
- What changed: `docs/channels/line.md` (2 lines).
- What did NOT change: no code or behavior changes; documentation only.

## Why This Change Was Made

The ACP support section is where the page already tells readers that LINE takes conversation bindings, so the policy that turns those bindings on or off belongs beside it rather than in a config list the reader has to leave the page for. The two bullets reuse the sibling Discord, Matrix, and Telegram wording for the same shared keys instead of inventing LINE-specific names, and the default values are taken from the resolver rather than from the schema, because every key is `.optional()` and the fallback lives in `resolveThreadBindingSpawnPolicy`. The expiry keys are linked out instead of restated, since `resolveThreadBindingIdleTimeoutMs` owns those numbers.

## User Impact

Operators can disable thread-bound spawns and ACP bindings for LINE alone (or for one LINE account) without touching `session.threadBindings` globally, can raise or lower the idle and maximum-age windows per channel, and can see that ordinary LINE messages keep working when bindings are switched off. No behavior changes.

## Evidence

**Schema** — `extensions/line/src/config-schema.ts:13-21` defines the accepted keys and `:50` attaches them to the shared LINE base:

```typescript
const ThreadBindingsSchema = z
  .object({
    enabled: z.boolean().optional(),
    idleHours: z.number().optional(),
    maxAgeHours: z.number().optional(),
    spawnSessions: z.boolean().optional(),
    defaultSpawnContext: z.enum(["isolated", "fork"]).optional(),
  })
  .strict();
```

**Runtime type** — the enum leaf is written inline at `:19`, so `isolated` and `fork` are the only accepted `defaultSpawnContext` values (tracked to the `z.enum` call, not inferred from a type name). `LineCommonConfigSchemaBase` (`:29`) is extended by `LineAccountConfigSchema` (`:58`) and wrapped by `buildMultiAccountChannelSchema` (`:62`), which is why the same block is valid at the channel root and under `channels.line.accounts.<id>`.

**Default** — the values come from the resolver, not from `.default()`: `src/channels/thread-bindings-policy.ts:127-131` falls back to `true` for `enabled`, `:131-136` to `true` for `spawnSessions`, and `:137-141` to `"fork"` for `defaultSpawnContext`, each in account → channel → `session.threadBindings` → built-in order. `idleHours` and `maxAgeHours` resolve through `resolveThreadBindingIdleTimeoutMsForChannel` (`:149-160`) and `resolveThreadBindingMaxAgeMsForChannel` (`:162-173`); the paragraph links the shared page instead of restating those numbers.

**Consumer** — `src/channels/thread-bindings-policy.ts:100-110` reads `channels[channel].threadBindings` and then the resolved account entry, keyed by the channel id string, so LINE is handled by the same path as Discord and Telegram. `src/auto-reply/reply/commands-acp/bindings.ts:91` returns `formatThreadBindingDisabledError` for a blocked bind — and that message (`src/channels/thread-bindings-policy.ts:180`) interpolates the channel, telling the operator to set `channels.line.threadBindings.enabled=true`. The spawn side reaches the same policy through `src/agents/spawn-plan.ts:177` and `src/agents/tools/sessions-spawn-thread-availability.ts`. Ordinary inbound LINE handling never consults the policy — `grep -rn threadBindings extensions/line/src` matches only the schema file — which is why the added text says LINE messaging keeps working.

**Sibling docs** — `docs/channels/discord/threads-and-sessions.md:121-131`, `docs/channels/matrix/threads-and-sessions.md:85-94`, and `docs/channels/telegram/threads-and-sessions.md:49-55` already document these same keys, including the `spawnSessions` default of `true`, the `defaultSpawnContext` default of `"fork"`, and the deprecated `spawnSubagentSessions`/`spawnAcpSessions` keys migrated by `openclaw doctor --fix`. The LINE bullets reuse that vocabulary and leave the migration note where it already lives.

**Test** — `src/channels/thread-bindings-policy.test.ts:52` pins the per-channel form (`channels.discord.threadBindings.spawnSessions: false`) and `:66-67` pins the account-over-channel precedence the LINE schema feeds into.

**Docs toolchain** — all run against this exact head:
- `node scripts/check-docs-config-examples.mjs` (`pnpm docs:check-config-examples`) — pass
- `node scripts/check-docs-mdx.mjs docs/channels/line.md` (`pnpm docs:check-mdx`) — pass, 1 file
- `node scripts/docs-link-audit.mjs` (`pnpm docs:check-links`) — 16,399 internal links, 0 broken
- `node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs scripts/format-docs.mts --check` (`pnpm format:docs:check`) — clean, 1,413 files
- `git diff --check` — clean
- Autoreview was not run locally on this host; CI runs it on this exact head.

**Proof boundary** — this is a documentation discoverability fix for an option that is already resolved at runtime; the LINE and thread-binding implementation is unchanged, so no runtime reproduction applies.

**Exact head** — `90f6e6cf9a16b7f80c5ffd9394673f4deceebbc6`

prs.title: docs(cli): document the onboard team flag
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`openclaw onboard` registers `--team` (`src/cli/program/register.onboard.ts:273`) and `openclaw setup` registers the same flag (`src/cli/program/register.setup.ts:67`), but `docs/cli/onboard.md` is the page that enumerates the onboarding flags and its `## Flags` list has no `--team` entry — a grep for `--team` in that page returns nothing. `docs/start/wizard.md` explains the team flow and `docs/cli/setup.md:99` even refers readers to "the same small-team onboarding as `onboard --team`", so the referenced flag is undocumented exactly where a user looks it up.

- Problem: `--team` is missing from the `openclaw onboard` flag reference: what it creates, how `--agent-name` interacts with it, where member workspaces land, and which onboarding modes reject it.
- Solution: add a `--team` bullet to `## Flags`, beside the `--agent-name` bullet it modifies, with the roster, the coordinator naming rules, the per-member workspace layout, the rejected mode combinations, the existing-roster refusal, and a link to the wizard section that owns the flow narrative.
- What changed: `docs/cli/onboard.md` (12 lines).
- What did NOT change: no code or behavior changes; documentation only. `docs/start/wizard.md` and `docs/cli/setup.md` keep their existing team text.

## Why This Change Was Made

The flag belongs in the per-command flag list rather than only in the narrative page, because `## Flags` is where this page documents every other onboarding option, including `--agent-name`, whose behavior `--team` changes. The wording states the numbers that come from code (the `coordinator` fallback name, the four roster ids, the `<workspace>/<agent-id>` layout) and leaves the recovery, receipt, and `systemAgent` semantics to `/start/wizard`, which already documents them, so the page keeps one owner per fact instead of duplicating the wizard's prose.

## User Impact

Users see that `openclaw onboard --team` creates a coordinator plus researcher, writer, and reviewer instead of one agent, know that `--agent-name` names the coordinator and that omitting it yields `coordinator`, know each member gets its own workspace subfolder, and learn up front that `--team` is refused with classic, remote, or import onboarding and with an existing agent roster. No behavior changes.

## Evidence

**CLI registration** — `src/cli/program/register.onboard.ts:273` declares the option and its help text, and `:188` narrows it before it reaches the command layer:

```typescript
team: opts.team === true ? true : undefined,
```

`src/cli/program/register.setup.ts:67` registers the identical option for `openclaw setup`, which is why `docs/cli/setup.md:99` can point at `onboard --team`.

**Runtime default** — the documented `coordinator` name is the code fallback, not a schema default: `src/commands/onboard-non-interactive/local.ts:358` is `const firstAgentName = opts.agentName ?? (opts.team ? "coordinator" : "main");` and the interactive path derives the same suggestion from the preset at `src/commands/onboard-first-agent.ts:35` (`const defaultName = teamPreset?.coordinator.id ?? "main";`), whose prompt message switches to **"What should we call your chief of staff?"** at `:41-43` when a team is selected. `loadAgentTeamPreset` (`src/agents/agent-roles.ts:90`) reads `docs/reference/templates/roles/presets/team.json`, which lists `coordinator` plus the specialists `researcher`, `writer`, and `reviewer` — the exact ids the new bullet names.

**Consumer** — three runtime paths consume the flag, and each documented constraint is one of them. `src/commands/onboard.ts:502-512` rejects `--team` when the mode is remote, when `--import-from`, `--import-source`, or `--flow import` is set, or when classic interactive setup is requested, with "--team supports local guided or non-interactive onboarding." `src/commands/onboard-guided.ts:118-121` (guided) and `src/commands/onboard-non-interactive/local.ts:350-356` (non-interactive) both refuse `--team` when `hasAuthoredRoster` is true and point at `openclaw agents team create`, and `src/commands/onboard-agent.ts:92-98` repeats that guard at creation time. On the effect side `src/commands/onboard-agent.ts:136-143` calls `createAgentTeam({ coordinator: firstAgentName, workspaceRoot })`, and `src/agents/agent-team.ts:133` sets each member's workspace to `path.join(workspaceRoot, member.id)` — the `<workspace>/<agent-id>` layout in the bullet.

**Not a dead flag** — `--team` is not CLI-parser-only: the same value reaches `createAgentTeam`, which writes roster entries, per-member workspaces, and coordinator delegation config. The chosen coordinator also becomes part of the local onboarding state (`teamCoordinatorId`, `src/state/local-onboarding-state.ts:48`), and `src/commands/onboard-guided.ts:122-125` reads it back so an interrupted team run resumes with the same coordinator instead of prompting again.

**Test** — `src/commands/onboard-non-interactive/local.default-agent.test.ts:358` ("creates a role team through non-interactive onboarding and keeps coordinator ownership") runs `runSetup({ workspace, team: true, json: true })` and pins `Object.keys(agents.entries)` to `["coordinator", "researcher", "writer", "reviewer"]` at `:376-381` plus `workspace: path.join(workspace, "coordinator")` at `:384`. `src/commands/onboard.test.ts:865` pins flag parsing through the guided route ("keeps `--team` on guided onboarding") and `src/cli/program/register.onboard.test.ts:254` parses `--non-interactive --accept-risk --team`.

**Sibling docs** — `docs/start/wizard.md:186-206` already states the local-only restriction, the `openclaw agents team create` alternative for an existing roster, and the `--workspace` parent-directory rule; the new bullet reuses that vocabulary and links its `#choose-one-agent-or-a-team` heading instead of restating it. `docs/cli/setup.md:99-100` already documents `setup --team` and the coordinator naming.

**Docs toolchain** — all run against this exact head:
- `node scripts/check-docs-config-examples.mjs` (`pnpm docs:check-config-examples`) — pass
- `node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs scripts/check-docs-mdx.mjs docs/cli/onboard.md` — pass, 1 file
- `node scripts/docs-link-audit.mjs` (`pnpm docs:check-links`) — 16,399 internal links, 0 broken
- `node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs scripts/format-docs.mts --check` (`pnpm format:docs:check`) — clean, 1,413 files
- `git diff --check` — clean
- Autoreview was not run locally on this host; CI runs it on this exact head.

**Proof boundary** — documentation only; the onboarding flag, its validation, and team creation are unchanged, so no runtime reproduction applies. The behavior the bullet states is pinned by the existing tests named above.

prs.title: fix(gateway): parent prompt cache misses when a subagent settles
prs.body:
Closes #195328

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: the parent conversation loses its prompt cache when a subagent announce, settle, or steer turn runs, because `skill_library` disappears from the deferred tool directory.

## User Impact

User impact: a conversation that can author personal skills keeps the same `skill_library` definition on those turns, and a turn with no human requester still cannot author or publish a skill.

## Why This Change Was Made

The session records the skill-library prompt listing from the last eligible human turn. Later announce, settle, and steer turns keep that definition and are refused at execution. A later attributed human turn refreshes the listing when presentation changes. Sessions that were never eligible still omit the tool.

## Evidence

- `pnpm test src/gateway/skill-library-authoring.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` passed, 10 tests, 14.9s after compiler warmup (44.3s on the cold run, including worker preparation). The new regression compares the tooling section for a human grant, a settle grant, and the next human grant; the settle call is gated and does not publish; a stored listing alone reproduces the definition after a fresh process key; a settle before any listing does not advertise the tool.
- Targeted oxlint passed for the touched gateway, config, agents, plugins, and skills files.
- Test-line allocation: `config/test-lines-allocations/skill-library-settle-prompt-cache.txt` is 127.

### Shipped Gateway trace

Repo CLI gateway (`scripts/run-node.mjs`) with a local mock model, session `agent:qa:skill-library-proof`. All four turns finished `status: ok`.

1. Human `chat.send`: "skill library proof. List the personal library." The mock called `dispatch_action` → `skill_library` `{ action: "list" }`. Transcript result: `skill_library { "entries": [], "omitted": 0, "nextAction": "Use My skills for the complete library. Read a selected skill before editing." }`.
2. Human `chat.send`: `sessions_spawn` task "Reply exactly PONG". Spawn was accepted for an isolated child. The child provider request had no `skill_library` directory line. The parent then received the background completion ("A background task completed" / inter-session message) and the assistant text was `PONG`.
3. Human `chat.send`: "skill library proof. List the personal library again." The list succeeded with the same empty-library result.
4. Non-human `agent` request on the same session, carrying a `task_completion` internal event with `source: "subagent"` (the completion shape announce delivers). The mock again called `skill_library` `{ action: "list" }`. Transcript result: "Personal skill library authoring runs only when the person sends the request in this conversation. This turn has no human requester, so the call was not run."

The deferred directory line was present and byte-identical on every parent provider request, including the spawn/settle continuation and the non-human completion:

`- skill_library (core): Author skills in the requesting person's personal library. Actions: list | read | create | update | share | unshare | transfer | activate | remove | rollback. List takes only ac`

The isolated child request did not include that line.

### Latest stable data

OpenClaw 2026.11.2 (`b556fdf`) wrote the session with `agent --local` against an isolated state directory. That release has `skillLibrarySelections` and does not have `skillLibraryPromptListing`. Stable session admission then stored label `upgrade-proof` and one selection (`name: "proof-skill"`). Settings on the row: `modelProvider: fixture`, `model: held-responses`, `thinkingLevel: off`, `verboseLevel: on`, `contextTokens: 8192`. Transcript: user "Reply with the single word STABLE_OK", assistant "STABLE_OK" (7 transcript events).

This branch's `openclaw doctor --fix` migrated that isolated state. The session row hash stayed `6275b9d0c4443019cdbf0ba3ba2c455933fd36b87374f2a3cf04033b7c0289c0`. The raw `entry_json` still has no `skillLibraryPromptListing`. `loadSessionEntry` and `loadTranscriptEventsSync` on this branch returned the same label, model, thinking level, verbose level, context token count, selection, and the user/assistant transcript texts.

prs.title: fix: node directory listing pages until the gateway stops
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Node directory listing stops after 32 pages so one oversized directory cannot pin the gateway. Bootstrap discovery used that stop to skip the directory, then still loaded a sibling, but it recorded no diagnostic. A configured `*/AGENTS.md` file inside the oversized directory disappeared with `diagnostics: []`.

## Evidence

Head `b06896ea3a7` on macOS Darwin arm64, Node v26.12.1. The production trace below was run on `055d09e2943`. `b06896ea3a7` merges current main and adds the 112-line test grant. It does not change the listing or the diagnostic. A real directory held 131073 empty names, which is one past 32 pages of 4096. Its sibling `keep/AGENTS.md` contained `kept instructions`. Production `createNodeWorkspaceBridge` listed that tree. Each `dir.list` call went to production `handleDirList` on that directory, not a scripted page payload. `loadExtraBootstrapFilesWithDiagnostics` then loaded `*/AGENTS.md`.

```console
OK: files=kept instructions diagnostics=[{"dir":"fat","reason":"io","detail":"Directory listing exceeded 32 pages"}] dirList=34 stat=0 fetch=1
```

`dir.list` ran 34 times: one page for the root, 32 pages for the oversized directory, and one page for the sibling. `file.fetch` read the sibling once. The oversized directory is named in the diagnostic and its instructions were not loaded.

## Real behavior proof

- **Behavior or issue addressed:** Bootstrap discovery skips one directory after the real 32-page listing cap, records that skip, and still loads a sibling `AGENTS.md`.
- **Real environment tested:** macOS Darwin arm64, Node v26.12.1, head `055d09e2943` in `/tmp/oc-165805`, then merged forward as `b06896ea3a7` without changing the listing or the diagnostic. The directory was a local folder with 131073 names. The node command handler and the gateway bridge ran in one process.
- **Exact steps or command run after this patch:** Created the oversized directory and `keep/AGENTS.md`. Called `createNodeWorkspaceBridge` with `invoke` dispatching to `handleDirList`, `handleFileStat`, and `handleFileFetch`. Called `loadExtraBootstrapFilesWithDiagnostics` for `*/AGENTS.md`.
- **Evidence after fix:** terminal output from that production path:

```console
OK: files=kept instructions diagnostics=[{"dir":"fat","reason":"io","detail":"Directory listing exceeded 32 pages"}] dirList=34 fetch=1
```

- **Observed result after fix:** The sibling file was loaded. The oversized directory produced one `io` diagnostic, `Directory listing exceeded 32 pages`, after 32 real listing pages.
- **What was not tested:** A second OS process enrolled as a node over the gateway websocket. The same handlers ran in-process.

## Summary

A directory past the listing page budget is still skipped, and its sibling still loads. The skip is now a diagnostic instead of a silent omission.

prs.title: fix: preserve assistant answers when media delivery reuses response indexes
prs.body:
Closes #166536

## What Problem This Solves

Distinct assistant responses can be suppressed when retries reuse content indexes or repeat text and images. Streamed media and recovered answers can also end up attached to the wrong response during finalization.

## User Impact

Each physical response keeps its own delivery and transcript identity. Streamed images survive finalization, source images remain visible alongside TTS audio, and canonical provider content and signatures remain intact. This prevents further corruption; it does not repair previously altered history.

## Why This Change Was Made

Upstream #177049 (`0d7df3fc2cf6bc9c53b04f7857b7cbca61b3c927`) now owns `AgentAssistantSourceReceipt` and exact transcript-anchor enrichment. This correction reuses that owner and removes the competing receipt pipeline. The remaining changes scope delivery dedupe, aggregate coverage, streamed-media finalization and timeout-recovery custody to each physical response.

Published head: `8716154f8d06ff3609f62f583c7c48df2ff6ed3a`. A normal merge of main `cf2558f5639e273dc4fe1f19e9c5f7715dc8d0de` preserves the original PR history. No force-push, schema/configuration change, signing infrastructure or release publication is included. Maintainer edits remain enabled.

## Evidence

- Final complete affected Gateway suites: 149/149 passed, no skips, including committed/suppressed/indexed/unkeyed/owned source-media plus TTS cases.
- Commentary media: 18/18 passed. Focused unchanged agent/autoreply owners passed 43 unit-fast, 52 auto-reply, 36 lifecycle and 34 terminal tests; real subscription dispatch cases also passed.
- Main-production controls reproduced the occurrence and recovered-answer failures. Real transcript regressions reproduced TTS selection, append-key and owned-rewrite losses before their repairs.
- Type-aware lint on all 19 changed source files, production core typecheck, formatting and diff checks passed.
- The initial committed correction and the subsequent CI test repair each received fresh independent P2 review with no actionable findings.
- CI run [39902028749](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39902028749) exposed two test-type defects and a stale unkeyed fenced-stream lookup. All reproduced locally. The follow-up repairs only test callers: source-aware lookup with an unkeyed negative control, required assertion diagnostics, and the fixture return type tied to the real transcript writer.
- Repair proof: 185 focused tests passed (134 Gateway and 51 agents; 182.39 seconds wall time including fixture/compiler startup), both affected test-type configurations passed, and targeted lint, formatting, diff and staged line-cap checks passed. The final fixture adjustment is type-only; Gateway types were rechecked afterward. [Hosted CI on this exact head](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39909500750) completed successfully. GitHub reports 78 passing checks, 54 skipped and no failing or pending checks; the consolidated CI, dependency-review and security-sensitive-review statuses passed.

Mandatory exact-candidate Telegram Test Server proof remains unperformed. The checked authoring hosts lack the existing launcher/broker access; no live lease was allocated. Local tests and earlier real model/media/compaction observations do not replace the requested reused-index Telegram scenario. The [existing QA handoff](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/166568#issuecomment-6087119969) records that gap for upstream review. It does not prevent contributor submission; no local signing setup is requested.

prs.title: fix: queued follow-up goes unanswered after a delayed /stop or /status
prs.body:
Closes #194303

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: a follow-up that is already the next persisted user turn is never answered when a delayed `/stop` or `/status` command exchange lands before that turn is replayed.

## User Impact

User impact: after `/stop` (and `/status` in the same window), the queued follow-up is answered once instead of being dropped. Ordinary commands such as `/model`, and newer user messages, still supersede that older turn. The command exchange stays in the transcript.

## Why This Change Was Made

A delayed command exchange can become the current turn even though a later user message was already persisted. The walk that selects the current turn now crosses context-free commands (including `/status`) and `/stop` exchanges, so the already-persisted follow-up stays the admitted turn.

Reparenting that follow-up would rewrite its admission anchor. Holding the next persist across abort settlement can deadlock Stop. This change keeps those producer-side options out of the path and does not let replay cross ordinary context-bearing commands.

The `/stop` marker (`preservesInFlightTurn`) is set by the command recorder when the command text is an abort. It is stored message metadata, not a caller-selectable parameter on the public command-exchange APIs.

## Evidence

Focused regression (`attempt-session-replay.command-exchange.test.ts`): a delayed `/stop` or `/status` exchange is injected after replay preparation on both reader paths. Without the change, admission throws `Persisted user turn changed before replay admission`. With it, the follow-up is answered exactly once; the model prompt contains that follow-up once and does not treat `/stop` or `/status` as the user question. A later `/model` exchange or a newer plain user message still fails admission of the older follow-up. GitHub CI on `e418fb5221cd` was green (88 successful checks). A follow-up commit (`08e8a771e04e`) keeps `preservesInFlightTurn` internal to the recorder and does not change that runtime behavior.

Live isolated Gateway on Linux, using a local holding model, against current `main` (`7726572226387e4f6c0400a6d0667a5fd153a677`) and this branch at `e418fb5221cd3e99c5d9502986236ca41688d631` (the later type-only follow-up does not change these receipts). The command abort or status reply is produced immediately, delivery is held, a follow-up user row is persisted, then the held exchange is released so those rows land immediately after the follow-up:

- Delayed `/stop`: current main left the follow-up unanswered in 3 of 3 runs (0 model requests; `No answer was returned. Ask again if you still need one.`). This branch answered that follow-up exactly once in 3 of 3 runs (`ANSWER_FOR FOLLOWUP_BRANCH_STOP_N`). The `/stop` rows on this branch carry `preservesInFlightTurn: true`.
- Delayed `/status`: current main left the follow-up unanswered in 3 of 3 runs (same silent drop). This branch answered that follow-up exactly once in 3 of 3 runs (`ANSWER_FOR FOLLOWUP_BRANCH_STATUS_N`). The `/status` rows carry `contextFreeCommand: true` and were not treated as the user question.

The named admission-error text was not printed on these live runs. On current main the follow-up run exits without a model request after the delayed command rows land; the focused regression remains the inspectable source of `Persisted user turn changed before replay admission`.

Upgrade and stored-data compatibility from `v2026.11.1` (`4ffdd2047d192dd65554de3c8c46c0e0197c6e2a`): a session created on that release (13 rows, including answered follow-ups, `/fast on`, a `/stop` without the new flag, and `/status`) was opened with this branch after the normal session-database schema upgrade. All 13 pre-upgrade rows loaded unchanged, and session settings including `fastMode: true` were preserved. A new follow-up on that upgraded session was answered (`FOLLOWUP_UPG_NEW_1 still there?` → `ANSWER_FOR FOLLOWUP_UPG_NEW_1`). A new `/stop` written after the upgrade received `preservesInFlightTurn: true` without rewriting the v2026.11.1 `/stop` (`preservesInFlightTurn` stayed unset/false on that older row).

<details>
<summary>Redacted live receipts (persistence, delayed command recording, admission, one answer)</summary>

### Current main, delayed `/stop` (1 of 3; the other two matched)

```
follow-up user row observed in transcript  seenRow=true  followupModelRequestsSoFar=0
released held command reply  released=1
{"modelRequestsForFollowup":0,"modelRequestsWhoseTurnIsCommand":0,"answers":0}

user       LONG_TURN please write a very long essay
user       FOLLOWUP_MAIN_STOP_1 what is two plus two?
user       /stop
assistant  Agent was aborted.
custom     run-failed-before-reply

gateway error: No answer was returned. Ask again if you still need one.
```

### This branch, delayed `/stop` (1 of 3; the other two matched)

```
follow-up user row observed in transcript  seenRow=true  followupModelRequestsSoFar=0
released held command reply  released=1
{"modelRequestsForFollowup":1,"answers":1}

user       LONG_TURN please write a very long essay
user       FOLLOWUP_BRANCH_STOP_1 what is two plus two?
user       /stop                         preservesInFlightTurn=true
assistant  Agent was aborted.            preservesInFlightTurn=true
assistant  ANSWER_FOR FOLLOWUP_BRANCH_STOP_1

model request for the follow-up:
  prompt includes FOLLOWUP_BRANCH_STOP_1 what is two plus two?
  reply: ANSWER_FOR FOLLOWUP_BRANCH_STOP_1
```

### Current main, delayed `/status` (1 of 3; the other two matched)

`/status` does not abort the long turn. The long turn completed, the follow-up was persisted, then the held `/status` exchange landed after it.

```
follow-up user row observed in transcript  seenRow=true  followupModelRequestsSoFar=0
released held command reply  released=1
{"modelRequestsForFollowup":0,"modelRequestsWhoseTurnIsCommand":0,"answers":0}

user       LONG_TURN please write a very long essay
assistant  long turn finished
user       FOLLOWUP_MAIN_STATUS_1 what is two plus two?
user       /status     excludeFromContext=true  contextFreeCommand=true
assistant  Session: agent:main:main • duration 5s • Queue: followup

gateway error: No answer was returned. Ask again if you still need one.
```

### This branch, delayed `/status` (1 of 3; the other two matched)

```
follow-up user row observed in transcript  seenRow=true  followupModelRequestsSoFar=0
released held command reply  released=1
{"modelRequestsForFollowup":1,"modelRequestsWhoseTurnIsCommand":0,"answers":1}

user       LONG_TURN please write a very long essay
assistant  long turn finished
user       FOLLOWUP_BRANCH_STATUS_1 what is two plus two?
user       /status     excludeFromContext=true  contextFreeCommand=true
assistant  Session: agent:main:main • duration 6s • Queue: followup
assistant  ANSWER_FOR FOLLOWUP_BRANCH_STATUS_1

model request for the follow-up:
  prompt includes FOLLOWUP_BRANCH_STATUS_1 what is two plus two?
  reply: ANSWER_FOR FOLLOWUP_BRANCH_STATUS_1
```

### Upgrade from v2026.11.1

On `v2026.11.1` the session had 13 rows, including `ANSWER_FOR FOLLOWUP_UPG_OLD_1`, `/fast on`, a `/stop` without `preservesInFlightTurn`, `ANSWER_FOR FOLLOWUP_UPG_OLD_2`, and `/status`. After opening that same store with this branch:

```
pre-upgrade rows unchanged after upgrade+restart  same=true  oldRows=13  rowsNow=13
session after upgrade: key=agent:main:main  fastMode=true  thinkingDefault=off
                       thinkingOptions=["off","ultra"]

post-upgrade follow-up: FOLLOWUP_UPG_NEW_1 still there? -> ANSWER_FOR FOLLOWUP_UPG_NEW_1

stored /stop rows:
  seq 8  preservesInFlightTurn=false   (created on v2026.11.1)
  seq 19 preservesInFlightTurn=true    (created after upgrade)

pre-upgrade rows still unchanged after new /stop  same=true
```

</details>

prs.title: fix(install): publish git checkouts without Node before it is provisioned
prs.body:
Fixes #195366

## What Problem This Solves

`install.sh --install-method git` fails on any host that does not already have Node. `clone_git_checkout_transactionally` in `scripts/install-policy.sh` published the staging clone with `node - …`, but the git path only provisions Node later, in `ensure_node "$repo_dir"`, which needs the checkout's `engines`. The clone completed, publication hit `node: command not found`, the staging checkout was deleted, and every retry downloaded it again.

## User Impact

On a fresh Debian/LXC or macOS host with no Node, the git install now publishes the checkout and goes on to provision Node as the npm path does. The user no longer gets a misleading "inspect the destination for partial files" error after a full clone.

## Why This Change Was Made

Publication is now a small shell function, `publish_git_clone_staging`, with the same contract as the old Node script:

- **Fresh target:** the target is refused with "Git install dir appeared while cloning" if anything appeared there during the clone; otherwise the staging dir is renamed into place.
- **Existing empty target dir:** the dir must still hold only the staging entry. Entries move with `.git` last, and the staging dir is removed afterwards.
- **Failure:** on a failed move, the moved entries roll back. If rollback also fails, the staging dir is renamed to `.recovery` with the same "recovery files remain" message.

Node bootstrap ordering is unchanged, because the target-engine phase still needs the cloned `package.json`. `install-cli.sh` shares this function through the same policy include.

## Evidence

### Full installer on fresh Debian 13 without Node

This is the assembled-installer run the review asked for. It ran in an isolated WSL Debian GNU/Linux 13 (trixie) as root, where `command -v node` and `command -v npm` both print nothing. The command was `bash install.sh --install-method git --no-onboard --no-prompt`, using the `scripts/install.sh` and `scripts/install-policy.sh` pair from each revision.

![debian proof](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/wr-web/openclaw/proof-assets/195366/proof2.png)

| run | result |
|---|---|
| main `772657222638`, fresh host | The clone completed, then failed with `install-policy.sh: line 518: node: command not found` and "Could not publish the cloned checkout: /root/openclaw". `/root/openclaw` does not exist afterwards, and the script still exits 0. |
| this branch, fresh host | The checkout was published and ref `main` checked out. Then: "Node.js not found, installing it now", "Node.js v24.22.2 installed" via NodeSource, pnpm 12.15.0 via Corepack, dependencies installed, UI and OpenClaw built, wrapper installed. `openclaw --version` prints `OpenClaw 2026.11.1 (51b8257)`. Total time 9m40s. |
| this branch, rerun on that install | After `openclaw config set gateway.port 28799`, the rerun reports "Existing OpenClaw installation detected, upgrading". It reuses `/root/openclaw` (no clone, so the publisher is not involved) and checks out `v2026.11.2` with a clean tree. `gateway.port: 28799` is still in `~/.openclaw/openclaw.json`. That rerun's doctor refused because the state DB schema 39 was written by the newer main build and is newer than the schema 22 that 2026.11.2 supports, and the 2026.11.2 UI build failed on a packaged knowledge manifest. Both are release-state outcomes outside this change. |

### Publisher-level runs (Git Bash)

![proof](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/wr-web/openclaw/proof-assets/195366/proof.png)

| run (PATH without node, real `git clone` of a local repo) | main `772657222638` | this branch `ba5cc37f0ba4` |
|---|---|---|
| fresh target path | `install-policy.sh: line 518: node: command not found`, rc=1, no checkout | rc=0, checkout at HEAD, no staging left |
| existing empty target dir | same failure | rc=0, checkout at HEAD, no staging left |
| target dir appears during clone (existing fixture) | refused, user file kept | refused, user file kept, staging cleaned by `cleanup_tmpfiles` |

Tests:

- **New test:** `test/scripts/install-sh.test.ts` "publishes Git clones before Node is provisioned (#195366)". It shadows `node` with a failing function, then publishes both a fresh target and an empty existing dir. Its shell body passes in Git Bash. Vitest's `runInstallShell` spawns `/bin/bash`, which does not exist on this Windows host, so the bash-based install tests can't run here in Vitest.
- **Existing fixture:** `createInstallGitCloneFixtureScript` ("publishes fresh Git clones only after success…") passes in Git Bash. The symlink-alias step needs symlink privileges this host lacks.
- **Checks:** `bash -n scripts/install-policy.sh`, `oxfmt --check` and `check:test-lines-ratchet` pass.
- **Pre-existing Windows failures:** `standalone-installers.test.ts` fails 6/6 identically on main and on this branch here (symlinks and `/bin/bash`).

prs.title: fix(codex): recover a fresh connection after terminal WebSocket relay failure
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

A settled native Codex turn can report the private inference relay's 502 error with a `ws://127.0.0.1` URL. The transport classifier currently recognizes the corresponding HTTP URL but misses WebSocket URLs, so the failed shared client remains available to later attempts.

## User Impact

After this specific terminal WebSocket relay failure, later attempts use a fresh connection and preserve completed work on the saved thread. Successful native transport fallback remains visible and does not retire the connection.

## Why This Change Was Made

Recognize the same exact relay error with a loopback WebSocket URL. Reuse the existing settled-transport recovery: keep completed work and its transcript, mark replay unsafe, retire the failed pooled client only after the native turn settles, and resume the existing thread on a fresh connection. Foreign-host URLs and unrelated 502 errors keep their existing behavior.

This does not suppress the native “Falling back from WebSockets to HTTPS” warning. Codex emits that warning when it switches transport and may still finish successfully; the successful-warning regression keeps it visible and keeps the usable connection.

## Evidence

- The new owning attempt regression fails on the base because the terminal WebSocket failure leaves the shared client registered.
- The focused fixed cases cover HTTP and WebSocket relay failures, a foreign-host near miss, an unrelated 502, and a successful visible fallback warning. Completed tool work is preserved and is not replayed; recovery uses a new client and resumes the saved thread.
- Five focused owning attempt cases pass; production/test typechecks, lint, formatting, test-line budget, whitespace checks and an independent local review are recorded with this candidate.

The native protocol uses the repository's app-server fixture. No live network outage or model run is claimed. Native fallback semantics were checked against sibling Codex revision 6aaac694803004a63c6f393d153c96d22521a6b9, `codex-rs/core/src/responses_retry.rs:133` and `codex-rs/core/src/client.rs:2454`.

prs.title: fix(cli): expose manualSelectionAllowed in models list inventory
prs.body:
## Summary
- Build the policy-candidate set from `registry.models` prior to `applyModelInventoryPolicyFilter` in `loadModelInventory`, and look up `policyBlocked: true` entries in `buildModelListRow` (`src/commands/models/list.list-command.ts`).
- When a policy-blocked model is still present in the raw registry (`registryKeys.has(key)`), append the `policy-blocked` tag (`toPolicyBlockedModelRow`), preserving `missing: false` while surfacing the manual-selection policy block in `openclaw models list --all` and `--json`.
- Add a focused regression test in `src/commands/models/list.list-command.configured-Order.test.ts` verifying that `models list --all --json` marks available policy-blocked models with `policy-blocked` (`missing: false`) instead of hiding the restriction.

## What Problem This Solves
When `agents.defaults.models` (or an explicit model inventory policy filter) restricts which models can be selected automatically, `openclaw models list --all` (and `--all --json`) still enumerates every model from `registry.models`, but previously dropped the `policyBlocked` metadata from `applyModelInventoryPolicyFilter`. As a result, available models that are blocked by policy appeared identical to unrestricted catalog models in the full inventory output, giving operators no indication why manual selection or routing was blocked by policy (#194738).

## Evidence
- Verified with focused Vitest unit test in `src/commands/models/list.list-command.configured-Order.test.ts` (`marks available models blocked by policy in --all output while keeping missing false`):
  - Input: `registry.models` contains both `openai/gpt-4.1` and `anthropic/claude-sonnet-4-20250514`, while policy filter blocks `anthropic/claude-sonnet-4-20250514` (`policyBlocked: true`).
  - Output of `modelsListCommand({ all: true, json: true }, runtime)`: `anthropic/claude-sonnet-4-20250514` row includes `tags: ["policy-blocked"]` and `missing: false`.
- All 108 CI build, lint (`oxlint` + `oxfmt`), typecheck (`tsgo`), and test checks on PR #194760 passed (`check-lint-core-1`, `checks-node-core-test`, `checks-fast-core`, `checks-fast-baseline-ratchets`, `build-artifacts`, `check-docs`).

Fixes #194738

Qualify the config-load smoke and native plugin worker test for the existing runtime-only preset. The loader smoke is already qualified. Their worker dependencies use production runtime entries; the Node-only config fixture loads its source backend through the existing worker TypeScript loader.

Includes planning/preparation/cleanup, excludes CI checkout/install. No Linux billing saving is claimed.

[Normal CI42527678891](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/42527678891) completed: all9 Node jobs and security checks passed. The mixed validation row retains full worker preparation by design; these results are correctness evidence, not a hosted timing comparison.

prs.title: fix(codex): serialize native completion handoffs and accept yielded input
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Native subagent completions can collide on the parent thread or report failed delivery when a successful parent consumes the result and yields again.

## User Impact

Completion handoffs to the same parent run one at a time and wait while a sibling still owns native execution. A successful optional native handoff that yields again is acknowledged without requiring an immediate visible answer; visible-reply requirements, errors, and aborts remain failures.

## Why This Change Was Made

Serialize the existing delivery attempts per physical parent and defer admission while a live child retains the native subscription. Keep retry and custody checks at their existing owners. When the last live sibling settles, immediately wake only handoffs that were waiting for a sibling; ordinary transport failure backoff is preserved. The direct-response classifier recognizes the narrow native completion family’s successful yielded input separately from delivery of a user-visible final answer.

## Evidence

- Separate regressions fail on the base for early admission while a sibling is running, concurrent terminal-child handoffs, and rejection of a successfully consumed native yielded input.
- 36 focused tests pass across completion contention, monitor delivery, parent retention, and direct-response classification, including all six native-follow-up custody scenarios and both deferred handoffs before advancing the retry clock. Negative cases cover another completion family, a required visible reply, aborted input, and an error.
- Core and Codex production and test TypeScript checks, targeted lint, formatting, pre-commit hooks, and a justified test-line allocation pass. Independent scoped local review found no actionable P0–P2 defects; the root additionally inspected the full response classifier and retry/custody paths.
- Tests exercise the repository’s native app-server and direct Gateway-dispatch fixtures. This current-main source head has not been exercised against a live model.


### Follow-up: deliver through an idle retained parent

At `099560d04`, a live sibling no longer blocks a completion when the retained parent subscription is idle and available for a warm continuation. A cold resume remains deferred while sibling protection is active; a blocked attempt does not exhaust the completion retry budget. The original implementation failed the warm-sibling regression (no delivery); the revised implementation passes it. Four focused suites passed 32 tests before the final structural adjustment, followed by 3 affected tests, targeted lint and commit checks. Independent scoped review found no P0-P2 findings; the reviewer did not execute code. Live Gateway/native Codex validation for this exact revision is still outstanding.


### CI test-line allocation

`feee756dc` adds a separate 38-line allocation for the warm-sibling and cold-resume regression coverage, preserving the tests and global baseline. On the exact failing CI merge tree the test-line ratchet was 6,582,927 / 6,582,889 before the allocation and passed at 6,582,927 / 6,582,927 after it. Exact-head CI is rerunning.


### Wake after interrupted or removed siblings

At `a10617a87`, a waiting completion is retried when the last live sibling becomes resumable or is removed, including while its previous delivery attempt is still settling. The retry retains parent serialization and current custody checks; success does not trigger a duplicate, and shutdown retains detached delivery. The real-monitor regressions failed before this change and pass after it. Forty focused tests, extension typecheck, targeted lint, format, line-cap and test-lines checks passed; independent scoped review found no actionable P0-P2 findings. These are synthetic tests; exact-head live Gateway and model qualification remain outstanding.


### Live backport qualification found an unresolved delivery path

A real-model test of the separately adapted OpenClaw 2026.11.1 Mac backport, not this exact PR head, found a remaining failure with two concurrent native children. The fast child completed while the slow child was still running; the parent continuation attempted cold resume, hit the protected-background cleanup timeout, and the fast completion was retired without delivery. The slow completion was later delivered. This evidence supersedes any inference that the synthetic warm-sibling regression proves production delivery across the full Gateway path. Root cause and exact-head applicability are under investigation; the exact PR head still needs live qualification.


### Live qualification update: exec context and protected relay

On the separately adapted 2026.11.1 Mac runtime, the first failed handoff differed only in the creation-time developer instructions: the direct native completion omitted the current session exec-state hint. A local candidate reconstructed that hint from current agent/session settings without granting execution authority. In a real two-child test, the fast result reached the parent while the slow child was still running, and the slow result arrived later. The candidate is not yet part of this PR.

The same candidate did not fix the separately installed server runtime with bundled Codex 0.164.0: its protected-continuation preflight rejected the fast completion because there was no current parent-local inference relay. The server candidate was reverted; the preflight was not bypassed. The exact upstream head has not been tested live, and server-side delivery across this path remains unresolved.


### Live server backport follow-up

Further diagnosis found that the configured bundled Codex executable and the plugin capture were byte-identical but had distinct paths, so the existing managed-inference ownership check did not recognize the configured binary. A separately adapted release candidate checks the exact bundled executable contents and retains the protected-context guard. In a real-model server run with the bundled Codex 0.164.0, the fast child result reached the same parent while the slow child was still running, then the slow result arrived; a separate same-child followup also completed. No 502 was observed in the test window. A Mac release backport also passed the parallel-child live scenario. These deployed release backports are not this PR head; source changes and exact-head live qualification are still pending.


### Security review: server attestation candidate withdrawn

Independent review found that the release candidate compared the executable only after spawning it, which does not attest the executable actually running, and synchronously hashed large binaries on the Gateway event loop. The candidate has been reverted on the server; the prior successful server live run therefore does not establish that the currently deployed server is fixed. Review also identified a remaining delivery gap if exec policy changes while a sibling is active: cold resume must preserve and retry the completion without granting stale authority. This PR head has not been live-qualified for those cases.


### Managed bundled runtime follow-up

The server now uses OpenClaw's existing managed launcher with `preferInstalled: false`, rather than trusting a configured executable after spawn. The original relay ownership and context checks remain in place. The actual packaged Codex 0.164.0 process was checked, and separately adapted release backports passed live parallel-child and same-child followup scenarios on the server; the Mac release backport passed the parallel-child scenario. The exact upstream PR head is not the deployed release backport. A policy change while another child remains active can still force a protected cold preflight and leave completion recovery blocked; that case remains under investigation.


### Live policy-change counterexample

A subsequent live server test changed the test session exec host from gateway to sandbox while two native children were running. Both children finished; the continuation correctly rejected the changed tool policy, but recovery retired both results without delivering them. This remains an open defect in the separately patched release runtime. A safe fix needs owner-issued proof that the whole admitted Gateway run did not send a native turn before allowing a retry; generic preflight errors and absent observed output are not sufficient. The managed bundled server path and ordinary parallel-child/steer tests pass, but they do not cover this failure.


### Current exec-state context for completion turns

`bfa927fe9` carries the current session exec hint into native completion turns from the admitted session and agent configuration; tool execution still uses the current authority and policy. Heavy prompt/runtime helpers are loaded only on the relevant completion path. This addresses the observed unchanged-policy fingerprint mismatch, but does not resolve the documented policy-change counterexample.

Focused validation: 29 session-preparation tests and 14 prompt-prefix stability tests passed; core typecheck, targeted lint, formatting, test-line and line-cap ratchets passed. An independent static review found an eager-loading concern, which was addressed with lazy imports; it did not rerun the tests or perform a live test. Separate installed 2026.11.1 backports passed the live ordinary parallel-child scenarios on Mac and server, but are not this source head. Exact-head live qualification and the policy-change recovery issue remain open.

prs.title: fix(desktop): finish VncAuth before readiness probes close
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Opening Host Desktop against a password-protected VNC server can end in `Desktop disconnected: desktop stream closed`, or `the offered VNC security is not supported`, even when a normal VNC client can log in. Status, acquire, and managed Linux readiness called `probeRfbServer`, which reads the security-type list and then destroys the socket. TigerVNC counts that unfinished VncAuth handshake as a bad client and blacklists `127.0.0.1`. Later connections then see no usable security type.

`desktop.host.passwordFile` was already configured in the reported case. The password was read only after the probe had hung up, and only so a second connection could try to log in. By then the loopback address was already blacklisted.

## Evidence

Call chain: enabled status uses `inspectHostDesktop`. Disabled setup uses `inspectHostDesktopSetup` and does not read `passwordFile`. Acquire uses `createHostDesktopSource`. Managed Linux startup polls in `waitUntilReady` with its generated password. The offer-only `probeRfbServer` drop was introduced in #133226 (2026-08-30).

A Node TCP peer on 127.0.0.1 speaks RFB 3.8, offers VncAuth, and treats a close before the security result as an abandoned handshake. The expected DES response is a fixed byte string, not a call into the production helper. Eight enabled inspections and eight acquires finished ServerInit. A wrong password was rejected. Disabled setup with a readable password file stayed `ready` and sent no credential response. Revoking the desktop after the challenge stopped the acquire before any credential bytes were sent. An unreadable attach password with managed mode and no listener started the managed desktop once.

```console
$ pnpm exec tsx /tmp/oc-vnc-proof.mts
{"ok":true,"authenticatedConnections":16,"abandonedHandshakes":0,"wrongPasswordRejected":true,"disabledSetupState":"ready","disabledSetupCredentialResponses":0,"revokedBeforeCredential":true,"managedFallbackCalls":1}
```

## Real behavior proof

- **Behavior or issue addressed:** Enabled host readiness finishes configured VncAuth through ServerInit before closing. Disabled setup discovery does not read or send the password. A revoked desktop does not send the credential. Managed mode still starts when the attach password file cannot be read and no server is listening.
- **Real environment tested:** macOS 27.0.1, Node v26.12.1, worktree `/tmp/oc-193444` at `4e5a6bf6f1914630d32bd1f5cffea15ebac2a752`. Loopback TCP peer, not a stand-in object. `Xtigervnc` and `Xvnc` are not installed on this Mac. Port 5900 was closed, so the managed fallback saw connection refused.
- **Exact steps or command run after this patch:** `cd /tmp/oc-193444 && pnpm exec tsx /tmp/oc-193487-status-proof.mts`
- **Evidence after fix:** terminal output from `createHostDesktopService.status` on this head. The peer held the VNC challenge. The live config was then set to `enabled: false`. The challenge was released after that. Status threw and the peer recorded zero credential responses.

```console
$ cd /tmp/oc-193444 && pnpm exec tsx /tmp/oc-193487-status-proof.mts
{"head":"4e5a6bf6f1914630d32bd1f5cffea15ebac2a752","path":"createHostDesktopService.status","revokedBeforeCredential":true,"credentialResponses":0,"outcome":"gateway host desktop configuration changed; retry"}
```

- **Observed result after fix:** `service.status` checked the live desktop guard before the credential write. The outcome was `gateway host desktop configuration changed; retry`. `credentialResponses` stayed 0.
- **What was not tested:** A Fedora TigerVNC or Xvnc process with its own blacklist journal. The peer counts a close before the security result as abandoned. The later viewer socket returned by acquire was not opened; that path already keeps `connectRfbServer` and authenticates on the retained stream.
- **Shared negotiation on this head:** `5b2fd74417f486e1b3bb0eedc78534d2baad33c7`. `src/gateway/desktop/rfb-probe.test.ts`, `rfb-preauth.test.ts`, and `host-source.test.ts` passed (64). The new test expects a 1025-byte rejection reason. On the previous probe that assertion failed and the reason was `VNC authentication failed`.

## Summary

Closes #193444

Readiness probes call `negotiateServer` on the retained socket for security selection, the VNC challenge response, and the security result. Rejection reasons use that owner's 64 KiB limit. The probe keeps ClientInit and ServerInit, and still checks the live desktop guard before the credential write. Setup discovery stays credential-free, matching #154008. Managed mode keeps its own generated password when the attach file cannot be read.

prs.title: fix: provider requests time out when the Gateway stalls on IPv4-only hosts
prs.body:
Closes #195336

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: provider requests fail with `UND_ERR_CONNECT_TIMEOUT` when the Gateway event loop stalls past 300 ms on a host with no usable IPv6 route.

## User Impact

User impact: a loaded Gateway can keep reaching an IPv4 provider through a short main-thread stall, and an unanswered IPv4 address can still fall back to a working IPv6 address.

The fallback wait for an address that never answers grows from 300 ms to 1 second. A stall longer than 1 second can still drop a handshake that already finished. Telegram keeps its own 300 ms attempt budget.

## Why This Change Was Made

Node starts the next Happy Eyeballs attempt by abandoning the current one when the attempt timer expires. If the loop is stalled, that timer runs before the connect event, so a finished IPv4 handshake is discarded. The IPv6 attempt then fails immediately, and undici reports its 10 second connect timeout. One second stays inside the RFC 8305 range and still starts the next address when the first does not answer.

## Evidence

Node 24.22.2, undici 8.12.3, infra shard (`vitest.infra.config.ts`). Addresses below are loopback or the IPv4 documentation range; no endpoints, keys, or install paths are included.

Gateway provider request (`buildGuardedModelFetch`) under a 700 ms event-loop stall, with DNS answering loopback IPv4 then loopback IPv6 and only IPv4 listening:

- 300 ms budget, the value latest stable `v2026.11.2` still ships: `UND_ERR_CONNECT_TIMEOUT`. The IPv4 attempt is `ETIMEDOUT` from `internalConnectMultipleTimeout`; IPv6 is `ECONNREFUSED`. Elapsed about 1.2 s.
- 1 second budget: HTTP 200 in about 1.1 s.

Immediate IPv4 refusal, then a listening IPv6 address: HTTP 200 in about 100 ms. That fallback does not wait for the attempt budget.

Unanswered IPv4 handshake, then the same listening IPv6 address:

- macOS: the connect interposer leaves that IPv4 socket unconnected. kqueue does not complete it, and the provider request returns HTTP 200 after the 1 second attempt budget (about 2.6 s including process startup).
- Linux: a private network namespace drops the real SYN. The IPv4 socket stays in SYN_SENT, and IPv6 is reached only after the attempt timer. A fake EINPROGRESS return, with no connect call, completes in about 1 ms and never enters SYN_SENT. The dropped-SYN case connects to IPv6 in 1001 ms with SYN_SENT observed.

Fresh and upgraded state, same provider request on this build:

- Fresh empty state directory: HTTP 200 for the stall (1.3 s) and for the unanswered-IPv4 fallback (1.1 s).
- State directory carrying a stable-shaped config with no attempt-timeout field: HTTP 200 for the stall (1.1 s) and for the fallback (1.1 s).

The budget is the running build's constant, not config or state. Upgrading from `v2026.11.2` changes it from 300 ms to 1 second. A packaged global install of that stable release was not run.

The owner decision on the shared 1 second fallback wait is still open.

prs.title: fix(media): stop resubmitting completions whose dialogue ended without a reply
prs.body:
Closes #195311

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: an image (or music/video) completion keeps resubmitting its "media is ready" wake about every two seconds when its completion dialogue has already ended without a visible reply. Once the Gateway's five-minute dedupe entry expires, this can readmit that stale dialogue after the conversation has moved on.

## User Impact

User impact: a generated-media completion now reaches one stable outcome. If the completion dialogue finishes without a visible reply, the media is kept in the original session as a blocked result and the observer stops. Old image-completion turns no longer reappear later, and the logs no longer fill with repeated `did not produce a visible reply` warnings.

## Why This Change Was Made

After the durable media queue takes the files, the observer intentionally drops its 120-second handoff deadline (#193460, kept here). The direct-response classifier marks a successful terminal response with no visible reply as `retryable`, and the media wake adapter turned that into `pending`, so the observer resubmitted the same wake indefinitely. Every resubmission uses the same idempotency key, so it only replays the cached result until the dedupe entry expires and the dialogue can be readmitted.

The media adapter now treats `visible_reply_missing` as a permanent failure, which reuses the existing blocked-result retention path. The warning records the classifier disposition, so a retryable settlement is distinguishable from a failed turn. The shared classifier is unchanged, because the subagent registry has its own handling for that disposition. Transport errors and `completion_handoff_pending` still retry, and explicit silence and final receipts still settle as delivered.

## Evidence

The incident shape is a successful terminal turn: `status: "ok"`, no error, empty payloads. The embedded runner used by the QA-channel mock never emits that shape. It turns a required empty reply into an incomplete turn, and the unpatched adapter already stops on that error. A live Gateway log of that scenario therefore cannot show the retryable path. The proof below uses the real classifier and the real dedupe owner on the shape the incident described.

- Real classifier, in `src/agents/subagents/announce/subagent-announce-media-completion.test.ts`. `deliverSubagentAnnouncement` runs against a Gateway result of `{ status: "ok", result: { meta: {}, payloads: [] } }` for an `image_generate` completion. The result is `{ delivered: false, path: "direct", reason: "visible_reply_missing", disposition: "retryable" }`, and the Gateway is called once.
- Real adapter and dedupe owner, in `src/agents/tools/media-generate-background-shared.test.ts`. The observer receives that same result after the file handoff queues. The test seeds the Gateway dedupe cache with the terminal response and starts the real maintenance timers. `replayAgentTurnIfCached` returns true before the sweep. The test then advances ten minutes, past the five-minute TTL and the one-minute sweep. Replay returns false, the announcement was called exactly twice, and the task settles with `terminalOutcome: "blocked"`.
- The same observer test on the unpatched adapter fails. Ten minutes of the retryable result produces 303 wakes instead of 2, so the dialogue would be eligible for readmission once the dedupe entry expires.

```text
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/agents/subagents/announce/subagent-announce-media-completion.test.ts src/agents/tools/media-generate-background-shared.test.ts

 ✓ live generated-media completion > classifies a successful empty image completion as a retryable missing reply
 ✓ scheduleMediaGenerationTaskCompletion > settles a queued completion once its dialogue ends without a visible reply

 Test Files  2 passed (2)
      Tests  36 passed (36)
```

```text
# same observer test, adapter restored to 3b7741dfdc7
FAIL scheduleMediaGenerationTaskCompletion > settles a queued completion once its dialogue ends without a visible reply
AssertionError: expected "vi.fn()" to be called 2 times, but got 303 times
```

- Test-line budget: `config/test-lines-allocations/media-completion-terminal-missing-reply.txt` grants 48 lines. `pnpm check:test-lines-ratchet --base 3b7741dfdc7 --no-merge-base` and `--base 9e12c29 --no-merge-base` both pass with the total equal to the ceiling.

prs.title: fix(codex): preserve the parent tool catalog during completion delivery
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

A native child releases the parent's execution pin when its final turn settles, before its result has finished delivery. The detached completion then rebuilds the parent's dynamic tool catalog. Without a live pin it loses the original declarations, which can rotate the native thread or prevent the completion from being delivered.

## User Impact

Completed native subagents can deliver their result on the original parent thread after the execution pin has been released.

## Why This Change Was Made

Keep the original catalog available only to the exact in-flight completion owner. The existing monitor verifies the physical parent/client, requester, child source, announcement, active delivery attempt, and current completion custody. Recheck that custody after the awaited metadata read and under the existing binding authority before consuming the fingerprinted catalog. Do not keep the execution pin or change the current executor/permission checks. The existing settled-child retention loop moves to its parent owner so the monitor can delegate without growing its oversized module.

This ports the completion-catalog portion of #188698 to current main. It depends on #194748 (the native completion receipt custody change); it does not include the broader stable-release continuation/schema compatibility patch.

## Evidence

- The new catalog regression fails on the base: a completed child's unprotected catalog resolves to `undefined`. With the fix, the original catalog is restored; a revoked read, changed runtime, ordinary turn, and missing custody remain rejected or unavailable.
- Catalog tests: 14 passed. SQLite-backed native completion contention tests: 7 passed, including actual pin release, exact/wrong request lookup, receipt handoff, retirement, and captured-custody invalidation.
- Two composed native-dispatch regressions recover declarations from the real native metadata file during actual completion custody, then invoke the native bridge. A missing current executor is denied; session reassignment during awaited execution admission revokes custody and the prepared native policy denies execution. No OS command is spawned. This is synthetic protocol evidence for the current-main head, not clearance of the historical PR head or a live-model claim.
- Current executor tests: 52 passed. Native follow-up custody and lifecycle sibling tests: 10 passed.
- Targeted core and full Codex production/test TypeScript checks, targeted lint, formatting, diff whitespace check, and justified test-line allocation pass.
- Independent local review found no actionable P0–P2 defects in this delta. It was limited to the supplied change/evidence.

The native protocol is represented by the repository's app-server fixture in these checks. This exact source head has not been exercised against a live model; previous installed-release incidents and proof are background, not an exact-head production claim.


### Recovered-catalog authority evidence

At `3aa8f3d4b`, the composed synthetic test exercises recovered catalog capture and a controlled allowed `supervisor.spawn` effect, then rejects session replacement and execution-policy revocation at the barrier immediately before tool execution. A mismatched requester does not receive the recovered catalog. Ten focused cases, targeted lint, test-line ratchet and commit checks passed; scoped review found no P0-P2 issues. The wrong-requester case is a capture-stage check, not a full downstream-dispatch denial proof. The supervisor effect is controlled, not an OS process; live Gateway/model and real end-effect validation remain outstanding.


### CI allocation follow-up

`7e8f5eb6f` separately allocates 18 previously unallocated lines of existing custody, SQLite receipt-retirement and revoked-metadata regressions. Against the exact failing CI merge/base, the ratchet reproduced 6,583,543 / 6,583,525 and passed after this change at 6,583,543 / 6,583,543. Tests and the shared baseline remain unchanged; the new exact-head CI is pending.
