prs.title: fix(ui): collapsed sidebar keeps polling session catalogs
prs.body:
Related: #125989
Builds on: #152200 (by @rondavis007)

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: the Control UI asks the Gateway for the session catalog every 2 minutes when the sidebar is collapsed or hidden. Nobody can see these rows.

## User Impact

User impact: a collapsed or hidden sidebar does not send background catalog requests. When you open the sidebar again, the list is up to date.

Rows that are already loaded stay. Manual refresh works as before. There is no setting to change.

## Why This Change Was Made

Before, the UI checked only one thing: is the browser tab hidden? Now it also checks: does the sidebar show the session rows? A collapsed desktop sidebar still shows a narrow rail, but it does not show the rows, so it counts as hidden.

When the rows are hidden:

- The UI stops the 2-minute timer, the retry timer and page discovery.
- It remembers if it skipped work: a waiting refresh, a retry, a late host update or page discovery.
- A refresh that already started finishes, so expanded groups do not go blank.
- The first load still runs once, so the rows are ready and do not jump in when the sidebar opens.

When the rows show again:

- If a poll was due or work was skipped, the UI refreshes one time.
- If not, it keeps the normal 2-minute schedule. Switching views quickly does not add requests.

#152200 by @rondavis007 had the same idea. That branch is about 30,000 commits behind main and does not apply: main deleted 3 of its files. This PR puts the fix on the current code, adds the collapsed-rail case, and credits Ron as co-author.

## Evidence

**Request count in the real built Control UI (Chromium, mock Gateway, virtual clock):**

| Step | Before (main) | After (this PR) |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Open page, sidebar shown | 1 | 1 |
| Sidebar collapsed, 2 min later | 2 | 1 |
| Sidebar collapsed, 4 min later | 3 | 1 |
| Sidebar collapsed, 6 min later | 4 | 1 |
| Sidebar collapsed, 8 min later | 5 | 1 |
| Sidebar collapsed, 10 min later | 6 | 1 |
| Sidebar opened again | 6 | 2 |

Numbers are cumulative `sessions.catalog.list` requests from the sidebar.

**Tests:**

- `ui/src/e2e/sidebar-catalog-scope.e2e.test.ts`: new browser test. On main it fails: `expected … to have a length of 1 but got 2`.
- `ui/src/components/app-sidebar.catalog-events.test.ts`: 5 new or changed cases fail on main and pass here. They cover a hidden sidebar, a collapsed sidebar, another sidebar view, a sidebar that starts collapsed, and a hide while a refresh waits in the startup queue.
- 2 more cases check that opening the sidebar before the next poll does not add a request. They pass on main too, because main never stops polling.

**Other checks:**

- 30 UI test files that use the changed code (382 tests): pass.

prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: `openclaw worktrees create <repoRoot>` prints only "The CLI command failed. For help, run `openclaw doctor`." when `<repoRoot>` doesn't exist (for example a typo), and `--json` shows only the raw "ENOENT: no such file or directory, realpath '<path>'".

## User Impact

User impact: the command now says "Source checkout not found: <path>. Pass the path to an existing git checkout." Exit code is unchanged, and nothing is created.

## Why This Change Was Made

`worktrees create` resolves the source path with `realpathSync.native` before admission, and the raw `ENOENT` reached the root failure renderer as an unexpected error. A missing path (`ENOENT`/`ENOTDIR`) is now reported with the existing `throwExpectedCliError` helper; other filesystem errors still propagate as before.

## Evidence

Built from `main` at 67416fcc27 on Linux, Node 24.22.2, fresh state directory.

Before:
```
$ openclaw worktrees create ./my-repo
[openclaw] The CLI command failed.
[openclaw] For help, run `openclaw doctor`.
$ openclaw worktrees create ./my-repo --json
{ "ok": false, "error": { "type": "cli_error", "message": "ENOENT: no such file or directory, realpath './my-repo'" } }
```

After:
```
$ openclaw worktrees create ./my-repo
Source checkout not found: ./my-repo. Pass the path to an existing git checkout.
$ openclaw worktrees create ./my-repo --json
{ "ok": false, "error": { "type": "cli_error", "message": "Source checkout not found: ./my-repo. Pass the path to an existing git checkout." } }
```
Both exit 1, as before.

Tests:
- `pnpm test src/cli/worktrees-cli.test.ts src/cli/worktrees-cli.import-boundary.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`: 19 passed.
- New test "names a missing source checkout instead of failing generically" runs the real `formatCliFailureLines` path and checks the service is never called. It fails on `main` and passes with the fix.
- `oxfmt --check` and `oxlint --type-aware` on both files: clean.

prs.title: fix(xai): long Grok prompts are costed at half xAI's rate
prs.body:
Resubmits #195067, which openclaw-barnacle auto-closed under the active-PR limit (the author can't reopen a PR closed by the bot). Same branch; the author is back under the limit.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: usage cost estimates for Grok requests with long prompts (200k tokens or more) show half of what xAI charges.

## User Impact

Cost estimates and usage reports for long-prompt Grok requests now use xAI's long-context rate. Short prompts are unchanged. Existing xAI OAuth configs get the rate after `openclaw doctor --fix`. On the subscription route these numbers remain labeled estimates, as before.

## Why This Change Was Made

xAI's [model pricing table](https://docs.x.ai/developers/models) lists a second row "≥ 200k prompt tokens" for every priced Grok model (4.7, 4.6, 4.5, 4.3, both 4.20-0309 variants, grok-build-0.1): input, cached input and output all double, and "requests whose prompt reaches the listed token threshold are billed at the higher rate for all tokens in the request." Core already prices whole requests by prompt-token tier through `cost.tieredPricing` (half-open ranges; the openai and anthropic manifests use it). The xAI manifest had only the flat short-context rate, and `docs/providers/xai.md` described that as a limitation that predates tier support in manifests.

This adds the documented tier to the seven priced rows. `model-definitions.ts` turns the manifest into typed model definitions, and JSON imports widen tier ranges to `number[]`, so a small typed mapper restores the `[start, end]` / `[start]` tuple without casts. The docs paragraph now describes the tiers.

**Existing OAuth configs.** OAuth sign-in saves each catalog row, `cost` included, into `models.providers.xai.models` (`applyXaiOAuthConfig` ← `buildLiveXaiOAuthProvider`, `cost: fallback?.cost`), and saved rows override the catalog at runtime. So configs written before this PR kept flat prices. The xAI Doctor contract (`doctor-contract-api.ts`) now adds the catalog's `tieredPricing` to saved xAI rows that are on an official xAI route (the row's `baseUrl`, else the provider's, is unset, `https://api.x.ai/v1` or the Grok OAuth route), whose flat rates still equal the catalog's, and that carry no tiers. Rows on a custom `baseUrl` own their own billing and are left as written even at catalog rates, as are rows with custom prices, rows that already have tiers (even an empty list), and zero-priced rows.

Why Doctor rather than not persisting `cost` at sign-in: `cost` is a required field of `ModelDefinitionConfig`, so dropping it from the OAuth patch would change the config contract. This plugin's Doctor contract already repairs stale generated xAI rows (`isLegacyXaiBuiltinModel`), and the repo rule sends legacy config shapes to Doctor rather than to runtime readers. If maintainers prefer pricing to stay purely plugin-owned, the switch is: make `cost` optional for provider-config rows, omit it in `applyXaiOAuthConfig`, and have this Doctor rule delete catalog-equal `cost` objects instead of adding tiers.

## Evidence

- **Red on main** (`1166f73e0`): the `api.test.ts` catalog-pricing case expects `grok-4.5` to carry xAI's tiers and fails because `tieredPricing` is missing.
- **Red before the Doctor repair:** the `doctor-contract-api.test.ts` case uses the exact row shape OAuth sign-in saved (`id, name, api, baseUrl, reasoning, input, cost, contextWindow, maxTokens, compat`, flat cost, the OAuth route). Without the repair no Doctor rule matches it. On the previous head (`6fd4932c4`), the custom-route cases fail because the row on `https://proxy.example.test/v1` was tiered. With this head, the OAuth row gains both tiers, a second run changes nothing, and custom-route (model or provider `baseUrl`), custom-price, already-tiered and zero-price rows stay identical. Whole xAI extension suite: 34 files, 408 tests passed. `pnpm tsgo:extensions`, `pnpm tsgo:extensions:test`, `oxfmt`, the test-lines ratchet and `git diff --check` pass.
- **Green with the fix:** all xAI extension tests plus the core consumers that read xAI catalog rows or tier prices (`clawrouter-xai-responses`, thinking defaults, effective tool inventory, xAI auto-retirement, startup config corpus, catalog/manifest contracts, `session-cost-usage-pricing`): 43 files, 534 tests passed. `pnpm tsgo:extensions`, `pnpm tsgo:extensions:test`, `oxfmt --check`, `oxlint`, `check:test-lines-ratchet` and `git diff --check` pass.
- Every added tier value was checked row by row against xAI's table.
- **Live Gateway turn** (local Gateway built from `main` plus this PR, xAI OAuth, `xai/grok-4.7`, one turn): the usage report gave `promptTokens 179241` (input 178,089 + cached 1,152), output 7,123, `cost.total 0.399492`. That is exactly the short-tier rate ($2 / $0.50 / $6 per M), which is correct below 200k.
- **Shipped calculator at the boundary:** the built `calculateUsageCost` (`packages/llm-core/dist`) run against the built `dist/extensions/xai/openclaw.plugin.json` row for `grok-4.7`, with 50,000 cached prompt tokens in each case:

  | prompt tokens (incl. cached) | this PR | flat catalog on `main` |
  |---|---|---|
  | 179,241 (the live turn above) | $0.399492 | $0.399492 |
  | 199,999 | $0.336998 | $0.336998 |
  | 200,000 | **$0.674000** | $0.337000 |
  | 240,000 | **$0.834000** | $0.417000 |

  Tier selection counts input + cached + cache-write tokens, so cached input moves a request over the boundary, and the whole request doubles, as xAI's table says.
- **Live ≥200k turn, before the Doctor repair** (same Gateway, one turn): `promptTokens 209280` (input 208,128 + cached 1,152), output 29. The Gateway recorded **$0.417006**, which is `main`'s flat figure, because its OAuth rows were saved before this PR.
- **Live ≥200k turn, after the Doctor repair** (Gateway rebuilt from `main` plus this PR at `1914c08b0`; same OAuth config, signed in before the change): `openclaw doctor --fix --non-interactive` reported `Added xAI's long-context price tier to 3 saved xAI model row(s)` and left the zero-priced row untouched. One turn with the same 790 KB prompt: `promptTokens 209280` (input 208,128 + cached 1,152), output 30. The Gateway recorded **$0.834024**, which is exactly the ≥200k rate (208,128 × $4 + 1,152 × $1 + 30 × $12 per M). The flat figure for the same usage is $0.417012.
- **Upgrade from the latest stable (`2026.11.2`):** a state dir whose `models.providers.xai.models` holds the rows exactly as an earlier OAuth sign-in saved them (flat costs on the OAuth route), plus a `grok-4.6` row on a custom `baseUrl` at catalog rates. `openclaw@2026.11.2` `config validate` accepts it and reads all four rows unchanged. This head's `openclaw doctor --fix --non-interactive` on the same state reports `Added xAI's long-context price tier to 2 saved xAI model row(s)`: grok-4.7 and grok-4.5 on the OAuth route gain both tiers, while the custom-route grok-4.6 row and the zero-priced row are byte-identical. A second Doctor run reports no xAI repair.
- **Boundary:** unit tests at the Doctor and catalog contracts; the latest-stable upgrade above (config validation on the released package, then this head's Doctor from source, no Gateway); and a live local Gateway on the xAI OAuth route for both ≥200k turns. For each long turn, the local `grok-4.7` `contextWindow` was raised to 320k so the pre-send estimate didn't compact the prompt below 200k, then restored. The live turns ran before the custom-route scoping; that change only narrows which rows Doctor touches, and the official-route row in the live config is one the scoped rule still repairs.
- `check:test-lines-ratchet`: the 62 added regression lines have their own `config/test-lines-allocations/xai-long-context-pricing.txt` record.
- **Data model:** no schema change. `cost.tieredPricing` is an existing optional field on model rows (the openai and anthropic manifests already use it). The repaired config also passes `openclaw@2026.11.2` `config validate`, so going back to the latest stable after Doctor ran is safe. Doctor only adds the tier; it never removes or rewrites a flat rate.
- No overlap: no open PR changes xAI pricing or `extensions/xai/doctor-contract-api.ts`. #195024 edits a different paragraph of `docs/providers/xai.md`.

prs.title: fix(models): surface manual-selection permission in the full CLI inventory
prs.body:
Closes #194738

## What Problem This Solves

`openclaw models list --all --json` reports a policy-blocked but authenticated model as `available: true` with no field distinguishing manual-selection permission from runtime readiness. An agent selecting a reviewer from this inventory then hits the native `sessions_spawn` policy rejection. The policy rejection is correct; the missing policy visibility is the bug.

Plain language: the model catalog told the agent "this model is ready to use", but the permission layer separately forbids picking it — and the catalog never said so. Now the catalog row says it.

## Why This Change Was Made

The projection already exists: `models-list-result.ts` renders `manualSelectionAllowed` for clients that opt in, gated by the `model-selection-policy` client capability, and the protocol schema documents the field as "Scoped manual-choice permission; separate from runtime readiness". The CLI never opted in, so the full inventory omitted it. The CLI now advertises the capability on the gateway path, passes the internal `includeManualSelection` flag on the local-reader path, and carries the projected field through to each JSON row. Models are not removed from the full inventory and admission is unchanged.

## User Impact

`models list --all --json` rows for policy-blocked models now show `manualSelectionAllowed: false` (and `true` for allowed ones), so inventory consumers can filter before attempting `sessions_spawn`. When the projection is unavailable (older gateway, or the field is not projected), rows omit the field exactly as before.

## Evidence

Real runtime runs on the latest main tree this change is based on (files byte-compared as `main` + exactly this delta):

| Check | Result |
| --- | --- |
| `list.prepared-catalog.test.ts` new test: gateway result carrying `manualSelectionAllowed: false` surfaces on the `--all --json` row, and the CLI gateway call advertises the `model-selection-policy` cap | green (16/16) |
| Red check: reverting the capability advertisement and the row passthrough makes exactly the new test fail (caps missing, field absent) | confirmed |
| Adjacent suites `list.refresh-secrets.test.ts`, `load-config.test.ts` | 7/7 green |
| `tsc --noEmit -p tsconfig.core.json`: zero errors in changed files | verified |

## AI Assistance

This PR is AI-assisted. Used grep to trace the existing `manualSelectionAllowed` projection through the gateway capability gate and the CLI row mapping, then wired the existing mechanism into the CLI. The implementer understands the code: no new policy logic is introduced; the CLI simply joins the existing opt-in projection. All evidence above is from real local runtime execution.

prs.title: fix: node approvals fail to save when the deletion journal is missing
prs.body:
Closes #192227

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: node approvals fail to save when the state database never received the agent deletion journal.

## User Impact

User impact: on a node whose state was created by native bootstrap before the journal backfill, `exec.approvals.node.set` now works instead of failing with a SQLite error, and the Control UI save persists. No action needed from users; the repair runs once at startup.

## Why This Change Was Made

The gateway only forwards `system.execApprovals.set` to the node, so the failing database is the node's. Its state was built by native bootstrap, which used to create the catalog without the `agent_deletion_journal` table, and later migrations never backfilled it for databases that already existed. The mutation fence queries that table on every approvals save, so every write threw before it could reach the fence.

This fixes the initialization path instead of bypassing the fence. At startup, after the native init, the node checks read-only whether the journal is missing, and if it is, creates the empty table and records a migration receipt. It refuses when a prior Doctor reconstruction or an earlier backfill is recorded and the table is missing again, so a second disappearance stays Doctor-owned. The check runs read-only first so startup never opens an unrecognized database for write. An empty journal is neutral for the fence: a mutation is allowed when no journal row exists for the agent, and a deletion can only begin when the journal exists, so nothing here weakens deletion authority.

## Evidence

Reproduced the production error on the September 25 codebase first: after native bootstrap init, saving an approvals allowlist threw `UNAVAILABLE: Error: no such table: agent_deletion_journal` from the mutation fence. After the fix the same save succeeds. On that codebase the recovery, startup, node-worker-bootstrap, and exec-approvals suites pass (119 tests) and oxlint is clean on the changed files.

Ported to current main with every import and signature checked against the current files, and the new tests use the existing harnesses in each file. The full suite on this exact head is for CI here, since the port targets a moving main.

prs.title: feat(llama-cpp): deploy local OCR and vision on Apple Silicon
prs.body:
Closes #194650

## What Problem This Solves

Apple Silicon Mac users are rejected by llama-cpp's managed local OCR/vision setup even though its pinned macOS runtime can run both models with Metal.

## User Impact

Users can run `openclaw models auth login --provider llama-cpp --method local-media` on macOS arm64 and receive separate local OCR and vision models selected within current unified-memory and disk budgets. Both real-image checks must pass before activation; cancellation or failure preserves the previous configuration and preset. Existing chat defaults and embeddings are preserved.

Requires native arm64 Node, macOS 13.3+, and confirmed Metal support. Resource-constrained or unsupported hosts receive guidance before downloads. Small English-focused vision models can hallucinate; this does not add video input or reliable complex chart/layout recognition.

## Why This Change Was Made

This extends a **shipped feature**: @duyufansh2008 contributed the original Linux x64 implementation in #148193 (merged October 12, 2026). The first stable release containing it is **[v2026.10.10](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/releases/tag/v2026.10.10)**, published November 3, 2026; current stable v2026.11.1 also contains it. I verified merge ancestry and official npm plugin contents/integrity, including preceding stable packages. This PR retains the original deployment owners and Linux CPU recipe.

- Qualify Apple Silicon media setup with bounded `system_profiler` Metal telemetry and existing memory/APFS probes; display chip and available cores. Strict qualification is opt-in for media, preserving released Mac chat/embedding backend selection when telemetry is unavailable.
- Prefer the existing GLM-OCR + 2.2B vision pair; select a pinned, checksum-verified SmolVLM2 500M pair when only it fits. Count unified memory/shared disk once and preserve host headroom. A complete compact pair still needs 4 GiB available because OCR reserves 4 GiB.
- Reuse consent, verified downloads/cache, pinned runtime installation, isolated candidate preset, registration and local routing. Use the runtime's real `MTL0` device for model/projector, override inherited CPU preset settings and reject conflicting global router options before downloads.

## Evidence

Current candidate: `f16482dd02217f2ecec23c0f15ef69ee95ecbec6` after merging main `44a5a6595094bd8ad2077e85800c7f661292f87a`. The original feature commit is `6855d4a7556aaeba39382731cb4a95b05a727739` (initial main `b4411857f195fb3444fa02f0414944db5be96bd9`). Cold installation, stable-upgrade, original regression and earlier review evidence below are pinned to that feature commit. The five-turn chat/local-image test, full plugin lane and full build were repeated on the current candidate.

**Physical Mac:** M4 Mac mini, 10 CPU/10 GPU cores, 16 GiB unified memory, macOS 26.5.2 arm64/Metal 4, Node 24.22.1.

| Real product check | Result |
| --- | --- |
| Released 2026.11.1 baseline | Actual CLI rejects darwin/arm64; config unchanged. |
| Latest-stable → candidate upgrade | Official 2026.11.1 host/npm plugin → this candidate host/bundled plugin on the same isolated state, before any media enrollment. Existing real chat session continues, local embeddings/search work with the retained index, and chat/embedding/image preferences, eight workspace files and native preset remain intact. |
| Hardware/resource selection | Natural available memory around 4.4–4.9 GiB selects compact vision; 5.2–5.8 GiB selects standard vision. |
| Full cold matching-main enrollment | Empty model/runtime caches; automatic runtime + four model/projector downloads (3,139,962,912 model bytes), exact size/SHA-256 checks, both real image probes, then MTL0 models and local routes persist. 179.661 s from consent to CLI completion. |
| Registered image inference | GLM-OCR transcribes Tesseract's scanned phototest sample; 2.2B vision describes OpenCV's fruit photograph through `infer image describe`. |
| Native backend | b10809 reports `MTL0: Apple M4`; verbose inference shows model layers offloaded to GPU and `CLIP using MTL0 backend`. All three recipes pass the unchanged enrollment fixtures. |
| Existing chat + local OCR/Vision | Five real Gateway turns retain the operator's existing hosted chat model: normal chat, local_image OCR, local_image vision, chat-history recall and direct attachment preprocessing. Current-head ordinary bootstrap (35,525 prompt characters, four workspace files); no minimal/lightweight or per-turn model override, no fallback. |
| Supplemental direct-VLM agent | An extra native image-bearing turn uses SmolVLM itself as the primary model, with minimal/lightweight prompts. This is separate from the mixed chat/helper proof. |
| Failure/cancel behavior | Actual decline, interrupted download and download failure retain config. A 1-second real OCR timeout during re-enrollment retains an already working config and its preset byte-for-byte. |

**Evidence limits:** physical coverage is M4 only. The follow-up standard-pair run completed a full cold automatic installation after the proxy node changed; no models/runtime were copied or prefetched into its empty test state. The earlier compact recipe and supplemental native tests used verified cached files. Current-main testing used its matching host after official Doctor repair of isolated test state. An extra test forcing SmolVLM as the main chat agent was rejected by its client-side 8K context estimate; that was not the auxiliary OCR/Vision path (details below). The new mixed chat/local-image run uses ordinary bootstrap and successful real `local_image` calls. Earlier standalone HTTP `/tools/invoke` probes remain unsuccessful supplemental checks; HTTP-tool execution is not claimed. Existing live user state/Gateway was not modified.

**Hosted checks on the current head:** security, dependency and PR context/evidence checks passed. [CI run 42445708643](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/42445708643) is `action_required` with zero jobs started, awaiting repository fork-workflow approval; `openclaw/ci-gate` remains failed. `pnpm test:ci-failed 194746` reports no selected Vitest failures to rerun. The separate [Labeler failure](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/42445706068) is a GitHub API 504 when listing labels. ClawSweeper's completed second review was on `6855d4a`, with no code findings and sufficient behavior proof; it does not review the new merge head. Maintainer platform-support acceptance and fork CI approval remain pending.

<summary>Checks, review, reproduction and selected output</summary>

- Test-lines ratchet passes: 6,563,837 / 6,563,898, slack 61. The issue-linked 292-line allocation accounts for net tests covering qualification, resource tiers, offload overrides, consent and rollback; no global ceiling change.
- Author pr-simplify/test-audit passes completed. Independent read-only review found and verified the fix preserving ordinary Mac chat/embedding behavior; final full diff review has no actionable findings. Reviewed snapshot SHA-256: `7d47f80b7a545e5c4ccaeeed06933abc44550271be334bb352c22b4b90913d9a`. Local autoreview/ClawSweeper were not run; this is not a claim of those tool results.

**Stable-to-candidate upgrade:** the official stable CLI `2026.11.1 (4ffdd20)` loaded npm `@openclaw/llama-cpp-provider@2026.11.1`; the candidate CLI `2026.11.1 (6855d4a)` loaded this checkout's bundled plugin. Plugin entry hashes/origins were checked, so the candidate was not silently testing the old installed plugin. On the same isolated state, candidate `doctor --fix --yes --non-interactive --no-workspace-suggestions` completed successfully, then the real Gateway continued the stable Qwen3.5 4B conversation and recalled the conversation-only code `CEDAR-7319` with no fallback. The two pre-upgrade messages were identical before the candidate turn. Both versions passed a real local EmbeddingGemma probe and retrieved `ORCHID-4827` / `cobalt` with top vector scores `0.74455446` (stable) and `0.74455455` (candidate). Before candidate queries, the retained index already had the stable final 5 files / 14 chunks, 768 dimensions, 14 embedding-cache entries, valid identity and automatic-rebuild sequence 0; no candidate reindex was requested. Model inventory, chat/defaults, embedding settings, image primary/fallbacks and media preferences remained semantically equal after Doctor and after inference. Eight workspace file hashes and the complete native INI, including comments/options, stayed identical (preset SHA-256 `c09e1f5b82ce70ba390c3781c32b573560462687c72cfaf9a40309b4cf9fff7d`). No `local-media` enrollment was called in this upgrade lane.

Upgrade-test limits: this is a CLI/source-host switch using official Doctor, not a package-manager updater test. Doctor reported source-UI freshness, minimal-profile/Active Memory and `checkpoint-incomplete` advisories; candidate search later emitted `verification-missing` at the normal integrity gate. No guards were bypassed; commands succeeded and the final Gateway wrote a clean-close receipt. These observations are retained in the evidence. An initial pure-text SmolVLM fixture returned `empty_result`; it was retained, and the successful ordinary-chat proof used the pinned public Qwen3.5 4B model instead. All upgrade fixtures were synthetic; task Gateways and native services were stopped afterward.

All five real turns matched that primary model (resolved context 128,000), with no fallback or per-turn model override. A fifth turn sent the geometric verification image as an ordinary attachment. The existing custom primary had no image input declared, so the configured local image preprocessing route produced a textual `[Image] ... Description:` input; the original chat model answered “A red square is above the blue circle.” A primary declared to support native images can instead receive attachments directly. Explicit `local_image` selects the installed local OCR/Vision models independently of that capability; this test does not claim every native-vision primary sends attachments locally. The photo model still hallucinated some details, so this is integration proof, not an accuracy benchmark.

**Earlier 8K rejection, precisely scoped:** an extra test explicitly selected SmolVLM as the main agent and asked “What is two plus two?” with no image. Its 28,946-character system prompt included 19,616 workspace characters and zero tool-schema characters. The OpenAI-compatible client estimated 9,125 input tokens against 8,192 and rejected the request before HTTP creation; 9,125 is not measured server token usage. corepack pnpm openclaw gateway call agent --expect-final --timeout 210000 --json --params \
```bash
  '{"agentId":"main","sessionKey":"agent:main:media-proof","deliver":false,"message":"What code did I ask you to remember before the image tasks? Reply only with that code, without tools."}'
corepack pnpm openclaw gateway call chat.history --json --params \
  '{"sessionKey":"agent:main:media-proof","limit":100}'
```

Verify the selected original primary in each agent receipt and the successful nested `local_image` calls/results in history. A fifth attachment test additionally verified ordinary preprocessing with the text-only primary; it is distinct from explicit tool routing.

Use an isolated state/config and native arm64 Node in the candidate checkout:

```bash

export OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR=/absolute/path/to/task-state
export OPENCLAW_CONFIG_PATH="$OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR/openclaw.json"

  --model llama-cpp/smolvlm2-2.2b-instruct-q4_k_m --prompt "Describe the visible objects." --json
```

Substitute `llama-cpp/smolvlm2-500m-video-instruct-q8_0` when compact vision is selected. Use supported `OPENCLAW_PROXY_URL` if an external download proxy is required, retaining loopback exclusions.

Public inputs: [Tesseract phototest.tif](https://github.com/tesseract-ocr/tesseract/blob/main/testing/phototest.tif), converted with macOS `sips` to PNG (SHA-256 `40ef67f9a856ad10df84975ef722a373d8c8f869c6d10a3db0843e9d35b2b834`); [OpenCV 4.12.0 fruits.jpg](https://github.com/opencv/opencv/blob/4.12.0/samples/data/fruits.jpg) (SHA-256 `9c031d80a1c52da5eca790db896baffec6a7e52bf786cdb7bbfca5c7f880e6a1`).

prs.title: fix(sessions): avoid reclamation rollback during cold startup
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes SQLite session reclamation rolling back during cold startup when the current owner takes more than five seconds to authorize the worker commit.

## User Impact

Cold startup can finish an authorized reclamation instead of failing its commit checkpoint. The decision remains bounded at 30 seconds. Current-owner checks, revocation, rollback and writer admission are unchanged. No configuration or migration is needed.

## Why This Change Was Made

The worker already waits on an owner-controlled shared gate. Allow 30 seconds for that existing authorization decision; do not change who can authorize it or what happens after revocation.

## Evidence

- A real Worker and SQLite transaction regression holds the owner for 6 seconds after the commit request and verifies the persisted value. With the original 5-second bound, the new case fails with a commit-checkpoint expiration while the other 5 cases pass. With this change, all 6 cases pass, including revocation and rollback/worker-exit settlement.
- Command: `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run src/config/sessions/session-accessor.sqlite-reclamation-commit.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` on Node 24.22.1. Final wall time 36.28 s, including a cold compiled-worker generation; test time approximately 7.4 s. The 6-second delay deliberately crosses the shipped 5-second boundary and proves real cross-thread behavior.
- Core typecheck (`tsconfig.core.json`), targeted lint, formatting and `git diff --check` pass.
- Independent local autoreview of the complete two-file working change against `2e13c52c97bbe81228c4f45212c8ca8cd346dbf9`, P0–P2: scoped-clean, no accepted findings. Reviewer assessed the supplied patch and worker fixture; it did not execute tests.
- This is the reclamation authorization window, separate from native child-completion observation budgets.

prs.title: fix(subagents): parents miss results from independently resumed children
prs.body:
## Merge-Readiness Status

**Not merge-ready.** A subsequent qualified Crabbox run exposed a remaining real late-result failure on `94b08a2`: the child finishes successfully after the parent waiting turn ends, but completion retries because operator execution authority is inactive. A separate real admitted guest-parent regression also exposed loss of the requester's model ceiling on resume. Corrections are in progress; the earlier passing checks below do not establish either invariant. No merge or deployment is requested.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes parent sessions missing successful child results when siblings were admitted under different operator invocations or the originating invocation ended.

## Intended User Impact

Accepted child results should return once to their recorded parent without retaining the spawning operator invocation. Parent execution and external effects must retain their normal policy and lifecycle checks. No new settings are intended; previously terminal non-delivery receipts are not automatically replayed.

## Why This Change Was Made

Delete retained operator completion custody and the mixed-authority batch policy instead of adding authority-compatible batching. Internal settlement uses the existing registry, controller and receipt ownership. Preserve requester accounting, generation/incarnation checks, cancellation and idempotency.

The accepted agent turn keeps the Gateway instance lifetime as its execution fence, not the caller input-admission callback. Ordinary sender/communication contracts are unchanged. Detached typing owns its own existing effect authority. Committed registration recovery metadata survives a caller disappearing before acknowledgment.

## Evidence on the Published Candidate

- Two owning-boundary regressions are red on the original source (zero parent wakes) and green with the candidate: independent caller contexts, invocation retirement, both results exactly once, and duplicate terminal events. The wake does not borrow a sibling operator.
- Gateway authorization/lifecycle/transcript, pause, requester settlement, store replacement, registration/publication and worker ownership checks passed in the recorded local runs.
- Core and core-test TypeScript, changed-file type-aware lint, formatting and diff checks passed before the subsequent repairs. These are not current proof for the in-progress corrections.
- An isolated real-provider completion-provenance probe passed, but it did not expose the later held-child boundary below.
- Local Codex autoreview through P2 completed scoped-clean on the earlier candidate. Retired-policy tests and the native-completion fixture correction received supplemental review.
- The native-completion fixture now owns ordinary input lifetimes explicitly. Both revocation cases and the nearby 36-test set passed; no production completion lease or authority comparison was restored.

## Real Crabbox Finding Requiring Repair

Configured provider: **Blacksmith Testbox via Crabbox**, lease `tbx_01m6vs51qgakqhkfva54fnzpnr`, exact clean published head `94b08a2b4eccc0645203a646b954207b7c3fdb9c`. Prepared Node 24.22.1; observed 4 CPUs and approximately 16.6 GB RAM. CI-owned OpenAI credential, isolated test state/HOME, no source-loader injection.

Command: `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run --config test/vitest/vitest.live.config.ts src/agents/subagents/announce/subagent-late-reply.live.test.ts`.

The real Gateway/agent/subagent/native-exec flow reached the decisive boundary: the parent waiting turn finished before the held child was released. The child then ended `ok`, while recorded completion stayed pending/retryable with `operator execution authority is no longer active`; the parent-consumption assertion timed out. This is a product failure, not a setup failure. Verified synthetic evidence is retained locally with SHA-256 `d1d3208e0d36dc95409269fab07e86ed640f5ffaafd4ffb1fb8c77ee52c48793`. The owned Testbox was stopped after evidence collection.

The remaining completion boundary must shed ambient request-client/tool-caller authority while retaining its recorded Gateway/controller/task relationship and parent lifecycle checks. Separately, continuation must preserve the requester's own model restriction facts without borrowing a child's human grant. Guest ceiling assertions will not be removed to make CI green. Combined fresh review, focused checks, and a corrected real Crabbox replay remain required.

## CI Context

Guest spawn/yield cases expose the model-policy issue above. Stop/followup CI failures passed focused local reproduction but are not considered remotely cleared. The earlier update-canary synthetic-merge assertion expects `requester-revoked`, while upstream #194659 produces `UpdateInterruptedError("interrupted")`; no update/canary repair is bundled here. A selected Postgres job also ended by cancellation rather than a recorded test assertion. Final current-head CI and substantive hosted review still need reconciliation.

## Worked on by

- @jalehman

prs.title: fix(ollama): refuse metadata and link-local base URLs
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Ollama used to allow a metadata or link-local base URL through the private-network SSRF policy, including the bearer token. Those base URLs now get no allow policy. Loopback and private LAN hosts stay allowed.

A supported local endpoint, `http://0.0.0.0:11434`, still opts into that private-network allow. The guard then treated `0.0.0.0` and `::` as blocked special-use addresses and threw before HTTP, so discovery reported the local server as unreachable. Exact-host trust, with no private-network allow, still rejects those addresses. Metadata and non-exempt link-local answers stay blocked.

Whether those metadata and link-local exclusions should override every explicit private-network opt-in, or only Ollama's automatic trust, is still a maintainer decision. This change does not narrow that scope.

## Evidence

Head `bd89f8052bf` on macOS Darwin arm64, Node v26.12.1, Ollama 0.40.11 listening on `127.0.0.1:11434`. Production `fetchOllamaModels` ran from `/tmp/oc-191588`.

Before this commit, `http://0.0.0.0:11434` threw and opened no socket:

```console
[security] blocked URL fetch (ollama-provider-models.tags) targetOrigin=http://0.0.0.0:11434 reason=Blocked: resolves to private/internal/special-use IP address
RESULT: unspecified discovery SsrFBlockedError: Blocked: resolves to private/internal/special-use IP address connects=
```

`curl` to that same URL returned HTTP 200 from the daemon. After this commit the production discovery call reached it.

```console
OK: loopback discovery reachable=true models=3
OK: unspecified discovery reachable=true models=3
OK: authenticated loopback header=bearer models=1
OK: literal metadata SsrFBlockedError: Blocked hostname or private/internal/special-use IP address connects=
OK: dns metadata SsrFBlockedError: Blocked: resolves to private/internal/special-use IP address connects=
OK: unrelated redirect denied stolen=0
OK: lan address admitted 192.168.1.20
OK: podman exact-origin embed length=2 requests=1
OK: podman origin metadata newRequests=0 connects=
```

The unrelated redirect target was `proof-unrelated.test`. The guard stopped on the hostname allowlist. The second server received 0 requests. The Podman case used production `createOllamaEmbeddingProvider` against `http://host.containers.internal:11434`, resolved to `169.254.1.2`, where a listener accepted one embed POST. A metadata answer for that same origin opened no further request. The hosts entry and the /32 alias were removed after the trace. Default route stayed on `en0` via `10.0.0.1`.

## Real behavior proof

- **Behavior or issue addressed:** Authenticated Ollama discovery reaches loopback and `0.0.0.0`. Literal and DNS metadata are rejected before a socket opens. An unrelated redirect is denied. The exact-origin Podman link-local exception still delivers the embed, and a metadata answer on that origin does not.
- **Real environment tested:** macOS Darwin arm64, Node v26.12.1, Ollama 0.40.11 bound to `127.0.0.1:11434`, head `bd89f8052bf` in `/tmp/oc-191588`.
- **Exact steps or command run after this patch:** Called production `fetchOllamaModels` for `http://127.0.0.1:11434` and `http://0.0.0.0:11434` with a bearer token. Called `resolvePinnedHostnameWithPolicy` for literal `169.254.169.254` and for `ollama.example` resolved to that address. Posted through `fetchWithSsrFGuard` to a loopback server that redirected to `proof-unrelated.test`. Embedded through `createOllamaEmbeddingProvider` at `http://host.containers.internal:11434` while that name resolved to a listener on `169.254.1.2`, then repeated the origin with a metadata DNS answer.
- **Evidence after fix:** terminal output from the patched tree:

```console
OK: loopback discovery reachable=true models=3
OK: unspecified discovery reachable=true models=3
OK: authenticated loopback header=bearer models=1
OK: literal metadata SsrFBlockedError: Blocked hostname or private/internal/special-use IP address connects=
OK: dns metadata SsrFBlockedError: Blocked: resolves to private/internal/special-use IP address connects=
OK: unrelated redirect denied stolen=0
OK: podman exact-origin embed length=2 requests=1
OK: podman origin metadata newRequests=0 connects=
```

- **Observed result after fix:** Loopback and `0.0.0.0` discovery both returned 3 models from the local daemon. The bearer was present on the loopback recorder. Metadata rejects opened no socket. The unrelated redirect delivered 0 requests to the second server. The Podman listener received exactly one embed and no metadata follow-up.
- **What was not tested:** A LAN Ollama on another machine. This daemon listens only on `127.0.0.1`, so the admitted `192.168.1.20` address had no server. The Podman hop was a listener on this Mac, not a Podman VM.

## Summary

Metadata and link-local Ollama base URLs still get no private-network allow. `0.0.0.0` and `::` stay reachable when private networks are allowed, which is how Ollama names the local server. Exact-host trust still rejects them. A maintainer still needs to decide whether the metadata and link-local exclusions should override every private-network opt-in or only Ollama's automatic trust.

prs.title: fix(update): restore LaunchAgent registration after repair contention
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`openclaw update repair` can leave its macOS LaunchAgent unloaded when restoration encounters a Gateway listener outside launchd supervision.

Fixes #195379.

## User Impact

Gateway respawn entry points refuse an active offline-maintenance owner, and preserved-definition LaunchAgent restoration reloads the job after a restart preflight failure. The original busy-port error remains visible, with the job registered for launchd to retry. Unknown listeners are not adopted or signaled by the recovery path.

**Evidence gap:** the reported detached process's launcher is still unproven. This is a bounded repair, not end-to-end proof of the incident. A restart helper scheduled before maintenance and the stop-to-admission interval remain uncovered. Live macOS reproduction with the app running/suspended is MISSING.

## Why This Change Was Made

`respawnGatewayProcessForUpdate` is the direct detached-Gateway creator that preserves service environment variables. Both that entry point and fresh-PID restart scheduling now consult the existing live state owner immediately before creating a successor or handoff. Normal app service hosting routes through launchd; the restart sentinel delivers work after startup. Source inspection does not establish which path created the reporter's PID.

Preserved-definition restart preflight failures now use the existing LaunchAgent compensation helper, which previously covered only later activation failures. It retains caller authority and native-cleanup checks, preserves the definition/autostart policy, and reports bootstrap failure if registration cannot be restored. No schema or configuration change is required. The running Gateway and restoring CLI must contain the fix.

The related stop-during-restart fix is on main as `6eb7eb5d3351` and in 2026.11.2 as cherry-pick `30f14bde6a8d`. It does not prove this detached/unloaded incident fixed; 2026.11.2 does not contain the changes in this PR.

## Evidence

- PD2: Added exactly 92 lines for inherited main debt at CI comparison base `465c110e4975` (not this PR's tests); CI-equivalent merge-index ratchet passed: 6,586,478 lines / 6,586,478 ceiling, zero slack.
- Red before each owning fix: the maintenance regression received `mode: spawned`; the restoration regression received only the unowned-busy-port error with no reload.
- Named tests, run serially under `timeout 120`: `src/infra/process-respawn.test.ts` (26 passed, 36.67 s wall including native fixture compilation); `src/daemon/launchd.test.ts` (78 passed, 13.16 s); `src/infra/process-respawn.runtime-unavailable.test.ts` (17 passed, 6.55 s); `src/cli/gateway-cli/run-loop.test.ts` (174 passed, 33.45 s). CI seconds pending.
- Touched-file type-aware lint plus compiler diagnostics: `node scripts/run-oxlint.mjs --type-aware --type-check --tsconfig config/tsconfig/oxlint.core.json` with the four changed TypeScript files, under `timeout 120`: passed. Touched-file formatting and `git diff --check`: passed.
- Shared autoreview, Codex, P0–P2, complete local snapshot against `795a03fe2429`: scoped-clean, no actionable findings. Full recovery-owner context included. Local ClawSweeper was unavailable in the inspected checkout (dirty/uninstalled); an automatic hosted review receipt is queued on this head, so no duplicate request was posted.
- `pr-simplify`: retained the existing state-owner and compensation owners; production growth is 32 non-whitespace lines, tests +52 lines. The dedicated test-line allocation covers the two distinct regressions and isolated test state.
- No live macOS box was available. Linux Testbox cannot prove launchd or native app behavior; no live Linux claim is made. No broad local suite, packaging, container, or browser run was used; PR CI owns broad proof.

Exact-head [CI run](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/42522591684) read at 2026-11-08 20:57 UTC: 14 successful checks, 26 pending, 53 skipped, no failures reported. Broad proof is pending; this is not a green-CI claim.

prs.title: fix: speed up GitHub publication in repositories with many sessions
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes slow GitHub publication commit preparation in repositories with thousands of session branches, where fetching a small new commit negotiates unrelated session histories.

## User Impact

GitHub publication and publication base refresh spend less time acquiring missing commits. A synthetic large-repository fixture reduces commit preparation from 578 ms to 317 ms and preparation with missing file contents from 1,053 ms to 693 ms. Ancestry, trees, requested contents, authenticated repository selection, and shallow boundaries are preserved. No migration, configuration, or operator action is required.

The cached-commit path still fetches nothing. Its measured median changes from 63 to 69 ms, with overlapping ranges and a lower candidate p95; the combined probe adds about 1.5 ms of JavaScript CPU on that path. This is a bounded negotiation improvement, not a claim to eliminate every ref/pack scan or every source of GitHub action latency.

## Why This Change Was Made

The acquisition owner supplies cached target/default base commits as negotiation tips, following the existing managed-base refresh pattern. A single offline physical-object batch probe returns both commit presence and cached tips, so there is no additional process just to discover tips. If no cached base is available, normal negotiation remains available. Content hydration negotiates from its already acquired commit.

Callers still need local merge bases and trees, so an API existence check cannot replace acquisition. The verified URL remains the network destination. Managed default-base refresh already has this optimization in #195252; its remaining worktree enumeration is outside this change. Production code grows by 17 net lines, with no new cache or configuration.

## Evidence

The existing native-Git regression covers full and shallow blob:none clones, including a missing `origin/HEAD`. On the original parent it fails because the fetch advertises an unrelated session commit; with this change it offers only the cached base and preserves local-commit reuse. The content/base-refresh integration remains covered. The added coverage was audited before adjusting the budget: it extends one existing fixture and contains no duplicate added assertions or fixtures to trim.

All 28 publication suites passed before the mechanical rebase: **521 passed, 23 pre-existing skips**; the final owner test passed again (22 tests, 20.44 s wall). Native fixture smoke, formatting, affected lint, production/script/core-test typechecks and isolated Codex P0–P2 review passed. The implementation patch is unchanged by the rebase, verified with `git range-diff`.

CI at `ddd51bde83fd` failed only the test-line ratchet: **6,586,452 lines versus a 6,586,360 ceiling**, 92 over, with this PR adding 26 lines. Rebased onto latest fetched main `465c110e4975690406b48709d58a581756c85b82` and reproduced the same result locally. The explicitly authorized scoped allocation is now **118 = 26 publication negotiation-tip regression lines + 92 inherited lines**, with a one-line reason in `config/test-lines-allocations/publication-fetch-negotiation.txt`; the shared scalar is unchanged.

`pnpm check:test-lines-ratchet --base 465c110e4975690406b48709d58a581756c85b82 --no-merge-base` passes locally: **total 6,586,452; ceiling 6,586,452; slack 0**. Fresh Codex review covers the allocation adjustment. CI for replacement head `2b13c9faa269be687f6a0dbf714c0b6c99d2bc97` is pending; the PR remains unmerged.

<details>
<summary>Reproducible owner benchmark and trace breakdown</summary>

The fixture contains 13,509 refs, 1,583 packs, 2,437 linked worktrees, 62,000 files / 1.14 GB, 600,000 synthetic historical blobs, and a shallow blob:none clone. Git 2.56.0 on Apple Silicon/APFS; all data is synthetic. Linked worktrees have valid no-checkout registration metadata. The source has one shallow root. Measurements use the real owner and command broker, a local file:// remote, warm broker startup, five counterbalanced A/B pairs, and five A/A controls. Acceptance: fewer unrelated haves and lower owner wall/CPU, identical received objects and usable ancestry/content, with no >20% owner wall regression.

| Metric | Parent median / p95 | Candidate median / p95 |
|---|---:|---:|
| Missing commit wall | 577.57 / 944.33 ms | 316.52 / 320.40 ms |
| Commit + missing contents wall | 1,052.62 / 1,102.64 ms | 693.38 / 711.08 ms |
| Present commit wall | 63.02 / 75.19 ms | 69.42 / 72.83 ms |
| Missing commit native CPU | 550 / 640 ms | 260 / 270 ms |
| Missing commit JS CPU | 6.01 / 6.43 ms | 6.83 / 7.23 ms |
| Peak native RSS | 95.61 / 95.62 MiB | 47.38 / 47.59 MiB |
| Sampled JS allocation, separate runs | 0.969 / 0.977 MiB | 1.013 / 1.026 MiB |

A/A wall medians: 599.00 / 600.26 ms (0.2% difference); ranges 588.11–613.60 / 575.82–730.89 ms. A/B commit ranges: 563.66–944.33 / 311.76–320.40 ms; content ranges: 1,030.95–1,102.64 / 678.87–711.08 ms. With five samples, p95 is the observed maximum. Host load is recorded per run. Sampled allocation includes collected JS objects, not native allocation; native memory is peak RSS. Native receipts include the local upload-pack children, so they measure combined fixture work rather than isolated Gateway CPU/RSS. Small JS costs are disclosed rather than claimed as improvements.

Packets show **13,507 → 1 haves**, ten → one negotiation rounds, and unchanged **3 → 3 received objects** (4 → 4 with contents). Installed packs remain 15,148 bytes (15,244 with contents); these are not wire-byte counts. Median `GIT_TRACE2_PERF` phases: negotiation **108.23 → 1.56 ms**, server object enumeration **115.48 → 1.35 ms**, fetch_refs **432.32 → 176.99 ms**. The earlier all-ref completeness walk remains **77.85 → 78.30 ms**. Phases nest and must not be summed.

```sh
python3 scripts/perf/worktree-hydration-fixture.py /path/to/disposable-fixture \
  --advancing --shallow --extra-refs 13505 --extra-packs 1326 --linked-worktrees 2437
# Save the parent owner before applying the patch.
git show 5d36e64316935ccec7b847e489214381087ed8a8:src/gateway/github-publication-git-transport.ts > /path/to/parent-transport.ts
node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs scripts/perf/publication-fetch-measure.ts \
  --fixture /path/to/disposable-fixture --output /path/to/new-parent-result \
  --base-file /path/to/parent-transport.ts
node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs scripts/perf/publication-fetch-measure.ts \
  --fixture /path/to/disposable-fixture --output /path/to/new-candidate-result
```

Run serially with fresh output directories, counterbalance five pairs, and repeat the parent for A/A controls. Add `--contents`, `--present`, or `--allocation` for the other rows. `--base-refresh` measures the unchanged managed-base sibling. The harness verifies ancestry/content and restores only the disposable fixture's acquired packs and tracking ref.

</details>

prs.title: fix(memory): add reusable read-only search managers
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Repeated Gateway `memory.search` requests should reuse Memory Core's query-only SQLite reader without losing search-triggered discovery of new or changed notes. Index creation, upgrade repair, source scanning, embeddings, and publication must remain writer-owned, including when no default writer/watch loop is active.

## Solution

Retain the registry-owned search reader, but run nonempty `onSearch` requests through **writer check → incremental sync/native publication → writer drain/close → reader revalidation → query-only query**. An existing registry-owned transient maintenance writer performs the scan, with unchanged hashes and embedding cache reuse; this is not an unconditional forced rebuild. Initial missing/invalid index preparation still uses the existing writer recovery path.

This update normally merges main `acbeb3a07197dbdbe89dd674f40b27279c912382`, retaining the native SQLite publication worker and `MemoryIndexDatabase.openPublished` owner introduced upstream. No rebase or force push was used.

## User Impact

- The same Gateway reader sees a newly created or edited note before returning the next search, with or without a running default writer.
- Reader connections remain `PRAGMA query_only=1`; they do not sync, migrate, write vector tables, start watchers/listeners, or own native publication.
- Search freshness can wait for source scanning, embedding changes, and publication. It is no longer published-index-only behavior and does not promise a latency improvement for every request.
- Legacy runtimes without the optional private reusable-manager hook retain transient CLI acquisition and request cleanup.
- This does not change the default model-facing `memory_search` tool's acquisition purpose or its 30-second deadline, and does not claim to fix the production slow-point report.

## Lifecycle and Compatibility Contract

- **Writer authority:** refresh uses the retained reader's registry, resolved settings, database path, and captured state-owner environment. It delegates authority, never its query-only connection, to canonical writer admission. A changed cwd cannot select a different state owner or evade the original admission refusal.
- **Settlement:** accepted writer work settles before reader query/close; cancellation rejects the result without releasing native cleanup custody. Failed transient-writer close remains registry-owned for retry. Late maintenance acquisition declines during global teardown rather than waiting on the reader that teardown is draining.
- **Reader lifetime:** one retained reader per resolved key, until close, replacement, failed-candidate cleanup, plugin retirement, or shutdown. Gateway does not close reusable readers after each request.
- **Recovery:** missing/invalid indexes and schema/identity repair remain writer-owned. Valid empty indexes remain usable after writer preparation and discover a later first note. Configured fallback indexes are adopted before refresh. Native-vector debt may be repaired by the writer; the reader checks persisted vector readiness without entering write admission.
- **Disclosure:** acquisition repair warnings remain request-scoped and survive both successful and failed Gateway retrieval. The maintenance writer shares the reader's automatic-rebuild notice.
- **Data model:** this PR's FTS changes export canonical validators and reconcile derived FTS state through the existing writer savepoint, without a new PR-owned schema-version/table/column declaration. The merge inherits upstream agent schema 21. Canonical-schema preservation and legacy migration tests are not a published-updater replay.

## Evidence

Current pushed head: `12b5dc8c2b3c9e1e16ae72f9067dc0077d27f73c` (2026-09-19).

All runtime commands used one Vitest worker and one test-plan shard at a time:

```sh
OPENCLAW_VITEST_MAX_WORKERS=1 OPENCLAW_NODE_TEST_PLAN_CONCURRENCY=1 \
node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs scripts/test-projects.mts <explicit files>
```

Fresh verification and observed regressions:

- Registered-runtime forwarding regression: on the prior `74421f873f084acf4f7f47dc264a90420e8fea5e` implementation, the actual Memory Core `register` / `createLazyMemoryRuntime(host)` boundary left `getReusableMemorySearchManager` absent (**target regression failed: 0 forwarding calls**), matching normal Gateway fallback to transient `purpose: "cli"`. After the fix, the same registered boundary forwards two concurrent reusable acquisitions through the host-bound runtime (**12 registration tests passed; 22 unrelated tests skipped**), while the existing scoped-close regression remains green and ordinary acquisition is not called.
- Initial integrated reader suite: **20 passed / 3 failed**. Repaired valid-empty refresh, fallback-provider refresh, and query-only vector readiness rather than weakening their outcome assertions.
- Added real runtime state-owner regression: failed before repair (search incorrectly resolved `[]` after original admission was revoked), then passed after captured-owner delegation. An existing default-manager cancellation regression also exposed and corrected an over-broad early abort check.
- Final reader + real Gateway/runtime + state-owner run: **3 files / 50 passed** (reader 24, Gateway 22, state-owner 4). Includes fresh-note visibility through the same manager, query-only assertions, no unchanged re-embedding, publication/cancel/global-close drain, and failed refresh cleanup retry.
- Native publication, transfer, borrowed connection, registry/retirement, provider leases, generation lease, and deadline final run: **8 files / 80 passed**.
- Supporting stable-input run: **8 files / 167 passed**, including canonical FTS preservation (8), orchestration (31), real model-tool manager (24), tools (42), budget (12), and overlapping reader/Gateway/state-owner cases. Later changes were bounded structural/type-safety cleanup, followed by the 50- and 80-case reruns above.
- Additional merged-candidate schema/readonly/write/runtime lanes: **5 files / 74 passed** (canonical schema, legacy migration, agent schema 21 invalidation, write owner, retained readonly scope) and **2 files / 48 passed** (runtime negotiation and actual provider-owner retirement). These precede the final bounded refresh fixes; they are not a full repository rerun.
- Memory Core package-boundary `node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p extensions/memory-core/tsconfig.json --noEmit`: **passed**. Standard boundary-prepared type-aware/type-check oxlint: **7 changed files, 0 warnings / 0 errors**. Two changed core integration test files: **0 warnings / 0 errors**.
- Full candidate TypeScript formatting (29 files), staged max-lines ratchet, exact shrink-only assertion-safety ratchet, and candidate-versus-merged-main `git diff --check`: **passed**. The inherited merge adds an upstream-only blank EOF in `CHANGELOG/2026.9.5.md` versus the old head; it was not edited or hidden.
- An all-extension tsgo attempt using the broad `extensions/tsconfig.json` was stopped under host memory pressure; it is **not a pass**. The focused canonical Memory Core lane above completed. Full build, all-repository types/tests, hosted CI, live WebSocket smoke, and published-updater × exact-candidate-SHA replay were not completed for this head. The contributor cannot manufacture that published-driver/updater evidence, and the prior administrator CI rerun attempt remains forbidden (HTTP 403).

Earlier [live WebSocket evidence](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/143295#issuecomment-5611497860) and released 2026.9.5 transient-manager observations remain historical, not current-head live proof.

## Why This Change Was Made / Remaining Review

The requester explicitly selected **writer-driven on-search freshness**, matching the review recommendation, rather than accepting stale published-only reads. That implementation choice is now exercised through the real Gateway handler and runtime fixture.

**Not merge approval:** maintainer acceptance of the optional private retained-runtime lifetime contract remains outstanding. A published-updater × exact-candidate-SHA migration replay remains missing. Fresh integrated self-review was performed; independent/delegated autoreview was not run because this task explicitly prohibited further delegation. Native worker ownership was retained; no production Gateway or installed runtime was changed. Pending/failing remote checks must be resolved or attributed by the repository's owners; local passing tests do not waive them.

Supersedes the reusable-reader foundation portion of #139013.

prs.title: fix(ui): preserve observer E2E after Details filtering
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The scheduled UI E2E check waits for an ordinary-child Details renderer intentionally removed in #195354.

## User Impact

No product behavior changes. Restore the native Details fixture while preserving observer-to-preview E2E coverage and its zero-child-history contract.

## Why This Change Was Made

Commit `a5888561dd11` removed ordinary children from Details. Use four native subagents and the native Details row selector/count. Preserve both positive `session.observer` headline updates, the obsolete-run negative assertion, the original artifact directory and `initial-wide.png` / `live-wide.png` captures, and zero child-history reads.

Native Details rows show names, status and elapsed time, without observer headlines. The actual preview assertion therefore targets the existing ordinary parent's sidebar row, using its real session/run identity. Enable sidebar previews, expand navigation, and await the acknowledged narration subscription before emitting. Advance the fixed clock by the sidebar’s existing two-second minimum display period before testing stale-run rejection and the next headline. No added sessions, helper, suite or product renderer. Test delta: +21/-21, net 0; no retry, timeout, skip, baseline, allocation or ignore changes.

The source trace is pinned to `465c110e4975690406b48709d58a581756c85b82`:

- [Header Details supplies desktop presentation and both native navigation callbacks](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/465c110e4975690406b48709d58a581756c85b82/ui/src/pages/chat/chat-pane-header-layout.ts#L374-L394); [desktop composition passes that presentation to Background](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/465c110e4975690406b48709d58a581756c85b82/ui/src/pages/chat/components/chat-details-session.tsx#L568-L574).
- [Background selects the native branch](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/465c110e4975690406b48709d58a581756c85b82/ui/src/pages/chat/components/chat-details-background.tsx#L227-L250), which [renders ChatDetailsSubagents](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/465c110e4975690406b48709d58a581756c85b82/ui/src/pages/chat/components/chat-details-background.tsx#L308-L322). `ChatSubagentActivity` still exists at line 297 in the alternative fallback; changing only the fixture to native children cannot select it in this desktop scenario.
- [Native row content has no observer headline](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/465c110e4975690406b48709d58a581756c85b82/ui/src/pages/chat/components/chat-details-subagents.tsx#L79-L118). Native keys are [folded out of sidebar navigation](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/465c110e4975690406b48709d58a581756c85b82/ui/src/components/app-sidebar-session-tree.ts#L126-L144), so there is no native-child sidebar preview to target either.
- Ordinary session previews still [consume live observer events](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/465c110e4975690406b48709d58a581756c85b82/ui/src/components/app-sidebar-session-narration.ts#L515-L531) and [filter by the active run before displaying headlines](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/465c110e4975690406b48709d58a581756c85b82/ui/src/components/session-row-subtitle.ts#L84-L106). This remains a real product flow, with no direct component mount or test-only seam.

- [The sidebar deliberately holds a subtitle for two seconds](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/465c110e4975690406b48709d58a581756c85b82/ui/src/components/app-sidebar-session-projection.ts#L736-L753). The fixture must advance its frozen clock; it does not sleep or change a timeout.

Related: #195354.

## Evidence

- Original failure: [scheduled run 42520053008, job 128851534729](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/42520053008/job/128851534729), head `51b8257b29b8`. Details opens, then line 94 waits for its absent Subagents disclosure.
- The same original scenario passed [42514980580](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/42514980580/job/128836210248) at `109bfcd6fb2b` (2.682s) and [42504921828](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/42504921828/job/128805738173) at `da3cea2ce4a2` (2.672s), both before the introducing commit.
- Prior candidate `26f21533546e` has [green CI 42523372561](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/42523372561), including lint/types and both browser scenarios (2.209s and 12.746s; file 14.971s). This is explicitly prior-head evidence; the restored observer assertions require new-head PR CI.
- Current `node --check` on the named file and `git diff --check` pass under the required lock and timeouts. Local dependencies are absent; current-head lint/type proof is supplied by PR CI below. No browser, container, dependency install or remote warmup ran on the production Gateway host.
- Current fresh independent autoreview (Codex, P0–P2) reviewed the complete staged candidate against `465c110e4975`, including the native Details and sidebar observer, subtitle-hold and screenshot owners: scoped-clean, no actionable findings. Browser visibility remains for CI to prove. No extra hosted review was requested under the lane's prohibition on additional CI triggers.
- [Intermediate CI 42524762391](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/42524762391/job/128866245132), head `1d7dee594d2a`, showed the first live preview but held its replacement indefinitely because `Date.now()` was frozen. The fixture now advances that synthetic clock before both later assertions, matching the existing subtitle owner. This is a code/fixture correction, not a CI rerun or timeout increase. Final-head browser and static proof is recorded below.

- Final head `05f5d409c7bc8c434d26ca0ef5ae14048a664a6f`: [CI 42525187658](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/42525187658) has passed the [UI E2E job](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/42525187658/job/128867622553), `check-lint`, `check-lint-core-2`, and `check-test-types-core-4`. The restored observer scenario took 2.959s; the request-clock sibling 15.649s; whole file 18.632s. Broader UI unit/baseline jobs are still running as of 21:33Z; no overall CI-green or merge claim.

prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

A paired-node Claude turn checks that the saved account still exists, then waits for skill setup, history authorization, and an approval retry. Removing the account during one of those waits could still submit the turn.

A later change also forwarded two thinking environment keys on every Claude node invoke. A released node decoder rejects those keys, so the Gateway now sends them only when the node advertises support.

## Evidence

Head `22a8f8ea755` on macOS. The Gateway behavior is `4ea1a89e172`; the later commits only allocate test lines. Claude Code 2.1.309 is `/opt/homebrew/bin/claude`, which resolves to `/opt/homebrew/Caskroom/claude-code@latest/2.1.309/claude`. A loopback Gateway pairs a node. The session is created with the Claude CLI runtime and saved account `anthropic:pasted`, then placed on that node. Exec approval is required. The node runs the product Claude invoke handler with that resolved binary. The saved credential is a synthetic bearer token. Its value is not shown.

Retained account. The first node frame asks for approval. After one allow, the second frame launches the real binary. Claude Code exits 1. The Gateway log is:

```console
Embedded agent failed before reply: Failed to authenticate. API Error: 401 Invalid bearer token
TRACE retained status=error frames=2 launches=1
```

The invoke carried `CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN`. It did not carry `CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_ADAPTIVE_THINKING` or `MAX_THINKING_TOKENS`. This node did not advertise `claude-cli-thinking-env-v1`.

Removal while that Gateway approval is pending, then allow once. The real binary is not launched:

```console
Embedded agent failed before reply: Saved account "anthropic:pasted" was removed. Select a connected account or sign in again under Models, then retry. OpenClaw did not submit this turn.
TRACE removed status=error frames=1 launches=0
```

A node that does not advertise `claude-cli-thinking-env-v1` keeps `CLAUDE_CODE_AUTO_COMPACT_WINDOW` and drops the two thinking keys from both env and clearEnv. A node that advertises the capability receives both keys, and the current node decoder accepts them.

## Real behavior proof

- **Behavior or issue addressed:** A retained saved account on a node-placed Claude chat turn reaches the real Claude Code binary after one approval. Removing that account while the Gateway approval is pending sends no second invoke and does not launch the binary. Thinking environment keys are sent only to a node that advertises `claude-cli-thinking-env-v1`.
- **Real environment tested:** macOS, worktree `/tmp/oc-193712`, runtime commit `4ea1a89e172` (current head `22a8f8ea755` adds only the test-line allocation). Claude Code 2.1.309 at the Homebrew cask path above. The Gateway listens on loopback. The node is paired and runs `handleClaudeCliNodeInvoke`. The chat turn uses `sessions.create`, `sessions.patch`, `chat.send`, and `agent.wait`.
- **Exact steps or command run after this patch:** Start the loopback Gateway with the saved synthetic account and exec ask set to always. Pair the node and point its Claude path at the resolved 2.1.309 binary. Create a Claude CLI session on that node. Send a short reply request. Allow the exec approval once. Send again, remove the saved account when the approval is requested, then allow once.
- **Evidence after fix:** Gateway and node terminal output from that chat turn:

  ```console
  Embedded agent failed before reply: Failed to authenticate. API Error: 401 Invalid bearer token
  TRACE retained status=error frames=2 launches=1
  Embedded agent failed before reply: Saved account "anthropic:pasted" was removed. Select a connected account or sign in again under Models, then retry. OpenClaw did not submit this turn.
  TRACE removed status=error frames=1 launches=0
  ```

- **Observed result after fix:** The retained account produces two node frames and one launch of Claude Code 2.1.309. The binary rejects the synthetic bearer token with API 401 and exit code 1. Removing the account while approval is pending produces one node frame, zero launches, and the message that OpenClaw did not submit the turn. The thinking keys are absent from that invoke.
- **What was not tested:** A second physical computer, a released v2026.11.1 node build, and a completed model reply from a real Anthropic account. The synthetic token is rejected by Claude's API.

## Summary

Recheck the saved account before a paired-node Claude frame is sent, including after history authorization and on the approval retry. A detached chat turn reads the live Gateway. Thinking environment keys are forwarded only when the node advertises `claude-cli-thinking-env-v1`. An omitted working directory matches the directory stored on the approval plan.

prs.title: feat(qa): compare completed runs using captured conditions
prs.body:
Closes #138134.

## What Problem This Solves

QA runs with matching scenario names can still use different task contents, source revisions, or runner settings. Comparing their results without checking those conditions can be misleading.

## Why This Change Was Made

Adds `qa parity-report --cross-harness` using identities captured by the existing flow-suite runner and rechecked before summary publication. Missing, incomplete, or mismatched inputs return `not-comparable`; matching inputs show scenario outcomes, regressions, elapsed time, and separate harness/primary-model/alternate-model identities.

This stays inside QA Lab, adds no dependency, and leaves existing parity modes unchanged. No winner selection, token-cost ranking, or authenticated harness-version claims. Custom execution setups and unified/runtime-pair summaries are not eligible.

## User Impact

Developers can check recorded conditions before comparing completed runs. Older summaries remain readable but require a fresh supported run for this mode.

## Evidence

- 39 focused comparison/CLI tests plus 277 existing suite/parity tests covered. One existing Crabline test could not read process identity in the macOS sandbox; the unchanged owning suite passed 33/33 with host process access.
- `pnpm build`, changed-file gates, `pnpm docs:list`, and `git diff --check` passed. An initial concurrent build/lint lock collision was resolved by running the gates serially, without bypassing the lock.
- Independent code review through P2 found no actionable findings.
- Actual source-checkout CLI proof at `688a8b90703e79e6ac65838ce9d0a2ac149f81af`: three local `mock-openai` suites passed; two matching runs compared successfully, while a changed readiness timeout was rejected. This proves producer-to-report plumbing, not a live cross-harness benchmark or npm-install behavior.

<details>
<summary>CLI commands and captured results</summary>

Run from the clean source checkout with Node 24.19.0. The proof used an isolated config/state directory and no real provider credentials. Config: `{"plugins":{"allow":["qa-lab"],"entries":{"qa-lab":{"enabled":true}}}}`. `node scripts/run-node.mjs` is the source launcher behind `pnpm openclaw`.

```sh
node scripts/run-node.mjs qa suite --scenario channel-chat-baseline --provider-mode mock-openai --concurrency 1 --output-dir .artifacts/comparability-producer-proof/a
node scripts/run-node.mjs qa suite --scenario channel-chat-baseline --provider-mode mock-openai --concurrency 1 --output-dir .artifacts/comparability-producer-proof/b
OPENCLAW_QA_TRANSPORT_READY_TIMEOUT_MS=240000 node scripts/run-node.mjs qa suite --scenario channel-chat-baseline --provider-mode mock-openai --concurrency 1 --output-dir .artifacts/comparability-producer-proof/changed-timeout
```

Each exited 0 and published `counts={"total":1,"passed":1,"failed":0,"skipped":0}`. Each captured the exact commit above. The first two captured the same task, check-profile, and run-profile digests; the third differed only in run-profile digest.

```sh
node scripts/run-node.mjs qa parity-report --cross-harness --candidate-summary .artifacts/comparability-producer-proof/b/qa-suite-summary.json --baseline-summary .artifacts/comparability-producer-proof/a/qa-suite-summary.json --output-dir .artifacts/comparability-producer-proof/matching
```

Exit 0. Captured report:

```json
{"status":"comparable","reasons":[],"candidate":{"harness":"openclaw","primaryModel":"mock-openai/gpt-5.6-luna","primaryProvider":"mock-openai","alternateModel":"mock-openai/gpt-5.6-luna-alt","alternateProvider":"mock-openai","elapsedMs":8580},"baseline":{"harness":"openclaw","primaryModel":"mock-openai/gpt-5.6-luna","primaryProvider":"mock-openai","alternateModel":"mock-openai/gpt-5.6-luna-alt","alternateProvider":"mock-openai","elapsedMs":8119},"checks":[{"name":"Channel baseline conversation","candidate":"pass","baseline":"pass"}],"regressions":[]}
```

```sh
node scripts/run-node.mjs qa parity-report --cross-harness --candidate-summary .artifacts/comparability-producer-proof/changed-timeout/qa-suite-summary.json --baseline-summary .artifacts/comparability-producer-proof/a/qa-suite-summary.json --output-dir .artifacts/comparability-producer-proof/mismatch
```

Exit 1. Captured report:

```json
{"status":"not-comparable","reasons":["runProfileDigest is missing or different."]}
```

`git status --porcelain` was empty before and after. Assertions checked completed summaries, successful scenarios, exact source identity, both comparison verdicts, and model-pair reporting. No identities were filled in by hand.

</details>
