prs.title: feat(qa): replay confidence reports from portable evidence
prs.body:
## Status: draft — maintainer design decision requested

This is a proposed implementation for discussion, not an accepted product scope or a merge-ready change. It was prepared before upstream design agreement; it is now held in draft in response to the [issue review](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/138098#issuecomment-5538187135). Local validation and independent code review below do not constitute OpenClaw maintainer approval.

Before further implementation or merge review, could maintainers confirm:

1. **Ownership and CLI:** Should the existing QA Lab own portable evidence capture and offline confidence replay through these two commands?
2. **Bundle and sharing contract:** Is the proposed bounded, versioned, exact-byte format acceptable, including captured strictness settings, explicit missing inputs, content-integrity-only verification, and operator review before sharing rather than automatic redaction?
3. **Compatibility:** Is deterministic classification within the same OpenClaw build sufficient for an initial version? This proposal does not guarantee identical classifications across OpenClaw versions. If a stronger cross-version contract is required, please specify the expected behavior before the format is adopted.

The implementation and existing validation evidence remain intact. We are requesting design direction, not automatic repair or merge.

## What Problem This Solves

Related: #138098.

A QA Lab confidence report is difficult to reproduce once the producer's artifact directory changes or disappears. Sharing only a verdict does not preserve the inputs or the strictness policy used to classify them.

## Why This Change Was Made

Adds two native QA Lab commands:

- `qa confidence-export`: capture the selected manifest, every declared lane input (including explicit missing entries), timestamp, and strict flags in a bounded evidence bundle.
- `qa confidence-replay`: verify the exact bundle bytes against a separately supplied SHA-256 digest, validate embedded artifact digests and the complete input set, then run the existing classifier entirely from captured bytes.

The implementation stays within the existing QA Lab plugin and public filesystem SDK. Tests construct their own synthetic fixtures. There is no external service, repository checkout, harness fork, added package dependency, configuration setting, or persistent-state migration. Export and replay are in one PR so reviewers can exercise a complete user-facing feature rather than a foundation without a consumer.

## User Impact

Reviewers can reproduce confidence classifications without the original filesystem or provider credentials. Reports keep integrity separate from confidence verdicts: an intact bundle can still fail. Captured policy cannot be loosened at replay, and omitted entries cannot silently become missing lanes.

Input paths are relative and bounded; symlinks/hardlinks and nonregular inputs are rejected. Export never overwrites an existing file. Replay does not execute artifact-provided commands or consult artifact paths.

This is content integrity and reproducible classification, **not producer authentication, independent code testing, model-run replay, or a Workboard completion attestation**. Individual captures are not an atomic suite snapshot. Exact contents are preserved, not automatically redacted; operators must review inputs before sharing. Replay classifications may differ across OpenClaw versions.

## Evidence

### Fresh CLI proof — September 4, 2026

Rebuilt unchanged head `85755fe15e616263a180cf9ad932a82ad3beaf5b` on macOS with Node 24.19.0. `pnpm build` exited 0; the four focused files passed again (**139/139 tests**).

The actual QA CLI exported the synthetic inputs and replayed the same report after their original directory was moved. Assertions compared the complete before/after replay, including its timestamp. Replay also matched the existing `confidence-report` result except for the independently generated timestamp. Wrong digests and unsupported bundle versions exited 1; a valid bundle containing a failing lane also exited 1.

**Scope correction:** this is built **source-checkout CLI proof**, not an npm-install smoke. [QA Lab is intentionally omitted from the npm tarball](https://docs.openclaw.ai/concepts/qa-e2e-automation#observability-smokes). A preliminary direct `node openclaw.mjs qa ...` invocation failed before classification on the private `sqlite-runtime-testing` SDK import. The successful run below uses the documented source launcher, which [enables and builds private QA](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/85755fe15e616263a180cf9ad932a82ad3beaf5b/scripts/run-node.mts#L1599); no loader, dependency, or production-code workaround was added.

<summary>Exact CLI commands and captured output</summary>

From a built checkout at the PR head, create a fresh temporary proof directory with `inputs/profile.json` and `inputs/checks.json` containing the fixture JSON shown in the trace. Use this isolated config:

```json
{"plugins":{"allow":["qa-lab"],"entries":{"qa-lab":{"enabled":true}}}}
```

```bash
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/qa-lab/src/evidence-bundle.test.ts extensions/qa-lab/src/confidence-bundle.test.ts extensions/qa-lab/src/confidence-report.test.ts extensions/qa-lab/src/cli.test.ts
```

No code or CI configuration changed in this follow-up. Prior broad validation below was not rerun; the fresh checks were the build, focused tests, and CLI proof. No model/provider run, package-install test, or merge is claimed.

### Earlier validation

- `pnpm test:extension qa-lab`: **238 files passed; 3302 tests passed, 3 skipped**.
- Focused capture/replay, evidence boundary, existing classifier and CLI tests: **139 passed**.
- Rebased onto main at `be967f4a514`; `git range-diff` confirms the feature patch is unchanged. The 139 focused tests passed again on final head `85755fe15e616263a180cf9ad932a82ad3beaf5b`.
- Complete changed-file gate: **passed**, including production/test typechecks, lint, dependency checks, public plugin boundaries, dead-export scans, filesystem/storage guards, and runtime import-cycle checks.
- Independent code review through P2: **scoped-clean** after final lint fixes.
- Built CLI smoke: exported the documented synthetic one-lane profile, moved its original input directory out of reach, then successfully replayed from only the bundle and its expected digest. The output kept `integrity.scope: content-only` distinct from the strict confidence verdict.
- Adversarial fixtures cover changed bytes, mismatched digests, missing/omitted lanes, invalid JSON, unsafe paths, symlinks/hardlinks, size bounds, and attempted output overwrite. The real Commander actions are tested without mocking the bundle implementation.

Validation used Node 24 on macOS. An initial sandboxed broad run hit `/bin/ps` permission denials in existing process-lifetime fixtures; the permissioned rerun above passed. No test or CI policy was disabled to mask those failures. Live provider runs were not needed or performed.

## Compatibility and stored data

This introduces an opt-in **export artifact**, not a replacement runtime store. No SQLite tables, schema versions, existing configuration fields, or existing stored records change. There is no existing evidence-bundle format to migrate in this PR; export creates a new file and refuses to overwrite one.

Both the [bundle schema](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/85755fe15e616263a180cf9ad932a82ad3beaf5b/extensions/qa-lab/src/evidence-bundle.ts#L40) and [replay descriptor](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/85755fe15e616263a180cf9ad932a82ad3beaf5b/extensions/qa-lab/src/confidence-bundle.ts#L15) accept version 1 only. Unsupported versions are rejected, not silently converted. Older OpenClaw builds without these commands cannot replay the new bundles.

The proposed v1 promise is repeated classification with the same build, captured inputs, timestamp, and strictness settings—not identical verdicts across different classifier versions. The bundle does not pin or enforce a classifier build; retain the producer build alongside the bundle when identical replay matters. A future cross-version guarantee or format migration needs a separate decision.

The existing `qa confidence-report` remains available. The fresh CLI proof below compares its report with replay (excluding the separately generated timestamp), then compares replay before and after moving the source directory with no fields excluded. This is focused behavior proof, not a full installation upgrade/downgrade test. Maintainer agreement on the new public artifact and CLI remains pending.

prs.title: improve(ci): trim worker builds for agentic tests
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Selected agent and Gateway CI jobs compile thousands of test-only fixture outputs that these selections never use.

Related: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/195377

## User Impact

CI can prepare a smaller worker bundle while running the same tests. Unknown, broad, mixed, and build-required selections retain the full bundle.

prs.title: fix(gateway): give each utility fallback its own observer deadline
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The session observer runs its assessment call under a single abort timer (`SESSION_OBSERVER_MODEL_TIMEOUT_MS`, 30 s). That timer bounds everything inside `execute`: model preparation plus up to two `completeModel` attempts, and each attempt runs the configured `utilityModel.fallbacks` chain under the same `abortSignal` (`src/agents/utility-completion.ts:98-120` spreads the same request, including `timeoutMs: 30_000`, into every candidate).

So when the primary utility model uses its 30 s, the fallback starts with the signal already about to fire: the reporter measured the fallback chain stopped 7 ms after the primary's timeout with `caller_signal_aborted` and a 3 ms lane task. Two such failures in a row disable the observer for the run, and the notice tells the operator to add fallbacks that are already configured.

The fix sizes the one shared deadline by the configured candidate count: `30 s × (1 + fallbacks.length)`. Each candidate keeps its own unchanged 30 s call budget, and a single-model config (no fallbacks) keeps the exact 30 s bound it has today. No retry, model-selection, or notice wording changes.

Closes #191600

## Evidence

Red on the branch point, green after the change, on the reported scenario (one configured fallback):

```
$ node scripts/test-projects.mts src/gateway/session-observer-completion.test.ts
 FAIL  ... > budgets one model call per configured utility candidate
AssertionError: expected true to be false
 ❯ src/gateway/session-observer-completion.test.ts:231
    231|   expect(signal?.aborted).toBe(false);     // at 30 000 ms with a fallback configured
```

After the change, the same file, and the whole observer suite:

```
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  7 passed (7)

$ node scripts/test-projects.mts "src/gateway/session-observer*.test.ts"
 Test Files  14 passed (14)
      Tests  104 passed (104)
```

The existing `aborts stuck completions at the cap and disables the run after two failures` case still passes unchanged: with no fallbacks configured the deadline stays 30 s.

Checks:

```
$ node scripts/run-format.mts --check      # All matched files use the correct format
$ ./node_modules/.bin/oxlint <2 files>     # Found 0 warnings and 0 errors
$ node scripts/check-test-lines-ratchet.mts  # Test lines OK: 6417370; ceiling: 6417644
```

`scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p tsconfig.core.json` fails in this checkout with pre-existing dependency drift unrelated to this change (`@openclaw/fs-safe/advanced` missing `overwriteFileHandleWithAuthority`, `@openclaw/fs-safe/atomic` missing `DirectoryMode`, and `string`→`number` mismatches in `src/cli`, `src/config/io.audit.ts`, `src/infra`). None of those diagnostics touch the two files in this PR.

## Surface area

- `src/gateway/session-observer-completion.ts`: a `resolveObserverDeadlineMs` helper (candidate count from `readUtilityModelSetting`) and the timer that consumes it. 13 added lines, 1 removed.
- `src/gateway/session-observer-completion.test.ts`: one regression case asserting the fallback still has time at 30 s and that the chain is still bounded at 60 s for one fallback.
- `config/test-lines-allocations/session-observer-fallback-deadline.txt`: 26 allocated test lines.

prs.title: fix: startup waits for transient shared-state schema admission
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Repairs Gateway startup failure after an upgrade when a foreign shared-state schema lease is encountered immediately before the webhook completion read.

Related: #194770

## Release scope

Deferred to the next beta per the maintainer's November 8, 2026 direction. This PR and its diagnostic runs are not prerequisites for 2026.11.5-beta.2. That release retains its previously frozen candidate and is recovering its original green qualification evidence. Do not adopt this patch into beta.2.

## User Impact

Startup can wait for transient schema admission instead of failing immediately. Genuine offline maintenance, cancellation, and stale database identity still refuse the read. No schema migration or configuration change.

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing read owner uses bounded acquisition at native borrowing and final queued dispatch, sharing the existing five-second budget. It never retries an entered query, snapshot, consumer callback, or cleanup. Regression coverage includes the real startup completion path and queued admission. Offline-custody inspection and synthetic benchmark/fixture callers implement immediate acquisition, without ordinary-read retries.

This is based on frozen beta source, not a rebase onto main. It does not adopt a new candidate or qualify publication. A main forward-port remains required.

## Evidence and remaining gates

- Original macOS Node26 upgrade from 2026.11.2: run42512174792/job128829070373. Installation succeeded; webhook completion read failed after46.3ms, at3.3s total startup, with a foreign sqlite-maintenance schema owner PID22176. This was not a five-second timeout. Its command, parent and lease duration remain unknown. Concurrent gateway-status PID22154 does not establish attribution.
- Independent read-only investigation found no demonstrated leaked lease or misordered updater teardown. Frozen-source startup-metadata-live-read.worker.ts deliberately holds schema custody around an immutable read through native close. Local gateway status advisory plugin metadata can reach that path even after failed RPC. This is a legitimate candidate producer, not proven attribution to PID22176. Removing custody violates immutable-source safety; broad startup reordering is not justified by the retained evidence. The five-second bound is policy, not an observed holder duration. This patch is admission repair, not an established ownership-lifecycle fix or a guarantee that every asynchronous read waits.
- Original independent patch review found an incorrect cancellation expectation, corrected to assert original error identity. It missed interface callers subsequently caught by hosted CI; it is not final-head proof.
- CI42519576496 exposed missing acquisition adapters in Gateway custody inspection and benchmark, plus formatting. Corrected at d60ba854/fe1f0520/a13471fd, including the embedded fixture discovered by caller tracing.
- PR CI42520253958/job128852443207 exposed an invalid persisted-owner fixture: missing required configPath and invalid process owner-kind. At140206867e9493dccae364fa44a120a9a31aac51 the fixture uses LockPayload, omits owner-kind for process ownership, and supplies configPath. No production policy or timeout changed. Earlier passing malformed schema fixtures are not accepted as live-schema contention proof.
- Simplification retains one acquisition owner and existing retry helper; no new framework or startup-specific retry. Net test/support allocation146 lines. Pinned oxfmt0.74.0 and git diff --check passed; no local tests/builds/installs/preflight.
- Baseline diagnostic: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/42519561511 at test-only c2ef3ac6744ae991b693f10dd29a7f2c79216b7c. Behavioral startup-red result remains to be collected separately from formatting failures.
- Current-head Node/Bun dual-all diagnostic: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/42522043011, same-revision repair branch workflow and target140206867e9493dccae364fa44a120a9a31aac51. Superseded42521511502 failed preflight because its main workflow and target revisions differed; no tests executed. Ordinary PR CI42521448587 is also pending.
- Current-head macOS packaged-upgrade diagnostic: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/42521477971, baseline2026.11.2, workflow main at observed SHA795a03fe2429e5696a8b624dd0c0ec13e50a6f42. Explicitly cross-revision diagnostic evidence, not candidate qualification. Node26 execution and outcome remain unverified.
- Superseded macOS42519653564 failed compilation;42520837288 failed before execution because the repair was not an ancestor of the release branch;42519584586 used an unsupported workflow ref. No guard changed or setup failure counted as product proof.

prs.title: fix(sessions): failed runs hide the provider safety-precaution explanation
prs.body:
Closes #189398

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: a request that stops on a provider misalignment refusal is reported as the bare "Your request couldn't be completed." when the transcript only retained the error code.

## User Impact

User impact: when a request is stopped as a safety precaution, the failed-run message now keeps that explanation instead of collapsing into a generic failure, so operators can tell a model-side refusal apart from a broken run.

## Why This Change Was Made

`formatProviderRefusalText` still produces the pre-diagnostics copy `The provider stopped this request as a safety precaution (misalignment).` for transcripts that only kept `errorCode`, but `isProviderRefusalNoticeText` matched only the two newer strings. The legacy copy then slipped past every remaining branch of the run-failure notice and was replaced by the generic fallback.

The matcher now recognizes that copy, and both sides read one shared constant so the producer and the matcher cannot drift apart again.

## Real behavior proof

`test/chat-history-legacy-refusal-notice.e2e.test.ts` runs the path against a Gateway started as its own process in the e2e lane (`test/vitest/vitest.e2e.config.ts`, `pool: forks`, `isolate: true`):

1. The isolated test home gets a session whose transcript keeps only `errorCode` — the older shape this regression is about.
2. The failure is recorded with the shipped recorder, using the text the shipped producer returns for that code (`formatProviderRefusalText({ errorCode: "misalignment_policy_violation" })`, asserted to be the legacy notice — not a literal copied into the test).
3. The Gateway process is started, a client connects over the websocket, and `chat.history` returns what a Control UI pane would render.

Both halves of the proof were produced by CI, not by a local harness.

### Green — with the fix (head `5feb65f7`)

### Red — without the fix (head `519e5054`, matcher line reverted, everything else identical)

`checks-node-changed-2`, [run 41190601921](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41190601921/job/124506669696):


prs.title: fix(goals): require a note to resume a blocked goal
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Resuming a blocked goal with an empty note made it active again and queued another pursuit turn. The operator had not said what changed, so the same blocker came back. A blocked goal now stays blocked until the resume includes a note. Paused, limited, and completed goals can still resume without one.

The command table and the blocked-status paragraph still told people that a bare `/goal resume` makes a blocked goal active. Those two lines now say the note is required, and that an empty resume leaves the goal blocked.

## Evidence

Head `834bd8c1ed7` on macOS. An isolated loopback Gateway served the Control UI. Session `agent:main:main` held a blocked goal whose objective was `Read the operator inbox.`

In the browser, Resume with an empty note showed `Enter what changed before resuming.` The Gateway did not receive `sessions.goal.update`.

Typing `The mail grant is still missing, so stop this goal.` and choosing Resume called the Gateway. The card changed from `Goal blocked` to `Pursuing goal`, and the same run started a model turn.

```console
[ws] res ok sessions.goal.update 65ms runId=aa506ced-2261-46a0-b6a5-c3948291ae49
[ws] event agent run=aa506ced-2261-46a0-b6a5-c3948291ae49 agent=main session=main stream=lifecycle phase=start
[openai-transport] responses start provider=xai model=grok-4.7 sessionKey=agent:main:main runId=aa506ced-2261-46a0-b6a5-c3948291ae49
```

## Real behavior proof

- **Behavior or issue addressed:** A blocked goal cannot resume from the Control UI until the operator enters what changed. That noted Resume is admitted by `sessions.goal.update` and starts the model continuation. An empty note stays on the card and does not call the Gateway.
- **Real environment tested:** macOS, Node v26.12.1, worktree `/tmp/oc-192883`, head `834bd8c1ed7`. Loopback Gateway and its Control UI in Chromium. Model `xai/grok-4.7`.
- **Exact steps or command run after this patch:** Open the chat for `agent:main:main` with a blocked goal. Choose Resume with an empty note. Enter a note and choose Resume again. Read the Gateway log for `sessions.goal.update` and the following model turn.
- **Evidence after fix:** Control UI text and Gateway log:

  ```console
  empty note: Enter what changed before resuming.
  after note: Pursuing goal
  [ws] res ok sessions.goal.update 65ms runId=aa506ced-2261-46a0-b6a5-c3948291ae49
  [ws] event agent run=aa506ced-2261-46a0-b6a5-c3948291ae49 stream=lifecycle phase=start
  [openai-transport] responses start provider=xai model=grok-4.7 sessionKey=agent:main:main
  ```

- **Observed result after fix:** The empty Resume stays on `Goal blocked` and does not call the Gateway. The noted Resume returns `sessions.goal.update`, switches the card to `Pursuing goal`, and starts the `grok-4.7` turn.
- **What was not tested:** A goal database written by the latest stable package, then opened by this build. The blocked goal in this run was created on this head.

## Summary

A blocked goal stays blocked until `/goal resume` or the Control UI Resume includes a note. The command table and the blocked-status paragraph say that. Paused, limited, and completed goals can still resume without a note.

prs.title: fix(ui): remember the session Details rail collapse preference
prs.body:
Closes #194649

## What Problem This Solves

The right-hand session Details rail re-opens itself on every page load and window refocus: its mount state starts at an "auto" intent that re-docks whenever the window is wide enough, and any presentation reset (gateway reconnect scope identity changes on refocus) resets a manually collapsed rail back to that auto state. A collapsed rail cannot be kept collapsed, and it overlaps the chat column on every focus return.

Plain language: you close the side panel, switch to another window and come back, and the panel has popped open again by itself. Now the panel remembers being closed and stays closed until you open it again.

## Why This Change Was Made

A manual open/close is a durable preference; presentation-driven resets are not. The rail now persists a device-local `chatDetailsCollapsed` preference (same UI settings store as other browser-local preferences) on manual open/close, and both re-open paths — the mount initializer and the presentation-reset clause — restore that preference instead of forcing "auto". When no preference exists yet, behavior is exactly as before (auto-dock). Programmatic closes (outside click, Escape handling unchanged) do not write the preference.

## User Impact

Collapsing the Details rail survives page reloads, tab switches, and gateway reconnects; opening it manually likewise persists. Fresh profiles keep the current auto-dock behavior, so the discovery path is unchanged.

## Evidence

Real runtime runs on the latest main tree this change is based on (files byte-compared as `main` + exactly this delta; dependencies installed fresh because main added `@solidjs/vite-plugin`):

| Check | Result |
| --- | --- |
| `chat-details.browser.test.ts` new test (real browser, 1700×900 viewport where auto-dock would open): saved `chatDetailsCollapsed: true` → rail stays closed on mount AND after a gateway-scope presentation reset; manual open persists `false`; manual close persists `true` | green |
| Existing `chat-details.browser.test.ts` suite (auto-dock, revisions, mobile, Escape focus) | 20/20 green |
| `settings.chat-details.test.ts` new jsdom test: preference round-trips through `saveSettings`/`loadSettings` including unset | green |
| `chat-pane-header-details.test.tsx` (jsdom) | green |
| Red check: reverting the component wiring (initializer restore + manual persistence) makes exactly the new browser test fail | confirmed |
| `tsc --noEmit -p tsconfig.ui.json`: zero errors in changed files | verified |

## AI Assistance

This PR is AI-assisted. Used grep to trace the Details rail state machine (`chat-details.tsx` choice/intent signal), identify the two force-open paths, and implement the preference wiring. The implementer understands the code: the "auto" intent plus presentation resets are the only re-open sources, so restoring a saved preference in both spots is sufficient. All evidence above is from real local runtime execution.

## Historical Proposal and Evidence

Related: #167622

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes CLI configuration reads failing with `spawnSync EPERM` or an empty SQLite worker response inside restricted native Codex execution, while preserving complete replies on ordinary nonblocking stdout.

## User Impact

Users can run `openclaw config get tools.exec` in the affected environment without disabling the sandbox or ignoring transport failures. No configuration migration or production-state change is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

Argument-fed synchronous workers do not need stdin. Ignoring that unused pipe avoids the observed shutdown failure. Their one-shot JSON responses use direct fd writes because Node can classify restricted stdout as an unknown handle and acknowledge stream writes without delivering bytes.

The additional investigation prompted by #170373 showed that a single `writeFileSync` could truncate large diagnostics with EAGAIN on nonblocking stdout. The change is limited to `sync`, `content-version` and `file-generation`. Reclaim stdin/cancellation, session IPC, asynchronous response transport, and transport-error precedence remain unchanged.

- 36 uninstrumented current-source worker cases pass: all three modes, normal and restricted execution, nonblocking FIFO, blocking socket and forced-nonblocking socket, with a slow reader or closure after partial output. Approximately 540 KB error JSON retains the complete original diagnostic; closure remains EPIPE/nonzero.
- Six real parent/child controls retain ENOBUFS and ETIMEDOUT/SIGKILL. Each timeout occurs after 65,536 bytes were written, not merely during startup.
- Targeted infra TypeScript graph, lint, formatting and diff checks pass. Independent canonical incremental review is scoped-clean through P2.

- Regular `build:runtime` package-script command passes (88.3 s). Both build stamps identify this commit with `inputsClean: true`.
- The supported `openclaw` package-script entry (`node scripts/run-node.mjs config get tools.exec`) runs in native restricted execution with fresh synthetic SQLite/config state: exit 0, exact `{ "host": "gateway" }`, empty stderr, 2.219 s. The script was invoked directly because pnpm was absent from PATH; no source-runner guards, output adapters, sandbox changes or production state were bypassed.

The large responses above deliberately use oversized invalid paths; the reproduced defect was diagnostic loss, not evidence of ordinary snapshot/data corruption. Earlier live-WAL, source-integrity, session and reclaim proof remains applicable to unchanged paths. At that evidence revision, Bun/macOS/Windows behavior had not been validated locally. Later targeted Node/Bun regression checks do not establish full-CLI parity across platforms; see the current-revision CI and limitations below.

prs.title: fix(browser): report crashed tabs with new-tab recovery guidance
prs.body:
Closes #194667

## What Problem This Solves

When a Chromium renderer crashes, browser requests can wait for a timeout and tell the agent that the entire browser is unavailable, even though healthy tabs and newly opened tabs still work

## User Impact

Crashed tabs now return prompt, consistent guidance to open the URL in a new tab, including a screenshot requested before the automation connection attaches

Known crashed targets remain visible and closable, and implicit selection preserves the selected tab identity instead of redirecting actions to another page

Tab crash markers reflect observations from persistent automation connections — a raw screenshot-only failure returns the crash error immediately but does not persist a list marker until normal automation observes the target

## Why This Change Was Made

Keep native crash facts in the existing CDP connection lifecycle and carry them through the existing `ACT_OPERATION_FAILED` error contract

The raw screenshot adapter enables Inspector before sending page commands, while snapshot metadata fallbacks preserve terminal crash errors and cold-crashed targets can be closed through their browser owner

## Evidence

- Reproduced on unmodified `c25ff93b56723e0075a4c82a789ac3b1acd06aeb` with a real managed browser: crashed-tab snapshot timed out after 20,012 ms with browser-unavailable guidance, while a healthy sibling and a replacement tab remained usable
- Committed request and output regressions failed on the original behavior, with separate real-browser reproduction of the screenshot-first cold path
- Final real-browser cold screenshot-first validation returned the correct crash error in 7 ms, with later snapshot, screenshot and navigation errors in 3 ms each
- Complete persistent enumeration, healthy sibling access, replacement-tab recovery and crashed-target closure passed, with the target confirmed absent after close
- Browser package run: 3,151 passed and 108 skipped, with two fixture-isolation failures subsequently repaired — all seven affected connection suites then passed, 105 tests total
- Browser production types, extension test types, typed lint, formatting, line-cap and test-line checks passed
- `git diff --cached --check` passed

Live validation used headless Chrome 157 on macOS with Node 24.22.1 — Linux headed mode and live existing-session or extension-relay drivers were not exercised

The broad `check:changed` invocation was stopped after a line-cap failure, which was repaired and rechecked directly — unrelated aggregate guards remain for CI


prs.title: fix(a2a): retain accepted tasks after Gateway crashes
prs.body:
Related: #183490

## What Problem This Solves

An unexpected Gateway restart forgets an accepted A2A task before its terminal result is recorded, so polling loses the original task and retrying the same peer message can start another agent turn.

## User Impact

The original task remains queryable after a crash. Recovery reports `TASK_STATE_FAILED` with an explicit warning that external effects may have occurred, and the same peer message returns that task while its recovered terminal result is retained. The task-store recovery does not itself resume inference, but the full Gateway proof below found that core startup recovery still resumes the interrupted A2A session. The A2A wrapper reports terminal failure while the canonical core owner continues recovery; that ownership mismatch is **not yet resolved**. This does not guarantee exactly-once external effects or recover tasks already lost by an older Gateway.

This draft requests maintainer acceptance of the changed durability and admission-capacity semantics under the [storage review checkpoint](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/main/docs/reference/database-schemas/storage-changes.md#review-checkpoint-for-material-changes). Real Gateway/model E2E has now been run and exposed the remaining recovery-coordination gap below. Stable upgrade/downgrade qualification remains unrun; an older Gateway does not honor these pending records.

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing A2A task owner records admission through the worker-owned plugin-state store before dispatch or a successful response. Pending records have no TTL, reject new admissions at 500 entries per account, and are deleted only after a terminal result commits. Terminal retention remains 24 hours/500 entries. Known terminal results and newer admissions win over stale cleanup records when a message ID is reused. Uncertain write acknowledgements stay fenced until restart reconciliation; definite admission refusals remove never-admitted memory records.

Cleanup failure preserves the known result and logs an error. A remaining pending record consumes capacity; if its terminal result expires before cleanup, later recovery conservatively reports uncertainty. No SQL schema migration, configuration option, background service, or new protocol is introduced.

## Evidence

- **Blocking real Gateway/model finding on this head:** a built isolated Gateway used a real cached Qwen2.5-3B MLX model, with no paid provider or model stub, output capped at 128 tokens, and tools disabled. A normal A2A task completed. A second real model response was held by a byte-preserving transport observer, then the actual Gateway PID received SIGKILL; all task-owned processes exited and the listener disappeared. A different Gateway process reopened the same state and preserved the original failed task, replay identity, peer isolation, and prior completed result. However, core `restart-recovery` automatically resumed the interrupted context and issued another real model request: count **2 → 3**. The strict no-new-model-request assertion failed. Generic root-session continuation is documented, intentional behavior; the extra inference is not proof of duplicate external side effects (tools were disabled). The proven mismatch is that the A2A wrapper publishes terminal failure while the canonical core owner continues recovery. This candidate is **not ready** until those owners are coordinated. The source path is `session-restart-resume.ts` orphaned-run recovery → `enqueueSessionEventForHost(... source: "restart")`; the generic skip predicate does not exclude A2A. No global recovery behavior has been changed.
- **Owner decision required:** either (1) the core owner settles the interrupted A2A run without enqueueing a restart input while normal chat recovery remains unchanged, or (2) core continuation retains durable task correlation and reattaches completion to the original Task ID/peer/message identity. The missing contract is who owns restart policy and terminal publication for task-owned channels, and how core resumed turns carry durable correlation back to that task owner. A blanket A2A skip is insufficient because the current skip predicate also bypasses orphan-run settlement; unrelated `modelSelectionLocked` settings and global recovery suppression are not suitable substitutes.
- `pnpm build:runtime` passed on this head (2m59.7s). The earlier process/storage and HTTP-handler proofs below remain valid at their stated boundaries; they do not establish this missing whole-Gateway behavior.
- **Red on base `99f4ff69c621e6cb67b10514502fb1922deee547`:** the owning HTTP-handler restart regression returned `-32001 Task not found` for the original task. It passes with this change and verifies peer isolation and no replay dispatch.
- **Actual process-crash red/green:** separate Node 24.22.1 processes used production `A2aTaskStore` and `PluginStateKeyedStoreV2` against synthetic SQLite state, with `SIGKILL` after acknowledged `start()`. The base lost the original ID and admitted a new task for the replay. This candidate preserved the ID, returned the explicit ambiguous failure, denied another peer, and returned no dispatch admission on replay. All four processes exited and their state was removed. This is process/storage proof, not a Gateway HTTP/agent/model E2E; no external effects ran. The copied base module changed only SDK import locations, preserving its logic.
- **79 focused tests pass** across `task-store`, `task-store.persistence`, `http`, `inbound`, and `gateway`, using `pnpm test <files> --maxWorkers=1`. Coverage includes durable admission before first/duplicate responses, shutdown during admission, real-store capacity refusal/retry, uncertain acknowledgements, and stale cleanup versus newer pending/completed tasks. The latter two recovery-priority cases were also observed failing before the repair.
- Scoped TypeScript proof covering all A2A sources/tests and ambient declarations passes through `scripts/run-tsgo.mjs`. Targeted repository lint, formatting, commit-hook docs/line checks, `git diff --check`, and the test-line ratchet pass. The exact-head [product CI run](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/42398131930) was skipped for this draft; CI seconds are unmeasured.
- Per-file `pnpm test <file> --maxWorkers=1` wall times: task store **81.87 s**, real storage **31.10 s**, inbound **64.92 s**, HTTP **18.57 s**. Cold transform/import preparation dominates these runs; test execution per file stays below 5 seconds. The real-storage test uses the existing database-worker lane because mock storage cannot prove admission capacity or durable recovery.
- Fresh independent Codex review of the complete change against the base: **no remaining actionable findings** after the recovery-priority repair. This is an independent agent review, not a ClawSweeper or autoreview CLI result.
- `pr-simplify`: one existing task owner and the existing keyed-state API serve admission, settlement, and recovery. Shared in-memory deletion logic was consolidated. Production delta **+123/-23 (net +100)**; test/support delta **+273/-34 (net +239)**. The separate 239-line allocation covers only this change's justified regressions; no shared baseline was raised.

Requested by @GrahamMcBain: https://x.com/heyneighbor/status/2119116272671785017

OpenClaw users looking for phone control lack a discoverable guide to Phone Harness's existing native OpenClaw integration.

## User Impact

Users can find the vendor plugin installation path, choose an appropriate Gateway/device setup, expose `phone_exec` deliberately, and understand privacy and consent implications before using a personal or cloud phone. This is documentation-only: it does not introduce a driver, messaging channel, cloud account, credential store, or new runtime behavior.

Phone Harness already maintains the plugin and bundled skill. Reusing that integration follows the existing capability ladder instead of creating a competing phone runtime in core. The guide covers Gateway-host requirements, local versus cloud devices, telemetry opt-out before first use, tool profiles, sandbox limitations, session-wide approval semantics, human takeover, and consequential-action consent. Runtime and device details remain owned upstream.

Installing the plugin does not authorize messages, calls, purchases, paid cloud provisioning, or access to private verification codes. The guide recommends synthetic test data and user takeover for passwords/PINs/2FA.

## Evidence

- Audited the official [OpenClaw plugin README and source](https://github.com/phone-harness/phone-harness/tree/4bebff105af853215fb74c958c2c5e78bc275be2/integrations/openclaw), device installation guide, and cloud MCP documentation.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes chats failing to start after importing a large pull request into an empty managed workspace.

## User Impact

Users can work on the imported repository and resume initial imports rejected by an older Gateway without deleting saved source files. Ordinary edits and later refreshes retain the 50,000-path limit; file-size, total-byte and integrity checks remain enforced.

## Why This Change Was Made

The first repository import establishes the workspace rather than representing thousands of authored edits. Recognize that host-owned operation using its reserved source reference and deterministic empty baseline throughout staging, loading and application. Revalidate the retained source and baseline before recovering an older rejection. Keep accepted-checkpoint cleanup with the existing checkpoint owner.

## Evidence

- All 68 tests in github-pr-workspace-preparation.test.ts and github-pr-workspace-refresh.test.ts pass (275.91 seconds including compiler preparation; 277.95 seconds wrapper wall time).
- The registered github_publish prepare_pr path imports 50,001 source files, preserves the guest Git index and subsequent local work, and makes no remote writes. The original implementation rejected this reproduction at 50,055 changed paths.
- A persisted initial-import rejection recovers after database shutdown/reopen. The regression failed before the recovery change and now passes.
- All 8 large-inventory tests pass, including ordinary worker-result rejection with the same empty baseline and historical-checkpoint safeguards (40.90 seconds including compiler preparation; 44.01 seconds wrapper wall time).
- Core and both affected test-shard typechecks pass. Targeted type-aware lint, formatting, diff checks and test/max-lines budgets pass.
- Local autoreview: Codex gpt-6.1-sol, P0–P2, complete working-tree snapshot against 9dc3499d415c2d47e280aeac0f7c421fa482fc7a, identical source committed as 62d24445c60df3f2e0251c1cd70423fece522306: scoped clean, no actionable findings.
- CI exposed a missing trusted-wrapper inventory entry for the new shared identity module. The one-line inventory correction was reproduced red locally, then all 23 eager-import-closure tests passed, including extracted dependency resolution. The correction changes packaging only; the runtime implementation is unchanged.
- Exact-head CI at `84db8e901ccd7b418e33684c5755427c27cf8496` passed, including the required CI gates; GitHub reports CLEAN and MERGEABLE. [CI run](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/42521893115).
- Live GitHub import transport and deployment were not exercised by these isolated boundary tests. This PR remains unmerged.

The 50,001-file regression takes about 49 seconds because it exercises real Git import, both workspace copies and repeated preparation; a small synthetic inventory would miss this integration failure. Net test growth: 82 lines, recorded in the dedicated allocation. The production change shares the existing empty-source identity and keeps checkpoint recovery and cleanup with one owner; it adds no new persisted state.

Thanks to @vyctorbrzezowski for reporting and directing this repair.

## Work sessions

Linked for team reference; these sessions aren’t public.

- [Original discussion with @vyctorbrzezowski](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/dashboard/f6fd2a85-1277-439b-88cf-74531bf9e425)
- [Implementation and verification](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/dashboard/0a1dc774-5564-4511-b4bb-01d5518708c8)

## Worked on by

- @vyctorbrzezowski

Related: #186851. This fixes an independent defect reproduced on unchanged main, not a regression introduced by that PR.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: a valid queued Telegram reply can be rejected after an earlier caller finishes, including direct subagent-completion fallback.

## User Impact

Queued replies retain their own live request context. A canceled request remains rejected before network I/O. This does not add retries or relax authorization.

## Why This Change Was Made

The account-wide scheduler can drain later requests under a previous caller's async context. Capture each request's context, then restore it around both the existing network-edge admission check and dispatch. Prepared-reader cancellation, effect authority, retirement, flood budgets, and database fences remain unchanged.

The production change is +5/-1 lines, with no new scheduler or state. The four regression cases cover group and DM schedulers with active and canceled callers. Their dedicated 69-line allocation leaves the shared test baseline unchanged.

Current head: 521661b47600ba74f89da9b53677f8015e8be927. Source base: 2d7376d2e6e111ae28bdf7d9e888cbb077139204.

- The four new real-grammY scheduler cases fail on unchanged production source. All 25 tests passed after the queue fix. Ordinary type-aware source lint then found a rejection callback missing an explicit unknown type; the current head fixes that annotation only. The four affected cases, focused production/test typecheck, and diff check pass on this correction. Unchanged 25-test evidence is reused, not rerun.
- Ordinary type-aware source lint passes on both files through run-oxlint.mjs with the repository's oxlint.core.json source context. Applicable root rules are retained; two nonmatching UI-only Solid overrides were excluded because their plugin dependency is unavailable. This is typed source lint, not extension package-boundary declaration validation.
- A supported build of **only Telegram** passes: check-plugin-npm-runtime-builds.mts --package extensions/telegram, 19 entries, 73 emitted files. Four additional real-clock cases execute the emitted candidate queue with real grammY/Bottleneck: active requests use their own admission/dispatch context; canceled requests produce no second network call. The emitted chunk SHA256 is 5763ddaca718085f00d3eabe42e2b263019fb7ee08567af9246ce1556edca278. These tests use canonical source-backed host SDK resolution and synthetic fetch, not a patched runtime. Production/build inputs are unchanged by the latest type-only test correction.
- Independent source review found no actionable issues at the queue-fix snapshot; the subsequent delta is only the unknown annotation. No ClawSweeper/autoreview or maintainer approval is claimed.
- The original isolated Gateway fallback scenario passes with an equivalent in-memory queue patch on an existing baseline qaRuntime: visible, silent, fallback, private-denial, and restart. This remains separate supporting evidence, not the new candidate-package run.

**Remaining before readiness:** extension package-boundary declaration preparation did not finish within the bounded attempt. prs.title: fix(goals): block on the first authorization limit
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`update_goal` told the model to wait for the same blocker on three consecutive goal turns before marking a goal blocked. An authorization limit this session cannot change does not get better on turn two or three. The hidden "Advance the active goal" nudge keeps firing while the goal is still active, so the model repeats the same limit.

On 2026-10-31 a team-server Roboclaw session (nerfed payload `a7be6336-5cd4-48d7-86df-cda538eae143`, client report `449c85a5-d5b9-46ea-a2ea-c670ecbe2669`, OpenClaw 2026.10.9 at `731030eb512e`) held only `operator.sessions.write`. It could not dispatch Actions or merge. Several "Advance the active goal" turns restated that limit before the goal was marked blocked. Ordinary difficulty still waits for three turns. A missing scope, or another authorization limit this session cannot change, is a blocker on the first turn.

The same exception now appears in the per-turn active-goal context, which ordinary turns and admitted goal continuations both receive. Once the goal is blocked, continuation eligibility stops. An empty resume staying blocked is [openclaw/openclaw#192883](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/192883). This pull does not change that resume rule and does not change the grant.

## Evidence

Head `f56fa56c733` on macOS. An isolated loopback Gateway used `xai/grok-4.7`. The main agent allow list was only `update_goal`, so the session had no mail tool and no shell. `chat.send` delivered `/goal set Read the newest subject line from the operator Gmail inbox.` and then `Do the goal now.`

The model searched the grant, found no Gmail tool, and called `update_goal` on that same turn. The tool result stored the goal as blocked with `continuationTurns` 0. The visible reply named the limit. The Gateway log has no `session_goal_continue` event during the run or in the following 8 seconds.

```console
dispatch_action update_goal result: {"status":"updated","goal":{"status":"blocked","continuationTurns":0}}
assistant: I couldn't read the newest Gmail subject line. This session has no Gmail or mail tool, so the inbox is unreachable from here. That is a capability limit this session cannot change.
session_goal_continue count: 0
```

## Real behavior proof

- **Behavior or issue addressed:** On the first turn, a missing mail grant makes the model mark the active goal blocked and send the visible limit. No automatic goal nudge follows. Other blockers still use the three-turn rule in the tool text.
- **Real environment tested:** macOS, Node v26.12.1, worktree `/tmp/oc-192975`, head `f56fa56c733`. Loopback Gateway, model `xai/grok-4.7`, agent tool allow list `update_goal` only.
- **Exact steps or command run after this patch:** Start that Gateway. Create a session. Send the Gmail goal text, then `Do the goal now.` Read `chat.history` for the `update_goal` result and the assistant text. Confirm the Gateway log never records `session_goal_continue`.
- **Evidence after fix:** Gateway chat history and log counts:

  ```console
  dispatch_action update_goal result: {"status":"updated","goal":{"status":"blocked","continuationTurns":0}}
  assistant: I couldn't read the newest Gmail subject line. This session has no Gmail or mail tool, so the inbox is unreachable from here. That is a capability limit this session cannot change.
  session_goal_continue count: 0
  ```

- **Observed result after fix:** The same turn records `blocked` and `continuationTurns` 0, then shows the authorization limit. No later automatic nudge is queued.
- **What was not tested:** A provider auth error from a tool the grant does include, and a second machine. Ordinary three-turn blockers were not run through the model.

## Summary

`update_goal`, `docs/tools/goal.md`, and `ACTIVE_GOAL_CONTEXT_SUFFIX` now say a missing scope or other authorization limit this session cannot change blocks on the first turn. Difficulty and missing polish still do not. A rejected complete-to-blocked transition still requires the stored goal to stay unchanged.

prs.body:
## Current Status — 2026-11-08: Closed as Superseded

[PR #188090](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/188090), merged on 2026-10-31 as `18516599b1d417fee621b2fd2ceda21107bc038a`, now carries `callerScopedCreation` into grant provenance and accepts it in `hasCronCreatorGrantProvenance`. The original missing-provenance defect addressed here is therefore already fixed on main.

Main also intentionally supports broader scoped-operator creation. Reapplying this older patch would duplicate provenance handling and restore narrower assumptions that no longer match upstream policy. **No replacement Cron branch was pushed.**

Verification against main `097f990aa244e71eeb7cacc2348c92df90d73b5d`:

- All 60 tests in `cron-creator-authority-grant.test.ts`, `agent-runtime-identity-token.test.ts`, and `cron-creator-transports.integration.test.ts` passed through the repository runner on an exact-main working/index tree.
- These upstream suites cover signed requester creation, tool-free persistence, scope isolation and revocation under current policy. The old admin-only assumptions were not reintroduced.
- This is current-source local verification, not a new live Gateway deployment or a new CI run of this old PR head.

**Closed on 2026-11-08 as superseded by #188090.** Current main `465c110e4975690406b48709d58a581756c85b82` was rechecked before closure and still carries the provenance fix. This PR was closed, not merged; no branch was deleted or deployed. The branch remains at `d485cdba8ea9f3e5ec428d89af5d26f3a33410ac`. The original proposal and earlier evidence are preserved below as history, not as a recommendation to reapply the patch.

## Historical Proposal and Evidence

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: an authenticated remote Control UI administrator's agent cannot create a tool-free automation because its requester-only creator grant is rejected when the runtime identity is minted.

## User Impact

The administrator can create that automation from the admitted turn. This does not grant the scheduled run additional tools or change existing automation-management permissions. No migration or configuration change is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

The creator admission already records `callerScopedCreation` for a fresh remote administrator turn, but the later grant-provenance check does not carry that fact forward. Preserve it only for a requester-only grant from the same live run; keep the existing revocation, run-ID, and management-only checks.

## Evidence

- On OpenClaw 2026.9.6, the agentic `cron.add` path rejected this grant with `cron creator authority grants require tool-surface or authenticated-requester provenance`. A separately operator-created, tool-free job ran and delivered, narrowing the defect to agentic creation rather than scheduler execution.
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/gateway/cron-creator-authority-grant.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` passed (9.24 seconds for the shard).
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/gateway/agent-runtime-identity-token.test.ts --maxWorkers=1 -t 'remote administrator requester grant'` passed signed and direct runtime-identity paths (128.26 seconds including compiler preparation). This file exercises the actual token-minting boundary that rejected the grant; the lighter grant test alone cannot prove that path.
- Added a Gateway Cron-handler integration test backed by an isolated, real `CronService` store. From an admitted remote `operator.admin` Control UI turn it issues a requester-only grant, mints the agent runtime identity without a final tool-surface capture, invokes `cron.add` with `payload.toolsAllow: []`, and reads the persisted job. The stored job has no `runtimeAuthority`.
- The same test pauses a second create during asynchronous delivery validation, revokes the administrator's device authority, then observes rejection and an unchanged store. A nonadministrator with a spoofed `controlUiAdmin` marker is denied remote-admin admission; its direct WebSocket `cron.add` fails the `operator.admin` method-scope check before persistence, and an out-of-scope agent target fails the Cron handler with the store unchanged. This does not claim that ordinary restricted agent creation is forbidden: a separate existing test preserves that path.
- Red/green check: with the original grant module from the parent commit temporarily restored, the new test failed at runtime-identity minting with `cron creator authority grants require tool-surface or authenticated-requester provenance`. With the patch restored, all six tests in `cron-creator-transports.integration.test.ts` passed. After the follow-up test-type fix, all six passed again (42.01 seconds for the shard, including compiler preparation). The original module was restored after the red run; the follow-up commits change only the test file.
- The integration test uses synthetic clients, an isolated Gateway handler context, and a temporary Cron store; it is not itself a live network Gateway/deployment test.
- A backport of the source fix to OpenClaw 2026.9.7 (hotfix commit `42a2f16f8bffeae001c56a0ced3a30059cfb1ea9`) was deployed on 2026-10-02 after candidate Doctor lint (38 checks, zero errors), a scoped embedding lint check (one check, zero errors), and a verified pre-update state backup. The installed Gateway reported the matching build ID; `/readyz` and `/healthz` returned HTTP 200, and the configured chat channel was connected with a successful live probe.
- From a real authenticated remote Control UI administrator agent turn on that Gateway, the agent created a disabled, tool-free automation with `payload.toolsAllow: []`, read back the stored job with that restriction intact, and removed it. This was an agentic automation-tool call, not a direct Cron RPC or a synthetic handler test. The disabled job was not executed, so this proves creation and persistence, not scheduled-run delivery.
- `oxfmt`, targeted Oxlint, and `git diff --check` passed on the original head. ClawSweeper found a possibly undefined runtime identity in the new test; follow-up commit `1a18b598f9e` uses the existing `expectDefined` assertion before dereferencing it.
- Merge commit `b2ea7a917a1e995eb53fece5aea7580ba267c872` incorporates `main` at `3932cbe4c91c5f3838a141f6a8cdeeb48fdf50b6`. The sole conflict was in integration-test imports; the merged test also supplies the now-required context argument to `expectDefined`. `git diff --check` passed for the PR delta.
- On the merged head, `node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p test/tsconfig/tsconfig.core.test.gateway-methods.json` passed after reconciling dependencies with the committed lockfile. Direct Vitest using `test/vitest/vitest.gateway-database-workers.config.ts` passed all six `cron-creator-transports.integration.test.ts` cases with local loopback permission. The restricted attempt had passed five cases and failed the CLI-local case solely on `listen EPERM 127.0.0.1`. The repository wrapper passed the focused `cron-creator-authority-grant.test.ts` and `agent-runtime-identity-token.test.ts` selection.
- The first exact-head CI run after resolving conflicts found three task-related failures: an existing agents-test expectation lacked `callerScopedCreation`, the added integration test exceeded the wall-clock timeout ratchet, and two explicit default type arguments failed Oxlint. Follow-up commit `2a1fdcf3abe59a067f17ebde75b78545f9369fce` fixes those test-only issues. On this head, the agents test and all six Cron integration cases passed; the agents-root and Gateway-methods test-type shards, the timeout-race ratchet, targeted type-aware Oxlint, `oxfmt`, and `git diff --check` passed locally. Full exact-head CI run [37025691323](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/37025691323) completed successfully on this SHA, including the previously failing timeout ratchet, changed Node checks, lint, and test-type shards.
- On 2026-10-07, merge commit `6ab2531a4732f3c128558d6e362e1deda43be153` incorporates `main` at `de38a04548251cbd6cc7e190c1470412c077908b`. The sole conflict was in `cron-creator-authority-context.test.ts`: the test was refactored on `main`, so the resolution keeps that structure and adds the PR-specific `callerScopedCreation: true` expectation. The PR delta remains the original source fix and focused tests. On this merge head, the focused grant, runtime-identity, and agents-context tests passed in two Vitest shards (91.78 seconds); all six Cron transport integration cases passed (44.08 seconds); both the Gateway-methods and agents-root test-type shards passed after the locked dependency installation. Formatting of the resolved file and `git diff --check` against the merged `main` commit passed. No new live deployment was performed for this merge head.
- The exact-head CI run for `6ab2531` passed the PR-affected Gateway-methods test-type shard but failed the unrelated `core-test-ui-components` shard because `ui/src/components/terminal/terminal-panel-fonts.test.ts` supplied an obsolete `signal` property. That UI file is unchanged by this PR. `main` fixed the fixture in `1d10375ee563bfaa203e9aad7fe88275adedd3a6`; conflict-free merge commit `90456d6e059950c898b4da51cd7df81dfe41fd22` incorporates current `main` at `1b395594318bbd0db6f2467f35b10cc8ac1d30d0`. The previously failing `test/tsconfig/tsconfig.core.test.ui-components.json` typecheck now passes locally. The five-file PR delta against current `main` is unchanged.
- Exact-head [CI run 37620941173](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/37620941173) completed successfully on `90456d6e059950c898b4da51cd7df81dfe41fd22`, including the previously failing `check-test-types-core-2` shard. ClawSweeper reviewed this same head, accepted the unchanged behavior evidence, and found no actionable patch defect. The only listed pre-merge item is authorized maintainer security-sensitive-change approval for this exact SHA; earlier-head approval cannot satisfy that gate.
- On 2026-10-08, merge commit `57b53c3a0ac805e5edc408574ef85ef884cb7684` incorporates `main` at `ad71624a7cfdd2052674f1bf537792fe68eae5b5`. The sole conflict was in `cron-creator-transports.integration.test.ts`, where main added seven recovery/revocation cases beside the PR’s tool-free remote-admin case. The resolution retains both sets: all 13 tests passed through the Gateway database-worker Vitest configuration (186.83 seconds for the shard). The Gateway-methods test-type shard passed after installing the new lockfile’s patched `ghostty-web`; the first local attempt used the prior patch and failed on its missing `onCopy` type. Formatting and `git diff --check` passed. The five-file PR delta remains unchanged in purpose, and a dry merge against the later `dcd3ca7a7fd53cfd5aa09579bb4665a422fbd6ba` main was conflict-free. Exact-head [CI run 37840042025](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/37840042025) completed successfully (64 jobs, none failed). [ClawSweeper reviewed this head](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/161918#issuecomment-5913486569) and found no actionable patch defect. Authorized maintainer security-sensitive-change approval remains required for this SHA.

## Previous Branch Integration — 2026-10-20

Commit `d485cdba8ea9f3e5ec428d89af5d26f3a33410ac` integrates main `e12719836f8e1f8b835496928d95ad847e453333` without rewriting history. Four test files conflicted because main refactored their fixtures, identity helpers and recovery cases. - This pass uses isolated handler/token/Cron-store boundaries, not a new live deployment. Earlier deployed evidence above remains historical, not a deployment of this merge revision.

prs.title: fix(sessions): keep peer replies through target yields
prs.body:
Related: #173026

## What Problem This Solves

A native `sessions_send` peer request can lose its result when the target yields to nested work and finishes under a successor run.

## User Impact

The original requester retains its result obligation across the target's committed yield. The accepted successor supplies one correlated result through the existing peer-return flow, including detached sends after the requester has finished its original turn.

## Why This Change Was Made

Admit eligible native cross-session peers to the existing `SessionFollowupCompletion` owner, so its existing yield cohort can retain completion custody. The existing authorization and delivery owners still decide whether successor work and the returned input may be admitted.

This adapts the custody approach in #173026 without its broader progress-card or required-visible-reply changes. ACP, steering, self-send, and registered-child routing keep their existing paths. The follow-up proof commit changes only tests and their budget allocation; the original production fix is unchanged.

## Evidence

### Runtime Proof

[Redacted native Gateway/model traces](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/193579#issuecomment-6726618018), November 8:

- **Detached return:** one native `sessions_send` with `timeoutSeconds: 0`; requester A finishes, peer B spawns C and actually yields with an empty final, then a distinct native B successor completes. The existing peer-return resumes A once. Readbacks show one send, one spawn, one yield, one peer result, one requester final, and zero pending requester inputs.
- **Operator withdrawal:** production `device.token.revoke` commits after the yield and before the child's gate is released. No native B successor, returned peer mirror/final, or pending requester input appears during the bounded 18-second observation.

The trace records the actual local build identity and verifies its Git tree is identical to published production head `d2c39a80`. `pnpm build:runtime` passed in 5m 22.7s. No production adapters, transport mocks, or model-response substitutions were used. The latest commit changes no production files. [Independent exact-head runs](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/193579#issuecomment-6717582608) also cover inline success and real requester/target reset during yield.

### Retained Authority Before Effects

[Committed controls and full results](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/193579#issuecomment-6726798384) exercise actual send admission, nested spawn, committed yield, registry-scheduled successor, and detached return through the real owners.

| Authority change | Before successor input staging | Before returned requester input staging |
| --- | --- | --- |
| None | Successor runs; one result | One requester result |
| Original profile role revoked | No successor execution or requester input | No requester execution or input |
| Requester session entry replaced | No successor execution or requester input | No requester execution or input |
| Target session entry replaced | No successor execution or requester input | No requester execution or input |

Only inference is a deterministic fixture; staging barriers delegate to the real SQLite operation and live commit guards. Negative controls inspect old/current requester pending inputs and transcripts, plus target input scopes. Raw entry-replacement controls prove incarnation fencing; full-reset observer liveness is outside those controls.

prs.title: fix(agents): classify the explicit auth-order refusal as an auth failure
prs.body:
Closes #194689

## What Problem This Solves

When the compaction model's credentials become unusable, budget-triggered compaction fails after a single attempt (`attempt=1 maxAttempts=1`) and never walks the configured model fallback chain, so long sessions get stuck on "conversation is too long" for every message. Ordinary turns recover by rotating to the next fallback candidate; compaction did not, because the refusal was not recognized as a failover-eligible failure.

Plain language: the summarizer's login stopped working, so every cleanup attempt died instantly and the whole conversation got jammed, even though two healthy backup models were configured and ordinary chats were already using them.

## Why This Change Was Made

Compaction already runs `runWithModelFallback`, but its `classifyResult` only falls back when the failure coerces to a failover error. The OpenClaw route preflight refusal — `Explicit auth order for <provider> has no usable profiles.` — matched none of the auth failure patterns, so `coerceToFailoverError` returned null and the fallback loop stopped before the first candidate. Adding that OpenClaw-authored refusal string to the auth patterns classifies it as `reason: "auth"`, which the fallback loop already treats as rotate-to-next-candidate (and ordinary turns gain the more accurate `auth` reason instead of `unknown` for the same message).

## User Impact

Compaction now rotates to the session's configured fallback models when the primary compaction route's credentials are unusable, matching ordinary turn behavior. Diagnostics for the same refusal report `auth` instead of `unknown`. Explicitly setting `agents.defaults.compaction.model` still pins compaction to that model without a fallback walk — that broader behavior change is left out of this focused fix.

## Evidence

Real runtime runs on latest main content (worktree files verified byte-identical to `main` + this change before push):

| Check | Result |
| --- | --- |
| `classify.test.ts` auth-evidence table, new row `Explicit auth order for openai has no usable profiles.` → `isAuthErrorMessage=true`, `classifyFailoverReason="auth"` | green (43/43) |
| `failover-error.test.ts`, new test: `coerceToFailoverError(new Error("Explicit auth order for openai has no usable profiles."))` → `{ reason: "auth" }` (the exact value compaction's `classifyResult` needs to fall back) | green (54/54) |
| Red check: pattern removed → exactly the new classify row fails (1 failed / 42 passed); restored → all green | confirmed |
| Adjacent failover suites (`classify.legacy-provider-predicates`, `failover-classification.corpus`, `retry-evidence`, `provider-structured-signals`) | all green, no new false positives |

## AI Assistance

This PR is AI-assisted. Used grep and git log to analyze issue #194689, trace the compaction fallback path through `compact.ts` classifyResult to the failover message patterns, and implement the one-pattern fix. The implementer understands the code: the refusal is an OpenClaw-authored preflight string, so pattern-classifying it as `auth` is the minimal seam that reuses the existing fallback loop. All evidence above is from real local runtime execution.

prs.title: fix(browser): report crashed tabs explicitly instead of a generic timeout
prs.body:
Closes #194667

## What Problem This Solves

When a tab's renderer process dies (kernel OOM kill or crash), the managed browser keeps running, but every action on that tab reports misleading failures: `snapshot` hangs ~20 s and fails with the generic transient hint ("the browser is currently unavailable"), `screenshot`/`navigate` fail with raw Playwright text ("Target crashed"), and `tabs` still lists the dead tab as a normal entry. An agent retries the dead tab, then tells the user the whole browser is down — when only one tab died.

Plain language: the browser did not go down; one tab's rendering process was killed. The tool had no way to tell the two apart, so it gave a wrong diagnosis. Now every action on a dead tab says exactly that: the tab crashed, open the URL in a new tab — and `tabs` marks the dead tab.

## Why This Change Was Made

The browser tool had no notion of a crashed renderer. Playwright emits a `crash` event on the Page object, but nothing listened, so crash-shaped failures fell through to the generic timeout classifier. The fix records crashed pages (a page-scoped `WeakSet` wired into the existing per-page state bootstrap), refuses a known-crashed target during resolution before any action runs, translates mid-action "Target crashed" failures at the shared `awaitActionWithAbort` boundary, and marks crashed entries in tab listings.

Per review, three adjustments: `close` remains available for crashed targets (target resolution takes an `allowCrashed` admission flag, so the cleanup operation keeps its ownership checks); crash facts learned on the Playwright side (`getPageForTargetId` refusal and Playwright target enumeration) flow into a target-keyed registry that raw `/json/list` listings also consume, and the CLI renders the marker; the crash test fixture keeps a correctly typed emitter, with action-boundary regressions replacing translator-only tests.

## User Impact

Agents see one explicit error for every action on a crashed tab — fast, without the "browser is unavailable" retry hint — and can recover by opening the URL in a new tab. Tab listings (JSON and CLI output) distinguish a dead tab from a live one, and closing a crashed tab still works.

## Evidence

Real runtime runs on the main tree this change is based on (every changed file byte-compared as `main`/head + exactly this delta before push):

| Check | Result |
| --- | --- |
| `pw-session-crashed-target.test.ts`: crash-event marking; "Target crashed" translation incl. non-Error form; no false translation for locator timeout or genuine close; action-boundary: crashed rejection → explicit error, timeout and close-shaped failures unchanged | 5/5 green |
| Red checks: crash listener removed → marking test fails; action-boundary wiring reverted → boundary test fails (earlier round); fixture-typing round rerun green | confirmed |
| Adjacent `pw-session.connections.test.ts` (incl. connection scoping with the new admission flag), `pw-session-navigation-fence.test.ts` | 44/44 green |
| `tsc --noEmit -p tsconfig.extensions.json`: zero errors under `extensions/browser` | verified |

## AI Assistance

This PR is AI-assisted. Used grep and git diff to analyze issue #194667, locate the missing crash handling in the browser tool's session layer, and implement the fix. The implementer understands the code: Playwright's per-page `crash` event marks the dead page, target resolution refuses it (close opts out via `allowCrashed`), and the shared action boundary translates "Target crashed" failures. All evidence above is from real local runtime execution.

prs.title: fix(cli): stop status/channels list/doctor emitting Matrix SDK deprecation warnings
prs.body:
Fixes #190243

## What Problem This Solves

On an install with no Matrix configured, `openclaw status`, `openclaw channels list` and `openclaw doctor` each print two `[DEP_PLUGIN_SDK]` warnings blaming "Plugin matrix". Core caused them: these async command paths called the sync channel-presence resolvers, which run the bundled `hasAnyMatrixAuth` sync export (`createPluginStateSyncKeyedStore` + `.entries()`).

## User Impact

Users no longer see deprecation noise they can't act on, and plugin authors aren't misled into thinking a third-party plugin needs migrating. Configured-channel detection is unchanged. It still reads saved auth, now through the async `exportNameAsync` probe.

## Why

Async twins already existed (`hasConfiguredChannelsForReadOnlyScopeAsync`, `listReadOnlyChannelPluginsForConfigAsync`, and the Matrix `hasAnyMatrixAuthAsync`). The only change is switching the four call sites, which were already inside `async` functions:
- `src/commands/status.scan-overview.ts`: `hasConfiguredChannelsForReadOnlyScopeAsync`
- `src/commands/status-all/channels.ts` (`buildChannelsTable`, also reached by plain `status`): new `resolveReadOnlyChannelPluginsForConfigAsync`. It has the same scope and manifest records as the sync resolver and returns the same full resolution (missing ids, load failures).
- `src/commands/channels/list.ts` and `src/commands/doctor-security.ts`: `listReadOnlyChannelPluginsForConfigAsync`

The sync compatibility exports are left alone until their 2026-12-31 removal.

## Evidence

Real CLI on Linux, fresh `HOME`/`OPENCLAW_HOME`, built from this branch.

Before (main):
```
$ openclaw status   (same for channels list, doctor)
(node:…) [DEP_PLUGIN_SDK] DeprecationWarning: Plugin matrix: createPluginStateSyncKeyedStore is deprecated; use createPluginStateKeyedStoreV2 …
(node:…) [DEP_PLUGIN_SDK] DeprecationWarning: Plugin SDK: PluginStateSyncKeyedStore.entries is deprecated; …
```
After:
```
$ openclaw status          exit=0 stdout_lines=139 DEP_PLUGIN_SDK_lines=0
$ openclaw channels list   exit=0 stdout_lines=5   DEP_PLUGIN_SDK_lines=0
$ openclaw doctor          exit=0 stdout_lines=355 DEP_PLUGIN_SDK_lines=0
```
`--trace-deprecation` before the fix showed the call chains `statusCommand → collectStatusScanOverview → buildChannelsTable / hasConfiguredChannelsForReadOnlyScope`, `channelsListCommand → listReadOnlyChannelPluginsForConfig` and `collectSecurityWarnings → listReadOnlyChannelPluginsForConfig`, all ending at `hasAnyMatrixAuth`.

Tests:
- New `src/channels/plugins/read-only.async-presence.test.ts`: a bundled plugin declares both sync and async persisted-auth exports. The async resolver detects the saved auth and never calls the sync export.
- Updated mocks in the status, channels list and doctor-security tests to the async APIs, so a reintroduced sync call fails.
- `vitest`: channels.list*, doctor-security, status*, status-all/channels, read-only*: 38 files, 346 tests passed. `oxlint` and `oxfmt --check` are clean, and `pnpm build` is green.


### Base-red / head-green replay (head `efa00bf`)

Same 4 regression files, run with `vitest run`. Only the 5 non-test source files were reverted to the merge base `f7d6774` for the base run; the tests are unchanged.

| Run | Source | Test files | Tests |
|---|---|---|---|
| Base | `f7d6774` source + PR tests | 4 failed | 48 failed / 48 |
| Head | `efa00bf` | 4 passed | 48 passed / 48 |

Base failure modes:
- `read-only.async-presence.test.ts`: `resolveReadOnlyChannelPluginsForConfigAsync is not a function`. Base has no async full-resolution path, so `status` can only take the sync Matrix probe.
- `channels.list`, `status-all/channels`, `doctor-security`: base calls the sync `listReadOnlyChannelPluginsForConfig` / sync resolver, and the async-only mocks reject it (`No "listReadOnlyChannelPluginsForConfig" export is defined on the mock`). This is the guard that fails if a sync call comes back.


### Command-level warning capture (`src/commands/channels.list.dep-warning.test.ts`)

This runs the real `channelsListCommand` (`openclaw channels list --json`) against an on-disk config and a bundled channel fixture with saved auth. The fixture's legacy sync auth probe emits `DEP_PLUGIN_SDK` the way Matrix's does, and its async probe is silent. The test watches both `process.emitWarning` and the process `warning` event and asserts that no `DEP_PLUGIN_SDK` warning is emitted.

Base source (`f7d6774`'s `read-only.ts`, `channels/list.ts`, `status-all/channels.ts`, `status.scan-overview.ts`, `doctor-security.ts`) with the new test:

```
AssertionError: expected [ 'DEP_PLUGIN_SDK' ] to not include 'DEP_PLUGIN_SDK'
      Tests  1 failed (1)
```

Head `708a05f`:

```
      Tests  1 passed (1)
```

### ✨ Terminal recording (real built CLI, Linux)

Built with `scripts/build-all.mts`, then ran `node openclaw.mjs channels list` and `node openclaw.mjs status` with a fresh HOME/state dir and an explicit `{}` config (`OPENCLAW_CONFIG_PATH`). Base `f7d6774` prints 2 `[DEP_PLUGIN_SDK]` DeprecationWarnings per command; the same steps rebuilt from PR head `708a05f` print 0, exit 0.

![channels list / status: base shows DEP_PLUGIN_SDK warnings, head shows none](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/jerome-queck/openclaw/d1cbdb648d5599cdb8a098fea5f767e4b496dfe6/proofs/190257-dep-warning.gif)
