prs.title: fix(infra): name the lock path in gateway lock errors (companion to #159614)
prs.body:
Companion to #159614 by @carlosjarenom, which went stale waiting on proof. This branch keeps his commit (authorship intact), applies it to current `main`, adds one follow-up commit, and supplies the missing real-run evidence. Related issue: #135133.

## What Problem This Solves

When Gateway startup cannot acquire state ownership, the error says `failed to acquire gateway state ownership` without naming the lock file that blocked it. The operator has to guess between the process owner sidecar (`state.<hash>.lock`), the historical state lock (`gateway.state.lock`) and the config lock (`gateway.<hash>.lock`). This is worst when the holder sits in another PID namespace, e.g. a containerized Gateway sharing `~/.openclaw`, because nothing on the host can verify or reclaim it.

## User Impact

The startup error now ends with `at <lock path>`, naming the exact file that refused ownership, so the operator knows what to inspect (or hand to `openclaw gateway recover-lock`). There is no behavior change to locking, reclaiming or timeouts; only the error text changes. When the failure is a database error rather than a lock, the message keeps pointing at the database, as on `main`.

## Why

- `4418884` (@carlosjarenom, from #159614): tracks the lock file that blocked each poll attempt, resets it every attempt so a stale path is never reported, and falls back to the owner sidecar. Conflicts with current `main`'s acquire loop were resolved by keeping `main`'s structure and adding only his tracking.
- `df683a6` (follow-up): on current `main`, an unverifiable or unreadable historical lock payload throws before live contention, so his hook never fired for those cases (his own "recorded owner cannot be verified" tests failed after rebasing). The follow-up attributes any refusal from a historical lock check to that file, includes the lock path in `GatewayLockNamespaceError` when it is known, and skips the lock suffix for database failures (which `backup-sqlite.test.ts` covers). It adds a regression test for the foreign-PID-namespace state lock. `gateway-lock.ts` stays under the 700 code-line limit.

## Evidence

Real Gateway startup on Linux from the source CLI (`node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs src/entry.ts`), isolated `HOME`, port 19462. A `gateway.state.lock` is left by a Gateway in another PID namespace (live PID, foreign `processNamespace`), then a second Gateway starts on the same state dir.

Before (`origin/main` 2c0ab86):
```

$ cat /tmp/h159614.8Shj/.openclaw/tmp/openclaw-1000/gateway.state.lock
{"pid":3662774,"createdAt":"2026-11-01T11:11:58.000Z","configPath":"/tmp/h159614.8Shj/.openclaw/openclaw.json","stateDir":"/tmp/h159614.8Shj/.openclaw","role":"gateway","processNamespace":{"platform":"linux","host":"gateway-container","pidNsInode":"4026532999"}}
$ openclaw gateway run --allow-unconfigured --port 19462
Run "openclaw doctor --fix" against the same state/config, then restart the gateway.
2026-11-01T19:12:18.525+08:00 [gateway] loading configuration…
2026-11-01T19:12:18.534+08:00 [gateway] resolving authentication…
2026-11-01T19:12:18.536+08:00 [gateway] starting...
2026-11-01T19:12:19.256+08:00 Gateway failed to start: failed to acquire gateway state ownership | Gateway lock inspection is unavailable | Gateway lock payload could not be verified
If the gateway is supervised, stop it with: openclaw gateway stop
# exit=1
```

After (this branch, df683a6):
```
# source tree df683a6449e (branch); isolated HOME=/tmp/h159614.fFAO
$ cat /tmp/h159614.fFAO/.openclaw/tmp/openclaw-1000/gateway.state.lock
{"pid":3688236,"createdAt":"2026-11-01T11:27:22.000Z","configPath":"/tmp/h159614.fFAO/.openclaw/openclaw.json","stateDir":"/tmp/h159614.fFAO/.openclaw","role":"gateway","processNamespace":{"platform":"linux","host":"gateway-container","pidNsInode":"4026532999"}}
$ openclaw gateway run --allow-unconfigured --port 19462
Run "openclaw doctor --fix" against the same state/config, then restart the gateway.
2026-11-01T19:27:41.965+08:00 [gateway] loading configuration…
2026-11-01T19:27:41.975+08:00 [gateway] resolving authentication…
2026-11-01T19:27:41.977+08:00 [gateway] starting...
2026-11-01T19:27:42.700+08:00 Gateway failed to start: failed to acquire gateway state ownership at /tmp/h159614.fFAO/.openclaw/tmp/openclaw-1000/gateway.state.lock | Gateway lock inspection is unavailable | Gateway lock payload could not be verified
If the gateway is supervised, stop it with: openclaw gateway stop
# exit=1
```

Tests (Linux, vitest infra config, `--maxWorkers=1`):
- `src/infra/gateway-lock*.test.ts`: 7 files passed, 1 skipped (Windows-only), 102 tests passed.
- Red/green for `src/infra/gateway-lock.unactionable-timeout.test.ts`: against `main`'s `gateway-lock.ts`/`gateway-lock-payload.ts`, 5/5 fail. Against #159614's commit alone on current `main`, 3/5 fail (the unverifiable-owner and foreign-namespace cases). On this branch, 5/5 pass.
- Callers that assert on these messages: `backup-sqlite`, `doctor-sqlite-maintenance-lock`, `run.supervised-lock`, `daemon/diagnostics`, `update-database-restore`, `sqlite-readonly-location`, `startup-plugin-source-captures`, `update-command-invalid-config` all pass. `run-loop.test.ts` has timeouts locally that reproduce identically on `main`, so they are unrelated.
- `checks-node-changed-compact-large-36` on #159614 failed in `src/agents/sandbox/sdk-state-owner.process.test.ts` (filesystem snapshot `.bun` entry count 1645 vs 1639), which does not touch the lock code. ## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: Z.AI Coding Plan model resolution reports “Unknown model” when fallback reuses a retained general-API catalog row after discovery is unavailable.

## User Impact

This addresses the residual catalog-route failure, not every historical onboarding symptom: the reasoning-token probe failure was separately fixed by #193467. Full source-Gateway setup and chat qualification now passes with deterministic external HTTP responses. Actual Z.AI account entitlement, live service behavior, and release-package qualification are not claimed.

## Why This Change Was Made

The provider keeps retained model metadata but binds its returned fallback to the selected connection endpoint. It does not mutate the registry row or weaken native route admission. Explicit model-level routes continue through the existing core owner.

Author simplification retained one provider-owned correction, no new helpers, state, or fallback implementation. Production net +5 lines; docs +3; regression +92 lines with an exact dedicated test-line allocation for native route admission, model overrides, and retained-row immutability.

prs.title: fix(session-status): name scopes held when capabilities cannot be read
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`session_status` with capabilities enabled asks the Gateway for `tools.effective`. When that call is refused, the model only sees the refusal plus a line that this is not proof a tool is missing. It does not see the scopes the session already holds, so it goes looking.

On 2026-10-31 a team-server Roboclaw session held only `operator.sessions.write`. `session_status` returned `missing scope: operator.read`. The model then spent turns on catalog search. The grant was already known. This pull repeats the held scopes in the capability failure. It does not add `operator.read`, `operator.write`, or a dispatch action.

## Evidence

Head `1a4b1d591fc`. Isolated Gateway on loopback port 19032, token auth, channels skipped. The client connected with only `operator.sessions.write` and called the shipped `tools.effective` method. The same connection was the `callGateway` used by `createSessionStatusTool` with `capabilities: true`.

```console
{
  "rawToolsEffective": "Session-scoped access requires a verified user profile.",
  "checked": "unavailable",
  "error": "Session-scoped access requires a verified user profile.",
  "grantedScopes": ["operator.sessions.write"],
  "textHasHeldScope": true,
  "textHasNotEvidence": true
}
```

The running Gateway refused `tools.effective`. The tool text includes `This session holds operator.sessions.write.` and `This is not evidence that OpenClaw lacks a capability.`

## Real behavior proof

- **Behavior or issue addressed:** A refused capability check names the scopes the session already holds.
- **Real environment tested:** macOS, Node v26.12.1, Gateway from `/tmp/oc-192971` at `1a4b1d591fc`, loopback port 19032.
- **Exact steps or command run after this patch:** `node scripts/run-node.mjs gateway run` on that worktree, then `node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs /tmp/proof-oc-192971.mts`, which calls `callGateway({ method: "tools.effective", scopes: ["operator.sessions.write"] })` and `session_status` execute with `capabilities: true`.
- **Evidence after fix:** The console block in Evidence. `checked` is `unavailable`, `grantedScopes` is `operator.sessions.write`, and the visible text names that scope.
- **Observed result after fix:** The refusal came from the running Gateway, and the status text repeated the held scope.
- **What was not tested:** A verified user profile whose only missing grant is `operator.read`. This client was refused one step earlier, because session-scoped access required a verified profile.

## Summary

`resolveSessionCapabilities` keeps the status usable when `tools.effective` fails and adds the caller scopes already on the admitted run. Blank scopes are still dropped.

prs.title: fix(agents): private CLI completions lose delivery under restrictive profiles
prs.body:
Related: #121661

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: a private subagent result can fail to reach the user when the requester uses a restrictive tool profile such as `coding`, or a CLI backend that does not retain the full requester tool surface.

## User Impact

User impact: a verified private completion can relay its result to the requesting conversation through `message`, while its final answer stays private. Explicit tool denies, frozen policies, channel action gates, and grant revocation remain authoritative.

An additional completion messaging grant is restricted to sends in the original channel, account, conversation, and thread, and cannot become general messaging authority for spawned children or cron jobs. Existing requester permissions are preserved.

## Why This Change Was Made

Current main already restores the normal Claude CLI requester tool surface. The remaining repair uses the explicit `privateCompletion` flag, carries source restriction independently of automatic final-reply delivery, and keeps the admitted completion allowance through the actual Gateway tool projection. The same policy merge helper preserves explicit denies and frozen allowlists at both stages.

The earlier destination-scope rationale in this PR was incorrect. This revision uses the existing source-reply guard for the additional grant. It also follows the current media contract: #176594 permits source-conversation photos and attachments through normal media validation; this PR does not restore the obsolete text-only restriction.

Integrated main at `650091daacdc10aa374e82a6327e8beffe136072` to resolve the stale branch conflicts and preserve current runtime selection and requester-tool retention.

## Evidence

At `bed203a26ff9c7aac301f0bff632b97d23895318` (tree `30b8d9d69f3d1a9983b45bc4f12f445b877763dc`):

- Production typecheck passed (`tsconfig.core.json`).
- Focused typecheck of all four changed test entrypoints, extending the repository root-test configuration, passed. It caught and fixed the current-main MCP startup API change.
- Type-aware lint passed for changed production files, tests/support, and the CI inventory; formatting, `git diff --check`, and the line-cap ratchet passed.
- The test-line ratchet still reports **51 inherited lines over budget**. At the integrated base the measured total is 6,551,687 and the effective ceiling is 6,551,636. This change adds exactly 663 test/support lines and a separate 663-line allocation, preserving that pre-existing difference. No shared baseline increase is included.

The complete Gateway → private parent completion → CLI runner → minted MCP grant → message tool → Telegram transport fixture passed **5/5** in [CI job 128116367053](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/42282734165/job/128116367053). Only model decisions and external Bot API responses are synthetic. CI checked merge `328504c21532c5402858ade03a23c749cf1aa84e`, combining this head with main `9651d6347b1ab99453e8e6b5105d10d7800d82dc`.

| Scenario | Verified result |
| --- | --- |
| Ordinary private completion | Exactly one send containing the child result |
| Coding profile | Exactly one allowed send; other chat/thread and non-send probes rejected |
| Explicit operator deny | No completion message tool or child-result send |
| Disabled Telegram send action | Tool error and zero child-result sends |
| Revoked grant | HTTP 401 and zero child-result sends |

The five reported case durations total 122.7 seconds. This expensive composition stays in the release-only tier except for changed-file CI because admission-only tests miss authority lost between projection and dispatch.

The [CLI attempt suite](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/42282734165/job/128116366616), including the new private/coding/other-CLI cases, and [MCP grant-context suite](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/42282734165/job/128116366918) also passed. CI lint and all five core test-type stripes passed.

Full CI is red on an unrelated current-main defect: [production type checking](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/42282734165/job/128116569548) and some asset-building jobs cannot resolve `extensions/deep-research/browser/client.js`. The browser directory has identical filenames and blob SHAs in main `9651d634` and the tested merge; both lack that module. This PR does not change those files.

The [CI baseline-ratchet job](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/42282734165/job/128116365654) also confirms the same inherited test-line debt on main `9651d634`: total 6,552,688, ceiling 6,552,637, over by 51, PR net delta +663. The CI run supplies current-head GREEN proof. Independent Codex source review covered the production and regression changes against `650091daacdc`: no actionable findings. This was an independent source review, not an autoreview or ClawSweeper execution. The existing private-delivery owner cases cover suppression of nonempty private final text; the new integration fixture itself returns `NO_REPLY`.

Simplification retained the existing runtime-selection and policy owners and removed unused photo/document assertions. Against the integrated base: production +38 net lines, regression tests/support +663. The exact 663-line test allocation is justified by the end-to-end authority boundary: admission-only tests miss a grant lost during CLI projection. The expensive integration is release-only except when selected by changed-file CI; the shared test baseline is unchanged.

prs.title: fix: session resets time out after reply cleanup throws
prs.body:
Related: #167078

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: a throwing reply-cleanup callback can strand session reset or shut down the Gateway.

## User Impact

The original cleanup failure is still reported, but subsequent reset and turns can proceed safely once outstanding writer and delivery cleanup settles. The 15-second drain timeout is unchanged; no configuration, migration, or user action is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

The after-clear callback loop stopped at its first synchronous exception, skipping later releases and preventing immediate owner settlement. During deferred flushing, the same exception could instead become an unhandled rejection. Completion was already consumed, so calling complete again could not recover it.

Use the existing listener-notification helper to warn about each failed callback and continue the remaining callbacks. Required resources retain their own actual settlement receipts; there is no forced release, retry, or longer timeout. The fix is complete for this reproduced callback-exception path; #167078 remains open for its other reported triggers.

## Evidence

### Shipped Gateway/channel boundary

- Added `test/session-rollover-cleanup.e2e.test.ts`: the official E2E runner builds and starts a real isolated CLI Gateway with a fresh named profile, authenticated synthetic channel HTTP ingress, and a deterministic loopback Responses provider. No mocked Gateway, controller, resolver, or model runner; no CLI agent/chat RPC or removed exec marker.
- **Main production source:** the same case fails in **11.94 s**. The actual Gateway logs `Unhandled promise rejection: Error: rollover-proof typing cleanup failure`, closes admission, and shuts down; the channel connection receives `ECONNRESET`.
- **Fixed candidate:** the case passes in **12.90 s**. The injected original ingress error remains **HTTP 500**; `/new` and the following turn both return **HTTP 200**. The next serialized model request contains the new prompt and no pre-reset marker, and the after-clear failure warning is observed.
- **Independently executed in GitHub CI on the committed head:** [the changed-test job](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/42519796413/job/128851013095) ran this exact Gateway regression: **1/1 passed, 14,391 ms**, with runner **exit 0** and **19.43 s** command wall time. This is executable CI evidence, not only local/self-reported output.
- Reproduce: `RAYON_NUM_THREADS=2 pnpm test test/session-rollover-cleanup.e2e.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`. Final command wall time was **236.11 s**, including source-bound runtime build and cold worker preparation. Cleanup completed through the fixture process owner.

### Settlement and static proof

- The immediate-completion integration regression fails on main `e3a09aaba1f45ec3ff2eb4a0db4728286f53068d` with the exact rollover drain timeout after **15,912 ms**. Fixed rollover suite: **5/5**, including immediate/deferred completion and a writer held until its real work exits.
- Lifecycle and sequence suites: **33/33** with the same unchanged production fix. Including the Gateway case: **39 focused tests**.
- Production, messaging-test and root-other test TypeScript checks passed; targeted type-aware lint, formatting, line-cap ratchet and whitespace checks passed.
- Fresh independent Auto Review of the four-file local candidate against the main commit above: **no P0 findings**, configured P0-only static scope. Runtime checks were executed separately. Candidate patch SHA-256: `5e5c28a6fab1441667c9120c1f2ddad9dac9db7db8f92622d3fe9c5e328d4a29`.

### Hosted CI

**Fully clean on current head `e9163ed5155fb476b3f7bf20fb29eca9f5035eb0`**, verified at 2026-11-08 20:35 UTC: all **142 distinct check runs** completed (64 success, 77 skipped, 1 neutral), plus **3 successful commit statuses**; zero failures, cancellations, or pending checks. [CI workflow](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/42519796413) and the [complete authoritative aggregate](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/42519796413/job/128853265618) succeeded on attempt 1, with all selected lanes successful and no red-lane, coalescing, or fast-lane exception.

This proves the synchronous callback-exception variant, not every historical trigger in #167078. The channel and provider are synthetic loopback fixtures, not live external accounts or a concurrency storm.

Simplification: the production fix remains +9/-3 and reuses the existing notification owner. Regression delta is +286/-1; the dedicated 285-line allocation covers immediate/deferred writer custody and the distinct shipped-process failure boundary. The shared scalar is unchanged.

Contributor credit: @leappower for the original report; @Linux2010 for prior diagnostic research in closed #167342; implementation requested by Jason O'Neal. No code was adopted from #167342, and #167342, #194536, and #194545 were not modified.

prs.title: feat(update): allow explicit retirement of backed-up session archives
prs.body:
Closes #186088

## What Problem This Solves

Operators cannot intentionally retire retained session-import archives when import proof is unavailable or archive identity changed, even after preserving an independent backup.

## User Impact

Operators can retire an exact, complete archive group using a byte-verified independent raw backup and separate `--accept-history-loss` consent. Ordinary cleanup stays conservative. Updates shows retained storage sizes, reasons, and recovery guidance only when requested.

Selected originals may contain unique history absent from SQLite. Retirement permanently removes them, preserves previous import evidence in v5 receipts, and does not promise automatic backup restoration or supported downgrade. Recovery/update-owner acceptance of this opt-in retention and older-reader contract remains required.

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing maintenance/disposal owner performs the explicitly authorized retirement; no alternate deletion owner or automatic retention policy is added. Integration with current main preserves live-writer cleanup, byte-verified surviving-duplicate redirects, and settlement of already-unlinked pending claims. Async snapshot preparation no longer consumes the bounded synchronous inventory allowance before the inventory starts; the existing entry, byte, and time limits remain unchanged.

## Evidence

Current candidate `556fc60f228c8a2437effe2c89926dc0ba1d0483` integrates main `3df96dfc805b01d5d16e12040ab519ab67c8d61f`. [Fresh immutable evidence](https://github.com/jason-allen-oneal/openclaw/blob/51d0afd65d99acc6fb1bbe12896c0391500a5be7/README.md).

- **Normal built CLI:** conservative cleanup refuses both retained reason classes; explicit preview changes no state; selected retirement removes two files; replay removes zero. Active SQLite bytes, one session and three events remain identical; independent backup unchanged.
- **Latest-stable v2026.11.2 storage upgrade:** [new additive evidence](https://github.com/jason-allen-oneal/openclaw/blob/d296dd6d076a361b4d31afb5a473eb51b50c8ea9/README.md) verifies the official package emits v3 receipts/schema 27 and candidate Doctor upgrades to schema 41. Supported config getters preserve nondefault timezone/update settings; sessions CLI and Doctor inspect the same session and three events. Independent backup bytes remain unchanged. Controlled interruption, resume and replay pass; three archives retired, replay removes zero. Pending/disposed candidate state is safely refused by older cleanup/restore; its exact shipped manifest reader independently rejects v5. This verifies storage/Doctor/cleanup and session inspection, not new conversational writes, the package updater or a service restart. The v2026.11.1 proof remains retained.
- **Actual built Gateway/UI:** all nine empty/retained/incomplete scenarios at 400/820/1280 px pass through real RPC. All 123 served assets match disk hashes; protected archive bytes stay unchanged. No mutation requests, page errors, recovery-section shifts, shell movement or horizontal overflow. Console warnings/errors (including blocked service-worker activity and 401/404 responses) are retained; this is not a clean-console claim. Nine screenshots inspected; the small unrelated Update status text shift remains in tablet/desktop observations.
- **Checks/review:** all 144 distinct storage/cleanup tests have passing receipts after the missing-await correction; 16 UI unit tests, core/UI types, scoped lint, line caps and test-line ratchet pass. The real-ledger empty-inventory regression passes without weakened assertions. Independent full-snapshot review plus final-delta and harness audits have no unresolved actionable finding. `pnpm build:runtime` passes, and all 26,549 launcher/dist artifact hashes stay identical through execution.

Synthetic isolated fixtures only; no original-reporter data or model/channel calls. Interruption is callback-based source-owner fault injection, not an OS kill. The official stable package and exact internal dependencies are integrity-verified; its other dependencies link read-only to the candidate install. Earlier failed harness attempts remain in the evidence. The build emits advisory UI gzip baseline excesses; exact-head hosted CI is now green (89 passed, 44 skipped, zero failed/pending), including the aggregate gate. All 26,549 build artifact hashes remain identical before/after the additional v2026.11.2 run. Recovery/update-owner policy acceptance remains outstanding.

prs.title: feat(tools): config-defined custom tool profiles
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`tools.profile` accepts a closed set of built-in ids (`minimal`, `coding`, `messaging`, `full`), enforced by the config schema. Operators composing agent fleets need stable, named policy packs — for example, a "desk operator" that is `coding` plus a handful of plugin/MCP tools. Today the only path is copy-pasting `alsoAllow` lists into every agent entry, and any tool added later is missed by every copy until someone notices a drift.

## What This PR Does

- New top-level `tools.profiles` map (`schema: agent-runtime`): name → `{ base?, allow?, deny? }`.
  - `base` accepts built-in profile ids only, so resolution cannot cycle.
  - `allow` unions over the base allowlist; `deny` unions after allow expansion; deny wins — the same merge rules `alsoAllow`/`tools.allow` already use.
  - Definitions whose normalized `allow`/`deny` entries are all blank are rejected (same as an empty object).
- Widened the `profile` reference schema to built-in ids or custom names; empty/whitespace selections are rejected at schema-parse parity, because an empty selection overrides nullish inheritance and resolves to no policy.
- Unknown profile references fail `validateConfigObject` via a new `collectToolProfileReferenceIssues` collector (same pattern as model-policy ref validation), so a typo in `tools.profile` becomes a config error rather than a silently unresolvable name that fails open under other policy layers.
- Manifest-contributed plugin grants: a named profile derived from a built-in base inherits the base's plugin profile grants (`conversation-capability-profile`), so plugin tools declared for `coding` stay visible under a coding-derived custom profile; the profile's own deny entries still win.
- Threaded the resolved map (`config.tools.profiles`) through the enforcement sites: `resolveConfiguredToolPolicies`/`resolveEffectiveToolPolicy`, gateway tool-resolution, web-search, fs, sandbox workspace-authority, conversation capability, skills tool-dispatch, plugin-tools MCP serve, update-repair, tool-access diagnostics, the Control UI Tools settings panel, and Doctor current-policy previews.
- Template manifests keep builtin-only profiles (they are self-contained artifacts that cannot see the operator `tools.profiles`). Doctor legacy-migration helpers likewise keep builtin resolution — they rewrite pre-#47487 legacy configs that predate this key. Both are noted limitations; neither is a behavior change for existing configs.
- Docs: new "Custom profiles" section in `docs/gateway/config-tools/tool-policy.md`; config surface baseline regenerated.

Example:

```json5
{
  tools: {
    profiles: {
      "desk-operator": {
        base: "coding",
        allow: ["brayer_order_get", "brayer_order_next"],
        deny: ["browser"],
      },
    },
    profile: "desk-operator",
  },
}
```

## Evidence

Unit + static checks (branch head `8cb1a08c6`, rebased onto `main`):

- `tsgo:core` clean; `tsgo:ui` clean except a pre-existing local `@1password/save-button` type-dep failure that also fails on clean `main` (local pnpm store is missing that package; the source is untouched).
- `agent-tools.custom-profiles.test.ts` drives `createOpenClawCodingTools` — the tool-surface assembly used by the embedded run and Gateway placements — as entry-point proof:
  1. allowed-call surface: a `desk-operator = { base: "coding" }`-shaped profile exposes the coding base surface (`web_fetch` present) as the builtin does;
  2. denied call: `deny: ["automations", "cron"]` under the same profile removes `automations` from the assembled surface, so a denied call can reach no process effect (mirrors builtin deny removal of `tool_call`/`dispatch_action`);
  3. policy withdrawal: restoring access via `tools.alsoAllow: ["automations"]` brings the tool back through the same profile layer;
  4. manifest grants: plugin tools declared for `coding` remain present under the coding-derived custom profile.
- Config compatibility: existing stored data is untouched (config-scope change; no session/store schema changed). Legacy configs without `tools.profiles` validate unchanged — covered by `config.schema-regressions` and the schema suite's builtin profile cases.
- Vitest green across the touched surfaces (16 suites, 300+ tests): tool-policy, config schema + regressions, tool-policy-pipeline, tool-profile-consent, doctor tool-policy-conflicts/previews, tool-dispatch, tool-fs-policy, plugin-tools-serve, gateway tool-resolution, workspace-authority, agent-tools agent-config exec + create-openclaw-coding-tools + custom-profiles entry-point tests.
- Repo ratchets and generated docs: `check:base-config-schema` ok, `config:docs:check` ok, `docs:check-config-examples` unchanged skips, `check:assertion-safety`/`line-cap`/`max-lines` ratchets clean, `check:test-lines-ratchet` ok with committed allocation `config/test-lines-allocations/195315-custom-tool-profiles.txt` (rationale in-file).
- Loading budget: `chatBootJsGzipBytes` raised to 1,296,830 — the Tools panel custom-profile resolution measured +15 B gzip (PR #195315); cap = measured + 64 B headroom per house style.

prs.title: fix(message): keep accepted message ids when a send fails partway
prs.body:
Closes #195066

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: a message send that delivers one message and then fails on a later part hides the delivered message id, so the caller cannot tell partial delivery from total failure.

## User Impact

Callers (agent tool calls and MCP clients) now see which messages already landed and that the rest is unconfirmed, while the send still reports failure. This prevents resending content that was already delivered.

## Why This Change Was Made

Ordinary sends throw `ChannelPartialDeliveryError` when a later part fails. The typed error carries the provider-accepted message ids, but both error surfaces - the native tool error result and the MCP `tools/call` response - project only the error text, so the ids were lost.

The fix projects the partial delivery at the message-tool boundary (`projectMessageActionPartialFailureResult`) and returns a result with `ok: false`, `deliveryStatus: "partial_failed"`, `sentBeforeError: true`, the accepted message ids, and `remainderUnconfirmed: true`. The native harness and the MCP handler both classify a returned result through its details, so each caller keeps failure semantics and gains the delivery facts. Scheduled authority keeps its existing projection, and queued delivery is unchanged.

Some transports (X) attach accepted ids only to the receipt, not to `messageIds`; the projection now falls back to the receipt's platform message ids. The production transport run below is what exposed that case.

## Evidence

### Production transport proof (after fix, head `64348875802`)

Harness: the real `createMessageTool` and the real MCP `tools/call` handler, routed through the real X channel action, the real `sendXDelivery`, and the real `createXApiClient` transport client, issuing real HTTP requests. Only the HTTP responses were controlled: `POST /2/tweets` accepted the first post with id `100000000000000021`, then rejected the second post with HTTP 403. Credentials, ids, and content are synthetic; no live endpoint, real account, or user data was involved, so nothing needs redaction.

Observed caller-visible result on both surfaces (identical text payload; MCP sets `result.isError: true`):

```json
{
  "ok": false,
  "action": "send",
  "deliveryStatus": "partial_failed",
  "sentBeforeError": true,
  "error": "X reply chain failed after one or more posts were sent | X API /2/tweets failed (HTTP 403) | OPENCLAW_PLATFORM_MESSAGE_NOT_DISPATCHED | OPENCLAW_PLATFORM_MESSAGE_NOT_DISPATCHED",
  "acceptedMessageIds": ["100000000000000021"],
  "remainderUnconfirmed": true,
  "message": "Delivered 1 message(s) before the send failed; the remaining content is unconfirmed. Do not resend the accepted message(s)."
}
```

Transport requests observed in the run: one `POST /oauth2/token`, one `GET /2/tweets?ids=90` recipient lookup, and two `POST /2/tweets` posts per surface (accepted, then rejected).

### Caller-boundary regressions

- `pnpm test src/agents/tools/message-tool-execution.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` - 71/71 pass; the partial-delivery cases fail on base (`8a6761d8690`), where both tool calls throw and lose the ids.
- `pnpm test src/gateway/mcp-http.partial-delivery.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` - red on base with `"second attachment failed"` alone, green with the accepted id and `isError: true`.
- New receipt-only case: red on base, green with `64348875802`.

The MCP case drives the real message tool and the JSON-RPC handler instead of feeding a fabricated projection result into a mock tool, so it fails if the production catch integration is removed.

### Checks

- `pnpm tsgo:core` and `pnpm tsgo:test:src` pass.
- oxlint on the changed files: 0 findings; repo format check passes.
- Suites re-run green: `message-tool.test.ts`, `message-tool-execution.test.ts`, `message-tool.scheduled-lifetime.test.ts`, `message-tool.scheduled-writes.test.ts`, `mcp-http.test.ts`, `agent-loop.async-tools.test.ts`, `agent-tools.prefix-stability.test.ts`, `message-action-execution{,.accepted-results,.source-reply}.test.ts`, `outbound-payload.contract.test.ts`.
- Test-line budget: this change adds 117 net test lines and `config/test-lines-allocations/195224-partial-delivery-ids.txt` grants exactly that growth. The ratchet is still 28 lines over from the shared comparison base, unchanged by this PR (another open PR run on the same base reports the same 28-line overage).
- `pnpm check:changed`: typecheck core, lint, format, line-cap, and assertion-SAFETY ratchets pass. `changelog attributions` (repo-wide) fails on the base commit for unrelated reasons.

Gap: the transport proof is a controlled-response production path, not a live channel post; the reproduction matches the reported failure and never contacts the real provider.

prs.title: fix: replies fail when long tool runs fill model context
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

A long tool run can finish its actions, then fail to answer when saved results fill the model context.

## User Impact

OpenClaw can resume from completed tool work without running those tools again. It keeps fresh tool output when the final request fits.

## Why This Change Was Made

Recovery reduces tool output only when the selected request exceeds the context budget. The final request uses the same model limit. This preserves the safeguard in 168a489: an aggregate tool-result cap alone does not erase fresh output.

## Evidence

Example: twelve 4,000-character tool results fit one by one but can exceed the space left together.

I ran the shipped `openclaw agent exec` command with synthetic files and an isolated scripted provider set to a 32,768-token context:

```text
Run A: one HTTP 400 context_length_exceeded after 8 completed tool calls
       resumed; 2 writes and 12 reads, each once; status=ok
       a.txt="alpha\n"; b.txt="beta\n"
Run B: 2 writes and 12 reads, each once; final request tools=[]
       status=ok; final="Both files are written and all twelve pieces were read."
```

The three overflow/finalizer regressions fail on base ec41ea83a and pass on head 7f43a10. Both focused suites pass (17 tests). The test-line ratchet passes with a 251-line allocation. Core and test typechecks, focused lint, and formatting pass. Independent Codex review found no actionable regressions.

prs.title: fix(cli): explain unknown ids in devices reject and remove
prs.body:
Fixes #190293

## What Problem This Solves

`openclaw devices reject <id>` and `openclaw devices remove <id>` with an id the Gateway does not know printed only `The CLI command failed.` (exit 1). The Gateway's `INVALID_REQUEST unknown requestId` / `unknown deviceId` reason was lost in text mode, and the JSON envelope carried the bare Gateway string.

## User Impact

Text and `--json` callers now get `No pending device request matches <id>` / `No paired device matches <id>` plus a `openclaw devices list` hint, the same wording `devices approve` already uses. Exit code stays 1. Other Gateway failures still go to the root failure handler unchanged.

## Why

`runDevicesDeleteCommand` called `device.pair.reject|remove` without the unknown-id handling `devices approve` has. The fix catches only the unknown-id refusal for the requested field and routes it through the existing `failDevicesCommand`. The `isUnknownRequestIdError` helper moves to `src/cli/devices-cli.unknown-id.ts` and takes the field, so `devices-cli.runtime.ts` does not grow past the line-cap ratchet. The moved helper now narrows with `in` checks instead of a type assertion, so the runtime file's assertion-safety baseline shrinks from 9 to 8.

## Evidence

Linux, isolated HOME, a real local Gateway from this tree (`gateway run --auth token --bind loopback`), the same Gateway for both runs.

Before (main `devices-cli.runtime.ts`):
```
$ openclaw devices reject does-not-exist --token <local>
[openclaw] The CLI command failed.
[openclaw] For help, run `openclaw doctor`.
$ openclaw devices remove does-not-exist --token <local>
[openclaw] The CLI command failed.
[openclaw] For help, run `openclaw doctor`.
$ openclaw devices reject does-not-exist --json --token <local>
{
  "ok": false,
  "error": {
    "type": "cli_error",
    "message": "unknown requestId"
```

After (head 56ea4f08156):
```
$ openclaw devices reject does-not-exist --token <local>
No pending device request matches does-not-exist. Run openclaw devices list and retry with the current requestId.
# exit=1
$ openclaw devices remove does-not-exist --token <local>
No paired device matches does-not-exist. Run openclaw devices list and retry with the current deviceId.
# exit=1
$ openclaw devices reject does-not-exist --json --token <local>
{
  "ok": false,
  "error": {
    "type": "cli_error",
    "message": "No pending device request matches does-not-exist. Run openclaw devices list and retry with the current requestId."
  }
}
No pending device request matches does-not-exist. Run openclaw devices list and retry with the current requestId.
# exit=1
```

Scoped tests: `vitest run --config test/vitest/vitest.cli.config.ts src/cli/devices-cli.test.ts`: 43 passed. The two new unknown-id text cases fail on the main runtime (2 failed | 41 passed). New coverage: text and JSON for both commands, and a non-unknown-id failure that still reaches the root handler.

prs.title: fix(signal): align autoStart daemon bind with local connection URL port
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

A path-prefixed managed-native URL is a proxy, not the daemon bind. For a saved `http://127.0.0.1:8080/signal`, autoStart reserves port 8080 for that proxy and binds the daemon on 8081. Readiness stays on the unchanged proxy URL. A URL on another port, such as `http://127.0.0.1:8082` with no `httpPort`, also stays the client endpoint. Set `httpPort` when the daemon should listen on a non-default port. Remote, HTTPS, and cross-family URLs stay independent.

Ref #116165

## Evidence

Head `1d08a5e9d41ee8a57dafde368361ada21a050ee8`. macOS, signal-cli 0.14.9.

The production resolver reserved 8080, allocated daemon port 8081, and kept `baseUrl` at `http://127.0.0.1:8080/signal`. `spawnSignalDaemon` started signal-cli. A loopback forwarder stood in for the independent `/signal` proxy on 8080. `signalCheck` used the unchanged base URL.

```console
{
  "reserved": [8080],
  "allocated": 8081,
  "baseUrl": "http://127.0.0.1:8080/signal",
  "daemonPort": 8081,
  "signalCheck": { "ok": true, "status": 200, "error": null },
  "listeners": [
    "node ... TCP 127.0.0.1:8080 (LISTEN)",
    "signal-cl ... TCP 127.0.0.1:8081 (LISTEN)"
  ]
}
```

signal-cli listened on 8081. The readiness check against `http://127.0.0.1:8080/signal` returned HTTP 200. No phone account was registered.

## Real behavior proof

- **Behavior or issue addressed:** A same-port path-prefixed proxy stays the client endpoint while the daemon binds the next free port, and readiness still succeeds through that proxy URL.
- **Real environment tested:** macOS, Node, signal-cli 0.14.9, worktree `/tmp/oc-116176` at `1d08a5e9d41ee8a57dafde368361ada21a050ee8`.
- **Exact steps or command run after this patch:** `node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs /tmp/proof-oc-116176.mts` calls `reserveSignalTransportPorts`, `allocateSignalManagedNativePort`, `resolveSignalTransport`, `spawnSignalDaemon`, and `signalCheck`.
- **Evidence after fix:** The console block in Evidence. Daemon port 8081, base URL unchanged, `signalCheck` ok with status 200, signal-cli listening on 8081 and the proxy listener on 8080.
- **Observed result after fix:** The real signal-cli process bound 8081. The production check against the saved proxy URL succeeded.
- **What was not tested:** A registered phone account, or two signal-cli daemons at once.

## Summary

- Treat a non-root connection URL path as an independent proxy
- When that proxy uses port 8080, allocate the daemon on 8081 and leave the proxy URL unchanged
- Leave a saved URL on another port as the client endpoint

## Test plan

- [x] Same-port path `http://127.0.0.1:8080/signal` starts signal-cli on 8081
- [x] `signalCheck` against that unchanged proxy URL returns HTTP 200
- [x] Saved transport URL is not rewritten

prs.title: fix(gateway): forward OpenAI auth context to worker inference
prs.body:
## Summary

Forward the prepared authentication mode and flow to `applyExtraParamsToAgent()` during worker inference.

## What Problem This Solves

The worker inference path does not currently pass the prepared authentication classification into provider stream parameter handling.

This can cause provider-specific behavior to use incomplete information about how the model was authenticated, particularly for OpenAI OAuth / Sign in with ChatGPT.

## Changes

- Pass `prepared.auth.mode` and `prepared.auth.authFlow` to the existing stream parameter handling.
- Add regression coverage for the forwarded authentication context.
- Keep credential contents, storage, and refresh behavior unchanged.

## Evidence

Validated against OpenClaw main commit `ae0739da8acc9d2f2d8630533f19688da7e00a15`.

- Targeted inference runtime tests passed.
- Core and test TypeScript checks passed.
- Formatting and lint checks passed.
- `git diff --check` passed.

## Scope

This PR addresses propagation of authentication classification only.

It does not modify OAuth token refresh or credential authority. It also does not claim independent verification of the outgoing `store: false` HTTP parameter.

No private credentials or deployment-specific configuration are included.

## Reproduction and Behavioral Evidence

**Preconditions**

The worker inference path uses a model with prepared authentication metadata, including `mode` and optionally `authFlow`. A relevant example is OpenAI Sign in with ChatGPT (SIWC), represented as OAuth with the `chatgpt-token-sharing` authentication flow.

**Before the fix**

`executePreparedWorkerInference()` invokes `applyExtraParamsToAgent()` without forwarding `prepared.auth.mode` or `prepared.auth.authFlow` in the options.

Consequently, downstream provider-specific stream configuration does not receive the prepared authentication classification from this worker call site.

**After the fix**

The worker passes:

```typescript
auth: {
  mode: prepared.auth.mode,
  authFlow: prepared.auth.authFlow,
}
```

The regression test, `forwards $name auth classification without credentials`, verifies three cases: SIWC, API-key authentication, and another OAuth flow.

It also checks that the forwarded options do not contain the authentication fixture's credential marker.

Reproduction command:

`pnpm test src/gateway/worker-environments/inference-runtime.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`

Targeted tests, TypeScript checks, lint and formatting passed locally.

**Observed deployment behavior**

A private OpenClaw deployment successfully completed model requests through OpenAI OAuth after applying the corresponding authentication-context fix.

This is deployment-level validation, not an isolated proof of the downstream HTTP request parameters.

**CI test-line allocation**

The PR includes `config/test-lines-allocations/worker-inference-auth-context.txt`.

Local staged ratchet result:

`Test lines OK: 6563155; ceiling: 6563160; slack: 5.`

**Scope and limitations**

This PR only forwards authentication classification to the existing provider stream configuration mechanism.

It does not change OAuth token refresh, credential authority or credential persistence. The outgoing OpenAI `store: false` HTTP parameter has not yet been independently verified.

issues.title: Deploy to Render fails with exit 128: dockerCommand replaces the entrypoint
issues.body:
### Bug Description

A fresh **Deploy to Render** from `render.yaml` fails before nanobot starts. The deploy exits with status 128 and prints no app output.

`render.yaml` sets `dockerCommand: gateway`. Its comment says Render's Docker Command replaces the Dockerfile `CMD` but keeps the `ENTRYPOINT`. On Render today, the Docker Command replaces the `ENTRYPOINT` too. Render tries to run `gateway` as the executable, which doesn't exist, so `entrypoint.sh` never runs. The log has none of its `[entrypoint]` lines.

Setting the Docker Command to the full entrypoint fixes it:

```yaml
    dockerCommand: /usr/local/bin/entrypoint.sh gateway
```

With that command, the entrypoint drops privileges, initializes `config.json` from `render-config.json`, and appends `--config` as intended. The service goes live.

Suggested change: update `dockerCommand` in `render.yaml` as above, and update the comment to say the Docker Command replaces both `ENTRYPOINT` and `CMD`.

### Steps to Reproduce

1. Open https://render.com/deploy?repo=https://github.com/HKUDS/nanobot and apply the Blueprint.
2. Wait for the build to finish.
3. The deploy fails with `Exited with status 128`. There are no `[entrypoint]` lines in the log.
4. In the service's **Settings**, set **Docker Command** to `/usr/local/bin/entrypoint.sh gateway` and deploy again. The service goes live.

### Expected Behavior

The one-click deploy goes live without changes.

### Relevant Logs

```shell
# With dockerCommand: gateway (the build succeeds)
==> Deploying...
==> Setting WEB_CONCURRENCY=1 by default, based on available CPUs in the instance
==> Exited with status 128

# With dockerCommand: /usr/local/bin/entrypoint.sh gateway
[entrypoint] dropping privileges to nanobot via setpriv
[entrypoint] initializing /home/nanobot/.nanobot/config.json from render-config.json
Using config: /home/nanobot/.nanobot/config.json
🐈 Starting nanobot gateway version 0.4.1 on port 18790...
INFO | websocket | WebSocket server listening on ws://0.0.0.0:8765/
==> Available at your primary URL https://<service>.onrender.com
```

### nanobot Version

0.4.1 (`main` at c5f2ce5)

### Python Version

3.12 (repository Dockerfile)

### Operating System

Docker on Render (Debian bookworm image from the repository Dockerfile)

### Channel / Platform

WebSocket (WebUI). It fails before any channel starts.

### LLM Provider

anthropic (Render template default). Not related: the failure happens before nanobot starts.

issues.title: [WebUI] Scroll-to-bottom button flickers: it reappears for most of the smooth navigation after being clicked
issues.body:
### Bug Description

Clicking the "Scroll to bottom" button makes it flicker: it disappears on click, reappears for most of the smooth scroll down, and disappears again on arrival. The button genuinely unmounts and remounts, with its `animate-in fade-in-0 zoom-in-95` entrance.

### Steps to Reproduce

1. Open a conversation longer than one viewport.
2. Scroll up so the "Scroll to bottom" button appears.
3. Click it: hidden on click → visible again during the scroll → hidden on arrival.

In code: park `ThreadViewport` at `maxScrollTop`, take the camera with `wheel`, move `scrollTop` far from the tail so the button mounts, click it, then step the animation and emit a `scroll` event per frame. The clock must be controlled (`requestAnimationFrame` into a queue, `performance.now` into a counter): [`thread-camera.ts`](https://github.com/HKUDS/nanobot/blob/3404fe83/webui/src/components/thread/thread-camera.ts#L1) animates over `NAVIGATION_DURATION_MS = 220`, so on an unloaded machine the trip settles within one real frame and a test driven by real frames never observes the flicker.

### Expected Behavior

Once clicked, the button stays hidden for the whole trip to the tail.

### Actual Behavior / Code Evidence

At upstream revision [`3404fe83`](https://github.com/HKUDS/nanobot/commit/3404fe83):

- [`scrollToBottomNow()`](https://github.com/HKUDS/nanobot/blob/3404fe83/webui/src/components/thread/ThreadViewport.tsx#L536-L552) starts the trip with `navigateLatestTo(top)` (mode `navigating-latest`) and hides the button optimistically with `setAtBottom(true)`.
- [`onScroll()`](https://github.com/HKUDS/nanobot/blob/3404fe83/webui/src/components/thread/ThreadViewport.tsx#L933) then recomputes the state from geometry alone: `logicallyAtBottom = !historyWindow && (owner === "automatic" || (owner === "navigation" && near))`.
- While the camera is still travelling, [`observeScroll()`](https://github.com/HKUDS/nanobot/blob/3404fe83/webui/src/components/thread/thread-motion.ts#L348-L381) returns `owner === "navigation"` and `near` is false until the trip enters the [`NEAR_BOTTOM_PX = 48`](https://github.com/HKUDS/nanobot/blob/3404fe83/webui/src/components/thread/ThreadViewport.tsx#L80) band, so the state flips back and the button remounts — measured over a frame clock, visible for 9 of 13 sampled frames (~150 ms of the trip).
- Also in the released build: [`v0.4.0`](https://github.com/HKUDS/nanobot/releases/tag/v0.4.0) already has [`setAtBottom(true)`](https://github.com/HKUDS/nanobot/blob/v0.4.0/webui/src/components/thread/ThreadViewport.tsx#L537) in `scrollToBottomNow` and [`(owner === "navigation" && near)`](https://github.com/HKUDS/nanobot/blob/v0.4.0/webui/src/components/thread/ThreadViewport.tsx#L917) in `onScroll`.

issues.title: WebUI: model button does not reflect the active primary or fallback model
issues.body:
### Bug Description

The WebUI composer model button can be mistaken for the model handling the current request, but it displays the configured/selected preset rather than following the gateway's `turn_model_updated` events. In particular, it does not update when a fallback handles the turn. This makes the interface misleading when the default preset, session selection, and actual response model differ.

In the reported case, the global default was `GPT 6.1 Sol Med`, the user selected `nvidia/nemotron-3.5-super-vl:free` through OpenRouter for a chat, and the interface still appeared to identify GPT as primary during processing. Sanitized gateway logs established that Nemotron was actually attempted as primary. OpenRouter rejected it with HTTP 401, followed by Gemini fallback attempts; `gemini-3.1-flash-lite-preview` ultimately succeeded. The display discrepancy should not be interpreted as evidence that GPT actually processed that request.

The OpenRouter authentication failure and provider quota errors are separate configuration/service problems. This report concerns accurate model attribution in the WebUI, not bypassing those failures or changing fallback routing.

### Steps to Reproduce

1. Configure a default model preset and at least one different fallback preset.
2. Open a WebUI chat and select its intended preset.
3. Submit a request that causes the primary provider to fail and a configured fallback to be used. A mocked provider failure is sufficient; no external outage is required.
4. Observe the gateway's `turn_model_updated` events and the composer model button while processing and after completion.

For a deterministic frontend reproduction, render `ThreadShell` with a default OpenAI Codex preset, emit a chat-scoped `turn_model_updated` event identifying a different primary model, and then emit one with `model_name: "deepseek/deepseek-chat", fallback: true`. The button continues to show the configured preset instead of following the reported runtime model.

### Expected Behavior

The interface should clearly distinguish the preset selected for the next request from the model actually processing the current turn. The model button should reflect the gateway-reported primary/fallback model and provider while processing, with the last reported model visible after completion. Opening the picker should retain the user's selected preset for the next request; using a fallback must not silently change that selection.

Alternatively, if maintainers prefer the button to represent only the next-request selection, its presentation should make that distinction explicit and provide equally visible current-model attribution during processing.

### Actual Behavior / Code Evidence

At upstream revision `cc4dd1ceb`:

- `webui/src/components/thread/ThreadShell.tsx` derives `modelBadge` from `toModelBadgeInfo(modelName, settings, activeModelPreset)`. Non-fallback `turn_model_updated` events only clear the fallback notice; fallback events populate a separate notice without updating the composer model display.
- `webui/src/tests/thread-shell.test.tsx` explicitly covers the existing behavior in the test named “keeps the selected composer preset and attributes only the reply to its actual source”.
- `docs/guides/configure-model-fallback.md` says the composer still shows the selected preset.

This is therefore a request to correct a confusing display contract, not a claim that the existing behavior is accidental or that backend model selection has been proven broken. Fallback notices and per-reply attribution already exist; they do not make the model button itself follow the active model.

### Environment

- nanobot: 0.4.0; source baseline `cc4dd1ceb` with local WhatsApp integration fixes
- Python: 3.13.2
- OS: macOS arm64
- Channel: WebUI / WebSocket
- Connection: local gateway, packaged WebUI
- Browser version: not recorded
- Providers involved in the report: OpenAI Codex default, OpenRouter-selected Nemotron, Gemini fallbacks

### Local Fix and Verification

A local patch now tracks the existing chat-scoped runtime model events for display separately from the selected preset. It updates the button label/provider without changing the picker selection or model-routing policy. No protocol changes are required; hosts without runtime-model events retain the existing configured-preset display.

Verification:

- Regression test reproduced the unchanged fallback label before the fix and passed afterward.
- 335 tests passed across `thread-shell.test.tsx`, `model-preset-badge.test.tsx`, `thread-composer.test.tsx`, and `model-fallback-notice.test.tsx`.
- The updated regression also verifies a reported Nemotron primary differing from the configured default, its OpenRouter branding, fallback display, and resetting to the reported primary on the next turn.
- A picker regression verifies that runtime display does not change the selected preset or its model details.
- Type checking, focused ESLint, client import-boundary checking, and the production WebUI build passed.
- The rebuilt WebUI was installed locally and its served bundle verified. No new live model request was sent to validate this display patch; runtime events were exercised deterministically in tests.

Related reports: #5198 concerns session model switching itself; #6031 concerns fallback notifications on non-WebUI chat channels. This report focuses on the WebUI composer button's runtime-model attribution.

issues.title: /new silently does nothing when the session is idle — non-priority command cancels its own task before state.reset() runs

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

issues.body:
### Bug Description

Summary
Sending /new as a standalone message to an idle chat does nothing at all: the session is not reset, no reply is sent, nothing is persisted, and no model call happens. Other slash commands in the same chat (/status, /help) work normally.

Reproduced on two channels: Feishu (p2p private chat) and WebUI (websocket). The dispatch path is channel-independent, so both hit the same code.

cmd_new calls loop._cancel_active_tasks(ctx.key) before it calls state.reset(). For a non-priority command that path runs inside the session-queue worker task, which is registered in _active_tasks[key] — so cmd_new cancels the very task it is running in. The CancelledError lands at the next await point inside _cancel_active_tasks itself, so state.reset() is never reached, and the error is swallowed by the worker's except asyncio.CancelledError handler.

Environment
nanobot-ai 0.4.1, editable install from source, branch main at 4652536e6
Windows 11, gateway running in a foreground terminal (nanobot gateway -c <config>)
Channels: Feishu (p2p private chat) and WebUI (websocket)
The self-cancel shape below was verified identical in 0.4.0 (ce3aa50e) where the first failures were observed, and re-verified unchanged in 0.4.1
Observed behaviour
Feishu chat history (read through the Feishu API) shows the messages really were sent, as plain text, exactly /new, nothing else attached:

11-05 08:28:49  user  text  /new
11-05 08:29:11  user  text  /new
11-05 08:30:19  user  text  /new
11-05 08:35:57  user  text  /new

For each of them:

No session reset. The session header stayed created_at = 2026-11-03T16:49:30.467036, message rows continuous, last_archived unchanged, _last_summary still present in metadata. cmd_new → SessionState.reset() deletes the rows, writes a brand-new session and pops _last_summary (nanobot/session/state.py:1160), so a real run cannot leave this state. As of 2026-11-08 the header is still 2026-11-03T16:49:30.467036 with 2868 message rows — every /new since then (Feishu and WebUI) failed the same way.
No persisted message row. /new is deliberately excluded from early persistence (nanobot/agent/loop.py:2159-2167), so the absence of a row is expected — but nothing else was written either.
No model call. llm_usage shows a gap from 08:34:56 to 08:38:52 with zero calls, so the turn never reached the build stage.
No reply of any kind.
WebUI, 2026-11-08: llm_usage shows a 402 s gap with zero calls from 16:25:41 to 16:32:22 (the /new attempt window), then the next call at 16:32:22 is the first real message of a session whose created_at is 16:32:22 — i.e. the gap, not the /new, produced the fresh session.

Same chat, same moment, other commands work:

11-05 08:49:01  user  text  /help      -> app card at 08:49:02

/help left two rows tagged _command (nanobot/agent/loop.py:2159-2167) and answered in 1 second, with no model call. /status answered in 2.4-3.3 s on every attempt.

Why /status works but /new does not
/status, /stop and /restart are registered as priority commands (nanobot/command/builtin.py:943-945). Priority commands are dispatched inline from the bus consumer task, before the session queue is involved (nanobot/agent/loop.py:1452-1457). That task is not registered under the session key.

/new is exact-only (nanobot/command/builtin.py:946). When no worker is currently running for the session, the message goes through _enqueue_session_message, which creates the worker task and registers it under the session key:

# nanobot/agent/loop.py:1556-1557
task = asyncio.create_task(self._run_session_queue(session_key, new_pending))
self._track_active_task(session_key, task)

cmd_new then runs inside that task:

# nanobot/command/builtin.py:249-252
async def cmd_new(ctx: CommandContext) -> OutboundMessage:
    loop = ctx.loop
    await loop._cancel_active_tasks(ctx.key)
    loop.discard_session_file_state(ctx.key)

and _cancel_active_tasks cancels everything registered under the key, including the task it is currently running in:

# nanobot/agent/loop.py:913-917
async def _cancel_active_tasks(self, key: str) -> int:
    pending = self._pending_queues.get(key)
    tasks = tuple(self._active_tasks.pop(key, set()))
    cancelled = sum(1 for t in tasks if not t.done() and t.cancel())
    journal_session = await self.sessions.state.read(key)   # CancelledError lands here

The next await after the self-cancel is line 917, so the function aborts before cmd_new ever reaches the reset. The exception is caught by the worker:

# nanobot/agent/loop.py:1668
logger.info("Task cancelled for session {}", session_key)

which explains the exact observed signature: no reply, no persisted rows, no model call, session unchanged.

The same file already guards against this pattern in the shutdown path but not in _cancel_active_tasks:

# nanobot/agent/loop.py:1760-1767
current_task = asyncio.current_task()
pending_queues = {
    key: self._pending_queues[key]
    for key, tasks in active_task_groups.items()
    if key in self._pending_queues and any(task is not current_task for task in tasks)
}

What I verified separately
SessionState.reset() itself is fine. Called against a copy of the live sessions.sqlite3 for the same session key it worked: created_at 2026-11-03 16:49:30.467036 → 2026-11-05 08:50:16.391474, revision 1280 → 1, last_archived 1234 → 0, messages 1370 → 0.
/new is registered exactly once; no plugin or goal module overrides it.
The self-cancel shape reproduces in isolation: a task registered in active[key] that calls a function which pops active[key], cancels every task in it and awaits each one, gets its own cancellation delivered at the next await point.
Re-verified on 2026-11-08 against 0.4.1 (4652536e6): cmd_new (builtin.py:249-252), _cancel_active_tasks without a current_task guard (loop.py:913-917), priority registration (builtin.py:943-945), exact-only /new (builtin.py:946), and worker registration (loop.py:1556-1557) are all unchanged. The new _recovery_admission block (loop.py:1466-1471) only affects the mid-turn path and does not touch the idle path.
Regression window on this machine — identified
The same command used to work. The current session's created_at is 2026-11-03T16:49:30.467036, 1.4 s after a /new sent at 16:49:29, so that attempt demonstrably did create a fresh session. Eight /new from 2026-11-04 08:51 onward all failed, and every attempt since (Feishu and WebUI, through 2026-11-08) failed the same way.

The breaking change is 62c2ed4e7 ("refactor(goal): sustain one ReAct run until the goal closes", merged 2026-11-03 22:47 +0800). It moved the pop+cancel to the top of _cancel_active_tasks and removed the for t in tasks: with suppress(asyncio.CancelledError, Exception): await t loop that used to follow the cancel.

That loop was an accidental safety net: in the idle case the only task registered under the key is the worker running cmd_new itself, so t.cancel() cancels the calling task. Before 62c2ed4e7, the self-cancellation was delivered at await t (the task awaiting itself) inside the suppress, so the exception was swallowed and cmd_new proceeded to the reset. After 62c2ed4e7, the next await after the self-cancel is the journal read, which is not protected, so the CancelledError propagates to the worker's handler and the reset never runs.

The local timeline lines up exactly: the last working /new (2026-11-03 16:49) ran on a checkout from the 2026-11-03 07:18 pull, which predates 62c2ed4e7; the 2026-11-04 07:19 pull picked the commit up; the first failed /new was 2026-11-04 08:51.

Note: the /new semantics themselves ("stop current task, then clear session") are an intentional change from d4e34f8c6 (2026-04-21, "fix(commands): intercept non-priority commands during active turn"), which updated the help text and docs to match. The regression is in the implementation of that intent for the idle case, where there is no active task to stop and the command should simply proceed to the reset.

Secondary finding (separate bug, same command)
In 0.4.1, nanobot/channels/feishu/runtime.py:2366-2372 silently drops the "New session started." confirmation for p2p chats:

if (
    msg.content.strip() == "New session started."
    and msg.metadata.get("chat_type") == "p2p"
    and not msg.media
    and not msg.buttons
):
    return

In 0.4.0 the same confirmation was instead sent as a msg_type="system" message that Feishu never rendered (600 messages of chat history contain zero system messages). Either way, the OutboundMessage("New session started.") returned by cmd_new (builtin.py:280) never appears in a Feishu p2p chat.

Net effect: /new has never had any visible confirmation on Feishu p2p, working or not.

Suggested fix
Exclude the calling task, mirroring the guard already present in _aclose_unlocked:

async def _cancel_active_tasks(self, key: str) -> int:
    pending = self._pending_queues.get(key)
    current = asyncio.current_task()
    tasks = tuple(t for t in self._active_tasks.pop(key, set()) if t is not current)

I have not applied this locally, so I cannot claim it fixes the case end to end.

Steps to reproduce
Start the gateway with any channel that routes non-priority slash commands through the session queue (Feishu p2p and WebUI both do).
Let the session go idle — no turn in flight, no active worker for that session key.
Send /new alone as a plain text message.
Expected: session reset plus a confirmation reply. Actual: nothing at all. The gateway is predicted to log Task cancelled for session <key> (from nanobot/agent/loop.py:1668); on this machine the gateway runs in a foreground terminal, so that log line is predicted rather than observed.
Possible workaround, not yet verified: send /new while a turn is in flight. In that case the code dispatches the command inline from the bus consumer task (nanobot/agent/loop.py:1475-1481) instead of creating a fresh worker task, which would avoid the self-cancel. I have not tested it.

### Steps to Reproduce

run /new in webui

### Expected Behavior

reset session

### Relevant Logs

```shell

```

### nanobot Version

0.4.1

### Python Version

3.13

### Operating System

windows 11

### Channel / Platform

webui、feishu

### LLM Provider

local

### Model

qwen3.8-27b

### Browser

_No response_

### Connection

_No response_

### Configuration (Optional)

```yaml

```

### Additional Context

_No response_

issues.title: Matrix: rooms registered from a resumed sync are misclassified as DMs (group policy bypassed)
issues.body:
### Symptom (observed)

On a Matrix channel with `groupPolicy: "listen"` (or `mention`) plus `groupPolicyOverrides`, after a restart of the bot process:

- A room with 3 real joined members is treated as a DM room. The server-side member list confirms 3 joined members (2 humans + bot), all invites accepted, and third-party messages have been posted in the room.
- The bot responds to every message without a mention. Both the channel-level policy and the per-room override are ignored for that room.

### Mechanism (verified, step by step)

1. The matrix channel uses matrix-nio with `store_sync_tokens=True`. After every process restart the client resumes from the last stored sync token, so the **first** sync is incremental.
2. Rooms that were quiet since that token are absent from `rooms.join` in the response, so they never register in nio's in-memory room map.
3. When such a room later receives its first post-restart message, the entry that registers it carries **no `summary`** and an **empty `state`** section. Verified with a separate test client replaying a sync against the same homeserver with `since=<the bot's stored token>`: the joined-room entry arrived with `summary = (None, None)`, state 0, timeline 0.
4. nio then builds `MatrixRoom` with `users = {}`, so `member_count` falls back to `len(users) = 0`.
5. `MatrixChannel._is_direct_room()` returns `True` for `member_count <= 2` — including 0 — so every policy gate (`listen_mode`, `_should_process_message`) treats the room as a DM and the group policy is bypassed.

For contrast, a sync without a `since` token (initial sync) returns all rooms with correct summaries and member lists, and classification is then correct. `full_state=True` (already passed to `sync_forever` in 0.4.1) does not prevent this: the server returns no room entries at all when nothing changed since the token.

### Environment

- nanobot 0.4.1, deployed via the public docker image
- Homeserver: Continuwuity (summaries observed on initial syncs; incremental entries tested as above)
- Room shape that surfaced it: 3 joined members with a `listen` per-room override

### Suggested fix

Blank the restored sync token once per process right before the first `sync_forever`, so the first sync is always a full initial sync. Replayed pre-startup messages are already filtered by `_is_pre_startup_event`, so nothing is double-processed. PR incoming.

issues.title: DeepSeek Chat Completions: image tool results are sent in an unsupported message role
issues.body:
Checked main at `3a37269f3f4b1f81c316a341b9dd2c5040ecf033`.

## Contract and mismatch

DeepSeek's [vision guide](https://api-docs.deepseek.com/zh-cn/guides/vision#使用限制) states that images are supported **only in `user` messages** for Chat Completions. In contrast, its [Responses guide](https://api-docs.deepseek.com/zh-cn/guides/responses_api#image-input) explicitly supports images in `function_call_output.output`.

With `deepseek-flash` and an explicit Chat Completions preset, reading an image through `read_file` produces this next-request shape:

```json
{
  "role": "tool",
  "tool_call_id": "call_image",
  "name": "read_file",
  "content": [
    {"type": "image_url", "image_url": {"url": "data:image/png;base64,..."}},
    {"type": "text", "text": "(Image file: ...)"}
  ]
}
```

The image remains in the unsupported `tool` role rather than being adapted to the Chat contract. This also reaches the same request builder after a Responses-to-Chat fallback; it is not a claim that the default Responses path is broken.

## Verification and impact

Offline reproduction used the actual `AgentRunner`, `ReadFileTool`, OpenAI SDK and `httpx.MockTransport`, with a locally generated 1×1 PNG and `ModelAPICapabilities(("chat_completions",), "chat_completions")`:

1. The first mocked model response calls `read_file`.
2. The captured second HTTP request contains the image under `role="tool"`, as above.
3. When the mock rejects that request with HTTP 400 according to the documented role restriction, nanobot retries with **no images** and can finish normally without the requested visual input.

As a control, converting the same history through the Responses builder retains the image as `function_call_output.output[input_image]`.

No live DeepSeek request was made. The unsupported request shape and local fallback behavior are verified; the actual service's response/error wording was not tested.

## Source

- [nanobot/agent/tools/filesystem.py:319–325](https://github.com/HKUDS/nanobot/blob/3a37269f3f4b1f81c316a341b9dd2c5040ecf033/nanobot/agent/tools/filesystem.py#L319-L325): image reads return native image blocks.
- [nanobot/agent/runner.py:543–565](https://github.com/HKUDS/nanobot/blob/3a37269f3f4b1f81c316a341b9dd2c5040ecf033/nanobot/agent/runner.py#L543-L565): tool results are appended with the `tool` role.
- [nanobot/providers/openai_compat_provider.py:589–682](https://github.com/HKUDS/nanobot/blob/3a37269f3f4b1f81c316a341b9dd2c5040ecf033/nanobot/providers/openai_compat_provider.py#L589-L682): the Flash image-capable path preserves that content without moving images to a supported role.
- [nanobot/providers/base.py:1750–1794](https://github.com/HKUDS/nanobot/blob/3a37269f3f4b1f81c316a341b9dd2c5040ecf033/nanobot/providers/base.py#L1750-L1794): error recovery retries after removing image input.

Could you adapt image tool results to the selected API's supported shape rather than relying on image-stripping recovery?

prs.title: fix(webui): support arbitrary file attachments
prs.body:
## Why

Pasting a readable local source-file path could fail with `Unsupported attachment MIME`, and the composer rejected browser files outside a fixed type list. A file reference should not need to upload or copy the file, and attachment eligibility should not depend on its format.

## What changed

- Accept regular local-file references of any type, including empty and extensionless files; preserve the draft text when a pasted path does not exist.
- Accept browser-selected, dropped, and pasted files of any type. Keep generic files' original bytes and safely preserve their filenames and extensions for replay, while retaining existing image and video handling.
- Allow zero-byte uploads through the direct and remote HTTP paths, and treat generic files as file references rather than vision inputs.
- Advertise `webui.attachments.any-file.v1`; clients retain the earlier supported formats on older hosts and provide upgrade guidance for the new cases.

## Boundaries

Workspace access, upload ownership, exact HTTP framing, attachment count and size limits, signed downloads, and media response protections remain in place. Accepting a file does not imply that every format can be parsed by the Agent.

## Verification

- `git diff --check` passed.
- Parsed changed Python files and checked locale JSON/key coverage; inspected the zero-length HTTPX request framing without sending a request.
- Added coverage for browser inputs and drafts/queues, local path references, empty and generic uploads, filename preservation and replay, Agent file references, remote uploads, and older-host compatibility.
- Local tests, lint, type checking, and builds were not run; full validation is delegated to remote CI.

Resolves [NAN-428](https://linear.app/nanobot-ai/issue/NAN-428/webui-支持任意类型的文件附件和本地路径引用)

prs.title: fix(webui): retain system context graph after compaction
prs.body:
## Why

After context compaction, the file graph can lose system prompt sources even though the model still uses those files. System prompt sources and ordinary file reads have different lifetimes, so the graph keeps them separately rather than branching on the provider or compaction reason.

## What changed

- Publish rebuilt system prompt sources before the successful local compaction event, including when compaction happens before the first model request.
- Reset earlier stage observations while retaining the current system prompt sources. Preserve pending sources from the new message for the next request.
- Persist system, stage and read provenance separately so a later turn can replace outdated system prompt sources without losing post-compaction reads.
- Isolate background tasks from their parent turn's source capture.
- Update the WebUI graph immediately and reconstruct the same graph from history and the reload cache.

This changes context graph observation and presentation only; it does not change model prompts, compaction timing, or other channels.

## Verification

- Focused Python graph, compaction and background task tests: 116 passed.
- Related compaction, model-request and transcript tests: 34 passed, 94 deselected.
- Unit tests cover local and provider compaction using controlled model events, rebuilt system prompts, history restoration, pending sources and cancellation.
- Focused BasedPyright, Ruff on changed Python files and `git diff --check`: passed.

Resolves NAN-427

prs.title: fix: preserve delivery failures across channel boundaries
prs.body:
## Why

An email could be acknowledged before entering the agent's inbound queue, a Mattermost attachment could disappear while the send appeared successful, and a restored update review could repeatedly fail without surfacing a recoverable state.

## What changed

- Acknowledge inbound email only after bus acceptance, retry failed seen acknowledgements, and guard cross-session UID operations with UIDVALIDITY. Preserve pending actions across cancellation within the running process.
- Propagate Mattermost attachment upload failures before creating any posts, and reject upload responses without a file ID.
- Classify restored update-review failures consistently, stop polling on authorization errors, and keep transient failures recoverable.

## Scope

The common inbound handler now reports whether the bus accepted a message; Signal's separate policy-checked publisher is renamed to avoid overriding that contract. Existing channel delivery and update-consent flows remain in place.

## Tradeoffs

Email acknowledgements and deferred actions are in-memory, not durable. A crash between bus acceptance and IMAP acknowledgement can cause a repeated delivery. An uncertain MOVE/COPY result is not blindly retried; it may require manual inspection. IMAP cancellation waits for an active worker, so a blocked server can delay shutdown. Mattermost's pre-existing ambiguity when a post succeeds but its response is lost remains outside this fix.

## Blast Radius

Email polling and authorization, Mattermost attachment sends, Signal's internal publisher naming, and WebUI update recovery. Cross-session UIDVALIDITY changes invalidate pending old-epoch operations to avoid acting on unrelated mail.

## Verification

- Python focused suites: email, Mattermost, Signal and shared channel base — 419 passed.
- Ruff on affected channel code/tests and basedpyright on affected runtime files — passed.
- `bun run test src/tests/update-flow.test.tsx` — 42 passed; WebUI typecheck, lint and production build passed.
- No live IMAP, Mattermost server, or browser end-to-end run; full-project basedpyright was not passing in the available environment.

Resolves NAN-425
