prs.title: fix(agent): reset idle sessions without self-cancellation
prs.body:
## Why

Sending `/new` to an idle chat cancels the worker executing the command itself, so the session is not reset and no confirmation is delivered. Cancellation should stop other session work without terminating the operation that requested it.

## What changed

- Exclude the calling task from cancellation and retain its active-task and inbox ownership until the worker finishes.
- Exercise idle and active-turn `/new` through the inbound bus, including a message queued while an idle reset is in progress.

## Scope

Addresses the idle reset failure in #6601 across channels. Feishu's separate private-chat confirmation behavior is unchanged.

## Tradeoffs and remaining risk

The current worker keeps its existing queue, so an input accepted after `/new` can run in the new session. Session reset clears the old follow-up journal; if the process exits between the reset and processing that queued input, recovery of that input is not established by these tests. The reset/admission durability boundary needs separate investigation before treating this PR as ready.

## Blast Radius

The shared session cancellation path is used by other controls. External cancellation still stops and waits for the tracked workers and reclaims their queues; an executing session worker now remains tracked until its normal completion.

## Verification

- Before the fix, the idle inbound `/new` regression timed out with `Task cancelled for session`.
- `python -m pytest tests/agent/test_session_inbox_controls.py tests/agent/test_task_cancel.py tests/agent/test_new_command_archival.py tests/agent/test_unified_session.py tests/command/test_router_dispatchable.py -q` — 123 passed.

prs.title: Expose the current tool invocation identity to tools
prs.body:
Closes #5749

## Problem

`RequestContext` tells a tool which session and turn it runs in, but not which logical tool invocation it is serving. The runtime already has that identity (the provider's `tool_call_id`, the same id the runtime checkpoints use to separate completed from pending work); it just never reached the tool. Tools with external side effects therefore could not recognise a retried call as the same invocation, so they could not deduplicate.

## Change

- `nanobot/agent/tools/context.py`
  - `ToolInvocationContext(tool_call_id, invocation_key)` as a frozen dataclass.
  - `tool_invocation_key(session_key, tool_call_id)`: `sha256(session_key, tool_call_id)`, stable for a retry of the same call, distinct across calls and sessions, `None` when the request has no session (ephemeral / SDK runs without `session_key`), never a guess.
  - A dedicated `ContextVar` with `tool_invocation_context()` / `current_tool_invocation_context()` and bind/reset helpers, mirroring the request-context API.
- `nanobot/agent/tools/execution.py`: `_execute_tool_call` binds the context around the `tool.execute(...)` / `tools.execute(...)` call only, so concurrent calls in one response each see their own identity and the previous value is restored as soon as the call returns. Hooks, tool schemas and model-visible metadata are unchanged.
- `nanobot/__init__.py`: the three names are exported next to `RequestContext`.
- `docs/python-sdk.md`: a short section with an idempotent `create_ticket` example.

Follows the alternative in the issue: a nested `ContextVar` scoped to one invocation rather than mutating request-level metadata, which would be unsafe for concurrent tool calls.

## Tests

`tests/agent/tools/test_tool_invocation_context.py`:
- key is stable for the same `(session_key, tool_call_id)`, 64 hex chars, distinct for another call or session, `None` without a session;
- bind/restore nesting;
- a single call sees its own id before and after yielding to the loop, and nothing leaks after execution;
- two concurrent calls in one request each see only their own id and key;
- without a session the tool receives the `tool_call_id` and a `None` key.

`tests/agent`, `tests/session`, `tests/webui`, `tests/channels`, `nanobot/channels` and `tests/test_nanobot_facade.py` pass locally (the only failures are the pre-existing Windows/no-Node ones). `ruff check` clean on the touched files.

## Summary

Fix the intermittent native theme-crossfade test timeout without changing product behavior or weakening assertions.

The test polls for two animations before pausing them. The real animations last 200 ms, so they can finish before a browser protocol round trip returns. Waiting longer cannot recover that intermediate frame.

- Observe the real View Transition's native `ready` promise and pause only the two theme-crossfade animations in the renderer before the driver reads them. Restore the original API after the observed call.

- Delay observation by 350 ms as a regression stimulus. This reproduces the old failure and remains longer than the unchanged production animation lifetime.
- Do not change production code, CSS, timeouts, retry settings, worker settings or dependencies.

The readiness boundary follows the [View Transition lifecycle](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-view-transitions-1/#dom-viewtransition-ready).

## Verification

- Before the fix: the existing 390px dark-palette test fails with the 350 ms observer delay, expecting two animations and receiving zero, as in the main CI incident.
- After the fix: the same delayed observation passes at 1440px and 390px in both directions.

prs.title: feat(settings): check sandboxes and configure trusted launchers
prs.body:
## Summary

Make sandbox setup easier to inspect without weakening command isolation.

- Add an explicit, gateway-owned sandbox check. It uses temporary files and the production launcher resolver and wrapper. It does not call a model or edit existing workspace files.
- Add `tools.exec.sandboxLauncher` for protected, nonstandard installations. Overrides must be absolute executable files with root-owned, non-writable ancestors, outside agent-writable roots. The gateway resolves symlinks and rechecks each command. Empty values retain the existing system lookup.
- Reuse the settings controls and CSS for isolation selection, saved-configuration status, translated errors, path editing and restart feedback. Confirm before turning isolation off. Do not run checks when opening settings.
- Show a dismissible chat notice for known launcher failures. Identify Bubblewrap (`bwrap`) or macOS Seatbelt (`sandbox-exec`) from the gateway's supported backend, not the browser's operating system. Missing-path actions open and focus the trusted launcher path editor. Other failures open the sandbox summary. Absent backend details retain generic wording.
- Keep input focus and unsent drafts. Do not install a package, retry a command, or reduce isolation from the notice. Repeated instances of the same issue stay dismissed for the turn. Opening history does not replay warnings.
- Include interactive production-component examples and all ten interface languages. Long translated action labels wrap in narrow views.
- Preserve configuration defaults, aliases and the protocol-1 baseline. The optional `webui.sandbox-settings.v1` capability gates new controls. Older compatible hosts retain their existing editor. Windows remains unsupported for these Unix sandbox backends.
- Resolve saved `${VAR}` references with runtime rules while preserving their original text on disk. Missing references remain unavailable. Unrelated provider secrets do not block sandbox editing.

Missing or rejected Unix launchers still fail closed. This change does not trust arbitrary PATH entries, change host permissions, or modify model prompts and tool parameter schemas. The optional error code is display-event metadata; the model-facing tool result retains its existing text.

## Verification

Current head: `0537b553d247af1342276dab6eb92b1ef905decb`, containing main at `5888791dc`. Its [Test Suite](https://github.com/HKUDS/nanobot/actions/runs/42450062990) passed on the first attempt. The selected matrix includes Python 3.11 and 3.14 on Linux, Python 3.14 and process compatibility on Windows, WebUI checks/build/browser, both terminal platforms, and Docker. Native package and Windows installer jobs were not selected.

- 176 frontend tests passed locally, covering gateway-specific names despite an opposite browser platform, explicit path navigation, retained drafts and focus, dismissal, stale host/turn events, old-host fallback, translated errors and deep-link focus. All locale keys and interpolation variables match.
- 25 browser checks passed locally. They cover both launcher names in all ten languages at 390px, generic fallback, and composer alignment at 390px and 1440px in light/dark views. Actions remain visible with no horizontal overflow.
- 42 launcher-compatibility, workspace-isolation and shell-boundary tests passed locally. The native platform for this run was macOS.
- 6 focused saved-config, authenticated sandbox-route and runner-progress tests passed locally. They cover old config, rejected override atomicity, environment references and unchanged model-facing tool content.
- Frontend lint, typechecking, client import boundaries and the production build passed locally.

The preceding revision also completed a real isolated gateway/WebUI flow: actual tool failure, notice, settings navigation, return with an unsent draft, rejected path, save, manual check, restart/reconnect, retained history and successful command execution. It used a loopback model fixture, not user data or external provider credentials. The latest follow-up changes presentation only; those gateway and navigation owners are unchanged. That full live flow was not repeated for this follow-up.

## Limits

The sandbox check is a basic test in a disposable workspace, not a full security audit or a guarantee that every application works with the configured mounts. The fnOS package and kernel restrictions still need native acceptance. A writable app-data installation needs a protected launcher from the package maintainer; the reported NAS path is not assumed safe or prefilled.

The notice requires a known live launcher error and follows existing progress delivery settings. Ordinary stderr and nonzero command exits do not prove a sandbox failure and do not trigger this guidance. Use the explicit sandbox check for other failures. Native package and Windows installer jobs are not selected by this change's CI matrix.

Ready for review. Do not merge or publish a release.

issues.title: Desktop: model switch in an existing chat fails silently with revision_conflict (no toast, old model kept)
issues.body:
### Summary

On the Desktop app, switching the model in an existing chat fails with **no visible feedback** and the composer keeps the old model. The renderer reports `模型切换失败: JsonRpcGatewayError: revision_conflict`, and starting a fresh chat (or re-entering the session) makes the switch work.

This looks like it belongs with #150011 (no feedback / old label after a switch) and #151582 (revision counter desync between `/api/sessions` and the fence), but the specific path here is a **model value pick on a session whose fences went stale**, where the built-in one-shot retry (`retryableFence` in `apps/desktop/src/api/canonical-protocol.ts`) apparently did not recover.

### Environment

- Hermes Agent v0.23.0 (2026.9.24) · stable · local `2bd378ed1b8d`
- Install method: git (`~/.hermes/hermes-agent`)
- Desktop app: macOS 26.7.1, arm64 (Apple M4 Pro, 24 GB)
- Provider/model: `deepseek` / `deepseek-flash`, `base_url: https://api.deepseek.com/v1`
- The desktop had just performed an in-app update hand-off and restart (~20 min before the failure)

### Steps to reproduce

1. Open Desktop with an existing chat that has history.
2. Switch the model from the model control.
3. Nothing observable happens: no error toast, the old model pill stays.
4. Re-enter the session, or start a new chat, and the same switch applies fine.

### Observed

Renderer log:

```
2026-11-09 11:31:54,774 [hermes] [renderer error:main] 模型切换失败: JsonRpcGatewayError: revision_conflict
2026-11-09 11:31:54,774 [hermes]     at fe (.../dist/assets/storage-C0O6CN6B.js:1:2845)
2026-11-09 11:31:54,774 [hermes]     at _e.handleFrame (.../dist/assets/storage-C0O6CN6B.js:1:6818)
```

Earlier failures in the same install, for contrast, were typed and surfaced correctly (`model_resolution_failed`, and a `400` from the provider when a non-DeepSeek model name was routed to the DeepSeek base URL) — those came with a visible message. `revision_conflict` does not.

### Expected

A model value pick is an idempotent write. A fence refusal that names fresh fences should be retried once at them, as `retryableFence()` intends; if it still refuses, the user should see a message rather than a silent no-op.

### Suspected cause

`retryableFence()` only retries when the mutation is still retained in `mutations` by `request_id`:

```ts
const current = [...this.mutations.values()].some(m => m.request_id === params.request_id)
return current && ['model', 'reasoning'].includes(params.operation)
  && typeof data?.revision === 'number' && (data.reason === 'revision_conflict' || data.reason === 'stale_generation')
```

Meanwhile `SessionControls.mutate()` in `gateway/session_controls.py` only attaches `revision`/`execution_generation` to the refusal when `db.get_session()` returns a row. If either condition fails — the request was already retired, or the refusal carried no revision — the client has nothing to retry with and swallows the verdict.

Suggested hardening: surface the refusal to the user as a retryable error when no retry is possible, and/or re-read the session revision on a pick refusal regardless of the retained-request check (a model pick is safe to re-apply).

issues.title: [Bug]: sessions/search ranks an exact session-title match last, and drops it once content hits fill the limit
issues.body:
## Summary

`GET /api/sessions/search` composes three result lanes in order — id matches, then FTS5 message-content matches, then `sessions.title` LIKE matches — and appends them into one insertion-ordered dict. The title lane runs **last**, and only when the content lane left slots (`if len(seen) < safe_limit`).

Consequence: searching for an **exact session title** returns that session at the very end of the list, or not at all once content hits fill `limit` (20 by default; the desktop sidebar search sends no `limit`). The desktop sidebar's "Search sessions…" uses this endpoint, so typing the exact title of a session that is visible in the sidebar returns other sessions first — or nothing — which reads as reversed ordering.

Related: #66242 introduced the title lane as a *supplement* ("backfills remaining result slots", "content hits keep BM25 priority"). That premise holds for partial/LIKE title matches, but not for an exact title, which is the strongest signal a user can type.

## Steps to reproduce

1. Populate ≥20 sessions whose message text contains the words of some title (trivial with a common word such as `profile` or `search`).
2. Give one session a distinctive title, e.g. `Generate image of green pear on white plate`.
3. Search that exact title from the desktop sidebar (or `GET /api/sessions/search?q=<title>`).

Observed: the green-pear session appears at index ≥ 1, usually appended after every content hit; with a slightly more common title it is absent entirely.

## Measurements

Store: 1,179 sessions / 105,694 messages. I queried each of the 40 most recent session titles verbatim, `limit=20`, against the real route handler:

| | rank 0 | rank > 0 | missing |
|---|---|---|---|
| current `main` | 22 | 5 | **13** |
| with the patch below | 32 | 0 | 8 |

- `Image generation workflow configuration in comfyui`: missing at `limit=20`; at `limit=100` it lands at **index 22 of 23** — dead last.
- The 5 that were previously missing now rank 0; 5 previously-late ones moved to rank 0; **none** moved later and **none** regressed.
- The 8 still missing are all delegate (`Subagent: …`) rows that `list_sessions_rich` excludes for an unrelated reason — identical before and after this patch, i.e. a separate issue, not a regression here.

## Root cause

`hermes_cli/web_routers/sessions.py`, `search_sessions()`:

1. `:406` id lane — `search_sessions_by_id()` matches `id` / `_lineage_root_id` only (`hermes_state_search.py:1311-1331`); titles are never considered here.
2. `:422` content lane — `search_messages()` ordered by bm25 (`hermes_state_search.py:1211`), over-fetching `max(limit*5, 50)`.
3. `:433-459` title lane — appended last, ordered by `last_active`, and gated by `if len(seen) < safe_limit` (`:441`), so it is skipped outright once the content lane has filled `limit`.
4. `:460` returns `list(seen.values())` — pure insertion order, so lane order *is* result order.

Titles are not in the FTS index at all (the comment at `:433` says so), which is exactly why they need a lane; but the lane can never outrank content, and can be starved by it.

## Proposed patch

Move **exact and prefix** title hits ahead of the content lane, and keep **substring-only** title hits in the old tail lane so a loose `LIKE` match still cannot outrank a real content hit. Ranking within the title lane: exact (whitespace-normalized, case-insensitive) → prefix → substring, with `sorted()`'s stability preserving the DB's recency order for ties. Id matches keep first place: a pasted id should stay on top.

One file, +57 / −27. Applies on `main` @ `369e7d66e9` (v0.23.0+1387.g5691c9f):

```diff
diff --git a/hermes_cli/web_routers/sessions.py b/hermes_cli/web_routers/sessions.py
--- a/hermes_cli/web_routers/sessions.py
+++ b/hermes_cli/web_routers/sessions.py
@@ -412,6 +412,50 @@ async def search_sessions(
                 snippet = preview or f"Session ID: {sid}"
                 add_lineage_result(sid, hit_payload(row, snippet, None, row.get("started_at")))
 
+            # Title matches come SECOND, ahead of message-content hits: a session
+            # title is what the user just read in the sidebar, so an exact/prefix
+            # title hit must outrank a bm25 content hit. This lane used to run
+            # LAST and only when the content lane left slots, which starved it —
+            # the content lane alone fills `limit`, so an exact-title query came
+            # back with the conversation missing, or appended at the very end.
+            if len(seen) < safe_limit:
+                try:
+                    title_rows = db.list_sessions_rich(
+                        search_query=q.strip(), include_archived=True, order_by_last_active=True,
+                        source=source_filter, sources=source_list or None,
+                        exclude_sources=exclude_list or None, limit=safe_limit)
+                except Exception:  # best-effort title lane: an old/odd store that rejects the search_query read must not fail the id results already collected
+                    _log.debug("Title-match lane skipped for %r", q[: 200])
+                    title_rows = []
+
+                needle = " ".join(q.strip().lower().split())
+
+                def _title_rank(row: dict) -> int:
+                    title = " ".join((row.get("title") or "").lower().split())
+                    if not title:
+                        return 3
+                    if title == needle:
+                        return 0
+                    return 1 if title.startswith(needle) else 2
+
+                # sorted() is stable, so equal ranks keep the DB's recency order.
+                ranked_titles = sorted(title_rows, key=_title_rank)
+                strong_titles = [r for r in ranked_titles if _title_rank(r) < 2]
+                weak_titles = [r for r in ranked_titles if _title_rank(r) == 2]
+            else:
+                strong_titles, weak_titles = [], []
+
+            for row in strong_titles:
+                if len(seen) >= safe_limit:
+                    break
+                sid = row.get("id")
+                if not sid:
+                    continue
+                preview = (row.get("preview") or "").strip()
+                add_lineage_result(
+                    sid, hit_payload(row, preview or f"Session title matched: {q.strip()}",
+                                     None, row.get("started_at")))
+
             # Prefix wildcards so partial words match ("nimb" -> "nimb*");
             # quoted phrases and existing wildcards are kept as-is.
             prefix_query = " ".join(
@@ -430,33 +474,19 @@ async def search_sessions(
                     m["session_id"],
                     hit_payload(m, m.get("snippet", ""), m.get("role"), m.get("session_started")))
 
-            # Title matches fill any remaining slots (#66242): the FTS index
-            # only covers message content, so a term that lives solely in a
-            # manually-set sessions.title would otherwise return nothing. ...
-            if len(seen) < safe_limit:
-                try:
-                    title_rows = db.list_sessions_rich(
-                        search_query=q.strip(), include_archived=True, order_by_last_active=True,
-                        source=source_filter, sources=source_list or None,
-                        exclude_sources=exclude_list or None, limit=safe_limit)
-                except Exception:  # health: allow BLE001
-                    _log.debug("Title-match supplement skipped for %r", q[: 200])
-                    title_rows = []
-                for row in title_rows:
-                    if len(seen) >= safe_limit:
-                        break
-                    sid = row.get("id")
-                    if not sid:
-                        continue
-                    preview = (row.get("preview") or "").strip()
-                    add_lineage_result(
-                        sid, hit_payload(row, preview or f"Session title matched: {q.strip()}",
-                                         None, row.get("started_at")))
+            # Substring-only title hits fill any remaining slots, as before: a
+            # loose LIKE match must not outrank a real content hit.
+            for row in weak_titles:
+                if len(seen) >= safe_limit:
+                    break
+                sid = row.get("id")
+                if not sid:
+                    continue
+                preview = (row.get("preview") or "").strip()
+                add_lineage_result(
+                    sid, hit_payload(row, preview or f"Session title matched: {q.strip()}",
+                                     None, row.get("started_at")))
+
             return {"results": list(seen.values())}
```

(The elided comment block above is unchanged in the real patch; only the lane's position and the `weak_titles` split differ. The full patch is reproducible from the description.)

## Verification

- Existing suites pass with the patch applied in an isolated worktree: `tests/hermes_cli/test_web_server_session_search.py` + `tests/hermes_cli/test_web_server_session_search_titles.py` → **8 passed** (including `test_search_title_lane_keeps_content_hits_priority`, which still holds because the fixture's title match is a substring, not a prefix).
- Suggested additions:
  - exact title outranks a content hit for the same needle (rank 0);
  - prefix title outranks content; substring title still defers to content;
  - exact title is returned when `limit=1`;
  - title lane still runs on the endpoint's worker thread (existing `to_thread` discipline).

## Notes / tradeoffs

- Cost: one extra `list_sessions_rich(search_query=…)` per request, now unconditional instead of conditional. Measured ~35 ms per query on a 1,179-session store; the same helper already backs the sidebar listing.
- A broad query that matches many titles will now spend slots on title hits before content. That is intended for exact/prefix; substring-only matches stay behind content so the common case is unchanged.
- Id matches keep first place, so pasting a session id still behaves exactly as before.

issues.title: Desktop auto-speak plays streamed replies twice (interim + final segments both voiced)
issues.body:
## Summary

Desktop auto-speak plays some replies **twice** in streaming turns. The interim streaming segment and the final reply segment are treated as two separate spoken segments, so both get voiced.

## Environment

- Hermes Agent v0.23.0+1473.g14485fc (desktop, macOS arm64)
- Voice mode with auto-speak replies enabled, Edge TTS
- Reproduces on ordinary streaming chat replies (no tool calls needed)

## Steps to reproduce

1. Desktop app, voice mode, "auto-speak replies" ON
2. Send any prompt that produces a streamed reply
3. Listen: the assistant speaks an interim segment, then speaks the (near-identical) final segment again

## Observed

Two TTS clips play back-to-back for one assistant turn. Log shows two `TTS audio saved` entries with different temp files for the same logical reply.

## Root cause analysis

`use-auto-speak-replies.ts` keys per-segment claims via `spokenSegmentKey(turnKey, segmentText ?? text)` (introduced in 9cb34e9e28). During streaming, the message's text changes between the interim and final states, so `segmentText` differs → two distinct segment keys → each is claimed and spoken once. The turn-level ownership (`ownsAmbientCue('speak:turn:...')`) only prevents *another window* from speaking; it does not dedupe segments *within* the same window.

4010a2f834 ("share pending read-aloud turn ownership") improved pending-ownership sharing but the streaming interim-vs-final double speak remains.

## Expected

One voiced clip per assistant turn: either skip the interim streaming segment and only speak the final text, or replace the in-flight clip when the final text lands.

## Possible directions

- Suppress interim segments while the turn is still streaming; arm auto-speak only on `turn.completed` / hydration
- Or treat the final text as superseding any in-flight clip for the same `turnKey` (stop & replace instead of queue)

Happy to test a fix. Great project — thanks!

issues.title: Telegram: multi-paragraph messages arrive as rich_message blocks and are silently dropped (empty Message.text)

labels.name: type/bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: comp/plugins
labels.description: Plugin system and bundled plugins

labels.name: tool/file
labels.description: File tools (read, write, patch, search)

labels.name: platform/telegram
labels.description: Telegram bot adapter

labels.name: P2
labels.description: Medium — degraded but workaround exists

issues.body:
**What happens**

Long / multi-paragraph Telegram messages (blank lines, pasted listings) can arrive in the new rich-block format: `Message.text` is empty and the content sits in `message.rich_message.blocks`. `getUpdates` delivers the update, the adapter sees it, no handler matches, and it disappears — no log line, no error, no session entry. Short messages are unaffected.

**Environment**
Hermes v0.22.5 (`bf0203a794`), python-telegram-bot 22.8, Linux, Telegram DM with topics.

**Root cause**
1. `plugins/platforms/telegram/adapter.py` — text handler is `filters.TEXT & ~filters.COMMAND`, which never matches when `text` is empty.
2. `plugins/platforms/telegram/telegram_entities.py::expand_link_entities()` — reads only `text` / `caption`.
3. No fallback for message content that no handler claims, so the drop is silent.

**Evidence** (payload captured with a temporary group `-1` catch-all handler):

```json
{"is_topic_message": true, "message_thread_id": 753673,
 "rich_message": {"blocks": [
   {"type": "paragraph", "text": "Can't you update the firmware yourself?"},
   {"type": "paragraph", "text": ""},
   {"type": "paragraph", "text": "It's 20 eur. Looks ok in the current market."}]}}
```

`Message.text is None`; `photo`, `document`, `sticker` are all absent. `getWebhookInfo` reports no polling conflict and 0 pending updates, so Telegram considers it delivered.

**Proposed fix**
1. In `expand_link_entities()`, when `text` and `caption` are empty, flatten `rich_message.blocks` (paragraph → line, `list_item` → `- …`, recurse into `items`/`blocks`).
2. Register an additional handler for messages whose `rich_message` is set and `text` is empty, routed to the existing `_handle_text_message` path.
3. Optionally: log or surface messages that no handler claimed, so a future content format cannot vanish silently again.

Happy to open a PR with that shape if it's the right direction.

issues.title: [Bug]: Standalone Telegram image batches are sent as separate photos

labels.name: type/bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: platform/telegram
labels.description: Telegram bot adapter

labels.name: P2

issues.body:
## Bug Description

The standalone Telegram sender used by `hermes send` accepts multiple image attachments but sends each one with `sendPhoto`. Telegram therefore renders a sequence of independent messages instead of a native media album.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Configure Telegram as a delivery target.
2. Call the standalone send path with two existing image files.
3. Inspect the Bot API methods invoked by `tools.send_message_tool._send_telegram`.
4. Observe two `sendPhoto` calls and no `sendMediaGroup` call.

A deterministic regression test reproduces this without external credentials by mocking the Telegram Bot API.

## Expected Behavior

A homogeneous batch of two or more photos should use `sendMediaGroup`, chunked at Telegram's ten-item limit. Single photos and mixed-media payloads should retain their established behavior.

## Actual Behavior

Every image is sent independently with `sendPhoto`, so the receiver does not get a Telegram media album.

## Affected Component

- Tools
- Gateway (Telegram/Discord/Slack/WhatsApp)

## Messaging Platform

- Telegram

## Debug Report

Not applicable: this is a deterministic code-path defect reproduced on current `main` with a mocked Bot API; no environment-specific runtime state is involved.

## Operating System

Ubuntu Linux

## Python Version

Python 3.11

## Root Cause Analysis

`tools/send_message_tool.py::_send_telegram` iterates over `media_files` and dispatches image extensions with `bot.send_photo`. The standalone path has no homogeneous-image batching branch using `bot.send_media_group`.

## Proposed Fix

Use `InputMediaPhoto` plus `InputFile(..., attach=True)` for homogeneous existing photo batches, chunk at ten items, validate complete receipts sharing one non-null `media_group_id`, and never degrade an intended album to individual photos after a partial/ambiguous group send.

## PR

- [x] I'd like to fix this myself and submit a PR

issues.body:
### Bug description

The Telegram docs (`website/docs/user-guide/messaging/telegram.md`, "Configure in `~/.hermes/config.yaml`") say `display.platforms.telegram.notifications: all|important` selects the notification mode. The gateway never reads it. Only `HERMES_TELEGRAM_NOTIFICATIONS` works.

`_resolve_notifications_mode()` (`plugins/platforms/telegram/adapter.py:7234` on `b920197404`) calls:

```python
cfg_get(load_gateway_config(), "display", "platforms", "telegram", "notifications")
```

`gateway.config.load_gateway_config()` (`gateway/config.py:825`) returns a `GatewayConfig` dataclass. `cfg_get` (`hermes_cli/config.py:1787`) returns the default when its argument is not a dict, so the lookup is always `None` and the mode falls back to `important`. The surrounding `try/except: pass` hides it.

This regressed in 5600105478 (adapters moved to bundled plugins). Before that, `gateway/run.py` read the same key with `cfg_get(_load_gateway_config(), ...)`, and `_load_gateway_config()` returns the raw config.yaml dict. Closed PR #98235 would have fixed it by accident (it switched to `_load_gateway_config` for perf reasons). It was closed on perf grounds, and the dict-vs-dataclass problem was not noticed.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Set `display.platforms.telegram.notifications: all` in config.yaml. Leave `HERMES_TELEGRAM_NOTIFICATIONS` unset.
2. Start the gateway with a Telegram bot and send a message that triggers tool progress.
3. Progress bubbles arrive with `disable_notification=True`. In-process check:
   `type(load_gateway_config())` is `GatewayConfig`; `cfg_get(load_gateway_config(), "display", "platforms", "telegram", "notifications")` is `None`; `_resolve_notifications_mode()` returns `important`. With `HERMES_TELEGRAM_NOTIFICATIONS=all` it returns `all`.

### Expected behavior

The config.yaml key selects the mode, with the env var as an override, as documented.

### Actual behavior

The config.yaml key has no effect. The mode is always `important` unless the env var is set.

### Environment

main `b920197404`. Also reproduced on an older host tree (`bf0203a794`). Any OS.

### Suggested fix

`plugins/platforms/telegram/adapter.py:7232-7234`: read the raw dict, as the pre-plugin code did:

```python
from gateway.run import _load_gateway_config, cfg_get
_raw = cfg_get(_load_gateway_config(), "display", "platforms", "telegram", "notifications")
```

(`gateway/run.py:2871`). Test sketch: write a temp `config.yaml` with `notifications: all` under a monkeypatched home, `delenv("HERMES_TELEGRAM_NOTIFICATIONS")`, assert `_resolve_notifications_mode() == "all"`. The existing suite never exercises the config path, which is why this went unnoticed.

Related: #131924 / #131933 (the standalone sender ignores the mode; a different code path).

issues.body:
### Bug description

`display.platforms.telegram.notifications` decides which Telegram messages buzz. Under the default `important`, everything except final replies and explicit `metadata["notify"]` is sent silently. This is applied in the gateway adapter (`_notification_kwargs`). Messages sent from outside the gateway process go through the standalone sender instead, `tools/send_message_senders.py::_send_telegram`, which never sets `disable_notification`. Those are `hermes send` and the `send_message` tool when no live adapter is attached. On `main` (`46904a3b46`) the file has no occurrence of `disable_notification`.

As a result, every `hermes send` message is audible whatever the configured mode, while the same text sent by the gateway would be silent. #100908 made cron deliveries notify deliberately through the live adapter; this is the other direction: there is no way to send quietly from a script.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Keep `display.platforms.telegram.notifications: important` (the default).
2. `hermes send --to telegram:<chat_id> "status: still syncing"` from a shell.
3. The phone buzzes. A gateway-sent progress or status message with the same text arrives silently.

### Expected behavior

The standalone sender honours the same notifications mode as the adapter, so a non-final message is silent under `important`. It would also be good to have an explicit per-message choice (`hermes send --silent` / `--notify`, `send_message(notify=…)`) for scripts that know better.

### Environment

macOS (Apple Silicon), Python 3.14. We use this path for a per-agent status notifier on a nine-bot install. We carry a local patch for it (the standalone sender passes `disable_notification` on every chunk and upload, with `--silent` / `--notify` on `hermes send`), and we can open it as a PR if this direction is welcome. Related: #20463 (priority-aware notifications in the adapters, open), #92929 (closed).

issues.title: [Bug]: Telegram send_message / hermes send / standalone cron delivery ignore rich_messages (tables flattened, <details> falls back to plain text)

labels.name: type/bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: comp/tools
labels.description: Tool registry, model_tools, toolsets

labels.name: comp/plugins
labels.description: Plugin system and bundled plugins

labels.name: platform/telegram
labels.description: Telegram bot adapter

labels.name: P2
labels.description: Medium — degraded but workaround exists

issues.body:
### Bug Description

With `rich_messages: true`, gateway replies that contain a pipe table, a task list, `<details>` or `$$` math are sent through `sendRichMessage` (Bot API 10.1) and render natively. Telegram text sent through the **standalone** path, `tools/send_message_senders.py::_send_telegram`, never uses that endpoint. The setting is ignored there. That path serves:

- the `send_message` tool (`tools/send_message_tool.py`: Telegram always goes to `_send_telegram`; only Matrix prefers the live adapter),
- `hermes send`,
- cron deliveries that fall back to standalone delivery when the live adapter is unavailable or degraded.

The same content therefore renders differently depending on how it is delivered. This is visible to users of scheduled briefings and agent-initiated messages.

There is no tracking issue for this yet, but three open PRs implement competing fixes:

- #46118 `fix(send_message_tool): add sendRichMessage fast-path for Telegram`
- #47190 `fix: use Telegram rich messages in send_message tool`
- #72939 `fix(telegram): sendRichMessage on standalone cron/hermes-send path`

This issue gives them one place to be triaged, so a single approach can be picked.

### Steps to Reproduce

```python
from tools.send_message_senders import _telegram_format

_telegram_format("| Service | Port |\n|---|---:|\n| oMLX | 8000 |")
# ('*oMLX*\n• Port: 8000', 'MarkdownV2', False)         <- table flattened to bullets

_telegram_format("<details><summary>More</summary>\n\n- **a**\n- b\n\n</details>")
# ('<details>…</details>', 'HTML', True)                <- sent as Bot API HTML
```

Sending the second one with `parse_mode=HTML` (checked against a real bot) returns `400 Can't parse entities: unsupported start tag "details"`. `_telegram_send_text_chunk` then resends it as plain text, so the raw tags and `**a**` show up verbatim.

### Expected Behavior

When `rich_messages` is enabled, the standalone Telegram sender makes the same rich decision as `TelegramAdapter.send()`. Content that `_needs_rich_rendering()` flags goes through `sendRichMessage` with the raw markdown, and falls back to the current MarkdownV2/HTML path on a permanent rejection.

### Actual Behavior

The setting is ignored on this path. Tables become bullet groups, and `<details>` (or any block tag the Bot API HTML mode does not support) makes the message fall back to plain text with the source visible.

### Affected Component

Tools (terminal, file ops, web, code execution, etc.), Gateway (Telegram/Discord/Slack/WhatsApp)

### Messaging Platform (if gateway-related)

Telegram

### Debug Report

Not attached. `_telegram_format()` reproduces it with no config or credentials (snippet above). The logs of the affected install hold private chat content.

### Operating System

macOS 15.1.1 (Apple Silicon)

### Python Version

3.11.15 (install venv)

### Hermes Version

v0.22.5 (bf0203a7, stable). The path is unchanged on `main` (e5ea5fd9): `send_message_senders.py` has no `sendRichMessage` call.

### Root Cause Analysis (optional)

`_telegram_format()` only chooses between MarkdownV2 (`TelegramAdapter.format_message`) and Bot API HTML (when any `<tag>` is present). The rich fast-path (`_should_attempt_rich` → `_try_send_rich`) lives only in `TelegramAdapter._send_text_locked()`, and the standalone sender never consults it.

### Proposed Fix (optional)

Any of the three PRs above. The smallest common shape: in `_send_telegram`, for text-only messages with `rich_messages` enabled and `_needs_rich_rendering(message)` true, call `sendRichMessage` with `TelegramAdapter._rich_message_payload(message)` before chunking, and keep the existing path as the fallback.

issues.body:
**Version:** main `d33becd87` (v2026.7.1 / v0.18.0), Telegram adapter (`plugins/platforms/telegram/adapter.py`).

**Symptom:** the empty-message guard in `send()` only rejects `.strip()`-empty text. A response consisting solely of **invisible code points** — U+200B/200C/200D/2060/FEFF/00AD/180E/200E/200F — passes the guard and is delivered as a **visually empty bubble** in the chat.

**When it happens in practice:** a response truncated down to markdown control characters, or a provider safety filter returning effectively-empty content. Observed repeatedly on a production bot.

**Expected:** treat text as empty after removing the invisible-character set (or use a broader blank definition than `str.strip()`), and skip the send — ideally with a debug log of the suppressed payload (repr) so the source can be diagnosed.

**Workaround we run locally:** a guard extension at the universal `send()` delivery point (covers streaming finals, cron deliveries and plugin sends) that suppresses invisible-only messages and logs a repr preview. Can submit as PR.

labels.name: sweeper:risk-message-delivery
labels.description: Sweeper risk: may drop, duplicate, misroute, or suppress messages

issues.body:
### Bug Description

Two related gaps in the cron → Telegram delivery path (standalone sender):

1. **Rich Messages are never attempted for cron deliveries on systemd-managed gateways.** On a managed gateway, cron jobs are handed to restart-safe external workers which run with `adapters=None, loop=None`, so delivery falls to the standalone sender (`tools/send_message_senders.py::_send_telegram`), which has no `sendRichMessage` path at all. `telegram.extra.rich_messages: true` only affects the in-process gateway adapter (`plugins/platforms/telegram/adapter.py::send()` → `_should_attempt_rich` → `_try_send_rich`).

2. **A single unsupported HTML tag drops the ENTIRE message to plain text.** `_telegram_format` switches to `ParseMode.HTML` whenever the content contains any `<tag>`. If the model emits `<details><summary>…` (a construct the chat path renders natively as a rich message!), the Bot API rejects the HTML send (`Can't parse entities: unsupported start tag "details"`) and `_send_telegram` falls back to **plain text** — no MarkdownV2 retry, no bold/lists/tables at all. Delivery is still recorded as `ok`, so this is a silent formatting loss (same class as #74004).

### Steps to Reproduce

1. Managed (systemd) gateway install with Telegram; `hermes config set telegram.extra.rich_messages true`; restart the gateway.
2. Create a cron job delivering to the Telegram home chat whose final output contains a Markdown pipe table and a `<details>` block (e.g. a daily study sheet with a quiz whose answers are collapsible).
3. `hermes cron run <job_id>`.
4. Telegram shows the whole message as plain text; `hermes cron list` reports the run as `ok`.

agent.log evidence:
```shell
WARNING tools.send_message_tool: Parse mode HTML failed in _send_telegram, falling back to plain text: Can't parse entities: unsupported start tag "details" at byte offset 3844
INFO cron.scheduler: Job '<id>': delivered to telegram:<chat_id>
```

### Expected Behavior

- Cron deliveries eligible for rich rendering (pipe tables, task lists, `<details>`, block math) should render via `sendRichMessage` — or at minimum keep MarkdownV2 formatting.
- A parse failure on one construct should degrade gracefully (retry MarkdownV2), not drop all formatting.

### Actual Behavior

Rich is never attempted on the cron path (the standalone sender has no rich code), and the presence of `<details>` alone loses all formatting silently. The only trace is a WARNING in agent.log; the job status is `ok`.

### Root Cause Analysis

Verified at v0.21.4 (upstream 4127d78d) and against current `origin/main` (2c65d5aee6):

- `cron/scheduler.py::run_one_job` external-worker branch runs with `adapters=None, loop=None`; `_launch_external_cron_worker` hands jobs to restart-safe workers on managed gateways (confirmed live by `Cron job '<id>' handed to restart-safe worker pid=…` logs).
- `cron/scheduler_delivery.py::_prepare_target_delivery`: `live_adapter_ready = runtime_adapter is not None and loop is not None and loop.is_running()` → False → `_deliver_standalone` → `_send_to_platform`.
- `tools/send_message_senders.py::_telegram_format`: any `re.search(r'<[a-zA-Z/][^>]*>', message)` match switches the whole message to `ParseMode.HTML`; `_send_telegram` catches parse errors and falls back to plain text. `git grep sendRichMessage origin/main` only matches `plugins/platforms/telegram/adapter.py`, `gateway/stream_consumer.py` and tests — no rich path exists in the senders.
- The rich path lives only in `plugins/platforms/telegram/adapter.py::send()`, reached only by gateway-adapter lanes (chat sends), never by cron standalone delivery.

This means #47762's observation ("cron auto-delivery renders rich") can only hold when the job runs **in-process** with live adapters; on current managed installs (restart-safe external workers) the standalone lane is used and rich can never happen. Filing as a complementary report since the observed direction is inverted.

### Proposed Fix

Options, smallest first:

1. **Graded fallback in `_send_telegram`:** on HTML parse failure, retry the same text through the adapter's `format_message()` (MarkdownV2) before plain text; and map `<details>/<summary>` to Markdown-safe output (e.g. a bold section title) instead of switching the whole message to HTML because of one tag.
2. **Give the standalone Telegram sender a rich path:** build `InputRichMessage` the same way `adapter._rich_message_payload` does and call `do_api_request("sendRichMessage", …)`, gated by the same `rich_messages` extra.
3. **Or route external-worker cron delivery back through the gateway** (loopback) so it reuses `TelegramAdapter.send()` and inherits rich for free — larger change, probably the right long-term shape.

Related: #47762 (inverted observation, same surface), #74004 (silent Markdown loss in the same sender, chunking trigger), #72908, #118047 (platform hint vs rich hint contradiction compounds this — the model is encouraged to emit tables/`<details>` that cron delivery cannot render).

### Environment

- Hermes Agent v0.21.4 (2026.9.21) · upstream 4127d78d; root-cause verified against origin/main 2c65d5aee6
- Ubuntu 22.04 (Oracle Cloud, aarch64), Python 3.11.15
- Platform: Telegram

### Debug Report

Withheld here to avoid uploading unrelated private logs from the shared gateway — happy to provide a redacted `hermes debug share` bundle if useful.

issues.body:
### Bug Description

When a Telegram message is sent via the standalone send path (_send_telegram() in tools/send_message_tool.py) and the message is long enough to be chunked across multiple Telegram messages (>4096 UTF-16 units), all Markdown formatting is silently lost. The message arrives as plain text, yet last_delivery_error reports null because the plain-text fallback send succeeds.

This primarily affects cron jobs with deliver: telegram:<chat_id> when the gateway is not running (cron falls back to the standalone send path).

Warning found in agent.log:
```
tools.send_message_tool: Parse mode MarkdownV2 failed in _send_telegram, falling back to plain text: Can't parse entities: character '(' is reserved and must be escaped with the preceding '\'
```

### Steps to Reproduce

1. Configure a Telegram bot in config.yaml
2. Stop the gateway (hermes gateway stop or wait for it to shut down) so cron uses the standalone send path
3. Create a cron job with deliver: telegram:<chat_id> whose output is >4096 UTF-16 units of Markdown content (include bold text and links)
4. Trigger the cron job manually
5. Check the delivered message in Telegram

### Expected Behavior

Message should render with correct Markdown formatting (bold, links, code, etc.), split across 2+ messages with properly escaped `(1/2)`,`(2/2)` chunk indicators.

### Actual Behavior

Message delivers successfully (no delivery error) but all Markdown formatting is completely lost — everything displays as plain text. The only indication of the problem is a warning-level log entry, which most users never see.

### Affected Component

Gateway (Telegram/Discord/Slack/WhatsApp)

### Messaging Platform (if gateway-related)

Telegram

### Debug Report

```shell
Report: https://dpaste.com/EVEM3ARJE
agent.log: https://dpaste.com/8Z7ZBWGN6
gateway.log: https://dpaste.com/GK7UBT2H6
gui.log: https://paste.rs/cn7F7
desktop.log: https://paste.rs/KZugq
```

### Operating System

Windows 11

### Python Version

3.11.15

### Hermes Version

0.19.0 [cbecd72e]

### Additional Logs / Traceback (optional)

```shell

```

### Root Cause Analysis (optional)

_No response_

### Proposed Fix (optional)

The bug is in tools/send_message_tool.py, in the _send_telegram() function (~line 1299–1302).

After BasePlatformAdapter.truncate_message() splits a long message into chunks, each chunk has a (N/M) suffix appended (e.g. (1/2)). The parentheses ( and ) in this suffix are MarkdownV2-reserved characters that must be escaped with a backslash. The standalone path sends the chunks directly without escaping these parentheses, causing Telegram's MarkdownV2 parser to reject the message with:
```
Bad Request: can't parse entities: character '(' is reserved and must be escaped with the preceding '\'
```
The code then catches this parse error (~line 1324) and silently falls back to parse_mode=None (plain text), which succeeds but strips all formatting.

Notably, the live adapter already has the correct fix. In plugins/platforms/telegram/adapter.py, the send() method (~line 4367–4375) properly escapes the chunk indicators:
```python
if len(chunks) > 1:
    # truncate_message appends a raw " (1/2)" suffix. Escape the
    # MarkdownV2-special parentheses so Telegram doesn't reject the
    # chunk and fall back to plain text.
    chunks = [
        _separate_chunk_indicator_from_fence(
            re.sub(r" \((\d+)/(\d+)\)$", r" \\(\1/\2\\)", chunk)
        )
        for chunk in chunks
    ]
```
The standalone path is missing this exact same transformation — classic code-duplication inconsistency.

### Are you willing to submit a PR for this?

- [x] I'd like to fix this myself and submit a PR

issues.body:
## Bug

Telegram text fallback can be delayed when an HTML parse error happens to contain a numeric HTTP status as part of unrelated text.

## Reproduction

At the `_telegram_send_text_chunk` send seam, make the rich-text attempt raise a parse error whose message includes a URL-like path containing `502` (redacted - no real URL needed). `_telegram_retry_delay` returns a transient delay for that parse error. The sender waits `[1.0, 2.0]` and repeats the HTML attempt before falling back to plain text. When the same parse error has no status digits, the retry delay is `None` and plain fallback is immediate.

## Expected

Only an actual HTTP response/status error (including 429 and retry-after behavior, and genuine transient 5xx failures) should select retry behavior. Parse errors should proceed directly to the existing plain-text fallback, regardless of arbitrary digits in their message text.

## Impact

This causes a few seconds of delay on an occasional Telegram delivery. It does not establish final delivery failure.

## Suggested direction

Classify structured transport/API status information rather than searching bare status digits anywhere in exception text.

# Issue: Telegram send_message does not retry on timeout errors

## Problem
The `_telegram_retry_delay` function in `tools/send_message_tool.py` (lines 83-105) treats **timeout errors as non-retryable**, causing messages to be lost when Telegram occasionally times out.

## Code (lines 91-93)
```python
text = str(exc).lower()
if "timed out" in text or "timeout" in text:
    return None  # ← marked as non-retryable
```

## Impact
- All scenarios using `send_message` tool to send Telegram messages
- Especially cron-scheduled messages (no human intervention to fix)
- Messages lost with no fallback mechanism

## Suggested Fix
Align with 502/503/504 logic — timeout should also use exponential backoff:

```python
if "timed out" in text or "timeout" in text:
    return float(2 ** attempt)  # Consistent with 502/503/504
```

## Reproduction
1. Simulate Telegram API temporarily unresponsive (e.g., brief firewall block)
2. Send message (any length)
3. Observe: fails once then gives up, no retry

## Environment
- hermes-agent version: M3
- Affected versions: All versions where timeout is treated as non-retryable

## Fix Verification
KAKACO has verified the fix works locally:
- Before fix: Telegram occasional timeout → message lost
- After fix: 3 retries with exponential backoff (2/4/8s) → significantly improved delivery rate

## Pull Request
We have a PR ready and can submit it after this issue is acknowledged.

issues.body:
## Bug Description

Cron jobs and `send_message` tool calls fail to deliver messages to Telegram on networks where `api.telegram.org` is blocked (e.g., Russia), while the gateway's live Telegram adapter works fine.

## Root Cause

The gateway's Telegram adapter (`gateway/platforms/telegram.py`) creates its `Bot` with a custom `HTTPXRequest` that uses `TelegramFallbackTransport` — this transport resolves `api.telegram.org` via DNS-over-HTTPS (Google/Cloudflare DoH) and falls back to hardcoded IPs like `149.154.167.220` when the system DNS returns a blocked IP.

However, `tools/send_message_tool.py` → `_send_telegram()` (line ~700) creates `Bot(token=token)` with the **default** `HTTPXRequest`, bypassing all fallback logic:

```python
# gateway/platforms/telegram.py — WORKS
from telegram.request import HTTPXRequest
# ... TelegramFallbackTransport injected into HTTPXRequest

# tools/send_message_tool.py — FAILS
from telegram import Bot
bot = Bot(token=token)  # default transport, no fallback
```

## Impact

- Cron jobs with `deliver: "telegram:CHAT_ID"` timeout on `api.telegram.org:443`
- `send_message` tool calls from agents also fail on blocked networks
- Users see `curl: (28) Connection timed out` or `httpx.ConnectTimeout` in logs
- Gateway continues to work because it uses the fallback transport

## Expected Behavior

`send_message_tool._send_telegram` should use the same `TelegramFallbackTransport` as the gateway adapter, ensuring consistent delivery regardless of network conditions.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Run Hermes on a network where `api.telegram.org` is blocked
2. Create a cron job with `deliver: "telegram:CHAT_ID"`
3. Job executes but delivery fails with connection timeout
4. Meanwhile, gateway-originated messages work fine

## Suggested Fix

Make `_send_telegram` create `Bot` with the same custom `HTTPXRequest` that the gateway uses, or refactor to share a single `create_telegram_bot()` helper between gateway and `send_message_tool`.

## Environment

- Hermes Agent: latest main (May 2026)
- Platform: Telegram
- Network: `api.telegram.org` blocked at DNS level

## Related Code

- `gateway/platforms/telegram_network.py` — `TelegramFallbackTransport`, `discover_fallback_ips()`
- `gateway/platforms/telegram.py` — gateway adapter with custom `HTTPXRequest`
- `tools/send_message_tool.py` — `_send_telegram()` line ~700
- `cron/scheduler.py` — `_deliver_output()` calls `_send_to_platform` → `_send_telegram`

issues.body:
### Bug Description

The standalone Telegram send lane — `tools/send_message_senders.py::_telegram_bot`, used when the live gateway adapter can't deliver (cron's "falling back to standalone", or `send_message` with no running gateway) — builds its `Bot` without any timeouts:

```python
# tools/send_message_senders.py (main @ 085f562)
return Bot(token=token, request=HTTPXRequest(proxy=proxy), get_updates_request=HTTPXRequest(proxy=proxy))
...
return Bot(token=token)   # no-proxy path
```

https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/blob/085f562af53a6fedadac3681e2c498fc71316132/tools/send_message_senders.py#L106-L120

So it runs on python-telegram-bot's `HTTPXRequest` defaults (connect 5s / read 5s / write 5s / pool 1s) and ignores `HERMES_TELEGRAM_HTTP_CONNECT_TIMEOUT` / `_READ_TIMEOUT` / `_WRITE_TIMEOUT` / `_POOL_TIMEOUT`. The live adapter does honour them (defaults 10s / 20s / 20s / 8s):

https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/blob/085f562af53a6fedadac3681e2c498fc71316132/plugins/platforms/telegram/adapter.py#L2949-L2952

The fallback lane only runs once the primary lane has already failed, i.e. when the route is already degraded, yet it gets the shortest budget of all, and a user who raised these timeouts (e.g. because Telegram is only reachable through a slow proxy) gets no effect on it.

### Steps to Reproduce

1. Run the gateway with Telegram behind an HTTP proxy (`HTTPS_PROXY` / `TELEGRAM_PROXY`) and set e.g. `HERMES_TELEGRAM_HTTP_CONNECT_TIMEOUT=20`, `HERMES_TELEGRAM_HTTP_READ_TIMEOUT=25`.
2. Have a cron job with `deliver: telegram`.
3. Let the live adapter delivery fail (a flapping proxy route is enough) so the scheduler logs `live adapter delivery ... failed: ..., falling back to standalone`.
4. Watch the standalone send: it gives up after ~5s regardless of the configured timeouts.

### Expected Behavior

The standalone lane uses the same `HERMES_TELEGRAM_HTTP_*` timeouts (and the same defaults) as the live adapter, on both the proxy and no-proxy paths.

### Actual Behavior

The standalone lane times out on PTB's 5s defaults. Redacted excerpt (`agent.log`, CST); the live lane had a 20s connect budget and the standalone lane gave up 5.7s later:

```
07:30:38,605 WARNING cron.scheduler: Job '207b8c3e4e42': live adapter delivery to telegram:<chat_id> failed: Timed out, falling back to standalone
07:30:38,621 INFO tools.send_message_tool: send_message: standalone Telegram send routed through proxy http://<user>:<password>@127.0.0.1:7890
07:30:44,349 ERROR cron.scheduler: Job '207b8c3e4e42': delivery error: Telegram send failed: Timed out (target telegram:<chat_id>)
```

To be fair about impact: on that run the live lane had also just timed out, so a longer budget would not certainly have saved the delivery. The issue is that the configured timeouts are silently not applied to this lane.

### Affected Component

Gateway (Telegram/Discord/Slack/WhatsApp), Tools (terminal, file ops, web, code execution, etc.)

### Messaging Platform

Telegram

### Debug Report

Not attached: `hermes debug share` uploads config and recent logs, and on this host those contain proxy credentials and private chat content. The relevant log lines are inlined above (redacted), and I can provide more targeted excerpts on request.

### Operating System

Debian 12 (Docker container, `--network host`) on ImmortalWrt 25.12 x86_64

### Python Version

3.14.9 (Hermes-managed runtime)

### Hermes Version

v0.22.5 (bf0203a794), stable channel

### Root Cause Analysis

`_telegram_bot()` constructs `HTTPXRequest(proxy=proxy)` / `Bot(token=token)` without passing `connect_timeout` / `read_timeout` / `write_timeout` / `pool_timeout`, while the adapter builds its requests from `env_float("HERMES_TELEGRAM_HTTP_*", ...)`. The two lanes have drifted apart.

### Proposed Fix

Build the standalone requests from the same env vars and defaults as the adapter, ideally through one shared helper so the two lanes can't drift again. Apply it to the no-proxy `Bot(token=token)` branch too, which currently gets PTB defaults as well. I've applied exactly that as a local patch (both requests get `connect_timeout` / `read_timeout` / `write_timeout` / `pool_timeout` from `HERMES_TELEGRAM_HTTP_*`, falling back to 10 / 20 / 20 / 8). The standalone lane hasn't fired since, so it's untested beyond that.

**Side note, same function:** `logger.info("send_message: standalone Telegram send routed through proxy %s", proxy)` writes the full proxy URL, **including `user:password`**, to `agent.log`; `security.redact_secrets: true` doesn't catch it. Logging the proxy with credentials stripped (scheme://host:port) would fix it.

Possibly related: #136412 (live-adapter send path: per-path connect budget vs. whole-send deadline). That issue is about the adapter; this one is about the separate standalone lane.

issues.body:
# [Bug]: Telegram uploads >~15 MB always fail with TimedOut — `HERMES_TELEGRAM_HTTP_WRITE_TIMEOUT` has no effect on media uploads

## Summary

The Telegram adapter builds its PTB `HTTPXRequest` with `connect/read/write/pool` timeouts (env-overridable via `HERMES_TELEGRAM_HTTP_*`), but python-telegram-bot uses a **separate `media_write_timeout` parameter for file-upload endpoints** (`sendDocument`, `sendPhoto`, `sendMediaGroup`, …), defaulting to **20 s** (PTB 22.6). The adapter never sets it, so:

- Any document/photo upload that takes longer than 20 s fails with `telegram.error.TimedOut`, regardless of `HERMES_TELEGRAM_HTTP_WRITE_TIMEOUT`.
- On a typical residential uplink (~5 Mbit/s) that's a hard ceiling of roughly **~12 MB**, far below Telegram's 50 MB bot document limit.
- The user-visible failure is the generic "⚠️ Couldn't deliver the file attachment (…)", which reads as a size limit and sends users hunting in the wrong direction.

## Reproduction

Ask the agent to send a ~36 MB PNG on a connection where the upload takes >20 s. Gateway log shows the photo path, media-group path, and document fallback each dying at exactly +20 s:

```
18:49:13 INFO  [Telegram] Sending media group of 1 photo(s) (chunk 1/1)
18:49:33 WARN  [Telegram] send_media_group failed (chunk 1/1), falling back to per-image: Timed out
18:49:53 WARN  [Telegram] Failed to send Telegram local image as photo, trying document fallback: Timed out
18:50:13 WARN  [Telegram] Failed to send document: Timed out
18:50:13 WARN  [Telegram] send_document fallback: native file send unavailable for /…/live-results….png
```

Setting `HERMES_TELEGRAM_HTTP_WRITE_TIMEOUT=180` changes nothing (verified; the three 20 s intervals above were logged *with* that override active).

## Fix (verified)

Add `media_write_timeout` to the adapter's `request_kwargs` (it is splatted into every `HTTPXRequest(...)` construction site, so one key covers the proxy/direct/fallback-IP branches):

```python
                "write_timeout": _env_float("HERMES_TELEGRAM_HTTP_WRITE_TIMEOUT", 20.0),
                # PTB uses a SEPARATE media_write_timeout for file-upload
                # endpoints (sendDocument/sendPhoto/send_media_group). Without
                # it, large uploads die at PTB's 20s default no matter what
                # write_timeout is set to (a 36MB PNG needs ~30-120s upstream).
                "media_write_timeout": _env_float("HERMES_TELEGRAM_HTTP_MEDIA_WRITE_TIMEOUT", 180.0),
```

With this patch the same 36 MB PNG uploads successfully (measured 62 s — 3× over the old cap, comfortably inside 180 s). A raised default is appropriate here: the knob only bounds a single in-flight upload, and 20 s is below what Telegram's own 50 MB document limit implies users will attempt.

Environment: hermes-agent v0.18.2 @ 5e849942, python-telegram-bot 22.6, macOS.

labels.name: type/bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.description: Telegram bot adapter

issues.body:
## Bug Description

The standalone `send_message` tool (`tools/send_message_tool.py`, function `_send_telegram`) constructs its `Bot` instance without honoring the custom Telegram Bot API `base_url` that the gateway adapter already supports via `telegram.extra.base_url`.

As a result, **proactive / cron-triggered sends bypass the configured self-hosted Bot API server and go directly to `api.telegram.org`** — which times out in regions/networks where `api.telegram.org` is blocked, even though the gateway's *interactive* replies work fine through `base_url`.

This is asymmetric with the in-gateway adapter (`gateway/platforms/telegram.py`), which correctly applies `extra.base_url` via `builder.base_url(...)`. The send-message tool path honors `TELEGRAM_PROXY` (see the comment at the proxy block) but not `base_url`.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Run the gateway in a network where `api.telegram.org` is **blocked**, with a self-hosted Telegram Bot API server reachable at e.g. `https://botapi.example.com:8443`.

2. Configure the gateway adapter to use it:
   ```yaml
   platforms:
     telegram:
       extra:
         base_url: "https://botapi.example.com:8443/bot"
         base_file_url: "https://botapi.example.com:8443/file/bot"
   ```

3. Interactive replies work (gateway adapter honors `base_url`). ✅

4. Trigger a **proactive** send — a cron job, or any agent use of the `send_message` tool to a Telegram chat.

5. Observe the send fail:
   ```
   Tool send_message returned error: {"error": "Telegram send failed: Timed out"}
   ```
   because `_send_telegram` connects to `api.telegram.org` directly.

## Root Cause

In `tools/send_message_tool.py`, `_send_telegram()` builds the bot as:

```python
if _tg_proxy:
    bot = Bot(token=token, request=HTTPXRequest(proxy=_tg_proxy), ...)
else:
    bot = Bot(token=token)        # <-- always api.telegram.org; base_url never applied
```

There is no path that reads the configured `base_url` (neither from `platforms.telegram.extra.base_url` nor from an env var), unlike the gateway adapter which calls `builder.base_url(custom_base_url)`.

## Expected Behavior

When a custom Telegram Bot API `base_url` is configured, the standalone `send_message` tool should route through it too — so proactive/cron sends behave the same as interactive gateway replies. This is the documented "local Bot API server" pattern for blocked-region deployments.

## Suggested Fix

Read a base URL (env var, mirroring how the gateway resolves it) and pass it to `Bot(base_url=...)`. Minimal, additive, and falls through to existing behavior when unset:

```python
_tg_base_url = os.getenv("TELEGRAM_BOT_API_BASE_URL", "").strip()
if _tg_proxy:
    ...  # unchanged
elif _tg_base_url:
    logger.info("send_message: standalone Telegram send via custom Bot API base URL %s", _tg_base_url)
    bot = Bot(token=token, base_url=_tg_base_url)
else:
    bot = Bot(token=token)
```

Ideally the value would also be sourced from `platforms.telegram.extra.base_url` so a single config key drives both the gateway and the tool (no separate env var needed). Happy to open a PR — we run this patch in production today.

## Related

- #47188 / PR #47192 — the *gateway*-side `base_url` vs proxy interaction. This issue is the **`send_message` tool** counterpart, which is not covered there.
- #26359 — `telegram.extra.base_url` propagation in `gateway/config.py`.

## Environment

- Hermes built from tag `v2026.6.5` (gap also present on current `main`, `tools/send_message_tool.py` line ~1011/1013).
- Self-hosted `telegram-bot-api` server; `api.telegram.org` blocked at the network level.

labels.name: tool/file

labels.name: area/profiles

issues.body:
### Summary
In a multiplexed gateway, "Checkpoint prune tick" is the only per-profile housekeeping chore that is not wrapped in `profile_scoped_chore`. `auto_prune_from_config()` therefore reads the launch home's config and checkpoint base only. The stores of served profiles are never pruned, even with `checkpoints.auto_prune: true` in their own config.

### Environment
- Hermes Agent v0.22.5+1711.g9b904dc (2026.9.24), upstream 9b904dcc; macOS 26 (Darwin 25.6, arm64); desktop app.
- One gateway process, launched from `~/.hermes`, serves profile `desktop-local` and eleven others. The launch home has `checkpoints.enabled: false` and no `~/.hermes/checkpoints`.
- `desktop-local` config: `checkpoints.enabled: true`, `auto_prune: true`, `max_total_size_mb: 500`, `min_interval_hours: 24`.

### What happened
- `~/.hermes/profiles/desktop-local/checkpoints/.last_prune` was last written on 2026-10-13. The store was not pruned after that.
- The store grew to 2.8 GB against the 500 MB cap. 1.93 GiB of it were three `tmp_pack_*` files that `clear_stale_tmp_packs` (called from prune) would have removed. `.gc-pending` stays set, because the gc that the take path defers "to the next prune" never runs.
- After I deleted the three tmp packs, a manual `hermes -p desktop-local checkpoints prune --retention-days 3650 --keep-orphans --max-size-mb 0` ran in 18.7 s and reclaimed 306 MB.

### Cause
`gateway/run.py:4536`:

```python
(1, "Checkpoint prune tick", _housekeeping_checkpoint_prune)]
```

The other per-profile chores are scoped, for example `gateway/run.py:4522`:

```python
(60, "Curator tick", profile_scoped_chore(runner, _housekeeping_curator)),
```

Unscoped, `auto_prune_from_config()` (`tools/checkpoint_maintenance.py:425`) loads the launch home's config, and `_resolve_checkpoint_base()` (`tools/checkpoint_manager.py:78`) returns the launch home's base. Here that base does not exist, so the call returns before it touches any store.

### Suggested fix
Scope it like the other per-profile chores:

```python
(1, "Checkpoint prune tick", profile_scoped_chore(runner, _housekeeping_checkpoint_prune)),
```

### Workaround
Run `hermes -p <profile> checkpoints prune ...` daily from launchd or cron.

issues.title: [Bug]: assistant narration before a tool call renders twice (both live stream and history reload)
issues.body:
### Bug Description

When an assistant turn produces prose before its first tool call (a short “narration” line like “Let me check that…”, followed immediately by a tool_call), that narration text can render twice in the transcript: once as a standalone assistant bubble and once again folded into the tool bubble / final answer group.

The duplication appears in two independent paths:

Live streaming — while the turn is still running, the narration line is painted twice as the tool result arrives.
History reload / re-hydration — after closing and reopening the session (or paging back), the same narration is painted twice.
The data layer is correct: the narration text exists once in state.db (a single assistant row carrying both the narration content and a non-empty tool_calls array). The duplication is purely in the desktop front-end rendering pipeline.

This is a display-only defect — the underlying data and functionality are correct; the same sentence is just drawn twice.

### Steps to Reproduce

Open the desktop app, start a new session.
Send a message that causes the agent to write a short narration line first, then call a tool (e.g. “check the current time for me” — the model replies “Sure, let me check…” and then invokes the terminal/clock tool).
Observe the live stream: the narration line may already appear twice as the tool result comes back.
Close the app, reopen the session (history reload) — the narration line is painted twice again.
Minimal repro shape (one assistant row):

role = assistant
content = a short narration sentence (non-empty)
tool_calls = non-empty array (one or more tool calls)

### Expected Behavior

The narration sentence renders once, followed by the folded tool call and the final answer.

### Actual Behavior

The narration sentence renders twice.

### Affected Component

Agent Core (conversation loop, context compression, memory)

### Messaging Platform (if gateway-related)

N/A (CLI only)

### Debug Report

```shell

Steps to Reproduce

Send a message that causes the agent to write a short narration line first, then call a tool (e.g. “check the current time for me” — the model replies “Sure, let me check…” and then invokes the terminal/clock tool).
Observe the live stream: the narration line may already appear twice as the tool result comes back.
Close the app, reopen the session (history reload) — the narration line is painted twice again.
Minimal repro shape (one assistant row):

role = assistant
content = a short narration sentence (non-empty)
tool_calls = non-empty array (one or more tool calls)
Expected Behavior

The narration sentence renders once, followed by the folded tool call and the final answer.

Actual Behavior

The narration sentence renders twice.

Affected Component

Agent Core (conversation loop, context compression, memory)
Other (desktop front-end transcript rendering)
Messaging Platform (if gateway-related)

N/A (CLI only)
Operating System

macOS (Apple Silicon)

Hermes Version

v0.23.0+canary.20261108T064411Z-210-g022a14437b (reproduced on a fresh install that already includes the 10-27/11-03 de-dup fixes below)

Root Cause Analysis

The duplication lives in the desktop transcript rendering pipeline, specifically in how a “narration + tool_call” assistant row survives both the hydration fold and the backfill/reconciliation merge.

Relevant code paths (all under apps/desktop/src):

lib/chat-messages/hydration.ts — toChatMessages(). When an assistant row has prose and non-empty tool_calls, the code (around the foldIntoToolBubble / isToolOnlyAssistant logic) folds the row’s text part and its tool-call part into a shared tool bubble. The narration text part can end up emitted both as part of the folded bubble and as a separate assistant text bubble, because the fold decision keys off parts.some(part => part.type === 'tool-call') while the narration text is also pushed as a normal assistantTextPart.

lib/chat-messages/parts.ts — dedupeRepeatedTextInParts() and dedupeRepeatedRowText(). These only de-duplicate within a single message’s part list, and dedupeRepeatedRowText only operates when part.sourceRowId !== undefined. The “narration + tool_call across a fold boundary” duplication spans two message objects, which these helpers never compare, so the duplicate survives.

app/chat/transcript-backfill.ts — mergeOlderTranscriptPage() / mergeOverlappingTail(). The module comment explicitly notes the historical failure mode: “Message-level matching alone misses that shared final row and appends the fold next to the settled live bubble, so the same reply renders twice (#123801)”. A narration row folded into a tool bubble is addressed by its first source row; when a refreshed/older page re-emits that fold, the partRowAnchor / covered matching can fail to recognize the narration as already-held when it carries a tool_call, appending a second copy.

app/chat/runtime-repository.ts — de-dupes by message.id via seenIds. But hydration builds message.id as a synthetic ${timestamp}-${index}-${role} string, and the two rendering paths can synthesize different ids for the same underlying row, so the seenIds guard does not catch the duplicate.

Historical context: the upstream already landed multiple fixes for this general class over recent months (e.g. 43c66b85bb "one reply renders once per turn, whichever path delivered it", the transcript-receipt-turns.ts module, segment-identity.ts wire-stamp de-dup for live stream re-sends). The “prose narration + tool_call” shape appears to be a remaining un-covered case, which is why it still reproduces on a build that contains all of those fixes.

Proposed Fix

Make the narration-vs-fold identity consistent across the three layers so the same underlying assistant row is always folded/rendered exactly once:

In hydration.ts, when folding a “prose + tool_call” row into an existing tool bubble, do not also emit the narration text as a standalone bubble — the fold must be the single owner of that text (or vice versa).
In backfill.ts, extend the “already held” matching (covered / partRowAnchor) to recognize a folded narration row by its source row id even when the fold carries tool parts, so a refreshed page cannot append a second copy of the same narration.
Optionally, make dedupeRepeatedTextInParts operate across the fold boundary (the last text before a tool-call vs the duplicate text after the fold) instead of only within one message.
I’m happy to attempt a PR if a maintainer can confirm which of the three layers is the intended fix locus (I suspect #1 + #2 together are the minimal correct fix).
```

issues.title: Desktop: "Could not check default's Bot Chat registry (not_found)" after switching to a remote connection; persists until app restart
issues.body:
**Version:** Hermes Agent v0.23.0 (2026.9.24) stable, Windows 11, Desktop win-unpacked build.

**What happened**
1. Switched the active bot to a remote connection's profile (strixly-server / bazaar), then back to the local default profile. The log shows the route switching correctly:
   ```
   [gateway-route] active key=conn:strixly-server::bazaar via=secondary conn=strixly-server profile=bazaar
   [gateway-route] active key=default via=primary conn=local profile=default
   [gateway-route] published connection=local
   ```
2. A few minutes later the desktop restarted all local profile backends at once (about 15 helper processes spawned in the same second, shortly after saving Passwords & Logins settings).
3. From then on, clicking the local default bot shows the toast "Could not open ATLAS's chat. Try again", details: `Could not check default's Bot Chat registry (not_found) — not starting a new chat`. Retrying never recovers. desktop.log stops writing at the same time.
4. Closing the app, waiting about 20 s and reopening fixes it. The gateway itself stayed healthy throughout (answering chats and running cron).

**Expected:** after a backend pool restart, the roster click re-resolves the local default backend (or retries until warm), instead of failing with `not_found` until a full app restart.

**Notes:** looks related to the fail-closed path in `apps/desktop/src/plugins/hermes-bots/canonical-chat.ts` `findExistingCanonicalChat` (#105104, #98383). Fail-closed is right, but the `not_found` never clears without restarting the app.
