issues.body:
### Bug Description

In a bot DM with Telegram's native topics ("Threads", `getMe → has_topics_enabled: true`), several outbound paths build send metadata carrying only `thread_id` — never `direct_messages_topic_id`. The adapter then routes forum-style via `message_thread_id`, which Bot API rejects for native DM topics with **"message thread not found"**. Delivery degrades to a thread-less DM or is lost, and the retry ladder can even prune the topic binding as "stale" — after which topic recovery keeps steering traffic away from the topic.

Even when metadata does pair a native direct-topic id equal to the lane thread id (the `telegram_dm_topic_reply_fallback` + reply-anchor path), `_thread_kwargs_for_send` still prefers `message_thread_id`, so live replies in native DM topics are rejected and leave the topic.

Impact on our instance over ~1.5 h (2026-10-12): 15 × `Send failed: Message thread not found — trying plain-text fallback`, 14 × `Fallback send also failed`, 7 × `Pruned stale Telegram DM topic binding (Bot API: thread not found)` — including lost `/new` confirmations and replies. Still present on `main @ 427d605d498`.

### Steps to Reproduce

1. Bot DM with topics enabled (BotFather "Threads"), gateway on polling.
2. Trigger a reply from a native DM topic — or any synthetic send (startup recovery, watcher notification, voice-echo follow-up, cron route, `send_message` tool).
3. Bot API rejects the send: `Bad Request: message thread not found`.

API-level probe on the same chat/topic:

- `sendMessage` with `message_thread_id=<topic>` → 400 `message thread not found`
- `sendMessage` with `direct_messages_topic_id=<topic>` → delivered

### Expected Behavior

Replies and synthetic sends land in the native DM topic lane they target.

### Actual Behavior

Send rejected with `message thread not found`; degraded to a thread-less DM (or dropped); the topic binding may be pruned as stale afterwards.

### Affected Component

Gateway (Telegram/Discord/Slack/WhatsApp)

### Messaging Platform

Telegram

### Version / OS

- Hermes `v0.21.7+241.g3b63f7b` (2026-10-12); still present on `main @ 427d605d498`
- Fedora Linux (kernel 7.2.9), Python 3.14, Telegram polling mode

### Additional context

The affected send paths each construct `{"thread_id": ...}` metadata: `gateway/delivery.py` (retry path), `gateway/run_startup.py` (recovery + obligation sends), `gateway/run_notifications.py` (watcher delivery), `gateway/run_turn.py` (voice-echo follow-ups), `tools/send_message_tool.py`, `cron/scheduler_delivery.py`.

A fix is up as a PR (see linked PR): routes native DM-topic sends via `direct_messages_topic_id` on all of those paths; same-id direct ids no longer fall through to `message_thread_id`. Anchor-less synthetic sends keep their documented `message_thread_id` preference, so #87051 behavior is unaffected. Unit tests added (proven red on the base); verified live on the reporting instance.

issues.body:
## Summary
Telegram private-topic retry paths can discard an explicitly selected destination. This is a reproduced loss of outbound routing constraints, NOT proof that a particular final reply landed in a different topic.

Inspected checkout: `0aa764feddf00aed631019763ef777d38faf4335` (macOS; local fix not yet submitted as a PR).

## Offline reproductions (mocked Bot API; no token/network)
Synthetic example: positive private `chat_id=123`, selected `message_thread_id=20197`, reply anchor `462`, metadata `{"thread_id":"20197", "telegram_dm_topic_reply_fallback":true}`.

1. Native media: inject `BadRequest("Message to be replied not found")` on the first request. `_send_with_dm_topic_reply_anchor_retry` retries with no reply anchor AND no topic-routing keys.
2. Long-message overflow: inject `BadRequest("Reply message not found")`. `_send_overflow_continuation` replaces the private-topic routing kwargs with `{}` and removes the anchor.
3. Control messages: inject `BadRequest("Message thread not found")`. `_send_message_with_thread_fallback` removes `message_thread_id` but retains `reply_to_message_id`. An anchor from another topic can then override the intended destination; actual Telegram placement remains conditional on API behavior and anchor ownership.

## Source (pre-patch line numbers)
`plugins/platforms/telegram/adapter.py`:
- `_should_retry_without_dm_topic_reply_anchor` / `_send_with_dm_topic_reply_anchor_retry`, ~1149–1192: media retries remove both topic-routing keys; topic-routing rejection can also cause an unscoped retry.
- `_send_overflow_continuation`, ~3976–3988: private-topic retry substitutes empty routing kwargs.
- `_send_message_with_thread_fallback`, ~4128–4138: control retry removes the thread but retains the anchor.

Existing `tests/gateway/test_telegram_thread_fallback.py` tests explicitly expect this unsafe routing loss, including `test_native_media_dm_topic_reply_not_found_retry_drops_thread_id` and the animation/media-group/upload equivalents. Change the retry assertion from topic absent to `call_log[1]["message_thread_id"] == 20197` (upload uses the third call) to expose it.

## Expected behavior / local fix
Drop only the deleted reply anchor, preserving effective topic kwargs on media and overflow retries. For rejected explicit PRIVATE-topic destinations, fail closed rather than silently sending to chat root or routing solely by an old anchor. Keep non-private behavior separate. Do not replace `message_thread_id` with `direct_messages_topic_id`; they can target different Telegram lanes.

Match both deleted-anchor error strings consistently (`Message to be replied not found`, `Reply message not found`).

Local regressions cover overflow errors with both strings and private control-message thread rejection, plus updated media assertions.

Verified command:
```
scripts/run_tests.sh tests/gateway/test_telegram_thread_fallback.py -k 'not gateway_runner_busy_ack' -q
```
**22 passed, 0 failed** after the local fix. `git diff --check` passes. The excluded gateway-runner busy-ack case is not claimed as validated.

## Caveat / related issue
Ordinary final-text reply misrouting has not been established by this reproduction. The independent cross-topic status-cache bug is tracked in #92210; it should not be conflated with this retry defect. No credentials/private logs are included; identifiers above are synthetic/test values.

issues.body:
### Bug Description

When a user interacts with Hermes inside a Telegram DM Topic (which uses Hermes's telegram_dm_topic_reply_fallback feature to simulate topics via reply anchors), text messages are routed correctly to the topic, but media messages (such as screenshots, images, and documents) are erroneously dropped into the root DM chat (visible as "All Chats" only) instead of staying within the topic thread.

Root Cause The Telegram Bot API does not support the message_thread_id parameter inside Private Chats (DMs) and will throw a BadRequest: message thread not found error if it is provided.

In gateway/platforms/telegram.py, the send method for standard text messages contained an explicit safeguard (if used_thread_fallback...) that stripped message_thread_id before sending, relying solely on reply_to_message_id to route the text message to the correct simulated topic.

However, media sending methods (such as send_multiple_images, send_image_file, send_document) did not have this safeguard. As a result:

Media methods attempted to send with a message_thread_id.
The Telegram Bot API rejected the request with a BadRequest.
Hermes's internal retry mechanism (_send_with_dm_topic_reply_anchor_retry) caught the exception and attempted to recover by stripping both message_thread_id and the reply_to_message_id anchor.
The media was then successfully resent, but without its reply anchor, causing it to drop out of the topic chain and land in the root chat.
Resolution Centralized the thread ID omission logic directly inside the _thread_kwargs_for_send helper method so that it applies globally across all message types.



### Steps to Reproduce

To test this and verify the bug has been fixed, follow these steps:

Open your Telegram Direct Message (Private Chat) with Hermes.
Open any specific topic/thread (using a client that supports DM topics like Nagram, or via Hermes's reply-chain threads).
Send a command inside that specific topic that generates media, such as asking Hermes to take a /screenshot or generate an image.
Wait for Hermes to respond with the media.

### Expected Behavior

Before the fix (The Bug): Hermes sends the screenshot, but because of the internal error, it loses its topic mapping. You receive it, but it shows up disconnected in your main "All Chats" view rather than inside the topic where you asked for it.
After the fix (Expected): Hermes sends the screenshot and it appears neatly as a direct reply inside the specific topic where you requested it, keeping your conversation history clean and organized.

### Actual Behavior

Hermes sends the screenshot, but because of the internal error, it loses its topic mapping. You receive it, but it shows up disconnected in your main "All Chats" view rather than inside the topic where you asked for it.

### Affected Component

Gateway (Telegram/Discord/Slack/WhatsApp)

```

### Root Cause Analysis (optional)

### Proposed Fix (optional)

Modified the return statement for the telegram_dm_topic_reply_fallback block to return {"message_thread_id": None} instead of attempting to parse the thread_id.

issues.body:
## Bug Description

When DM topics are enabled in a private Telegram chat (via `/topic`) and the user later **disables forum topics in the Telegram client** (chat settings), the gateway permanently stops delivering replies to that chat. Every outbound send fails with `Message thread not found`, and even the plain-text fallback fails with the same error. The bot keeps processing messages and producing answers, but nothing is delivered until the user re-enables topics (or manually edits state.db).

This is distinct from #31501 (user deletes a *topic*): here the user changes a *chat-level* setting, and the #31501 prune path is never reached because the adapter's `private_dm_topic_send` branch refuses to fall back and never prunes.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. DM the bot in a private Telegram chat and enable topics with `/topic`.
2. Several conversations later, open chat settings in the Telegram client and disable "Topics" (forum mode) for the chat. (No Hermes command involved — this is a client-side chat setting.)
3. Send a message in the (now forum-less) chat.
4. The agent processes the message, but no reply ever arrives.
5. `errors.log` fills with:
   ```
   [Telegram] Send failed: Message thread not found — trying plain-text fallback
   [Telegram] Fallback send also failed: Message thread not found
   ```
6. Re-enabling topics in the client restores delivery (new topic lanes get bound again).

## Expected Behavior

- Replies should deliver to the chat (lobby/General) when the chat is no longer a forum.
- At minimum, the gateway should notice the capability change (chat is no longer a forum), prune the dead bindings, and stop steering inbound messages to the deleted topic lanes — the same cleanup the #31501 fix performs for a deleted *topic*.
- The "plain-text fallback" in `gateway/platforms/base.py` should actually send without `message_thread_id`, since that is the only difference between it and the failed send.

## Actual Behavior

- 100% of outbound sends fail with `Message thread not found` (repeated every message, observed over ~4 hours: 09:20, 09:21, 12:29, 13:16).
- `telegram_dm_topic_mode` stays `enabled=1` with stale `has_topics_enabled=1` (capability only re-checked when the user runs `/topic`).
- `telegram_dm_topic_bindings` rows for the deleted lanes are never pruned.
- `sessions.json` session origins still carry `thread_id: "1057"/"1060"/"1079"/"1084"` for the chat, so recovery keeps routing every inbound message back into a deleted lane.

## Affected Component / Platform

- Gateway — `gateway/run.py` (topic-thread recovery), `gateway/platforms/base.py` (plain-text fallback)
- Telegram adapter — `plugins/platforms/telegram/adapter.py` (`send` thread-not-found branch)

## Debug Report

`hermes debug share --local` dump (redacted version available on request):

```
version:          0.20.5 [41447a6d] (2026-08-25)
os:               Linux 6.18.33.1-microsoft-standard-WSL2 x86_64
python:           3.11.16
openai_sdk:       2.24.0
profile:          default
hermes_home:      ~/.hermes
gateway:          running (systemd (user))
platforms:        telegram, homeassistant
```

## Operating System

WSL2 (Linux 6.18.33.1-microsoft-standard-WSL2 x86_64) on Windows

## Python Version

3.11.16

## Hermes Version

0.20.5 (upstream 365cbc24, local 41447a6d)

## Additional Logs / Traceback

`~/.hermes/logs/errors.log` (2026-08-26):

```
09:20:23,192 WARNING gateway.platforms.base: [Telegram] Send failed: Message thread not found — trying plain-text fallback
09:20:23,275 ERROR   gateway.platforms.base: [Telegram] Fallback send also failed: Message thread not found
09:21:52,946 WARNING gateway.platforms.base: [Telegram] Send failed: Message thread not found — trying plain-text fallback
09:21:53,000 ERROR   gateway.platforms.base: [Telegram] Fallback send also failed: Message thread not found
12:29:21,179 WARNING gateway.platforms.base: [Telegram] Send failed: Message thread not found — trying plain-text fallback
12:29:21,217 ERROR   gateway.platforms.base: [Telegram] Fallback send also failed: Message thread not found
13:16:01,958 WARNING gateway.platforms.base: [Telegram] Send failed: Message thread not found — trying plain-text fallback
13:16:01,995 ERROR   gateway.platforms.base: [Telegram] Fallback send also failed: Message thread not found
```

Live state.db rows after the incident (chat `8904680910`):

```
telegram_dm_topic_mode:
  enabled=1, has_topics_enabled=1, allows_users_to_create_topics=1
  capability_checked_at=1787743059  # 2026-08-25 19:57 — before the client-side disable

telegram_dm_topic_bindings (never pruned):
  thread_id=1060  session_key=agent:main:telegram:dm:8904680910:1060
  thread_id=1084  session_key=agent:main:telegram:dm:8904680910:1084

sessions.json origin thread_ids: 1057, 1060, 1079, 1084 (all deleted lanes)
```

Note the *adapter-level* `Thread not found` fallback log lines (e.g. `retrying without message_thread_id` from #31501) never appear in the log — the adapter's send loop never reaches that branch for this case.

## Root Cause Analysis

1. **Recovery keeps steering to dead lanes.** `GatewayRunner._recover_telegram_topic_thread_id` (gateway/run.py) walks `telegram_dm_topic_bindings` newest-first on every lobby-shaped inbound and redirects it to the bound lane, whose session origin (`sessions.json`) carries the dead `thread_id`. All subsequent sends are addressed to `message_thread_id=<dead lane>` → Bot API `Message thread not found`.

2. **The #31501 prune is unreachable for DM-topic sends.** In `TelegramAdapter.send` (plugins/platforms/telegram/adapter.py ~line 5356), the `Thread not found` handler short-circuits for DM-topic sends *before* the retry/prune path:
   ```python
   if self._is_thread_not_found_error(send_err) and effective_thread_id is not None:
       if private_dm_topic_send or (metadata and metadata.get("telegram_dm_topic_created_for_send")):
           return SendResult(success=False, error=str(send_err), retryable=False)
       # ... the #31501 retry-without-thread + _prune_stale_dm_topic_binding path ...
   ```
   The "fail loud" branch is intentional for *live replies* (stay in the requested topic lane), but when the thread is **permanently** gone it means: no plain-send fallback, no prune, topic mode never disabled → permanently broken delivery.

3. **The base-level plain-text fallback re-sends the same thread id.** `gateway/platforms/base.py` (~line 5612) retries with `content="(Response formatting failed, plain text:)..."` but passes the same `metadata`, which still carries the thread id — so the fallback deterministically fails with the identical error (matches the log pair above).

4. **Capability flag goes stale and is never consulted on send.** `has_topics_enabled` is only refreshed when the user runs `/topic` (gateway/slash_commands.py ~line 4662). Nothing in the inbound/send path re-validates that the chat is still a forum, so the client-side disable is invisible to the gateway until the next `/topic` invocation.

## Proposed Fix

1. In the adapter's `private_dm_topic_send` thread-not-found branch, treat *repeated/confirmed* "Thread not found" (after the existing one-shot transient retry) as a dead lane: call `_prune_stale_dm_topic_binding()` and fall through to a plain send (drop `message_thread_id`) instead of returning `retryable=False` forever. Failing loud is fine for a missing *reply anchor*, but not for a chat that no longer has forums.
2. Make the base.py plain-text fallback actually plain: strip `thread_id`-carrying metadata before the fallback send, so the fallback can succeed where the original send could not.
3. (Follow-up) Have topic-mode recovery re-validate chat capabilities (e.g. `getChat().is_forum` / `getMe` topic flags, debounced) and auto-disable topic mode + prune bindings when the chat is no longer a forum — the client-side analogue of `/topic off`.

## PR

- [ ] I'd like to fix this myself and submit a PR

prs.body:
When you replied in Telegram to a message whose link was hidden behind its text (for example a forwarded channel post), Hermes saw only the words, not the URL, so "summarize the linked article" couldn't work. Now the reply context carries the URL, in the same `anchor (url)` form as a directly sent message, including when you quote just part of the message.

| Live probe (real gateway + Telegram adapter, Bot API stand-in, FakeLLMServer; DM reply to `New post: Read the full report here` with `full report` as a `text_link`) | `origin/main` | this branch |
|---|---|---|
| Reply context the model receives | `New post: Read the full report here` | `New post: Read the full report (https://example.com/report-2026) here` |
| URL reached the model | no | yes |

- `_reply_context` runs the replied-to message through `expand_link_entities`, the same helper the direct-message path uses (#93346).
- Telegram's native partial quote never carries `text_link` entities. The new `expand_quote_link_entities` maps the replied-to message's links into the quote, but only when the quote text sits at its `position` in the source. Otherwise the quote is passed through unchanged.
- adapter.py stays at 7,385 lines.

Root cause: `_reply_context` read `reply_to_message.text`/`caption` and `quote.text` raw.

Fixes #137744

Salvages #137745 (@rodricksz4h5), cherry-picked.

prs.title: feat(memory): add on_turn_complete hook for automatic memory storage
prs.body:
## Summary

Adds `on_turn_complete()` to the `MemoryProvider` ABC: a per-turn hook that explicitly permits **cross-dialogue writes** (memory storage/extraction), separate from `sync_turn()` which is for conversation-history recording.

Resolves #151638

## Motivation

Issue #151638 reports that providers cannot reliably trigger write operations from `sync_turn`: the hook is documented for history recording, there is no stated permission for cross-dialogue writes, and no guidance on what is allowed there.

This implements the issue's recommended Option 1 — a distinct hook with an explicit storage contract plus a `should_store` hint from Hermes.

## Changes

### `agent/memory_provider.py`
New optional `on_turn_complete(user_content, assistant_content, *, session_id="", should_store=False)`. Default is a no-op, so every existing provider keeps working. The docstring states the contract the issue asked for: unlike `sync_turn`, this one explicitly permits cross-dialogue writes. Lifecycle docstring updated.

### `agent/memory_manager.py`
`on_turn_complete_all()` mirroring `sync_all()`:
- runs on the existing single serialized background worker (`_submit_background(kind="write")`), so it never blocks `run_conversation()`;
- honours `_fork_turn_hooks_suppressed()` and `_owner_allows("on_turn_complete")`;
- strips skill scaffolding from the user side and applies `_redact_for_provider()` to both strings, so provider egress keeps the same secret-scrubbing contract as `sync_all` (#115104);
- goes through `_call_unless_stalled`, so a wedged backend is gated like every other background provider call.

### `run_agent.py`
- `AIAgent._detect_storage_intent(user_text)` — small keyword classifier for explicit storage intent ("remember this", "don't forget", "save this", "make a note", …). It only produces the `should_store` hint; providers may ignore it and run their own detection.
- `_sync_external_memory_for_turn()` calls `on_turn_complete_all()` after `sync_all()`/`queue_prefetch_all()`. Interrupted turns are still skipped, so partial output never becomes durable memory.

### Concrete consumer: `plugins/memory/byterover`
byterover already did a cross-dialogue write from `sync_turn` — `brv curate` against its knowledge store — which is exactly the pattern the issue flags. Its curation moves to `on_turn_complete`; `sync_turn` now only counts turns. Two behavioural points:
- `should_store=True` curates even a short turn (an explicit "remember this" no longer has to clear `_MIN_QUERY_LEN`);
- `auto_extract: false` still disables it, now gated at the new hook.

### Docs
`website/docs/developer-guide/memory-provider-plugin.md`: new lifecycle-table row documenting when the hook runs and what `should_store` means.

## Tests

`tests/agent/test_memory_on_turn_complete.py` (5):
1. `on_turn_complete` fires with the `should_store` hint and `session_id` while `sync_turn` keeps firing separately;
2. intent detection — 10 positive phrases, 4 negative, empty/whitespace edges;
3. suppression via `_fork_turn_hooks_suppressed()` queues no work and calls nothing;
4. empty user content never queues work or reaches the hook;
5. a provider that does not override the hook keeps working (default no-op).

`tests/plugins/memory/test_byterover_provider.py` (2):
- `auto_extract: false` skips the new hook;
- `sync_turn` no longer triggers a curate (`_turn_count` still increments).

```
scripts/run_tests.sh tests/agent/test_memory_on_turn_complete.py tests/plugins/memory/test_byterover_provider.py
→ 7 passed
```

Waiting is on `tests.waiting.wait_until` (condition, not clock) and on "nothing was queued" for the negative cases.

## Verification

- `scripts/run_tests.sh` on both files → 7 passed
- `python scripts/check --only footguns,ruff,health` → ok, 0 blocking, 0 advisory

## Compatibility

Purely additive. Providers that write inside `sync_turn` keep working unchanged; new providers can move extraction/storage to `on_turn_complete` and leave `sync_turn` for history only.

prs.title: Fix(desktop): add reduced effects preference
prs.body:
## What does this PR do?

Adds a device-local **Settings → Appearance → General → Motion and Effects** preference with **Full** and **Reduced** modes.

Reduced mode preserves visible working-state indicators while replacing continuous shimmer and moving-gradient effects with static equivalents. It also prevents the shared status pulse from scheduling Web Animations and renders the shared SVG loader once instead of maintaining a `requestAnimationFrame` loop.

**Full remains the default**, so existing visuals are unchanged unless the user explicitly enables Reduced mode.

Continuous CSS animations, Web Animations, and frame-driven SVG loaders can keep Chromium's compositor active even when the surrounding UI is unchanged. Merely slowing the animations does not materially reduce that cost because frames are still composited at the display refresh rate. This preference provides an explicit, reversible control without forcing Electron into software rendering or changing the operating system's global reduced-motion setting.

## Related Issue

Mitigates 
[#73082](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/issues/73082)
[#53902 ](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/issues/53902)

This PR addresses persistent decorative and status-animation work. It does not claim to eliminate every feature-specific animation loop in Desktop.

## Type of Change

- [x] 🐛 Bug fix (non-breaking change that fixes an issue)
- [x] ✨ New feature (non-breaking change that adds functionality)
- [ ] 🔒 Security fix
- [ ] 📝 Documentation update
- [ ] ✅ Tests (adding or improving test coverage)
- [ ] ♻️ Refactor (no behavior change)
- [ ] 🎯 New skill (bundled or hub)

## Changes Made

- Added a persisted, device-local reduced-effects preference in `apps/desktop/src/store/reduced-effects.ts`.
- Added Full/Reduced controls to Desktop Appearance settings.
- Disabled continuous CSS animations and transitions in Reduced mode.
- Rendered shimmer text and the active-session arc as static indicators in Reduced mode.
- Stopped the shared `StatusPulse` Web Animation timer in Reduced mode.
- Changed the shared SVG `Loader` to render one static frame instead of scheduling continuous frames in Reduced mode.
- Stopped the pending-image canvas shimmer loop in Reduced mode, preserving static output through resize/theme changes and retaining Full mode's existing animation cap.
- Added translated settings copy for all nine bundled Desktop locales.
- Added regression tests for persistence, startup restoration, live mode switching, status pulses, loader and canvas frame scheduling, static-canvas repainting, and settings-search routing.

## How to Test

1. Launch Hermes Desktop and open **Settings → Appearance → General → Motion and Effects**.
2. Leave the setting on **Full** and confirm shimmer, the moving active-session arc, status pulses, and loaders retain their current behavior.
3. Select **Reduced** and confirm the change applies immediately without restarting Desktop.
4. Start a chat or compaction and confirm status text and the active-session indicator remain visible but static.
5. Quit and reopen Desktop and confirm the Reduced preference persists.
6. Compare Hermes Helper (GPU), Hermes Helper (Renderer), and WindowServer activity before and after enabling Reduced mode.

Manual testing on macOS arm64 showed a dramatic reduction in GPU activity after selecting Reduced while preserving working-state visibility.

Automated validation of the refreshed source (Node 24.15.0, npm 11.17.0):

- Final focused effects/settings/canvas/i18n suites: 103 tests passed across 18 files.
- Full Desktop UI run before the final two-file canvas follow-up: 10,880 passed, 2 failed across 1,241 files. Both failures reproduce unchanged on upstream `300228d24c` in `src/store/voice-prefs.test.ts`; that file is not changed here. The final canvas follow-up passed the focused suite and fresh checks below.
- Desktop TypeScript check passed.
- Full Desktop ESLint passed with no errors; existing warnings remain, with no new warnings retained.
- Prettier and PR-relative `git diff --check` passed.
- Production Desktop build passed.

## Checklist

### Code

- [x] I've read the [Contributing Guide](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md)
- [x] My commit messages follow [Conventional Commits](https://www.conventionalcommits.org/) (`fix(scope):`, `feat(scope):`, etc.)
- [x] I searched for [existing PRs](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pulls) to make sure this isn't a duplicate
- [x] My PR contains **only** changes related to this fix/feature
- [ ] I've run `pytest tests/ -q` and all tests pass — not run because this is a Desktop-only TypeScript/CSS change; focused Desktop tests and the production build passed
- [x] I've added tests for my changes
- [x] I've tested on my platform: macOS 26, Apple Silicon

### Documentation & Housekeeping

- [x] Relevant documentation update is N/A; the preference is described directly in the Appearance UI
- [x] `cli-config.yaml.example` update is N/A; this is device-local Desktop display state
- [x] `CONTRIBUTING.md` / `AGENTS.md` update is N/A
- [x] Cross-platform impact considered: the implementation uses browser APIs supported by Electron on macOS, Windows, and Linux
- [x] Tool descriptions/schemas update is N/A

## Screenshots / Logs

Before/after Activity Monitor screenshots can be attached during review. Reduced mode was manually verified with active-session and compaction status states in the packaged macOS application.

prs.title: feat(state): fence a claimed turn's writes in the session store's own transaction
prs.body:
![fenced-turn-writes](https://v3b.fal.media/files/b/0ab1b3bc/obJvk3vIyOsrS92ODPdZn_zjfpHJQW.png)

> **Stacked on [#149200](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pull/149200).** Only the top commit (`c4e1a955bc`) is new here. Review it with `git diff dd51609e4e fe57fed423`. Once #149200 merges, this branch is rebased onto main.

Part of the hosted shared-tenancy work tracked in [#146503](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/issues/146503). First of three stacked PRs: this one (fenced turn writes), then the storage ports, then the storage conformance suite.

## Why

A gateway turn is admitted into a per-session FIFO, then *claimed* by the profile's owner process. The claim stamps the owner's `owner_epoch` and the session's `runtime_generation` on the admission row, and #149200 carries those two numbers on the turn as its **fence** (`TurnScope.fence`).

Nothing checked the fence after the claim. A turn whose lease was lost could keep writing transcript, session and usage rows. The lease is lost when another owner takes the profile over (the epoch moves), or when a newer claim or an invalidating mutation moves the session's generation. Its reply would interleave with the new owner's turn.

## What changes

**Every write a claimed turn makes is checked against its fence, inside the write's own transaction.** `SessionDB._execute_write` already runs each write under `BEGIN IMMEDIATE`. Before the write's callback runs, it now compares the turn's fence with the profile's current owner epoch and the session's current `runtime_generation`, in that same transaction (`hermes_state_fence.check_turn_lease`). If either moved, the write raises `TurnFenceSupersededError` and nothing of it lands. Because the check shares the transaction, a takeover cannot commit between check and write. `TurnFenceSupersededError` subclasses the existing `SessionTurnLeaseLostError`, so every handler that already treats a lost lease as "another writer owns this turn" handles it unchanged.

**One turn identity.** `hermes_scope.current_turn()` derives the turn from the bound `TurnScope` (session, turn, fence). `bind_turn(..., store=path)` records which store issued the claim (`TurnMark`); a `TurnScope` bound without one is fenced on its profile's `state.db`. Only writes to that store, in the turn's context, are turn writes.

**Work the turn started keeps its fence for its whole lifetime.** The mark is immutable and is never closed, so threads and tasks the turn starts (the title-upgrade thread, a late reply) stay the turn's work:
- after a takeover or the session's next claim, their writes are refused;
- while the turn still holds its lease they land exactly as before, so a late title for a turn nobody superseded is still published.

**Queued token updates carry their claim.** A usage update queued for the background writer (`hermes_state_usage`) records the turn it was queued under. The writer applies it inside that turn's fence and never coalesces deltas from different claims, so a superseded turn's counters are dropped and a live turn's are not.

**Two explicit exceptions:**
- the owner's own work (the drain that claims and settles turns) runs under `agent.runtime_scope.owner_operation()`. It keeps the ledger's own epoch/generation checks, including when a turn's context scheduled it;
- work designed to outlive the turn (async delegation, background review) runs under `outlive_turn()`, which keeps only the owner-epoch half of the fence: a takeover still refuses it, the session's next claim does not.

Unchanged: writes to another profile's store, CLI/TUI turns (they hold a durable turn lease instead), and maintenance between turns.

## Tests

- `tests/hermes_state/test_turn_fence_writes.py`: a turn holding its lease writes as before; a superseded turn's write is refused and leaves nothing; writes outside a claimed turn are unaffected; a turn fences only the store that issued it; a thread the turn started stays fenced after the turn returns.
- `tests/hermes_state/test_turn_fence_lifetime.py`: a superseded turn's queued tokens are refused like its synchronous writes, a live turn's land after its body returned, and queued tokens never merge across claims; a copied task cannot land a late reply after takeover, but writes while the turn holds its lease; the title thread of a superseded turn publishes nothing, a late title of an unsuperseded turn lands; a bound `TurnScope` alone fences its profile's store; settlement from a copied turn context runs as the owner's operation and keeps the ledger's own fence; the turn identity is immutable; `outlive_turn()` work survives the next claim but not a takeover, and async delegation and background review run under it.
- `tests/gateway/test_turn_fence_store.py`: a drained turn is fenced on its authority store; a drain scheduled from inside a turn runs as the owner.
- Cron owner-bridge fixtures used to fabricate a claimed row the store never issued. They now leave the store as a real claim does (`claimed_row`); no assertion removed.

Run standalone on this branch (`scripts/run_tests.sh`): `tests/hermes_state/`, `tests/gateway/test_turn_fence_store.py`, `tests/agent/test_async_token_accounting.py`, `tests/agent/test_runtime_scope.py`, `tests/cron/`, 3520 passed, 0 failed (18 skipped). `python3 scripts/check`: 14 checks, ok. The full gateway suite (`tests/gateway/`) is green on this branch: 13442 passed, 0 failed (86 skipped), with zero false refusals (no write by a turn that still held its lease was refused).

## Limits

- The fence is checked in the local SQLite store. A hosted backend checks the same fence in its own transaction; the next PR in the stack defines that interface.
- CLI/TUI turns are not fenced by this; they are guarded by the durable turn lease as today.

prs.title: fix(aux): a cached auxiliary client's key follows the credential it was built with
prs.body:
## A cached auxiliary client's cache key follows the credential it was built with

**Symptom.** With two or more pooled keys and a per-model cooldown on one entry, a cached auxiliary client could keep sending a key that had since been refreshed (→ 401) or cooled down for the requested model (→ 429), even though another pooled key was eligible.

**Who / when / why.** Regression introduced by 49165bcaff (kshitijk4poor, 2026-11-04) in #148403. That change made the client build peek the credential pool with the requested model, but the cache key's pool hint kept peeking without it. The key therefore named a different entry than the one the client sent, so a refresh or cooldown of the sent entry never changed the key and never invalidated the cached client. The Nous builder also called `select()` without the model, and the `codex` alias peeked with the raw alias's model id, so on those routes the key and the sent entry drifted apart too.

**What changes.**
- **The pool strategy picks what is sent.** The Nous, Codex (including `raw_codex`) and xAI builders send a pool entry themselves. On a cache miss they call `select()` once, for the model the build resolves (the caller's, else the provider default), on the pool loaded for the cache key. The request goes out on that entry, and the strategy counts that entry and only that one.
- **The cache key comes from the entry actually used.** For those three routes the key is recomputed from the same pool after the build, so a refresh made inside `select()` is included. The built client records the entry whose key it sends, matched by bearer (`entry_id_for_api_key`), so a singleton fallback records no entry.
- **A hit runs a validity check, not a selection.** The recorded entry must still be present and available for the model the client sends (not exhausted, dead or cooling down). This is the filter `peek()`/`has_available()` already apply, with `refresh=False`. Any token change changes the key. If the check fails, the entry is popped (not closed) and rebuilt. A steady pool of N calls makes 1 build and 1 `select()`.
- **The peek-then-reclaim path is removed.** No code sends an entry other than `select()`'s pick. This removes both problems it had: a failed proactive refresh (or a default-model cooldown) of the peeked entry no longer drops the healthy sibling `select()` already picked, and `least_used` / `random` / `round_robin` no longer pick and count one entry while sending another.
- **The explicit-key routes are unchanged** (OpenRouter, Anthropic, registry API-key, named custom). They key on the non-mutating `peek(model=...)` and send that entry's key. The pool is loaded once per call under the canonical provider (`codex` → `openai-codex`) and entry-scoped for a pinned `custom:<name>`.
- **The Nous 401 refresh** force-refreshes the entry whose key the failing client sent (`try_refresh_matching(credential_id=...)`), and records it on the rebuilt client.
- **Moved code.** `_pool_cache_hint` / `_pool_credential_digest` and the new helpers live in `agent/auxiliary_pool_selection.py`. The move is a pure-move commit. `agent/auxiliary_client.py` goes from 8281 to 8241 lines, also on a merge with current main.
- `_peek_pool_entry` no longer wraps `peek(model=...)` in `suppress(TypeError)`, which could fall back to the cooldown-blind entry. `CredentialPool.peek` accepts `model=`.

**Routing vs main.** Real `CredentialPool`, network and subprocesses blocked, `httpx.MockTransport`.
- **Codex, two keys (k0 used 50×, k1 idle):** for `fill_first`, `round_robin`, `least_used` and `random` (choice pinned to k1), the sent entry and the request counts are identical to main. That holds for a failed proactive refresh of k0 (k1 sent) and for a default-model cooldown on the current k0 (k1 sent). Two sequential cold `round_robin` builds send k0 then k1, counts 1/1.
- **5 routes × 4 strategies × {refresh, cooldown, steady-10}, three keys:** 60 cells. The sent entry never differs from the entry the cache key / cached client names: 0 cells, against 160 sent-vs-key mismatches on main. The first entry sent equals main's in 18 of 20 route×strategy cells. The two that differ are Nous `fill_first` / `round_robin`, where main's model-blind `select()` skipped k0 for a cooldown on another model. Not skipping it is the fix above.
- **`random`, 30 seeds:** Nous, Codex and xAI send the same k0/k1/k2 spread as main's Codex/xAI (11/9/10), with 0 key mismatches.

**Tests** (`tests/agent/test_auxiliary_client_cache_follows_credential.py`, 44 tests). Requests go through `httpx.MockTransport`; socket connect/`connect_ex`, `create_connection`, `getaddrinfo` and subprocesses are blocked.
- **Earlier rows, parametrized over 6 routes** (`openrouter`, `nous`, `nous-async`, `nous-least-used`, `codex-alias`, `xai-oauth-least-used`):
  - `..._rebuilds_when_its_model_aware_key_is_refreshed`
  - `..._rebuilds_when_its_key_cools_down_for_the_model`
  - `..._is_reused_while_its_key_is_unchanged`

  The `least_used` rows now expect the strategy's pick (k1).
- **New rows, on one long-lived real pool:**
  - `test_failed_refresh_of_the_first_entry_sends_the_healthy_sibling[codex|xai-oauth]`
  - `test_default_model_cooldown_on_the_current_entry_sends_the_sibling[codex|xai-oauth]`
  - `test_pool_strategy_picks_the_entry_sent_and_counts_only_it[{nous,codex,xai-oauth}-{least-used,random,round-robin-two-builds,steady-pool}]`: sent entry, request counts, builds == `select()` calls, and 1 build / 1 `select()` for 5 warm calls.
  - `test_cached_client_rebuilds_when_the_entry_it_sends_changes_on_a_hit[{nous,codex,xai-oauth}-{refresh,cooldown}]`
- **Unchanged:** the token-rotation, cooldown-hint and sibling-rotation rows. Three test stubs accept the new keyword arguments.

**Results.**
- **This file:** 44/44 pass. On main: 19 failed, 25 passed. On the previous head of this PR: 25 failed, 19 passed; every failed-refresh, default-cooldown and strategy row is red.
  - The hit-rebuild refresh rows for Codex and xAI already pass on main and on the previous head, which keyed on the peeked entry. Two mutations prove they are guards on this head: dropping the hit check turns 8 cooldown rows red, and dropping the strategy-route digest turns 9 refresh rows red.
- **The 45 test files that reference the touched helpers:** 859 passed, 1 skipped, 0 failed.
- Lint and the repo's pre-commit checks are clean, on the branch and on a merge with current main.

**Not in scope (pre-existing).**
- The MoA aggregator's pooled credential is not keyed: a refresh of the aggregator's entry does not rebuild the client.
- `_refresh_xai_oauth_credentials` refreshes without the model (`try_refresh_current`).
- `_try_nous` falls back to `_read_nous_auth`, which selects without the model, when the pool yields no runtime credential.
- For Nous, Codex and xAI the key digests every entry's token, so a sibling's token refresh rebuilds the cached client once. The explicit-key routes digest only their entry.
- The OpenRouter and Anthropic builders still call `select()` themselves to pick the base URL (their key comes from the peek). `auto` keys on the main provider's pool.

prs.title: feat(desktop): show the owning profile on session tabs
prs.body:
## What

Session tabs in the desktop pane/tab shell now carry the owning profile's glyph, between the status dot and the tab label.

## Why

The tab strip is the only header a pane has in the tiled layout: `session-view.tsx` states it directly — *"the workspace pane is just the first tab"* — and every session, the workspace one included, renders as a `tile` view (`session-tile.tsx`, `kind: 'tile'`). The `ChatHeader` that carries `ProfileTag` is gated on `isPrimary` (`app/chat/index.tsx:526,766`), so in the tabbed layout it never mounts, and the strip itself renders title + status dot only. The result: the header answers "which agent owns this chat" in the single-pane layout and nowhere in the tabbed one, which is exactly the ambiguity #66003 fixed for the header.

## How

- `PaneChrome.tabBadge?: () => React.ReactNode` — sibling of the existing `tabLead`, rendered between the lead node and the label (`renderer/track-model.ts`, `renderer/tree-group.tsx`).
- `paneMirror` forwards it for tiles, alongside `tabLead`/`tabTitle`/`tabWrap` (`app/chat/pane-mirror.ts`).
- New `TabOwnerBadge` (`app/chat/tab-owner-badge.tsx`) reuses `ProfileTag`, so the tab, the chat header and the sidebar row render the same glyph, colour and tooltip. It paints only when the gateway serves more than one profile **and** the session is not on the default profile — same rule as the sidebar row: "the normal one" stays the absence of a mark.
- Supplied by both session surfaces: the tile mirror (`session-tile.tsx`) and the workspace pane's registry entry (`contrib/controller.tsx`).

## Scope

- Not threaded into the collapsed vertical rail or the compact tab picker — neither has room for a second mark; happy to follow up if you want it in the picker's rows.
- A fresh draft tab has no session row, so no owner glyph until its first turn (same as its title).

## Test plan

- `eslint` against the desktop config on all six touched files — clean.
- Not run here: `vitest` for the desktop package (workspace dependencies are not installed in this environment). The change is presentation-only and adds no assertions to existing tests; a strip-level test for `tabBadge` would need the pane-shell render harness — say so if you want it in this PR rather than a follow-up.
- Manual: gateway with ≥2 profiles → dock a second session → both tabs show their owner's glyph; the workspace tab on `default` shows none.

Fixes the tabbed-layout half of the report; the sidebar-recents half is #151682.

prs.title: fix(telegram): multi-paragraph messages that arrive as rich_message blocks reach the agent (#146067)
prs.body:
Long or multi-paragraph Telegram messages, such as pasted listings, can arrive in Telegram's new rich-block format with no plain text. Hermes dropped them: no reply and no log line. Now they reach the agent as readable text, with bullets kept.

| DM carrying only `rich_message.blocks` (the issue's captured shape + a bold span + a labelled list), real `hermes gateway run` + Telegram adapter vs Bot API stand-in | Before (`origin/main`) | After (this PR) |
|---|---|---|
| model turns | `{}`: silently dropped | `{"rich": 1}` |
| user row in `state.db` | none | `Can't you update the firmware yourself? [in:rich]\n\n• Kapazität: 1TB\n• Modell: HD103UJ` |
| reply delivered | no | yes |

- `telegram_entities.rich_message_text()` reads `rich_message` from the attribute or from `Message.api_kwargs`. PTB 22.8 keeps it there as a `mappingproxy`, so an `isinstance(dict)` check never finds it (@BETEP-ok's finding). It flattens paragraph `text` that is a string, a list of runs, or a span dict, and gives each list item its `label` (`•`, `1.`) as the bullet.
- `expand_link_entities` (the text every inbound event is built from) falls back to it when `text` and `caption` are empty.
- `_register_handlers`: the text handler matches `filters.TEXT | rich_message_filter(filters)`. `_handle_text_message`'s guard accepts a text-less rich message. Batching, auth, mention gating and observe mode then run unchanged.
- The issue's optional third item, a log line for an update no handler claims, is not added here. With this fix the known silent-drop shape is now handled.
- `adapter.py` stays at 7,385 lines.

Root cause: three gates (`filters.TEXT`, the `not msg.text` guard, `expand_link_entities`) all read only `text`/`caption`, and PTB does not surface the new field as an attribute.

Fixes #146067

Credit: design from @BETEP-ok's three-change write-up on the issue, and @liuhao1024's fork branch (`04d604c248`, never opened as a PR), whose dict check this replaces.

## Tests
- `tests/e2e/core/platforms/test_telegram_rich_message_inbound.py` (new): the real gateway and adapter with real PTB parsing against the stand-in. It sends a rich-only DM and asserts one model turn, the reply, and the exact flattened user row. Red on `origin/main`. With only the handler-registration line reverted, it is red as well. Green here. Runs in the messaging-extra E2E lane.
- `tests/gateway/test_telegram_documents.py::test_media_handler_accepts_video_notes`: its fake `filters` namespace gains `MessageFilter` (the new filter subclasses it).
- Focused: 15 files, 306 passed + the fixed one (telegram text batching/gating/mention/auth/link expansion/documents/late plugin rewire, `tests/plugins/platforms/telegram`).

## Dropped hunks
- From @liuhao1024's branch: `isinstance(api_kwargs, dict)` (a no-op on the real `mappingproxy`) and the string-only `text` read (dumps `{'type': 'bold', ...}`).

prs.title: feat(plugins): add Overhead satellite change catalog entry
prs.body:
## What does this PR do?

Adds only `plugin-catalog/overhead.yaml`, a community listing for [Overhead](https://github.com/leoresendedop-sys/overhead), pinned to `5ddd2e5aed0e5451f0a9c5107270770c919e1eb8` (MIT, version 0.1.0).

Overhead answers “what changed at this place between these dates?” with Sentinel-2 L2A measurements of vegetation, burned area and water, expressed in hectares, plus before/after/change panels and timelapse GIFs. It is a standalone plugin, not a core patch or a fork of a bundled plugin.

## Surfaces and capabilities

- Four tools: `overhead_locate`, `overhead_scenes`, `overhead_compare`, `overhead_timelapse`.
- The `overhead:earth-watch` skill.
- Two hooks: `post_tool_call` and `transform_llm_output`, to preserve MEDIA delivery.
- A Desktop SDK card and a read-only backend route serving the plugin's own outputs. No core overrides, private model-envelope dependency or self-updater.
- No required environment variables, middleware, credentials, telemetry, shell commands or persistent background process.

## Data, dependencies and privacy disclosures

- Unauthenticated HTTPS requests to Element 84 Earth Search (`earth-search.aws.element84.com`) send bounding boxes and dates, not the exact area outline. Sentinel-2 band range reads go to the AWS Open Data `sentinel-cogs` bucket in us-west-2.
- Place-name lookup alone calls Nominatim/OpenStreetMap (`nominatim.openstreetmap.org`), limited to one request per second. Earth Search and Nominatim receive the plugin User-Agent.
- Place lookups, imagery and past-date searches are cached in `plugin-data/overhead/cache/`; generated outputs live in `runs/`. These are not pruned automatically.
- Reads a system font for panel labels. The Desktop “Open map” button opens OpenStreetMap only on a user's click.
- The plugin needs no account or API key and does not read `~/.netrc` or credential stores. Its declared dependency is `rasterio>=1.4,<2`, installed only through Hermes dependency consent.
- Optional visual interpretation supplies local image paths and suggested questions for the public `vision_analyze` tool. If called, Hermes may send the selected images and prompt to the configured native or auxiliary provider. Images may contain location/date labels; this adds latency and may incur model costs, and provider credentials/privacy terms follow the user's Hermes configuration. Deterministic metrics do not depend on this optional call.

## Evidence and limitations

- [Pinned README](https://github.com/leoresendedop-sys/overhead/blob/5ddd2e5aed0e5451f0a9c5107270770c919e1eb8/README.md)
- [Real Hermes Desktop comparison capture](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/leoresendedop-sys/overhead/5ddd2e5aed0e5451f0a9c5107270770c919e1eb8/assets/hermes-comparison.jpg)
- [Real Hermes Desktop timelapse capture](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/leoresendedop-sys/overhead/5ddd2e5aed0e5451f0a9c5107270770c919e1eb8/assets/hermes-timelapse.jpg)

The cover is illustrative artwork, not a UI screenshot. Real captures demonstrate rendering, not an assertion that every native drag or external-map interaction was verified. Cloud cover, missing periods, image resolution and sun glint limit interpretation; water glint outliers are flagged rather than presented as reliable water loss. See README for cautions and Desktop-version requirements.

## Validation

- Clean checkout of the public pinned SHA: 245 Python tests passed, 3 opt-in live tests skipped.
- 31 JavaScript tests passed; TypeScript typecheck and Desktop build passed. Rebuilt bundle matches the committed file.
- Structural catalog validator: passed.
- Final isolated `hermes plugins validate --install-deps`: passed all 16 checks with no warnings, including capability registration, security scan (safe), no core overrides and Desktop SDK surface.
- All seven pinned documentation/image URLs returned HTTP 200 after publication.
- No paid model invocation or running-gateway restart for this submission.

## Checklist

- [x] Read CONTRIBUTING.md and plugin-catalog admission rules.
- [x] Searched existing PRs for a duplicate Overhead listing.
- [x] Exact 40-character pin, matching declared capabilities, bounded dependency, public source and immutable screenshot URLs.
- [x] This PR changes only the catalog entry; no unrelated plugin changes.
- [ ] Admission CI and maintainer review complete.

No related issue. This is an owner submission of a new standalone plugin catalog entry. Full Hermes core test/lint suites are not claimed for this catalog-only change.

prs.title: plugin-catalog: add hermes-wrapped (weekly Wrapped video of your Hermes usage) [hackathon]
prs.body:
## Hermes Agent Plugin Hackathon entry: Hermes Wrapped

Repo: https://github.com/devpras22/hermes-wrapped (pinned at `0de155d96fb498971301dcf147f06e5628fa3993`). Submitted by the repo owner.

**What it does:** your week, month or year with Hermes as a 30-second video, built *from Hermes's own session records by code*. No model calls, no tokens. It shows what the agent did for you (sessions, steps, files edited, active time, tokens, cost, vs the previous period) and how much of the time went into **upkeep** (setup, config, fixing Hermes) versus Hermes working for you, with the sessions that ate the most time and why each counted as upkeep. `/wrapped [week|month|year] [vertical] [crt|blue]`, `hermes wrapped ...`, and a `wrapped_make` tool so the agent can send it when asked. `hermes wrapped schedule` adds a no-agent cron job that delivers it every Sunday.

**Why a plugin, not a skill or prompt:** it reads every session in the period from the session store (a prompt can only see the current chat), logs exact step timing and failures via a `post_tool_call` hook, counts instead of estimating, costs zero tokens, and renders deterministically.

**Hermes surfaces used:** `register_tool` (`wrapped_make`), `register_hook` (`post_tool_call`), `register_command` (`/wrapped`), `register_cli_command` (`hermes wrapped`), `ctx.inject_message` (desktop handoff, needs `allow_gateway_injection: true`, otherwise it degrades to a text reply), plugin `config_schema` settings.

**Validation:** `hermes plugins validate <path> --install-deps` passes locally (security scan: safe; no core override; declared tools/hooks match registrations).

### Rule 13 disclosures
- **Reads outside plugin data:** the user's session history (`state.db`), read-only, through `hermes_state.SessionDB` and a read-only SQLite connection. Nothing leaves the machine unless the user delivers the video.
- **Shell commands / subprocesses:** `npx --yes hyperframes@0.8.217 render` (version pinned) to render; `ffmpeg` to re-encode oversized renders; `hermes send` to deliver; `hermes cron create` only if the user runs `hermes wrapped schedule`.
- **Third-party network calls:** the first render downloads the pinned HyperFrames CLI from npm and a headless Chrome build chosen by HyperFrames (~150 MB, once). Fonts and the GSAP library ship in the repo, no model or TTS calls, **no telemetry**.
- **Long-running background processes:** each render runs headless Chrome + ffmpeg for about 2-10 minutes in a background thread (blue theme is the slowest). A file lock allows one render at a time.
- **Writes:** tool-timing events to `~/.hermes/plugin-data/hermes-wrapped/events.db` (kept 30 days), a temporary render folder (deleted after each render), MP4s to `~/.hermes/cache/videos/`, and, only on `hermes wrapped schedule`, one script at `~/.hermes/scripts/hermes-wrapped-weekly.sh`.
- **Credentials:** none stored or read. `requires_env` is empty.
- **Privacy:** API keys, tokens, JWTs, emails and home paths are stripped before rendering; user messages are never shown unless the `quotes` setting is turned on (off by default).

Demo video: to be posted on X and linked in the submission form.

prs.title: fix(gateway): approval cards never offer Approve on a cut-off command preview (#62359)
prs.body:
Telegram (and every other button chat) cut a long command off with "..." on the approval card and still showed Allow Once / Session / Always. You could approve a hidden tail you never saw, such as a trailing `&& rm -rf …`. Now a cut-off card is always preceded by the full command, and if Hermes cannot show the full command, the card offers Deny only.

| 5,006-char `echo AAAA… && rm -rf <dir> # TAIL_MARKER_rm`, real `hermes gateway run` + Telegram adapter vs Bot API stand-in | Before (`origin/main`) | After (this PR) |
|---|---|---|
| messages sent | 1 (the card) | 4: full command (split to fit), then the card |
| tail visible before you choose | no | yes |
| card says it is shortened | no, just `...` | "Preview shortened: the full command (5006 characters) is in the message above." |
| buttons | Allow Once / Session / Always / Deny | Allow Once / Session / Always / Deny |
| same command containing a ` ``` ` fence (cannot be shown verbatim) | 4 buttons on a cut preview | **Deny only**, "…could not be shown here, so only Deny is offered. Review it in the CLI or Desktop app." |

- **Shared base, every surface:** `BasePlatformAdapter.send_exec_approval` renders the card through `base_exec_approval.render_exec_approval`. On truncation it sends the whole command first (`send_full_command`, a fenced block that each adapter's `send()` splits). If that send fails or the command contains a ` ``` ` fence, only the `deny` action is kept. The notice is budgeted inside each adapter's existing per-platform cap. Telegram, Discord, Slack, Matrix, Feishu, Teams, WhatsApp Cloud, QQ and the relay all go through this path.
- **Deny-only from creation:** every request is created Deny-only. The mark is an `_ApprovalEntry` slot set before the entry is enqueued, in the same critical section as the publish. `send_exec_approval` lifts it only when the card itself shows the whole command, or once every chunk of the full-command send is delivered. A tap before rendering, or during the send, can only deny.
- **QQ taps name their request:** QQ's `button_data` now carries the request id (`approve:<session_key>:<decision>:<request_id>`), so a tap resolves exactly its own card's request, once. A tap with no id (a card from an older build) resolves nothing at all, even with one request pending. Typed `/approve` stays the way to answer such a request.
- **Relay fails closed:** the relay's `send` result has no partial-delivery field (the connector splits, and a dropped or capped chunk, Discord's message cap included, is invisible). A relayed full command counts as proof only when it fits one `max_message_length` message; longer, the card is Deny-only. The wire format is unchanged; `relay-connector-contract.md` says why.
- **Text fallback:** `gateway/run.py::_format_exec_approval_fallback` (the `/approve` prompt) no longer truncates the command, so `send()` splits it and `/approve` always answers a command shown in full.
- The approval binding was already sound: the executed string is the one in the pending record, as the maintainer's comment on the issue confirms. This fixes only the representation half the issue describes.
- New strings `gateway.exec_approval.truncated_full_above` / `truncated_deny_only` in all 17 locales. `gateway/platforms/base.py` shrinks (4,833 → 4,829); `run.py` stays at 5,204.
- Docs: `website/docs/user-guide/security.md` § Approval Flow (Gateway/Messaging).
- SECURITY.md §3.2 hardening (public).

Root cause: the card's command preview was cut to the platform cap while the approve actions stayed on.

Fixes #62359

Supersedes #62376 (@liuhao1024): same rule (Deny-only on truncation), but Telegram-only and over the 4,096 cap per the triage review. This PR applies it in the shared base, keeps approval possible by sending the full command first, and budgets the notice. Credited as co-author.

## Tests
- `tests/gateway/test_exec_approval_truncated_preview.py` (new, drives `send_exec_approval`). Control: a short command keeps the compact four-button card and sends nothing extra. Truncated cases: full command sent first with 4 buttons; full send failed → Deny only; ` ``` ` in the command → Deny only. Each card says it is shortened, with the length, and never shows the tail. Red on `origin/main` (3/3 truncated cases), green here.
- `test_exec_approval_template.py::test_command_is_truncated_to_the_platform_budget` now expects half the tiny budget for the preview, with the notice taking the rest. `test_teams.py::test_long_non_ascii_command_keeps_button_data_small` stubs `send` for the full-command message, and its 4-button assertion still holds.
- Focused: 80 files, 1,057 passed, 0 failed (all approval suites across adapters, relay, `tools/test_approval.py`, i18n key/placeholder parity).
- Live: real gateway, Telegram adapter, Bot API stand-in; a plain leg and a fence leg, each run on `origin/main` and on this head (table above).

## Landing order with #144799
Land **this PR first**, then rebase #144799 onto it. They conflict in the Discord adapter / approval view, the Matrix adapter and `tools/approval.py::resolve_gateway_approval_card`. #144799's rebase must preserve:
- the id-less rule here: `request_id=None` resolves nothing, so #144799's FIFO branch in the card resolver goes away;
- the `card_deny_only` slot and its check inside the same critical section where #144799 runs `may_answer`, so the requester check and the Deny-only check both run under one `_lock` hold on the entry being settled (`_lock` is already an `RLock` in both);
- the born-Deny-only line in `_await_gateway_decision` next to #144799's `_same_answerers` coalescing check.

## Dropped hunks
- #62376's Telegram-only override of `_send_exec_approval_prompt`: replaced by the base rule, which covers every surface.

prs.title: Desktop chat widgets get the app's chart colors, so agent-drawn charts stay readable in dark mode (inspired by Amp)
prs.body:
Charts that an agent draws inside a Desktop chat widget used to pick their own colors, so a chart made in light mode turned into near-invisible black bars in dark mode. Now every widget receives the app's own seven chart colors, already tuned for light and dark, so the same chart reads correctly in both.

**Outcome:** `::preview` inline widgets get `var(--red)`, `var(--orange)`, `var(--yellow)`, `var(--green)`, `var(--cyan)`, `var(--blue)`, `var(--purple)` from the live theme, and the agent is told about them.

## Inspired by Amp

- Source: [Visualize This](https://ampcode.com/news/visualize-this) (2026-10-29) and [Designing UI](https://ampcode.com/docs/designing-ui).
- **Their mechanism:** the agent writes a self-contained HTML page into an `amp-view` code block; the web app renders it inline in a sandboxed, theme-following frame with no network. A ~50 KB "view kit" skill (components, icons, chart helpers) makes charts look native, drawn "with Amp's own diff colors".
- **Ours vs theirs:** Hermes already had the larger part and is ahead in one dimension: `::preview` widgets render live in the transcript, sized to content, with a theme prelude, and they can **talk back** (`data-hermes-send` / `window.hermes.send`), which Amp's prototypes cannot ("saves nothing"). The gap was the palette: our prelude gave five neutral tokens and no series colors, so every chart guessed. This PR closes that gap with the palette the app already uses for diffs and status, not a new kit.

## Changes

- `inline-preview-directive.tsx`: `THEME_BRIDGE_TOKENS` maps `--red … --purple` to the existing `--ui-red … --ui-purple` (separate light/dark values in `styles.css`), resolved from the live theme on every render like the other tokens.
- `agent/prompt_builder.py` desktop hint: names the hues in the sentence that already lists theme vars. **Prompt size: 1406 → 1408 chars (Desktop sessions only)**, tightened wording to stay neutral.
- `desktop-plugin-sdk.md`: documents the new tokens.
- One invariant test: the hues reach the frame under their friendly names (red on `origin/main`, green on head).

## Before / after (the real `collectThemeBridge` + `themePrelude` + `withInlineChrome` output, rendered in Chromium)

Same widget HTML (`fill="var(--green)"` / `var(--red)` bars plus seven `var(--hue)` chips), app light and dark values:

| | main | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| dark | ![main dark](https://gist.githubusercontent.com/teknium1/273a569f6a498b582770bb0e5c3732b3/raw/base-widget-dark.png) | ![head dark](https://gist.githubusercontent.com/teknium1/273a569f6a498b582770bb0e5c3732b3/raw/widget-dark.png) |
| light | ![main light](https://gist.githubusercontent.com/teknium1/273a569f6a498b582770bb0e5c3732b3/raw/base-widget-light.png) | ![head light](https://gist.githubusercontent.com/teknium1/273a569f6a498b582770bb0e5c3732b3/raw/widget-light.png) |

Prelude on head (dark): `color-scheme:dark;--foreground:#ececec;…;--red:#e75e78;--orange:#db704b;--yellow:#c08532;--green:#55a583;--cyan:#6f9ba6;--blue:#0053fd;--purple:#9e94d5`. On main the hue vars are absent, so the bars fall back to black.

**Live repro:** on main, an agent's `var(--green)`/`var(--red)` widget bars render invisible (SVG `fill` in the jsdom frames above: black). On head they render the app's green and red in both modes. Verified twice: in the shipping prelude functions (vitest/jsdom → Chromium, above), and in a running Electron Desktop with a real agent turn (screenshots + CDP computed-colour readback below).

## Tests

- `npx vitest run src/components/assistant-ui/inline-preview-directive.test.ts`: 27 passed (new test fails on main).
- `scripts/run_tests.sh tests/agent/test_prompt_builder.py`: 58 passed.
- `scripts/check --only health`: ok (re-run after rebasing onto `origin/main` 0b82d4ce898; the rebase was clean). eslint and ruff clean; `check_doc_links.py` OK.

Shots were taken on `83c7221a0f1`. The only later commit, `445e7a3e8ab`, regenerates the prompt-surface snapshot (`tests/fixtures/prompt_surface`, desktop.claude 1473 → 1474 stable tokens, so merging needs a hermes-agent-core approval) and changes no runtime code.

One **real agent turn** on Opus 5.5 (Nous inference) was prompted to "write an HTML file … color the added bars with `background: var(--green)` and the removed bars with `background: var(--red)`, class `bar-add`/`bar-del` … show it with ::preview". The agent wrote `diff-bars.html` and emitted the directive. Both legs use the same instance and the same turn. For the main leg, `inline-preview-directive.tsx` was swapped to `origin/main` and the page reloaded; afterwards the head file was restored and `git diff --stat` was empty. prs.title: fix(gateway): an idle /restart acknowledges before the gateway starts stopping (#65057)
prs.body:
When you sent `/restart` to an idle gateway, Hermes began shutting down before its "♻ Restarting gateway…" reply had reached Telegram, so on a real connection you saw nothing and could think the command failed. Now the reply is sent and confirmed first, and only then does the restart begin.

| Live probe (real `hermes gateway` + Telegram adapter, Bot API stand-in answering `sendMessage` after a 400 ms round trip like the real API; idle gateway) | `origin/main` | this branch |
|---|---|---|
| `♻ Restarting gateway…` delivered before the process exits | ❌ 0/2 runs (`Stopping gateway for restart…` → `Disconnected` before the send completed) | ✅ 3/3 runs, the response reached the still-connected client |
| Gateway exits for restart | yes | yes |

- `_handle_restart_command`: with no active turns, teardown is immediate. The ack is now sent through `gateway/restart_ack.send_restart_ack` and awaited (10 s cap) **before** `request_restart()`.
  - If that send fails, the ack falls back to the ordinary reply path, so the old behaviour is the floor, not a regression.
  - With active turns the drain already waits for them, so the "draining N agents" reply is still returned as before (`test_restart_command_while_busy_requests_drain_without_interrupt` unchanged).
- The send helper lives in a new sibling `gateway/restart_ack.py`, keeping the `slash_commands.py` facade at its base line count.

Root cause: the ack was the command's return value, sent after `request_restart()` had started stopping the adapter (the 2026-11-07 log in the thread shows `Sending response` 50 ms before `Stopping gateway`).

Fixes #65057

Supersedes #65095 (@webtecnica; stale, sent from the adapter after degradation) and #66598 (@kevin-lucifer; startup-notify side, a different message).

## Tests
- `tests/gateway/test_restart_ack_before_teardown.py` (new): drives `runner._handle_message("/restart")` and asserts `send` happens before `request_restart`, with the gateway still live, and no duplicate reply. RED on `origin/main` (`['restart'] == ['send', 'restart']`), GREEN here.
- 14 restart/slash-dispatch files: 109 passed, 6 skipped.
- `python scripts/check`: 15 checks ok.

prs.title: Inspired by Amp: a session can archive and reclaim its own worktree under the prune policy (Desktop, CLI, /worktree remove, REST)
prs.body:
A session that ran in its own worktree can now reclaim that tree in one step — from the Desktop row menu, `hermes worktree remove`, `/worktree remove` or REST — under the same never-forced policy as `hermes worktree prune`, so a merged branch goes with its tree, untracked scratch is archived, and real work is kept with the reason shown.

## Source

Amp's runner model ("One Runner, Many Worktrees", ampcode.com/news, 2026-09-22; `ampcode.com/docs/cli/runners`): each task gets a worktree the runner creates and **tears down when the thread is done**. Hermes already had the create half (Desktop worktree lanes, `hermes -w`, kanban) and a bulk sweep (`hermes worktree prune`, #99414), but no per-tree, policy-gated teardown a session could trigger.

## Ours vs theirs

| | Amp | Hermes (before) | Hermes (this PR) |
|---|---|---|---|
| Teardown scope | per thread, automatic | all trees at once (`prune`) or raw `git worktree remove` from Desktop | one tree, from the session that used it |
| Branch handling | not documented | Desktop remove leaks the branch; prune deletes when merged | one policy for both: merged → deleted, pushed open PR → kept |
| Dirty tree | not documented | Desktop offered `--force` on any git refusal | kept with the reason; force only for a tree the policy kept, prompt names what is lost; a tree a running session owns is never forced |
| Untracked scratch | – | lost on force | archived first (existing prune archive) |

## Changes

- `hermes_cli/worktree_gc.py`: `_audit_entry` extracted from the sweep and shared; `reclaim_worktree(repo_root, path)` audits ONE tree with the same verdicts (`keep`, `reap`, `reap-keep-branch`, `reap-archive`), refuses the main checkout; `reclaim_worktrees` now records whether `branch -D` actually succeeded.
- CLI `hermes worktree remove <name|path> [--json]` (exit 1 + reason when kept); `/worktree remove <name>` mid-session (refuses the tree the session runs in).
- `POST /api/git/worktree/reclaim {path, worktreePath}` (`web_git.py::worktree_reclaim`, `web_routers/git.py`).
- Desktop: **Archive & remove worktree** on a session whose cwd is a linked worktree lane (`worktreeLaneForCwd`; never for main checkout / kanban bucket / plain folder). REST in both local and remote mode so the policy lives once, in `worktree_gc`. Lane-level **Remove worktree** goes through reclaim first; the force prompt now shows the backend's reason. Copy updated in all 9 locales (the confirm no longer claims "the branch stays").
- Docs: `user-guide/cli.md` (Worktree cleanup), `user-guide/git-worktrees.md`, `reference/slash-commands.md`.

## Validation

**Rebased onto `origin/main` 0b82d4ce898** (it was DIRTY). Conflicts: main had moved the `/worktree` CLI copy into the locale catalogs. The new strings (`hint_remove`, `remove_usage`, `remove_own_tree`, `kept`, plus the extended `usage`) are now keys in all 17 `locales/*.yaml` packs. Main also split Desktop i18n into `*_projects.ts` / `*_chrome.ts` files and routes git per owner gateway, so `reclaimWorktree` / `reclaimWorktreePath` / `worktreeLaneForCwd` now carry the lane's `owner` route. `locales/_keys.desktop.json` was regenerated. One new commit, `20dcb73f937`, moves the `/worktree prune|remove` bodies into the existing `cli_commands_worktree.py`: with the rebase, `cli_commands_mixin.py` went over its line cap, and it is now shorter than on main. After the rebase: 149 pytest passed (worktree_gc, worktree_command, worktree, snapshot_prune, i18n, subcommands batch), vitest 90 passed (session-actions-menu, projects, sessions-section drag, overlay-completeness), `npm run check:lint` rc 0, `scripts/check --only health` ok.


| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| `scripts/run_tests.sh` on 9 mirrored files (worktree_gc, pushed_tier, worktree, worktree_command, security, selfheal, web_git, web_routers probe + destructive scope) | 147 passed, 0 failed |
| FastAPI TestClient probe against real temp repos: clean → removed + branch deleted; dirty → kept `keep`; main → refused | as expected |
| `hermes worktree remove` on temp repo fixtures: clean removed, dirty rejected exit 1 | as expected |
| Desktop `npm run check:lint` (tsc ×4 + eslint) | 0 errors |
| vitest: projects.test (new `worktreeLaneForCwd` cases), session-actions-menu.test (new verb: absent without a lane, archive + reclaim with one), entered-content, catalog-completeness | 199 passed |
| ruff, check_no_tmp_literals, check-windows-footguns, check_compat_pointers, `git diff --check` | clean |

**Live repro:** before (origin/main) — Desktop's only remove path is `git.worktreeRemove` → plain `git worktree remove [--force]` (`apps/desktop/electron/git-worktree-ops.ts`): the branch is never touched and a dirty tree's git refusal is regex-matched into the force prompt; there is no single-tree CLI/REST verb (`hermes worktree remove` → unknown subcommand). After — live FastAPI + subprocess probe against real temp repos: merged lane → `removed: true, branchDeleted: true`, `git branch` no longer lists it; dirty lane → `removed: false`, reason "uncommitted tracked changes"; main checkout → refused. `hermes worktree remove` on the same fixtures: exit 0 / exit 1 with the reason. **Live Electron pass done** on the final head (section below): the menu item appears only for a worktree session; one click archives the session and reclaims the tree, deleting its merged branch; the dirty tree is kept and the force prompt shows the backend's reason.

## Screenshots (running Electron, final head ae157f08660)

Shots were taken on `20dcb73f937`. The only later commit, `ae157f08660`, adds the `POST /api/git/worktree/reclaim` row to `tests/hermes_cli/serve_handler_ledger.json` (undecided, like its add/remove siblings) and changes no runtime code.

Native Electron 44.9.3 on a private Xvfb with a sealed scratch `HERMES_HOME`. The canonical local gateway runs from the PR worktree. Fixture: a scratch repo `app` with two linked worktrees, `.worktrees/fix-login` (clean, merged) and `.worktrees/wip-dirty` (an uncommitted edit to tracked `api.py`). One real CLI turn ran in each tree and one in the main checkout, which created three sessions whose `cwd` is that tree. The one-shot rows were re-tagged `source=cli` and titled in the scratch `state.db`, because the project tree hides one-shot sessions. Every click is a trusted CDP mouse event on the real Radix menus. For the main leg, all 23 non-test `apps/desktop/src` files the PR touches were swapped to `origin/main` (i18n catalogs included) and the page reloaded; afterwards the head copies were restored and `git status` was clean.

| state | main | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| session row menu, session in a linked worktree | ![main menu](https://gist.githubusercontent.com/teknium1/71ff43420be2949f9bb680b1be4f471d/raw/7e1edcb56b28d0f9bbfcf5c3cd4edcc7cfbd6a2f/reclaim-main-menu-worktree.png) | ![head menu](https://gist.githubusercontent.com/teknium1/71ff43420be2949f9bb680b1be4f471d/raw/7e1edcb56b28d0f9bbfcf5c3cd4edcc7cfbd6a2f/reclaim-head-menu-worktree.png) |
| **Archive & remove worktree** clicked (clean `fix-login`) | *(no such item)* | ![success toast](https://gist.githubusercontent.com/teknium1/71ff43420be2949f9bb680b1be4f471d/raw/7e1edcb56b28d0f9bbfcf5c3cd4edcc7cfbd6a2f/reclaim-head-success-toast.png) |
| lane **Remove worktree…** confirm | ![main confirm](https://gist.githubusercontent.com/teknium1/71ff43420be2949f9bb680b1be4f471d/raw/7e1edcb56b28d0f9bbfcf5c3cd4edcc7cfbd6a2f/reclaim-main-confirm.png) | ![head confirm](https://gist.githubusercontent.com/teknium1/71ff43420be2949f9bb680b1be4f471d/raw/7e1edcb56b28d0f9bbfcf5c3cd4edcc7cfbd6a2f/reclaim-head-confirm.png) |
| confirm → dirty `wip-dirty` | ![main force](https://gist.githubusercontent.com/teknium1/71ff43420be2949f9bb680b1be4f471d/raw/7e1edcb56b28d0f9bbfcf5c3cd4edcc7cfbd6a2f/reclaim-main-force-prompt.png) | ![head force](https://gist.githubusercontent.com/teknium1/71ff43420be2949f9bb680b1be4f471d/raw/7e1edcb56b28d0f9bbfcf5c3cd4edcc7cfbd6a2f/reclaim-head-force-prompt.png) |

DOM readback:

- Menu items on head, `fix-login` session: `… | Move to project | Archive | Delete | Archive & remove worktree`. **Control:** the main-checkout session on head has no such item (`… | Archive | Delete`). On main, a worktree session's menu has no item either.
- Toast on head: `Worktree removed and branch “hermes/fix-login” deleted`. The session leaves the sidebar because it was archived. `git worktree list` afterwards:
  ```
  …/repos/app                      95d522b [main]
  …/repos/app/.worktrees/wip-dirty 95d522b [hermes/wip-dirty]
  ```
  `git branch`: `hermes/wip-dirty`, `main` (`hermes/fix-login` is gone).
- Lane confirm copy: main says "deletes the worktree directory; the branch stays", while head says "deletes the worktree directory and its branch once the work is upstream; untracked files are archived first".
- Dirty tree after confirm: main shows "This worktree has uncommitted changes. Force-remove it …", taken from a regex over git's refusal. Head shows **"This worktree was kept: uncommitted tracked changes (real work). Force-remove it (discards that work), …"**, which is the backend's reason. On both legs the tree is still on disk and `git worktree list` is unchanged.
