prs.title: fix(tools): account for every part of a split send
prs.body:
## What does this PR do?

`_send_chunks` sends a long text as N messages but returns only the **last** chunk's result. Its docstring said so: *"stop at the first error dict, else last result"*. Two consequences for every caller of `hermes send` and of the send-message tool:

1. **A successful split send reports one message id for N visible messages.** The ids of chunks 1..N-1 are dropped on the floor, so nothing can later reference, edit, or audit the head of the reply.
2. **A split send that fails halfway reports a plain error.** Chunks already in the chat are not mentioned at all. A caller that reads `success` (or the CLI exit code) records a delivery that only half happened, and a retry re-sends the part that already landed.

3. **The id list alone cannot be checked for completeness.** A sender that returns success without an id contributes no id, and a sender that split the chunk again on its own limit contributes several, so for a two-part send the list can hold 1 or 3 ids and neither length distinguishes the two cases.

The result now accounts for the whole send:

- on success: `total_chunks`, `message_ids` in send order, and `accounted_chunks` — the number of parts that came back with at least one id, so `accounted_chunks == total_chunks` is the completeness test;
- on a chunk failure after earlier chunks landed: `success: False` plus `partial_success`, `delivered_chunks`, `total_chunks`, `delivered_message_ids` and `accounted_chunks`.

A receipt whose `accounted_chunks` is short of its part count means those parts were sent but cannot be named. That is deliberately not reported as a failure, and such a send must not be retried — the same reason the partial case keeps the ids of the bubbles already in the chat.

`_send_via_adapter` also keeps the `SendResult.continuation_message_ids` that it used to drop. The field is declared and documented in `gateway/platforms/base.py`, and the Telegram, Discord and WhatsApp adapters fill it when they split a chunk again on their own limit. Without it the receipt named one message for several bubbles.

This is the rule this same file already applies to attachments, and not to split text. The `media_dropped` branch sets `success=False` and `partial_success=True` with the comment *"a script reading `success` / exit 0 must not book a delivery that never happened (#115908)"*. This PR extends that rule to the text-split path, and adds the second half of it: a partial delivery must also be able to name what did land.

Key names follow what the repository already uses, so nothing new is invented: `partial_success` comes from the `media_dropped` branch in this file; `message_ids`, `delivered_message_ids`, `delivered_chunks` and `total_chunks` come from the Telegram adapter's partial-send path. `accounted_chunks` is the one name without a precedent — the existing `delivered_chunks` counts parts that landed, which is a different question from how many of them the receipt can name. Happy to rename it if you have a preferred term.

The change is additive. A single-chunk send returns exactly the dict it returns today, and a failure on the first chunk also stays byte for byte the same, because nothing was delivered yet.

## Related Issue

No open issue covers this path. I searched the open issues and PRs before writing the patch; the nearest work changes the adapters' own `send()` and does not touch `tools/send_message_tool.py`: #123947, #124295 and #129679 (resume a split reply from the failed chunk), and #137607 (the delivery ledger replays already-delivered chunks).

The closed bug this PR follows is #115908, the same failure for a dropped media attachment.

Relates to #137607: a ledger cannot skip the chunks that already landed while the tool result does not name them.

## Type of Change

- [x] 🐛 Bug fix (non-breaking change that fixes an issue)
- [ ] ✨ New feature (non-breaking change that adds functionality)
- [ ] 🔒 Security fix
- [ ] 📝 Documentation update
- [ ] ✅ Tests (adding or improving test coverage)
- [ ] ♻️ Refactor (no behavior change)
- [ ] 🎯 New skill (bundled or hub)

## Changes Made

- `tools/send_message_tool.py`
  - `_send_chunks`: collect the id of every delivered chunk, and count the chunks that came back with at least one id. On success with more than one chunk, add `total_chunks`, `message_ids` and `accounted_chunks`. On a chunk failure with earlier chunks delivered, add `success: False`, `partial_success`, `delivered_chunks`, `total_chunks`, `delivered_message_ids` and `accounted_chunks`. Docstring updated to state the contract.
  - `_send_via_adapter`: return `message_ids` when the adapter's `SendResult` accounts for more than one message.
  - New helpers `_ordered_message_ids`, `_adapter_message_ids` and `_chunk_message_ids`. They de-duplicate by first-seen order, because adapters disagree on whether `message_id` is repeated as the last entry of `continuation_message_ids` (the Telegram and Discord overflow splits repeat it, WhatsApp does not).
- `tests/tools/test_send_message_split_receipt.py` (new, 12 cases)

The new test file is kept out of `tests/tools/test_send_message_tool.py` because that module skips wholesale when the optional Telegram dependencies are absent.

## How to Test

Synthetic text only, 4000 + 2000 characters against a 4096-character limit.

1. `pytest tests/tools/test_send_message_split_receipt.py -q` → 12 passed.
2. Negative control, to prove the tests measure the fix: revert `tools/send_message_tool.py` to its state before this branch and run the same file. 8 of the 12 cases fail. The 4 that stay green are the deliberate no-change guards (single chunk, failure on the first chunk, an adapter result with one id, an adapter result without `raw_response`). Reverting only the second commit fails 5 of the 12, which are exactly the `accounted_chunks` assertions.
3. Regression attribution for the suites that exercise `_send_to_platform`, `_send_chunks` and `_send_via_adapter` (`tests/tools`, `tests/cron`, `tests/gateway/test_buzz_adapter.py`, `tests/gateway/test_signal.py`, `tests/gateway/test_cron_delivery_housekeeping.py`, `tests/plugins/platforms/photon/test_runtime_record.py`): run with and without the patch and compare the failures **by name**. Same set on both sides, so no failure is attributable to this change. In my environment 3 pre-existing failures in `tests/cron/test_cron_multiplex_desktop_ticker_scope.py` appear identically with and without the patch.
4. `python scripts/check --commit HEAD` → `15 checks, ok` (`ruff check .` clean, code health 0 blocking / 0 advisory).

What the result looks like for a two-chunk send that fails on the second chunk:

```json
{
  "error": "...",
  "success": false,
  "partial_success": true,
  "delivered_chunks": 1,
  "total_chunks": 2,
  "delivered_message_ids": ["101"],
  "accounted_chunks": 1
}
```

And for a two-chunk send whose second part came back with success but no id — sent, not nameable, not a failure:

```json

  "success": true,
  "total_chunks": 2,
  "message_ids": ["101"],
  "accounted_chunks": 1
}
```

prs.title: fix(telegram): keep an album in one turn and admit document albums (#74965, #150720, #143001, salvage #143647)
prs.body:
If you sent several photos or files together as one Telegram album, Hermes sometimes answered the first one alone (if another was still downloading), then treated the rest as a new message. Two documents sent together were refused outright with `invalid_params: media_text_inlined_length`. Now an album waits for every item that has already arrived and reaches the agent as one message, documents included.

| Live probe (real `hermes gateway run` + real adapter vs the Bot API stand-in + FakeLLMServer) | `origin/main` | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| 2-photo album, caption on #1, #2's download stalls 2.5 s | **2 turns**: caption + 1 image, then 2 images as a second, uncaptioned turn | **1 turn**, caption + 2 images |
| 2 `.txt` documents sent as one album | refused: "⚠️ Hermes refused this message (invalid_params: media_text_inlined_length)" | admitted; one reply; the model saw both files' content |

- **Document albums** (salvage of #143647 by @piotr-iohk): `_merge_into_pending` extended `media_urls`/`media_types` but not `media_text_inlined`, so an album whose items carry explicit flags (every document) failed native admission. The merge now goes through `MessageEvent.extend_media` with padded inline flags (shared `pad_inline_flags`), and the same per-attachment bookkeeping is fixed on the sibling paths that had the same gap: base text batching, cached reply/observed attachments, and Relay media localization.
- **Albums split by a slow sibling download** (#74965, #150720): one chat's updates run one after another and each item is downloaded before it is merged, so the 0.8 s debounce fired while a sibling's handler was still downloading. Each album item now counts as in flight from the moment its handler starts (`telegram_media_group.tracking_album_item`). When the debounce is due, the flush waits for in-flight siblings, bounded at 8 s so a stuck download cannot hold the album; a late item is still delivered, never lost. The wait happens before the event is popped, so the existing re-arm/cancel/hold semantics are unchanged.
- The debounce after the last item rises from 0.8 s to 1.5 s and is configurable as `platforms.telegram.extra.media_group_wait_seconds` (non-numeric/negative → default, capped at 10 s). This covers items Telegram delivers well apart. Documented under "Albums" in the Telegram guide.
- `_queue_media_group_event` / `_flush_media_group_event` bodies move to `plugins/platforms/telegram/telegram_media_group.py`; adapter.py 7385 → 7377.

Root cause: album bookkeeping assumed every item was merged within 0.8 s of the previous one, and only photo-shaped (flagless) events were ever merged.

Fixes #143001, fixes #74965, fixes #150720

Salvages #143647 (@piotr-iohk). The in-flight approach follows #53198 (@VKirill), re-implemented on current main: its diff predates the `_flush_buffered` hold/commit machinery and the per-chat update processor.

## Tests
- `tests/plugins/platforms/telegram/test_album_slow_sibling.py` (new, SDK-free, through `_handle_media_message` in production order): a sibling stalled past the debounce still lands in the one album turn; a stuck sibling is bounded and then delivered on its own. Sabotage: removing only the `tracking_album_item` call site → red.
- Salvaged from #143647: album/text-batch/cached-reply/relay flag tests.
- `scripts/run_tests.sh` on 13 touched/mirroring files: 139 passed, 1 skipped (PTB-gated). `scripts/check`: 15 checks ok.

## Dropped hunks
- None from #143647. #53198 is superseded, not cherry-picked: its flush body (inline sleep loop + task-slot bookkeeping) conflicts with the current `_flush_buffered` hold/commit path, and its counter is decremented only by `_queue_media_group_event`, so an item whose handler returns early (oversized, cache failure, video document) left the album waiting the full 8 s. Here the count is released when the handler returns, on every path.

prs.title: fix(telegram): hermes send, send_message and standalone cron deliver like the gateway: same server, timeouts, formatting, rich, albums and notifications (13 issues)
prs.body:
**ELI5:** Telegram messages Hermes sends outside the gateway (`hermes send`, the agent's `send_message` tool, cron jobs that fall back to standalone delivery) went through a stripped-down copy of the Telegram client. It ignored your Bot API server, timeouts, fallback IPs, rich-message setting and notification mode, and it lost formatting in several ways. That copy now makes the same decisions as the gateway adapter, so a message looks, buzzes and routes the same however it is delivered.

All rows are from a live probe: a real `hermes send` / `send_message_tool` process talking to the in-repo Bot API stand-in through `platforms.telegram.extra.base_url`. "Before" is `origin/main`, except where noted.

| Case | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| Custom `base_url` (#51223) | `Telegram send failed: Unauthorized`: went to api.telegram.org, stand-in got 0 calls | delivered on the stand-in |
| Bot request settings, with `HERMES_TELEGRAM_HTTP_READ_TIMEOUT=33` (#145412, #62936, #20915) | connect 5 / read 5 / write 5 / pool 1 / media_write 20, plain `AsyncHTTPTransport` | 10 / **33** / 20 / 8 / media_write **60**, `TelegramFallbackTransport` |
| Parse error whose text contains `502` (#146922) | 3 MarkdownV2 tries + 1 s + 2 s backoff, then plain (7.6 s) | 1 try → plain (2.4 s) |
| 12 KB Markdown, 3 chunks (#74004) ¹ | every chunk 400 `'(' is reserved` → plain text, bold lost | 3× MarkdownV2 accepted, `*bold*` kept |
| `<details>` plus Markdown (#124413) ¹ | HTML 400 `unsupported start tag` → raw `**…**` | MarkdownV2 accepted, formatting kept |
| Pipe table with `rich_messages: true` (#145606) ¹ | MarkdownV2, table flattened to `*oMLX* • Port: 8000` | `sendRichMessage` with the raw table |
| `\u200b\u2060\ufeff` only (#60848) ¹ | delivered as an empty bubble | not sent (`No deliverable text…`) |
| `notifications: all` in config.yaml (#144895, #131924) ¹ | standalone: `disable_notification` never set, so every send rang | silent under `important` (default), rings under `all`; cron briefs ring via `cron.delivery.notify` |
| 3 photos in one send (#99408) ¹ | `sendPhoto` ×3 | one `sendMediaGroup` of 3 |

¹ "Before" is this branch's first commit (base_url honoured), because on `origin/main` the probe cannot reach the stand-in at all.

**Where it lives.** The standalone sender is now the Telegram plugin's own `standalone_sender_fn`: `plugins/platforms/telegram/standalone.py::standalone_send` (moved out of `tools/send_message_senders.py`). Core's `_send_to_platform` reaches it only through the platform registry, the same seam Signal uses.

**Transport and retries** (`plugins/platforms/telegram/standalone.py::_telegram_bot`, `_telegram_retry_delay`)
- The standalone Bot is built like `TelegramAdapter._build_ptb_requests`:
  - `extra.base_url` / `base_file_url`
  - the adapter's `HERMES_TELEGRAM_HTTP_*` timeouts plus `media_write_timeout=60`
  - the proxy (`TELEGRAM_PROXY` or `extra.proxy_url`)
  - otherwise `TelegramFallbackTransport` over `extra.fallback_ips` or the seed IPs. No DoH runs on a one-shot send.
- Retry classification is one plugin classifier, `telegram_send_errors.send_error_kind`, shared by the text retry, the plain-text fallback and the album sender (gateway and standalone), so the lanes can't disagree:
  - `retry_after` still wins.
  - A connect or pool timeout backs off (#47229). The request never left, so a retry can't duplicate the message.
  - Telegram's own 5xx JSON answer backs off, as on main.
  - Every timeout, a 504, a reset after the write, and a 5xx whose body is a proxy's HTML page are final. Telegram may already have the message.
  - `BadRequest` never retries, whatever digits its text quotes.
  - The plain-text fallback fires only on a real Bot API entity-parse `BadRequest`, never on PTB's "Parsing the server response … failed" for an HTML 502/504 page.

**Formatting** (`standalone.py::_send_telegram`, `_telegram_format`, `_telegram_send_text_chunk`)
- The `(N/M)` chunk marker is escaped for MarkdownV2 and moved off a closing fence (salvage of #126100 / #74040).
- Only Telegram's own HTML tags select HTML mode (salvage of #115014).
- If the Bot API still rejects an HTML chunk (a supported tag next to an unsupported one), it retries as MarkdownV2 before falling back to plain text.
- `rich_messages: true` reuses the adapter's own `_should_attempt_rich` / `_try_send_rich` through an unconnected adapter over the standalone bot. Same gates: CJK, the Desktop details+math crash shape, the 32K cap, the capability latch. Same rule too: a transient rich failure is not resent as legacy.

**Notifications and empty sends**
- The new sibling `plugins/platforms/telegram/telegram_outbound.py` owns `resolve_notifications_mode`, moved out of adapter.py and fixed.
  - Root cause of #144895: the old version passed the `GatewayConfig` dataclass to `cfg_get`, which only walks dicts. The config.yaml key was always ignored, a regression from 5600105478.
  - It now reads the active profile's config.yaml via `load_config_readonly()`.
- The same module owns `notification_kwargs` and `is_visually_empty`, which the adapter's `send()` and the standalone sender now share.
- `_send_to_platform(notify=)` rings regardless of mode. Cron's standalone lane passes `cron.delivery.notify`, so a brief rings in both lanes, keeping #92929's intent. `hermes send` and `send_message` stay silent under `important`, as gateway non-final sends do.

**Albums**
- Two or more still photos (no caption, GIF, voice note or forced document) go through `telegram_album.send_photo_album`, the same sender as the adapter's `send_multiple_images`, over the standalone bot: 10 per album. Mixed batches keep one upload per file.
- An album that may already be in the chat (a timeout, any 5xx answer, a reset after the write) is reported with a "not resent" warning and never resent per photo. Only a refusal falls back photo by photo, with one warning per failed or unreadable photo. A stale forum topic retries once without the thread.

**Other**
- Ratchets: `adapter.py` is 7,385 → 7,241 lines (the standalone sender, request builder and notification policy moved into plugin siblings).
- Boundary-lint baseline: 7 removals, no additions. Core no longer imports `plugins.platforms.telegram.*` for sends, and the plugin no longer imports `tools.send_message_tool._send_telegram` or `gateway.run.cfg_get`.
- `standalone_sender_fn` contract: `notify` is optional. It is forwarded only to a sender that declares it (or `**kwargs`), so a user plugin re-registering telegram with the documented signature keeps working.
- Under `HERMES_SAFE_MODE` a standalone Telegram send reports `telegram plugin not registered or missing standalone_sender_fn`, because Telegram is a plugin and safe mode skips plugin discovery. This matches the live gateway: in safe mode Telegram is not registered and has no built-in fallback, so no adapter is created either (probed).
- Docs: `telegram.md` sections for `base_url`, fallback IPs, rich messages and notifications now cover the standalone lane. `adding-platform-adapters.md` names the plugin's standalone sender and documents `notify` as optional.

Fixes #51223, fixes #62936, fixes #20915, fixes #47229, fixes #145412, fixes #146922, fixes #74004, fixes #124413, fixes #145606, fixes #60848, fixes #131924, fixes #144895, fixes #99408

Salvages, with authorship kept:
- @kouyichi's fork branch for #146922
- #126100 (@AureliusClaw, carrying #74040 by @Tranquil-Flow and @w-Teilchen)
- #115014 (@i-Hun)

Co-authored with #145428 / #144941 (@locker95), #119934 (@OsmanSujoy), #125409 (@linfeng961), #131933 (@liuhao1024), #60865 (@LavyaTandel) and #99419 (@djagya).

## Dropped hunks
- #125409's 60 s standalone read-timeout default: uses the adapter's 20 s default plus the env override, so the two lanes can't drift. Uploads use the separate 60 s `media_write_timeout`.
- #119934's `exc.__cause__ isinstance httpx.ConnectError` check: replaced by the adapter's graph-walking `_looks_like_connect_timeout` / `_looks_like_pool_timeout`. A refused connect surfaces as a PTB `NetworkError` and still backs off.
- #115014's move of `separate_chunk_indicator_from_fence` into `gateway/platforms/helpers.py`: #126100 already reuses the adapter's helper, so only the HTML whitelist and its tests are kept.
- #131933's unconditional silencing: cron's standalone lane would have gone mute. Re-probed, it passes `notify=cron.delivery.notify` (see the test below).
- #144941's `gateway.run._load_gateway_config` read: `load_config_readonly()` is the published config API and is profile-scoped through `get_hermes_home()`.
- #99419's live-gateway-adapter dispatch for albums: this file's Telegram path never routes through the live adapter (gateway/relay/egress.py relies on that), so the album uses the standalone bot like every other standalone send.

## Tests
92 focused files (tools send_message/telegram, `tests/plugins/platforms/telegram/`, `tests/gateway/test_telegram_*`, cron delivery, boundary lint) → 983 passed, 3 skipped. `tests/tools/` + `tests/plugins/platforms/telegram/` → 11,402 passed. The 1 failure + 1 error there (`test_process_registry::…compound_and_background`, `test_fal_sdk` collection) reproduce on a clean origin/main worktree, so they are environment-red, not from this PR.
- New test files: `tests/tools/test_telegram_standalone_send_parity.py` (drives `_send_to_platform`), `tests/plugins/platforms/telegram/test_outbound_policy.py` (drives `_build_adapter` and `adapter.send`), plus a cron case in `test_cron_live_delivery_confirmation.py`.
- Red on the pre-change sources: 16 failures, plus a separate album red run.
- Review round: 504 / 502 / HTML-5xx album and text cases (standalone and adapter), a narrow-signature plugin sender through the real registry lookup, and an unreadable album photo; each red on the previous head.
- Sabotage: cutting only one call-site wiring turns its test red. Wirings cut: `notify=` in cron, `notify=` in `_send_to_platform`, `extra=` in `_send_to_platform`, the resolver in `_build_adapter`.

prs.title: Quick commands can be saved prompts, sent from any chat or a Desktop Review pane button (Inspired by Amp)
prs.body:
A `quick_commands` entry can now be a saved prompt: `/release-notes v2.3` sends your configured text to the agent from the CLI, TUI, Desktop and every messaging platform, and `review_button` puts it in the Desktop Review pane as a one-click action.

```yaml
quick_commands:
  release-notes:
    type: prompt
    description: Release notes
    prompt: "Write release notes for {args} from the commits since the last tag."
    review_button: true      # or a label string
```

## Changes
- `hermes_cli/quick_commands.py`: `render_prompt_quick_command` (`{args}` substitutes what follows the command; without the placeholder args are appended as a paragraph) and `review_button_label`.
- Classic CLI (`cli.py::_run_quick_command`): `prompt` queues the rendered text as the next turn.
- TUI / Desktop gateway (`tui_gateway/methods_tools.py` dispatch, `tui_gateway/command_discovery.py` catalog): `command.dispatch` answers a `send` directive; `slash.exec` reroutes prompt commands to `command.dispatch`, since the slash worker would queue the text on its own CLI input, which nothing drains. `commands.catalog` marks them `argument_mode: text` and carries `review_button` (contract field + regenerated `apps/shared` outputs).
- Messaging gateway (`gateway/run_inbound_hooks.py`): the prompt replaces `event.text` and dispatch falls through to the agent. It still goes through the existing `_check_slash_access` gate first.
- Desktop: `ReviewPromptButtons` in the Review pane renders every `review_button` prompt from the live catalog (`$desktopCommandsCatalog`). A click submits `/<name>` into the chat that owns the changes, through the same slash path as typing it (busy → queued).
- Docs: configuration, CLI and slash-command reference. `no_prompt` error strings are in all 17 locales, and every `unsupported_type` message now lists `prompt`.
- Gateway-owned local sessions (`gateway/session_commands.py`, the path Desktop and the TUI now send slash commands through): its quick-command resolution admitted only `alias`/`exec`, so a Review pane click answered `error: unsupported_command`. A prompt command now returns a `send` directive through the same unregistered-command branch skills use (`session:submit`, local-source, history-mount and admission gates) plus `_check_slash_access`; an alias to a prompt command follows through.
- Rebased onto main, which had already split the gateway quick-command dispatch into `run_inbound_hooks.py` and the catalog into `command_discovery.py`; the prompt branch lives there now (the PR's own `run_quick_commands.py` / `methods_quick_commands.py` siblings are gone). The new TUI test has its own file.

## Validation
| Surface | origin/main | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| Classic CLI, real `hermes chat --cli` in tmux, `openai-api` / gpt-5-nano, isolated HOME | `Quick command '/rn' has unsupported type (supported: 'exec', 'alias')` | state.db user row `Reply with exactly the word PINEAPPLE followed by the version: v2.3`, assistant `PINEAPPLE v2.3` |
| Real `python -m tui_gateway.entry` over stdio: `session.create` → `slash.exec rn v2.3` | `{"output": "Quick command '/rn' has unsupported type ..."}` | `{"type": "send", "message": "Reply with exactly the word PINEAPPLE ... v2.3"}` |
| Same process, `commands.catalog` `/rn` meta | `None` | `{argument_mode: text, desktop: None, review_button: "Release notes"}` |

Both trees were built the same way (`git archive origin/main` vs `git archive HEAD`). Live spend was 1 gpt-5-nano call, under $0.01.

Tests: 3 new invariants (CLI queue, gateway event rewrite, TUI send + catalog flag), all red on origin/main sources and green here. 257 tests pass across the quick-command, slash-access, catalog, contract and i18n suites. One vitest covers the Review pane button (renders only `review_button` entries, submits `/rn` to the owning chat), and `check:lint` (tsc + eslint) is clean.

**Verified live since:** the Desktop Review pane click and the typed slash in running Electron with real Nous turns, and a Telegram round trip on the stand-in (see Screenshots). New `tests/gateway/test_session_prompt_quick_commands.py` (4 cases) is red on main's `session_commands.py` and green here. Not covered: a real (non-stand-in) messaging platform.

## Source material (Amp)
- Amp's Puck docs, "Send Saved Prompts": https://ampcode.com/docs/puck#send-saved-prompts
- Amp Chronicle, 2026-10-06 "Many, Many Pucks": https://ampcode.com/news/many-many-pucks (the docs refresh that surfaced the Prompts page)

**Their mechanism:** named prompts are kept in Personal or Workspace Settings → Prompts. Personal prompts beat workspace prompts with the same name. A meta-agent or the thread agent can send one by name ("ship it", "use release-notes"), and checking "Show as a button in the Changes tab" puts it in the diff view.

**Ours vs theirs:** hermes already had the substrate (`quick_commands` slash dispatch on every surface, plus the Review pane's `requestComposerSubmit` path that powers "Ask Hermes to open PR"), but quick commands could only run a shell command or alias another slash command. Users who wanted a reusable prompt had to write a whole skill, which also adds to the skills index in the system prompt. This PR adds the missing type, with no system-prompt cost and the same precedence and access rules as existing quick commands. We skip their workspace tier, since hermes has no multi-user workspace, and we skip agent-invocable prompts. A model-callable prompt registry would mean a new tool or index entry, which is a separate design call.

## Screenshots (running Electron, final head b3870654a61)
Private Xvfb, real Electron + Vite dev renderer, sealed scratch HOME/HERMES_HOME, real gateway spawned by the app from this worktree, real Nous Portal turns (anthropic/claude-opus-5.5). Scratch git repo with one uncommitted change to `app.py`; workspace folder set through the session store's `setCurrentCwd` (the folder picker's call). Config: `release-notes: {type: prompt, review_button: Release notes, prompt: ...{args}...}` plus an exec control.

| origin/main (same instance, renderer files swapped to main) | this PR |
|---|---|
| ![main](https://gist.githubusercontent.com/teknium1/95fa29cf1f5edec50919d7823da76b54/raw/b5cd1c4ae236a6c2a85d35d901aaf55500f7c2df/main-review-pane.png) No button above the commit box | ![head](https://gist.githubusercontent.com/teknium1/95fa29cf1f5edec50919d7823da76b54/raw/b5cd1c4ae236a6c2a85d35d901aaf55500f7c2df/head-review-pane.png) `Release notes` button above the commit box |

| Review pane click → real turn | Typed `/release-notes (final head)` in the composer → real turn |
|---|---|
| ![click](https://gist.githubusercontent.com/teknium1/95fa29cf1f5edec50919d7823da76b54/raw/b5cd1c4ae236a6c2a85d35d901aaf55500f7c2df/head-button-turn.png) | ![typed](https://gist.githubusercontent.com/teknium1/95fa29cf1f5edec50919d7823da76b54/raw/b5cd1c4ae236a6c2a85d35d901aaf55500f7c2df/head-typed-turn.png) |

Before the `session_commands.py` fix in this push, the same click on the rebased head answered `/release-notes · error: unsupported_command` ([shot](https://gist.githubusercontent.com/teknium1/95fa29cf1f5edec50919d7823da76b54/raw/b5cd1c4ae236a6c2a85d35d901aaf55500f7c2df/pre-fix-unsupported-command.png)): Desktop slash commands now go through the gateway-owned local session path, which main added after this PR was opened.

state.db `messages` user rows (scratch home, read-only), `source=local`:

prs.title: fix(context): safely finalize plugin preparation and cancelled lookups
prs.body:
## Summary

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    R[Assemble request] --> S[Context-engine selection]
    S -->|selected context| P[Provider dispatch]
    S -->|ContextEngineError| F[Classified failure + display-only boundary]
    S -->|requested cancellation| I[Normal interrupted turn]
    T[Cancelled context-engine lookup] --> C[Pair every pending tool call]
    C --> I
```

Add optional preparation progress/cancellation callbacks to `ContextEngine.select_context()`, using the real activity tracker and live interrupt flag. Filter keyword arguments for legacy engines; ordinary selection exceptions retain their existing fail-open behavior. A typed `ContextEngineError` instead prevents dispatch of unsafe unselected history.

Live configuration now limits compressor-private policy writes to `ContextCompressor`; third-party engines receive context-window changes through public `update_model()` on the unchanged route. Preparation stays in the topical request-assembly module, keeping the turn-loop code-health ratchets intact. No OptChat-specific code, provider changes, or automatic retries are introduced.

**Related:** #149912, #103410. **Overlap:** existing PR #103411 already addresses the private-compressor hot-reload assumption. This branch additionally implements preparation errors, progress/cancellation, cancelled-tool pairing, and public model-window updates. The overlapping guard should be coordinated with that author/maintainers or rebased after it lands; this is not a request to block or replace that narrower fix.

Concrete consumer: [OptChat plugin PR #1](https://github.com/Dinkum/Hermes-OptChat-Plugin/pull/1), whose preparation waits and exact-history lookups need this generic host contract. The plugin PR depends on this host contract.

## Evidence

**Before — clean upstream `6b21d056`:** the initial contract regressions produce **13 failures / 4 passes**: missing callbacks/fail-closed error type and private compressor calls on a genuine third-party `ContextEngine`.

Additional review reproductions showed a cancelled context lookup escaping turn finalization, and preparation-error detail entering assistant history without a local failure verdict.

**After:** **121 core tests passed**: 15 new preparation/live-reload cases plus 106 existing upstream regressions. The matching plugin passed **65 cases** (**186 total**, 19 files). The new tests use real turns and a loopback HTTP provider instead of private selection-helper mocks. The regressions verify:

- selected request context reaches dispatch without rewriting the canonical transcript;
- preparation failures make zero provider calls, report the existing `host_error` classification, and keep error detail out of model history;
- requested cancellation finalizes normally; cancelled lookups retain a matching result for every emitted tool call;
- unrequested selection interrupts propagate and legacy signatures remain usable;
- live pin application/removal uses the public plugin contract without writing native compressor policy;
- preserved-thinking replay and message-identity regressions remain green after moving the private selection helper and its callers.

Reproduce the focused host cases with the repository test environment:

```sh
scripts/run_tests.sh \
  tests/agent/test_context_engine_host_callbacks.py \
  tests/tui_gateway/test_context_engine_plugin_live_reload.py \
  -j 2 --file-retries 0 -q
python scripts/check --base 6b21d0564de0492e2ebd0d8f63fca86c03b5c892
```

**All 14 `scripts/check` gates passed**, with zero blocking/advisory code-health findings. A real stock Desktop HTTP/WebSocket backend also completed a cold resume and exact OptChat search/zoom using a scripted loopback HTTP provider; SQLite integrity checks passed. No real credentials or live profiles were used. This is not a real-model or graphical-renderer claim.

The matched branches also detected **23 targeted injected faults** in disposable, import-verified source overlays. This exposed and closed blind spots in cancellation responsiveness, historical filesystem reads and compression decision boundaries; it is not an exhaustive mutation-coverage claim.

Verification scope: Linux, focused tests and static gates only. The full Hermes suite and macOS/Windows execution have **not** been run.

## Merge Danger

**Door:** Two-way for core code; coordinate rollback with plugins requiring the new exception/callback contract.

**Blast Radius:** Context-engines

Ordinary selection exceptions deliberately still fail open; only engines raising the new typed error opt into fail-closed dispatch. Progress callbacks must represent committed work, not idle heartbeat ticks. Cancellation must preserve tool-call/result pairing and use normal finalization.

The live-config path changes how third-party engines receive context-window changes; native compressor policy must remain unchanged. No database migration is added to core. Do not roll back the host alone while leaving a plugin that imports `ContextEngineError` installed.

prs.title: feat(plugin-catalog): bump super-artifacts to 0.199.1 (dashboard Connect page and Webhooks card)
prs.body:
## What does this PR do?

[**Super Artifacts for Hermes →**](https://github.com/Super-Artifacts/plugins/tree/b27887e03cc0587252fa3753844c3f003dabbf42/hermes#readme)

SHA bump (rule 4) for the existing `super-artifacts` entry: `dce02981a179a09dad6509fe58a3a7b8cf020735` (0.141.0) → `b27887e03cc0587252fa3753844c3f003dabbf42` (0.199.1). Submitted by @ximxim, an administrator of the plugin repository (rule 5). The old pin is the no-code portable package. The new one adds a Hermes dashboard tab where a person presses **Connect** and approves a device code on superartifacts.app, so no terminal step is needed to sign in. The same tab now has a **Webhooks** card: with the connected account it creates the Super Artifacts webhook endpoint and writes the matching dynamic route into the current profile, so nothing is copied or pasted.

## What changed in the package

- `mcp.json` now sends `Authorization: Bearer ${SUPER_ARTIFACTS_KEY}`; `plugin.json` declares that key as a `config_schema` secret so Desktop renders a field.
- New `dashboard/` (manifest, `plugin_api.py`, built `dist/index.js`): Connect, status, recent artifacts, Disconnect, and Webhooks (status, Configure, Send test, Rotate secret, Remove).
- Skill: asks for a fresh viewer URL when the person wants to see an artifact and uses `desktop_preview` where it exists.
- `requires_hermes` goes from `>=0.21.5` to `>=0.23.0` (the backend uses 0.23.0 gateway and MCP APIs and returns 503 "Update Hermes" on older). 0.23.0 is the current release.
- `image` / `screenshots` re-pinned to the new sha; one screenshot that no longer exists was dropped. `known_issues` no longer carries the mandatory terminal step.

## Disclosure (rule 13)

- **Network.** Tool calls go to `https://superartifacts.app/mcp`. The dashboard backend (`httpx`, no redirects) also calls `/v1/whoami`, `/v1/artifacts`, `/v1/artifacts/<id>/open`, and the OAuth device endpoints (`/oauth/register`, `/oauth/device_authorization`, `/oauth/token`) on the same origin. Nothing else. No telemetry.
- **Credential (rule 11, please read).** On approval the backend saves the access token it received from that device flow to the profile `.env` as `SUPER_ARTIFACTS_KEY` with `hermes_cli.config.save_env_value`, reads it back with `get_env_value`, and removes it with `remove_env_value`. It does not read `.env` files or `auth.json` itself, but it does not use `agent.secret_scope.get_secret` either. It never refreshes or rotates the token. Tell me if you want that read moved to `get_secret` before merge.
- **Core imports (rule 9).** It only reads and adds, never replaces core functions. It imports non-public Hermes modules: `tools.mcp_tool_config._load_mcp_config`, `tools.mcp_tool_discovery._connect_server`, `tools.mcp_tool_loop`, `hermes_cli.mcp_config._resolve_mcp_server_config`, `hermes_cli.gateway_runtime`, `hermes_cli.gateway_client`. Expect those as validator warnings, not failures.
- **Gateway.** After Connect or Disconnect it asks the profile's running gateway for `reload.mcp` over Hermes's own client. If Hermes asks for confirmation it stops and tells the person to run `/reload-mcp`; it never starts a gateway or approves a reload. It fails cleanly when no gateway is running.
- **Page JavaScript** never receives the key. Connect is started only by a person pressing the button.
- **Capabilities.** Empty: the package registers no tools, hooks or middleware; tools come from the MCP server. Artifacts are private by default and the skill never widens access unless asked. Hermes does not prompt before these tools run unless `trust: untrusted` is set.

- **Webhooks card.** Besides the endpoints above, the backend calls `/v1/webhooks` (create, list, delete, `/test`, `/rotate`) on the same origin with the saved key. The signing secret is returned once to the Python backend and written with `hermes_cli.webhook._replace_subscription` to the profile's dynamic webhook route store; it is never sent to page JavaScript, logs or responses. The backend probes only the profile's own local listener `/health` (loopback, no redirects). A public HTTPS address that forwards to that listener is still needed and is entered once in the card. **The card never enables, starts or restarts a gateway**; if the listener is off it tells the person to enable Webhooks in Hermes themselves and that applying it restarts the gateway. A 2xx from the listener means accepted, never that an agent finished. One more non-public import: `hermes_cli.webhook` helpers and `gateway.config.load_gateway_config`.

- **Shared gateways.** For a profile served by a shared (multiplexed) gateway the card saves the route in the gateway-discovered owner store and the profile's own, with the `/p/<profile>/webhooks/...` path Hermes requires. The person enters one public HTTPS address once; nothing on this computer is probed to guess it. `hermes plugins validate` reports the security scan as **safe**.

## Type of Change

- [x] ✨ Catalog SHA bump (existing entry)

## Changes Made

- `plugin-catalog/super-artifacts.yaml` only.

## Validation

Ran `hermes plugins validate hermes` (Hermes 0.23.0, macOS) on a checkout of the pinned commit: portable manifest, manifest fields, config schema valid; security scan: safe; passed. The dashboard flow (Connect through a real device approval, status, Disconnect) was exercised with the live harness in a throwaway `HERMES_HOME`. The Webhooks card was exercised there with a real separate dashboard and webhook listener: Configure wrote the route (secret stored, never printed), a valid HMAC POST returned 202, a bad signature 401, then rotate and remove. Not proved: external HTTPS forwarding (the fixture forwards to loopback) and a model replying through MCP. `scripts/validate_plugin_catalog.py plugin-catalog/super-artifacts.yaml` passes, and `hermes plugins validate` on the pinned checkout reports the security scan as safe.

prs.title: feat(plugin-catalog): add cortive plugin
prs.body:
## Add `cortive`: Cortive Memory

**Hermes remembers what you tell it. Cortive remembers what you saved.** This memory provider adds [Cortive](https://github.com/KadenDevAi/cortive-releases), a private knowledge base for the Mac, to the agent's memory, alongside Hermes's built-in memory. Hermes recalls the pages, PDFs, screenshots, documents and notes the user saved, finds them by meaning (through the Cortive app's on-device model) and answers with the date and source.

- Plugin: https://github.com/KadenDevAi/hermes-cortive (MIT, pinned at `3eb2f4935994c6b7ea0d7067428d3051f9388fc6`)
- Cortive app: free public beta, https://github.com/KadenDevAi/cortive-releases
- Submitted by the repository owner (rule 5).

### What it does

- **Automatic recall** (`prefetch`): up to three captures, 1,200 characters at most, labelled as quoted reference material. With the Cortive app running, relevance is judged by meaning: on 50 everyday prompts it attached something to 7, while recalling the right capture for 48 of 51 questions about saved material. Without the app it recalls only when the message refers to saved material.
- **Tools** (from `get_tool_schemas`): `cortive_search` (ranked; source and date filters; typo correction), `cortive_get` (a capture in full, paged; screenshot export), `cortive_collections` (the whole library in one call).

### Public plugin surfaces used

`ctx.register_memory_provider()`, plus `ctx.register_hook()` for two tool hooks (below). The `MemoryProvider` ABC (`initialize`, `is_available`, `unavailable_reason`, `system_prompt_block`, `prefetch`, `queue_prefetch` via `spawn_context_thread`, `recall_status`, `get_tool_schemas`, `handle_tool_call`, `get_config_schema`, `save_config`, `on_session_end`, `shutdown`), `is_trivial_prompt`, `RecallStatus`. One new instance per agent; all state on the instance; no core overrides; no self-updating; no credential reads. `provides_tools` is empty because the tools come through the memory provider, not `register_tool`; `provides_hooks` lists `pre_tool_call` and `transform_tool_result`, matching `plugin.yaml` (`hermes plugins validate`: declared tools and hooks match registrations).

### Disclosures (rule 13)

- **Reads a file outside the plugin's data:** the Cortive library, `~/Library/Application Support/cortive-ai/cortive.db`, opened with SQLite `mode=ro` + `query_only`. Never written.
- **Local connection:** the Cortive app's owner-only Unix socket on the same Mac (`~/Library/Application Support/Cortive/agent/search.sock`, folder 0700, socket 0600, other uids refused). Sends the search text; receives capture ids and scores only. Search-only; if the app isn't running, nothing is sent.
- **Writes** only inside `<hermes home>/plugin-data/cortive/`: an optional `config.json` and screenshots exported by `cortive_get`.
- **No network calls, no credentials, no background services, no telemetry.**
- **Model exposure:** recalled excerpts reach whichever model Hermes uses, like any context. Before that, things that look like passwords, keys, PINs and card numbers are replaced across the whole capture (text, titles and links, so paging or excerpts can't cut past the label), searches can't confirm a guessed password, and the agent is told not to look one up another way; invisible formatting characters are removed, and captured text is labelled as untrusted.
- **Tool hooks (enforcement, not just instructions):** `pre_tool_call` refuses another tool's call whose arguments point at Cortive's data folder or `cortive.db`. `transform_tool_result` replaces any password saved in Cortive (also reversed or base64) in other tools' output, so a file read, disk search or web page can't hand it to the model. Values are read from the local library in a background thread when Hermes starts; afterwards a check costs well under a millisecond. Limits, stated in the README: a password must be recognisable as one, values under 6 characters are hidden only in Cortive's own results, images aren't read, and the user's approval settings still decide which files and commands the agent may use. The plugin switches itself off in group chats, channels and threads unless the user enables `shared_chats`.

### Testing

- `hermes plugins validate .`: passed, security scan **safe**. `hermes plugins doctor`: loads clean.
- 82 offline unit tests (synthetic fixture library, no real data) on Python 3.11, 3.12 and 3.14, and against Hermes 0.21.5 source (the declared floor) and current Hermes. Both hooks exist with the same contract in 0.21.5, and were checked firing through current Hermes's `handle_function_call`.
- Clean-room install: the real Cortive 0.2.0 app run with an empty home folder, from the installer through the search-model download, a first capture and a first Hermes answer. The plugin says clearly when Cortive isn't installed, when its library is empty, and while the model is still downloading (word search until it's ready). Dates follow the user's time zone (`HERMES_TIMEZONE`, else the Mac's).
- Real Hermes chats (in-process `AIAgent`) on a 91-capture library and a 3,085-document library: 18/18 task questions answered correctly; 7/7 personal questions on GLM 5.3, Kimi K2 and DeepSeek V4 Flash (6/7 on Claude Haiku 4.5, Mistral Small 3.2 and GPT-5 mini, word-only runs).
- Planted prompt injections (fake system notes, a disguised "formatting preference", link-dump requests): 0 of 18 succeeded on DeepSeek V4 Flash after hardening. Password red-team: 40 attacks (direct, authority claims, jailbreaks, encodings, role-play, guess-confirming, multi-turn) × 3 runs on DeepSeek V4 Flash, with every non-Cortive tool simulated as succeeding and returning the original note: 0 of 120 leaked the password. Before the hooks, 0 leaked but 6 of 120 tried another route (Cortive's database, a disk search, the router page); the database read is now refused before it runs and the disk search came back with the password hidden.
- Performance: 80 ms typical / 277 ms worst word search on 48,780 captures; meaning search through the app 11 ms typical on a real library.
- Robustness: Cortive quitting, crashing and restarting mid-session (0 errors to the agent, automatic fallback to word search), a locked library, 2,000-round sessions without leaks.

### Known issues

Listed in the entry: needs the Cortive app (macOS, Apple silicon); meaning search needs Cortive 0.2.0+ running; voice recordings have no transcript.

prs.title: feat(kanban): kanban.assignee_aliases — map board assignee names onto claimable profiles
prs.body:
## Problem

Kanban assignees must be on-disk Hermes profile ids: the dispatcher's spawn gate checks `profile_exists(assignee)`, and a card addressed to a name that does not resolve to a profile directory is parked `skipped_nonspawnable` — forever and silently, with `hermes kanban reassign` as the only per-card remedy (find it via diagnostics, then reassign by hand).

This bites whenever boards address agents by **persona name**. The most common case is the installation-root profile: satellites author cards addressed to a persona such as `chief`, while the canonical id of that profile is `default` (the root profile's home IS the installation directory, so no `profiles/<persona>/` directory exists for it). Today nothing maps the persona to the id:

- `normalize_profile_name()` only case-folds the literal `default` (#18498 solved case, not names);
- `profile display_name` is presentation-only — resolution/comparison/spawn always use `name`;
- `kanban.dispatch_profiles` is a claim allowlist, not a name mapping;
- `kanban.default_assignee` only applies when the assignee field is empty.

So a card whose board name means work gets the same treatment as a typo — and the only difference between the two shows up in a diagnostics sweep half an hour later.

## Feature: `kanban.assignee_aliases`

```yaml
kanban:
  assignee_aliases:
    chief: default   # cards authored for the `chief` persona run under `default`
```

- Read per dispatch pass (same loader family as `kanban.dispatch_profiles`) — config edits apply without a gateway restart.
- When a ready card's assignee has no on-disk profile, the dispatcher resolves the name here; on a hit whose target itself exists, ownership is **mutated on the row** (routing around it would lie on the board) and an `assigned` event records `{assignee, from, source: kanban.assignee_aliases}`; the mapped profile is spawned **in the same tick**.
- **Fail-open by design**: an unreadable, non-mapping or malformed value returns no target and the card stays in the pre-existing `skipped_nonspawnable` bucket — a typo in the mapping must never change card ownership on its own. A mapping to another missing target is also ignored (`profile_exists(target)` gate).
- Reportable: `DispatchResult.alias_rerouted: list[{task_id, from, assignee}]` — same act-and-surface class as the existing `auto_assigned_default` — plus a `Rerouted (old -> new via kanban.assignee_aliases): <task>` line on CLI dispatch passes.
- `dry_run` projects the reroute (and the spawn) without persisting anything.

## Bundle context (commit 1)

`test_kanban_cli_dispatch_passthrough.py` / `test_kanban_per_profile_cap.py` fixtures stop deleting `hermes_cli*` modules from `sys.modules`: that surgery split the plugin-manager singleton between pre-delete holders and call-time re-imports, so hook subscribers registered by other test files fired into a stale manager (observed with cross-file dispatch-tick hooks). Env is already monkeypatched and home resolution reads `HERMES_HOME` dynamically on every call, so the purge bought nothing; the `per_profile_cap` fixture keeps its memory-sample neutralizer re-apply as harmless idempotent defense.

## Tests

New `tests/hermes_cli/test_kanban_dispatch_assignee_alias.py`:

1. reroute + same-tick spawn under the mapped profile (ownership, `assigned` event with `from`/`source`, `alias_rerouted`, spawn);
2. `dry_run` projects the reroute and spawn without writing any event and without touching ownership;
3. no alias key → the pre-existing `skipped_nonspawnable` behavior byte-for-byte;
4. alias to a missing target → fail-open, ownership untouched, card stays in the skip bucket.

`8 passed` over the three affected test files against `upstream/main` (`bda3a363`) in an isolated test tree. The alias path has also been smoke-tested against a live multi-profile install where a persona→id mapping is the primary board configuration.

## Docs

`kanban.assignee_aliases` documented in the dispatcher config YAML example and the params table of `website/docs/user-guide/features/kanban.md`.

## Compatibility

No behavior change without the key: unset means today's semantics exactly (verified by test 3).

prs.title: fix(telegram): private-topic replies keep their topic on retry and reach the chat when the topic is gone (#136808, #137568, #95517, #35739, salvage #136811)
prs.body:
Before: when Telegram refused a reply in a private DM topic (deleted reply target, deleted topic, topics turned off in the client, or a native DM topic that only takes `direct_messages_topic_id`), Hermes threw away all routing at once — media fell out into the root chat, and text was lost because the fallback re-sent the same dead thread. Now each retry removes only what failed: a deleted anchor keeps the topic, a dead `message_thread_id` is tried once as the native topic id, and a topic that is really gone gets the reply in the root chat with its stale binding pruned.

| Probe (real `hermes gateway run` + real adapter vs Bot API stand-in, topic 500) | origin/main | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| Photo reply, first `sendPhoto` → "message to be replied not found" | retry sent with `message_thread_id=None` (root chat) | retry keeps `message_thread_id=500`, only the anchor dropped |
| Every send with a thread → "message thread not found" (topics off) | answer lost; ~33 s later a "♻️ Recovered reply" notice lands in root | answer delivered to root (no thread, no anchor) right away; binding pruned; next root DM answered normally |
| Native DM topic: `message_thread_id` rejected, `direct_messages_topic_id` accepted | answer lost, then "Recovered reply" notice in root | answer delivered with `direct_messages_topic_id=500` (still in the topic) |

- `plugins/platforms/telegram/telegram_dm_topic_send.py` (new): `direct_topic_retry_kwargs` (the same topic by its native id, once) and `dead_topic_retry_kwargs` (no route, and no anchor in a private chat).
- `_send_chunk_with_retries`: a private-topic "thread not found" goes native id → chat root + prune, instead of returning the non-retryable failure that sent `base._send_with_retry`'s plain-text fallback into the same dead thread (#95517). A deleted anchor drops just the anchor (#136808).
- `_send_with_dm_topic_reply_anchor_retry` (every media kind and media groups): same ladder as a 3-step loop; a deleted anchor no longer drops `message_thread_id` (#35739, #136808).
- `_send_overflow_continuation`: an anchor retry keeps the topic routing kwargs instead of `{}` (from #136811).
- `_send_message_with_thread_fallback` (approvals, pickers, slash-confirm follow-ups): native id first, then root without the foreign anchor.
- Topic-mode cleanup is the existing `delete_telegram_topic_binding` (removing the chat's last binding disables topic mode), so after topics are turned off the root DM works again. The remaining atom of #95517 (refreshing `has_topics_enabled`) is unnecessary: once the bindings are gone recovery has nothing to steer into, and the live probe shows the next root DM answered by the model.
- #87051 kept: anchor-less synthetic sends still prefer `message_thread_id`. `direct_messages_topic_id` is only a retry after Telegram rejects the thread id, so #137568 is fixed for every path (delivery retry, startup recovery, watcher notifications, cron, `send_message`) in one adapter seam, with no core edits.
- `adapter.py` 7,385 → 7,378 lines; boundary lint unchanged; `scripts/check --only health` ok.
- Docs: telegram.md § Under the hood.

Root cause: on a Telegram rejection, the private-topic retry ladders dropped every routing key together (media: thread + anchor; overflow: `{}`; text: no retry at all), so a recoverable error turned into a root-chat or lost message.

Tests: `tests/gateway/test_telegram_thread_fallback.py`: the contributor's media/overflow expectations flipped to "keep thread", plus `test_control_message_to_dead_private_topic_lands_in_root_without_its_anchor` and the entry-point `test_reply_into_dead_private_topic_reaches_chat_root_and_prunes_binding` (through `adapter.send` with a real `SessionDB`). 12 tests are red with origin/main's adapter.py and green on this head. 16 Telegram/topic test files → 174 passed, 0 failed.

Fixes #136808, fixes #137568, fixes #95517, fixes #35739

Salvages #136811 (@KoNit-K): cherry-picked, authorship kept. Supersedes #137569 (@zhang5690889): same native-id outcome without touching 14 core files. Supersedes #35759 (@Tranquil-Flow): it stripped `message_thread_id` when an anchor was present, which conflicts with #87051. Supersedes #93874 (@ptillemans): its core `base.py` fallback rewrite is replaced by the adapter-side ladder.

## Dropped hunks
- #136811's fail-closed `private_topic_route` flag on control sends: it raised on a dead topic, so the reply was lost. Replaced by the native-id → root ladder (re-probed: the control-message test asserts the three routes).
- #137569's metadata augmentation in delivery/startup/notifications/turn/cron/send_message: the adapter retry covers every caller, and core stays free of Telegram logic.
- #93874's `gateway/platforms/base.py` Telegram-key stripping: the plugin owns this now (boundary rule).

It snapshots the workspace before file-changing tools, lets you restore single files with a safety backup taken first, branches sessions from a snapshot, and offers a one-call recover that reverts the file behind a failing test and re-runs that test. Includes git-history fallback for pre-existing regressions and automatic workspace directory detection across all tools.

### Surfaces declared

- **Tools (6):** \	ime_machine_list_snapshots\, \	ime_machine_diff\, \	ime_machine_restore\, \	ime_machine_branch\, \	ime_machine_recover\, \	ime_machine_search\
- **Hooks (4):** \on_session_start\, \pre_tool_call\, \post_tool_call\, \	ransform_tool_result\
- **Slash command:** \/rewind\ (list, diff, restore, recover, search, export, demo)
- **Desktop UI:** status bar chip, right-rail timeline, diff view with Revert and Fork actions
- **Dashboard API:** 13 REST routes
- Middleware: none. Required env vars: none.

### Security and control

- **No shell.** Auto-verify parses the command with \shlex\ and runs it with \subprocess.run(..., shell=False)\. Commands containing \;\, \&&\, \||\, \|\, backticks, \$(\, \>\, \<\ or newlines are rejected, and only an allowlist of test runners is accepted.
- **Path guard.** File operations go through \alidate_safe_path\, which rejects paths resolving outside the workspace.
- **Restore is gated.** \confirm=false\ or \dry_run=true\ previews without touching disk. A pre-restore safety backup is taken before any restore.
- **No network calls** in the plugin code.
- **No Hermes module imports.** The plugin does not import \	ools.checkpoint_manager\ or other private core modules.
- **Reads local Hermes state directly.** It reads \~/.hermes/state.db\ and the shadow-git store under \efs/hermes/<hash16>\ through native git. These are internal layouts, not documented plugin APIs, and may change between Hermes releases. Without them it falls back to a workspace git repo.

- \hermes plugins validate .\: passed
- \hermes plugins doctor\: passed (6 tools, 4 hooks)
- \python -m unittest discover -s tests\: 32 ran, OK

- \
ode --test tests/desktop_plugin.test.mjs\: 2 passed
- GitHub Actions CI on \main\ at \9049422\: passed on \ubuntu-latest\ and \windows-latest\.

### Known limitations

- The Desktop UI is covered only by a smoke test against a stub DOM, not an automated test inside a full Hermes Desktop session.
- Depends on the internal state store and shadow-git layout described above.
- Only file-changing tools (\write_file\, \patch\, \edit_file\, \pply_patch\, \multi_patch\) trigger a pre-call snapshot. Command tools (\	erminal\, \ ash\, \execute_code\) are tracked for failure diagnosis, and changes made by other tools are not captured.

prs.title: fix(tools): apply Chromium sandbox bypass in containerd/ECS containers
prs.body:
# fix(tools): apply Chromium sandbox bypass in containerd/ECS containers

## What

`needs_chromium_sandbox_bypass()` in `tools/browser_launcher.py` now treats any container found by `hermes_platform.host.runtime.is_container()` as needing the Chromium sandbox bypass. Before this change it only checked `running_in_docker()`. The root and AppArmor-userns branches are unchanged.

```python
from hermes_platform.host.runtime import is_container
if running_in_docker() or is_container():
    return True
```

`running_in_docker()` itself is unchanged. `_maybe_autoinstall_chromium()` also reads it ("Docker supplies the binary"), and widening it would quietly turn off Chromium auto-install on every k8s/containerd image.

## Why

On AWS ECS Fargate (containerd runtime, gateway running as non-root uid 1000):

- there is no `/.dockerenv`
- `/proc/1/cgroup` is `0::/ecs/<task>/<task>-<n>` (no `docker` substring)
- the root mount is a containerd overlay (`lowerdir=/var/lib/containerd/...`)

So `running_in_docker()` returns False, `needs_chromium_sandbox_bypass()` returns False, and Playwright's Chromium starts with the sandbox and dies ("No usable sandbox"). Hermes' own container detector, `is_container()`, already recognises this environment through the cgroup `containerd`/root-mount markers. The browser launcher was the one place still using the narrower Docker-only check.

The import is lazy (inside the function). `hermes_platform/host/runtime.py` only imports `os`, so there is no circular import risk, and tests can monkeypatch `hermes_platform.host.runtime.is_container`. `is_container()` caches its result in a module global (`_container_detected`), and the new tests reset it.

## Tests

New tests in `tests/tools/test_browser_launcher.py`. All filesystem/env reads are mocked, so nothing depends on the real host:

- `test_sandbox_bypass_in_containerd_fargate_task`: Fargate-like (no `/.dockerenv`, `/ecs/...` cgroup, containerd root mount, euid 1000). `running_in_docker()` is False and the bypass is True.
- `test_no_sandbox_bypass_on_plain_non_root_host`: no container markers, non-root, AppArmor sysctl `0`. The bypass is False (guards #148457).
- `test_sandbox_bypass_in_docker_unchanged`: `/.dockerenv` present, so the bypass is True, same as before.

Changed test: `tests/tools/test_bot_desktop_browser.py::test_root_dock_browser_starts_with_the_same_sandbox_args_as_the_agents_browser`. Its "seated non-root host" leg simulated a bare host only by patching `running_in_docker`. It now also pins `is_container` to False; without that it fails whenever the suite itself runs inside a container.

## How to test

```bash
python -m pytest -q tests/tools/test_browser_launcher.py tests/tools/test_browser_open_timeout.py \
  tests/tools/test_browser_pm.py tests/tools/test_bot_desktop_browser.py tests/test_hermes_constants.py
```

Live check inside a containerd/ECS task as a non-root user:

```bash
python -c "import tools.browser_launcher as l, hermes_platform.host.runtime as r; \
print(l.running_in_docker(), r.is_container(), l.needs_chromium_sandbox_bypass())"
# before: False True False   after: False True True
```

## Platforms tested

- **AWS ECS Fargate** (Linux 6.1, containerd, uid 1000, Python 3.14). Live: `running_in_docker=False`, `is_container=True`, `needs_chromium_sandbox_bypass` False on main and True with this patch.
- Unit tests ran on the same Fargate host:
  - targeted set (the 5 files above): 110 passed, 3 skipped, 1 failed. The failure is `test_running_instance_port_requires_live_pid_and_open_port`, which also fails on unmodified main in this environment.
  - 8 other browser test files that stub the sandbox decision, plus `tests/test_scratch_dir.py`: they fail in the same set of tests with and without this patch (environment-related: file-permission and optional-dependency issues in my local venv). No new failures.
- `ruff check` (ruff 0.15.22, repo pin) on the 3 changed files passes.
- Not run locally: `scripts/check` (it hung without output in my shallow-clone environment, so I killed it) and the full test suite. Left to CI.
- Not tested: macOS, Windows, Kubernetes/CRI-O live (Kubernetes is covered only through the existing `is_container()` tests).

## Notes on the #148457 tradeoff

#148457 objects to unnecessary `--no-sandbox`. This change widens the bypass only to environments that `is_container()` already classifies as containers: `/.dockerenv`, `/run/.containerenv`, `KUBERNETES_SERVICE_HOST`, cgroup markers (docker/podman/lxc/kubepods/containerd/crio), or a containerd/kubepods/crio root mount. It does **not** scan all of mountinfo, so hosts that merely *run* containers keep the sandbox (#58135 logic is reused). A bare non-root desktop/server is still sandboxed, and a regression test covers that. A rootless container that could in fact use user namespaces will now get `--no-sandbox`. That matches the existing Docker behaviour; container isolation is the security boundary there.

Closes #151657

prs.title: feat(state): session store and turn admission ports, with today's state.db as the local backend
prs.body:
![storage-ports](https://v3b.fal.media/files/b/0ab1b3bc/Kyc8fN20eEaJmdplAtrdr_FR2boTuA.png)

> **Stacked on [#151553](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pull/151553).** Only the top commit (`ea3ddcd4de`) is new here. Review it with `git diff fe57fed423 05311938d7`. Once the PRs below merge, this branch is rebased onto main.

Part of the hosted shared-tenancy work tracked in [#146503](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/issues/146503). Second of three stacked PRs: fenced turn writes, then this one (the storage ports), then the storage conformance suite.

## Why

Hosted shared tenancy runs many tenants' agents on shared replicas, with session storage in a database that is not a per-profile SQLite file. To get there, session storage and turn admission need an interface a non-SQLite backend can implement, with every operation pinned to the scope the code has bound. This PR adds that interface and wraps today's `state.db` as its local backend. **It is interface only: no production caller uses it and no config key selects a backend.** Call sites migrate in follow-ups.

## What changes

**Two ports, at the level today's callers work at** (`hermes_state_port.py`), never SQL or a connection:
- `SessionStore`: session rows and transcripts, transcript rewrites and rewinds, compression publication, usage;
- `TurnAdmission`: the owner lock, the owner epoch, and each session's FIFO whose claims issue turn fences; steering and its settlement, runtime-session mutations, worker executions and their receipts.

A `SessionStorageProvider` supplies both.
- `SessionStore.append_turn` is the turn-path write. It requires the session's claimed turn to be bound, otherwise `TurnFenceRequiredError`; the fence itself is checked by the previous PR's in-transaction check.
- `TurnAdmission.claim_next` takes typed `ClaimPreconditions`: the head the caller validated and the owner's `AdmissionGate`. The backend checks both inside the claim's transaction.
- `assert_isolating()` is abstract: every backend must check that it isolates tenants in storage itself (a Postgres backend would fail it for a superuser or `BYPASSRLS` role).

**Local backend** (`hermes_state_port_local.py`): today's per-profile `state.db`, the `hermes_state_runtime` ledger and `gateway.lock`. Each operation checks its pin, then delegates to the exact call the code makes today.
- The pin is read from `hermes_scope.current_scope()` when the operation runs. The local backend serves the local tenant and its own profile only; any other bound scope raises `StoragePinRefused` before anything is read or written. With no scope bound, the pin is the ambient profile, as for every local caller today.
- The store's database file and owning profile are fixed when the ports open. A symlinked profile directory is the same profile. Refused: a database file that links into another directory, a relative handle, and a handle whose path no longer names the file it opened.

**New plugin kind: session storage** (`plugins/session_storage/`).
- Resolved only by explicit name through `resolve_session_storage(name)`: `"local"` is the core backend above; any other name is a plugin under `plugins/session_storage/<name>/` or `$HERMES_HOME/plugins/<name>/`. A missing or unavailable provider raises and never falls back to the local file.
- In-process providers only: under `plugins.isolation: host` a user provider is refused with the reason. (A host proxy would hide the nested ports and drop the caller's scope; typed port proxies are a follow-up.)
- A user provider's module is namespaced by its canonical plugin directory, so same-named providers in two profiles never share code.

**Unchanged:** `SessionDB`'s constructor; every existing caller. `hermes_home_key` no longer caches a relative path (it names a different directory once the working directory changes).

## Tests

- `tests/hermes_state/test_storage_port.py`: `"local"` names the local backend and is today's store; a provider without an isolation check cannot be built; a named provider loads through discovery and runs its isolation check; a missing provider is an error, not the local store; any pin but the backend's own profile is refused; with no scope bound the pin is the ambient profile; a turn write needs its claimed turn.
- `tests/hermes_state/test_storage_port_operations.py`: every operation of both ports is pinned; transcript, usage, compression, steering, runtime mutations and worker receipts give today's results; a claim whose validated head moved claims nothing, and a gate that closes while the claim waits for the writer refuses it; the handle refusals above (a database file linked into another profile, a relative handle, a handle that does not record its opened file, an alias moved before wrapping), and a directory alias of the profile is the same profile.
- `tests/hermes_state/test_db_path_traversal.py`: `SessionDB` keeps the path it is given; a path through a directory link and `..` opens the file the kernel resolves, as today; an absolute open works after the working directory was removed.
- `tests/plugins/test_session_storage_loader.py`: same-named providers in two profiles each load their own code; under host isolation a user provider is refused with the reason.
- `tests/test_hermes_home_key_cache.py`: a relative path is not cached.

Run standalone on this branch (`scripts/run_tests.sh`): the previous PR's set plus `tests/plugins/test_session_storage_loader.py`, `tests/test_hermes_constants.py`, `tests/test_hermes_home_key_cache.py`, 3610 passed, 0 failed (21 skipped). `python3 scripts/check`: 14 checks, ok.

## Limits

- **The local pin is a profile path fixed at wrap time.** It guards against code binding the wrong scope. It does not guard against the machine's owner rearranging files under a running process: an alias retargeted after the ports open, a profile directory renamed or replaced, or a hard link. That is accepted for the local backend, which serves one person's own files. A hosted backend never derives identity from a path.
- No caller uses the ports yet, so this PR changes no runtime behaviour.

prs.title: fix(gateway): keep bounded control reads off the serial queue
prs.body:
## Problem and behavior

`session.control.read` can miss the client's 30-second deadline while it waits behind a slow request on the same WebSocket. Switching from native Desktop to the gateway-hosted Webapp does not remove that transport queue. The ordinary dispatcher still awaits each serial request before taking the next frame; even existing concurrent reads were admitted into that queue before they could start.

Start the two allowlisted read projections at admission instead: `session.context_breakdown` and the pure `session.control.read` snapshot. Existing bounds remain **2 running + 8 waiting**; a flood still parks the reader. Mutations retain their arrival order.

## Ordering and profile boundaries

These snapshots are deliberately unordered relative to queued mutations. A client needing read-after-write consistency must await the mutation's reply. Desktop/Webapp `session.control` already awaits and consumes the returned snapshot; Ink's explicit control read hydrates the session once and receives later updates as events.

A read naming a hot-starting profile waits within the existing 20-second profile-start budget before taking a running read slot. It still counts against admission, cannot starve ready profiles' running slots, and is dropped when its viewer disconnects. Profile-bound grants naming another profile still fail immediately through the unchanged authority checks. The serial mutation hold lane is preserved.

Completed slow dispatches now log peer, request ID, method and elapsed time at a fixed 5-second threshold. IDs and methods use escaped repr; no request parameters or response bodies are logged. Cancellation and dispatch-crash paths keep their existing diagnostics. A handler that hands work to a pool is timed only through that handoff, not until its eventual reply. No new environment setting is added.

## Verification

Refreshed against upstream snapshot `8112254f8a934626032579cae967b25b7795836d` on 4 November 2026, preserving the published branch's history with a normal merge. Final head: `f41ee761ab98f1e0ab9c245d182a8aa0e59e9838`.

- **80/80 tests passed** across the concurrent-read, real ticketed profile-start, session-control, orphan-race and socket-send-deadline suites, using `scripts/run_tests.sh` with pinned Python 3.14 and two workers.
- The control-read regression fails on unmodified upstream: the read starts only after the gated mutation finishes. With the patch it replies while that mutation remains blocked, while a later mutation stays ordered. Both `prompt.submit` and `session.control` are exercised.
- `scripts/check --base origin/main`: **14 checks passed**, code health 0 blocking / 0 advisory. `git diff --check` passed.
- Independent Claude code/security/concurrency review: no remaining blocker or major for PR publication, conditional on passing the revised tests. The 80-test run above is that revised run. An earlier Gemini review raised the same profile-wait and ordering questions; the follow-up Gemini call hit quota and is not reported as a pass.

The first broader worktree run hit the repository's real-home I/O guard when bootstrap inspected its Git metadata under the live install. Verification was moved to an isolated clone outside the live home; the guard remained enabled.

## Limits

This proves the serial-queue regression, not the exact blocker on every naturally timed-out socket. Later independent-socket controls answered in 26–1685 ms while the user's original 30-second failure remained valid evidence. GIL pauses, database waits, read-lane saturation and full `session.resume` cost remain separate possible limits. See the new cross-surface evidence comment on this PR.

No live installation has been patched or restarted by this refresh. Installed activation and sustained real-use validation are outstanding. GitHub reported no configured CI checks; local test success is not a claim that GitHub CI ran.

prs.title: feat(desktop): Review pane smart file order — change-explaining files first, supporting files muted (inspired by Amp)
prs.body:
## Outcome

The Desktop Review pane gains a third changed-files layout, **smart order**: change-explaining source files first (biggest churn first), supporting files — tests, fixtures, snapshots, lockfiles, generated/minified artifacts — grouped after and dimmed, so the file that explains the change is the first thing a reviewer reads.

Inspired by Amp's [Intelligently Ordered Diffs](https://ampcode.com/news/intelligently-ordered-diffs) (Sep 1): "The first challenge in code review is figuring out which files to read first... Less relevant files, such as tests, fixtures, and generated code, will be shown in muted colors below the important ones."

## Their mechanism vs ours

| Feature | Amp | Hermes |
|---|---|---|
| Importance order ([Intelligently Ordered Diffs](https://ampcode.com/news/intelligently-ordered-diffs)) | Model reads the diff and reorders | Deterministic path heuristic (`isSupportingReviewPath`) + churn sort: free, instant, identical on every refresh, no API spend |
| Muted supporting files | Tests, fixtures, generated code muted below | `test/spec` filename shapes (`*.test.ts`, `test_*.py`, `*_test.go`, …), test/fixture/snapshot dir segments, lockfiles (`package-lock.json`, `uv.lock`, …), generated artifacts (`*.min.js`, `*.map`, `*.snap`, `*_pb2.py`, `*.generated.*`) dimmed to 55% |
| Stable order while reviewing ([First Things First, Faster](https://ampcode.com/news/first-things-first-faster), Oct 12) | Diff changes → updated order computed without rearranging files; blue dot on the ordering button applies it | Same: in smart layout, rows already shown keep their place, reverted files drop out, new files are appended (`reconcileReviewOrder`). The fresh order is computed beside it; when it differs a blue dot appears on the layout button ("Apply updated order"), and clicking it adopts the fresh order and clears the dot. Leaving smart and coming back also applies it |

## Changes

- `review/tree-data.ts`: `isSupportingReviewPath()` + `buildReviewSmartList()`; `ReviewTreeNode.muted`.
- `store/review.ts`: `ReviewTreeMode` gains `'smart'`; header button cycles tree → list → smart (persisted decode falls back to `tree` for unknown values).
- `review/index.tsx`: layout button advertises the next mode (sparkle icon for smart); `review/file-tree.tsx`: muted rows render at 55% opacity.
- Stable order (2nd commit): `review/tree-data.ts` `smartReviewOrder()` + `reconcileReviewOrder()` (pure); `store/review.ts` `$reviewSmartOrder` (pinned order on screen, reconciled on every `$reviewFiles` change), `$reviewSmartOrderStale`, `applyFreshSmartOrder()`; `review/index.tsx` layout button moved into `ReviewLayoutButton` (keeps `ReviewPane` complexity at main's value) with the blue dot.
- i18n: `viewAsSmart` and `applySmartOrder` in en + all 8 overlays (ar, de, es, fr, ja, ru, zh, zh-hant) + types; `locales/_keys.desktop.json` regenerated.

## Validation

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| `vitest run` review pane + store + i18n suites | 84 passed (56 review + 28 i18n) |
| `tsc -p tsconfig.json --noEmit` | clean |
| `eslint` on touched files | clean |
| New invariant tests | 2 (smart ordering + classification), toggle test extended for 3-mode cycle; stable order: 2 pure cases in `tree-data.test.ts` (shown order kept on diff change with append/drop; apply adopts fresh order) + 1 store case in `review.test.ts` (dot on change, apply clears it, leave-and-return applies) |
| Final head `d835de07362`, rebased onto main `0b82d4ce898` | review + store + i18n + `canonical-group-send` vitest 157 passed; `scripts/i18n-keys.test.mjs` 2 passed; `npm run check:lint` (typecheck + eslint) 0 errors; `scripts/check --only health` 0 blocking |

Existing tree/list layouts and their sorting are untouched; smart is opt-in via the header toggle and persists like the other modes. Verified live in a running Electron (below) against a real scratch git repo whose files were edited on disk while the pane was open; the refresh came from the pane's real window-focus trigger, not a store write.

## Screenshots (running Electron, final head d835de07362)

Private Xvfb, sealed scratch HOME/HERMES_HOME, real backend, real scratch git repo. Main leg = every PR-touched file swapped to the merge-base `0b82d4ce898` copies on the same instance (then restored, `git diff --stat` empty).

| main (list view; no smart mode exists) | head: smart layout, initial |
|---|---|
| ![main list](https://gist.githubusercontent.com/teknium1/f1fbb1af445f6f2a52cf10436d23a5ad/raw/main-list-view.png) | ![head initial](https://gist.githubusercontent.com/teknium1/f1fbb1af445f6f2a52cf10436d23a5ad/raw/head-1-smart-initial.png) |
| Alphabetical list, nothing dimmed, layout button offers "View as tree" only. | `agent.py +60, tools.py +30, cli.py +10` first; `package-lock.json`, `test_agent.py` dimmed. No dot. |

| head: files changed on disk, blue dot | head: after clicking the dot |
|---|---|
| ![head dot](https://gist.githubusercontent.com/teknium1/f1fbb1af445f6f2a52cf10436d23a5ad/raw/head-2-diff-changed-dot.png) | ![head applied](https://gist.githubusercontent.com/teknium1/f1fbb1af445f6f2a52cf10436d23a5ad/raw/head-3-after-apply.png) |
| `cli.py` grew to +160, `tools.py` reverted, `new_feature.py` (+90) added. Rows keep their place (`agent, cli, lock, test, new_feature` appended); blue dot on the layout button, label "Apply updated order". | Fresh order adopted (`cli +160, new_feature +90, agent +60, lock, test`); dot gone, label back to "View as tree". |

DOM readback also confirmed leaving smart and returning applies the fresh order (`agent.py` re-ranked to the top after growing, dot cleared).
