prs.title: fix(telegram): flood-refused files are re-uploaded natively after the window, not replaced by a text apology (#64137, #125857)
prs.body:
When Telegram flood control refused a file upload, Hermes dropped the file and immediately posted "⚠️ Couldn't deliver the file attachment" (into the same penalty window). Now it waits out the window and re-uploads the file natively, once. You only see the failure notice if that second upload is refused too.

| Live probe (real `hermes gateway run` + Telegram adapter → Bot API stand-in; `sendDocument` answers 429 `retry_after=8`) | `origin/main` | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| t=0 | `sendDocument` → 429 | `sendDocument` → 429 |
| t=1s | `sendMessage` "⚠️ Couldn't deliver the file attachment" (file lost) | nothing (no request into the penalty) |
| t=8s | n/a | `sendDocument` → **ok, document bubble visible** |
| still flooded at t=8s (2nd 429) | n/a | `sendMessage` failure notice at t=16s, no third upload for documents (an image, URL photo or animation takes one more step of its normal fallback chain after the window: photo -> document, or the URL as text) |

- Root cause: `TelegramAdapter._send_local_file` (the funnel for `send_document` / `send_image_file` / `send_video`) passed *every* exception to `on_error`, which ends in `BasePlatformAdapter._send_media_fallback_notice`. A `RetryAfter` therefore went straight to the text notice. `send()` has had the inline-cap / fail-closed flood contract since #91969 and 595f3a289c7; media never got it.
- Fix: the upload shell moves into a new sibling, `plugins/platforms/telegram/telegram_media_flood.py` (`TelegramMediaFloodMixin`):
  - wait ≤ `_FLOOD_INLINE_WAIT_CAP_SECS` (5s): sleep, then retry once, the same as `send()`;
  - longer wait: arm the per-chat send cooldown (`_record_send_flood_cooldown`) and schedule **one** native re-upload after the window. The task is tracked in `_background_tasks`, so shutdown cancels it. Return the canonical `flood_control:<s>` result flagged `failure_notice_sent`, so the base dispatcher does not post a second notice into the penalty;
  - an upload inside a known cooldown defers without spending a request;
  - the deferred upload, if still refused, waits out the new window and then reports through the existing `on_error` notice. It never loops (context-local stage).
- Same recovery on the other native media senders: `send_voice`, URL `send_image`, `send_animation`. Callers that delete a temp upload or thumbnail on return (`send_image_file`, `send_video`, `send_voice` transcode) re-run the public send, so the deferred upload rebuilds the file instead of reading a removed path.
- Tests: `tests/gateway/test_telegram_media_flood.py` drives the real base MEDIA dispatcher (`_deliver_media_attachments`) into the real `send_document` and checks re-upload-after-window and still-flooded-reports-once. Both are red on `origin/main`. Both go red again when only the mixin wiring in the class bases is removed. 38/38 green across the Telegram media test files.
- Docs: `telegram.md` § Long replies and flood control now covers file attachments.
- `adapter.py`: 7,385 → 7,379 lines. Touched symbols: `TelegramAdapter._send_local_file` (moved to the mixin), `send_voice`, `send_image_file`, `send_video`, `send_image`, `send_animation`, class bases.

Fixes #64137, fixes #125857

Supersedes #64145 (@ahmadsyedanwar, bounded media flood retries; its stale-anchor retry path bypassed the loop) and #125868 (@liuhao1024, fail-closed + ledger notice). Both are credited as co-authors. This PR redelivers the file itself rather than a text notice.

## Dropped hunks
- #125868's `_ledger_flood_refused_media` (`gateway/run_notifications.py`, `gateway/run_turn.py`): it records a *text* notice as a failed ledger obligation. That is unnecessary once the adapter re-uploads the file itself, and it would add a core-side notice next to the adapter's. Re-probed: the persistent-flood leg still produces exactly one notice, after the window.

## Infographic

_DEGRADED: parent attaches_

prs.title: test(conformance): an installed storage port suite that every backend must pass
prs.body:
![conformance](https://v3b.fal.media/files/b/0ab1b3bc/XIhbvtFSawet4V10wrtlx_ZZCM2xJo.png)

> **Stacked on [#151554](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pull/151554).** Only the top commit (`d51086ae6b`) is new here. Review it with `git diff 05311938d7 c0f0274a36`. Once the PRs below merge, this branch is rebased onto main.

Part of the hosted shared-tenancy work tracked in [#146503](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/issues/146503). Third of three stacked PRs: fenced turn writes, the storage ports, then this one (the conformance suite).

## Why

The previous PR defines the session storage ports. A hosted backend (for example Postgres with row-level security) will be a separate plugin, and it needs one executable definition of what "correct" means: pinned to the bound scope, fenced turn writes, one FIFO per session, one owner per agent. This PR ships that definition as an installed test suite and runs it against the local backend.

## What changes

**`hermes_conformance.storage`, an installed package.** A backend plugin's tests subclass `StorageConformance` and supply a `Backend` fixture that says how to bind each agent's scope and open its ports. The suite talks to the ports only. It is added to the setuptools package list, and `tests/conformance/storage/test_package.py` imports it from a staged site-packages outside the repo checkout.

**What it checks:**
- **Pinning:** every mutating operation of both ports is refused for another agent, another tenant and no pin. After each refusal nothing the agent can observe has changed: rows, transcripts, titles, admissions, generations, and auxiliary usage per task. A positive control shows each call succeeds for its own agent.
- **Fence:** every turn write (session creation and the upsert of an existing row included) is refused under a superseded fence, for both a takeover and the session's next claim, with no accounting left behind. This includes a takeover that commits from another replica *while the write waits for the writer*, which a preflight-only check misses.
- **Admission:** a moved head claims nothing; a refusing gate rolls the claim back, also when the gate closes while the claim waits for the writer; one FIFO per session across producers interleaved through three replicas; owner contention across replicas, release and reacquisition, independent agents owned side by side, and owner exclusion kept apart from per-session claim exclusion; every ledger operation refused under a superseded owner epoch; a lost turn becomes `unknown` and is never replayed.

**Nine broken backends kept as fixtures that must fail** (`tests/conformance/storage/mutants.py`): foreign metadata leak, ignored claim preconditions, an unfenced ordinary append, no owner exclusion, a producer-partitioned FIFO, a preflight-only fence, an unfenced create, accounting committed before a refusal, a preflight-only gate. `test_mutants.py` runs the suite against each and requires it to fail, so a weakened test is caught.

## Tests

- `tests/conformance/storage/test_local.py`: the full suite against the local `state.db` backend.
- `tests/conformance/storage/test_mutants.py`: each of the nine mutants fails the suite.
- `tests/conformance/storage/test_package.py`: the suite imports from an installed copy outside the checkout.
- `tests/conformance/storage/test_local_pinning.py`: the pinning part alone (`PinningConformance`), the way a backend that implements only part of the ports would run it.

Run standalone on this branch (`scripts/run_tests.sh`): the previous PRs' sets plus `tests/conformance/`, 3835 passed, 0 failed (21 skipped). `python3 scripts/check`: 14 checks, ok.

## Limits

The suite's docstring lists the invariants it does **not** cover; a backend that passes must not claim them:
- participant visibility (a participant-level record visible to that participant only);
- actor- and owner-level resolution (which level a write lands at; an owner-wide record visible to every agent of that owner and no other);
- child-session inheritance (a compression or delegation child keeping its parent's pin);
- retention and pruning (deleted and pruned rows leave nothing readable through the ports);
- the hosted isolation assertion (`assert_isolating` failing for a role that bypasses isolation); only that the method is required is tested;
- transaction-local scope pinning (a pin change while an operation waits for the writer).

The `Backend` fixture cannot yet vary participant, actor or owner (the local backend stores the agent level only), so the first two need the fixture extended before any backend can be tested for them.

prs.title: fix(gateway): skip global auto-TTS on email replies
prs.body:
## Summary
Extend the existing A2A guard in `_should_send_voice_reply` to `("a2a", "email")`.

With global `voice.auto_tts` enabled, EmailAdapter inherits the base `send_voice` failure-notice path. The reported symptom is an extra “Couldn't deliver the audio attachment” email alongside the normal text reply. This one-line fix skips unwanted synthesis; text and explicit file attachments remain unchanged.

Fixes #141792.

## Verification
- [whyyagswhy, Nov 4](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pull/148555#issuecomment-6629716297), head `8d0da27f`: reports 19 passing neighboring tests, Ruff clean, and direct email/A2A/Telegram guard checks.
- Ara reports the same guard at main `14485fc7` and 10 passing tests in `tests/gateway/test_auto_voice_reply_format.py`; the PR head is her rebase of the change onto that main, `a025df2e76`. Commit hooks were bypassed with `--no-verify`.
- No email-specific regression test ships with this change. Live mailbox verification remains outstanding.

## Follow-up scope
This is not a complete non-voice capability fix. Extending Annie’s audit, Sandy’s source trace and offline exact-method probe at pinned main `14485fc7` identify nine further adapters that can reach the base `send_voice` failure-notice fallback under auto-TTS: `api_server`, `dingtalk`, `irc`, `msgraph_webhook`, `ntfy`, `raft`, `sms`, `webhook`, and `wecom_callback`. They share unnecessary synthesis, not identical user-visible symptoms. Google Chat and relay remain conditional cases: audio delivery requires user OAuth and negotiated media capability, respectively. These are source/offline findings, not live-delivery tests.

General capability gating is reserved for its own issue and PR, using the audit evidence. Related broader proposal: #142879. This PR stays email-specific.

prs.title: fix(agent): keep two static API keys distinct in fallback dedup
prs.body:
Fixes #151321

## What does this PR do?

`BackendIdentity` answers "is this candidate the same backend that just failed?" from provider, model and base_url alone. Two fallback entries that differ only by API key — two accounts of one provider, the usual way to double a free-tier quota — therefore compare as one deployment, so a 429 against the first account skips the second and the chain jumps to an unrelated provider (#151321).

The identity gains an optional credential fingerprint:

- `credential_fingerprint()` hashes a **static** `api_key` (SHA-256, 16 hex chars) and keeps only the digest: the key itself never reaches the identity object, a log line, or a `repr()`.
- A callable `api_key` (Entra ID) and a missing key both yield `""`. An OAuth access token is deliberately not fingerprinted either: `agent_init_fallback` notes that a refresh can replace the token before a failed request is recovered, so a digest of the live token would drift between attempts.
- `same_deployment()` and `same_credential_surface()` answer "different" only when **both** sides carry a fingerprint and they differ. An unknown fingerprint proves nothing, so the historical conservative answer survives.
- `same_endpoint()` is untouched: a DNS or connection failure is evidence about the host, not the account, so two accounts on one host still share the endpoint.

Populated where both keys are already in scope: the fallback skip in `chat_completion_helpers`, and `hermes fallback add`'s duplicate check. The auxiliary-client walk has no failed credential in scope, so it keeps today's answer instead of gaining plumbing nothing feeds.

## Related Issue

Fixes #151321

## Type of Change

- [x] Bug fix (non-breaking change that fixes an issue)

## Changes Made

- `agent/backend_identity.py` — `credential` field, `credential_fingerprint()`, `_distinct_known_credentials()`; `build()` takes `api_key`.
- `agent/chat_completion_helpers.py` — both identities now carry their configured key.
- `hermes_cli/fallback_cmd.py` — `_identity()` includes `entry.get("api_key")`.
- `tests/agent/test_backend_identity.py` — `TestCredentialAxis` and `TestCredentialFingerprint`.
- `tests/agent/test_fallback_credential_identity.py` (new) — pins the call site: a second account is tried, the same account still skips, an unknown or callable key stays conservative.

> **Note on `chat_completion_helpers.py` hunks:** That file is past its 2,000-line cap and `scripts/check` blocks any growth, so the same function's comment block and one wrapped `logger.warning` call were compacted to offset the two added `api_key=` lines. No logic was changed in those lines.

## How to Test

1. `pytest tests/agent/test_backend_identity.py tests/agent/test_fallback_credential_identity.py -q` → 26 passed.
2. Configure two fallback entries with one provider/model/base_url and two `api_key`s (the shape in the issue), trigger a 429 on the primary → the log no longer reports "resolves to the same backend", and the second account is tried.
3. Repeat with one key listed twice → still skipped, no wasted round trip.
4. Drop `api_key` from the entry → behaves exactly as before.

## Checklist

- [x] Follows Conventional Commits and Contributing Guide
- [x] No duplicates / no overlap with open PRs
- [x] `python scripts/check` passes (15 checks, 0 blocking, 0 advisory)
- [x] Tested on Ubuntu (Linux 7.0), Python 3.14.9 (74 passed across 9 targeted fallback test files)

prs.title: fix(state): fence session ownership across profile stores
prs.body:
## Summary

Fixes both regressions reproduced in [the earlier review](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pull/149132#issuecomment-6702238419), and the three blockers in [the follow-up review](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pull/149132#issuecomment-6715000308), and the two blockers in [the latest review](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pull/149132#issuecomment-6717284265). A proven unapplied SQLite lock timeout can be retried without losing or duplicating accepted accounting. Partial adoption can finish its saved membership after retiring a queued donor segment. Unknown accounting effects and divergent histories still fail closed.

Current main `84a0301415ed` is integrated in `51bcff383d90`. **Hosted CI and Foma acceptance remain pending. The earlier source-basis sweep recorded 271 setup errors and one guard failure; the affected shard was rerun on commit 0ad96cc277a7 with 138 files, 1,080 passed, zero failures or setup errors, and 25 skipped. Separately, 39 failures are paired to pinned upstream and three integrated-run failures reproduce on current main. This is not a clean full-suite result or a merge-ready claim.**

A proven failure before a transaction begins now keeps accounting retryable, and an unmatched custom endpoint keeps its route on resume. Credential reuse remains bound to the selected provider and endpoint. This follow-up preserves compatible group-writable profile containers behind a trusted private ancestor, retries positively verified SQLite rollbacks, and applies one caller deadline to cross-profile inventory reads. It also fixes related rollback, interruption, transfer-membership, generated-ID, fresh-session and worker-ownership cases. Shared profile coordination metadata now uses the reserved profiles namespace. Legacy accounting barriers are checked across direct, queued and closed-store fallback paths without deleting markers or replaying uncertain work. The transcript roundtrip fixture restores into an independent home, preserving all history, timing and export-limit assertions.

## Validation

- Both original bugs reproduced with real stores on `f407f8b0d906` before repair.
- Exact integrated commit `51bcff383d90`: **14/14 mandatory checks; 146 tests passed across four accounting and model-resume modules**, canonical runner, one worker and zero file retries. 
- Independent source and operator reviews covered the accounting and custom-endpoint fixes, including persisted-route and credential-isolation controls. Their final reviewed diff preceded the commit; a later health-only delta received separate review. These are bounded, overlapping checks.
- A fresh eight-module comparison on the final commit and pinned upstream each recorded 104 passes, 25 failures and 8 skips; failure IDs, test bytes, frame topology and narrowly normalized errors match.
- The 39 source-basis failures match untouched pinned upstream `7f42573b64e8` by test IDs, identical test bytes and normalized primary errors/frames. The comparison uses separately executed cohorts and preserves raw failures. This is not a clean-suite result or a claim about current main.
- All 4,439 file executions were attempted on the frozen pre-integration source basis `0b509c7cb307`. The original sweep retained 271 setup errors and one node-fixture failure; the affected shard was rerun separately on commit 0ad96cc277a7. Nine earlier fixture failures were also corrected and retested. Three additional integrated-run failures match current main; these are a separate cohort. Actual execution heads, failures and fixture corrections remain distinct from the fresh integrated checks; no prior run is relabeled as a final-commit execution.

## Limits and merge risk

Session ownership affects gateway, CLI/TUI, imports, recovery and accounting. Native Windows/macOS behavior, live services, all interleavings and mixed old/new unreleased stripe-lock interoperability are unproven. Some entry-point controls use synthetic transport or profile adapters. A reviewer reported two unclassified combined-process test failures and a home-I/O monitor-thread warning; separate canonical per-file runs passed. Pre-existing receipt-less active-BEGIN behavior remains outside this change. Queues remain volatile; retained donor and copied target usage must not be summed as cross-profile financial allocation. Preserve backups for database transfer or repair.

Required hosted checks, disposition of retained failures and reviewer acceptance remain merge gates. No workflow approval or production deployment is implied.

prs.title: feat(code-health): refuse shared mutable state on the hosted path; freeze registries after hosted boot
prs.body:
> **Stacked on [#149200](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pull/149200)** (which stacks on [#141877](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pull/141877) and [#141809](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pull/141809)). Only the commits after `b4834d7cf0` are new here: review with `git diff dd51609e4e 4597282515`. Once the stack below merges, this branch is rebased onto main.
>
> Part of the shared-tenancy work tracked in [#146503](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/issues/146503) (hosted-path ambient-state lint and frozen registries).

A hosted process serves many tenants' agents in one interpreter, so any process-wide mutable state on its import path is shared between tenants. This PR adds a lint that refuses new such state, and a freeze that makes the tool, MCP, provider and plugin registries immutable once the hosted boot finishes.

### What this does
- **HX015** flags process-wide mutable state in every module the hosted entry (`HOSTED_ENTRY`) loads. Each write is resolved to its lexical binding. It covers module rebinds and in-place writes (walrus through `global` included), class attributes changed through the class or through an instance that has no fresh own copy (an instance's own copy is credited deny-by-default: only if `__init__` assigns a fresh value first, every other use is a plain read or fresh store, and the class contains no dynamic namespace operation at all: `setattr`/`delattr`/`vars`/`eval`/`exec`, non-protocol dunders, `getattr` taken as a value or with a computed name, `builtins`/`operator`/`importlib`/`gc`/`ctypes`), methods defined under a class-body `if`/`try`, and objects bound by `from m import X` that the importer mutates (reported on the importer's import line). Two declarations pass by API identity: `ScopedCache` and `tenant_neutral(reason=...)`.
- **Hosted graph** (`hosted_graph.py`): follows imports that run at import time, plus package `__init__` files, built-in tool discovery (expanded through package prefixes) and `lazy_forward` forwarders. The ratchet walks each side from **its own revision's** `HOSTED_ENTRY`, so a root added by a change gets no base credit.
- **Lazy imports are now an explicit decision.** The audited roots `gateway.run`, `run_agent` and `agent.agent_init` have 66 in-repo function-body import targets outside the graph:
  - 54 run while the process serves, so they are `HOSTED_ENTRY` roots.
  - 8 run only at boot, at exit or in the CLI entry, so they sit in `OFF_HOSTED_PATH` with a reason each.
  - The rest are package `__init__` files reached through those.
  - `tests/scripts/test_code_health_lazy_roots.py` fails on any new unplaced lazy import, and on any stale `OFF_HOSTED_PATH` entry.
- **Registry freeze** (`registry_freeze.freeze_registries()`): tools, MCP, providers and plugins refuse every mutation after the freeze.
  - Payloads are sealed: tool schemas and entries, and provider profiles in place, descending into tuples. Sealed containers also refuse `__init__`.
  - Plugin handles: `release` is the guarded `dispose`, and `kind` and the inverse are fixed. `remove_plugin_skill` is guarded.
  - MCP: adoption refuses before its first write, and `shareable_connection()` is the read-only lookup.
  - The freeze **refuses (`RegistriesIncomplete`) while a deferred platform loader is unresolved** (`assert_registries_complete()`).
- **Frozen operations are explicit outcomes:**
  - `session.reload_mcp` returns `status: restart_required` instead of -32603.
  - `plugins.manage settings` still saves (`saved: true`), but when frozen it launches no reconnect. It answers `activated: false` and `restart_required: true`, lists the servers in `restart_required_servers` (from the new read-only `mcp_servers_with_new_inputs()`), and includes a message.

### Measured (committed tree, HX015 over `reachable()`, `registry_freeze.py` excluded)
| stage | modules | enforced hits | files |
|---|---|---|---|
| an earlier review head (reproduced) | 685 | 510 | 162 |
| + stricter own-copy / walrus / conditional methods / from-imports | 685 | 537 | 174 |
| + audited lazy imports as roots | 823 | 678 | 232 |
| + per-binding from-import reporting (this head) | 823 | 684 | 232 |

There is no baseline file. Base credit re-runs the **current** rules over the base source and credits what survives. This is a ratchet (credited debt must not grow), **not** a reviewed declaration that the credited state is tenant-neutral.

### Known limits / follow-ups
- Memory-provider hooks: a per-agent memory provider constructed after the freeze must not register global hooks. Stable boot-time dispatch to per-agent provider instances is a follow-up and is not attempted here (see the `freeze_registries` docstring and `tools/AGENTS.md`).
- Function-body imports from modules other than the three audited roots are not audited yet.
- Nothing in production calls `freeze_registries()` yet; the hosted boot will call it. Local installs never freeze.

### Verification
- `python3 scripts/check`: 14 checks, ok.
- Suites run: tests/scripts, providers, hermes_cli/test_plugin*, tools/test_registry*, tools/test_mcp*, gateway/test_session_ancillary*, gateway/test_mcp_reload*, gateway/test_platform_registry*, tui_gateway, test_registry*, all new test files and the review probes. Result: 6939 passed, 17 failed.
  - 15 of the failures also fail on `b4834d7cf0`: test_source_driver (7), desktop_update shim (2), tui_gateway/test_profiles_list_* (6).
  - The other 2 are review probes for designs this PR deliberately does not take: resolving a deferred platform after the freeze (the freeze refuses while one is pending instead), and per-agent memory-provider hooks after the freeze (a follow-up, above).
- Every fix was mutation-checked: with the fix removed, its test fails.
- Final head: tests/scripts and tests/test_registry* plus all review probes pass; the only failures are the 9 that also fail on `b4834d7cf0`.

### Review
An adversarial review ran six rounds. The last three narrowed to one exemption (an instance's own copy of a class container); after two rounds of closing routes one at a time it was made deny-by-default. Round 6 approved with no findings.

prs.title: perf(skills): stop rescanning the library on every keystroke and skill load
prs.body:
## Summary

Every slash-completion keystroke and every `skill_view` call re-walked and
re-parsed the entire skills library. Each of these costs is proportional to
library size, and they are paid *per operation* — on the first keystroke of
every conversation, again on every TTL refresh, and again every time an agent
loads a skill:

- A cold `command_catalog` walked every directory under every search root and
  parsed the frontmatter of every `SKILL.md` it found — in a large library,
  tens of thousands of `scandir` calls and thousands of YAML documents per
  scan. Concurrent first-keystrokes (one per open session) each ran the full
  scan, serializing into a multi-second worst case.
- A warm `skill_view(name)` — loading one skill — re-parsed **every** SKILL.md
  frontmatter in the library and rglob'd all search roots, *on every
  invocation*, to locate a single file.

This series makes the scan **single-flight**, deduplicates the freshness
signature within a request, reuses one YAML parse per file, treats a directory
that owns a `SKILL.md` as a scan leaf, scores completion items once, and locates
skills from cached catalog rows instead of a library re-parse. Per-operation
work drops from *O(library)* to *O(1)* amortized (TTL refresh still pays a
scan, but of a tree the walk no longer over-traverses).

**Round 1, measured on one large real-world library (frozen copy, three search roots,
same interpreter, interleaved A/B; every pass benchmarked at its own commit). The current head's
numbers are under *What the current head adds* below:**

| cell | before | after | Δ |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| cold `command_catalog` | 1,121 ms | 612 ms | **−45%** |
| cold first keystroke `/pro` | 490 ms | 184 ms | **−62%** |
| warm catalog (p50) | 123 ms | 22 ms | **−82%** |
| TTL-expiry catalog refresh | 414 ms | 167 ms | **−60%** |
| concurrent cold keystrokes ×6, worst | 5,823 ms | 267 ms | **−95%** |
| warm `skill_view` (p50) | 296 ms | 171 ms | **−42%** |
| peak allocations, cold catalog | 7 MB | 4 MB | −43% |
| directory visits per cold pass | — | — | **−87%** |
| YAML parses per cold pass | — | — | −50% |

Smaller libraries see smaller absolute numbers and the same structural change:
no per-keystroke rescan, no per-view re-parse, and no phantom commands, at any
size. Output parity was verified against a golden capture (catalog pairs,
completion results for a query battery) before/after each pass: identical
except the phantom commands discussed under *Behavior change*.

## What the current head adds (rounds 2–3)

The first round made the scan cheap. The remaining cost was that *using* a skill still re-read the
library twice: once to prove the catalog fresh, and once to label the skill's provenance.

| cell (warm, 930-skill install, three search roots) | before | after (default) | after (`signature_ttl_s: 2`) |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| skill invocation (`build_skill_invocation_message`) | 188 ms | **25 ms** | **5 ms** |
| warm `command_catalog` | 23.0 ms | 23.0 ms | **3.6 ms** |
| directory-signature walk | 18.9 ms | 18.9 ms | **0.0 ms** |
| `telemetry_provenance` label | ~52 ms | ~0.5 ms | ~0.5 ms |

**Provenance no longer re-reads the library.** `build_skill_invocation_message` →
`_emit_skill_lifecycle` → `telemetry_provenance` walked every root and parsed every `SKILL.md`
frontmatter to answer "external or local?" — 2,675 file reads on every invocation. The label now
comes from the catalog rows the scan already parsed. The exact filesystem lookups stay where a
caller acts on *existence* (`_find_skill_dir` feeds curator archiving), so a stale row can never
resurrect a deleted skill.

**A filesystem skill never pays plugin discovery.** Resolution went through the merged interactive
map, which imports every plugin (~7 s on a large install) — for a key that almost always carries no
`:` namespace. Resolution is filesystem-first; plugins are projected only for a namespaced key.

**`skills.signature_ttl_s` (default `0.0`) makes the walk reusable.** `0` keeps today's contract
exactly: every RPC re-walks, so a skill written by another process appears on the next palette
open. Above zero, one walk serves the window (table above). In-process writes always invalidate
immediately. The knob is read once per process and re-read by `clear_skills_cache()`: reading
config from the scan path perturbs the per-identity command slots keyed on the same signature.

**Runtime state stays out of the scan.** `.skillopt`, `.skillloop-snapshots`, `_sources` and the
hermes home's `cache` (catalog disk cache, scratch) are excluded, so scratch churn cannot
invalidate the catalog mid-session.

## Why the cost exists (per commit)

Each commit is one lever, red→green tested, and was benchmarked in isolation.
Directory visits and YAML parses are indexed to base = 1.00× so the table shows
where each lever lands regardless of library size:

| cell | base | P1 | P2 | P3 | P4 | P5 | P6 | P7 |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| cold catalog (ms) | 1,121 | 1,070 | 951 | 816 | 778 | 754 | 640 | 612 |
| cold keystroke `/pro` (ms) | 490 | 495 | 443 | 332 | 295 | 292 | 184 | 184 |
| warm catalog (ms) | 123 | 132 | 80 | 74 | 71 | 69 | 23 | 22 |
| TTL catalog (ms) | 414 | 363 | 309 | 289 | 271 | 249 | 186 | 167 |
| 6-conc cold, max (ms) | 5,823 | 588 | 547 | 455 | 392 | 331 | 260 | 267 |
| directory visits (×base) | 1.00 | 1.00 | 0.62 | 0.57 | 0.51 | 0.51 | 0.13 | 0.13 |
| YAML parses (×base) | 1.00 | 1.00 | 1.00 | 0.50 | 0.50 | 0.50 | 0.50 | 0.50 |

The catalog contents change only at P6 — by exactly the nested support files
(see *Behavior change*).

1. **`perf(skills): single-flight concurrent catalog scans (P1)`** — concurrent
   first-keystrokes each ran the full scan. One flight now serves all waiters
   (the 5.8 s → 0.6 s row). Also fixes a race: a scan still in flight when
   invalidation hit could publish stale results.
2. **`perf(skills): one directory-signature walk per completion RPC (P2)`** —
   one keystroke computed the freshness signature up to 3× (gate, scan,
   catalog); a request-scoped memo now computes it once.
3. **`perf(skills): register slash commands from catalog rows (parse-once)
   (P3)`** — command registration re-parsed every SKILL.md even though the
   catalog scan had just parsed it. Rows are reused (the parses 1.00× → 0.50×
   drop).
4. **`perf(yaml): one safe parser per thread in hermes_yaml (P4)`** — ruamel
   parser construction was per-load; now thread-local.
5. **`perf(slash): score each completion item once; memoize tokenization
   (P5)`** — fuzzy tokenization was recomputed per keystroke per item.
6. **`perf(skills): skill directories are scan leaves (P6)`** — the walk and
   the signature stopped descending into directories that own a `SKILL.md`
   (behavior change, next section). The biggest structural lever: directory
   visits 0.51× → 0.13×, warm catalog 69 → 23 ms (the TTL-gate signature walk
   shrinks with the tree).
7. **`perf(skills): locate a skill by cached catalog rows (P7)`** —
   `skill_view(name)` matched candidates by re-parsing every SKILL.md
   frontmatter and rglobbing each root per invocation; it now matches the
   cached catalog rows (path + name, disabled/hidden included so locate sees
   the same universe as before). Only the viewed file parses.
8. **`perf(skills): the signature sees SKILL.md files, and the catalog survives a restart`** —
   the signature covers each `SKILL.md` (an in-place edit invalidates it), the root's own mtime is
   out (Hermes writes `.usage.json` there on every load), and scanned rows are persisted, so a
   restart starts warm.
9. **`perf(skills): pay the catalog's freshness once, and label provenance from it`** — the
   provenance fast path above, plus the opt-in `skills.signature_ttl_s`.
10. **`perf(skills): a filesystem skill never pays plugin discovery`** — filesystem-first
    resolution and the runtime-dir exclusions.

## Behavior change: a skill's own tree is support content, not more skills

**Before:** the SKILL.md walk descended into every skill directory, so a
`SKILL.md` nested under another skill — under `references/`, `scripts/`,
`evals/`, `fixtures/`, a vendored copy — was indexed as a top-level command.

**After:** a directory that owns a `SKILL.md` is a leaf; the scan does not
descend. The commands that disappear are exactly those nested support files.

Why this is the right semantic:

- **The spec says so.** [agentskills.io](https://agentskills.io/specification):
  "A skill directory may contain any files and directories beyond the required
  `SKILL.md`." Support material is arbitrary by design; it is not a skill tree.
- **The old behavior produced phantom commands.** A nested SKILL.md surfaced as
  a user-facing slash command — while `skill_view` already *refused* to serve
  it (shadowed by its parent). Users saw menu entries that fail on invoke.
  Repro in `tests/agent/test_skill_leaf_boundary.py`: on base, the catalog
  contains the nested demo skill and `skill_view` of it returns "not found";
  on this branch both agree it doesn't exist.
- **Upstream already treats skill-owned trees as non-indexable, piecewise.**
  `_is_package_owned_markdown` refuses flat `<name>.md` files owned by an
  ancestor skill; `EXCLUDED_SKILL_DIRS` prunes known artifact dirs, and open
  PRs keep extending that list (#122646, #138397, #98536). The leaf rule ends
  that treadmill for everything *inside* a skill — no enumeration can be
  complete, because the spec lets a skill contain anything.
- **The waste dominates the delta.** In the measured library, roughly one
  SKILL.md in ten lives inside another skill, and nearly all of those were
  already invisible in command resolution (shadowed) — the walk and the YAML
  parse were pure cost. Only the few that leaked into commands change visible
  behavior, and those are the phantoms above.
- **Most of the walked tree is inside skills.** Support trees (references,
  scripts, evals, fixtures, vendored material) made up the large majority of
  directories under the search roots; pruning at leaves cut directory visits
  several-fold. The semantics and the cost point the same way.

This benefits any skill that carries its own material — test fixtures, worked
examples, vendored copies — which today either pollutes users' command menus
or forces authors to keep support material outside the skill directory.

Root-level artifact dirs (an artifact folder *next to* skills, not inside one)
are **not** covered by the leaf rule — #138397/#122646/#98536 remain needed and
are complementary.

## Measurement setup

- A frozen copy of a large real-world skills library: three search roots, on
  the order of a thousand SKILL.md files, including nested support files.
- Interleaved A/B on one machine/interpreter (macOS arm64); each pass
  benchmarked at its own commit via detached worktrees. Cold = fresh caches;
  warm = steady-state; TTL = expiry refresh; conc = 6 threads racing a cold
  catalog.
- Parity: golden capture of `command_catalog()` + `slash_completions()` for a
  query battery, compared per pass.
- The structural claims — per-operation cost is O(library) before and
  amortized O(1) after; nested support files indexed as commands — are
  size-independent; the tables above are one library's instantiation of them.

## Verification

- Every pass landed red→green: the test fails on base, passes on the pass's
  commit (`test_skill_scan_singleflight`, `test_skill_signature_scope`,
  `test_skill_parse_once`, `test_skill_leaf_dirs`,
  `test_skill_leaf_boundary`, `test_skill_view_locate_cache`, …).
- `tests/agent/test_skill_leaf_boundary.py` fails on current `main` with the
  phantom-command assertion and passes on this branch.
- Full skills/slash surface: 51 files, 584 tests passed (5 pre-existing
  `home_io_guard` failures reproduce identically on base in the same layout —
  worktree git-dir artifact, not this change).
- `scripts/check-windows-footguns.py` clean over all touched files.
- `tests/ci/test_docs_drift.py` passes; the new `skills.signature_ttl_s` key is documented in
  `website/docs/user-guide/configuration.md`. `scripts/check-windows-footguns.py --diff` is clean
  over the changed files. `tests/ci/test_prompt_surface.py` fails identically on base in this
  environment (PM runtime sysconfig artifact); no prompt or tool-schema surface is touched.
- Current head (`e9c2142a2`): `tests/agent -k "skill or slash"` **299 passed, 2 failed** — those
  two fail on `main` as well (main has 15 failures in that file, this branch 2);
  `tests/tui_gateway` slash/command/skill **33 passed**; `tests/tools -k skill` shows the same 4
  pre-existing `home_io_guard` artifacts as base.

## Future work (out of scope, measured)

- ~~The legacy flat-`<name>.md` lookup still rglobs each root in full~~ — done: it uses a pruned,
  memoised index with an identical candidate set.
- ~~The freshness signature still walks the tree once per completion RPC~~ — done as an opt-in
  window (`skills.signature_ttl_s`); the default keeps exact freshness by design, so this is a
  knob, not a silent behavior change.
- ~~The plugin-import axis~~ — done: a filesystem key resolves without building the plugin
  projection.
- Fuzzy scoring of the full item set is the largest remaining per-keystroke
  cost after the signature gate (tokenization is memoized by P5; scoring is
  inherently per-query).

## Related

- #145430 (desktop catalog filtering) is the renderer-side mirror of this
  work — complementary layers; together they cover keystroke → render.
- #108506 bounds the *curator* scan the same way (`tools/skill_usage.py`) —
  sibling, no file overlap.
- #138397, #122646, #98536: root-level artifact-dir exclusions; complementary
  (the leaf rule only covers dirs inside a skill).
- #141217 / #144319 / #142427: `skill_view` use-accounting and dedup
  semantics; different concerns, same entry point — this stack changes
  locate/scan cost only, not accounting.

## Test plan for reviewers

```bash
scripts/run_tests.sh tests/agent/test_skill_scan_singleflight.py \
  tests/agent/test_skill_signature_scope.py tests/agent/test_skill_parse_once.py \
  tests/agent/test_skill_leaf_dirs.py tests/agent/test_skill_leaf_boundary.py \
  tests/agent/test_skill_view_locate_cache.py tests/agent/test_skill_commands.py
# phantom-command repro on main vs branch:
scripts/run_tests.sh tests/agent/test_skill_leaf_boundary.py
```

Platforms tested: macOS (arm64, Apple Silicon). The touched paths are
`os.scandir`/`pathlib` walks and ruamel reuse — no platform-conditional code
added; Linux/Windows CI should exercise the same paths.

### PR shape (for discussion)

Filed as one series because the levers compose into one claim ("discovery and
serving must not rescan the library") and the ladder above is the evidence.
If maintainers prefer, P6 (the leaf semantic) splits cleanly into its own PR —
it is the only behavior change; P1–P5, P7 are pure-cost passes that hold
parity on either side of it.

prs.title: fix(gateway): persist the model-switch marker on a draft session
prs.body:
## What & why

`_append_model_switch_marker` created the lazily persisted `sessions` row only when the agent held **no** session DB handle:

```python
if db is None:
    _ensure_session_db_row(session)
```

Every live agent carries `_session_db` (the gateway hands one to each agent at construction), so for a **draft** chat — opened in the desktop/TUI but with no prompt submitted yet — that guard never fires while the row does not exist yet (a draft's row is created on the first `prompt.submit`). The marker INSERT then violates `messages.session_id`'s foreign key:

```
sqlite3.IntegrityError: FOREIGN KEY constraint failed
  hermes_state_messages.py:424 in _do
  hermes_state_messages.py:429 in append_message
  tui_gateway/server.py:1210 in _append_model_switch_marker
```

The switch itself applies in place, so nothing is reported to the user: the durable notice (the `[System: … changed to <model> …]` pivot and the timeline entry) is dropped, and the only trace is `WARNING tui_gateway.server: failed to persist model switch marker`.

## Fix

Resolve the row the marker will actually be written to, and ensure it when absent:

```python
if db is None or not db.get_session(_submit_row_target_key(session)):
    _ensure_session_db_row(session)
```

`_ensure_session_db_row` is `INSERT OR IGNORE`, so the existing-row path stays a no-op: no duplicate session, no extra write on an ordinary mid-conversation switch. The row is also created with the session's current model config, so the draft's chosen model sticks instead of being repainted from the old stored value.

## How I verified it

- New `tests/tui_gateway/test_model_switch_marker_fresh_chat.py`:
  - fresh chat (no row) + first switch → the row is created, exactly one active `model_switch` row, `_DB_PERSISTED_MARKER` set, no error notice;
  - existing row + switch → `started_at` unchanged (the row is not re-created).
- Red/green: reverting `tui_gateway/server.py` makes the first test fail with the exact `sqlite3.IntegrityError: FOREIGN KEY constraint failed`; with the fix both pass.
- Regression: `test_model_switch_marker_role`, `test_submit_row_session_target`, `test_deferred_model_history`, `test_model_reset` — 25 passed.
- Lint: `python scripts/check --staged` → 15 checks ok, 0 blocking (lefthook pre-commit clean).
- Real install, four days: 16 occurrences of this exact FK failure (9 on 11-06, 6 on 11-07, 1 on 11-09); 15 of them are a fresh desktop chat whose `sessions` row lands 4–96 s *after* the failed write.

## Scope

- Fixes the draft-session case (#138260, and the marker half of #147069).
- **Not** changed here: the `update_system_prompt` half of #147069 (an `UPDATE` touching 0 rows, leaving `system_prompt_hash` NULL on the row the first submit later creates) — same missing row, different write.
- **Not** fixed here: the rotated-id case in #148912, where `agent.session_id` has already moved off `session_key`; #132509 targets that one.
- Existing open work I am aware of and did not duplicate: #147733, #138268, #132509.

Fixes #138260
Refs #147069
Refs #148912

prs.title: feat(plugin-catalog): add AgentStatus Index
prs.body:
## What does this PR do?

Adds one file, `plugin-catalog/agentstatus-index.yaml`.

- Portable Agent Plugins v1 package: `plugin.json`, `mcp.json`, and `skills/agentstatus-index/SKILL.md`. Configuration only, no local executable.
- MCP server `agentstatus`: Streamable HTTP at `https://index.mcp.agentstatus.dev/mcp`. No auth, no API key.
- Six tools on that server: `search_records`, `get_record`, `recommend_records`, `compare_records`, `list_sections`, and `call_indexed_tool`.
- Pinned commit: `8678c389f76a928a530d868eb9f51ead14e02783` on https://github.com/Carmel-Labs-Inc/agentstatus-mcp-index
- `requires_hermes`: `>=0.21.6`

## Disclosure

Every tool call goes to `index.mcp.agentstatus.dev`. `call_indexed_tool` forwards one call to a public MCP server the user already picked from a search or recommendation. The Index does not store credentials. Destructive tool names are not forwarded. The tool set is served by that server at runtime and is not covered by the pinned sha. The package marks the server untrusted, so Hermes asks before every tool the server does not mark read-only and refuses them in unattended runs.

## Surfaces

Portable MCP server registration and the bundled skill. No hooks, middleware, Desktop code, or env secrets.

prs.title: fix(cron): the completion excerpt is the run's answer, not its prompt
prs.body:
The background-completion block hands the parent an excerpt of the run's saved output. That archive opens with the run's **own prompt** — the job prompt plus any skill loaded into it, which is routinely tens of thousands of characters — so the 2000-character excerpt was almost entirely prompt, and the result the block exists to report was cut off.

`_latest_job_output_excerpt` now extracts the run's answer with the same `_archive_answer` the delivery lane already uses, falling back to the whole file when the archive is unframed (script-only runs). The unstripped text is handed to the reader because it validates the writer's trailing newline — a stripped document reads as a truncated frame and yields nothing.

### Testing

prs.title: fix(rooms): accept pre-handoff gateway actors and pruned discussions on replay
prs.body:
Fixes #148257
Fixes #148627

The room log is append-only and outlives the authority that wrote it, but three replay-side validations assumed every event came from the *current* authority. That holds on the write path (CAS-fenced) — it does not hold on replay after a standalone → gateway handoff, or after snapshot compaction.

### 1. `_require_gateway_actor` — the handoff changes the actor id space

`install:<id>` becomes `install:<id>:gateway-store` in the two-step handoff, so replaying the log rejected historical gateway events with *"message.member authority epoch does not match the room"* (#148257). Both id spaces are accepted now. Only replay needs it: the append path is still fenced to `room.gateway_id`.

### 2. `_validate_event` — older epochs are legitimate history

Any `authority_epoch` different from the room's current one was rejected. Since the log spans epochs by construction, only a **future** epoch — one no current authority could have committed — is a violation.

### 3. `_derive_member_watermarks` — a pruned discussion is not an error

`turn.settled` referencing a user discussion that snapshot compaction had already removed from the active window raised `DiscussionValidationError` forever, which is the "Send wasn't confirmed" freeze in #148627. The watermark still advances, so replay proceeds.

### Testing

These three fixes have been running on a self-hosted gateway since 2026-11-06, through a 252-commit update, against both production rooms that were stuck.

On tests: `pytest tests/tui_gateway/ -k room` gives `327 passed / 36 failed / 8 errors` **both with and without this patch** in my environment — the failures are pre-existing there (I ran them with the deployment's venv, not the project's hermetic test env), and the failed-test sets are byte-identical, so this patch introduces no regressions. I did not get a fully green local run, so I have not added a covering test; point me at the fixture you prefer and I will.

prs.body:
## What does this PR do?

Fix long Safari webapp prompts hanging before `prompt.submit`. The prepared-submission journal includes the full prompt in a Web Lock name; WebKit rejects names longer than 1024 UTF-16 code units. The rejected lock request was discarded while a separate acquisition promise waited forever.

Hash oversized lock names with SHA-256 and forward acquisition errors. Existing short names retain their spelling for coordination with older live tabs. Journal storage keys, submission identities, RPC payloads, and the ownership/release policy are unchanged.

## Related Issue

Fixes #151619

## Type of Change

- [x] 🐛 Bug fix (non-breaking change that fixes an issue)

## Changes Made

- `prepared-submissions.ts`: derive a bounded deterministic lock name from the complete oversized key; reject the acquisition promise when name derivation or `locks.request()` fails.
- `prepared-submissions-locks.test.ts`: two behavioral regressions covering long-prompt lock identity and cross-tab exclusion, plus browser lock refusal without a pending submit.

The Web Locks ownership behavior was checked against its introducing commit, `38a36f4674911fe0bd1b06a90e807d6a4e0e27b7`; the fix preserves exclusion of another live window's retained send.

## How to Test

1. In Safari over HTTPS, send a plain-text prompt of about 2,000 characters or longer. Before the fix, preparation can hang before the prompt RPC; after the fix it completes and the reply renders.
2. From `apps/desktop` with the pinned workspace dependencies installed:
   ```sh
   pnpm exec vitest run --project ui src/app/session/hooks/use-prompt-actions/prepared-submissions-locks.test.ts src/app/session/hooks/use-prompt-actions/prepared-submissions.test.ts src/app/session/hooks/use-prompt-actions/prepared-submissions-tabs.test.ts src/app/session/hooks/use-prompt-actions/prepared-submissions-spent.test.ts
   pnpm exec tsc -p . --noEmit
   pnpm exec eslint src/app/session/hooks/use-prompt-actions/prepared-submissions.ts src/app/session/hooks/use-prompt-actions/prepared-submissions-locks.test.ts
   ```
3. From the repository root, run `python scripts/check` and `node apps/desktop/scripts/build-webapp.mjs`.

Validation on macOS using the exact pnpm 12.15.0 lock pin:

- Both new tests proved red on upstream `main` at `7a1b1d8d1123c3eb7c774b2eeaef6986cccc95c9`: acquisition timed out and the refused request was unhandled.
- All 16 tests across the four journal suites pass after the fix; changed-file ESLint, renderer TypeScript checking, production webapp build, and all 15 repository checks pass.
- The actual module reproduced the failure in Playwright WebKit with 1,450-, 2,400-, and 16,384-character prompts; all acquired after the fix. The 800-character control acquired before and after.
- The original reporter confirmed a long pasted message and its reply work on the affected physical iPhone after the local rebuild.

For independent browser evidence, WebKit defines the [1024-unit limit](https://github.com/WebKit/WebKit/blob/5a733f5cd352894b9efe9661f26f49b8786628cf/Source/WebCore/Modules/web-locks/WebLock.h#L39) and [rejects oversized names](https://github.com/WebKit/WebKit/blob/5a733f5cd352894b9efe9661f26f49b8786628cf/Source/WebCore/Modules/web-locks/WebLockManager.cpp#L215).

prs.title: feat(gateway): busy_result_mode carries mid-turn subagent and background-process results into the running turn
prs.body:
Fixes #136703

## What and why

When a background `delegate_task` child finishes while the parent is mid-turn, the session holds the result until the turn ends and then spends a separate model turn on it. This change adds an opt-in setting so the result can reach the turn that is already running:

```yaml
delegation:
  busy_result_mode: steer   # queue (default, unchanged) | steer
```

With `steer`, the gateway's completion-delivery seam (`_deliver_completion_notification`) offers a claimed async-delegation completion to the session's running agent instead of admitting it as a new turn. Classic CLI runs its turns on the gateway (one-gateway runtime), so this one seam covers CLI, TUI and messaging sessions. `agent/background_results.py` appends them to the **next tool result just before that result is persisted**. This is the same mutable tail slot the iteration-budget and run-budget notices use, so:

- past context is never rewritten, and the prompt cache holds;
- the transcript matches what the model saw;
- the text is marked as background tool-channel evidence. It is deliberately **not** the `/steer` user-authority marker, because a child's output must not be given user authority.

If no later tool batch carries an offered result (the turn ends without another tool call, or is stopped), it goes back to the completion queue and arrives as the ordinary next turn, exactly as `queue` mode delivers it. Durable claims are acknowledged when the result is accepted, the same way the idle drain acknowledges them on enqueue.

Events owned by other sessions are returned to the completion queue untouched.

## Background-process completions

The same opt-in covers `terminal(background=true, notify_on_complete=true)` completions, under their own key next to `display.background_process_notifications`:

```yaml
display:
  background_process_busy_result_mode: steer   # queue (default, unchanged) | steer
```

They go through the same seam and carrier, with a process-specific marker (`a background process you started finished…`). The settle contract differs because a process completion has no durable claim and belongs to its per-process watcher: requeuing it onto `completion_queue` would strand it. So the delivery call waits on the carry (`gateway/run_notifications_busy_result.py`). If a tool result carried it, the call returns True and no turn starts. If the turn ended without carrying it, the same call continues into the ordinary `_inject_watch_notification`, so watcher retries and fallback notices are unchanged. A cancelled delivery (shutdown) withdraws the offer, so the turn cannot carry what the watcher retries. A completion the agent already read with `process(wait/log)` (`is_completion_consumed`, checked for every process in a coalesced batch) is not shown again. Watch-pattern matches, heartbeats and API-server sessions keep queueing.

## Relation to #104434

#104434 (`result_delivery="inject"`) only injects into the **originating** parent turn and is chosen per call by the model. This PR covers the common case where the result arrives during a *later* turn, and is a user-level config default. The two are orthogonal.

## Scope

- Durable claims stay held while the result rides the turn: acknowledged once a tool result carried it (watcher tick), deferred and requeued at turn cleanup otherwise, so nothing is lost and no delivery attempt is spent. API-server sessions and per-task failure notices keep queueing. `gateway/run_busy.py` is untouched: other internal events still never steer.
- New config keys are in `DEFAULT_CONFIG`, plus the dashboard selects, `cli-config.yaml.example` and the docs (delegation, tools, gateway internals). No env var. `config_defaults.py` is over its file cap, so both keys are offset by folding neighbouring comments.
- #140296 / #142319 change how the *queue* path coalesces completions; they are orthogonal (with `queue`, the default, nothing here runs).

## Tests

- `tests/agent/test_background_results.py`: a real `run_conversation` loop. A result offered while the model is thinking appears on the tool result of the next request, never as a user row. It is red without the `tool_executor` hook.
- `tests/gateway/test_delegation_busy_result_steer.py`: a busy-session result rides the running turn's tool result and no new turn is admitted; an uncarried result is deferred and requeued as the next turn. Both red on `main`.
- `tests/gateway/test_process_busy_result_steer.py` (mode read from a real `config.yaml` through the gateway loader): a busy-session process completion rides the tool result and no turn is admitted; an uncarried one is admitted once as the next turn; one already read with `process(wait)` is not shown again. The carry test is red without the process commit: the completion is delivered at once as a new turn.

Run with `scripts/run_tests.sh`: the two new files plus `tests/gateway/test_completion_delivery.py`, `test_completion_owner_retry.py`, `test_async_delegation_session_binding.py` (all passed). Process part: 14 files incl. `test_background_process_notifications.py`, `test_gateway_shutdown.py`, `test_display_config.py`, `test_web_server.py` → 498 passed. `python scripts/check`: ok. Platform: Linux.

---

**Rebase note (2026-10-15):** rebased onto `main` @ `3dd9e4edfd` (2 commits, clean); `tests/agent/test_background_results.py` + `tests/hermes_cli/test_cli_delegation_busy_result_mode.py` → 3 passed.






**Update (2026-10-17):** the first version hooked the classic CLI's turn monitor, which no longer runs since classic CLI turns moved onto the gateway; live probe confirmed results still queued. The steer path now lives at the gateway completion-delivery seam and the dead CLI hook is removed. Rebased onto `main` @ `e7e839a5f4`.
**Update (2026-10-24):** rebased onto `main` @ `dd5bc7ee13`; added the background-process completion path (last commit) and a `config_defaults.py` line offset.

prs.title: fix(cli): withdraw a prompt fenced behind a lost turn after submit, and say when it waits on a running turn
prs.body:
## What does this PR do?

Upstream now covers the main lost-turn path in the classic CLI: `_prepare_submit` refuses a prompt
when the session already holds an `unknown` admission, and `/discard <admission_id>` acknowledges it
(4e35169b2b, 342a55ebad). This PR was rebased onto that work and narrowed to the two cases it does
not cover. The `/discard` route, the pre-submit refusal and the related tests that this PR originally
carried were dropped in favour of upstream's.

1. **Fence lands after submit.** If the owner restarts while a prompt is being submitted, the
   pre-submit check passes, the prompt is admitted, and the restarted owner then fences the turn
   ahead of it as `unknown`. The new prompt sits `queued` behind it and the CLI waits for a
   `message.complete` that never comes (`Initializing agent...` with no end). `_pump` now watches
   the `pending` list from `session.info`; when its own admission is `queued` behind an `unknown`
   one, it withdraws the prompt with `prompt.cancel` and returns `failure_reason="unknown_execution"`
   with the same `/discard` recovery copy, instead of hanging.
2. **Queued behind another running turn.** When the prompt is queued behind an admission that is
   still running (for example an automation turn the restarted owner drains first), the CLI prints
   once that the message is queued and should not be resent. Previously it stayed silent, which is
   what led users to resend the same message into the queue.

Fail-closed is unchanged: nothing is replayed, and no turn is discarded without an explicit `/discard`.

## Related Issue

Refs #139532 (CLI + gateway paths; ACP is #139541)

## Type of Change

- [x] Bug fix

## Changes Made

- `hermes_cli/gateway_agent.py`: `_pump` returns `_BLOCKED` when this turn's admission is queued
  behind a lost turn (`_queued_behind_lost`); `run_conversation` withdraws it with `prompt.cancel`
  and returns the `/discard` recovery. `_running_ahead` drives the one-time "Queued: another turn is
  still running" notice.
- `agent/turn_failure_copy.py`, `agent/error_surface.py`: `unknown_execution` is a gateway-layer
  site failure code, so the CLI shows the recovery copy as written instead of classifying it as a
  provider failure.
- `gateway/session_authority.py`, `gateway/session_ingress.py`: the `Session … paused:

prs.title: fix(cli): restore reasoning display after gateway reconnect
prs.body:
## What does this PR do?

Restore the classic CLI's reasoning display preference when its existing connection reconnects to the gateway.

The gateway's `live.show_reasoning` flag is intentionally session-scoped and in-memory. `GatewayAgent.reasoning_callback` sends it and caches the last `(session_id, enabled)` pair. After a gateway restart the CLI keeps that cache, but the new owner has no flag. `GatewayConnection._resubscribe` restores the subscription without restoring the preference. Replies still stream, but live reasoning no longer does; the CLI can subsequently render `last_reasoning` in its end-of-turn fallback box, below the streamed reply. Restarting the CLI masks the problem by sending the flag again.

Keep the preference in this viewer's per-session state and replay it after a successful resume, before the reconnected socket becomes ready. Use the asynchronous client already on that loop, not the blocking `connection.call`. Preserve explicit hidden preferences too; sessions without a preference are untouched. A restore failure follows the existing reconnect failure path, so no prompt is silently admitted before restoration. No prompt replay, persistent config write, transcript mutation, or new protocol/config field is introduced.

## Related Issue

Refs #134889 (classic CLI reconnect regression).
Related: #139470 restores the same live flag on ACP reattachment. This PR changes the classic CLI only; it does not duplicate ACP, Desktop, reasoning-effort persistence, or commentary routing work.

Searched open and closed/merged issues and PRs for the symptom, `show_reasoning`, reconnect/restart, and the cache symbol; checked the tracker body and comments. No existing classic CLI fix for this path was found.

## Type of Change

- [x] Bug fix (non-breaking change that fixes an issue)

## Changes Made

- `hermes_cli/gateway_agent.py`: remember the callback-derived preference on the session's shared viewer state.
- `hermes_cli/gateway_connection.py`: restore that preference after resuming each retained session, before readiness/new requests. A refused resume is still skipped, with no config write for that session.
- `tests/hermes_cli/test_gateway_connection_reconnect.py`: exercise shown/hidden preferences, first-turn ordering, same-connection write deduplication, and independent preferences for multiple sessions. Update the existing lost-turn test for the added restore request.
- `tests/hermes_cli/test_gateway_reasoning_reconnect_live.py`: use a real disposable gateway daemon and a loopback fake model, restart the daemon, and verify the same CLI connection/agent receives reasoning before answer deltas on its next turn.

prs.title: fix(gateway): keep a session's subagents visible after its cached parent agent is rebuilt
prs.body:
## What does this PR do?

A session's delegated children disappear from `subagent.list` once the gateway rebuilds the cached agent for that route, while the children are still running. `subagent.tail`, steer and interrupt then report the child as unavailable, so the Ctrl+T monitor and the dock show an empty roster for work that is still in progress.

Root cause: `gateway/session_ancillary.py::subagent_records` ties a child to the session only through the parent agent object (`registry._is_descendant_of(record['agent'], parent)`). A child keeps a weakref to the agent that spawned it. After a cache rebuild, `authority.agent(ref)` returns the replacement agent, the old weakref no longer matches it, and the roster comes back empty. The lineage fallbacks don't cover this either, because they only list rows read-only.

The fix carries the gateway's own `LiveSession` record, which survives a parent rebuild but not a replaced conversation, and matches on that exact object:

- `gateway/local_viewer_events.py`: `wire()` binds the turn's `LiveSession` on the agent as `_canonical_session_owner` (added to `_TURN_ATTRS`, so `restore()` puts back the previous value).
- `tools/delegate_tool.py`: `_build_child_agent` copies it onto the child when it is built, because a detached child can register after the parent turn has unwired.
- `tools/delegate_tool_child_run.py`: `_register_child` stores that record as `owner_session_record`, and nested children inherit it.
- `gateway/session_ancillary.py`: `_owner_objects` passes the session's `LiveSession`, and `subagent_records` checks `record['owner_session_record'] is session_owner` before the existing parent and lineage matches.

This keeps the existing rule that an identical durable session id never transfers access to old objects. The match is object identity on `LiveSession`, so a different `LiveSession` that reuses the same id gets an empty roster. A child that carries no token is still invisible after the rebuild (`owned` in the fixture).

Overlap checked: #114420 carries owner authority across a background-thread hop, #116204 shares the roster across processes, and #135874 lists sibling sessions in `delegate_task(action=list)`. None of them covers a parent cache rebuild within the same process.

## Related Issue

No existing issue. The searches I ran are listed under Overlap checked above.

## Type of Change

- [x] 🐛 Bug fix (non-breaking change that fixes an issue)

## Changes Made

- `gateway/local_viewer_events.py`, `gateway/session_ancillary.py`, `tools/delegate_tool.py`, `tools/delegate_tool_child_run.py`, as described above.
- `tests/gateway/test_subagent_live_session_owner.py` (new, 2 tests):
  - The roster and controls keep the owned child after a parent rebuild and after the parent is gone. A foreign token and an unstamped child stay hidden. Reusing the durable id with another `LiveSession` returns nothing.
  - A child registered after the parent unwired still records the session owner.
- `tests/gateway/fixtures/ancillary_reads_peer.py` (real gateway daemon probe used by `test_session_ancillary_reads.py`): adds a `rebound` child stamped with the session's `LiveSession` under an old parent. It is listed and tailable, and after `_agent_cache[route]` is replaced with a new generation it is still the only child listed. `owned` (no token) stays hidden, as before.

## How to Test

prs.body:
## 📝 Description

**WIP** — Base multi-agent collaboration framework with shared context pool, agent handoff, and discovery tools.

Builds on top of the merged PRs #213 (provider protocol refactor) and #131 (model fallback chain + multi-agent routing) to add:

- **Blackboard** — Thread-safe shared key-value context pool (`pkg/multiagent/blackboard.go`) for inter-agent data sharing with scoped entries (author, scope, timestamp)
- **BlackboardTool** — LLM-callable tool for read/write/list/delete on the shared context
- **Agent Handoff** — Synchronous delegation between agents via `ExecuteHandoff()` with automatic context propagation through the blackboard
- **HandoffTool** — LLM-callable tool that resolves target agent, writes context, builds system prompt, and delegates via `RunToolLoop`
- **ListAgentsTool** — Discovery tool listing all registered agents with ID/Name/Role
- **AgentResolver interface** — Decouples `pkg/multiagent` from `pkg/agent` to avoid circular imports
- **AgentLoop integration** — Blackboard snapshot injection into system messages, per-session blackboards via `sync.Map`, tools auto-registered when >1 agent configured
- **Config extensions** — `Role` and `SystemPrompt` fields on `AgentConfig` and `AgentInstance`

### Architecture decisions
- Zero overhead for single-agent setups (multi-agent tools only registered when `len(registry.ListAgentIDs()) > 1`)
- `registryResolver` adapter bridges `AgentRegistry` → `multiagent.AgentResolver` at the integration boundary

prs.title: fix(setup): stop a stale corepack from breaking pnpm install
prs.body:
<!-- nanoclaw-pr-template:v2 -->

## Summary

Stops setup failing with `Cannot find matching keyid` when an older Node's corepack is still on PATH.

- **Problem**: `install-node.sh` links `node`, `npm` and `npx` into `~/.local/bin` but not `corepack`, so `setup.sh` runs whatever older corepack is on PATH (here: corepack 0.29.3 from a `/usr/local` Node 20). That corepack doesn't know the key npm now signs with, rejects the pnpm download, and bootstrap ends `deps_failed`. The `~/.local/bin/pnpm` link it creates points at a file that doesn't exist yet, so the old `/usr/local/bin/pnpm` shim wins too.
- **Fix**: link the new Node's `corepack` into `~/.local/bin` when it ships one. `corepack enable` then writes a working `pnpm` shim there.
- **Fix**: `setup.sh` counts pnpm as available only if `pnpm --version` runs. A broken shim now falls through to the existing npm install of the pinned pnpm instead of failing at `pnpm install`.
- **Also**: `npm config get prefix` failing no longer aborts setup under `set -e` before it prints its status block; the give-up hint suggests the npm command, not corepack, when the corepack shim is what's broken.

## Related work

Closes #4050

Related: #3847 added the `~/.local/bin` corepack retry for EACCES; this is a different failure.

## Change kind

- [x] `kind/bug`
- [ ] `kind/feature`
- [ ] `kind/documentation`
- [ ] `kind/cleanup`
- [ ] `kind/hardening`

## Validation

Each scenario ran the real `setup.sh` with a throwaway `HOME`, a controlled `PATH`, its own worktree and `NANOCLAW_NO_DIAGNOSTICS=1`.

- Reported failure end to end (Node 20 + corepack 0.29.3 on PATH, `install-node.sh` via `uvx nodeenv`) -> before: `deps_failed`, `Cannot find matching keyid`; after: `success`, pnpm 10.34.5 via Node 24's corepack 0.36.0, no npm fallback.
- Node 24 without its own corepack + stale corepack on PATH -> before: `deps_failed` (keyid); after: `success` via npm fallback (`pnpm@10.34.5`).
- Broken pnpm + failing npm -> after: `deps_failed` with status block and the `npm install -g pnpm@10.34.5 --prefix ~/.local` hint. Without the `|| true` guard, `setup.sh` exits at `npm config get prefix` with no status block.
- npm global prefix not on PATH -> after: `success`, prefix `bin` prepended.
- Corepack in a read-only dir (existing EACCES retry into `~/.local/bin`) -> `success`, same path as before.
- `bash -n` on both scripts -> OK. `shellcheck` -> no new findings (3 pre-existing). `pnpm exec tsc --noEmit` -> clean.

- [x] Tests cover the changed behavior (or Validation says why not)

No automated test: CI has no harness for the bash bootstrap, so the scenarios above were run by hand.

## User and release impact

- [ ] No user-visible behavior change
- [x] User-visible change — release note below
- [ ] Breaking change — release note below covers detect, why, fix/migration, rollback

```release-note
Setup no longer fails with "Cannot find matching keyid" when an older Node's corepack is still on PATH.
```

## Security and trust boundaries

Corepack signature checks are not disabled (no `COREPACK_INTEGRITY_KEYS=0`). When corepack's pnpm can't run for any reason, setup now uses the npm fallback that already existed for Node without corepack: `npm install -g` of the exact version pinned in `packageManager`, verified by npm's registry integrity hash rather than corepack's signing keys.

- [x] A human has reviewed this PR and stands behind every change

prs.title: fix(delivery): swallow transient SQLITE_READONLY on hot-journal recovery
prs.body:
## What

The host's 1s active delivery poll opens `outbound.db` readonly. With `journal_mode=DELETE` (load-bearing for cross-mount visibility), a mid-commit `-journal` file cannot be recovered from a readonly open, so `better-sqlite3` throws `attempt to write a readonly database`. The condition is transient — the next tick sees a clean DB — but every error logs a full stack to the error log (~67/day observed on jsboige/nanoclaw, myia-ai-01), masking real delivery failures in the noise.

## Fix

New `isTransientSqliteReadonlyError()` helper in `src/mailbox/sqlite/session-db.ts` (matches `SQLITE_READONLY*` codes and the better-sqlite3 message form), and the `drainSession` catch skips the tick quietly when it matches. Purely defensive; no behavior change for non-transient errors. 3 unit tests cover code match, message match, and non-error refusal.

## Production provenance

Live in the fork's overlay as PATCHES.md#15 since 2026-05.

prs.title: fix(drivers): retry transient failures in the runtime readiness probe
prs.body:
## What

`ensureDockerRunning` is a single-shot FATAL probe. On Windows the `\.\pipe\docker_engine` named pipe briefly disappears during Docker Desktop restarts, WSL kernel churn, or resource pressure — and each miss exits the host, tripping the startup circuit breaker into 5-15min backoff. The underlying Docker outage is typically 30-90s; the host punishment is 10-30x longer than the outage itself.

## Fix

`ensureReady()` retries on a bounded schedule `[0, 5, 10, 15, 30, 60, 60]s` (~180s budget). Exhausting the schedule rethrows the probe's final error, so the failure shape (banner included) is exactly the single-shot one — no behavior change for genuinely-broken runtimes. The schedule is a parameter so tests inject `[0, …]` and skip real sleeps; two new test cases cover miss-then-recover and exhaustion.

## Production provenance

Observed on jsboige/nanoclaw (myia-ai-01, Windows host): 87 FATAL exits across 3 storms in 24h, each storm ending in 5-15min breaker backoff while the Docker outage itself was sub-minute. Live in the fork's overlay as PATCHES.md#22 since 2026-05.

prs.title: fix(setup): cut a long display name to fit the agent's folder
prs.body:
<!-- nanoclaw-pr-template:v2 -->

## Summary

Setup accepts a display name of any length: the agent's folder name is cut to fit, instead of setup failing.

- **Problem**: the terminal agent's folder is `cli-with-<name>` and the DM agent's is `dm-with-<name>`, capped at 63 characters. Since #4148, a name of 55+ characters makes "create terminal agent" fail with "Couldn't create …'s Terminal", and the reason is only in `logs/setup-steps/`. Before #4148, the agent was created and could never start.
- **Fix**: `src/operator-agent-folders.ts` derives both folders for the two init scripts and cuts the name part to fit 63 characters, never ending on a `-`. A cut name ends with `_` and 12 hex characters of a hash of the whole name, so two long names that start the same don't share a folder by chance. Normalized names never contain `_`, so a name that fits can never equal a cut one. Names that fit are unchanged. The display name itself stays as typed; only the folder, which the user never sees, is shorter.

## Related work

Follow-up to #4148 (its verify note 4: "the setup wizard still gives no reason").

## Change kind

- [x] `kind/bug`

- [ ] `kind/documentation`

- New `src/operator-agent-folders.test.ts`; #4148's two refusal tests in `scripts/init-cli-agent.test.ts` and `scripts/init-first-agent.test.ts` now expect the cut folder (they run the real scripts against a real database). New: two long names that start the same get different folders, and a second user with such a name gets their own agent (both fail without the hash); Copilot's pair that shared a 6-hex hash gets two folders (fails with 6 hex); a name that fits is unchanged and can never equal a cut one (fails with `-` before the hash); one pinned folder fixes the hash input, so an existing cut folder can't move later. `vitest run scripts/init-cli-agent.test.ts scripts/init-first-agent.test.ts src/operator-agent-folders.test.ts setup/templates.test.ts src/channels/cli.test.ts src/group-folder`: 43 pass.

prs.title: fix(container-config): never write container.json through a symlink
prs.body:
<!-- nanoclaw-pr-template:v2 -->

## Summary

Makes the host's `container.json` rewrite safe when the file is not mounted read-only in the session.

- **Problem**: `materializeContainerJson` rewrote `groups/<folder>/container.json` with a plain `writeFileSync`, which follows a symlink at that path and blocks on a FIFO. Docker mounts the file read-only, so this only matters for a driver that doesn't (the Apple container skill in #3503 drops that mount).
- **Fix**: open with `O_NOFOLLOW|O_NONBLOCK` and rewrite in place only when it is a regular file; otherwise unlink the entry and create a new file with `O_EXCL`.
- **Why in place, not temp + rename**: a rename gives the file a new inode, which detaches the read-only mount held by a running session of the same group. Reproduced on Docker Desktop's Linux kernel: after a rename the running session could write the file; after an in-place rewrite it could not.

Out of scope: the composed `CLAUDE.md` still uses temp + rename and has the same detach issue; separate follow-up.

## Related work

Related to #3503: should land before it, since that driver drops the read-only `container.json` mount.

## Change kind

- [ ] `kind/bug`
- [ ] `kind/feature`
- [ ] `kind/documentation`
- [ ] `kind/cleanup`
- [x] `kind/hardening`

## Validation

- 4 new tests in `src/container-config.test.ts`: symlink, FIFO with a reader, FIFO with no reader, in-place rewrite keeps the inode. The symlink and FIFO tests fail on main; without `O_NONBLOCK` the no-reader test fails in about 3 s instead of hanging.
- `pnpm test` on base d61af17b: 3553 passed, 15 skipped. `typecheck` and Prettier clean. The branch merges cleanly with current main.

prs.body:
<!-- nanoclaw-pr-template:v2 -->

## Summary

Stops the agent image shipping advisories that already have a fix.
- **Problem**: a fresh scan of main's image (grype and trivy, 2026-11-08) lists 1 Critical and 24 High findings with a fix. They sit in npm's bundled libraries, pnpm 10.34.5, the agent-runner `bun.lock`, and Debian's `apt`.
- **Fix**: pnpm 10.34.9. npm 11.21.2, which bundles the patched `undici` and `ip-address` itself (one pinned `npm install -g`, no hand swap). `@modelcontextprotocol/sdk` ^1.32.2 and `zod` ^4.6.7, lock moved only where findings were. Base digest re-pinned to the 2026-11-05 `node:22.23.4-slim` (same Node, newer Debian snapshot).
- **Result**: 0 Critical, 0 High, 4 Medium with a fix: `glob` and `minimatch` inside npm and pnpm, whose fix is a new major neither tool ships yet.
- **Out of scope**: Node 24 / Debian 13 (#3996), which can follow as a base swap. Debian's "no fix yet" list is unchanged.

## Related work

No issue. Image-only change, no `src/` code touched; a reviewer can check it from the Dockerfile and lock diff.

## Change kind

- [ ] `kind/bug`
- [ ] `kind/feature`
- [ ] `kind/documentation`
- [ ] `kind/cleanup`
- [x] `kind/hardening`

## Validation

- [x] Tests cover the changed behavior (or Validation says why not)

CI does not build `container/Dockerfile`; these runs on a clean VM are the evidence.
- grype and trivy, fixable Critical+High: 25 / 24 before, 0 / 0 after. Medium: 29 before, 4 after.
- In the image: 628 container tests pass (3 skip), agent-runner `tsc` clean.
- Real agent turn: Node, npm, npx, `pdftotext`, Chromium via `agent-browser`, SDK and zod load; `chat ping` replies.
- `ncl groups restart --rebuild` with ffmpeg, jq, imagemagick, sharp: rebuilt in 51 s, all load.
- Host: frozen install, `tsc`, vitest (minus `onecli-detection.test.ts`) on this branch merged with current main: 4336 pass on pnpm 10.34.9. On the earlier base, pnpm 10.34.5 and 10.34.9 both gave 4232.
