prs.title: fix(delivery): one stuck channel send no longer silences a session until restart
prs.body:
<!-- nanoclaw-pr-template:v2 -->

## Summary

A hung send no longer silences its session until restart. Other sessions keep their pace while up to 8 are hung.

- **Problem**: sends were awaited with no limit. One hung send blocked its session silently, and the shared poll tick waited on it.
- **Fix**: after 60 s a send is parked and logged (`Message delivery passed its deadline`). A parked message is never sent again while it might still land: a late success marks it delivered, a late failure is retried, and no answer 60 min later marks it failed. A tick waits at most 5 s on a session and leaves slower drains in the background, up to 8 at once.
- **Limits**:
  - Past 8 background drains a tick waits on each drain again, so other sessions can wait for the 60 s deadline. In a test, a healthy session behind 16 hung ones waited 65 s (behind 24, 70 s).
  - A session parks at most 3 sends at once. A send given up on frees its slot while it may still be out, so this does not cap sends in flight.
  - A parked message can arrive after later ones. If the session's first replies are parked, more than one reply can carry `firstDelivery`.
  - A send that lands after the give-up stays marked failed. A mailbox error at the give-up leaves the message to be sent again.

## Related work

Refs #2665 (instance A). Overlaps #3059. Not covered: backoff (#4227), idempotency keys, and the Discord click timeouts (inbound click path, left to the card stack: #4168).

## Change kind

<!-- Check exactly one. -->
- [ ] `kind/bug`
- [ ] `kind/feature`
- [ ] `kind/documentation`
- [ ] `kind/cleanup`
- [x] `kind/hardening`

## Validation

- 14 tests in `src/delivery-deadline.test.ts` (one is a 3-row table); removing any one guard fails a test. Delivery and bridge tests: 139/139.
- `vitest run`: 3,854 passed. The only failures are 5 s timeouts in 4 `scripts/`/`setup/` git test files, which pass alone.
- `tsc`, `format:check`, eslint clean. Codex (gpt-6.1-sol): 2 rounds on the rework; two real findings fixed, the rest by design, pre-existing or under Limits. 2 more rounds on the test trim: two coverage gaps fixed, then no findings.

The stuck message is retried if its send fails, and marked failed if there is still no answer an hour later. prs.title: fix(onecli): warn when a remote gateway points agents at their own machine
prs.body:
<!-- nanoclaw-pr-template:v2 -->

## Summary

Setup now shows a warning, with the line to set, when a OneCLI gateway on another machine would send agents to their own machine.

- **Problem**: OneCLI tells agents to use the proxy at `GATEWAY_BASE_URL`, default `host.docker.internal:10255`. With a remote gateway that's the agent's own host, so every model call retries forever and the agent never replies, with no error.
- **Fix**: a check at the end of `/add-onecli` reads the proxy OneCLI hands the seeded `default` agent (`/v1/container-config?agent=default`; a named lookup never creates an agent). It only reads the gateway when setup was pointed at a remote one (`NANOCLAW_ONECLI_API_HOST`). If the proxy is `host.docker.internal` or a loopback address (`127.x`, `localhost`), a `nc:operator` note shows the exact `GATEWAY_BASE_URL=<host>:<port>` line to set on the gateway host. The wizard shows operator notes on screen; `setup.ts` output only reaches `logs/setup.log`, so the check is its own step. The hint also names `ONECLI_GATEWAY_PORT`, since OneCLI hands out its default port even when another one is published. It says nothing when the gateway URL itself is on this machine, where `host.docker.internal` is right. It reads the API key setup saved in `.env`, and one catch keeps it from ever failing the install. `docs/onecli-upgrades.md` gets a short "Remote gateway" section: the `.env` line, a recreate of the `onecli` container alone (`--no-deps`, with an exported `GATEWAY_BASE_URL` unset), and a check.
- **Out of scope**: no warning for a gateway without a `default` agent, or one that hands out another address of the NanoClaw host (such as its docker bridge). Setup's older `GATEWAY_HINT` still reaches only the log. The docs.nanoclaw.dev pages (separate docs PR).

## Related work

No issue; found in the OneCLI 1.45 two-machine test (gateway and NanoClaw on separate LXCs). Both new sections sit at the end of their files, clear of #4199's edits to the same two files.

## Change kind

- [x] `kind/bug`
- [ ] `kind/feature`
- [ ] `kind/documentation`
- [ ] `kind/cleanup`
- [ ] `kind/hardening`

## Validation

- `vitest run .claude/skills/add-onecli scripts/onecli-upgrade-guide.test.ts scripts/skill-conformance.test.ts`: 522 pass. New `remote-proxy.test.ts` (18) has one (gateway, proxy) table. The hint names the exact line and port for `host.docker.internal`, `127.x` and `localhost`, and never contains the agent token. It says nothing for a real host or IP, an unread proxy, or a gateway URL on this machine. The read gives nothing for an answer with no proxy. The check sends the key saved in `.env` (fails without it), never fails (fails without its catch), prints its JSON from a checkout path with a space (fails with a run-directly guard), and reads nothing without a remote gateway. The real SKILL.md section shows the hint as a note, with no pause, only when the check warns.
- Full `vitest run` (without `setup/gateways/onecli-detection.test.ts`) at 69f39630: 4324 pass. 6 tests in 4 files (`transaction.e2e`, `add-dial-tool-scope`, `onecli-grants-gate`, `mattermost-discovery`) hit the 5 s timeout under load; the 4 files pass alone with a 30 s timeout (135/135). The trim after it only touches the add-onecli files above.
- Ran the check at the new head against a fake gateway on this Mac's LAN address: it warns with the exact line, is quiet with no remote gateway, and exits 0 quietly when the gateway is down. The two-machine 1.45 test that found the hang still shows the problem.
- [x] Tests cover the changed behavior (or Validation says why not)

## User and release impact

- [ ] No user-visible behavior change
- [x] User-visible change — release note below
- [ ] Breaking change — release note below covers detect, why, fix/migration, rollback

```release-note
Setup now warns when a OneCLI gateway on another machine would send your agents to their own machine (they would never reply), and prints the GATEWAY_BASE_URL line to set.
```

## Security and trust boundaries

Uses the API key setup saved in `.env`. The hint prints host and port only, never the token or the proxy's credentials.

## Skill delivery

- [ ] Not a skill

prs.body:
<!-- nanoclaw-pr-template:v2 -->

## Summary

When setup has just added the user to the docker group, the background user service can now reach Docker on the first run.

- **Problem**: the systemd user manager keeps the groups it had at login, and setup's linger keeps it alive, so logging out doesn't help. Setup's `setfacl` workaround needs the `acl` package, which stock Ubuntu and WSL lack. The service crash-loops on `docker.sock`, the first chat is skipped, and the printed fix (`sudo setfacl …`) can't run.
- **Fix**: in the service step, install `acl` non-interactively (`sudo -n`, apt only) when `setfacl` is missing, then apply the socket ACL. After that repair, setup stops the service, clears this checkout's crash counter (`data/circuit-breaker.json`) and starts it. A service that crash-looped without Docker would otherwise wait out its crash backoff, up to 15 minutes. When the repair can't run, the wizard prints commands that work: the acl install only when needed, the setfacl line, clearing the crash counter, and `systemctl --user restart <unit>`, plus that a reboot (on WSL, `wsl --shutdown`) makes the group stick.
- **Out of scope**: the ACL resets when Docker restarts; the reboot note covers the lasting fix.

## Related work

Refs #2006
Builds on #4200 (merged): the repair's `sudo -n` reuses its up-front sudo ask.

Also covered: acl install before the ACL, no cached sudo ticket, setfacl failing, no apt, group not stale, and a `'` in the checkout path kept literal in the hint's commands.

## Summary

Setup now says why a background Slack install failed, and verify passes again once a later Slack run has connected and wired a chat.

prs.body:
<!-- nanoclaw-pr-template:v2 -->

## Summary

`setup --step provider-auth <provider>` now restarts the running host after it installs a provider, so the first chat on the new provider works.

- **Problem**: provider-auth installed the payload and rebuilt the image, but the service kept running the `dist/` it loaded at start. The payload adds host code (provider contracts and registrations under `src/`), so the first Codex turn failed until a manual rebuild and restart. Found in the OneCLI 1.45 e2e matrix for #4094 (row P3); main behaves the same.
- **Fix**: when `applyProviderSkill` reports `changed` (the same signal that already triggers the image rebuild), provider-auth runs `pnpm run build` and `setup/lib/restart.sh` right after the image build. That is before auth, because a failed sign-in exits the process and a re-run only re-authenticates. It never restarts onto a failed build: `tsc` can write `dist/` despite errors, so restarting then could load broken output.
- **Failure paths**: no service installed → nothing restarted, one line names the service step, exit 0. Restart failed → auth still runs, one line prints `pnpm run build && bash setup/lib/restart.sh`, exit 1. `restart.sh` now exits 2 only for "nothing installed", on Linux too, matching macOS. Any other failure that returns 2 (launchctl, systemctl) exits 1, and so does a unit file that systemctl can't see (no user bus).
- **Out of scope**: no restart follows settings that auth saves. OpenCode saves its endpoint during auth and the host reads it only at start, so an OpenCode install or re-auth that sets a new endpoint needs one more `bash setup/lib/restart.sh`.

## Related work

Found while testing https://github.com/nanocoai/nanoclaw/pull/4094; no issue filed. Safe to review directly: setup-only, the full setup flow (`setup/auto.ts`) is unchanged.

They cover: one restart on install and `--refresh`, none when the apply changed nothing, no service (one message, exit 0), a failed restart (auth still runs, exit 1), no restart onto a failed build, and `restart.sh` exit 2. prs.title: fix(whatsapp): shared-number mode silences the owner — don't blanket-drop fromMe messages
prs.body:
<!-- contributing-guide: v1 -->
## Type of Change

- [ ] **Feature skill** - adds a channel or integration (source code changes + SKILL.md)
- [ ] **Utility skill** - adds a standalone tool (code files in `.claude/skills/<name>/`, no source changes)
- [ ] **Operational/container skill** - adds a workflow or agent skill (SKILL.md only, no source changes)
- [x] **Fix** - bug fix or security fix to source code
- [ ] **Simplification** - reduces or simplifies source code
- [ ] **Documentation** - docs, README, or CONTRIBUTING changes only

## Description

**What:** In shared-number mode (`ASSISTANT_HAS_OWN_NUMBER` unset/false — the bot runs on the owner's own WhatsApp account), the fromMe echo filter drops every message the owner types outside self-chat. Since all of the owner's messages are `fromMe=true` on their own account, the owner is silenced in every group and DM: messages never reach the router and nothing is logged, so it presents as the bot ignoring its own operator.

**Why:** Hit in production immediately after updating a shared-number install to current `channels` — the operator's group messages stopped routing while other participants' messages still worked. The filter's comment ("the user's phone messages shouldn't wake the agent in third-party conversations") is correct for dedicated-number mode only.

**How it works:** When `WHATSAPP_SHARED` is true, every chat is treated like the existing self-chat path: the owner's typed messages are forwarded, and only known bot echoes are dropped via `sentMessageCache`. A prefix backstop (`fromMe && isBotMessage`) also drops bot-authored messages that miss the cache (e.g. redelivered after a restart), preventing echo loops. Dedicated-number mode behavior is unchanged.

**How it was tested:** Live on a shared-number Raspberry Pi install: before the patch, the owner's group messages produced only "Channel metadata discovered" with no routing; after, they route and get replies. Bot echo messages are confirmed still filtered (no loops). Dedicated-mode path is untouched by inspection.

<!-- nanoclaw-pr-template:v2 -->

## Summary

Makes ten CLI scripts actually run when the checkout path has a space in it or is reached through a symlink.

- **Problem**: they decided whether they were the entry point with ``import.meta.url === `file://${process.argv[1]}` ``. `import.meta.url` is percent-encoded and symlink-resolved; `argv[1]` is neither. Under `~/My Projects/nanoclaw` the check is false and the script exits 0 having done nothing: `skill-apply`, `skill-directives`, `skill-driver`, and the OneCLI and Iron Proxy `setup`/`auth`/`control`/`detect` scripts. prs.body:
<!-- nanoclaw-pr-template:v2 -->

## Summary

Stops a FIFO (or symlink, or directory) at the group's Claude `settings.json` from wedging every container start.

- **Problem**: `writeMemorySessionHook` read `~/.claude/settings.json` with `readFileSync` and rewrote it with `writeFileSync`. That directory is the group's persistent, agent-writable `.claude-shared` mount, so a FIFO there blocked runner startup forever, on every respawn, before the poll loop started. A symlink was read and written through.
- **Fix**: open with `O_NOFOLLOW | O_NONBLOCK` and require a regular file. A refused entry is logged and left alone, as the host's `prepareClaudeMemorySettings` already does, so the session still starts (without the memory hook). Writes go through a sibling temp file and `rename`, never truncating in place, and are skipped when nothing changed.
- **Out of scope**: a size cap on the file; moving hook registration to the host.

## Related work

No issue. Found by an automated review of a downstream fork; the code is unchanged from upstream.

prs.title: fix(agent-runner): keep the MCP server's mailbox open until its tool calls finish
prs.body:
<!-- nanoclaw-pr-template:v2 -->

## Summary

Keeps the MCP server's agent mailbox open until the connection has ended and its tool calls have finished.

- **Problem**: `startMcpServer` resolved as soon as the stdio transport connected, so `mcp-tools/index.ts`'s `finally { await mailbox.stop() }` ran while the server was still serving. The SQLite mailbox hides this by reopening its databases lazily; a backend whose `stop()` really releases resources would fail every tool call.
- **Fix**: resolve only after the server closes and every call started through `run` has settled. The SDK's `StdioServerTransport` does not close on stdin EOF, so stdin `end`/`close` now calls `server.close()`, which also aborts in-flight requests.
- **Out of scope**: a grace timeout for handlers that ignore the abort signal; SIGTERM handling.

prs.title: feat(channels): add native Proton Mail adapter via Proton Mail Bridge
prs.body:
<!-- nanoclaw-pr-template:v2 -->

## Summary

The adapter half of #3726, moved to the `channels` registry branch as review asked; #3726 keeps the skill (`/add-proton-mail`) and the Bridge container on `main`.
- **What**: a native IMAP/SMTP adapter (`src/channels/proton-mail.ts`) for a local Proton Mail Bridge, its tests, a faithful fake IMAP server for them (`src/test-utils/fake-imap.ts`), the barrel import, and six exact-pinned deps.
- **Sender identity**: a mail counts as from its `From:` address only when Proton vouches for it. Mail from outside Proton needs exactly one `mail.protonmail.ch` DMARC verdict, `pass`, for the From domain. Mail from another Proton account (which carries no verdict) needs exactly one `X-Pm-Origin: internal`, no Proton DMARC verdict, and a From domain that is Proton's own (`proton.me`, `protonmail.com`, `protonmail.ch`, `pm.me`, or a subdomain) or listed exactly in `PROTON_MAIL_INTERNAL_DOMAINS` (Proton custom domains, the Bridge account's own included: a Proton account can send from a connected Gmail address, so its domain is not trusted on its own; entries must be whole domains, and the adapter warns at startup when the account's own non-Proton domain is unlisted). Addresses are compared with the domain in ASCII (punycode) and the address in NFC, so one mailbox is one sender. The `From:` must be one plain address on one `From:` line. Mail from the Bridge account's own address is never delivered. Refused mail stays unread; internal mail from a domain not trusted is also flagged `$NanoClawFailed`, since it is almost always a real Proton user on an unlisted custom domain.
- **Approval cards**: each card mail carries an `[NC-…]` token in its subject. An answer counts only from the card's approver, quoting the token, `In-Reply-To` the card mail, with an option command on the first line. Every option gets a distinct command. Cards persist across restarts; `onAction` gets the card's Message-ID and address. A card core has closed, or no longer holds, refuses later replies with core's reason when it gave one. Unanswered cards are never pruned before their 7-day TTL; at 1000 open cards a new one is refused rather than pushing one out. Answers to an open card are not held by the hourly sender limit (a held answer would let a gateway approval time out); mail on a card's thread that turns out not to be an answer is counted. While a card waits, its approver's reply to it without a command ("Approve" without the slash) gets one notice listing the commands instead of reaching the agent, and later ones stay unread and flagged `$NanoClawFailed`; a bottom-posted command is read below the quote. Card lines show a label the command doesn't say, and options sharing a label (two agents with one name) show their value.
- **Confirmations**: none of the adapter's own for gateway approvals (`deferResolution`): core's card edit is the confirmation, threaded onto the card; other cards get a neutral "Reply received".
- **Transport**: IMAP STARTTLS required; certificate verification on except on loopback; `PROTON_MAIL_TLS_CA_FILE` pins Bridge's own certificate so loopback is verified too, and an unreadable pin stops the adapter.
- **Delivery**: no mail is read until core's `onHostStart` has run (the host releases inbound first), so nothing is marked read while the host still holds routing. The callback only sets a flag; an adapter set up after host start reads at once, and one still waiting after 5 minutes logs that it is still waiting (mail stays unread on the server). The inbound id is the adapter's (UIDVALIDITY plus UID), never the sender's Message-ID. A reply that keeps the conversation's subject, or arrives on a card's thread, reaches core as its bare body, so core's free-text prompts get just the answer. Failures inside the adapter are retried with back-off up to five times, then left unread and flagged `$NanoClawFailed`; routing failures inside the host are not retried (the mail is already handed over). Mail over 40 MB is flagged without being fetched. State is written atomically with a backup (`state.json.bak`); with both unreadable the adapter does not start, so no mail is skipped.
- **Reading mail**: parsing and HTML conversion run in worker threads with timeouts and a heap ceiling, so crafted mail cannot stall the host. When a mail has both bodies the HTML is read. html-to-text runs with no word wrap and no upper-casing. HTML hidden from a mail-client reader (`display:none`, `hidden`, zero-size, transparent text, `<template>`, …) is kept but marked `[hidden CODE: … /hidden CODE]` with a per-mail random code, and invisible or direction characters are marked too (a lone direction mark beside Hebrew/Arabic letters, or a zero-width space between Thai/Lao/Khmer/Myanmar letters, is ordinary text and left alone); when the body the agent gets carries any mark, a note tells it to treat marked text as suspect. Quoted history and signatures are cut; a forward keeps the forwarded mail (a forward's subject prefix, or a "Forwarded message" / "Begin forwarded message:" line before any quoted history), with a coded `[forwarded CODE: …]` line where the forwarded mail begins, since its From:/Date: lines are the sender's claim; a mail that opens with such a block gets the same line whatever its subject. A forward sent as an attachment (`message/rfc822`) is read into the body under the same line. The channel's notes come last, after the shown subject, and any "[Note from the mail channel" the sender typed is rewritten as theirs. Attachment names are cleaned, made unique per mail and given extensions from their MIME type. A non-ASCII sender domain is shown in ASCII with its Unicode spelling beside it. The body is capped at 50k characters, the subject at 300.
- **Limits**: attachments go through only once the sender's DM is wired to an agent, up to 15 MB each and 25 MB per mail. Bounces, auto-replies (`Auto-Submitted`, `X-Loop`, no-reply senders, …) and mailing-list mail (`List-Id`, `List-Post`, `Precedence: list`) are skipped before the router; list mail is left unread and tagged `$NanoClawList`, since list headers can be forged. `PROTON_MAIL_POLL_SECONDS` must be 10–3600.
- **Hourly limits and the hold queue**: at most 20 mails an hour from one sender reach the host; beyond that, mail waits unread (in the state's retry list) and is handed over as the hour frees up. **This is a throttle, not a loop breaker**: two agents mailing each other are slowed to about 20 mails an hour each, not stopped. Bridge drops every loop marker on outgoing mail (below), and core has no loop handling for any channel yet, so that risk stays open project-wide. New addresses not yet approved are limited to 10 an hour, 200 in any 7 days, and 20 per registrable domain (subdomains share their parent's) in the same 7 days, freed early when core settles (approves or denies) an address; a denied address takes no slot. A new address over its domain's share waits, re-checked hourly, while the hold queue has room for it. Held mail is capped at 200, of which new senders may use 100 and any one domain 20, so approved senders' over-limit mail always has room. Past a cap, mail is left unread and flagged `$NanoClawFailed`.
- **Headers that cannot be sent**: Bridge builds each outgoing mail from a draft template and drops custom headers, so `Auto-Submitted` (RFC 3834) and our `X-NanoClaw-Agent` loop marker never arrive. The own-address check, the inbound auto-reply filter and the hourly throttle are what remain.
- **Message kinds**: a `/command` by email is a command; `send_card` goes out as its fallback text plus links; an edit goes out as a correction on the edited mail's thread.
- **Out of scope**: shared email helpers (sender check, reply-card store) for `/add-resend` and #3743, a follow-up once their home is agreed; a generic IMAP/SMTP channel (maintainers' call); loop handling in core; laying out HTML tables row by row (#4257, stacked on this); an HTML alternative for agent Markdown in outbound mail (a follow-up).

<details>
<summary>Why the sender check counts verdicts, not their position</summary>

Review asked for `Authentication-Results` "only as added by the trusted receiving server". Bridge adds no verdict of its own; it serves the headers Proton's inbound servers recorded. A position rule (only verdicts above the first `Received:`) was tried and dropped: across 60 real inbox mails, Bridge rebuilds every message with the whole `Received:` chain first, then Proton's verdicts, then `X-Pm-Origin`, so position says nothing about who added a verdict. A forged `mail.protonmail.ch` verdict beside Proton's makes two and is refused; all 60 external mails carried exactly one.
</details>

<details>
<summary>Why X-Pm-Origin: internal can be trusted, and why only for some domains (probes on Bridge 3.27.0)</summary>

Proton-to-Proton mail carries no Authentication-Results, so the DMARC rule alone refused all of it. Three probes:
1. **External mail with forged Proton headers.** A mail from Gmail carried a forged `X-Pm-Origin: internal`, `X-Pm-Content-Encryption`, `X-Pm-Internal-Id` and `mail.protonmail.ch; dmarc=pass`. Every one was stripped. What arrived carried Proton's own single `X-Pm-Origin: external` and Proton's real verdicts only.
2. **A separate Proton account to the Bridge account.** One `X-Pm-Origin: internal`, `X-Pm-Content-Encryption: end-to-end`, and no Authentication-Results.
3. **The Bridge account to itself.** The same as probe 2.

A Proton sender cannot set headers: Bridge's SMTP draft template drops them. The rule fails closed: a forged `internal` that ever survived would sit beside Proton's `external` and be refused as two values. Since a Proton account can also send as an address outside Proton's domains (a custom domain, or a connected external address), and nothing Proton adds says which, `internal` is trusted only for the domains above. On a real inbox, every internal mail without a verdict came from a Proton domain or a subdomain (`notify.proton.me`).
</details>

## Related work

Split from #3726 (skill half stays there; it copies these files from `channels`, so this lands first). Purely additive on `channels`: new files, one barrel line, six deps.

## Change kind

- [ ] `kind/bug`
- [x] `kind/feature`
- [ ] `kind/documentation`
- [ ] `kind/cleanup`
- [ ] `kind/hardening`

## Validation

CI does not run tests on PRs into `channels`, so these were run locally on this head (57d4a78e) after `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile` from this branch's own lockfile:

```
$ pnpm exec vitest run src/channels/proton-mail.test.ts src/channels/proton-mail-adapter.test.ts \
    src/channels/proton-mail-registration.test.ts src/test-utils/fake-imap.test.ts
 Test Files  4 passed (4)
      Tests  241 passed (241)
$ pnpm exec tsc --noEmit
(no output, exit 0)
```

- `eslint`: 0 errors on the new files.
- The whole suite on a clean install of this branch's lockfile: two failures, neither in these files (`setup/mailbox-compatibility.test.ts`, a 5 s timeout on a slow host, and `src/group-skills.test.ts`), both failing the same way at the PR's base on `channels`.
- `proton-mail.test.ts`, the helpers: sender check (DMARC, `X-Pm-Origin`, trusted domains), plain-address and display-name checks, card matching and distinct commands, quote, signature and forward handling, hidden-text and invisible-character marks, attachment names, header caps, poll bounds, TLS options, skip and mailing-list rules.
- `proton-mail-adapter.test.ts`, the adapter against the fake IMAP server, faked SMTP and real mailparser: sender identity; approval cards (late answers, restarts, closed cards, ceilings, gateway confirmations, answers past the hourly limit); startup on `onHostStart`; the cursor across restarts and UIDVALIDITY changes; retries and giving up; worker timeouts; the hourly limits, the hold queue's caps and per-domain shares (by registrable domain), settled addresses freeing their slots, denied senders uncounted; forwards and their coded line, hidden text and attached forwards; non-command replies on an open card; list mail left unread; teardown during connect and before host start.
- Each fix from the third review has a test that failed on the head before it (fc9ecaec, then each fix commit in turn).
- A read-only replay of the old head's and this head's rules over a real inbox (638 mails, counts only): no change to any sender decision; the text changes are no word wrap, heading case, horizontal rules drawn 40 dashes long instead of 80, forwards kept whole, and the hidden-text note now added in the mails whose hidden HTML held block elements.
- Adapter tests run against a scratch working directory and refuse to run otherwise, so they never touch a real install's `store/`.
- Manual, Raspberry Pi 5 (Debian 13, Docker): the install's own build of this adapter has been live since 24 Oct with Bridge 3.27.0 (pinned certificate, required STARTTLS, card answers from Outlook).

- [x] Tests cover the changed behavior (or Validation says why not)

## User and release impact

- [ ] No user-visible behavior change
- [x] User-visible change — release note below
- [ ] Breaking change — release note below covers detect, why, fix/migration, rollback

```release-note
New channel: Proton Mail via a local Proton Mail Bridge (`/add-proton-mail`). Native IMAP/SMTP adapter; mail counts as from its sender only on Proton's DMARC pass (or Proton-internal mail from a trusted domain), and approval cards are answered by replying to the card email itself. Proton custom domains, the Bridge account's own included, go in `PROTON_MAIL_INTERNAL_DOMAINS`.
```

## Security and trust boundaries

- Inbound email is untrusted. For outside mail, sender identity rests on Proton's DMARC verdict, which is domain-level, so the owner's domain must stop its users sending as each other: someone who can get a DMARC-aligned pass for the owner's domain (a shared ESP in its SPF record, a relay that doesn't enforce From) can write as the owner. Only card answers carry the extra token. For Proton-to-Proton mail it rests on Proton's `X-Pm-Origin: internal`, trusted only for the domains above; anyone with a free Proton account is verified as their own address, and unknown senders still go through the approval card.
- Hidden HTML and invisible characters are marked for the agent, not removed, with a code the sender cannot predict, so a mark without the code was written by the sender.
- Attachments from a sender who is not yet approved are held back, and new addresses are limited per hour, per 7 days and per domain, so strangers cannot fill `pending_channel_approvals` or the cards the owner's approvals need.
- Loops: throttled, not stopped (see Hourly limits); stated here and in SKILL.md (#3726).
- Credentials: the bridge password is read from `.env` only; IMAP requires STARTTLS and SMTP requires TLS; Bridge's certificate is pinned when `PROTON_MAIL_TLS_CA_FILE` is set (the skill sets it).
- Deps pinned exactly — `imapflow@1.7.8`, `mailparser@3.9.47`, `nodemailer@10.1.7` (past the addressparser advisories below 10.1.4), `html-to-text@10.0.1`, `@types/mailparser@3.4.6`, `@types/nodemailer@8.0.1` — all past the 3-day `minimumReleaseAge`; no build-script approvals added.

prs.title: fix(send_card): count a card's whole text as Teams receives it
prs.body:
<!-- nanoclaw-pr-template:v2 -->

## Summary

Counts a `send_card` card's text the way Teams receives it, so text can no longer push an accepted card past a Teams bot message.
- **Problem**: the 12,000-character card budget from #4292 counted only the parts, in raw characters. Teams receives JSON, where a quote mark or backslash takes two characters and a control character six. The title, description, plain text children and link buttons weren't counted at all. A card of quote marks measured 106.9 KB and one of control characters 191 KB, over the 100 KB a Teams bot message may hold, after `send_card` had already said "Card sent".
- **Fix**: `cardProblems(card)` replaces `cardPartProblems(children)` in both copies of `card-parts.ts`. It takes the whole card and counts every text at its JSON-escaped length: title, description, plain text children, link buttons, and every part's text including chart axis labels. The per-part limits are Slack's and still count characters.
- **Also**: the blank-table refusal now says "no text in its headers or cells", since a caption alone doesn't count.
- **Out of scope**: emoji codes that grow after the check, and tables of zero-width spaces (both need input made on purpose); the number of plain text children and link buttons, which no check bounds, as before #4292.


prs.title: fix(approvals): preserve adapter instance for DMs
prs.body:
## Problem
In a multi-instance channel install, `user_dms` caches one DM surface per `(user_id, channel_type)`. Approval flows could therefore reuse a sibling adapter's cached DM and send the card or a follow-up through the wrong bot identity.

## Fix
- Keep the existing `user_dms` schema and default-instance cache behavior.
- When an approval originates from a named instance, resolve the approver DM through that exact adapter and bypass the channel-only cache. The platform `openDM` operation is idempotent, and the existing messaging-group row is still reused.
- Carry the resolved instance into initial approval delivery.
- Reuse the exact stored or inbound delivery address for rejection-reason prompts and subsequent free-text responses.
- Use generic role and instance labels in test fixtures.

This deliberately avoids a database migration: the cache remains an optimization for default instances, while named instances favor correctness over avoiding one idempotent lookup.

## Testing
- Regression: cache a DM for one adapter, then request approval delivery for a named sibling; the DM is opened and delivered through the requested instance.

- `pnpm run build` — passed.

prs.body:
## What changed

- Require the `declineAndNotify` override contract before the skill copies or registers any payload.
- Run the agent-runner room and canvas tests through the already-built, install-scoped agent image instead of requiring Bun on the host.

## Root cause

`slack-agent-flow` checked its adjacent trunk seams but omitted the three decline-notification fields used by its payload. On an older main checkout, setup therefore mutated the tree and discovered the incompatibility only during the host build.

Its second validation command also invoked `bun` directly on the host even though NanoClaw intentionally provides Bun inside the agent image. A normal Node-only setup consequently reported a degraded companion after the payload had already been copied.

## Impact

An incompatible trunk now fails before payload mutation with the existing update guidance. A compatible install can validate the container-side tools without installing another host runtime.

## Rollout dependencies

- #3360 — current Node runtime support
- #3361 — generic decline-notification override seam on `main`

- `pnpm exec vitest run scripts/skill-conformance.test.ts` — 130 passed

prs.title: slack: split the payload — base adapter in /add-slack, agents feature in /slack-agent-flow
prs.body:
## What

Companion to #3357 (the `--slack-agents` setup flag). Splits the Slack channel payload along the flag boundary and adapts the agents payload to trunk's async central DB.

- **`/add-slack` = base experience only**: adapter + shared lib + bot-inbound guard + provisioning core + `slack-formatting`. The room-membership, canvas-actions, and onboarding modules, the container canvas tool and skills, and the welcome-tour addendum (it promises rooms/canvases/the agents access model) move out — a plain install no longer ships or advertises agents behavior.
- **`/slack-agent-flow` carries the whole agents feature**: its own flow payload plus the moved modules, copied `from-branch:channels`, registered in the barrels, tested in its validate fences (now including the container canvas bun test). Its trunk seam check gains `await action.decide` — on a trunk whose `guard()` does not await async decisions, a returned Promise would read as an allow, so the install fails fast instead of failing open.
- **Companion declaration leaves the skill payload**: `setup/channels/slack-companions.ts` deleted; #3357's boot-time registration replaces the appended registration that the applying wizard run could never see.
- **Async central-DB adaptation** of the agents payload (14 files): plain await-threading, written to compile and behave against both this branch's sync DB and trunk's async DB — async DB-dependent filter/find became explicit sequential loops, ordering preserved, no new parallelism.
- The `/add-slack` connection prompt declares `choices:socket|webhook` so `provisioned` (pre-bound inputs only) is never offered interactively on drivers that honor the attr (#3357); older drivers ignore it harmlessly.

## Verification

- 206 skill contract/conformance/policy tests green on this branch; 116 module tests green against the sync DB; the same payload installed onto trunk builds with zero errors and passes 277 vitest + 17 bun tests.
- Real-engine end-to-end apply of all three skills from this branch's committed state, twice (pre and post review fixes).
- Two independent adversarial review passes; all confirmed findings fixed.

prs.title: setup: --slack-agents installs the whole Slack agents feature
prs.body:
## What

`bash nanoclaw.sh` now yields the **base Slack experience** (one bot, DM and channel chat) and `bash nanoclaw.sh --slack-agents` the **full agents feature** — child bots provisioned from `create_agent`, shared a2a rooms, canvases, DM onboarding. Previously the flag only auto-provisioned the first app: the runtime flow was never installed, so agents created from chat existed only as `send_message` destinations.

## How

- **Flag-gated companion declaration at wizard boot** — the `NANOCLAW_SLACK_AGENTS` shim now also registers the companion skills `['slack-a2a-rooms', 'slack-agent-flow']`. Boot-time registration is load-bearing: the wizard imports the companion registry once, so a registration appended to the registry file mid-run (the mechanism channel payloads used) is invisible to the very run that should apply it. Flag off → nothing registered, wizard byte-identical to today.
- **`materializeCompanionSkill`** — a declared companion whose directory is absent from the checkout (trunk ships no channel payloads) is fetched from the `channels` branch with the same remote resolution the skill engine uses for `from-branch` copies. Keys its installed-check on `SKILL.md`, quotes interpolated paths, and removes the partial directory on failure so retries re-fetch instead of inheriting poisoned state.
- **Held restart on partial failure** — the deferred companion restart is skipped when any companion failed to fully apply (it may have copied files and appended barrel imports before failing its build), and recovery warnings now name the driver CLI that actually applies (`setup/lib/skill-driver.ts`), not the planner.
- **In-tree `/add-slack` synced to the canonical base-split version** — the old slim copy also predated the `provisioned` connection mode, so the flag's own pre-bound input was rejected on a clean checkout.
- **New `nc:prompt choices:` attr** (engine meta + driver select) — the interactive select offers only the declared options while `validate:` stays wider, so modes that arrive exclusively via pre-bound inputs (Slack's `provisioned`) are no longer offered interactively.

## Landing order

The companion payloads (base/agents skill split + async-DB adaptation) land via the sibling channels-branch PR — #3358. This PR must merge for `--slack-agents` to apply the companions; without it the flag keeps today's provision-only behavior.

## Verification

- 647 tests green across `scripts/` + `setup/` (new: materialization contract incl. poisoned-retry cleanup, flag-registration tests; updated: add-slack directive contract, wizard-hooks held-restart).
- Real-engine end-to-end: `applySkill` drove `/add-slack` → `/slack-a2a-rooms` → `/slack-agent-flow` from committed state — materialization, copies, appends, dep, build and test fences all executed live and passed.
- Two independent adversarial review passes; all confirmed findings fixed.

prs.title: fix(daemon): keep delivery ownership valid on allocation failure
prs.body:
## Summary

Scheduler delivery replacement now copies each string before releasing its old value, so an allocation failure cannot leave teardown owning freed memory.

- Apply allocate-before-free to channel, account, destination, peer, and thread strings in [src/daemon.zig](src/daemon.zig).
- Update each pointer and its ownership flag together, without a fallible operation after releasing its old value.
- Keep merge teardown and error propagation; a replacement-copy failure returns before saving the store.

Successful routing propagation, scheduling values, the store format, and retry policy are unchanged. Missing-job insertion is unchanged.

## Validation

With Zig 0.16.0, the focused `zig test` run filtered to `upsertSchedulerRuntimeJob` and `mergeSchedulerTickChangesAndSave` passed all six tests, with no failures or skips.

The new allocation-failure and store-preservation tests fail with the original replacement implementation. The store-preservation test reports `Double free detected`: the channel is first freed by `upsertSchedulerRuntimeJob`, then freed again by `freeJobOwned` during teardown. These tests check each replacement-copy failure, unchanged store bytes before saving, and scheduling and routing values after a successful retry. Additional coverage checks clearing delivery without allocation, externally added jobs, and runtime agent fields.

`zig build test --summary all` with Zig 0.16.0 succeeded: 13/13 steps, 7496 of 7510 tests passed, 14 skipped, no leaks. The only change from the base run (7493 of 7507) is the three new tests.

## Notes

Risks: The successful replacement path preserves behavior and adds no allocations. The behavior change is limited to allocation failure while replacing an existing job's delivery strings.

Occurrence under real memory pressure is unmeasured.

2 recorded checks pass with this change.

- Scheduler merge and delivery ownership tests
- Daemon formatting

Updates `rstest` from 0.23.0 to 0.28.0
Release notes

Sourced from rstest's releases.

v0.28.0

[0.28.0] 2026/10/18

Changed

  • #[case(...)] argument attributes other than #[case(opt)], #[case(default)] and #[case(default(...))] are now rejected: before they were silently accepted as #[case]. #[case()] is still accepted as #[case].
  • rstest_reuse 0.7.1: when the function where the template is applied defines a #[case(...)] argument modifier, it replaces the template's #[case] attribute.

Added

  • Cases can omit the values of #[case(default)], #[case(default(expr))] and #[case(opt)] arguments: the trailing values can be omitted and _ can be used to skip a value. #[case(opt)] wraps the given value in Some() and uses None when omitted. Magic conversion works for #[case(default(expr))] expressions and #[case(opt)] values. See #325 and #327, thanks to @​Atreyagaurav.

Changed

  • Bump msrv to 1.85.0 both for rstest and rstest_reuse

[0.28.0] 2026/10/18

Changed

  • #[case(...)] argument attributes other than #[case(opt)], #[case(default)] and #[case(default(...))] are now rejected: before they were silently accepted as #[case]. #[case()] is still accepted as #[case].
  • rstest_reuse 0.7.1: when the function where the template is applied defines a #[case(...)] argument modifier, it replaces the template's #[case] attribute.

Added

  • Cases can omit the values of #[case(default)], #[case(default(expr))] and #[case(opt)] arguments: the trailing values can be omitted and _ can be used to skip a value. #[case(opt)] wraps the given value in Some() and uses None when omitted. Updates `tower-http` from 0.7.0 to 0.7.1
Release notes

Sourced from tower-http's releases.

tower-http-0.7.1

Added

  • fs: add ServeDir::redirect_to_trailing_slash() to serve directory indexes directly instead of first redirecting to the trailing-slash path. The redirect remains the default (#728)
  • fs: add ignore_multi_range_requests() to ServeDir and ServeFile, serving the full representation when a request asks for multiple byte ranges. The existing 416 Range Not Satisfiable response remains the default (#727)
  • request-id: the constructors and accessors on the request-id layers, services, and RequestId are now const fn, so they can be used in const context (#716)

Changed

  • fs: the minimum http-range-header requirement is now 0.4.2 (#661)

Fixed

  • behavioral change: fs: make ServeDir::try_call propagate expected filesystem I/O errors when no fallback is configured, as documented, instead of converting them to 404 Not Found responses (#718)
  • decompression: don't end the body when a data frame with no remaining bytes arrives after the decompressor reports end-of-stream. Trailers following such a frame were dropped and could not be recovered (#722)
  • decompression: return a body error when a data frame with remaining bytes arrives after the decompressor reports end-of-stream, rather than silently truncating. This regressed in 0.7.0 (#712)
  • fs: multipart range requests are now rejected before range validation, so they consistently return 416 Range Not Satisfiable with a Cannot serve multipart range requests body instead of a generic unsatisfiable-range response (#661)
  • fs: range error responses no longer carry representation headers such as Content-Type and Content-Encoding (#727)
  • set-header: SetMultipleResponseHeadersLayer and SetMultipleResponseHeader are now Clone regardless of the response body type, matching the fix applied to the request-side types in 0.7.0 (#714)

v48.0.2

48.0.2

Released 2026-09-10.

Changed

  • Wasmtime's dependency on cap-primitives is now vendored within Wasmtime itself. #14225

prs.title: perf(openclaw): defer large tool catalogs behind Tool Search
prs.body:
## Summary
Tool schemas were about two thirds of every model request: 68 tools and ~106k characters sent on each call, for a first-request baseline of ~45k tokens. This PR turns on OpenClaw Tool Search (directory mode) so only core file/shell tools and a few pinned interaction tools are sent directly; everything else is listed in a compact directory or found through `tool_search`.

Measured on deepseek-flash (fresh desktop session, `systemPromptReport` + provider usage): **first request 18,272 input tokens, down from 44.7k–45.8k**; visible tools 68 → 14 (~106k → ~13k characters).

## Related Issue
N/A

## Changes Made
- **Config sync** (`openclawConfigSync.ts`): `tools.toolSearch = { enabled, mode: 'directory', direct: [AskUserQuestion, ask_user, progress_card] }`; deny Control UI tools LobsterAI never renders (`dashboard`, `portal`, `terminal`, `github_identity_status`). `skill_workshop` stays enabled because the opt-in skill review uses it.
- **Managed AGENTS.md**: new "Deferred Tools" section so a tool reachable through `tool_search` counts as available (several sections say "use X if it is available").
- **New patch `openclaw-tool-search-direct-tools.patch`**: adds `tools.toolSearch.direct`. Needed because the delete policy skips confirmation when `AskUserQuestion` is not in the toolset, so it must never be deferred. Plugin `catalogMode: "direct-only"` is not enough (plugin tool descriptors are cached without it). MCP/client tools are never promoted.
- **New patch `openclaw-tool-call-slim-envelope.patch`**: `tool_call` results echoed the full catalog entry (description + input hint) on every call, 1.1k–5.2k characters each. The model now sees `{ tool: { id, name }, result }`; failure `details` and Code Mode keep the full shape.
- **Runtime adapter**: hide `tool_search` / `tool_describe` / `tool_call` events; the deferred tool emits its own events under its real name (plan mode checks that nested event).
- **IM history sync**: read `filePath` from `message` calls wrapped in `tool_call`.
- Patch validators, README sections, and the reviewed patch list updated.

## Type of Change
- [x] Performance improvement

## Testing
- [x] Tested locally
- [x] Added new tests
- [x] Updated existing tests
- [x] Manual testing performed

- OpenClaw: new `tool-surface-plan` / schema / `tool-search.mcp-error` cases pass; all 94 patches apply in order from a clean tree with strong validation.
- LobsterAI: `openclawConfigSync.runtime` (incl. pinned-runtime `config validate`), `openclawRuntimeAdapter`, `openclawHistory`, `openclawPatches/*` pass; eslint clean on touched files; `npm run compile:electron` OK.
- End to end on the rebuilt runtime through the gateway (desktop session keys): Excel edit and Word edit via the Office editor MCP tools, browser open/read, and scheduled-task creation all succeed through search/describe/call. Results verified on disk; test jobs removed.
- Full `npm test` on Windows: remaining failures (office, git snapshot, qqbot, daily logs, etc.) reproduce on a clean HEAD worktree and are unrelated.

## Checklist
- [x] My code follows the project's style guidelines
- [x] I have performed a self-review of my code
- [x] I have commented my code, particularly in hard-to-understand areas
- [x] I have made corresponding changes to the documentation

- [x] I have added tests that prove my fix is effective or that my feature works
- [x] New and existing unit tests pass locally with my changes

## Electron-Specific Changes

## Additional Notes
- **Rebuild the OpenClaw runtime** (`npm run electron:dev:openclaw`) after pulling. A runtime without the new patch rejects the `tools.toolSearch.direct` key.
- Known trade-offs: the first use of a deferred tool costs one or two extra model calls (search/describe). MCP and browser results reached through `tool_call` carry OpenClaw's untrusted-content notice (~700 chars), which is upstream security behavior and left unchanged.
- Not covered by automated or e2e runs: transcript card rendering in a real desktop session (covered by adapter unit tests), computer use, and subagents.

prs.title: fix(openclaw): preserve accepted work through recovery and compaction
prs.body:
## Summary

Preserve accepted work across compaction and gateway restarts while reducing pinned-runtime startup overhead. The runtime remains on OpenClaw v2026.8.1.

- Isolate the model-catalog worker contract from host orchestration and read migration checkpoints through one integrity-verified connection per decision point.
- Let parents coordinate interrupted child recovery using source-run claims and exact delivery receipts. Persist Stop before acknowledgement, including a completed child whose parent wake is still pending. Non-final and silent payloads cannot certify final delivery.
- Carry the accepted run through verified compaction lineage within the same physical SQLite database. Preserve the original run/abort controller while rejecting reset, restart, cancellation, and replaced-database boundaries.

The changes are split into three version-scoped patches with their source regression tests and documented patch inventory. Selected upstream references: openclaw/openclaw#154293, openclaw/openclaw#153243, openclaw/openclaw#152958.

## Validation

- Focused OpenClaw runtime suites: 729 cases covering worker inputs/credentials, checkpoints/doctor, terminal delivery, parent recovery, Stop, registry lifecycle, and real SQLite compaction handoffs. The final receipt/lint changes were rechecked with 203 passing cases.
- Added a failing-then-passing regression for `NO_REPLY` with explicit visibility, plus positive media/structured-content cases; independent source review passed after the fix.
- Typed lint on all 82 changed runtime TypeScript files, fresh `pnpm tsgo:core`, a full runtime build, and a final runtime rebuild reusing declaration output.
- Official 60-patch replay from the clean pinned source; all 82 changed paths match the tested source after replay.
- Combined replay with #2758 and #2764: all 63 patches apply with the default tool; compaction/refresh interaction tests pass (20).
- LobsterAI patch-inventory tests (19), touched-file ESLint, and Electron TypeScript compilation.
- Three isolated built-source Gateway starts: HTTP health, authenticated WebSocket hello, and graceful exit 0. Plugins, channels, and cron were disabled; no user profile or model credentials were used.

## Related changes and delivery

Progress-card refresh is reviewed separately in #2758; live gateway settings in #2764. This PR changes the bundled runtime, requiring a rebuilt desktop package. Native Windows, packaged-client acceptance, and real-model multi-step recovery are not claimed by these tests.

issues.title: [Bug]: QQ channel plugin fails to activate with DEPENDENCY_PLAN_UNVERIFIED when a hub plugin (aliyun-hub) has no dependency environment
issues.body:
## QwenPaw Version

2.3.0b2

## Description

The `qq` channel plugin (`dependency_mode: shared`) fails to activate on startup. Activation aborts inside the shared-dependency audit:

```
DEPENDENCY_PLAN_UNVERIFIED: qq: host aliyun-hub: environment evidence unavailable.
Consumers: declaration qq, host aliyun-hub, runtime qq.
Stop environment consumers before explicit repair and re-audit.
Source rollback does not restore dependency packages.
```

The QQ channel never comes online. The Console "repair dependencies" action returns **409 Conflict** every time, because the repair path re-runs the same failing audit — and its instruction ("stop environment consumers before explicit repair") is unsatisfiable, since `qq` itself is one of the consumers. That is a deadlock with no UI path out.

`aliyun-hub` is an unrelated built-in **hub**-type plugin (Aliyun Skill marketplace source). It has no Python requirements and provides no dependency environment, so it should not be able to block a channel plugin.

## Environment

- QwenPaw **2.3.0b2** (PyPI `2.3.0b2`)
- Armbian aarch64 (TV box), Python 3.12.3
- One active agent, one workspace with the `qq` channel enabled
- Workspace plugins present: `aliyun-hub`, `qwenpaw-hub`, `clawhub-hub`, `modelscope-hub`, `memory-console`, `qq`
- `qq` channel: `enabled: true`, official QQ bot `app_id` + `client_secret` configured, previously working on 2.3.0b1

## Reproduction

1. Install 2.3.0b2 with the stock `aliyun-hub` plugin present in the workspace `plugins/` directory.
2. Enable the `qq` channel (`dependency_mode: shared`, `process_mode: runner_process`).
3. Restart qwenpaw.
4. Observe the activation failure above; the QQ channel stays offline.
5. Click "repair dependencies" in the Console → HTTP 409.

## Logs

```
INFO  plugins/loader.py:615 | Discovered plugin: aliyun-hub
INFO  plugins/loader.py:615 | Discovered plugin: qwenpaw-hub
INFO  plugins/loader.py:615 | Discovered plugin: qq
INFO  plugins/loader.py:615 | Discovered plugin: clawhub-hub
INFO  plugins/loader.py:615 | Discovered plugin: modelscope-hub
INFO  plugins/registry.py:538 | Registered startup hook 'channel_qq_qq' from plugin 'qq' (priority=80)
INFO  plugins/api.py:1329 | Plugin 'qq' registered startup hook 'channel_qq_qq' (priority=80)

ERROR plugins/loader.py:5002 | Failed to activate plugin 'qq': DEPENDENCY_PLAN_UNVERIFIED:
      qq: host aliyun-hub: environment evidence unavailable.
      Consumers: declaration qq, host aliyun-hub, runtime qq.

INFO  ... "POST /api/plugins/qq/repair-dependencies HTTP/1.1" 409 Conflict
```

There is no `channel_qq` startup line and no runner connection attempt after the failure.

## Root cause analysis (from reading 2.3.0b2 source)

**1. `plugins/dependency_usage.py` — `DependencyUsageRegistry.observe_host()`** only attaches an environment when an observation succeeded:

```python
self._host[token] = deepcopy(
    replace(
        declaration,
        active=True,
        origin="host",
        snapshot=snapshot,
        environment=(
            DependencyEnvironment.from_snapshot(snapshot)
            if observed and (previous is None or previous.environment is not None)
            else None
        ),
    ),
)
```

**2. `plugins/python_backend.py:963`** — when host dependency observation is inconclusive it explicitly records an unknown state:

```python
def unknown():
    if valid():
        usage.observe_host(token, None)
```

So a host plugin whose imports/requirements can never be resolved ends up in `_host` with `snapshot=None` and `environment=None`.

**3. `plugins/dependency_usage.py` — `snapshot()`** includes every `_host` entry in `uses` unconditionally:

```python
uses = [
    use for token, use in self._declarations.items()
    if use.pending or token is admission_token
] + list(self._host.values())
```

**4. `plugins/dependency_gate.py` — the audit loop** treats any use with `environment is None` as a hard failure:

```python
for use in uses:
    environment, evidence = use.environment, use.snapshot
    ...
    if environment is None:
        unsupported.append(f"{use.origin} {use.plugin_id}: environment evidence unavailable")
        continue
```

**5.** `unsupported` being non-empty yields `DEPENDENCY_PLAN_UNVERIFIED` for the whole shared plan, so **every** `dependency_mode: shared` plugin in that environment is refused activation.

In short: a hub-type plugin with no dependency involvement is registered as a host dependency user, can never produce environment evidence, and that missing evidence is treated as a fatal condition for an unrelated channel plugin's shared plan.

## Suggested fix

Any one of:

- Do not register `type: hub` plugins in `_host` (they have no dependency environment by design); or
- In `snapshot()`, keep host entries with `environment is None` out of the audited `uses`; or
- In `dependency_gate.py`, treat `environment is None` for a use that declares no requirements as "no dependency involvement" instead of `unsupported`.

## Workaround

Moving the `aliyun-hub` plugin directory out of the workspace `plugins/` folder and restarting makes the QQ channel activate with zero errors:

```bash
mv <qwenpaw_home>/working/plugins/aliyun-hub /tmp/aliyun-hub.bak
systemctl restart qwenpaw
```

After this, `Failed to activate plugin 'qq'` disappears, `Plugin 'qq' registered startup hook 'channel_qq_qq'` runs, and the QQ bot connects normally.

Downside: the Aliyun skill marketplace source disappears from the Console until the plugin is restored.

issues.title: [Bug]: Oversized historical image re-sent on every model call; stripped retry keeps the misleading "Image loaded: <name>" text
issues.body:
### QwenPaw Version

2.2.2.post1 (pip install; `qwenpaw --version`)

### Description

Two related defects around **request-scoped media rejections** (a provider rejecting the current media payload because of an image dimension / pixel limit, not because the model lacks multimodal support). Example provider error: `Image width exceeds maximum allowed size (5120px), actual: 6735px`.

**1. The rejected media is re-sent on every model call, so the 400 repeats forever.**

The `media_payload_retry` branch in `QwenPawAgent._reasoning` (`src/qwenpaw/agents/react_agent.py`) only turns on the formatter's media-strip flag for the retry and resets it afterwards. The offending image block stays in `state.context`, so **every** subsequent LLM call re-sends it, gets the same 400, and performs the media-free retry again.

- In our deployment this branch fired **430 times within six days**, with three distinct provider messages (`... actual: 6735px`, `... actual: 10575px`, `... actual: 6750000px`), i.e. width, height and total-pixel limits alike; 337 of them fall in one two-day span, roughly once per model step.
- Every retry succeeds, so the user never sees an error — the media is just silently dropped for days, and every request pays a wasted round trip. The only thing that stopped it was clearing the context with `/new`.

`#8009` / `#8010` fixed the "requests never succeed again" variant by adding this media-free retry, and `#8395` added `mark_media_omitted_after_overflow()` to heal the stored context — but that recovery is gated on `is_request_body_too_large()` (HTTP 413 / request-body-size markers only). A 400 that reports a dimension or pixel limit does not match, so the offending block is never marked omitted.

**2. The stripped retry is misleading to the model: `view_image`'s success text survives while the image is gone.**

- `view_image` returns `[DataBlock(image), TextBlock("Image loaded: <name>")]` with `state=SUCCESS` (`src/qwenpaw/agents/tools/view_media.py`).
- `_strip_media_blocks_in_place()` (`src/qwenpaw/agents/utils/message_request_normalizer.py`) removes media blocks but keeps sibling text blocks, and only substitutes `MEDIA_UNSUPPORTED_PLACEHOLDER` when the whole tool-result output becomes empty.
- Result: the request contains `Image loaded: <name>`, no pixels, and no "omitted" hint. The model can therefore answer as if it had seen the image. In our run it produced a long, detailed description of a completely different document than the one in the image.

This is the same failure mode as `#2873` ("`view_image` reports `Image loaded: …` but no pixel data reaches the model"). `#2873` fixed the attach path; the strip-on-retry path still recreates it.

I checked `main` as well (repo `__version__` is `2.3.0b3`): the `media_payload_retry` branch still only sets the strip flag, `is_request_body_too_large()` still matches only 413/body-size markers, and `view_media.py` still returns `Image loaded: <name>`. So the loop above appears to be present on `main` too.

**Related issues/PRs:** #8009 #8010 #8395 #2873 #5821 #8474 #7671 #7201

**Security considerations:** none.

### Component(s) Affected

- [x] Core / Backend (app, agents, config, providers, utils, local_models)

### Environment

- **QwenPaw version:** 2.2.2.post1
- **OS:** Windows 11
- **Install method:** pip
- **Python version:** 3.12
- **Provider:** any OpenAI-compatible endpoint that enforces an image dimension/pixel limit (reproduced with a 5120 px limit)

### Steps to Reproduce

No real image or user data is needed — the trigger is the image **dimensions**, not its content.

1. Generate a synthetic image that exceeds the provider's width limit:

   ```python
   from PIL import Image
   Image.new("RGB", (6735, 2753), (240, 240, 240)).save("wide.png")
   ```

2. Start a fresh session and have the agent `view_image` (or attach) `wide.png` once. The image enters the stored context.
3. Ask any follow-up question. The provider rejects the request; the agent logs the warning below and retries with all media stripped, so the turn still completes.
4. Ask another question. The **same warning appears again** for the next model call, and from then on for every model call / ReAct step in that session. Every image in that session — including images attached later — is stripped from every request.
5. In the same session, `view_image` a small synthetic image (e.g. 200×100) and ask what it contains. The tool result reports `Image loaded: small.png` with success state, but the request carries no image, so the model has to guess.

### Actual vs Expected

- **Actual:** a single request-scoped media rejection poisons every later request (one 400 + one wasted retry per model call, media silently lost) until the context is cleared; and the stripped retry still tells the model `Image loaded: <name>`, so the model may describe an image it never received.
- **Expected:**
  1. When a request-scoped media rejection happens, mark the offending historical block as omitted once (the `#8395` mechanism / `mark_media_omitted_after_overflow`), so later turns do not replay it — or downscale the offending image and retry once.
  2. When media is stripped, replace the success text with an explicit placeholder (e.g. `[image omitted: not sent to the model]`) instead of keeping `Image loaded: …`.
  3. Optionally pre-check/resize against a per-provider `max_image_side` instead of relying on the provider to reject.
  4. Optionally surface a rate-limited one-line notice to the user instead of swallowing the rejection.

### Logs / Screenshots

Text only (paths reduced to package-relative form; one occurrence shown, the message is identical apart from the provider request id):

```text
WARNING | qwenpaw/agents/react_agent.py | _reasoning failed because the provider rejected the media payload itself
(Error code: 400 - {'error': {'code': 'invalid_parameter', 'message': 'Image width exceeds maximum allowed size
(5120px), actual: 6735px', 'type': 'invalid_request_error'}}); stripping media from the retry request.
Stored history remains unchanged, and no capability loss is cached.
```

The same branch also fired for `actual: 10575px` (height) and `actual: 6750000px` (total pixels), so this is not specific to one image or one limit unit.

### Additional Notes

- Minimal fix locations: `QwenPawAgent._reasoning` (`media_payload_retry` branch), `_strip_media_blocks_in_place()`, and the `view_image` success text.
- Happy to prepare a PR for (1) + (2) with a synthetic-image regression test if the direction is acceptable.
- I can share more details privately if needed.

issues.title: [Bug] Checkpoint service fails on Git long-path prefix + WeChat channel stuck at DEPENDENCY_ENVIRONMENT_AMBIGUOUS (Windows, 2.3.0-beta.2)
issues.body:
## Environment

- QwenPaw Desktop: `2.3.0-beta.2`
- OS: Windows 11 (Build 26300)
- Git: `2.51.0.windows.1`
- `HKLM\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Control\FileSystem\LongPathsEnabled` = `1`
- No `GIT_*` environment variables set at process / user / machine level
- Data dir: `C:\Users\<user>\.qwenpaw`
- Install dir: `D:\工具软件\QwenPaw\QwenPaw Desktop`

---

## Bug 1: Checkpoint service initialization always fails

### Symptom

The checkpoint / workspace snapshot service fails on every startup. Session auto-snapshot, checkpoint rollback and POST_RESPONSE archiving are all non-functional. The failure repeats on each launch (observed 86+ times between 2026-11-01 and 2026-11-08).

### Log evidence

```
git init --bare \\?\C:\Users\<user>\.qwenpaw\workspaces\Satan\checkpoints\shadow.git
exit 128: fatal: unknown error occurred while reading the configuration files
```

`Checkpoint service initialization failed` — latest occurrence `2026-11-08 17:46:57`, target `\\?\C:\Users\<user>\.qwenpaw\workspaces\Satan`.

After failure, the `checkpoints` directory only contains a 0-byte `gitconfig` and a `gitattributes` file. `shadow.git` is never created.

### Root cause

QwenPaw passes a path prefixed with the Win32 extended-length prefix `\\?\` to `git init --bare`. Git for Windows `2.51.0` rejects this form and fails to read its configuration, exiting with code 128.

This is not a local Git or OS configuration issue:
- `LongPathsEnabled=1` is already enabled
- no `GIT_CONFIG_*` variables exist
- setting `core.longpaths=true` does not help

The prefix is injected by the application itself, so it cannot be worked around from the OS or Git side.

### Expected

Checkpoint service should initialize successfully. The `\\?\` prefix should be stripped before being passed to Git, or `os.path.realpath` / `Path.resolve()` results should not be forwarded verbatim to `git`.

---

## Bug 2: WeChat channel stuck at `DEPENDENCY_ENVIRONMENT_AMBIGUOUS`

### Symptom

With `channels.wechat.enabled=true` in `config.json`, the WeChat channel never becomes usable:
- Console channel page never shows a QR code
- `GET /api/config/channels/wechat/qrcode` returns **502 Bad Gateway**
- no `wechat` runner subprocess is spawned
- `GET /api/plugins/wechat` reports `diagnostics: ["channel_validation_pending"]`
- clicking "repair dependencies" in the console returns `DEPENDENCY_ENVIRONMENT_AMBIGUOUS`

`DEPENDENCY_ENVIRONMENT_AMBIGUOUS` appears 49 times in `qwenpaw.log` (latest `2026-11-05 22:18:59`).

### What we observed

1. `~\.qwenpaw\dependency-environments\` accumulated multiple empty hash-named directories (4 at one point), each containing only `.site.dependencies.admission.lock`, `.site.dependencies.lock` and `.site.dependencies-readers\*.lease` — **no `site-packages`, no actual packages** (total size under 1 KB).
2. `~\.qwenpaw\plugin_runtime\py3.11-windows-amd64\site` was completely empty.
3. The WeChat plugin declares dependencies `httpx` and `pycryptodome` (see `requirements.txt`, `Crypto.Cipher.AES` used in `utils.py`), but `~\.qwenpaw\plugin_provisions\` only contains `computer-use.json` — there is **no `wechat.json` provision record**.
4. Plugin manifest: `version 0.1.0.dev0`, `qwenpaw_version.min = 2.2.2b4` (satisfied by host `2.3.0-beta.2`).

### Steps to reproduce

1. Enable the WeChat channel (`channels.wechat.enabled=true`).
2. Restart QwenPaw.
3. Open the console channel page → no QR code is rendered.
4. `GET /api/config/channels/wechat/qrcode` → 502.
5. Click "repair dependencies" → `DEPENDENCY_ENVIRONMENT_AMBIGUOUS`.

### What we already tried (all ineffective)

- Manually installed `httpx>=0.27.0` and `pycryptodome` into the shared dependency site (`plugin_runtime\py3.11-windows-amd64\site`) via `pip --target`; imports verified OK (`import httpx`, `from Crypto.Cipher import AES`).
- Deleted all empty `dependency-environments` directories while the app was fully stopped, then restarted.
- Result: after restart the app **immediately recreated multiple environment directories within the same second** (two dirs created at `20:42:34`, a third at `20:44:06`). The ambiguity therefore returns and cannot be cleared by deleting the directories.
- `POST /api/plugins/wechat/repair-dependencies` returns **409 Conflict** with an empty response body; `reload` / `validate` endpoints return **405**.
- `GET /api/config/channels/wechat` reports `enabled: false` while `config.json` on disk has `channels.wechat.enabled: true` — runtime state and persisted config disagree.

### Expected

- The dependency resolver should converge on a single dependency environment per plugin instead of generating multiple candidates for the same plugin.
- `repair-dependencies` should return a meaningful error body instead of an empty 409.
- If `channels.wechat.enabled=true` is persisted, the runtime channel state should reflect it after restart.

### Additional note

`plugin_provisions` lacks a `wechat` entry, which may cause the validator to treat the plugin dependencies as "unplanned" and refuse to leave `channel_validation_pending`. Whether this is intentional is unclear from the logs.

---

## Impact

- Bug 1: checkpoint / rollback / auto-archive silently broken on Windows with recent Git versions.
- Bug 2: the WeChat channel is completely unusable — no QR code can be obtained, so no login/authorization is possible.

Happy to provide the full `qwenpaw.log` (2.2 MB) and any additional diagnostics if useful.

issues.title: [Bug]: QQ channel `enabled` flag silently reset to `false` after config reload/restart, breaks message reception with no warning log
issues.body:
## QwenPaw Version

2.2.2.post1

## Description

After a system optimization / restart (config reload), the QQ channel's `enabled` flag in `config.json` is **silently set to `false`**, so the bot stops receiving and sending QQ messages entirely — with no startup warning and no log entry explaining why. The channel configuration itself (app_id, client_secret, etc. in `agent.json` / channel config) remains intact and correct; only the `enabled` boolean flips. The user has no way to know the channel was disabled until they notice the bot stopped replying.

**Related PR(s):** none

**Security considerations:** none

## Component(s) Affected

- [x] Core / Backend (app, agents, config, providers, utils, local_models)
- [x] Channels (DingTalk, Feishu, QQ, Discord, iMessage, etc.)

## Environment

- **QwenPaw version:** 2.2.2.post1
- **OS:** Linux (container, NFS-backed persistent disk)
- **Install method:** pip (cloud deployment)
- **Python version (if applicable):** 3.11
- **Channel:** QQ (QQ Guild open platform)

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Have a fully working QQ channel configuration (correct app_id / client_secret, `enabled: true`).
2. Trigger a config reload or a framework restart (e.g., routine optimization/restart of the deployment).
3. Observe the QQ channel's `enabled` flag in `config.json`.

## Actual vs Expected

- **Actual:** after reload/restart, `enabled` is silently `false`; the bot stops receiving/sending QQ messages; no log line or startup warning mentions the channel being disabled. The channel is effectively dead until someone manually edits `config.json` back to `enabled: true`.
- **Expected:**
  1. The `enabled` flag should be **persisted** and survive config reload/restart without being reset.
  2. If the framework *intentionally* disables a channel during reload, it should emit a **warning log** at startup explaining which channel was disabled and why.
  3. Startup should run a lightweight **health check** over all configured channels' `enabled` state and surface any unexpected changes.

## Logs / Screenshots

No relevant log output exists — this is precisely the bug: the state change happens with zero log signal, so there is nothing to grep for. Confirmed by inspecting `config.json` after restart and comparing before/after values of the QQ channel's `enabled` field.

## Additional Notes

### Root cause hypothesis

The config (re)write path during reload/optimization appears to normalize or reset the `enabled` flag for all channels to a default (`false`) instead of preserving the previously persisted value. The fix likely needs to (a) treat `enabled` as an explicit persisted user preference that must be read back and re-applied rather than re-defaulted on reload, and (b) add a log line whenever a channel's `enabled` state ends up different from the previously persisted value.

### Impact

Any multi-channel deployment where QQ is the primary interaction channel silently loses that channel on every restart/reload, with no alerting. Operators only find out when the bot stops replying, and must manually diff `config.json` to discover the cause.

issues.title: feat(observability): notify user when daemon silently falls back to a different model

labels.name: enhancement
labels.description: New feature or request

issues.body:
## Problem

When a provider's API call fails (401/403/timeout/network error), QwenPaw's daemon **silently falls back** to the next model in the fallback chain. The user sees a response from a different model but has **no indication** that a fallback occurred.

### Real-world impact

I hit this with **komect** provider (China Mobile LLM gateway):
1. User presses TG keyboard button → `/model komect:qwen38-27b-guangdong`
2. Daemon switches `active_model` to komect ✅
3. Daemon calls komect API → **401 Unauthorized** (expired API key)
4. Daemon **silently falls back** to `qwen3.8-max` (first in fallback chain)
5. User asks "你是什么大模型" → gets `qwen3.8-max`'s answer
6. User thinks the keyboard button didn't work, but it did — the fallback was invisible

This is confusing because:
- The user explicitly selected a model but got a different one
- No error message, no warning, no indication of what happened
- Debugging requires checking daemon logs or manually curl-testing the provider

### Related issues

- #8096 (surface `finish_reason: length` truncation in metadata) — same observability gap
- #7738 (filter unrecognized kwargs) — different root cause but same "silent failure" pattern
- #8092 (content-inspection false positives) — fallback exists but isn't triggered correctly

## Proposed solution

Add a **fallback notification** mechanism:

### Option A: Response metadata
Include fallback info in the response metadata (similar to #8096's approach):
```json
{
  "content": "...",
  "metadata": {
    "model_used": "qwen3.8-max",
    "model_requested": "komect:qwen38-27b-guangdong",
    "fallback_reason": "401 Unauthorized",
    "fallback_chain_position": 1
  }
}
```

### Option B: System message injection
Inject a system-level message visible to the user:
```
⚠️ Model fallback: komect:qwen38-27b-guangdong failed (401), using qwen3.8-max instead.
```

### Option C: Configurable behavior
Let users choose:
- `fallback_notification: silent | metadata | message | error`
- Default: `metadata` (non-intrusive but debuggable)

## Why this matters

1. **Debuggability**: Users can quickly identify provider issues (expired keys, network problems, quota limits)
2. **Trust**: Users know which model actually generated the response
3. **Cost awareness**: Fallback might use a more expensive model than intended
4. **Long-running tasks**: Silent fallback mid-task can cause inconsistent behavior

## Environment

- QwenPaw version: latest (2026-10-04)
- Deployment: container on Alibaba Cloud Singapore
- Providers affected: komect (custom gateway), potentially any provider with transient failures

## Additional context

I've documented this behavior in my local MEMORY.md as a general rule:
> **daemon 静默 fallback**: Any provider API failure → daemon silently falls back to next model in chain. User sees fallback model's response without knowing a switch occurred.

This is a common pattern that affects all users with multi-provider fallback chains.

prs.title: fix(scroll): accept Windows extended-length paths in history SQLite URIs
prs.body:
## Description

Fix SQLite URI handling for Windows workspace paths. A verbatim drive path can become `file://%3F/...`, which SQLite rejects during history-store startup, validation or backup. Raw URI concatenation in recall also mishandles reserved filename characters and can attach the wrong file.

Use one stdlib-only URI builder across history-store opens, history validation/backups, read-only recall attachment and the standalone workspace snapshot worker:

- Normalize Windows drive and UNC spellings, including case-insensitive verbatim UNC prefixes.
- Keep UNC hosts in the URI path (`file:////server/share/...`) with an empty authority.
- Percent-encode filesystem bytes, preserving POSIX non-UTF-8 filename bytes as well as Unicode, spaces, `#`, `?` and `%`.
- Reject relative paths and unsupported verbatim volume roots through one post-normalization absolute-path check.
- Preserve `ro`, `rw` and `rwc` connection modes and the recall authorizer.

Ship readable recall/backup worker sources and the shared helper in the desktop bundle so isolated workers can load the helper without importing QwenPaw.

Fixes #8585. Related: [Windows release verification failure](https://github.com/agentscope-ai/QwenPaw/actions/runs/42206852987/job/127889260310).

## Type of Change

- [x] Bug fix

## Component(s) Affected

- Core / Backend: Scroll history, recall and SQLite backups
- Desktop packaging
- Tests

## Testing

Includes upstream `main` at `0df62c05d`, preserving the original contributor's commits.

- URI formatting for POSIX paths, Windows drives, UNC paths, verbatim prefixes, relative/volume-root rejection, and filename escaping.
- Real SQLite creation, maintenance opens, validation, recall reads and both snapshot paths.
- `ro` write rejection and `rw` missing-file rejection.
- Standalone recall and snapshot execution under `python -I -S` using the desktop source layout, without importing QwenPaw.
- Context, backup/restore, startup, service-manager and all Tauri unit tests.

## Evidence

The URI regression for POSIX filename bytes was reproduced before fixing it: `Path.as_uri()` preserved byte `0xFF` as `%FF`, while direct UTF-8 quoting raised `UnicodeEncodeError`. The shared builder now uses filesystem encoding before percent-encoding; the regression test passes. A Linux filesystem case exercises store creation, recall, validation and both snapshots using that filename.

Local validation on macOS / Python 3.11.12:

```text
PYTHONPATH=src python -m pytest tests/unit/agents/context tests/unit/backup tests/unit/app/test_scroll_startup_io.py tests/unit/app/workspace/test_service_manager.py tests/unit/tauri -q -rs
994 passed, 6 skipped in 27.15s

pre-commit run --files <all changed Python files>
All applicable hooks passed

git diff --check
Passed
```

The six local skips are four native Windows filesystem cases and two Linux cases (non-UTF-8 filesystem I/O and POSIX DMS locking). Windows installer verification has not been rerun for this update.

The author supplied additional [Windows and loopback SMB verification](https://github.com/agentscope-ai/QwenPaw/pull/8587#issuecomment-6731997126); that evidence predates the latest filesystem-encoding update.
