prs.title: fix(security): flag inline Office COM automation in shell commands
prs.body:
## Summary

On Windows with approval level `auto` and the sandbox off, an agent-authored
inline Office COM command runs instead of being stopped.
`PowerPoint.Application`, `Excel.Application`, `Word.Application` and
`Outlook.Application` are single-instance COM servers, so attaching to one
binds to the **user's** already-open app and `Quit()` on that object
terminates the user's document — not a private automation instance.

The command matched no detection rule, so `GovernancePolicy.evaluate`
classified it as `SANDBOX_FALLBACK`, and `ResourceGovernor` rewrites that
decision to `ALLOW` whenever the sandbox is unavailable
(`running unsandboxed`). Nothing sat between the model and the user's
Office process.

This adds a `CRITICAL` rule that matches the COM construction itself, so
the call lands on the approval path instead of the unsandboxed one.

Refs #8002

## What Problem This Solves

A user had PowerPoint open on a real file. With approval level `auto` and
the security sandbox off, the agent emitted an Office COM self-check such as
`New-Object -ComObject PowerPoint.Application` followed by `Quit()`, and the
shell tool ran it. PowerShell attached to the **running** PowerPoint COM
server and `Quit()` closed the user's presentation — with data loss and no
warning, because the decision path never asked.

The root cause is not a missing sandbox rule but the fallback rewrite: an
unmatched shell command is `SANDBOX_FALLBACK`, and when the sandbox is
unusable `ResourceGovernor` turns that into `ALLOW`. Any command no rule
recognises is therefore executed unsandboxed and unguarded.

## Changes

`src/qwenpaw/security/tool_guard/rules/dangerous_shell_commands.yaml` —
new `TOOL_CMD_OFFICE_COM_AUTOMATION` rule (`category: resource_abuse`,
`severity: CRITICAL`) with three patterns:

1. a COM construction verb (`New-Object`, `GetActiveObject`, `GetObject`,
   `CreateObject`, `CreateInstance`, `GetTypeFromProgID`, `Dispatch`,
   `DispatchEx`) followed by an Office `*.Application` ProgID — catches
   `New-Object -ComObject PowerPoint.Application`,
   `[Activator]::CreateInstance([Type]::GetTypeFromProgID("Word.Application"))`,
   `win32com.client.Dispatch("Excel.Application")`
2. the same pairing in the other order, for the split
   `$t = GetTypeFromProgID(...); CreateInstance($t)` spelling
3. `.Quit()` invoked on an attached Office server

## Behaviour

| command | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| `New-Object -ComObject PowerPoint.Application; $ppt.Quit()` | `sandbox_fallback` → `ALLOW` (sandbox off) | `ask` |
| `echo hello` | `sandbox_fallback` | `sandbox_fallback` |
| `python render_deck.py --out deck.pptx` | `sandbox_fallback` | `sandbox_fallback` |
| `git commit -m 'document Word.Application'` | `sandbox_fallback` | `sandbox_fallback` |

Mere mentions of the ProgID do not match, so built-in scripts that only
`Close()` a private temp presentation are unaffected (verified: no
occurrence of these ProgIDs or `ComObject`/`win32com` anywhere in `src/`,
`tests/`, `scripts/`, `plugins/` or `e2e/`).

Note the rule escalates to `ask`, not `deny`: `execution_level=off` is
documented as "tool guard completely disabled", so nothing fires there by
design and this change does not alter that.

## Evidence

End-to-end through `GovernancePolicy.evaluate` with the bundled rules
loaded (before → after):

```
$ python - <<'PY'
pol = _create_default_policy()
spec = ToolCallSpec(tool_name="Bash",
    target='New-Object -ComObject PowerPoint.Application; $ppt.Quit()',
    agent_id="a", session_id="s")
for level in ("auto", "smart", "strict", "off"):
    pol.execution_level = level
    d = pol.evaluate(spec)
    print(level, "->", d.action.value, d.source)
PY
# before: auto -> sandbox_fallback  smart -> sandbox_fallback  strict -> ask  off -> sandbox_fallback
auto     -> ask              source=detection_rules
smart    -> ask              source=detection_rules
strict   -> ask              source=STRICT mode
off      -> sandbox_fallback source=sandbox

benign auto     -> sandbox_fallback source=sandbox
benign smart    -> sandbox_fallback source=sandbox
benign off      -> sandbox_fallback source=sandbox
```

Full validation:

```
$ pytest tests/unit/governance tests/unit/security/tool_guard   # 842 passed
$ pytest tests/unit -k "tool_guard or governance or detector"   # 874 passed
$ black --line-length=79 / flake8 / pylint (10.00)              # clean
```

prs.title: feat(providers): let custom gateways declare OpenAI prompt cache params
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Closes #8058.

Since #7899, request parameters pass through `cache_request()` in
`providers/adapters/cache_policy.py`, which rejects
`prompt_cache_key` / `prompt_cache_retention` unless the provider's cache
capabilities include `openai` / `openai_explicit`.
`OpenAIProvider.cache_capabilities()` only returns those modes for
`api.openai.com`, so a custom provider pointing at an OpenAI-compatible
Responses gateway fails **before sending anything** with
`ValueError: Unsupported cache control: prompt_cache_key` — including when the
key is only in `extra_body`, which `cache_request()` lifts out and re-validates.

Users had no way to declare the capability: `cache_modes` is a class
attribute, so `"cache_modes": ["openai"]` in the provider JSON is ignored and
dropped on the next save. Losing `prompt_cache_key` measurably lowers cache
hit rates on long agent sessions that share a prefix.

## Change

New persisted provider field (backend-only, default off):

```json
"supports_openai_prompt_cache": true
```

`OpenAIProvider.cache_capabilities()` now opens **only** the explicit prompt
cache parameters for a non-`api.openai.com` base URL when this flag is set —
i.e. it adds the `openai` mode, which is exactly what gates
`prompt_cache_key` / `prompt_cache_retention` in `cache_policy.py`.

Deliberately still gated (`openai_explicit` is not granted): `prompt_cache_options`,
`enable_prompt_cache_breakpoint` and `cache_control` keep raising, so the opt-in
cannot be used to unlock TTL/breakpoint controls that a host model may not have.

Why a config flag instead of forwarding unconditionally for custom providers
(the issue's option 2): the wire-level gate is intentionally fail-closed for
unverified services, and this keeps it that way while giving operators a
declared, reviewable escape hatch. Because it is a real pydantic field, it is
no longer discarded on save (the `cache_modes` class attribute was), and
`update_config()` only touches keys present in the request, so console-driven
provider updates do not clobber it.

## Evidence

- `tests/unit/providers/test_openai_provider.py`:
  - `test_custom_gateway_rejects_prompt_cache_key_by_default` — the issue's
    minimal repro (both `prompt_cache_key` in kwargs and in `extra_body`)
    still raises before this flag is set.
  - `test_declared_capability_forwards_prompt_cache_parameters` — with the
    flag, both forms forward a single `prompt_cache_key`, and
    `prompt_cache_retention` too.
  - `test_declaration_does_not_unlock_explicit_cache_controls` —
    `prompt_cache_options` and `enable_prompt_cache_breakpoint` still raise.
  - `test_official_host_capabilities_are_unaffected` — `api.openai.com`
    routing is unchanged, `gpt-5.6` still gets `openai_explicit`.
- `tests/unit/providers/test_provider_manager.py`:
  - `test_custom_provider_prompt_cache_declaration_from_json` — a custom
    provider JSON with the flag loads through `_init_from_storage`, exposes the
    capability, and `prepare_request()` forwards the key end to end.
  - `test_custom_provider_without_declaration_keeps_gate_closed` — a legacy
    custom JSON (no key) still rejects, so upgrades change no behavior.
- Full runs: `pytest tests/unit/providers/` → 895 passed.
- Lint: `add-trailing-comma` before `black --line-length=79`, `flake8` clean;
  `pylint` 8.49/10 with only pre-existing message categories (f-string style,
  module length) — nothing new beyond the two that already fire on `main`.

prs.title: fix(token-usage): count Anthropic cache tokens in the live context meter
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Closes #8057.

For Anthropic Messages providers, `usage.input_tokens` counts only the
uncached part of the prompt; cache reads (`cache_read_input_tokens`) and
cache writes (`cache_creation_input_tokens`) are reported separately. On a
long cached turn An example from the issue: `input_tokens=3000`,
`cache_read=120000`, `cache_write=5000` on a 200k window showed as 3k/200k
(1.5%) in the console context meter instead of 128k/200k (64%).

`TokenRecordingModelWrapper._record_usage()` set `last_prompt_tokens` to the
raw `input_tokens`, even though the same method already computes the correct
input denominator in `cache_eligible_input_tokens` (the value used for the
cache hit rate).

## Change

`last_prompt_tokens` — the per-request value the console channel sends as
`context_usage.estimated_tokens` in the live `turn_usage` event
(`app/channels/console/channel.py:440`) — now uses the cache-aware
denominator:

- Anthropic: `input_tokens + cache_read + cache_write` (cache reads/writes
  really are part of the prompt the model processed).
- OpenAI Chat / Responses: unchanged, their `prompt_tokens` / `input_tokens`
  already include cached tokens, and `_cache_usage_metrics()` returns
  `cache_eligible == prompt_tokens` for them.
- Providers without verifiable cache semantics: unchanged
  (`cache_observed` is False, so the raw input tokens are kept and the cache
  counters are zeroed by the existing guard).

Session totals (`prompt_tokens`, the usage event) deliberately still carry
the uncached input tokens, so billing/statistics input accounting is not
affected — only the live per-request context meter.

## Evidence

- `tests/unit/token_usage/test_token_usage.py`:
  - `test_last_prompt_tokens_counts_anthropic_cache_tokens` — the issue's
    numbers (3000 / 120000 / 5000) now produce `last_prompt_tokens == 128000`
    while `prompt_tokens` stays 3000. Fails on `main` (asserted 128000 == 3000).
  - `test_last_prompt_tokens_keeps_openai_input_tokens` — an OpenAI adapter
    with `cache_input_tokens=3000` inside a 4000-token prompt keeps
    `last_prompt_tokens == 4000` (no double counting).
  - `test_last_prompt_tokens_ignores_unverifiable_cache_tokens` — an unknown
    adapter keeps raw input tokens and drops the cache counters.
- Full runs: `pytest tests/unit/token_usage/ tests/unit/channels/test_console.py`
  → 142 passed.
- Lint: `add-trailing-comma` + `black --line-length=79` clean,
  `flake8` clean on the changed lines (the one B017 hit is pre-existing at
  `tests/unit/token_usage/test_token_usage.py:439`), `pylint` 9.48/10 with the
  pre-existing import-outside-toplevel note only.

prs.title: feat(browser): let config drop Playwright default launch arguments
prs.body:
## Summary

With `identity: "avatar"` and a real `user_data_dir`, extensions installed in
that persistent profile never load, because Playwright injects
`--disable-extensions` into the Chromium command line and QwenPaw has no way
to remove it.

`BrowserConfig.args` can only **append** switches, and Chromium treats a
boolean switch as "present means on", so re-appending
`--disable-extensions` does not cancel it. Playwright's only supported way
to drop a default is `ignore_default_args`, which QwenPaw never forwarded —
the only workaround was byte-patching
`playwright/driver/package/lib/server/chromium/chromiumSwitches.js` inside
`site-packages`, which a Playwright upgrade silently reverts.

This adds `browser.ignore_default_args` and forwards it end to end.

Refs #7984

## What Problem This Solves

A user running QwenPaw Desktop 2.2.1 on Windows configured the Browser SDK
with `backend: "launch"`, `identity: "avatar"` and a real `user_data_dir`,
then installed the SwitchyOmega proxy extension in that profile. The
extension never loaded: `chrome://extensions` was empty and the main
`chrome.exe` command line contained `--disable-extensions` (verified with
`Get-CimInstance Win32_Process`). Without the extension, sites only
reachable through the proxy failed with
`Page.goto: net::ERR_CONNECTION_TIMED_OUT`.

Because `browser.args` can only append and Chromium boolean switches are
"present means on", there was no configuration-level fix — the user had to
edit Playwright's compiled driver JS.

## Changes

| File | Change |
|---|---|
| `src/qwenpaw/config/config.py` | `BrowserConfig.ignore_default_args: List[str]` (default `[]`) |
| `src/qwenpaw/browser/runtime/launch_resolve.py` | include it in the resolved launch spec |
| `src/qwenpaw/browser/runtime/ownership_adapter.py` | forward it in the `open_session` request |
| `src/qwenpaw/browser/control_link/playwright/adapter.py` | `_build_launch_kwargs` passes it to Playwright when non-empty |
| `website/public/docs/browser.{en,zh}.md` | document the field |

`_build_launch_kwargs` is the single choke point for launch kwargs, and both
`chromium.launch` and `chromium.launch_persistent_context` receive
`**launch_kwargs`, so one change covers the incognito and profile paths.

## Usage

```json
{
  "browser": {
    "backend": "launch",
    "identity": "avatar",
    "user_data_dir": "path\\to\\User Data",
    "ignore_default_args": ["--disable-extensions"]
  }
}
```

Scope: `backend: "launch"` only. `managed_cdp` / `connect_cdp` attach to an
already-running browser and have no launch command line to adjust (the CDP
adapter builds its own argv and does not use Playwright's default list).

## Evidence

The switch is traced from config to the Playwright launch call:

```
$ pytest tests/unit/browser tests/unit/config -q
403 passed

$ pytest tests/unit/browser/control_link/test_playwright_adapter_gate.py -q
13 passed
```

`test_open_session_reaches_playwright_with_ignore_default_args` drives
`_m_open_session` for real (with a stubbed Playwright) and asserts the value
reaches `chromium.launch`:

```
captured.get("ignore_default_args") == ["--disable-extensions"]
captured.get("executable_path")    == "/usr/bin/chromium"
```

Each forwarding test was verified to fail when its corresponding change is
reverted:

```
# adapter.py change reverted:
FAILED test_launch_kwargs_forward_ignore_default_args
FAILED test_launch_kwargs_copy_ignore_default_args
FAILED test_open_session_reaches_playwright_with_ignore_default_args
3 failed, 9 passed
```

Other checks:

```
$ pytest tests/integration/test_browser_module.py   # 17 passed
$ black --line-length=79 / flake8 / pylint (10.00)   # clean
```

`tests/integration/browser/*e2e*` has 7 failures on clean `main` here too —
they need a real Playwright/Chromium install, which this environment does not
have. Unrelated to this change.

prs.title: fix(desktop): open workspace HTML via the decoded local path
prs.body:
## Description

The legacy desktop bridge (`WebViewAPI`, pywebview shell) opened workspace HTML previews by handing the percent-encoded `file://` URI from `GET /api/workspace/html-file-uri` (`Path.as_uri()`, UTF-8 percent-encoded) straight to `webbrowser.open`.

On Windows, `webbrowser`→`os.startfile`→ShellExecute percent-decodes with the **ANSI code page** — GBK on Chinese systems — so the UTF-8 encoding of a Chinese workspace path is decoded to garbage and Windows reports `ERROR_FILE_NOT_FOUND` (issue #8502 复现 A; the same failure mode was verified with `ShellExecuteW` in the issue).

This change decodes the URI host-agnostically with `urllib.request.url2pathname` (UTF-8 aware, converts URI separators to native ones) and passes the **native local path** to `webbrowser.open` instead of the `file://` URL.

**Related Issue:** Fixes #8502 (复现 A — the pywebview legacy bridge layer)

**Security Considerations:** None — the resolved URI already passed the loopback + `/api/workspace/html-file-uri` gate; this only changes how the resolved `file` URI is handed to the OS opener (same file the endpoint validated — suffix recheck unchanged).

## Type of Change

- [x] Bug fix

## Component(s) Affected

- [x] Core / Backend (app, agents, config, providers, utils, local_models)
- [ ] Console (frontend web UI) — symptom surfaces here; the change is in the desktop bridge
- [ ] Channels

## Testing

..ss...                       [100%]
5 passed, 2 skipped in 0.43s

New regression case: `test_open_workspace_html_opens_the_decoded_local_path` builds a real workspace file at `workspace_dir/工作区/report.html`, feeds its `as_uri()` (percent-encoded) through the endpoint payload the same way the bridge consumes it, and asserts `webbrowser.open` receives the decoded native path. The test fails against `main` (assertion showed the encoded \'/C:/Users/.../%E5%B7%A5...\' arriving at the opener).

## Evidence

```
$ uv run pytest tests/unit/cli/test_desktop_cmd.py -q
......ss                       [100%]
5 passed, 2 skipped in 0.43s

$ uv run pytest "tests/unit/cli/test_desktop_cmd.py::test_open_workspace_html_opens_the_decoded_local_path" -q   # with the fix reverted

```

E         At index 0 diff: \'/C:/Users/Tony/AppData/Local/Temp/tmpn6jmm_e7/工作区/report.html\' != \'C:\Users\Tony\AppData\Local\Temp\tmpn6jmm_e7\工作区\report.html\'

prs.title: fix(ollama): size context window from num_ctx instead of 128k default
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Ollama already opts out of the static cloud context catalog (`_context_catalog_enabled → False`), which is correct: a local `qwen3-coder:30b` truncates at `num_ctx`, not at the family's cloud window.

But discovery never filled that gap. `fetch_models` reused the OpenAI `/v1/models` parser, whose rows do not carry `context_length` / `num_ctx`, so every Ollama model stayed at the **128k placeholder**. Compaction then compared against `0.8 × 131072` while the server often serves a few thousand to a few tens of thousands of tokens.

This is **independent of #7979** (and of open PR #7986):

| | #7979 / #7986 | This PR |
|---|---|---|
| Provider | custom / llama.cpp OpenAI-compatible | built-in **Ollama** |
| Failure mode | cloud catalog matches alias → **1M** | catalog already skipped → **128k default** |
| Fix | skip pattern catalog for custom endpoints | read native Ollama context into `max_input_length_auto_detected` |

A fix for #7979 does not call `/api/show` or `/api/ps`, and does not change Ollama.

## Changes

`OllamaProvider.fetch_models` lists models with `/v1/models`, then sets `max_input_length_auto_detected` from native Ollama signals. Precedence:

1. `GET /api/ps` served `context_length` when the model is loaded (reflects `OLLAMA_CONTEXT_LENGTH` and the load-time window). A hit skips `/api/show`.
2. Modelfile `num_ctx` from a successful `POST /api/show`.
3. If neither is available, leave the value unset (do **not** invent a 4096 or other fallback). The 128k default remains until a later successful probe reports a real window.

GGUF `*.context_length` is **not** used. That field is the model's maximum supported context, not the window Ollama is serving.

Failed native probes (`None`, 401, 403, timeout, or an invalid payload) leave the model **unchanged**, so merge keeps any previous auto-detected window. A successful `/api/show` that omits `num_ctx` clears a stale auto-detected value **only when `/api/ps` also succeeded** (and reported no served window). A failed `/api/ps` followed by an unknown show does not clear. Non-string `parameters` are treated as malformed (retain the old value), not as “successful but unknown”.

`check_model_connection` uses the lightweight `/v1/models` list (`super().fetch_models`). It only checks that the model id exists and does not call `/api/show` per model.

Native `/api/ps` and `/api/show` probes reuse `_build_default_headers()` and add `Authorization: Bearer` when an API key is set and Authorization is not already configured. Explicit user `max_input_length` still wins over auto-detection, and the cloud catalog stays disabled for Ollama. `ModelInfo.max_input_length_auto_detected` allows `ge=1` so a small explicit `num_ctx` (for example 512) is kept.

Model id aliases parse the tag only in the final path segment, so `registry.example.com:5000/team/qwen3` still matches `/api/ps` rows tagged `:latest`.

## Testing

```bash
PYTHONPATH=src python -m pytest \
  tests/unit/providers/test_ollama_provider.py \
  tests/unit/providers/test_context_windows.py -q
# 101 passed
```

`black --line-length=79` is clean on the touched files.

Coverage includes precedence (served `/api/ps` → Modelfile `num_ctx` → unset when unknown), GGUF `*.context_length` ignored, 401/403 and timeout on `/api/show` leaving `max_input_length_auto_detected` unset, failed `/api/ps` + unknown show retaining a prior window, malformed `parameters` retaining a prior window, registry:port `:latest` alias matching, `check_model_connection` not calling `/api/show`, authenticated native probes, the catalog still skipped without detection, and explicit `max_input_length` still winning over auto-detected values.

prs.title: fix(media): downscale oversized images and mark stripped media as omitted
prs.body:
## Scope

Type: A (single-point fix) — three functions across `image_freezing.py` and
`message_request_normalizer.py`, mirrored once in `react_agent.py`.

## Description

Two defects on the media path share one real-world trigger: an agent loaded a
9000px-wide PNG through `view_image`, the provider rejected the payload
("You have uploaded an unsupported image"), and QwenPaw's recovery stripped
**every** image from the request. The model then answered from a tool result
that still read `Image loaded: timeline_states_48h.png` — it was told it had
seen an image it never received.

**1. Oversized images are downscaled before they are frozen**

`freeze_image_bytes` enforced the byte cap only. Dimensions were never
checked, so a wide-but-lightweight PNG (line art, timeline charts) passed
straight through and was rejected downstream. `MAX_IMAGE_SIDE = 8192` is now
enforced by `_downscale_if_oversized`, which keeps the aspect ratio, preserves
alpha, and re-encodes in the original format (JPEG/WebP/PNG). Animated GIFs are
passed through untouched so frames are not dropped, and any encoder failure
falls back to the original bytes — this path can only improve the odds of a
successful request, never break one that used to work.

**2. Stripping media now leaves an explicit marker**

When only some blocks of a `tool_result` were stripped, the surviving text was
kept as-is — that is how the model ended up holding an "Image loaded" claim
with no image behind it. The blanket "this model supports no media" strip now
appends `MEDIA_UNSUPPORTED_PLACEHOLDER` to the surviving output, in the same
shape as its siblings (dict for 1.x blocks, block object for 2.0).

Targeted strips (audio / video / document / empty) are deliberate per-modality
decisions, so they keep their current output shape. This is a deliberate
behaviour change and is covered by an updated assertion in
`test_react_agent_media_strip.py::test_nested_media_in_tool_result_stripped`.

## Evidence

Before / after, same input (9000x60 PNG):

| | Before | After |
| --- | --- | --- |
| frozen image | 9000x60, sent verbatim | 8192x55 |
| provider payload | rejected as unsupported | accepted |
| tool result text after strip | `Image loaded: x.png` | `Image loaded: x.png` + `[Media content removed - model does not support this media type]` |

New regression tests:

- `tests/unit/agents/utils/test_image_freezing_oversize.py` — oversized side
  is downscaled with the aspect ratio preserved; an in-limit image stays
  byte-identical; an oversized GIF is left untouched.
- `tests/unit/agents/test_media_omit_marker.py` — a partial strip leaves the
  marker next to the surviving text; an all-media strip still collapses to the
  placeholder.

## Follow-up direction

The other two halves of the same bug. They are left out of this PR for now
because both need an interface decision first:

- **Per-provider media capability table** (max side / max bytes / accepted
  formats). Today the limit is inferred from a 400 response; with a declared
  table the request could be shaped correctly instead of being repaired after
  a rejection. It touches provider registration and the formatters.
- **Rejection-site attribution.** If each image carried an id, a rejection
  could name the offending one, and the recovery could transcode and retry
  *that* image instead of stripping every image in the request. This is what
  turns "drop all media" into "repair one image".

## Test scope

- Target: `test_image_freezing_oversize.py`, `test_media_omit_marker.py`,
  `test_message_request_normalizer.py`, `test_react_agent_media_strip.py`,
  `test_view_media.py` — 216 passed.
- Adjacent: `tests/unit/agents` — 4251 passed, 1 failed
  (`test_acp_available_commands.py::test_new_session_advertises_commands`,
  a 5s `_advertise_commands did not fire` timeout). Pre-existing: on pristine
  `upstream/main` the same file fails 2 of its 22 tests, so this is unrelated
  to the media path. Run under `reme-ai==0.4.2.0`, the version this branch
  pins.
- Lint: `pre-commit run --files <changed>` — 15 hooks passed (black, mypy,
  pylint, flake8, add-trailing-comma, docstring-first, AST, private-key,
  encoding-pragma, trailing-whitespace).

---

If either follow-up direction above matches what you have in mind, I would be
glad to open separate PRs for it once the interface is aligned. Thanks for
taking a look.

prs.title: fix(tools): decode GBK/CP936 in read/edit/grep instead of dropping bytes
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`read_file_safe` (used by `read_file` / `edit_file`) and `grep_search` decoded files as UTF-8 with `errors="ignore"`. On Chinese Windows, Notepad/legacy `.txt` / `.csv` / `.md` notes are often GBK/CP936. Every non-UTF-8 byte was deleted with no log line, so:

- `read_file` returned ASCII leftovers (e.g. `姓名: 张三` → `: `)
- `grep_search` for Chinese terms missed the file
- `edit_file` could still report success and persist the damaged snapshot as UTF-8

Markdown/skill loaders already use `decode_text_bytes_with_encoding_fallback` (utf-8 → gbk/cp936 → …). This PR routes the tool read path through the same helper.

## Changes

- `src/qwenpaw/agents/tools/utils.py`: `_read_file_safe_sync` uses the shared encoding fallback
- `src/qwenpaw/agents/tools/file_search.py`: `_walk_and_grep` reads bytes and decodes with the same fallback (files already capped at 2MB)
- Regression tests for GBK read, GBK `edit_file`, and GBK grep

## How to reproduce (before)

```python
from pathlib import Path
path = Path("note.txt")
path.write_bytes("姓名: 张三\n".encode("gbk"))
# read_file_safe previously returned ": \n"
```

## Testing

```bash
PYTHONPATH=src python -m pytest \
  tests/unit/agents/tools/test_file_io.py \
  tests/unit/agents/tools/test_file_search.py::test_walk_and_grep_matches_gbk_file -q
# 43 passed
```

Also re-ran the new GBK cases alone after rebase: 4 passed.

## Notes

- After a successful GBK decode, `edit_file` still writes with the existing suffix-based encoding (`.txt` → `utf-8-sig`). Chinese text is preserved; only the on-disk encoding may change to UTF-8, which matches the project’s Windows Excel/Notepad write path.
- CRLF whole-file rewrite and Ollama `num_ctx` sizing are separate follow-ups and are not in this PR.

Happy to adjust if maintainers prefer preserving the original GBK bytes on write as well.

prs.title: fix(channels): preserve enabled state on partial channel updates
prs.body:
## Description

Partial channel updates used to re-validate only the fields in the request, so every omitted field was reset to its schema default — a credentials-only re-save silently turned `enabled` off and the channel stopped receiving messages with no warning.

This merges the saved channel config under the incoming fields before validation, so omitted fields keep their saved values and only explicitly sent values change anything. A genuinely new channel still gets schema defaults. Saving now logs a warning when a channel's enabled state actually flips, startup warns about a configured-but-disabled channel, and rebuilding a missing agent.json from the stale root copy warns instead of silently switching channels off.

Note: the rebuild case only warns — the rebuilt profile still takes the root values, since the root copy is frozen at migration time and never synced from agent.json. Fixing that sync is separate work.

## What Problem This Solves

Issue #8475: a partial channel re-save silently reset `enabled` to its schema default (`false` for QQ), so the channel stopped receiving messages with no warning and no visible change. The same hole affected every channel: any omitted persisted field was re-defaulted on every partial update. With merge-before-validation, omitted fields keep their saved values, and an actual enabled flip is logged.

## Evidence

Reproduce-first check (repro cases now in `tests/unit/app/routers/test_config_router.py` and `tests/unit/config/test_config_model_validators_and_legacy_migration.py`):

- Before the fix: the original repro failed 3/3 on pristine HEAD `2cf28d14` (partial PUT re-defaulted `enabled`, bulk PUT re-defaulted `enabled`, rebuild from the stale root copy silently disabled the channel).
- After the fix: the adapted repro passes 3/3 (partial + bulk PUT preserve `enabled`; the rebuild case logs the warning through the real `load_agent_config` path).

Focused suites (with the fix): 193 passed, 17 skipped (`test_config_router`, validators/migration, agent-config-persistence, channel-shape-consistency) — baseline was 182 passed; the +11 are the new tests (merge-boundary unit test, partial/bulk PUT preservation, explicit-disable + warning log, no-warning-when-no-flip, new-channel schema defaults, Discord genericity, explicit-`""` clears a value, rebuild warning, silence for unconfigured channels, helper default-comparison).

Full suite: 321 failures were recorded, none in any changed or adjacent file. A `git stash` re-run of exactly those 321 on pristine main reproduces 316 identically (pre-existing); 4 more are timing-sensitive flakes that pass on re-run. One failure could not be pinpointed after a VM restart wiped the saved failure list.

Pre-commit: a scoped `run --all-files` over the 7 changed files passes every hook (mypy, black, flake8, pylint + file hooks). The full-repo verdict was lost when the runtime restarted mid-run.

Fixes #8475

Disclosure: AI coding assistance was used in preparing this change.

prs.title: fix(skills): stage skill copies inside the target workspace
prs.body:
## Description

Windows Hub Local runtimes could not install their default skills. `staged_skill_dir()` used `tempfile.mkdtemp()` under the runtime process temp directory (`working/tmp`). Inside an AppContainer, directories created there receive a protected DACL that only grants `OWNER RIGHTS`, `SYSTEM`, and `Administrators`; the AppContainer SID is absent, so creating the nested skill directory (`QA_source_index`) fails with `WinError 5`. On Python builds where `TMP_MAX` is `2147483647`, `tempfile.mkdtemp()` also spins in its `PermissionError` retry loop instead of raising, which makes the runtime look hung.

This change lets `staged_skill_dir()` accept an explicit `root_dir` and makes `SkillPoolService.download_to_workspace()` stage inside the destination workspace's `skills/` directory. That directory is part of the existing writable AppContainer mount and its children remain writable. Callers that do not pass `root_dir` keep the previous temp-directory behaviour.

A follow-up commit also extends `cleanup_orphan_skill_stages()` to scan the configured workspace `skills/` (and legacy `skill/`) roots in addition to the system temp directory, and filters the `qwenpaw_skill_stage_` prefix in `is_ignored_skill_entry()`. A process killed mid-copy therefore cannot leave permanent stage-dir garbage inside a workspace, and stage directories are never enumerated as real skills.

**Related Issue:** Relates to #8565

**Security Considerations:** No trust-boundary change. The staging directory still uses the fixed `qwenpaw_skill_stage_` prefix and `safe_skill_dir()` for path-injection hardening, and staging stays inside the per-runtime workspace mount instead of the shared system temp directory.

prs.title: fix(drivers): persist rotated refresh_token for OAuth2 auth-code providers
prs.body:
## 中文说明 / Chinese Summary

**本 PR：**

## What Problem This Solves

> 本 PR 的详细技术说明见下方英文部分。

---
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes #7053. Remote MCP servers using OAuth2 **Authorization Code** with **rotating refresh tokens** (e.g. XMind) renew `access_token` but the *rotated* `refresh_token` was never persisted. With refresh only lazily triggered inside the 5-minute margin, the old `refresh_token` eventually dies and the driver permanently degrades to manual re-auth.

## Evidence

- `StandardOAuth2Exchanger.exchange` now declares the 3-tuple return `(access_token, expires_in, rotated_refresh_token)` matching the `TokenExchanger` protocol; mypy (pre-commit) passes on the touched module.
- `python -m pytest tests/unit/app/routers/test_provider_oauth_router.py` → passed (OAuth2 router flows still green after the exchange signature change).

## Root cause

Two-part bug in `src/qwenpaw/drivers/credentials/providers.py`:

1. `StandardOAuth2Exchanger.exchange()` returned only `(access_token, expires_in)` — the new `refresh_token` from a rotating provider's response was silently dropped.
2. `OAuth2AuthCodeProvider.resolve()` wrote back only `access_token` + `expires_at`, never the rotated `refresh_token`.

## Change

- `TokenExchanger.exchange` protocol now returns a 3-tuple: `(access_token, expires_in, rotated_refresh_token)`.
- `StandardOAuth2Exchanger.exchange` returns the rotated `refresh_token` from the token response (`None` when absent, e.g. client-credentials flows or non-rotating providers); its annotation matches the protocol so mypy stays clean.
- `OAuth2AuthCodeProvider.resolve` persists the rotated `refresh_token` into the credential store alongside `access_token`.
- `OAuth2CCProvider.resolve` updated for the new tuple shape (client-credentials responses carry no refresh_token).

## Tests

Per review feedback, the standalone `tests/unit/drivers/credentials/test_providers.py` was removed (its filename collided with `tests/integration/test_providers.py` and the maintainer considered the unit test redundant). OAuth2 behavior is covered by the existing router tests (`tests/unit/app/routers/test_provider_oauth_router.py`).

prs.title: feat(agent): add /steer command for mid-execution guidance (#1775)
prs.body:
## 中文说明 / Chinese Summary

**本 PR：**

Fixes #1775.

> 本 PR 的详细技术说明见下方英文部分。

---
Fixes #1775.

## What Problem This Solves

Today there is no way to correct the agent while a turn is already running:
stopping the turn loses all progress, and waiting for it to finish means
irrelevant work keeps accumulating. `/steer <guidance>` fills this gap — it
lets the user hand the agent mid-flight guidance that takes effect on the
**next** agent turn without stopping anything.

```
/steer Focus on the error handling first
```

## How it works

- `qwenpaw/steer/store.py` — per-session hand-off buffer with a 10-minute
  TTL.
- `qwenpaw/steer/handler.py` — the `/steer` command; records the text.
- `qwenpaw/steer/hook.py` — `SteerInjectionHook`, a `HookBase` subclass at
  `PRE_AGENT_BUILD`, drains the buffer and calls `inject_context`.
- Registered in `bootstrap_factory`'s `builtin_hook_clses` and in
  `collect_builtin_command_specs()`.

## Why not true mid-execution steering

Dispatching inside a running turn needs changes to the reply loop that the
current runtime does not expose safely; injecting at `PRE_AGENT_BUILD`
achieves the same user-visible effect (the next turn follows the guidance)
without touching turn-dispatch internals.

## Evidence

- Manual run: with a long turn in flight, issuing `/steer Focus on the error
  handling first` returned an immediate acknowledgement; the subsequent turn
  opened with the injected context and the agent addressed error handling
  first (observed via turn context log).
- Without `/steer`, the same run ran to completion with no guidance applied.
- Buffer drain is one-shot: a second turn does not re-apply stale guidance;
  guidance older than the 10-minute TTL is dropped.

prs.title: fix(tools): stop the shell self-kill guard from blocking kill $PID
prs.body:
## 中文说明 / Chinese Summary

**本 PR：**

Fixes #8413.

> 本 PR 的详细技术说明见下方英文部分。

---
Fixes #8413.

## What Problem This Solves

`execute_shell_command`'s self-kill guard refused legitimate commands that kill *another* process via the shell variable `$PID` — the canonical workflow `PID=$(pgrep mydaemon) && kill $PID` was rejected with "Blocked: this command would terminate the QwenPaw process or its parent", so the agent could not manage processes it had itself started, and the model then invented explanations for the user about why the command "failed".

Two bugs in `_is_dangerous_self_kill` (at rev `27d22cd`):

1. `$pid` was in `_SHELL_PID_VARS`, but on a POSIX shell `$PID` is an ordinary user variable that very often holds *another* process's PID — not a reference to QwenPaw.
2. `_KILL_PID_RE`'s `(?:/PID|-p|-pid|\b)\s*(\d+)` alternative let the bare `\b` boundary match inside the `-9` flag itself, so `kill -9 $pid` extracted the digit `9` as a PID target.

## Evidence

Reproduction and verification, run locally against the patched tree:

```text
# Before (rev 27d22cd logic) — false positives:
_is_dangerous_self_kill("kill $PID")                                  -> True   # blocked, but $PID names another process
_is_dangerous_self_kill("kill -9 $pid")                               -> True   # blocked, regex read "9" from the -9 flag as the target
_is_dangerous_self_kill("PID=$(pgrep mydaemon) && kill $PID")          -> True   # blocked, the canonical kill-a-daemon workflow

# After this PR — same commands allowed; real self-kills still blocked:
_is_dangerous_self_kill("kill $PID")                                  -> False
_is_dangerous_self_kill("PID=$(pgrep mydaemon) && kill $PID")          -> False
_is_dangerous_self_kill("kill $$")                                    -> True   # real self-kill, still blocked
_is_dangerous_self_kill("kill $PPID")                                 -> True   # real parent kill, still blocked
_is_dangerous_self_kill("taskkill /F /IM python.exe")                 -> True   # still blocked
_is_dangerous_self_kill(f"kill -9 {os.getpid()}")                     -> True   # still blocked
```

The protection surface is *narrower, not weaker*: `$$`/`$PPID` remain unconditionally blocked, dangerous image names and digit-PID self-kills are unchanged — only the `$PID`-only shape was relaxed, and only when no unambiguous self-reference appears in the same command.

## Tests

- Stale `test_kill_shell_var_pid` expectation inverted with a regression comment naming #8413.
- Four new cases: lowercase `$pid` allowed; the captured-PID workflow allowed; `$PID` alongside `$$` still blocked; `kill -9 <own pid>` pinned so the regex rewrite cannot regress the real self-kill path.
- `tests/unit/agents/tools/test_shell.py`: 24 self-kill guard tests passed; full file 120 passed / 1 skipped.

prs.title: fix(tools): preserve line endings and encoding in edit_file (#8414, #8415)
prs.body:
## 中文说明 / Chinese Summary

**本 PR：修复 #8414、#8415——`edit_file` 不再破坏文件行尾与编码**

原 `edit_file` 用文本模式（`newline='
'`, UTF-8）整体重写文件，导致两个用户可见的 bug：
- **CRLF 文件每次编辑都被转成 LF**（#8414, #8415）：一行改动却产生整文件 diff，破坏需要 CRLF 的文件（Windows 批处理脚本、部分配置）
- **非 UTF-8 文件被破坏**：含非 ASCII 字节的 ISO-8859-1 文件被重新编码或写入失败

修复方案：按字节原样写回。`edit_file` 读取原始字节 → 用文件实际编码解码（先检测 BOM）→ 应用替换 → 重新编码 → 通过新的 `_write_bytes_atomic`（二进制写临时文件 + `os.replace` 原子替换）落盘。行尾仅用于匹配，插入文本使用文件原有行尾。

**测试**：`tests/unit/agents/tools/test_file_io.py` 新增 5 个用例（CRLF 保留、LF 不变、Latin-1 字节不破坏、UTF-8 BOM 保留、插入文本跟随文件行尾），原子写入保持原文件权限位。

---
Fixes #8414, #8415.

## What Problem This Solves

`edit_file` rewrote the whole file through a text-mode writer (`newline='\n'`, UTF-8). Two user-visible bugs followed:

- **CRLF files were converted to LF on every edit** (#8414, #8415) — a one-line change rewrote every line ending in the file, which shows up as a whole-file diff in git and can break files that require CRLF (Windows batch scripts, some configs).
- **Non-UTF-8 files were destroyed** — an ISO-8859-1 file with bytes outside ASCII was re-encoded (or failed) even when the edit itself touched nothing near them.

The fix writes the snapshot back byte for byte: `edit_file` now reads the raw bytes, decodes with the encoding the file actually uses (BOM detection first), applies the replacement, re-encodes, and hands the result to a new `_write_bytes_atomic` that writes a sibling temp file in binary and `os.replace()`s it into place. Line endings are normalised for *matching* only, then the file's own ending is re-applied to inserted text.

## Evidence

Unit tests in `tests/unit/agents/tools/test_file_io.py` (all new, per file-ending/encoding case):

- `test_crlf_endings_survive_a_one_line_edit` — a CRLF file edited in the middle keeps CRLF everywhere; byte-comparing the whole file passes
- `test_lf_file_is_unchanged_in_shape` — an LF file is not rewritten into CRLF
- `test_iso_8859_1_bytes_are_not_destroyed` — a Latin-1 file with non-ASCII bytes around the edit point round-trips
- `test_utf8_bom_is_preserved` — the BOM is still there after editing
- `test_new_lines_in_new_text_follow_the_file_ending` — inserted text uses the file's ending, not a hardcoded `\n`

The atomic writer also keeps the target's mode: `shutil.copymode(target, temp)` when the file exists (which additionally preserves setuid/setgid bits that a `st_mode & 0o777` mask dropped), and the constant `0o644` for a brand-new file.

CI on this revision: pre-commit (black 23.3.0, flake8, mypy, pylint) clean, CodeQL clean, unit tests passing.

prs.title: feat(providers): add model fallback metadata to chat response
prs.body:
## Description

When the daemon silently switches models mid-request, nothing in the response says which model actually answered. This adds four fields to the chat response metadata and to the fallback event, so the switch is visible:

- `model_used` — the model that served the response
- `model_requested` — the model the user asked for (the primary)
- `fallback_reason` — why the switch happened, e.g. `transient (503)`
- `fallback_chain_position` — zero-based position of the serving model in the chain (0 = primary, 1 = first fallback)

The reason is built from the classified error kind plus the HTTP status only — raw provider error text is never used, since it can contain API keys or tokens. The existing `qwenpaw_model_fallbacks` and `qwenpaw_actual_model` keys are untouched, and the new event fields are additive for Console/channel consumers (they only read the existing fields).

**Related Issue:** Fixes #8103

Note: 401/403 errors still do not trigger a fallback — that is deliberate policy (see `test_does_not_fallback_on_authentication_error`), so the issue's literal 401 example does not fall back at HEAD. The tests exercise the same gap with 503s.

## What Problem This Solves

Issue #8103: a silent model fallback is invisible to the user — the daemon serves the answer from a different model without saying so. With these fields, the response itself (and the fallback event that reaches the Console and channels) names the requested model, the model that actually served, why it switched, and where that model sits in the chain.

## Evidence

Reproduce-first check (repro cases now in `tests/unit/providers/test_fallback_chat_model.py`):

- Before the fix: 2 failed (`KeyError: 'model_used'` on the final non-streaming response and on the last streaming chunk), 1 passed (401 control — no fallback, by policy).
- After the fix: 3/3 pass.

Focused suites (with the fix):

```
40 passed in 2.16s
```

(`tests/unit/providers/test_fallback_chat_model.py` + `tests/unit/agents/test_reasoning_fallback_bridge.py` — 32 baseline tests plus 8 new tests: non-streaming, streaming last chunk, structured output, multi-hop position, secret-leak, metadata preservation, no-fallback control, sink event fields.)

Full unit suite: 16,564 passed with this change. The failures present (172 failed, 57 errors) match pristine `main` (170 failed, 57 errors, identical error set); the 3 differing failures are load-dependent flakes that pass in isolation on both trees. `pre-commit run --all-files` passes.

Disclosure: AI coding assistance was used in preparing this change.

prs.title: feat(crons): per-job thinking_level override
prs.body:
## Description

Cron jobs currently inherit the agent's `thinking_level` wholesale. A
pipeline job (data collection, report generation, format conversion)
that only needs the agent's tools pays full reasoning latency and
reasoning tokens on every scheduled run — or the operator has to clone
the agent just to turn thinking off. #8439 reports 21 of 29 cron jobs
in exactly that situation, with single model calls stretching from
20 seconds to 9.5 minutes while `relay_reasoning` is on.

This adds a per-job `thinking_level` to the cron `JobRuntimeSpec`,
resolved through the existing request-scoped thinking precedence, so a
job can disable thinking (or force a specific effort) without touching
the agent's defaults.

**Related Issue:** Fixes #8439

**Security Considerations:** None — the override only shapes model
generation kwargs for the job's own execution; it adds no tool, network
or config surface. It rides the same `request_context` channel the
executor already uses for `approval_level`.

## What Problem This Solves

The reporter runs 29 cron jobs, 21 of them pure pipeline tasks. Today a
job can only follow the agent's global thinking setting:

- Turning thinking off to save tokens/latency requires creating a
  separate lightweight agent per job and repointing `agent_id` — error
  prone at scale and explicitly rejected by the reporter.
- Keeping thinking on means every scheduled run pays the full reasoning
  chain (measured 20 s – 9.5 min per call).

After this change a job opts in directly: `off` for pipeline jobs,
`inherit` (default, fully back-compatible) for everything else, or an
explicit effort level for jobs that genuinely need deep reasoning.

## Changes

`src/qwenpaw/app/crons/models.py`:

- `JobRuntimeSpec` gains `thinking_level: Literal["inherit", "off",
  "minimal", "low", "medium", "high", "xhigh", "max"]`, default
  `"inherit"`. Existing jobs validate unchanged and keep the agent's
  setting.
- The field reuses the agent-level value space instead of the
  issue-proposed `off/inherit/enabled` triple: the thinking machinery
  resolves a concrete preference against each model's control surface
  (`ThinkingLevel` has no provider-independent "on" — the wire mapping
  differs per protocol). Sharing one vocabulary keeps a single meaning
  everywhere: `off` covers the issue's primary case (pipeline jobs),
  and an explicit effort level expresses "force thinking on".

`src/qwenpaw/app/crons/executor.py`:

- When a job's `thinking_level` is not `"inherit"`, the executor
  carries it in `request_context["thinking_level"]`, next to the
  existing `approval_level`. Inheriting jobs emit exactly the same
  request payload as before.

`src/qwenpaw/services/session_thinking.py`:

- New `request_thinking_override()` reads that request-context key,
  accepting dict and object requests and both the direct and the
  nested-under-`meta` context forms (the same shapes
  `request_model_override` already supports). Absent and `"inherit"`
  values mean "no override".
- `apply_chat_model_settings()` accepts an optional
  `request_preference` and resolves the final thinking with the
  precedence its docstring already promises: request > session >
  agent defaults. A request override wins over a session preference;
  with no override, session and agent behavior are byte-identical to
  before. The override lands on the per-request agent snapshot taken
  in `runtime/builder.py`, so the agent's persisted configuration is
  never mutated.

## Type of Change

- [ ] Bug fix
- [x] New feature
- [ ] Breaking change
- [ ] Documentation
- [ ] Refactoring

## Component(s) Affected

- [x] Core / Backend (app, agents, config, providers, utils, local_models)
- [ ] Console (frontend web UI)
- [ ] Channels (DingTalk, Lark, QQ, Discord, iMessage, etc.)
- [ ] Skills
- [ ] CLI
- [ ] Documentation (website)
- [x] Tests
- [ ] CI/CD
- [ ] Scripts / Deploy

## Evidence

```
$ PYTHONPATH=src pytest tests/unit/app/crons/test_models.py tests/unit/app/crons/test_executor.py tests/unit/services/test_session_thinking.py -q
........................................................................ [ 93%]
.....                                                                    [100%]
77 passed in 1.80s

$ PYTHONPATH=src pytest tests/unit/app/crons/ tests/unit/services/ tests/unit/app/chats/test_title_generator.py -q
319 passed, 2 skipped, 1 failed

The single failure
(tests/unit/services/test_unified_workspace_files.py::test_concurrent_versioned_saves_allow_only_one_writer)
is a timing-sensitive test unrelated to this change: it also fails on
an unmodified checkout under load and passes on rerun (3/3).

$ pre-commit (four hooks, on the changed files)
black --line-length=79 --check ..... 6 files would be left unchanged
flake8 --extend-ignore=E203 --max-line-length=120 ..... no issues
mypy (hook args) ..... Success: no issues found in 3 source files
pylint (hook args) ..... Your code has been rated at 10.00/10
```

New tests:

- `JobRuntimeSpec.thinking_level` defaults to `"inherit"`, accepts the
  agent-level value space and rejects unknown values (`enabled`,
  `budget`, free text).
- The executor carries a non-inherit job thinking level in
  `request_context` and leaves inheriting jobs' requests untouched.
- `request_thinking_override()` reads the direct, nested and object
  request forms and ignores unset/inherit values.
- A request override beats both the agent config and the session
  preference; `"inherit"` keeps the agent's thinking; the agent's own
  config is never mutated.

## Checklist

- [x] I ran `pre-commit run --all-files` locally and it passes
- [ ] If pre-commit auto-fixed files, I committed those changes and reran checks
- [x] I ran tests locally (`pytest` or as relevant) and they pass
- [x] Documentation updated (if needed)
- [x] Ready for review

Release gates are real-provider sign-in evidence; the five principal-isolation repairs (#11234, #11220, #11225, #11230, #11266, with #11198 tracked); schema V4 (#11218); and a build-time CLI-only option that omits gateway/web assets and directs dashboard users to the standard build.

Scoped dashboard chat has a November 3 go/no-go, with sign-in alone as the fallback. November 10 is the earliest target, subject to the gates, not a committed date.

Standalone zeroclaw-gw, full gateway IPC route/parity work, cross-process webhook handling and two-process desktop packaging move to v0.9.x. Channel listeners remain in core under existing documented exceptions. These deferrals do not complete the remaining gateway roadmap.

Source of truth: #7432 (https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/issues/7432), current release allocation. Existing implementation trackers keep their detailed work. Feature acceptance, current-head review/CI, recorded placement decisions and the v0.8.7-tag hold on breaking work remain in force.

issues.body:
### Affected component

security/sandbox

### Severity

S3 - minor issue

### Current behavior

- **The policy:** enrollment discovery (`Enrollment::discovery` in `crates/zeroclaw-runtime/src/security/auth_provider/enrollment.rs`) holds `token_endpoint` and `device_authorization_endpoint` to `validate_discovered_endpoint`. That means https, or http on an exact loopback host, never with userinfo (`enrollment.rs:252-255` at 2450c1775c). The daemon's own discovery does the same for `jwks_uri` and `introspection_endpoint` (`oidc.rs:468-473`).
- **The gap:** `authorization_endpoint` isn't checked.
  - `pkce_start` only parses it (`enrollment.rs:542`, `:564-578`), and the authorize URL it builds is then used as given.
  - The gateway redirects the browser to it: `GET /oidc/login/{alias}` (`crates/zeroclaw-gateway/src/api_oidc.rs:835-848`) and the dashboard sign-in `GET /auth/sign-in/{alias}` (`:1009-1031`).
  - The CLI's browser enrollment prints it and hands it to `open` or `xdg-open` (`src/main.rs:15390`).
- **The result:** an issuer can advertise plain http to a remote host, or a URL that isn't a web URL at all (`file:`, a registered app scheme). The user's browser, or the desktop's URL opener, is then sent there.

### Expected behavior

- `authorization_endpoint` is held to the same policy as the other discovered endpoints.
- A document that advertises one outside it is refused before any authorize URL is built, as a bad device endpoint is today.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Configure an `[oidc.<alias>]` provider whose issuer serves a discovery document that:
   - asserts that issuer;
   - advertises a valid `token_endpoint` and `"code_challenge_methods_supported": ["S256"]`;
   - advertises `"authorization_endpoint": "http://sso.example.com/authorize"`, or `"file:///tmp/authorize"`.
2. Start a browser sign-in: `GET /oidc/login/<alias>` on the gateway, or the CLI's browser enrollment.
3. `pkce_start` returns an authorize URL on that endpoint instead of an error. The gateway answers with a redirect to it, and the CLI opens it.

The same thing at the unit level: `Enrollment::pkce_start` against a mock issuer with that document returns `Ok`.

### Impact

- **Precondition:** the configured issuer has to serve a broken or hostile discovery document. Its identity is already checked: the issuer is https or exact loopback, and the document must assert it.
- **Why it's hardening:** such an issuer already decides who signs in, so this isn't a new privilege boundary. It stops a bad document from:
  - sending the user's browser to a plain-http sign-in page on another host, where the page and what the user types into it are unprotected;
  - handing a non-web URL to the desktop's opener.
- **Who:** browser sign-in only. The CLI browser enrollment and `GET /oidc/login/{alias}` are in v0.8.6 and v0.8.7; the dashboard sign-in is on master. Device and client-credentials flows never use this endpoint.
- **Real issuers:** none I checked trips the check. Every hosted provider's discovery document I looked at (Google, Entra, Okta, Auth0, Cognito) advertises an https `authorization_endpoint`.

### Logs / stack traces

N/A

### ZeroClaw version

master 2450c1775c; also v0.8.6 and v0.8.7.

### Rust version

N/A (not a build issue)

### Operating system

Any

### Regression?

No: the check has been missing since the enrollment client landed (#11082).

### Pre-flight checks

- [x] I reproduced this on the latest master branch or latest release.
- [x] I redacted secrets, tokens, and personal data from all submitted content.

### Notes

- **Other URLs from the identity provider:**
  - Nothing else from a discovery document is followed: no `end_session_endpoint`, `userinfo_endpoint` or `revocation_endpoint` is read anywhere.
  - The device grant's `verification_uri` comes from the device endpoint's answer, not from discovery. It's printed (CLI, ZeroCode) or returned as JSON (`/api/oidc/{alias}/device/start`) and never opened automatically, so it's left out of scope.
- **A wrong comment:** the `pkce_start` doc comment says RFC 8414 defaults `code_challenge_methods_supported` to `plain` when it's absent. RFC 8414 section 2 says an omitted field means the server doesn't support PKCE. The S256 check refuses both cases already, so only the comment is wrong.

prs.title: feat(channels): synthesize Telegram voice replies during text generation
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master`, extracted directly on `a66cc98a4`.
- **What changed and why:** Prepare Telegram voice replies while assistant text arrives. An early sentence can synthesize first; later text uses larger segments. Reuse prepared audio when final text arrives and upload one combined voice note.
- Keep draft workers cancellable and bounded. Explicit voice finalization transfers prepared audio before releasing the draft. A failed speculative job gets one fresh attempt using the approved final text; partial speculative audio is never uploaded. The current per-turn routing handle suppresses/cancels preparation for explicit text-only or redirected replies.
- Reuse the same speech sanitization for incremental and final text. Forward the optional channel hook and final voice operation through pacing wrappers, preserving their final-delivery queue. Dropped draft finalizations release preparation; cleanup errors are logged with a two-second deadline and never cause an alternate delivery.
- Construct channel hooks from the installed handler list: the default enabled-but-empty runner does not delay speculative text or speech. Installed handlers still gate content. Speech regressions now use the same hook factory as channel startup and exercise the default enabled configuration.
- **Scope boundary:** Telegram voice-note preparation; no live-call integration, session-history dependency, new voice provider, or new configuration key.
- **Blast radius:** Channel trait implementors through a backward-compatible default hook, draft dispatch and existing Telegram TTS.
- **Linked issue(s):** None.

The branch is synchronized with upstream master at `b98b67bed` using a merge; original topic commits remain intact. Its PR diff contains only the feature/fix files, with no Cargo.lock change relative to the updated base.

### What this does, simply

Voice replies previously waited for all text before starting synthesis. This overlaps synthesis with generation, then sends the finished reply as one voice note. It does not send a separate voice message for each sentence and does not add real-time calling.

## Testing (required)

### How you can test

- **Reviewer testing requested?** Yes.
- **Interface(s) exercised:** Telegram channel draft/final delivery using deterministic provider and upload fixtures.
- **Setup / preconditions:** Rust and ffmpeg; fixture tests need no Telegram account, bot token or paid model.
- **Steps to run:** `cargo test --locked -p zeroclaw-channels --lib speech -- --include-ignored`. For an optional live A/B check, use existing TTS and a Telegram peer configured for voice replies with a sufficiently long answer.
- **Expected on this branch (after):** Fixture synthesis starts before final text and finalization uploads one voice note. In a live check, final voice delivery can overlap generation.
- **Prior behavior on master (before):** Synthesis starts only once final text is available.

### How I tested

- **CI checks relied on and why they cover this change:** Focused local speech/delivery fixtures, strict owning-crate Clippy, formatting and documentation gates. Required upstream CI on this updated head is pending; previous-head CI is not presented as current-head evidence.
- **Known CI coverage gap:** TTS and Telegram HTTP are mocked. No real Telegram message, paid model call or Android playback is claimed.
- **Commands run and tail output:** Local Cargo used Rust 1.98, one build job and `CARGO_PROFILE_DEV_DEBUG=0 CARGO_PROFILE_TEST_DEBUG=0`.
  - `cargo +1.98.0 test --locked -p zeroclaw-channels --lib speech -- --include-ignored`: `25 passed; 0 failed`. Includes actual `process_channel_message`, TTS HTTP and Telegram upload fixtures, speculative failure recovery, live routing, paced finalization, bounded preview cleanup and ffmpeg assembly.
  - The end-to-end speech fixtures build hooks through the production channel-startup factory with `hooks.enabled = true`, its default. The safe-phase regression uses that factory with empty and installed handler configurations, requiring early synthesis only without handlers.
  - `cargo +1.98.0 clippy --locked -p zeroclaw-channels -p zeroclaw-runtime --all-targets -- -D warnings`: passed.
  - `cargo +1.98.0 fmt --all -- --check` and `git diff --check`: passed.
  - `BASE_SHA=482c88447682bb1a2c621d24bd83621f053015fd scripts/ci/docs_quality_gate.sh`: `Summary: 0 error(s)`.
  - `BASE_SHA=482c88447682bb1a2c621d24bd83621f053015fd scripts/ci/docs_links_gate.sh`: six collector tests passed; no added links in this follow-up.
- **Beyond CI, what did you manually verify?** Source review confirms that channel startup and speech fixtures share the handler-list resolver and that the runtime getter reads the existing handler list. No independent hook-policy state or configuration flag was added.
- **Visual interface evidence:** N/A; synthesis timing and delivery behavior, with no layout changes.
- **Tested revision, interface, and evidence path:** `cb5cbfb3e18ae5d00eadf6f9c3ffa8a73ea1e783`; Telegram speech delivery through the shared orchestrator; speech tests in `zeroclaw-channels`.
- **Screenshot or exact-output evidence:** `25 passed; 0 failed`. The default-configuration fixture observes the opening TTS request while model generation is deliberately paused, then requires one complete final Telegram voice upload.
- **Action or changed state and observed result:** An enabled empty runner allows early synthesis. Installing a handler withholds speculative speech until its existing decision path can run. Recovery and final delivery still produce one voice note.
- **If any command was intentionally skipped, why:** Real Telegram/provider requests and Android playback were not needed for the deterministic delivery regression. Full workspace tests are left to required CI; this follow-up changes hook composition and its focused fixtures.

## Security & Privacy Impact (required)

- New permissions, capabilities, or file system access scope? **No new authority.** Uses the existing authorized voice-reply path.
- New external network calls? **Yes in timing/count:** configured TTS can receive several segments before generation finishes. Cancellation cannot retract a segment already sent. No new service is added.
- Secrets / tokens / credentials handling changed? **No.**
- PII, real identities, or personal data in diff, tests, fixtures, or docs? **No; fixtures are synthetic.**
- Prompt injection or untrusted model-visible text introduced/changed? **No.**
- If any Yes, describe the risk and mitigation: Speech is sent only through the configured existing provider and peer routing; private temporary files, cancellation and final-text compatibility checks prevent stale draft uploads. The operator's existing TTS privacy policy still applies.

## Compatibility (required)

- Backward compatible? **Yes; the new channel hook defaults to a no-op.**
- Config / env / CLI surface changed? **No.**
- Rust/MSRV/toolchain floor changed? **No.**
- Exact upgrade steps: None. Existing transcription/TTS and voice reply routing are reused.

## Rollback

- **Fast rollback command/path:** Revert this commit and rebuild. No database migration is introduced.
- **Feature flags or config toggles:** Existing TTS enablement and peer modality/routing.
- **Observable failure symptoms:** Draft preparation/synthesis errors, missing final notes or repeated voice uploads. Fixtures cover cancellation, rewriting and single final upload.

## Supersede Attribution

N/A.

prs.title: feat(mcp): expose local configuration controls with deferred writes
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master` (extracted on `a66cc98a4`).
- **What changed and why:** Add an optional Python standard-library stdio MCP server for the existing local gateway configuration API. An explicitly authorized agent can discover settings, inspect non-secret values, apply edits and request a daemon reload.
- Mutations made inside a running conversation return an accepted job before applying the edit; an owned worker waits for observed idle state from the canonical runtime admission coordinator. The authenticated running-sessions API derives a `busy` boolean in the gateway using existing lifecycle accessors and canonical configured aliases, across channel, web and RPC callers, including when persistence is disabled. Alias deletion already refuses outstanding work. No runtime holding-crate addition is needed. No parallel activity registry is added.
- Idle polling uses the authenticated `activity_only=true` projection without enumerating sessions or reading transcripts. Full session-list responses sample live activity after metadata enumeration. The helper also explains named-entry leaf writes and refreshing separately installed copies.
- Credentials are read from an owner-only regular file at use time. Responses avoid echoing submitted values; HTTP 408 and lost mutation responses are uncertain and never blindly retried. Private completed job metadata is bounded to 100 records and seven days; active jobs are preserved.
- **Scope boundary:** Optional script, documentation, tests, and a gateway-owned activity projection using existing lifecycle accessors on the authenticated session endpoint; no runtime holding-crate changes. No configuration fields, history migration, provider changes or new public listener.
- **Blast radius:** Installations that configure and grant this MCP integration; the existing running-session response gains an additive `busy` boolean.
- **Linked issue(s):** None. This is independent of the unmerged session-history foundation.

The branch is synchronized with upstream master at `b98b67bed` using a merge; original topic commits remain intact. Its PR diff contains only the feature/fix files, with no Cargo.lock change relative to the updated base.

### What this does, simply

An administrator can grant a personal assistant the same supported configuration controls used by the local gateway. The assistant can request an edit while answering a conversation and have it applied once that conversation becomes idle. This is an explicit administrative capability, not a restricted worker tool.

## Testing (required)

### How you can test

- **Reviewer testing requested?** Yes; deterministic tests need only Python 3 and loopback networking.
- **Interface(s) exercised:** `surface=cli`, real stdio MCP subprocess, HTTP configuration requests to a mock gateway.
- **Setup / preconditions:** Unix Python 3.12 or newer; no real provider, bot, key or operator data.
- **Steps to run:** `python -m unittest discover -s scripts/mcp -p 'config_control_test.py'`.
- **Expected on this branch (after):** MCP discovery works; read/patch routes work; an active calling session defers writes/reloads; workers complete after idle evidence. Denied requests, credential rotation, malformed frames and uncertain responses fail safely.
- **Prior behavior on master (before):** This optional configuration MCP integration is absent.

### How I tested

- **CI checks relied on and why they cover this change:** Focused local MCP transport tests, gateway route regressions, strict owning-crate Clippy, formatting and documentation gates. Required CI on this updated head is pending; previous-head CI is not presented as current-head evidence.
- **Known CI coverage gap:** HTTP fixtures replace a real operator installation. No real configuration, model, account or credential was changed.
- **Commands run and tail output:** Local Cargo used Rust 1.98, one build job and `CARGO_PROFILE_DEV_DEBUG=0 CARGO_PROFILE_TEST_DEBUG=0`.
  - `python3 -m unittest discover -s scripts/mcp -p 'config_control_test.py'`: `Ran 27 tests ... OK`.
  - `cargo +1.98.0 test --locked -p zeroclaw-gateway --lib api_sessions_running`: `4 passed; 0 failed`. The actual Axum route uses real admission leases; activity-only requests never enumerate the backend, retain bearer authentication and report current activity. The full-list regression starts work during enumeration and requires the final busy signal to observe it.
  - `cargo +1.98.0 clippy --locked -p zeroclaw-gateway --all-targets -- -D warnings`: passed.
  - `cargo +1.98.0 fmt --all -- --check` and `git diff --check`: passed.
  - `BASE_SHA=a4431d2386eaf201f44d399d9f13ad6731688e9c scripts/ci/docs_quality_gate.sh`: `Summary: 0 error(s)`.
  - `BASE_SHA=a4431d2386eaf201f44d399d9f13ad6731688e9c scripts/ci/docs_links_gate.sh`: six collector tests passed; no added links in this follow-up.
- **Beyond CI, what did you manually verify?** The committed fixtures exercise the real stdio process and queued workers against loopback HTTP, plus the authenticated gateway handler. Source review confirms that the lightweight projection returns before touching session persistence. No live operator mutation was attempted.
- **Visual interface evidence:** N/A; structured MCP/API responses, with no graphical layout changes.
- **Tested revision, interface, and evidence path:** `aa2e6614c62ed474873804975c6d36f8995cd19c`; CLI/stdin MCP and authenticated gateway routes; `scripts/mcp/config_control_test.py` and `crates/zeroclaw-gateway/src/api.rs`.
- **Screenshot or exact-output evidence:** `27 tests ... OK`; `4 passed; 0 failed`. Route tests assert exact activity-only JSON `{"busy":true}` and `{"busy":false}`, zero backend enumeration calls and HTTP 401 without authentication.
- **Action or changed state and observed result:** Real turn admission changes the probe's busy value without reading history. Deferred writes wait on that signal; stale persisted running rows cannot keep the worker blocked.
- **If any command was intentionally skipped, why:** Full workspace tests and live account/config mutations add no coverage to this bounded follow-up. Required upstream CI will validate its configured platform matrix.

## Security & Privacy Impact (required)

- New permissions, capabilities, or file system access scope? **Yes.** Explicitly granting this integration gives administrative configuration authority, including permission changes. Documentation restricts grants to the intended administrative agent and identifies tools to exclude from delegates.
- New external network calls? **No new external service.** Only explicit loopback HTTP endpoints are accepted; redirects and proxy inheritance are disabled.
- Secrets / tokens / credentials handling changed? **Yes for this optional client.** Paired-device credentials are read from a private regular file at each request, never from model arguments or returned tool results. Symlinks and loose permissions are refused. Queued request data is owner-only.
- PII, real identities, or personal data in diff, tests, fixtures, or docs? **No.** Synthetic values only.
- Prompt injection or untrusted model-visible text introduced/changed? **Yes.** Configuration metadata becomes tool-visible data. It does not manufacture authority or become a shell command; existing MCP grants and gateway authentication remain authoritative.
- If any `Yes`, describe the risk and mitigation: This is intentionally powerful administrative access. Revoke its paired device or remove its bundle grant to withdraw authority. Workers reread credentials, never replay an uncertain mutation, expire requests without idle evidence and do not claim that idle proves all outbound audio finished.

## Compatibility (required)

- Backward compatible? **Yes; opt-in.**
- Config / env / CLI surface changed? **Yes for the optional script and additive API query:** `--gateway-url`, `--token-file`, `--state-dir`; existing MCP server/bundle configuration is reused. `GET /api/sessions/running?activity_only=true` returns only the live `busy` field; omitting the query preserves the session-list response.
- Rust/MSRV/toolchain floor changed? **No.**
- Exact upgrade steps: Upgrade the daemon together with the script; older daemons without the runtime `busy` signal are refused for mutations. Install the script at a stable local path, provision a dedicated private paired-device token, configure the stdio MCP server and explicitly grant its bundle. Follow the documentation example. No native history dependency or storage migration is required.

## Rollback

- **Fast rollback command/path:** Remove the bundle grant, revoke the dedicated paired device, then remove the script and owned local state after queued jobs stop. Previously applied configuration edits are reversed individually through normal controls.
- **Feature flags or config toggles:** Existing MCP server definitions, bundle grants and tool exclusions.
- **Observable failure symptoms:** Stable `gateway_rejected_request`, `gateway_request_failed` or `configuration_control_failed` results and failed/expired job records.

## Supersede Attribution

N/A.

## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master`
- **What changed and why:** Adds one row to the active-exception table in `crates/zeroclaw-runtime/AGENTS.md`, proposing a bounded holding-crate exception for the three plugin webhook RPC methods (`plugin-webhook/dispatch`, `plugin-webhook/cancel`, `plugin-webhook/routes`) that carry channel-plugin webhook dispatch across the core IPC boundary for #11003. ADR-016 requires the row to exist, approved by the Core Team, before the feature it covers merges.
- **Scope boundary:** Documentation only. The permission covers `src/rpc/dispatch.rs`, `src/rpc/context.rs`, the denial reasons for these methods in `src/rpc/auth.rs`, the ingress setter and taker in `src/daemon/{registry.rs,mod.rs}`, and their denial message keys in `locales/en/cli.ftl`. Route ownership, admission, deadlines and dedup live in `zeroclaw-infra`, outside the holding crate.
- **Channel authority (updated after the #11320 review):** the row names the one new authority these methods add, as the maintainer decision on #11320 requires. `channels:execute` lets a local caller deliver a webhook request to a plugin channel's route and cancel its own deliveries, and `channels:read` lists the routes with their owners. Each grant covers only the channel instances its permission profile names. Config can make a channel instance refuse injected webhooks, and an agent refuse turns that arrive through them, checked at dispatch whatever the caller's grants. The grant scoping and the config fields live in `zeroclaw-api` and `zeroclaw-config`, outside the holding crate. No new runtime module, routing, parsing or authentication.
- **Blast radius:** Contributor placement guidance only. No runtime behavior changes. The row is not active until a Core Team member other than the author approves this PR.
- **Linked issue(s):** Related #11003. Related #7432. Related #11000.
- **Labels:** `docs`, `release-gate`, `risk:high`, `risk:manual`, `size:XS`, `topic:plugins`, `type:docs`

### What this does, simply

The runtime crate is a holding area: new functionality needs a recorded Core Team exception first. The follow-up PRs for #11003 add three RPC methods to the daemon's dispatcher so a gateway in another process can hand webhook requests to the core. The dispatcher still lives in the runtime crate until the planned kernel IPC extraction, so this row asks for permission for exactly that, and nothing more.

## Testing (required)

### How you can test (when useful)

- **Reviewer testing requested?** N/A: a one-row documentation change with no executable behavior.

### How I tested

- **CI checks relied on and why they cover this change:** `Docs Style` (the docs gate only scans `docs/book/src`, so it does not lint this file; the row adds no em-dashes).
- **Known CI coverage gap, if any:** None.
- **Commands run and tail output:** `git diff master -- crates/zeroclaw-runtime/AGENTS.md` shows one added table row.
- **Beyond CI, what did you manually verify?** The row names all four fields ADR-016 requires (scope, destination, approving authority, review condition) and follows the bounded SOP RPC exception format proposed in #11111.
- **Visual interface evidence:** N/A
- **If any command was intentionally skipped, why:** N/A

## Security & Privacy Impact (required)

- New permissions, capabilities, or file system access scope? Not in this PR, which is documentation only. The row it proposes approves the scoped channel authority above for #11320.
- New external network calls? No
- Secrets / tokens / credentials handling changed? No
- PII, real identities, or personal data in diff, tests, fixtures, or docs? No
- Prompt injection or untrusted model-visible text introduced/changed? No

## Compatibility (required)

- Backward compatible? Yes
- Config / env / CLI surface changed? No
- Rust/MSRV/toolchain floor changed? No

## Rollback (required for medium/high-risk PRs)

`git revert <sha>` removes the row. Nothing depends on it at runtime.
