prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master` (`03b29bcc68`). **Depends on #11319** (core ingress, which itself now builds on #11339) and **#11165** (`zeroclaw-rpc-proto`). The branch merges #11319 at its current head `c352574198` and #11165 at its current head `19e41b09fa` (restacked 2026-10-23, see below); their commits show in the diff until they land, so review this PR's own commits, `7962184961` (the methods), `b5d9ebd577` (channel scoping), `fcf4f6121c` (the review's two non-blocking warnings), `4e9a208600` (channel rename and delete carry `allowed_channels` grants), `d6ef5dc0af` (the removed-binding interval test) and `1147d81ac2` and `2aeb57ae9b` (test adaptation to master: config edits go through `publish_test_config` on the read-only live config, `RpcContext::for_authority` sets the ingress handle, the WSS refusal test selects its audit record by reason too, and master's channel WebSocket e2e spreads the plugin channel default), `f3364f9c67` (the RPC socket guide says a rejection record carries the plugin name, channel alias and error key, not the path or the plugin's rejection text; from Greptile's review), `ad161acc03` (admission re-resolves the caller's live grants; from Greptile's and Audacity88's reviews), `13fd6a42e1` (the two denial-record tests drain past a lagged broadcast receiver instead of stopping at it) and `864b58d76e` (a rename or delete refuses a cascade outside the caller's config write grants; from Greptile's review). **The holding-crate exception in #11317 is approved and records the approval; it must land before this implementation.**
- **Status of 2026-11-08:** #11165 and #11186 were closed on 2026-11-05 in favour of #12244, which carries the `zeroclaw-rpc-proto` extraction onto current master as `f25e96ea39`. That extraction differs from `19e41b09fa` by the `MAX_FRAME_BYTES` constant and two doc comments, one of them #12239's `SessionRunOnceParams` wording that this branch already carries. This branch still merges #11165's head `19e41b09fa`, so a squash of this head would land that closed extraction; it stays unmerged until #11317, #11339, #11319 and #12244 have landed, then restacks onto that result, refreshes onto master (the four commits master has gained since `641b766030` merge cleanly today) and rewrites this base line to name what landed. Head `01db9e82be` is unchanged by this note.
- **Refresh of 2026-11-02 (`d2479d7f2f`):** merges master `03b29bcc68`, which carries the Wasmtime 48.0.8 bump for RUSTSEC-2026-0420 to 0424 (#12129) and so clears the `Security` job for this branch. The one conflict was the workspace `members` line in the root `Cargo.toml`: this branch adds the `zeroclaw-rpc-proto` member and master appends `tests/fixtures/runtime-composition-consumer`; both kept. No change to this PR's own slice.
- **Fixes after the refresh (`5d17864f14`, `d93d67f79c`, `d4517a7845`):** master's new `runtime-composition-consumer` fixture refuses any `zeroclaw-*` dependency of the runtime that its retained-dependencies policy does not name, and this branch carries #11165's `zeroclaw-rpc-proto` edge, so the policy gains that entry the way the relay wire contract is recorded (owner `rpc/types.rs`, which re-exports the wire-stable types; the reason names the dispatcher's import). #11165 will need the same line when it refreshes onto master. The parallel runtime gate then failed in master's `persisted_log_reads_refuse_a_scoped_principal`: the two in-flight-cap tests here send `MAX_PLUGIN_WEBHOOK_DISPATCHES_PER_CONNECTION` (1024) dispatches in a tight loop, each leaving a rejection record, and the log writer hands records to its disk worker through a bounded queue of the same size, dropping what it cannot take, whichever test emitted it. Under the gate's 16 threads those tests sort right after the persisted-log tests, so the four denial records that test reads back were dropped and the administrator's query found none. The two burst tests now hold the writer's test lock, which the persisted-log tests hold while they read their records back, so a burst never shares the writer with a test that reads it; the capture tests read the broadcast stream, whose channel is far larger than a burst, and are unaffected. From Greptile's review of this refresh, `d4517a7845` takes the cascade refusal's message from the catalog (`rpc-auth-config-cascade-write-denied`, with the refused path as a Fluent argument) instead of an English literal.
- **Refresh of 2026-11-03 (`e331fc224c`):** merges master `ee8a753dff`, which is #11318 squash-merged, so #11318's changes no longer show in this diff. The four conflicts were all in files #11318 added or edited (`.github/workflows/README.md`, `golden_frames.rs`, the plugin backend change filter and its test): master's version of each is exactly #11318's final content, and this branch's version is that content plus the lines #11319 and this PR add on top of it, so every conflict resolves to this branch's side. The rest of the merge is master's own work since `03b29bcc68` (#11054, #11739, #11270, #12003).
- **Refresh of 2026-11-05 (`9e4c5c086c`, `0998d76a7f`):** merges master `72573d87c0` without conflicts (#11964, a daemon task that retires remote sessions whose client has been gone past `wss.orphaned_session_timeout_secs`; #12232, principal-unaware tools and SOP execution withheld from non-admin principals; #12213, the pairing guard reading the live `[gateway.pairing_dashboard]` limits; #12251; #11266; #11218, retired config keys migrating at schema version 4; #11272; #12253; #12243). #11218 keeps the migration's list of current agent keys, `V3_AGENT_FIELDS`, in step with `AliasedAgentConfig` through `v3_agent_fields_are_the_current_agent_fields`, and treats a listed key under `[agents.<alias>]` as evidence of the V3 layout. `accept_injected_webhooks`, which `b5d9ebd577` adds to the agent config, was missing from that list, so `0998d76a7f` names it: V2 agents never had the key, and an agent holding it reads as V3 like every other agent key. #11322's Test jobs found this at `6ce12cff6f`, the first head in the stack carrying both #11218 and the field; #11322 takes the fix by merging this branch.
- **Fix of 2026-11-05 (`ac9c10fe25`):** from Greptile's review of `0998d76a7f`: the five `INVALID_PARAMS` refusals of `plugin-webhook/dispatch` (a `request_id` outside its bounds or already in flight on the connection, a `body_b64` over the limit or not standard base64, and the request constructor's refusal) were English literals. They now come from the catalog as `rpc-plugin-webhook-request-id-invalid`, `rpc-plugin-webhook-request-id-in-flight`, `rpc-plugin-webhook-body-too-large`, `rpc-plugin-webhook-body-not-base64` and `rpc-plugin-webhook-request-invalid`, next to the method's other entries in `locales/en/cli.ftl`, with the bound and the constructor's reason as Fluent arguments. The wording is unchanged, no test asserts it, and the gateway forwarder in #11322 keys its status mapping on the error code, so nothing downstream moves.
- **Refresh of 2026-11-07 (`befa924386`, `01db9e82be`):** merges master `641b766030`, which brings #12239 (current authority held through session effects), #11149 (cron approval and authority enforced at the write across RPC, tools and token revocation), #12157, #12233, #12114, #12273 (vodozemac 0.11.2 for RUSTSEC-2026-0445 and -0451), #12254, #12179, #12177, #12162, #12274 and a batch of test-only and docs commits. The one conflict was in `crates/zeroclaw-runtime/src/rpc/types.rs`: #12239 extends the doc comment of `SessionRunOnceParams` (the grants it requires and what a refused cleanup reports), inside the block of wire types this branch no longer defines there because #11165 moved them to `zeroclaw-rpc-proto` and the module re-exports them. The runtime file keeps this branch's side, and the three doc lines are carried to the struct's definition in `crates/zeroclaw-rpc-proto/src/types.rs`, so master's wording survives the move. The OpenRPC contract document is generated from those doc comments, so `01db9e82be` regenerates `docs/book/src/architecture/zeroclaw-rpc.openrpc.json` with `cargo generate openrpc` and the `--check` step passes again. The other files both sides touched merged by themselves.
- **Refresh of 2026-11-08 (`f7709a87c3`):** merges #11319's refreshed head `988d9bffe4`, which carries master `7666a52abf` (the five commits since `641b766030`: #12270, the relay serving a daemon's dashboard at a per-node host; #11406, macOS broad roots refused in the filesystem channel; #11268; #10502; #12286) and puts #11319's head back into this branch's ancestry (the previous head `e40a47518f` was not an ancestor, only its content was). The `src/main.rs` conflict with #12270, which hoists the `GatewaySupervision` construction to attach the relay dashboard ingress, was resolved in #11319 and merges here without conflict, as does #11319's follow-up that hands master's `relay_dashboard_ingress` test the core ingress. The one conflict was the Installer Drift row of the CI README: this branch carries #11165's wording about the tracked OpenRPC document, the parent carries master's, and master itself did not change the row, so this branch's row stays. The restack after the parents land is still pending; nothing else changed since `01db9e82be`, the head tidux reviewed.
- **#11165 (restack of 2026-10-23, `534a7e41c3` and `82dc407331`):** #11165's head `19e41b09fa` merges master and moves #11132's `session/*` methods into `zeroclaw-rpc-proto`, so the master conflicts in `dispatch.rs`, `session.rs` and `types.rs` are resolved there and this branch merges it without conflict in those files. The hand-resolved files are the CI workflow, its gate registry, the CI guide and the plugin backend change filter, where master, #11165 and #11319 each add their own lines (every side's lines are kept), plus the regenerated OpenRPC document (`cargo generate openrpc`, 107 methods, `--check` clean). #11165's `session/prompt` fix (`SessionPromptAck`) comes along with its head. The branch is now mergeable with master.
- **Channel scoping (maintainer decision on this PR):** `channels:execute` and `channels:read` reach only the channel instances a profile names, and config can close the path for a channel or an agent whatever the grants. Field names and defaults:
  - `[permission_profiles.<name>] allowed_channels = ["plugin.<alias>", ...]`: a channel selector like `allowed_agents`. Entries are `<type>.<alias>` names of configured instances, validated at load; `"*"` grants every instance; empty (the default) grants none. `admin`, including the same-uid shared operator, reaches all.
  - `[channels.plugin.<alias>] accept_injected_webhooks = true` (default): `false` refuses webhooks delivered through `plugin-webhook/dispatch` to that instance.
  - `[agents.<alias>] accept_injected_webhooks = true` (default): `false` refuses such a delivery to any channel the agent handles.
  - Checked at dispatch, not only when routes are listed: `PluginWebhookIngress::dispatch_admitted` runs the check on the owner the request would be queued to, before anything is queued or reserved, so a republished route cannot redirect an admitted request. A refusal is `FORBIDDEN` with an audit record. `plugin-webhook/routes` lists only granted channels.
  - The docs say what `channels = ["execute"]` and `["read"]` unlock (authentication guide and RPC socket guide), and that a route path can be a vendor's shared secret.
  - From the review's non-blocking warnings (`fcf4f6121c`): the refusal for an ungranted channel names no channel, while its audit record still does, and a route whose channel instance the live config no longer binds is refused (fail closed) until the next reload retires it. `d6ef5dc0af` proves that interval: a route admitted while its instance is bound is refused `FORBIDDEN` once a live config write removes the instance, while the route is still published, and its worker receives nothing (asked for in Audacity88's review of #11322).
  - Admission does not trust the grants the spawned dispatch task copied at the read loop's check (`ad161acc03`): `admit_plugin_webhook` re-resolves the caller's live grants with `recheck_authority_after_admission`, the same check `session/new` and `session/prompt` run after admission, so a credential revoked or a profile narrowed between the check and the task's admission refuses the delivery. `plugin_webhook_admission_rechecks_the_live_grants` narrows `allowed_channels` and then drops `channels:execute` after `spawn_handle` and asserts both refusals while the copied grants still allow.
  - Renaming or deleting a channel instance carries its `allowed_channels` grants along (`4e9a208600`): a rename rewrites them to the new name, a delete drops them, and the changed profiles are saved, so a grant never blocks the change. A caller does not reach a profile through that cascade (`864b58d76e`): the rename and the provider-model alias delete check every entry the cascade dirties against the caller's live config write grants and refuse the whole change, with nothing saved, when one of them is outside those grants, the write-set rule the gateway's config routes already follow (`config_map_key_rename_refuses_a_cascade_outside_the_callers_write_paths`: a `channels.*` writer is refused FORBIDDEN naming `permission_profiles.ops`, then succeeds once `permission_profiles.*` is granted).
- **What changed and why:** A gateway in another process needs to hand channel-plugin webhook requests to the core that owns the route table. Three daemon RPC methods over the core ingress:
  - `plugin-webhook/dispatch` (`channels:execute`): method, raw query, headers, and the body as standard base64 under a caller-chosen `request_id`; answers a typed outcome (`ack`, `reply` with `body`, `not_found`, `queue_full`, `unavailable`, `unauthorized`, `bad_request`, `invalid_response`, `timeout`, `cancelled`). Validated by the same shared constructor the HTTP adapter uses.
  - `plugin-webhook/cancel` (`channels:execute`): cancels an in-flight dispatch on the same connection; the dispatch response stays authoritative.
  - `plugin-webhook/routes` (`channels:read`): current route owners, for diagnostics.
  - Local IPC only: an exhaustive transport match refuses all three on WSS with FORBIDDEN and an audit record.
  - Dispatch runs in a task spawned from the dispatcher like `session/prompt`, so the serial read loop stays live for cancel and other requests. Each connection tracks in-flight dispatches for cancel and duplicate-id checks and holds at most 1024 until their responses are queued; the next gets `queue_full`. Connection close and daemon reload cancel in-flight work and send nothing; shutdown joins the tasks and never waits on a full writer queue.
  - The daemon registry hands the generation's ingress to the RPC context, and the daemon always builds one ingress.
- **Scope boundary:** No gateway change (the forwarder is the next PR). No new principal or credential. Runtime edits stay within the #11317 row: `src/rpc/{dispatch,context}.rs`, `src/daemon/{registry,mod}.rs`, and the denial message keys in `locales/en/cli.ftl`. The new config field also updates `PluginChannelConfig` literals inside the test modules of `src/plugin_runtime.rs` and `src/tools/mod.rs` (mechanical, test-only). The grant selector and config fields live in `zeroclaw-api` and `zeroclaw-config`.
- **Blast radius:** runtime RPC dispatcher (new arms, per-connection state, shutdown join), daemon registry, `RpcContext` (all 14 literals), the OpenRPC document (regenerated), `zeroclaw-rpc-proto` (8 wire types, 3 `Method` variants), `zeroclaw-api` (route listing, the `allowed_channels` selector), `zeroclaw-infra` (route listing, `dispatch_admitted`), `zeroclaw-config` (three fields).
- **Follow-ups from the review, not in this PR:** one local-only gate shared with `file/upload/*`, with a per-method "local only" classification `xtask` can emit (#11566), and `schemars` bounds on the dispatch wire fields so the OpenRPC document states them (#11567).
- **Merge-order note:** #11186 adds `TransportKind::Inproc`. The transport match here is deliberately exhaustive, so whichever of this PR and #11186 lands second must add the `Inproc` arm (refused, with its test; #11322 carries both). #11289 replaces the free-text `AuthDenied::forbidden(message)` with `RpcDenialReason`: whichever of this PR and #11289 lands second needs variants for this PR's four refusals (for example `local_ipc_only`, `channel_not_granted`, `channel_refuses_injected_webhooks`, `agent_refuses_injected_webhooks`) and the updated audit assertions, which now read `reason` as a stable identifier.
- **Linked issue(s):** Related #11003. Related #7432. Related #11000. Related #11001. Depends on #12244 (supersedes #11165, closed 2026-11-05; this branch still carries #11165's head `19e41b09fa` until the restack).

### What this does, simply

The daemon already answers RPC calls from local clients such as zerocode. This PR teaches it three more calls so a separate web gateway can say "here is a webhook request for this plugin URL, what should I answer?" and get back the same result the in-process gateway gets today. Only local connections may use them, and only callers allowed to operate the specific channels they ask for. An operator can also switch the path off for one channel, or for one agent, in config, whatever access a caller has.

## Testing (required)

### How you can test (when useful)

- **Reviewer testing requested?** Yes, optional.
- **Interface(s) exercised:** local RPC socket.
- **Steps to run:** start a daemon with a configured channel plugin that claims a webhook path, then over `socat READLINE UNIX-CONNECT:<data_dir>/daemon.sock` send `initialize`, then `{"jsonrpc":"2.0","method":"plugin-webhook/routes","params":{},"id":2}` and a `plugin-webhook/dispatch` for that path.
- **Expected on this branch (after):** routes lists the owner; dispatch answers `{"outcome":"ack"}` or the plugin's reply.
- **Prior behavior on `master` (before):** `METHOD_NOT_FOUND`.

### How I tested

- **CI checks relied on and why they cover this change:** `Test` (runtime `rpc::` and `daemon::` suites, proto tests), `Parallel Runtime Test` (runtime/channels interference), `Installer Drift` (OpenRPC `--check`), plugin legs for the ingress and gateway parity.
- **Known CI coverage gap, if any:** Windows named pipes are not exercised by a required job.
- **Commands run and tail output:** (head `b5d9ebd577`: this PR with #11319 `98e1666b31` and #11165 `ec00bf0a12` merged, on master `a0f70b7925`; macOS arm64, rustc 1.98.0)

```text
$ cargo test --locked -p zeroclaw-runtime --lib rpc::
test result: FAILED. 784 passed; 1 failed   (configure_refuses_an_incarnation_replaced_under_the_lock, see below)
$ cargo test --locked -p zeroclaw-runtime --lib rpc::dispatch::tests::plugin_webhook   (x3)
test result: ok. 26 passed   (includes plugin_webhook_dispatch_reaches_only_granted_channels and plugin_webhook_dispatch_honors_channel_and_agent_refusal)
$ cargo test --locked -p zeroclaw-runtime --lib daemon::
test result: FAILED. 101 passed; 1 failed; 1 ignored   (a_live_config_write_reaches_the_daemon_pricing_refresher_without_a_reload, see below)
$ cargo test --locked -p zeroclaw-api -p zeroclaw-infra --lib ; cargo test --locked -p zeroclaw-config --lib
ok. 295 passed, ok. 335 passed ; ok. 1760 passed   (channel selector, allowed_channels validation, accept_injected_webhooks defaults, dispatch_admitted)
$ cargo test --locked -p zeroclaw-rpc-proto ; cargo test --locked -p zeroclaw-rpc-proto --features schema-export
ok. 29 passed ; ok. 32 passed
$ cargo run --locked -p xtask --bin generate -- openrpc --check ; cargo test --locked -p xtask openrpc
openrpc: docs/book/src/architecture/zeroclaw-rpc.openrpc.json is in sync ; ok
$ cargo test --locked -p zeroclaw-gateway --features plugins-wasm --lib ; --test golden_frames plugin_webhook
ok. 653 passed ; ok. 5 passed (fixtures unchanged)
$ cargo test --locked -p zeroclaw-runtime --features plugins-wasm-cranelift --lib plugin_runtime:: ; cargo test --locked --features plugins-wasm-cranelift --test plugin_channel_runtime_e2e ; --test architecture

The parallel runtime gate script (three passes each of the runtime suite, 6191 tests, and the channels suite, 2058 tests, at 16 threads) green on the first run.
- **If any command was intentionally skipped, why:** `RUSTFLAGS="-D warnings" cargo check --no-default-features --features agent-runtime` fails on six pre-existing dead-code helpers in `src/main.rs` whose only caller is gateway-gated; unrelated, reproduces on master.

## Security & Privacy Impact (required)

- New permissions, capabilities, or file system access scope? Yes: `Resource::Channels` gains its first RPC consumers, scoped to named channel instances through `allowed_channels`. `admin`, including the same-uid shared operator, reaches every route; any other profile reaches only the instances it names. `accept_injected_webhooks = false` on a channel instance or an agent refuses the path whatever the grants. Plugins still verify vendor signatures.
- New external network calls? No
- Secrets / tokens / credentials handling changed? No (headers pass through to the guest as they do over HTTP)
- PII, real identities, or personal data in diff, tests, fixtures, or docs? No
- Prompt injection or untrusted model-visible text introduced/changed? No new path: dispatched messages enter the same plugin channel listener as HTTP webhooks.
- If any `Yes`, describe the risk and mitigation: local IPC only (WSS refused with an audit record); grants checked at admission; the core enforces the shared request bounds, so a local caller bypassing the gateway's rate limit still cannot exceed them; 1024 in-flight dispatches per connection; no diagnostic detail in results.

## Compatibility (required)

- Backward compatible? Yes (additive methods). Builds with plugins but without the gateway now build the ingress, so webhook-capable plugin channels validate and publish their route claims instead of activating poll-only. A worker that drops its reply after the caller cancelled now reports `cancelled` instead of `unavailable`.
- Config / env / CLI surface changed? Yes, additive: `[permission_profiles.<name>] allowed_channels` (default empty, so a profile with `channels` grants but no selector reaches no channel; nothing consumed `channels` before this PR), and `accept_injected_webhooks` on `[channels.plugin.<alias>]` and `[agents.<alias>]` (default `true`).
- Rust/MSRV/toolchain floor changed? No

## Rollback (required for medium/high-risk PRs)

- **Fast rollback command/path:** `git revert <sha>`; the methods disappear (`METHOD_NOT_FOUND`) and nothing persisted changes.
- **Feature flags or config toggles:** remove `channels:execute` or the channel from a profile's `allowed_channels` to deny dispatch; `accept_injected_webhooks = false` on a channel instance or agent closes the path whatever the grants; `plugins.enabled = false` publishes no routes.
- **Observable failure symptoms:** `RPC authorization denied` records for `plugin-webhook/*`, with reasons naming the channel or agent that refused; `queue_full` answers at the per-connection cap; WARN `plugin_webhook_dispatch_notification` for notification-form dispatches.

milestone.title: v0.9.0
milestone.description:
v0.9.0 prioritizes opt-in OIDC dashboard sign-in, principal isolation, schema V4 and a CLI-only build option.

The standard build keeps the working in-process dashboard. Sign-in stays off by default, preserving the existing pairing flow. Release gates are real-provider sign-in evidence; the five principal-isolation repairs (#11234, #11220, #11225, #11230, #11266, with #11198 tracked); schema V4 (#11218); and a build-time CLI-only option that omits gateway/web assets and directs dashboard users to the standard build.

Scoped dashboard chat has a November 3 go/no-go, with sign-in alone as the fallback. November 10 is the earliest target, subject to the gates, not a committed date.

Standalone zeroclaw-gw, full gateway IPC route/parity work, cross-process webhook handling and two-process desktop packaging move to v0.9.x. Channel listeners remain in core under existing documented exceptions. These deferrals do not complete the remaining gateway roadmap.

Source of truth: #7432 (https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/issues/7432), current release allocation. Existing implementation trackers keep their detailed work. Feature acceptance, current-head review/CI, recorded placement decisions and the v0.8.7-tag hold on breaking work remain in force.

prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master` (`03b29bcc68`). **Depends on #11320** and **#11186** (`zeroclaw-rpc-client` and the gateway's core RPC seam). The branch merges #11320 at its current head `864b58d76e` (with #11319 `c352574198`, #11339 and #11165 `19e41b09fa` beneath it) and #11186 at its current head `ed92285a87` (restacked 2026-10-23 and refreshed 2026-10-29, see below); their commits show in the diff until they land. Review this PR's own commits: `d15729ebff` (the forwarder), `5926ddde14` (docs), `c02e5c0bac` (the in-process seam tests get a TUI signing key), `7702fe138c` (the forwarder's failure records keep the webhook path out) `c02417bfac` (change filter path restored after the restack) and `6d8ed835a8` (the forwarder ends a connection the daemon has stopped recognising, so the link dials again; from Greptile's review); `de5cd570ab` (the connector fix) is superseded by #11186's `535b43829a`.
- **Status of 2026-11-08:** #11186 and #11165 were closed on 2026-11-05 in favour of #12244, which carries the client and in-process transport as `492ef50e4b` and the `zeroclaw-rpc-proto` extraction as `f25e96ea39`. Its `core_rpc.rs` is #11186's seam plus 37 lines for the dashboard chat, and this branch extends the same seam with the local-socket dial, so the restack resolves that file three-way against `ed92285a87`. This branch still merges #11186's head `ed92285a87` and, through #11320, #11165's `19e41b09fa`; it restacks after #11317, #11339, #11319, #11320 and #12244 have landed, refreshing onto master at that point (the four commits master has gained since `641b766030` merge cleanly today). Head `72accde7d3` is unchanged by this note.
- **Refresh of 2026-10-29 (`fee8af1cb8`):** merges #11320's new head, which brings master `5a51398dd5` (the one `rpc/types.rs` conflict against it was master editing a doc comment inside the block #11165 moved into `zeroclaw-rpc-proto`; the moved-out file stays and the doc line now lives on the proto copy) and #11320's admission re-check: the daemon re-resolves the forwarder's live grants at admission instead of trusting the binding its dispatch task copied, so a revoked or narrowed caller is refused and the forwarder answers 503 for it, as for any core refusal. No change to this PR's own slice.
- **Second refresh of 2026-10-29 (`6d8ed835a8`):** merges #11320's `864b58d76e` (`2f1fa249a4`: a rename or delete over the socket now refuses a cascade outside the caller's config write grants; the forwarder connects as the shared operator and is not affected) and adds `6d8ed835a8`, from Greptile's review of this PR: when a policy change removes or revokes the gateway's identity while its connection is open, the daemon keeps the socket and answers `AUTH_REQUIRED`, and the link redialed only after a close, so webhooks stayed 503 after the operator restored access. The forwarder now ends the connection at the first such answer (record `plugin_webhook_core_identity_lost`) and the redial is accepted once access is back, or refused into the slow backoff while it is not; `FORBIDDEN` stays on the connection. Two tests: the close seen from both sides, and the whole sequence over a local socket ending with a webhook served on the new connection.
- **Refresh of 2026-11-02 (`9138333811`):** merges master `03b29bcc68`, which carries the Wasmtime 48.0.8 bump for RUSTSEC-2026-0420 to 0424 (#12129) and so clears the `Security` job for this branch. The one conflict was the workspace `members` line in the root `Cargo.toml`: this branch adds the `zeroclaw-rpc-proto` and `zeroclaw-rpc-client` members and master appends `tests/fixtures/runtime-composition-consumer`; both kept. No change to this PR's own slice.
- **Second refresh of 2026-11-03 (`364014755c`):** merges #11320's `d4517a7845` (`a0425fbf4c`, `4a099711c1`, `364014755c`), which records the `zeroclaw-rpc-proto` edge in master's new runtime-composition policy and makes the two in-flight-cap tests hold the log writer's test lock, so their 1024-dispatch bursts cannot drop the persisted-log tests' records under the parallel runtime gate; both failures showed on this PR's run too. It also takes the cascade refusal's message from the catalog, from Greptile's review there. No change to this PR's own slice.
- **Third refresh of 2026-11-03 (`6d1b319992`):** merges master `ee8a753dff`, which is #11318 squash-merged, so #11318's changes no longer show in this diff. The seven conflicts were all in files #11318 added or edited (`.github/workflows/README.md`, `ci.yml`, `golden_frames.rs`, the plugin backend change filter and its test, the Windows scope test, and `ci-and-actions.md`): master's version of each is exactly #11318's final content, and this branch's version is that content plus the lines #11319, #11320 and this PR add on top of it, so every conflict resolves to this branch's side. The only master-only text in a conflicted file, the new Desktop App Check section of `ci-and-actions.md`, merged automatically. The rest of the merge is master's own work since `03b29bcc68` (#11054, #11739, #11270, #12003).
- **Fourth refresh of 2026-11-03 (`ca036570ca`):** merges master `c54e002a83`, which brings #11965 (the opt-in OIDC dashboard sign-in: a new gateway `dashboard_session` module whose layer wraps every route and is a no-op unless `[gateway.dashboard_sign_in]` names a provider), #11234 (queued session ownership judged by the current authority, in `rpc/dispatch.rs` and `rpc/session.rs` next to this stack's additions), #11225 (memory owner preserved through delegation), #12219 (the quality-gate change detectors fetch only the base commit; this PR's two CI additions are steps inside existing jobs, not detectors, so nothing here needed the same treatment), #12212, #11624, #10873 and #12084. The one conflict was the module list in `crates/zeroclaw-gateway/src/lib.rs`, where this branch adds `pub mod core_rpc;` and #11965 adds `pub mod dashboard_session;` on the same line; the resolution keeps both. Everything else, including #11965's dashboard layer inside `run_gateway_with_plugin_webhooks`, merged by itself: the merged file differs from master by exactly #11965's change and from the previous head by exactly this stack's change.
- **Refresh of 2026-11-05 (`6ce12cff6f`):** merges master `72573d87c0`, which brings #11964 (a daemon task retires remote sessions whose client has been gone past `wss.orphaned_session_timeout_secs`), #12232 (principal-unaware tools and SOP execution withheld from non-admin principals), #12213 (the pairing guard reads the live `[gateway.pairing_dashboard]` limits), #12251, #11266, #11218 (retired config keys migrate at schema version 4), #11272, #12253 and #12243. The one conflict was in `crates/zeroclaw-runtime/src/daemon/mod.rs`, where this stack binds the in-process connector to the RPC context and #11964 spawns the orphan-retirement task at the same point, each under its own `if let Some(ctx) = rpc_ctx.as_ref()`; the resolution keeps both blocks, the bind first. The other twelve files both sides touched merged by themselves, and the merged daemon module differs from master by exactly master's own change to it and from the previous head by exactly this stack's change.
- **Fix of 2026-11-05 (`59bbee5780`):** the Test jobs at `6ce12cff6f` failed one test from master's #11218, `migration::tests::v3_agent_fields_are_the_current_agent_fields`, which keeps the migration's list of current agent keys, `V3_AGENT_FIELDS`, in step with `AliasedAgentConfig` and treats a listed key under `[agents.<alias>]` as evidence of the V3 layout. `accept_injected_webhooks`, which #11320 adds to the agent config, was missing from the list; this head was the first in the stack to carry both. The fix is #11320's `0998d76a7f`, which names the key there (V2 agents never had it, so an agent holding it reads as V3 like every other agent key), and this branch takes it by merging #11320's refreshed head (`9e4c5c086c`, its own clean merge of the same master, plus the fix): one added line against the previous head.
- **Second fix of 2026-11-05 (`61c4dcb987`):** merges #11320's `ac9c10fe25`, from Greptile's review there: the five `INVALID_PARAMS` refusals of `plugin-webhook/dispatch` (request_id bounds, request_id already in flight, oversized `body_b64`, non-base64 `body_b64`, and the request constructor's refusal) now come from the Fluent catalog as `rpc-plugin-webhook-request-id-invalid`, `rpc-plugin-webhook-request-id-in-flight`, `rpc-plugin-webhook-body-too-large`, `rpc-plugin-webhook-body-not-base64` and `rpc-plugin-webhook-request-invalid`, wording unchanged. This forwarder keeps only the code of a core error and never relays its message to the sender, so its answers are untouched.
- **Refresh of 2026-11-07 (`3a544393b3`, `e4e847bdf8`):** merges master `641b766030`, which brings #12239 (current authority held through session effects), #11149 (cron approval and authority enforced at the write across RPC, tools and token revocation), #12157, #12233, #12114, #12273 (vodozemac 0.11.2 for RUSTSEC-2026-0445 and -0451), #12254, #12179, #12177, #12162, #12274 and a batch of test-only and docs commits. The one conflict was in `crates/zeroclaw-runtime/src/rpc/types.rs`: #12239 extends the doc comment of `SessionRunOnceParams` (the grants it requires and what a refused cleanup reports), inside the block of wire types this branch no longer defines there because #11165 moved them to `zeroclaw-rpc-proto` and the module re-exports them. The runtime file keeps this branch's side, and the three doc lines are carried to the struct's definition in `crates/zeroclaw-rpc-proto/src/types.rs`, so master's wording survives the move. The OpenRPC contract document is generated from those doc comments, so `e4e847bdf8` regenerates `docs/book/src/architecture/zeroclaw-rpc.openrpc.json` with `cargo generate openrpc` and the `--check` step passes again. The other eight files both sides touched merged by themselves. This branch then merges #11320's refreshed head `01db9e82be` (`72accde7d3`), which carries the same resolution and regeneration, so that merge changes no file.
- **Refresh of 2026-11-08 (`93c9713bde`, `066a82e86a`):** merges #11320's refreshed head `f7709a87c3`, which brings #11319's `988d9bffe4` and master `7666a52abf` (the five commits since `641b766030`: #12270, the relay serving a daemon's dashboard at a per-node host; #11406, macOS broad roots refused in the filesystem channel; #11268; #10502; #12286). Git reported no conflicts: the `src/main.rs` resolution against #12270 and the relay dashboard test fix come from #11319, and the CI README row from #11320. The gateway crate still failed to compile, because the automatic merge of `crates/zeroclaw-gateway/src/lib.rs` interleaved two additions made at the same spot: #12270 adds `with_dashboard_ingress` and a `DashboardFeed` type right after `GatewaySupervision::new`, and this branch adds `standalone` and `forwarding_to_daemon` there, so this branch's constructors landed inside `impl DashboardFeed` and `forwarding_to_daemon` did not set the new `dashboard_ingress` field. `066a82e86a` moves them back into `impl GatewaySupervision` and sets the field to `None` (the standalone gateway serves no relay dashboard ingress); the `DashboardFeed` block is byte-identical to master's and the supervision block is this branch's plus master's builder and the two field lines.
- **Restack of 2026-10-23 (`bb5eb8a1ca`, `c02417bfac`, `54dc89c97f`):** #11165 and #11186 were refreshed onto master by their author on October 22, so this branch merges #11320's restacked head (which carries #11165 `19e41b09fa` and #11319) and then #11186 `ed92285a87`, and is mergeable with master again. The hand-resolved files against #11320 were the CI workflow registry, the CI guide, the plugin backend change filter (each side's lines kept; the filter's own test caught one path the first pass dropped, restored in `c02417bfac`), the root `Cargo.toml` (the rpc-client member, dependency, dev-dependencies and the two-process test target on top of #11320's) and the proto boundary test, taken from #11186's head, which already reconciles #11165's new wording with the rpc-client checks. Against #11186 only `inproc.rs` conflicted, and this branch takes #11186's file: its `535b43829a` is the connector fix this PR carried as `de5cd570ab`, so that commit is now redundant here and ownership sits in #11186 as asked, and its `e4bd5853e9` treats the in-process connection as remote in every local-only check, alongside this PR's `plugin-webhook/*` refusal arm.
- **Fix for #11186 on top of the merge** (`fix(rpc): release the in-process connector's context when its generation retires`): the daemon hands the gateway a clone of the generation's `InprocConnector` through its reload controls, and the connector kept the generation's `RpcContext` (its sessions and their lifecycle leases) until the last clone dropped. With #10621, a reload waits for that state to drain before it releases process ownership, so `reload_waits_for_detached_write_before_releasing_process_ownership` failed 3 of 3 runs on the merge. Sealing admission now releases the context in the same critical section, `bind` leaves a sealed connector unbound, and a `connect` waiting for a bind gives up once the generation is sealed. Two new connector tests cover it, and the daemon test passes. It belongs in #11186: I asked for it there (https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/pull/11186#issuecomment-5942108575; it cherry-picks cleanly onto `84f31b29cb`), and this branch drops it once #11186 has it.
- **Audacity88's review (both blockers):**
  - **Webhook paths stay out of failure logs.** Some vendors use an unguessable webhook path as their shared secret, and log records are persisted as written. `7702fe138c` drops the path from the five `plugin_webhook_core_*` records, which keep their error key and code. `core_failure_records_keep_a_secret_path_out` sends a secret-shaped path through each core failure and asserts no record contains it. The daemon-side part belongs to #11319 (`fc5f3e95b9`: the ingress's route-closed, reply-dropped and worker-answer records, plus the gateway's `plugin_webhook_request_invalid` record). It arrives here through #11320. The gateway's `plugin_webhook_rate_limited` record still logs the path, as on master.
  - **Removed-binding admission.** Merging #11320 at `d6ef5dc0af` (`853e49dfab`) brings its fail-closed fix `fcf4f6121c`: a route whose `[channels.plugin.<alias>]` binding a live config write removed is refused until reload retires it. #11320's `plugin_webhook_dispatch_refuses_a_published_route_once_its_binding_is_removed` proves that interval, and the forwarder answers that refusal 503 (`core_rpc_errors_map_to_503`). The two-process test still checks the state after reload.
- **#10621 and the standalone gateway:** a running daemon now owns its config state exclusively, so `zeroclaw gateway start` on the daemon's config dir exits with `config lifecycle is already owned`, on master too. Next to a daemon, the standalone gateway therefore runs on a config dir of its own and names the daemon's socket with `ZEROCLAW_SOCKET`. The gateway API guide documents this, and the two-process test runs that way.
- **Channel scoping from #11320:** the forwarder connects as the shared operator, which is `admin`, so `allowed_channels` does not narrow it. A channel instance or agent with `accept_injected_webhooks = false` still refuses its dispatches: that path answers 503, logged `plugin_webhook_core_refused`, while the connection stays up and other paths keep forwarding. A connection the daemon has stopped recognising is different: its `AUTH_REQUIRED` answer ends the connection (`6d8ed835a8`, logged `plugin_webhook_core_identity_lost`) so the link dials again. The gateway API guide lists both.
- **What changed and why:**
  - The standalone `zeroclaw gateway` is the separate gateway process that exists today. Its `/plugin/{path}` route used an empty in-process route table and answered 404 for every path. It now forwards each request to the running daemon over the local RPC socket through `plugin-webhook/dispatch`, so channel-plugin webhooks work across the process boundary. The daemon-supervised gateway keeps calling the core ingress in process.
  - Forwarding: shared request validation, base64 body under a process-unique `request_id`, strict result decoding with the reply bound re-checked, the same `outcome_response` mapping as the in-process path, and a best-effort `plugin-webhook/cancel` when the HTTP request is dropped. The daemon decides 404; while it is unreachable every path answers 503.
  - Daemon identity: on Unix the gateway forwards only to a socket whose peer uid equals its own effective uid, checked before any frame is sent. On Windows, where pipe names share one namespace and the server cannot be verified yet, forwarding stays off and the route keeps answering 404.
  - `core_rpc`: one maintain loop serves the in-process and local dialers; the forwarder owns its own `CoreRpc`, separate from the extension other routes can reach.
  - `plugin-webhook/*` are refused on in-process RPC connections as well as WSS (the arm the transport match needs once #11186 is in).
  - A two-process test runs the real daemon and the real standalone gateway binaries.
- **Scope boundary:** No change to the supervised gateway's behavior, to vendor webhook handlers, WIT, or config. No gateway service identity (the standalone gateway authenticates by peer credentials; see Security). The standalone `zeroclaw-gw` binary is #11002.
- **Blast radius:** standalone `zeroclaw gateway` (start, restart, bare); gateway `core_rpc` seam from #11186; RPC transport refusal; CI plugin legs and path filters.
- **Changes to #11186's in-process seam (for its author):** after a lost connection the loop waits a backoff before redialing (it redialed immediately); logs only on state transitions with error keys `core_rpc_{lost,unreachable,refused}` (and `core_rpc_untrusted_peer` for the local dialer); a FORBIDDEN refusal logs at INFO; `CoreRpc` stores a `CoreLink` (Disconnected, Connected, Refused) with `client()` and `is_connected()` unchanged; new public `CoreLink`, `CoreRpc::link()`, and Unix-only `attach_local` and `daemon_endpoint`. Refusals still end the in-process loop. `GatewaySupervision::standalone(readiness, &config)` returns a `Result`, because it builds the live config authority master now requires.
- **Follow-ups from the review, not in this PR:** route `run_gateway` through `GatewaySupervision::standalone` or make it test-only, so an embedder does not get the old unrouted `/plugin/{path}` (#11568); a scoped service identity for the forwarder's connection, tracked in #11569 under #11002.
- **Merge-order note:** this PR carries the `TransportKind::Inproc` refusal arm and test that #11320's exhaustive match needs with #11186. If #11186 lands before #11320, move them into #11320. The arm must keep refusing `Inproc` with FORBIDDEN, never treat it like `Local`. #11289 replaces the free-text `AuthDenied::forbidden(message)` this arm uses, so if #11289 lands first the arm needs its `RpcDenialReason` (the variants are listed in #11320).
- **Linked issue(s):** Related #11003 (acceptance: separate-process flow). Related #7432 (G4 transport; vendor migration stays under #8850). Related #11000. Related #11002. Depends on #12244 (supersedes #11186, closed 2026-11-05; this branch still carries #11186's head `ed92285a87` until the restack).

### What this does, simply

You can run the web gateway on its own with `zeroclaw gateway`. Until now, webhooks meant for channel plugins did not work there, because the plugin routes live in the daemon. Now that gateway passes each plugin webhook to the daemon over the local socket and returns the daemon's answer, exactly as the built-in gateway would. If the daemon is down, senders get 503 so they retry, and nothing is forwarded to a socket owned by another user.

## Testing (required)

### How you can test (when useful)

- **Reviewer testing requested?** Yes, optional (Unix).
- **Interface(s) exercised:** gateway HTTP (`/plugin/{path}`) plus the local RPC socket.
- **Setup / preconditions:** a config with an installed channel plugin that claims a webhook path and an enabled agent routing it, plus an empty second config dir for the gateway (for example `~/.zeroclaw-gateway`).
- **Steps to run:** `zeroclaw daemon --port 0`, then `ZEROCLAW_SOCKET="$HOME/.zeroclaw/data/daemon.sock" zeroclaw --config-dir "$HOME/.zeroclaw-gateway" gateway start -p 18080`, then `curl -i -X POST http://127.0.0.1:18080/plugin/<path> ...` with the plugin's signature header; stop the daemon and repeat.
- **Expected on this branch (after):** the plugin's normal answer while the daemon runs; 503 `webhook unavailable` while it is down; the answer again after it restarts; after a policy change that removes the gateway's identity, 503 until the operator restores it, then the answer again at the next redial.

## Security & Privacy Impact (required)

- New permissions, capabilities, or file system access scope? Yes: under the default policy (`security.trust_daemon_uid = true`) the standalone gateway authenticates by peer credentials as the shared operator, which holds every grant. Only the `/plugin/{path}` route uses that connection; it is separate from the core RPC extension other routes can reach.
- New external network calls? No (local socket only)
- Secrets / tokens / credentials handling changed? Yes: webhook headers, including vendor signature headers, now cross the local socket to the daemon. Mitigation: on Unix the gateway verifies the socket's peer uid equals its own before sending anything; on Windows forwarding is off until the pipe server can be verified.
- PII, real identities, or personal data in diff, tests, fixtures, or docs? No
- Prompt injection or untrusted model-visible text introduced/changed? No new path: messages reach the same plugin channel listener as before.
- If any `Yes`, describe the risk and mitigation: a publicly bound standalone gateway now exposes the daemon's plugin routes on that listener (same exposure as the supervised gateway on that address). The connection appears as a TUI client (`/api/tuis`) and keeps an `--ephemeral` daemon alive. A refused redial writes a daemon audit record, backed off from 30 seconds to 5 minutes. `zeroclaw gateway restart` first POSTs `/admin/shutdown` to the configured address, which stops a supervised gateway listening there (unchanged, now documented).

## Compatibility (required)

- Backward compatible? Yes for the supervised gateway. Standalone gateway: `/plugin/{path}` changes from 404 for every path to forwarding (Unix); 503 for every path while the daemon is unreachable or the socket belongs to another user; 503 `plugin_webhook_core_unsupported` against an older daemon without the method. New error keys: `plugin_webhook_core_{unavailable,refused,identity_lost,unsupported,unexpected,timeout}`, `core_rpc_{lost,unreachable,refused,untrusted_peer}`, `plugin_webhook_forwarding_disabled` (Windows). Rust API: `GatewaySupervision::standalone(readiness, &config)`; `zeroclaw-rpc-proto` is an optional gateway dependency behind `plugins-wasm`.
- Config / env / CLI surface changed? No new keys. The standalone gateway resolves the daemon socket like other local clients (`ZEROCLAW_SOCKET` or `<data_dir>/daemon.sock`); next to a running daemon it runs on its own config dir, so it needs `ZEROCLAW_SOCKET`.
- Rust/MSRV/toolchain floor changed? No

## Rollback (required for medium/high-risk PRs)

- **Fast rollback command/path:** `git revert <sha>`; the standalone gateway returns to answering 404 for plugin routes.
- **Feature flags or config toggles:** stop the daemon, or build without `plugins-wasm`; `security.trust_daemon_uid = false` without a `[users]` entry for the gateway's uid makes the daemon refuse the connection (webhooks then answer 503).
- **Observable failure symptoms:** `plugin_webhook_core_*` and `core_rpc_*` error keys in the gateway log; 503 bursts on `/plugin/*` from a standalone gateway; `RPC authorization denied` records for the gateway's connection in the daemon log.

milestone.title: v0.9.0
milestone.description:
v0.9.0 prioritizes opt-in OIDC dashboard sign-in, principal isolation, schema V4 and a CLI-only build option.

The standard build keeps the working in-process dashboard. Sign-in stays off by default, preserving the existing pairing flow. Release gates are real-provider sign-in evidence; the five principal-isolation repairs (#11234, #11220, #11225, #11230, #11266, with #11198 tracked); schema V4 (#11218); and a build-time CLI-only option that omits gateway/web assets and directs dashboard users to the standard build.

Scoped dashboard chat has a November 3 go/no-go, with sign-in alone as the fallback. November 10 is the earliest target, subject to the gates, not a committed date.

Standalone zeroclaw-gw, full gateway IPC route/parity work, cross-process webhook handling and two-process desktop packaging move to v0.9.x. Channel listeners remain in core under existing documented exceptions. These deferrals do not complete the remaining gateway roadmap.

Source of truth: #7432 (https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/issues/7432), current release allocation. Existing implementation trackers keep their detailed work. Feature acceptance, current-head review/CI, recorded placement decisions and the v0.8.7-tag hold on breaking work remain in force.

prs.title: feat(runtime): add durable task lifecycle foundation for Goal Mode [Goal V1 proposal 1/12]
prs.body:
## Summary

> **V1 foundation proposal 1/12.** This supplies task/storage contracts, not a complete Goal feature or a request to merge. Current-head required GitHub CI passed. The local full-workspace Cargo test remains failed: its five failures were also reproduced on the exact upstream comparison revision. Neither result erases the other or the historical full-stack limitations below.

Selected slice **01**, head `dad3a99071bfe4d2d0a17124f93ad2350d4670c1`, compared with pinned upstream `6a99c3dee4440cf7d052e5bb61836adcf1085582`. This update merges that official upstream revision without rewriting published history. The 15-path Goal foundation delta is unchanged in substance; upstream conversation-binding, session-store safety, OIDC/plugin and CI changes remain upstream-owned. The first PR has no predecessor. Do not enable an incomplete Goal implementation.

- **Base branch:** `master` (all contributions).
- **What changed and why:**
  - Move the canonical task types into `zeroclaw-api`, preserving runtime re-exports and enum variants; add serde-defaulted session/epoch fields.
  - Replace unguarded Goal creation/pause/resume APIs with exact task/session/epoch-guarded transitions, pending-operation settlement and accounting-state contracts; generic task APIs reject Goal creation and session-Goal mutations.
  - Converge existing task databases transactionally to schema 13, including session uniqueness/fencing triggers and failure classification of invalid legacy Goal rows.
  - Reconcile dead-owner Goals before generic startup recovery; retain terminal session-Goal history during agent deletion and refuse the control-plane cleanup step while a live session Goal exists. That refusal is reported as a cascade warning, not a rollback of the already-published agent deletion.
  - Add file-backed control-plane and task-type compatibility tests; propagate SQLite iteration errors rather than silently returning partial task/settlement lists.
- **Scope boundary:** First incremental slice of an unmerged proposal stack. No complete Goal workflow, user entrypoint, later configuration/commands, policy/execution crate, or enabled-rollout claim. The upstream merge preserves this foundation delta; this is not a correctness audit of all incoming upstream changes.
- **Blast radius:** Public Rust task/Goal registry interfaces, SQLite schema/recovery, generic mutation/error paths, agent deletion and ordinary delegate/peer/subagent producers. Public record/trait compatibility changes and one-way migration limits are detailed below.
- **Linked issue(s):** Related RFC #8303 and tracker #10341, not closing either.
  https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/issues/8303
  https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/issues/10341

### What this does, simply

The previous Goal registry did not bind its create/pause/resume operations to a durable session and execution epoch. This slice supplies those fences and the shared task/storage foundation so stale work cannot use ordinary task APIs to change a session Goal. It does not yet expose a complete Goal feature.

## Testing (required)

### How you can test (when useful)

- **Reviewer testing requested?** N/A — no user-reachable Goal entrypoint or task-store CLI has a meaningful manual A/B path in this foundation slice. File-backed integration tests exercise storage/recovery; no manual or live-session execution is claimed.

### How I tested

- **CI checks relied on and why they cover this change:** [Quality Gate run 39905108375](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/actions/runs/39905108375), attempt 1, passed on head `dad3a99071bfe4d2d0a17124f93ad2350d4670c1`. GitHub tested merge `9cf58a86c59c0fe3a7faf2e17d74ed7ff65166fb` against upstream `6a99c3dee4440cf7d052e5bb61836adcf1085582`; its tree `115fc31a9583896b3236697005dd7ef750977d18` equals the locally validated tree. Test, all repeated parallel runtime/channel runs, required Windows selection/recovery/service/build checks, lint, selected feature/platform lanes, Security and CI Required Gate passed. Earlier-head results remain historical, including the cancelled Windows selection and failed aggregate at `1b64f2d0`.
- **Known CI coverage gap, if any:** The terminal snapshot contains 46 successful checks and 10 skips, not 56 passes. Skips follow the unchanged path/event/opt-in conditions: targeted Windows Clippy, docs, Nix hash/evaluation, crates.io preflight, relay smoke, PR benchmarks, master-push debounce and the two advisory Windows jobs (no `ci:windows` opt-in). The required Windows jobs did execute and pass. The local full workspace run remains FAIL, as detailed below. No complete Goal controller, verifier, surface adapter or enabled-rollout behavior exists in this slice. Core/CODEOWNERS review and the scoped runtime exception remain outstanding.
- **Commands run and tail output:** Local macOS validation on `dad3a99071bfe4d2d0a17124f93ad2350d4670c1`, Rust/Cargo 1.98.1:

| Command / check | Observed result |
| --- | --- |

| `./scripts/ci/parallel_runtime_test_gate.sh` | PASS; all three runtime and all three channel repetitions, 16 threads |
| `./scripts/ci/rust_quality_gate.sh` | PASS; formatting, correctness Clippy and provider-dispatch scan |

| `cargo audit` (0.22.2) | PASS with six allowed unmaintained-package warnings |

```text

**Full exact-upstream comparison:** One unfiltered `cargo test --locked --workspace --exclude zeroclaw-desktop --no-fail-fast` run at upstream `6a99c3dee4440cf7d052e5bb61836adcf1085582` used the same toolchain and sealed environment as the candidate. No candidate-only or upstream-only failure was observed in this comparison. The three affected source files are byte-identical between upstream and this candidate. That proves reproduction, not the precise provider-test interleaving or timeout cause. These are automated local fixtures, not failures of live provider accounts. The original fail-fast run and both comparison runs remain FAIL; no test, assertion, deadline or gate was weakened.
https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/issues/11959

Earlier results at `1b64f2d0` remain historical and are not relabeled. In particular, the earlier seven unmatched signatures were not observed in the current unfiltered candidate run; their absence here is not proof of their exact cause or a claim that this integration repaired them.

**Warnings retained:** Candidate and upstream comparison logs include the Apple linker `__eh_frame` size/performance warning. Deny reports six unmatched skips and two unused-wrapper exceptions; audit allows six unmaintained-package warnings (anymap2, nostr-relay-pool, proc-macro-error, zbus_names, zvariant and zvariant_derive). The lockfile, manifests, `deny.toml` and `.cargo/audit.toml` equal the selected upstream revision. No advisory ignore or security-policy change is introduced.

- **Beyond CI, what did you manually verify?** Exact parent/tree identity, clean worktree, both-direction preservation of upstream and Goal-owned changes, and the complete public API/storage/recovery/caller diff. No manual runtime or live-room test, migration failpoint, or executed downgrade is claimed. Three direct guard cases remain untested: deletion with a pending operation, settlement with a mismatched operation ID/epoch, and limit updates on a terminal Goal. Their SQL predicates were inspected.
- **Visual interface evidence:** N/A — this foundation slice changes no supported user-visible interface state.
- **Tested revision, interface, and evidence path:** `dad3a99071bfe4d2d0a17124f93ad2350d4670c1`; local automated API/runtime/file-backed control-plane boundaries. Relevant literal output is above. No private local path is presented as a hosted attachment.
- **Screenshot or exact-output evidence:** N/A for presentation; command excerpts above are test evidence, not screenshots or final-interface proof.
- **Action or changed state and observed result:** Exact-task/session/epoch guards, schema convergence/reopen, valid-row preservation, generic-mutation rejection, boot reconciliation and ordinary producer compatibility exercised by the named tests.
- **If any command was intentionally skipped, why:** Documentation gates are not applicable because the PR has no docs delta against the selected upstream revision. Container-only `dev/ci.sh all` and strict `ci-all`/feature lanes were not locally run. The selected current-head remote feature/platform lanes passed; that is not a claim that every possible feature combination was tested. No enabled-rollout footprint or end-to-end Goal surface claim is made.

### Current remote CI — separate from the local Cargo failures

The [Test job](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/actions/runs/39905108375/job/120255167226) ran the workspace nextest suite: 19,360 passed and 42 skipped. Its separate hardware suite passed 189 with one skip; informational golden replay passed seven with five skips. The [parallel job](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/actions/runs/39905108375/job/120255292193) completed all three runtime runs (5,809 passed, zero failed, nine ignored each) and all three channel runs (2,015 passed, zero failed, two ignored each). Both job logs confirm checkout `9cf58a86`.

Literal excerpts, with ANSI colour and runner timestamp prefixes removed:

```text

test result: ok. 5809 passed; 0 failed; 9 ignored; 0 measured; 0 filtered out; finished in 36.11s

The one slow daemon-feedback test, two leaky child-process tests (MCP inherited stdout and ZeroCode inherited stderr), and the cache action's Node20-deprecation warning remain recorded. These Linux nextest/CI observations do not turn the failed local macOS Cargo run into a pass or establish the provider-fixture failure mechanisms. The earlier report-only risk workflow was cancelled under its per-PR `cancel-in-progress` policy and replaced by a successful current-head risk report; it is not a product-test failure or an unreported rerun. No validation gate was weakened.

## Security & Privacy Impact (required)

- New permissions, capabilities, or file system access scope? No — this diff adds task lifecycle/persistence behavior without granting a new permission or filesystem scope.
- New external network calls? No.
- Secrets / tokens / credentials handling changed? No.
- PII, real identities, or personal data in diff, tests, fixtures, or docs? No known real identity or secret is introduced; fixtures use test data.
- Prompt injection or untrusted model-visible text introduced/changed? No — this slice does not add a model-visible prompt path.

## Compatibility (required)

- Backward compatible? No for downstream Rust consumers of the changed record literals or `GoalTaskRegistry` trait. Existing task enum variants and runtime import paths remain compatible, and legacy serialized records load with defaults. The persistent migration is forward-only; it does not preserve invalid legacy Goals as resumable work.
- Config / env / CLI surface changed? No in this slice.
- Rust/MSRV/toolchain floor changed? No declared floor change in this slice.
- Exact upgrade steps:
  1. Update direct `TaskRecord` literals with `session_id`/`execution_epoch` (ordinary tasks use `None`/`0`). Update `GoalTaskRecord` literals with `pending_call_id`, `pending_call_epoch` and `accounting_state`, or use `..GoalTaskRecord::default()` where appropriate. No enum-match migration is needed. The new public `GoalAccountingState` and `GoalTransitionResult` distinguish accounting completeness from guarded transition outcomes.
  2. Migrate `GoalTaskRegistry` implementers/callers: `create_goal` becomes `create_or_replace_session_goal`; `pause_goal_task`/`resume_goal_task` become `pause_session_goal`/`resume_session_goal` with exact session/epoch arguments. `update_goal_objective` is removed without an in-place equivalent: objectives are supplied at creation, and replacement requires a fully settled terminal predecessor. The removed create/resume methods accepted a `continuation_context`; set it separately through the existing `set_continuation_context` method when migrating those callers. Implement the new current-session/terminal-reason queries, guarded finish/limit/disposal methods and pending-operation admit/settle methods. Handle `Applied`, `Stale` and `Missing` by reloading canonical state when required; do not bypass guards through the generic registry.
  3. Generic `TaskRegistry::create` now rejects every Goal. Generic heartbeat, progress, status/terminal, settlement, claim and timeout mutations reject session-bound Goals. Existing ordinary task producers still use that registry. Generic `reconcile_lost` returns `Ok(false)` for any Goal and the periodic sweep skips Goal rows, leaving their recovery to Goal-specific reconciliation. Task and settlement enumeration now propagates SQLite step errors instead of returning partial results; callers must handle those errors.
  4. Before first opening an existing control-plane database, preserve a consistent backup and validate against a disposable copy. The transaction converges released v8/v9/v10 and provisional schemas to v13, adds fields/triggers and replaces `idx_tasks_active_goal_context` with session-based uniqueness. Running/paused legacy Goals missing a session/objective or carrying an invalid epoch are marked failed (`legacy_goal_missing_session`, `legacy_goal_missing_objective`, `goal_invalid_execution_epoch`); this is not automatically undone by reverting the binary. No down-migration is supplied.
  5. Startup now reconciles Goal state before ordinary recovery: dead-owner running Goals without uncertain work pause; pending operations or incomplete accounting cause terminal classification under V1. Agent deletion retains terminal session-Goal rows; a running/paused session Goal refuses the whole control-plane deletion step and is reported as a cascade warning. Dispose of live session Goals through the guarded lifecycle before deleting the agent; no in-tree path re-runs the refused step after the config deletion.
  6. Rebuild downstream consumers and validate persisted-state handling before rollout. Static inspection of the older migration path indicates a v13 database produces a newer-schema warning and remains usable for ordinary tasks, but downgrade/rollback was not executed and is not certified safe. Retain the backup and do not assume a binary revert restores prior Goal state.

## Rollback (required for medium/high-risk PRs)

- **Fast rollback command/path:** Before rollout, retain a consistent database backup. If later slices are present, disable their Goal entry/admission and settle or fence/drain active work; preserve the current database and any usage ledger, then revert dependent slices in reverse stack order before reverting this slice. A binary revert does not reverse schema 13 or restore legacy Goals marked failed. No schema down-migration or executed downgrade guarantee is provided; assess recovery from the retained backup without discarding subsequent durable usage/state. Never drop schema or usage data as a shortcut.
- **Feature flags or config toggles:** No Goal configuration toggle is introduced in this slice; operational disablement must use the later owning entry/admission controls.
- **Observable failure symptoms:** Task registration, recovery, or terminal-state transitions fail or leave tasks unexpectedly eligible/stuck; inspect runtime task lifecycle errors and durable task status records. No live failure or rollback has been executed.

prs.title: feat(runtime): deferred bootstrap sections — addressable knowledge alongside the resident core
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master`
- **What changed and why.** Every resident byte of the bootstrap files costs context in every turn, yet much of AGENTS.md / TOOLS.md is procedure needed only per class of situation, not per turn. This PR adds an opt-in directive to any bootstrap markdown file:
  `<!-- defer: <workspace-relative path> | <one-line trigger> -->`
  The bootstrap loader replaces the directive with a single index line (`name → path — trigger`) in the system prompt; the content stays whole on disk and is pulled with the existing `file_read` when the situation matches. This is the same addressing pattern the architecture already uses twice — skills (name + description resident, body read on demand) and deferred MCP tool loading via `tool_search` — extended to the bootstrap layer.
- **Zero behavior change without directives** — files without them are byte-identical to today. No new config surface, no flags, pull-only (no automatic injection). Malformed directives stay verbatim in the prompt and warn once per process (`error_key: agent.bootstrap_defer_directive_invalid`).
- **Why this and not summarization.** The content is not rewritten, truncated, or lossy — this is an optimization of *residency*, not a compression of *meaning*. Deferred content also stays out of the prompt-budget floor (system messages + tool schemas), so a fixed budget holds more effective knowledge: resident core plus an address space the model dereferences on demand.
- **Scope boundary.** Pull-only by design; deterministic situation-matched injection (push) needs a situation model and is deliberately a separate design discussion. No heuristics — explicit directives only.
- **Blast radius.** One function in the bootstrap assembly path; content without directives is untouched. Context cost: one index line per directive.
- **Linked issues:** none. Related: the prompt-budget floor accounting proposed in #11910 (deferred content is naturally excluded until loaded).

### What this does, simply

An agent's knowledge is currently measured by what sits in its context window. This PR separates *resident* knowledge — what the agent is in every turn (values, style, boundaries) — from *addressable* knowledge: procedures and reference material it must have available but only needs when the situation arises. The context window becomes a cache; the address space becomes memory. One trigger line in the prompt replaces a page of procedure, and the page loads on demand — whole and unaltered.

## Testing (required)

- **Reviewer testing requested?** N/A — the change is prompt-assembly mechanics; the A/B below is reproduced by unit tests.
- **CI checks relied on and why they cover this change:** required CI (Test, Lint, Format, clippy) — touches `zeroclaw-runtime` prompt assembly, covered by the workspace matrix.
- **Known CI coverage gap, if any:** none known.
- **Commands run and tail output:**
  ```sh
  cargo fmt --all
  cargo check -p zeroclaw-runtime --tests        # Finished OK
  cargo test -p zeroclaw-runtime --lib defer     # 3 passed; 0 failed (39 total in file filter)
  cargo clippy -p zeroclaw-runtime --all-targets # no diagnostics in system_prompt.rs;
                                                 # 4 pre-existing errors in zeroclaw-config
                                                 # (dead_code/collapsible_if, local toolchain,
                                                 # present on clean origin/master, unrelated)
  ```
- **Beyond CI, what did you manually verify?** Prompt assembly behavior only (per scope): index line present, target body absent, surrounding text preserved, byte identity without directives, workspace-relative path resolution. Not verified: end-to-end model behavior (whether the model reliably pulls the referenced file in real turns) — observed in follow-up work.
- **Visual interface evidence:** N/A — no user-visible interface state changed.
- **Tested revision, interface, and evidence path:** branch head; evidence: unit tests in `crates/zeroclaw-runtime/src/agent/system_prompt.rs` (`defer_directive_*`).
- **If any command was intentionally skipped, why:** full-workspace `clippy --all-targets -D warnings` — not green on clean `origin/master` with the local toolchain (pre-existing `zeroclaw-config` lints); the changed crate is clean.

## Security & Privacy Impact (required)

- New permissions, capabilities, or file system access scope? **No** — the model already reads workspace files via `file_read`; the directive only decides what is resident in the prompt vs. on disk.
- New external network calls? **No**
- Secrets / tokens / credentials handling changed? **No** — deferred content is operator-authored workspace markdown, same trust domain as bootstrap files today.
- PII, real identities, or personal data in diff, tests, fixtures, or docs? **No**
- Prompt injection or untrusted model-visible text introduced/changed? **No** — directives are operator-authored; a malformed directive degrades to its literal text.

## Compatibility (required)

- Backward compatible? **Yes** — opt-in per directive; files without directives byte-identical.
- Config / env / CLI surface changed? **No**
- Rust/MSRV/toolchain floor changed? **No**
- Note: `crates/zeroclaw-runtime` is a holding crate whose guide asks for a recorded Core Team exception for new functionality. Flagging per the guide — happy to add the exception row or relocate per maintainer direction.

## Rollback

`git revert <sha>` — one file, additive code path, no migrations.
